The eleven-and-a-half-week siege ended after the Royalist defeat at Preston, and Charles Lucas and George Lisle were shot in the castle yard. Matthew Hopkins's witch trials filled Chelmsford gaol in the same decade, and Colchester served as the Eastern District garrison during the Napoleonic wars.
zh:
埃塞克斯是伦敦与北海之间的广阔沿海郡，科尔恩河、布莱克沃特河和泰晤士河河口切过海岸。潮湿牧场养育大群绵羊，道路和小港又把各地市场同伦敦连在一起。科尔切斯特的前身是卡姆洛杜努姆，先是铁器时代的一处王城，后来成为罗马在不列颠的第一座殖民城。60或61年，布狄卡率领的起义者焚毁此城；中世纪城镇保留了罗马城墙，一座宏伟的诺曼城堡又建在被毁的克劳狄神庙上方。切姆斯福德围绕卡恩河上的桥梁发展，1218年成为巡回法庭所在的郡城。1381年6月1日，农民起义在布伦特伍德爆发；埃塞克斯神父约翰·鲍尔长期传播反对农奴制的主张，数千人在博金集结后进军伦敦，起义失败后，理查二世亲临切姆斯福德绞死首领。1444年的埃塞克斯是人口稠密的织布郡，科尔切斯特的赤褐粗呢织工是当地最繁忙的商人群体之一。

1516年，亨利八世购入切姆斯福德附近的博林家族地产，并在那里修建比尤利宫。玛丽一世在位时，至少十九名新教徒在科尔切斯特被火刑处死。1560年代，佛兰德和瓦隆难民定居在城里的荷兰区，织造经贝呢厅检验的「贝呢」与「塞呢」；这些布料和科尔切斯特牡蛎把城市名声带到北欧各地。1588年无敌舰队来犯时，伊丽莎白一世在蒂尔伯里向集结的军队发表演说。内战中埃塞克斯支持议会，但1648年一支王军退入科尔切斯特，托马斯·费尔法克斯把他们困在旧城墙后。围城持续十一个半星期，直到王军在普雷斯顿战败后才结束，查尔斯·卢卡斯和乔治·莱尔随后在城堡院中被枪决。同一十年里，马修·霍普金斯的审巫案塞满切姆斯福德监狱；拿破仑战争期间，科尔切斯特是东部军区的驻军地。

en:
The lower Severn crosses Gloucestershire between the wool towns of the Cotswolds and the ironworks of the Forest of Dean, then opens into a wide tidal estuary. Gloucester, the Roman colonia of Glevum, held the lowest crossing on the river. At its Benedictine abbey of St Peter, William the Conqueror held his Christmas court in 1085 and ordered the Domesday survey; in 1216 the nine-year-old Henry III was crowned there, reputedly with his mother's bracelet in place of a crown; and in 1327 the body of Edward II, deposed and murdered at nearby Berkeley Castle, was brought to the abbey for burial, and pilgrims' offerings at his shrine helped pay for the new choir and the earliest surviving fan vaulting in England. Downstream on the Avon, Bristol had grown from a fortified burh into one of the three richest towns in the kingdom after London, and in 1373 it became the first English town made a county in its own right. Its ships carried cloth and wine to Gascony, Ireland and Iceland and took out the iron of the Forest of Dean. In 1444 the shire belonged to the English Crown, its abbeys and market towns quietly prosperous while the wars in France dragged on.

The wars of the next reigns reached the shire itself. At Tewkesbury on 4 May 1471 Edward IV destroyed the Lancastrian army and the Prince of Wales was killed, finishing the cause of Henry VI. In 1497 the Venetian John Cabot sailed from Bristol in the Matthew and made landfall in North America, and William Weston followed in 1499 on the first voyage to those coasts commanded by an Englishman. At the Dissolution St Peter's became Gloucester cathedral in 1541 and Bristol's abbey church followed in 1542. In the Civil War the Royalists took Bristol in 1643 and besieged Gloucester the same summer, but the city held for Parliament behind its walls, and Sir Thomas Fairfax retook Bristol in September 1645. Through the eighteenth century Bristol lived by the Atlantic: sugar and tobacco came from the West Indies, and between 1700 and 1807 over 2,000 slaving voyages carried an estimated 500,000 Africans from its docks to the Americas, until Parliament ended the trade in 1807.
zh:
塞文河下游穿过格洛斯特郡，东边是科茨沃尔德的呢绒集镇，西边是迪恩森林的铁场，再往下便展成宽阔的潮汐河口。格洛斯特原为罗马殖民城格莱乌姆，扼守塞文河上最下游的渡口。1085年，威廉一世在城中本笃会的圣彼得修道院过圣诞节，下令编纂《末日审判书》；1216年，九岁的亨利三世在此加冕，据说仓促间以母亲的手镯权充王冠；1327年，被废黜的爱德华二世在附近的伯克利城堡遇害，遗体葬入院中，陵前朝圣者的布施帮助建起了新唱诗席和英格兰现存最早的扇形拱顶。下游埃文河畔的布里斯托尔从设防堡镇起家，跻身英格兰仅次于伦敦的三大富城，1373年自成一郡，是英格兰第一个享此地位的城镇。商船载呢绒和葡萄酒往来加斯科涅、爱尔兰与冰岛，又把迪恩森林的铁料运出海。1444年，全郡在英格兰王冠治下，法兰西的长年战事还在打着，修道院和集镇依旧殷实。

此后几朝的战争打进了郡里。1471年5月4日，爱德华四世在蒂克斯伯里歼灭兰开斯特军，威尔士亲王战死，亨利六世一系大势已去。1497年，威尼斯人约翰·卡博特乘「马修号」从布里斯托尔出航，在北美登陆；1499年，威廉·韦斯顿再赴那片海岸，完成首次由英格兰人指挥的北美远航。解散修道院时，圣彼得修道院于1541年改为格洛斯特主教座堂，布里斯托尔的修道院教堂也在1542年跟进。内战期间，王党1643年攻下布里斯托尔，同年夏天围攻格洛斯特，城市却凭城墙站在议会一方；1645年9月，托马斯·费尔法克斯爵士攻克布里斯托尔。整个18世纪，布里斯托尔靠大西洋过活：糖和烟草从西印度群岛运来，1700至1807年间，两千多趟贩奴航行从这里的码头把约五十万名非洲人运往美洲，直到议会1807年废止奴隶贸易。

en:
Shrewsbury fills a loop of the River Severn nine miles from the Welsh border, the chief garrison and market town of the Shropshire Marches. The Mercians fortified the site against the Welsh, and after the Norman Conquest Roger de Montgomery raised a red sandstone castle and an abbey there as the seat of his earldom. The Marches' wars reached the town on 21 July 1403, when Henry IV met Henry 'Hotspur' Percy's rebels at Battlefield, three miles to the north. It was the first battle on English soil in which English longbowmen fought each other: Hotspur was killed by an arrow, and the king's teenage son Henry was shot through the face, saved when the surgeon John Bradmore drew the buried arrowhead out of his skull at Kenilworth with a screw-pointed instrument of his own devising. Hotspur's body was salted, impaled on a spear between two millstones in the market place, and later quartered and sent around the cities for display. In 1444 Shrewsbury lived by the Severn carrying trade and the wool coming out of Wales, a garrison market on a turbulent border.

Edward IV made the town the seat of the Council in the Marches of Wales in the 1470s, and his younger son Richard, born there in 1473 and later one of the Princes in the Tower, was known as Richard of Shrewsbury. Henry Tudor passed through in 1485 on his march to Bosworth. The Shrewsbury Drapers handled most of the Welsh wool clip and built Drapers' Hall in 1560 and Ireland's Mansion in 1575. The town was royalist in the Civil War until February 1645, when Thomas Mytton led Parliament's men in through St Mary's Water Gate at night. The abbey was dissolved in 1540, and in 1552 Edward VI chartered the free grammar school that became Shrewsbury School; William Camden called it the best-filled school in England, and its pupils included the poet and soldier Philip Sidney and Charles Darwin, who was born in the town in 1809.
zh:
什鲁斯伯里坐落在塞文河的一处河套里，距威尔士边界九英里，是什罗普郡边区的首要驻军城镇和集市。麦西亚人早在此筑堡抵御威尔士人；诺曼征服后，罗杰·德·蒙哥马利在这里建起红砂岩城堡和修道院，作为其伯爵领的治所。1403年7月21日，边区的战火烧到城北：亨利四世在城北三英里的战场村迎战「热刺」亨利·珀西的叛军。这是英格兰土地上头一次双方长弓手互相对射的会战，珀西中箭身亡，国王十几岁的儿子亨利也被箭射穿面部，外科医生约翰·布拉德莫在凯尼尔沃思用自制的螺纹器械把深陷颅骨的箭头取出，才保住他的性命。珀西的尸体被撒上盐，用长矛挑起、支在集市两块磨盘之间示众，后来又被肢解送往各城。1444年的什鲁斯伯里靠塞文河航运和威尔士出产的羊毛为生，是动荡边界上的驻军集市。

1470年代，爱德华四世把威尔士边区理事会的驻地设在什鲁斯伯里；他1473年出生于此的幼子理查，即后来塔中王子之一，被称为「什鲁斯伯里的理查」。1485年亨利·都铎进军博斯沃思时取道该城。什鲁斯伯里布商行会经营着威尔士羊毛的大部分货源，1560年建成布商行会厅，1575年建成爱尔兰宅邸。内战中该城站在王党一边，直到1645年2月托马斯·米顿夜率议会军经圣玛丽水门入城。修道院在1540年的解散运动中被毁，1552年爱德华六世颁诏设立免费文法学校，即后来的什鲁斯伯里公学；威廉·卡姆登称它是英格兰学生最多的学校，诗人兼军人菲利普·西德尼、以及1809年生于本城的查尔斯·达尔文都曾在此就读。

en:
The lowlands facing the Bristol Channel were the Welsh kingdom of Morgannwg, with the Gower peninsula beyond them to the west. The Normans came with Robert Fitzhamon around 1080, carved out the Marcher Lordship of Glamorgan and ruled it from Cardiff, ringing the vale with castles and founding the abbeys of Margam and Neath. Gilbert de Clare raised Caerphilly from 1268, ringed by artificial lakes, the largest castle in Wales and the first in Britain built on concentric lines, the model for Edward I's later castles in the north. Gower became a separate lordship with its new borough of Swansea, chartered between 1158 and 1184. Owain Glyndŵr's bands stormed the region's castles during the revolt of 1400–1415 and several were never repaired. In 1444 Glamorgan, held by the Beauchamp earls of Warwick, and Gower, held by the Mowbray dukes of Norfolk, were Welsh-speaking Catholic marcher lands, manorial in the vale and pastoral in the hills.

In the Wars of the Roses the Yorkist William Herbert gained Gower in 1468 and was beheaded after Edgcote the next year; after Bosworth Henry VII granted Glamorgan to his uncle Jasper Tudor in 1486. The Acts of Union merged Glamorgan, Gower and Kilvey into one shire in 1536, and the Reformation closed Margam and Neath abbeys. Henry Morgan, born on the Monmouthshire side of what is now Cardiff, made a very different name abroad. His privateers took Porto Bello and Maracaibo and sacked Panama in 1671, and he came home a knight and lieutenant-governor of Jamaica. In the Second Civil War a New Model Army detachment cut down a Royalist rising at St Fagans in 1648. Industry then took the county over. Copper was smelted near Neath from about 1584 and Swansea drew Cornish ore to its own coal from 1717, earning the name 'Copperopolis'; the Dowlais and Cyfarthfa ironworks rose at Merthyr, where in 1804 Richard Trevithick ran the world's first steam locomotive along the Penydarren tramway, and the Swansea and Mumbles line became the first fare-paying passenger railway three years later.
zh:
面向布里斯托尔湾的低地曾是威尔士人的摩尔甘努格王国，西边突出的是高尔半岛。约1080年，罗伯特·菲茨哈蒙随诺曼人前来，辟出以加的夫为治所的边境领地格拉摩根，在谷地四周广筑城堡，又建起马格姆和尼思两处修道院。吉尔伯特·德·克莱尔从1268年起修筑卡菲利城堡，人工湖环绕，是威尔士最大的城堡，也是不列颠第一座同心式要塞，后来成为爱德华一世北方诸堡的范本。高尔另成一个领地，辖下的新自治镇斯旺西在1158至1184年间获得特许状。欧文·格兰道尔1400至1415年起义时，他的队伍攻占当地多座城堡，有些再未修复。1444年，博尚家沃里克伯爵名下的格拉摩根和莫布雷家诺福克公爵名下的高尔，都是说威尔士语、信天主教的边境领地，谷地行庄园制，山区以畜牧为生。

玫瑰战争中，约克党的威廉·赫伯特1468年得到高尔，次年就在埃德科特兵败后被斩首；亨利七世博斯沃思取胜后，于1486年把格拉摩根封给叔父贾斯珀·都铎。1536年的《联合法案》把格拉摩根、高尔和基尔维并为一郡，宗教改革关闭了马格姆和尼思的修道院。出生在今加的夫一带旧蒙茅斯郡地界的亨利·摩根，在海外闯出全然不同的名声。他的私掠船队攻下波托韦洛和马拉开波，1671年洗劫巴拿马，回国时已受封爵士，官拜牙买加副总督。第二次内战中，新模范军一支部队1648年在圣费根斯剿灭了一场王党起事。此后工业改变了全郡。约1584年尼思附近开始炼铜，斯旺西从1717年起把康沃尔矿石运来就煤冶炼，得名「铜都」；道莱斯和塞法斯法铁厂在梅瑟蒂德菲尔兴起，1804年，理查·特里维西克在佩尼达伦矿车道上开动了世界上第一台蒸汽机车，三年后斯旺西-曼布尔斯线又成为第一条载客收费铁路。

en:
Gwynedd is the old Welsh kingdom of the north-west: the mountains of Snowdonia, the Menai Strait and the Llyn coast, ruled after the conquest from English-built castles. Edward I began Caernarfon Castle in 1283 and made the walled borough below it the seat of government in north Wales; his son Edward of Caernarfon was born there in 1284. No expense was spared: at some 20,000 to 25,000 pounds it was the costliest of Edward's Welsh castles, and its banded stone walls went up beside the Roman fort of Segontium to call the walls of Constantinople to mind. Harlech, on its crag above the sea, was the work of the Savoyard master James of St George, with a water-gate to the shore so the garrison could be supplied from Ireland by sea. Owain Glyndwr's rising tested them hard: Harlech fell in 1404 and became the prince's residence, headquarters and parliament house until English forces retook it in 1409, while Caernarfon fought off every siege. In 1444 this Welsh-speaking Catholic country was governed through royal castles, a generation after the revolt and the anti-Welsh laws that followed it.

The Wars of the Roses gave Harlech one of the famous sieges of England's civil wars. Margaret of Anjou took shelter there in 1460, and a Lancastrian garrison under Dafydd ap Ieuan held the rock for seven years against Edward IV, supplied from the sea. Jasper Tudor landed French reinforcements there in 1468, before William Herbert's army, said to number 10,000 men, forced the garrison's surrender on 14 August; the long defence is the siege the song 'Men of Harlech' remembers. Henry Tudor's win at Bosworth in 1485 put a Welsh dynasty on the English throne, and Edward I's castles were left to decay, and in 1538 Caernarfon was reported ruinous for lack of repairs. Both were armed again for Charles I in the Civil War: John Byron surrendered Caernarfon to Parliament in 1646, and Harlech, held by just 44 men, followed on 15 March 1647, the last royalist fortress on the British mainland to fall. An order after the Restoration to dismantle it was only partly carried out.
zh:
格温内斯是威尔士西北的古老王国，据有斯诺登尼亚群山、梅奈海峡和利恩半岛海岸；英格兰征服后，这里靠专为统治而建的城堡把守。爱德华一世1283年动工修建卡那封城堡，把崖下有城墙的自治镇设为北威尔士统治中心，他的儿子卡那封的爱德华1284年出生于此。工程不惜工本：约两万至两万五千英镑的造价居爱德华一世诸威尔士城堡之首，条带色石墙傍着罗马要塞塞贡提乌姆而建，意在追摹君士坦丁堡的城墙。哈莱克城堡踞海崖而立，出自萨伏依匠师詹姆斯·圣乔治之手，水门和长阶直通海边，围城期间守军可由爱尔兰从海上补给。欧文·格林杜尔1401至1404年的叛乱给了这些城堡严峻考验：哈莱克1404年陷落，成为格林杜尔的宅邸、大本营和召开议会的地方，1409年才被英军夺回；卡那封则扛住了历次围攻。1444年，这片讲威尔士语的天主教土地由王室城堡统辖，距叛乱的破坏和随后的反威尔士法律只过去一代人。

玫瑰战争中，哈莱克打出了英格兰内战史上有名的一场守城。1460年，安茹的玛格丽特到这里避难；达菲德·阿普·叶安率领兰开斯特守军据守巨岩七年，靠海路补给与爱德华四世抗衡。1468年，贾斯珀·都铎率法国援军在此登陆，随后威廉·赫伯特的军队（据说达一万人）围城，守军于8月14日投降；这场漫长的守城就是歌曲《哈莱克男儿》所唱的那一仗。1485年亨利·都铎在博斯沃思获胜，一个威尔士出身的王朝登上英格兰王位，爱德华一世诸堡日渐荒废，1538年已有报告称卡那封因缺乏修缮而严重朽坏。内战中两堡为查理一世重新武装：约翰·拜伦1646年把卡那封交给议会军；哈莱克仅有44名守军，1647年3月15日随之投降，是不列颠大陆最后陷落的王党要塞。王政复辟后下达的拆除令只执行了一部分。

en:
Lincolnshire takes its name from Lincoln, the Roman Lindum Colonia on the River Witham. William I ordered Lincoln Castle in 1068 and moved the diocese there a few years later; the cathedral, rebuilt by St Hugh after the earthquake of 1185, was given a lead-sheathed spire between 1307 and 1311, said to have reached 525 feet and to have been the tallest building in the world until a storm blew the spire down in 1548. The cathedral also held one of the original copies of Magna Carta from 1215. The wolds around became wealthy sheep country: Lincoln weavers sent dyed cloth to Flanders, and Boston on the Haven grew into one of England's leading wool ports, where work on the vast St Botolph's Church began in 1309. At Tattershall, Ralph Cromwell, Treasurer of England, had raised a 130-foot brick great tower called the finest piece of medieval brick-work in England. In 1444 this Catholic shire was a land of market towns, abbeys and clothiers, though plague, silting and the shift to domestic weaving had shaken Boston's old trade.

The Reformation struck the county early. In October 1536 crowds gathered at Louth and then Lincoln to defend the monasteries; as many as 60,000 may have joined the Lincolnshire Rising before it was put down, opening the way to the Pilgrimage of Grace. Nonconformity then took root: William Brewster and William Bradford's Separatists were held at Boston in 1607 on their first attempt to leave England, and John Cotton, vicar of St Botolph's from 1612, carried the town's name to New England in 1633. Another Lincolnshire man, John Smith, baptised at Willoughby near Alford in 1580, led the settlers of Jamestown in Virginia from 1608. In the Civil War the shire supported Parliament, whose cavalry defeated a Royalist force at Winceby on 11 October 1643 and stormed Lincoln Castle in May 1644. Isaac Newton, born at Woolsthorpe near Grantham in 1642, returned there in the plague year of 1666 and worked on optics and gravitation. After an Act of 1762 improved the Witham and drained more fenland, Boston exported grain from the new farmland.
zh:
林肯郡得名于威瑟姆河畔的林肯，其前身是罗马殖民地林杜姆。威廉一世1068年下令修建林肯城堡，几年后又把主教区迁来；大教堂在1185年地震后由圣休主持重建，1307至1311年间中央塔顶竖起包铅的巨尖顶，据说高达525英尺、为当时世界最高建筑，直到1548年被风暴吹落。教堂还保存着1215年《大宪章》四份存世原件之一。周围的丘陵成为富庶的牧羊区，林肯织工把染色布匹输往佛兰德，黑文河畔的波士顿崛起为英格兰最重要的羊毛港口之一，宏伟的圣博托尔夫堂1309年动工。在泰特歇尔，英格兰财政大臣拉尔夫·克伦威尔筑起130英尺高的砖砌大塔楼，被誉为英格兰最精美的中世纪砖作。1444年，这片天主教郡地遍布集镇、修道院和布商，只是瘟疫、河道淤塞和本土织业兴起，已经动摇了波士顿旧日的贸易。

宗教改革很早便冲击此地。1536年10月，民众在劳斯继而在林肯聚集，保卫修道院；可能多至六万人参加这场林肯郡起事，却很快被镇压，随后又引发求恩巡礼。非国教传统后来在此扎根：威廉·布鲁斯特和威廉·布拉德福德率领的分离派1607年首次试图离英时曾被拘押在波士顿；1612年起担任圣博托尔夫堂牧师的约翰·科顿，1633年把这个市镇的名字带到新英格兰。另一个林肯郡人、1580年在奥尔福德附近威洛比受洗的约翰·史密斯，1608年起主持弗吉尼亚的詹姆斯敦定居点。内战期间，林肯郡站在议会一方，其骑兵1643年10月11日在温斯比击败王党军队，又于1644年5月强攻林肯城堡。1642年生于格兰瑟姆附近伍尔索普的艾萨克·牛顿，在1666年瘟疫期间回到故乡，研究光学和引力。1762年的一项法令整治威瑟姆河并排干更多沼泽后，波士顿从新开垦的沃野输出谷物。

en:
Lancashire takes its name from Lancaster, the borough below a Roman fort on the River Lune. Its lands were long assessed with Yorkshire or Cheshire, and the separate shire is first recorded in 1182. Henry of Grosmont received palatine jurisdiction in 1351; through John of Gaunt the honour passed to Henry Bolingbroke, who took the throne as Henry IV in 1399 and kept the Duchy of Lancaster as crown property. Scottish raiders burned Lancaster more than once in the fourteenth century, and John of Gaunt strengthened the castle above the rebuilt town. In 1444 this Catholic English shire was a comparatively poor north-western march of wool villages, coastal marshes and small markets, governed through the duchy's separate courts.

The red rose of Lancaster gave the shire its side in the Wars of the Roses, and in 1461 Edward IV attached the palatinate directly to the Duchy of Lancaster. Under the Tudors the castle held the northern assizes and their executions: at least eleven Catholic priests died there during the Reformation, and in August 1612 ten people from Pendle were condemned after the Lancashire witch trials, nine of them hanged at Lancaster. In 1652 George Fox climbed Pendle Hill and had the vision there that began the Quaker movement. Jacobite defeat at Preston in 1715 checked the Stuart rising, and Bonnie Prince Charlie's army marched through the shire in 1745. By 1700 Lancaster had about 5,000 people; its new quays made it an Atlantic port, with shipbuilding, rope and sailcloth, and Britain's fourth-largest slave trade. Silt weakened the Lune harbour, whose last slaver was built there in 1806.
zh:
兰开夏得名于卢恩河畔的兰开斯特，这座城镇建在罗马要塞下方。其地长期随约克郡或柴郡计税，独立的郡1182年才见记载。1351年，亨利·格罗斯蒙特获得巴拉丁管辖权；领地经约翰·冈特传给亨利·博林布鲁克，后者1399年即位为亨利四世，并把兰开斯特公爵领地保留为王室财产。14世纪里苏格兰袭掠者不止一次焚毁兰开斯特，约翰·冈特加固了俯瞰重建城镇的城堡。1444年，这个信奉天主教的英格兰郡还是相对贫穷的西北边陲，散布着羊毛村落、海滨沼泽和小市集，由公爵领地的独立法庭治理。

兰开斯特的红玫瑰为这个郡标出玫瑰战争中的阵营，1461年爱德华四世下令把巴拉丁领地直接并入兰开斯特公爵领地。都铎时期，城堡是北方法庭和刑场所在：宗教改革期间至少有十一名天主教神父在此遇害；1612年8月，兰开夏女巫审判后十名彭德尔人被判死刑，其中九人在兰开斯特处绞。1652年，乔治·福克斯登上彭德尔山，在山上见到的异象开启了贵格会运动。1715年詹姆斯党在普雷斯顿战败，斯图亚特复辟受挫；1745年查理王子的军队穿郡而过。到1700年，兰开斯特约有五千居民，新码头使它成为大西洋港口，造船、绳索和帆布业兴盛，奴隶贸易规模在英国港口中列第四。卢恩河淤积削弱了港口，1806年这里还建造了最后一艘贩奴船。

en:
York sits where the Ouse meets the Foss, ringed by the ridings of Yorkshire, and for most of its history it has been the capital of northern England. The Romans laid out the fortress of Eboracum in AD 71, and in 306 the army there proclaimed Constantine the Great emperor; the Vikings later made the city their capital of Jorvik, and after the Norman conquest it became the seat of the archbishop of York, the second prelate of the English Church. Its merchants grew rich on the wool and cloth of the West Riding, carried down the Ouse and south along the Great North Road, and in 1396 Richard II confirmed the city's liberties by charter. In 1444 York ranked with Bristol and Norwich among the richest towns in England after London, while the great minster, under construction since 1220, still stood half wrapped in scaffolding as work on its western towers dragged on.

The dynastic and religious wars of later centuries were fought on its doorstep. On Palm Sunday, 29 March 1461, Edward IV destroyed the Lancastrian army at Towton, ten miles to the south-west, in a snowstorm and entered York; the minster was at last consecrated in 1472. At the Reformation the great abbeys were dissolved, the Pilgrimage of Grace marched out of the shire under its religious banners in 1536, and Henry VIII afterwards set up the Council of the North in St Mary's Abbey. The city kept its Catholic grievances: Guy Fawkes was born and schooled in York in 1570 and carried them into the Gunpowder Plot, while Margaret Clitherow, the 'Pearl of York', was pressed to death under heavy weights in 1586 for harbouring priests. On 2 July 1644 Prince Rupert's 15,000-strong royal army was broken seven miles west at Marston Moor by Cromwell's cavalry, four thousand of his men were killed, and York surrendered to Sir Thomas Fairfax a fortnight later. The highwayman Dick Turpin was hanged at York in 1739. By then the Ouse was silting and Leeds and Hull had drawn off the cloth trade, and York had settled into its new role as the social capital of the northern gentry, its racecourse and assembly rooms drawing the county families through the eighteenth century.
zh:
约克地处乌斯河与福斯河汇合处，四周环着约克郡的各个瑞丁，长期是英格兰北方的首府。公元71年，罗马人在此建埃伯拉肯要塞，306年驻军在此拥立君士坦丁为帝；维京人后来以此为都城，称约维克；诺曼征服之后，这里成为约克大主教的驻地，大主教位列英格兰教界第二。城中商人靠西瑞丁的羊毛和呢绒发财，货物顺乌斯河而下，再沿北方大道运往南方；1396年，理查二世以特许状确认城市的各项自由。1444年，约克与布里斯托尔、诺里奇并列，是仅次于伦敦的英格兰最富庶城镇之一；而自1220年动工的大教堂仍半裹在脚手架里，西塔的工程还在拖延。

后来几百年的王朝战争和宗教战争都打到了城门口。1461年3月29日棕枝主日，天降大雪，爱德华四世在城西南十英里的陶顿歼灭兰开斯特军队，随即进入约克；大教堂终于1472年祝圣。宗教改革中，大修道院相继解散，1536年「求恩巡礼」举着宗教旗帜从约克郡起事，事后亨利八世在圣玛丽修道院设立北方委员会。城里的天主教怨气不散：盖伊·福克斯1570年生于约克、在约克读书，后来把这股怨气带进火药阴谋；有「约克之珠」之称的玛格丽特·克利瑟罗则因藏匿神父，于1586年被重物压死。1644年7月2日，鲁珀特亲王一万五千人的王党军队在城西七英里的马斯顿荒原被克伦威尔的骑兵击溃，四千人战死，两周后约克向托马斯·费尔法克斯爵士投降。1739年，拦路强盗迪克·特平在约克被处以绞刑。此时乌斯河日渐淤积，呢绒贸易又被利兹和赫尔吸走，约克转而当起北方乡绅的社交首府：整个18世纪，赛马场和集会厅吸引着全郡的世家大族。

en:
Northumberland is England's northern march, running from the Cheviots and the Tweed down to the Tyne, with the bishop of Durham's palatine lands between the Tyne and the Tees. Hadrian's Wall once reached the Tyne at Newcastle, where Robert Curthose raised a castle in 1080 and gave the town its name; walled and made a county of itself in 1400, Newcastle was the frontier's chief fortress and port. Upriver the bishop of Durham ruled his own county palatine from the castle and cathedral above the Wear, while the moorland to the north was a country of peel towers and armed surnames. The Percys and Nevilles held its great castles at Alnwick, Bamburgh and Warkworth, and the border reivers on both sides of the line drove off cattle, took hostages and settled their quarrels on Truce Days rather than in royal courts. In 1444 this was a Catholic English marcher province: wool off the moors, fish and sea trade out of Newcastle, and a living made from border service.

The north took sides in the Wars of the Roses, and John Neville broke the Lancastrians near Hexham in 1464 and sent Somerset to the block. Its bloodiest field was Flodden by Branxton in 1513: the Earl of Surrey's army destroyed the invading Scots and left James IV dead on the ground, the last British king to fall in battle, with much of his nobility lying around him. Catholic anger at the Reformation fed the Pilgrimage of Grace and then the Rising of the North, whose earls heard Mass in Durham Cathedral in 1569 before the rising collapsed and the Earl of Northumberland was beheaded. When the two crowns united in 1603 the reivers lost the trade of the frontier, and during the civil wars Scottish Covenanters stormed and sacked Newcastle after a long siege in 1644 and kept Charles I prisoner there in 1646 and 1647. From 1530 the Hostmen of Newcastle controlled all coal shipments from the Tyne, and it was on this coalfield that George Stephenson, born at Wylam in 1781, built his first locomotive, the Blücher, at Killingworth in 1814 and tried his own miners' safety lamp in the pit in 1815.
zh:
诺森伯兰是英格兰的北部边地，北起切维奥特山和特威德河，南抵泰恩河；泰恩河与蒂斯河之间是达勒姆主教的巴拉丁领地。哈德良长城曾一直延伸到泰恩河畔的纽卡斯尔，1080年罗伯特·柯索斯在此修建城堡，城市也因这座新城堡得名；纽卡斯尔筑有城墙，1400年成为独立的城市郡，是整条边地上首要的堡垒和港口。往内陆去，达勒姆主教从威尔河畔的城堡和主教座堂统治自己的巴拉丁郡；北方的旷野上则遍布碉楼和带武装的宗族。珀西与内维尔两大家族据有阿尼克、班堡和沃克沃思的大城堡；边境两侧的流寇盗赶牛群、掳人勒赎，纠纷多在「休战日」上了结，而不是诉至王家法庭。1444年，这里是信天主教的英格兰边疆省份：旷野出产羊毛，纽卡斯尔做鱼货和海贸生意，许多人靠边防当差为生。

玫瑰战争中北方也选了边：1464年，约翰·内维尔在赫克瑟姆附近击溃兰开斯特派，萨默塞特公爵被送上断头台。最惨烈的一仗是1513年布兰克斯顿旁的弗洛登：萨里伯爵的军队歼灭入侵的苏格兰军，詹姆斯四世战死阵中，他是最后一位阵亡的不列颠国王，身边倒下大群苏格兰贵族。宗教改革激起的天主教不满汇为求恩巡礼，后来又有北方起义，起事的伯爵们1569年在达勒姆主教座堂望弥撒，但叛乱很快失败，诺森伯兰伯爵被斩首。1603年两王冠联合，流寇失去了边境这碗饭；内战中，苏格兰誓约派1644年在长期围城后攻破并劫掠纽卡斯尔，1646至1647年又把查理一世关押在此。从1530年起，纽卡斯尔的霍斯特曼商人专营泰恩河的煤炭外运；正是在这片煤田上，1781年生于怀勒姆的乔治·斯蒂芬森于1814年在基林沃思造出他的第一台机车「布吕歇尔号」，第二年又把自己设计的矿工安全灯带进矿井试用。

en:
Cumbria covers the old border lands of Cumberland and Westmorland, from the Solway flats and Eden valley south to the Kent dale, facing Scotland across the Solway Firth. Carlisle Castle, begun after William Rufus took the city in 1092, was the hinge of the Anglo-Scottish west march and changed hands repeatedly in the Scottish wars; David I of Scotland died there in 1153. Around it stretched reiver country, where peel towers overlooked every valley, Scottish and English surnames drove off each other's cattle under March law, and protection money gave the language the word blackmail; the wardens settled blood feuds at truce days. Further south, Kendal lived by wool: its hard green cloth, Kendal Green, was said to clothe the English archers at Agincourt, and Shakespeare dressed his foresters in it. In 1444 Carlisle and Appleby guarded Catholic England's troubled north-western frontier, and Kendal throve on its woollen trade.

No pitched battle of the Wars of the Roses was fought in Cumbria, though the Percy, Neville, Dacre and Clifford kindreds fed the war and Richard, Duke of Gloucester, the future Richard III, became Warden of the West March. Seventy-four Cumbrians were executed after the Pilgrimage of Grace failed at Carlisle in 1537, while Henry VIII rebuilt the castle for artillery. Mary, Queen of Scots landed at Workington in 1568 and was held in the Warden's Tower, where she was seen watching two football matches on the green outside before being moved south. After the Union of the Crowns in 1603 the Crown hanged the leading reivers and broke the old surnames. A Royalist garrison held Carlisle for eight months in 1644-45 against Scottish Covenanter and Parliamentarian besiegers. In 1745, in the last siege of an English fortress, Charles Edward Stuart's Jacobites took the city and the Duke of Cumberland retook it; thirty-one Jacobites were executed. On the coast the Lowthers built a stone pier at Whitehaven in 1634 and turned it into a coal and tobacco harbour, second among English ports by tonnage from 1750 to 1772; sixty-four slaving voyages sailed from it between 1711 and 1768. Glasgow later took the tobacco trade, and Whitehaven fell back on coal.
zh:
坎布里亚涵盖坎伯兰和威斯特摩兰两处旧边地，北起索尔威低地和伊登河谷，南至肯特河谷，与苏格兰隔索尔威湾相望。卡莱尔城堡是英苏西部边道的枢纽，1092年威廉·鲁弗斯夺取卡莱尔后动工，在苏格兰战争中几经易手，苏格兰国王大卫一世于1153年死在堡中。城堡周围是劫掠者的地界：每处河谷都立着佩尔塔，苏格兰和英格兰的宗族依边道法互相赶走牛群，收买平安的保护钱还给英语添了blackmail（勒索）一词，边道长官则在休战日裁断仇杀。南边的肯德尔靠羊毛为生：当地结实的绿色毛呢「肯德尔绿」，相传曾穿在阿让库尔战役的英格兰弓箭手身上，莎士比亚也让他笔下的林中人穿这种呢子。1444年，卡莱尔和阿普比扼守着信奉天主教的英格兰动荡西北边疆，肯德尔的毛呢生意正兴旺。

玫瑰战争期间没有大仗打到坎布里亚，但珀西、内维尔、达克和克利福德诸宗族为战局推波助澜，后来的理查三世、格洛斯特公爵理查出任西部边道长官。1537年求恩巡礼在卡莱尔失败后，七十四名坎布里亚人被处死，亨利八世则把城堡改造成火炮要塞。1568年，苏格兰女王玛丽从沃金顿登岸，被关在城堡的长官塔里，有人看见她在塔外草地上看了两场球赛，之后她才被转送南方。1603年两国王位联合后，王权处死为首的劫掠者，拆散旧宗族。1644—1645年，卡莱尔的王党守军在苏格兰誓约派和议会军围攻下坚守八个月。1745年，在英格兰最后一次要塞围攻中，查理·爱德华·斯图亚特的詹姆斯党占城，坎伯兰公爵收复，三十一名詹姆斯党人被处死。海岸上，劳瑟家族1634年在怀特黑文筑起石码头，把它变成煤炭和烟草港，1750—1772年按吨位居英格兰港口第二，1711—1768年还有六十四次贩奴航行从这里出发。后来格拉斯哥夺走烟草生意，怀特黑文便只剩煤炭。

en:
This corner of Scotland is the Firth of Forth, with the Lothian plain on its south shore, Fife on the north, and Stirling at the first bridgeable crossing. Edinburgh Castle, on its rock above Leith, was Britain's most besieged fortress; its oldest building is the twelfth-century St Margaret's Chapel. Fife was older royal ground: Dunfermline Abbey housed the royal tombs, and Scotland's first university was founded at St Andrews in 1413. Stirling guarded the lowest Forth crossing, site of Bannockburn in 1314. After Berwick fell in the 1330s, wool and hides went out through Leith and Fife shipped coal and salt. In November 1440 the young Earl of Douglas and his brother were killed at the Black Dinner before the ten-year-old James II; in 1444 his Catholic Lowland realm had its court and trade on the Forth.

In 1457 Philip the Good of Burgundy sent James II the giant bombard Mons Meg, still on the castle rock. English forces burned Edinburgh in 1544 and destroyed a Scottish army at Pinkie on 10 September 1547; in 1560 English and Protestant troops besieged the French at Leith. Mary, Queen of Scots, saw David Rizzio murdered at Holyrood in 1566; her son James VI was born in the castle that year and crowned at Stirling in 1567, and her last supporters held out there until 1573. Edinburgh University was founded in 1582. After James inherited England in 1603 the court moved south, though Edinburgh kept Scotland's laws, church and parliament.

Cromwell won at Dunbar on 3 September 1650, took Edinburgh and drove the Scottish government to Stirling before winning at Worcester in 1651. The Company of Scotland, chartered in 1695, lost about a fifth of the nation's money in its New Caledonia colony at Darien in 1698; disease and a Spanish siege ended it by 1700, helping to carry the Union of 1 May 1707 that closed the Edinburgh parliament. Jacobite Highlanders held the city briefly in 1745; after Culloden the New Town was laid out from 1767, and Hume, Smith, Hutton and Black made Edinburgh the centre of the Scottish Enlightenment. By 1821 it was still Scotland's legal and financial capital, though Glasgow was larger.
zh:
苏格兰的这一角环抱福斯湾：南岸是洛锡安平原，北岸是法夫，福斯河最早能架桥之处则是斯特灵。爱丁堡城堡踞于利斯港上方的岩丘之上，是不列颠遭受围攻最多的要塞，城中最古老的建筑是12世纪的圣玛格丽特礼拜堂。法夫是更古老的王畿：邓弗姆林修道院收葬历代国王，苏格兰第一所大学1413年在圣安德鲁斯创立。斯特灵扼守福斯河最靠下游的渡口，1314年班诺克本战役就打在这里。14世纪30年代贝里克陷落后，羊毛和兽皮经利斯输出，法夫则输出煤炭和盐。1440年11月，年轻的道格拉斯伯爵和弟弟在城堡中的「黑色晚宴」上、当着十岁的詹姆士二世的面被杀；1444年，他的天主教低地王国以福斯湾为宫廷与贸易的中心。

1457年，勃艮第公爵「好人」腓力把巨型臼炮「蒙斯梅格」送给詹姆士二世，这门巨炮现陈列在城堡岩上。英军1544年焚毁爱丁堡，1547年9月10日又在平基摧毁苏格兰军队；1560年，英格兰与新教联军在利斯围攻法军。苏格兰女王玛丽1566年在荷里路德宫亲眼看着秘书大卫·里奇奥被杀；她的儿子詹姆士六世同年生于城堡之中，1567年在斯特灵加冕，女王最后的支持者则据守城堡直到1573年。爱丁堡大学创立于1582年。1603年詹姆士继承英格兰王位后宫廷南迁，爱丁堡仍保留苏格兰的法律、教会和议会。

1650年9月3日，克伦威尔在邓巴获胜，占领爱丁堡，把苏格兰政府逼到斯特灵，最终于1651年在伍斯特取胜。1695年获特许的苏格兰公司，把全国约五分之一的钱财投入1698年在达连地峡建立的「新喀里多尼亚」殖民地；疾病和西班牙人的围攻到1700年将它断送，这场破产促成1707年5月1日联合生效，爱丁堡议会随之关闭。1745年，詹姆斯党高地军队曾短暂占领城市；卡洛登战役后新城自1767年动工，休谟、斯密、赫顿和布莱克使爱丁堡成为苏格兰启蒙运动的中心。到1821年，它仍是苏格兰的法律与金融之都，只是格拉斯哥已经更大。

en:
Ayrshire runs along the Firth of Clyde from the Largs coast to the hills of Carrick, its river valleys dividing the shire into Cunninghame, Kyle and Carrick. Its early fame is bound up with the Bruces: Carrick was the family's comital land, and Turnberry Castle on its sea cliff was the boyhood home of Robert Bruce, born in 1274 to Robert de Brus and Marjorie, Countess of Carrick. Scottish barons who backed his claim to the crown met secretly in the castle in 1286, and during the wars with England Bruce had it slighted in 1310 rather than leave an English garrison on his own coast; he held a parliament at Ayr in 1315. The sea off Largs had already seen the kingdom fight for its western seaboard in 1263, when a storm drove King Haakon of Norway's longships ashore and the Scots beat back the landing; by the Treaty of Perth in 1266 the Hebrides passed to Scotland. William the Lion had made Ayr a royal burgh in 1205, and in 1444 its harbour shipped wool, hides, fish and cattle and brought back salt and wine, with Irvine a second royal burgh.

After 1444 Ayr sent out more settlers than any other Scottish port for the Plantation of Ulster, most of them bound for the Ards Peninsula and the country around Belfast. In 1652 and 1653 Cromwell's men built the six-sided Ayr Citadel at the river mouth, the largest of their strongholds in Scotland, taking stone from Ardrossan Castle; the medieval parish church was pulled down in the works and replaced by the Auld Kirk in 1654. The moors and hidden coves of Carrick sheltered Covenanter field-meetings and, later, smuggler cargoes. Robert Burns, born in the clay-built cottage at Alloway in 1759, carried the shire's place names into every Scottish household: 'Tam o' Shanter' rides from Ayr market past Alloway Kirk to the Brig o' Doon, and his first collection, 'Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect,' was printed at Kilmarnock in 1786. In his last years Burns rode the Carrick coast as an exciseman, hunting the very smugglers whose coves his poems describe.
zh:
艾尔郡位于克莱德湾沿岸，北起拉格斯海岸，南抵卡里克丘陵，河谷把全郡分成坎宁安、凯尔和卡里克三区。这里早年的名声和布鲁斯家族连在一起：卡里克是布鲁斯家的伯爵领地，海边崖上的特恩贝里城堡是罗伯特·布鲁斯长大的地方，他1274年出生，父亲是罗伯特·德·布鲁斯，母亲是卡里克女伯爵玛乔丽。1286年，支持他继承王位的苏格兰贵族在城堡密会；对英战争期间，布鲁斯于1310年下令拆毁城堡，不愿自己的海岸上留着英军据点，1315年又在艾尔召开议会。拉格斯外海更早打过一场争夺西海疆的仗：1263年一场风暴把挪威国王哈康的长船刮上海岸，苏格兰军击退登陆者，1266年《珀斯条约》把赫布里底划归苏格兰。早在1205年，狮子威廉就把艾尔设为皇家自治镇；1444年，艾尔港运出羊毛、兽皮、鱼和牲畜，换回盐与葡萄酒，欧文是另一座皇家自治镇。

1444年以后，在阿尔斯特种植中，艾尔输出的移民多过苏格兰任何一个港口，主要前往阿尔兹半岛和贝尔法斯特一带。1652至1653年，克伦威尔的军队在河口建起六边形的艾尔要塞，这是他们在苏格兰最大的据点，石料拆自阿德罗森城堡；施工时拆了中世纪老教堂，1654年由艾尔老教堂接替。卡里克的荒野和隐蔽海湾藏过誓约派的野外集会，后来又窝藏走私货物。罗伯特·彭斯1759年生于阿洛韦的土坯农舍，他让全郡的地名走进苏格兰每户人家：《汤姆·奥桑特》里的主角从艾尔集市纵马经过阿洛韦教堂，逃到杜恩桥，第一部诗集《主要用苏格兰方言写的诗》1786年在基尔马诺克印行。彭斯晚年在卡里克海岸当税务官，骑马巡缉的正是他诗里写过的那些走私者藏身的海湾。

en:
Perth stands at the head of the Tay's tideway, the lowest ford between the Lowland plain and the Highland passes; its burgesses long called it St John's Toun after their kirk of St John the Baptist. Two miles upstream at Scone, kings of Scots were inaugurated on the Stone of Destiny in the Augustinian abbey until Edward I carried the stone south in 1296. William the Lion made Perth a royal burgh, and its merchants traded Tay salmon, wool and hides for French wine, Spanish silk and Baltic timber. Robert the Bruce retook the town from the English in 1312; the English came back in 1336 and ringed it with stone walls. In September 1396 a clan feud was settled by staged combat on the North Inch, when thirty men of Clan Chattan and thirty of Clan Quhele fought before Robert III and his court; nineteen Chattan men fell and all but one of their opponents were killed. In February 1437 James I was murdered at the Blackfriars by the Earl of Atholl's followers, and his widow carried the young James II to Edinburgh, where the court then settled. In 1444 Perth remained one of Scotland's richest burghs, though the king was rarely seen there.

The Reformation reached Perth as a riot: after John Knox preached in St John's Kirk in May 1559, townspeople gutted the friaries and sacked Scone Abbey. In 1618 James VI forced five articles on the church assembly at Perth, pulling Scottish worship towards English practice over presbyterian resistance. On 1 September 1644 Montrose's Royalists scattered the Covenanters at Tippermuir and plundered Perth for two days. Charles II was crowned at Scone on 1 January 1651, and later that year Cromwell built a five-sided citadel on the South Inch to hold the town. Warfare then moved into the Highland straths: at Killiecrankie on 27 July 1689 the Jacobites routed Mackay's redcoats but lost their leader Dundee, and the fight at Sheriffmuir in November 1715 ended in a bloody draw. Jacobite garrisons held Perth itself in 1689, 1715 and 1745. Afterwards drove roads carried cattle from the glens to the trysts at Crieff, and after Perth Academy was founded in 1760 the linen, leather and whisky trades gave the town a quieter prosperity.
zh:
珀斯地处泰河潮汐尽头，是低地平原与高地山口之间最下游的渡口；市民因圣约翰教堂，长期把本城唤作「圣约翰城」。上游两英里的斯昆有奥斯定会修道院，苏格兰国王在那里的命运之石上加冕，直到1296年爱德华一世把圣石南运。「狮子」威廉把珀斯设为皇家自治镇，商人用泰河鲑鱼、羊毛和兽皮换回法国葡萄酒、西班牙丝绸和波罗的海木材。罗伯特·布鲁斯1312年从英军手中收复此城，英军1336年再度占领，绕城筑起石墙。1396年9月，一场部族世仇在北因奇以约定的对阵战作了断：查坦族与克赫尔族各出三十人，在罗伯特三世和满朝文武面前厮杀，查坦一方折了十九人，对方只活下来一个。1437年2月，詹姆斯一世在黑衣修士修道院被阿索尔伯爵的党羽刺杀，寡后携年幼的詹姆斯二世退守爱丁堡，宫廷后来常驻南方。1444年的珀斯仍是苏格兰最富庶的自治镇之一，只是王驾已鲜少至此。

宗教改革在珀斯始于一场骚乱：1559年5月约翰·诺克斯在圣约翰教堂布道之后，市民捣毁城中各派修道院，又出城洗劫斯昆修道院。1618年，詹姆斯六世在珀斯召开的教会会议上强行通过五项条款，不顾长老会的反对，要把苏格兰的礼拜拉向英格兰的做法。1644年9月1日，蒙特罗斯麾下的王军在蒂珀缪尔击溃誓约派军队，随后纵兵在珀斯劫掠两日。1651年1月1日查理二世在斯昆加冕，同年晚些时候克伦威尔在南因奇修建五边形要塞以控制此城。此后战火烧进高地河谷：1689年7月27日，詹姆斯党在基利克兰基大败麦凯的红衫军，却折了统帅邓迪；1715年11月的谢里夫缪尔之战打成一场血腥平局。珀斯本身也在1689、1715和1745年三度驻有詹姆斯党的守军。后来赶牛大道把峡谷里的牛群南送到克里夫的集市，1760年珀斯学院创立后，亚麻、皮革和威士忌等行当给这座城镇带来了较为安稳的生计。

en:
Aberdeen began as two burghs between the mouths of the Don and the Dee: Old Aberdeen, the bishop's seat by St Machar's Cathedral, and New Aberdeen, the fishing and trading port where the Denburn runs into the Dee estuary. David I made the town a royal burgh, William the Lion confirmed its rights in 1179, and Robert the Bruce's Great Charter of 1319 handed the townsmen the Forest of Stocket and made the burgh financially independent. Bruce took the English-held castle in 1308 and had it destroyed, and Edward III burned the town in 1336, after which it was rebuilt and walled. In 1411 the provost Robert Davidson, a merchant and privateer, led three dozen burgesses out with the Earl of Mar against Donald, Lord of the Isles, and fell at Harlaw. In 1444 Aberdeen was the chief town and port of the north-east, living by its salmon and herring fisheries, and its council registers already ran back to 1398.

Bishop William Elphinstone secured a papal bull from Alexander VI in 1495 for King's College, the first university in northern Scotland, modelled on Paris, and with Hector Boece he compiled the Aberdeen Breviary, the first book printed in Scotland, which came off Walter Chepman's Edinburgh press in 1510. Margaret Tudor's visit in 1511 moved William Dunbar to his poem 'Blyth Aberdeane', and in 1593 the fifth Earl Marischal, George Keith, founded a second seat of learning, Marischal College. George Jamesone, born in Aberdeen around 1587, became the first Scottish painter to win a wide reputation for portraits. On 13 September 1644 Montrose's royalists routed a Covenanter army outside the walls and sacked the town, and plague in 1647-48 killed about a quarter of its people. The eighteenth century brought shipyards and textile mills and dressed the streets in local grey granite, though the harbour and street works left the burgh bankrupt in 1817.
zh:
阿伯丁最早是唐河河口与迪河河口之间的两座城镇：老阿伯丁是圣马查尔座堂旁的主教驻地，新阿伯丁是登伯恩溪注入迪河河口处的渔业与贸易港。大卫一世赐予其皇家自治镇地位，狮子王威廉于1179年以特许状确认镇民权利，罗伯特·布鲁斯1319年的《大宪章》又把斯托克特森林交给镇民，使自治镇在财政上独立。独立战争中英军据守的城堡于1308年被布鲁斯攻取摧毁，1336年爱德华三世焚毁全镇，阿伯丁此后重建并筑起城墙。1411年，镇长、商人出身的罗伯特·戴维森率三十余名市民随马尔伯爵迎战群岛领主唐纳德，本人战死哈洛。1444年的阿伯丁是苏格兰东北部的首要城镇与港口，以鲑鱼和鲱鱼渔业为生，镇议会档案已可追溯到1398年。

1495年，阿伯丁主教威廉·艾尔芬斯通取得教宗亚历山大六世的诏书，创办苏格兰北部的第一所大学国王学院，以巴黎大学为范本；他又与赫克托·波伊斯合编《阿伯丁日课经》，1510年由沃尔特·查普曼在爱丁堡印出，是苏格兰第一部印刷书籍。1511年玛格丽特·都铎到访，威廉·邓巴为之写下诗篇《欢悦的阿伯丁》；1593年第五代马修伯爵乔治·基斯创办第二所学府马修学院。约1587年出生于此的画家乔治·詹姆森（George Jamesone）是第一个以肖像画赢得广泛名声的苏格兰画家。1644年9月13日，蒙特罗斯的王党军在城外击溃誓约派军队并洗劫全城，1647至1648年的瘟疫又夺去约四分之一居民的生命。18世纪造船与纺织业兴起，街道两旁的建筑渐以本地灰色花岗岩砌成，但宏大的港口和街道工程使自治镇在1817年破产。

en:
Inverness lies at the mouth of the River Ness where it enters the Moray Firth, the sea gate of the Great Glen and long the leading town of the Highlands. It was a chief stronghold of the Pictish kings when St Columba came in 569 to preach to King Brude at the vitrified fort of Craig Phadrig, and Macbeth, the king Shakespeare made famous, held a castle here as mormaer of Moray and Ross before his killing of Duncan took him to the Scottish throne. William the Lion made the town a royal burgh, whose four fairs and Dominican friary of 1233 drew trade from a wide Gaelic hinterland. The MacDonald Lords of the Isles were more feared than welcomed: in 1411 Donald of Islay seized the town and burned the Ness bridge on his march to Harlaw, and in 1427 James I summoned the northern chiefs to a parliament in the castle and clapped three in irons. In 1444 Inverness was a small, rough burgh beneath its royal castle, the crown's furthest outpost among the Mackintoshes, Frasers and Munros, shipping wool, hides and salmon south and across the North Sea.

Feuding kept the castle busy: the Munros cut down the Mackintoshes at Clachnaharry in 1454, and Clan Donald stormed it during the Raid on Ross in 1491. In 1562 the governor shut the gates on Mary, Queen of Scots, during Huntly's rising; the Frasers and Munros took the castle for her and she hanged him. Cromwell built a citadel north of the burgh big enough for a thousand men, which was demolished at the Restoration. In May 1689 MacDonell of Keppoch besieged the town until Dundee arrived with the Jacobite army, swore the burgh to James VII and marched south to his victory and death at Killiecrankie. Jacobites used the royal fortress as a barracks in 1715, and the first Fort George, built in 1727, surrendered to them and was blown up in 1746. On 16 April 1746, on Culloden Moor just outside the town, the duke of Cumberland's army destroyed the Jacobite host in the last pitched battle on British soil. From 1783 the lairds of Inverness-shire began clearing the glens for sheep, and the Gaelic north began a long depopulation.
zh:
因弗内斯坐落在尼斯河注入马里湾的河口，是大峡谷的海上门户，历来是高地首屈一指的重镇。569年圣哥伦巴到克雷格法德里格的石砌堡垒向皮克特国王布鲁德传教时，这里已是皮克特诸王的主要据点；后来因莎士比亚的戏剧为人熟知的麦克白，在杀死邓肯、登上苏格兰王位之前，身为马里和罗斯的首领，在城里拥有一座城堡。「狮子」威廉在位时它成为皇家自治镇，四大集市与1233年创立的多明我会修道院吸引着广阔盖尔语腹地的商货。群岛之主麦克唐纳家族带来的恐惧远多于欢迎：1411年艾拉的唐纳德在进军哈劳途中夺取此镇，烧毁尼斯河桥；1427年詹姆斯一世在城堡召集北方首领议事，当场锁拿三人。1444年的因弗内斯是一座粗粝的小自治镇，依托王家城堡，是王权伸入麦肯托什、弗雷泽和门罗诸族地盘的最前哨，羊毛、兽皮和鲑鱼从这里南运并横渡北海。

族间仇杀让城堡难得安宁：1454年门罗家族在克拉赫纳里重创麦肯托什家族，1491年唐纳德一族又在罗斯之掠中攻破城堡。1562年亨特利叛乱期间，守将闭门拒绝苏格兰女王玛丽入城，弗雷泽与门罗两族为女王拿下城堡，守将随后被绞死。克伦威尔在镇北修建了可容千人的要塞，王政复辟时被拆毁。1689年5月，凯波奇的麦克唐奈围攻此镇，邓迪率詹姆斯党主力赶到，逼全镇向詹姆斯七世宣誓效忠，随后南下，在基利克兰基取胜并战死。1715年詹姆斯党把王家要塞充作兵营；1727年建成的第一座乔治堡于1746年向他们投降并被炸毁。1746年4月16日，就在城外的卡洛登沼地，坎伯兰公爵的军队歼灭了詹姆斯党大军，这是不列颠土地上最后一场对阵会战。从1783年起，因弗内斯郡的领主们清空峡谷、改牧绵羊，盖尔语的北方开始了漫长的人口凋零。

en:
The Outer Hebrides, Na h-Eileanan an Iar in Gaelic and also called the Long Island, run from Lewis and Harris south to Barra beyond the stormy Minch. Norse settlers once made them part of the Norse kingdom of the Isles, but the 1266 Treaty of Perth transferred the islands from Norway to Scotland. Gaelic chiefs then took root under the MacDonald Lord of the Isles based at Islay: MacLeods held Lewis and Harris, MacDonalds the Uists, and in Barra the MacNeils kept Kisimul Castle on a rock in Castlebay, which could be reached only by boat. Stornoway grew round a sheltered Lewis harbour where Vikings had settled in the early ninth century. In 1444 Alexander MacDonald, Lord of the Isles and Earl of Ross, headed a Catholic, Gaelic-speaking maritime lordship whose people lived from livestock, fishing and sea-borne trade rather than the crown government of the Lowlands.

Alexander died in 1449, and James IV forfeited the lordship in 1493. In 1506 the Earl of Huntly battered Stornoway Castle with cannon. James V toured the islands in 1540 on promises of safe conduct, then arrested the chiefs who came to meet him at Portree. On Barra, Ruari MacNeil, called the Tatar, raided shipping from Kisimul so often that the Privy Council named him a hereditary outlaw and the last of the Viking raiders, until his own nephews took him in chains. In 1598 James VI leased Lewis to eleven gentlemen from Fife, but Murdoch and Neil MacLeod drove the colonists out and a second attempt failed in 1605; the Mackenzies of Seaforth took the island in 1610 and built up its fisheries. Lewismen fought for Charles I at Auldearn in 1645, and a Cromwellian garrison later tore down Stornoway Castle. Islanders rose for the Stuarts in 1715 and again in 1745, before defeat at Culloden ended the old order. Kelp burning carried the islands through the eighteenth century, and when the trade collapsed after 1815 the tenants faced emigration and the clearances.
zh:
外赫布里底群岛盖尔语称西部群岛（Na h-Eileanan an Iar），又称长岛，隔着风浪险恶的明奇海峡，从刘易斯—哈里斯向南延伸到巴拉。诺斯定居者曾把这里并入诺斯人的群岛王国，1266年《珀斯条约》把群岛从挪威移交苏格兰。此后，盖尔语氏族在以艾莱岛为基地的麦克唐纳「群岛领主」治下扎根：麦克劳德家族据有刘易斯和哈里斯，麦克唐纳家族据有尤伊斯特群岛，巴拉则归麦克尼尔家族，他们把守着卡斯尔贝湾中礁石上的基斯缪尔城堡，那里只有坐船才能到达。斯托诺韦围绕刘易斯岛一处避风港发展，维京人9世纪初便在此定居。1444年，群岛领主兼罗斯伯爵亚历山大·麦克唐纳统领着这个信奉天主教、使用盖尔语的海洋领地；岛民靠畜牧、捕鱼和海上贸易为生，不像低地那样受王权直接治理。

亚历山大于1449年去世，詹姆斯四世在1493年没收群岛领地。1506年，亨特利伯爵用火炮夺取斯托诺韦城堡。1540年，詹姆斯五世以保障安全为诺巡视群岛，把前来波特里会面的首领们尽数逮捕。巴拉的鲁阿里·麦克尼尔外号「鞑靼人」，他以基斯缪尔城堡为巢频频劫掠船只，枢密院称他为「世袭的亡命徒」、「最后的维京袭掠者」，最终被自己的外甥锁拿下狱。1598年，詹姆斯六世把刘易斯租给十一名法夫绅士，默多克·麦克劳德和尼尔·麦克劳德却赶走殖民者，第二次尝试又在1605年失败；西福思的麦肯齐家族1610年取得该岛，着手发展渔业。刘易斯人1645年在奥尔德恩战役中为查理一世作战，后来克伦威尔的驻军拆毁了斯托诺韦城堡。岛民1715年起兵拥戴斯图亚特王朝，1745年再度起事，卡洛顿的败亡终结了旧秩序。烧海藻灰的营生支撑群岛走过18世纪，这门生意1815年后崩溃，佃户们只能面对外迁移民和高地清洗。

en:
Poznań began on Ostrów Tumski, the island between the Warta and Cybina where the Western Polans built one of their main strongholds. Mieszko I may have been baptised there in 966, Bishop Jordan established Poland's first see in 968, and the early Piast rulers, including Mieszko and Bolesław the Brave, were buried in the cathedral. Bretislaus I of Bohemia sacked the island in 1038, and the royal court moved to Kraków, but Poznań remained a residence of the Greater Poland Piasts. The dukes chartered a new left-bank town under Magdeburg law in 1253; Przemysł II kept his residence there before his coronation at Gniezno in 1295. Staple rights in 1394 tied the Warta crossing to the carrying trade from Lithuania toward western markets. In 1444 Poznań was a walled, Polish-speaking Catholic royal city living by river traffic, salt, cloth and fur.

The Jagiellonian period enlarged its merchant houses and schools. The Lubrański Academy opened in 1519, and a Jesuit college followed in 1571. Fire destroyed the castle, town hall and 175 other buildings on 2 May 1536. Giovanni Battista di Quadro rebuilt the town hall between 1550 and 1560 with a high loggia and Renaissance attic; its new clock of 1551 carried the mechanical fighting goats that became the city's familiar curiosity. Merchants handled furs from the east and wine, cloth and metals from western and southern markets, while the cathedral canons, nobles and religious orders filled the town with churches and mansions.

War broke that prosperity. Swedish troops took Poznań in 1655 during the Deluge, abused its Jewish inhabitants and held out through a two-month siege in 1657 before the city was retaken. Saxon and Swedish forces fought another Battle of Poznań on 19 August 1704, and plague, warfare and the flood of 1736 reduced much of the population; settlers from Bamberg and the Netherlands rebuilt the suburbs. The Second Partition gave Poznań to Prussia in 1793. Local Poles rose in 1794 and again drove out the Prussian garrison when Napoleon approached in 1806. The Duchy of Warsaw ruled the city from 1807 until the Congress of Vienna returned it to Prussia in 1815 as capital of the Grand Duchy of Posen.
zh:
波兹南起于瓦尔塔河与齐比纳河之间的奥斯特鲁夫·图姆斯基岛，西波良人曾在岛上修建主要寨堡。梅什科一世966年可能就是在此受洗，968年主教约尔丹设立波兰第一个主教区，梅什科一世和「勇者」波列斯瓦夫等早期皮雅斯特君主都葬在岛上的主教座堂。1038年，波希米亚的布热季斯拉夫一世洗劫此岛，王廷后来迁往克拉科夫，但波兹南仍是大波兰皮雅斯特支系的居所。1253年，公爵们按马格德堡法特许在瓦尔塔河左岸建设新城；普热梅斯瓦夫二世1295年赴格涅兹诺加冕前，就把宫廷设在这里。1394年的货物集散特权把瓦尔塔河渡口同立陶宛输往西方市场的转运贸易连在一起。1444年，波兹南是一座有城墙、居民说波兰语并信奉天主教的王家城市，靠河运、盐、布匹和毛皮为生。

雅盖隆时期，商号和学校不断增多。卢布兰斯基学院1519年成立，耶稣会学院1571年创办。1536年5月2日的大火烧毁城堡、市政厅和另外175座建筑。1550年至1560年，乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·迪·夸德罗重建市政厅，加上高高的敞廊和文艺复兴式山墙；1551年的新钟装有两只相斗的机械山羊，后来成为城市人熟悉的奇景。商人在这里经销东方毛皮，也买卖来自西方和南方市场的葡萄酒、布匹与金属；主教座堂的法政牧师、贵族和修会则在城中修建教堂与宅邸。

战争打断了这种富庶。大洪水时代，瑞典军队1655年占领波兹南，虐待犹太居民，并在1657年坚守两个月围城后才被逐出。1704年8月19日，萨克森和瑞典军队又在波兹南交战；瘟疫、兵祸和1736年的洪水使人口大减，班贝格与尼德兰移民后来重建郊区。1793年第二次瓜分，波兹南划归普鲁士。1794年当地波兰人起事，1806年拿破仑逼近时他们又驱逐普军守军。1807年起城市归入华沙公国，1815年维也纳会议把它交还普鲁士，成为波兹南大公国的都城。

en:
Kalisz stands on the Prosna in eastern Greater Poland, on the old amber road that carried Baltic amber south toward the Roman provinces; the Calisia marked on Ptolemy's map in the 2nd century is traditionally placed here. From the mid-9th century Piast rulers kept one of their chief strongholds on the site, and Kalisz became one of the two traditional capitals of Greater Poland alongside Poznań; Mieszko III the Old died and was buried here in 1202. Bolesław the Pious granted town rights between 1253 and 1260, and on 8 September 1264 issued the Statute of Kalisz, which gave Jewish settlers their own courts and fixed the rules of evidence for cases between Christians and Jews. Ratified by Casimir the Great in 1334 and by later kings, the charter helped draw Jewish migrants to Poland for centuries. In 1314 Ladislaus the Short made the town capital of the Kalisz Voivodeship. Teutonic troops ravaged the old town in 1331 but could not storm the new town, and in 1343 Casimir the Great signed peace with the Order at Kalisz. A new town hall rose in 1426, and in 1444 the royal city remained a voivodeship seat and a centre of weaving and woodworking.

Kalisz received the staple right in 1496, and Stanisław Karnkowski founded a Jesuit college in 1583 and a seminary in 1593; in 1613 scholars used a telescope brought to the town for the first astronomical observations of their kind in Poland. Czech Brethren expelled from Bohemia after 1620 settled around Kalisz and strengthened its cloth trade. On 29 October 1706, during the Great Northern War, Russian, Saxon and Polish troops under Augustus the Strong and Menshikov defeated the Swedish army of Mardefelt and the followers of Stanisław Leszczyński outside the town, Sweden's only major defeat in Poland during the war. Prussia annexed Kalisz in the Second Partition of 1793. Wojciech Bogusławski opened a permanent theatre there in 1801, and after the 1806 Greater Poland rising the town became a departmental capital in the Duchy of Warsaw. The Russo-Prussian Treaty of Kalisz in 1813 brought Prussia into the war against Napoleon, and in 1815 the city passed to Congress Poland.
zh:
卡利什位于大波兰东部的普罗斯纳河畔，古老的琥珀商路经此把波罗的海的琥珀南运罗马各行省；托勒密2世纪地图上的卡利西亚，传统上就被认为在这里。9世纪中叶起，皮雅斯特王公在此营建最重要的堡寨之一，卡利什后来与波兹南并称大波兰的两座传统都城；1202年，梅什科三世（老者）在此去世并安葬。1253至1260年间，「虔敬者」博莱斯瓦夫授予城市特许状，1264年9月8日又颁布《卡利什法》，允许犹太定居者设立自己的法庭，并规定基督徒与犹太人之间案件的取证规则。该法1334年经卡齐米日大帝、其后又经多位国王确认，几个世纪里吸引犹太移民前来波兰。1314年，瓦迪斯瓦夫一世把卡利什定为卡利什省首府。1331年条顿军队劫掠旧城，却没能攻下新城；1343年卡齐米日大帝在卡利什与骑士团签订和约。新市政厅建于1426年；1444年时，这座王家城市仍是省治和纺织、木器业中心。

1496年，卡利什获得货物集散权；斯坦尼斯瓦夫·卡尔恩科夫斯基1583年创立耶稣会学院，1593年再设神学院；1613年，学者用运到城里的望远镜进行了波兰最早的天文观测。1620年后，被逐出波希米亚的捷克兄弟会在卡利什一带定居，壮大了织布业。1706年10月29日大北方战争期间，奥古斯特二世和缅希科夫指挥的俄国、萨克森和波兰军队，在城外击败马德费尔特的瑞典军及斯坦尼斯瓦夫·莱什琴斯基的追随者，这是瑞典在这场战争中于波兰境内唯一一次重大失利。1793年第二次瓜分波兰时，普鲁士吞并卡利什。沃伊切赫·博古斯瓦夫斯基1801年在此开设常驻剧场；1806年大波兰起义后，卡利什成为华沙公国的省府。1813年的俄普《卡利什条约》使普鲁士加入对拿破仑的战争，1815年城市划归波兰会议王国。

en:
Płock crowns a steep bluff above the Vistula where the Toruń–Warsaw trade route crossed the river. A gord raised there under the first Piasts served Mieszko I and Bolesław the Brave, and from 1079 to 1138 the city was the capital of Poland, the favoured seat of Władysław Herman and of Bolesław III Wrymouth, who was born in the town. The bishopric founded in 1075 and the Romanesque cathedral of 1130–1144, holding the sarcophagi of Masovian dukes, made it the church centre of Mazovia. Its bronze cathedral doors, cast in Magdeburg for Bishop Alexander of Malonne, reached Novgorod in the later thirteenth century and were hung in the cathedral of St Sophia there. The school founded at St Michael's collegiate church around 1180 is the oldest in Poland; Paweł Włodkowic, who told the Council of Constance that pagan peoples held a natural right to their own lands and rulers, studied there as a boy. After the fragmentation of 1138 Płock headed its own duchy: in 1329 John of Luxembourg besieged it and forced the dukes into Bohemian vassalage, and in 1410 the town was the main supply base for Jagiełło's armies marching on Grunwald. In 1444 it was the capital of the Duchy of Płock under the Masovian Piasts, a river port shipping grain.

When the last Płock duke, Janusz II, died in 1495, the duchy escheated to the Crown and Płock became a voivodeship seat; Queen Bona later held its starosty. Fire and a Vistula landslide wrecked the old castle early in the sixteenth century, yet burgomaster Jan Alantsee laid piped water through the streets in 1534, and by 1564 Płock counted 600 houses, as many as Warsaw. Plague carried off some 2,000 people in 1603 and fire burned most of the town in 1616. Swedish troops destroyed Płock in 1657, and the Great Northern War brought fresh ruin. After the Second Partition of 1793 it passed to Prussia, whose authorities pulled down the medieval walls and gates, and in 1815 it became a voivodeship city of Congress Poland.
zh:
普沃茨克雄踞维斯瓦河畔的陡峭高岗，托伦通往华沙的商路在这里渡河。皮雅斯特王朝初年的王公在此筑堡，梅什科一世和波列斯瓦夫一世都曾驻跸；1079至1138年这里是波兰首都，瓦迪斯瓦夫一世和出生于此的波列斯瓦夫三世最常住此。1075年设立的主教区和1130至1144年建成的罗曼式主教座堂使它成为马佐夫舍的教会中心，马佐夫舍诸公爵的石棺就安放在堂内。主教座堂那两扇在马格德堡为马隆的亚历山大主教铸造的青铜大门，13世纪下半叶流落到诺夫哥罗德，挂进了当地的圣索菲亚大教堂。约1180年在圣米迦勒协同教堂创办的学校是波兰最古老的学校，曾在康斯坦茨会议上主张异教民族对自己的土地和统治者拥有自然权利的帕韦乌·沃德科维奇早年就读于此。1138年分封之后，普沃茨克是普沃茨克公国的都城：1329年卢森堡的约翰围攻该城，逼公爵向波希米亚称臣；1410年雅盖沃的大军进击格伦瓦德时，这里是主要补给基地。1444年的普沃茨克是马佐夫舍皮雅斯特王公治下公国的首都，一座输出谷物的河港。

1495年末代公爵雅努什二世去世，公国作为无人继承的采邑收归王国，普沃茨克成为行省省会，王后博娜后来还领有当地的行政长官辖区。16世纪初的大火和维斯瓦河塌方毁了旧城堡，但市长扬·阿兰塞1534年仍把输水管道铺进城里，到1564年普沃茨克已有600栋房屋，与当时的华沙相当。1603年瘟疫夺去约两千人的生命，1616年大火又烧掉大半个城市。1657年瑞典军队摧毁普沃茨克，大北方战争时再遭破坏。1793年第二次瓜分后它并入普鲁士，中世纪城墙和城门在普方治下拆除；1815年起普沃茨克成为波兰王国的省辖市。

en:
Warsaw occupies a line of Masovian bluffs above the Vistula, with landing places below its ducal castle. Bródno and Jazdów were the earlier strongholds here; after Lithuanian raiders destroyed Jazdów in 1262, Bolesław II of Masovia built a new fort by the fishing village of Warszowa. Old Warsaw received a Kulm-law charter around 1300, St John's Cathedral was completed in 1390, and New Town was laid out beyond the walls in 1408. The dukes settled their main court there in 1413. In 1444 about 4,500 Polish-speaking Catholic craftsmen, boatmen and traders lived around the Masovian Piast castle; Warsaw was still the small capital of an independent duchy, not a city of the Polish Crown.

The duchy escheated to Poland after the death of Janusz III in 1526. Warsaw's site between Kraków and Vilnius suited the joined Polish-Lithuanian state: the General Sejm met there for the first time in 1529 and regularly after 1569. The Warsaw Confederation of 1573 promised peace between rival confessions, and nobles later gathered at Wola to elect the king. Sigismund III moved his court from Kraków in 1596, and Italian architects rebuilt the Royal Castle into a parliament and royal residence. In 1611 the captured Russian tsar Vasili IV did homage to Sigismund in its Senator's Chamber. During the Deluge, Swedish, Brandenburg and Transylvanian troops sacked Warsaw, and the Swedish-Brandenburg army defeated John II Casimir in the three-day Battle of Warsaw on 28-30 July 1656.

The Saxon kings later gave the city its long Saxon Axis, the public Saxon Garden in 1727 and the Załuski Library in 1747. Stanisław August added palaces, a state theatre and the remodelled castle interiors, and contemporaries called his capital the 'Paris of the North'. The Great Sejm passed the Constitution of 3 May 1791 in the Royal Castle. Kościuszko's rising ended outside the city when Suvorov stormed the Praga suburb on 4 November 1794; the Third Partition gave Warsaw to Prussia in 1795. Napoleon's victory made it capital of the Duchy of Warsaw in 1807, Austrian troops held it briefly after Raszyn in 1809, and the Congress of Vienna assigned the city to Russian-ruled Congress Poland in 1815. The Royal University opened the next year.
zh:
华沙位于马佐夫舍的维斯瓦河陡岸上，公爵城堡下便是河船停靠的地方。布鲁德诺和亚兹杜夫是更早的寨堡；1262年立陶宛袭扰者摧毁亚兹杜夫后，马佐夫舍的波列斯瓦夫二世在渔村瓦尔绍瓦旁另筑新城。旧华沙约在1300年依库尔姆法获得建城特许，圣若望主教座堂1390年落成，1408年城墙外又辟出新镇，1413年公爵把主要宫廷迁到这里。1444年，约四千五百名说波兰语、信奉天主教的工匠、船夫和商人环绕着马佐夫舍皮雅斯特家族的城堡生活；此时华沙还是独立的马佐夫舍公国小都城，尚未归入波兰王冠。

1526年雅努什三世去世，马佐夫舍公国并入波兰。华沙处在克拉科夫和维尔纽斯之间，适合合并后的波兰立陶宛联邦议事：全国瑟姆1529年首次在此召开，1569年后固定会址。1573年的《华沙联盟誓约》承诺不同教派和平共处，后来贵族又到沃拉原野选举国王。齐格蒙特三世1596年把宫廷从克拉科夫迁来，意大利建筑师将皇家城堡改建成王宫兼议会。1611年，被俘的俄国沙皇瓦西里四世在城堡的参议员厅向齐格蒙特三世致敬。大洪水时代，瑞典、勃兰登堡和特兰西瓦尼亚军队洗劫华沙；1656年7月28日至30日，瑞典与勃兰登堡联军又在三日华沙之战中击败扬二世·卡齐米日的军队。

萨克森王朝时期，华沙有了萨克森轴线、1727年开放的萨克森花园和1747年建成的扎武斯基图书馆。斯坦尼斯瓦夫·奥古斯特增修宫殿、国家剧院和城堡内殿，时人把这座都城称作「北方的巴黎」。1791年5月3日，四年瑟姆在皇家城堡通过《五三宪法》。1794年11月4日，苏沃洛夫强攻普拉加郊区，科希丘什科起义在此败亡；1795年第三次瓜分后，华沙划归普鲁士。1807年拿破仑获胜后，华沙成为华沙公国都城；1809年拉申之战后奥军曾短暂占领；1815年维也纳会议又把它划给俄罗斯治下的波兰王国。华沙皇家大学在次年开学。

en:
Sieradz stands on the Warta in central Poland, the chief town of the Sieradz Land. A castellan's gord here was already named in the Bull of Gniezno in 1136, and the town received Magdeburg rights in the mid-thirteenth century, which makes it one of the oldest in the kingdom. It was the seat of the Duchy of Sieradz during the feudal fragmentation, and when the duchy reverted to the Crown in 1339 Casimir the Great strengthened its castle and the town became the capital of the Sieradz Voivodeship, which also took in the Wieluń Land. Armies passed through in nearly every century: the Mongols sacked Sieradz in all three of their invasions of Poland, and Bohemian and Teutonic raids followed. The town owed its standing above all to the assemblies held within its walls. In 1383 the nobility acclaimed Jadwiga as their queen here, and in 1445 they elected Casimir IV Jagiellon king; Sieradz knights had fought at Grunwald, and Jagiełło afterwards founded a chapel in the castle. In 1444 Sieradz was a royal town living from the grain trade on the Warta, while nearby Łódź, chartered in 1423, was still a small market town belonging to the bishops of Włocławek.

A Jewish community settled in Sieradz in 1453, and the voivodeship's sejmiks met here into the sixteenth century, drawing Spanish and Portuguese merchants to its markets. The Swedish Deluge of 1655–56, followed by plague, fires and floods, ended that prosperity; by the eighteenth century the town held only about 1,500 people. Prussia annexed it in the Second Partition of 1793. On 13 November 1806 the townspeople rose against the Prussian garrison, and from 1807 Sieradz belonged to the Duchy of Warsaw. In 1815 the Congress of Vienna assigned it to Congress Poland under the Russian tsar, as a district seat in the Kalisz province.
zh:
谢拉兹位于波兰中部的瓦尔塔河畔，是谢拉兹地区的首城。1136年的格涅兹诺诏书已提到这里的城堡长官驻地；13世纪中叶它获得马格德堡城市权，是王国最古老的城市之一。分裂割据时期，这里是谢拉兹公国的都城；1339年公国并回王国，卡齐米日大王扩建了当地城堡，谢拉兹成为谢拉兹省的首府，辖区还包括维隆地区。军队几乎每个世纪都要经过这里：蒙古人三次入侵波兰都洗劫过此城，波希米亚和条顿骑士的袭扰随后而至。这座城市的地位尤其得自城墙内召开的集会：1383年贵族在这里拥立雅德维加为女王，1445年又在这里选举卡齐米日四世·雅盖隆契克为国王；谢拉兹的骑士参加过格伦瓦德战役，战后雅盖沃在城堡中捐建了一座小教堂。1444年，谢拉兹是一座靠瓦尔塔河粮食贸易为生的王家城市；附近1423年取得特许状的罗兹，当时还是弗沃茨瓦韦克主教名下的小集镇。

1453年，犹太社区来此定居；直到16世纪，谢拉兹省的地方议会都在这里召开，连西班牙和葡萄牙商人也来到它的市集。1655至1656年瑞典入侵的「大洪水」，加上随后的瘟疫、火灾和洪水，终结了这份繁荣，到18世纪全城只剩约一千五百人。1793年第二次瓜分波兰时，谢拉兹被普鲁士吞并。1806年11月13日，市民起兵反抗普鲁士驻军；1807年起，谢拉兹并入华沙公国。1815年维也纳和会把它划给俄皇治下的波兰会议王国，成为卡利什省下辖的县城。

en:
Sandomierz stands on the Vistula along a line of seven hills, near where the San flows in and the old road from western Europe to Ruthenia forded the river. Gallus Anonymus numbered it with Krakow and Wroclaw among the three chief seats of the Polish kingdom, and Boleslaw III's will, dividing Poland among his sons, made it the capital of the Duchy of Sandomierz. The Dominicans built their second Polish priory there early in the thirteenth century, and in the Mongol sack of 1259 to 1260 the raiders killed Blessed Sadok and forty-eight of his friars at their prayers in the church. Leszek the Black refounded the burnt town under Magdeburg law in 1286, and Casimir III rebuilt it, raising the royal castle above the river and the Gothic Opatow Gate in its walls. As the seat of Sandomierz Voivodeship the city grew rich on grain floated down the Vistula, with some 3,000 inhabitants, and from 1437 to 1441 it sheltered the exiled Empress Barbara of Cilli, widow of Sigismund of Luxembourg. In 1444 Sandomierz was a royal city of the Crown, where the king's court and the nobility's assemblies often met.

In April 1570 Lutheran, Calvinist and Bohemian Brethren envoys gathered there and signed the Consensus of Sandomierz, a pact to face the Counter-Reformation together while each confession kept its own rites. The Jesuits founded their college in 1602, later called Gostomianum. In 1606 rebellious nobles raised the Sandomierz Rokosz against Sigismund III, until royal troops broke it in 1607. The Deluge ended the city's standing: Swedish armies passed through in 1655 and 1656, and retreating Swedish troops blew up the royal castle in 1656, killing about fifty Poles who had entered behind them; only the west wing stood, rebuilt under John III Sobieski. Sandomierz never recovered its old size. Austria took it with the Third Partition in 1795, and it later passed to the Duchy of Warsaw and the Russian-ruled Congress Kingdom.
zh:
桑多梅日位于维斯瓦河畔，依七座丘陵而建，临近桑河汇入处，西欧通往罗斯的古商道在此渡河。编年史家高卢·阿诺尼穆斯把它和克拉科夫、弗罗茨瓦夫并列为波兰王国三大重镇，波列斯瓦夫三世的遗嘱将它定为桑多梅日公国的都城。13世纪初，多明我会在此设立波兰第二座修道院；1259至1260年蒙古人洗劫城市时，真福萨多克和四十八名修士在教堂祈祷时被杀。1286年，莱谢克二世按马格德堡法重建焚毁的城市并授予仓储权，卡齐米日三世再次营建，在河畔筑起王室城堡，又在城墙中修起哥特式的奥帕图夫门。作为桑多梅日省治所，城市靠顺维斯瓦河而下的粮食贸易致富，人口约有三千；1437至1441年，遭放逐的皇后芭芭拉·采列（神圣罗马帝国皇帝西吉斯蒙德的遗孀）在此栖身。1444年的桑多梅日是波兰王国的王家城市，国王宫廷和贵族集会常在此举行。

1570年4月，路德宗、加尔文宗和捷克弟兄会的代表在此签订《桑多梅日共识》，约定各派共抗反宗教改革，同时保留各自仪轨。1602年耶稣会创办学院，即后来的戈斯托米亚努姆。1606年，不满的贵族举兵反对齐格蒙特三世，史称桑多梅日叛乱，1607年被王军平定。大洪水时代终结了城市的地位：瑞典军队1655至1656年过境，撤退的瑞军1656年炸毁王室城堡，约五十名随之进入城堡的波兰人被炸死，仅存的西翼后来在扬三世·索别斯基治下重建。桑多梅日再未恢复往日的规模。1795年第三次瓜分时它被奥地利取得，此后先后归属华沙公国和俄国控制的波兰会议王国。

en:
Lublin occupies the heights between the Czechówka and Bystrzyca valleys, where the road from Kraków split toward Vilnius and the Black Sea on the old Lendian border. Its name first appears in a document of 1198. Casimir III built the stone castle and town walls on this exposed eastern frontier, and the surviving Magdeburg charter is the one Władysław I granted on 15 August 1317. The union with Lithuania turned a border fortress into a merchants' meeting place: a general sejm at Lublin accepted Jogaila as king in 1386, and in 1392 he gave the townsmen free trade throughout the Grand Duchy. The castle's Holy Trinity Chapel was painted with Latin and Byzantine frescoes. In 1444 Lublin was a prospering Catholic royal town, and in the following century the largest trade fairs in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth were held on its market square.

Lublin became the seat of its own voivodeship in 1474. The Sejm meeting in the castle proclaimed the Union of Lublin on 26 June 1569, joining Poland and Lithuania into a single commonwealth, and from 1578 the Crown Tribunal made the town the highest court of appeal for Lesser Poland. Jan Kochanowski, the leading poet of the Polish Renaissance, died there in 1584. Calvinists and Polish Brethren made Lublin a Reformation centre, while the Jewish yeshiva taught the Talmud and Kabbalah and drew students from far away; in 1567 its head received from the king the title and rights of a university rector, and the town was called the Jewish Oxford, its Jewish quarter entered through the Grodzka Gate. The Deluge ended the prosperity when Russo-Cossack troops sacked Lublin in 1655 and Swedish troops in 1656. The Hasidic master Yaakov Yitzchak, known as the Seer of Lublin, taught there in the later eighteenth century. A renewal commission of 1780 rebuilt the town hall and paved the streets, but Russian troops entered in 1792; the Third Partition assigned the town to Austria in 1795, the Duchy of Warsaw took it in 1809, and from 1815 it belonged to Russian-ruled Congress Poland.
zh:
卢布林占据切胡夫卡河与贝斯特日察河谷之间的高地，地处古伦第人故地的东缘，克拉科夫通往维尔纽斯和黑海的道路在此分岔。其名最早见于1198年的一份文件。卡齐米日三世在这条暴露的东部边防线上修筑石城堡和城墙，现存的马格德堡法特许状则是1317年8月15日瓦迪斯瓦夫一世所颁。与立陶宛的联合把边境要塞变成商人汇聚之地：1386年一次全国议会在卢布林召开，接受雅盖沃为波兰国王，1392年雅盖沃又赐予市民在立陶宛大公国全境自由贸易的权利。城堡中的圣三一礼拜堂绘有拉丁与拜占庭两种风格的壁画。1444年，卢布林是繁荣的天主教王室城镇；进入下个世纪，波兰立陶宛联邦最大的市集就开在它的市场广场上。

1474年，卢布林成为本省的省会。1569年6月26日，在城堡召开的议会宣布卢布林联合，把波兰和立陶宛合成一个联邦；1578年起，王室法庭又使这座城市成为小波兰的最高上诉法院。波兰文艺复兴的代表诗人扬·科哈诺夫斯基于1584年在这里去世。加尔文派和波兰兄弟会把卢布林变成宗教改革的一个中心；犹太经学院讲授塔木德和卡巴拉，吸引远方学生，1567年其院长从国王手中领得与大学校长同等的头衔和权利，卢布林因而被称为「犹太人的牛津」，犹太街区要从格罗兹卡门进入。大洪水时代终结了繁荣：1655年俄罗斯-哥萨克军队、1656年瑞典军队先后洗劫城市。18世纪后期，人称「卢布林先见」的哈西迪派名师雅各布·伊茨哈克在此讲学。1780年城市改良委员会翻建市政厅、铺整街道，但俄军1792年入城；1795年第三次瓜分把卢布林划归奥地利，1809年华沙公国将其夺取，1815年起归入俄国统治的波兰会议王国。

en:
Halicz grew up on the Dniester as the river port of a much older capital, whose ruins lie five kilometres upstream at Krylos. It was there, at princely Halych, that Volodymyrko set his seat in 1141 after uniting Peremyshl, Zvenyhorod and Terebovlia into the Principality of Halych; Roman joined it to Volhynia in 1199, and under Danylo, crowned a king of Ruthenia, the chronicles counted the city among the largest in Kievan Rus, with ten white-stone churches around its Dormition Cathedral, where Yaroslav Osmomysl lay buried. Batu Khan's Mongols sacked it in 1241, and Lviv slowly took its place. The surviving town stands at the old Dniester landing, where the Lithuanian prince Liubartas built a wooden castle in 1367. Casimir III of Poland annexed Halicz in 1349 and granted it Magdeburg rights, and the Roman Catholic archbishopric set up there moved to Lviv in 1409. Hungarian governors held Red Ruthenia until Queen Jadwiga removed them in 1387. In 1444 Halicz was an Orthodox Ruthenian town and an administrative centre of the Polish-ruled Ruthenian Voivodeship, its river landing serving the grain lands around it.

From 1564 the town ran its own dietine for the Land of Halicz, taking in the Halicz, Trembowla and Kolomyja districts, and Stephen Báthory settled Karaim families there. It lay open to the Podolian steppe. Crimean Tatars burned it in 1621, and Hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski caught the raiders at nearby Martynów on 20 June 1624. Cossacks of Bohdan Khmelnytsky seized and destroyed Halicz in 1649, and Turkish and Tatar forces sacked it again in 1676. A survey of 1765 found only 110 houses and three churches. Austrian troops occupied the town in the First Partition of 1772, and under Habsburg rule it became part of the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria, a title taken from the medieval Latin name of Halych itself.
zh:
哈利奇在德涅斯特河畔发展起来，本是一座更古老都城的河港，那座都城的遗址就在上游五公里的克雷洛斯。1141年，沃洛迪米尔科合并佩列梅什利、兹韦尼哥罗德和捷列博夫利亚之后，在「王公哈利奇」设都；1199年罗曼又把哈利奇与沃里尼亚合并。在加冕为罗斯国王的丹尼洛治下，史书把这座城列为基辅罗斯最大的城市之一，圣母安息大教堂周围有十座白石教堂，雅罗斯拉夫·奥斯莫梅斯尔就安葬在堂内。1241年拔都的蒙古军队洗劫该城，利沃夫后来慢慢取代它的地位。现存的哈利奇镇坐落在旧河码头上，1367年立陶宛王公柳巴尔塔斯在这里修过一座木堡。1349年波兰国王卡齐米日三世兼并哈利奇，授予马格德堡法，当地设立的罗马天主教大主教区1409年迁往利沃夫。红鲁塞尼亚一度由匈牙利总督控制，1387年雅德维加将他们逐走。1444年时，哈利奇是波兰治下鲁塞尼亚省的一座东正教鲁塞尼亚城镇和行政中心，河上码头服务着周围产粮的土地。

1564年起，哈利奇为哈利奇地区单设地方议会，下辖哈利奇、捷列博夫利亚和科洛梅亚三县，斯特凡·巴托里还把卡拉伊姆人家族安置在城中。这里正对着波多利亚草原：1621年克里米亚鞑靼人焚毁哈利奇，1624年6月20日，盖特曼斯坦尼斯瓦夫·科涅茨波尔斯基在附近的马尔蒂努夫截住归途上的袭掠者并将其击败。1649年博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基的哥萨克攻占并摧毁哈利奇，1676年土耳其和鞑靼军队再次洗劫。1765年的调查只记下110栋房屋和三座教堂。1772年第一次瓜分时奥地利军队占领该城，哈利奇被划入哈布斯堡君主的加利西亚和洛多梅里亚王国，而「加利西亚」本就是哈利奇中世纪拉丁名的一部分。

en:
Kraków stands on the Vistula at the foot of Wawel Hill, where the Vistulans built their stronghold before the Piast kings made it the seat of the Polish monarchy. Legend calls its founder Krakus, who ruled above the cave of the Wawel dragon. The Mongols burned the town in 1241, and Bolesław V refounded it in 1257 under Magdeburg law, laying out the grid around the Main Market Square, the largest medieval market square in Europe. Revenues from the royal salt mines at nearby Wieliczka and Bochnia flowed through the city, and Hanseatic membership drew foreign merchants and craftsmen. In 1444, as Władysław III marched to Varna, Wawel remained the Jagiellons' palace, coronation church and royal burial place.

Casimir III founded the Cracow Academy in 1364, central Europe's second university after Prague, where Nicolaus Copernicus later studied. Under the later Jagiellons Kraków had its golden age: Kasper Straube printed the first book produced in Poland in 1473, Veit Stoss carved the great altar of St Mary's Church, Bartolommeo Berrecci rebuilt Wawel Castle in Italian style, and Hans Behem cast the Sigismund Bell in 1520. The Cloth Hall stood in the middle of the Main Market, and the city's Jews were moved to Kazimierz, whose Old Synagogue headed a major Jewish quarter. When the Jagiellon line ended, succession war reached the capital: in 1587 Jan Zamoyski beat off Archduke Maximilian III of Austria's main assault on 24 November. Sigismund III moved the court to Warsaw in 1596, but kings were still crowned and buried at Wawel. Swedish troops took the city in 1655, and George II Rákóczi's Transylvanian army occupied it in 1656 and 1657.

Bar confederates held the city until Alexander Suvorov's Russians stormed Wawel Castle on 24 April 1772; the First Partition nevertheless left it in the reduced Commonwealth. On 24 March 1794 Tadeusz Kościuszko swore in the Main Market Square to lead a national rising; Prussian troops entered that June and carried off the crown regalia, and after the Third Partition of 1795 the city passed to Austria. Polish forces took it for the Duchy of Warsaw in 1809, Russian troops followed in 1813, and the Congress of Vienna made Kraków a free city in 1815.
zh:
克拉科夫坐落于维斯瓦河畔、瓦维尔山下。维斯瓦兰人最早在山上修筑要塞，后来皮雅斯特诸王把这里定为波兰君主的都城。相传建城者是王公克拉库斯，城址就在瓦维尔龙所居洞穴上方的山丘。1241年蒙古人焚城，1257年博莱斯瓦夫五世按马格德堡法重新设城，围绕欧洲最大的中世纪集市广场主市场铺出棋盘式街道。附近维利奇卡和博赫尼亚的皇家盐矿把收入送往这座城市，加入汉萨同盟后又有外国商人和工匠前来落户。1444年瓦迪斯瓦夫三世出征瓦尔纳时，瓦维尔是雅盖隆诸王的王宫、加冕教堂和王陵所在。

卡齐米日三世1364年创办克拉科夫学院，是中欧仅次于布拉格的第二所大学，哥白尼后来曾在此求学。雅盖隆王朝后期是克拉科夫的黄金时代：1473年卡斯珀·施特劳贝印出波兰第一部印刷书籍，法伊特·施托斯为圣母圣殿雕成大祭坛，巴尔托洛梅奥·贝雷奇按意大利风格重建瓦维尔城堡，汉斯·贝赫姆1520年铸成齐格蒙特钟。主市场中央是纺织会馆；城里的犹太人被迁往卡齐米日，老会堂是那一大片犹太街区的中心。雅盖隆王统断绝后，继承战争波及都城：1587年扬·扎莫伊斯基据城抵御奥地利大公马克西米连三世，11月24日击退总攻。齐格蒙特三世1596年把宫廷迁往华沙，但国王照旧在瓦维尔加冕、下葬。1655年瑞典军队攻陷城市，1656至1657年拉科齐·捷尔吉二世的特兰西瓦尼亚军队又占领此地。

巴尔联盟以克拉科夫为据点，直到1772年4月24日亚历山大·苏沃洛夫率俄军强攻瓦维尔城堡；即便如此，第一次瓜分后城市仍属缩小后的波兰共和国。1794年3月24日，塔德乌什·柯斯丘什科在主市场宣誓领导全民起义；普军6月入城并劫走王冠珍宝，1795年第三次瓜分后城市划归奥地利。1809年波兰军队为华沙公国夺取此城，1813年俄军接踵而至，1815年维也纳会议把克拉科夫定为自由城市。

en:
Ratibor guards the Oder crossing where the old road from the Moravian Gate runs on toward Kraków. The Slavic Ślężanie kept a hill fort there, and the town's name is traditionally traced to a Duke Racibor; its first confirmed mention comes in 1108, when Bolesław III of Poland defended the place against an invasion from Bohemia. The townsmen held brewing privileges as early as the twelfth century, and Ratibor beer was sold across Silesia and Bohemia. In 1172 the Piast duke Mieszko I made the settlement the seat of his new Duchy of Racibórz, the first historical capital of Upper Silesia, settled Flemish merchants below the castle, and in 1211 struck a coin bearing the Polish word MILOST. His son Casimir I granted civic rights in 1217, and from 1299 an autonomous council ruled under Magdeburg law. A Mongol raid was beaten back at the Battle of Racibórz in 1241 under Duke Mieszko II, who then founded the town's Dominican monastery. In 1327 Duke Leszek did homage to John of Bohemia, and after 1336 the Opava Přemyslids held the duchy. In 1444 Ratibor was a Catholic Silesian town of the Bohemian Crown, living by breweries, tanneries and cloth works and by traffic on the upper Oder.

The Přemyslid line died out with Duke Valentin in 1521, and Ratibor was united with Opole; when Jan II the Good died in 1532 the duchy reverted to the Habsburg kings of Bohemia and was pledged to George of Brandenburg-Ansbach. Emperor Rudolf II's privilege of 1586 regulated navigation on the Oder, confirming the river port. The united duchy was held by the Polish Vasas from 1645 to 1666, and in 1683 John III Sobieski banqueted in the castle on his march to relieve Vienna. Frederick the Great's Silesian wars and the Treaty of Breslau brought Ratibor to Prussia in 1742, and a would-be assassin attacked Frederick II in the town in 1788. After the Holy Roman Empire was dissolved in 1806 it stayed a Prussian Silesian district town, whose gymnasium opened in 1819.
zh:
拉蒂博尔（波兰语今译拉齐布日）扼守奥德河渡口，摩拉维亚门通往克拉科夫的古道在此过河。斯拉夫希隆斯克部落曾在山上设堡，城名相传来自一位名叫拉齐布日的公爵；现存最早的确凿记载是1108年，当时波兰的博莱斯瓦夫三世在此抵御波希米亚来犯。市民早在12世纪就享有酿酒特权，拉蒂博尔啤酒销往整个西里西亚和波希米亚。1172年，皮雅斯特公爵梅什科一世以此为新封的拉齐布日公国都城，这是上西里西亚历史上第一个都城；他在城堡下安置佛兰德商人，1211年还铸出一枚带波兰语铭文「MILOST」的钱币。其子卡齐米日一世1217年授予城市特权，1299年起自治市议会依据马格德堡法治理。1241年，梅什科二世公爵在拉齐布日之战击退一支蒙古袭掠军，随后在城中修建多明我会修道院。1327年公爵莱谢克向波希米亚国王约翰行臣服礼，1336年以后公国由普热米斯尔王朝的奥帕瓦支系统治。1444年时，拉蒂博尔是波希米亚王冠领内的天主教西里西亚城市，靠酿酒、制革、织布作坊和奥德河上游航运为生。

1521年末代公爵瓦伦丁去世，普热米斯尔支系统绝，拉蒂博尔与奥波莱合并；1532年「善人」扬二世死后，公国收归波希米亚的哈布斯堡国王，随即抵押给勃兰登堡-安斯巴赫的格奥尔格。1586年鲁道夫二世颁布特权令规范奥德河航运，确认了这里的河港地位。1645至1666年，联合公国在波兰瓦萨王朝手中；1683年，扬三世·索别斯基在驰援维也纳途中曾在城堡宴饮。腓特烈大帝的西里西亚战争和1742年《布雷斯劳条约》使拉蒂博尔归入普鲁士，1788年又有人在城中行刺腓特烈二世未遂。1806年神圣罗马帝国解体后，它仍是普鲁士治下的西里西亚地区城镇，当地文理中学1819年开办。

en:
Breslau is the chief town of the Silesian lowlands, on the Oder where the overland Via Regia met the Amber Road. Its bishops took their see on Cathedral Island in 1000, and the Silesian Piasts made the town their ducal capital. Magdeburg rights in 1261 and staple rights in 1274 let its merchants hold goods moving between the Baltic, Hungary, Nuremberg and the Netherlands; Breslau joined the Hanseatic League in 1387. After the last local Piast, Henry VI, died in 1335, the city passed to the Bohemian Crown, while Brieg, Öls, Wohlau and neighbouring duchies remained Piast fiefs. An earthquake damaged it on 5 June 1443. In 1444 Breslau was a largely self-governing, German-speaking Catholic city with a great market, Brick Gothic churches and the leading mint and trade houses of Silesia.

Matthias Corvinus of Hungary ruled Silesia from Breslau as rival king of Bohemia between 1469 and 1490. A Polish-Czech army besieged the city in 1474, the same year it left the Hanse. The printer Kasper Elyan produced the Statuta Synodalia there in 1475, the first printed book in Polish. Protestant teaching reached Breslau early and the city became mainly Lutheran after 1518, although Habsburg rule after 1526 brought Jesuit churches and schools. Saxon and Swedish troops occupied it during the Thirty Years' War, and plague cut through its population. The pastor Caspar Neumann kept detailed baptism and burial registers; Edmond Halley used them in 1693 to publish the first actuarial life tables. The Jesuit Leopoldina University opened in 1702.

Frederick the Great's first Silesian War made Breslau a Prussian city, confirmed by the Peace of Breslau in 1742. Austrian troops retook it after the Battle on the Lohe on 22 November 1757, but Frederick's victory at Leuthen the following month returned Silesia to Prussia. General Vandamme's Napoleonic soldiers forced the city's surrender in January 1807 and later pulled down its fortifications. In 1811 Prussia merged the Viadrina University of Frankfurt an der Oder into the Leopoldina. Two years later, King Frederick William III issued his call to arms in Breslau, and Prussian volunteers assembled there for the war against Napoleon.
zh:
布雷斯劳（今弗罗茨瓦夫）是西里西亚低地的首城，位于奥得河畔，陆上的国王大道与琥珀之路在此相接。1000年，主教座堂设在堂岛，西里西亚皮雅斯特公爵以这里为都城。城市1261年获得马格德堡法，1274年又取得货物集散特权，商人得以控制波罗的海、匈牙利、纽伦堡与尼德兰之间的货物；1387年，布雷斯劳加入汉萨同盟。末代本地皮雅斯特公爵亨里克六世1335年去世后，城市转归波希米亚王冠，布热格、奥莱希尼察、沃武夫等周边公国仍是皮雅斯特家族的封地。1443年6月5日，地震破坏了城市。1444年的布雷斯劳是一座高度自治、居民多说德语的天主教城市，有大集市、砖砌哥特式教堂，也掌握着西里西亚最重要的铸币和商号。

1469年至1490年，匈牙利的马加什·科尔温以波希米亚对立国王的身份，从布雷斯劳统治西里西亚。1474年，波兰和捷克联军围城，布雷斯劳也在同年退出汉萨同盟。1475年，印刷商卡斯珀·埃利安在此印成《主教会议法令集》，这是第一部波兰文印本书。新教学说很早传入，1518年后城市主要改宗路德宗；1526年哈布斯堡家族接掌此地，耶稣会则修建教堂、开办学校。三十年战争中，萨克森和瑞典军队占领布雷斯劳，瘟疫也夺去许多居民。牧师卡斯帕尔·诺伊曼留下详细的受洗和丧葬登记，爱德蒙·哈雷利用这些资料在1693年发表第一张精算生命表。1702年，耶稣会的莱奥波尔迪纳大学开学。

腓特烈大帝发动第一次西里西亚战争后，布雷斯劳成为普鲁士城市，1742年的《布雷斯劳和约》确认了这一归属。1757年11月22日洛厄河之战后，奥军一度重夺城市，但腓特烈次月在洛伊滕取胜，西里西亚又回到普鲁士手中。1807年1月，旺达姆将军麾下的拿破仑军队迫使城市投降，后来又拆除城防。1811年，普鲁士把奥得河畔法兰克福的维亚德里纳大学并入莱奥波尔迪纳大学。两年后，腓特烈·威廉三世在布雷斯劳发布对拿破仑作战的号召，普鲁士志愿兵也在此集结。

en:
Brno lies between the Svitava and Svratka rivers in southern Moravia, under the Petrov and Špilberk hills. The castle, a Přemyslid seat from the eleventh century, is first named in Cosmas' chronicle of 1091. King Wenceslaus I chartered the town in 1243, and from the mid-fourteenth century the Moravian Luxembourgers kept their seat at Špilberk. The last of them, Jobst, elected King of the Romans in 1410, died at the castle early the next year and was buried in St Thomas's church. It shared Moravia's diet, land court and land tables with the older bishop's city Olomouc, and local wine was cellared beneath the vegetable market. Hussite attacks in 1428 and 1430 failed against its walls, so in 1444 Brno was a firmly Catholic, German-speaking patrician town of the Bohemian Crown while the Hussite question still split the rest of the kingdom.

Its rivalry with Olomouc ended in the Thirty Years' War, when Ferdinand III moved Moravia's diet, court and land tables to Brno in 1641 and 1642. In 1645 Lennart Torstensson besieged it for nearly four months with some 28,000 men; about 1,500 soldiers and burghers under Jean-Louis Raduit de Souches held out, and the Swedes lost roughly 8,000 men and withdrew. Legend says the defenders rang Petrov's noon bells an hour early: the Swedes had sworn to take the city by midday or lift the siege, and they marched away. A stuffed crocodile called the Brno Dragon, under repair at civic cost in 1578, hangs in the Old Town Hall passage. A Prusso-Saxon siege under Frederick the Great failed in 1742.

The first textile works opened in 1763, beginning the industry that earned Brno the name Moravian Manchester; in December 1767 the eleven-year-old Mozart and his sister Nannerl played at the Taverna theatre on the vegetable market. Brno became a bishop's see in 1777, and Joseph II confirmed it as Moravia's sole capital in 1782. Napoleon stayed here from 20 November to 12 December 1805 while Austerlitz was fought a short march to the east; the French occupation brought requisitions and typhoid, and in 1809 French troops returned for four months and dismantled Špilberk's fortress works.
zh:
布尔诺位于摩拉维亚南部的斯维塔瓦河与斯夫拉特卡河之间，彼得罗夫主教山和史皮尔伯克城堡山俯临全城。11世纪时普舍美斯王公在此设庭，城堡之名最早见于1091年的《科斯马斯编年史》。1243年，瓦茨拉夫一世授予城市特许状；14世纪中期起，卢森堡王朝的摩拉维亚藩侯以史皮尔伯克为驻地。末代摩拉维亚藩侯约布斯特1410年当选罗马人的国王，次年初在城堡中去世，葬于圣多马教堂。布尔诺与更古老的主教城市奥洛穆茨轮流承办摩拉维亚等级会议、地方法院和土地簿，周围葡萄园的葡萄酒藏在菜市场下的地窖里。胡斯军队1428年和1430年两度攻城不克，因此1444年的布尔诺是波希米亚王冠领内一座坚定的天主教城市，由说德语的城市贵族治理，而胡斯问题仍在分裂王国其余各地。

它与奥洛穆茨的竞争在三十年战争中终结：1641年和1642年，斐迪南三世把摩拉维亚等级会议、法院和土地簿迁往布尔诺。1645年，伦纳特·托尔斯滕松麾下约两万八千瑞典军在城外耗了近四个月，被让-路易·拉迪伊·德·苏什率领的约一千五百名士兵和市民挡住，损失约八千人后撤围。相传瑞典主帅曾发誓中午前攻不下城池便撤围，守城者便在11点敲响彼得罗夫山报午的钟声，瑞典军拔营而去。旧市政厅通道里挂着一只鳄鱼标本，人称「布尔诺龙」，1578年的市政账目已有为它修缮除虫的支出。1742年，腓特烈大帝麾下的普鲁士-萨克森军队围城失败。

1763年第一家纺织工场开办，呢绒业日后为布尔诺赢得「摩拉维亚的曼彻斯特」之名；1767年12月，11岁的莫扎特和姐姐娜奈尔在菜市场的酒馆剧院登台。1777年布尔诺教区成立，1782年约瑟夫二世确认它为摩拉维亚唯一首府。1805年11月20日至12月12日拿破仑驻留于此，奥斯特里茨战役在城东不远的行军路程上打响，法国占领带来征发和伤寒；1809年法军又占领四个月，并拆毁史皮尔伯克的要塞工事。

en:
Prague grew up at a Vltava ford beneath the castle raised around 880 by Duke Bořivoj. Charles IV made it the capital of the Empire: St Vitus Cathedral was begun in 1344, Charles University and the New Town date from 1348, and the Charles Bridge rose on the site of the Judith Bridge swept away by flood. In 1410 the Old Town Hall received its astronomical clock, made by the horologist Mikuláš of Kadaň and the astronomer Jan Šindel; a later legend names a Master Hanuš as its maker and says the councillors blinded him so he could never build another. Jan Hus preached at the Bethlehem Chapel from 1402 and was burned at Constance in 1415; in 1419 his followers threw the town councillors out of the windows, opening the Hussite Wars, and Jan Žižka routed Emperor Sigismund's crusaders on Vítkov Hill in 1420. The Compacts ended the wars but left Bohemia half Hussite, half Catholic. In 1444 King Ladislaus was a child at the emperor's court in Austria, and the Prague towns ran their own affairs under their councils.

George of Poděbrady marched on Prague from Kutná Hora in 1448 and was elected king by the estates in 1458; Benedikt Rejt vaulted the Castle's Vladislav Hall in 1490–1502, vast enough for mounted tournaments. After the estates chose Ferdinand of Habsburg in 1526, Rudolf II moved his court here in 1583, and Tycho Brahe, Kepler and Arcimboldo worked in the city. Rabbi Loew, whom Rudolf received to discuss the Kabbalah in 1592, is the hero of a later legend in which he fashioned a clay golem to guard the Jewish ghetto. The second defenestration, on 23 May 1618, began the Thirty Years' War; after the White Mountain defeat of 1620, twenty-seven rebel lords were executed in the Old Town Square in 1621 and Prague was forced back to Catholicism. In 1648 Swedish troops looted the Castle's collections, and the wars cut the city from 60,000 people to 20,000.

Fire devastated Prague in 1689, and the plague of 1713–1715 killed about 13,000, a quarter of its inhabitants; Frederick the Great bombarded it in 1757, destroying about 880 houses. Joseph II merged the four old towns in 1784, and on 29 October 1787 Mozart conducted the premiere of Don Giovanni at the Nostitz Theatre.
zh:
布拉格兴起于伏尔塔瓦河的一处渡口，880年前后，王公博日沃伊在河畔高地上建起城堡。查理四世把这里定为帝国首都：1344年圣维特大教堂动工，1348年查理大学开学、新城开建，查理大桥架在被洪水冲毁的尤迪特桥故址上。1410年，老城市政厅装上天文钟，钟出自钟表匠卡丹的米库拉什和天文学家扬·辛德尔之手；后世传说却把它记在匠人哈努什名下，说议员们怕他替别处再造一座，刺瞎了他的眼睛。扬·胡斯自1402年起在伯利恒礼拜堂讲道，1415年在康斯坦茨被处以火刑；1419年，他的追随者把议员掷出窗外，胡斯战争爆发，1420年扬·杰式卡在维特科夫山击溃皇帝西吉斯蒙德的十字军。布拉格协定结束战争，却让波希米亚一半是胡斯派、一半是天主教徒。1444年，国王拉迪斯拉夫还是奥地利皇帝宫廷里的幼童，布拉格诸城由各自的市议会自行治理。

1448年，波杰布拉德的伊日从库特纳霍拉进军布拉格，1458年被议会推举为国王；1490至1502年，本尼迪克特·列特为城堡的弗拉迪斯拉夫大厅架起拱顶，厅内宽大得可以跑马比武。1526年议会选立哈布斯堡的斐迪南一世，1583年鲁道夫二世把宫廷迁到布拉格，第谷·布拉赫、开普勒和阿尔钦博托都在此供职。勒乌拉比1592年还曾入宫与鲁道夫谈论卡巴拉，后世传说他用泥土造出会动的戈仑（Golem）守护犹太隔都。1618年5月23日第二次掷出窗外事件引爆三十年战争；1620年白山战败后，二十七名叛乱贵族1621年在老城广场被处死，布拉格被强制重皈天主教。1648年瑞典军队抢走城堡珍藏，战乱使布拉格人口从六万降到两万。

1689年大火焚毁大片城区，1713至1715年的鼠疫夺命约一万三千条，占全城人口的四分之一；腓特烈大王1757年炮轰布拉格，约八百八十栋房屋被毁。1784年约瑟夫二世合并四座旧城；1787年10月29日，莫扎特在诺斯蒂茨剧院亲自指挥《唐璜》首演。

en:
Plzeň lies at the meeting of the Mže, Radbuza, Úhlava and Úslava, whose waters form the Berounka on the road from Prague to Bavaria. Wenceslaus II laid out New Plzeň in 1295, and the regular royal town soon ranked behind only Prague and Kutná Hora in Bohemia; its brewers were at work by 1307. The Hussite wars gave the town its defining cause. Near Nekmíř, about seventeen kilometres to the north-west, Jan Žižka's small band used the first recorded wagon fort of the wars to defeat a Catholic Landesfriede army at the end of 1419. Radical clergy left Plzeň with Žižka in 1420, and the town stayed on the Catholic side. Žižka besieged it once and Prokop the Great twice without breaking the walls. In 1444 the royal city guarded Bohemia's western road and made its living from the border carrying trade.

After the wars the Prague cathedral chapter moved to Plzeň in 1467, and a local press produced the Statuta of Arnošt of Pardubice in 1476, the oldest printed book recorded in Bohemia. Rudolf II brought the imperial court to Plzeň from September 1599 to June 1600 while he avoided the plague in Prague. The Thirty Years' War reached the town in 1618, when Mansfeld's estates army took it; imperial forces recovered it in 1621. Albrecht von Wallenstein made Plzeň his winter quarters in 1633, months before his murder in Cheb. Swedish sieges failed in 1637 and 1648, while Jan van der Croon rebuilt the walls as bastions between 1645 and 1649. In 1695 Jan Sladký Kozina, leader of the Chod rising, was executed in the main square.
zh:
