16世纪初，哈萨克人的压力把诺盖人赶过伏尔加河以西，空旷的沙地转手卡尔梅克人：1628至1630年，和鄂尔勒克率土尔扈特卫拉特人渡过亚伊克河，把莱恩沙地变成自己的冬牧场。他们一直占有此地，直到1771年土尔扈特人拔营东归准噶尔，沙漠几乎空无一人。1773至1774年普加乔夫起义期间，亚伊克河以东的哈萨克队伍随起义军驰骋过这片牧场。1801年，沙皇保罗准许小玉兹苏丹布克依率五千帐、两万两千余人渡过亚伊克河，进入空旷的草原；他们的布克依斡耳朵又称内帐，在俄国宗主权下领有莱恩沙地。

en:
Bayuly is open grazing country east of the middle Yaik, running toward the Irgiz and the dry steppe beyond it. No walled town held these pastures. Horses, sheep and cattle moved between summer grass up the rivers and winter camps in the warmer south, with wells marking every stage; caravans from Saraychik to the Syr Darya used the same chain of water points. In 1444 Sunni Manghit clans of the Nogai Horde pastured their herds here. The name Bayuly belongs to the later Kazakh order, when twelve rods including the Adai, Berish and Zhappas formed one of the two great branches of the Alshyn tribe in the Little Jüz.

The twelve rods followed Abulkhair Khan when he took the Russian oath in 1731, but the frontier soon restricted the old movements of their herds. Their best-known leader, Syrym Datuly, rode with Pugachev's Cossacks in 1774 and then led the Little Jüz rising from 1783 to 1797. The Ural Cossacks captured him in the first year, and Khan Nuraly ransomed him; the same khan became one of the rebels' targets after Cossack patrols barred herders from the Yaik's right bank. Nuraly was driven out in 1786, and when the rising collapsed Syrym took his followers to Khiva in 1797. In 1801 Nuraly's son Bukey led about five thousand families across the Yaik into the thinly populated Volga steppe and founded the Inner, or Bukey, Horde with Russian permission.
zh:
巴伊乌勒是亚伊克河中游以东的开阔牧地，一直延伸到伊尔吉兹河和更干燥的草原。这里没有城墙围起的城镇，马、羊、牛沿着一处处水井，往返于河流上游的夏牧场与温暖南方的冬营地；从萨莱楚克前往锡尔河的商队也靠这串水井前行。1444年时，诺盖汗国的逊尼派曼吉特各部在此放牧。巴伊乌勒这个名称属于后来的哈萨克部落格局：阿代、别里什、扎帕斯等十二支，成为小玉兹阿尔申部落两大分支之一。

1731年，十二部随阿布勒海尔汗向俄罗斯宣誓，但边防很快限制了牧民旧有的转场路线。各部最知名的首领瑟雷姆·达托夫1774年曾随普加乔夫的哥萨克作战，1783至1797年又领导小玉兹起义。起义头一年，乌拉尔哥萨克俘获了他，努拉里汗将他赎出；后来哥萨克巡哨禁止牧民前往亚伊克河右岸，努拉里也成了起义者反对的目标之一。努拉里1786年被逐，起义失败后，瑟雷姆在1797年率部众退往希瓦。1801年，努拉里之子布克依经俄罗斯允许，率约五千户越过亚伊克河，进入人烟稀少的伏尔加草原，建立内帐，也称布克依斡耳朵。

en:
Alimuly covers the drier southern pastures of the Nogai steppe. The stony Mugodzhar hills rise between the Yaik and the Irgiz, and the grazing runs south-east to the reedy north-eastern shore of the Aral Sea and the edge of the Ustyurt plateau. Wells along this line carried caravan traffic from Saraychik toward Khiva. In 1444 Sunni Manghit herders moved between Mugodzhar springs and Aral reed beds, choosing camps by water rather than by any fixed town. The later Kazakh name belongs to six Alshyn rods, the Shekty and Tortkara among them; the Shekty used especially the north-eastern Aral lands.

During the seventeenth century these pastures were exposed to Kalmyk raids from the west and Dzungar pressure from the east. The great Dzungar invasion of the 1720s drew the six rods behind Abulkhair Khan, whose strongest tribal following lay among them. Kazakh oral tradition preserves the battle at Añyraqai as a victory for the Kazakh army under his overall command. Abulkhair took the Russian oath in 1731, which left the Little Jüz with a khan backed by the tsar while quarrels over his Russian alignment continued. Baraq Sultan killed him in 1748; the Shekty tradition adds that Sultan Batyr helped plan the killing. The Shekty then rejected Abulkhair's son Nuraly, proclaimed Batyr their khan, and split the Little Jüz into two rival khanates.
zh:
艾力木乌勒是诺盖草原上更干旱的南部牧场。多石的穆戈贾雷山隆起在亚伊克河与伊尔吉兹河之间，牧地向东南延伸到芦苇丛生的咸海东北岸和乌斯秋尔特高原边缘。沿这条线分布的水井，支撑着从萨莱楚克通向希瓦的商队。1444年时，逊尼派曼吉特牧人在穆戈贾雷山泉水和咸海芦苇滩之间转场，按水源而不是城镇选择营地。这个省名来自后来哈萨克阿尔申部落的六个分支，谢克特、托尔特卡拉都在其中，谢克特人尤其常在咸海东北一带游牧。

17世纪时，这片牧场西受卡尔梅克人袭扰，东遭准噶尔人进逼。1720年代准噶尔大举入侵，六部聚集到阿布勒海尔汗麾下，他最稳固的部众也来自这些分支。哈萨克口头传说把安拉凯之战传为其统一指挥下哈萨克军队的一场胜仗。阿布勒海尔1731年向俄罗斯宣誓，使小玉兹有了沙皇支持的汗，但部众对他亲俄路线的争执没有停止。1748年，巴拉克苏丹杀死阿布勒海尔；谢克特人的说法还称巴蒂尔苏丹参与谋划。谢克特人随后拒认阿布勒海尔之子努拉里，拥立巴蒂尔为汗，小玉兹分裂成两个对立的汗廷。

en:
The Zhetyru steppe lies where dry grassland climbs into the wooded southern Urals. Along the upper Yaik and the Tobol headwaters, birch and pine cover the ridges while black-earth glades open below them, giving herds both summer grazing and sheltered winter camps. Bashkir herders already used the nearby mountains, and the forest edge marked the limit between herders who lived in felt tents and trappers who worked the Ural valleys. In 1444 this was the north-eastern march of the Nogai Horde, where Sunni Manghit clans camped close to Bashkir pastures.

The later Kazakh name belongs to seven old Desht-i-Kipchak rods, Tabyn and Tama among them. Kazakh genealogies say Tauke Khan joined the weak clans in the late seventeenth century, an account also preserved through Abulkhair Khan's report to the Russian envoy Tevkelev. Each rod kept its own tamga mark and war cry, and the new union was attached to the Little Jüz. Dzungar raids in the 1720s pushed the seven rods into Abulkhair's alliance and the Russian oath of 1731. Ivan Kirilov's Orenburg expedition then built its first fort at the mouth of the Or in 1735, the post later called Orsk, and Kirilov presented it as a step toward routes to Bukhara and India. The Bashkir rising of 1735–1740 swept these hills while the line was being built; Chelyaba covered the Miass flank to the north-east and Orenburg became the final headquarters in 1743.
zh:
杰特鲁草原位于干旱草地抬升为南乌拉尔林地的地带。亚伊克河上游和托博尔河源头一带，山脊上长满桦树和松树，山下展开黑土林间空地，既有夏牧场，也有可避风寒的冬营地。巴什基尔牧人已在附近山地活动，林缘大致分开了住毡帐的牧人和乌拉尔山谷中的猎户。1444年时，这里是诺盖汗国的东北边地，逊尼派曼吉特各部在巴什基尔牧场旁扎营。

杰特鲁这个名称来自塔本、塔马等七个古老的钦察草原氏族。哈萨克谱系说，17世纪末头克汗把这些弱小氏族合并起来；俄国使者捷夫克列夫转述阿布勒海尔汗的说法，也留下了同样记载。每一支都保留自己的塔姆加印记和战吼，这个新联合体后来并入小玉兹。1720年代准噶尔袭扰，七部加入阿布勒海尔的联盟，并于1731年随他向俄罗斯宣誓。随后，伊万·基里洛夫的奥伦堡考察团在1735年把第一座要塞修在奥尔河口，即后来的奥尔斯克；基里洛夫把它看作通向布哈拉和印度商路的一步。要塞线修建期间，1735至1740年的巴什基尔起义席卷这片山地；切利亚巴拱卫东北方的米阿斯河侧翼，奥伦堡则在1743年成为整条防线的最终大本营。

en:
Samara lies where the Samara River joins the Volga, on the great loop called the Samara Bend. Ahmad ibn Fadlan, travelling to the Volga Bulgars in 921, noted the river, and Italian charts of the fourteenth century already mark a Volga port named Samara. Under the Golden Horde the peninsula of the bend was a pirates' nest: lookouts watched for passing boats, crossed the neck of the peninsula to give warning, and the freebooters put out after their prey. In 1444 the left bank was the steppe edge of the new Khanate of Kazan, pasture for Nogai herds, with no Russian town yet built.

After Moscow took Kazan in 1552 it moved to secure the Volga road to Astrakhan. In 1586, on Tsar Fyodor's order, voevoda Grigory Zasekin built a wooden fortress at the river mouth between 9 May and 6 August, manned by streltsy, gunners and gate guards; to keep the Nogai mirza friendly Moscow told him the fort was there only to shield his people from Cossack raiders. A customs house followed in 1600, and Samara became a meeting place for Russian merchants and envoys travelling to the East. Stepan Razin's rebels took it in 1670, and in 1773 it was the first town to go over to Yemelyan Pugachev. In the 1740s the Orenburg Expedition made the town its base; Vasily Tatishchev was one of its heads, and the expedition founded Orenburg and Stavropol on the Volga. Catherine II made Samara an uyezd town of Simbirsk Governorate in 1780.
zh:
萨马拉位于萨马拉河注入伏尔加河处，坐落在萨马拉河湾的大弯环上。阿拉伯使者艾哈迈德·伊本·法德兰921年出使伏尔加保加利亚途中记下了这条河，14世纪的意大利海图上也已标出伏尔加河畔一处叫萨马拉的港口。金帐汗国时期，河湾围出的半岛是盗匪盘踞之地：望手盯梢过往船只，穿过半岛地峡报信，匪徒便驾船出掠。1444年时，伏尔加左岸是新兴喀山汗国的草原边缘，诺盖牧人在此放牧，俄国人的城镇尚未出现。

1552年莫斯科攻陷喀山后，着手保障通往阿斯特拉罕的伏尔加水路。1586年奉费奥多尔沙皇诏令，督军格里戈里·扎谢金于5月9日至8月6日间在河口筑起木堡，由射手、炮手和守门兵戍守；为安抚诺盖米尔扎，莫斯科对他说，筑堡只是为了保护其部众不受哥萨克盗匪袭扰。1600年这里设立海关，萨马拉成为俄国商人和使者前往东方的会集地。1670年，斯捷潘·拉辛的起义军攻占此城；1773年，它又是第一座倒向叶梅利扬·普加乔夫的城市。1740年代，奥伦堡考察团以该城为驻地，瓦西里·塔季谢夫是负责人之一，奥伦堡和伏尔加河畔的斯塔夫罗波尔都由该考察团主持建立。1780年，叶卡捷琳娜二世把萨马拉设为辛比尔斯克省的县城。

en:
The Yaik carries the snowmelt of the southern Urals some twelve hundred kilometres to the Caspian, and in 1444 its middle course was Nogai country. Manghit clans pastured sheep and horses along the banks and camped on the river islands to fish, and the sturgeon runs were already prized. No town stood on this stretch; the Horde's only city, Saray-Jük, lay far downstream near the mouth.

Fugitive Volga Cossacks who had helped sack Saray-Jük settled the middle river in the 1580s. The Nogais destroyed their first fort in 1613, and the survivors refounded it on the peninsula between the Yaik and the Chagan; 1613 became the accepted founding year of Yaitsk. A charter from Tsar Michael granted the host the entire river from source to mouth, and sturgeon and caviar made the Cossacks rich, though fifteen hundred of them died on Bekovich-Cherkassky's Khiva expedition of 1717. Quarrels over fishing rights and the loss of their self-government brought a rising in 1772, when they cut down General von Traubenberg, and the repression that followed drove them to Yemelyan Pugachev. On 17 September 1773 the Don Cossack deserter proclaimed himself Tsar Peter III at the Budarinsky outpost and raised his standard. Yaitsk fell to him, and a loyal garrison held out for months in the fortified cathedral of the Archangel Michael until relieved in April 1774. In January 1775 Catherine II erased the name Yaik from the map: the river became the Ural, the host the Ural Cossacks and the town Uralsk.
zh:
亚伊克河承接南乌拉尔山的融雪，流过约一千二百公里注入里海。1444年，其中游是诺盖人的土地：曼格特诸部在两岸放牧羊马，在河洲上扎营捕鱼，河中的鲟鱼鱼汛已为人看重。这一河段没有城镇，汗国唯一的城市萨莱楚克远在靠近河口的下游。

1580年代，参与洗劫萨莱楚克的一批出逃伏尔加河哥萨克在中游落脚。1613年他们的第一座堡寨被诺盖人摧毁，幸存者在亚伊克河与恰甘河之间的半岛上重建，1613年便被定为亚伊茨克的建城年份。米哈伊尔沙皇的诏书把整条河自源头到河口赐给哥萨克军，鲟鱼和鱼子酱让他们富足，1717年却有一千五百人在别科维奇-切尔卡斯基的希瓦远征中丧命。渔业权益之争加上自治被夺，引发1772年暴动，哥萨克杀死冯·特劳本贝格将军，随之而来的镇压把他们推向叶梅利扬·普加乔夫。1773年9月17日，这个顿河哥萨克逃兵在布达林斯基哨所自称沙皇彼得三世，举旗起事。亚伊茨克陷落，忠于政府的守军据守天使长米哈伊尔大教堂数月，直到1774年4月解围。1775年1月，叶卡捷琳娜二世把「亚伊克」一名从地图上抹去：河改名乌拉尔河，哥萨克军改称乌拉尔哥萨克军，城镇改称乌拉尔斯克。

en:
Bashkortostan covers the middle course of the Belaya, called Aghidhel in Bashkir, where the forest belt opens into steppe and Bashkir tribes grazed cattle and horses between the two. On the hill above the river medieval maps already mark a substantial town: the Pizzigano map of 1367 and the Catalan Atlas of 1375 call it Pascherti, Mercator keeps the name in 1554, and Ibn Khaldun lists Bashkort among the great cities of the Golden Horde. In the sixteenth century the same ground held Imen-kala, the oak-built seat of the Nogai governors. When the Golden Horde broke up, the western Bashkir tribes fell to the Kazan khanate. In 1444 they were Hanafi Sunni herdsmen, Kazan's subjects, exposed to Nogai raids out of the open steppe.

After Ivan the Terrible took Kazan in October 1552, Bashkir embassies treated with his governors in 1554 to 1557 and took charters confirming their ancestral pasturelands. In 1574 the voevoda Mikhail Nagoy raised a wooden fortress on the Tura-Tau hill, the future Ufa, granted town status in 1586; for two centuries it was the main Russian strongpoint east of the Volga. Its garrison beat off the Siberian tsarevich Ablai and his Kalmyks in 1635 and took him prisoner. Bashkir risings swept the country round the walls more than once; the bloodiest, in 1735 to 1740, answered the building of the Orenburg chain of forts across the pasturelands. In the winter of 1773 to 1774 Ufa withstood a months-long siege and assault by Pugachev's rebels, even as Bashkir horsemen joined the rising.

Catherine II's government made the town the seat of the Ufa viceroyalty in December 1781. On 4 December 1789 the Orenburg Mohammedan Spiritual Assembly opened here under her charter of 1788, a state muftiate that appointed imams and judged family law for the Muslims of the Volga, Urals and Siberia. In 1798 the Bashkirs were mustered into a Cossack-style irregular host, their cavalry posted on the empire's eastern edge.
zh:
巴什科尔托斯坦占据别拉亚河（巴什基尔语称阿吉代尔）中游一带，林带在此铺展为草原，巴什基尔诸部在林草之间放牧牛马。河畔山丘上曾有一座颇具规模的城镇：1367年的皮齐加诺地图和1375年的《加泰罗尼亚地图集》把它标作帕什凯尔季，1554年墨卡托的地图沿用此名，伊本·赫勒敦也把巴什科特列入金帐汗国的大城市。16世纪时，同一处地点是诺盖比伊的橡木驻地伊缅卡拉。金帐汗国解体后，巴什基尔西部诸部归于喀山汗国。1444年时，他们是奉哈乃斐教法的逊尼派牧人，臣服喀山，南面草原上的诺盖骑兵随时可能来袭。

1552年10月伊凡雷帝攻灭喀山后，巴什基尔各部使团在1554至1557年与沙皇的总督谈判，领到确认祖传牧场的特许状。1574年，督军米哈伊尔·纳戈伊在山丘上筑起木要塞，即后来的乌法，1586年获准设城；此后两百年间，它是伏尔加河以东俄国最主要的据点。1635年，守军击退西伯利亚王公阿布莱及其卡尔梅克盟军的来犯，将阿布莱生擒。巴什基尔人的起义一再席卷城外四乡，最惨烈的一次在1735至1740年，起因是奥伦堡要塞链穿过牧场修筑。1773至1774年冬，乌法顶住普加乔夫义军长达数月的围攻和强攻，与此同时大批巴什基尔骑兵加入了起义。

1781年12月，叶卡捷琳娜二世的政府把乌法设为乌法总督区驻地。依女皇1788年的诏令，奥伦堡穆罕默德宗教会议于1789年12月4日在此开幕：这是国家管理的穆夫提公署，为伏尔加、乌拉尔和西伯利亚的穆斯林任命伊玛目、裁断家事教法。1798年，巴什基尔人被编为哥萨克式的非正规军，其骑兵驻守帝国东缘。

en:
Kypshak is the central Kazakh steppe used by Kipchak clans, a country of dispersed wells and seasonal pastures later counted among the tribes of the Middle Jüz. There were few walled towns here; authority moved with tents, herds and cavalry between summer and winter grazing. After the eastern Golden Horde fragmented, Abu'l-Khayr Khan united the Shibanid clans of Dasht-i Qipchaq and took the khan's title in 1429. He campaigned toward Khwarezm and the lower Volga, and in 1431-32 seized Orda-Bazar. Russian sources describe it chiefly as a nomadic khan's headquarters and market rather than a fixed city, a place where coin could be struck for an ulus on the move. In 1444 Orda-Bazar was the camp centre of Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek confederation; two years later he took Sighnaq, Sozak and other Syr Darya towns. Kipchak, Kerey and Naiman clans pastured horses and sheep under his uneasy rule.

Two Chinggisid sultans, Kerei and Janibek, rejected that authority and withdrew toward Moghulistan; Kazakh tradition dates their khanate from 1465. Abu'l-Khayr died in battle in 1468, and when the sultans returned to central Kazakhstan much of the steppe followed them. Under Burunduk from 1480 and Qasim Khan from 1511 to 1521, the Kazakh confederation became the leading power of the eastern steppe, with its authority reaching toward the Urals. Dzungar armies overran the pastures in spring 1723, sending Middle Jüz refugees toward Samarkand and Khujand; Kazakh forces recovered after victories in 1728 and 1730. The Middle Jüz accepted nominal Russian suzerainty soon after 1731, while Ablai Khan used the collapse of Dzungaria between 1771 and 1781 to rebuild Kazakh power. After Vali Khan died in 1817, Russian forts and frontier officials pressed increasingly close to the old Kipchak grazing grounds.
zh:
钦察是哈萨克中部草原上钦察氏族的牧地，水井分散，牧场随季节转换，这里后来归入中玉兹诸部。这片土地上少有城墙环绕的城镇；权力跟着毡帐、畜群和骑兵在夏冬牧场之间移动。金帐汗国东翼瓦解后，阿布勒海尔汗统一钦察草原上的昔班尼诸部，于1429年称汗。他向花剌子模和伏尔加河下游用兵，并在1431至1432年夺取奥尔达-巴扎尔。俄罗斯资料主要把它记作游牧汗廷和市集，而非固定城市，却可以为移动的兀鲁思铸造钱币。1444年，奥尔达-巴扎尔是阿布勒海尔乌兹别克联盟的驻营中心；两年后，他攻取昔格纳黑、苏扎克等锡尔河城市。钦察、克列和乃蛮等氏族在其并不稳固的统治下放牧马和羊。

克列和贾尼别克两位成吉思汗系苏丹拒绝接受这一权威，率部迁往蒙兀儿斯坦；哈萨克传统把他们建国定在1465年。1468年阿布勒海尔战死，两位苏丹返回哈萨克中部后，草原上的许多部众随之归附。1480年起在位的布伦杜克和1511至1521年在位的卡西姆汗，使哈萨克联盟成为东部草原的首要强权，势力向西延伸到乌拉尔河一带。1723年春，准噶尔军队席卷各牧场，中玉兹难民涌向撒马尔罕和苦盏；哈萨克人在1728年和1730年取胜后逐渐恢复。1731年后不久，中玉兹接受俄国名义上的宗主权；1771至1781年，阿布赉汗趁准噶尔崩溃重建哈萨克权势。瓦里汗1817年去世后，俄国要塞和边疆官员日益逼近旧日的钦察牧场。

en:
The Nadym pasture is the dry middle course of the Sarysu, arid grassland between the oasis towns of the Talas valley and the low ridges of the Sary-Arka. Wells are few and often brackish, and southward the grass thins into the hunger-steppe of Betpak-Dala. Clans that wanted grain, cloth or metal goods drove their herds down to the Syr Darya, above all to the walled market of Sighnaq, which had been the capital of the Blue Horde in the thirteenth century. In 1444 the Kipchak clans camping here belonged to Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Uzbek ulus, the strongest power on the eastern Dasht-i Qipchaq, whose khan still held court at Tura in western Siberia; its horses and wool moved south along the caravan tracks to Sighnaq.

In 1457 Oirats under Uz-Temur-tayishi routed Abu'l-Khayr's army near Sighnaq, and when he died on campaign in 1468 the ulus fell apart. Kerei and Janibek, Jochid princes who had led their followers off to the Zhetysu a few years before, returned at the head of the clans now called Kazakhs, and the Sarysu pastures became grazing ground of the Middle Jüz. The worst blow came in 1723, when Dzungar armies overran the southern steppe in the 'Years of the Great Disaster': the auls left their winter camps and stock behind and fled to the Syr Darya. The united militia answered with victories at Bulanty in 1726 and near Lake Balkhash in 1729. The rulers of the Middle Jüz accepted Russian suzerainty in 1740, and Abylai Khan, a veteran commander of the Dzungar wars who was elected khan of all three jüzes at Turkestan in 1771, held the confederation together until his death in 1781.
zh:
纳德姆牧地是萨雷苏河中游一带的干旱草原，处在塔拉斯河谷的绿洲城镇与萨雷阿尔卡丘陵之间。水井稀少，水多苦咸；向南草木渐稀，没入别特帕克-达拉「饥饿草原」。需要粮食、布匹或金属器的部落，赶着牲畜南下锡尔河，主要去往筑有城墙的市集昔格纳克，它在13世纪曾是蓝帐汗国的都城。1444年，在此游牧的钦察诸部属于阿布勒海尔汗的乌兹别克兀鲁思，他是东钦察草原最强的势力，汗廷还设在西西伯利亚的图拉城；马匹和羊毛沿商道南下，运到昔格纳克售卖。

1457年，乌兹帖木儿太师率领的卫拉特人在昔格纳克附近大败阿布勒海尔；1468年他死于出征途中，兀鲁思随之瓦解。数年前率领部众迁往七河之地的术赤系宗王克烈与贾尼别克，此时率领改称哈萨克的诸部重返草原，萨雷苏牧场后来成为中玉兹的游牧地。最重的一击在1723年：准噶尔军队席卷南部草原，史称「大灾难年代」，诸部抛下冬营地和牲畜逃往锡尔河。联军1726年在布兰泰、1729年在巴尔喀什湖附近先后取胜。1740年中玉兹诸汗接受俄国宗主权；阿布莱汗本是准噶尔战争中打出来的将领，1771年在突厥斯坦被三玉兹推举为汗，把联盟维系到1781年去世。

en:
The Argyn are the most numerous tribe of the Kazakh Middle Jüz. Their clans range over the dry Sary-Arka steppe from the Turgai plateau in the west to the Chingiz mountains below the Altai, and south to the north-western shore of Lake Balkhash, moving sheep, horses and wool-bearing flocks between summer and winter pastures. Their genealogies name Karakhodzha, a fourteenth-century emir of the Golden Horde, as their ancestor; his descendants split into the Meiram and Momyn branches, and the tribe charges to the cry 'Akzhol'. In 1444 the Argyn auls pastured within the Uzbek ulus of Abu'l-Khayr Khan, between his Syr Darya towns and the Irtysh frontier.

Abu'l-Khayr's death in 1468 undid his ulus, and the Argyns went over to the sultans Kerei and Janibek, becoming the leading tribe of the Middle Jüz. Their biys sat in the khan's council. The most famous was Kazybek (1667–1763) of the Karakesek clan, one of the three great judges of the Kazakhs, an orator and envoy who under Tauke Khan helped compile the Zhety Zhargy, the code of steppe customary law; he was born on the Syr Darya and died at his winter camp by the Terakty spring in the Sary-Arka. The Dzungar war brought forward Abylai, who had risen as leader of the large Atygai clan. The invasion of 1741 carried him off to Galdan Tseren's camp, where he was held until 1743, a year after the Middle Jüz accepted Russian suzerainty. In 1771 the three jüzes raised him as their khan at Turkestan.
zh:
阿尔浑是哈萨克中玉兹人数最多的部落。各部在干旱的萨雷阿尔卡草原游牧，在夏牧场与冬营地之间辗转，地域西起图尔盖高原，东到阿尔泰麓的成吉思山脉，南抵巴尔喀什湖西北岸，牧放绵羊、马匹和毛用羊群。谱系把始祖追溯到14世纪金帐汗国的埃米尔卡拉霍加，后裔分为梅拉姆、莫温两大支，部族冲锋时高呼「阿克卓勒」。1444年，阿尔浑的阿乌尔在阿布勒海尔汗的乌兹别克兀鲁思中游牧，牧地夹在他的锡尔河城镇与额尔齐斯河边地之间。

1468年阿布勒海尔一死，兀鲁思瓦解，阿尔浑人投奔克烈、贾尼别克两位苏丹，成为中玉兹首屈一指的部落。阿尔浑的比位列汗廷，其中最有名的是喀拉克塞克氏族的哈孜别克（1667—1763）：他是哈萨克三大比之一，以雄辩和出使闻名，头克汗时期参与编纂草原习惯法典《七项法典》；他生于锡尔河畔，晚年在萨雷阿尔卡捷拉克特泉边的冬营地去世。准噶尔战争中，因统领大阿提盖部而起家的阿布莱崭露头角。1741年的入侵把他掳往噶尔丹策零的营地，一直囚禁到1743年；此前一年，中玉兹接受了俄国宗主权。1771年，三玉兹在突厥斯坦推举他为汗。

en:
Kerey is named for both a closed salt lake in the basin of Lake Tengiz and the river that drains the dry pasture around it. The camps along their shores belonged to the Kerei, a Kazakh tribe whose genealogies reached back to the Altai; most scholars trace them to the Keraites of Wang Khan, broken by Genghis Khan in the early thirteenth century. In later tribal reckonings the Kerei were counted among the six tribes of the Middle Jüz. In 1444 these pastures owed allegiance to Abu'l-Khayr, the Shibanid khan of the Uzbek nomads, while the herdsmen who moved across them spoke Kazakh and were Sunni Muslims.

The secession that produced the Kazakh khanate began among steppe tribes like these. In the late 1450s the sultans Kerei and Janibek led perhaps 200,000 nomads away from Abu'l-Khayr to the Chu and Talas valleys in Moghulistan. Abu'l-Khayr marched against them in 1468 and died on campaign, and Kerei ruled as the first Kazakh khan until he was killed fighting the Shibanids. The Kerei clans stayed with the Middle Jüz through the long wars against the Dzungars. The invasion of 1739-1741 forced its sultans to surrender hostages, and the Middle Jüz khan accepted Russian subjecthood in 1740. Ablai Khan, the last independent Kazakh khan, led the struggle against the Dzungars and later the Qing, and kept room to negotiate until his death in 1781; afterwards the northern pastures faced the Russian fortified lines with no khan between them.
zh:
凯里既是田吉兹湖流域一座没有出流的咸水湖之名，也是排泄湖畔干草原的同名河之名。湖河沿岸的营地属于克烈部，其谱系追溯到阿尔泰山，多数学者认为他们是王罕克烈部人的后裔，该部在13世纪初被成吉思汗击败。后来的部落划分把克烈列为中玉兹六大部落之一。1444年，这片牧场臣属于乌兹别克游牧人的昔班尼系汗王阿布勒海尔，而在牧场上转场的牧民说哈萨克语，是逊尼派穆斯林。

哈萨克汗国的分立正是从这样的草原部落中发端的。15世纪50年代末，克列汗与贾尼别克苏丹率约20万游牧人脱离阿布勒海尔，西迁蒙兀儿斯坦的楚河与塔拉斯河谷。阿布勒海尔1468年发兵来攻，死在出征途中，克列成为第一位哈萨克汗，后来在同昔班尼系的战争中被杀。克烈诸部留在中玉兹，经历了同准噶尔的长期战事。1739—1741年的入侵迫使中玉兹诸苏丹交出人质，中玉兹汗于1740年接受俄国臣属。最后一位独立的哈萨克汗阿布赉汗先后领导对抗准噶尔和清朝的战事，把周旋的余地维持到1781年去世；此后北部牧场直接面对俄国的筑垒防线，中间再没有汗王缓冲。

en:
Pegaya Orda covers the Kulunda steppe, the grassland and salt-lake country south of Baraba, reaching from the Ob and Irtysh lowlands toward the Altai foothills. Its wealth moved on four legs: sheep supplied wool, horses and cattle supported the camps, and hunting and the salt of inland lakes added to the herds' value. The Telengets, usually called Teleuts in Russian records and later named White Kalmyks there, pastured these lands in seasonal camps and winter quarters. They spoke a Turkic language and called their polity the Telenget ulus. In 1444 no walled town or fixed frontier stood here; the camps lay within the Oirat world and owed service or tribute when Oirat power reached the steppe.

Around 1600, Russian documents describe about 4,000 Telenget tents between the Irtysh and the Ob. The ulus then became a buffer between Muscovy and the Dzungar Khanate, and its princes changed alliances as the two powers pressed in. Prince Abak made an agreement with Moscow in 1609 and joined Russian campaigns in 1611 and 1615. Prince Koka swore to the Dzungars in 1645, submitted to the tsar in 1658 and resumed war in 1659. Russian voevodes drove him from the Meret camp across the Ob in 1661, and the Dzungar ruler Sengge subdued the ulus in 1663. In 1703 more than 20,000 Telengets were removed towards the Altai and the Ili. By 1717 the Telenget princes had become Dzungar officials, and the old steppe ulus no longer acted as an independent power.
zh:
佩加亚奥尔达地处库伦达草原，牧地和盐湖从巴拉巴草原以南铺展，由鄂毕河与额尔齐斯河之间的低地伸向阿尔泰山麓。这里的财富随牲畜移动：绵羊提供羊毛，马匹和牛支撑营地，狩猎和内流湖泊出产的盐也增加了牧群的价值。捷连格特人在俄国文献中多称捷列乌特人，后来又被称为「白卡尔梅克人」；他们按季节在这片土地上扎营、过冬。他们操突厥语，把自己的政治联合体称为捷连格特兀鲁思。1444年，这里没有城墙城镇或固定边界；各营地处在瓦剌势力范围内，瓦剌军力抵达草原时便要服役、纳贡。

约1600年前后，俄国文献记载额尔齐斯河与鄂毕河之间约有四千顶捷连格特人的毡帐。这个兀鲁思随后夹在莫斯科与准噶尔汗国之间，历代王公在两大势力挤压下反复改换盟邦。阿巴克王公1609年与莫斯科订约，并在1611年和1615年参加俄国远征。科卡王公1645年向准噶尔宣誓，1658年臣服沙皇，1659年又重启战事。1661年，俄国督军把他从梅列特营地逐过鄂毕河；1663年，准噶尔首领僧格征服这个兀鲁思。1703年，两万多名捷连格特人被迁往阿尔泰和伊犁方向。到1717年，捷连格特王公已成为准噶尔官吏，旧的草原兀鲁思不再作为独立势力行动。

en:
Bermuda is a remote North Atlantic archipelago of cedar-covered islands and encircling coral reefs, far beyond the nearest American coast. Seabirds and turtles nested on its shores, but storm-wracked approaches and hidden reefs made the waters dangerous to shipping. No Indigenous people lived there when Europeans first reached the islands. In November 1444, Bermuda was therefore uninhabited, unknown to European pilots and absent from their Atlantic charts.

Early in the sixteenth century the Spanish captain Juan de Bermúdez sighted the islands that took his name; by 1511 they appeared in print and on Spanish charts, although Spain and Portugal used them only for water and fresh meat. On 3 August 1609 the Virginia Company ship Sea Venture, driven off course by a hurricane while bound for Jamestown, was deliberately run onto the reefs; her company survived, built the Deliverance and Patience, and their report opened the way for the Plough to found St George's in 1612. The Somers Isles Company took over in 1615, the assembly met from 1620, and the first enslaved people, one Black and one Native American brought from the West Indies, arrived in 1616. After the company's charter was revoked in 1684, Bermuda turned from weak tobacco crops to shipbuilding, whaling, salt and privateering. During the American Revolutionary War islanders shipped gunpowder to the rebels in 1775, and from 1811 the Royal Naval Dockyard on Ireland Island made Bermuda a base for Atlantic operations, including the War of 1812.
zh:
百慕大是北大西洋深处的遥远群岛，岛上有刺柏林，海岸有海鸟和海龟栖息，外围则被珊瑚暗礁环绕。这里远离美洲大陆，风暴和险滩让船只难以靠近；欧洲人最初抵达时，岛上并无原住民。1444年11月的百慕大因此仍是一片无人居住的岛群，欧洲领航员还不知道它的位置，海图上也没有它的踪影。

16世纪初，西班牙船长胡安·百慕大望见这片后来以其姓氏命名的群岛；到1511年，百慕大已见诸文献和西班牙海图，但西班牙、葡萄牙都只把这里当作补给淡水和鲜肉的停泊地。1609年8月3日，驶往詹姆斯敦的弗吉尼亚公司船只「海洋冒险号」在飓风中偏离航线，为避免沉没而主动冲上暗礁。船员和乘客全部生还，随后造出「拯救号」和「忍耐号」；他们的记述促成1612年「犁号」运来移民，建立圣乔治镇。萨默斯岛公司1615年接管殖民地，议会自1620年召开，1616年则有两名奴隶自西印度群岛运来，一人为黑人，一人为美洲原住民。公司特许状1684年被撤销后，百慕大放弃收成不佳的烟草，转向造船、捕鲸、盐业和私掠巡航。美国独立战争期间，岛民在1775年向革命者偷运火药；1811年起，爱尔兰岛上的皇家海军造船厂使百慕大成为大西洋作战基地，1812年战争中的行动也由此发起。

en:
The Bahamas are a long chain of low islands and cays on the Great Bahama Bank, north of Cuba and Hispaniola. The Lucayans, who called themselves Lukku-Cairi, or people of the islands, were related to the Taíno and had crossed from Cuba or Hispaniola in dugout canoes centuries earlier, spreading through the nineteen largest islands. In 1444 they lived in small chiefdoms, fished the grass flats and reefs, gathered queen conch and sea turtles, tended cassava and other crops, wove cotton, and traded pottery and stone tools across the shallow bank. On the eve of European contact their population has been estimated at about 30,000; no European settlement yet guarded the harbour that would become Nassau.

On 12 October 1492 Columbus landed at Guanahani, which he named San Salvador, and met the Lucayans. Vespucci carried 232 islanders away as slaves in 1500, and after a royal order of 1509 Spanish raiders took Lucayans to Hispaniola and Cubagua as labourers and pearl divers; by 1520 a search found only eleven islanders in the Bahamas, leaving the cays deserted for roughly 130 years. In 1648 William Sayle's Eleutheran Adventurers came from Bermuda and made the first permanent English settlement on Eleuthera. Charles Town was founded on New Providence in 1670, burned by Spanish raiders in 1684, and rebuilt under Nicholas Trott in 1695 as Nassau, honouring William III of Orange-Nassau. The port later became a pirate republic, but Woodes Rogers arrived as royal governor in 1718, pardoning pirates who submitted and hanging those who did not; he also held the town against a Spanish attack in 1720. An assembly followed in 1729. Americans briefly took Nassau in 1776, Spain captured it in 1782, and British rule returned in 1783, bringing Loyalist planters, cotton estates, and enslaved African majorities. Britain ended the slave trade in 1807, and by 1818 Africans brought into the Bahamas on foreign ships could obtain manumission.
zh:
巴哈马是大巴哈马浅滩上一长串低矮岛屿和珊瑚礁，位于古巴与伊斯帕尼奥拉以北。卢卡扬人自称卢库凯里（Lukku-Cairi），意为「岛屿之人」，与泰诺人有亲缘关系；他们在几个世纪前乘独木舟从古巴或伊斯帕尼奥拉渡来，逐渐扩散到十九个最大的岛屿。1444年，他们以小型酋邦为社会组织，在海草浅滩和礁岩间捕鱼，采集女王凤凰螺和海龟，种植木薯等作物，纺织棉花，并在浅水浅滩之间贸易陶器和石器。欧洲人到来前夕，他们的人口估计约有30000人；那时还没有欧洲人据点守卫后来成为拿骚的港湾。

1492年10月12日，哥伦布在瓜纳哈尼登陆，将其命名为圣萨尔瓦多，并第一次见到卢卡扬人。1500年，韦斯普奇带走232名岛民为奴；1509年西班牙王室下令输入劳力后，掠奴者把卢卡扬人带往伊斯帕尼奥拉和库瓦瓜，充当劳工和采珠人。到1520年，一场搜索在整个巴哈马只找到11名岛民，此后群岛荒芜了约130年。1648年，威廉·塞尔率领的埃留特拉冒险者从百慕大前来，在埃留特拉建立第一个永久性英格兰定居点。查尔斯顿1670年建于新普罗维登斯，1684年被西班牙袭掠者焚毁，1695年由尼古拉斯·特罗特重建并改名拿骚，以奥兰治-拿骚家族的威廉三世命名。这里后来成为海盗共和国，但伍兹·罗杰斯1718年以皇家总督身份抵达，归顺者赦、抗拒者绞，恢复了秩序，并在1720年守住城镇、击退西班牙进攻。1729年，殖民地设立议会。美国军队1776年短暂攻占拿骚，西班牙1782年夺取该城，1783年英国恢复统治，随后到来的效忠派种植园主建立棉花庄园，也使被奴役的非洲人成为人口主体。英国1807年废止奴隶贸易，到1818年，乘外国船只抵达巴哈马的非洲人已可获得解放。

en:
The Turks Islands are the small, arid south-eastern edge of the Lucayan Archipelago: Grand Turk, called Abawana by its Lucayan people, Salt Cay, and their surrounding keys. Arawakan-speaking islanders from Hispaniola began settling the southern islands after about 500, and a Classic Taíno settlement wave from Hispaniola renewed the southern cays around 1200, partly to use natural salt pans. In 1444 villages on Grand Turk and nearby Caicos fished the banks, gathered conch, tended gardens, made pottery, and moved goods by dugout canoe. The shallow salinas were already the land's most distinctive resource.

The first documented European sighting was Juan Ponce de León's in 1512; a possible Columbus landfall in 1492 remains unproven. Spanish slave raiding and disease emptied the islands by about 1513. Bermudians began seasonal salt raking in the 1660s: Balfour Town on Salt Cay is dated to 1673, and Cockburn Town, the first permanent settlement, was founded on Grand Turk in 1681. Spanish forces seized Grand Turk in 1710 before Bermudan privateers reclaimed it. France pressed a claim in 1753, and on 21 January 1754 crews from HMS Jamaica and HMS Shoreham cut down French crosses and royal arms on Grand Key, Salt Key, and Seal Key. Year-round salt working expanded in the 1750s, Britain asserted ownership in 1764, and Grand Turk became the seat of government in 1766. French troops took the island in February 1783, and Horatio Nelson's counterattack in HMS Albemarle failed on 9 March, but the Treaty of Paris restored the islands to Britain later that year. Loyalists then brought more than 1,000 enslaved Africans and tried cotton and sisal; by 1820 most planters had left, leaving sea salt as the decisive trade.
zh:
特克斯群岛是卢卡亚群岛东南缘的干旱小岛群，包括卢卡扬人称作阿巴瓦纳（Abawana）的大特克、盐岛和周围礁屿。约500年以后，来自伊斯帕尼奥拉、操阿拉瓦克语的岛民开始在南部岛屿定居；约1200年，又有一批古典泰诺人从伊斯帕尼奥拉前来重新经营南部礁屿，部分原因是利用天然盐池。1444年，大特克和邻近凯科斯岛上的村庄在浅滩捕鱼、采集凤凰螺、经营园圃、制作陶器，并用独木舟转运货物。浅浅的盐田已是这片土地最具特色的资源。

首次有文献记载的欧洲望见是1512年胡安·庞塞·德莱昂的航行；1492年哥伦布曾登陆此地的说法仍未证实。到约1513年，西班牙掠奴和疫病已使群岛人口绝迹。1660年代，百慕大人开始季节性前来刮盐：盐岛上的鲍尔弗镇可追溯至1673年，大特克的科伯恩城则于1681年建立，是第一个永久定居点。1710年西班牙军队夺取大特克，随后百慕大私掠者又将其收复。法国1753年提出主权主张，1754年1月21日，英国军舰「牙买加」号和「肖勒姆」号的船员拆除了法军在大礁、盐礁和海豹礁竖立的十字架与王徽。1750年代，全年制盐业扩大，英国1764年宣布主权，大特克1766年成为政府驻地。1783年2月法军攻占大特克，霍雷肖·纳尔逊乘「阿尔伯马尔」号在3月9日反攻失败，但同年《巴黎条约》将群岛归还英国。此后效忠派带来1000多名被奴役非洲人，试种棉花和剑麻；到1820年大多数种植园主已经离开，海盐仍是决定群岛生计的贸易。

en:
The finest harbor on Cuba's north coast opens on the island's northwest shore, a sheltered bay of narrow entrance and deep anchorages. In 1444 the land around it belonged to the Taíno chief Habaguanex; his people planted conucos of cassava and maize, fished the bay, and paddled the coast in dugout canoes. No European had yet entered the careening anchorage later called Puerto de Carenas, and the whole of Cuba remained in indigenous hands.

Sebastián de Ocampo, circumnavigating Cuba in 1508, was the first Spaniard to careen his ships in the bay. Diego Velázquez had San Cristóbal de la Habana founded in 1514 on the swampy south coast, but in 1519 the town was moved to the harbor it has kept ever since. In 1555 the French corsair Jacques de Sores sacked and burned it; the crown answered with the Castillo de la Real Fuerza, and in 1561 made Havana the rendezvous of the treasure fleets sailing for Seville. The governor moved his seat from Santiago, El Morro and La Punta guarded the mouth of the bay, and in 1592 Philip II granted the town the title of city, 'Key to the New World and Rampart of the West Indies'. A yellow fever epidemic brought from Cartagena in 1649 killed a third of its people; the city walls went up between 1674 and 1740; the university opened in 1728; and by 1740 Havana had the only dry dock in the New World. With more than 70,000 inhabitants it ranked third among the cities of the Americas when, on 13 August 1762, British troops entered after a two-month siege in which El Morro fell. Havana was returned to Spain under the Treaty of Paris in 1763 at the price of Florida, and the Spanish then raised the vast Fortress of San Carlos de la Cabaña above the bay. Columbus's remains were brought from Santo Domingo in 1796, and by 1821 Havana presided over a slave-grown sugar boom that made Cuba Spain's richest colony.
zh:
古巴北岸最好的港湾开在岛屿西北岸，入口狭窄、锚地幽深。1444年，港湾四周是泰诺酋长阿瓦瓜内克斯的领地；部民在木薯和玉米的田园里耕作，在湾中捕鱼，划着独木舟往来沿岸。还没有欧洲人驶入这个后来被称作卡雷纳斯港的倾船修泊之所，整个古巴仍在原住民手中。

塞瓦斯蒂安·奥坎波1508年环航古巴，最先在湾中倾修船底。迭戈·贝拉斯克斯1514年在泥泞的南海岸建起圣克里斯托瓦尔·德拉阿瓦纳，城镇却在1519年迁到这座港湾，此后再未移动。1555年，法兰西海盗雅克·德·索雷斯攻陷并焚毁城镇；西班牙王室随即修建皇家力量城堡，又在1561年把哈瓦那定为驶往塞维利亚的珍宝船队集结地。都督把驻地从圣地亚哥迁来，莫罗城堡与蓬塔城堡扼守海口，1592年腓力二世授予城镇城市头衔，号称「新世界的钥匙、西印度的壁垒」。1649年，一场来自卡塔赫纳的黄热病夺去三分之一居民的性命；城墙于1674至1740年间筑成，大学1728年开办，到1740年哈瓦那已拥有新大陆唯一的干船坞。城中居民超过七万、位居美洲城市第三时，英军在两个多月的围城中攻陷莫罗城堡，于1762年8月13日入城。根据1763年的《巴黎条约》，西班牙以佛罗里达换回哈瓦那，随后在湾畔筑起宏大的圣卡洛斯·德拉卡瓦尼亚要塞。1796年，哥伦布的遗骨从圣多明各迁葬到此；到1821年，哈瓦那统领着由奴隶劳动支撑的蔗糖繁荣，古巴也由此成为西班牙最富庶的殖民地。

en:
Morón lies on the marshy north coast of central Cuba, behind a chain of offshore cays and reefs cut through by mangrove channels. In 1444 Taíno communities fished those channels and tended conucos along the shore; the low, wet savanna stretching inland was only thinly peopled.

Spaniards first sailed these waters with Sebastián de Ocampo's voyage around Cuba in 1508, and after the conquest the country became cattle land. On 24 May 1543 the cabildo of Sancti Spíritus granted the hato of Morón, a stock ranch on the Río del Roble, to Luis de Almeida; its first settlers were creoles from Sancti Spíritus together with Andalusian and Canary Island sailors, and floods later moved the hamlet to higher ground. For two centuries Morón stayed a remote ranching town on a smuggler's coast, supplying passing ships with hides and dried meat while its cays sheltered pirates. The Andalusian proverb about the rooster of Morón, 'without feathers and still crowing', was already current in Cuba by 1763, though it originally belonged to Morón de la Frontera in Spain. Sugar was ground on a few small trapiches, but in 1821 Morón remained a quiet cattle town at the end of a mule track.
zh:
莫龙位于古巴中部多沼泽的北海岸，外海是一串礁岛和珊瑚礁，近岸遍布红树林水道。1444年，泰诺人的村落在此捕鱼、耕作岸边田园，向内陆延伸的低洼湿草原上人烟稀少。

1508年塞瓦斯蒂安·奥坎波环航古巴，最先驶过这片海域；征服完成后，此地成了牧牛之乡。1543年5月24日，圣斯皮里图斯市政会把罗布莱河畔的养牛庄园「莫龙牧场」授予路易斯·德·阿尔梅达；最早的居民是来自圣斯皮里图斯的土生白人和安达卢西亚、加那利水手，后来村落又因河水泛滥迁到地势较高处。两个世纪里，莫龙始终是走私者海岸边一座偏远的牧牛小镇，用皮革和肉干接济过往船只，近海礁岛则为海盗提供藏身之处。安达卢西亚谚语「像莫龙的公鸡，掉光了毛还在打鸣」至迟在1763年已在古巴流传，尽管它说的原本是西班牙的莫龙-德拉弗龙特拉。当地只有少数小糖坊榨糖，到1821年，莫龙仍是骡道尽头一座安静的牧牛小镇。

en:
Guantánamo occupies a fertile valley in southeastern Cuba, watered by the Bano, Jaibo and Guaso rivers as they run toward a broad bay on the island's southern coast. Taíno farmers and potters lived in the valley before European contact, while fishermen used the harbor they called Guantánamo, 'land between the rivers'. In 1444 the region was still a network of Taíno villages, manioc fields and coastal canoe landings, untouched by the Spanish conquest that would soon transform Cuba.

Christopher Columbus reached the bay in 1494 and named it Puerto Grande, where his men found Taíno fishermen preparing a feast for their chief. After the Spanish conquest reached eastern Cuba, the Taíno chief Guamá began a long revolt in 1522, using surprise raids and quick retreats in the mountains until he was killed in his sleep on 6 June 1533. The harbor remained strategically valuable: in 1741 Edward Vernon entered it with eight warships and 4,000 soldiers during the War of Jenkins' Ear, but local guerrilla fighters checked his march toward Santiago and forced him to withdraw. Santa Catalina de Guantánamo was formally founded in the valley in 1796; sugar mills and coffee farms then spread along the three rivers.
zh:
关塔那摩位于古巴东部肥沃的河谷，巴诺河、海博河和瓜索河流经此地，注入岛屿南岸一处宽阔海湾。欧洲人到来之前，泰诺农民和制陶者居住在河谷中，渔民则使用他们称为关塔那摩的港湾；这个地名在泰诺语中意为「河流之间的土地」。1444年，这里仍是泰诺村落、木薯田和沿岸独木舟停泊点组成的世界，尚未被不久后改变古巴的西班牙征服波及。

1494年，哥伦布抵达这个海湾并命名为大港，他的部下遇到正在为首领准备宴会的泰诺渔民。西班牙征服扩展到古巴东部后，泰诺首领瓜马于1522年发动长期反抗，在山区以突袭和快速撤退周旋，直至1533年6月6日在睡梦中被杀。这个港湾始终具有战略价值：1741年詹金斯耳朵战争期间，爱德华·弗农率八艘战舰和四千名士兵进入海湾，但当地游击武装阻截了他向圣地亚哥的进军，迫使其撤退。1796年，圣卡塔利娜·德·关塔那摩在河谷中正式建立，糖厂和咖啡种植园随后沿三条河发展起来。

en:
Jamaica is the third-largest island of the Greater Antilles, a rugged land of forested mountains, rivers and south-coast harbours. The Taíno called it Xaymaca, the land of wood and water. By the fifteenth century they lived from farming and fishing in villages governed by caciques, with their densest settlement along the southern plain; their population on the island may once have reached about 60,000. In 1444 the island belonged entirely to that Taíno world, still beyond the routes of Spanish caravels.

Christopher Columbus landed in 1494 and claimed Jamaica for Spain, and in 1503 he was stranded there for a year. Juan de Esquivel founded Sevilla in 1509, but the unhealthy settlement was abandoned around 1524 and Spanish Town became the island's chief town around 1534. Disease and enslavement shattered Taíno society, while African slaves were brought in to replace it; runaways joined surviving Taíno in the mountains as Maroons. An English force under William Penn and Robert Venables seized the island in May 1655, defeated Spanish counterattacks in 1657 and 1658, and gained formal recognition in the 1670 Treaty of Madrid. Port Royal became a buccaneering base associated with Henry Morgan until an earthquake destroyed much of it in 1692, after which Kingston rose. Sugar plantations made enslaved Africans a majority by the early 1670s, and in the eighteenth century sugar, coffee, cotton and indigo drove a brutal economy. The First Maroon War ended with treaties in 1739 and 1740; Tacky's Revolt shook the plantations in 1760; the Second Maroon War followed in 1795 and 1796. Britain abolished the slave trade in 1807, while slavery itself still shaped Jamaica in 1821.
zh:
牙买加是大安的列斯群岛第三大岛，岛上多林木茂密的山地与河流，南部分布着港口和平原。泰诺人称此地为沙伊马卡（Xaymaca），意为水和树木之地。到15世纪，他们以农耕和渔猎为生，聚居于酋长管辖的村落中，南部平原人口最为稠密；岛上人口一度可能约有六万。1444年的牙买加完全属于泰诺人的世界，西班牙卡拉维尔帆船尚未来到这里的航路。

哥伦布1494年登陆并宣布牙买加归属西班牙，1503年又曾在此困居一年。胡安·德·埃斯基维尔1509年建立塞维利亚，但这处环境不利健康的定居点约1524年被放弃，西班牙城约1534年成为岛上首要城镇。疾病和奴役摧毁了泰诺社会，非洲奴隶被运来补充劳力；逃亡者与幸存的泰诺人进入山区结合成马龙人。1655年5月，威廉·宾和罗伯特·维纳布尔斯率领英军夺取岛屿，并在1657年、1658年击退西班牙反攻；1670年的《马德里条约》正式确认英国占有。罗亚尔港成为海盗基地，亨利·摩根便由此成名，直到1692年地震摧毁港城大部，京斯敦随后兴起。17世纪70年代初，甘蔗种植园已使非洲黑奴成为岛上人口主体；18世纪，蔗糖、咖啡、棉花和靛蓝支撑起残酷的种植园经济。第一次马龙战争以1739年和1740年的条约告终，塔基起义1760年震动各种植园，第二次马龙战争则发生于1795年至1796年。英国1807年废除奴隶贸易，但到1821年，奴隶制本身仍支配着牙买加。

en:
The low coast around the Bay of Les Cayes, sheltered by offshore cays and Île-à-Vache, was Zui, Taíno country on the southern side of Hispaniola's Tiburon Peninsula. Villages fished the Caribbean, cultivated cassava, and traded along the shore; inland rose the mountains later called the Massif de la Hotte. In 1444 local caciques still governed the district before any European settlement. Spanish accounts later described Zui and neighboring Yáquimo as the two parts from which Jaragua, largest of the island's five chiefdoms, had been formed.

In 1503, during Nicolás de Ovando's governorship, Spanish colonists established Salvatierra de la Zabana on the bay, but the settlement was abandoned in 1540. A French town was laid out in 1726 by M. de la Lance and became Aux Cayes, a southern port of Saint-Domingue shipping sugar and coffee. Hurricanes destroyed it in 1781 and 1788. The Haitian rising of 1791 spread to the southern plantations, and in July 1793 the white inhabitants of Les Cayes were killed amid the civil war. André Rigaud and Toussaint Louverture contested the south in 1800, and after independence the town served as seat of the Conseil du Sud, which broke with Alexandre Pétion in 1810 and 1811. In December 1815 Simón Bolívar landed there; Pétion supplied his expedition after Bolívar promised to abolish slavery in the lands he liberated.
zh:
莱凯湾一带的低地海岸受近海沙洲和瓦什岛屏护，是伊斯帕尼奥拉岛蒂伯朗半岛南侧的泰诺人之地祖伊。村落居民在加勒比海捕鱼、种植木薯，并沿海岸交换物产；内陆矗立着后来称为拉霍特山的山地。1444年，地方酋长仍统治着这片地区，欧洲人尚未在此定居。后来的西班牙记载把祖伊和相邻的亚基莫称为哈拉瓜的两个组成部分，而哈拉瓜是岛上五大酋长国中疆域最大的一个。

1503年，在尼古拉斯·德·奥万多总督任内，西班牙殖民者在湾畔建立萨尔瓦铁拉·德拉萨瓦纳，但该据点于1540年废弃。1726年，德·拉朗斯按规划建立法国城镇，即后来的莱凯，使这里成为法属圣多明各南部输出蔗糖和咖啡的港口。1781年和1788年，飓风两度摧毁城镇。1791年海地起义蔓延到南部种植园，1793年7月，莱凯的白人居民在内战中被杀。1800年，安德烈·里戈与杜桑·卢维杜尔争夺南方；海地独立后，莱凯成为南方委员会所在地，该委员会于1810年至1811年与亚历山大·佩蒂翁政府决裂。1815年12月，西蒙·玻利瓦尔抵达这里；在他承诺于解放的土地上废除奴隶制后，佩蒂翁为其远征提供物资。

en:
Tortuga is a long, mountainous island in the Windward Passage off Marien, north-western Hispaniola. Its iron-bound northern shore gives way to the sheltered southern roadstead later called Cayona. In 1444 the island lay within the Taíno maritime world of the neighbouring mainland, and no European power yet occupied it or used the Columbus name that later made its anchorage famous.

Columbus sighted Tortuga in December 1492 and named it for its turtle-like outline. French and English settlers from Saint Kitts arrived in 1625, but Spanish forces under Fadrique de Toledo drove them out in 1629. Settlers returned around 1630, and in 1640 the French officer Le Vasseur seized the island after another Spanish occupation and built Fort de Rocher above Cayona; by 1641 the buccaneers called themselves the Brethren of the Coast. Spanish troops retook the island in 1654 and lost it to French and English adventurers in 1655. In June 1665 Bertrand d'Ogeron became French governor, bringing settlers and tobacco planting under the French West India Company; Tortuga was the first base of French Saint-Domingue until administration moved to Port-de-Paix in 1676. Spain recognized French possession at Ryswick in 1697. During the Haitian Revolution General Charles Leclerc died on Tortuga on 2 November 1802, and French forces abandoned the island in April 1803.
zh:
托尔图加（中文常译托尔蒂岛）是向风海峡中的狭长多山岛屿，位于伊斯帕尼奥拉岛西北的马里安外海。岛的北岸崖壁陡峻，南岸则有后来称为卡约纳的避风锚地。1444年，该岛属于邻近大陆的泰诺人海世界，尚无欧洲势力占据，也还没有哥伦布将赋予它的名字。

1492年12月，哥伦布望见托尔图加，因岛的轮廓像海龟而以此命名。1625年，来自圣基茨的法国和英国移民抵达，但法德里克·德·托莱多率领的西班牙军队在1629年将他们驱逐。移民约在1630年返回；1640年，法国军官勒瓦瑟尔在西班牙又一次占领后夺取该岛，并在卡约纳上方修筑罗谢堡。到1641年，岛上的布坎尼尔海盗已自称海岸兄弟会。西班牙军队1654年攻占托尔图加，又在1655年被法国和英国冒险者夺回。1665年6月，贝特朗·多热龙出任法国总督，在法国西印度公司体制下招徕移民、种植烟草；在殖民行政中心于1676年迁往和平港之前，托尔图加是法属圣多明各最早的据点。1697年，《里斯维克条约》确认法国占有该岛。海地革命期间，夏尔·勒克莱尔将军于1802年11月2日在托尔图加去世，法军则在1803年4月弃守该岛。

en:
The southern coast of Hispaniola, from the Nizao and Ocoa lowlands toward the bay later called Barahona, was Taíno country in 1444. The Baní plain was a nitainato, a district governed by a local noble, attached to the chiefdom of Maguana, while the southwest around Barahona belonged to Jaragua, largest of the island's five chiefdoms. Taíno villages farmed the river valleys and fished the Caribbean under their caciques, untouched as yet by European ships.

Followers of Christopher Columbus reached the coast in the 1490s, and Spaniards named Francisco, Gabriel, Luis and Juan de Barahona gave the southwestern bay its name. In July 1503 Governor Nicolás de Ovando broke Jaragua's power, killing Anacaona and the chiefdom's nobles during a staged celebration. Sugar mills soon appeared along the rivers, including an important one founded on the Ocoa by Alonso de Suazo, judge of the Audiencia of Santo Domingo. Canary Islander families settled the Baní plain from 1680 to 1684, and Baní was formally founded on 3 March 1764, when its residents bought the Cerro Gordo site for 370 pesos fuertes. In 1802 Toussaint Louverture's administration began developing the Barahona valley as a military post of Azua; Jean-Jacques Dessalines burned Baní in 1805, and the rebuilt town received its first council in 1810.
zh:
1444年，伊斯帕尼奥拉岛南部从尼萨奥、奥科阿低地到后来称巴拉奥纳的海湾，都是泰诺人的土地。巴尼平原是附属于马瓜纳酋长领地的尼塔伊纳托，即由地方贵族治理的辖区；更西南的巴拉奥纳一带则属于岛上五大酋长领地中最大的哈拉瓜。泰诺人的村落耕种河谷、在加勒比海捕鱼，由各村首领管辖，此时还没有欧洲船只到来。

1490年代，克里斯托弗·哥伦布的追随者来到这片海岸，弗朗西斯科、加夫列尔、路易斯和胡安·德·巴拉奥纳等西班牙人使西南这座海湾得名。1503年7月，圣多明各总督尼古拉斯·德·奥万多在一场安排好的庆典中摧毁哈拉瓜的统治层，阿纳卡奥娜与诸首领遇害。糖坊很快沿河出现，圣多明各检审庭法官阿隆索·德·苏亚索便在奥科阿河畔建有一座重要糖坊。1680年至1684年，加那利群岛移民家庭定居巴尼平原；1764年3月3日，居民以370枚银比索买下塞罗戈多址，巴尼正式建镇。1802年，杜桑·卢维杜尔政权开始开发巴拉奥纳河谷，将其设为阿苏阿下属的军事据点。让-雅克·德萨林1805年焚毁巴尼，重建后的城镇在1810年设立首个市政会。

en:
Aruba and Curaçao are dry, reef-bound islands off the Paraguaná Peninsula of Venezuela, where cactus scrub, gullies and sheltered bays mark a southern Caribbean very different from the wetter islands to the north. Caquetío farmers and fishers had reached them from the mainland before 1000, and in 1444 their villages formed the western edge of an Arawakan world joined by canoes. They traded salt, canoes, tobacco and beads with the Venezuelan coast and grazed no European cattle on the thin pasture.

A Spanish expedition under Alonso de Ojeda reached the area in 1499. Between 1513 and 1515 Diego Salazar deported roughly 2,000 Caquetío from the ABC islands to Hispaniola, and after formal Spanish settlement of Curaçao in 1527 the islands were treated chiefly as cattle ranches. The Dutch West India Company captured Curaçao in 1634 and occupied Aruba in 1636, turning Willemstad's Schottegat inlet into a harbour for shipping, salt and privateering. From 1662 Curaçao became a major mart of the Atlantic slave trade, and in 1674 it was made a free port; Sephardic merchants helped make Willemstad one of the Caribbean's leading commercial towns. A French fleet sent against the island lost several ships on reefs off Las Aves in 1678. In 1795 Tula Rigaud led a slave rising of as many as 4,000 people in north-western Curaçao. British forces held the islands for intervals during the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars, and Dutch rule was restored by 1816.
zh:
阿鲁巴和库拉索是委内瑞拉巴拉瓜纳半岛外海的干旱岛屿，周围多暗礁，陆上有仙人掌灌丛和冲沟，避风海湾则面向南美海岸。这里的风貌与北方湿润的加勒比岛屿截然不同。卡克蒂奥农民和渔民在1000年以前已从大陆来到岛上；1444年，他们的村落构成阿拉瓦克世界的西缘，独木舟把各岛与大陆连在一起。岛民同委内瑞拉海岸交易盐、独木舟、烟草和珠饰，当时薄瘦的牧场上还没有欧洲人带来的牛群。

1499年，阿隆索·德·奥赫达率领的西班牙探险队到达这一带。1513年至1515年间，迭戈·萨拉萨尔把阿鲁巴、博奈尔和库拉索三岛约二千名卡克蒂奥人强行迁往伊斯帕尼奥拉；1527年西班牙正式殖民库拉索后，这些岛屿主要被当作牧场。荷兰西印度公司1634年夺取库拉索，1636年占领阿鲁巴，并把威廉斯塔德的斯霍特加特湾经营成航运、盐业和私掠活动的港口。1662年起，库拉索成为大西洋奴隶贸易的重要集散地，1674年又成为自由港，塞法迪犹太商人助力威廉斯塔德崛起为加勒比主要商镇之一。1678年，一支奉命来攻的法国舰队在拉斯阿韦斯群岛外海触礁，损失多艘船只。1795年，图拉·里戈在库拉索西北部领导多达四千人参加的奴隶起义。法国革命战争和拿破仑战争期间，英军曾阶段性占领这些岛屿，到1816年荷兰统治已完全恢复。

en:
Borikén was the Taíno name for the easternmost and smallest of the Greater Antilles, a mountainous island set between the Atlantic and the Caribbean and ringed by smaller cays. Its people lived in yucayeques, or villages, under caciques, farming their plots, fishing and making canoes and pottery; the best land lay along coastal plains and river valleys. In November 1444 there were no Spanish towns, missions or forts on the island. Borikén remained a Taíno world, its chiefdoms linked by language and exchange but still untouched by the caravels that were beginning to reshape the Atlantic.

Columbus reached it on 19 November 1493 and named it San Juan Bautista. Juan Ponce de León founded Caparra in 1508; the settlement moved to the sheltered bay that became Ciudad de Puerto Rico in 1521, and in time island and city exchanged the names Puerto Rico and San Juan. Gold washing and encomiendas brought war: after Agüeybaná II's coalition killed Cristóbal de Sotomayor, Ponce de León defeated the first Taíno rising in 1511, Caparra was burned in 1513, and fugitive fighting continued into the 1520s. The Crown allowed African slave imports from 1517; the first major slave revolt came in 1527, and survivors fled to the mountains alongside remaining Taíno. After gold gave out around 1570, tobacco, cotton, cacao and ginger sustained the island while El Morro guarded the fleet route. Its gunners repelled Francis Drake in 1595; the Earl of Cumberland held San Juan briefly in 1598 but withdrew through disease. Balduino Enrico's Dutch force sacked and burned the city in 1625, yet never took El Morro. Ralph Abercromby's siege also failed in 1797. Sugar expanded soon afterward, and the 1815 Royal Decree of Graces offered land to Catholic immigrants as Spain tried to hold one of its last American strongholds.
zh:
博里肯是泰诺人对大安的列斯群岛最东端、也是四大岛中最小一岛的称呼。岛屿多山，夹在大西洋与加勒比海之间，周围散布着小礁；岛民住在称为「尤卡耶克」的村落中，由酋长统辖，耕种土地、捕鱼，也制造独木舟和陶器，最好的农田分布在沿海平原和河谷。1444年11月，岛上还没有西班牙人的城镇、传教站或要塞。博里肯仍是泰诺人的世界，各酋长领地以语言和交换相互联系，而此时改变大西洋的卡拉维尔帆船尚未到来。

1493年11月19日，哥伦布抵达这里，将其命名为圣胡安包蒂斯塔。胡安·庞塞·德·莱昂1508年建立卡帕拉；殖民地后来迁到避风港湾，1521年正式建立波多黎各城，日久之后，岛名与城名互换，岛屿称波多黎各，城市称圣胡安。淘金和监护征赋引发战争：阿圭巴纳二世联合各酋长杀死克里斯托瓦尔·德·索托马约尔后，庞塞·德·莱昂在1511年击退第一次大起义；1513年卡帕拉被焚毁，逃亡者的战斗延续到16世纪20年代。西班牙王室1517年起允许输入非洲奴隶，1527年爆发第一次大规模奴隶起义，幸存者与残留泰诺人一同退入山区。到1570年前后金矿枯竭，烟草、棉花、可可和生姜成为岛上重要物产，埃尔莫罗堡则扼守西班牙舰队航路。1595年，要塞炮火击退弗朗西斯·德雷克；1598年坎伯兰伯爵一度占领圣胡安，却因疾病撤军。1625年，巴尔多伊诺·恩里科率领荷兰军队洗劫并焚毁城市，却始终未能攻下埃尔莫罗堡。1797年，拉尔夫·阿伯克龙比的围城同样失败。此后蔗糖业扩张，1815年的《皇家恩典法令》向天主教移民授予土地，西班牙试图以此保住它在美洲最后的据点之一。

en:
St. Thomas is a hilly island in the Virgin group, with one of the finest natural harbours in the Lesser Antilles. The Ciboney reached it around 1500 BC, and Arawak-speaking villagers followed; Carib groups had also settled in the Virgin Islands by the fifteenth century. In 1444 Taino families farmed and fished along its bays, their thatched settlements untouched by Europeans, who did not yet know the island existed.

Columbus sighted St. Thomas in 1493 on his second voyage, but Spain never settled it. The Dutch West India Company opened a post in 1657, the Danes raised their flag and claimed the island in 1666, and a permanent colony came ashore on 25 May 1672. The first slave ships arrived the next year, and sugar plantations spread inland. In 1685 the Danish company leased trading rights to a Brandenburg company, while governors such as the Esmit brothers dealt openly with the buccaneers who used the harbour. The port town was renamed Charlotte Amalie in 1691 in honour of Christian V's queen, and its free harbour drew ships of every flag. Moravian missionaries came to live among the enslaved in 1732. The British seized the island in 1801 and returned it under the Peace of Amiens, then occupied it again from 1807 to 1815.
zh:
圣托马斯是维尔京群岛中一座多山的岛屿，拥有小安的列斯群岛最好的天然良港之一。约公元前1500年，西沃内人首先在此定居，讲阿拉瓦克语的村民随后迁入，到15世纪加勒比人也已在维尔京群岛定居。1444年时，泰诺人在各海湾边农耕渔猎，茅草村落散布全岛，欧洲人尚不知这座岛屿的存在。

1493年，哥伦布在第二次航行中望见圣托马斯，但西班牙始终没有殖民。荷兰西印度公司1657年在此设立商站，丹麦人1666年升旗宣称主权，1672年5月25日正式建立永久殖民地，第一批贩奴船次年即抵达，甘蔗种植园随之向岛内扩展。1685年，丹麦公司把岛上贸易权租给勃兰登堡公司；埃斯米特兄弟等几任总督则公开与盘踞港口的海盗做生意。港口城镇1691年以克里斯蒂安五世王后之名改称夏洛特阿马利亚，港口辟为自由港后各国商船云集。1732年，摩拉维亚弟兄会的传教士来到奴隶中间生活传教。英军1801年攻占该岛，依《亚眠和约》归还，1807年再度占领，直到1815年才交还丹麦。

en:
St. Kitts, called Liamuiga, 'the fertile isle', by its people, is a volcanic island in the northern Leewards, its centre crowned by the forested cone of Mount Liamuiga. Archaic fishers gave way to Arawak-speaking villagers, and around 1300 the Kalinago, a Carib people, seized the island and pushed the older inhabitants north. In 1444 Kalinago farmers lived along the shore, untroubled by any European power.

Columbus reached St. Kitts in 1493 and claimed it for Spain, but English settlers established the first colony in 1623, with the French following in 1625. Forewarned of a Kalinago ambush, the two nations fell on the islanders first and then partitioned the land, the English holding the centre and the French the two ends, where they laid out Basseterre. A Spanish expedition expelled both peoples in 1629, though the English returned after peace in 1630. Tobacco gave way to sugar in 1640, and the cane brought the mass importation of enslaved Africans. The island changed hands repeatedly in the wars that followed: French guns on Brimstone Hill helped take Fort Charles in 1689 and English forces retook it the next year, and in 1782 de Grasse and Bouillé forced the great hilltop fortress, the 'Gibraltar of the Caribbean', to surrender. The Treaty of Paris returned St. Kitts to Britain in 1783, and a French naval attack on the rebuilt works failed in 1806.
zh:
圣基茨是背风群岛北部的一座火山岛，岛民曾称之为「利亚穆伊加」，意为「肥沃之岛」，岛中央矗立着林木覆盖的火山峰利亚穆伊加山。远古渔猎民族之后，讲阿拉瓦克语的村民在此定居；约1300年，加勒比族的卡利纳戈人攻占该岛，把早先的居民逐向北方。1444年时，卡利纳戈农人沿海岸而居，尚无任何欧洲势力涉足。

1493年哥伦布抵达圣基茨，以西班牙之名宣布占有，但英格兰移民1623年率先建立殖民地，法国人1625年接踵而至。两国移民预先得知卡利纳戈人设伏的消息，先下手袭击岛民，随即瓜分岛屿：英格兰人占据中部，法国人据有两端，并在南端修建巴斯特尔。1629年一支西班牙远征军把两国人都赶走，1630年议和后英格兰人重返该岛。1640年烟草改种甘蔗，随之而来的是大规模贩运非洲奴隶。此后的战争中圣基茨屡次易手：法军1689年在硫磺山上架炮助攻，拿下查尔斯堡，英军次年即夺回；1782年，德格拉斯与布耶迫使山上号称「加勒比直布罗陀」的巨型要塞投降。1783年《巴黎条约》将圣基茨归还英国，1806年法国海军进攻重建后的要塞仍告失败。

en:
Antigua is a Leeward island whose south-eastern coast shelters the deep anchorage of English Harbour. Its indigenous name Waladli meant roughly 'our own'. The Guanahatabey were its first known inhabitants, and Arawak farmers later grew cassava, cotton and the dark Antiguan pineapple. Most Arawak communities left around 1100 as Carib canoe parties pressed north from Venezuela. In 1444 Carib parties used its beaches and cays, and no European had yet landed there.

Columbus sighted Antigua on his second voyage in 1493 and named it Santa María de la Antigua, after the old Virgin's chapel in Seville Cathedral, but the Spanish never stayed. English colonists left St. Kitts to settle the island in 1632. Around 1674 Christopher Codrington settled Betty's Hope and brought Barbadian sugar methods; sugar then drove out tobacco, and by the mid-1770s the island held about 37,500 enslaved Africans. In 1736 Prince Klaas, called Court by his enslavers, was crowned 'King of the Coromantees' outside St. John's and planned to destroy the planters' government and found an African kingdom. After an enslaved informer revealed the plot, Klaas and four accomplices were broken on the wheel, six others were hanged or starved, and fifty-eight more were burned. A naval dockyard was begun at English Harbour in 1725, where Captain Horatio Nelson enforced the Navigation Acts from 1784 to 1787, to the fury of Antigua's merchants.
zh:
安提瓜是背风群岛中的一座岛屿，东南海岸有英吉利港这处深水锚地。其原住民名称「瓦拉德利」大意是「我们自己的」。已知最早的居民是瓜纳哈塔贝人，后来阿拉瓦克农夫在此种植木薯、棉花和安提瓜黑菠萝。约1100年，随着加勒比独木船队从委内瑞拉向北进逼，大多数阿拉瓦克社群离去。1444年时，加勒比队伍利用岛上的海滩和礁屿，欧洲人尚未在此登陆。

1493年哥伦布第二次航行时望见安提瓜，依塞维利亚大教堂中的古老圣母礼拜堂将其命名为圣玛利亚·拉安提瓜，但西班牙人从未在此长住。1632年，一批英格兰移民离开圣基茨，到安提瓜定居。约1674年，克里斯托弗·科德林顿在「贝蒂的希望」种植园定居，并带来巴巴多斯的制糖技术；甘蔗随后取代烟草，到1770年代中期，岛上约有三万七千五百名非洲奴隶。1736年，被奴隶主称作考特的克拉斯亲王在圣约翰郊外加冕为「科罗曼特人之王」，计划摧毁种植园主政权并建立非洲人王国。由于一名奴隶告密，密谋败露，克拉斯与四名同谋被处轮刑，另有六人被绞死或饿死、五十八人被烧死。英吉利港的海军船坞1725年动工；1784至1787年，霍雷肖·纳尔逊舰长在此执行《航海条例》，令安提瓜商人极为不满。

en:
Guadeloupe is really two islands divided by the narrow channel of the Rivière Salée: mountainous Basse-Terre in the west and the flatter Grande-Terre in the east, with Marie-Galante and the Saintes nearby. Arawak farmers were the first identifiable inhabitants, before Kalinago groups displaced them and called Basse-Terre Karukera, 'the island of beautiful waters'. In 1444 Kalinago villages held the coasts and anchorages, and no European power had yet forced a settlement there.

Columbus landed on 4 November 1493 and named the islands Santa María de Guadalupe after the Extremaduran shrine, but Spanish attempts at settlement broke against Kalinago resistance. In 1635 the Compagnie des Îles de l'Amérique occupied Guadeloupe under Charles Liénard de L'Olive and Jean du Plessis d'Ossonville. Charles Houël made Basse-Terre a fortified trading post in 1650, the year the first enslaved Africans arrived, and an open slave revolt broke out in 1656. The crown annexed the island in 1674, and the Code Noir of 1685 regimented a booming sugar economy later joined by coffee and cocoa. The British held Guadeloupe from 1759 to 1763, and France surrendered Canada in the peace settlement to win the sugar island back. The British seized Guadeloupe again in April 1794, but Victor Hugues arrived with republican troops, drove them out by June and proclaimed abolition on 7 June 1794. In 1802 General Richepanse's expedition arrived to restore slavery, and on 28 May Louis Delgrès and his last followers blew up their powder stores at Matouba rather than surrender; slavery was formally reimposed on 14 May 1803. The British conquered the island in 1810, ceded it nominally to Sweden in 1813 without the Swedes ever taking possession, and returned it to France in 1814.
zh:
瓜德罗普实为被狭窄的萨莱水道隔开的两座岛屿：西面多山的巴斯特尔岛与东面低平的格朗德特尔岛，附近还有玛丽加朗特岛和桑特群岛。最早可辨识的居民是阿拉瓦克农夫，后来卡利纳戈人将他们逐走，并把巴斯特尔岛称作卡鲁克拉，意为「碧水之岛」。1444年时，沿海和锚地仍掌握在卡利纳戈村落手中，尚无欧洲势力能在此建立定居点。

1493年11月4日哥伦布登陆，以埃斯特雷马杜拉的瓜达卢佩圣母圣地将其命名为圣玛利亚·德瓜达卢佩，但西班牙人的定居尝试都在卡利纳戈人的抵抗下失败。1635年，美洲群岛公司在夏尔·利埃纳尔·德·洛利夫和让·迪普莱西·多松维尔率领下占领瓜德罗普。夏尔·乌埃尔1650年把巴斯特尔建成设防商站，第一批非洲奴隶也在同年抵达，1656年即爆发公开的奴隶起义。1674年法兰西王室把该岛并入王领，1685年的《黑人法典》将繁荣的蔗糖经济纳入规制，后来咖啡和可可也加入其列。英军1759年攻占瓜德罗普并占据到1763年，法国在和议中割舍加拿大以换回这座糖岛。1794年4月英军再度夺岛，维克托·于格率共和军抵达，在6月将其逐出，并于1794年6月7日宣布废除奴隶制。1802年里什庞斯将军率远征军前来恢复奴隶制；5月28日，路易·德尔格雷斯与最后的随从在马图巴引爆火药库，宁死不降。1803年5月14日，奴隶制被正式恢复。英军1810年再占全岛，1813年名义上将其割让给瑞典，瑞典人却始终没有接收，瓜德罗普1814年归还法国。

en:
Dominica is a steep, rainforested volcanic island between Guadeloupe and Martinique, called Wai'tu kubuli, 'tall is her body', by its people. Arawakan villagers had settled there from the fifth century, but by the fourteenth century Kalinago canoe-warriors, moving up the Lesser Antilles from the South American coast, had made the island their own. In 1444 it was a land of Carib villages, garden plots and fast rivers, its forested ridges never yet seen by a European.

Columbus sighted the island on Sunday 3 November 1493, during his second voyage, and named it Dominica, but Spanish expeditions through the 1500s broke against Carib resistance. In 1660 France and England declared Dominica and St Vincent neutral Carib ground; French woodcutters from Martinique and Guadeloupe nonetheless moved in from 1690, and in 1727 the first French commander made Dominique a colony of coffee quarters worked by enslaved Africans. Andrew Rollo's British expedition took it in 1761, and the Treaty of Paris ceded it to Britain two years later. A French fleet recaptured it with the colonists' help in 1778; Rodney's victory off the Saintes on 12 April 1782 and the peace of 1783 gave it back. French attacks of 1795 and 1805 failed, although on 22 February 1805 the invaders burned much of Roseau, by then the island's capital.
zh:
多米尼克是瓜德罗普与马提尼克之间一座山势陡峭、雨林密布的火山岛，岛上居民称之为瓦伊图库布利，意为「她身躯高大」。阿拉瓦克人自5世纪起在此定居，但到14世纪，从南美海岸沿小安的列斯群岛逐岛北上的卡利纳戈独木舟战士已成为岛屿的主人。1444年时，这里仍是一片由加勒比村落、园圃和湍急河流组成的土地，林木覆盖的山岭还从未有欧洲人见过。

1493年11月3日星期日，哥伦布第二次远航时望见该岛，为之取名多米尼克，意为「星期日」，但整个16世纪西班牙人的多次远征都在加勒比人的抵抗下失败。1660年，法国与英国约定把多米尼克和圣文森特留作加勒比人的中立之地；然而来自马提尼克和瓜德罗普的法国伐木者自1690年起陆续迁入，1727年首任法国长官把多米尼克正式变为殖民地，全岛划分为若干区，靠被贩卖来的西非黑奴在咖啡种植园劳作。1761年安德鲁·罗洛率英国远征军攻占该岛，两年后《巴黎条约》将其割让给英国。1778年法国舰队在当地居民协助下夺回岛屿；1782年4月12日罗德尼在桑特群岛附近取胜，1783年的和约又把它归还英国。法国1795年和1805年的两次进攻均告失败，但1805年2月22日入侵者焚毁了当时已是岛府的罗索的大半城区。

en:
Martinique is a rugged island between Dominica and St Lucia, dominated by the volcano of Mount Pelée; the Kalinago knew it as Madinina. Arawak farmers from the Orinoco had lived there from the first century, and Carib groups from the Venezuelan coast reached it around the seventh. In 1444 Kalinago clans held its valleys and coasts.

Columbus only anchored there on 15 June 1502, during his fourth voyage, and Spain left the island alone. On 15 September 1635 Pierre Belain d'Esnambuc landed at Saint-Pierre with about 150 settlers from St Kitts and claimed Martinique for Louis XIII's Company of the American Islands. Sugar spread from the 1640s; the Kalinago rising of 1658 was crushed and the survivors expelled to Dominica and St Vincent, and after 1674, when Louis XIV took the island into direct royal rule, enslaved Africans made up most of its people. A British army took Fort-Royal on 12 February 1762, only to hand the island back at the peace of 1763. In 1794, as the Revolution reached the Caribbean, planters who feared the abolition of slavery called the British in; after a siege they took Saint-Pierre and stayed until the Treaty of Amiens returned Martinique to France in 1802. General Beckwith's 12,000 men conquered it again in February 1809, and the Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814 gave it back once more, with slavery restored.
zh:
马提尼克是多米尼克与圣卢西亚之间一座地势崎岖的岛屿，佩莱火山雄峙其间，卡利纳戈人称之为马迪尼纳。来自奥里诺科流域的阿拉瓦克农人自1世纪起在此生活，来自委内瑞拉海岸的加勒比人约在7世纪抵达。1444年时，岛上的谷地与海岸都掌握在卡利纳戈各氏族手中。

哥伦布迟至1502年6月15日第四次远航时才在此停泊，西班牙对该岛始终没有兴趣。1635年9月15日，皮埃尔·贝兰·德南比克率约150名来自圣基茨的殖民者在圣皮埃尔登陆，以路易十三的美洲群岛公司名义宣布占领马提尼克。甘蔗种植园自1640年代兴起；1658年卡利纳戈人起义被镇压，幸存者或遭驱逐，或逃往多米尼克和圣文森特。1674年路易十四把该岛收归国王直接统治，此后被贩运而来的非洲黑奴很快占了岛上人口的大多数。1762年2月12日英军攻陷法兰西堡，却在次年议和时把岛屿归还法国。1794年革命波及加勒比，唯恐奴隶制被废除的种植园主把英军请进岛来；英军经围城战拿下圣皮埃尔，一直占领到1802年《亚眠条约》把马提尼克归还法国。1809年2月贝克威思将军率一万二千人大举征服该岛，1814年5月30日的《巴黎条约》又把它还给法国，奴隶制也随之恢复。

en:
Saint Lucia is a volcanic island south of Martinique, with an open Atlantic shore and a sheltered western roadstead; the Kalinago who mastered it around 800 called it Hewanorra. Arawak farmers from the South American coast had first settled the island in the third or fourth century. In 1444 it held only Carib villages and gardens, and no European had yet set foot on it.

An English ship blown off course landed 67 colonists in 1605, but Carib attacks left only 19 to flee five weeks later, and another attempt in 1638 was destroyed. The first lasting French settlement came from Martinique in 1651 under the sieur de Rousselan, and a Franco-Carib treaty followed in 1660; English claimants under Philip Warner were gone by the Treaty of Breda in 1667, and from 1674 Saint Lucia was a French crown colony attached to Martinique. Britain and France then exchanged it so often that it was called the Helen of the West: Rodney and Monckton took it in 1762, France got it back in 1763 and laid out sugar plantations from 1765, and the British held it from 1778 to 1783. The Revolutionary Wars brought three more changes, as Jervis's fleet took it in April 1794, Victor Hugues recaptured it in June 1795 and a British expedition retook it in 1796, when Castries was burned. The Treaty of Amiens restored it to France in 1802, the British seized it again in 1803, and the Treaty of Paris of 1814 confirmed British control of Saint Lucia.
zh:
圣卢西亚是马提尼克以南的一座火山岛，东岸直面大西洋，西岸有一处隐蔽的锚地；约在800年成为岛上主人的卡利纳戈人把这里称作埃瓦诺拉。最早在3、4世纪来此定居的是来自南美海岸的阿拉瓦克农人。1444年时，岛上还只有加勒比人的村落和园圃，欧洲人从未踏足。

1605年，一艘偏离航线的英国船送来67名殖民者，但加勒比人的进攻使他们五周后只剩19人仓皇逃离，1638年的又一次尝试也被摧毁。1651年，鲁瑟朗骑士率人从马提尼克前来，建立第一个持久的法国定居点，1660年法国与加勒比人缔约；菲利普·沃纳代表英国夺岛，可到1667年《布雷达条约》签订时英国人已撤离，1674年起圣卢西亚成为附属于马提尼克的法国王室殖民地。此后英法反复易手之频繁，使它得到「西方的海伦」之称：罗德尼与蒙克顿1762年攻占该岛，法国1763年将其收回，自1765年起开辟大片甘蔗种植园，英国又在1778年至1783年间占领。革命战争期间再经三易其主：杰维斯的舰队1794年4月占岛，维克多·于格1795年6月夺回，1796年英国远征军重新攻占，卡斯特里在战火中被焚。1802年《亚眠条约》把它归还法国，1803年英国再度夺取，1814年的《巴黎条约》确认了英国对圣卢西亚的统治。

en:
Saint Vincent is a mountainous volcanic island between St Lucia and the Grenadines, crowned by La Soufrière; its Kalinago people called it Hairun. Arawak farmers had settled there around the third century, and Carib groups had made the island their own by the fourteenth. Its rugged windward coast made it a stronghold: in 1444 it was one of the most independent Carib islands of the Lesser Antilles, and it would later shelter both native refugees and escaped Africans, who together became the Garifuna, or Black Caribs.

Columbus is thought to have sighted it on 22 January 1498, the feast of St Vincent, but Spain never settled. In 1660 France and England declared the island neutral Carib ground; French planters from Martinique nonetheless established themselves at Barrouallie around 1700, and from 1719 sugar, coffee and indigo plantations spread on enslaved African labour while runaways merged with the Caribs to form the Garifuna. General Monckton's British force took the island in 1762 and the Treaty of Paris confirmed it a year later, when Fort Charlotte was begun. The Garifuna fought the First Carib War of 1769–1773; the French retook the island in 1779 but handed it back in 1783. Led by Joseph Chatoyer and backed by Victor Hugues from Martinique, they rose again in 1795, and after their defeat in 1797 Ralph Abercromby deported nearly 5,000 Garifuna to Roatán and the Bay Islands. When La Soufrière erupted in 1812, the colony was firmly in British hands.
zh:
圣文森特是圣卢西亚与格林纳丁斯群岛之间一座多山的火山岛，苏弗里耶尔火山耸立其间，岛上的卡利纳戈人称之为海伦。阿拉瓦克农人约在3世纪来此定居，到14世纪加勒比人已成为岛屿的主人。陡峭的向风海岸使这里易守难攻：1444年时，它是小安的列斯群岛中最独立的加勒比人岛屿之一，日后还会收留土著难民和逃亡黑奴，两者融合形成加里富纳人，即黑加勒比人。

一般认为哥伦布在1498年1月22日圣文生瞻礼日望见该岛，为之取名圣文森特，但西班牙人从未在此殖民。1660年法国与英国宣布该岛为加勒比人的中立之地；然而来自马提尼克的法国种植园主约在1700年在巴鲁阿利落脚，自1719年起靠非洲黑奴劳力开辟甘蔗、咖啡和靛蓝种植园，逃亡奴隶则与加勒比人融合为加里富纳人。1762年蒙克顿将军率英军攻占该岛，次年《巴黎条约》予以确认，夏洛特堡也在同年动工。加里富纳人在1769—1773年进行了第一次加勒比战争；法国1779年夺回该岛，1783年又把它交出。1795年，加里富纳人在约瑟夫·查托耶率领下、得到马提尼克的维克多·于格支持再度起义，1797年被拉尔夫·阿伯克龙比击败，近五千人被放逐到罗阿坦和海湾群岛。1812年苏弗里耶尔火山喷发时，这座殖民地已牢牢掌握在英国手中。

en:
Barbados is a low, flat coral island far out in the Atlantic, east of the Windward chain, called Ichirouganaim by its Arawak villagers. Arawak farmers from the South American mainland had settled there from around 800, and a new wave arrived in the thirteenth century; Carib canoe parties came and went, though they left no permanent villages. In 1444 small Amerindian communities farmed and fished along its wind-swept coasts, unaware that Spanish slave raids within two generations would strip the island and leave it almost uninhabited.

The Portuguese navigator Pedro a Campos named the island Os Barbados in 1536, but Portugal never settled it, leaving only wild boar for passing ships to hunt. An English ship under John Powell claimed it on 14 May 1625, and on 17 February 1627 eighty settlers founded Jamestown, later Holetown; the island's House of Assembly first met in 1639. Sugar arrived from Dutch Brazil in the 1640s and the island was remade: by 1680 some 46,000 enslaved Africans outnumbered 20,000 whites, and the Barbados Slave Code became a model for other colonies. After Charles I was executed the island declared for the Stuarts, surrendering to Sir George Ayscue only with the Treaty of Oistins in January 1652. Alone among the major Caribbean islands it was never taken by a foreign fleet, though the hurricane of October 1780 killed more than 4,000 people. When Parliament ended the slave trade in 1807, Bussa led some 20,000 enslaved men and women from seventy plantations in the rising of 14 April 1816; it was crushed within days, leaving about 120 rebels dead in the fighting and 144 more executed after trial.
zh:
巴巴多斯是远悬大西洋、位于向风群岛以东的一座低平珊瑚岛，岛上的阿拉瓦克居民称之为伊奇鲁加奈姆。来自南美大陆的阿拉瓦克农人约在800年已在此定居，13世纪又有新的一批人到来；加勒比人的独木舟队往来于此，却没有留下永久村落。1444年时，一个个美洲原住民小社群在多风的海岸耕作捕鱼，尚不知不出两代人之后，西班牙奴隶贩子的袭击就会把岛屿劫掠一空，使它几乎荒无人烟。

1536年，葡萄牙航海家佩德罗·阿·坎波斯把该岛命名为「巴尔巴多斯」，意为「长胡子的人」，但葡萄牙从未在此定居，只留下野猪供过往船只猎取。1625年5月14日，约翰·鲍威尔的英国船宣布占岛；1627年2月17日，八十名殖民者建立詹姆斯敦，即今霍尔敦；岛上的议会首次召开于1639年。1640年代，甘蔗随荷属巴西的技术与资金传入，全岛为之一变：到1680年，约四万六千名非洲黑奴在人数上已超过两万名白人，《巴巴多斯奴隶法典》也成为其他殖民地效仿的样板。查理一世被处死后，巴巴多斯宣布效忠斯图亚特王朝，直到1652年1月乔治·艾斯丘爵士兵临、《奥伊斯廷斯条约》签订才投降。在加勒比各主要岛屿中，它是唯一从未被外国舰队攻占的一个，但1780年10月的飓风夺去了四千多人的生命。英国议会1807年废除奴隶贸易后，布萨于1816年4月14日率领约七十座种植园的两万名黑奴起义；起义数日内即被镇压，约120人战死，另有144人经审判被处决。

en:
Trinidad is a broad continental island only 11 kilometres off the Venezuelan coast, set between the Gulf of Paria and the Atlantic approaches to the Orinoco. In 1444 its people included Arawakan-speaking Nepoya and Shebaya and Cariban-speaking Yao, whose canoes and trails linked the island to mainland villages and the Lesser Antilles. Its Arawakan name, Iëre, is commonly translated as the Land of the Hummingbird; no European fleet had yet entered the Dragon's Mouths or claimed its anchorages.

Christopher Columbus sighted Trinidad on 31 July 1498 and renamed it La Isla de la Trinidad. Antonio de Sedeño campaigned there in the 1530s, and in 1592 Antonio de Berrío founded San José de Oruña, the island's first permanent Spanish town and capital. Walter Raleigh arrived on 22 March 1595, captured Berrío and sacked San José, then used Trinidad as a base for his Orinoco expedition in search of El Dorado. Catalan Capuchins began missions in 1687; abuses at San Fernando de los Arenales led to the Arena revolt of 1 December 1699, in which Amerindians killed the missionaries and Governor José de León y Echales before the rising was bloodily suppressed. The 1783 Cedula of Population then opened land grants to loyal Catholic settlers, especially French planters from the eastern Caribbean, and the colony held 18,627 people by 1797. That February an 18-ship British fleet under Ralph Abercromby invaded, and Governor José María Chacón surrendered; British possession was confirmed by the 1802 Treaty of Amiens.
zh:
特立尼达是一座宽阔的大陆岛，距委内瑞拉海岸仅11公里，位于帕里亚湾与通往奥里诺科河的大西洋水道之间。1444年，岛上居民包括讲阿拉瓦克语的内波亚人、谢巴亚人，以及讲加勒比语的姚人；他们的独木舟和陆路把岛屿同大陆村落及小安的列斯群岛连接起来。岛的阿拉瓦克语名称耶雷通常译为「蜂鸟之地」，此时还没有欧洲舰队进入龙口海峡或占据这里的锚地。

1498年7月31日，克里斯托弗·哥伦布望见特立尼达，并将其改名为「特立尼达岛」。1530年代，安东尼奥·德·塞德尼奥在此作战；1592年，安东尼奥·德·贝里奥建立圣何塞·德·奥鲁尼亚，这是岛上第一座永久西班牙城镇和首府。1595年3月22日，沃尔特·雷利抵达，俘获贝里奥并洗劫圣何塞，随后以特立尼达为基地前往奥里诺科河寻找黄金国。1687年，加泰罗尼亚嘉布遣会开始建立传教站；阿雷纳莱斯的圣费尔南多传教站的压榨引发1699年12月1日的阿里纳起义，印第安人杀死传教士和总督何塞·德·莱昂-埃查莱斯，起事随后遭到血腥镇压。1783年的《人口敕令》向效忠西班牙王室的天主教定居者授予土地，尤其吸引东加勒比的法裔种植园主，到1797年殖民地已有18627人。同年2月，拉尔夫·阿伯克龙比率领18艘英国战舰入侵，总督何塞·马里亚·查孔投降；英国的占有在1802年《亚眠条约》中得到确认。

en:
Kutch is the peninsula boxed in by the Gulf of Kutch and the Great and Little Rann. In the monsoon the Rann is a sheet of shallow water, in the dry season a white salt crust crossed only at the known fords, so armies enter the peninsula with difficulty and its coast dwellers live on salt pans, fishing and herds rather than field taxes. Its chiefs in 1444 are Jadeja Rajputs, a Samma house that had moved east out of Sindh two centuries earlier and split into kinsmen's branches seated at Lakhiarviro, Kanthkot, Gajod and Bara. The Lakhiarviro branch speaks first among them, but no chief holds all Kutch, and the houses manoeuvre between pressure from Sindh and the Gujarat Sultanate.

Outside intervention made the kingdom. Mahmud Begada of Gujarat defeated a Kutchi army in 1472, and a blood feud did the rest: in 1537 Jam Rawal murdered his kinsman Jam Hamirji and seized the country, until Hamirji's son Khengarji returned with Morbi and troops granted by the Gujarat court and drove Jam Rawal out in 1548. Khengarji united Kutch, set his capital at Bhuj, and in 1580 founded Mandvi on the south coast. Mandvi grew into the peninsula's sea port: its carpenters built the wooden dhows that carried Kutchi merchants to East Africa, the Malabar coast and the Persian Gulf, and in the eighteenth century the town's merchants owned some four hundred vessels. Gujarati tradition names a Kutchi sailor, Kanji Malam, as the pilot who took Vasco da Gama from Malindi to Calicut, though historians dispute the man's identity. Kutch accepted Mughal overlordship after two campaigns in 1590 and 1591, keeping several thousand cavalry and paying little tribute; under Rao Lakhpatji the state struck its silver kori. Sindhi invasions in the 1760s and the British and Baroda occupation of Anjar in 1815 narrowed the kingdom, which accepted East India Company suzerainty in 1819, the year an earthquake shook the Rann.
zh:
卡奇是被卡奇湾和大、小卡奇盐沼围在中间的半岛。雨季时盐沼是一片浅水，旱季结成白色盐壳，只有熟悉的渡口才能通行，大军难以进入；沿海居民靠晒盐、捕鱼和畜牧为生，不靠田赋。1444年，半岛上的首领都是贾德贾拉杰普特人，这个萨姆马家族在两个世纪前由信德东迁，后分成拉基阿尔维罗、坎特科特、加佐德和巴拉几支亲族。拉基阿尔维罗一支地位最高，但没有哪位首领能统领全卡奇，各家在信德与古吉拉特苏丹国的压力之间周旋。

卡奇王国是在外力介入下成形的。1472年古吉拉特的马哈茂德·贝加达击败卡奇军队，随后一场血仇完成了剩下的事：1537年贾姆·拉瓦尔谋害亲族贾姆·哈米尔吉、夺占其地，哈米尔吉之子肯加吉带着古吉拉特宫廷封给他的莫尔维和军队打回来，1548年驱逐贾姆·拉瓦尔。肯加吉统一卡奇，定都普杰，1580年在南岸建起曼德维。曼德维后来成为半岛的出海港，船工在这里建造木帆船，载着卡奇商人驶往东非、马拉巴尔海岸和波斯湾；18世纪，城中商人拥有约四百艘商船。古吉拉特人的传说里，瓦斯科·达伽马从马林迪驶往卡利卡特时，为他引航的正是卡奇水手坎吉·马拉姆，不过史学家对引航员的身份说法不一。1590和1591年两度用兵后，卡奇接受莫卧儿宗主权，仍保有数千骑兵，贡赋很轻；拉克帕特吉在位时国家铸造了银币科里。1760年代信德两度入侵，1815年英国与巴罗达联军占领安贾尔，王国日渐局促，1819年接受东印度公司宗主权，同年一场地震震动了盐沼。

en:
Thatta stands in the Indus Delta, where shifting channels carried Sindhi grain and cloth out to the Arabian Sea. The Samma chiefs overthrew Sumra power and broke from Delhi in 1351, making the town, also called Samanagar, their capital, and on the nearby Makli ridge they began burying their governors and saints. Over four centuries the ridge filled with tiled and carved tombs in the style of lower Sindh and became one of the largest funerary cities in the world. In 1444, after Jam Sikandar's death, Jam Raidhan was raised to the throne at Thatta, a Muslim jam who ruled lower Sindh through delta tribes and river traffic.

Jam Nizamuddin II's long reign from 1461 to 1508 was remembered as the Samma golden age, and in 1495 he ordered a new Thatta built. Shah Beg Arghun's invasion ended Samma rule in 1523. In 1555 Isa Khan Tarkhan called in seven hundred Portuguese troops carried by twenty-eight ships; when their pay was refused the soldiers sacked the town and carried off its gold treasury. Akbar's forces annexed Sindh in 1592. Prince Shah Jahan once sheltered here from his father Jahangir, and his son Lutfallah was born in the city in 1626; as emperor he founded the Shah Jahan Mosque in thanks for that hospitality, begun in 1647 and finished in 1659, its walls covered in glazed tilework. English merchants opened a factory in 1635, a storm wrecked much of the city in 1637, and the Dutch set up their own post in 1652; visitors in those years counted about 2,000 looms, and its silk and leather also sold abroad. Late in the century siltation drew the Indus eastward and the sea trade left Thatta. The Kalhoras took the city in 1736, Nadir Shah received Sindh in 1739, and the lower Sindh capital moved to Hyderabad in 1789; by the early nineteenth century perhaps 20,000 people remained.
zh:
特达位于印度河三角洲，纵横改道的河汊把信德的谷物和布匹送往阿拉伯海。1351年，萨姆马首领推翻苏姆拉人的势力并脱离德里，以又称萨马纳加尔的特达为都，又开始把长官和圣徒葬在附近的马克利山脊。此后四百年间，山脊上布满下信德风格的琉璃砖雕陵墓，成了世界上规模最大的墓葬之城之一。1444年贾姆·西坎达尔去世，贾姆·拉伊丹在特达被拥立为贾姆；这位穆斯林君主凭借三角洲部落与河运统治下信德。

贾姆·尼扎姆丁二世1461至1508年的长期治世被视为萨姆马王朝的黄金时代，1495年他下令营建一座新的特达城。1523年，沙赫·贝格·阿尔洪的入侵终结萨姆马统治。1555年，伊萨汗·塔尔汗召来二十八艘船载运的七百名葡萄牙士兵；因酬劳遭拒，这些士兵洗劫城市，掠走了宫中的黄金。阿克巴的军队1592年吞并信德。沙贾汗还是王子时曾为躲避父亲贾汉吉尔在此避难，他的儿子卢特夫拉1626年出生在城中；登基后他为报答这段收留敕建沙贾汗清真寺，工程1647年动工、1659年完工，墙面满饰琉璃砖。英国商人1635年开设商馆，1637年一场风暴摧毁了大半个城市，荷兰人1652年也设立商馆；那几年间的来访者数出城中约有两千台织机，丝绸和皮革同样远销外地。十七世纪末印度河淤积东移，海路贸易随之离开特达。卡尔霍拉人1736年取得此城，1739年纳迪尔沙获得信德，1789年下信德都城迁往海得拉巴；到十九世纪初，城中大约只剩两万人。

en:
Sehwan stands on the west bank of the Indus below the Lakki Hills, at one of the river's old crossing places. The mound north of the town still bears the name Kafir Qila, the fort of the pagans: Greek sources knew the place as Sindomana, capital of King Sambos, and the Arab army of Muhammad bin Qasim took it in 711. Sehwan's fame rests on the tomb of Lal Shahbaz Qalandar, a wandering Sufi born in Marwand in Azerbaijan who wore red robes, settled here in the thirteenth century and died in 1274. Firuz Shah Tughlaq raised the shrine in 1356, Ibn Battuta prayed there on his way through Sindh, and pilgrims came to visit the tomb and join the dhamaal, the shrine's devotional dance. In 1444 the town was a Sunni garrison on the Indus caravan road, answering to the Samma Jam at Thatta.

Humayun, driven out of northern India by Sher Shah Suri, besieged Sehwan in 1542 without success and moved on to Umarkot, where his son Akbar was born. Akbar's generals took the town in the 1590s, and the shrine was rebuilt on a grand scale in 1639. The Kalhoras held it as Mughal governors from about 1701, Durrani overlordship followed at mid-century, and in 1783 the Talpur Mirs defeated the Kalhoras at Halani and took Sindh for themselves.
zh:
塞赫万位于勒基山下的印度河西岸，守着印度河上的一处古渡口。城北的古丘仍叫卡菲尔堡，意为「异教徒之堡」；古希腊文献把这片地方称作辛多马纳，是国王桑博斯的都城，711年穆罕默德·伊本·卡西姆的阿拉伯军队攻取了它。塞赫万的声名系于拉尔·沙赫巴兹·卡兰达尔的圣祠：他出生于阿塞拜疆的马尔万德，是个常着红衣的游方苏非，13世纪在此定居，1274年终老于此。菲鲁兹沙·图格鲁克1356年为他建祠，伊本·白图泰路过信德时也曾拜谒，朝圣者来墓前祈祷，参加圣祠的旋舞仪式（dhamaal）。1444年，这座城镇是印度河商路上的逊尼派驻军要地，听命于坐镇特达的萨姆马贾姆。

1542年，被舍尔沙·苏利逐出北印度的胡马雍围攻塞赫万不克，转赴乌默科特，他的儿子阿克巴就出生在那里。阿克巴的将领们在1590年代拿下此城，圣祠于1639年按宏大规制重修。约1701年起，卡尔霍拉家族以莫卧儿总督身份领有塞赫万；18世纪中叶杜兰尼王朝成为宗主，1783年塔尔普尔的米尔们在哈拉尼击败卡尔霍拉家族，把信德掌握在自己手中。

en:
Multan lies on an old bank of the Chenab in the hot southern Punjab plain, where caravans from Khorasan and Central Asia met India's trade on the road through Kandahar and Herat; Ibn Battuta in the 1330s found its market selling steppe horses. Arab armies took it in 712. Its Sun temple drew pilgrims and, by Arab accounts, yielded up to thirty per cent of the rulers' revenues; Mahmud of Ghazni ended its Ismaili emirate in 1005 and 1010, and Multan became a frontier province of Delhi. The shrines of Bahauddin Zakariya and Shah Rukn-e-Alam gave it the name City of Saints; the Rukn-e-Alam tomb was the first Tughluq monument, begun for Ghiyath al-Din, who as governor fought twenty-eight battles against the Mongols. After Timur sacked it in 1398 the city broke away, and in 1444 it was ruled by a mild scholar, Shaikh Yousaf Qureshi, while the Langah clans held the real power.

In 1445 Rai Sahra Langah seized Multan in a night attack and founded the Langah sultanate. His grandson Husayn, reigning from 1469 to 1498, beat off Delhi's invasions and settled Baloch in the Derajat as soldiers. Multani merchants kept a caravanserai at Baku and bought land in Bukhara by the 1550s. Shah Husayn Arghun of Sindh took the city after a long siege in 1527, and Sher Shah Suri linked it to his Grand Trunk Road in 1541. Akbar retook it in 1557, and in 1580 it became one of the twelve original Mughal subahs. Aurangzeb governed it from 1648 to 1652, and the next two centuries were its Dar al-Aman, when cotton cloth, coinage and blue glazed tiles sold across the empire.

The Chenab silted away from the city after 1650, cutting off its sea trade. After Nader Shah overran the region in 1739 it passed to Ahmad Shah Durrani, born in Multan, who made it part of his Afghan kingdom in 1752. Afghan, Maratha and Sikh armies fought over it for two generations; in 1818 Ranjit Singh's men breached the fort with the Zamzama cannon, Nawab Muzaffar Khan and seven of his sons died in its defence, and Multan passed to the Sikh Empire.
zh:
木尔坦位于南旁遮普炎热平原上的奇纳布河旧岸，经坎大哈、赫拉特而来的呼罗珊与中亚商队在这里接上印度的商路；14世纪30年代伊本·白图泰路过时，见市上售卖草原贩来的马匹。712年阿拉伯军队攻占此城。城中的太阳神庙吸引四方香客，据阿拉伯人记载，神庙贡献的岁入多达统治者总收入的三成；伽色尼的马哈茂德在1005年和1010年的征伐中终结了伊斯玛仪派埃米尔国，木尔坦成为德里的边疆省份。巴哈乌丁·扎卡里亚与沙阿·鲁克尼·阿拉姆的圣陵为它赢得「圣徒之城」之名；鲁克尼·阿拉姆陵是图格鲁克朝第一座纪念建筑，本是为吉亚斯—乌德—丁所建，他任总督期间与蒙古人打了二十八仗。1398年帖木儿洗城后木尔坦脱离德里；1444年，性情温和的学者谢赫·优素福·库雷希统治此城，真正掌权的却是朗加部族。

1445年，拉伊·萨赫拉·朗加夜袭夺城，建立朗加苏丹国。其孙侯赛因1469至1498年在位，击退德里的来犯，把俾路支人安置在德拉加特当兵戍守。木尔坦商人在巴库开有商队客栈，到1550年代已在布哈拉置产。1527年信德的沙阿·侯赛因·阿尔浑久攻克城；1541年舍尔沙·苏尔把木尔坦接入大干道。1557年阿克巴收复此城，1580年它成为莫卧儿最初十二个苏巴之一。1648至1652年奥朗则布曾任该省总督；此后两百年是它的「达尔阿曼」之世，棉布、铸币和蓝色琉璃砖行销整个帝国。

1650年后奇纳布河淤塞改道，断了它的海路商运。1739年纳迪尔沙阿横扫此地后，木尔坦转入出生于此的艾哈迈德沙阿·杜兰尼之手，1752年并入他的阿富汗王国。阿富汗、马拉塔和锡克三方军队争夺了两代人；1818年，兰季特·辛格的部下用扎姆扎马巨炮轰破堡垒，纳瓦布·穆扎法尔汗与七个儿子战死，木尔坦并入锡克帝国。

en:
Lahore stands on the Ravi, the first great city of the plains for armies marching down from Kabul and the last on the road north; whoever held Lahore held the gate of Hindustan. The Ghaznavids made it their eastern capital, and the early sultans of Delhi for a time kept their court here. Mongol raids battered the city for two centuries, and when Timur passed through in 1398 it was too ruined to be worth sacking. In 1444 it is a scarred frontier town in the hands of Bahlul Lodi, the Afghan lord of Sirhind, who holds it for a moribund Delhi while building his own power; its fame rests on its Persian-writing poets and the shrines of Sufi saints that draw pilgrims across the Punjab.

Bahlul went on to seize Delhi and found the Lodi dynasty; in 1525 Babur's army took Lahore on the march to Panipat. Sher Shah Suri and the returning Humayun held it in turn, before the Great Mughals made it a residence fit for emperors. Akbar replaced the old mud fort with a brick citadel and new walls and kept his court here for fourteen years from 1584, and the Akbari Mandi became the grain market of the Punjab. His successors filled the fort with marble: Jahangir gave it the long Picture Wall, its glazed tiles showing elephant fights and polo players, and in 1606 held the Sikh Guru Arjan prisoner there before putting him to death; Shah Jahan, born in Lahore, added the Sheesh Mahal and the Naulakha pavilion, while the governor Wazir Khan raised his tile-clad mosque in the lanes below. Beyond the walls Shah Jahan laid out the Shalimar Gardens in 1641 and built his father's mausoleum across the Ravi at Shahdara, and Aurangzeb set the Badshahi Mosque and the fort's Alamgiri Gate facing each other in the 1670s. After Nader Shah's army passed through in 1739, Afghans, Mughals and Sikh militias fought over the city for sixty years, until Ranjit Singh entered in 1799 and made the old citadel the seat of a Sikh court. His men later stripped much of the stone from Jahangir's tomb at Shahdara to decorate the Golden Temple at Amritsar.
zh:
拉合尔坐落在拉维河畔，从喀布尔南下的军队进入平原后遇到的第一座大城，也是北上大道的最后一站，得此城者便握住了印度斯坦的门户。伽色尼王朝曾以它为东都，德里早期诸苏丹也一度在此驻跸。两个世纪里蒙古人一再蹂躏此城，1398年帖木儿路过时，它已残破得不值得一掠。1444年，这是一座伤痕累累的边镇，握在西尔欣德的阿富汗领主巴赫鲁尔·洛迪手里——他替气数将尽的德里守边，暗中经营自己的势力；它的声名系于波斯语诗人和苏非圣徒的陵寝，香客从旁遮普各处前来。

巴赫鲁尔后来夺取德里、建立洛迪王朝；1525年，巴布尔的军队在进军帕尼帕特的路上攻占拉合尔。舍尔沙·苏利和重返印度的胡马雍先后据有此城，到大莫卧儿时代，这里成了配得上皇帝的居所。阿克巴拆去旧土堡，改建砖砌城塞与城墙，1584年起在此驻跸十四年，阿克巴里曼迪成为旁遮普的粮食市集。后继诸帝用大理石填满城堡：贾汉吉尔留下长长的画壁，琉璃砖上是斗象与马球的图景；1606年他把锡克古鲁阿尔琼囚在堡中，随后处死。生于拉合尔的沙贾汗增建镜宫和瑙拉克哈亭，总督瓦齐尔·汗则在城下街巷中筑起琉璃砖清真寺。城外，沙贾汗1641年开辟沙利马尔花园，又在拉维河对岸的沙赫德拉修建父皇的陵寝；1670年代，奥朗则布让巴德夏希清真寺与城堡的阿拉姆吉尔门隔街相对。1739年纳迪尔沙的军队过境，此后六十年间阿富汗人、莫卧儿和锡克武装反复争夺，1799年兰季特·辛格入城，把旧城堡变成锡克朝廷的所在。他的部下后来拆走沙赫德拉贾汉吉尔陵的大量石料，运去装饰阿姆利则金庙。

en:
The Vale of Kashmir is a high, fertile basin shut in by the Pir Panjal Range and the Great Himalayas. Armies and caravans entered through a small number of difficult passes, while the Jhelum and Dal Lake carried traffic to Srinagar, the valley's capital since the sixth century. Earlier Hindu and Buddhist courts made the city a place of learning, and their chronicles survive in the Rajatarangini. Shah Mir founded the Muslim sultanate in 1339, and the disciples of Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani later spread Islam through the valleys.
