南撤发生在1526年：苏洪蒙的阿洪军队攻占迪马普尔，把王廷赶进山里。16至18世纪，迈邦格一直是底马撒都城，国王们在这里改奉印度教。巴拉克河下游，科奇名将奇拉莱已于1562年从特里普拉手中夺取河谷，其弟卡马尔·纳拉扬的后裔建起卡斯普尔的科奇王国。1745年，末代国王比姆·辛哈没有子嗣，其女坎查尼嫁给底马撒王子拉克什米·钱德拉，两国合并，王廷迁往卡斯普尔，婆罗门把底马撒贵族立为佩圣线的巴尔曼刹帝利。1802年，国王克里希纳钱德拉娶曼尼普尔国王摩杜钱德拉之女因杜普拉巴为后，来自曼尼坡方向的缅甸战事很快也把卡恰尔卷了进去。

en:
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands form two chains between the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea, separated by the Ten Degree Channel. On the northern islands the Andamanese, among them the Jarawa and Sentinelese, lived by hunting, fishing and gathering and kept their distance from passing ships. The Nicobarese farther south spoke Austroasiatic languages and sold coconuts to vessels on the sea route between India and Southeast Asia. The Chola king Rajendra I used the islands as a naval base for his expeditions against Srivijaya, and the Thanjavur inscription of 1050 records their Tamil name, Ma-Nakkavaram; the early fifteenth-century Mao Kun chart marked Great Nicobar as Cuilan. In 1444 no mainland kingdom garrisoned either chain, and village societies ran their own affairs.

European powers later tried to turn these anchorages into permanent posts. A Danish East India Company expedition sailed from Tranquebar in 1755, founded New Denmark on Great Nicobar in 1756 and established New Zealand on Nancowry in 1757. Malaria and local resistance drove the survivors out by April 1759. Moravian missionaries and soldiers returned to Nancowry in 1768 and planted coffee and cotton, and in 1778 the British merchant William Bolts, acting on the assumption that Denmark had given up its claim, sent an Austrian expedition that occupied Kamorta. Neither outpost endured. In 1789 Archibald Blair opened a British naval base and penal settlement on Chatham Island; it moved to Port Cornwallis two years later and was abandoned in May 1796 because of disease. Danish troops left Nancowry in 1809, so by 1821 no European garrison remained on either island chain.
zh:
安达曼群岛和尼科巴群岛是孟加拉湾与安达曼海之间的两串岛链，由十度海峡隔开。北部群岛上的安达曼人包括加洛瓦人和桑提内尔人等部族，以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生，对过往船只避而远之。更南面的尼科巴人使用南亚语系语言，把椰子卖给往返印度与东南亚的商船。朱罗国王拉金德拉一世曾把这些岛屿当作进攻室利佛逝的海军基地，1050年的坦贾武尔铭文记下了它们的泰米尔语名马纳卡瓦兰（Ma-Nakkavaram）；15世纪初的《郑和航海图》则把大尼科巴岛标作翠兰屿。1444年，没有大陆王国在两串岛上驻军，岛务由本地村社自理。

欧洲列强后来试图把这些停泊地变成永久据点。丹麦东印度公司的远征队1755年从特兰奎巴出发，1756年在大尼科巴岛建立新丹麦，1757年又在楠考里岛建立新西兰。疟疾和本地人反抗迫使幸存者在1759年4月前撤离。1768年，摩拉维亚传教士和士兵重返楠考里岛，种植咖啡和棉花；1778年，英国商人博尔茨（William Bolts）误以为丹麦已放弃主权，派出一支奥地利远征队占据格莫尔达岛。两处据点都没有维持多久。1789年，阿奇博尔德·布莱尔在查塔姆岛开设英国海军基地和流放地，两年后迁往康沃利斯港，终因疾病流行于1796年5月废弃。丹麦军队也于1809年撤出楠考里岛；到1821年，两组群岛上都已没有欧洲驻军。

en:
Gwadar sits on a hammerhead peninsula that encloses a deep anchorage on the Makran coast; its Balochi name means 'gate of the winds'. Alexander's admiral Nearchus sailed past in 325 BC and recorded fishermen among the people the Greeks called Ichthyophagoi. The Ming chart based on Zheng He's voyages later marks the headland as Kewata'er. For two centuries before 1444 the Buledai Baloch kept the settlement, combining fishing, herding and coastal carrying. In that year Gwadar was a small Sunni town under a Baloch malik. Its people lived mostly from fish, while dhow sailors on the run between Sindh and Oman knew the sheltered water outside the peninsula.

The Ottoman admiral Seydi Ali Reis called there in the 1550s and named the local chief in his Mirror of Countries of 1557 as Malik Jalal al-Din, son of Malik Dinar. Portuguese raiders burned Gwadar and nearby Pasni in 1581, but won no permanent foothold. The Gichkis displaced the Buledais in 1740, and Nasir Khan I of Kalat secured a share of their revenues. Gwadar's future changed in 1783, when Nasir Khan granted the port to Sultan bin Ahmad, an exiled prince of Muscat. After Sultan made himself ruler of Oman he kept Gwadar instead of returning it to Kalat. An Omani wali built the fort and handled cargoes of ivory, spices, woollens and slaves. The Buledais briefly took the town after Sultan died in 1804, before Omani troops restored the enclave.
zh:
瓜达尔坐落在莫克兰海岸一个锤形半岛上，半岛围出深水锚地；俾路支语地名为「风之门」的意思。公元前325年，亚历山大的海军将领涅阿尔霍斯航经此地，记下当地渔民和被希腊人称为「食鱼者」的人群。依据郑和远航绘成的《郑和航海图》后来把这个海角标作克瓦塔儿。1444年之前的两百年间，布莱迪家的俾路支首领掌管此地，居民捕鱼、放牧，也兼做沿海转运。那一年，瓜达尔是俾路支马利克治下的逊尼派小镇，多数人靠渔获为生，来往信德与阿曼之间的独桅帆船水手则熟知半岛外的避风水域。

奥斯曼海军将领赛义迪·阿里·赖斯在1550年代停泊于此，并在1557年成书的《列国镜》中记下当地首领是马利克·迪纳尔之子马利克·贾拉勒丁。1581年，葡萄牙袭掠者焚毁瓜达尔和附近的帕斯尼，却没有建立长期据点。1740年，吉奇基家取代布莱迪家，卡拉特汗纳西尔汗一世随后取得一部分岁入。1783年，纳西尔汗把港口封给流亡的马斯喀特王公苏丹·本·艾哈迈德，瓜达尔的命运随之改变。苏丹成为阿曼统治者后没有按约把瓜达尔交还卡拉特，而是留作属地。阿曼派来的瓦利修建城堡，经管象牙、香料、毛织物和奴隶贸易。苏丹于1804年死后，布莱迪人一度夺城，阿曼军队很快又恢复了这块海外领地。

en:
Kalat is a high plateau fortress in the Central Brahui Range, looking down on the Bolan road that caravans and armies used between Kandahar, Sindh and the Indus plains. Its older names point to the peoples who held it before the Brahui khans: Kalat-i-Sewa recalled a Sewa ruling line, while Kalat-i-Nichari linked the fort with the Nichari Brahuis of the highlands. In 662 Arab raiders moving into Qiqan met Jat defenders near the Bolan and lost their commander al-Harith ibn Murra al-Abdi. In 1444 Kalat was still a local hill-fort above the trade route, with chiefs giving or withholding allegiance as stronger powers passed below it; during the fifteenth century the Mirwari Brahuis took it from the Sewa rulers.

The fort became the seat of a Brahui state in 1666, when Mir Ahmad Khan I brought the clans out from Mughal Kandahar, seized Quetta, Mastung and Pishin, and fought as an ally of Aurangzeb. Mir Samandar Khan defeated a Safavid invasion and received Karachi from the Mughals, and Mir Abdullah Khan led raiding columns through Sindh and Makran as far as Bandar Abbas before he was killed in 1734 by Hussain Hotak and the Kalhoras; Nader Shah later granted Kacchi to Abdullah's heir as blood-price. Nasir Khan I, called the Great by his own people, gave the confederacy its firmest government. After serving Ahmad Shah Durrani he revolted in 1758, routed Shah Wali Khan's force and held Kalat through Ahmad Shah's forty-day siege. The settlement that followed ended tribute payments. Nasir organised a standing army, a vizier's office and a state coinage, sent envoys to the Ottomans, Iran and Oman, and in 1784 gave Gwadar to Oman's fugitive Sultan bin Ahmad. When Nasir died in 1794, Kalat controlled the strongest highland power between Kandahar and the Arabian Sea.
zh:
喀拉特是中布拉灰山脉中的高原要塞，俯视波伦商道；往来坎大哈、信德和印度河平原的商队、军队多经这条山路。它的旧名提示着布拉灰诸汗以前的主人：「塞瓦之堡」来自塞瓦统治者，「尼查里之堡」则把山寨同高地的尼查里布拉灰人联系起来。662年，攻入基坎的阿拉伯袭击者在波伦一带遭遇贾特守军，指挥官哈里斯·伊本·穆拉·阿卜迪战死。1444年，喀拉特仍是商道上方的地方山寨，强邻从山下经过时，酋长们便称臣或抗命；15世纪，米尔瓦里布拉灰人从塞瓦统治者手中夺取此堡。

1666年，这座堡垒成为布拉灰国家的都城：米尔·艾哈迈德汗一世率领诸部脱离莫卧儿治下的坎大哈，攻取奎达、马斯通和皮欣，并作为奥朗则布的盟友作战。米尔·萨曼达尔汗击退萨法维入侵，又从莫卧儿人手中得到卡拉奇。米尔·阿卜杜拉汗率部横扫信德、莫克兰，远至阿巴斯港，1734年被侯赛因·霍塔基与卡尔霍拉联军所杀；纳迪尔沙后来把卡奇封给阿卜杜拉的继承人，作为血偿。被本族人称为「大帝」的纳西尔汗一世，把部落联盟改造成最稳固的政权。他曾随艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼出征，1758年却起兵反抗，击溃沙·瓦利汗的军队，并在艾哈迈德沙亲征时守住喀拉特四十天。随后的协议免除了贡赋。纳西尔设立常备军、维齐尔官署和国家铸币，向奥斯曼、伊朗和阿曼派遣使节，还在1784年把瓜达尔交给流亡的阿曼苏丹本·艾哈迈德。1794年纳西尔去世时，喀拉特已是坎大哈与阿拉伯海之间最强的高地政权。

en:
Quetta, long called Shal or Shalkot, fills a high enclosed valley just above the Bolan Pass. The Pashto name kwatta means a fort, and the mud-walled Miri citadel stood over the early settlement and its fields. The land belonged chiefly to the Kasi Pashtuns, whose arbabs apportioned orchards, grazing grounds and the water of the karez channels; apples, grapes and grain grew well in the upland soil. Below the valley, the Bolan road ran south toward Sibi and Sindh, linking the country of Kandahar with the Indian plains. In 1444 Kasi headmen still held Shal, governors in Kandahar claimed their allegiance, and Baloch confederacies pressed upward from the hot country beyond the pass.

The valley usually followed whoever held Kandahar. A Timurid ruler of Herat granted Shal to Shah Beg Arghun in the late fifteenth century, before the Arghuns moved south to conquer Sindh. In 1543 Humayun passed through with the broken remnant of his army after defeat by Sher Shah Suri, on his way to exile at the Safavid court. Mughal records later listed Shal and neighbouring Pishin among the lands supplying Akbar with troops and revenue, and in the seventeenth century they changed hands with Kandahar during its wars between Mughals and Safavids. The Hotak Afghans drew the valley into their revolt in 1709, and Ahmad Shah Durrani incorporated it into his new empire in 1747 before using the Bolan route for his Indian campaigns. Ahmad Shah granted Quetta's revenue and administration to Nasir Khan I of Kalat as payment for Baloch military help, while the sanad confirmed the Kasi families in their lands and water rights. Caravans continued to carry the valley's fruit, grain and wool through the pass between India, Kandahar and Persia.
zh:
奎达旧称沙尔或沙尔科特，位于波伦山口上方一处群山环抱的高谷。普什图语「kwatta」意为堡垒，早年聚落和农田上方矗立着夯土筑成的米尔堡。谷地土地主要归普什图卡西部所有，各部阿尔巴布分配果园、牧场和坎儿井水道；高地土壤适宜苹果、葡萄和谷物生长。谷地以南，波伦山道通向锡维和信德，把坎大哈一带与印度河平原连接起来。1444年，卡西头人仍据有沙尔，坎大哈的总督要求他们臣服，山口外炎热低地的俾路支联盟则向北施压。

谁占有坎大哈，通常也就支配沙尔。15世纪末，赫拉特的帖木儿统治者把沙尔封给沙赫·贝格·阿尔洪，后来阿尔洪家族南下征服信德。1543年，胡马雍被舍尔沙·苏利击败后，率残部穿过谷地，前往萨法维宫廷流亡。莫卧儿官修记载后来把沙尔和邻近的皮辛列为向阿克巴提供兵役与贡赋之地；17世纪，两地又随坎大哈在莫卧儿与萨法维战争中几度易手。1709年，霍塔克普什图人把谷地卷入起兵；1747年，艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼将其纳入新帝国，随后取道波伦远征印度。为酬谢俾路支援军，艾哈迈德沙把奎达的赋税和行政授予喀拉特的纳西尔汗一世，特许状也确认了卡西家族对土地和水源的权利。商队继续穿过山口，把谷地的水果、谷物和羊毛运往印度、坎大哈和波斯。

en:
Roh is the name the chroniclers of India gave to the Pashtun hill country running from the Kabul River to the Indus, and its market town is Peshawar, set at the eastern mouth of the Khyber Pass. Every army and caravan between Kabul and India filed through this gap. Ancient Purushapura, winter capital of the Kushan emperors, held Kanishka's great stupa, which Chinese pilgrims called the tallest tower on earth, a ruin by the seventh century. Mahmud of Ghazni defeated the Hindu Shahis there on 28 November 1001, and after the Ghurids the Mongols wrecked the town early in the thirteenth century. By the fifteenth century Dilazak and other Pashtun tribes held the valley, selling flocks and horses down the road into India. In 1444 Peshawar was a caravan staging post in tribal hands, its bazaars kept busy by the Khyber traffic.

Babur took the town, then called Begram, in July 1526 and rebuilt its Bala Hissar fort, and the Mughals tied it to India on Sher Shah Suri's Grand Trunk Road. Akbar restored the name Peshawar, Shah Jahan laid out a Shalimar Garden for the city, and the Kabul governor Mohabbat Khan, who wintered here, built his mosque in 1630. The hill clans never accepted the empire: Pir Roshan's Roshani followers besieged the town in 1586, when a fort fire burned up more than a thousand camel-loads of goods, and in 1672 the Afridis cut a Mughal battalion to pieces in the Khyber and shut the pass until Aurangzeb marched through himself two years later. Bahadur Shah I had governed Peshawar before taking the Mughal throne.

Nader Shah's Persians seized Peshawar on 18 November 1738, and under Timur Shah the Durrani Afghans made it their winter capital; the kings lodged in the Bala Hissar while Bukhara caravans traded horses and dried fruit for Indian cloth. Marathas and Sikhs took it in 1758; Ahmad Shah Durrani won it back the next year. In 1809 Elphinstone's mission, the first British embassy to Afghanistan, met Shah Shuja in the fort. Ranjit Singh's Sikhs overran the valley in 1818 and left the Barakzai sardar Yar Mohammad Khan to rule as their tributary.
zh:
罗兴伽（Roh）是印度史籍对喀布尔河到印度河之间这片普什图人山地的称呼，它的门户城镇是白沙瓦，城在开伯尔山口东端。喀布尔与印度之间的每一支军队、每一队商旅都要穿过这道山口。古城布路沙布逻是贵霜皇帝的冬都，城中有迦腻色迦大佛塔，中国求法僧称它是世间最高的塔，到7世纪时已成废墟。1001年11月28日，加兹尼的马哈茂德在此击败印度沙希王朝的军队；此后此地经古尔王朝之手，13世纪初被蒙古人摧毁。到15世纪，迪拉扎克等普什图部族据有谷地，把羊群和马匹沿路贩往印度。1444年的白沙瓦是部族掌握中的一座商队驿站，集市全靠开伯尔山口的往来维持。

1526年7月，巴布尔攻取当时称贝格拉姆的白沙瓦，重建巴拉希萨尔堡，莫卧儿人又把它接上舍尔沙·苏利的大干道，与印度连为一体。阿克巴恢复了白沙瓦之名，沙贾汗为城里修了一座夏利马尔花园，在此过冬的喀布尔总督莫哈巴特汗1630年建成了他的清真寺。山地部族从不接受帝国：皮尔·罗尚的罗沙尼派信徒1586年围攻此城，同年城堡失火，烧掉上千驮货物；1672年阿夫里迪人在开伯尔山口歼灭一支莫卧儿军队并封锁山口，直到奥朗则布两年后亲自率军打通。巴哈杜尔沙一世登上莫卧儿皇位之前，就曾任白沙瓦总督。

1738年11月18日，纳迪尔沙的波斯大军夺取白沙瓦；帖木儿沙时代，杜兰尼的阿富汗人把此城作为冬都，国王们驻跸巴拉希萨尔堡，布哈拉来的商队则在市中以马匹和干果交换印度布匹。1758年马拉塔人与锡克人攻下此城，艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼次年将其夺回。1809年，埃尔芬斯通率领的使团在堡中觐见沙阿·舒贾，这是英国派往阿富汗的第一个使团。1818年，兰季特·辛格的锡克军队席卷谷地，留下巴拉克扎伊酋长亚尔·穆罕默德汗作为臣属统治。

en:
Mrauk U lies a little inland from the Bay of Bengal on the Arakan plain, where tidal creeks wind between low hill ranges. Its founders turned the creeks into moats and the streams into canals, so boats could be rowed up to the palace walls. Min Saw Mon, back from years of exile at the Bengal court, founded the city in 1430 with Bengali troops and made it the capital of a restored Arakanese kingdom; his brother took Sandoway to the south in 1437. In 1444 the court was Theravada Buddhist but deeply marked by Bengal: the kings struck coins and used royal titles in the Sultanate style, while Arab, Indian and Portuguese ships already called along the coast.

Min Bin, who came to the throne in 1531, ringed the city with walls and pagodas, above all the fortress-like Shitthaung temple, and within a decade his governors held Chittagong. When Tabinshwehti marched on Arakan in 1546 his army could not force the walls and withdrew, and a second Toungoo invasion in 1580 failed the same way. At the end of the century an Arakanese fleet joined the sack of Pegu in 1599 and brought home the spoil, among it a white elephant, bronze cannon and thirty bronze statues the Siamese had carried off from Angkor. By then Mrauk U held perhaps 160,000 people behind thirty kilometres of walls; the Dutch East India Company kept a factory there, and Bengali poets wrote at the court. One of them, Alaol, had been seized by Portuguese slavers as a boy, rose from royal bodyguard to court poet, and wrote his Padmavati in the city. Much of the wealth behind all this came from slave raids on the Bengal coast. After a Mughal army took Chittagong in 1666 the kingdom never recovered. Its end came in 1785, when Konbaung Burmese armies overran the capital; they cut the Mahamuni Buddha, Arakan's most sacred image, into sections and carried it to Amarapura, along with the Angkor bronzes.
zh:
妙乌位于阿拉干平原，距孟加拉湾不远，潮汐河汊穿行于低矮丘陵之间。建城者把河汊修成壕沟、溪流凿成运河，船只可以一直划到宫墙之下。明苏蒙从孟加拉宫廷流亡多年归来，1430年借孟加拉军队建立此城，作为复兴的阿拉干王国都城；其弟明克意1437年南取丹兑。1444年的妙乌朝廷信奉上座部佛教，却处处带着孟加拉的印记：国王铸造的钱币、使用的王号都仿效苏丹国，阿拉伯、印度和葡萄牙船只也已往来于沿岸。

1531年即位的明彬环城修筑城墙与佛塔，最著名的是形如要塞的瑞特杭寺；不出十年，他的官员已控制吉大港。1546年德彬瑞蒂进军阿拉干，攻不破妙乌的城墙，只得退兵；1580年东吁第二次来犯，同样无功而返。16世纪末，若开舰队参与1599年洗劫勃固，带回的战利品中有白象、铜炮，还有三十尊暹罗人从吴哥掠走的铜像。那时妙乌在三十公里长的城墙内容纳约十六万人，荷兰东印度公司设有商馆，孟加拉诗人也在宫廷中写作。诗人阿拉奥尔少年时被葡萄牙掳奴者劫走，从王宫护卫做到宫廷诗人，他的《帕德玛瓦蒂》就写成于妙乌。支撑这一切的财富，很大一部分来自在孟加拉沿海掳人为奴的勾当。1666年莫卧儿军队夺取吉大港后，王国再未恢复元气。1785年，贡榜大军攻破都城；阿拉干最受尊崇的马哈穆尼大佛被肢解成数段，与吴哥铜像一起运往阿马拉布拉。

en:
Kale, in the Myittha valley where the Chin Hills descend toward the Chindwin, was the chief town of the Kale-Kabaw country. Tracks from its market ran west through the Kabaw Valley to Manipur, carrying ivory and hill produce between Shan lowlanders and Chin hill villagers. Local tradition dates the town to 966. After the fall of Pagan it became a small Shan principality, and in 1406 King Minkhaung sent his son Prince Min Nyo to govern it. Min Nyo kept the frontier quiet and rose to senior command in Ava's wars, then took the Ava throne in 1425 with Queen Shin Bo-Me's support before Mohnyin Thado overthrew him months later. In 1444 Kale was held for King Narapati by a saopha who was also the king's son-in-law.

The Kabaw road kept Kale in wars it could not control. Manipur and the Pong kingdom divided Thaungdut and Khampat after their campaign of 1470; from the 1470s Mohnyin raided into the valley, and by the 1520s Kale supplied men to the Shan confederation that took Ava in 1527. Bayinnaung's Toungoo armies drove the confederation up the Chindwin in 1555 and secured the northern Shan states two years later. Manipuri raiders used the same corridor into Upper Burma between 1724 and 1741. Alaungpaya reversed the route in November 1758, invaded Manipur, posted garrisons at Tamu and Thaungdut, and brought back horsemen for his 'Cassay Horse'. In 1813 Bodawpaya moved forward bases into Kabaw to install his own candidate on the Manipuri throne.
zh:
格礼（今吉灵庙）位于钦敦江支流的河谷，钦山丘陵在此降到平原，是格礼—格包一带的首镇。镇上的商路向西穿过格包河谷通往曼尼普尔，河谷掸人、山中钦人和象牙、山货贩子在此交易。当地传说把建城时间追溯到966年。蒲甘崩溃后，这里成为小型掸邦；1406年，阿瓦王明康派王子明纽前来镇守。明纽稳住边疆，凭战功升为阿瓦高级将领，1425年又在王后支持下夺取王位，数月后被孟养的他託推翻，史称格礼杰当纽。1444年，镇守格礼的诏法是那腊勃底的女婿，边镇仍为阿瓦守边。

格包通道使格礼一再卷入它无法左右的战争。1470年，曼尼普尔和蓬国在战役后瓜分了当都与坎帕一带；从1470年代起，孟养不断袭入河谷，到1520年代，格礼已向1527年攻陷阿瓦的掸邦联盟出兵。1555年，勃印曩的东吁大军把联盟沿钦敦江逐走，两年后平定北方诸掸邦。1724至1741年间，曼尼普尔袭掠者又沿这条走廊深入上缅甸。1758年11月，雍籍牙反向取道远征曼尼普尔，在德穆和当都设置驻军，带回的骑手编入他的「卡赛骑兵」。1813年，波道帕耶把前进基地推入格包河谷，把自己的代理人扶上曼尼普尔王位。

en:
Sagaing sits on the Irrawaddy opposite Ava, on a long ridge where pagodas and forest monasteries crowd every hill. Behind the town opens the Mu valley, one of the three main granaries of the Irrawaddy plain. After the fall of Pagan, the teenage Prince Saw Yun, a discontented son of King Thihathu of Pinya, walked out of his father's court in 1315 and made the town his seat. Backed by a sect of forest monks, he rebuilt the timber walls in brick without leave, finishing in 1316, and beat off the two expeditions Pinya sent against him. His small kingdom bore the brunt of the Maw Shan raids on Upper Burma, and in 1364 the Shans sacked both Sagaing and Pinya in turn. Saw Yun's grandson Thado Minbya seized the two ruined capitals and in 1365 founded Ava across the river, and under the Ava kings Sagaing became the usual fief of the crown prince. In 1444 it is a prosperous river town beside the Mu granary, its hills a retreat for monks, looking straight across the water at the royal capital.

In 1636 King Thalun dedicated the Kaunghmudaw at the town's northwestern edge, an egg-shaped relic stupa modeled on the Ruwanwelisaya of Sri Lanka, its round silhouette unlike the pyramid-like pagodas usual in Burma. The older Soon U Ponya Shin pagoda crowns the ridge above the river, reached by covered stairways climbing the 240-metre hill. When the Mon armies of Pegu took Ava in 1752, Sagaing fell with it, but Alaungpaya of the new Konbaung dynasty won the river back within a few years and his son Naungdawgyi kept his court at Sagaing from 1760 to 1763 before the capital returned to Ava. Kings and nobles went on endowing the hillside monasteries through the long wars with Siam and Qing China: monks came to study and meditate on the ridge while the capitals downstream changed hands.
zh:
实皆坐落在伊洛瓦底江畔，与阿瓦隔河相望，沿江的丘陵上佛塔与林间寺院一座挨一座，城后就是伊洛瓦底平原三大粮仓之一的穆河谷。蒲甘王朝衰落后，彬牙王底哈都之子、年少的苏云因受封后心怀不满，于1315年离开父王的宫廷，在实皆立足。他在一派林间僧侣的支持下，不等朝廷准许便把木栅城墙改成砖墙，1316年完工，又击退了彬牙两度派来的军队。这个小国独力承受着麓川掸军对上缅甸的连年侵扰，1364年掸军接连攻破实皆和彬牙。苏云的孙子他拖弥婆耶占据两座废墟般的都城，于1365年在对岸建起阿瓦城；阿瓦诸王治下，实皆成了王储通常受封的食邑。1444年的实皆是毗邻穆河谷粮仓的富庶江城，山丘上是僧侣修行的去处，隔江便望见王都。

1636年，他隆王在城西北郊建成贡慕陶佛塔，供奉佛骨舍利；塔身仿照斯里兰卡的鲁万韦利萨雅塔，呈蛋形，圆润的轮廓与缅甸常见的锥状佛塔大不相同。山脊上更古老的佛塔高居江面之上，有带顶长廊沿240米高的山坡拾级而上。1752年勃固孟族军队攻陷阿瓦，实皆一同陷落，但新兴贡榜王朝的雍笈牙数年内便收复沿江诸城，其子瑙道吉于1760至1763年以实皆为王廷，之后朝廷才迁回阿瓦。在与暹罗和清朝连年交战的岁月里，国王与贵族仍不断布施营建山坡上的寺院：下游的都城几度易手，僧侣照旧来山脊上求学修行。

en:
Möng Yang, Mohnyin to the Burmese, was the northernmost of the Shan states, centred on the town of Mohnyin on the plain below the Kachin hills and looking south over the kingdom of Ava. Its Shan name means 'land of the snipe'. It broke from Mong Mao around 1400 and was recognised as a Ming pacification commission in 1404, and in 1410 the king of Ava posted a commander named Thado to hold it as sawbwa. The fief repaid Ava strangely. In 1426 Thado marched south, drove the usurping prince and queen from Ava and took the crown himself, founding the Mohnyin dynasty that ruled the kingdom for the next century. In 1444 the sawbwa at Mohnyin steered between Ava and Ming China: three years earlier Si Renfa, the broken ruler of Mong Mao, had fled to Möng Yang, and Chinese envoys were still demanding he be handed over.

From the 1470s Möng Yang turned on Ava, raiding into the Kabaw Valley and Kale. In the 1520s its sawbwa Sawlon built a confederation of Shan states with the kingdom of Prome, and in 1526 his armies took Ava; King Shwenankyawshin fell fighting before the city and Sawlon set his son Thohanbwa on the throne, ending 163 years of Ava's rule over Upper Burma. Many Burmese families fled south to Toungoo. Sawlon enjoyed his victory only a few years. In 1533, after taking Prome, he was murdered by his own ministers on the road home. Thohanbwa was in turn killed by Burmese ministers in 1543, the alliance quarrelled through the rest of the decade, and Bayinnaung retook Ava and received Möng Yang's submission in 1557.

The state rose with Mogaung against Bayinnaung in 1571, and after years of hill war its chief Si Ge was handed over by his own followers and put to death in 1579; the Ming generals Liu Ting and Deng Zilong won the country back for a moment soon after. In 1769 Fu Heng's Qing army marched through Möng Yang, storming four stockades, until the Kaungton peace returned it to Burma. Under the Konbaung kings the Shan sawbwas gave way to Burmese governors, and Mohnyin became a royal myo.
zh:
孟养，缅语称莫宁，是诸掸邦中位置最北的一个，治所莫宁在克钦丘陵南缘的平原上，向南俯视阿瓦王国，掸语里「孟养」意为「鹬鸟之地」。1400年前后它脱离麓川，1404年被明朝册封为宣慰使司；1410年，阿瓦王派部将德多出任孟养诏法。这个安排后来以出人意料的方式还报了阿瓦：1426年德多南下，赶走篡位的王子和王后，自己登上王位，开创了此后统治阿瓦一个世纪的孟养王朝。1444年，坐镇莫宁的诏法在阿瓦与明朝之间周旋：三年前麓川首领思任法战败逃入孟养，明朝的使节还在不断催着交人。

从1470年代起，孟养反过来攻打阿瓦，兵锋遍及格包河谷和格礼。1520年代，诏法色隆法联合诸掸邦和卑谬组成联军，1526年攻陷阿瓦，阿瓦王瑞南觉欣战死于城前，色隆法把儿子多汉发扶上王位，终结了阿瓦对上缅甸163年的统治，大批缅人南逃东吁。色隆法没受用几年：1533年他攻下卑谬后，在回师途中被自己的大臣刺杀。多汉发1543年也被缅甸朝臣所杀，掸邦联盟在余下的十年里争吵不休，莽应龙收复阿瓦，又在1557年接受孟养臣服。

1571年，孟养联合孟拱起兵反抗莽应龙；多年山地征战后，首领思个被自己的部下献出，1579年遇害，明将刘綎、邓子龙随后一度收复其地。1769年，傅恒的清军取道孟养，连破四座寨栅，直到老官屯和议才把这片地方交还缅甸。贡榜王朝时期，掸族诏法由中央任命的缅人总督取代，莫宁成为王国治下的一个谬。

en:
Hsenwi, Theinni to the Burmese and Mubang in Ming records, held the upper Nam Tu valley, the natural route from Yunnan into the Shan hills and down to Ava. It was by far the largest Shan state west of the Salween; its saopha drew men and tribute from the Nam Tu and Shweli valleys, while Wa lands east of the river stood in a looser protectorate. Shan chronicles traced the court to two princes said to have come down from heaven and called the old realm Kawsampi. Its walled capital was remembered as a large and well-built town. Ming China enrolled the ruler as pacification commissioner of Mubang and called out Hsenwi levies in the Luchuan war. In 1444 the saopha still ruled dozens of subordinate towns from that capital, the strongest Shan power on the road between Yunnan and Ava.

Bayinnaung's Toungoo army reduced Hsenwi with the other Shan states in 1557, keeping a saopha but tying the court to Burmese administration. When that empire broke apart, Nyaungyan Min and his son Anaukpetlun forced Hsenwi back under Ava in 1605; Nyaungyan died on the march south of Hsipaw. About 1738 the Burmese court at Ava suppressed the old Kawsampi polity and apportioned its lands among approved chiefs. Hsenwi again lay across the main Yunnan-to-Ava route in 1767, when Ming Rui's Qing army seized it within days, left 5,000 men to guard its supplies, and marched toward Ava. Maha Thiha Thura was repulsed outside Hsenwi, but Ming Rui's deeper advance ended in destruction at Maymyo three months later.
zh:
兴威，缅语称登尼，明朝史籍称木邦，控制南杜河上游谷地；这条谷地从云南伸入掸邦山地，再沿河南下阿瓦。它是萨尔温江以西最大的掸邦，诏法从南杜河与瑞丽江谷地征调人力和贡赋，萨尔温江以东的佤人地区也处在较松散的保护关系下。掸族编年史把王统追溯到两位相传自天而降的王子，称古国为侨赏弥；其都城墙广大、营建坚固。明朝封统治者为木邦宣慰使，并在麓川之役中征调木邦军队。1444年，诏法仍从这座都城统属数十个城镇，是云南通往阿瓦路上最强的掸邦势力。

1557年，勃印曩的东吁军队在征服诸掸邦时拿下兴威，保留诏法，同时把其宫廷纳入缅甸行政体系。东吁帝国瓦解后，良渊王与王子阿那毕隆在1605年迫使兴威重新臣服阿瓦，良渊王本人在行军途中死于昔卜以南。约1738年，阿瓦的缅人朝廷压服古老的侨赏弥政权，把土地分给获准效忠的头人。1767年，兴威再次横在云南到阿瓦的主路上：明瑞的清军数日攻占此地，留五千人守护粮草，自己继续向阿瓦进军。玛哈·希哈修亚在兴威城下被击退，但明瑞深入后的主力三个月后在眉苗被歼。

en:
Ava, or Inwa, occupies an artificial island in the Irrawaddy at the mouth of the Myitnge, where canals cut the surrounding swamps into a walled royal city. Its outer wall zigzags in the outline of a seated lion, the Burmese chinthe, and twelve gates lead into the inner citadel. Thado Minbya founded the city in 1365 after uniting Sagaing and Pinya. Holding the Kyaukse rice lands to the south, his successors became the chief Burmese power of Upper Burma, at a court where monks wrote the first Burmese chronicles and law codes in their own language. In 1444 Narapati I was two years into his reign. The Forty Years' War against Pegu had drained the kingdom, Shan raids pressed from the north, and Ming armies campaigning on the Yunnan frontier were striking the same sawbwas who owed Ava tribute.

On 25 March 1527 a Shan confederation led by Mohnyin, with troops from Prome, sacked Ava and ruled it for a generation, until Bayinnaung of Toungoo captured the city in January 1555. After the Toungoo collapse, Kings Nyaungyan and Anaukpetlun rebuilt the kingdom from Ava, and Thalun brought the court back from Pegu in 1635. In 1659 Zhu Youlang, last claimant of the Southern Ming, fled across the border, and King Pindale settled him across the river at Sagaing after his men gave up their arms. His followers soon laid waste the country around Ava and besieged the capital, whose defence rested partly on Portuguese gunners. After Pye Min seized the throne he had the Chinese followers put to death, and in January 1662 delivered the emperor to the Qing general Wu Sangui, who had him strangled in Yunnan. Restored Hanthawaddy forces sacked and burned Ava in 1752. Hsinbyushin rebuilt the city a decade later and brought the court back, but Bodawpaya later moved the capital to Amarapura, and the island city never ruled Burma again.
zh:
阿瓦，又译因瓦，位于伊洛瓦底江在密埃河口的一座人工岛上；运河穿过周围沼泽，围成一座有城墙的王都。外城城墙蜿蜒曲折，轮廓像一头蹲坐的护法狮「钦特」，内城则开有十二座城门。1365年，他拖弥婆耶统一实皆和彬牙后建立此城。阿瓦南控叫栖稻米产区，继承者据此成为上缅甸最主要的缅人政权，宫廷僧侣还以缅文写下最早的缅人编年史和法典。1444年，那腊勃底即位已有两年。对勃固的四十年战争耗尽了国力，北方掸人不断袭扰，明朝在云南边境用兵，攻打的正是那些向阿瓦称臣的掸族土司。

1527年3月25日，以孟养为首的掸族联盟会同卑谬军队洗劫阿瓦，统治此城近一代人，直到1555年1月东吁的勃印曩将其攻占。东吁政权崩溃后，良渊王和阿那毕隆以阿瓦为基地复兴王国，他隆王又在1635年把朝廷从勃固迁回。1659年，南明最后一位君主朱由榔逃入缅甸，随从解除武装后，彬德莱王把他安置在江对岸的实皆。这些人很快蹂躏阿瓦周边、围攻都城，城防多赖葡萄牙炮手支撑。莽白夺位后诛杀朱由榔的随从，又在1662年1月把这位皇帝交给清军主将吴三桂，朱由榔随后在云南被缢死。1752年，复兴的汉达瓦底军队洗劫并焚毁阿瓦。辛标信在十多年后重建城市、迎回朝廷，但波道帕耶又把首都迁往阿马拉布拉，这座岛上都城再未成为缅甸的统治中心。

en:
Taungoo was founded in 1279 as Pagan pushed settlers into the Sittaung valley, a hill-backed corridor between Upper Burma and the Mon country. After Pagan collapsed in 1287, the town passed through Myinsaing and Pinya, broke away in 1358, and then acknowledged Ava only nominally after 1367. Its governors kept room to manoeuvre by balancing Ava against Hanthawaddy. Its classical Pali name, Ketumadi, meant 'endowed with the royal standard'. In 1444 Taungoo was a Theravada Burmese frontier principality with its own brick walls, a southern approach to the Irrawaddy basin and a refuge from the wars of Upper Burma.

Ava crushed another local revolt in 1470 and gave the governorship to its general Sithu Kyawhtin. His grandson Mingyi Nyo took office in 1485 and kept the small state out of the fighting around Ava; its stability attracted refugees as Shan raids weakened Upper Burma. In October 1510 he renounced Ava's overlordship and founded the Taungoo Kingdom. From this landlocked base, Tabinshwehti and Bayinnaung built the First Toungoo Empire. Tabinshwehti began his wars against Hanthawaddy in 1534, moved the capital to Pegu in 1539, and completed the conquest of the Mon kingdom by 1541, gaining its wealth and access to Portuguese mercenaries and firearms.

The old capital became a viceregal seat, not a quiet one. In 1599 Viceroy Minye Thihathu II joined Arakanese forces and Portuguese mercenaries in the sack of Pegu and declared himself king. Natshinnaung succeeded in 1609, but King Anaukpetlun captured Taungoo in 1610 and ended the city's separate ruling line.
zh:
东吁建于1279年，是蒲甘向锡当河谷移民时形成的山前据点，正处在上缅甸与孟人地区之间的走廊。1287年蒲甘崩溃后，这里先后受制于敏象和宾亚，1358年自立，1367年后仅在名义上臣服阿瓦。地方统治者借阿瓦与罕礁越利相互牵制，保住了自治。它的巴利语古典名称意为「配有王旗之地」。1444年的东吁是上座部佛教的缅人边境侯国，拥有砖砌城墙，既是通往伊洛瓦底江流域的南路，也收容躲避上缅甸战祸的人。

1470年，阿瓦镇压东吁再叛，把这里交给平叛将领西都觉廷。其孙明基纽1485年就任总督，尽力让小国避开阿瓦周围的战事；上缅甸遭掸人连年攻扰时，东吁的安定反而吸引了流民。1510年10月，他正式拒绝阿瓦的宗主权，建立东吁王国。德彬瑞蒂和勃印曩后来就从这个没有出海口的基地出发，建立第一东吁帝国。德彬瑞蒂1534年开始进攻罕礁越利，1539年迁都勃固，到1541年征服孟人王国，并取得沿海王国的财富以及葡萄牙雇佣军和火器来源。

旧都此后成为副王驻地，却没有远离战争。1599年，副王明耶底哈都二世联合若开军队和葡萄牙雇佣军洗劫勃固，随后自立为王。那信南于1609年继位，但阿那毕隆在1610年攻占东吁，终结了这座城市自成一系的统治。

en:
Pegu lies on the tidal plains of Lower Burma, where the Pegu River meets a web of mangrove creeks running out to the Gulf of Martaban. It grew from a Mon fishing town into the capital of Hanthawaddy after King Binnya U moved his court there in 1369, and Razadarit held it through the long Forty Years' War against Ava. The Shwemawdaw Pagoda, enlarged by the Hanthawaddy kings on a hill in the town, drew pilgrims from across the Mon country. In 1444 Binnya Ran I ruled a kingdom at peace: delta rice, spices and forest goods from the hinterland, and Indian Ocean merchants at the river mouth made Pegu one of the wealthiest ports between Bengal and Malacca.

The old queen Shin Sawbu, the only woman to reign over Hanthawaddy, chose the monk Dhammazedi as her successor. He kept the peace, patronised the sangha, and in 1484 cast a bronze bell of about 294 tons for the Shwedagon Pagoda at nearby Dagon, said to be the largest bell ever made. Portuguese ships began trading at Pegu in the 1510s, but Tabinshwehti of Toungoo took the city in 1538–39 and made it his seat. Bayinnaung rebuilt it as the capital of his empire: after resettled Shans burned the palace in 1565, he raised the Kanbawzathadi Palace and twenty gates, each built by a different vassal, and crowned the Shwemawdaw with a new hti set with jewels from his own crown. The Venetian gem merchant Gasparo Balbi and the English traveller Ralph Fitch both saw the gilded city in the 1580s. In 1599 the viceroy of Toungoo and an Arakanese fleet sacked Pegu. Filipe de Brito, a Portuguese mercenary who had come with the Arakanese, later ruled Syriam and in 1608 dragged Dhammazedi's bell away to melt into cannon; the raft broke up where the Pegu meets the Yangon, and the bell sank with his flagship and was never recovered. Burmese troops retook Syriam and had de Brito impaled. A Mon restoration of the 1740s ended when Alaungpaya stormed the city in May 1757. Bodawpaya later rebuilt Pegu, by which time the river had shifted away and the sea trade was gone.
zh:
勃固位于下缅甸的潮汐平原，勃固河与密布的红树林潮沟在此汇合，通向马达班湾。它本是孟人的渔镇，1369年彬尼亚乌王建都于此，成为汉达瓦底的都城，罗娑陀利又据此与阿瓦相持于漫长的四十年战争。城中高地上的瑞摩屠塔经历代孟人国王扩建，吸引着孟族各地的香客。1444年，彬尼亚仰一世治下的王国太平无事：三角洲的稻米、内陆的香料和山货，加上云集河口的印度洋商船，使勃固成为孟加拉与马六甲之间最富庶的港口之一。

老王后信绍布是汉达瓦底唯一在位的女性君主，她选了僧人达摩悉提继位。达摩悉提维持和平、护持僧团，并于1484年为邻近大光的瑞德宫大金塔铸了一口约二百九十四吨重的铜钟，相传是有史以来最大的钟。葡萄牙船只在1510年代来此贸易，但东吁的德彬瑞蒂在1538至1539年攻占此城、定为王都。勃印曩把它重建为帝国的都城：1565年被迁徙来的掸人烧毁王宫后，他筑起甘菩遮塔迪宫和二十座城门，每座由一名藩属督造，又为瑞摩屠塔加上镶有自己王冠珠宝的新塔伞。威尼斯珠宝商加斯帕罗·巴尔比和英国人拉尔夫·菲奇都在1580年代见过这座金饰满城的都市。1599年，东吁诸侯与若开舰队联手洗劫勃固。随若开军而来的葡萄牙雇佣兵德·布里托后来割据沙廉，1608年把达摩悉提大钟拖走，打算熔铸大炮；木排在勃固河与仰光河汇流处解体，大钟连同他的座船沉入河底，再没打捞上来。东吁军队夺回沙廉后，将他处以木桩刑。孟人在1740年代一度复国，但雍笈牙在1757年5月攻破此城，复国告终。波道帕耶后来重建勃固，那时河道已经改道，海上贸易不复存在。

en:
Kengtung lies in a broad valley of the eastern Shan hills, on the old tracks between Sipsongpanna and Lanna. The Wa held the country first by their own tradition, until Tai princes of King Mangrai's line drove them out around the thirteenth century; the town then became the seat of the Tai Khun saophas, whose dynasty claimed descent from the Chiang Mai kings. Tai Khun, Tai Lu and Tai Yai farmed the valley floor, while Akha, Lahu and Wa villages kept the surrounding mountains. The Salween separated Kengtung from the Burmese kings, who took a yearly offering of ritual gold flowers and otherwise left the hills to themselves, and Ming China registered the principality as a tusi in 1405 under the name Menggen. In 1444 the saopha kept his own government and steered between Burma, China and Lanna.

Bayinnaung conquered Lanna in 1558 and Kengtung submitted, its local Mangrai-line prince confirmed as saopha by the Burmese court. The fighting returned in 1802, when Thammalangka, brother of the Chiang Mai ruler Kawila, took the town and carried off thousands of Tai Khun to repopulate Chiang Mai. Sao Kawng Tai submitted in 1804, while his brother Maha Hkanan held out at Mong Yawng; in 1813 he too accepted Burmese suzerainty, and Kengtung resumed as a Shan principality under Konbaung protection.
zh:
景栋坐落在掸邦东部山岭中的一片宽谷里，地当十二版纳与兰纳之间的旧山路。按佤族自己的说法，这里最早是佤人的土地，直到13世纪前后，孟莱王系的傣族王子把他们逐出；此后城镇成为傣坤诏法的驻地，王朝自称是清迈诸王的后裔。傣坤、傣仂和傣亚在谷底耕作，阿卡、拉祜和佤族村寨散居周围山地。景栋与缅甸诸王之间隔着萨尔温江，缅王每年只收一轮仪式性的金花，此外任由山地自理；1405年，明朝把这个土邦册为土司，称孟艮。1444年，诏法自掌政务，周旋于缅甸、中国和兰纳之间。

1558年勃印曩征服兰纳，景栋随之归顺，缅甸宫廷确认孟莱血统的本地王公继续担任诏法。1802年战火重起，清迈王卡维拉之弟探玛兰伽攻占城镇，把数千名傣坤人掳走，去补充清迈的人口。诏法绍考泰于1804年臣服，其弟玛哈卡南则据守孟永抵抗；1813年，连他也接受了缅甸宗主权，景栋才作为贡榜王朝庇护下的掸邦恢复。

en:
Mong Nai, Mone in Burmese, occupies a broad rice and cotton valley in the eastern southern Shan hills. The town stood in a repeatedly disturbed corridor: its records burned in several fires, and later accounts remembered it as a frequent centre of risings. Its early line is correspondingly hard to trace. Shan chronicles say Sam Long Hpa conquered it in 1223 and installed rulers tied to Mong Mao; Northern Thai chronicles say Khun Khua, a son of King Mangrai of Lan Na, founded it in 1318. The Lan Na connection was dynastic as well as cultural, for Mone's rulers were kin to the Mengrai court at Chiang Mai. In 1444 its saopha kept one of the strongest courts in the southern Shan country, ruling from a timber haw over rice land, cotton villages and smaller hill settlements.

Mone bought safety from Bayinnaung with tribute in 1556, but rebelled the next year with Lan Na support, seized Hsipaw and killed the Burmese nominee. Bayinnaung led five armies, about 33,000 men, into the hills and retook Hsipaw and Mone in November 1557. Mone broke away after the Toungoo empire collapsed, until Nyaungyan Min captured it in 1603. Naresuan of Ayutthaya died while marching into the Shan country during the war that followed in 1605, and in 1614 Anaukpetlun used Mone as the staging point for his reconquest of Lan Na. Burmese kings afterwards kept troops and officials there, making the town their main seat in the southern Shan states; by the early nineteenth century its ruler governed with the Burmese title myoza.
zh:
孟乃，缅语称莫内，地处掸邦高原南部东段一处盛产稻米和棉花的宽谷。孟乃城位于反复起事的山地带，本地档案多次在火灾中焚毁，早期世系也因此难以理清。掸史说三隆法1223年征服此地，安置了与勐卯有关系的王系；泰北编年史则说1318年由兰纳国王芒莱之子坤夸建城。它与兰纳的关系既有文化往来，也有王朝亲缘，孟乃统治者与清迈的孟莱宫廷同族。1444年，孟乃诏法在木宫中听政，是南掸最强的宫廷之一，治下有稻田、棉村和更小的山区聚落。

1556年，孟乃以进贡换得勃印曩退兵，第二年却在兰纳支持下起兵，攻占昔卜并杀死缅方任命的诏法。1557年11月，勃印曩亲率五军、约三万三千人入山，收复昔卜和孟乃。东吁帝国崩溃后孟乃自立，1603年被良渊王攻占。1605年，阿瑜陀耶的纳黎萱在随后的战事中进军掸地，病死军中；1614年，阿那毕隆又以孟乃为集结地，重新征服兰纳。此后缅王在孟乃驻军设官，把它作为控制南掸的首要据点；到19世纪初，其统治者以缅人封号「谬沙」治邦。

en:
Chiang Mai, the 'new city', sits on the Ping River, a river town on the caravan road between the Siamese plains and Yunnan. King Mangrai founded it in 1296 after uniting his Tai chiefdoms with Mon Hariphunchai and leaving flood-prone Wiang Kum Kam, and laid out its brick walls and moat with his allies Ngam Mueang of Phayao and Ram Khamhaeng of Sukhothai. Wat Chiang Man was the first temple within the walls; later kings raised Wat Phra Singh and the great brick Chedi Luang, and in 1386 a relic stupa went up on Doi Suthep above the valley. Legend says the Buddha's shoulder relic was set on a white elephant, which climbed Doi Suthep, trumpeted three times and died on the summit where the shrine stands. Ivory, teak and lac from the caravans made Lan Na rich. In 1441 Tilokkarat seized the throne from his father, and the next year routed an Ayutthayan army marching to aid his brother's revolt. In 1444 it was the leading city of the northern Tai, where Yunnanese and Shan caravans met the goods of the southern plains.

Tilokkarat fought Ayutthaya for the old Sukhothai lands, took Phayao in 1456 and called a Buddhist council at Wat Chet Yot in 1477 to recompile the Tripitaka. After him Lan Na weakened: King Ket was assassinated in 1545, and on 2 April 1558 the Shan ruler Mekuti surrendered Chiang Mai to Bayinnaung. Two centuries of Burmese rule followed, broken for a dozen years after the city submitted to Naresuan in 1602. Ralph Fitch, passing through in 1586, found Yunnanese caravans still trading gold, silver and civet under the Burmese garrison. Heavy taxes provoked revolt in 1727; the townspeople threw the Burmese out twice and ruled the Ping valley themselves until the Konbaung retook it in 1757. Kawila of Lampang took the city with Siamese help on 15 January 1775, but a Burmese counterstroke the next year left it deserted and overgrown for fifteen years. Kawila returned in the 1790s as a vassal of Bangkok, rebuilt the city and campaigned as far as Chiang Saen, bringing captives back to people it.
zh:
清迈意为「新城」，位于宾河畔，地当暹罗平原通往云南的商队大道。1296年，孟莱王兼并泰人诸邦与孟人古国哈里奔猜，又因魏功甘（Wiang Kum Kam）屡遭水患而弃用，便在宾河畔另建新城，与盟邦帕夭王恩孟、素可泰王兰甘亨共同规划砖城与护城河。清曼寺是城内第一座寺院，后来的国王又建帕辛寺、大修砖砌的斋里銮佛塔；1386年，城郊素贴山顶建起一座舍利塔。相传佛的肩骨舍利被放上一头白象，白象登上素贴山、长鸣三声后死于山顶，塔寺就建在那里。商队贩运象牙、柚木和紫胶，使兰纳富足。1441年蒂洛卡拉逼父夺位，次年击溃一支前来支援其兄叛乱的阿瑜陀耶军队；1444年，清迈是北部泰人的第一大城，云南与掸邦商队在此和南方平原的货物相会。

蒂洛卡拉与阿瑜陀耶争夺旧素可泰之地，1456年吞并帕夭，1477年在他所建的七塔寺（Wat Chet Yot）召集佛教结集，重新校订三藏。他身后兰纳转衰：国王盖1545年被弑，1558年4月2日，掸邦出身的统治者美古提（Mekuti）向勃印曩献城。此后是两百年缅统，只有1602年臣服纳黎萱后的十余年脱离缅甸。英国商人拉尔夫·菲奇1586年路过，见到缅军驻守之下仍有云南商队买卖黄金、白银和灵猫香。1727年重税激起民变，城中军民两度驱逐缅军，宾河谷地自立，直到1757年被贡榜王朝重新征服。1775年1月15日，南邦的卡维拉（Kawila）在暹罗支援下攻克清迈；次年缅军反攻，清迈荒废、野草丛生达十五年。1790年代卡维拉以曼谷藩臣的身份重返筑城，远征远至清盛，掳回人口充实这座空城。

en:
Martaban, called Mottama in Burmese, lies on the west bank of the Salween estuary on the Gulf of Martaban, facing Moulmein across the water. The Mon knew the old city as Sampanago, and its glazed storage jars were carried so far by sea that the port's name became the word for the jar itself in harbours from Arabia to Java. When Pagan collapsed in 1287 a Mon merchant chief, Wareru, seized the town and made it the capital of the Mon kingdom; the court moved to Pegu only in the 1360s. The quays stayed busy long afterwards, as junks cleared for Siam, Java and Sumatra, and the Chinese traveller Wang Dayuan found a crowded market dealing in ivory, silk and metals. In 1444 Martaban was the chief port of the Mon kings of Hanthawaddy Pegu, a Theravada Buddhist kingdom grown rich on the Bay of Bengal trade.

In the early sixteenth century its viceroy Saw Binnya ruled Martaban as his own, hiring Portuguese mercenaries and gunners and refusing to help the court at Pegu against Toungoo. Tabinshwehti took Pegu in 1538-1539 and Martaban stood alone. In 1541 Toungoo troops under Bayinnaung forced the harbour, stormed the walls after a long siege, sacked the town and put Saw Binnya to death, and the port never recovered. For the next three centuries it was only a fortress on the coast fought over between Burma and Siam. In 1740 the Mon of Pegu rose in a brief restoration of Hanthawaddy, but Alaungpaya of the new Konbaung dynasty crushed it and took Pegu in 1757, after which thousands of Mon fled east into Siam.
zh:
马达班，缅语称莫塔马，位于萨尔温江口西岸、马达班湾畔，隔水与摩棉相望。孟人古称此城为三巴纳哥，当地烧制的釉陶瓮随海船远销各地，从阿拉伯到爪哇的港口干脆把这种大瓮叫作「马达班」。1287年蒲甘崩溃后，孟人商人首领瓦里鲁夺取此城，立为孟人王国的都城，直到14世纪60年代朝廷才迁往勃固。迁都之后很久，码头依旧繁忙，帆船从这里驶往暹罗、爪哇和苏门答腊；中国航海家汪大渊见到的，是一座买卖象牙、丝绸和金属的热闹商镇。1444年，马达班是孟人勃固王国的首要港口，这是一个靠孟加拉湾贸易致富的上座部佛教国家。

16世纪初，总督苏毕尼亚（Saw Binnya）把马达班当作自家领地，雇用葡萄牙雇佣兵和炮手，正与东吁交战的勃固朝廷向他求援，他却按兵不动。1538至1539年德彬瑞梯攻占勃固，马达班陷入孤立。1541年，莽应龙率领的东吁军攻入港湾，经长期围城后破城，洗劫全城，处死苏毕尼亚，这座港口再未恢复往日的富庶。此后三百年间，它只是缅甸与暹罗反复争夺的沿海要塞。1740年，勃固孟人起兵，短暂复兴勃固王国，但新建贡榜王朝的雍笈牙将其镇压，1757年攻占勃固，数以千计的孟人随后东逃暹罗。

en:
Tavoy stands thirty kilometres up the Dawei River estuary from the Andaman Sea, on low ground the monsoon floods every year. Its Mon name means 'to sit cross-legged', after the Buddha's posture on his throne. Six miles north of the present city lies Sagara, old Tavoy, a Pyu provincial capital where burial urns, beads and coins have been dug up. From the eleventh to the thirteenth century the coast belonged to the Pagan Empire, and after Pagan fell in 1287 the estuary passed to Sukhothai and then to Ayutthaya. In 1444 Tavoy was a Mon-speaking, Theravada Buddhist port on Siam's remote western shore, worked by Dawei, Mon, Karen and Thai mariners.

The port changed hands in almost every Burmese–Siamese war. Bayinnaung of Toungoo took it with the rest of Siam in 1564; the Siamese recovered it in 1594; and Anaukpetlun retook the coast as far as Tavoy in 1614, stationing a garrison in his southernmost town. During the Burmese civil wars of the 1740s the Siamese reoccupied the estuary, until Alaungpaya, founder of the Konbaung dynasty, drove them out in 1760. His son Hsinbyushin held the whole Tenasserim coast by 1765, and Tavoy became the base of Maha Nawrahta's southern army, the column that closed on Ayutthaya and helped destroy the four-hundred-year-old capital in 1767. Burmese armies kept marching out of the estuary for another generation of wars, and two late-century Siamese attempts to retake the coast both failed.
zh:
土瓦在土瓦河河口上游，距安达曼海约三十公里，地势低洼，雨季常被淹没。它的孟语名意为「盘腿而坐」，取自佛陀登座的姿势。现城以北约十公里的萨加拉是古土瓦所在，曾是骠人的一处重镇，出土过骨灰瓮、串珠和钱币。11至13世纪，这段海岸属蒲甘王国；1287年蒲甘崩溃后，河口先后归入素可泰与阿瑜陀耶。1444年的土瓦是暹罗偏远西岸一座讲孟语、信上座部佛教的港口，土瓦人、孟人、克伦人和泰人的水手在此营生。

这座港口几乎在每一场缅暹战争中易手。1564年，东吁的勃印曩在征服全暹罗时拿下土瓦；1594年暹罗将其收复；1614年阿拿毕隆又攻占海岸直至土瓦，在这座最南端的城池屯驻缅军。18世纪40年代缅甸内战，暹罗重新进占河口，1760年贡榜王朝开国之主雍笈牙将其逐出。其子辛标信到1765年已控制整条丹那沙林海岸，土瓦成为玛哈·瑙亚塔南路大军的基地，这支军队与北路军合围，1767年攻灭立国四百余年的阿瑜陀耶。此后近半个世纪，缅军仍一再从河口出师征暹，暹罗在18世纪末两次反攻海岸，都未能得手。

en:
Ratchaburi sits on the Mae Klong River, where the road west from Ayutthaya enters the Tenasserim Hills and the passes toward Burma; its name is Sanskrit for 'the king's town'. Twelve kilometres to the south-east lie the ruins of Khu Bua, a moated Dvaravati city of the sixth century and one of the chief Mon towns of its day, whose Buddhist stucco figures and tablets are kept in the museum at Ratchaburi. In the thirteenth century Ram Khamhaeng brought the town under Sukhothai, and the kings of Ayutthaya kept it as a market and a fortress on the western road. In 1444 it was a Siamese, Theravada Buddhist town whose boats carried the rice of the Mae Klong plain to the markets of the capital.

The Burmese wars gave the fortress its work. After Ayutthaya fell in 1767 a Burmese garrison held Ratchaburi until Taksin drove it out the next year, on his campaign to reunite Siam. The town had a tie to the dynasty that followed: before the fall, under King Ekkathat, a young officer named Thongduang had been its deputy governor. He came to the throne as Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty, and as king he led troops against the Burmese in this district again and again, most heavily in the Nine Armies' War of 1785–1786. In 1817 his son Rama II ordered a new city wall built along the left bank of the Mae Klong.
zh:
叻武里临夜功河，阿瑜陀耶西去丹那沙林山脉、通往缅甸各山口的道路从这里入山；「叻武里」一名出自梵语，意为「王城」。城东南约十二公里是库布古城（Khu Bua）遗址，那是6世纪一座有土城墙和壕沟的堕罗钵底城市，也是当时孟人的主要城邑之一，出土的佛教灰塑造像和石刻现存叻武里的博物馆。13世纪兰甘亨将此城并入素可泰，阿瑜陀耶诸王则把它当作西道上的商镇兼要塞。1444年，这里是一座暹罗人的上座部佛教城镇，河船把夜功平原的米粮运往都城的市集。

后来的缅暹战争让这座要塞派上了用场。1767年阿瑜陀耶陷落，叻武里被缅军戍守，次年郑信出师收复此城，逐走缅军，继续他统一暹罗的战事。此城还与接下来的王朝有一层渊源：城破之前，厄伽陀王在位时，年轻军官通銮曾任叻武里副长官，他就是后来建立扎克里王朝的拉玛一世。即位之后，拉玛一世仍一再在这一带统兵抵御缅军，最激烈的是1785—1786年的九军之战。1817年，其子拉玛二世下令沿夜功河左岸修筑一道新城墙。

en:
Nakhon Si Thammarat lies on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula, the chief city of southern Siam. It began on the shore, but silting moved the coastline away from the walls; at Tha Rua, ten kilometres south, twelfth-century Song ceramics have been found. As Tambralinga, Sanskrit for 'Red Linga', it sent tribute to Song China, and an inscription records a Srivijayan king there as early as 775. King Sri Thammasok, ruling in 1231, built Wat Phra Mahathat, the great relic-stupa, and introduced Sinhalese Theravada Buddhism; his twelve dependent cities stretched from Chumphon to Pahang. The Ramkhamhaeng stele of 1292 names it the southernmost tributary of Sukhothai. After a fourteenth-century collapse a prince of Phetchaburi re-founded the city inside Ayutthaya's orbit. In 1444 its old dynasty still ruled, the Mahathat drew pilgrims from around the Gulf of Siam, and foreign sailors knew the port as Ligor.

Within Ayutthaya Ligor ranked first among the southern cities. King Trailok's palatine law of 1468 numbered it among the eight great cities, yet governorship passed from father to son in the old dynasty, and its wealth from Portuguese and Dutch trade fed a long claim to autonomy. When Ligor rebelled against King Prasat Thong in 1629, he sent Yamada Nagamasa south. Yamada headed Ban Yipun, Ayutthaya's Japanese quarter of roughly a thousand traders, Christian refugees and ronin; with these mercenaries he crushed the rising and briefly ruled Ligor before dying in 1630. Under King Narai the French engineer de Lamare rebuilt the walls in the 1680s, and after the Siamese revolution of 1688 Ligor rose again and was subdued four years later.

When Ayutthaya fell to the Burmese in 1767, vice-governor Nu made Ligor independent; Taksin defeated him in 1769 and later restored him as a tributary ruler. Rama I ended that in 1784, making the ruler an appointed governor and transferring his Malay vassals, Patani among them, to Songkhla. Two years later a Burmese army sacked the city. From 1811 its governor was Nakhon Noi, called the Raja of Ligor by the British; in 1821 Bangkok sent him south against a rising in Kedah, and his army put it down.
zh:
那空是贪玛叻（外国商人称洛坤）位于马来半岛东岸，是暹罗南部的首城。它本是一座临海城池，泥沙淤积使海岸线退离城墙；他鲁哇遗址在城南十公里，出土过12世纪的宋朝瓷器。这里古称单马令，一名源自梵语「红林伽」，曾向中国宋朝朝贡；有铭文记载，早在775年，一位三佛齐国王已在此立足。1231年在位的室利昙摩索王建起玛哈泰寺，寺中供奉佛舍利的大塔是全城的标志，他又引入锡兰系上座部佛教；其王国下辖十二城，北起春蓬，南至彭亨。1292年的兰甘亨碑铭把此城列为素可泰最南端的属邦。该城在14世纪衰亡后，碧武里的一位王子将它重建，随后它转入阿瑜陀耶的势力范围。1444年，旧王朝仍在此统治，玛哈泰寺吸引着暹罗湾各地的香客，外国水手都把这座港口称作洛坤。

在阿瑜陀耶，洛坤位列南方诸城之首。戴莱洛迦纳王1468年的宫廷法把它列为王国八大都城之一，但总督之位仍在旧王朝内父子相传；与葡萄牙人和荷兰人贸易得来的财富，支撑着它长期的自立之心。1629年洛坤起兵反对巴萨通王，国王派山田长政南下去平叛。山田长政统领阿瑜陀耶的日本人町「日本村」，村中约有一千名商人、基督徒难民和浪人；他率这批雇佣兵镇压叛乱，一度统治洛坤，1630年死去。那莱王时代，法国工程师拉马尔在1680年代重修城墙；1688年暹罗革命后，洛坤再次反叛，四年后被讨平。

1767年阿瑜陀耶陷落后，副都督努据洛坤自立；郑信1769年将他击败，后来又恢复他臣属统治者的地位。拉玛一世1784年结束这种地位，把洛坤之主改为任命的总督，原属他的马来邦国（包括北大年）也转交宋卡。两年后，一支缅军洗劫了这座城。1811年起，洛坤总督为那空·诺依，英国人称之为「洛坤罗阇」；1821年，曼谷派他南下平定吉打的叛乱，他的军队将事态平息。

en:
Patani, successor to older Malay sea-realms such as Langkasuka, lies at a river mouth on the north-eastern coast of the Malay Peninsula opening on the Gulf of Siam, where Chinese junks and archipelago traders sheltered between the South China Sea and the Strait of Malacca. Local tradition credits the court's conversion to a sheikh from Pasai who cured the ruler of a skin disease; sources place it between the late fourteenth century and 1470, and in 1444 many river villages still kept the older rites. Pepper, timber, ivory and hides came down from the forested interior, rice from the coastal plain, and Pasai merchants and Chinese junks kept warehouses along the river. Patani stood within Ayutthaya's orbit, though the long road to the Siamese capital left the harbour largely its own.

After the Portuguese took Malacca in 1511, Muslim and Chinese merchants moved up the peninsula, and Patani became the busiest port on its eastern shore. Portuguese factors arrived in 1516 and a Portuguese fleet raided it in 1524; Japanese, Dutch and English warehouses followed. Chinese settlers included followers of the Teochew pirate Lin Daoqian, who made Patani his home and died here. Sultan Mudhaffar Shah marched on Ayutthaya in 1563 while Bayinnaung's Burmese armies pressed Siam, failed and died on the way home. Succession murders then killed off the royal men, and from 1584 four sisters ruled in turn: the Green, Blue, Purple and Yellow Rajas. The Green Queen's thirty-two years brought stability: she crushed her chief minister's rising and had a channel dug to water the town. The Blue Queen absorbed Kelantan; the Purple Queen stopped the tribute to Siam, dropped the Siamese royal title, allied herself with Johor and beat off a Siamese invasion in 1633–1634.

In 1688 Patani refused to recognise Ayutthaya's new ruler Phetracha, who sent fifty thousand men against it; decades of disorder drove the merchants away. When Ayutthaya fell to the Burmese in 1767 Patani broke free again, but in 1786 Prince Surasi, brother of King Rama I, stormed and destroyed the town and deported much of its people. Bangkok divided the remnant into seven small principalities under its own governors.
zh:
北大年是狼牙修等更古老的马来海洋政权的后继者，位于马来半岛东北岸，城在一个朝向暹罗湾的河口，中国帆船和群岛商人往返南海与马六甲海峡时多在此停泊。当地相传，宫廷改奉伊斯兰教，全靠一位来自巴赛的谢赫治好统治者的皮肤病；史家把皈依放在14世纪末到1470年之间的不同年份，1444年时许多河畔渔村还守着旧俗。胡椒、木材、象牙和皮革从丛林腹地顺流而下，沿海平原出产稻米，巴赛商人与中国商船在河边开有货栈。北大年名义上处在阿瑜陀耶的势力范围内，只是距暹罗都城路途遥远，港口基本由自己做主。

1511年葡萄牙人攻占马六甲后，穆斯林和中国商人北迁，北大年成了半岛东岸最繁忙的港口。葡萄牙商行1516年到此，1524年又有一支葡萄牙舰队袭掠此城；日本、荷兰、英国也在1600年前后相继开设商馆。华人居民中有潮州籍海盗林道乾的部众，林道乾后来定居并终老于北大年。1563年，苏丹穆扎法尔沙趁勃印曩的缅甸大军压境暹罗，出兵攻打阿瑜陀耶，未能破城，回师途中死去。此后继位仇杀使王族男丁断绝，1584年起四姐妹相继执政，即绿、蓝、紫、黄四位女王。绿女王在位三十二年，朝局安定，她平定宰相的叛乱，又下令开凿渠道引水入城。蓝女王把吉兰丹并入版图；紫女王停止向暹罗纳贡，弃用暹罗王号，与柔佛结盟，并在1633至1634年击退暹军入侵。

1688年，北大年拒绝承认阿瑜陀耶新王帕碧罗阇，阿瑜陀耶发兵五万来攻；此后乱了几十年，外商纷纷离去。1767年阿瑜陀耶被缅甸攻灭，北大年重获自由，但1786年拉玛一世之弟素拉西亲王率军攻陷并摧毁城市，掳走大批居民，曼谷把残余之地拆成七个由本国官吏管辖的小邦。

en:
The Perak River winds out of the tin-bearing highlands to a mangrove coast on the Strait of Malacca. Hindu-Buddhist chiefdoms had grown rich on the river trade before Islam, and by the fifteenth century the kingdom of Beruas held the lower valley; Muslim graves around the river ports mark merchants from Malacca and Sumatra who had settled there. The country had no ruler of its own, and its river chiefs held their titles from the Sultan of Malacca. In 1444 Perak tin and forest produce move south in Malaccan and Sumatran bottoms to Malacca's market.

After the Portuguese took Malacca in 1511, the dead sultan's son Muzaffar Shah lived quietly in Kampar on Sumatra, until Tun Saban, a trader-chief who ran the traffic between the Perak River and Klang, fetched him home; in 1528 he was installed as Perak's first sultan, and the Malacca royal line continued upriver. Tin drew predators. In 1573 an Acehnese army overran the country and carried the royal family off to Sumatra, where one captive prince married an Acehnese princess and himself became Sultan of Aceh; Perak nobles had to go to Aceh to bring his younger brother back as their ruler, and in 1620 Aceh struck again and carried off the reigning sultan. Dutch pressure then took Aceh's place. The Company blockaded the Perak River to force a contract, treaties in the 1650s gave it the tin monopoly, and from 1670 it kept a fortified warehouse on Pangkor Island, destroyed more than once and rebuilt. Forty years of civil war over tin revenues let Bugis war fleets make and unmake sultans, until in 1747 the hard-pressed ruler leased the monopoly afresh to the Dutch, who moved their factory to the Perak estuary. In 1776 the sultan brought Chinese miners in from Dutch Malacca to work the inland tin fields; the Anglo-Dutch war of 1780 wrecked the trade and many of them left. A poorer, feud-torn Perak entered the new century.
zh:
霹雳河从产锡的高地蜿蜒西行，穿过红树林海岸注入马六甲海峡。伊斯兰教传入之前，印度教与佛教小邦已凭河上贸易致富；到15世纪，下游谷地有木威王国，河口港口周围的穆斯林墓葬，是落户此地的马六甲和苏门答腊商人留下的。这片土地没有自己的君主，各河首领的头衔都由马六甲苏丹授予。1444年，霹雳的锡砂和林产品由马六甲、苏门答腊商船南运，进入马六甲的市集。

1511年葡萄牙攻占马六甲后，末代苏丹之子目扎法沙在苏门答腊的甘巴避居，直到经营霹雳河与巴生贸易的商人首领敦沙班把他接回，于1528年立为霹雳第一任苏丹，马六甲的王统便在霹雳河畔延续。锡矿引来了觊觎者：1573年亚齐军队攻破霹雳，把王室掳往苏门答腊；被掳的一位王子在亚齐娶了公主，自己当上了亚齐苏丹，霹雳贵族反倒要前往亚齐，迎回他的弟弟继位；1620年亚齐再度来犯，又俘走在位苏丹。此后荷兰人的压力取代亚齐成为大患：公司封锁霹雳河强订商约，1650年代的几项条约把锡矿专营权交给荷兰东印度公司，1670年起又在邦咯岛设了一座设防仓库，几度被毁、几度重修。为争夺锡矿收入，霹雳打了四十年内战，武吉斯战船在其中废立苏丹；1747年，处境窘迫的苏丹把专营权再度租给荷兰人，商站随之迁到霹雳河口。1776年，苏丹从荷属马六甲引入华工开采内陆锡砂，1780年英荷战争摧毁了这门生意，许多华工离去。进入新世纪的霹雳更为贫穷，纷争不断。

en:
Malacca lies on the west coast of the Malay Peninsula, on the eastern side of the Strait of Malacca, where ships sailing between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea often put in. Legend says that Parameswara, fleeing Singapura, rested under a Malacca tree at the river mouth and watched a mouse deer outwit his hunting dog and drive it into the water; he founded his city on the spot and named it after the tree. Ming China recognised the new port quickly: the Yongle Emperor sent envoys in 1405, Zheng He's fleets called repeatedly, and Parameswara sailed with Zheng He to visit the imperial court. Regular tribute bought Malacca Chinese protection against Siam. In 1444 it was the capital of a Sunni Malay sultanate, where Chinese, Indian, Arab and Persian merchants traded spices, tin, Indian cloth, and Chinese porcelain and silk, and four shahbandars each looked after a different group of foreign traders.

The sultanate's strongest half-century owed much to the bendahara Tun Perak. He helped beat back two Siamese invasions and served four sultans in turn, and in his time Malacca's power reached Pahang, Johor, Riau and the east coast of Sumatra, whose rulers adopted Islam. The Malay Annals add that Sultan Mansur Shah married Hang Li Po, a princess sent from Ming China, and gave her retinue the hill later called Bukit Cina, though no Ming record mentions her.

In 1511 Afonso de Albuquerque took Malacca for Portugal. Sultan Mahmud Shah fled south, and his descendants founded the sultanates of Johor and Perak. The treasure looted from the sultan's palace was loaded onto the flagship Flor de la Mar for the voyage to Portugal; in November that year she was wrecked in a storm off Sumatra and was never recovered. The Portuguese pulled down mosques and tombs and used the stone to build A Famosa around a hill by the sea. The apothecary Tomé Pires wrote the Suma Oriental while working at the royal factory here, a survey of the coasts and trade from the Red Sea to Japan, and the Jesuit Francis Xavier came three times. In 1641 the Dutch East India Company took the city with help from Johor, but the Dutch ran their trade from Batavia and the old port slowly declined. The British took over in 1795 and ordered the fortress demolished. The walls were almost all gone when Stamford Raffles, later the founder of Singapore, intervened, and the Porta de Santiago gate was saved.
zh:
马六甲位于马来半岛西岸、马六甲海峡东侧，往来印度洋和南海的商船多在这里停泊。相传拜里米苏拉逃离新加坡拉后，在河口一棵马六甲树下歇脚，看见一只鼷鹿智胜他的猎犬、把它逼进了水里，便在此建城，以树为名。明朝很快承认了这个新港：1405年永乐帝遣使来航，郑和船队此后多次停泊，拜里米苏拉还随郑和入朝；马六甲按时朝贡，换来明朝的庇护，用以对抗暹罗。1444年，这里是逊尼派马来苏丹国的都城，中国、印度、阿拉伯和波斯的商人在港中交易香料、锡、印度布匹和中国瓷器丝绸，四名沙班达分管不同来路的商团。

苏丹国最强盛的半个世纪，靠的是宰相敦·霹雳。暹罗两度来犯都被击退，他先后辅佐四位苏丹，其间马六甲的势力扩展到彭亨、柔佛、廖内和苏门答腊东岸，这些地方的统治者也随之改信伊斯兰教。《马来纪年》还记载，曼苏尔沙苏丹迎娶了明朝送来的公主汉丽宝，赐给她和随从居住的山丘就是后来的「中国山」；不过明朝史料里并没有这位公主。

1511年，阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克率葡萄牙舰队攻占马六甲，苏丹马哈茂德沙南逃，其后人另建柔佛和霹雳两个王朝。从苏丹宫中掠得的财宝装上旗舰「海之花号」运往葡萄牙，同年11月船在苏门答腊外海遇风暴沉没，再也没有找到。葡萄牙人拆了清真寺和陵墓，用石料在海边小山周围筑起法摩沙堡。药剂师托梅·皮列士在城中的王室商馆任职时写成《东方志》，记下了从红海到日本的海岸和商路；耶稣会士方济各·沙勿略也三次到访。1641年，荷兰东印度公司在柔佛协助下攻下马六甲，但荷兰人的重心在巴达维亚，这座老港渐渐冷落。英国人1795年接管后下令拆毁要塞，城墙几乎拆光，后来创建新加坡的莱佛士出面干预，圣地亚哥城门才保存下来。

en:
Johor fills the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, mangrove-fringed river mouths looking across a narrow strait to the Riau Islands. The Johor River opens a route deep inland; the Muar to its west joins the Penarikan, a short portage where traders dragged their boats across to the Pahang River and the South China Sea. These waters were home to the Orang Laut, whose sea patrols and loyalty helped the founders of Malacca build their sultanate around 1400. It became the sultanate's southern hinterland, sending jungle and sea produce up the strait for Chinese porcelain. In 1444 it is a quiet Sunni Malay dependency of Malacca, run by the port's chiefs with no court of its own.

After Malacca fell and the Portuguese destroyed Sultan Mahmud Shah's exile court on Bintan, his son Alauddin Riayat Shah II returned to the Johor River, founded the sultanate in 1528 and fortified Kota Batu, later Johor Lama, as his capital. Muslim merchants avoiding Portuguese Malacca brought it trade. Aceh sacked Kota Batu and carried Alauddin off to his death; when Sultan Ali Jalla forced shipping into his port and attacked Malacca, the Portuguese stormed the town in 1587. A Portuguese-Johor fleet later destroyed the Acehnese armada off Malacca. Johor joined the Dutch, and in 1641 the allies took Malacca, Bendahara Skudai leading the Johor army. The upriver court at Batu Sawar fell to Jambi in 1673; Johor fought on with Bugis help while Riau became one of the archipelago's richest pepper, tin and spice marts. In 1699 the murder of Sultan Mahmud II ended the old Malacca royal line and put the bendahara on the throne. The pretender Raja Kecil, claiming to be the murdered sultan's posthumous son, seized Johor in 1718; Bugis warriors drove him out four years later and he withdrew to Sumatra and founded the Siak sultanate. The Bugis underkings, the Yam Tuan Muda, then ran Johor until the Dutch expelled them from Riau. Mahmud Shah III's death set off a succession dispute: the Dutch backed Abdul Rahman, while in 1819 Stamford Raffles recognised the elder Hussein and obtained Singapore from the Temenggong. In 1821 the Johor mainland stands under the Temenggong's house, the islands within the Dutch orbit.
zh:
柔佛位于马来半岛最南端，红树林夹岸的河口隔着一道窄海峡与廖内群岛相望。柔佛河可上溯内陆深处，西边的麻河上游衔接「佩纳里坎」短途拖船陆运，商旅把小船拖过地峡，即可进入彭亨河，驶往南海。这片水域本是海人的家园，凭借他们的巡弋与效忠，马六甲的开国者才在1400年前后建起苏丹国。柔佛成为该苏丹国的南方腹地，丛林与海产沿海峡北运，换回中国瓷器。1444年的柔佛是马六甲治下安静的逊尼派马来人属地，由港城的酋长治理，尚无自己的宫廷。

马六甲陷落后，葡萄牙人又摧毁苏丹马末沙在民丹的流亡朝廷，其子阿拉乌丁·里阿亚特沙二世回到柔佛河，于1528年建立柔佛苏丹国，在哥打峇株（即后来的旧柔佛）筑城设都。回避葡属马六甲的穆斯林商人给新港带来了生意。亚齐洗劫哥打峇株，把阿拉乌丁掳走处死；阿里·贾拉苏丹强令商船驶入自己的河港、又出兵攻打马六甲，葡萄牙人遂于1587年攻陷该城。后来葡萄牙和柔佛联军又在马六甲外海摧毁亚齐大舰队。柔佛随后与荷兰联手，1641年联军攻下马六甲，柔佛军由班达哈拉·斯库代率领。柔佛河上游的巴都沙哇朝廷于1673年被占碑攻陷，柔佛靠武吉斯援兵继续作战，廖内则发展成群岛上最富庶的胡椒、锡与香料商埠之一。1699年马哈茂德二世遇刺，马六甲一系绝嗣，班达哈拉登上王位。僭位者拉惹·克奇尔自称是遇害苏丹的遗腹子，1718年攻占柔佛；武吉斯武士四年后把他赶走，他退到苏门答腊建立锡亚克苏丹国。武吉斯副王「杨端·慕达」此后把持柔佛朝政，直到被荷兰人逐出廖内。马哈茂德沙三世一死又引发继承之争：荷兰支持阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼，莱佛士则在1819年承认长兄侯赛因，从天猛公手中取得新加坡。1821年，柔佛本土处在天猛公家族治下，群岛落入荷兰势力范围。

en:
Pahang fills the wide basin of its namesake river, which opens on the South China Sea at Pekan, the old Inderapura. Its rivers carried gold: the washings had been worked since the early centuries of the Common Era, and in the fourteenth century its maharaja ruled the southern peninsula as far as Temasek; Chinese annals knew the country as Pohuang and record its embassies of 449 and 456. It later became one of the twelve vassal cities of Ligor, itself under Siam. In 1444 Maharaja Dewa Sura, its last native ruler, still reigns at Pekan and sends tribute to Siam unwillingly, while Malacca gathers strength on the opposite coast.

In 1454 a Malaccan fleet of two hundred ships under the bendahara Tun Perak conquered Pahang and carried Dewa Sura and his daughter to Malacca; she married Raja Abdullah, the sultan's son, and bore Raja Muhammad. That prince came back in disgrace. When he was about fifteen, a mis-hit ball in a sepak raga game knocked off his headdress, and in a rage he drew his kris and killed Tun Besar, the bendahara's son; the bendahara's kin swore Muhammad should never rule them, and Sultan Mansur Shah exiled him to his grandfather's old seat. Around 1470 he was installed at Tanjung Langgar in Pekan as Sultan Muhammad Shah, with a bendahara of his own and a hundred noble youths and maidens, and Pahang grew into a rival of Malacca before the Portuguese took the mother city in 1511. Its gold kept moving west: Pahang ships joined Johor's siege of Portuguese Malacca in 1551, and under Sultan Abdul Kadir the gold sold in quantity in the city's market; in 1586 he sent its governor a block of gold-bearing quartz.

The Dutch courted Pahang in their turn: in 1607 Admiral Matelief de Jonge anchored at Kuala Pahang to build an alliance against Portugal, and left with a promise of two thousand men. Aceh was the sharper danger, and Sultan Iskandar Muda's armies overran the country in 1615 and again in 1617. In 1623 the Pahang ruler inherited Johor and the two crowns joined; thereafter Pahang was governed by Johor's bendaharas, until Tun Abdul Majid made it an autonomous kingdom in 1770.
zh:
彭亨地处同名大河的广阔流域，河口的北根古称因陀罗补罗，面向南海。这里的河川出黄金：早在公元初几百年，河畔就有人淘金；14世纪时，彭亨摩诃罗阇的势力南下直至淡马锡。中国史书称这里为「婆皇」，记下了它449年和456年的遣使。后来彭亨成为洛坤的十二属邦之一，而洛坤本身臣服于暹罗。1444年，末代本土君主摩诃罗阇·提婆素罗仍在北根在位，被迫向暹罗纳贡，半岛另一海岸的马六甲则正在崛起。

1454年，宰相敦霹雳率两百艘战船的马六甲舰队征服彭亨，把提婆素罗和他的女儿掳回马六甲；公主嫁给王子拉惹·阿卜杜拉，生下拉惹·穆罕默德。这位王子后来以戴罪之身回到外祖父的王国：他十五岁上下时，在一场藤球游戏中被踢偏的球打落头巾，一怒之下拔剑杀了宰相之子敦贝萨尔，宰相族人立誓不奉他为主，曼苏尔沙苏丹便把他放逐到彭亨。约1470年，他在北根的丹绒朗加即位，称苏丹穆罕默德沙，随行的有专为他任命的宰相和百名贵族男女；彭亨日渐强盛，到1511年葡萄牙攻占马六甲时，已足以与旧主争雄。彭亨的黄金继续西运：1551年彭亨战船参加柔佛围攻葡属马六甲之役，阿卜杜勒·卡迪尔苏丹在位时，黄金在马六甲市集大量出售，1586年他还把一块含金石英送给马六甲总督。

1607年荷兰人前来结盟，海军上将马特列夫停泊瓜拉彭亨，共图葡萄牙，带走了彭亨出兵两千的许诺。亚齐才是更凶险的敌人：苏丹伊斯坎达尔·穆达的大军于1615年和1617年两度攻陷彭亨。1623年彭亨君主继承柔佛王位，两顶王冠合而为一；此后彭亨由柔佛的宰相世代治理，1770年敦阿都·马吉德将它建为自治王国。

en:
Kelantan occupies the north-eastern corner of the Malay Peninsula, a broad plain of rice fields around the Kelantan River delta on the South China Sea. The Titiwangsa mountains cut it off from the west coast, so its fishing villages and river ports looked out to sea, and Chinese junks anchored off the river mouth to trade. Chinese records place in this region a mission of 607 to the Sui court from a kingdom called Chih Tu; later tributary lists assign the coast in turn to Srivijaya and, in 1365, to Majapahit. Around 1411 its Muslim ruler, Raja Kumar, asserted independence from Siam and sent an embassy to the Ming court, and the Malay Annals describe Kelantan in those years as a kingdom strong enough to rival Patani. In 1444 its own rajas still ruled from the estuary, a Muslim state on the fringe of the Siamese world.

Malacca conquered Kelantan in the reign of Sultan Mansur Shah, and from 1499 it was a Malaccan vassal. When the Portuguese took Malacca in 1511 the country broke into chiefdoms, most of them tributary to Patani. Kelantan turned on its neighbour in the next century: in 1651 its ruler Raja Sakti I deposed Patani's last queen and put his own son on her throne. Tradition sets in these years the rule of Cik Siti Wan Kembang, Kelantan's warrior queen, the heroine of local hikayat; on her abdication the throne passed to her adopted daughter Puteri Saadong, heiress of the small kingdom of Jembal, and the two lands were joined. Around 1760 Long Yunus, an aristocratic warlord of Patani origin, reunified Kelantan and was enthroned through his father-in-law, Ku Tanang Wangsa, the Regent of Terengganu. Terengganu tried in 1795 to install Long Yunus's son-in-law as ruler; his eldest son Long Muhammad fought the war, won in 1800 and ruled as Sultan Muhammad I. By 1812 Kelantan dealt with Bangkok as a tributary of Siam in its own right.
zh:
吉兰丹地处马来半岛东北角，吉兰丹河三角洲是一片广阔的稻田，面朝南海。蒂迪旺沙山脉把它与西海岸隔开，沿海渔村和河港多面向大海，中国帆船常在河口外停泊贸易。中国史籍记载，607年此地有赤土国遣使隋朝；后世的属国名录中，这片海岸先后被系于室利佛逝，1365年又被列入满者伯夷名下。约1411年，穆斯林君主拉惹·库马尔摆脱暹罗统治，遣使明朝；《马来纪年》称这一时期的吉兰丹国力足以与北大年匹敌。1444年，本地罗阇仍在河口实施统治，这是暹罗世界边缘的一个穆斯林国家。

满速沙苏丹在位时吉兰丹被马六甲征服，1499年起成为马六甲属邦。1511年葡萄牙人攻占马六甲后，吉兰丹分裂为众多酋长领地，大多向北大年纳贡。进入17世纪，吉兰丹反客为主：1651年君主罗阇·萨克蒂一世废黜北大年末代女王，把自己的儿子扶上她的王位。相传吉兰丹的巾帼君主西蒂·旺·肯邦正是在这些年间临朝，她是本地民间故事里最有名的女王；她退位后，王位传给养女、小国珍巴的继承人普特里·萨东，珍巴与吉兰丹合为一体。约1760年，有北大年血统的贵族军阀隆·尤努斯重新统一吉兰丹，由其岳父、丁加奴摄政古达南·旺萨扶立登基。1795年丁加奴试图改立隆·尤努斯的女婿，长子隆·莫哈末迎战，1800年获胜，即位为苏丹莫哈末一世。到1812年，吉兰丹已不再经由丁加奴，而是单独向暹罗称臣纳贡，与曼谷直接往来。

en:
Ayutthaya stands on an island in the lower Chao Phraya plain, girdled by the Chao Phraya, Lopburi and Pa Sak rivers, where the northern river trade meets the sea lanes of the Gulf of Siam. In 1351 King Ramathibodi I, Uthong, raised his capital on the older port of Ayodhya, uniting Lavo and Suphannaphum and naming the city for Ayodhya of the Ramayana. Sixty missions went to Ming China between 1369 and 1429, more than from any other Southeast Asian court, and Ryukyu junks and Persians who called the place Shahr-i Naw moored below the walls. In 1444, under Borommarachathirat II, the walled island was one of the great emporia of Southeast Asia, its riverfront crowded with Chinese, Malay and Indian shipping.

From 1448 King Borommatrailokkanat turned the old palace into Wat Phra Si Sanphet, where three chedis later held royal ashes and Ramathibodi II raised a sixteen-metre gilded bronze Buddha. The Portuguese reached the city in 1511 and signed a trade treaty five years later. Burma remained the city's great danger: Bayinnaung stormed it in 1569 and his garrisons held it until Naresuan renounced Burmese rule in 1584 and killed the Burmese crown prince Mingyi Swa in an elephant fight in 1593.

Peace brought sixty-one markets inside the walls; beside the Dutch and Chinese factories stood Ban Yipun, a Japanese quarter of a thousand traders and rōnin led by Yamada Nagamasa. Under King Narai the Greek adventurer Phaulkon ran foreign affairs and French troops garrisoned Bangkok, until Phetracha's coup of 1688 killed Phaulkon and expelled the French. The Burmese failed to take the city in 1760, returned in 1766 and ringed it with twenty-seven forts. After a fourteen-month siege they dug tunnels under the ramparts and fired the timber props; the northeast wall collapsed and Ayutthaya fell on 7 April 1767. Palaces and temples burned, the gold was stripped from the great Buddha images, and 30,000 craftsmen and courtiers were marched off to Burma. Taksin retook the ruins the same year but built downstream at Thonburi, leaving the island a provincial town among its foundations.
zh:
阿瑜陀耶位于昭披耶河下游平原的一座江心岛上，昭披耶河、华富里河与巴萨克河绕城而流，北方内河商路在此接暹罗湾的海道。1351年，乌通王拉玛铁菩提一世在旧港阿约陀雅上营建都城，合并罗涡与素攀那蓬两大城邦，并以《罗摩衍那》中的圣城阿约陀雅为新都命名。1369至1429年间派出赴明朝贡使团六十个，多于东南亚其他任何一国，把这里称作「新城」（Shahr-i Naw）的波斯商人和琉球戎克船都在城下停泊。1444年波隆摩罗阇二世在位时，这座环水的城墙之城是东南亚有数的大商埠，河畔挤满华人、马来人和印度人的商船。

1448年继位的波隆摩戴莱洛迦纳把旧王宫改为帕喜善佩寺，寺中三座佛塔后来安放王室骨灰，拉玛铁菩提二世时又铸成一尊高十六米的鎏金铜佛。葡萄牙人1511年来航，五年后签订通商条约。缅甸始终是此城大患：勃印曩1569年攻陷阿瑜陀耶，缅军驻守到纳黎萱1584年宣布脱离缅甸，他又在1593年的象战中斩杀缅甸王储敏基苏瓦。

承平年月，城内有六十一处市集开市。荷兰与华人商馆旁是日本人町，约千名商人流亡浪人居于此，由山田长政统领。那莱王在位时，希腊冒险家华尔康主持外交，法军进驻曼谷；1688年帕碧罗阇发动政变，诛杀华尔康、驱逐法人。缅军1760年攻城不克，1766年再度来犯，以二十七座营垒合围。围城十四个月后，缅军在城墙下挖掘地道、焚烧支撑的木柱，东北角城墙坍塌，阿瑜陀耶于1767年4月7日陷落。宫殿寺院被焚，大佛像上的金箔遭熔取，三万名工匠与王室成员被掳往缅甸。郑信同年收复残城，却把都城建在下游的吞武里，这座江心老城便成了废墟之间的省城。

en:
Sukhothai, the 'dawn of happiness', lies on the Yom river in the north-central plain, the first city ruled by a Thai king. In 1238 local Tai chiefs drove out its Khmer governor and founded here the Phra Ruang dynasty. Under Ram Khamhaeng the Great, who reigned from 1279 to 1298, Theravada Buddhism and the Thai script of 1283 took root, and embassies to Yuan China brought back the craft of glazed stoneware. Upriver at Si Satchanalai the kilns of Chaliang grew until more than a hundred fired at once, and their sangkhalok celadon sailed to ports across Southeast Asia; inside Sukhothai's own walls stood twenty-six temples, the largest Wat Mahathat with its tall lotus-bud chedi. After Ram Khamhaeng the kingdom shrank, and when its last king Borommapan died in 1438 it was fully joined to Ayutthaya. In 1444 the old royal city is a northern march of Borommarachathirat II, its shrines crowded with Buddha images and the Yom still busy with pottery boats.

The city rose against Ayutthaya in 1462, and King Borommatrailokkanat answered by moving his whole court to Phitsanulok in 1463, from where he ran his long wars with Tilokkarat of Lan Na for Chaliang and the upper Yom. Sawankhalok became one of Ayutthaya's six second-class provinces, and the kilns kept exporting until 1584, when Naresuan carried off the populations of the northern towns to clear the ground before a Burmese invasion; the old cities sat half empty and the ceramic trade died, reviving only partly after an officer was posted to hold Sawankhalok in 1592. In 1765 the Burmese northern army under Nemyo Thihapate swept through the valley on its march to Ayutthaya, which fell in April 1767. Taksin's forces retook the region after the war, and in 1793 Rama I founded New Sukhothai twelve kilometres east of the walled city and left the old capital to the trees; in 1801 the eight-metre bronze Buddha of Wat Mahathat was taken to Bangkok and installed as the principal image of Wat Suthat. By 1821 the province answered to Bangkok and the old capital survived only in its ruins.
zh:
素可泰意为「幸福的曙光」，位于中北部平原的永河畔，是泰人国王统治的第一座都城。1238年，本地泰人首领驱逐高棉太守，在此建立帕銮王朝。兰甘亨大帝1279至1298年在位时，上座部佛教与1283年创制的泰文在此扎根，出使元朝的使团带回了施釉瓷器的工艺。上游西萨查那莱的查良窑场多时上百座窑同时生火，宋加洛青瓷随船远销东南亚各港；素可泰城内有二十六座寺院，最大的玛哈泰寺矗立着高高的莲苞佛塔。兰甘亨之后王国日蹙，1438年末代国王波罗蒙潘去世，素可泰被完全并入阿瑜陀耶。1444年的旧王城是波隆摩罗阇二世治下的北方边镇，寺院里佛像林立，永河上运瓷的船只往来不绝。

1462年此城起兵反抗阿瑜陀耶，波隆摩戴莱洛迦纳随即在1463年把整个朝廷迁往彭世洛，在那里指挥与兰纳国王蒂洛卡拉争夺查良和永河上游的长期战事。宋加洛列为阿瑜陀耶六个二等府之一，窑场继续外销瓷器，直到1584年纳黎萱为在缅甸入侵前清空北境，迁走北方诸城的人口；旧城大半空置，瓷业随之断绝，1592年派兵驻守宋加洛后才略有恢复。1765年，内苗·西哈波底率领的缅甸北路大军横扫谷地，长驱直扑阿瑜陀耶，该城于1767年4月陷落。郑信在战后收复这一带；1793年拉玛一世在砖城以东十二公里建素可泰新城，听任旧城荒芜；1801年玛哈泰寺那尊八米高的铜佛被运往曼谷，成为苏泰寺（Wat Suthat）的主佛。1821年时，这片土地作为一个府听命于曼谷，旧都只剩残垣。

en:
Chiang Rai holds the rice lands of the Kok River in upper Lan Na, where the road north from Chiang Mai runs on toward the older mueang of Chiang Saen and Kengtung. Mangrai united the mueangs of Ngoenyang and founded the city in 1262, ruling from it as his first capital until he moved south to build Chiang Mai in 1296. Above the city, the Doi Tung stupa had held a Buddha collarbone relic since about the tenth century, and northern pilgrims climbed the mountain to honour it. In 1432, in the reign of Sam Fang Kaen, an earthquake split the chedi of Wat Phra Kaeo and opened a stucco image to reveal a jade Buddha inside: the Emerald Buddha, later the palladium of the kings of Siam, had come to light. In 1444 Chiang Rai was a Mangrai-dynasty city of a still-powerful Lan Na, three years into the reign of Tilokaraj.

The image did not stay. The elephant sent to carry it to Chiang Mai turned three times toward Lampang, so it remained there for thirty-two years until Tilokaraj brought it to Chedi Luang in 1468; Setthathirat took it to Luang Prabang in 1552 and then to Vientiane, from where a Siamese army carried it off in 1779 to Bangkok. By then Chiang Rai had long passed between empires: Bayinnaung's Toungoo forces made Lan Na a Burmese vassal in 1558, and local kings kept real autonomy until heavy Toungoo taxation touched off the Chiang Mai revolts of 1727-1728 and 1731-1732, which freed the Ping valley for a generation. In January 1775 Kawila of Lampang and Siamese troops took Chiang Mai, and after the war of 1775-1776 the Burmese withdrew and Chiang Rai entered Siam's northern tributary order.
sources: https://th.wikipedia.org/wiki/จังหวัดเชียงราย
https://th.wikipedia.org/wiki/อาณาจักรล้านนา
zh:
清莱据有兰纳北部廓克河流域的稻米之地，清迈北上的道路从这里继续通往更古老的清盛、景栋诸勐。孟莱统一恩央诸城后于1262年建立清莱，并以此为最初都城，直到1296年南下另建清迈。城郊敦山（Doi Tung）上的佛塔安奉佛锁骨舍利，按泰北编年史约建于10世纪，北方信徒登山朝礼。1432年，一场地震震裂玉佛寺的佛塔，一尊灰泥佛像裂开，露出其中的碧玉佛像——这就是后来成为暹罗王室护国宝的玉佛。1444年，滴洛拉阇即位第三年，清莱仍是强盛兰纳境内的孟莱王朝王城。

玉佛并没有留在清莱。奉命把它送往清迈的大象三次改道南邦，时人视为神意，玉佛便在南邦供奉了32年，1468年滴洛拉阇才把它迎到清迈契迪龙寺；1552年赛塔提拉将它带往琅勃拉邦，后来又移至万象，1779年暹罗军队攻破万象，把玉佛带回曼谷。那时清莱自己也早已在大国之间易手：1558年勃印曩的东吁大军使兰纳成为缅甸属邦，当地国王长期保留实权，直到东吁重税激起1727-1728年和1731-1732年的清迈起义，宾河流域获得一代人的自主。1775年1月，南邦的咖威拉联合暹罗军队攻占清迈；1775-1776年战争后缅军撤走，清莱进入暹罗的北方藩属秩序。

en:
At the easternmost corner of the Gulf of Siam the Cardamom Mountains run down to the sea, forested ridges giving way to fishing harbours and a scatter of islands; the largest of them, Ko Chang, is the third biggest island in the country. The Ayutthaya court knew this remote eastern seaboard as Mueang Thung Yai, 'the great field town', an old name for Trat. Its gem-bearing hills were already famous when the Chinese voyager Ma Huan noted the rubies and sapphires of the Chanthaburi–Trat country in 1408. In 1444 it was a lightly held fringe of Ayutthaya's eastern maritime provinces, a string of small ports floating forest goods down to the capital.

Trat became a customs seaport in the reign of King Prasat Thong (1629–1656), when it was placed under the Phra Khlang, the treasury department: hides and deer antlers, aromatic woods and spices came down the Khao Saming River from the eastern hills to the Chinese junks waiting at the river mouth. In mid-1767, after Taksin broke out of the Burmese siege of Ayutthaya and took Chanthaburi in a night assault, he sailed on to Trat. The town submitted without a fight, but the Chinese junks at anchor opened fire, and his war-boats took half a day to seize them all. The Burmese armies had never reached this coast, so Trat and Chanthaburi escaped the ruin of the rest of the kingdom and became Taksin's base for men and ships; with the junks' cargoes paying and arming his troops, he sailed for the Chao Phraya that November with 5,000 men and 100 ships and reconquered Siam.
sources: https://th.wikipedia.org/wiki/จังหวัดตราด
zh:
在暹罗湾最东端，豆蔻山余脉直逼海岸，林莽覆盖的丘陵尽头是渔村港湾和一连串岛屿，最大的象岛是全国第三大岛。阿瑜陀耶朝廷把这片偏远的东部滨海之地称作童艾城，意为「大田之城」，即桐艾（又译达叻）的旧称；内地丘陵出产宝石，中国航海家马欢1408年就记下了尖竹汶—桐艾一带的红宝石与蓝宝石。1444年，这里是阿瑜陀耶东部沿海诸府控制较松的边缘，一串小港把山货漂运到京城。

桐艾成为正式税港是在巴沙通王（1629—1656年在位）时期，归财政衙门（Phra Khlang）管辖：东部山区的兽皮、鹿角、香木和香料沿考萨明河而下，在河口换上等候的中国帆船。1767年年中，郑信从缅甸军围困中的阿瑜陀耶突围、夜袭尖竹汶得手后挥师桐艾，城中不战而降，泊在港里的中国帆船却开炮抗拒，他的战船打了半天才将其全数缴获。缅甸军队从未打到这片海岸，桐艾和尖竹汶因而躲过了王国其他地方遭受的残破，成了郑信募兵造船的基地；船上财货充当军饷军械，这年11月他率五千之众、百艘战船驶向湄南河，重新夺回暹罗。

en:
Oudong is named after Phnom Oudong, a long sandstone ridge in the alluvial plain northwest of Chaktomuk, where the Mekong meets the Tonlé Sap; its name goes back to a Sanskrit word for 'lofty'. After Ayutthayan troops sacked Angkor in 1431, King Ponhea Yat carried his court south to Chaktomuk, the future Phnom Penh, while the ridge stayed royal ground of monasteries and rice fields. In 1444 it belonged to a Theravada Buddhist Khmer kingdom whose kings held river crossings rather than temple cities and kept a wary eye on Siam.

Ang Chan I moved his court in 1529 to Lovek, a fortified town just north of the ridge where Chinese, Malay and Portuguese traders did business and the Spanish adventurers Blas Ruiz and Diogo Veloso sat at the court of King Satha; European visitors called the city simply 'Cambodia'. King Naresuan of Siam stormed Lovek in 1593. King Srei Soryapor laid out a new royal town on the slopes of Phnom Oudong in 1601, and from 1618 Oudong Meanchey served as the capital for two and a half centuries, its crest filling with the burial stupas of Khmer kings.

The court at Oudong knew the oddest reign of the dynasty. Ramathipadi I seized the throne with Malay support in 1642, took the name Sultan Ibrahim, and became the only Cambodian king to convert to Islam. His Malay followers killed the Dutch East India Company's residents in 1643, and a Company fleet sent up the Mekong to punish him was defeated the next year, with 156 of its 432 soldiers dead, its ambassador killed and several ships taken. Siam came to decide the Cambodian succession. King Taksin marched on Oudong in 1771 after sacking Hà Tiên, the Siamese-backed prince Ang Non seized the throne in 1775, and in 1811–1813 a Vietnamese army under Lê Văn Duyệt retook the town and restored King Ang Chan II. In 1821 Oudong was still the royal capital, and its king ruled under Vietnamese protection.
zh:
乌栋得名于乌栋山——一道横亘在四臂湾西北冲积平原上的砂岩长岭，四臂湾即湄公河与洞里萨河交汇处，山名则来自梵语，意为「高峻」。1431年阿瑜陀耶军队攻陷吴哥后，国王奔哈·亚率宫廷南迁四臂湾（后来的金边），乌栋山仍是王畿旧地，遍布寺院与稻田。1444年，这里属上座部佛教的高棉王国：国王们凭河津要冲而非石庙王城维系统治，对西邻的暹罗戒心重重。

1529年，安赞一世把宫廷迁到岭北设防的洛韦。中国、马来和葡萄牙商人在此通商，西班牙冒险者布拉斯·鲁伊斯和迪奥戈·维洛佐曾出入萨塔王的宫廷，欧洲访客干脆把这座城叫作「柬埔寨」。1593年，暹罗国王纳黎萱攻破洛韦。1601年，国王斯雷·索里约波在乌栋山南麓另建王城，1618年起「乌栋梦谢」成为高棉都城，历时两个半世纪，山脊上渐渐立满历代国王的舍利塔。

乌栋的宫廷还出过王朝里最奇特的君主。1642年，博涅赞在马来商人支持下夺位，改名苏丹易卜拉欣，是柬埔寨唯一改宗伊斯兰教的国王。1643年，他的马来部下袭杀荷兰东印度公司的商馆人员；公司舰队溯湄公河前来问罪，次年被击败，432名士兵折损156人，大使战死，数艘战船被俘。此后暹罗屡屡左右高棉的王位：1771年达信洗劫河仙后进兵乌栋，受暹罗支持的安农于1775年夺位；1811至1813年，黎文悦率越南军队收复乌栋，扶安赞二世复位。1821年的乌栋仍是王都，国王却在越南的保护下治国。

en:
Prey Nokor, 'the forest kingdom' in Khmer, was the thinly settled eastern fringe of the Cambodian delta, a country of fishing hamlets and heavy timber along the lower Saigon River. Khmer fishermen worked its creeks, Cham refugees and the Châu Ro and S'Tiêng hill peoples lived among them, and Chinese and Vietnamese junks already used the river road from the sea toward the Mekong. Zhou Daguan, sent to Angkor by the Yuan court in the 1290s, noted a riverside district he called Trĩ Côn, usually read as the earliest trace of the name Sài Gòn. In 1444 all of it still belonged to the Cambodian king at Phnom Penh, whose officers rarely came so far downstream.

The delta entered Vietnamese history through a marriage: after King Chey Chettha II wedded the Nguyễn princess Nguyễn Phúc Ngọc Vạn of Huế, her kinsmen the Nguyễn lords were allowed in 1623 to post tax collectors at Prey Nokor. Settlers drifted down through the long Trịnh–Nguyễn wars, and in 1679 the Nguyễn planted on these waterways a whole Ming loyalist fleet fleeing the Qing; the port the refugees opened at Cù Lao Phố grew into one of the busiest markets of the lower Mekong. In 1698 the general Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh came to organise the frontier: he founded Gia Định prefecture with the counties of Tân Bình and Phước Long and registered some ten thousand households, perhaps 200,000 settlers, and a Cambodian attempt to dislodge him failed. During the Tây Sơn wars the place became the seat of Nguyễn Ánh, and in 1790 his French officers Théodore Lebrun and Victor Olivier de Puymanel built the Bát Quái citadel, an eight-sided fortress laid out in the Vauban manner; the Tây Sơn never attacked the south again. After Nguyễn Ánh was crowned the emperor Gia Long in 1802, Gia Định governed Vietnam's five southern provinces, while at the Chinese rice town of Chợ Lớn beside it, delta grain was loaded onto junks sailing up the coast.
zh:
波雷诺哥在高棉语中意为「林中之国」，本是柬埔寨三角洲东部人烟稀疏的边地，西贡河下游一带渔村与密林相间。高棉人在河汊捕鱼，村寨之间杂居着占婆流民和遮罗、斯丁等山地部族；中国和越南的商船早已取道这条河，从海口深入湄公河。1290年代元朝遣使真腊的周达观，在《真腊风土记》里记下一个河滨属郡「雉棍」，学者多认为这是「柴棍」一名最早的痕迹。1444年，这片土地仍属金边的柬埔寨国王，只是王室官吏很少走到这么靠下游的地方。

这片三角洲是通过一桩婚姻进入越南历史的：柬埔寨国王吉·哲塔二世娶了顺化阮氏的公主阮氏玉万，1623年，她的母家阮主获准在波雷诺哥设关征税。郑阮长期纷争，越南流民不断南下；1679年，阮主把一支逃避清朝的南明遗民船队整个安置在这一带水道，遗民开辟的浦岛港后来成为下湄公河最繁忙的商埠之一。1698年，大将阮有镜奉命经略边地，置嘉定府及新平、福隆两县，新编户籍约一万户、二十万口，柬埔寨出兵驱逐也告失败。西山战争中，柴棍成为阮福映的驻地；1790年，他手下的法国军官西奥多·勒布朗和奥利维耶·德·皮曼纽尔修筑了八卦城，这是一座按沃邦样式布置的八边形要塞，此后西山军再没有南犯。1802年阮福映称帝、建元嘉隆，嘉定统辖越南南方五镇；城旁华人米市堤岸，把三角洲的稻米装上沿海北上的商船。

en:
Panduranga was the southernmost of the Cham lands and the one its own kings held longest, with its centre at Pan Rang on the dry coast south of the Central Highlands. Above Pan Rang stands Po Klong Garai, three brick towers of the Thap Mam style raised by King Chế Mân (Jaya Simhavarman III) at the end of the thirteenth century over the shrine of a like-named Panduranga king; legend makes that king a cowherd who beat a Khmer invasion in a tower-building contest, and the mukhalinga within is venerated as him. Its own kings ruled with only loose obedience to Vijaya. In 1444, while Maha Vijaya's war with Đại Việt raged around Hóa Châu far to the north, its court sat at Biuh Bal Batsinâng and its people lived by fish, salt and the southern sea roads.

When Vijaya fell in March 1471, the Cham general Bố Trì Trì fled to Pan Rang and submitted, and was enfeoffed with the rump of Champa: Panduranga, Kauthara and the highland vassals. Trade revived in the next century, when Cham ships sailed to Siam, the Malay ports and Macao; in 1594 a Cham fleet helped Johor fight the Portuguese at Malacca. Its best-known king is Po Rome (r. 1627–1651), a Churu highlander who had passed several years in Kelantan and held the Muslim title Sultan Abdul Hamid Shah. He reconciled the Muslim Bani with the Hindu Balamon, dug dams and canals in the Phan Rang basin, settled the sakawi calendar, married a daughter of the Nguyễn lord and opened the country to Dutch trade; Cham legend adds that the princess tricked him into felling the sacred ironwood that guarded Champa. He was killed fighting in Phú Yên in 1651, and the Po Rome tower at Ninh Phước is where the Cham worship him.

Phú Yên had already fallen to the Nguyễn in 1611. In 1692 Po Saut attacked Diên Ninh prefecture; Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh captured him the next spring and turned the kingdom into Thuận Thành prefecture. A Cham rising under A Ban retook Phan Rang and Phan Rí that winter, and the Nguyễn restored the vassal throne, fixing its rights in the five-article treaty of 1712. In the Tây Sơn wars the rebels enthroned Po Tisuntiraidapuran in 1780; Nguyễn Ánh took Pan Rang and put him to death in 1793, and later Cham revolts were crushed. With the Nguyễn reunification of 1802, Thuận Thành kept its autonomy, ranked with Laos and Cambodia as the last Cham land ruled by its own kings.
zh:
宾童龙是占婆诸邦中地处最南、由本地君王统治最久的一地，中心在中央高地以南干旱海滨的潘郎。城北高地上立着波克朗加莱塔：这是一组塔布曼风格的砖塔，共三座，主塔高三层，占婆王制旻（阇耶·僧伽跋摩三世）在13世纪末建于同名的宾童龙王之祠上；相传这位国王本是牧童，靠一场造塔比赛退走了来犯的高棉人，神祠中的带人面林伽（mukhalinga）被占人当作国王本人奉祀。宾童龙的本地王世袭统治，只对阇盘松散称臣。1444年，摩诃贲该与大越在北方遥远的化州鏖战时，宾童龙仍在比乌巴尔巴西囊（Biuh Bal Batsinâng）设有朝廷，百姓以渔盐和南海商路为生。

1471年3月黎圣宗攻陷阇盘后，占将逋持持南奔潘郎称臣，受封统治只剩宾童龙、古笪罗和西原诸藩的占婆余土。此后一个世纪海运复兴，占船重新往来暹罗、马来诸港和澳门，1594年还派出舰队助柔佛攻打葡据马六甲。宾童龙最有名的王是波·罗姆（1627—1651年在位）：他本是朱鲁（Churu）山地人，曾在吉兰丹居留多年，取了苏丹阿卜杜勒·哈米德·沙的穆斯林名号。他让穆斯林巴尼派与印度教巴蒙派和解，在潘郎盆地修筑堤坝渠堰，厘定萨卡维历，娶阮主之女，又准许荷兰人通商；占人传说还讲，这位阮氏公主设计使他砍倒了护佑占婆的神铁木。1651年他在富安的战事中被杀，后人在宁福建起波·罗姆塔，占人在那里祭祀他。

阮主早在1611年就已夺取富安。1692年婆争王攻打延庆府，招来了亡国之师：阮有镜次年春将他俘获，把占婆改为顺城镇。当年冬季阿班领导的占人起义收复潘郎、潘里，阮主只得恢复占人王统、列为藩封，并在1712年以五条之约确认其权利。西山战事随后把这片土地变成战场：西山军1780年扶立阮文佐，阮福映攻取潘郎后于1793年将他处死，后来的占人起事也都被镇压。1802年阮朝统一，顺城仍保自治，与哀牢、高蛮同列藩封，是占人最后一个由本族君王统治的地方。

en:
Vijaya, called Đồ Bàn by the Vietnamese, was the brick-walled royal citadel of Champa on a tributary of the Côn River, a short march from its seaport Thị Nại on the bay of Quy Nhơn.
