After France ceded its lands east of the Mississippi in 1763, many Peoria withdrew west of the river. Americans built Fort Clark at Peoria Lake in September 1813, and the 1818 Treaty of Edwardsville ceded Peoria lands in Illinois to the United States.
zh:
佩瓦雷瓦是伊利诺伊河中游的皮奥里亚人土地，河道在此展宽为皮奥里亚湖，法国人称之为皮米特威。皮奥里亚人自称佩瓦雷瓦（peewaareewa），是说阿尔冈昆语的伊利尼联盟成员之一。1444年，他们的季节性村落设在林木繁茂的河漫滩与相邻草原上，屋舍附近有玉米田，猎队穿过草原猎捕野牛，伊利诺伊河则把他们与邻近的伊利尼群体连在一起。

法国探险在1673年抵达伊利尼地区。1680年1月，拉萨尔和亨利·德·通蒂在皮米特威附近东岸修建克雷夫科尔堡，但易洛魁战队进逼河谷时，守军于1680年4月16日哗变并摧毁堡垒。1691年，通蒂在附近建立圣路易·德·皮米特威堡，这里成为毛皮贸易据点。战争和疫病使伊利尼人从欧洲人密集接触初期约一万零五百人，在一个世纪内减至不足五百。1763年法国割让密西西比河以东土地后，许多皮奥里亚人撤往河西。1813年9月，美国人在皮奥里亚湖修建克拉克堡；1818年的《爱德华兹维尔条约》把伊利诺伊境内的皮奥里亚土地割让给美国。

en:
Kaskankaham covers the lower Kaskaskia River country near the Mississippi, where oak woods and tallgrass prairie meet fertile alluvial bottoms. The people whose name it bears, the Kaskaskia or Kaaskaaskia, were one of the Algonquian-speaking bands of the Illinois Confederation. In 1444 the river valleys were Illini planting and hunting range; corn, beans and squash grew in rich soil, bison hunts crossed the prairies, and dugout canoes carried pelts and dried food along the Mississippi system.

Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet met the Kaskaskia at the Grand Village on the upper Illinois River in 1673. A French mission and fur post grew there in 1675, but Iroquois pressure scattered the village; around 1691 its people began moving south, and in 1703 the Jesuit mission of the Immaculate Conception became the nucleus of Kaskaskia on the Mississippi. The mixed French-Illinois settlement held about 2,200 people in 1707. French farms shipped wheat, corn and flour to New Orleans, voyageurs opened fur and lead routes west, Fort de Chartres was built nearby in 1719, and Louis XV sent a church bell in 1741. After the cession of 1763 many French and Illinois families crossed into Spanish-held Missouri. An American force under George Rogers Clark seized Kaskaskia on 4 July 1778; the town became capital of Illinois Territory in 1809 and the first state capital in 1818–1819.
zh:
卡斯坎卡哈姆是卡斯卡斯基亚河下游临近密西西比河的土地，橡树林与高草草原在此接上肥沃的冲积低地。省名所指的卡斯卡斯基亚人在迈阿密—伊利尼语中称卡斯卡斯基亚（Kaaskaaskia），是说阿尔冈昆语的伊利尼联盟一支。1444年，这些河谷属于伊利尼人的种植和游猎范围；玉米、豆类和南瓜生长在沃土上，野牛猎队穿过草原，独木舟则沿密西西比水系运送毛皮和干粮。

1673年，雅克·马凯特和路易·若利埃在伊利诺伊河上游的大村遇到卡斯卡斯基亚人。1675年，法国传教站和毛皮据点在那里发展起来，但易洛魁人的压力使村落离散；约1691年，居民开始南移，1703年，圣母无原罪耶稣会传教站成为密西西比河畔卡斯卡斯基亚的核心。1707年，这座法国人与伊利尼人共同居住的聚落约有二千二百人。法国农场把小麦、玉米和面粉运往新奥尔良，船工向西开辟毛皮和铅矿商路；沙特尔堡于1719年在附近建成，路易十五又在1741年送来教堂钟。1763年割地后，许多法国和伊利尼家庭渡河西迁，进入西班牙控制的密苏里。1778年7月4日，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克率领的美军夺取卡斯卡斯基亚；这座城镇1809年成为伊利诺伊领地首府，1818—1819年担任伊利诺伊州第一个首府。

en:
Cahokia lies on the east side of the Mississippi, where bottomland lakes and woods meet tallgrass prairie in the fertile floodplain later called the American Bottom. In 1444 the great earthworks north of the later colonial village marked the site of a Mississippian town that had reached its peak in the thirteenth century; it was abandoned long before Europeans reached the river. The Cahokia, Kahokiaki in Miami-Illinois, were one of the Illini clans later met by the French.

In late 1696 Father Pinet and the Quebec Seminary of Foreign Missions founded the Holy Family mission among the Cahokia and Tamaroa, building a log church on the Mississippi bank. Cahokia became a major market for furs and Indian goods and grew to roughly 3,000 people, while French habitants planted wheat across the lowlands toward Kaskaskia. After France ceded the east bank in 1763, many Catholic families crossed to Ste Genevieve and the new settlement of St Louis. The Odawa leader Pontiac was killed in or near Cahokia on 20 April 1769. George Rogers Clark established a court there in 1778, 105 Cahokia household heads pledged loyalty to the Continental Congress, and after 1787 the old French courthouse served the Northwest Territory's vast St. Clair County.
zh:
卡霍基亚位于密西西比河东岸，河迹湖与林地在此接上高草草原，这片肥沃泛滥平原后来被称为阿梅里肯洼地。1444年，后来殖民村以北的巨大土丘标志着一座密西西比文化城镇的遗址；这座城镇曾在13世纪达到鼎盛，在欧洲人抵达河流之前早已荒废。卡霍基亚人在迈阿密—伊利尼语中称卡霍基亚基（Kahokiaki），是后来法国人遇到的伊利尼氏族之一。

1696年末，皮内神父与魁北克外方传教会神学院在卡霍基亚人和塔马罗亚人中建立圣家堂传教站，并在密西西比河畔修建木构教堂。卡霍基亚随后成为毛皮和印第安货物的重要市场，人口增至约三千，法国定居者则在通往卡斯卡斯基亚的低地上种植小麦。1763年法国割让河东土地后，许多天主教家庭渡河西往圣热纳维耶夫和新建的圣路易斯。1769年4月20日，奥达瓦人领袖庞蒂亚克在卡霍基亚或其附近被杀。1778年，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克在此设立法庭，一百零五名卡霍基亚户主向大陆会议宣誓效忠；1787年后，古老的法国法院又为西北领地辖境广阔的圣克莱尔县服务。

en:
The high Chickasaw Bluffs above the Mississippi once held Mississippian villages whose people raised mounds on the ground later named Chucalissa, 'abandoned house' in the Chickasaw language. By the fifteenth century those villages had emptied, and the country west of the Tennessee River had become hunting ground for the Chickasaw, whose towns lay to the south in the upper Yazoo and Tombigbee valleys. In 1444 the bluffs carried no town or fort; Chickasaw parties camped there on the hunt and crossed the great river by canoe, and no European flag had yet been seen on its banks.

Hernando de Soto's Spaniards, after wintering among the Chickasaw in 1540–41, crossed the Mississippi near these bluffs in May 1541, the first Europeans to reach them. In late February 1682 La Salle's canoe expedition threw up a stockade, Fort Prudhomme, while searching for a lost hunter — the first French structure in Tennessee, occupied for only ten days, though La Salle himself lay ill there for forty on his way back upriver. In 1739 Bienville led more than 3,000 French, African and Indian troops to the fourth bluff and built Fort Assumption there on 15 August; disease, desertion and drink broke the army, which abandoned the post on 31 March 1740 and left the Chickasaw in possession. They held the bluffs until the Treaty of Tuscaloosa of 19 October 1818, when Andrew Jackson and Isaac Shelby bought all Chickasaw land east of the Mississippi. Memphis was laid out on the fourth bluff on 22 May 1819 by Jackson, John Overton and James Winchester.
zh:
密西西比河畔高耸的奇克索崖上，曾有密西西比文化的村落，村民在后来被称作丘卡利萨的地方垒筑土丘——这个名字在奇克索语中意为「废弃的房屋」。到15世纪，这些村落已经荒废，田纳西河以西的土地成了奇克索人的猎场，他们的村镇在南边的亚祖河与汤比格比河上游。1444年的崖上没有城镇也没有要塞，只有奇克索猎手在此宿营、乘独木舟渡过大河，欧洲人的旗帜还没有出现在河岸边。

1540至1541年冬，埃尔南多·德·索托率领的西班牙人在奇克索人那里过冬后，于1541年5月在这一带渡过密西西比河，成为最早到达此地的欧洲人。1682年2月底，拉萨尔的独木舟探险队为寻找一名走失的猎人，仓促筑起一座栅栏堡——普鲁多姆堡，这是法国人在田纳西修建的第一处建筑，只使用了十天；拉萨尔返航途中还曾在此养病四十天。1739年，边维尔率三千多名法军、黑人士兵和印第安盟军来到第四道崖，于8月15日建成圣母升天堡；疾病、逃亡和酗酒击垮了这支军队，1740年3月31日法军弃堡而去，奇克索人仍是这片土地的主人。直到1818年10月19日签订《塔斯卡卢萨条约》，安德鲁·杰克逊与艾萨克·谢尔比买下密西西比河以东的全部奇克索土地。1819年5月22日，杰克逊、约翰·奥弗顿和詹姆斯·温彻斯特在第四道崖上规划兴建孟菲斯。

en:
The black-soil hills of northeast Mississippi were the homeland of the Chickasaw, a Muskogean-speaking people whose maize fields and scattered towns lay along the upper Yazoo and Pearl River valleys. They had left the Tombigbee country in the fifteenth century, when the old Moundville chiefdom collapsed. In 1444 no single king ruled them: their towns answered to matrilineal clans and two moieties, and their warriors already had a name for fierceness that the first European visitors would record with dread.

Hernando de Soto's Spaniards wintered in a Chickasaw town in 1540-41, in the heart of the Chickasaw country. When de Soto demanded two hundred bearers, the Chickasaw burned his camp in a night attack and nearly destroyed the expedition before it broke away to the Mississippi River. Traders from Carolina reached them after 1670, bartering guns for captives taken in raids on the Choctaw, until the French armed the Choctaw in answer. Louisiana's armies fared no better: on 26 May 1736 Bienville's French and Choctaw force was bloodily repulsed from the palisaded town of Ackia, and the Chickasaw kept their hills until France ceded its claims east of the Mississippi in 1763. The 1786 Treaty of Hopewell fixed their first boundary with the United States, and in 1821 the Chickasaw still ruled the country of their birth.
zh:
密西西比州东北部的黑土丘陵是奇克谢（奇克索人之地），在亚祖河与珍珠河上游的谷地间，散布着他们的玉米田和一座座城镇。15世纪，古老的蒙德维尔酋邦瓦解，他们离开汤比格比河谷迁来此地。1444年的奇克索人没有共主，各城镇由母系氏族和两个半族按血缘统辖；他们的战士早已以悍勇闻名，最早到来的欧洲访客也将这份悍勇记入史料。

1540至1541年冬，埃尔南多·德·索托的西班牙队伍在奇克索腹地的一座城镇过冬。德·索托强征两百名挑夫，奇克索人趁夜火攻营地，几乎将这支远征队彻底消灭，残部只得脱身逃往密西西比河。1670年后，卡罗来纳的英国商人深入此地，用火枪交换奇克索人袭击乔克托人掳来的俘虏，法国随后以武装乔克托人回应。路易斯安那殖民当局的大军同样讨不到便宜：1736年5月26日，比安维尔率领的法国-乔克托联军攻打栅栏坚固的阿基亚（Ackia）村，被血腥击退；直到1763年法国放弃密西西比河以东的领地，奇克索人始终守住了自己的丘陵。1786年的《霍普韦尔条约》首次划定他们与美国的边界，到1821年，奇克索人仍是这片生息之地的主人。

en:
Central Mississippi, from the upper Pearl River to the Chickasawhay, is the country of the Choctaw, who call themselves Chahta. In 1444 its prairies and creek bottoms held dozens of farming towns of late Plaquemine stock, their maize fields watched over from the old sacred mound of Nanih Waiya. No emperor ruled here: towns and matrilineal clans managed their own affairs, and disputes were as often fought out in a brutal stickball game, the 'little brother of war', as with weapons. Within two centuries these villages had coalesced into one nation in three great divisions, the western Okla Falaya, the eastern Okla Tannap and the southern Okla Hannali.

Hernando de Soto crossed the region's northern edge in 1540-41 without recording the Choctaw name, which first appears in French records after Iberville made the first documented contact in 1699. French guns helped the Choctaw answer Chickasaw slave raids; their warriors helped crush the Natchez rising in 1730 and marched with Bienville against Ackia in 1736. Trade rivalry between Britain and France then split the nation in a civil war from 1747 to 1750, which left the pro-French faction on top. The Treaty of Hopewell in 1786 fixed their first boundary with the United States, and under Pushmataha Choctaw warriors fought with the Americans at New Orleans in 1815. The treaties of Fort Adams in 1801 and Doak's Stand in 1820 opened millions of acres to planters, leaving the Choctaw of 1821 surrounded on every side.
zh:
密西西比腹地——从珍珠河上游到奇克索海河（Chickasawhay）——是乔克托人的家园，他们自称查塔。1444年，在这片草原与河谷低地上，散布着数十座普拉克明文化（Plaquemine）传统的农耕城镇，玉米田由古老的圣丘纳尼怀亚（Nanih Waiya）俯看着。这里没有君王：城镇与母系氏族各自为政，争端常以激烈的棍球赛——「战争的小兄弟」——代替刀兵。此后两百年间，这些村镇凝聚为一个民族，分作三大部：西部的奥克拉法拉亚（Okla Falaya）、东部的奥克拉坦纳普（Okla Tannap）和南部的奥克拉汉纳利（Okla Hannali）。

1540至1541年，德·索托从这片地区的北缘经过，却没有记下乔克托之名；这个名字最早见于法国记载——1699年，伊贝维尔与他们首次有了可考的接触。法国提供的火器让乔克托人得以回击奇克索人的掳掠；1730年，他们出兵协助法国人镇压纳奇兹起事，1736年又随比安维尔攻打阿基亚。随后，英法之间的贸易争夺使乔克托社会在1747至1750年内战分裂，亲法一派最终占了上风。1786年的《霍普韦尔条约》首次划定他们与美国的边界；在普什马塔哈率领下，乔克托战士于1815年在新奥尔良与美军并肩作战。1801年的《亚当斯堡条约》和1820年的《多克斯坦德条约》（Doak's Stand）把数百万英亩土地让给种植园主，到1821年，乔克托人的家园已四面受困。

en:
Ishenoca lies on the lower Mississippi above the delta, near the Bayagoula river village by the Bayou Goula of present Iberville Parish. Burial mounds on the parish ground mark earlier Indigenous societies along the same banks. In 1444 the river, canoes, maize fields and hunting grounds belonged to a world of neighboring Bayagoula, Houma, Mugulasha and Quinipissa settlements; no European fort or mission had yet been built there.

La Salle entered the lower river in 1682 and claimed Louisiana for France, but direct contact came only in 1699, when Iberville met the Bayagoula sharing a village with the Mugulasha and Quinipissa. The Houma attacked that winter, and in the spring of 1700 the Bayagoula destroyed their village-mates. Raids by Taensa and Tunica in 1706 and smallpox by 1721 broke the surviving community; about forty warriors were counted in 1715, and by 1739 the remnant lived between the Houma and Acolapissa and was being absorbed. The river country later passed from France to Spain in 1763 and became part of the Louisiana Purchase in 1803.
zh:
伊谢诺卡位于密西西比河三角洲以上，巴尤古拉人的河畔村落靠近今伊贝维尔堂区境内的贝尤古拉。堂区内留存的墓葬丘，说明更早的原住民社会也曾生活在同一片河岸。1444年，河流、独木舟、玉米田和猎场都属于巴尤古拉、霍马、穆古拉沙与基尼皮萨等相邻村落构成的世界；这里还没有欧洲人的要塞或传教站。

拉萨尔1682年进入密西西比河下游，代表法国宣布占有路易斯安那，但直接接触要到1699年才到来：伊贝维尔在那里见到巴尤古拉人同穆古拉沙人、基尼皮萨人共居一村。霍马人在那年冬天发动袭击，1700年春，巴尤古拉人又消灭了同村的伙伴。1706年坦萨人与图尼卡人的袭击，以及到1721年已蔓延的天花，摧垮了幸存社群；1715年他们尚有约四十名战士，到1739年，残余部众已住在霍马人与阿科拉皮萨人之间并逐渐被吸收。这片河地后来在1763年由法国转入西班牙之手，1803年成为路易斯安那购地的一部分。

en:
At the head of Mobile Bay, the Mobile River meets sheltered water leading into the Gulf of Mexico. In 1444 this was the country of Mobile and Tohomé towns, whose canoes linked river villages, fishing grounds, maize fields and coastal exchange networks; their speech later supplied much of Mobilian Jargon, the trade language used across the central Gulf Coast. No European post yet stood on the bay.

Álvarez de Pineda's Spanish expedition mapped the Gulf shore in 1519, but lasting contact began when Iberville entered Mobile Bay on 31 January 1699. In 1702 Iberville and Bienville founded La Mobile and Fort Louis twenty-seven miles up the river, capital of French Louisiana until 1711. A Catholic parish followed in 1703, and the Pélican's 1704 call brought yellow fever; a supply ship from Saint-Domingue also brought African slaves to Mobile. Around 1709 the Mobile and Tohomé received leave to settle near the fort; floods and disease then pushed the town down to the bay in 1711. Work on brick Fort Condé began in 1723. Britain took Mobile in 1763 and renamed the post Fort Charlotte, Bernardo de Gálvez captured it after a siege in 1780, and United States forces under James Wilkinson occupied it in 1813.
zh:
莫比尔河在莫比尔湾顶端注入这片通向墨西哥湾的隐蔽水域。1444年，这里是莫比尔人与托霍梅人的土地，独木舟连接着河畔村落、渔场、玉米田和海岸交换网络；他们的语言后来构成莫比尔行话的主要基础，这种贸易通语曾通行于墨西哥湾中部沿岸。此时湾畔还没有欧洲人的据点。

阿尔瓦雷斯·德·皮内达的西班牙远征队1519年测绘了这段墨西哥湾海岸，但持久接触要到1699年1月31日伊贝维尔驶入莫比尔湾才开始。1702年，伊贝维尔与边维尔兄弟在河上游二十七英里处建立拉莫比尔和圣路易堡，这里作为法属路易斯安那首府直至1711年。1703年天主教堂区设立，1704年「鹈鹕号」到来，带来了黄热病；一艘来自圣多明各的补给船也将非洲奴隶运至莫比尔。约1709年，莫比尔人与托霍梅人获准在要塞附近定居；洪水和疾病随后迫使城镇在1711年下移到湾畔。砖砌康德堡1723年动工。1763年英国取得莫比尔并将要塞改名夏洛特堡；贝尔纳多·德·加尔维斯1780年围城后将其攻占，1813年詹姆斯·威尔金森率领美军占领此地。

en:
Sheltered by Santa Rosa Island, Pensacola Bay offered one of the deepest harbors on the northern Gulf Coast. In 1444 its shores and inland waters were Muskogean country, lived over by the people later called Pensacola; dugout canoes linked their villages to fishing grounds, trade paths and the mound-centered ceremonial world of Bottle Creek. Creek visitors from the north were part of that wider network, but no European fortress yet commanded the bay.

Spanish expeditions reached the water in 1528 and 1539, the latter naming it the Bay of Ochuse. On 15 August 1559 Tristán de Luna landed from Veracruz with about 1,500 people and eleven ships to found Santa María de Ochuse, but a hurricane on 19 September sank six ships and destroyed most supplies; the survivors abandoned the post in 1561. Spain returned permanently in 1698, building Presidio Santa María de Galve. Bienville's French force seized Pensacola in May 1719, and it reverted to Spain before new presidios were opened on Santa Rosa Island in 1722 and the mainland in 1754. Britain took Florida in 1763 and made Pensacola capital of West Florida. Bernardo de Gálvez besieged it from 9 March to 10 May 1781 with nearly 8,000 troops, and Spain received it formally in 1783. Andrew Jackson captured the town in November 1814 and again in 1818; in 1821 the last Spanish garrison gave way to United States rule.
zh:
圣罗莎岛环抱的彭萨科拉湾，是墨西哥湾北岸最优良的深水港湾之一。1444年，湾岸与内水都是穆斯科格语人群的土地，住在这里的人后来被称为彭萨科拉人；独木舟把他们的村落同渔场、贸易小路以及以土丘为中心的博特尔克里克礼仪世界连接起来。北方来的克里克访客也属于这个更广的交往网络，但此时还没有欧洲要塞控制海湾。

西班牙远征队先后在1528年和1539年抵达这片水域，后一次将其记为奥丘塞湾。1559年8月15日，特里斯坦·德·卢纳率约一千五百人、分乘十一艘船从韦拉克鲁斯登陆，建立圣玛丽亚·德·奥丘塞；但9月19日的飓风击沉六艘船、毁掉大部分物资，幸存者最终在1561年放弃据点。1698年西班牙人重返并长期驻守，修建圣玛丽亚·德·加尔韦要塞。边维尔率领的法军1719年5月夺取彭萨科拉，此后此地又归还西班牙，1722年在圣罗莎岛、1754年在大陆另设要塞城镇。1763年英国取得佛罗里达，把彭萨科拉定为西佛罗里达首府。1781年3月9日至5月10日，贝尔纳多·德·加尔维斯率近八千军队围城，1783年西班牙正式获得此地。安德鲁·杰克逊1814年11月攻占城镇，1818年再次进占；1821年，最后的西班牙驻军让位于美国统治。

en:
The middle Alabama winds through cane bottoms and fertile red bluffs between the fall-line hills and the coastal plain. In towns such as Tawasa and Atagi ('pure water') lived the people later called the Tawasa, villagers who grew maize and beans in the long aftermath of the mound-building chiefdoms whose earthworks still stood up and down the valley. They were close to the Alibamu on the upper river and to the Choctaw in the west, bound by trade and kinship rather than by any single chief. In 1444 these towns went their own way, and no European was yet within a thousand miles of the Alabama.

Hernando de Soto's army crossed the valley in 1540, and the palisaded town of Mabila fell to him nearby on 18 October after a day's slaughter. In 1560 the starving colonists of Tristán de Luna, who had landed at Pensacola in 1559, occupied the abandoned river town of Nanipacana not far downstream before the expedition collapsed. Around 1707 the Tawasa were raided and carried off into the slave trade; one captive, Lamhatty, reached Virginia, where the sixty-word list taken from him became the only record of the Tawasa tongue, seemingly akin to the distant Timucua. Survivors sheltered with the French at Mobile after 1702, and about sixty of them joined the Alibamu beside Fort Toulouse, raised in 1717 at the forks of the Coosa and Tallapoosa; in time they were absorbed into the Creek Confederacy. Their descendants fought with the Red Sticks in the Creek War of 1813–14, and Andrew Jackson's victory at Horseshoe Bend and the Treaty of Fort Jackson in August 1814 opened the Alabama valley to American settlement.
zh:
中亚拉巴马河蜿蜒穿过河蔗密布的滩地与肥沃的红色崖岸，介于瀑布线丘陵和沿海平原之间。塔瓦萨、阿塔吉（Atagi，意为「清水」）等城镇就坐落于此，居民后来被称为塔瓦萨人。他们是村民，在筑丘酋邦衰落之后的漫长岁月里种植玉米和豆类，河谷上下仍可见到先人的土筑工程。他们与上游的阿拉巴马人、西边的乔克托人关系密切，靠贸易和姻亲往来相连，却不奉共同的首领。1444年，这些城镇各自为政，欧洲人距亚拉巴马河尚有千里之遥。

1540年，埃尔南多·德·索托的军队穿过这片河谷，10月18日，栅寨环绕的马比拉在附近经一天血战之后被他攻陷。1559年特里斯坦·德·卢纳率殖民队在彭萨科拉登陆，1560年，饥饿的殖民者占据了下游不远处已遭遗弃的河畔城镇纳尼帕卡纳，但远征最终瓦解。约1707年，塔瓦萨人遭袭掠，被掳入奴隶贸易；俘虏之一拉姆哈蒂辗转到达弗吉尼亚，人们据他的口述记下60个词，成为塔瓦萨语唯一的记录——这种语言似乎与遥远的蒂穆夸语相近。1702年后，幸存者在法国人的莫比尔避难，约60人在1717年建于库萨河与塔拉普萨河交汇处的图卢兹堡旁投奔阿拉巴马人，最终并入克里克联盟。他们的后裔在1813至1814年的克里克战争中加入「红棍」一方；安德鲁·杰克逊在马蹄湾取胜，1814年8月的杰克逊堡条约把亚拉巴马河谷开放给美国人定居。

en:
Coweta stands on the lower Chattahoochee, among river-bottom fields of maize, beans and squash beneath the long fall line of the river. In 1444 the valley was held by the farming towns of a South Appalachian Mississippian chiefdom, with platform mounds and plazas and Hitchiti-speaking villagers; Coweta and its neighbour Tuskegee came to the valley later. The towns were linked by kinship and by the old trade that carried shell and copper through the Southeast; the Spaniards had not yet come.

The de Soto expedition of 1540 passed to the east, and the epidemics it set loose broke the old chiefdom; the valley's towns shrank and reshaped themselves. In 1685 they welcomed the English trader Henry Woodward, and after Spanish retaliation most of them moved east in 1690 to the Ochese Creek post on the Ocmulgee, where English muskets and the deerskin trade made them the Ochese Creeks. They raided the Florida missions in 1704, joined the Yamasee War in 1715, and then fell back to the Chattahoochee as the Lower Creeks. In May 1718 Brims, mico of Coweta, summoned British, French and Spanish agents to his town and declared Creek neutrality, playing the three empires off one another until his death in 1733; his half-sister Mary Musgrove became James Oglethorpe's interpreter when Georgia was founded in 1733, and Savannah shipped up to 50,000 deerskins a year by the 1750s. The American Revolution split the towns, and in 1790 Alexander McGillivray signed the Treaty of New York with Washington. In the Red Stick War of 1813-14 the Lower Creeks under William McIntosh fought with Andrew Jackson, whose victory at Horseshoe Bend on 27 March 1814 was sealed by the Treaty of Fort Jackson, ceding 22 million acres; in 1821 McIntosh set his name to the first Treaty of Indian Springs, opening the first Lower Creek lands to the cotton frontier.
zh:
考维塔地处查特胡奇河下游，河滨滩地里玉米、豆类和南瓜连绵，上游不远便是河流的瀑布线。1444年，河谷里散布着南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化的农耕城邦，筑有高台墩和广场，居民操希奇蒂语；考维塔和邻近的塔斯克吉则是后来迁入河谷的。各镇靠亲缘和东南古商道联系，商道上流通着贝壳与铜器；此时西班牙人尚未来到。

1540年德索托远征从东边经过，随之而来的疫病瓦解了旧邦国，河谷城邦人口锐减、重新组合。1685年他们接纳了英国商人亨利·伍德沃德，遭西班牙报复后，多数城镇于1690年东迁到奥克马尔吉河畔的奥切塞溪商栈，靠英军火枪和鹿皮贸易被称为奥切塞克里克人。1704年他们随英军劫掠佛罗里达布道所，1715年又参加雅马西战争，战后退回查特胡奇河，成为下克里克人。1718年5月，考维塔酋长布里姆把英、法、西三国代表召到镇上，宣布克里克中立，在三大帝国间左右逢源，直至1733年去世；他的异母妹玛丽·马斯格罗夫在1733年佐治亚建立时为奥格尔索普担任翻译，到1750年代萨凡纳每年输出多达五万张鹿皮。美国独立战争使诸镇分裂，1790年麦吉利夫雷与华盛顿签订《纽约条约》。1813至1814年的红棍战争中，麦金托什率领的下克里克人随安德鲁·杰克逊作战；1814年3月27日杰克逊在蹄铁湾取胜，8月9日的《杰克逊堡条约》割让2200万英亩土地；1821年麦金托什签署第一个《印第安斯普林斯条约》，首批下克里克土地向棉花种植边疆开放。

en:
The Ais, or Ays, lived on the sheltered islands and mainland shore of the long lagoon the Spanish called the River of Ais, now the Indian River, their land running from Cape Canaveral south to the St. Lucie Inlet. Fish, turtle and shellfish teemed in the brackish water and palm berries and cocoplums ripened along its banks, so that the Ais sowed no crops yet wanted for little. Theirs was a chiefdom of towns, each led by its own cacique under a paramount chief at the town of Ais. In 1444 no European had yet touched this coast, and the lagoon towns traded little even with other Florida peoples.

Juan Ponce de León sailed along this shore in 1513. By the 1550s the Ais were allied with Carlos, the powerful king of the Calusa, to whom their chief Oathchaqua had given his daughter. In November 1565 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés, fresh from founding St. Augustine, visited the Ais town and received its chief's oath to Philip II; the presidio he left behind was abandoned within months amid hunger and bloodshed, and a formal peace followed in 1570. Governor Méndez de Canço reported in 1597 that the Ais chief could field more warriors than any chief in Florida, and in 1605 the soldier Álvaro Mexía mapped the lagoon and agreed a ransom for shipwrecked sailors. Jonathan Dickinson, shipwrecked with his party in 1696, left the fullest account of Ais life; friars sent in 1699 made no converts. After 1700 Carolinian slavers and their Indian allies raided the coast; some 88 'coast Indians' were removed to the northern missions in 1726 and only 52 remained by 1728. In 1763 the last of the Ais sailed for Cuba with the Spaniards and the Calusa.
zh:
艾斯人（Ais，又作Ays）住在一条狭长潟湖的障壁岛与大陆沿岸，西班牙人把这片水域称作「艾斯河」，即今印第安河；其地北起卡纳维拉尔角，南至圣露西入海口。潟湖里鱼、龟和贝类繁庶，岸边棕榈浆果与可可李成熟，艾斯人不事农耕却衣食丰足。他们的社会是由多个村镇组成的酋邦，各镇自有首领，统属于坐镇艾斯镇的大酋。1444年，还没有欧洲人到过这片海岸，潟湖诸镇与佛罗里达其他族群也很少往来。

1513年，胡安·庞塞·德莱昂的船队沿这一带海岸南下。16世纪50年代，艾斯人已与势力强盛的卡卢萨王卡洛斯结盟，大酋奥阿奇夸把女儿嫁给他。1565年11月，刚建立圣奥古斯丁的佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯造访艾斯镇，大酋向腓力二世宣誓效忠；留守的要塞却因缺粮和流血冲突数月后即告废弃，双方1570年正式议和。1597年，门德斯·德·坎索总督奏称艾斯首领能调集的武士冠于佛罗里达诸部；1605年，士兵阿尔瓦罗·梅希亚在艾斯人协助下测绘潟湖，并定下赎救失事船员的约定。1696年随船遇险的乔纳森·迪金森留下了关于艾斯生活最详尽的记载，1699年派来的修士则未赢得一名信徒。1700年后，卡罗来纳的奴隶贩子及其印第安盟友不断洗劫海岸：1726年约88名「沿海印第安人」被迁往北方传教站，1728年仅剩52人。1763年，最后的艾斯人随西班牙人和卡卢萨人登船前往古巴。

en:
The lands between the Suwannee and Santa Fe rivers were held in 1444 by the Northern Utina, the Timucua-speaking people whose dialect the Spanish later called Timucua proper. Their scattered villages belonged to small chiefdoms linked by language, marriage, and the Suwannee Valley ceramic tradition; maize fields, river crossings, and a principal settlement perhaps near Fig Springs gave the country its centers. Across the Suwannee lived the closely related Yustaga, while raids and shifting alliances separated the Northern Utina from other Florida chiefdoms.

In 1539 Hernando de Soto marched through this region, seized Chief Aguacaleycuen, and after a clash near Napituca put many Timucua to death. Franciscan missions entered the chiefdom in 1597, and San Martín de Timucua, likely at Fig Springs, became the leading station among missions founded between 1608 and 1616. The Northern Utina joined the Timucua Rebellion of 1656; Spanish forces then burned their towns and moved survivors along the road from St. Augustine to Apalachee. Creek and Yamasee raids, epidemics, and Carolinian slave raids further reduced the province. The remaining Timucua were withdrawn toward St. Augustine and, when Spain ceded Florida in 1763, left for Cuba with the Spanish.
zh:
1444年，萨旺尼河与圣菲河之间的土地由北乌蒂纳人占据，他们是蒂穆夸语人群的一支，西班牙人后来把他们的方言称为「正宗蒂穆夸语」。分散的村落分属各个小酋邦，依靠共同语言、联姻和萨旺尼河谷陶器传统联系在一起；玉米地、渡口，以及菲格泉附近可能存在的主要村镇，构成这片土地的中心。萨旺尼河对岸是关系密切的尤斯塔加人，而袭击与不断变化的同盟，又使北乌蒂纳人与佛罗里达其他酋邦保持距离。

1539年，埃尔南多·德·索托率军穿过这里，俘获酋长阿瓜卡莱昆，并在纳皮图卡附近的冲突后处死许多蒂穆夸人。1597年，方济各会传教站进入这一酋邦；可能位于菲格泉的圣马丁·德·蒂穆夸，是1608年至1616年间建立的各传教站中最重要的一处。北乌蒂纳人参加1656年的蒂穆夸叛乱，事后西班牙军队焚毁村镇，把幸存者迁往圣奥古斯丁通往阿巴拉契的道路沿线。克里克人与亚马西人的袭击、疫病以及卡罗来纳奴隶劫掠使教区人口继续锐减。残余的蒂穆夸人被撤往圣奥古斯丁附近，1763年西班牙割让佛罗里达后又随西班牙人前往古巴。

en:
In 1444 Apalachee was a densely settled Muskogean-speaking country between the Aucilla and Ochlockonee rivers, opening onto Apalachee Bay. Farming villages lived under powerful regional chiefs in a Mississippian world of mound ceremonialism and long-distance trade reaching toward the Great Lakes. Anhaica was the principal town, and the province's stored grain, copper ornaments, and strict hierarchy made it one of the strongest chiefdoms in Florida. The peoples to the east along the Aucilla were Timucuan speakers, and alliances and raids shifted with every generation.

Pánfilo de Narváez entered Apalachee on 15 June 1528 and met fierce resistance before fleeing to the coast. Hernando de Soto seized Anhaica eleven years later and wintered there in 1539 and 1540 despite ambushes and raids on his horses. Franciscan missionaries began work around 1600, and in 1656 San Luis de Talimali became the western capital of Spanish Florida, linking Apalachee farms and ranches to St. Augustine. From the 1670s, Apalachicola, Yamasee, and other Creek raiders carried captives to Carolina, and in 1704 Colonel James Moore led fifty colonists and about a thousand Creek warriors through the missions. Moore carried off roughly 1,300 surrendered Apalachee and another thousand enslaved people; the Spanish burned San Luis and abandoned the province. Survivors fled toward Pensacola, Mobile, and the Carolinas, with only a small band returning near St. Marks in 1718.
zh:
1444年的阿巴拉契是一片人口稠密的穆斯科格语地区，位于奥西拉河与奥洛克洛尼河之间，通向阿巴拉契湾。务农村落受强有力的地区酋长统辖，属于有土墩仪式和远途贸易的密西西比社会，贸易联系远达五大湖方向。安海卡是主要城镇，储存的谷物、铜饰和森严等级使阿巴拉契成为佛罗里达最强盛的酋邦之一。奥西拉河以东是蒂穆夸语人群，各代人之间的同盟与侵袭不断变化。

1528年6月15日，潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯进入阿巴拉契，遭到猛烈抵抗，最后逃向海岸。十一年后，埃尔南多·德·索托夺取安海卡，并在当地人伏击和射杀马匹的袭扰中于1539年至1540年在此过冬。约1600年，方济各会传教士开始传教；1656年，圣路易斯·德·塔利马利成为西属佛罗里达的西部首府，把阿巴拉契的农庄和牧场与圣奥古斯丁连接起来。1670年代起，阿巴拉奇科拉人、亚马西人和其他克里克袭掠者把俘虏带往卡罗来纳。1704年，詹姆斯·摩尔上校率领五十名殖民者和约一千名克里克战士横扫各传教站，带走约一千三百名投降的阿巴拉契人，另有一千人被掳为奴；西班牙人焚毁圣路易斯并放弃教区。幸存者逃往彭萨科拉、莫比尔和南北卡罗来纳，只有一小群人在1718年回到圣马可斯附近。

en:
In 1444 Guale was a string of towns and island settlements among Georgia's tidal waterways and Sea Islands, including Sapelo and St. Catherines and the lower Altamaha and Ogeechee rivers. Chiefs called micos ruled with town councils and matrilineal lineages; plazas, platform mounds, shell deposits, and ceramics place the country in the Savannah and Irene phases of coastal Mississippian life. Families raised maize and beans, hunted on the mainland, and took fish and shellfish from the estuaries, while island and river towns exchanged food, shells, and marriage alliances.

Jean Ribault's French expedition met the Guale in 1562, when Chief Oade supplied maize and beans to the Charlesfort settlement on Parris Island. Jesuits arrived in the 1560s, and Franciscans were working in at least five principal towns by 1595. In September 1597 five friars were killed; the older story centered on Juanillo's revolt against the suppression of polygyny, while later accounts also stress rivalries among Guale chiefs. Governor Gonzalo Méndez de Canzo burned towns and crops, and in 1601 Domingo of Asao killed Don Francisco and Juanillo. Missions returned early in the new century, six being listed in 1655, among them Santa Catalina de Guale, San Joseph de Sapala, and Santo Domingo de Talaje. Forced labor, epidemics, Westo raids, and piracy then weakened the province, and Spain withdrew all six coastal missions in 1684. Many Guale joined the emerging Yamasee, forming most of the Upper Towns, and became entangled in slave raids armed through the Scottish settlement of Stuarts Town. James Moore overran the remaining settlements in 1702; after the Yamasee War of 1715 the survivors scattered, leaving too few Guale to resist James Oglethorpe's founding of Georgia in 1733.
zh:
1444年，瓜莱是佐治亚潮汐水道与海岛上的一串村镇，分布在萨佩洛岛、圣凯瑟琳斯岛以及阿尔塔马哈河、奥吉奇河下游一带。称为米科（mico）的酋长依靠镇议会和母系氏族行使权力；广场、土墩、贝壳堆积和陶器表明，这里属于沿海密西西比社会的萨凡纳阶段与艾琳阶段。居民种植玉米和豆类，在大陆狩猎，也在河口捕捞鱼虾和贝类，海岛与河畔村镇之间交换食物、贝壳并互通婚姻。

1562年，让·里博率领的法国探险队遇到瓜莱人，酋长奥阿德向帕里斯岛上的查尔斯堡供应玉米和豆类。耶稣会士在1560年代首先到来，到1595年方济各会已在至少五个主要村镇传教。1597年9月，五名修士被杀；传统叙述把事件核心归于胡安尼略反抗多妻制被禁，后来的解释也强调瓜莱酋长之间的权力争斗。总督贡萨洛·门德斯·德·坎索出兵焚毁村镇和作物，1601年阿萨奥的多明戈杀死唐·弗朗西斯科和胡安尼略。传教站在17世纪初恢复，1655年已有六座，包括圣卡塔利娜·德·瓜莱、圣何塞·德·萨帕拉和圣多明各·德·塔拉赫。劳役征调、疫病、韦斯托人袭掠和海盗随后削弱教区，1684年西班牙撤出全部六座海岸传教站。许多瓜莱人加入正在形成的亚马西人，并在亚马西上镇中占多数，又因苏格兰斯图尔特镇提供火器而卷入奴隶袭掠。1702年，詹姆斯·摩尔摧毁残余定居点；1715年亚马西战争后幸存者四散，到1733年詹姆斯·奥格尔索普建立佐治亚时，瓜莱人已无力阻挡。

en:
The fall-line hills and creek-cut valleys of the lower Chattahoochee are the country of the Lower Creek towns, Muskogean-speaking villagers of the South Appalachian Mississippian world. Maize fields climbed the river terraces below platform mounds that carried temples and the houses of chiefs, and the towns governed their own affairs in the long peace after the old mound centers broke up. Kasihta, which the Spanish would write as Casista, ranked with Coweta as the oldest and foremost of the Chattahoochee towns, a 'white' or peace town where councils were held and blood could not be spilled. In 1444 its people traded along the ridge paths with neighbours near and far and had never met a European.

Franciscans and soldiers first reached the Chattahoochee towns from Apalachee in 1638, and by the 1670s their deerskins were going by way of Florida to Havana, even as English traders from Charleston appeared at Coweta. Slave raids and imperial rivalry soon pulled most of the towns east to the Ocmulgee, where Carolina knew them as the Ochese. Kasihta and Coweta people were counted among the Yamasee, the armed confederation that raided for slaves on Carolina's behalf until debt and abuse drove it to revolt on 15 April 1715, opening the Yamasee War. Defeat scattered the Yamasee, and the towns returned to the Chattahoochee as the Lower Towns of the Creek confederacy. For a century Kasihta shared in the deerskin trade with Carolina and Georgia, a peace town that sheltered refugees as smaller peoples folded into the Creek world. The American Revolution and the treaties that followed bit into the town lands, and when the Creek civil war of 1813–14 ended in Andrew Jackson's victory the defeated nation was forced to cede its Georgia country; by 1821 the old Kasihta lands lay open to American settlement.
zh:
查特胡奇河下游的瀑布线丘陵与溪谷纵横之地，是下克里克诸镇的家园。这些讲穆斯科格语的村镇属于南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化圈，玉米地沿河畔台地拾级而上，平顶土丘上矗立着神庙和酋长的居所；古老的土丘中心瓦解后，诸镇在漫长岁月里各自治理内部事务。卡西塔（西班牙人写作Casista）与考维塔并列为查特胡奇河畔最古老、最首要的城镇，是一座「白镇」，即讲和议事、禁止流血的和平镇。1444年的卡西塔人沿山脊商路与远近邻族贸易，还从未见过欧洲人。

方济各会修士和士兵1638年从阿巴拉奇首次抵达查特胡奇诸镇；到1670年代，这里的鹿皮已经佛罗里达远销哈瓦那，与此同时，来自查尔斯顿的英国商人也出现在考维塔。贩奴袭扰和列强争夺很快把大多数城镇向东引向奥克马尔吉河，卡罗来纳人把他们称作奥切斯人。卡西塔人和考维塔人也被计入亚马西联盟——这个武装联盟替卡罗来纳掳掠人口为奴，直到债务盘剥和种种凌虐把他们逼反：1715年4月15日，亚马西战争爆发。战败使亚马西人四散，诸镇重返查特胡奇河，组成克里克联盟的下镇。此后一个世纪里，卡西塔参与对卡罗来纳和佐治亚的鹿皮贸易，作为和平镇收容难民，看着较小的族群陆续并入克里克世界。美国独立战争及随后的条约不断蚕食城镇土地；1813至1814年克里克内战以安德鲁·杰克逊的胜利告终，战败的联盟被迫割让佐治亚故土，到1821年，古老的卡西塔土地已向美国拓殖者敞开。

en:
The mountain-fringed valleys of the upper Coosa were the heart of Coosa, the greatest of the South Appalachian paramount chiefdoms. Its capital on the Coosawattee, a town of plazas and three platform mounds, headed eight villages of perhaps a few thousand people, while its mico drew tribute from subject chiefdoms strung four hundred miles along the Appalachians, as far north as Chiaha on the French Broad, where maize, bean, squash and tobacco fields overlooked the river. In 1444 Coosa stood at the height of its power, its merchants and war parties known from the Tennessee to the Alabama piedmont.

Hernando de Soto entered the chiefdom in the summer of 1540, his chroniclers spelling its name Coça and remarking on the fertile gardens and abundance of food rather than any single city. Tristán de Luna came in 1560 and Juan Pardo in 1566–68, building Fort San Pedro beside Chiaha; when the inland forts rose in 1568 Pardo's garrisons were killed and Spain gave up the interior. Old World diseases proved more destructive than soldiers: by 1600 the Coosa heartland was largely abandoned, and the survivors withdrew into fortified villages down the Coosa River in Alabama, while Cherokee warriors from the mountains made themselves masters of the empty northern valleys. The name of Coosa lived on as one of the four mother towns of the Creek confederacy among the Upper Towns, deep in the deerskin trade of the eighteenth century. The Creek civil war of 1813–14 ended in Andrew Jackson's victory over the Upper Towns, and the forced cessions that followed stripped the old Coosa country of its self-rule.
zh:
群山环抱的上库萨河谷，是南阿巴拉契亚诸最高酋邦中最强大的库萨的腹地。其首府坐落库萨瓦蒂河畔，镇中有广场和三座平顶土丘，统辖着八座村落、约数千人口；大酋长（mico）向沿阿巴拉契亚山脉绵延四百英里的臣属酋邦索取贡赋，势力最北抵达弗伦奇布罗德河畔的奇亚哈——那里的玉米、豆类、南瓜和烟田俯瞰着河面。1444年正值库萨鼎盛之时，它的商队和战队闻名于从田纳西到亚拉巴马皮德蒙特的广阔地带。

1540年夏，埃尔南多·德索托进入库萨（随行记事拼作Coça），他们记下的不是某一座雄城，而是遍地肥沃田园、粮食丰足的一串村镇。特里斯坦·德·卢纳1560年、胡安·帕尔多1566至1568年先后来到，帕尔多还在奇亚哈旁修建圣佩德罗堡；1568年内陆各堡据点的西班牙驻军尽被歼灭，西班牙从此放弃内陆。旧大陆带来的疫病比军队更具毁灭性：到1600年，库萨腹地已大半荒废，幸存者退入亚拉巴马境内库萨河下游筑有防御工事的村落，山里的切罗基战士则成了空旷北方谷地的主人。「库萨」之名延续下来，成为克里克联盟四大母镇之一，位列上镇之中，深度参与18世纪的鹿皮贸易。1813至1814年的克里克内战以安德鲁·杰克逊击败上镇告终，随后的强迫割地终结了古老库萨故土的自治。

en:
Issati covers the Santee country, where the Santee River gathers piedmont streams such as the Congaree and Wateree and crosses the South Carolina coastal plain to the Atlantic. The Santee were a small Catawban-speaking people whose villages, burial mounds and hunting grounds followed the middle river. In 1444 their paths and canoe routes linked them with the Winyah, Congaree and Catawba, while Spanish ships had not yet explored the river mouth.

A Spanish party led by Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón reached this coast in 1526, and Francisco Fernández de Écija, sent from St Augustine in 1605 and 1609, documented Santee villages on the river. English settlement at Charles Town in 1670 soon drew the Santee into colonial diplomacy and trade. John Lawson found their settlements extending for miles along the Santee in 1700, and Santee warriors served with John Barnwell in the Tuscarora War of 1711-12. They joined the Yamasee War against the colonists in 1715; a census shortly before the rising counted two villages and forty-three men, and in late 1716 English forces with Etiwan and Cusabo allies captured the river villages and sold many of the men into West Indian slavery. During the Revolution the British stockaded Fort Watson on the Santee as a link between Charleston and the interior, but Francis Marion and Henry Lee besieged it from 15 to 23 April 1781 and used a rough sharpshooter's tower to force its surrender. The Santee Canal, chartered in 1786 and opened in 1800, ran twenty-two miles to the Cooper River, opening a shallow inland route between the upcountry and Charleston.
zh:
伊萨蒂是桑蒂人的土地，桑蒂河汇集资河、沃特里河等皮德蒙特河流，穿过南卡罗来纳沿海平原注入大西洋。桑蒂人是人口不多的卡塔万语族群，村落、墓冢和猎场沿河中游分布。1444年时，他们的小路和独木舟航线把自己与温亚人、康加里人和卡托巴人联系起来，西班牙船只也尚未探入河口。

1526年，卢卡斯·巴斯克斯·德·艾永率领的西班牙队伍到达这段海岸；1605年和1609年，圣奥古斯丁派出的弗朗西斯科·费尔南德斯·德·埃西哈两次记录了河畔的桑蒂村落。1670年英国人建立查尔斯镇，桑蒂人很快被卷入殖民外交与贸易。1700年，约翰·劳森看到桑蒂人的聚落在沿河数英里间延展；1711至1712年，桑蒂战士随约翰·巴恩韦尔参加图斯卡罗拉战争。1715年他们在亚马西战争中转攻殖民者，战前一次人口调查记载当地有两座村落、四十三名男子；1716年底，英军联合埃蒂万人和库萨博人袭取河畔村落，许多男子被贩往西印度群岛为奴。独立战争期间，英军在桑蒂河畔修筑沃森堡，作为查尔斯顿与内陆之间的联络据点；1781年4月15日至23日，弗朗西斯·马里昂和亨利·李围攻该堡，以简陋的狙击手高台压制守军，迫使英军投降。桑蒂运河1786年获准修建、1800年通航，长二十二英里，连通库珀河，为内陆与查尔斯顿之间打开了一条浅水内河航路。

en:
The rolling Piedmont of the Wateree and Catawba rivers is the homeland of the Iswa, 'people of the river' — Ye Iswąˀ, the name later rendered as Catawba. In the fifteenth century its mound towns answered to the mico of Cofitachequi, the paramount chief seated at Talimeco on the Wateree, where a temple crowning the greatest earthen mound kept the bones of rulers and stores of freshwater pearls. Long wars with Ocute in Georgia had emptied the Savannah, Saluda and Broad basins into a wide no-man's-land, leaving Cofitachequi in 1444 the strongest power between the mountains and the coast, its reach extending up toward the North Carolina piedmont.

Spanish ships raiding the coast in 1521 carried off tales of a pearl-rich ruler, Datha, and in 1540 Hernando de Soto crossed the empty buffer into Cofitachequi. A woman, the Lady of Cofitachequi, met him borne on a litter; the Spaniards took her hostage while hunting gold, but she escaped. Juan Pardo found the chiefdom much weakened in 1566–68, calling its town Canosi, and his forts were burned within two years. Slave raids by the Westo and Occaneechi savaged the region through the 1600s, though Henry Woodward still met an 'emperor' said to command a thousand bowmen in 1670, who even visited Charleston. The old chiefdom was abandoned soon after; in 1701 John Lawson found only Congaree hamlets, and the survivors merged into the Catawba confederacy. As the Catawba the river people became the Piedmont's leading tribe, allied with Carolina against the Seneca and Shawnee, until smallpox epidemics in 1738 and 1759 — the second killing nearly half the nation — broke their power. Chief King Hagler was killed by Shawnee raiders in 1763, when South Carolina also confirmed the Catawba a 144,000-acre reservation on the river. They supported the American revolutionaries, withdrawing to Virginia when British troops marched through in 1780 and returning after Guilford Court House in 1781.
zh:
沃特里河与卡托巴河流经的起伏皮德蒙特，是伊斯瓦人的家园——伊斯瓦意为「河上人」，耶伊斯瓦（Ye Iswąˀ）后来被英国人写作卡托巴。15世纪时，这一带的土丘城镇都听命于科菲塔切基的大酋长（mico）；其首府塔利梅科位于沃特里河畔，最大的土丘顶上建有神庙，供奉历代统治者的遗骨和淡水珍珠储藏。与佐治亚奥库特的长期战争使萨凡纳河、萨卢达河和布罗德河流域沦为大片无人地带，到1444年，科菲塔切基已是山地与海岸之间最强的势力，影响一直向北伸向北卡罗来纳皮德蒙特。

1521年劫掠海岸的西班牙船带走了一位坐拥珍珠的君主达塔的传闻；1540年春，埃尔南多·德索托穿过那片空旷缓冲地，开进科菲塔切基。一位被称为「科菲塔切基女主」的女性乘肩舆接见了他，西班牙人在搜寻黄金期间将她扣为人质，但她最终逃脱。胡安·帕尔多1566至1568年再到时，酋邦已大为衰弱，他把其城镇称作卡诺西；他修建的西班牙要塞两年内全被烧毁。整个17世纪，韦斯托人和奥卡尼奇人的贩奴袭扰使这一地区人口凋敝，不过亨利·伍德沃德1670年仍见到一位据称能调动上千弓箭手的「皇帝」，此人还访问过查尔斯顿。此后不久这座老酋邦便遭废弃；1701年约翰·劳森路经此地，只见到康加里人的小村落，幸存者陆续并入卡托巴联盟。以卡托巴之名，河上居民成为皮德蒙特最强大的部族，与卡罗来纳结盟对抗塞内卡人和肖尼人，直到1738年和1759年两度天花流行——后一次夺去近半数族人的生命——才瓦解其势力。1763年，首领哈格勒王被肖尼袭扰者杀害，同年南卡罗来纳为卡托巴人确认了横跨卡托巴河、面积14.4万英亩的保留地。独立战争中他们支持美方；1780年英军过境时卡托巴人暂避弗吉尼亚，1781年吉尔福德县府战役后才返回家园。

en:
The gorges and tablelands of the upper Cumberland were, in 1444, a meeting-ground of peoples. The Yuchi — Tsoyaha, 'children of the sun', as they called themselves in a language with no known kin — held the Tennessee valley to the south and ranged across these headwaters, planting corn in the river bottoms, while Shawnee hunters from the Ohio country knew the Cumberland as Wasioto. The hills carried deer and elk herds, and no European had yet crossed the ridges to the east.

Hernando de Soto's men heard of these people as the Uchi when they passed through the Tennessee valley in 1541. The first English reach over the mountains came in 1671, when Thomas Batts and Robert Fallam, sent from Fort Henry by Abraham Wood, crossed the divide to the western rivers. By then the old country was emptying: in the 1670s Iroquois war parties, claiming the Ohio valley for the fur trade, drove the Shawnee out of Kentucky, and in 1714 the Cherokee destroyed the Yuchi town of Chestowee. For two generations the upper Cumberland was left to passing hunters, until March 1775, when the Cherokee at Sycamore Shoals sold the Kentucky and Cumberland country to Richard Henderson's Transylvania Company. Daniel Boone blazed the Wilderness Road through Cumberland Gap, and by the end of the century settlers' stations had taken root along the upper river.
zh:
1444年，坎伯兰河上游的峡谷与台原是几支人群交会之地。尤奇人按他们那种与任何语言都不亲缘的语言自称「措亚哈」，意为「太阳之子」；他们据有南方的田纳西河谷，游猎范围遍及这一带河源，并在河谷低地种植玉米，来自俄亥俄方向的肖尼猎人则把坎伯兰河称作瓦西奥托。山林里奔走著鹿和麋鹿，东面的山脊之外还不曾有欧洲人翻越而来。

1541年，埃尔南多·德·索托的队伍穿过田纳西河谷时，已听说这些人，记作「乌奇」（Uchi）。英格兰人最早翻越山脉是在1671年：亚伯拉罕·伍德从亨利堡派出托马斯·巴茨和罗伯特·法勒姆，首次越过阿巴拉契亚分水岭抵达西向的河水。此时这片故地正在变空——1670年代，易洛魁武装为毛皮贸易宣称俄亥俄河谷为猎场，把肖尼人逐出肯塔基；1714年切罗基人又摧毁尤奇城镇切斯托维。此后两代人的时间里，坎伯兰河上游只剩往来的猎手，直到1775年3月，切罗基人在锡卡莫尔浅滩将肯塔基与坎伯兰的土地卖给理查德·亨德森的特兰西瓦尼亚公司。丹尼尔·布恩开辟了穿过坎伯兰峡的荒野之路，到18世纪末，移民的据点已在上游河畔扎下根。

en:
The Chiaha were a Mississippian chiefdom of the lower French Broad River valley in East Tennessee, one of the Dallas-phase farming peoples whose raised-house villages had dotted the Appalachian valleys since about 1300. Beneath the towns lay fields of maize, beans, squash and tobacco, and the chiefdom stood at the northern edge of Coosa's sphere of influence. In 1444 its principal village remained the centre of the river valley's maize lands, and no European had yet crossed the mountains.

Hernando de Soto's entrada reached Chiaha in 1540 and stayed about three weeks at its principal village. Juan Pardo followed in 1567, and his men built Fort San Pedro nearby, one of a chain of garrisons reaching west from Joara. In 1568 the inland peoples rose, burned the forts and killed the garrisons; all but one of Pardo's soldiers died, and Spain abandoned its attempt to colonize the southeastern interior. European diseases then emptied and rearranged these chiefdoms, so that when the Virginians James Needham and Gabriel Arthur crossed the mountains in 1673 seeking the Tomahittans, the French Broad valley was already passing under Cherokee sway.
zh:
奇亚哈人是东田纳西弗伦奇布罗德河下游谷地的密西西比文化酋邦，属达拉斯期农耕人群：自约1300年起，他们的高脚屋村落散布在阿巴拉契亚的河谷间，镇外是玉米、豆类、南瓜和烟草田，其酋邦地处库萨势力范围的北缘。1444年，奇亚哈的主镇仍是这片河谷玉米地的中心，此时还没有欧洲人翻山而来。

1540年，埃尔南多·德·索托的远征队抵达奇亚哈，在主镇停留约三周。1567年胡安·帕尔多接踵而至，部下在附近建起圣佩德罗堡，它是从乔阿拉向西延伸的一连串要塞之一。1568年，内陆各族群起事，焚毁要塞、杀死驻军，帕尔多的士兵仅一人生还，西班牙此后放弃了殖民东南部内陆的尝试。欧洲人带来的疫病使各酋邦人口锐减、聚落重组，到1673年弗吉尼亚人詹姆斯·尼达姆与加布里埃尔·阿瑟为寻找托马希坦人翻山到来时，弗伦奇布罗德河谷已渐入切罗基人的势力范围。

en:
Joara, founded around AD 1000 in the upper Catawba valley at the foot of the Blue Ridge, was the largest Mississippian town in what is now North Carolina. Its earthen mound rose above a prosperous river centre whose people traded copper and salt through the hills, one of three chiefdoms—with Cofitachequi and Guatari—that held the Carolina Piedmont in turn. In 1444 the chiefdom still ruled the fertile upper Catawba bottoms near present Morganton, its granaries and towns untouched by Europeans.

De Soto's chroniclers recorded Joara in 1540. In January 1567 Juan Pardo wintered there, named the town Cuenca and built Fort San Juan, the first European settlement in the North Carolina interior, linking it to five more forts reaching west to Chiaha. In 1568 the townspeople burned the fort, and across the six forts all but one of Pardo's 120 soldiers were killed; Spain abandoned its attempt to colonize the southeastern interior. Disease emptied the upper Catawba soon after: neighbours still knew the place as Hoada in 1605, after which all mention ceases. Its survivors, the Sara or Cheraw, drifted east to the Yadkin and Dan and were absorbed into the Catawba Nation between 1726 and 1739. English, Scots-Irish and German farmers settled the abandoned valley in the later eighteenth century.
zh:
乔阿拉约于公元1000年兴起于蓝岭山麓的卡托巴河上游，是日后北卡罗来纳境内最大的密西西比文化城镇。土筑墩台矗立在这座繁华的河贸中心，居民以铜和盐同山地各部交易；它与科菲塔切基、瓜塔里并称卡罗来纳皮德蒙特三大酋邦，权势在三者间轮替。1444年，乔阿拉仍统治着今摩根顿附近肥沃的卡托巴河上游滩地，粮仓和市镇尚未遭欧洲人染指。

1540年，德·索托的书记官记下了乔阿拉。1567年1月，胡安·帕尔多在此过冬，把镇子命名为昆卡，建起圣胡安堡——欧洲人在北卡罗来纳内陆的第一个定居点，又以五座要塞向西连到奇亚哈。1568年，镇民焚毁圣胡安堡，六座要塞的一百二十名驻军仅一人生还，西班牙此后放弃了殖民东南部内陆的尝试。疫病很快使卡托巴河上游人口凋零：1605年邻族仍以「霍阿达」之名提到此地，此后记载断绝；余部即萨拉人（又称切罗人）向东退入亚德金河与丹河流域，于1726至1739年间并入卡托巴联盟。18世纪后期，英格兰、苏格兰-爱尔兰和德意志农户迁入这片废弃的河谷。

en:
The pinewoods and river bottoms between the North Carolina coast and the Piedmont are the country of the Tuscarora, whose name Skarù·ręˀ means 'hemp gatherers', after one of the three tribes of their Iroquoian confederacy. Their large towns stood on the Roanoke, Tar, Neuse and Pamlico, rivers that carried dugout canoes from inland villages down to the coastal sounds, and seven matrilineal clans, among them Bear, Beaver, Turtle and Wolf, bound the towns together. The wild hemp they gathered supplied fibre, cord and medicine. In 1444 these were populous, self-ruling towns, linked by language and kin to the Iroquois far to the north but untouched as yet by any European.

By 1700 English colonists were pushing up the rivers from the coast, raiding villages for the slave trade and bringing diseases that thinned the towns. In September 1711 the southern chief Hancock, joined by the Pamlico, Coree and other neighbouring peoples, launched a coordinated assault on the settlements, opening the Tuscarora War. South Carolina militia under John Barnwell stormed his fort on the Neuse in 1712 and Hancock was captured and executed; in 1713 the stronghold of Neoheroka fell, with about 900 killed or taken. Tom Blount, the northern chief who had held aloof, made a treaty in June 1718 securing his followers a 56,000-acre tract on the Roanoke, chartered in 1722 as the Indian Woods reservation. Other bands moved north to the Iroquois, who admitted the Tuscarora as their sixth nation the same year. Cessions and sickness shrank Indian Woods to 104 people by 1767, and in 1804 the last band left for New York.
zh:
北卡罗来纳海岸与皮德蒙特之间的松林和河滨低地，是斯卡鲁雷（塔斯卡洛拉人）的家园。斯卡鲁雷意为「采麻者」，原是其易洛魁语三族联盟中一支的称呼。他们的大镇坐落在洛亚诺克河、塔尔河、纽斯河和帕姆利科河畔，独木舟顺流而下，可从内陆村落直达海岸潟湖；熊、河狸、龟、狼等七个母系氏族把各镇联结在一起，采来的野麻用来搓绳、织布和制药。1444年的塔斯卡洛拉各镇人烟稠密、自主其政，语言和亲缘虽与遥远北方的易洛魁人相通，欧洲人的足迹却尚未到此。

1700年前后，英国殖民者从海岸沿河道不断深入，掳掠村民贩卖为奴，带来的疫病也使各镇人口锐减。1711年9月，南支首领汉考克联合帕姆利科人、科里人等邻族，对殖民点发动协同进攻，塔斯卡罗拉战争爆发。1712年，约翰·巴恩韦尔率领的南卡罗来纳民兵攻破他在纽斯河畔的堡垒，汉考克被俘处死；1713年内奥赫罗卡堡陷落，约九百人战死或被俘。保持中立的北支首领汤姆·布朗特于1718年6月缔约，为部下争得洛亚诺克河畔5.6万英亩土地，1722年正式划为印第安伍兹保留地。另一些人北上投奔易洛魁联盟，同年被接纳为第六族。此后土地不断割让、疫病流行，到1767年保留地上只剩104人；1804年，最后一支塔斯卡洛拉人离开北卡罗来纳，迁往纽约。

en:
The sheltered waters of the Pamlico River and Pamlico Sound, guarded from the Atlantic by the long line of the Outer Banks, were the country of the Pamlico, a Carolina Algonquian people whom Raleigh's men recorded in 1585 as the Pomoui. They planted corn and beans in riverside fields and drew shad and herring from the sound, sharing its inlets and shoals with the Croatan, Machapunga and Secotan, their kin in language and trade. In 1444 no European sail had yet crossed this horizon; the inlets later charted as Wococon and Hatteras were known only to the canoe men who fished them.

English ships of the Roanoke voyages began calling here in 1585, but settlement waited until the 1690s, when English farmers and French Huguenots took up the Pamlico River. Bath, chartered on 8 March 1705, was the first town in North Carolina and prospered on naval stores, furs and tobacco. A smallpox 'great mortality' of 1696 shattered the Pamlico, and by 1710 John Lawson found them living in one small village of perhaps fifteen fighting men. On 22 September 1711 the southern Tuscarora, with the Pamlico and other allies, struck Bath, New Bern and the plantations along the Neuse and Trent rivers, opening the Tuscarora War; Lawson was among the killed and more than a hundred settlers died in the New Bern raids. The pirate Blackbeard took the king's pardon at Bath in 1718, only to be hunted down and killed by Lieutenant Robert Maynard at Ocracoke Inlet on 22 November 1718. Rebuilt New Bern became the colony's capital in 1770 and held the seat until 1792.
zh:
帕姆利科河与帕姆利科湾水面平静，外滩群岛如长堤横在外面，挡住大西洋的风浪。这里是波莫伊克（帕姆利科）人的土地，他们操卡罗来纳阿尔冈昆语，雷利的手下1585年把他们记作「波莫伊」。他们在河畔田地里种玉米和豆子，在湾中捕捞西鲱和鲱鱼，与语言相通、贸易往来的克罗阿坦人、马查邦加人和塞科坦人共用各处水口和浅滩。1444年，欧洲人的船帆还没有出现在海平线上；后来被标作沃科康和哈特勒斯的水道口，那时只有打鱼的独木舟船夫知晓。

1585年起，罗阿诺克远航的英国船只开始在此停靠，但真正的殖民要等到1690年代——英格兰农户和法国胡格诺教徒陆续迁居帕姆利科河畔。1705年3月8日获许建城的巴斯是北卡罗来纳第一座城镇，靠柏油松脂、毛皮和烟草兴旺起来。1696年一场被称为「大死亡」的天花重创帕姆利科人，到1710年，约翰·劳森发现他们只剩一个小村子，能作战的人不过十五名上下。1711年9月22日，南部图斯卡罗拉人联合帕姆利科等盟邦袭击巴斯、新伯尔尼以及纽斯河、特伦特河沿岸的种植园，图斯卡罗拉战争爆发；劳森也在遇害者之列，新伯尔尼一带有一百多名殖民者被杀。海盗黑胡子1718年在巴斯接受国王赦免，却在同年11月22日于奥克拉科克水口被罗伯特·梅纳德中尉追上击毙。战后重建的新伯尔尼1770年成为殖民地首府，一直延续到1792年。

en:
The Pennyrile is a rolling karst tableland between the lower Cumberland and the Green, its limestone split by sinkholes, springs and river caves. In 1444 it was the southern ground of the Shawnee, whose bark-covered houses and cornfields stood in the bottoms and whose hunters followed deer and bison to the salt licks; the lower Cumberland would later appear on French maps as the Rivière des Chaouanons, the River of the Shawnee. No European had yet set eyes on the Green or the Cumberland.

In the 1670s Iroquois raids waged for the fur trade drove the Shawnee out of Kentucky, leaving the tableland to passing Cherokee and Chickasaw hunting parties, and by the 1680s French canoes on the Mississippi had marked the Cumberland's mouth as the Shawnee River. In 1750 Thomas Walker crossed the mountains to the south-east and gave the Cumberland its name. Long hunters followed him: in 1766 James Smith's party traced the Cumberland all the way down to the Ohio through this country, and in 1769 Kasper Mansker, Isaac Bledsoe and Uriah Stone returned to mark its licks and trails. The Treaty of Sycamore Shoals in 1775 brought the tableland within Richard Henderson's Transylvania purchase, and settlers' stations began to take root. In 1797 tradition places a hunter named Houchin chasing a wounded bear into a vast cave mouth on the Green; Valentine Simon registered the land in 1798 and worked its saltpeter, and in July 1812 Charles Wilkins and Hyman Gratz bought the cave and mined calcium nitrate there on an industrial scale with seventy slaves, feeding the gunpowder mills of the War of 1812.
zh:
卡斯基南波（彭尼罗尔）是坎伯兰河下游与格林河之间一片起伏的喀斯特台原，石灰岩上遍布落水洞、泉眼和溶洞。1444年，这里是肖尼人南部的活动之地：他们树皮为顶的房屋和玉米地坐落在河谷低地，猎手追逐鹿和野牛前往盐渍地；下游的坎伯兰河后来在法国人的地图上被标作「肖尼人之河」。此时格林河与坎伯兰河还不曾被欧洲人看见。

1670年代，为毛皮贸易而来的易洛魁袭掠把肖尼人逐出肯塔基，台原上只剩切罗基和奇克索的猎手往来；到1680年代，密西西比河上的法国独木舟已把坎伯兰河口记作肖尼人之河。1750年，托马斯·沃克在东南方向翻山而过，为坎伯兰河命名。随后而来的是「长猎人」：1766年詹姆斯·史密斯的队伍沿坎伯兰河一直探到俄亥俄河口，1769年卡斯珀·曼斯克、艾萨克·布莱德索和尤赖亚·斯通又来到这里，记下沿途的盐渍地和小径。1775年的锡卡莫尔浅滩条约把台原纳入理查德·亨德森的特兰西瓦尼亚购置，移民据点开始扎下根。1797年，据传一个姓霍钦的猎人追一头受伤的熊，追到了格林河畔一个巨大的洞口；1798年瓦伦丁·西蒙登记这块土地并开采硝石，1812年7月查尔斯·威尔金斯和海曼·格拉茨买下洞穴，驱使七十名奴隶大规模开采硝酸钙，为1812年战争的火药厂供料。

en:
Kentahke is the flat western end of Kentucky, where prairie-like barrens and Green River bottoms slope toward the Ohio and Mississippi. From about 1000 Mississippian farmers built mound towns in this country; Wickliffe, occupied until about 1350, had two large platform mounds around a plaza, a hereditary chief, maize stores and trade links reaching Wisconsin, North Carolina and the Gulf of Mexico. As those Angel-phase chiefdoms declined and reorganized, the land was not emptied. In 1444 Native hunters, farmers and traders still knew its trails, cane flats and river landings, though no European had mapped the country later glossed as “at the field” or “on the prairie.”

By the sixteenth century the Algonquian-speaking Kispoko controlled much of the interior. The Beaver Wars of 1640–1680 displaced Mascouten and Kispoko groups, with Kispoko survivors merging into the Shawnee; epidemics and fur-trade wars explain why later travelers found few large towns rather than the country having always been only a hunting ground. Thomas Walker and Christopher Gist surveyed Kentucky in 1750 and 1751, and the 1768 Treaty of Fort Stanwix opened the floodgate of colonial claims. In 1780 George Rogers Clark built Fort Jefferson near the Ohio's mouth without Chickasaw consent; Chickasaw resistance forced its abandonment in June 1781. Veterans took claims along the Green River after the Revolution, and Kentucky became a state in 1792, but the western tip remained Chickasaw land until Andrew Jackson and Isaac Shelby signed the Treaty of Tuscaloosa on 19 October 1818. The United States promised $300,000 over fifteen years, and by 1821 surveyors and settlers were entering the purchased plains.
zh:
肯塔基是肯塔基西部的平坦边地，草原般的贫瘠地与格林河河洲朝俄亥俄河和密西西比河方向倾斜。约1000年起，密西西比文化农民在此建立土墩城镇。威克利夫遗址延续至约1350年，广场周围有两座大型台墩，城镇由世袭首领统治，存有玉米，并与威斯康星、北卡罗来纳和墨西哥湾等地贸易。安吉尔阶段诸邦衰落重组后，这片土地并未空无一人。1444年，原住民猎人、农民和商人仍熟悉这里的小路、藤丛平地和河边登陆点；欧洲人尚未测绘这片后来被解释为「在原野上」「在草地上」的土地。

16世纪时，说阿尔冈昆语的基斯波科人控制着内陆大部。1640年至1680年的海狸战争迫使莫斯科腾人和基斯波科人迁徙，幸存的基斯波科人并入肖尼人。后来旅人少见大镇，是疫病和毛皮战争造成的结果，并非这里从来只是猎场。托马斯·沃克与克里斯托弗·吉斯特分别在1750年、1751年测量肯塔基，1768年《斯坦威克斯堡条约》更打开了殖民索地的闸门。1780年，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克未获奇克索人同意，便在俄亥俄河口附近修建杰斐逊堡；奇克索人的抵抗迫使守军于1781年6月弃堡。独立战争后，退伍军人沿格林河领取土地，肯塔基本身在1792年建州，但西端仍属奇克索人，直到安德鲁·杰克逊与艾萨克·谢尔比在1818年10月19日签订《塔斯卡卢萨条约》。美国承诺在十五年内支付三十万美元，到1821年，测量员和定居者已开始进入这片购得的平原。

en:
Ouasioto was an older name for the forested Cumberland ridge country on the eastern edge of Kentucky. The Shawnee called the river winding out of these mountains Wasioto, and hunters followed its valleys and the high gap where Kentucky, Virginia and Tennessee meet. In 1444 there was no European town or frontier here; the ridges were a country of game, furs and native trails, linked to the Chisca and Yuchi peoples later met by Spanish expeditions near the upper Tennessee.

Abraham Wood's Virginia traders left the earliest written report of the Cumberland Gap in the 1670s. Thomas Walker explored the pass in 1750 and gave the Cumberland name to the river and mountains. In March 1775 Richard Henderson's Transylvania Company purchased Cherokee lands beyond the mountains and sent Daniel Boone to mark the Wilderness Road through the gap. Boone's trace opened southeastern Kentucky to packhorse settlers, while Cherokee raids during the wars of 1776–1794 made the route a war path as well. After the Treaty of Tellico Blockhouse in 1794, the road was improved for wagons in 1796, by which time tens of thousands of migrants were crossing into Kentucky.
zh:
奥瓦西奥托是肯塔基东部森林茂密的坎伯兰山岭一带的旧称。肖尼人把从群山中流出的大河叫作瓦西奥托，猎人们沿河谷穿行，并利用肯塔基、弗吉尼亚和田纳西交界处的高山隘口往来。1444年时，这里还没有欧洲人的城镇或边界，山岭间是猎物、毛皮和原住民小路交织之地，与后来西班牙人在田纳西河上游遇到的奇斯卡人和尤奇人联系在一起。

17世纪70年代，亚伯拉罕·伍德派出的弗吉尼亚商人留下了关于坎伯兰峡的最早文字记录。1750年，托马斯·沃克探查这个隘口，并把坎伯兰之名带给河流与群山。1775年3月，理查德·亨德森的特兰西瓦尼亚公司购买山外的切罗基土地，派丹尼尔·布恩标出穿过隘口的荒野之路。布恩开辟的小径让驮马移民得以进入肯塔基东南部；1776年至1794年的切罗基战争中，这条路也成了行军和袭掠之路。1794年《特利科堡条约》后，道路于1796年拓宽到可通行马车，此时已有数以万计的移民翻山进入肯塔基。

en:
Waayaahtanwa is the middle Wabash country of the Wea, whose Miami-Illinois name means the people of Waayaahtanonki, the 'place of the whirlpool'. In 1444 their bark-covered lodges and cornfields occupied wooded bottoms between present Terre Haute and Logansport, above the later town of Ouiatenon near Lafayette. The river carried canoes toward the Ohio and the Mississippi, while trails linked them with the Miami, Piankeshaw, Pepikokia and Illini. They were then wholly beyond the reach of French traders or missionaries.

The Wea first appear in written records in 1673. After the disruptions of the Beaver Wars, French firearms and trade helped Miami-speaking bands reoccupy the Wabash, and in 1717 François Picote de Beletre built Fort Ouiatenon as a fur post and barrier against English expansion. Wea villages faced the French settlement, and by the mid-eighteenth century Ouiatenon was the hub of five Wea and two Kickapoo villages. Wea, Kickapoo and Mascouten warriors seized the post without bloodshed on 1 June 1763 during Pontiac's War. American militia under Charles Scott burned Ouiatenon in June 1791, and the Wea made peace in the 1795 Treaty of Greenville. On 7 November 1811 William Henry Harrison destroyed Prophetstown on the nearby Tippecanoe, breaking Tecumseh's confederacy; the 1818 Treaty of St Mary's ceded most Wea lands, and in 1820 the band agreed to leave the Wabash for Missouri and Arkansas.
zh:
瓦亚坦瓦是韦阿人在沃巴什河中游的土地；他们的迈阿密—伊利尼语自称瓦亚坦瓦（Waayaahtanwa），来自瓦亚塔农基（waayaahtanonki），意为「漩涡之地的人」。1444年，他们覆着树皮的屋舍和玉米田分布在今特雷霍特至洛根斯波特之间林木繁茂的河漫滩，下临后来乌亚塔农（Ouiatenon）和拉斐特所在的河段。沃巴什河的独木舟可通向俄亥俄河与密西西比河，陆路则把他们与迈阿密人、皮安克肖人、佩皮科基亚人和伊利尼人相连。那时法国商人和传教士还完全没有到过这里。

韦阿人最早在1673年出现于文字记载。海狸战争造成流徙后，法国火器与贸易帮助说迈阿密语的各支重回沃巴什河；1717年，弗朗索瓦·皮科特·德·贝莱特尔在此修建乌亚塔农堡，作为毛皮贸易站和阻挡英国扩张的据点。韦阿村落与法国聚落隔河相对，到18世纪中叶，乌亚塔农已成为五个韦阿村落和两个基卡普村落的中心。1763年6月1日，韦阿、基卡普和马斯库滕战士在庞蒂亚克战争中兵不血刃夺取据点。1791年6月，查尔斯·斯科特率领的美国民团焚毁乌亚塔农，韦阿人随后在1795年《格林维尔条约》中和谈。1811年11月7日，威廉·亨利·哈里森在附近的蒂珀卡努摧毁先知镇，瓦解特库姆塞联盟；1818年《圣玛丽斯条约》割让大部分韦阿土地，1820年这支人同意离开沃巴什，迁往密苏里和阿肯色。

en:
In the fifteenth century the rivers at the head of the Maumee were Atchakangouen country. This Miami band, later called the Crane band, planted maize in the bottomlands, hunted beaver and deer in the woods, and kept a short portage from the Maumee to the Little River. That carry linked Lake Erie with the Wabash and the Mississippi. Kekionga, their principal village, stood where the Saint Joseph and Saint Marys join to form the Maumee, on the edge of the Great Black Swamp. In 1444 Europeans had not yet entered the country, and furs, food, and shell ornaments moved along older Miami trade paths.

French missionaries first found Miami bands around western Lake Michigan in the mid-seventeenth century, after the Beaver Wars had driven them west from Indiana. French firearms and trade helped the Atchakangouen return to the Maumee about 1700, and Jean-Baptiste Bissot de Vincennes established a post and fort at Kekionga in 1704. Smallpox emptied the village for a year in 1733. In 1749 the pro-British chief Memeskia, called La Demoiselle, broke away to found Pickawillany; the French rebuilt Fort Miamis in 1752 and their Native allies destroyed the rival town. Kekionga joined Pontiac's rising in 1763, accepting British posts by 1765. In 1780 Little Turtle destroyed Augustin de La Balme's raiders near the village. His Western Confederacy defeated Josiah Harmar in 1790 and Arthur St. Clair in 1791, but Anthony Wayne's victory at Fallen Timbers in 1794 opened the way to Fort Wayne. The Treaty of Greenville in 1795 took the portage, while the Maumee and Saint Mary's treaties of 1817 and 1818 ceded the country around the fort and south of the Wabash to the United States.
zh:
15世纪时，莫米河源头一带的河汊是阿恰坎戈恩人的土地。这个迈阿密支派后来被称为鹤部，在河畔低地种植玉米，在林中猎取河狸与鹿，并控制着从莫米河到利特尔河的短途陆运。这条水陆联运道把伊利湖、沃巴什河与密西西比河连接起来。他们的主要村落凯基翁加位于圣约瑟夫河与圣玛丽斯河汇成莫米河之处，紧邻大黑沼泽边缘。1444年时欧洲人尚未进入此地，毛皮、粮食和贝饰仍沿着迈阿密人更古老的商路往来。

17世纪中叶，法国传教士最初在密歇根湖西岸见到迈阿密诸部；此前海狸战争已把他们从印第安纳驱向西方。约1700年，依靠法国火器与贸易，阿恰坎戈恩人回到莫米河流域，让—巴蒂斯特·比索·德·万塞讷于1704年在凯基翁加设立贸易站和堡垒。1733年，天花使村民撤离村落一年。1749年，亲英的首领梅梅斯基亚（人称拉·德穆瓦泽勒）另立皮卡维兰尼；法国人1752年重建迈阿密堡，其原住民盟友随即摧毁这座竞争村镇。凯基翁加1763年参加庞蒂亚克起义，到1765年接受英国商站。1780年，「小乌龟」在村落附近击溃奥古斯丁·德·拉尔姆的袭击队。他的西部联盟1790年击败乔赛亚·哈马尔、1791年击败阿瑟·圣克莱尔，但安东尼·韦恩1794年在福伦廷伯斯获胜，为韦恩堡打开道路。1795年《格林维尔条约》夺走陆运道，1817年和1818年的《莫米条约》与《圣玛丽斯条约》又把堡垒周围及沃巴什河以南土地割让给美国。

en:
The lower Michigan peninsula stretches between Lake Michigan and Lake Huron, its southern prairies and oak openings cut by rivers running west to the lake. In 1444 this is Algonquian country, and the Bodéwadmi — the Potawatomi, 'keepers of the fire' and youngest brother of the Council of Three Fires with the Ojibwe and Odawa — hold its southwestern reaches, with Mascouten and Miami neighbours beyond. Their bands live in bark-mat lodges, raising maize, beans and squash in river-bottom fields, spearing fish through winter ice, gathering wild rice and maple sugar as the seasons turn, and taking beaver and deer in the woods. Furs and the native trails that cross the peninsula give the land its place in the wider lake world.

French records first mention the Bodéwadmi in southwestern Michigan, but the Beaver Wars drove them west to Green Bay before Iroquois and Neutral raiders; in 1659 the coureurs de bois des Groseilliers and Radisson passed through the upper lakes on their way to Lake Superior. La Salle built Fort Miami at the mouth of the St. Joseph River in November 1679, and after Claude Allouez's mission of the 1680s a permanent Fort St. Joseph rose near present-day Niles on the lower river in 1691, anchoring the southern Lake Michigan fur trade among Potawatomi and Miami villages. With the Great Peace of 1701 the bands drifted back east: Cadillac founded Detroit that same year, and Potawatomi villages gathered beneath its walls and along the St. Joseph. Faithful allies of France through the colonial wars, they turned on the incoming British garrisons during Pontiac's rising of 1763 and seized Fort St. Joseph, taking every frontier post in the region save Detroit.
zh:
密歇根下半岛伸展于密歇根湖与休伦湖之间，南部草原与橡树林间有一条条向西入湖的河流。1444年，这里是阿尔冈昆人的土地：博德瓦德米克（波塔瓦托米人），意为「守火者」，在与奥吉布瓦人、奥达瓦人结成的「三火议会」中排行幼弟，据有半岛西南部，东北与马斯库滕人、迈阿密人为邻。他们住在树皮席小屋组成的村落，在河畔低地种玉米、豆类和南瓜，冬季凿冰叉鱼，按季节采集野米、熬制枫糖，在林中猎取河狸与鹿。毛皮和纵贯半岛的古道，使这片土地在大湖族群的交往网络中占有一席之地。

法国文献最早提到博德瓦德米克人时，他们住在密歇根西南部；河狸战争中，为躲避易洛魁人与中立联盟的攻掠，他们西撤到格林贝一带，1659年德·格罗塞耶与拉迪松即经上游大湖前往苏必利尔湖。1679年11月，拉萨尔在圣约瑟夫河口修筑迈阿密堡；1680年代阿卢埃神父传教后，1691年永久性的圣约瑟夫堡在河流下游、今奈尔斯附近设立，成为密歇根湖南部毛皮贸易的支柱，堡周是博德瓦德米克人与迈阿密人的村庄。1701年《蒙特利尔大和约》后，各部陆续东归；同年卡迪亚克建立底特律，博德瓦德米克人的村庄聚到城墙脚下与圣约瑟夫河畔。在历次殖民地战争中他们始终与法国结盟，1763年趁庞蒂亚克起兵转而攻打新来的英国驻军，攻克圣约瑟夫堡，湖区一带的边疆据点除底特律外尽数落入其手。

en:
Michigami takes its name from the Anishinaabe word for the great lake at its western edge, but this province is the river country behind that shore: forest and oak openings drained west by the Grand River, called Owashtanong by the Odawa and later La Grande Rivière by the French. In 1444 its trails belong to the Anishinaabe lake world, where Bodéwadmi (Potawatomi) bands and Mascouten neighbours move between hunting camps and river-bottom fields. They raise maize, beans and squash, take sturgeon and whitefish, gather wild rice and maple sugar, and trap beaver.

The Beaver Wars of the mid-seventeenth century scattered the peninsula's villages, and by the late 1600s Odawa bands had settled the Grand River rapids and the later sites of Grand Rapids, Lowell and Lyons. French voyageurs followed the lake-and-river route, yet the valley remained Indigenous fur country long after France ceded Michigan to Britain in 1763 and Britain withdrew from the lower lake posts in 1796. In 1806 Joseph and Madeline La Framboise opened the first trading post in West Michigan near the mouth of the Thornapple; after Joseph was killed that autumn, Madeline, whose mother was Odawa, maintained and expanded the business. By 1810 Chief Noonday's village at the rapids held about 500 Odawa. He fought beside Tecumseh at the Thames in 1813, and in 1821 the Odawa, Ojibwe and Potawatomi signed the Treaty of Chicago, ceding Michigan lands south of the Grand River to the United States.
zh:
密歇加米得名于阿尼什纳比语中对西边大湖的称呼；这个省份写的却是湖岸背后的河乡：林地与橡树草原之间，格兰德河向西汇水入湖。奥达瓦人称它奥瓦什塔农，法国人后来称它「大河」。1444年，这里的陆路属于阿尼什纳比人的大湖世界，波塔瓦托米游群与马斯库滕邻人往来于猎营和河畔田地之间。他们种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，捕捞鲟鱼和白鱼，按季节采集野米、熬制枫糖，并猎捕河狸。

17世纪中叶的河狸战争打散了下半岛村落；到17世纪末，奥达瓦游群已在格兰德河急流一带，以及后来大急流城、洛厄尔和莱昂的位置建立村庄。法国船夫沿着湖河航路而来，但即使法国在1763年把密歇根割让给英国、英国又于1796年撤出下游湖堡，河谷仍长期由原住民掌控毛皮贸易。1806年，约瑟夫与马德琳·拉弗朗布瓦兹在山楂河注入格兰德河处附近设立西密歇根最早的贸易站；同年秋天约瑟夫遇害后，母亲为奥达瓦人的马德琳继续经营并扩展生意。到1810年，诺戴酋长在急流边的村庄约有五百名奥达瓦人。1813年，他随特库姆塞参加泰晤士河战役；1821年，奥达瓦人、奥吉布瓦人和波塔瓦托米人签订《芝加哥条约》，把密歇根领地内格兰德河以南的土地割让给美国。

en:
In the fifteenth century Hotaawathipi was the northwestern Ohio country between the Maumee and Sandusky rivers, where oak ridges and prairie islands rose out of the Great Black Swamp and the waters drained north to Lake Erie. Miami-speaking bands used the higher ground for camps and maize fields, taking fish, waterfowl, beaver and deer from marsh and forest. River trails linked them with Kekionga to the west, Lake Erie to the north, and Shawnee country farther south. In 1444 no European fort or mission stood there; the region remained an Indigenous world of village councils, hunting grounds and old exchange paths.

During the Beaver Wars, Iroquois raiding turned much of the Ohio Country into a contested fur ground, and Miami bands returned only with French support around 1700. In 1738 a Wyandot band from Detroit moved to Sandusky Bay; Nicholas Orontony's followers founded Junundat about 1740 and welcomed British traders. The English post built there in 1745 was the first European fort in the Ohio Country, but it and the village were soon abandoned. Reoccupied in the 1750s, the Sandusky towns sided with France in the French and Indian War and rose with Pontiac in May 1763, when Wyandots seized Fort Sandusky. The village was burned in reprisal and the people moved up the Sandusky River. Upper Sandusky became their principal town, and Native delegates met there in September 1783 to organize the confederacy that fought the Northwest Indian War. Anthony Wayne's victory at Fallen Timbers in 1794 and the Treaty of Greenville in 1795 opened the country to American forts and settlement, while the Treaty of Fort Meigs in 1817 confined the Wyandot to a reservation around Upper Sandusky.
zh:
15世纪时，霍塔瓦西皮是俄亥俄西北部莫米河与桑达斯基河之间的土地，橡树林高岗和草原岛屿从大黑沼泽中隆起，河水向北注入伊利湖。操迈阿密语的群体在较高处设立营地、种植玉米，从沼泽与森林中获取鱼、水禽、河狸和鹿。河路把他们同西边的凯基翁加、北边的伊利湖以及更南方的肖尼人地区连接起来。1444年时这里还没有欧洲人的堡垒或传教站，仍是村落议事会、猎场和古老交换道路构成的原住民世界。

河狸战争期间，易洛魁人的袭掠使俄亥俄地区大部分成为各方争夺的毛皮猎场，迈阿密诸部直到约1700年才在法国支持下返回。1738年，一支怀安多特人从底特律迁往桑达斯基湾；尼古拉·奥龙托尼的追随者约1740年建立朱嫩达特（Junundat）村，并接纳英国商人。英国人1745年在那里设立的商站是俄亥俄地区第一座欧洲人堡垒，但商站和村落不久都被放弃。18世纪50年代村落重新有人居住，桑达斯基诸镇在法国—印第安人战争中支持法国，又在1763年5月随庞蒂亚克起事，怀安多特人袭取桑达斯基堡。村落随后被报复焚毁，居民沿桑达斯基河上迁。上桑达斯基成为他们的主要村镇，1783年9月，原住民代表在那里集会，筹组后来投身西北印第安战争的联盟。安东尼·韦恩1794年在福伦廷伯斯获胜，1795年《格林维尔条约》为美国堡垒和定居者打开这一地区；1817年《梅格斯堡条约》又把怀安多特人限制在上桑达斯基周围的保留地内。

en:
Kentaientonga was the western Erie country around Presque Isle Bay, where a sandy peninsula almost enclosed one of the finest anchorages on Lake Erie. These Iroquoian villagers, whom French sources would call the Cat Nation, lived in palisaded towns and raised maize, beans and squash on the Erie Plain, while hunting deer and beaver in the woods behind the shore. Trails ran south from the bay toward the Allegheny portages and the Ohio headwaters. In 1444 Europeans had not seen the peninsula, and the fur rivalries of the next century still lay ahead.

War with the Haudenosaunee began in 1653; in 1654 about 1,800 Iroquois warriors destroyed Rique, the largest Erie town near modern Erie, and by 1656 the Erie had ceased to be a separate people, most survivors being adopted into Seneca communities. French soldiers returned to the shore in summer 1753, building Fort Presque Isle at the northern end of the Venango Path, the first post in their Ohio Country chain. They burned it after losing Fort Niagara in 1759; the British rebuilt it, only to lose it on 19 June 1763, when about 250 Ottawas, Ojibwas, Wyandots and Senecas overwhelmed the garrison during Pontiac's War. Pennsylvania bought the Erie Triangle in 1792, Americans laid out Erie and built a new blockhouse in 1795, and in 1813 Oliver Hazard Perry used the sheltered bay to prepare the squadron that won the Battle of Lake Erie.
zh:
肯泰恩通加是普雷斯克岛湾周围的伊利人西部土地，沙质半岛几乎围住伊利湖上最好的锚地之一。这些说易洛魁语的村民后来被法国文献称为「猫族」，住在栅栏村镇中，在伊利平原种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，也在湖岸后方林地猎鹿与河狸。小径从湖湾南通向阿勒格尼水陆联运道和俄亥俄河源。1444年时欧洲人尚未见过这座半岛，下一个世纪的毛皮争夺也还未到来。

与豪德诺索尼的战争始于1653年；1654年，约一千八百名易洛魁战士摧毁了今伊利附近最大的伊利人村镇里克（Rique），到1656年伊利人已不再是独立族群，多数幸存者被塞内卡社群接纳。1753年夏，法军回到这片湖岸，在韦南戈通道北端修建普雷斯克岛堡，这是他们俄亥俄堡垒链的第一座据点。1759年失去尼亚加拉堡后，法军烧毁该堡；英军将其重建，却又在1763年6月19日失去它，庞蒂亚克战争中约二百五十名渥太华、奥吉布瓦、怀安多特和塞内卡战士攻陷堡垒。宾夕法尼亚1792年购得伊利三角地，美国人1795年规划伊利镇并修建新木堡；1813年，奥利弗·哈泽德·佩里利用这个受庇护的湖湾装备舰队，最终赢得伊利湖战役。

en:
Ohiyo names the upper Ohio's passage through wooded hills where western Pennsylvania gives way to the Virginia frontier. In 1444 this was late Fort Ancient country, a river world that historical memory would connect with the Shawnee. Bark-covered villages and maize fields occupied fertile bottoms; canoes carried shell, tobacco, furs and people between the Mississippi system and trails climbing toward the Alleghenies, while hunters took deer and turkey in the hills. No European had yet mapped the river that the Seneca would call Ohi:yo', the Good River.

Virginian parties brought back the first reports of the valley in the trans-Appalachian expeditions of 1671 and 1673–74, and Arnout Viele traveled from the Allegheny to Shawnee towns on the Ohio in 1692–93. Gaspard-Joseph Chaussegros de Léry made the first French river survey in 1729; in 1749 Céloron de Blainville buried a lead plate at Wheeling Creek to proclaim France's claim. After Britain won the Ohio Country, the 1768 Treaty of Fort Stanwix made the Ohio the southern boundary of Native territory, but Virginia frontiersmen kept crossing. Ebenezer Zane settled the Wheeling bottom in 1769, and Fort Fincastle, soon renamed Fort Henry, was built in June 1774 during Dunmore's War. Shawnee, Wyandot and Mingo fighters besieged it in 1777 and returned with British support in 1782, when Betty Zane carried powder from her family's blockhouse to save the garrison. The river became the Northwest Territory's southern edge in 1787, and in 1818 the National Road reached Wheeling, tying the Ohio landing to the Potomac.
zh:
俄亥俄（Ohiyo）指上俄亥俄河穿过林木丘陵的一段，即西宾夕法尼亚转入弗吉尼亚边疆之地。1444年，这里属于晚期堡古文化圈，是历史记忆常与肖尼人联系起来的河上世界。树皮屋村落和玉米地占据肥沃河洲，独木舟转运贝壳、烟草、毛皮和人员，把密西西比水系与通向阿勒格尼山脉的小路连接起来，猎人则在丘陵间猎鹿与火鸡。欧洲人尚未测绘这条后来被塞内卡人称为俄希约（Ohi:yo'，意为「好河」）的大河。

弗吉尼亚探险队在1671年、1673年至1674年的跨阿巴拉契亚行动中最早传回河谷消息；1692年至1693年，阿尔瑙特·维勒从阿勒格尼河进入俄亥俄河畔的肖尼村镇。加斯帕尔—约瑟夫·肖斯格罗·德·莱里1729年完成法国人的首次河道测绘；1749年，塞洛隆·德·布兰维尔在惠灵溪口埋下铅牌，宣告法国的领属。英国赢得俄亥俄地区后，1768年《斯坦威克斯堡条约》把俄亥俄河定为原住民领地南界，但弗吉尼亚边疆居民仍不断渡河。埃比尼泽·赞恩1769年在惠灵河洲定居；1774年6月邓莫尔战争期间，芬卡斯尔堡建成，不久改名亨利堡。肖尼、怀安多特和明戈战士1777年围攻此堡，1782年又与英军一道再来；贝蒂·赞恩从家族木屋取回火药，使守军支撑下来。1787年，俄亥俄河成为西北领地南界；1818年国家公路通到惠灵，把这个河港与波托马克河连接起来。

en:
The Monacan country is the rolling Virginia piedmont between the falls of the James River and the Blue Ridge Mountains. Its Siouan-speaking people planted corn and beans on the river bottoms, handled the copper that moved along the upland trails, and raised earthen burial mounds above their towns. Their capital Rassawek stood where the Rivanna joins the James, while Mowhemencho guarded the eastern approaches above the falls. Beyond the falls the Algonquian Powhatan were their sworn enemies, and the Monacan held the upland with their kinsmen and allies the Manahoac. In 1444 no European had yet entered their country.

In November 1608 Christopher Newport led forty Jamestown men up the James to the towns of Massinacak and Mowhemencho and carried off a headman to guide them. John Lederer, visiting the same two towns in 1670, found a nation of only about thirty bowmen, already carrying muskets. Their leader Surenough signed the Treaty of Middle Plantation in 1677 after Bacon's Rebellion, and by 1702 the last Monacan had drifted away; Virginia granted their old fields to Huguenot refugees, who founded Manakin town from 1700. The survivors merged with the Nahyssan and Saponi, and as Tutelo-Saponi they were adopted by the Cayuga of the Iroquois in 1753. In 1784 Thomas Jefferson excavated one of their ancient burial mounds on the Rivanna and described it in his Notes on the State of Virginia.
zh:
莫纳坎人的家园在詹姆斯河瀑布线与蓝岭山脉之间起伏的弗吉尼亚皮德蒙特丘陵。这支操苏语的部族在河滩种植玉米和豆类，经营沿山麓小路流通的铜料，并在村镇旁堆起泥土坟丘。首镇拉萨韦克坐落在里瓦纳河汇入詹姆斯河之处，莫赫门乔则扼守瀑布上游的东部门户。瀑布以东说阿尔冈昆语的波瓦坦联盟是世仇，莫纳坎人与北方的亲族盟友马纳霍克人共守这片山地。1444年，还没有任何欧洲人踏入他们的土地。

1608年11月，克里斯托弗·纽波特率领四十名詹姆斯敦移民溯詹姆斯河而上，到达马西纳卡克和莫赫门乔两镇，并掳走一名头人充当向导。1670年约翰·莱德勒重访这两镇时，发现整个部族只剩约三十名弓箭手，而且已经持有火枪。首领萨雷诺夫在1677年培根叛乱后签署了《中种植园条约》，到1702年最后的莫纳坎人已离散而去；弗吉尼亚殖民当局把他们的旧地拨给胡格诺派难民，后者自1700年起建起马金镇。幸存者并入纳赫桑人与萨波尼人，以「图特洛－萨波尼」之名在1753年被易洛魁联盟的卡尤加人接纳。1784年，托马斯·杰斐逊在里瓦纳河畔发掘了他们的一座古坟丘，并写入《弗吉尼亚纪事》。

en:
The Chesepian, whose Algonquian name meant 'the country on a great river', lived where the Elizabeth River meets the Chesapeake Bay, in what is now southern Hampton Roads. Their Late Woodland culture rested on the bay's fish and oysters, with cornfields beyond the marshes, and their town of Skicoak was described to early English visitors as the greatest settlement of the region. In 1444 no European sail had entered the bay, and the Chesepian lived independently, outside the chiefdoms taking shape on the James River.

Philip Amadas, exploring the bay from Roanoke in the winter of 1585-86, found Skicoak a plainer place than native report had promised. Before the English founded Jamestown in 1607, Powhatan destroyed the tribe after his priests warned that a nation rising from the Chesapeake would dissolve his empire; perhaps 350 Chesepian remained in 1607, possibly joined by survivors of the Lost Colony, and by 1669 they existed no longer as a tribe. Planters bought the Elizabeth River shore for tobacco, the House of Burgesses established Norfolk town in 1680, and it was incorporated in 1705. The Battle of Great Bridge in December 1775 drove Governor Dunmore out of the district; his fleet bombarded Norfolk on 1 January 1776, and two weeks later the patriots burned the remaining houses, leaving only the walls of St Paul's Church.
zh:
切萨皮克人的阿尔冈昆语族名意为「大河之畔的地方」，他们住在伊丽莎白河注入切萨皮克湾之处，即今汉普顿锚地南部。他们的晚期林地文化以湾中的鱼蚝为生，沼泽之外广种玉米；村镇斯基科阿克曾被邻人形容为这一带最大的城邑。1444年，欧洲船帆尚未进入海湾，切萨皮克人自成一方，不在詹姆斯河流域正在成形的酋长联盟之内。

1585至1586年冬，菲利普·阿马达斯从罗阿诺克北上探湾，发现斯基科阿克其实远比传闻中平常。1607年英国人建立詹姆斯敦之前，波瓦坦因祭司警告「切萨皮克湾将兴起一个瓦解其帝国的民族」，发兵灭掉了该部；1607年切萨皮克人仅剩约三百五十人，其中或许还收留了「失落殖民地」的幸存者，到1669年他们已不再作为部落存在。种植园主为种植烟草买下伊丽莎白河岸，弗吉尼亚议会1680年设立诺福克镇，1705年建市。1775年12月的大桥战役把总督邓莫尔逐出此地；1776年1月1日他的舰队炮轰诺福克，两周后爱国者又焚毁残存屋舍，唯有圣保罗教堂的四壁留存。

en:
The Kanawha is formed by the confluence of the New and Gauley rivers and winds about 97 miles northwest through the wooded Allegheny Plateau to the Ohio. Early hunters left Clovis points in its valley, Adena communities raised earthen mounds there, and later Fort Ancient farmers occupied bottomland villages including Buffalo and Marmet. In 1444 the river was still a Native corridor of fields, hunting camps and canoe travel, far beyond the recorded knowledge of Europeans.

During the seventeenth century, Haudenosaunee raids from what is now New York dispersed or subjugated Fort Ancient, Wyandot and Conoy-Kanawha communities, and the Haudenosaunee, Lenape and Shawnee came to use the valley chiefly as a hunting ground. In 1671 Abraham Wood sent the Batts and Fallam party into the upper watershed, the first recorded English exploration of the New River. Virginia surveyors were already marking tracts along the Coal River in April 1774, and on 10 October that year Andrew Lewis's militia met Cornstalk's Shawnee and Mingo warriors at the Kanawha's mouth in the Battle of Point Pleasant. Cornstalk withdrew after a hard-fought day, and late-eighteenth-century Virginia land grants near the mouth brought permanent settlement up the valley.
zh:
卡诺瓦河由纽河与高利河汇流而成，在林木覆盖的阿勒格尼高原间向西北蜿蜒约97英里，最终注入俄亥俄河。远古猎人曾在河谷留下克洛维斯尖状器，阿德纳文化社群在此堆筑土墩，后来的古堡文化农民则居住在布法罗、马梅特等河漫滩村落。1444年时，这条河仍是原住民往来耕作、狩猎和乘独木舟穿行的通道，完全不为欧洲人所知。

17世纪，来自今纽约一带的易洛魁军队侵袭并驱散或征服了古堡文化、休伦和科诺伊—卡诺瓦社群，此后易洛魁、莱纳佩与肖尼人主要把这片河谷用作猎场。1671年，亚伯拉罕·伍德派出巴茨和法伦姆小队进入上游流域，这是有记录以来英国人对纽河最早的一次探险。1774年4月，弗吉尼亚测量员已在科尔河沿岸划分土地；同年10月10日，安德鲁·刘易斯率领的民兵在卡诺瓦河口与科恩斯托克率领的肖尼、明戈战士交战，史称波因特普莱森特战役。科恩斯托克在激战后撤退，18世纪末弗吉尼亚在河口附近授地，永久定居点随即沿河谷发展起来。

en:
The broad tidewater peninsulas between the James, York and Rappahannock are Tsenacommacah, the thickly settled country of the Virginia Algonquians. Bark-covered longhouse towns stood beside maize fields renewed by the river floods, and dugout canoes carried fish, oysters and surplus corn through the Chesapeake's inlets; each town obeyed its own weroance or weroansqua. One upstream town at the falls of the James was called Powhatan, a name the English would later give both to its people and to the chief who ruled them. In 1444 these were independent, rivalrous villages, with no sign yet of the paramountcy built in the late 1500s, and no European had yet settled the bay.

That empire was the work of Wahunsenacawh, who inherited six tribes from his mother and by 1607 held more than thirty between the bay and the falls, ruling from Werowocomoco on the York over some 14,000 to 21,000 people. In 1607 the English built Jamestown on his doorstep, and after parleys and corn trade their hunger for tobacco land brought fourteen years of war. John Smith, captured on the Chickahominy in December 1607, was carried before the mamanatowick in the episode his memoirs later tied to Pocahontas. Wahunsenacawh died in 1618, and in March 1622 his brother Opechancanough's warriors fell on the outlying plantations, killing hundreds of settlers; the reprisals destroyed half the confederacy's towns. His last rising, in 1644, ended in 1646 when the aged chief was captured and shot by his guard; the treaty of that year dissolved the confederacy and confined the survivors beyond the York and Blackwater, on some of Virginia's first reservations. A law of 1665 made their chiefs appointees of the governor, and the Treaty of Albany in 1684 marked the confederacy's end. By 1821 only the Pamunkey and Mattaponi still held reservation lands first set aside in the 1600s.
zh:
詹姆斯河、约克河与拉帕汉诺克河之间开阔的潮汐水半岛，是弗吉尼亚阿冈昆人村落密布的家园塞纳科马卡。覆以树皮的长屋城镇旁是借河水泛滥保持肥力的玉米地，独木舟载着鱼、牡蛎和余粮穿行于切萨皮克湾的水汊之间；每座城镇各有自己的首领，男称维罗安斯，女称维罗安斯夸。詹姆斯河瀑布附近一座上游城镇名叫波瓦坦，后来英国人把这个名字同时给了它的居民和统治他们的大酋长。1444年的这些村落彼此独立、时有纷争，16世纪末才建立的最高酋邦此时尚无踪影，海湾边也还没有欧洲人落脚。

这个酋邦是瓦洪苏纳科一手缔造的：他从母亲手中继承六个部落，到1607年已统辖海湾与瀑布线之间的三十多个部族，以约克河畔的韦罗沃科莫科为都，治下约有14,000至21,000人。1607年，英国人就在他眼皮底下建起詹姆斯敦，几番交涉和玉米交易之后，对烟草种植用地的贪欲引发了长达十四年的战争。约翰·史密斯1607年12月在奇克哈莫尼河畔被俘，被带到大酋长面前——他后来在回忆录里把这段经历与宝嘉康蒂联系在一起。瓦洪苏纳科1618年去世；1622年3月，其弟奥普查纳卡诺的战士突袭外围种植园，杀死数百名殖民者，报复行动又摧毁了联盟半数城镇。1644年他发动最后一次起义，1646年这位年迈酋长被俘，遭看守士兵枪杀；同年的条约解散了联盟，幸存者被限制在约克河与布莱克沃特河之外，住进弗吉尼亚最早的一批保留地。1665年的法律规定各部首领改由总督任命，1684年的奥尔巴尼条约标志着联盟彻底终结。到1821年，只剩帕蒙基人和马塔波尼人仍守着17世纪划出的保留地。

en:
Piscataway is the lower Potomac country of southern Maryland, where tidal creeks and marshes meet the western shore of Chesapeake Bay. Its Algonquian-speaking people raised maize, beans, and squash in the river bottoms, fished the shallows, and drew together under hereditary chiefs as pressure from the Susquehannock and other northern peoples increased. The tayac's principal town was Moyaone, on Accokeek Creek above the Potomac. Neighbouring Iroquoians called these people Conoy. In 1444 the Piscataway still controlled the creek mouths, fields, and canoe routes that later colonizers called Piscataway land.

John Smith visited the upper Potomac in 1608 and recorded the people as Moyaons, after their ruler's town. On 25 March 1634 the English ships Ark and Dove reached St Clement's Island; Leonard Calvert's settlers bought ground from the Yaocomico and founded St Mary's, beginning the Catholic Calvert family's Maryland colony. English friendship soon became land pressure: by 1668 western-shore Algonquian communities were confined to two reservations, and after 1680 Piscataway families took shelter at Zekiah Swamp, crossed into Virginia in 1697, and lived on Conoy Island in the Potomac from 1699. During the eighteenth century Maryland extinguished the remaining reservations as tobacco plantations spread along the river.
zh:
皮斯卡塔韦位于马里兰南部的波托马克河下游，感潮河溪与沼泽在此通向切萨皮克湾西岸。说阿尔冈昆语的居民在河滨低地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在浅水捕鱼；随着萨斯奎汉诺克人和北方其他群体压力增大，各村落逐渐团结在世袭首领之下。最高首领塔亚克的主要城镇莫亚翁位于波托马克河畔的阿科基克溪。邻近的易洛魁语族群称他们为科诺伊。1444年时，皮斯卡塔韦人仍控制着后来被殖民者称作皮斯卡塔韦之地的河口、田地和独木舟水路。

约翰·史密斯1608年进入波托马克河上游，根据其首领城镇把这些人记为莫亚翁人。1634年3月25日，英国船只「方舟号」和「鸽子号」抵达圣克莱门特岛；伦纳德·卡尔弗特率领的移民从约科米科人手中购地，建立圣玛丽斯，开启卡尔弗特家族信奉天主教的马里兰殖民地。英国式友谊很快变成土地压力：到1668年，西岸阿尔冈昆社群已被限制在两块保留地内；1680年后，皮斯卡塔韦家族避入泽基亚沼泽，1697年渡波托马克河进入弗吉尼亚，1699年起居住在河中的科诺伊岛。18世纪，随着烟草种植园沿河扩展，马里兰取消了剩余保留地。

en:
The upper Allegheny and French Creek wind through a wooded plateau that formed the southern country of the Erielhonan, the Erie, whom the French called the Cat Nation. These Iroquoian villagers farmed maize, beans and squash around palisaded towns while hunting beaver and deer in the creek bottoms; trails and short portages linked their watershed to Lake Erie. In 1444 Europeans had not entered the valleys, and Erie communities still controlled the furs, crossings and hunting grounds between the lake plain and the Ohio headwaters.

Epidemics and the competition for beaver pelts drew the Erie into the Beaver Wars, and by the mid-1650s they had ceased to be an independent polity; survivors were absorbed into Haudenosaunee communities, after which Shawnee and Iroquois parties contested the Allegheny valley. In 1753 the French occupied Scottish trader John Fraser's post at Venango, a Lenape town at the mouth of French Creek, and secured the Venango route from Lake Erie. Fort Le Boeuf guarded the portage when George Washington reached it that December with Virginia's demand for withdrawal, and Fort Machault was built at Venango in 1754. The French burned both posts in August 1759 after losing Fort Niagara. The British rebuilt the Venango post as Fort Venango in 1760, but it was burned during Pontiac's Rebellion in 1763.
zh:
上阿勒格尼河与弗伦奇溪蜿蜒穿过林木覆盖的高原，这里是伊利霍南人，即伊利人的南部土地，法国人称他们为「猫族」。这些说易洛魁语的村民在栅栏村镇周围种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，也在溪谷猎取河狸与鹿；小径和短途水陆联运把他们的流域与伊利湖连接起来。1444年时，欧洲人尚未进入这些河谷，伊利人仍控制着湖滨平原与俄亥俄河源之间的毛皮、渡口和猎场。

流行病与河狸皮竞争把伊利人卷入海狸战争，到1650年代中期，他们已不再是独立政治实体；幸存者多被豪德诺索尼（即易洛魁）社群吸收，此后肖尼人与易洛魁人又反复争夺阿勒格尼河谷。1753年，法军占领苏格兰商人约翰·弗雷泽在弗伦奇河口莱纳佩村镇韦南戈的商栈，控制了从伊利湖南下的韦南戈通道。同年12月乔治·华盛顿抵达守卫水陆联运线的勒伯夫堡，递交弗吉尼亚要求法军撤退的信函；马绍尔堡则于1754年在韦南戈建成。1759年8月，法军在失去尼亚加拉堡后烧毁两座要塞。英军1760年将韦南戈据点重建为韦南戈堡，但它又在1763年庞蒂亚克战争中被焚毁。

en:
Conestoga is the Susquehanna lowland around the later Conestoga River, where wooded ridges open into fertile flats above Chesapeake Bay. In 1444 this was Susquehannock country in the broad sense, although the Iroquoian-speaking people then lived chiefly in palisaded hamlets on the North Branch, in present northern Pennsylvania and southern New York. Their longhouse communities raised corn, beans and squash, fished the river and used canoe routes through the valley; the southward move that brought fortified towns to the lower Susquehanna came during the next century.

John Smith met Susquehannock warriors near the river mouth in 1608 and described fortified towns able to send out hundreds of men.
