From the 1620s the Susquehannock exchanged beaver pelts for cloth, kettles, axes and, by the 1630s, muskets with Virginian, Dutch and Swedish traders. War with Maryland ended only with a treaty in 1652. Disease and raids then broke their power: after abandoning their Susquehanna town in the 1670s, they suffered a Maryland and Virginia siege in 1675 and the survivors scattered or joined the Iroquois. A remnant returned with Seneca families in the late 1680s and founded Conestoga Town. William Penn's government treated with them in 1701, and Conestoga Manor was surveyed for their use in 1718, but settler encroachment reduced both land and people. By December 1763 only twenty Conestoga remained; Paxton Boys vigilantes killed six at their village on 14 December and slaughtered the fourteen sheltered in Lancaster on 27 December. Settler farms and a small village laid out as Conestoga Centre in 1805 later took their place along the river.
zh:
科内斯托加是萨斯奎哈纳河下游低地，位于后来的科内斯托加河一带，林木覆被的山脊在此展成切萨皮克湾上方的肥沃平地。1444年，广义上这里属于萨斯奎汉诺克人的地域，但这些操易洛魁语的人当时主要住在北支沿岸设有栅栏的村落，也就是今宾州北部与纽约州南部一带。他们的长屋社群种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在河中捕鱼，并利用河谷独木舟路线往来；要到下一个世纪，他们才南迁并在萨斯奎哈纳河下游建立设防城镇。

1608年，约翰·史密斯在河口附近见到萨斯奎汉诺克战士，并记载他们的设防城镇能出动数百人。1620年代起，萨斯奎汉诺克人用河狸皮同弗吉尼亚、荷兰和瑞典商人交换布匹、铜锅、斧头，并在1630年代开始换得火枪。他们与马里兰的战争直到1652年缔约才告结束。随后疫病和突袭削弱了他们的力量：1670年代放弃萨斯奎哈纳河畔城镇后，他们又在1675年遭到马里兰与弗吉尼亚民兵围攻，幸存者四散，或加入易洛魁人。1680年代末，一批遗民同塞内卡家庭返回，建立科内斯托加镇。威廉·佩恩政府于1701年同他们缔约，1718年又勘定供他们使用的科内斯托加庄园，但移民侵夺使土地和人口不断缩减。到1763年12月，科内斯托加人只剩二十名；帕克斯顿帮治安队员于12月14日在村里杀死六人，又于12月27日在兰开斯特杀害受庇护的十四人。此后，移民农场和1805年规划的小村科内斯托加森特沿河岸取代了旧聚落。

en:
Sakimauchheening is the Lenape council ground later written Shackamaxon, on the west bank of the Delaware, called Lënapei Sipu, near its meeting with the Schuylkill. Lenape villages lined the deep river, fished its estuary and used the Great Minquas Path to carry furs toward Susquehannock country; canoes could come up from Delaware Bay to the chiefs' meeting place. In 1444 the councils, crossings and fur traffic at the future Philadelphia riverside remained entirely in Lenape hands, with no European claim on the valley.

Henry Hudson entered the Delaware valley in 1609, and the Dutch later built Fort Beversreede near the Schuylkill mouth to guard the fur route. New Sweden was founded on the lower Delaware in 1638 and contested the trade until Peter Stuyvesant conquered it in 1655; England took the river from the Dutch in 1664. In 1682 Tamanend met William Penn at Shackamaxon to make peace, and Penn laid out Philadelphia between the Delaware and Schuylkill as the capital of his Quaker colony. Its wharves made it a leading colonial port, while the Walking Purchase of 1737 displaced Lenape communities up the Delaware as settlement spread. Independence was declared at Philadelphia on 4 July 1776. After winning at Brandywine on 11 September 1777, William Howe's army entered the city on 26 September and wintered there while Washington's army suffered at Valley Forge; the British evacuated in 1778. The United States Constitution was drafted here in 1787, and Philadelphia served as the republic's temporary capital from 1790 to 1800.
zh:
萨基毛切宁是莱纳佩酋长议事地，殖民者后来写作沙卡马克逊，位于莱纳佩语称作莱纳佩西普的特拉华河与斯库尔基尔河汇流一带。莱纳佩村落依深水河岸而居，在河口捕鱼，并沿大米因夸斯小道把毛皮运往萨斯奎汉诺克人的地方；独木舟可从特拉华湾直达酋长会盟之地。1444年，后来费城所在河岸的议事会、渡口和毛皮贸易仍完全掌握在莱纳佩人手中，欧洲人尚未对河谷提出任何主权要求。

1609年，亨利·哈德孙驶入特拉华河谷，荷兰人后来在斯库尔基尔河口附近修建贝弗斯雷德堡，守护毛皮商路。1638年，瑞典在下游特拉华河畔建立新瑞典并争夺贸易，直到1655年被彼得·施托伊弗桑特征服，英格兰又于1664年从荷兰手中夺取这条河。1682年，塔曼恩德在沙卡马克逊与威廉·佩恩缔和，佩恩随后在特拉华河与斯库尔基尔河之间规划费城，作为贵格会殖民地的首府。码头使费城成为殖民地大港，1737年的《步行购地》又迫使特拉华河上游的莱纳佩社群迁离，英裔定居点随之扩展。1776年7月4日，《独立宣言》在费城通过。1777年9月11日布兰迪万战役获胜后，威廉·豪所部于9月26日入城并在此过冬，华盛顿的军队则在福吉谷苦守；英军于1778年撤离。1787年，美国宪法在这里起草，1790年至1800年费城又成为共和国的临时首都。

en:
The low western shore of Delaware Bay, from the sand-spit of Cape Henlopen to the falls above the future Wilmington, was Unami Lenape country in 1444. Bands of the Turtle, Turkey and Wolf clans kept villages along the bay and the Christina and Brandywine creeks, raising maize, beans and squash on the coastal plain, netting fish in the shallows and hunting inland, while their Algonquian kin the Nanticoke held the creeks farther south. They called the broad river Lenapewihittuk, and no European had yet entered its bay.

Henry Hudson's Half Moon nosed into the bay in 1609. In 1631 the Dutch planted Zwaanendael near Cape Henlopen, the first European settlement in what is now Delaware, and within a year all thirty-two settlers were killed in a quarrel over a Dutch West India Company signboard. Peter Minuit founded New Sweden at Fort Christina in 1638; Peter Stuyvesant built Fort Casimir at New Castle in 1651 and overran the Swedes in 1655, only for an English fleet to take the bay in 1664. In 1682 the Duke of York granted these 'Lower Counties on the Delaware' to William Penn, and from 1704 they kept their own assembly at New Castle. Caesar Rodney's midnight ride to Philadelphia carried Delaware's vote for independence in July 1776, and the skirmish at Cooch's Bridge in 1777 was the only fighting on Delaware soil. On 7 December 1787 Delaware became the first state to ratify the federal Constitution.
zh:
维康蒂斯位于特拉华湾西岸的低地，从亨洛彭角的沙嘴延伸到日后威明顿以北的瀑布线，1444年是乌纳米特拉华人的土地。龟氏、火鸡氏和狼氏氏族的群体在湾岸及克里斯蒂娜溪、布兰迪万溪畔建立村落，在沿海平原种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在浅滩捕鱼、入内陆狩猎；更南边的河湾则属于他们阿尔冈昆语的亲族南蒂科克人。他们把这条宽阔的大河称为莱纳佩希图克，当时还没有欧洲人进入过这片海湾。

1609年，亨利·哈得孙的「半月号」探入湾中。1631年，荷兰人在亨洛彭角附近建立兹瓦南代尔——今特拉华境内第一个欧洲人定居点，不出一年，因一面荷兰西印度公司徽章招牌引起的冲突，三十二名殖民者全数被杀。1638年，彼得·米纽伊特在克里斯蒂娜堡建起新瑞典；1651年彼得·施托伊弗桑特在纽卡斯尔修筑卡西米尔堡，1655年攻灭瑞典殖民地，而1664年一支英国舰队又夺取了海湾。1682年，约克公爵把这片「特拉华下游三县」授予威廉·佩恩，1704年起三县在纽卡斯尔自开议会。1776年7月，西泽·罗德尼星夜驰赴费城，为特拉华投下赞成独立的一票；1777年的库奇桥前哨战是这片土地上唯一的战斗。1787年12月7日，特拉华成为第一个批准联邦宪法的州。

en:
Onodowaga, the Seneca name for the Great Hill People, belonged to the westernmost Iroquoian nation south of Lake Ontario. In 1444 its palisaded towns stood between the Genesee River and Canandaigua Lake, with longhouses set among fields of corn, beans and squash and hunting camps reaching toward the Allegheny. The rivers and the Seneca Trail linked the villages to fur-bearing forests and western raiding paths, making this country the western doorway of the Iroquoian world long before Europeans saw it.

Dutch and later English trade drew the Seneca deeper into the Beaver Wars, and captives taken in mourning raids replaced relatives lost after a smallpox epidemic in 1635. Ganondagan, their principal town, had about 150 longhouses when English visitors reached it in 1677; Jesuits had opened the mission of St. Jacques there in 1668, but rising tension with New France forced them out in 1684. In July 1687 the Marquis de Denonville's French and allied army marched from Irondequoit, burned Seneca towns and destroyed their stores. Most Seneca fought for Britain during the American Revolution, and in 1779 John Sullivan's scorched-earth campaign drove thousands of Haudenosaunee toward Fort Niagara. The 1784 Treaty of Fort Stanwix opened the old country to cession; the Seneca sold lands east of the Genesee in 1788, received peace guarantees in the 1794 Treaty of Canandaigua, and in 1797 sold their western New York lands while retaining reservations.
zh:
奥诺多瓦加（Onodowaga）是塞尼卡人的自称，意为「大丘之人」；他们是安大略湖以南位置最西的易洛魁语族群。1444年，塞尼卡人的栅栏村镇分布在杰纳西河与卡南代瓜湖之间，长屋周围种着玉米、菜豆和南瓜，狩猎营地一直延伸向阿勒格尼方向。河流与塞尼卡小径把各村镇同产毛皮的森林、西侧的征战道路连接起来，使这片土地在欧洲人到来很久以前就是易洛魁世界的西部门户。

与荷兰人、后来的英国人通商后，塞尼卡人更深地卷入海狸战争；1635年天花疫后，他们以「哀悼战争」中掳来的俘虏补入失去的族人。塞尼卡首要村镇加农达甘在1677年已有约一百五十座长屋。耶稣会士1668年在那里建立圣雅克传教站，但与新法兰西的紧张关系在1684年迫使传教士离开。1687年7月，德农维尔侯爵率领法军及原住民盟军从伊龙德夸湾进军，焚毁塞尼卡村镇并破坏储粮。美国独立战争中，多数塞尼卡人站在英国一方；1779年，约翰·沙利文的焦土远征把数千名豪德诺索尼人逼向尼亚加拉堡。1784年的斯坦威克斯堡条约开启了故土割让，塞尼卡人1788年出售杰纳西河以东土地，1794年通过《卡南代瓜条约》获得和平保障，又在1797年出售纽约西部土地，只保留若干保留地。

en:
Gayogohono, the People of the Great Swamp, was the Cayuga country around Cayuga Lake in the Finger Lakes, between Onondaga to the east and Seneca to the west. In 1444 elm-bark longhouses stood beside fields of corn, beans and squash, while the long lake carried canoes through fishing waters rich in salmon and eels. Marshland, oak plains and deer herds gave the towns their name and their food; forest trails linked them to neighboring Iroquoian nations and to the fur country south of the lakes.

In 1656 Cayuga chief Saonchiogwa invited Jesuits Joseph Chaumonot and René Ménard from Onondaga, and their mission of St. Joseph was founded near Goiogouen, the village later called Cayuga Castle. Étienne de Carheil and Pierre Raffeix later served there; in 1671 Raffeix described the plains between the lakes as rich in fish, deer and salt springs. In 1753 the Cayuga took in Tutelo and Saponi refugees, who built Coreorgonel near the southern inlet of Cayuga Lake. During the American Revolution Cayuga allegiances were divided, though most bands who went to war joined the British frontier raids. Sullivan and Clinton's 1779 campaign destroyed Goiogouen on 23 September with its fifteen large longhouses and cornfields, burned Chonodote the next day, and also destroyed Coreorgonel. Survivors fled to other Haudenosaunee towns, the Seneca country or Upper Canada; on 11 November 1794 the Cayuga joined the Treaty of Canandaigua, which recognized Haudenosaunee sovereignty even after the loss of most of the lake country.
zh:
加约戈霍诺（Gayogohono）意为「大沼泽之人」，是卡尤加人在五指湖之一卡尤加湖周围的乡土，东接奥农多加，西连塞尼卡。1444年，榆树皮覆盖的长屋坐落于玉米、菜豆和南瓜田边；狭长的湖泊让独木舟穿行于盛产鲑鱼、鳗鲡的渔场之间。沼泽、橡树林平原和鹿群既解释了族名，也供养着村镇；林间小路把卡尤加人同邻近易洛魁族群、湖泊以南的毛皮产地连接起来。

1656年，卡尤加首领萨翁奇奥格瓦（Saonchiogwa）从奥农多加邀来耶稣会士约瑟夫·肖莫诺和勒内·梅纳尔，圣约瑟传教站在后来被称为「卡尤加堡」的戈约戈恩（Goiogouen）附近建立。艾蒂安·德·卡埃尔和皮埃尔·拉费后来在此传教；1671年，拉费称两湖之间的平原鱼群、鹿群和盐泉都很丰饶。1753年，卡尤加人收留了图特洛人和萨波尼人，后者在卡尤加湖南口附近建立科雷奥戈内尔（Coreorgonel）。美国独立战争时，卡尤加人立场不一，但参战的多数队伍加入了英国支持的边境袭掠。1779年，沙利文与克林顿远征在9月23日摧毁拥有十五座大长屋和大片玉米田的戈约戈恩，次日焚毁乔诺多特（Chonodote），科雷奥戈内尔也被破坏。幸存者逃往其他豪德诺索尼村镇、塞尼卡地方或上加拿大；1794年11月11日，卡尤加人加入《卡南代瓜条约》，虽然湖乡大部已经丧失，条约仍承认豪德诺索尼诸族的主权。

en:
Onondagaono, the People of the Hills, took its name from the ridges above Onondaga Lake and Onondaga Creek. In 1444 its bark longhouses stood among cornfields and fishing waters, with paths crossing between the eastern and western Iroquoian nations. Brine springs rose near the lake, and its outlet led through the Seneca and Oswego rivers toward Lake Ontario, giving the hill towns fish, waterfowl, furs and a place on the northern canoe routes. This central country would later keep the council fire of the Haudenosaunee.

Around 1600 the principal Onondaga town stood near Cazenovia, from 1609 to 1615 near Pompey, and in 1640 it moved toward Manlius. The Jesuit Simon Le Moyne visited in 1654 and learned of the salt springs; in 1656 the French built Sainte-Marie de Gannentaha on Onondaga Lake, but the fortified mission was abandoned in 1658. The principal town moved to Onondaga Creek in 1720 and remained the meeting place of the Grand Council. The Onondaga tried neutrality at the opening of the American Revolution, but on 20 April 1779 Colonel Goose Van Schaick led 558 Continental troops from Fort Stanwix against their settlements, burning about fifty houses and winter stores. Most Onondaga then joined the British, and after the war many followed Joseph Brant to Upper Canada. The Treaty of Canandaigua acknowledged Onondaga land rights in 1794, while settlers around the lake began boiling its brine into salt.
zh:
奥农多高诺（Onondagaono）意为「山丘之人」，得名于奥农多加湖与奥农多加溪上方的丘陵。1444年，这里的榆树皮长屋坐落在玉米田和渔场之间，小路把东部与西部的易洛魁语各族连接起来。湖畔有盐水泉，湖水出口经塞尼卡河、奥斯威戈河通向安大略湖，使这些丘陵村镇获得鱼、水禽、毛皮，并处在北方独木舟商路上。后来，正是在这片居中的土地上燃起了豪德诺索尼联盟的议事火塘。

1600年前后，奥农多加主城在卡泽诺维亚附近，1609年至1615年间位于庞培一带，1640年迁往曼利厄斯附近。耶稣会士西蒙·勒穆瓦纳1654年到访并得知湖畔盐泉；1656年，法兰西人在奥农多加湖畔建立圣玛丽·德·甘嫩塔哈传教据点，但这座设防传教站1658年即遭放弃。主城1720年迁往奥农多加溪畔，并继续作为大议事会集会地。美国独立战争爆发时，奥农多加人曾试图中立，但1779年4月20日，古斯·范·沙伊克上校率领五百五十八名大陆军从斯坦威克斯堡出击，焚毁约五十座房屋和过冬储粮。多数奥农多加人随后加入英国一方，战后许多人随约瑟夫·布兰特前往上加拿大。1794年的《卡南代瓜条约》承认奥农多加人的土地权利；与此同时，湖畔定居者开始煎煮盐水制盐。

en:
Onyo'taaka is the Oneida country around Oneida Lake and the streams that lead toward Lake Ontario, lying between Mohawk lands to the east and Onondaga lands to the west. The Onʌyoteˀa·ká, the People of the Standing Stone, were one of the five nations of the Haudenosaunee, dwelling in bark-covered longhouse towns and farming maize, beans, and squash while fishing and hunting across the lake plain. Their trails met at the Oneida Carry, a short passage between the Mohawk River and the Wood Creek–Oneida Lake waterway. In 1444 this was still a world untouched by European traders; its value lay in cornfields, fishing places, furs, and the Oneida seat between the eastern and western doors of the longhouse.

Dutch and French trade goods reached Iroquoia in the seventeenth century, drawing Oneida hunters into the fur trade and the Beaver Wars. In the early colonial period the nation held roughly six million acres of central New York. Samuel Kirkland began missionary and school work among the Oneida in 1764, and many allied with the American revolutionaries; their warriors fought at Oriskany on 6 August 1777 after the Haudenosaunee had split into British and Patriot factions. In 1780 Joseph Brant's Loyalist and Mohawk volunteers destroyed Kanonwalohale, the principal pro-American Oneida village. The treaties of Fort Stanwix in 1784 and Canandaigua in 1794 were followed by relentless land cessions, while the Oneida Carry was canalized between 1792 and 1803 to carry more commerce toward Oneida Lake. By 1821 settler New York pressed closely around a reduced Oneida homeland.
zh:
奥尼约塔卡是奥奈达人围绕奥奈达湖及通向安大略湖诸水道的家园，东接莫霍克人之地，西连奥农达加人之地。奥奈达人自称奥尼约塔卡（Onʌyoteˀa·ká），意为「立石之人」，是豪德诺索尼五族之一；他们住在树皮覆盖的长屋村镇，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，也在湖原上渔猎。各条小路在奥奈达陆运道汇合，那里是莫霍克河与伍德溪—奥奈达湖水路之间的短途通道。1444年，欧洲商人尚未进入这里，此地的重要性来自玉米田、渔场、毛皮，以及奥奈达人在长屋东门与西门之间的位置。

17世纪，荷兰和法国商货进入易洛魁地区，奥奈达猎人被卷入毛皮贸易和海狸战争。殖民时代早期，奥奈达人在纽约中部保有约六百万英亩土地。塞缪尔·柯克兰1764年开始在奥奈达人中传教和办学，许多人随后与美国革命者结盟；豪德诺索尼联盟分裂为亲英与亲美两派后，奥奈达战士在1777年8月6日参加奥里斯卡尼战役。1780年，约瑟夫·布兰特率领的效忠派与莫霍克志愿军摧毁了亲美奥奈达人的主村卡农瓦洛黑尔。1784年《斯坦维克斯堡条约》和1794年《卡南代瓜条约》之后，土地割让仍接踵而至；1792年至1803年，奥奈达陆运道被改建为运河，更多商货得以运往奥奈达湖。到1821年，纽约定居者已紧紧逼近大幅缩小的奥奈达家园。

en:
The land between the lower Delaware and the sea, from the falls where Trenton now stands down to the dunes of Cape May, was the heart of the Unami-speaking Lenape; they called the country Scheyichbi. Turtle, Turkey and Wolf clans kept shifting villages on the tidewater creeks, tending maize fields, harvesting fish and shellfish from the bay and hunting the pine woods of the interior. In 1444 these bands answered to no outside power, and the only ships they knew were dugout canoes.

Henry Hudson charted this coast in 1609. The Dutch built Fort Nassau, a beaver-trading factorij, near present Gloucester City in 1626, and in 1643 Governor Printz of New Sweden raised Fort Nya Elfsborg on the Salem River, soon abandoned to the mosquitoes that earned it the nickname Fort Mosquito and burned when the Dutch moved against the Swedes in 1651; New Sweden itself fell to Stuyvesant in 1655, and the whole river passed to England in 1664. Quakers bought West Jersey in 1674, planted Salem in 1675 and Burlington in 1677, while East and West Jersey ran as separate proprietorships until the crown reunited them in 1702. In 1758 the colony set aside Brotherton in the Pine Barrens, its first reservation for the remaining Lenape; many families accepted an Oneida invitation and moved to New Stockbridge in 1801. Washington crossed the Delaware to strike Trenton on 26 December 1776 and won again at Princeton on 3 January 1777, while the hard-fought draw at Monmouth in June 1778 earned New Jersey its name of the Crossroads of the Revolution. On 18 December 1787 it became the third state to ratify the Constitution.
zh:
特拉华下游与大海之间的这片土地，从今日特伦顿所在的瀑布地带一直延伸到梅角的沙丘，是操乌纳米语的特拉华人的腹地，他们把这片乡土称作斯海奇比。龟氏、火鸡氏和狼氏氏族在潮汐溪畔迁徙设村，耕种玉米地，从海湾捕捞鱼贝，在内陆的松林里狩猎。1444年，这些群体不受任何外来政权管辖，他们所知的船只是挖空树干做成的独木舟。

1609年，亨利·哈得孙测绘了这段海岸。1626年，荷兰人在今格洛斯特城附近修筑做海狸皮贸易的商站拿骚堡；1643年，新瑞典总督普林茨在塞勒姆河畔建起新埃尔夫斯堡，这座堡垒很快因蚊虫肆虐被弃，得了「蚊子堡」的绰号，1651年荷兰人对瑞典人动手时又被烧毁。新瑞典本身于1655年被施托伊弗桑特征服，整条河在1664年落入英国之手。贵格会1674年买下西泽西，1675年建立塞勒姆、1677年建立伯灵顿；东泽西与西泽西作为两个业主殖民地分治，直到1702年被英王重新合并。1758年，殖民地在松林荒地里为留下的特拉华人辟出布拉泽顿保留地——这是新泽西第一个印第安人保留地；1801年，许多家庭接受奥奈达人的邀请迁往新斯托克布里奇。1776年12月26日，华盛顿渡过特拉华河奇袭特伦顿，1777年1月3日又在普林斯顿获胜；1778年6月的蒙茅斯之战打成惨烈的平手，新泽西由此得到「独立战争的十字路口」之名。1787年12月18日，它成为第三个批准宪法的州。

en:
The west bank of the upper Hudson, above the mouth of Catskill Creek, was the country of the Mechkentowoon, one of the five tribes of the Mahican confederacy. Their longhouse towns stood on the river flats, where women grew maize, beans and squash and men took shad, sturgeon and beaver. Villages at the head of tidewater drew furs from the northern forests, and the carrying places between the Hudson and Connecticut rivers were in Mahican hands. In 1444 no European had yet entered the river; their rivals were the Mohawk, easternmost of the Iroquois, whose towns lay up the Mohawk River to the west.

In September 1609 Henry Hudson traded for furs at Mahican villages just below the site of Albany. Dutch merchants built Fort Nassau on Castle Island in 1614 and replaced it with Fort Orange in 1624. Rivalry over the trade brought war with the Mohawk: in 1626 a Dutch party marching to aid the Mahicans was ambushed near the fort and its commander killed, and by 1629 the Mohawk held the west bank and many Mahicans had crossed the Hudson. The English took New Netherland in 1664 and renamed Fort Orange Fort Albany; they lost the colony to a Dutch fleet in 1673 and recovered it by treaty in 1674. In 1755 the British built Fort William Henry at the south end of Lake George; it fell to Montcalm in 1757 and its surrendered garrison was massacred. Burgoyne's army surrendered at Saratoga in October 1777, and in 1778 the Americans fortified West Point and stretched a great iron chain across the Hudson.
zh:
卡茨基尔溪口以上的哈得孙河上游西岸，是莫希干联盟五部之一马奇坎托文（Mechkentowoon）部的土地。他们的长屋村镇坐落在河畔滩地，妇女种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，男子捕捞西鲱、鲟鱼，猎取河狸；潮水尽头的村镇汇集北方森林的毛皮，哈得孙河与康涅狄格河之间的陆运道也在莫希干人掌握之中。1444年时还没有欧洲人进入这条河；他们的劲敌是西边莫霍克河谷的莫霍克人，即易洛魁诸部最东的一支。

1609年9月，亨利·哈德逊在今奥尔巴尼以南的莫希干村镇以货物换取毛皮。荷兰商人1614年在卡斯尔岛修建拿骚堡，1624年另建奥兰治堡取而代之。毛皮之争演变为与莫霍克人的战争：1626年，一支出堡援助莫希干人的荷兰队伍在要塞附近遇伏，指挥官战死；到1629年莫霍克人已占据西岸，许多莫希干人东渡哈得孙河。1664年英国人夺取新尼德兰，将奥兰治堡改名奥尔巴尼堡；1673年荷兰舰队收复殖民地，1674年依条约再度归英。1755年，英军在乔治湖南端修建威廉·亨利堡；该堡1757年陷于蒙卡尔姆之手，投降的守军随后遭到屠杀。1777年10月伯戈因所部英军在萨拉托加投降；1778年美军在西点筑垒，并在哈得孙河上横亘巨大的铁链。

en:
Kanien'kehaka, the Mohawk country, follows the Mohawk River through the fertile valley between the Adirondack and Catskill highlands, from the Oneida border in the west to the Hudson-Mohawk fork in the east. The Kanien'kehá:ka, People of the Flint Place, were the easternmost of the five Haudenosaunee nations and keepers of the Eastern Door. In 1444 their bark-covered longhouse towns stood above maize fields on the river flats, and hunting and war trails ran north toward the St. Lawrence and east toward Mahican country. Furs, corn, and command of the natural road from the Hudson into Iroquoia gave this valley its strategic weight.

Contact with Europeans began in 1609, when Samuel de Champlain joined a Wendat war party and his firearms struck down Mohawk chiefs near Ticonderoga. The Dutch built Fort Nassau near the Hudson-Mohawk fork in 1614, and after the Mohawks pushed back the Mohicans in 1628 they gained direct access to the European fur trade. Alexandre de Prouville de Tracy's French expedition burned Mohawk towns and food stores in 1666; the peace opened the country to Jesuit missionaries, and converts settled on the St. Lawrence. William Johnson built Fort Johnson about 1749 and moved to Johnson Hall in 1763, making the valley a center of British-Indigenous diplomacy. Most Mohawks supported Britain during the American Revolution, and in October 1780 forces under John Johnson, John Butler, and Joseph Brant burned through the Schoharie and lower Mohawk valleys. Defeat brought dispossession in New York, while the Haldimand Proclamation of 25 October 1784 granted Mohawk refugees land on the Grand River in Canada. By 1821 the old valley was largely a landscape of settler farms and mills.
zh:
卡尼恩凯哈卡是莫霍克人的家园，沿莫霍克河展开，处在阿迪朗达克山地与卡茨基尔山地之间的肥沃河谷中，西接奥奈达边界，东抵哈得孙河与莫霍克河交汇处。卡尼恩凯哈卡（Kanien'kehá:ka）意为「燧石之地的人」，莫霍克人是豪德诺索尼五族中最东的一族，负责守护联盟东门。1444年，他们以树皮覆盖的长屋村镇矗立在河畔玉米田旁，狩猎和征战小路向北通往圣劳伦斯河，向东伸入莫希干人之地。毛皮、玉米以及对哈得孙河通往易洛魁内陆天然通道的控制，使这座河谷举足轻重。

与欧洲人的接触始于1609年，萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰随一支温达特战队行动，在泰孔德罗加附近用火器击杀莫霍克首领。荷兰人1614年在哈得孙河与莫霍克河交汇处附近修建拿骚堡；1628年莫霍克人击退莫希干人后，得以直接进入欧洲毛皮贸易。1666年，亚历山大·德·普鲁维尔·德·特拉西率领法军焚毁莫霍克村镇和粮仓，议和后耶稣会传教士进入此地，皈依者逐渐迁往圣劳伦斯河畔。威廉·约翰逊约1749年修建约翰逊堡，1763年迁入约翰逊厅，使这座河谷成为英国与原住民外交的中心。美国独立战争中，多数莫霍克人支持英国；1780年10月，约翰·约翰逊、约翰·巴特勒和约瑟夫·布兰特率领的部队焚毁斯科哈里和莫霍克河下游谷地。战败导致他们在纽约失去土地，1784年10月25日的《哈尔迪曼德公告》将加拿大格兰德河畔的土地授予莫霍克难民。到1821年，旧日河谷已大多变成定居者的农场和磨坊。

en:
Manhattan is a long island in the Hudson estuary, sheltered by the waters that form New York Harbor. It was part of Lenapehoking, and Lenape-speaking Munsee and Wappinger bands kept villages, fishing stations and maize fields there; their main island trail ran from the northern woods toward the southern landing place later followed by Broadway. In 1444 the harbor knew bark canoes rather than European ships. No foreign fort stood on the shore, and the island's value to its inhabitants lay in fish, shellfish, planted ground and easy passage between the coast and the Hudson valley.

After Henry Hudson visited in 1609, Dutch traders saw that the anchorage could secure the Hudson River beaver trade. A Dutch post was planted on Governors Island in 1624, Fort Amsterdam was begun on southern Manhattan in 1625, and Peter Stuyvesant, appointed director-general in 1647, granted New Amsterdam city rights on 2 February 1653. Four English frigates entered the harbor in 1664 and took the town without a fight, renaming it New York for the Duke of York. The Dutch briefly recovered it as New Orange in 1673, but returned it to England in 1674. During the American Revolutionary War, the Continental Army lost the Battle of Fort Washington on 16 November 1776; the city was damaged by fire during the campaign, and British occupation lasted until 25 November 1783. New York served as the capital of the United States from 1785 to 1790, and by 1810 it had overtaken Philadelphia as the country's largest city. The Commissioners' Plan of 1811 laid its famous street grid over the island.
zh:
曼哈顿是哈德逊河口的一座长岛，受纽约港水域环抱。它原属莱纳佩人的莱纳佩霍京，操莱纳佩语的芒西人和瓦平格尔人各支在这里设有村落、渔场和玉米地；岛上的主要步道从北部林地通往南端渡口，后来的百老汇大道大体沿此线延伸。1444年，港中往来的还只是树皮独木舟，欧洲船舰尚未出现。岸上没有外来堡垒，居民倚重的是鱼、贝类、耕地以及海岸与哈德逊河谷之间便利的水路。

1609年亨利·哈德逊到访后，荷兰商人意识到这个锚地可以控制哈德逊河的河狸皮贸易。1624年，荷兰人在总督岛设立贸易站；1625年，曼哈顿南端开始修建阿姆斯特丹堡。1647年出任总干事的彼得·斯泰弗森特于1653年2月2日授予新阿姆斯特丹城市权利。1664年，四艘英国护卫舰驶入港中，兵不血刃夺取城镇，并按约克公爵的封号改称纽约。荷兰人1673年一度收复，改名新奥兰治，但在1674年又将它交还英国。美国独立战争期间，大陆军在1776年11月16日的华盛顿堡战役后失去曼哈顿；城镇在战役期间遭大火破坏，英国占领一直持续到1783年11月25日。1785年至1790年，纽约是美国首都；到1810年，它已超过费城成为美国最大城市，1811年的《专员计划》为全岛划定了著名的方格街道。

en:
Nipmuc is Nippenet, the freshwater-pond country of central Massachusetts, a rolling inland network of ponds, streams, maize fields, hunting grounds, and trails between the Massachusett coast, Wampanoag and Narragansett country, the Connecticut valley, and the Mahican lands. The Nipmuc were not a single centralized chiefdom but related village bands speaking an Eastern Algonquian language, living in movable wetus and moving between farmland, fishing places, and hunting camps. In 1444 their furs, food, and paths gave them a place among stronger neighboring nations, while the inland ponds and forests remained entirely their own world.

Recorded contact came in 1630, when Nipmuc people carried maize to hungry Boston colonists. The fur and metal trade was followed by epidemics, debt, and land sales. John Eliot began preaching in Massachusett in 1646, Hassanamesit was made a praying town in 1647, and Eliot's Indian Bible appeared in 1663. When King Philip's War began in 1675, many Nipmuc joined Metacom; they struck Brookfield, Sudbury, Bloody Brook, and Lancaster, where the 10 February 1676 raid led by Monoco and Sagamore Sam captured Mary Rowlandson for eleven weeks. Christian Nipmuc were also suspected by the colonists: hundreds from praying towns were interned on Deer Island in the winter of 1675–1676, and many died of cold and hunger. Survivors were killed, sold to the West Indies, exiled, or absorbed into Abenaki, Mahican, and Stockbridge communities. Families who regrouped around Hassanamesit and Chaubunagungamaug saw Hassanamesit shrink from 7,500 to 500 acres by 1727 and Chaubunagungamaug from 200 to 26 acres in 1797. By 1821 their old country had become the towns and farms of central Massachusetts, with small Nipmuc communities holding only fragments of Nippenet.
zh:
尼普马克即尼佩内特，意为「淡水塘之地」，位于马萨诸塞中部，是一片起伏内陆中的池塘、溪流、玉米田、猎场与小路网络，连接马萨诸特海岸、万帕诺亚格和纳拉甘西特之地、康涅狄格河谷以及莫希干人地区。尼普马克人并非一个高度集权的酋邦，而是彼此关联的村社群体，使用东阿尔冈昆语，住在可迁移的圆顶棚屋中，随农地、渔场和猎营轮换生活。1444年，他们的毛皮、粮食和小路使其在周边更强的各部族之间保有位置，而内陆池塘与森林仍完全属于他们自己的世界。

有记载的接触发生在1630年，尼普马克人把玉米运给断粮的波士顿殖民者。毛皮与金属器贸易之后，疫病、债务和土地出售接踵而至。约翰·艾略特1646年开始用马萨诸特语传教，哈萨纳梅西特在1647年被设为祈祷镇，他的印第安语《圣经》于1663年问世。1675年菲利普国王战争爆发后，许多尼普马克人加入梅塔卡姆一方，袭击布鲁克菲尔德、萨德伯里、血溪和兰开斯特；在1676年2月10日的兰开斯特袭击中，莫诺科和萨加莫尔·萨姆的部队俘虏玛丽·罗兰森达十一周。信奉基督教的尼普马克人也遭到殖民者猜疑，数百名祈祷镇居民在1675年至1676年冬被囚禁于迪尔岛，许多人死于寒冷和饥饿。幸存者或被杀、被卖到西印度群岛、被迫流亡，或并入阿贝纳基、莫希干和斯托克布里奇社群。重新聚集在哈萨纳梅西特和乔布纳贡加莫格周围的家族，则眼见哈萨纳梅西特到1727年从7500英亩缩至500英亩，乔布纳贡加莫格也在1797年从200英亩缩至26英亩。到1821年，他们的故土已成为马萨诸塞中部的城镇与农场，尼普马克小社群只保有尼佩内特的零星残土。

en:
Narraganset is the bay country west of Narragansett Bay, from the Providence River toward the Pawcatuck, a shore of salt ponds, tidal inlets, cleared fields and oak woods. In 1444 its Algonquian-speaking people wintered in bark-covered longhouses, moved to coastal camps in summer, farmed and hunted inland, and paddled large dugouts between fishing grounds and neighboring communities. Their sachems drew authority from the western inlets and points of the bay, a country already linked by canoe, trail and exchange before any European ship entered those waters.

Giovanni da Verrazzano visited the bay in 1524 while sailing for France, and Adriaen Block charted it during his 1614 Dutch voyage. The epidemics of 1616-1619 devastated coastal peoples farther south but largely spared the Narragansetts, leaving them unusually strong when English settlement reached their territory in 1635. In 1636 Roger Williams, exiled from Massachusetts Bay, acquired land from sachems Canonicus and Miantonomo and founded Providence Plantations; he learned their language and published A Key into the Language of America in 1643. The Narragansetts joined the English against the Pequots in 1637, but the brutality at Mystic turned them against the alliance. During King Philip's War their neutrality did not spare them: on 19 December 1675 colonial forces stormed their palisaded Great Swamp fort and killed hundreds of non-combatants. The Narragansetts burned Providence on 27 March 1676 before Canonchet was captured and the nation broken; survivors were enslaved or merged with Eastern Niantic communities. In the 1740s the Narragansett Indian Church became a center of conversion, and after King Tom became sachem in 1746 much of the remaining land passed to colonial buyers.
zh:
纳拉甘西特是纳拉甘西特湾西岸的乡土，从普罗维登斯河一直延伸向波卡塔克河，沿岸遍布咸水塘、潮汐湾、开垦地和橡树林。1444年，说阿尔冈昆语的纳拉甘西特人冬季住在树皮覆盖的长屋，夏季迁往海岸营地，在内地农耕狩猎，也划着大型独木舟往来于渔场和邻近社群之间。酋长的权威来自海湾西侧的水口与岬角；在欧洲船只驶入这些水域之前，独木舟、小径和交换网络已把这片土地连成一体。

1524年，为法国效力的乔瓦尼·达·韦拉扎诺到访海湾；1614年，阿德里安·布洛克在荷兰航行中测绘了这里。1616至1619年的疫病重创更南方的沿海族群，却基本没有波及纳拉甘西特人，所以1635年英格兰拓殖抵达时，他们仍相当强盛。1636年，被马萨诸塞湾放逐的罗杰·威廉姆斯从酋长卡诺尼库斯和米安托诺莫手中取得土地，建立普罗维登斯种植园；他学习纳拉甘西特语，并在1643年出版《美洲语言钥匙》。1637年，纳拉甘西特人与英格兰人联手进攻佩科特人，但米斯蒂克屠寨的残酷使他们疏远这一同盟。菲利普王战争期间，中立并未保护他们：1675年12月19日，殖民地军队强攻大沼泽中的木栅要塞，数百名非战斗人员遇害。纳拉甘西特人于1676年3月27日焚毁普罗维登斯，随后卡农切特酋长被俘，族群力量瓦解；幸存者或被卖为奴隶，或并入东尼安蒂克社群。1740年代，纳拉甘西特印第安教会成为传教中心；1746年汤姆酋长继任后，大部分剩余土地转入殖民地买主手中。

en:
The shores of Massachusetts Bay, between the Charles and Neponset rivers beneath the wooded Great Blue Hill, take their name from the Massachusett, the 'people of the great hill'. Their villages stood on the bay's inlets and harbor islands; under sachems they raised maize, beans and squash, took herring and shellfish at their weirs, and spoke Massachusett, an Eastern Algonquian tongue understood along much of the neighboring coast. In 1444 this was among the more thickly settled shorelands of the northeast, its paths and planting grounds long established, and no European had yet been seen there.

European ships began to appear after 1600: Bartholomew Gosnold cruised the coast in 1602, Samuel de Champlain anchored in the harbor in 1605 and traded with its sachems, and John Smith mapped the bay as part of New England in 1614. Then in 1616–19 the 'Great Dying', an epidemic now often identified as leptospirosis spread by shipboard rats, emptied village after village, and smallpox returned in 1633. A short-lived fishing station on Cape Ann, founded in 1623, moved to Naumkeag, soon renamed Salem, in 1626. The Massachusetts Bay Colony received its royal charter in 1629, and in September 1630 John Winthrop's Puritans crossed from Charlestown to the nearly deserted Shawmut Peninsula and named their town Boston. Harvard College was founded nearby in 1636, the first press in English North America began work at Cambridge in 1638, and John Eliot's Massachusett translation of the Bible was printed there in 1663, after many converts had settled in Christian 'praying towns'. King Philip's War of 1675–76 shattered those communities, and in 1692 the Salem witch trials shook the colony's north shore. Boston then became the storm center of quarrel with the crown: the Boston Massacre in 1770, the Tea Party in 1773, and in 1775–76 the Battle of Bunker Hill and the siege that ended only when the British evacuated the town.
zh:
马萨诸塞湾的海岸位于查尔斯河与内邦西特河之间，林木葱郁的大蓝山俯瞰其上，地名来自马萨诸塞人，意为「大山之人」。他们的村落散布在海湾水湾和港中诸岛，在酋长带领下种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，在鱼堰捕捞鲱鱼、采挖贝类，所说的马萨诸塞语属东阿尔冈昆语，邻近海岸的许多族群都能听懂。1444年时，这里是北美东北海岸人烟较稠密的地方之一，小径和玉米田由来已久，欧洲人尚未出现。

1600年以后，欧洲船只陆续到来：巴塞洛缪·戈斯诺尔德1602年沿海航行，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰1605年在港中停泊并与当地酋长交易，约翰·史密斯1614年测绘海湾，把这里标作新英格兰的一部分。1616至1619年的「大死亡」（今人多认为是船上老鼠传播的钩端螺旋体病）使一座座村庄为之一空，1633年天花又至。安角上1623年建立的渔业据点未能持久，1626年迁往瑙姆基格，不久改名塞勒姆。马萨诸塞湾殖民地1629年获得王室特许状；1630年9月，约翰·温思罗普率领清教徒从查尔斯敦渡过海湾，登上几乎荒无人烟的肖马特半岛，将新城命名为波士顿。1636年哈佛学院在附近创立，1638年英属北美的第一台印刷机在坎布里奇开工，1663年印出约翰·艾略特翻译的马萨诸塞语《圣经》；此前许多皈依者已迁入基督徒的「祈祷镇」。1675至1676年的菲利普国王战争摧毁了这些社区，1692年塞勒姆审巫案震动殖民地北岸。此后波士顿成为与王室争端的风暴中心：1770年的波士顿惨案、1773年的倾茶事件，以及1775至1776年的邦克山战役与围城战，最终以英军撤离波士顿告终。

en:
Mahican is the name given here to an Algonquian borderland stretching from the upper Hudson and Lake George country toward the Green Mountains and the upper Connecticut River. Pocumtuk, later Deerfield, was a major Pocomtuc village on rich river intervales, where maize, beans, and squash were grown and the Connecticut supplied fish and water routes. In 1444 Abenaki trails crossed the northern woods, Mohawk war paths entered from the west, and Mahican hunters ranged toward Lake Champlain. Pine timber, furs, river crossings, and the meetings of these nations gave the region its importance before any European town had been planted.

Samuel de Champlain reached Lake Champlain in 1609, opening the valley to French rivalry with the Mohawk and New England. English purchasers obtained Pocumtuc land in the 1660s, and Deerfield was laid out in 1670. During King Philip's War the Pocomtuc victory at Bloody Brook in September 1675 was answered by the settler attack at Peskeompskut in May 1676; many survivors fled to Schaghticoke and later joined Abenaki communities. On 29 February 1704, French, Abenaki, Mohawk, and Pocomtuc raiders under Jean-Baptiste Hertel de Rouville burned much of Deerfield and carried 112 captives toward Montreal. Farther north, Benning Wentworth issued the New Hampshire Grants between 1749 and 1764. Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys, formed in 1770, resisted New York's claims and captured Fort Ticonderoga on 10 May 1775. Delegates of the grants proclaimed the independent Vermont Republic on 15 January 1777; after the Hubbardton and Bennington campaigns of that year, it entered the United States as the fourteenth state on 4 March 1791.
zh:
莫希干是这片阿尔冈昆边地的名称，地域从上哈得孙河与乔治湖一带延伸到绿山和康涅狄格河上游。波康塔克（Pocumtuk）即后来的迪尔菲尔德，是波康塔克人在肥沃河滨低地上的重要村镇；人们种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，也依靠康涅狄格河捕鱼和通行。1444年，阿贝纳基人的小路穿过北方林地，莫霍克人的战道从西面伸入，莫希干猎人则活动到尚普兰湖一带。在欧洲人建立任何城镇之前，松木、毛皮、河流渡口以及各部族的会集便已赋予此地重要性。

1609年，萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰到达尚普兰湖，使这座河谷卷入法国人与莫霍克人及新英格兰的争夺。英国购地者在1660年代取得波康塔克土地，迪尔菲尔德于1670年划建。菲利普国王战争期间，波康塔克人1675年9月在血溪取胜，1676年5月定居者又袭击佩斯基奥姆普斯库特；许多幸存者逃到斯卡蒂科克，后来加入阿贝纳基社群。1704年2月29日，让-巴蒂斯特·埃尔泰尔·德·鲁维尔率领法国人、阿贝纳基人、莫霍克人和波康塔克人焚毁大半个迪尔菲尔德，并将112名俘虏带往蒙特利尔。更北面，本宁·温特沃思在1749年至1764年间发放新罕布什尔授地。伊桑·艾伦的绿山男孩1770年组成，抵抗纽约的土地要求，并于1775年5月10日夺取泰孔德罗加堡。授地居民代表在1777年1月15日宣布成立独立的佛蒙特共和国；经历同年哈巴顿和本宁顿战役后，它于1791年3月4日作为美国第十四个州加入联邦。

en:
At Amoskeag the Merrimack narrows and drops fifty feet over ledges in a quarter of a mile, and its Pennacook name, Namoskeag, means 'good fishing place'. Sturgeon, salmon and alewife ran the rapids in such numbers that the Pennacook strung great nets across the river and kept their largest settlements on the high bluffs above, where bands of the loose Pennacook alliance gathered seasonally to fish and take council. The valley also led west toward the Mohawk and north toward the Mi'kmaq, whose raids were long known there. In 1444 the falls were one of the busy centers of the Merrimack country, its camps and weirs older than memory.

The great epidemic of 1616–19 thinned the Pennacook villages, and the bashaba Passaconaway chose peace with the English rather than war. Wonalancet, his son and successor, tried to hold neutrality in King Philip's War of 1675–76, but Pennacook bands were drawn in anyway; afterwards some were sold into slavery and others fled north to the Abenaki or west to Schaghticoke. Massachusetts had already granted Dunstable on the lower Merrimack in 1673. In 1719 Scots-Irish families out of Ulster settled Nutfield, chartered as Londonderry in 1722, and John Goffe settled beside Cohas Brook at Amoskeag the same year; the township, granted as Tyngstown in 1727, was voided when New Hampshire separated from Massachusetts in 1741 and rechartered as Derryfield in 1751. John Stark, brought at the age of eight to his family's homestead at the falls, served in Rogers' Rangers against the French and led New Hampshire troops at Bunker Hill in 1775 and to victory at Bennington on 16 August 1777. In 1807 Samuel Blodget built a canal and locks around the falls; Derryfield was renamed Manchester in 1810, and the first Amoskeag cotton mills rose on the water power he had opened.
zh:
阿莫斯凯阿格（阿莫斯凯格）一带，梅里马克河在约四分之一英里内收窄、从岩壁间跌落五十英尺；佩纳库克语称此地为纳莫斯凯格，意为「好渔场」。鲟鱼、鲑鱼和灰西鲱成群涌上急流，佩纳库克人在河面张起大网捕鱼，最大的几处村落就建在俯瞰瀑布的高崖上，佩纳库克联盟的各支族群按季到此聚集，捕鱼议事。河谷向西通向莫霍克人的地界，向北则是米克马克人的地盘，这两处的袭扰由来已久。1444年时，这片瀑布是梅里马克地区最热闹的中心之一，营地和鱼堰古老得无人能说清其来历。

1616至1619年的大瘟疫使佩纳库克诸村人口锐减，大酋长帕萨科纳韦选择与英人讲和而非开战。他的继任者、儿子沃纳兰塞特在1675至1676年的菲利普国王战争中力图保持中立，佩纳库克人的队伍却仍被卷入；战后一些人被卖为奴，另一些人向北投奔阿布纳基人，或向西逃入斯凯蒂科克。此前马萨诸塞已于1673年在梅里马克下游授予邓斯特布尔镇地。1719年，来自阿尔斯特的苏格兰裔爱尔兰人在附近的纳特菲尔德落脚，1722年获特许为伦敦德里；同年约翰·戈夫在阿莫斯凯阿格的科哈斯溪畔定居。这片镇区1727年曾被授予为廷斯敦，1741年新罕布什尔与马萨诸塞分治时授地作废，1751年重新设治为德里菲尔德。八岁便随家迁居瀑布边的约翰·斯塔克曾在罗杰斯游骑兵中对法作战，1775年率新罕布什尔部队奔赴邦克山，1777年8月16日又取得本宁顿大捷。1807年，塞缪尔·布洛杰特绕瀑布修成运河船闸；1810年德里菲尔德改名曼彻斯特，最早的阿莫斯凯阿格棉纺厂也借他开通的水力在瀑布边兴起。

en:
Penapawsket is the country of the Penobscot around the broad estuary where the Penobscot River meets Penobscot Bay. Their name means 'the people of where the white rocks extend out'. Seasonal villages and camps followed moose, caribou, beaver, fish runs and shellfish beds between the northern woods and the cold coast, while birchbark canoes linked river, islands and bay. In 1444 no European trading post had yet been built there, and Penobscot bands controlled the furs, fish, canoe routes and deep-water anchorages of this severe-winter Wabanaki shore east of the Kennebec.

George Weymouth explored Penobscot Bay in 1605 and carried five Abenaki people to England. A French post opened at Majabigwaduce, later Castine, in 1613, and Charles de la Tour built Fort Pentagouët there in 1625. Plymouth forces seized it in 1628, the French retook it in 1635, and Robert Sedgwick's New England troops sacked it in 1654. After 1667 Jean-Vincent de Saint-Castin made the post a French-Abenaki trade and diplomacy centre by marrying the daughter of sachem Modockawando. The Dutch took it in 1674, Saint-Castin recovered it in 1676, and after Edmund Andros plundered it in 1688 he led an Abenaki raid on Pemaquid in August 1689; Benjamin Church destroyed the settlement in 1692. The Penobscot lost their main French protector after Quebec fell in 1759. In 1779, although the Penobscot supported the Patriots, Britain built Fort George at Majabigwaduce. Massachusetts forces besieged it from 25 July until George Collier's relief on 13 August, losing all 44 ships of the expedition. Land cessions from 1794 increasingly confined the Penobscot toward Indian Island.
zh:
佩那保斯凯特是佩诺布斯科特人的土地，环绕佩诺布斯科特河注入佩诺布斯科特湾的宽阔河口。他们的族名意为「白色岩石向外伸出之地的人」。季节性村落和营地随北方森林与寒冷海岸之间的驼鹿、驯鹿、河狸、鱼群和贝场迁移，桦皮独木舟则把河流、岛屿与海湾连成一路。1444年，欧洲商栈尚未在此建立，佩诺布斯科特诸群体仍控制着肯纳贝克河以东、严冬漫长的瓦巴纳基海岸上的毛皮、鱼获、独木舟水道和深水锚地。

1605年，乔治·韦茅斯探查佩诺布斯科特湾，并把五名阿布纳基人带往英格兰。1613年，法国人在后来卡斯廷所在的马贾比瓜杜斯设立贸易站，夏尔·德·拉图尔又于1625年修建彭塔古埃堡。普利茅斯武装1628年夺取该堡，法军1635年收复，罗伯特·塞奇威克率领的新英格兰部队则在1654年洗劫此地。1667年后，让-樊尚·德·圣卡斯坦迎娶酋长莫多达卡万多之女，把据点变成法国与阿布纳基人的贸易和外交中心。荷兰人1674年占堡，圣卡斯坦1676年将其夺回；埃德蒙·安德罗斯1688年劫掠后，他又在1689年8月率阿布纳基战队袭击佩马奎德。1692年，本杰明·彻奇摧毁这一定居点。1759年魁北克陷落后，佩诺布斯科特人失去法国这一主要后盾。1779年，尽管佩诺布斯科特人支持爱国者，英军仍在马贾比瓜杜斯修建乔治堡；马萨诸塞军队从7月25日起围攻，乔治·科利尔8月13日率援军到达，远征军44艘船全部损失。1794年起的土地割让，使佩诺布斯科特人日益被限制到印第安岛一带。

en:
The rugged inlets around Nootka Sound, Mowichat to the Nuu-chah-nulth, were the Pacific coast of related Wakashan-speaking nations. Each nation had its own hereditary chief, and the Mowachaht kept Yuquot on Friendly Cove as a harbour village facing the open ocean. In 1444 the sound was unknown to European charts and remained entirely within the alliances, rivalries and sea routes of the peoples of western Vancouver Island.

Juan Pérez's Santiago anchored off the sound on 8 August 1774, though the Spanish did not land; Nuu-chah-nulth canoes came out to trade. James Cook reached Yuquot in March 1778, and a misunderstanding of the local word nuutkaa may have fixed 'Nootka' on European maps. James Hanna's iron-for-furs voyage in August 1785 opened the maritime fur trade there. When Esteban José Martínez occupied Friendly Cove in 1789, he built Santa Cruz de Nuca and Fort San Miguel and seized British ships, bringing Spain and Britain close to war; the Nootka Conventions of 1790 to 1794 settled the crisis and left Maquinna's Mowachaht still central to trade and diplomacy at Yuquot. In March 1803, after quarrels with traders, Maquinna captured the Boston and kept two of its crew, including John R. Jewitt, for nearly three years.
zh:
努特卡湾（努查努阿特语称莫维查特）周围岛礁错落的海岸，是努查努尔斯人（Nuu-chah-nulth，中文资料常作努查努阿特人）的太平洋家园；这些彼此关联、操瓦卡什语的族群各有世袭首领。莫瓦查特人在友谊湾的尤阔特保有一座面向大洋的港湾村落。1444年，欧洲海图上还没有这片海峡，温哥华岛西岸的联盟、争端与海上往来完全属于当地诸族。

1774年8月8日，胡安·佩雷斯的「圣地亚哥号」在湾外停泊，西班牙人没有上岸，努查努阿特人则划独木舟前来交易。1778年3月，詹姆斯·库克抵达尤阔特，「努特卡」这一名称可能源于对当地语中意为「绕行」的努特卡（nuutkaa）一词的误解。1785年8月，詹姆斯·哈纳以铁货交换毛皮，开启了这里的海上毛皮贸易。1789年，埃斯特万·何塞·马丁内斯占领友谊湾，建起圣克鲁斯·德·努卡和圣米格尔堡，并扣押英国船只，几乎使西班牙与英国开战；1790至1794年的《努特卡公约》化解危机，马金纳的莫瓦查特人仍是尤阔特贸易与外交的核心。1803年3月，在与商人接连发生冲突后，马金纳夺取「波士顿号」，留下包括约翰·R·朱伊特在内的两名船员近三年。

en:
Howe Sound is a fjord-like arm of the Strait of Georgia, whose Squamish name means 'paddling north'. At its head the Squamish River joins the sea, while the Cheakamus, Mamquam and Elaho valleys lead into the mountains. Squamish villages and camps were spread through the sound and its islands, together with places used by the Shishalh, and salmon runs supplied much of the winter food stored at the river mouths. In 1444 this was Coast Salish country, ordered by Squamish families and waterways, with no European ship yet in the sound.

Smallpox reached the coast before direct European contact, and the epidemic of the 1770s devastated many Squamish camps and villages. José María Narváez observed the sound in 1791 and named it Boca del Carmelo; George Vancouver entered it in 1792 and renamed it after Earl Howe. The first recorded Squamish meetings with Vancouver's and Narváez's expeditions took place in these same years around the adjacent inlets, and another smallpox epidemic struck in 1800-01. Through 1821 no European fort or permanent settlement stood at the head of Howe Sound, which remained a network of Squamish villages, camps, fishing places and river routes.
zh:
豪湾是乔治亚海峡一条峡湾般的支海，斯阔米什语中的含义为「向北划行」。湾头有斯阔米什河入海，奇卡穆斯河、马姆夸姆河和埃拉霍河则通向群山。斯阔米什人的村落与营地遍布海湾和岛群，希沙尔人（Shishalh）也使用这里的多处地方；鲑鱼洄游为河口各村提供了大量冬季储粮。1444年，这里仍是沿海萨利什人的土地，由斯阔米什人的家族与水路关系维系，欧洲船只尚未进入海湾。

天花在欧洲人直接接触之前已传到海岸，1770年代的疫病摧毁了许多斯阔米什营地和村落。1791年，何塞·玛丽亚·纳瓦埃斯观察到豪湾，将其命名为卡梅洛口（Boca del Carmelo）；1792年乔治·温哥华驶入湾内，又以豪伯爵之名称之为豪湾。斯阔米什人与温哥华、纳瓦埃斯船队最早有记载的接触，也发生在这两年间邻近各处海湾；1800至1801年，天花再度袭来。到1821年，豪湾湾头仍没有欧洲要塞或永久定居点，依旧是斯阔米什人的村落、营地、捕鱼地与河路网络。

en:
'Kwakiutl' originally meant one Kwak'wala-speaking community whose village of Tsaxis later became Fort Rupert on Beaver Harbour, near the northern tip of Vancouver Island. Around it lay the wider Kwakwaka'wakw country, stretching through Queen Charlotte Strait, Johnstone Strait and the Discovery Islands. Fishing was the base of life, supplemented by hunting, wild berries, weaving and carved woodwork. Rank and wealth were shown not by hoarding but by lavish distribution at potlatches. In 1444 the villages followed their own chiefs and seasonal rounds, linked by related dialects and canoe routes.

On 5 August 1786, a British fur-trading expedition reached Goletas Channel; the commander of Experiment named the opening Queen Charlotte's Sound. George Vancouver's expedition made the first documented European contact with the Kwakwaka'wakw in 1792, while British ships surveyed the maze of island channels. The coastal fur trade brought new goods and pressures, but through 1821 Tsaxis had not become a European fort or town; the Hudson's Bay Company post later built there still lay in the future. Village life remained in Kwakiutl and neighbouring hands, with rank and wealth still expressed through ceremony and potlatch gifts.
zh:
「夸扣特尔」本指一个说夸夸拉语的社群，其村址察克西斯后来成为温哥华岛北端附近海狸港的鲁珀特堡。其周边是更广阔的夸夸嘉夸诸族之地，穿过夏洛特皇后海峡、约翰斯通海峡和发现群岛。渔业是生计基础，辅以狩猎、采集野果野莓、编织和木雕。地位与财富不靠囤积显现，而在夸富宴上以丰厚馈赠展示。1444年，这些村落仍按各自首领和季节节律生活，由相近方言与独木舟水路联系。

1786年8月5日，一支英国毛皮贸易探险队到达戈莱塔斯海峡；「实验号」的指挥官将前方水道命名为夏洛特皇后湾。1792年，乔治·温哥华的船队测绘这片岛群交错的海峡时，与夸夸嘉夸人发生欧洲人最早有记载的接触。沿海毛皮贸易带来新货物和新压力，但到1821年，察克西斯仍未成为欧洲人的要塞或城镇，后来的哈德逊湾公司商站尚未出现。村落仍由夸扣特尔及邻近诸族掌握，地位与财富继续通过仪式和夸富宴馈赠来表达。

en:
The Tsimshian, whose name Ts'msyen means 'inside the Skeena River', hold the foggy islands and inlets where the lower Skeena meets Hecate Strait. Their oral history recalls earlier homes on the upper Skeena, but chiefly houses had moved down to the coast by the fifteenth century. In 1444 families wintered in villages around Prince Rupert Harbour and Metlakatla, then followed the salmon to summer stations along the lower river. Matrilineal clans and hereditary chiefs controlled names, fishing grounds and ceremonial privileges, while canoes linked the harbour with neighbouring nations.

European ships did not break that seasonal round for more than three centuries. In 1787 the British captains Charles Duncan and James Colnett reached Gitxaala on the outer coast, perhaps the first Tsimshian village recorded as visited by Europeans, although Russian traders may have met northern groups earlier. The coastal fur trade then reached the Skeena estuary, bringing new goods and rival shipping into Hecate Strait. Through 1821, however, Tsimshian chiefs still controlled the winter villages, salmon fisheries and canoe passages of their own coast.
zh:
钦西安人自称钦西安（Ts'msyen），意为「斯基纳河内」，居住在斯基纳河下游注入赫卡特海峡一带的雾中岛屿与峡湾。口传历史说他们早先住在斯基纳河上游，但到15世纪，各世袭首领家族已迁居海岸。1444年，各部族在鲁珀特港和梅特拉卡特拉一带的村落过冬，鲑鱼洄游时再前往下游河滨的夏季渔场。社会按母系氏族划分，世袭首领掌管名号、渔场和仪式特权；独木舟航线把港湾与邻近各族连接起来。

此后三个多世纪里，欧洲船只并未改变这套随季节转徙的生活。1787年，英国船长查尔斯·邓肯和詹姆斯·科尔内特抵达外海的吉特克萨拉（Gitxaala），这可能是欧洲人到访钦西安村落的最早记录，不过俄国毛皮商也许更早接触过北部群体。海上毛皮贸易随后延伸到斯基纳河口，把新货物和彼此竞争的船只带进赫卡特海峡。但直到1821年，钦西安首领仍控制着本族海岸上的冬村、鲑鱼渔场和独木舟航道。

en: The forested islands, fjords and Taku River mouth of the central Alaska Panhandle are Tlingit country. In 1444 its people lived in plank-house winter villages facing the water, then moved to seasonal salmon, herring and sea-otter camps. Matrilineal clans and moieties governed inheritance, while large canoes carried dried fish, furs, hides and cedar goods to Athabascan-speaking peoples inland. Russian explorers made the first recorded European contact with the Tlingit in 1741, and Spanish ships followed in 1775. The sea-otter trade then drew foreign vessels along the coast, but the Taku kept their place as middlemen on the river and entered 1821 without a permanent European fort in their homeland.
zh: 阿拉斯加狭地中部林木密布的岛屿、峡湾和塔库河口，是特林吉特人的土地。1444年时，人们住在面向水面的木板长屋冬村，再按季节前往鲑鱼、鲱鱼和海獭营地。世系与财产沿母系氏族传承，大型独木舟把鱼干、毛皮、兽皮和雪松制品运往内陆，与说阿萨巴斯卡语的族群交易。俄国探险者在1741年留下欧洲人与特林吉特人接触的最早记录，西班牙船只则在1775年到来。此后海獭贸易把外国帆船引到海岸，但塔库人仍守着河道上的中介地位；到1821年，他们的家园还没有出现欧洲人的永久要塞。

en:
Yakutat Bay opens between the Gulf of Alaska and glacier-cut mountains at the northern end of the Alaska Panhandle. Its Tlingit name, Yaakwdáat, means the place where canoes rest. Before European ships reached the coast, Eyak-speaking people from the Copper River country lived here, and incoming Tlingit families gradually absorbed them; by 1444 Yakutat was one of several Tlingit and mixed Tlingit-Eyak settlements drawing salmon, seals and sea otters from the bay.

Jean-François de La Pérouse visited the bay in 1786, and Alessandro Malaspina and José de Bustamante followed in 1791. In 1795 the Shelikhov-Golikov Company, managed by Alexander Baranov, founded New Russia, also called Slavorossiya, to trade for sea-otter pelts. When the colonists cut off nearby fishing grounds, a Tlingit war party attacked and destroyed the post in 1805, keeping Yakutat free of a permanent Russian settlement through 1821.
zh:
亚库塔特湾位于阿拉斯加狭地北端，处在阿拉斯加湾与冰川切割的群山之间。特林吉特语称亚库塔特（Yaakwdáat），意为独木舟停泊之地。欧洲船只到来前，来自铜河地区、说埃亚克语的渔人住在此地，后来迁入的特林吉特家族逐渐与他们融合；到1444年，亚库塔特已是若干特林吉特及特林吉特—埃亚克混合聚落之一，人们从湾中获取鲑鱼、海豹和海獭。

拉彼鲁兹在1786年到访此湾，马拉斯皮纳与何塞·德·布斯塔曼特于1791年相继前来。1795年，由亚历山大·巴拉诺夫管理的舍利霍夫—戈利科夫公司建立「新俄罗斯」，又称斯拉沃罗西亚，用以收购海獭皮。殖民者阻断附近渔场后，特林吉特战团在1805年攻毁据点；直到1821年，亚库塔特都没有俄国人的永久定居点。

en:
The Kenai Peninsula (Dena'ina Yaghanen, 'the good land') juts into the Gulf of Alaska between Cook Inlet and Prince William Sound. Dena'ina Athabascans, the only Alaskan Athabaskan people who made their home on salt water, lived in settled villages along the inlet and the Kenai River, taking king salmon from the river and seals and beluga from its tides; Chugach Alutiiq villages held the foggy Pacific coast. In 1444 its people traded and warred with their inlet and island neighbours, and no European ship had yet entered their waters.

Europeans came only in 1778, when James Cook sailed into the inlet and, with William Bligh charting its arms, found mudflats instead of the Northwest Passage; George Vancouver named Cook Inlet for him in 1794. In the late 1780s the Lebedev-Lastochkin company built the stockaded Fort Nikolaevskaia at the mouth of the Kenai River, the first Russian post on the Alaskan mainland, and its sea-otter crews nearly stripped the inlet. In 1797 the Dena'ina stormed the fort and the company's camps, and more than a hundred died on both sides; after 1799 the post passed to the Russian-American Company.
zh:
基奈半岛（德内因语称亚加嫩，意为「好地方」）伸入阿拉斯加湾，夹在库克湾与威廉王子湾之间。德内因阿塔帕斯克人是唯一在海边定居的阿拉斯加阿塔帕斯克族群，在库克湾沿岸和基奈河畔聚村而居，捕捞基奈河的王鲑，在潮水中猎取海豹和白鲸；多雾的太平洋沿岸则是楚加奇阿留特克人的村落。1444年时，他们与海湾和岛屿上的邻族贸易、争战，还没有一艘欧洲船驶入过这片水域。

欧洲人直到1778年才到来：詹姆斯·库克驶入海湾，威廉·布莱测绘两处分汊，发现尽头是泥滩而非西北航道；乔治·温哥华1794年将此湾以库克命名。1780年代末，列别杰夫-拉斯托奇金公司在基奈河口建起木栅围护的尼古拉堡，这是俄罗斯人在阿拉斯加大陆上的第一个据点，猎取海獭的船队几乎将湾内海獭捕尽。1797年，德内因人攻打堡垒和公司营地，双方共有一百多人丧生；1799年后该据点归入俄美公司。

en:
The Aleutian Islands stretch some twelve hundred miles from the Alaskan Peninsula almost to Kamchatka, a wind-scoured volcanic chain between the Pacific and the Bering Sea. Their people, the Unangan or Aleuts—'the original people'—lived in semi-subterranean houses in coastal villages and took nearly everything from the water: they built the swift skin-covered baidarka and hunted sea otters, seals and whales far out in the ocean. In 1444 the eastern islands were the most populous; the Unangan traded along the chain, warred with rival islands, and had never seen an outsider from beyond the fog.

Vitus Bering and Alexei Chirikov sighted the islands in 1741, and Bering died on the island later named for him; the sea-otter furs carried home by his survivors brought Siberian promyshlenniki within years, the first wintering at Attu in 1745. Hostages and the fur tribute turned Unangan men into forced hunters, and in 1763–65 the Fox Islanders burned four Russian ships; Stepan Glotov's punitive campaign killed thousands in reprisal. In 1778 James Cook fixed the islands on the map from Unalaska, trading charts there with the Russian navigator Gerasim Izmailov. The Russian-American Company then ruled the chain and Orthodox monks arrived in the 1790s. Within a generation, disease and the fur trade had cut a people once perhaps 25,000 strong to a fraction of that number.
zh:
阿留申群岛自阿拉斯加半岛向西绵延约一千九百公里，直逼堪察加，是太平洋与白令海之间一条狂风不断的火山岛链。岛上的乌南甘人（即阿留申人，族名意为「原住民」）在海岸村落里居住半地穴式房屋，几乎一切取之于海：他们造出轻快的兽皮小艇「拜达卡」，远出外海猎捕海獭、海豹和鲸。1444年时东端诸岛人口最密，乌南甘人沿岛链贸易，也与敌对岛屿争战，还从未见过雾霭之外来的外人。

1741年，白令和奇里科夫望见了这片群岛，白令本人死在后来以他命名的岛上；幸存者带回的海獭皮几年内就引来西伯利亚的猎皮人，他们1745年首次在阿图岛过冬。人质制度和毛皮贡赋把乌南甘男子变成被迫出猎的猎手，1763至1765年福克斯群岛的岛民焚毁四艘俄国船，斯捷潘·格洛托夫的讨伐队随即屠杀数千人报复。1778年，詹姆斯·库克在乌纳拉斯卡与俄国航海者格拉西姆·伊兹梅洛夫交换海图，把群岛准确地标在地图上。此后群岛归俄美公司统辖，东正教修士在1790年代到来。短短一代人的时间里，疾病和毛皮贸易就把一度约两万五千的人口削减到只剩零头。

en:
The bays, rivers and interior caribou grounds of northern and central Newfoundland were Beothuk country in 1444. Their camps were concentrated around Notre Dame and Bonavista bays, though family bands moved with the seasons between sealing coasts, salmon rivers and winter hunting grounds. They built conical bark-covered mamateeks, painted bodies and possessions with red ochre each spring, and drove migrating caribou behind long fences of brush. Each band of a few dozen kin managed its own route through a land still untouched by European settlement.

After John Cabot's 1497 voyage, Portuguese, French and English fishing ships increasingly used Newfoundland's shores, and Humphrey Gilbert claimed the island for England in 1583. At Cuper's Cove, Governor John Guy sought trade rather than flight: on 6 November 1612 his party shared a meal and gifts with Beothuk in Trinity Bay. That opening did not last. Seasonal fishing stations crowded the coast, and the Beothuk withdrew toward the Exploits River and its lakes. David Buchan's attempted friendship mission upriver in January 1811 ended with two marines dead. On 1 March 1819 John Peyton Jr.'s armed party seized a Beothuk woman and killed her husband, the band's leader; she died of tuberculosis on 8 January 1820, by which time only about thirty-one Beothuk were said to remain.
zh:
1444年，纽芬兰岛北部和中部的海湾、河流与内陆驯鹿场仍是贝奥图克人的土地。他们的营地集中在圣母湾和博纳维斯塔湾一带，各个家族群随季节在海豹海岸、鲑鱼河流与冬季猎场之间迁徙。他们搭建锥形桦皮屋，每年春天用赭红涂染身体和器物，还会设置长长的灌木栅栏，把迁徙中的驯鹿驱向猎手。每个数十人的亲族群都沿着自己的路线，在尚无欧洲人定居的土地上轮转。

约翰·卡博特1497年航行之后，葡萄牙、法国和英国渔船越来越多地使用纽芬兰海岸；汉弗莱·吉尔伯特1583年代表英格兰宣称占有此岛。在卡珀斯湾，总督约翰·盖伊试图建立贸易而非迫使对方逃离：1612年11月6日，他的队伍在三一湾与一群贝奥图克人共餐并交换礼物。这次接触未能延续。季节性渔场逐渐挤满海岸，贝奥图克人退向埃克斯普洛伊茨河及上游湖泊。1811年1月，戴维·巴肯沿河而上的友好尝试以两名海军士兵死亡告终。1819年3月1日，小约翰·佩顿的武装队伍掳走一名贝奥图克妇女，并杀死她的丈夫、也就是该群首领；她于1820年1月8日死于肺结核，当时据说只剩约三十一名贝奥图克人。

en:
Taqamkuk, later the Mi'kmaq name for Newfoundland, fits the island's broken southern shore: foggy headlands, island shelters, salmon rivers and grounds where seals, seabirds and caribou supported seasonal camps. In 1444 the island itself was Beothuk country, while the Cabot Strait coast also lay open to hunting and fishing parties crossing from the lands to the west. No European station yet ruled these bays, though the Great Banks beyond them were already among the richest cod waters in the North Atlantic.

John Cabot's 1497 voyage opened the coast to Breton, Norman, Portuguese and English fishermen; English sources place Mi'kmaq villages at St. George's Bay and Placentia by 1594. During the seventeenth century Mi'kmaq boat crews crossed the Cabot Strait to hunt along the south coast as far east as Placentia Bay, exchanging furs and provisions in French harbours. France's colonial claims ended with the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713, although French fishermen retained seasonal shore rights. In the 1760s, after the British conquest of Acadia, Chief Jeannot Pequidalouet led families from Cape Breton toward permanent camps at St. George's Bay and Bay d'Espoir; James Cook encountered a Mi'kmaq band there in May 1767. By 1818 a British visitor found another settled band at Flat Bay, holding land through loyalty to the Crown.
zh:
塔卡姆库克后来成为米克马克语中对纽芬兰的称呼，用来称呼岛南破碎的海岸十分贴切：雾中岬角、可供避浪的岛屿、鲑鱼河流，以及能以海豹、海鸟和驯鹿维持季节性营地的渔场和猎场。1444年，这座岛本身仍是贝奥图克人的土地，而卡伯特海峡沿岸也向西方各地渡海而来的狩猎和捕鱼队伍敞开。当时还没有欧洲人的据点统治这些海湾，但外侧的大浅滩已是北大西洋最丰饶的鳕鱼场之一。

约翰·卡博特1497年的航行把这片海岸带入布列塔尼、诺曼、葡萄牙和英格兰渔民的活动范围；到1594年，圣乔治湾和普拉森西亚已有米克马克村庄的记载。17世纪，米克马克人驾船渡过卡伯特海峡，沿南海岸狩猎，最东可达普拉森西亚湾，并在法国渔港用毛皮和给养交易。1713年《乌得勒支条约》结束了法国对纽芬兰的殖民主张，但法国渔民仍保留季节性上岸权。1760年代阿卡迪亚被英国征服后，首领让诺·佩基达卢埃（Jeannot Pequidalouet）率族人从布雷顿角岛迁来，在圣乔治湾和希望湾一带形成永久营地；詹姆斯·库克1767年5月就在圣乔治湾遇到一群米克马克人。到1818年，英国来访者已在弗拉特湾见到另一支定居族群，他们因效忠英国王室而获得土地。

en:
Onamagag is the Mi'kmaq land of Unama'ki, the rugged island later called Cape Breton, where Atlantic headlands meet the Gulf of St Lawrence. The Bras d'Or lake and ice-free harbours suited a people who moved with the fishing, sealing and hunting seasons rather than ploughing the thin soil. Family bands and district chiefs formed part of the wider Mi'kma'ki country. In 1444 the island had no European settlement; its shores and canoe routes belonged to Mi'kmaq fishermen and hunters, while European voyages into these waters still lay in the future.

John Cabot's 1497 voyage was later credited with reaching the island, though contemporary records cannot distinguish Cape Breton from Newfoundland. By the 1520s Mi'kmaq parties were trading with European fishing crews, and around 1521-22 João Álvares Fagundes planted a short-lived Portuguese fishing settlement, possibly near Ingonish. A Scottish post at Baleine in 1629 was soon destroyed by the French, who then founded small posts at Englishtown and St. Peter's. After the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713, France made the island its colony of Île Royale, moved settlers from Plaisance there, and raised Louisbourg to guard the Gulf of St Lawrence and the Grand Banks fishery; its lighthouse was built in 1734. New England troops with a British fleet took Louisbourg in 1745, and the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle returned it in 1748. British forces captured the fortress again in 1758, and the Treaty of Paris transferred Île Royale to Britain in 1763.
zh:
奥纳马加格是米克马克人所说的乌纳马基，即后来的布雷顿角岛；崎岖岛屿处在大西洋岬角与圣劳伦斯湾之间。布拉多尔湖和不冻港湾适合随渔汛、海豹猎季和狩猎季迁徙的生活，却不适合耕作贫瘠土地。岛上的家族群和地区酋长，属于更广的米克马克基世界的一部分。1444年时，这里没有欧洲人定居点，海岸与独木舟航路都属于米克马克渔人和猎人，欧洲船只尚未驶入这片水域。

约翰·卡伯特1497年的航行后来被认为可能到过此岛，但同时代记载无法区分布雷顿角与纽芬兰。到1520年代，米克马克人已同欧洲渔民交易；1521年至1522年前后，若昂·阿尔瓦雷斯·法贡德斯在此建立过一个短暂的葡萄牙渔业定居点，位置可能在英戈尼什附近。1629年苏格兰人在贝莱讷设立的据点很快被法国人摧毁，法国人随后在英吉利敦和圣彼得斯建立小据点。1713年《乌得勒支和约》后，法国把此岛建为皇家岛殖民地，把普莱桑斯移民迁来，并修筑路易斯堡以拱卫圣劳伦斯湾入口和大浅滩渔场；岛上灯塔建于1734年。新英格兰军队在英国舰队协助下于1745年攻克路易斯堡，1748年《亚琛和约》又将其归还法国。1758年英军再次占领要塞，1763年《巴黎和约》把皇家岛割让给英国。

en:
Epekwitk, ‘cradled on the waves’, lies low and red-soiled in the Gulf of St. Lawrence, cut off from the mainland by a narrow strait. The Mi'kmaq knew it also as Minegoo, and their shell middens and campsites mark shores where families took mackerel, herring, lobster and seal before moving inland to hunt moose and caribou. The island made up the Epekwitk half of the Mi'kma'ki district Epekwitk aq Piktuk, ruled by community saqamaq, a women's council and wampum keepers under the Grand Council, and its people sat with the Wolastoqiyik, Passamaquoddy and Abenaki in the Wabanaki confederacy. In 1444 no European keel had yet entered the gulf, and the island belonged wholly to its seasonal round.

In late June 1534 Jacques Cartier, coasting westward on his first voyage, became the first known European to sight its shores, and in 1604 France claimed it with the rest of Acadia as Île Saint-Jean, a claim the Mi'kmaq never acknowledged. France kept the island after Utrecht in 1713, and in 1720 Port-la-Joye became the seat of government, receiving Acadian settlers and a French garrison. A New England force out of captured Louisbourg burned the post in 1745, only to be driven to its boats by Acadian militia and Mi'kmaq fighters, who overwhelmed its garrison near the York River in 1746. Refugees from the expulsions in Nova Scotia swelled the population to nearly five thousand, but after Louisbourg fell again, Colonel Andrew Rollo landed five hundred men in August 1758, built Fort Amherst above Port-la-Joye and deported most of the population; the sinking of the transports Violet, Duke William and Ruby alone drowned more than eight hundred. Ceded outright in 1763 and surveyed into sixty-seven lots granted by an absentee-landlord lottery in 1767, the island became the separate colony of St. John's Island in 1769, with the new town of Charlottetown as its capital; in 1798 it was renamed Prince Edward Island, for the Duke of Kent.
zh:
埃帕戈伊特格纳格（埃佩奎特克）意为「浪涛摇荡的摇篮」，低伏在圣劳伦斯湾中，红土遍布，与大陆仅隔一道狭窄海峡。米克马克人又称它米尼古；沿岸贝丘和营地遗址表明，他们的氏族曾在此捕捞鲭鱼、鲱鱼、龙虾和海豹，再转入内陆猎取驼鹿和驯鹿。本岛与大陆上的皮克图共同构成米克马克基七区之一的「埃佩奎特克-皮克图」，由各村酋长、妇女议事会和贝壳串珠保管人在大议事会统辖下治理，岛民并与沃拉斯托基伊克人、帕萨马科迪人、阿布纳基人同属瓦巴纳基联盟。1444年，还没有任何欧洲船底驶入过这片海湾，全岛完全按他们的季节节律而存在。

1534年6月底，雅克·卡蒂亚在第一次航行中沿海岸西行，成为有记载最早望见此岛的欧洲人；1604年，法国将它与阿卡迪亚其余土地一并宣称占有，命名为圣让岛，但米克马克人从未承认这一主权。1713年《乌得勒支和约》后法国保住了该岛，1720年在拉乔伊港设治，迁来阿卡迪亚移民并驻扎法军。1745年，一支新英格兰军队从攻陷的路易斯堡出击，焚毁拉乔伊港，却被阿卡迪亚民兵和米克马克战士赶回船上；1746年，他们又在约克河附近全歼这支驻军。新斯科舍驱逐行动中的难民使岛上人口增至近五千人，但路易斯堡再度陷落后，安德鲁·罗洛上校于1758年8月率五百人登陆，在拉乔伊港上方修建阿默斯特堡，并将大部分居民驱逐出境；仅维奥莱特号、威廉公爵号和鲁比号三艘运输船沉没，就有八百多人溺亡。1763年该岛被正式割让给英国，经测绘分为67块份地，1767年以抽签方式授予身在英国的外地业主；1769年它成为独立的圣约翰岛殖民地，以新建的夏洛特敦为首府，1798年为纪念肯特公爵改名为爱德华王子岛。

en:
Segepenegatic is the Mi'kmaq district of Sipekne'katik, the wooded centre of peninsular Nova Scotia between the Bay of Fundy approaches and the deep harbour later called Halifax. Its name means a place rich in wapato, the water plant whose tubers grew in the wet ground of the Shubenacadie river country. Mi'kmaq families summered on the sheltered waters of the harbour and moved inland for winter hunting, while district chiefs took part in the councils of Mi'kma'ki. In 1444 this was a country of seasonal camps and canoe portages, with no Acadian farms or British blockhouses.

France planted its wider Acadian colony on Saint Croix Island in 1604 and moved the settlement to Port-Royal in 1605, but European power long remained concentrated on the coasts. Louis-Pierre Thury opened Mission Sainte-Anne on the Shubenacadie in 1699; Antoine Gaulin gave it a permanent station during Dummer's War in 1722-25. Port-Royal fell to a British siege in 1710, and the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713 assigned peninsular Acadia to Britain without ending Mi'kmaq and French influence at Shubenacadie. Jean-Louis Le Loutre arrived in 1738, and the mission served as both chapel and military base in the border wars. The disease-ruined Duc d'Anville expedition sheltered in the harbour in 1746, its commander dying before the projected counterattack collapsed. British settlers founded Halifax in 1749, and during Father Le Loutre's War Mi'kmaq warriors used Shubenacadie as a base for raids on Halifax and Dartmouth. British forces destroyed Mission Sainte-Anne in October 1755, as the Acadian deportation began. The Halifax Naval Yard was established in 1759 and supported British operations through the American Revolution and the War of 1812.
zh:
塞格佩内加蒂克是米克马克人的锡佩克内卡蒂克地区，位于新斯科舍半岛中部林地，一边通向芬迪湾，一边连接后来哈利法克斯所在的深水港。地名意为瓦帕托水生块茎丰生之地，这种植物的球茎生长在舒贝纳卡迪河流域的湿地中。米克马克家族夏季在港湾避风水域捕鱼，冬季转入内陆狩猎，地区酋长则参加米克马克基的议事会。1444年，这里只有季节性营地和独木舟搬运道，还没有阿卡迪亚农庄或英国人的堡垒。

1604年，法国在圣十字岛建立范围更广的阿卡迪亚殖民地，次年把定居点迁至皇家港，但欧洲势力长期集中在沿海。路易-皮埃尔·蒂里1699年在舒贝纳卡迪河畔开设圣安妮传教站；安托万·戈兰在1722年至1725年的达默战争期间把它建成常驻站点。皇家港于1710年在英军围攻下陷落，1713年《乌得勒支和约》把阿卡迪亚半岛部分划归英国，却没有终结米克马克人和法国在舒贝纳卡迪的影响。让-路易·勒卢特尔1738年来到这里，传教站在此后的边境战争中兼具礼拜场所和军事据点的作用。1746年，疫病横行的昂维尔公爵远征队在港湾避泊，主帅病死，计划中的反攻也告失败。1749年，英国移民建立哈利法克斯；勒卢特尔神父战争期间，米克马克战士以舒贝纳卡迪为基地袭击哈利法克斯和达特茅斯。1755年10月阿卡迪亚大驱逐开始时，英军摧毁圣安妮传教站。哈利法克斯海军船坞于1759年设立，并在美国独立战争和1812年战争中支援英国军事行动。

en:
The Petkootkweak, or Petitcodiac, winds through wooded ridges to Shepody Bay at the head of the Bay of Fundy, bending almost at a right angle where Moncton now stands. Before its tide raced one of the great bores of the Fundy shore, a wall of brown water rushing in with a noise like a storm: the Mi'kmaq called the river Petkootkweak, ‘the river that bends like a bow’, and Wolastoqey speakers heard in its name the sound of thunder. The valley belonged to Siknikt, ‘the drainage place’, the south-eastern district of Mi'kma'ki, whose villages kept their own saqamaq under the Grand Council of the Wabanaki confederacy. Families wintered at the headwaters, where a carry led over to the Shubenacadie, and took salmon, sturgeon and waterfowl from the river and its marshes; their kinsmen the Wolastoqiyik held the Saint John to the west. In 1444 no European had yet settled the bay.

In 1604 the expedition of Dugua de Mons, with Champlain aboard, entered the Bay of Fundy but passed the river mouth, and Acadians from Port-Royal were the first to settle: in 1698 Pierre Thibodeau founded Chipoudie on Shepody Bay and Guillaume Blanchard opened Petitcoudiac, which with Memramcook made up the Trois-Rivières; by 1733 dyked marsh farms had climbed the river to Le Coude, the elbow bend. Utrecht in 1713 left the region under the British flag, its people the ‘neutral French’ who would not swear an unconditional oath. After Fort Beauséjour fell in June 1755, Major Joseph Frye led two hundred men to burn the Trois-Rivières, but on 4 September Charles Deschamps de Boishébert's Acadians and Mi'kmaq struck his column at Village-des-Blanchard, leaving twenty-three of his men casualties for one of their own and driving the expedition out. Some seven hundred villagers were evacuated up the gulf to the Miramichi, where famine swept the refugee camps in 1756–1758. British expeditions returned to the river in 1758, their boats harried by Joseph Broussard's partisans, and the last holdouts surrendered at Fort Cumberland in November 1759. In 1766 eight families of Pennsylvania Germans, among them Heinrich Stief, settled the deserted elbow as ‘The Bend’, the seed of the later Moncton.
zh:
佩特库特奎阿克河（法国人写作 Petitcoudiac，后作 Petitcodiac）穿过林木覆盖的丘陵，注入芬迪湾湾头的希波迪湾，在今蒙克顿附近折出一个近乎直角的大弯。河口的涌潮是芬迪湾畔最壮观的潮景之一，一道黄褐色的水墙轰然逆河而上，声如雷鸣：米克马克人称之为佩特库特奎阿克，意为「弯如弓弦的河」，而在沃拉斯托基伊克语里，这个名字的意思正是雷鸣之声。河谷属于米克马克基东南的希格尼克特区——「排水之地」，各村由酋长在瓦巴纳基联盟大议事会下自行治理。氏族在河源地带过冬，那里有一条联运道通往舒贝纳卡迪；人们在河中与沼泽间捕捞鲑鱼、鲟鱼，猎取水鸟，西边圣约翰河上住着同族的沃拉斯托基伊克人。1444年，湾畔还没有欧洲人定居。

1604年，迪瓜·德·蒙斯的探险队（尚普兰随行）驶入芬迪湾，却从河口外驶过；最先来此定居的是从罗亚尔港迁来的阿卡迪亚人：1698年，皮埃尔·蒂博多在希波迪湾畔建立希波迪村，纪尧姆·布朗沙尔开辟佩蒂特库迪亚克，二者与梅拉姆库克合称「三河」；到1733年，靠海塘围垦的沼泽农庄已沿河上溯到河弯处的勒库德。1713年《乌得勒支和约》后此地归英国所有，而居民是不肯无条件宣誓效忠的「中立法兰西人」。1755年6月博塞茹尔堡陷落后，约瑟夫·弗莱少校率两百人前去焚毁三河，但在9月4日，夏尔·德尚·德·布瓦埃贝尔率领的阿卡迪亚人与米克马克人在布朗沙尔村突袭其纵队，以己方一人的代价造成英军23人伤亡，将其逐出。约七百名村民沿湾岸撤往米拉米希，1756至1758年间饥荒席卷难民营。1758年英军再度溯河进剿，船队不断遭到约瑟夫·布鲁萨尔游击队的袭扰；最后的抵抗者于1759年11月在坎伯兰堡投降。1766年，八户宾夕法尼亚德意志移民（其中有海因里希·施蒂夫一家）在荒废的河弯处定居，称此地为「弯镇」，即后来蒙克顿的雏形。

en:
Gespegeogag, 'the end of the land' in Mi'kmaq, is the wooded finger of the Gaspé Peninsula, where the Appalachian hills run out into the Gulf of St. Lawrence around Gaspé Bay. In 1444 it was Mi'kmaq country: family bands summered on the bay and its offshore islands, fishing mackerel and salmon and taking seal and walrus, then moved inland after moose and caribou, their bark camps following the season. No European had yet charted the bay; the first sail came ninety years later.

On 24 July 1534 Jacques Cartier raised a ten-metre cross bearing the arms of Francis I on the shore of Gaspé Bay and carried off the two sons of Stadaconan chief Donnacona, the first French taking of possession in what would become Canada. For more than a century Europeans came only for the fishing season, drying cod on the beaches, until Pierre Denys de la Ronde set up the first permanent fishing post in 1676. Around 1740 the whole peninsula held only about five hundred settlers, and in 1750 the seigneurie of Pabos was its most important fishing post. In September 1758, after Louisbourg fell, Wolfe and Hardy burned Gaspé, Grande-Rivière and Pabos, destroyed some two hundred fishing vessels and shipped the fishermen back to France. The coast passed to Britain with the conquest of 1760; Acadians fleeing the expulsions and, after 1784, Loyalists settled its coves, and by the early nineteenth century Jersey merchant houses ran most of the cod trade.
zh:
盖斯佩盖奥加格在米克马克语里意为「陆地的尽头」，是加斯佩半岛林木覆盖的尖端：阿巴拉契亚丘陵在此伸入圣劳伦斯湾，环抱出加斯佩湾。1444年时这里是米克马克人的土地：各家族群夏天在海湾和海岛上捕捞鲭鱼、鲑鱼，猎取海豹和海象，入冬转入内陆追逐驼鹿和驯鹿，树皮帐篷随季节搬移。此时还没有欧洲人测绘过这个海湾，第一面船帆要到九十年后才出现。

1534年7月24日，雅克·卡蒂亚在加斯佩湾岸边竖起一面十米高、刻有弗朗索瓦一世纹章的十字架，又带走斯塔达科纳酋长多纳科纳的两个儿子——这是法国在未来的加拿大第一次宣示占有。此后一个多世纪里，欧洲人只在渔季前来、在海滩上晾晒鳕鱼，直到1676年皮埃尔·德尼·德·拉龙德建立第一个常住渔业据点。1740年前后，整个半岛只有约五百名定居者；1750年，帕博领地是此地最重要的渔业据点。1758年9月，路易堡陷落后，沃尔夫和哈代焚毁加斯佩、格朗德里维耶尔和帕博，毁掉约两百艘渔船，把渔民遣送回法国。1760年征服之后，海岸归入英国；逃避大流放的阿卡迪亚人、以及1784年之后到来的效忠派在各个小湾安家，到19世纪初，鳕鱼贸易大半落入泽西岛商号之手。

en:
Onguhiara takes its name from Onguiaahra, the Neutral community on the strait between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario. In 1444 the Niagara Peninsula belonged to the Attiwandaron, later called Neutrals because they could trade with both the Wendat and the Haudenosaunee. Their Iroquoian villages kept maize fields in the fertile lowland and deer hunt in the surrounding woods, while furs and dressed deerskins moved through the river corridor. The Niagara linked two Great Lakes, but its falls forced travellers onto a portage, giving Onguiaahra value out of proportion to its size.

The French interpreter Étienne Brûlé crossed Attiwandaron country around 1615, and the Récollet Joseph de La Roche Daillon wintered with a Neutral chief in 1626-1627; Jesuits later listed Onguioaahra on the Niagara among their villages. Epidemics and then the Beaver Wars broke that power, and in 1651 Haudenosaunee attacks dispersed the Neutral confederacy. La Salle built Fort Conti at the river mouth in 1678, where Louis Hennepin saw the falls; the Marquis de Denonville raised a short-lived second fort in 1687. Louis-Thomas Chabert de Joncaire obtained Seneca consent for a trading post in 1720, and the machicolated stone house begun in 1726 became the core of Fort Niagara, which Pierre Pouchot surrendered to Sir William Johnson in July 1759. During the American Revolution the fort was a British, Loyalist and Seneca base. Butlersburg on the west bank began in 1781, became Newark and in 1792 served as the first capital of Upper Canada, before John Graves Simcoe moved the government to York in 1797; Fort George was built nearby in the 1790s. Isaac Brock was killed at Queenston Heights on 13 October 1812 while repelling an American crossing. American troops took Fort George in May 1813 and burned Niagara on their retreat that December, and British forces stormed Fort Niagara on 19 December. The town was rebuilt after the peace.
zh:
昂古希亚拉得名于昂吉亚赫拉（Onguiaahra），即住在伊利湖与安大略湖之间水道旁的中立人聚落。1444年，尼亚加拉半岛属于阿蒂万达伦人，他们后来被法兰西传教士称为「中立人」，因为能够同时与温达特人和豪德诺索尼人贸易。这些说易洛魁语的村民在肥沃低地种植玉米，在周围林地猎鹿，毛皮和鞣制鹿皮沿河流走廊流通。尼亚加拉河连通两大湖，瀑布却迫使旅人改行陆路转运，使昂古希亚拉的重要性远超其聚落规模。

法兰西译员艾蒂安·布吕莱约在1615年穿过阿蒂万达伦人的地域；1626年至1627年冬，重整派修士约瑟夫·德·拉罗什·达永在一位中立人首领处过冬，后来的耶稣会士把尼亚加拉河畔的昂吉亚赫拉（Onguioaahra）列入其村落。疫病与随后的海狸战争摧毁了这一势力，1651年，豪德诺索尼人的进攻使中立联盟溃散。1678年，拉萨尔在河口兴建孔蒂堡，路易·亨内平在此见到瀑布；1687年，德农维尔侯爵又修建了一座短命的要塞。1720年，路易-托马·沙贝尔·德·容凯尔取得塞内卡人同意设立商站；1726年动工的石造雉堞楼成为尼亚加拉堡的核心，皮埃尔·普绍最终于1759年7月把它交给威廉·约翰逊爵士。美国独立战争期间，这座堡垒是英军、效忠派与塞内卡人的基地。西岸的巴特勒斯堡始于1781年，后改称纽瓦克，1792年成为上加拿大第一个首府，约翰·格雷夫斯·西姆科于1797年把政府迁往约克；乔治堡则于1790年代建在附近。1812年10月13日，艾萨克·布洛克在昆士顿高地击退美军渡河时阵亡。1813年5月美军攻占乔治堡，12月撤退时焚毁尼亚加拉，英军随即在12月19日强袭尼亚加拉堡。战争结束后，城镇在河畔重建。

en:
Attignawantan was the country of the Bear People, the largest nation of the Wendat confederacy, on the wooded peninsula between Matchedash Bay and Nottawasaga Bay. Wendat farmers had moved north from Lake Ontario by the late thirteenth century; their bark-covered longhouse villages were ringed with palisades, and fields of maize, beans and squash opened beyond the hunt paths. In the fifteenth century the Bear People joined their Cord neighbours to the southeast in the first Wendat league. By 1444, their country was already a settled western core of Wendake, connected to Algonquin fur routes leading toward Lake Nipissing and the Ottawa River.

Étienne Brûlé probably reached this country before 1615, and that summer Samuel de Champlain and the Récollet Joseph Le Caron were at Carhagouha, where Le Caron said the first recorded Catholic mass in Wendake. The Bear village of Ossossané was a principal Wendat settlement from 1632 to 1636, and Jean de Brébeuf saw its Feast of the Dead there in 1636. Jesuits had begun work among the Wendat in 1626 and built the fortified mission of Sainte-Marie near the Bear village of Quieunonascaranas in 1639; the Bear nation then had thirteen villages. Epidemics from 1634 to 1640 killed much of the population, and Haudenosaunee raids destroyed Saint-Ignace and Saint-Louis in March 1649. Sainte-Marie was burned and abandoned, while survivors starved on Christian Island before fleeing toward Quebec in 1650. Ojibwe families later used the emptied shore; after a fur post opened on Matchedash Bay in the late 1770s, British treaties of 1785, 1798 and 1815 opened the way for Penetanguishene Road and its garrison.
zh:
阿蒂格纳万坦是温达特（休伦）联盟中人口最多的熊族之地，位于马奇特达什湾与诺塔瓦萨加湾之间的林木半岛。温达特农人在13世纪后期已从安大略湖北迁，树皮长屋村落外筑木栅，猎路之后是玉米、菜豆和南瓜田。15世纪时，熊族与东南邻的绳族结成温达特最早的联盟。到1444年，这里已是温达克西部定居密集的核心，并同通往尼皮辛湖和渥太华河的阿尔冈昆毛皮商路相连。

艾蒂安·布吕莱可能在1615年以前抵达此地；同年夏天，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰和重整奥斯定会传教士约瑟夫·勒卡龙来到卡尔加古阿（Carhagouha），勒卡龙在那里主持了温达克有记载的第一场天主教弥撒。熊族村落奥索萨内（Ossossané）在1632年至1636年间是温达特的主要村落之一，让·德·布雷伯夫1636年在此目睹亡者之宴。耶稣会士1626年开始向温达特传教，1639年在熊族村落基厄诺纳斯卡拉纳斯（Quieunonascaranas）附近修建设防的圣玛丽传教站；当时熊族共有十三座村落。1634年至1640年的疫病夺去大量人口，1649年3月，豪德诺索尼人的袭击摧毁圣伊尼亚斯和圣路易。圣玛丽被焚毁放弃，幸存者在克里斯蒂安岛挨饿，1650年逃往魁北克方向。后来阿尔冈昆人的奥吉布瓦家族使用这片空出的湖岸；1770年代末马奇特达什湾开设毛皮站后，英国在1785年、1798年和1815年的条约为佩内唐吉申道路和驻军据点打开了通路。

en:
Attigneenongnahac was the country of the Cord People, one of the oldest Wendat nations, on the well-drained rises of Mount St. Louis Ridge between the Sturgeon and Coldwater rivers. Wendat farmers built palisaded longhouse villages here and planted maize, beans and squash on the lighter upland soils. In the fifteenth century the Cord People joined the neighbouring Bear People to form the first league within Wendake. In 1444 their ridge was therefore the southeastern agricultural core of the emerging Huron confederacy, with tracks leading west to Bear towns, east toward Rock country and south toward other Iroquoian peoples.

By the time Samuel de Champlain travelled through Wendake in 1615, the Cord People were one of its four nations, and in 1640 their territory contained three principal villages. Jesuit missionaries passed through these fields in the 1630s, but the epidemics of 1634 to 1640 weakened the villages before the Haudenosaunee invasion of the spring of 1649. More than 300 Wendat survivors reached Quebec under Father Paul Ragueneau in the summer of 1650. Of the groups there, the Cord People alone refused to leave the protection of Fort Saint-Louis the following spring, becoming part of the Huron community that later took root at Lorette. Their old ridge was left largely empty; Ojibwe families later travelled through it, and the British treaties of 1798 and 1815 opened the district around Penetanguishene and Lake Simcoe.
zh:
阿蒂格内农纳哈克是绳族之地。绳族是温达特最古老的族群之一，住在斯特金河与科尔德沃特河之间、排水良好的圣路易斯岭高地上。温达特农人在此筑起木栅环绕的长屋村，在较轻的高地土壤中种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜。15世纪时，绳族与相邻的熊族结成温达克最早的联盟。因此到1444年，这片山岭已是形成中的休伦联盟东南面的农业核心，小路向西通往熊族村落，向东通往岩族之地，向南则连接其他易洛魁语族群。

塞缪尔·德·尚普兰1615年穿行温达克时，绳族已是联盟四大族群之一；到1640年，其境内有三座主要村落。1630年代，耶稣会传教士经过这些农田，但1634年至1640年的疫病先削弱了村落，1649年春豪德诺索尼人又大举入侵。1650年夏，三百多名温达特幸存者在保罗·拉格诺神父带领下抵达魁北克。在当地各族群中，唯有绳族在第二年春天不愿离开圣路易堡的保护，后来成为定居于洛雷特的休伦社群的一部分。他们原来的山岭大体荒弃，后来奥吉布瓦家族在此往来；1798年和1815年的英国条约使佩内唐吉申与锡姆科湖周围地区向殖民开拓开放。

en:
Maisouna covered the lower valley of the river later called the Saint-Maurice, where islands split the current into three channels before it entered the St. Lawrence and the French later built Trois-Rivières. In 1444 no European post stood there. Laurentian peoples lived in semi-sedentary riverside communities, cultivating maize, beans and squash around longhouse villages, while Algonquian-speaking hunters used the forests and river crossings; later French regional histories place the Maisouna between Stadacona and Hochelaga.

Jacques Cartier stopped at the site on 12 October 1535, named the river the Fouez, and planted a cross on Île Saint-Quentin. The Laurentian settlements had vanished before French traders returned around 1600. Laviolette founded the permanent post of Trois-Rivières on 4 July 1634, and it became a fur market between Quebec and Montreal, exposed to Mohawk raids; in June 1641 about 350 Mohawk warriors came there seeking firearms. The town became seat of a regional government in 1665, Ursuline nuns opened a school in 1697, and the Great Peace of Montreal ended the long raiding wars on 4 August 1701. The Forges Saint-Maurice were established in 1730, Trois-Rivières passed to Britain in 1760, and a Continental Army invasion force was defeated outside the town on 8 June 1776.
zh:
迈索纳位于后来得名圣莫里斯河的下游，河水流经岛屿时分作三道水口，再注入圣劳伦斯河，法国人后来便在这处要冲建立三河城。1444年时，欧洲人尚未在此设立据点。劳伦提亚人在河畔半定居，围绕长屋村落种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，阿尔冈昆语猎人则穿行于森林和渡口之间；后来的法语地方史把迈索纳人置于斯塔达科纳与奥谢拉加之间。

1535年10月12日，雅克·卡蒂埃途经此地，把这条河命名为富瓦河，并在圣康坦岛竖起十字架。等到法国商人在1600年前后重返时，劳伦提亚人的聚落已经消失。1634年7月4日，拉维奥莱特建立永久据点三河城，使这里成为魁北克与蒙特利尔之间的毛皮市场，也长期暴露在莫霍克人的袭掠之下；1641年6月，约三百五十名莫霍克战士前来索要火枪。1665年，三河城成为地方政府驻地；1697年，乌尔苏拉会修女在此开办学校；1701年8月4日，《蒙特利尔大和平》结束了漫长的袭掠战争。圣莫里斯锻铁厂于1730年创立，三河城在1760年随新法兰西转入英国之手；1776年6月8日，一支大陆军进攻部队在城外战败。

en:
Lake Nipissing is a broad, shallow water between the Ottawa River and Georgian Bay, reaching Lake Huron through the French River. The Nipissing, an Anishinaabe people of Ojibwe and Algonquin kin, kept their villages on its shores and islands, took sturgeon from its shoals and passed on the furs of the northern forests along the canoe corridor that ran by the Mattawa River to the Ottawa and the St Lawrence; later French visitors, struck by their seers, would call them the 'Sorcerers'. In 1444 the lake country belonged to these middlemen of the northern trade and no European had yet entered it.

Étienne Brûlé, travelling with Huron bands, was the first European to reach the lake about 1610, and Samuel de Champlain followed in 1615 on his way to Huronia; Jean Nicolet kept a cabin and trading house there from the mid-1620s until 1633. The Jesuit Claude Pijart spent nine years among the Nipissing and gathered a small Christian flock, but in 1649–50 the Iroquois overran the country and the Nipissing fled with the Amikwa to distant Lake Nipigon, where Claude Allouez found them in 1667. By 1671 they were back on their own lake. Voyageurs then made it a link on the Montreal fur route, and around 1780 the North West Company raised Fort La Ronde on its shores; the post passed to the Hudson's Bay Company with the merger of 1821.
zh:
奥迪什夸加米格，即尼皮辛湖地区，湖泊宽阔而水浅，地处渥太华河与乔治亚湾之间，湖水经弗伦奇河注入休伦湖。尼皮辛人是兼有奥吉布瓦与阿尔冈昆渊源的阿尼什纳贝人，村落散布在湖岸与岛上，在浅滩捕捞鲟鱼，并沿马塔瓦河—渥太华河—圣劳伦斯河的独木舟走廊转销北方森林的毛皮；后来的法国人震慑于他们的先知，称他们为「巫师」。1444年，这片湖区属于这些北方贸易的中间人，欧洲人尚未涉足。

1610年前后，随休伦人队伍游历的艾蒂安·布吕莱成为第一个见到此湖的欧洲人；1615年，萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰在前往休伦尼亚途中经过此地，让·尼科莱则在1620年代中期至1633年住在湖畔，设有木屋与贸易站。耶稣会士克洛德·皮雅尔在尼皮辛人中传教九年，聚集起一小群信徒，但1649—1650年易洛魁人攻入此地，尼皮辛人随阿米克瓦人远逃至尼皮贡湖，克洛德·阿卢埃1667年在那里找到了他们；到1671年，他们已回到故乡的湖边。此后船夫们把这里当作通往蒙特利尔毛皮商路的一站，1780年前后西北公司在湖畔建起拉龙德堡；1821年公司合并，这座贸易站归入哈德逊湾公司。

en:
The Weskarini, the Wàwàckeciriniwak or 'people of the deer', were the Algonquin band the French called La Petite Nation, the Little Nation, to distinguish them from the Kichesipirini of the upper Ottawa. Their country ran along the north bank of the Ottawa and up the Lièvre, Rouge and Petite-Nation rivers, whose name remembers them. They lived by the seasonal hunt, fishing and gathering, their beaver pelts feeding the trade networks of the Ottawa valley, and they held the forested mountain the French named Mont Tremblant as Manitonga Soutana, the mountain of the spirits. In 1444 these Laurentian valleys belonged to the Weskarini alone, and no European canoe had yet entered them.

Champlain met Ouescharini bands on his way up the Ottawa in 1613, and they became French allies, trading at the mouths of the Gatineau, Saint-Maurice and Dumoine and wintering with their Huron friends. The Beaver Wars undid them: when the Iroquois struck in 1654, the main band was cut to pieces and survivors fled toward Trois-Rivières, where the Jesuits sheltered only those who accepted baptism. By the later seventeenth century the Weskarini ceased to appear as a people, their kin merged into other Algonquin communities, and their valleys were left to passing fur brigades. On 16 May 1674 the French West India Company granted the empty country as the seigneury of La Petite-Nation, the westernmost in New France, to Bishop François de Laval; he planned an Algonquin mission there, then thought better of it and gave the seigneury to the Séminaire de Québec in 1680. Joseph Papineau bought it in 1801 and 1803, set a sawmill on the river and brought in New England lumbermen, and in 1817 the estate passed to his son Louis-Joseph.
zh:
韦斯卡里尼人自称瓦瓦克齐里尼瓦克，意为「鹿族」，是阿尔冈昆人的一支；法国人称他们为「小民族」（La Petite Nation），以区别于渥太华河上游的「大民族」基奇西皮里尼人。他们的家园沿渥太华河北岸展开，深入列夫尔河、鲁日河和因他们得名的小民族河上游。他们按季节狩猎、捕鱼、采集为生，所产海狸皮进入渥太华河谷的贸易网络；那座被法国人叫作蒙特朗布朗的山林，在他们心中是神灵之山马尼通加·苏塔纳。1444年时，这些劳伦琴山谷只属于韦斯卡里尼人，还没有欧洲人的独木舟驶入。

1613年，尚普兰溯渥太华河而上时遇见了韦斯卡里尼人；他们后来成为法国盟友，在加蒂诺河、圣莫里斯河和迪穆万河口贸易，并与交好的休伦人一同过冬。海狸战争葬送了他们：1654年易洛魁人来袭，主体队伍被击溃，幸存者逃向三河市，而耶稣会只收留接受洗礼的人。到17世纪后期，韦斯卡里尼作为一个族群不再见于记载，余部并入其他阿尔冈昆社群，山谷只剩过往的毛皮商队。1674年5月16日，法国西印度公司把这片人烟稀少的土地封为主教方济各·德·拉瓦尔的「小民族领地」，那是新法兰西最西端的领地；他原想在此为阿尔冈昆人设传教站，后来作罢，1680年将领地赠予魁北克神学院。约瑟夫·帕皮诺1801年和1803年分两次买下领地，在河上建起锯木厂，招来新英格兰伐木工人；1817年，产业传到他的儿子路易-约瑟夫手中。

en:
The island beneath Mount Royal lies where the Ottawa River meets the St. Lawrence, just short of the Lachine Rapids that give the place its Iroquoian name, Osheaga, the 'big rapids'. In 1444 it is Laurentian country: St. Lawrence Iroquoians tend fields of maize, beans and squash around stockaded villages of bark-covered longhouses and fish one of the river's richest fisheries. Hochelaga, girdled by its wooden palisade near the mountain, is the greatest of these towns, and the rapids at its gate mark the head of sea navigation, where inland canoe brigades meet ocean-going vessels.

Jacques Cartier, sailing upstream in search of a route to China, landed on 2 October 1535 and was led through Hochelaga the next day; he named the hill above the village Mount Royal. By the end of the century warfare and dispersal had emptied the valley of its Iroquoians; in 1603 Champlain found only an abandoned hunting ground. In 1611 he cleared a fur-trade station, Place Royale, below the rapids, and on 17 May 1642 Maisonneuve's company of the Société Notre-Dame founded Ville-Marie, where Jeanne Mance opened the Hôtel-Dieu. Beset by Iroquois raids — the settlement of Lachine was destroyed in 1689 — the town grew into the hub of the western fur trade and the launching point for Jolliet, La Salle and the Vérendryes. The Great Peace of Montreal brought 1,300 Indigenous delegates to the town in August 1701, but after the fall of Quebec, Vaudreuil surrendered it to Amherst without a fight on 8 September 1760.
zh:
皇家山下的岛屿坐落在渥太华河注入圣劳伦斯河之处，上游便是拉欣急流——「奥谢阿加」这个易洛魁语地名意为「大急流」。1444年时，这里是劳伦提亚人的土地：圣劳伦斯易洛魁人在木栅环绕、树皮长屋组成的村庄周围种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，又在河上经营全流域最丰饶的渔场。奥什拉加是这些村镇中最大的一座，木栅圈起的村子依皇家山而立；村前的急流是海船航道的尽头，内陆独木舟商队与海船在此交接货物。

1535年10月2日，为寻找通往中国水道而溯河上行的雅克·卡蒂埃登岛，次日被迎入奥什拉加，并把村旁的山丘命名为皇家山。到16世纪末，战乱与流徙使河谷中的易洛魁人散失殆尽，1603年尚普兰见到的只是一片荒废的猎场。1611年，他在急流脚下辟出名为「皇家广场」的毛皮贸易站；1642年5月17日，迈松纳夫率领蒙特利尔圣母使团的人马建立维尔马利，让娜·芒斯在此办起主宫医院。小镇顶住了易洛魁人的反复袭扰——1689年拉欣村即遭其摧毁——日后成为西部毛皮贸易的枢纽，若利埃、拉萨尔、拉韦朗德里等探险家都由此深入大陆。1701年8月，1300名原住民代表会聚于此，缔结《蒙特利尔大和约》；魁北克陷落后，沃德勒伊于1760年9月8日不战而降，城市归入英国之手。

en:
At the narrows where the St. Lawrence squeezes between Cape Diamant and the heights opposite — Kebec, 'where the river narrows', in Algonquin — stood Stadacona, a St. Lawrence Iroquoian town on the Saint-Charles River. Its people lived in bark longhouses above fields of maize, beans and squash and took fish and eel from the great river; their word kanata, a village, would become Canada. In 1444 the river belonged to such towns, and no European sail had yet entered the gulf.

That ended in September 1535, when Jacques Cartier wintered beside the town: scurvy killed a quarter of his men until the Stadaconans showed him annedda, a white-cedar brew that cured the rest. In May 1536 he carried off chief Donnacona and his two sons; none ever returned.
