In August 1541 he came back with five ships and raised Charlesbourg-Royal on the Cap-Rouge, France's first settlement in North America, but sickness and hostility drove the last colonists out in June 1543. When Champlain passed the narrows, Stadacona had vanished, wasted by war, disease and the cooling climate, and only Innu and Algonquin bands still came to fish eel. On 3 July 1608 Champlain built his Habitation below Cape Diamant, the seed of Quebec. The Kirkes took it in July 1629, the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye restored it in 1632, and Champlain died there in 1635.

From 1663 Quebec was the capital of royal New France, seat of a bishopric from 1674. Frontenac drove off Phips's invasion in 1690, and Walker's great fleet was wrecked in the river fogs in 1711 before reaching the town. In 1759 Wolfe's men climbed the heights and on 13 September beat Montcalm on the Plains of Abraham, where both generals fell; the city surrendered five days later. Lévis defeated the British at Sainte-Foy in April 1760 but failed to take Quebec in the ensuing siege, and France ceded Canada in 1763. The Quebec Act of 1774 let the French keep faith and laws, so the American assault on New Year's Eve 1775 died in the snow with Montgomery; the siege ended in May 1776. In 1791 Quebec became capital of Lower Canada, and by the early nineteenth century it was North America's third-largest port, busy with timber ships.
zh:
圣劳伦斯河在钻石角与对岸高地之间骤然收窄——阿尔冈昆语称这里为凯贝克（Kébec），意即「河流变窄之处」。北岸圣夏尔河畔坐落着圣劳伦斯易洛魁人的城镇斯塔达科纳，居民住树皮长屋，屋前是玉米、菜豆和南瓜田，又在大河里捕鱼，尤其是鳗鱼；他们表示村庄的词卡纳塔（kanata）日后演成了「加拿大」。1444年时，大河仍属于这样的村镇，还没有欧洲船帆驶入海湾。

这一切在1535年9月终结：雅克·卡蒂亚在城边过冬，坏血病夺走他四分之一的人手，直到斯塔达科纳人教他用白雪杉熬制安内达（annedda）汤剂，其余人才被治愈。1536年5月他带走酋长多纳科纳和他的两个儿子，三人再无一人归来。1541年8月，他率五艘船重返故地，在卡普魯日筑起法国在北美的第一个定居点「皇家夏尔堡」，但疾病和敌意使最后一批殖民者在1543年6月撤离。等尚普兰经过窄峡时，斯塔达科纳已经消失——一般认为毁于战争、疫病和气候转冷，只有因努和阿尔冈昆游群还来此捕鳗。1608年7月3日，尚普兰在钻石角下建起「居所」，这便是魁北克的起点。1629年7月柯克兄弟夺城，1632年《圣日耳曼昂莱条约》将其归还，尚普兰1635年在此去世。

1663年起，魁北克成为王家新法兰西的首府，1674年起设主教区。1690年，弗龙特纳克击退菲普斯的入侵；1711年，沃克的大舰队还没抵达城市，就在河上浓雾中覆没。1759年，沃尔夫的部队攀上峭壁，9月13日在亚伯拉罕平原击败蒙卡尔姆，两位将领双双殒命，城市于五天后投降。莱维1760年4月在圣福瓦击败英军，随后围攻魁北克未果，1763年法国割让加拿大。1774年《魁北克法案》保住了法裔的信仰与法律，所以1775年新年前夜美军的强攻和蒙哥马利一起死在雪里，围城延续到1776年5月。1791年魁北克成为下加拿大首府，到19世纪初已是北美第三大港，满是运木材的船只。

en:
Toutouskak is the bay the French called Tadoussac, where the Saguenay fjord's black water meets the St. Lawrence estuary. In 1444 it was summer country of the Innu, whom the French would name the Montagnais: they camped on the shore to hunt seal and meet the canoes that came down the Saguenay with furs. When Jacques Cartier stopped there in 1535 he found Innu sealing parties, and by the end of the century Basque whalers flensed their catch on the beach while more than a thousand Innu, Algonquin and Etchemin gathered each summer to barter beaver pelts with the European ships, the busiest fur rendezvous in North America by 1600.

In 1600 Pierre de Chauvin and François Gravé Du Pont, holding Henri IV's monopoly, built a trading house at the mouth of the Saguenay; sixteen men wintered and only five survived, yet Tadoussac became France's first enduring settlement in North America. At a solemn summer feast in 1603 Gravé and Champlain made alliance with the Innu, Algonquin and Etchemin. In 1608 Basque captains answered Gravé's monopoly claims with cannon fire and wounded him before Champlain negotiated a truce. Franciscan Recollet friars opened a mission in 1615, and for thirty years Tadoussac was the only seaport on the St. Lawrence; settlers whaled out of the bay from 1632, and a new mission chapel was raised in 1747. The post joined the royal King's Posts in 1720, kept trading after the British conquest, was leased to the North West Company in 1802, and passed to the Hudson's Bay Company in 1821.
zh:
塔杜萨克位于萨格奈峡湾深色的江水与圣劳伦斯河口湾交汇处。1444年，这里是因努人——法国人后来称他们为蒙塔涅人——的夏日之地：他们在岸边扎营捕猎海豹，并接应从萨格奈河载着毛皮顺流而下的独木舟。1535年卡蒂亚途经此地，见到的正是捕猎海豹的因努人。到16世纪末，巴斯克捕鲸人在海滩上解剖鲸尸、熬炼鲸油，每年夏天还有上千名因努人、阿尔冈昆人和埃切明人聚集于此，用河狸皮与欧洲商船交易；到1600年，这里已是北美最繁忙的毛皮会市。

1600年，持有亨利四世垄断权的皮埃尔·德·肖万与弗朗索瓦·格拉韦·迪蓬在萨格奈河口建起贸易屋；十六人留下过冬，仅五人生还，而塔杜萨克却就此成为法国在北美第一个延续下来的定居点。1603年夏天，迪蓬与尚普兰在一场隆重的宴会上同因努人、阿尔冈昆人和埃切明人结盟。1608年，巴斯克船长们以炮火回应迪蓬的垄断要求、将他击伤，最后由尚普兰谈成休战。1615年方济各重整派修士开设传教点；此后三十年塔杜萨克是圣劳伦斯河上唯一的海港，1632年起定居者从湾口出航捕鲸，1747年又建起一座新的传教小教堂。商站1720年并入王室直辖的国王据点，英国征服后贸易不辍，1802年租给西北公司，1821年转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
The wide bay the Innu called Uashat, 'the great bay', is guarded by seven islands and by the mouths of the Moisie and Sainte-Marguerite rivers. It was the summer ground of two Montagnais bands, the Chisedec — a Mi'kmaq name for the Moisie — and the Oumamiwek west of the Sainte-Marguerite. Families came down from inland hunting grounds to spear salmon, hunt seal and whale and meet in trade, then turned back upriver to winter on caribou in the country they called Nitassinan. By the early 1500s Basque whalers were sailing in each season, yet in 1444 the coast had no European settlement and the year still followed the old round.

Jacques Cartier entered the bay on 18 August 1535 and set down the seven islands as the Ysles Rondes, finding Basque fishermen there before him. In 1603 Champlain anchored off the river he called Saincte Marguerite. On 7 June 1651 the Jesuit Jean de Quen said the first mass and opened the Ange-Gardien mission. François Bissot set up the Sept-Îles fur post in 1661, trading from about 1676 within the king's reserved Domaine du roy, and Louis Jolliet opened another at the Moisie mouth in 1679. The Innu signed the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701. In August 1711 Admiral Walker's expedition against Quebec, groping through fog, lost eight ships and more than 900 men on the Île-aux-Œufs reefs west of the bay, and the point facing the reefs was named Pointe-aux-Anglais. British raiders destroyed the post more than once until it was rebuilt in 1761; the North West Company held it from 1802, and it passed to the Hudson's Bay Company in 1821.
zh:
因努人称作乌阿沙特（Uashat，意即「大海湾」）的宽阔海湾被七座岛屿环护，穆瓦西河与圣玛格丽特河分别从东西两侧在此入海。湾畔夏天是两支蒙塔涅人的聚地：切斯迪克人（Chisedec本是米克马克人对穆瓦西河的旧称），以及圣玛格丽特河以西的奥马米韦克人。各家从内陆猎场赶来叉鲑鱼、捕海豹和鲸、彼此交易，入冬再溯河返回他们称作尼塔希南的故地，靠驯鹿过冬。到16世纪初，巴斯克捕鲸船已年年到此，但1444年时沿岸还没有欧洲人定居，岁月仍按古老的节律轮转。

1535年8月18日，雅克·卡蒂亚驶入海湾，把七岛记作圆岛（Ysles Rondes），发现已有巴斯克渔人先他而至。1603年，尚普兰在他称作圣玛格丽特河（Saincte Marguerite）的河口外抛锚。1651年6月7日，耶稣会士让·德康做了第一场弥撒，并创立守护天使传教所。1661年，弗朗索瓦·比索在国王保留的王家领地内建起七岛毛皮站，约1676年起营业；路易·若列又于1679年在穆瓦西河口另设一站。1701年，因努人签署《蒙特利尔大和约》。1711年8月，沃克海军上将远征魁北克的舰队在雾中摸路，八艘船在湾西的蛋岛礁群失事，九百多人丧生，正对礁群的海角遂得名「英格兰角」。殖民战争中贸易站几度被英军摧毁，1761年重建；该站自1802年归西北公司经营，1821年转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Chisedec was the name later given to the Innu band around Uashat, the great bay that became Sept-Îles, and Mishta-shipu, the Moisie River. The river cuts south through spruce and birch country to the Gulf of St Lawrence and is one of eastern North America's richest salmon waters. In 1444 its people, whom the French would later call Montagnais, moved between coast and boreal interior in portable skin tents. They took salmon and marine mammals in season and followed caribou and moose through Nitassinan, their homeland, while no European mission or trading post yet stood on the bay.

When Jacques Cartier sailed past the islands in 1535, he found Basque fishermen already coming annually for cod and whales, and recorded them as the Ysles Rondes. The fish and fur trades drew the French to settle at the anchorage. Jean de Quen founded the L'Ange-Gardien mission there in 1650, a fur post was operating by 1658, and Louis Jolliet established another in 1679. Chisedec hunters were thus tied to New France's commerce and its wars with the English and Haudenosaunee. After Britain took Canada in 1763, the North West Company took over the Sept-Îles post in 1802; in 1821, the year of its merger with the Hudson's Bay Company, the bay became a Hudson's Bay post.
zh:
切斯迪克是后来文献对一支因努人群的称呼，其活动中心是乌阿沙特大湾与米什塔希普大河；前者日后成为七岛，后者即穆瓦西河。穆瓦西河穿过云杉和桦木林地，南入圣劳伦斯湾，是北美东部鲑鱼最丰沛的河流之一。1444年，这些后来被法国人称作蒙塔格奈人的居民带着可搬运的兽皮帐篷，在海岸与北方森林内陆间往返：渔季捕捞鲑鱼和海兽，狩猎季则在故土尼塔希南内追逐驯鹿与驼鹿。那时海湾边还没有欧洲传教站或贸易栈。

1535年雅克·卡蒂埃驶过群岛时，已有巴斯克渔民年年到此捕鳕和捕鲸；他把这群岛屿记作圆岛。渔业和毛皮贸易随后吸引法国人来到这个锚地。1650年，让·德·康在此创立「守护天使」传教站；1658年当地已有毛皮贸易栈，路易·若列又于1679年另设一处。切斯迪克猎人由此被卷入新法兰西的商业网络，以及它同英格兰人和易洛魁联盟的战争。1763年英国夺取加拿大后，西北公司于1802年接掌七岛贸易站；1821年西北公司与哈德逊湾公司合并，海湾边的据点也转入哈德逊湾公司名下。

en:
Qikirmiut takes its name from the Qikirtamiut, the Inuit islanders of the Belcher Islands. The archipelago's roughly 1,500 treeless islands lie in southeastern Hudson Bay, off the eastern shore of the bay. Dorset communities used them between 500 BCE and 1000 CE, and Thule hunters arrived between 1200 and 1500. In 1444 their Inuit descendants moved by kayak and umiak among islands and sea ice, taking seals, walrus, Arctic char, eiders and caribou; no European fort or boundary had yet entered these waters.

Henry Hudson sighted the archipelago in 1610. The successful fur voyage of 1668 prepared Charles II's 1670 charter, which folded the islands into the Hudson's Bay Company's Rupert's Land. Anglo-French rivalry then swept the bay: Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville defeated the Royal Navy in 1697, and the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht confirmed British rights, though forts and fighting centred on the busier southern routes. No permanent European post was built on the Belchers before 1821, so the islanders continued their seasonal rounds on ice and open water.
zh:
基蒂克美奥特（Qikirmiut）得名自基基尔塔米乌特人（Qikirtamiut），即贝尔彻群岛的因纽特岛民。约一千五百个无树岛屿散布在哈得孙湾东南部，临近哈得孙湾东岸。多塞特人在公元前500年至公元1000年间使用这些岛屿，1200年至1500年间，图勒猎手来到这里。1444年，他们的因纽特后裔乘皮艇和木架皮舟往来于岛屿与浮冰之间，猎捕海豹、海象、北极红点鲑、欧绒鸭和驯鹿；欧洲人的要塞和边界此时尚未进入这片水域。

亨利·哈德逊于1610年望见这座群岛。1668年英国商船在哈得孙湾成功进行毛皮贸易，为查理二世1670年颁发特许状铺平道路，群岛也被划入哈得孙湾公司的鲁伯特地。英法争夺随后席卷海湾：皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德·伊贝维尔1697年击败英国皇家海军舰队，1713年《乌得勒支和约》确认英国的权利，但要塞和战事主要集中在更繁忙的南方航路。直到1821年以前，贝尔彻群岛仍未建立欧洲人常设商站，岛民继续依季节在冰面和开阔水域间往来营生。

en:
Cisasipi is a spelling of Cisâsîpî, Chisasibi, 'Great River', the East Cree country around the mouth of the La Grande on the rocky eastern shore of James Bay. At European contact, the peoples on both shores were Cree, and for centuries families moved nomadically between coast and interior, fishing, hunting and trapping along rivers that froze through the long winter. In 1444 no Atlantic ship had yet entered James Bay, and the riverside camps lived on fish, game and furs taken for their own use.

Henry Hudson entered James Bay in 1610, and the successful fur voyage of 1668, followed by Charles II's 1670 charter, opened the shore to the Hudson's Bay Company. Because French and independent traders could reach this East Main overland from the Saint Lawrence, the Company long found it harder to control than posts farther west. In 1803 it built Fort George near the mouth of the Great River. The post drew Cree hunters into a regular fur trade, but in 1821 most families still kept their seasonal round rather than a permanent village.
zh:
奇萨西比（Cisasipi）是克里语奇萨西比（Cisâsîpî）的异写，意为「大河」，指东克里人在詹姆斯湾岩石东岸、拉格朗德河口一带的土地。欧洲人到来时，海湾两岸的居民都是克里人；许多世纪以来，家族在海岸与内陆间迁徙，沿河流捕鱼、狩猎和设陷阱，度过漫长的冰封冬季。1444年，尚无来自大西洋的船只进入詹姆斯湾，河畔营地以鱼、猎物和自用毛皮为生。

亨利·哈德逊于1610年驶入詹姆斯湾；1668年毛皮航行成功后，查理二世1670年颁发特许状，哈得孙湾公司由此进入这片海岸。由于法国商人和独立商人可从圣劳伦斯方向由陆路抵达东岸，公司长期难以像控制更西的商站那样控制这里。1803年，公司在大河口一带设立乔治堡。商站把克里猎手纳入固定的毛皮贸易，但到1821年，多数家族仍按季节迁徙，尚未形成永久村落。

en:
Iyiyiw is a spelling of iiyiyuu, the East Cree or Eeyou self-designation, meaning 'human being'. This taiga-and-lake country southeast of James Bay is part of Eeyou Istchee, its routes running by the Eastmain and Rupert rivers toward Lake Mistassini. In 1444 it had neither town nor fixed border: Eeyou families summered by the lakes, then moved to inland hunting and trapping grounds for caribou, beaver, marten, fish and waterfowl. Mistassini means 'big rock' in Cree or Innu, and Cree and Innu travellers already knew the portage chain from the Saguenay to the Rupert.

Henry Hudson reached James Bay in 1610, opening the Eeyou coast to Europeans. In 1663 Guillaume Couture's party, guided by Indigenous travellers, took forty-four canoes up the Saguenay to Lake Mistassini and on toward the Rupert. In 1671 Jean Talon sent the Jesuit Charles Albanel with Paul Denys de Saint-Simon; they wintered among the Mistassini, baptised about a hundred adults and as many children, and reached James Bay on 28 June 1672. In 1674 the English seized Albanel on the Rupert, a sign of the Anglo-French struggle for the fur route. Lakeside trading posts moved several times before the Hudson's Bay Company fixed the post at present Mistissini in 1821.
zh:
伊伊尤（Iyiyiw）是东克里人自称伊伊尤（iiyiyuu，亦写作Eeyou）的异写，意为「人」。这片詹姆斯湾东南的泰加林与湖沼地带属于东克里祖地埃尤乌伊斯特奇，通路沿东梅因河和鲁珀特河伸向米斯塔西尼湖。1444年，这里既无城镇也无固定边界：东克里家族在湖畔度夏，入秋后转入内陆猎场和陷阱地，获取驯鹿、河狸、貂、鱼和水鸟。米斯塔西尼在克里语或因努语中意为「大岩石」，克里人与因努旅行者早已知道从萨格奈河到鲁珀特河的水陆联运路线。

亨利·哈德逊于1610年到达詹姆斯湾，欧洲人由此打开东克里海岸的门户。1663年，纪尧姆·库蒂尔一行在原住民向导带领下，乘四十四艘独木舟上溯萨格奈河，抵达米斯塔西尼湖，再继续前往鲁珀特河。1671年，让·塔隆派遣耶稣会士夏尔·阿尔巴内尔与保罗·德尼·德·圣西蒙北上；他们在米斯塔西尼人中过冬，为约一百名成人和同样数目的儿童施洗，并于1672年6月28日到达詹姆斯湾。1674年，英国人在鲁珀特河拘押阿尔巴内尔，显示法英对毛皮通道的争夺。湖畔商站此后多次迁移，哈得孙湾公司最终于1821年把商站设在今米斯塔西尼的位置。

en:
At Baawitigong, the 'place of the rapids', the waters of Lake Superior race down the St. Marys River into Lake Huron. The Ojibwe kept a permanent village beside the white water, taking sturgeon in spring and whitefish in autumn, when thousands gathered from the surrounding Anishinaabe nations to fish and trade; the Odawa and Potawatomi came too, and the catfish-named Marameg belonged to the same country. In 1444 the Sault was one of the great meeting-places of the upper lakes, and its people knew nothing as yet of Europeans.

Étienne Brûlé, travelling with Huron guides, was the first European to see the rapids in 1623 according to French reckoning, and the French named them the Sault de Gaston after the brother of Louis XIII. In 1668 Claude Dablon and Jacques Marquette founded a Jesuit mission there and renamed the place Sault Sainte-Marie, and on 4 June 1671 Saint-Lusson, before chiefs of fourteen nations, proclaimed the whole Lake Superior country for France. In 1736 Louis Denys de La Ronde opened a shipyard at Pointe-aux-Pins on the north shore, launching the first decked vessel onto Lake Superior to search for copper. The country passed to Britain in 1763; around 1790 the North West Company built a post and in 1798 the first lock past the rapids. On 20 July 1814 an American raid burned the company depot and the lock, but the British held the Sault.
zh:
在巴维蒂冈——奥吉布瓦语意为「瀑布之地」，苏必利尔湖的湖水经圣玛丽斯河急泻入休伦湖。奥吉布瓦人在激流边设有定居村落，春天捕捞鲟鱼，秋天捕捞白鱼；每到白鱼季，阿尼什纳贝各族数千人到此捕鱼交易，奥达瓦人和波塔瓦托米人也会前来，以鲶鱼为名的马拉梅格人就生活在这片地方。1444年，圣玛丽瀑布是五大湖上游最大的聚会地之一，居民还不知欧洲人为何物。

据法国方面记载，1623年艾蒂安·布吕莱在休伦向导带领下成为第一个见到这处急流的欧洲人，法国人随后以路易十三之弟加斯东之名称之为加斯东瀑布。1668年，克洛德·达布隆与雅克·马凯特在此建立耶稣会传教站，将此地改名为圣玛丽瀑布；1671年6月4日，圣吕松在十四个部族的首领面前宣布整个苏必利尔湖地区归属法国。1736年，路易·德尼·德·拉龙德在北岸的潘角开设船坞，造出第一艘驶入苏必利尔湖的甲板船，用以寻访铜矿。1763年，此地随新法兰西转入英国之手；1790年前后西北公司在此设站，1798年又修成绕过急流的第一座船闸。1814年7月20日，美军的一支突击队焚毁了公司货栈和船闸，但圣玛丽瀑布仍在英国人手中。

en:
Shallow, island-dotted Lake Abitibi and the river draining it northwest toward the Moose River and James Bay form a canoe country between the Ottawa valley and Hudson Bay. The Algonquian-speaking Abitibi people gathered at Pointe Abitibi in summer and dispersed through the surrounding forests and waterways in winter, taking fish, moose, and caribou. French sources explain their name as the people of the dark-water lake. In 1444 no European fort or boundary had reached this cold forest belt, and the shoreline camps and portages remained in Indigenous hands.

From the mid-17th century French missionaries and fur travellers learned the route. In 1686 Pierre de Troyes led a French expedition through the lake on its way to seize English Hudson's Bay posts on James Bay and built a post on the shore; it became a fur station on the Montreal-James Bay canoe route. After Britain acquired Canada in 1763, independent traders and the North West Company competed on the lake. The Hudson's Bay Company opened Abitibi House in 1794 but found it unprofitable against its rivals and abandoned it in 1811. When the two companies merged in 1821, the remaining lake post passed into the Hudson's Bay Company system.
zh:
水浅、岛群散布的阿比蒂比湖，与向西北汇入穆斯河、通向詹姆斯湾的阿比蒂比河，构成渥太华河谷与哈得孙湾之间的独木舟通道。阿尔冈昆语的阿比蒂比人在阿比蒂比角聚集度夏，冬季分散到周围森林和水道，捕鱼并猎取驼鹿与驯鹿。法文资料把他们的自称解释为「深色湖水之人」。1444年，欧洲人的堡垒和疆界尚未进入这片寒冷林带，湖岸营地与搬运路线仍由原住民自主使用。

17世纪中期以后，法国传教士和毛皮旅人逐渐知道这条路线。1686年，皮埃尔·德·特鲁瓦率领法国远征队经阿比蒂比湖前往詹姆斯湾，夺取英格兰人的哈得孙湾商站，并在湖畔设立据点；这里后来成为蒙特利尔至詹姆斯湾独木舟路线上的毛皮商站。英国1763年取得加拿大后，独立商人和西北公司相继在湖畔竞争。哈得孙湾公司1794年开设阿比蒂比屋，却因竞争无利可图，于1811年放弃。1821年两家公司合并，湖畔剩余商站并入哈得孙湾公司的贸易体系。

en:
Mosoni is a form of Môsonî, the Moose Cree or Ililiw country around the mouth of the Moose River on James Bay. In 1444 the Moose Cree kept an annual round rather than a fixed town: summer canoe parties fished and gathered berries, autumn camps hunted geese and ducks along the bay shore, families moved inland for winter game and fur traps, and spring hunts met the birds flying north. The broad Moose River linked the winter forest to the estuary, but no European had yet entered the bay.

Henry Hudson sailed into James Bay in 1610, and the Jesuit Relations of 1671 already located Moose Cree on the bay and river. Pierre-Esprit Radisson reconnoitred the area in the winter of 1670-71, and in 1673 the Hudson's Bay Company governor Charles Bayly founded Moose Fort. Cree traders brought pelts, provisions and labour to the post. In March 1686 the Chevalier de Troyes led thirty French soldiers, seventy Canadian volunteers and Indigenous guides more than 800 miles in eighty-two days from Montreal by the Ottawa, Abitibi and Moose rivers; Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville helped storm the sleeping garrison. Renamed Fort St Louis, it was retaken and burned by the English in 1696, confirmed to Britain in 1713 and rebuilt in 1730. After a fire in 1735 it took seven years to rebuild. The 1821 merger with the North West Company removed the rivalry, the post expanded beyond its palisade as Moose Factory and became the Company's principal James Bay base.
zh:
莫索尼（Mosoni）是克里语莫索尼（Môsonî）的异写，指驼鹿克里人（Ililiw）在詹姆斯湾麋河口一带的土地。1444年，驼鹿克里人没有固定城镇，而是遵循年复一年的迁徙周期：夏季乘独木舟捕鱼、采集浆果，秋季在湾岸猎捕雁鸭，冬季举家迁入内陆猎取大型猎物和毛皮兽，春季再趁水鸟北返狩猎。宽阔的麋河把冬季森林与河口相连，欧洲人此时尚未进入海湾。

亨利·哈德逊于1610年驶入詹姆斯湾，1671年的《耶稣会报道》已在湾岸和麋河畔提到驼鹿克里人。皮埃尔-埃斯普里·拉迪松于1670年至1671年冬侦察这一带；1673年，哈得孙湾公司总督查尔斯·贝利设立麋河堡。克里商人把毛皮、食物和劳力带到商站。1686年3月，德·特鲁瓦骑士率领三十名法国士兵、七十名加拿大志愿兵和原住民向导，从蒙特利尔出发，经渥太华河、阿比蒂比河和麋河行军八十二天、八百多英里，皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德·伊贝维尔随军突袭睡梦中的守军。法军将其改名圣路易堡，英军1696年夺回后焚毁，1713年《乌得勒支和约》确认英国主权，商站又于1730年重建。1735年火灾后，重建历时七年。1821年哈得孙湾公司与西北公司合并，竞争随之消失，商站越过栅栏扩展为驼鹿工厂，成为公司在詹姆斯湾的主要基地。

en:
Attawapiskat takes its name from the Swampy Cree, or Mushkegowuk, name for a people of the divided rocks. Their country followed the Attawapiskat River from inland lakes to Akimiski Strait on James Bay, opposite Akimiski Island. In 1444 the river mouth was a spring and summer gathering place where bands came for the fishing; in winter families dispersed to the coast, inland woods and the island, trapping, hunting and gathering roots, berries and nuts. No European post stood on the river; canoe, toboggan and seasonal trails joined the camps.

Henry Hudson's 1610 voyage opened James Bay to Europeans, but Attawapiskat long felt the fur trade only through posts farther south. A French overland force captured the Hudson's Bay Company's bay forts in 1686, and Jesuits made only brief contacts while the French held Fort Albany. An English four-ship fleet retook Albany in 1693, and the post became the nearest fixed point in a commercial fur economy that drew Cree hunters and trappers southward; Company influence still reached this river only weakly in the early nineteenth century. In 1814 George Budge built a wintering Hudson's Bay post on Attawapiskat Lake, abandoned in 1817, reopened in 1820 and given up in 1821. At the end of the period the mouth remained chiefly a seasonal Mushkegowuk camp.
zh:
阿塔瓦皮斯基特（Attawapiskat）出自沼泽克里人（Mushkegowuk）的名称，意为「岩石分隔之地的人」。他们的土地沿阿塔瓦皮斯基特河，从内陆湖沼延伸到詹姆斯湾的阿基米斯基海峡，与阿基米斯基岛相望。1444年，河口是各群体春季和夏季聚集捕鱼的地方；入冬后，家族分散到海岸、内陆林地或岛上设陷阱、狩猎，采集根块、浆果和坚果。河上没有欧洲商站，独木舟、平底雪橇和季节小径连接着各处营地。

亨利·哈德逊1610年的航行使欧洲人得见詹姆斯湾，但阿塔瓦皮斯基特长期只通过更南方的商站感受毛皮贸易。1686年，法国陆上远征军夺取哈得孙湾公司的湾岸要塞；法军控制奥尔巴尼堡期间，耶稣会士只与这一地区有过短暂接触。1693年，一支由四艘船组成的英国舰队夺回奥尔巴尼堡，这里成为最近的固定商站，把克里猎手和陷阱猎人引入商业毛皮经济；但直到19世纪初，公司势力对阿塔瓦皮斯基特河仍很薄弱。1814年，乔治·巴奇在阿塔瓦皮斯基特湖设立哈得孙湾公司冬站，1817年废弃，1820年重开又于1821年放弃。到1821年，河口仍主要是沼泽克里人的季节性营地。

en:
The Nelson and Hayes rivers break the swampy south-western shore of Hudson Bay, draining the Saskatchewan and Red River countries into the ice through a maze of tidal flats and muskeg. The people of the coast call themselves Mushkegowuk, 'people of the muskeg' — the western Swampy Cree — who summered on the bay fishing and hunting goose in the marshes, and wintered inland at the caribou hunt, their bark canoes the only masters of that river network. In 1444 no European had entered their waters, and the furs of the interior moved along their canoe roads without passing a single foreign post.

English ships followed soon after the bay was found. Thomas Button reached the Nelson in 1612, buried his sailing master Robert Nelson at its mouth, wintered at Port Nelson and claimed the coast as New Wales. The Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Nelson there in 1684, its first headquarters, and then York Factory on the handier Hayes. Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville failed to take the post in 1690, captured it in 1694 and renamed it Fort Bourbon, lost it back to the English in 1695, and retook it on 13 September 1697 after sinking the Hampshire in the bay's greatest sea fight; France held it until Utrecht, and the Company returned in 1714. Henry Kelsey had already set out from York in June 1690 to pioneer the inland fur route, and for the rest of the period the coastal Mushkegowuk — the Company's 'Homeguard Cree' — provisioned the ships and manned the trade that drew the Saskatchewan country down to the bay.
zh:
纳尔逊河与海斯河在哈得孙湾西南岸切开泥泞的低地，把萨斯喀彻温河、雷德河流域的来水，经由潮滩与泥炭沼组成的迷宫送入冰海。沿岸居民自称穆什凯戈乌克人（Mushkegowuk），意为「泥炭沼之人」，即西部沼泽克里人：他们夏天到海湾捕鱼、在沼泽猎雁，冬天退回内陆猎驯鹿，树皮独木舟是纵横这方水网唯一的主人。1444年，还没有欧洲人进入这片水面，内陆的毛皮沿他们的独木舟之路流动，不经过任何外人的商栈。

海湾被发现后，英国船很快循迹而来。托马斯·巴顿1612年驶抵纳尔逊河，把领航员罗伯特·纳尔逊安葬在河口，随后在纳尔逊港过冬，并宣布这片海岸为新威尔士。哈得孙湾公司1684年在河口建起尼尔森堡——公司的第一个总部——随后又在更便于航行的海斯河上设立约克堡。皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·迪贝维尔1690年攻城受挫，1694年攻陷该堡并改名波旁堡，1695年又被英军夺回；1697年9月13日，他在哈得孙湾规模最大的海战中击沉「汉普郡」号，再次拿下要塞。法国一直占据此地，直到《乌得勒支和约》签订，公司1714年才返回。早在1690年6月，亨利·凯尔西已从约克堡出发，开辟通往内陆的毛皮之路；此后整个年代里，沿海的穆什凯戈乌克人——公司所称的「卫堡克里人」——为船队提供给养，支撑起把萨斯喀彻温腹地引向海湾的贸易。

en:
West of Hudson Bay the forest ends and the Barren Lands begin: treeless tundra cut by the Kazan River and strewn with lakes, swept each year by the great caribou migration. The Ahiarmiut — the Ihalmiut, 'people from beyond' — hunted that herd along the inland rivers, while other Inuit wintered on the coast taking seal, walrus and beluga; Chipewyan Dene, caribou-eaters from the taiga edge, likewise ranged east to the bay shore. In 1444 this was a country measured by the caribou walk, where no ship had yet watered.

In 1619 the Dane Jens Munk brought two ships into the Churchill River; winter and scurvy killed all but three of his 64 men. The Hudson's Bay Company built the Churchill River Post in 1717 and raised the stone Prince of Wales Fort there between 1731 and 1741, drawing the Chipewyan into trade after their peace with the Cree of 1715-16. Through that century, as the caribou failed, the Dene drew south and Kivallirmiut bands took to wintering inland year-round. Samuel Hearne first set out from Churchill in 1769; in 1770 he set out again with Chipewyan guides under Matonabbee, crossed the Kazan and Dubawnt barrens to the Coppermine, and on 17 July 1771 watched his Dene companions massacre an Inuit camp at Bloody Falls. In 1782 the French admiral La Pérouse accepted the surrender of the great stone fort without a shot.
zh:
哈得孙湾以西，森林走到尽头，便是「不毛之地」：没有树木的苔原被卡赞河切开，湖泊星罗棋布，驯鹿群的年度大迁徙年复一年扫过旷野。阿希亚尔米尤特人——自称伊哈尔米乌特，意为「来自远方之人」——沿内陆河流追逐鹿群；另一些因纽特人则在海岸过冬，捕猎海豹、海象和白鲸；来自泰加林边缘、以驯鹿为食的奇佩瓦恩迪纳人，也向东活动到湾岸。1444年的这片土地以驯鹿的脚步丈量，还没有一条船在这里补过淡水。

1619年，丹麦人延斯·蒙克率两艘船驶入丘吉尔河；寒冬与坏血病夺去64名船员中61人的性命，只有3人驾船返国。哈得孙湾公司1717年建起丘吉尔河商栈，又在1731至1741年间筑成石砌的威尔士亲王堡；1715至1716年奇佩瓦恩人与克里人议和后，他们开始成批前来贸易。同一世纪里，驯鹿减少，迪纳人逐渐南撤，基瓦利尔米乌特（驯鹿因纽特人）转为终年在内陆生活。塞缪尔·赫恩1769年首次从丘吉尔堡出发，1770年再度启程，由马顿纳比率领的奇佩瓦恩人做向导，越过卡赞河与迪邦特湖一带的荒原，抵达科珀曼河；1771年7月17日，同行的迪纳人在血腥瀑布突袭一处因纽特营地，大开杀戒，赫恩只能在一旁看着。1782年，法国海军将领拉佩鲁斯兵不血刃，接受了这座巨大石堡的投降。

en:
Rainy Lake, Gojiji-zaaga'igan to the Ojibwe after its many inlets and Tekamamiouen to the Cree for the rain that sweeps it, drains westward by the Rainy River into the Lake of the Woods and the Winnipeg River, the canoe road from Lake Superior into the far interior. Its people, the Gojijiwininiwag, were Saulteaux of the Monsoni country, living on fish and the wild rice of its bays and trading along that road; the Cree dwelt to their west and the Sioux to the south, and war with the southerners was never far off. In 1444 the lake was still entirely their own.

In 1688 Jacques de Noyon became the first European to reach Rainy Lake and threw up a temporary post, and a fort Robutel de La Noue built there in 1717 was abandoned before long under Sioux pressure. In 1731 Christopher Dufrost de La Jemeraye, pushing ahead of his uncle La Vérendrye, raised Fort Saint-Pierre at the lake's outlet, the first French post west of Lake Superior; a Cree chief named La Colle gave the French his aid against the Sioux, though war with them came anyway in 1741. The fort served the western trade until 1758, and between 1775 and 1787 the North West Company built Fort Lac la Pluie on the same ground. The Hudson's Bay Company set up Lac la Pluie House there in 1818, three years before the two companies were joined.
zh:
雷尼湖在奥吉布瓦语中称戈吉吉湖，因湖岸多湾而得名；克里人则称之为特卡马米温，意即「雨总是下个不停」。湖水向西经雷尼河注入伍兹湖与温尼伯河，这条水路正是从苏必利尔湖通往西部内陆的独木舟干道。湖畔居民是戈吉吉维尼尼瓦格人，即蒙索尼一带的索尔托人，以捕鱼和采食湖湾中生长的野稻为生，并沿这条商路贸易；他们西边住着克里人，南边住着苏人，与南方邻居的战事从未真正远去。1444年，这座湖还完全属于他们自己。

1688年，雅克·德努永成为第一个到达雷尼湖的欧洲人，并搭起一座临时驿站；1717年罗比泰尔·德拉努在那里修建的堡垒，不久便因苏人的威胁而废弃。1731年，克里斯托夫·迪弗罗·德拉热默赖赶在舅父拉韦朗德里之前，在湖的出口处建起圣皮埃尔堡，这是苏必利尔湖以西第一座法国驿站；克里人首领拉科勒帮助法国人对付苏人，但对苏战争还是在1741年爆发。堡垒维持西部贸易直到1758年；1775至1787年间，西北公司在同一地点建起雨湖堡，1818年哈德逊湾公司又在此设立雨湖商馆，三年后两家公司合二为一。

en:
The Red River comes down out of the plains to Lake Winnipeg, and at its meeting with the Assiniboine lies the Forks, a canoe crossroads and trading ground used by First Nations for thousands of years. The great lake to the north was winipīhk, 'muddy water', in Western Cree. Before contact, corn grew in fields along the Red, and the waterways linked the bison hunters of the plains with the fishing and trapping camps of the forests; Cree, Anishinaabe, Assiniboine and Dakota all met here. In 1444 no European had ever seen the lake, and the Forks was an indigenous crossroads where only furs, hides and dried meat changed hands between nations.

Henry Kelsey of the Hudson's Bay Company may have been the first European to sight Lake Winnipeg in 1690. In 1738 the French under La Vérendrye built Fort Rouge at the Forks, their first post on the Red River. British traders took over after 1763: the North West Company raised Fort Gibraltar in 1809, and in 1812 the Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Douglas while Lord Selkirk's Scottish settlers founded the Red River Colony beside it. On 19 June 1816 the rivalry over the pemmican trade came to bloodshed at Seven Oaks, where Cuthbert Grant's Métis killed Governor Robert Semple and twenty of his men for the loss of one Métis. The two companies merged in 1821, ending their long feud at the Forks.
zh:
雷德河自草原北流入温尼伯湖，在与阿西尼博因河交汇处形成「福克斯」河汊，是原住民使用了数千年的独木舟枢纽和贸易地。北边的大湖在西克里语中称温尼皮赫克，意为「浑水」。与欧洲人接触之前，雷德河沿岸已种有玉米，水网把草原上的野牛猎人与林间捕鱼设阱的营地连成一片，克里人、奥吉布瓦人、阿西尼博因人和达科他人都在此往来。1444年时还没有任何欧洲人见过这座湖，河汊完全是原住民的通衢，往来的只有各族之间的毛皮、兽皮和肉干。

1690年，哈德逊湾公司的亨利·凯尔西可能是第一个望见温尼伯湖的欧洲人。1738年，拉韦朗德里麾下的法国人在河汊建起鲁日堡，这是他们在雷德河上的第一座商栈。1763年后英国商人接手：西北公司1809年筑起直布罗陀堡；1812年，哈德逊湾公司建起道格拉斯堡，塞尔扣克伯爵的苏格兰移民同时在旁建立雷德河殖民地。1816年6月19日，争夺肉糜饼贸易的冲突在七株橡树流血收场，卡斯伯特·格兰特率领的梅蒂人击杀总督罗伯特·森普尔及其部下二十人，梅蒂一方仅死一人。1821年两公司合并，河汊上的长期争斗随之结束。

en:
Lake Winnipeg — wīnipēk, 'muddy water', in Cree — is a vast, shallow remnant of glacial Lake Agassiz, and its eastern shore rises into the Atikaki, 'caribou country' in Anishinaabe: granite ridges and black spruce where the Bloodvein, Berens and Poplar rivers come down out of the Shield. Cree bands netted whitefish and sturgeon on the lake and hunted moose and caribou in the woods; Anishinaabe peoples lived to the south-east and Assiniboine on the prairie edge. In 1444 the lake's long sand beaches were empty of Europeans.

Henry Kelsey, travelling out from York Factory, is thought to have been the first European to sight the lake in 1690. In 1733 a son of La Vérendrye came within twenty miles of it before ice stopped him; the French reached the lake in 1734, mapped it as Ouinipigon and raised Fort Maurepas on its southern shore, and the lake's furs began to slide toward Montreal instead of the bay. Traders first descended the Berens from the Severn country in 1767, and the Hudson's Bay Company established a post in the Berens River area in 1814; the lake route linked York Factory with the Red River.
zh:
温尼伯湖——克里语名温尼佩克（wīnipēk），意为「浑水」——是冰川时代阿加西斯湖残留的一片广阔浅湖；湖东岸地势隆起，便是阿蒂卡基（Atikaki），阿尼什纳比语意为「驯鹿之地」：花岗岩脊与黑云杉林间，布拉德维恩河、贝伦河、波普勒河从加拿大地盾奔流而下。克里人部落在湖上捕捞白鱼和鲟鱼，在林中猎驼鹿与驯鹿；东南方住着阿尼什纳比人，草原边缘则是阿西尼博因人。1444年，长长的湖滩上还没有一个欧洲人。

一般认为，1690年从约克堡方向而来的亨利·凯尔西，是最早见到此湖的欧洲人。1733年，拉韦朗德里的一个儿子前进到距湖仅二十英里处，被浮冰挡住；法国人1734年抵达大湖，把它记作韦尼皮贡（Ouinipigon），并在湖南岸建起莫勒帕堡，湖中的毛皮也随之改向蒙特利尔，而不再流向海湾。1767年，商人首次从塞文河地方顺贝伦河而下；1814年，哈得孙湾公司在贝伦河一带设立商栈，这条湖路把约克堡与雷德河连在一起。

en:
Lake Manitoba runs from the edge of the plains into the boreal woods, its two basins pinched together at the Narrows, where wind and water over the shallow strait made a sound heard as the voice of the Great Spirit — manitou-wapow in Cree, manidoobaa in Ojibwe, the straits of Manitou from which Manitoba takes its name. Assiniboine and Cree camps lined its shores, taking fish and waterfowl from the reed beds and meeting the bison hunters of the grassland to the south. Through the Narrows, linked by short portages, a canoe road ran between the Assiniboine River and the great lake to the north. In 1444 only those nations knew the waterway; no European had yet mapped a league of it.

La Vérendrye's French parties reached the lake in the mid-1730s, calling it Lac des Prairies and canoeing through it from Fort La Reine on their way to the Saskatchewan, and it became a link in the fur route to Hudson Bay. In 1767 French fur traders built a second Fort Dauphin on the north shore of neighbouring Dauphin Lake, and after the wars the Hudson's Bay Company and the North West Company both ran posts on that lake, vying for the lake-country furs until their merger in 1821 ended the rivalry there.
zh:
马尼托巴湖从草原边缘伸入北方针叶林，两座湖盆在最窄处收束为大窄口：风浪穿过浅水海峡，声若大神的低语——克里语称马尼图瓦波，奥吉布瓦语称马尼多巴，意为「大神的海峡」，马尼托巴一名即出于此。湖岸散布着阿西尼博因人和克里人的营地，他们在芦苇荡中捕鱼、猎取水禽，与南边草原上的野牛猎人相会。穿过大窄口、经几段短途陆运，独木舟可在阿西尼博因河与北方大湖之间往来。1444年时，只有这些部族认得这条水道，欧洲人尚未绘出它的一里水程。

1730年代中期，拉韦朗德里的法国队伍抵达此湖，称之为草原湖，从拉雷讷堡出发经此划向萨斯喀彻温河，马尼托巴湖由此成为通往哈得孙湾皮毛商路的一环。1767年，法国毛皮商人在邻近的多芬湖北岸建起第二座多芬堡；战乱之后，哈德逊湾公司与西北公司都在多芬湖畔经营商栈，争夺湖间地带的毛皮，直至1821年两公司合并，湖上的相争才告结束。

en:
West of Lake Winnipeg the Saskatchewan River breaks out of the boreal forest into Cedar Lake, then runs through Grand Rapids into Lake Winnipeg; Lake Winnipegosis lies to the south. Swampy Cree bands have gathered here for thousands of years; at the wooded narrows of the Saskatchewan, Opaskwayak in their language, families met each summer to fish, harvest and keep the rites of the Midewiwin. The river was also a highway, and most of the furs taken in the west and northwest came down it by canoe. In 1444 the lakes and the narrows were the country of the woods Cree, while the grassland to the south was Assiniboine ground.

Henry Kelsey came this way between 1690 and 1692, the first European on the Saskatchewan. In 1741–42 the La Vérendryes built Fort Dauphin on Lake Winnipegosis, Fort Bourbon near the river's outflow and Fort Paskoya on Cedar Lake, later moved upstream to The Pas — posts meant to turn the canoe brigades away from Hudson Bay. Anthony Henday visited Paskoya in 1754 and dismissed the post as a hogsty, and as New France collapsed the French burned and abandoned the chain in 1758–59. Independent winterers and then the North West Company reopened the old sites, which the Hudson's Bay Company eventually took over.
zh:
杰诺利尼位于温尼伯湖以西，萨斯喀彻温河钻出北方针叶林，注入锡达湖，再经大急流汇入温尼伯湖；温尼伯戈西斯湖位于南侧。沼泽克里人的支系在此聚居数千年：萨斯喀彻温河林木丛生的窄口，克里语称奥帕斯夸亚克，各家族每年夏天到此捕鱼、采集、举行米德维温仪式。这条河又是一条通衢，西部和西北部出产的毛皮大半顺河由独木舟运出。1444年时，湖泊与窄口是林地克里人的家园，南边的草原则是阿西尼博因人的地界。

1690年至1692年间，亨利·凯尔西经此前往野牛草原，是第一个抵达萨斯喀彻温河的欧洲人。1741至1742年，拉韦朗德里父子在温尼伯戈西斯湖畔建起多芬堡、在河口附近建起波旁堡，又在锡达湖畔建起帕斯科亚堡（后来上移至帕斯），意在把独木舟商队从哈得孙湾引开。1754年安东尼·亨迪到访帕斯科亚堡，把这座商栈贬为猪圈；新法兰西崩溃之际，法国人于1758至1759年焚毁并放弃了这一串堡垒。此后先是个体冬猎者、继而西北公司重开旧址，最终由哈德逊湾公司接管。

en:
Satsuma covers the Satsuma Peninsula and the East China Sea coast of southern Kyushu, the western half of the later Kagoshima mainland. Its sheltered inlet at Kagoshima looks toward Sakurajima, while coastal villages, iron-bearing hills and mountain valleys feed traffic into Kinko Bay. The court province was separated from Hyuga after a Satsuma-Hayato rising in 702, and its old provincial seat stood near Satsumasendai. The Shimazu had served as military governors since the Kamakura period, and by the late 1300s their Shimizu Castle at Kagoshima was the chief warrior base. In 1444 the old provincial administration had already given way before the Shimazu, whose ships and retainers tied the province more closely to the bay than to the old court offices.

Kagoshima brought Christianity into Japan when Francis Xavier landed at nearby Gionnosu on 15 August 1549. Under Shimazu Takahisa and Yoshihisa, the Shimazu brothers united Satsuma, Ōsumi and Hyūga, crushed the Ōtomo at Mimigawa and defeated the Ryūzōji at Okitanawate; for a time they held nearly all Kyushu. Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Kyushu campaign of 1587 forced them back to their home provinces. The Shimazu joined the western army at Sekigahara in 1600 yet kept their lands, and Shimazu Iehisa began Kagoshima Castle the next year.

In 1609 a Satsuma expedition captured Shuri and King Shō Nei in Ryukyu after fighting through the islands. The Amami Islands came under Satsuma, while the Ryukyu court kept its throne and its tributary trade with China. That arrangement allowed Chinese and Southeast Asian goods to keep reaching Kagoshima even after the Tokugawa maritime restrictions. Sengan-en, the Shimazu villa garden, was laid out for Shimazu Mitsuhisa in 1658. Satsuma remained one of the largest outer lordships in 1821.
zh:
萨摩位于九州南部的萨摩半岛和东海沿岸，相当于后来鹿儿岛本土的西半部。鹿儿岛海湾遮蔽风浪，与樱岛相望；沿海村落、产铁山地和山谷中的物产都汇集到锦江湾。702年萨摩隼人叛乱后，该地从日向国分置为令制国，古国府靠近萨摩川内。镰仓时代以来，岛津氏担任守护；到14世纪后期，鹿儿岛的清水城已成为其主要武家据点。1444年，旧国衙体制早已让位于岛津氏，把萨摩联系起来的是家臣团以及鹿儿岛湾里的船只。

1549年8月15日，方济各·沙勿略在鹿儿岛附近的祇园之洲登陆，开始在日本传教。岛津贵久、义久在位时，岛津兄弟统一萨摩、大隅和日向，在耳川击败大友氏，又在冲田畷击破龙造寺氏，一度控制九州大部。1587年，丰臣秀吉发动九州征伐，将他们压回本国诸郡。1600年，岛津氏在关原之战中加入西军，却保全了领地；第二年，岛津家久开始修筑鹿儿岛城。

1609年，萨摩军沿琉球各岛作战后攻陷首里，俘虏尚宁王。奄美群岛改由萨摩控制，琉球朝廷则保留王位和对中国的朝贡贸易。凭借这种安排，即使德川幕府施行海禁，中国和东南亚货物仍能运抵鹿儿岛。1658年，岛津光久营建岛津氏别邸庭园仙岩园。到1821年，萨摩仍是最大的外样大名领地之一。

en:
Cheongju lies in the Musimcheon valley in central Korea, where the road from Hanyang to the south-western provinces crosses the grain country of Chungcheong. The mountain fortress of Sangdang Sanseong has guarded the heights above it since Baekje times, and below it Unified Silla laid out Seowon, one of its five secondary capitals, in 685; Goryeo gave the town the name Cheongju in 940. The town's surest title to fame is a book. In 1377 monks at Heungdeok Temple printed the Jikji, an anthology of Zen patriarchs' teachings, with movable metal type, the oldest surviving book printed that way, seventy-eight years before Gutenberg's Bible. An iron flagpole from Yongdu Temple, cast in 962, still stands on the old temple site in the town centre. In 1444 Cheongju was a quiet prefectural town beneath its fortress, sending its grain up the road to Hanyang.

Cheongju was fought over twice under the Joseon kings. Early in 1592 Kuroda Nagamasa's division took the town and the Chungcheong defence commissioner fled. Cho Hon, a former magistrate of Okcheon, raised a thousand civilian volunteers, and the monk Yeonggyu joined him with five hundred warrior monks; about fifteen hundred men stormed the west gate and retook Cheongju, the first victory of the war won by righteous army and monk-soldiers together. Cho Hon and Yeonggyu both fell later that year at Geumsan, and Sangdang Sanseong was repaired in 1596. In March 1728 Yi In-jwa's Soron and Namin rebels seized Cheongju Castle as the first move of the Musin Rebellion against King Yeongjo, claiming the king was not the true heir. The royal army retook the castle within weeks, Yi In-jwa was captured and executed, and the rising collapsed.
zh:
清州位于朝鲜中部的无心川谷地，汉阳通往西南诸道的大路穿过忠清道的产粮区，打这里经过。上党山城自百济时代起就扼守着城北的高地；685年，统一新罗在山下设西原小京，为五小京之一，940年高丽改其名为清州。清州最出名的是一本书：1377年，兴德寺僧众用金属活字印出禅门祖师法语集《直指心体要节》，这是现存最古老的金属活字印本，比古腾堡圣经早七十八年。城中的龙头寺旧址上，立着一根962年铸造的铁幢杆。1444年的清州，是山城脚下一处安静的州治，所产谷物沿大路运往汉阳。

朝鲜时代，清州两度沦为战场。1592年开战之初，黑田长政所部攻占清州，忠清道防御使弃城而逃。玉川前县监赵宪募集义兵一千，灵圭率僧兵五百来会，两军共约一千五百人猛攻西门，收复清州，这是义兵与僧兵首次联手告捷。赵宪与灵圭后来都在同年的金山之战中战死，上党山城也于1596年重修。1728年3月，李麟佐率少论派与南人叛军袭取清州城，作为反对英祖的戊申乱第一着，声称英祖并非正当的王位继承人。官军数周内夺回城池，李麟佐被俘处死，各地叛乱随之瓦解。

en:
Bungo occupied eastern Kyushu, from the Kunisaki Peninsula and the harbour of Funai to the mountain valleys bordering Hyuga and Higo. Old Toyo was divided into Bungo and Buzen in 701, and in 1185 Minamoto no Yoritomo sent the Otomo clan east from Kanto as shugo to subdue pro-Taira warriors in Kyushu. The clan held Bungo through the Kamakura and Muromachi centuries, ruling from Funai over a timbered, deeply indented coast; in 1444 local gentry and shrine and temple estates still kept much of the countryside in their own hands.

Bungo's Nanban years centre on Otomo Sorin. Francis Xavier visited him at Funai in 1551, after which Portuguese, Chinese and Ryukyu shipping made the port one of the busiest in Kyushu. The Portuguese surgeon Luis de Almeida founded an orphanage there and in 1556 a hospital with wards for surgery, internal medicine and leprosy, the first in Japan to practise Western medicine. Jesuit records called Sorin the King of Bungo, and the Tensho embassy sent by the Christian lords of Kyushu sailed for Rome in 1582. Baptised in 1578 with the name Francisco, he pulled down Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines and pressed his subjects to convert, but defeat by the Shimazu at the Mimikawa later that year broke Otomo power. Shimazu armies overran Bungo in 1586 and took Funai, where Almeida's hospital was destroyed in the invasion; Sorin appealed to Toyotomi Hideyoshi, whose Kyushu campaign restored his son Yoshimune, though Sorin himself died in 1587 before the fighting ended. Yoshimune later renounced Christianity and was dispossessed for cowardice in the Korean wars, and under the Tokugawa Bungo was divided between shogunal land and the small domains of Funai, Kitsuki, Usuki and Saeki.
zh:
丰后在九州东部，从国东半岛和府内港湾延伸到毗邻日向、肥后的山地河谷。701年，旧丰国被分为丰前和丰后；1185年，源赖朝为压制九州的亲平氏武士，把出身关东的大友氏派任守护。大友氏历经镰仓、室町时代保有丰后，以府内为本据统治这片森林密布、海岸曲折的土地；1444年，地方豪族和寺社庄园在乡间仍掌握很大实权。

丰后的南蛮时代以大友宗麟为中心。1551年，方济各·沙勿略到府内与他会面，此后葡萄牙、中国和琉球的商船使府内成为九州最繁忙的港口之一。葡萄牙外科医生路易斯·德·阿尔梅达先在府内开办孤儿院，又于1556年建起分设外科、内科和麻风病科的医院，这是日本第一所施行西医的医院。耶稣会文献称宗麟为「丰后之王」，九州基督教大名派遣的天正遣欧使节也于1582年启程前往罗马。1578年他受洗，取教名方济各，随后拆毁佛寺神社、强令领民改宗；同年在耳川之战中败于岛津氏，大友家由盛转衰。1586年岛津军攻占丰后、拿下府内，阿尔梅达的医院毁于战火；宗麟向丰臣秀吉求援，秀吉发动九州征伐，恢复了其子大友义统的领国，宗麟本人却在1587年战事结束前病殁。义统后来弃教，又在朝鲜之役中因怯战被除封；德川时代，丰后被分为幕府天领和府内、杵筑、臼杵、佐伯诸小藩。

en:
Okinawa is the chief island of the Ryukyu chain, lying between the East China Sea and the Pacific about 640 kilometres south of Kyushu. Its gusuku lords formed the three realms of Hokuzan, Chuzan and Nanzan, with Chuzan holding Shuri and the neighbouring port of Naha. Ming investiture tied the court to the Chinese tribute system, and Fujianese families settled in 1392 supplied diplomats, interpreters and shipbuilders. Shō Hashi united the three realms in 1429 and made Shuri Castle the royal seat. In 1444, only fifteen years later, Naha junks carried silver, swords, ceramics, spices, sappanwood and sugar between China, Japan, Korea and Southeast Asia, while noro priestesses kept the island rites at the Shuri court.

Naha's harbour works soon matched that trade. In 1451 a Chinese engineer built the roughly one-kilometre Chōkōtei causeway to link the port islands with Okinawa and receive Ming envoys; warehouses and the Mie and Yarazamori forts covered the anchorage. In 1458 the court hung the newly cast Bell of Many Nations in Shuri's main hall, its inscription presenting Ryukyu as a maritime intermediary. The Second Shō dynasty took power in 1469. Under Shō Shin, who reigned from 1477 to 1527, local lords were brought to Shuri, the priestesses were placed under court order, and Ryukyu extended its control over the Sakishima Islands and, by 1571, the northern Amami group.

Satsuma invaded in 1609 and met stiff resistance on almost every island on the route before taking Shuri and King Shō Nei. The Fifteen Articles placed Ryukyuan diplomacy and commerce under Satsuma supervision, and the Amami Islands were ceded, but Shuri kept its throne and most internal government. The court also continued its tributary missions to China, which let Chinese goods pass toward Kagoshima under the Tokugawa maritime restrictions. Naha's Tsuboya potters established their enameled Ryukyuan ware in 1682, and the Shuri court still administered Okinawa's internal affairs in 1821.
zh:
冲绳是琉球群岛的主岛，位于东海与太平洋之间，北距九州约640公里。岛上按司曾形成北山、中山、南山三个政权，其中中山据守首里和邻近的那霸港。明朝的册封把琉球宫廷纳入朝贡体制，1392年定居的福建人后裔则为王府提供外交官、通译和造船工匠。1429年，尚巴志统一三山，以首里城为王都。1444年，距统一仅十五年，那霸的帆船已在中国、日本、朝鲜和东南亚之间运载白银、刀剑、瓷器、香料、苏木和糖；祝女则在首里宫廷维持岛上祭祀。

那霸的港埠设施很快跟上贸易规模。1451年，一名中国工匠主持修筑长约1公里的长虹堤，把港中诸岛与冲绳本岛连接起来，以便迎接明朝使节；仓库和三重城、屋良座森城拱卫泊地。1458年，王府把新铸的万国津梁之钟悬挂在首里城正殿，铭文把琉球称作海上往来的津梁。1469年，第二尚氏取得王位。尚真1477年至1527年在位期间，各地按司被集中到首里，祝女也被纳入宫廷秩序；琉球将先岛群岛纳入治下，到1571年又控制了奄美群岛北部。

1609年，萨摩军队入侵，在航线上的几乎每座岛屿都遇到顽强抵抗，最终攻陷首里、俘虏尚宁王。《掟十五条》把琉球的外交和贸易置于萨摩监管之下，奄美群岛被割让，但首里朝廷保留王位和大部分内政。琉球继续向中国派遣朝贡使节，中国货物也因此能在德川海禁之下输往鹿儿岛。1682年，那霸壶屋工匠烧出釉彩琉球陶器；直到1821年，冲绳内政仍由首里朝廷管理。

en:
Ha Tinh is the narrow shelf where the Hong Linh hills press the coastal road against the Gulf of Tonkin. At its southern end the Hoanh Son range runs into the sea, and the Ngang pass is the one level road between the northern plain and the lands beyond; inland are rice fields, and the coast faces fishing inlets and salt pans. The Ming ruled Dai Viet from 1407, but in 1418 Le Loi raised the Lam Son revolt just to the north, and in 1424, taking a lieutenant's advice, the rebels came down this coast to seize Nghe An, the base from which they drove the Ming out in 1427. In 1444 Ha Tinh is the southern march of the restored Later Le, a line of soldier-settler villages, salt pans and fishing harbours guarding the road south.

Every army moving between the Red River plain and the southern coast used that road. After the Mac seized the throne, the men of Thanh Hoa and Nghe An kept the Le cause alive. Nguyen Hoang, whose elder brother had been killed by their brother-in-law Trinh Kiem, had his sister, Kiem's own wife, plead for a distant posting, and in 1558 he led the men of Thanh-Nghe south through the Ngang pass to hold Thuan Hoa, the march that grew into the Nguyen lordship. For a century Ha Tinh lay just behind the Trinh-Nguyen front, its coast crowded with troops and supply junks; in 1774 Hoang Ngu Phuc took 30,000 men down the road to storm the Nguyen capital Phu Xuan, and Tay Son armies marched it in both directions. Tien Dien village here was the ancestral home of the poet Nguyen Du. Born in 1766, he served through the fall of the Le and then the Nguyen, led the embassy to the Qing in 1813 and 1814, and recast the Chinese novel Jin Yun Qiao as a 3,254-line verse tale in nom, The Tale of Kieu, before his death in 1820.
zh:
河静是洪岭余脉把沿海官道挤向北部湾的一道狭长海岸，南端横山直插入海，横山关是北方平原与南来之地之间唯一平缓的通道；内陆开稻田，海边列着渔港和盐田。1407年起明朝统治大虞，1418年黎利在北面举兵蓝山，1424年义军纳部将之计沿这条海岸南下夺取乂安，并以此为根基在1427年逼退明军。1444年的河静是复国后黎朝的南陲，一连串军屯村寨、盐灶和渔港守着南下的大路。

往来红河平原与南方海岸之间的军队，都要走这条路。莫氏篡位后，清化、乂安的军民支撑着后黎残局。阮潢的兄长被姐夫郑检所杀，他由身为郑检之妻的姐姐求情，求得外放边地；1558年，阮潢率清乂子弟过横山关南下镇守顺化，这支人马后来长成阮主基业。此后百余年，河静紧贴郑阮前线，沿岸挤满兵马与粮船；1774年黄五福率兵三万沿这条路攻克阮都富春，西山军又在道上来回奔波。本省仙田村是诗人阮攸的祖籍，他1766年出生，历事后黎与阮朝，1813至1814年出使清朝，把中国小说《金云翘传》改写为3254句的喃字长诗《传翘》，1820年病故。

en:
Suō occupies the south-western tip of Honshu on the Seto Inland Sea, with sheltered harbours looking across to Kyushu, Korea and the China coast. Its provincial capital of the law-code age stood at Hōfu, seat of the Tamanooya Shrine, the province's ichinomiya. From the fourteenth century the land belonged to the Ōuchi, a warrior house that claimed descent from the kings of Baekje and grew rich on the tally trade with Ming China and Joseon Korea, shipping out copper, sulphur and swords and bringing back silk and porcelain. In 1360 Ōuchi Hiroyo moved the clan seat to Yamaguchi, a new town laid out on Kyoto's grid and later called the 'Kyoto of the west'; its five-story Kōshaku-ji pagoda, raised for Ōuchi Yoshihiro, was completed in 1442. In 1444 Ōuchi Mochiyo rules a trading city whose wealth draws monks, scholars and merchants fleeing Kyoto's wars.

The Ōuchi pushed their way into national politics. Masahiro led the western host through the Ōnin War from 1467, and his son Yoshioki marched on Kyoto in 1508 and restored the deposed shogun Ashikaga Yoshitane. The ink painter Sesshū, lately returned from the Ming ports, worked in Yamaguchi under the clan's patronage. Their feud with the Hosokawa over the China trade came to blows at Ningbo in 1523, after which Ming cargoes moved mainly on Ōuchi ships. Under Ōuchi Yoshitaka the city was Japan's main meeting point with foreign learning, and the Jesuit Francis Xavier was received there in 1550 and given leave to preach. Yoshitaka then planned to move the emperor and his court from war-torn Kyoto to Yamaguchi; his generals took it for court intrigue, rose under Sue Harukata in 1551 and forced him to kill himself. Mōri Motonari, another former vassal, destroyed Sue at Itsukushima in 1555 and took Suō two years later.

After Sekigahara in 1600 the victorious Tokugawa cut the Mōri down to Suō and Nagato, and the clan built its new capital at Hagi on the Sea of Japan coast, the domain later known as Chōshū. Yamaguchi shrank to a posting town between Hagi and the port of Mitajiri. The Kikkawa, kinsmen of the Mōri, kept Iwakuni, and in 1673 raised the five-arched Kintai Bridge over the Nishiki River.
zh:
周防地处本州西端，面朝濑户内海，良港隔海望向九州、朝鲜和中国沿海。律令时代的国衙在防府，一之宫玉祖神社坐落于此。14世纪起周防归大内氏统治；这一武家自称百济王族后裔，靠对明朝和朝鲜李朝的勘合贸易致富，运出铜、硫磺和刀剑，换回丝绸与瓷器。1360年大内弘世把本据迁到按京都条坊营建的山口，这里后来有「西京」之称；大内氏在香积寺为纪念大内义弘而建的五重塔1442年落成。1444年大内持世在此统治，贸易之财把躲避京都战火的僧侣、学者和商人吸引到这座城里。

大内氏既插手全国政局，也经营文化。政弘自1467年起统率应仁之乱的西军，其子义兴1508年进兵京都，拥戴被废的将军足利义稙复职。刚从明朝港口归国的画僧雪舟，受大内氏庇护在山口作画。与细川氏争夺对明贸易的冲突1523年在宁波爆发，此后对明贸易主要由大内的船只经营。大内义隆时，山口是日本接触海外学问的主要去处，耶稣会士方济各·沙勿略1550年在此谒见义隆，获准传教。后来义隆想把天皇和朝廷从战火中的京都迎到山口，家臣认定这是公卿弄权，1551年拥陶晴贤起兵，逼他自尽。另一家旧臣毛利元就1555年在严岛攻灭陶晴贤，两年后平定周防。

1600年关原合战后，得胜的德川氏把毛利氏减封到周防、长门两国，毛利氏在日本海沿岸的萩另建居城，即后来的长州藩。山口沦为萩与三田尻港之间道路上的宿场町。毛利一门吉川氏领有岩国，1673年在锦川上建起五拱的锦带桥。

en:
Izumo faces the Sea of Japan on the San'indo coast of western Honshu, where short rivers running off the Chugoku mountains water small coastal plains. It is the sacred country of the Izumo Taisha, shrine of Okuninushi, the god who built the land and binds human marriages, counted among the oldest shrines in Japan; after the Yamato court brought Izumo under its rule the shrine kept its priestly standing, and local belief held that in the tenth month all the gods gathered there, so Izumo called that month kamiarizuki while the rest of Japan called it kannazuki. The same rivers carried iron sand, which tatara furnaces smelted into steel for swordsmiths and armourers. The medieval shugo, Sasaki, Yamana and finally Kyogoku, rarely came to the province; in 1444 the Kyogoku lived in distant Omi while their deputies the Amago ruled from Gassan Toda, a mountain castle above the coast.

Expelled for seizing manors, Amago Tsunehisa retook Gassan Toda by surprise in 1486 and built the clan into Sengoku lords holding Izumo and Hoki and the steel trade; under his grandson Haruhisa, shogun and court named him shugo of eight San'in and Sanyo provinces in 1552. Haruhisa's sudden death opened the way for Mori Motonari, whose blockade starved Gassan Toda into surrender in 1566, when Amago Yoshihisa was led captive to Aki. The loyal retainer Yamanaka Yukimori, shown in later portraits with a crescent moon on his helmet, raised restoration armies from 1569 in the name of Amago Katsuhisa and fought on until he was captured and killed after Kozuki Castle fell in 1578. After Sekigahara the Horio received Izumo and Oki at 240,000 koku, and Horio Yoshiharu built Matsue Castle among the lakes in 1607-1611, moving the seat from the mountain fastness to a new castle town. A short Kyogoku tenure followed, and then Matsudaira Naomasa held Matsue at 186,000 koku, his line ruling into the nineteenth century; the present hall of the Izumo Taisha was raised in an eighteenth-century rebuilding.
zh:
出云在本州西部山阴道的日本海沿岸，中国山地流下的小河在海边灌出一片片小平野。这里是出云大社所在的神国，大社祭祀开辟国土、司掌姻缘的大国主，是日本最古老的神社之一；并入大和朝廷后，大社仍保有特殊的神职地位。按当地信仰，旧历十月全国诸神都聚集到出云，所以日本别处称十月为神无月，出云却称神在月。这些河川还冲下铁砂，踏鞴炉把铁砂炼成钢铁，供给刀匠和甲具工匠。中世的守护佐佐木氏、山名氏到最后的京极氏都很少来国中；1444年，京极氏远居近江，守护代尼子氏据临海山丘上的月山富田城统治此地。

尼子经久因侵吞庄园被逐，却在1486年以奇袭夺回月山富田城，此后把尼子家经营成领有出云、伯耆、掌控制铁之利的战国大名；其孙晴久时，幕府和朝廷在1552年任命他为山阴、山阳八国守护。晴久暴卒后，毛利元就趁机围城，1566年城中粮尽开城，尼子义久被押往安艺。忠臣山中幸盛在后世画像中总戴着饰有新月的头盔，他自1569年起兵拥立尼子胜久谋求复兴，一直打到1578年上月城陷落，被俘后遭毛利氏杀害。关原之战后，堀尾氏以二十四万石领有出云和隐岐，堀尾吉晴在1607至1611年于湖水之间修筑松江城，把居城从山上旧城迁到新的城下町。其后京极氏短暂入封，松平直政再以十八万六千石入主松江，其家族一直统治到19世纪；出云大社的本殿则在18世纪重建。

en:
Harima, or Banshū, faces the Seto Inland Sea on the San'yō road between the capital region and western Honshū. Its coastal plain grew rice for the sea lanes, and Himeji, below Himeyama hill, controlled both the road and the nearby port. The province's 713 gazetteer, the Harima no Kuni Fudoki, is one of only five provincial gazetteers to survive from that age. The Akamatsu governors first fortified Himeyama in 1333. Their house nearly fell in 1441, when Akamatsu Mitsusuke murdered Shōgun Ashikaga Yoshinori at a Kyōto banquet; Yamana Sōzen's army invaded Harima, and Mitsusuke killed himself at Shōyama Castle. In 1444 the Yamana held the province newly granted to them, with local loyalties still unsettled.

The Akamatsu returned during the Ōnin War, but Sengoku fighting split Harima among local houses. The Kuroda kept Himeji for the Kodera until Kuroda Yoshitaka opened the castle to Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1580. East of Himeji, Bessho Nagaharu held Miki Castle for the Mōri through Hideyoshi's siege of 1578–1580, later called the starvation of Miki; the castle fell only when its food was exhausted. Hideyoshi built a three-storey keep at Himeji in 1581 and used it as his base for the Chūgoku campaign.

After Sekigahara, Tokugawa Ieyasu gave Himeji to his son-in-law Ikeda Terumasa. From 1601 to 1609 Ikeda rebuilt it with three moats and 83 connected structures, a project estimated at 2.5 million labour days; its white walls gave it the names White Egret or White Heron Castle. Honda Tadamasa added more towers in 1617–1618, including the Dressing Tower built for Princess Sen. Harima was then divided into smaller domains. At Akō, the forty-seven rōnin avenged Asano Naganori in 1703; the shogunate ordered forty-six of them to commit seppuku and pardoned the youngest.
zh:
播磨别称播州，南临濑户内海，位于畿内通往西本州的山阳道上。沿海平原出产稻米，由海路外运；姬山脚下的姬路同时控住道路和附近港口。713年成书的《播磨国风土记》，是流传下来的五国风土记之一。赤松氏1333年开始在姬山筑城。1441年，赤松满祐在京都的宴席上刺杀幕府将军足利义教，山名宗全的军队攻入播磨，满祐在城山城自尽。1444年，山名氏新领播磨，当地豪族的向背仍未安定。

赤松氏在应仁之乱中复兴，但战国纷争把播磨分到多家豪族手中。黑田氏替小寺氏驻守姬路，直到1580年黑田孝高把城交给丰臣秀吉。在姬路东面，别所长治据三木城呼应毛利氏，承受秀吉1578至1580年的围攻，也就是后来所说的「三木干杀」；城中粮尽后城才陷落。秀吉1581年建起三层天守，把姬路城作为中国征伐的大本营。

关原之战后，德川家康把姬路封给女婿池田辉政。1601至1609年，辉政重修三重护城河和八十三座相连建筑，工程估计耗费二百五十万人次人工；白色城墙使它得到「白鹭城」之称。本多忠政1617至1618年增建角楼，包括为千姬修建的化妆楼。播磨随后被分成多个小藩。在赤穗，四十七士于1703年为主君浅野长矩复仇；幕府命令其中四十六人切腹，赦免了年纪最小的一人。

en:
Kyoto is the city of the Yamashiro basin that Emperor Kanmu founded in 794 as Heian-kyo, a grid of broad avenues modelled on the Tang capital Chang'an; the imperial court stayed there through every change of military government. The Ashikaga shoguns kept their Flower Palace in the Muromachi district, which gave the age its name. Aristocratic Kamigyo lived around the court and the great Zen temples, while merchant Shimogyo wove and sold the silk that clothed court and clergy. In 1441 a retainer murdered the shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori, and by 1444 the shogunate could no longer overawe the provincial lords. Kyoto was still the ceremonial capital of Japan, home to the court and to Yoshimitsu's gold-leafed Kinkaku-ji built half a century earlier, but the provinces were slipping from its grasp.

In 1467 rival shogunal deputies carried their feud into the streets: the Onin War was fought across Kyoto for ten years, mansions and temple grounds became fortresses and most of Kamigyo burned. Weavers who came back afterwards settled on the site of Yamana Sozen's western encampment, and their district took the name Nishijin, the western camp; Nishijin silk clothed court and daimyo houses for the rest of the period. Oda Nobunaga entered the city in 1568 and ended the Muromachi shogunate five years later. In 1582 Akechi Mitsuhide attacked him at the Honno-ji temple with only a small guard present, and Nobunaga took his own life. Toyotomi Hideyoshi replanned the streets, gathered the city's temples into Teramachi and raised the Odoi earthworks around the city in 1591. Tokugawa Ieyasu built Nijō Castle as his Kyoto residence from 1601, its buildings partly brought from Fushimi, and through the Edo centuries Kyoto stood with Edo and Osaka as one of Japan's three great cities.
zh:
京都是山城国盆地里的都城。794年桓武天皇迁都于此，定名平安京，仿照唐都长安的棋盘形制营建；此后武家政权几度更迭，朝廷始终没有离开。足利将军的「花之御所」位于室町，这个时代便因室町得名。上京的公家环绕朝廷和禅宗大寺居住，下京的商人则织造、贩卖供应朝廷与僧俗的丝绸。1441年，足利义教被家臣刺杀，到1444年，幕府已无力压服地方大名。京都仍是日本礼仪上的都城，有朝廷在，有半个世纪前足利义满所建的金阁寺，但诸国正一步步脱离它的掌控。

1467年，对立的管领把仇杀带进京都街巷：应仁之乱在城里打了十年，公家宅邸和寺社境内变成堡垒，上京大半焚毁。战后回城的织工在山名宗全的西阵旧址上定居，这一带便得名西阵；西阵织的丝绸在此后两个世纪里供应朝廷与各大名家。1568年织田信长入京，五年后终结室町幕府。1582年，明智光秀袭击驻在本能寺、身边仅有少量随从的信长，信长自尽。丰臣秀吉重新划分街区，把诸寺集中到寺町，又在1591年沿城筑起御土居。1601年起，德川家康营建二条城作为将军在京都的居馆，部分建筑移自伏见城；整个江户时代，京都与江户、大坂并称三都。

en:
Settsu faces the Seto Inland Sea at the mouth of the Yodo, where western sea lanes meet the river route to Kyoto. Its old harbour of Naniwa held Emperor Kotoku's court in the 7th century, and the province kept two enduring landmarks in Shitennō-ji and Sumiyoshi Taisha. Taira no Kiyomori developed the anchorage of Ōwada no Tomari, later Hyōgo, which Muromachi merchants used for the official trade with Ming China. In 1444 the province was in the hands of the Hosokawa, the house that supplied Muromachi shogunal deputies, though rival deputy houses and local lords held much of the countryside. Whoever controlled the bay could move troops and provisions toward Kyoto.

In 1496 Rennyo, leader of the Jōdo Shinshū, built a retreat on the long slope called Ōsaka. The houses gathering around it became Ishiyama Hongan-ji, and after the Yamashina Hongan-ji burned in 1532 it served as the sect's headquarters. About a hundred monks patrolled the fortified temple, a bell could summon thousands of defenders, and the Mōri kept it supplied by sea. Oda Nobunaga's forces opened the siege in 1570; eleven years passed before imperial mediation secured the surrender in 1580, and the temple was burned as it was abandoned. Toyotomi Hideyoshi began Ōsaka Castle on the site in 1583, modelling it on Azuchi and enlarging it until his death in 1598. Tokugawa Ieyasu attacked the Toyotomi there in the winter campaign of 1614 and summer campaign of 1615, after which Toyotomi Hideyori died and the castle burned. The Tokugawa rebuilt it as their own stronghold during the 1620s.

The shogunal city then lived by warehouses and rice. Daimyō kept their tax rice in riverside storehouses, giving Ōsaka the name 'kitchen of the realm'. The rice market moved to Dōjima in 1697, where rice tickets supported both spot transactions and book-transfer trades. In 1730 the shogunate licensed the Dōjima rice exchange and its futures business; the prices set there governed domain finances across Japan.
zh:
摄津位于淀川入海口，面向濑户内海，西海航路与通往京都的水路在此相接。古老的难波津在7世纪曾是孝德天皇朝廷所在，四天王寺和住吉大社则是境内长期沿用的佛教、神道地标。平清盛经营大轮田泊，也就是后来的兵库津；室町商人又以此港开展对明朝的官方贸易。1444年的摄津掌握在细川氏手中，这一族出任室町幕府管领，但其他管领家族和地方豪族仍控制着国内大量土地。控制海湾的一方，就能向京都运送军队和粮秣。

1496年，净土真宗法主莲如在名为「大坂」的长坡修建隐居所。周围聚集的屋舍发展为石山本愿寺；1532年山科本愿寺被焚后，这里成为本山。寺堡约有百名僧人巡逻，钟声可召集数千守兵，毛利氏还从海上输送补给。织田信长的军队1570年开始围城，直到十一年后的1580年才靠朝廷调解使其投降；寺坊在撤离时被焚毁。丰臣秀吉1583年在原址动工修建大坂城，以安土城为范本并持续扩建，直到1598年他去世。德川家康随后在1614年冬之阵和1615年夏之阵进攻丰臣氏，丰臣秀赖败死，大坂城烧毁。德川家又在17世纪20年代把它重建为自己的要塞。

此后的大坂靠仓廪和米粮贸易立身。诸大名把年贡米存在河畔藏屋敷，使大坂得到「天下的台所」之称。1697年米市场迁至堂岛，米切手同时支撑正米现物交易和账合米交易。1730年，幕府公许堂岛米会所及其期货业务；这里定出的米价牵动日本各地藩国的财政。

en:
Indrapura, modern Đồng Dương, was raised as a capital of Champa around 875 by the Buddhist king Indravarman II; his Bhrgu dynasty ruled from it for a century and built the great Mahayana monastery of Lasmindra Lokesvara, while nearby stood the shrine valley of Mỹ Sơn and a roadstead on the Thu Bồn that later became Hội An. Power moved south to Vijaya in the twelfth century, but Indrapura remained the chief place of northern Champa. In 1402 the Hồ dynasty of Đại Việt forced King Indravarman VI to cede Chiêm Động, the coast of present Quảng Nam; the Cham took it back in 1407 when the Ming overthrew the Hồ. By 1444 the restored Lê dynasty and Champa faced each other along this coast, and in May that year Maha Vijaya's attack on Hóa Châu reopened the war on the frontier.

In 1446 the expedition of Trịnh Khả and Lê Thụ captured Vijaya and led Maha Vijaya captive to Thăng Long, though the Cham retook the city the next year. Lê Thánh Tông struck the finishing blow: his navy forced the Đại Áp and Tiểu Áp sea gates off present Tam Kỳ and sacked Vijaya on 2 March 1471, after which Amaravati and Vijaya became the Vietnamese province of Quảng Nam under a Thăng Hoa garrison. In 1558 Nguyễn Hoàng entered Thuận Hóa and soon governed Quảng Nam as well, drawing settlers and soldiers from the north. Under his successors the old Cham roadstead grew into Hội An, called Faifo by foreigners, one of the busiest ports in Southeast Asia: Japanese merchants threw a covered bridge over a canal of the town in 1593–1595 and put a temple on it in 1653 to appease the earthquake monster Namazu, and through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries Japanese red-seal ships, Chinese junks and Portuguese and Dutch traders exchanged silk, porcelain and aloewood. The Tây Sơn rising that began at Quy Nhơn in 1771 turned Quảng Nam into campaigning country and scattered Hội An's foreign trade; with the Nguyễn reunification of 1802 the old kingdom of Indrapura passed into the new dynasty's Quảng Nam domain.
zh:
因陀罗补罗即今东阳，约875年由崇佛的占婆王因陀罗跋摩二世建为都城；他开创的婆利古（Bhrgu）王朝在此统治约一个世纪，营建了大乘大寺罗湿弥因陀罗卢吉湿伐罗（Lasmindra Lokesvara），近旁是美山圣谷，秋盆河下游的一处锚地日后发展为会安。12世纪占婆王城南移阇盘，因陀罗补罗仍是北占婆的首镇。1402年，大越胡朝逼迫占王因陀罗跋摩六世割让占洞，即今广南沿海；1407年明朝灭胡，占人乘机收复故土。到1444年，复国的后黎朝与占婆沿这段海岸对峙，当年五月摩诃贲该攻打化州，边境战端再启。

1446年，郑可、黎受的远征军攻陷阇盘，把摩诃贲该俘回升龙，占人次年又收复都城。黎圣宗给出最后一击：越军水军攻破今三岐近海的大压门、小压门，1471年3月2日洗劫阇盘，阿摩罗伐底与阇盘被吞并，改设广南承宣，驻军升华卫。1558年阮潢入镇顺化，不久兼领广南，招徕北方流民军户。在其后继者治下，占婆古港发展为会安（外国商人称作Faifo），跻身东南亚最繁忙的港口之列：日本商人于1593至1595年在城内运河上架起廊桥，1653年又在桥上建祠，以镇伏引发地震的大鲶（Namazu）；17至18世纪，日本朱印船、中国帆船以及葡萄牙、荷兰商人在此交易丝绸、瓷器和沉香。1771年西山起义在归仁爆发后，广南沦为战场，会安的外商贸易星散；1802年阮朝重新统一，因陀罗补罗故地归入新王朝的广南辖地。

en:
Echizen faces the Sea of Japan and opens inland to the fertile Fukui basin, on the Hokuriku route between Kyoto and northern Honshu. Fuchu in the Takefu district held the old provincial headquarters. Coastal shipping and rice lands gave the province revenue, while papermakers in the Imadate valleys had been producing paper since the Kamakura period and formed a guild at Otaki during the Muromachi period. In 1444 the Shiba still held the title of provincial governor, but the Asakura warriors based at Ichijodani held the armed power that mattered.

Asakura Toshikage displaced the Shiba in 1471 and fortified Ichijodani, a narrow valley enclosed by mountains and the Asuwa River. Gates sealed its northern and southern ends, while the lord's house, samurai residences, temples and artisan streets filled the ground within. Nobles, priests, scholars and performers fleeing the Onin War settled there, and the town held more than 10,000 people at its height. Under Asakura Yoshikage the clan resisted Oda Nobunaga, but Oda and Tokugawa forces defeated the Asakura and Azai at Anegawa in 1570. Nobunaga burned Ichijodani three years later, and after the Echizen Ikko uprising of 1574 the province passed to Shibata Katsuie at Kita-no-sho.

In 1601 Tokugawa Ieyasu enfeoffed his son Yuki Hideyasu in Echizen. Hideyasu rebuilt Fukui Castle and founded the Matsudaira domain, whose officials made local paper a domain monopoly. In 1665 Echizen hosho paper received the privileged mark honoring it as the finest paper in the land.
zh:
越前临日本海，向内连接肥沃的福井盆地，地处京都与本州北部之间的北陆道。武生一带的府中设有旧国衙。沿海船运和稻田供给国用，今立诸谷的纸匠则从镰仓时代开始造纸，室町时代又在大泷组成纸座。1444年，斯波氏仍保有守护头衔，但真正掌握军力的是以一乘谷为据点的朝仓氏。

1471年，朝仓敏景取代斯波氏，把一乘谷筑成要塞。这是一条被群山和足羽川围起的狭窄山谷，南北两端设门，谷内分布馆舍、武家屋敷、寺院和工匠町。应仁之乱期间，公家、僧侣、学者和艺人从京都避乱前来，町中人口极盛时超过一万。朝仓义景与织田信长对抗，却在1570年的姊川之战中随朝仓、浅井联军败给织田和德川军。三年后，信长焚毁一乘谷；1574年越前一向一揆爆发，此后越前落入以北之庄为本据的柴田胜家手中。

1601年，德川家康把越前封给儿子结城秀康。秀康重修福井城，开创松平氏福井藩，藩方把当地和纸列为专卖品。1665年，越前奉书获准使用「御上天下一」印，得到天下第一纸的称誉。

en:
Echigo faces the Sea of Japan on the northern side of Hokuriku, running from the grain plains of Kubiki north to the Shinano and Agano river mouths; most of it later became Niigata Prefecture. Snow piles deep through winter, the Kubiki and Uonuma basins grow rice, and Naoetsu ships the surplus down the coast. The Yamato court set it up as a frontier province facing the Emishi, and under the Muromachi shogunate the Uesugi held the governorship while their Nagao deputies, based at Kasugayama above Naoetsu, ran the province. In 1444 the Nagao and other warrior houses managed the Kubiki heartland, and the grain-rich inland valleys answered mostly to themselves.

The deputy house soon overtopped its masters. In 1507 Nagao Tamekage attacked Governor Uesugi Fusayoshi and turned the Uesugi into puppets; his son Kagetora took Kasugayama in 1548, adopted the Uesugi name and eventually the monk-name Kenshin. A devotee of Bishamonten, the god of war, he fought under a dragon banner and was called the Dragon of Echigo, and Kasugayama, one of Japan's five greatest mountain castles, was his base for the five Kawanakajima battles against Takeda Shingen of Kai between 1553 and 1564; the encounter of 1561 was among the bloodiest of the age. Later tradition says he kept salt flowing to landlocked Kai when other lords cut Shingen off, holding that wars were won with bows and arrows, not salt. After Kenshin died in 1578 the Otate succession war crippled the Uesugi; Toyotomi Hideyoshi moved Uesugi Kagekatsu to Aizu in 1598, and in 1607 Hori Hideharu transferred the seat from Kasugayama down to Fukushima Castle near Naoetsu, leaving the mountain fortress to fall into ruin.

Under the Tokugawa, Echigo was divided among Takada, Nagaoka, Shibata and other domains. Matsudaira Tadateru, a son of Ieyasu, built Takada Castle on the Kubiki plain before he was stripped of the domain in 1616. Niigata, at the Shinano mouth, prospered as a port for the kitamaebune ships that worked the Sea of Japan between Osaka and the northern fisheries, carrying rice south and western goods back north.
zh:
越后位于北陆道北侧、面朝日本海，疆域从颈城平原向北延伸到信浓川、阿贺野川河口，大体相当于后来的新潟县本州部分。这里冬季积雪深厚，颈城、鱼沼诸盆地盛产稻米，直江津港把余粮海运南下。大和政权最初把越后作为面向虾夷的边境国经营，室町时代上杉氏担任守护，世居春日山城的守护代长尾氏替他们打理国政。1444年，长尾氏等武家管理着颈城腹地，盛产谷物的内陆诸谷则大多自行其是。

守护代家很快反客为主。1507年，长尾为景袭击守护上杉房能，把上杉氏变成傀儡；其子景虎1548年入主春日山城，后来继承上杉家，最终取法名谦信。他笃信战神毗沙门天，阵中高悬乱龙旗，人称「越后之龙」；春日山城位列日本五大山城，他以此为基地，在1553至1564年间与甲斐的武田信玄五次会战川中岛，1561年一战尤为惨烈。后世流传他在诸大名断绝武田领食盐时仍照常输盐，说战争要靠弓箭取胜，而不是靠盐。1578年谦信死后，御馆之乱重创上杉氏；1598年丰臣秀吉把上杉景胜转封会津，1607年堀秀治把本据从春日山迁到直江津附近的福岛城，这座山城就此荒废。

江户时代，越后被分给高田、长冈、新发田等藩。德川家康之子松平忠辉在颈城平原修筑高田城，1616年被除封。信浓川河口的新潟作为北前船停靠港繁荣起来，这种货船往来于大阪与北方渔场之间的日本海航线，把稻米运向南方，又把西国货物载回北国。

en:
Uzen covers the Yamagata and Yonezawa basins of southern Dewa. The Ōu Mountains shut these grain lands off from the Pacific, while the Mogami River carries their rice and timber west toward the Sea of Japan. Shiba Kaneyori entered the valley in 1356 as the shogunate's Ushū tandai and raised Yamagata Castle around 1360; his descendants took the local name Mogami. In 1444 the Mogami ruled from Yamagata as a cadet branch of the Shiba, but ties with their armed retainer families were already fraying. The southern basin around Yonezawa remained one of the prizes of northern politics.

Mogami Yoshiaki, later called the Fox of Dewa and an uncle of Date Masamune, brought the Yamagata house to its height. Toyotomi Hideyoshi confirmed him at about 200,000 koku after the 1590 Odawara campaign, and in 1600 he withstood Naoe Kanetsugu's Uesugi invasion while Tokugawa Ieyasu fought at Sekigahara. The victory left Yoshiaki with 570,000 koku, the fifth-largest fief outside the Tokugawa lands. He rebuilt Yamagata Castle and its town and improved the Mogami River for boats and irrigation, but after his death in 1614 succession quarrels weakened the house; the shogunate confiscated the domain in 1622, and Yamagata later passed through the Torii, Hoshina and other families before ending with the Mizuno at 50,000 koku. Defeated with the western side, the Uesugi were moved to the Yonezawa basin with 300,000 koku, reduced to 150,000 in 1664. Uesugi Harunori, remembered as Yōzan, then cut stipends, promoted new industries and enforced years of austerity; the reforms restored Yonezawa enough to carry it through the Tenmei famine of 1781–1789.
zh:
羽前包括出羽南部的山形盆地与米泽盆地，奥羽山脉把这些产粮谷地同太平洋隔开，最上川则把米、木材带向日本海方向。1356年，斯波兼赖以幕府羽州探题身份进入山形，约1360年筑起山形城；其后代取地名改称最上氏。1444年，斯波旁支最上氏据山形统治此地，但他们同武家家臣之间的纽带已经松动。南边的米泽盆地，则仍是北方政局中的一块要地。

最上氏在人称「出羽之狐」的最上义光时达到势力顶点，他也是伊达政宗的舅父。1590年小田原征伐后，丰臣秀吉承认他约二十万石的领地；1600年德川家康在关原作战时，义光挡住了直江兼续率领的上杉军。战后他领有五十七万石，是德川直辖领之外的第五大藩。义光改建山形城与城下町，整治最上川以通舟楫、利灌溉；但他1614年去世后，继嗣纷争削弱了最上家，1622年领地被幕府没收，山形后来经鸟居氏、保科氏等家转封，最后成为五万石的水野氏领。关原战败的上杉氏被移封米泽盆地，初封三十万石，1664年削为十五万石。此后上杉治宪（鹰山）削减俸禄、兴办产业，推行多年俭政，使米泽恢复财力，并撑过了1781至1789年的天明大饥荒。

en:
Rikuzen joins the Pacific lowlands of southern Mutsu with the Aizu basin behind the western hills. In 1189 Minamoto no Yoritomo rewarded Isa Tomomune for his service in the Genpei War with the Date district, and the house founded there became one of the great warrior families of the north. Farther inland, the Ashina held Kurokawa in the Aizu basin and called themselves its governors. In 1444 the Date ruled the eastern lowlands and the Ashina the mountain-girt basin; the passes between them were watched as closely as any border.

Date Masamune, the One-Eyed Dragon of Ōshū, broke Ashina power at Suriagehara in 1589 and made Kurokawa his base. He held it for only a short time. After the 1590 Odawara campaign, Toyotomi Hideyoshi took Aizu from him and enfeoffed Gamō Ujisato, who renamed Kurokawa Wakamatsu, built a seven-storey keep and laid out the castle town around Tsuruga Castle. Gamō rule ended after Ujisato's death in 1595, and in 1598 Uesugi Kagekatsu moved in from Echigo with 1,200,000 koku. Fortifications directed by his minister Naoe Kanetsugu gave Tokugawa Ieyasu a reason to launch the Aizu expedition of 1600, and after Sekigahara the Uesugi were moved to the reduced Yonezawa Domain. The Gamō returned, followed by the Katō, who rebuilt the keep after the earthquake of 1611. In 1643 Katō Akinari was attainted and Aizu passed to Hoshina Masayuki, half-brother of Shōgun Iemitsu and regent for the young Ietsuna; he promoted commerce and agriculture and founded the Nisshinkan domain school, and his Aizu-Matsudaira line kept Tsuruga Castle as a major Tokugawa garrison in the north.

Masamune himself left Aizu for Iwadeyama Castle and then developed Sendai as his new centre. The Date entered the Edo order with about 620,000 koku, the third-largest domain in Japan, though even that house was torn by succession bloodshed in the Date Disturbance of 1671.
zh:
陆前连接陆奥南部的太平洋低地与西山深处的会津盆地。1189年，源赖朝把伊达郡封给在源平合战中效力的伊佐朝宗，他开创的伊达氏后来成为北国大武士家族之一。更深入内陆的芦名氏则以黑川为据点领有会津盆地，自称会津守护。1444年，伊达氏统治东部低地，芦名氏保有群山环抱的盆地，两地之间的山口像边界一样被严密把守。

人称「奥州独眼龙」的伊达政宗1589年在摺上原击破芦名氏，把黑川作为据点。他占据会津的时间并不长。1590年小田原征伐后，丰臣秀吉收回会津，封给蒲生氏乡；氏乡把黑川改名若松，筑起七层天守，并在鹤城（会津若松城）下规划城下町。1595年氏乡死后蒲生氏失势，1598年上杉景胜以一百二十万石从越后入封。家老直江兼续主持修筑的军备，为德川家康1600年发动会津征伐提供了口实；关原之战后，上杉氏被移封到减封后的米泽藩。蒲生氏一度回归，其后加藤氏入封，并在1611年地震后重建天守。1643年加藤明成被改易，会津转封给德川家光的异母弟、幼主家纲的后见人保科正之；他发展商业和农业，创办藩校日新馆，其会津松平家此后把鹤城经营成德川家在北方的重要驻防城。

伊达政宗本人离开会津，先入岩出山城，随后把仙台发展成新的统治中心。伊达氏以约六十二万石位列江户幕府第三大藩，但即便如此，这个家族仍在1671年的伊达骚动中卷入继嗣流血冲突。

en:
Hitachi faced the Pacific on the eastern side of Kanto and covered most of what became Ibaraki, its estates rising from fishing shores and the lower Naka River to wooded northern hills. Its provincial capital and kokubunji stood near Ishioka, while Kashima Shrine on the coastal lowlands honoured Takemikazuchi and drew fighting men as the spiritual home of Japanese swordsmanship. The Satake of Ota Castle held the shugo title for the Ashikaga, but their hold was incomplete: in 1427 the Edo family seized Baba Castle, the stronghold later rebuilt as Mito, and often defied them. In 1444 the province was a patchwork of Satake retainers and independent local houses.

The shrine's martial tradition produced Tsukahara Bokuden, born a vassal of the Kashima clan in 1489 and later called a kensei, a sword saint; he founded the Kashima Shintō-ryū, taught swordsmanship to Shōgun Ashikaga Yoshiteru, and was buried at Kashima after his death in 1571. In the wars of unification the Satake joined Toyotomi Hideyoshi before Odawara in 1590 and were confirmed over 540,000 koku, while the Edo backed the Hōjō and lost Baba, rebuilt as Mito Castle in 1594. Tokugawa Ieyasu distrusted Satake Yoshinobu's conduct at Sekigahara and in 1602 moved him to the much smaller Kubota domain in Dewa. Seven years later Ieyasu's eleventh son Tokugawa Yorifusa entered Mito at 250,000 koku and founded the Mito Tokugawa house, one of the three chief Tokugawa branches. His son Mitsukuni, known as Mito Kōmon, opened the Shōkōkan after becoming lord in 1661 to compile the Dai Nihon-shi, and its annals and biographies were presented to the shogunate in 1720.
zh:
常陆位于关东东部，临太平洋，辖境大体相当于后来的茨城县，领地从渔业海岸和那珂川下游一直延伸到北面的山林丘陵。国衙与国分寺建在石冈附近，沿海低地上的鹿岛神宫祭祀武瓮槌大神，作为日本剑术的圣地吸引武人。太田城的佐竹氏以守护之职侍奉室町幕府，控制却不完整：1427年江户氏夺取后来改建为水户城的马场城，屡次与佐竹氏对抗。1444年，常陆仍是佐竹家臣与独立豪族交杂的局面。

鹿岛的尚武之风出了塚原卜传：他1489年生于鹿岛氏的家臣之家，后来被称为剑圣，开创鹿岛新当流，曾向将军足利义辉授剑，1571年死后葬在鹿岛。统一战争中，佐竹氏1590年参加小田原征伐、从属于丰臣秀吉，本领54万石得到确认；站在后北条一方的江户氏失去马场城，该城1594年改建为水户城。德川家康不放心佐竹义宣在关原之战中的暧昧态度，1602年把他转封到出羽小得多的久保田藩。七年后，家康第十一子德川赖房以25万石入主水户，开创御三家之一的水户德川家。其子光圀世称水户黄门，1661年继任后开设彰考馆编纂《大日本史》，本纪与列传于1720年上呈幕府。

en:
Musashi, the largest province of the Kantō, is the plain between the Chichibu hills and Edo Bay, crossed by the Arakawa and the Tone. Its ancient capital stood at Fuchū and its ichinomiya was the Hikawa Shrine; native copper found at Chichibu in 708 gave the court its Wadō era name and supplied the Wadōkaichin, Japan's first circulating coinage. Under the Kamakura shoguns the province raised the eastern warrior bands called the Musashi shichitō. In the Muromachi age it was governed by the Uesugi, the Kantō kanrei, while fishing boats and traders used the Shinagawa and Asakusa moorings on the bay. In 1444 the Uesugi had just crushed the Kamakura kubo in the Eikyō war, but the Kantō was far from settled and Edo itself was still a small fortified homestead.

In 1457 the Ogigayatsu-Uesugi had their steward Ōta Dōkan fortify Kawagoe and Edo and link the two with a military road. The Later Hōjō of Odawara seized Edo in 1524, and in the night battle of Kawagoe in 1546 Hōjō Ujiyasu overwhelmed the two besieging Uesugi armies and made himself master of the Kantō. Toyotomi Hideyoshi destroyed the Hōjō at Odawara in 1590 and moved Tokugawa Ieyasu to the east; Ieyasu entered Edo that August and built it into his capital, and from 1603 the city was the seat of his shogunate. The Kannon temple of Sensō-ji at Asakusa, said to have begun when two fishermen netted a tiny golden Kannon in the Sumida in 628 and formally founded in 645, became Ieyasu's official place of prayer, and the third shogun Iemitsu rebuilt its pagoda and main hall; by 1685 stalls lined the temple approach. The Tamagawa aqueduct reached Edo in 1653, the Meireki fire swept the city in 1657, and by the early eighteenth century Edo held over a million people. Kawagoe, seat of Musashi's greatest domain and the shogunate's northern guard, fed the city by river barge and was known as 'little Edo', famed for its sweet potatoes.
zh:
武藏是关东最大的令制国，地处秩父山地与江户湾之间的平原，荒川、利根川流贯其间。古代国府在府中，一之宫为冰川神社；708年秩父发现自然铜，朝廷因此改元「和铜」，并以这批铜铸造日本最早的流通货币和同开珎。镰仓时代，武藏七党的东国武士从这里随源氏起家。室町时代，担任关东管领的上杉氏统治此国，江户湾边的品川凑、浅草凑是渔船和商船往来之处。1444年，上杉氏刚在永享之乱中压服镰仓公方，但关东远未安定，江户还只是一座小小的武士馆。

1457年，扇谷上杉氏命家宰太田道灌修筑河越城与江户城，并用军路把两城连为一线。1524年，小田原的后北条氏夺取江户城；1546年河越夜战，北条氏康以奇袭击溃围城的两上杉大军，就此成为关东之主。1590年丰臣秀吉攻灭小田原北条氏，把德川家康转封关东；家康同年8月入主江户，将其营建为居城，1603年在此开设幕府。浅草的观音寺浅草寺相传因628年渔人在隅田川网得小金像而建、645年创寺，家康入主江户当年将其定为德川氏祈愿寺，三代将军家光重建五重塔与本堂，1685年门前参道已排满店铺。1653年玉川上水通水，1657年明历大火焚毁大半市区，到18世纪初江户人口已逾百万。川越是武藏最大藩川越藩的城下町、幕府的北方屏障，靠新河岸川舟运为江户供给物资，被称为「小江户」，川越芋尤为有名。

en:
Kai, later abbreviated Kōshū, fills the mountain-girt Kōfu Basin of central Honshū, with Mount Fuji standing on its border with Suruga and Sagami. A Taihō Code 'superior country', it was counted among the Tōkaidō provinces though the highway passed it by. The steep highland pastures bred sturdy horses, while the basin floor, laced by the Fuefuki and Kamanashi rivers, yielded rice and flooded in equal measure. The Takeda, a line of the Kai Genji branch of the Minamoto, held the shugo post through the Kamakura and Muromachi ages; but when Takeda Nobumitsu perished in the Uesugi Zenshū rebellion of 1416–17 the province lost its shugo, and by 1444 the deputy Atobe clan and local landowners had divided the basin between them, leaving the Takeda lord little but his title.

The Takeda made themselves masters of Kai before the century was out. In 1519 Takeda Nobutora built his Tsutsujigasaki residence in mid-basin and laid out the castle town of Kōfu. His son Harunobu, later Shingen, drove him out in 1541 and made Kai the arsenal of a war state. Gold from the Kurokawa mines, first recorded in 1498, was cast into Kōshū gold pieces, and at Ryūō, where the Midai river joins the Kamanashi, his men raised the dikes and diversion channels later named the Shingen-zutsumi, keeping floods off new rice fields. Into battle he carried the Suwa Myōjin banner and another bearing the Sunzi words 'swift as wind, orderly as forest, fierce as fire, immovable as mountain'. From Kōfu he conquered Shinano, fought Uesugi Kenshin in the five Kawanakajima battles of 1553–64, overran Suruga in 1568, and died on campaign in Mikawa in 1573.

His son Katsuyori was broken at Nagashino in 1575, his cavalry cut down by Oda Nobunaga's musket volley fire, and in 1582 Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu overran Kai: Katsuyori burned his new Shinpu Castle and killed himself at Tenmokuzan. After Nobunaga's death Ieyasu and the Go-Hōjō disputed the province in the Tenshō-Jingo disturbance, and after Odawara fell in 1590 Hideyoshi stationed loyalist daimyō in Kai to watch Ieyasu's Kantō. The Kōshū Kaidō joined Kōfu to Edo, and after spells under Tokugawa kinsmen and the Yanagisawa family, most of Kai became direct shogunal land.
zh:
甲斐（简称甲州）地处本州中部群山环抱的甲府盆地，东南与骏河、相模交界处耸立着富士山。它是《大宝律令》设定的令制国，定为上国，虽不在东海道干线沿线，仍被归入东海道诸国。山间陡坡的牧场出产良马，笛吹川、釜无川纵横的盆底能种稻，也常闹水患。武田氏出自源氏支流甲斐源氏，镰仓、室町两代世袭守护；1416至1417年的上杉禅秀之乱中守护武田信满败亡，甲斐失去守护，到1444年，守护代迹部氏与各地国人已把盆地瓜分，武田氏徒有守护之名。

15世纪后期，武田氏重新成为甲斐之主。1519年，武田信虎在盆地中央筑起踯躅崎馆，营建甲府城下町。其子晴信（即信玄）1541年将他放逐，把甲斐变成战争机器的腹地：黑川金山的黄金（现存最早记载见于1498年）被铸成甲州金；在御敕使川汇入釜无川的龙王，他征发民夫修筑堤防和分洪渠，挡住洪水、开出新田，这套工程后来被称作信玄堤。上阵时，他的军旗一面书诹访明神的神号，一面写着《孙子》名言「其疾如风，其徐如林，侵掠如火，不动如山」。他以甲府为基地征服信浓，1553至1564年间与上杉谦信五度鏖战川中岛，1568年攻占骏河，1573年在三河军中病亡。

其子胜赖1575年惨败于长篠，骑兵成片倒在织田信长的铁炮齐射之下；1582年信长与家康攻入甲斐，胜赖烧毁新建的新府城，在天目山自尽。信长死后，德川与后北条为争夺甲斐爆发天正壬午之乱；1590年小田原落城后，秀吉把丰臣系大名安置在甲斐，监视坐拥关东的家康。后来甲州街道把甲府与江户相连，甲府藩先后由德川一族执掌，柳泽氏也曾一度入封，最后甲斐大部收为幕府直辖的天领。

en:
Owari fills a flat corner of the Ise Bay shore, where the lower Kiso runs out to the sea and the Tokaido highway passes between Kyoto and the eastern provinces. Its black soil grew heavy rice crops, and the ancient Atsuta Shrine drew pilgrims along that road: it holds Kusanagi, the grass-cutter sword, one of the three imperial regalia. The Shiba, the province's military governors, raised Kiyosu Castle in 1405, but by 1444 their deputies the Oda governed from Kiyosu in the Shiba name, over a rich and populous farming country on the eastern seaboard.

The Oda rose from this province. Oda Nobuhide took Nagoya Castle from an Imagawa garrison in 1532, and his son Nobunaga was born there in 1534. The Onin War split the Oda into rival Kiyosu and Iwakura houses; Nobunaga seized Kiyosu in 1555 and overthrew Iwakura in 1559, and on 12 June 1560, with a small army, he fell on the host of Imagawa Yoshimoto at Okehazama and killed him, the victory that put the Oda among the contenders for national power. After Nobunaga died in 1582 his generals met at Kiyosu to divide the succession, and in 1584 the fields of Komaki and Nagakute were the ground of Toyotomi Hideyoshi's stand-off with Tokugawa Ieyasu. When Oda Nobukatsu refused a transfer after the Hojo war of 1590, Hideyoshi split the province among his own generals, Fukushima Masanori taking the largest share.

In 1607 the province went to Ieyasu's ninth son Tokugawa Yoshinao, whose Owari Tokugawa house, rated at some 620,000 koku, ranked first of the three collateral branches that could supply a shogun. From 1610 some twenty daimyo, put to the work by Ieyasu, built Nagoya Castle on the site of the old Oda fort, and the keep of dismantled Kiyosu was carried there to become one of its turrets; the main keep was crowned with a pair of gilded shachi, the tiger-headed fish that marked a great lord's castle. A large castle town grew up below it, and the kilns of nearby Seto sent their pottery to buyers across the country.
zh:
尾张地处伊势湾畔的平原一角，木曾川下游在此入海，连接京都与东国的东海道穿境而过。黑土沃野盛产稻米，古道旁的热田神宫引来络绎参拜客，宫中供奉着三种神器之一的草薙剑。守护斯波氏1405年修筑清洲城，但到1444年，治国的已是其守护代织田氏，他们在清洲以斯波的名义发号施令，治下是东海道上富庶人众的农业之国。

织田氏正是从尾张起家。织田信秀1532年从今川守军手中夺取那古野城，其子信长1534年出生在城中。应仁之乱后织田分裂为清洲、岩仓两家，信长1555年取得清洲，1559年攻灭岩仓；1560年6月12日，他以寡兵在桶狭间突袭今川义元的大军、取下义元首级，这一仗把织田家送进了争夺天下者的行列。1582年信长死后，诸将在清洲会议上分割家业；1584年，小牧、长久手的田野又是丰臣秀吉与德川家康对峙的战场。1590年北条氏灭亡，织田信雄拒绝转封，秀吉便把尾张分给麾下诸将，福岛正则所得最多。

1607年，尾张封给家康九子德川义直，其尾张德川家石高约六十二万石，在可继嗣将军的御三家中排名居首。1610年起，家康命二十余家大名在织田旧城址上修筑名古屋城，拆毁的清洲城天守被运来改作城的一座角楼，主天守顶上还立着一对黄金铸造的虎鱼形兽饰。大型城下町在城郭下成形，附近濑户窑场的陶器销往全国各地。

en:
Kamikawa covers the cold northern interior of Ezo, from the forested upper basin of the Ishikari River, called Peni Unguri Kotan by the Ainu, or 'the village of the upstream people', north to Cape Sōya and the Sea of Okhotsk. Ainu villages stood along the Ishikari and Teshio rivers and on the northern shore, where people took salmon, deer, seals and other sea mammals. In 1444 no Japanese lord taxed the province. Canoes carried furs across the Sōya Strait to Sakhalin and peoples of the Amur, while rice and iron moved north by barter from the Japanese settlements on the Oshima Peninsula.

Sōya was the point where those distant trades came within reach of Matsumae. The domain placed its northernmost station there in 1603, with authority over both Sōya and Sakhalin. Ulch and Nivkh traders from the lower Amur sent Qing robes and silk brocade through Sakhalin Ainu hands; the cloth reached Edo and Osaka as prized Ezo brocade. French ships under Lapérouse surveyed the strait off Cape Sōya in 1787, and Russian probes among the Kurils later persuaded the shogunate to take East Ezo under direct rule in 1799 and West Ezo, including Sōya, in 1807. In 1809 Matsuda Denjūrō settled debts left by the Santan trade, while Mamiya Rinzō crossed to Sakhalin and reached the Amur. The forested Kamikawa basin remained Ainu hunting ground through these years.
zh:
上川位于虾夷地北部，南起石狩川上游的森林盆地，北至宗谷岬和鄂霍次克海岸。阿伊努语称石狩川上游为「佩尼温古里科坦」，意为上游人之村，上川之名便来自这个称呼。阿伊努人的村落分布在石狩川、天盐川和北部海岸，村民捕鲑鱼、猎鹿，也猎取海豹等海兽。1444年，这里还没有和人领主征税。独木舟载着毛皮渡过宗谷海峡，前往桦太和黑龙江流域族群；稻米和铁器则从渡岛半岛的和人聚落以物易物，一路北上。

宗谷是松前藩能够触及这些远方贸易的最北端。1603年，松前藩在此设置番所，管辖宗谷和桦太。黑龙江下游的乌尔奇人、尼夫赫商人通过桦太阿伊努人转来清朝官服和织锦，这些织物以「虾夷锦」之名在江户和大坂高价售出。1787年，拉彼鲁兹率领法国船只测量宗谷岬外的海峡；俄罗斯船只在千岛活动后，幕府又于1799年直辖东虾夷地，1807年接管包括宗谷在内的西虾夷地。1809年，松田传十郎清理山丹交易留下的债务，间宫林藏则前往桦太并抵达黑龙江流域。那些年里，上川的森林盆地仍是阿伊努人的猎场。

en:
