Marco Polo, sailing from here in 1291 with a Mongol princess bound for Persia, called Zaiton one of the world's two greatest ports, and Ibn Battuta counted over a hundred great junks in its roads around 1342. Silk, celadon, sugar and iron paid for spices and gems, and tens of thousands of foreigners made their homes here. They left the Qingjing Mosque of 1009, the saints' tombs on Lingshan, and at Cao'an the only surviving Manichaean temple. At the Luoyang estuary the prefect Cai Xiang finished China's first sea-crossing stone bridge in 1059, its piers fixed with cultivated oysters. In 1277 the Arab-descended trade superintendent Pu Shougeng handed Quanzhou to the Mongols; Song forces under Zhang Shijie besieged it for ninety days in vain. The Persian-Arab Ispah fighting of 1357-1366 then wrecked the city. In 1444 it remained a rich manufacturing prefecture, though its Zaiton days were over.

In 1387 the Ming placed the Zhongzuo garrison on Jiahe Islet off Tong'an; its walls of 1394 were the nucleus of Xiamen. In 1472 the maritime trade office moved to Fuzhou, and sea bans drove local sailors into armed smuggling. Jinjiang produced the thinker Li Zhi (1527-1602), who derided official Confucian orthodoxy in his A Book to Burn. In 1628 the smuggler chief Zheng Zhilong took Ming service at Anping and built the coast's strongest fleet. His son Zheng Chenggong, the Europeans' Koxinga, came of a Nan'an family of this prefecture; from his Xiamen base he renamed the island Siming in 1655 and sailed in 1661 to take Taiwan from the Dutch. Qing and Dutch troops took Xiamen in 1663, Zheng Jing retook it in 1674, and the Qing retook it in 1680. The coastal evacuation emptied the shores until Taiwan submitted in 1683.

A customs station opened at Xiamen in 1684, and in 1689 an East India Company ship carried Chinese tea directly from there to England. After the circuit administration moved to Xiamen in 1727 and the Hanjiang-Lukang ferry opened in 1784, the new port overshadowed old Quanzhou.
zh:
泉州位于福建南部晋江下游，同安县和后来称作厦门的岛屿扼守其出海门户。宋元两代，这里以「刺桐」之名成为欧亚大陆最大的港口之一。1291年，马可·波罗护送蒙古公主远嫁波斯，从泉州放洋，称刺桐是世界两大港之一；约1342年，伊本·白图泰在港中见到大船百余艘，小船不计其数。丝绸、青瓷、糖和铁器从这里出口，换回香料和宝石，城中常住的外国人数以万计。他们留下了1009年始建的清净寺、灵山圣墓，以及草庵——世上仅存的摩尼教寺院，庵中石像雕于1339年。城北洛阳江入海口，知州蔡襄主持在1059年建成洛阳桥，这是中国第一座跨海石桥，桥墩靠养殖牡蛎胶结加固。1277年，阿拉伯人后裔、提举市舶蒲寿庚以泉州降元，张世杰率宋军攻城九十天不下。1357年至1366年波斯、阿拉伯军户混战的亦思巴奚兵乱，最终毁了这座大港。1444年的泉州仍是富庶的手工业府城，刺桐的时代却已结束。

1387年，明朝在同安嘉禾里设中左守御千户所，1394年所城落成，是为厦门的雏形；1472年福建市舶司从泉州迁往福州。倭寇与海禁把当地船民逼进武装走私。晋江县出了思想家李贽（1527—1602年），他讥讪士大夫奉为正统的道学，把个人判断放在经典之上，著作题名《焚书》《藏书》。1628年，走私海商首领郑芝龙在安平接受明朝招抚，建起东南沿海最强的水师。其子郑成功在欧洲记载中称Koxinga，籍贯本府南安县；他以厦门为抗清基地，1655年改名思明州，1661年东征，从荷兰人手中夺取台湾。清军与荷兰联军1663年攻占厦门，郑经1674年收复，1680年又落入清军之手。清初迁界使沿海尽空，直到1683年台湾归附。

1684年厦门设立海关，1689年英国东印度公司商船从厦门把中国茶叶直接运往英国。1727年兴泉道治移驻厦门，1784年蚶江至鹿港对渡开通，海外贸易都归向新港，旧日泉州缩为地方性港口。

en:
Tajima lies on the Sea of Japan in the middle of the San'indo, a chain of river valleys between the Chugoku mountains and the coast, reaching west into the Inaba country around Tottori. The Yamana made this their home ground and served the Muromachi shogunate as shugo from Konosumiyama Castle in Tajima. The Meitoku rising of 1391 nearly destroyed the clan, but Yamana Sozen, a monk nicknamed the Red Monk for his florid complexion, rebuilt its power and won Harima in the Kakitsu affair of 1441. In 1444 he held a wide bloc of San'in and Sanyo provinces, and the rice fields in his mountain valleys were the country's chief wealth.

Sozen's feud with Hosokawa Katsumoto, at once his rival at the shogun's court and his son-in-law, grew into the Onin War of 1467 over the shogunal succession; Kyoto burned for years, and after Sozen died in 1473 his bloc of provinces broke into local strongholds. To hold off the Amago of Izumo, who had seized Hoki, the Yamana built Tottori Castle above Inaba in the mid-sixteenth century, but it passed to the Mori in 1575. Hideyoshi overran Tajima and its Ikuno silver mines in 1580, and in 1581 he starved Tottori out. He bought up every sack of rice in Inaba at several times its price, drove thousands of villagers into the castle and ringed the mountain with a twelve-kilometre palisade. The fourteen hundred defenders had provisions for twenty days; after months of hunger, eating their horses and then grass, the keeper Kikkawa Tsuneie opened the gates and took his own life in exchange for his men's, a siege later called the starving of Tottori. Under the Tokugawa, Ikeda Mitsumasa received Inaba and Hoki and made Tottori a castle town, while Tajima itself was split between the small domains of Toyooka and Izushi and the shogun's silver lands at Ikuno.
zh:
但马在山阴道中段的日本海沿岸，是中国山地与海岸之间一连串河谷，向西延伸到鸟取一带的因幡地方。山名氏以此为根基，从但马的此隅山城出仕室町幕府，历任各国守护。1391年的明德之乱几乎使家族倾灭；山名宗全面色赤红，人称「赤入道」，他重新振作山名家，在1441年的嘉吉之乱中击败赤松氏，得到播磨。1444年，宗全统辖山阴、山阳的大片领国，山中河谷的稻田是这片地方最大的财富。

宗全与细川胜元既是幕政上的对头，又有翁婿关系，二人围绕将军继嗣的争斗演成1467年的应仁之乱，京都连年焚于战火；宗全1473年病死，他的大片领国随之散成各处据点。为抵御夺取伯耆的出云尼子氏，山名氏在16世纪中叶于因幡山上修筑鸟取城，城却在1575年落入毛利氏之手。1580年，秀吉攻落但马，夺下生野银山；1581年再攻鸟取，以数倍高价买尽因幡的米粮，把数千乡民驱入城中，又沿山筑起约十二公里长的阵地太阁坪。城中一千四百守军只备了二十天粮食，几个月里先吃战马、再吃草木，饿死者不断；守将吉川经家最终开城，以自己切腹换取将兵活命，这就是后世所称的「鸟取渴杀」。德川时代，池田光政领有因幡和伯耆，把鸟取建成城下町；但马本国则分属丰冈、出石等小藩，生野银山列为幕府天领。

en:
The coastlands and bare karst hills between Ragusa and the Bay of Kotor were old Travunia, whose župas looked to Trebinje and for centuries belonged to the Serbian realm. When Nikola Altomanović's lands were partitioned in 1373, they passed to the Bosnian crown: Trebinje went to the Pavlovići and from 1435 to the Kosača, Herceg Stjepan's dynasty. Bosnia's strip of Adriatic coast had no real harbour, so in early 1382 King Tvrtko I raised a fortress on a fishing cove in the Bay of Kotor as a salt port and named it Sveti Stefan, though everyone called it Novi, the New. Ragusa answered with an embargo and forced Tvrtko to acknowledge its salt monopoly. The Kosača kept the town as their winter seat, and Stjepan Vukčić added his own herceg title to its name: Herceg Novi. In 1444 salt, wool and hides moved through its quays, the southernmost port of his Herzegovina.

Ottoman troops took Trebinje in 1465 and overran the hinterland, while Novi held out as the last Kosača stronghold until 1482. The Turks built the Kanli Tower above the quays and kept the town for two centuries, except for a single year. In 1538 Spanish tercios seized it, and when Hayreddin Barbarossa brought the Ottoman fleet and army against it in July 1539, the commander Francisco de Sarmiento refused an honourable surrender; his captains answered that the Turks might come when they pleased, and nearly all the Spaniards died in the assault. The hillside fort they began still bears the name Španjola, the Spanish fort. Evliya Çelebi later found Croats, Bosnians and Albanians living in the town, and an earthquake devastated it in 1608. Venice took Novi in 1687 and held it until the Republic's fall in 1797. The little port then passed between Austria, Russia, France and a short-lived Montenegrin government during the Napoleonic wars, until Austria returned in 1814; its flag flew over the Bay of Kotor in 1821.
zh:
拉古萨与科托尔湾之间的海岸和光秃的喀斯特丘陵，是古老的特拉武尼亚，下辖诸茹帕以特雷比涅为中心，数百年来属于塞尔维亚。1373年尼古拉·阿尔托马诺维奇的领地被瓜分，这片土地归入波斯尼亚王室：特雷比涅先封给帕夫洛维奇家族，1435年起转归赫尔采格·斯捷潘的科萨察家族。波斯尼亚分得的亚得里亚海岸没有一座像样的港口，于是1382年初，特尔特科一世在科托尔湾一处渔村小湾修筑要塞，作为盐港，取名圣斯特凡，但人人都只管它叫诺维，即「新城」。拉古萨以禁运回应，迫使特尔特科承认其食盐专卖。科萨察家族把此城作为冬宫，斯捷潘·武克契奇又把自己的「赫尔采格」爵号加在城名上，是为新海尔采格。1444年，食盐、羊毛和皮革在码头上装卸，这里是他的黑塞哥维那最南端的港口。

奥斯曼军队1465年攻占特雷比涅、席卷内地，诺维则作为科萨察家族最后的据点坚守到1482年。土耳其人在码头上方建起血塔，统治此城两百年，中间只断过一年。1538年，西班牙方阵部队夺取诺维；1539年7月，海雷丁·巴巴罗萨率奥斯曼舰队和大军水陆并至，守将弗朗西斯科·德·萨米恩托拒绝了体面投降的条件，他的军官们回答说土耳其人尽管来攻，结果几乎所有西班牙人都战死在强攻中。他们动工修筑的山坡要塞后来仍叫「西班牙堡」。旅行家爱维亚·瑟勒布后来在城中见到克罗地亚人、波斯尼亚人和阿尔巴尼亚人；1608年一场地震又把城镇摧毁。威尼斯1687年攻取诺维，统治到1797年共和国灭亡。拿破仑战争期间，这座小港在奥地利、俄国、法国和一个短命的黑山政权之间几度易手，1814年再归奥地利；1821年，科托尔湾上空飘扬的是奥地利旗帜。

en:
Yamato is the Nara basin south of Kyoto, the homeland of the early Yamato kings who gave the country its name. Its great religious houses long outlasted the court's departure: Tōdai-ji housed the Great Buddha dedicated in 752, the Kōfuku-ji monastery and Kasuga Shrine kept wide estates with armed monk retinues, and pilgrim towns grew around their gates. No Muromachi governor ever controlled the whole province; the Tsutsui, Ochi, Hashio and Toichi warrior families shared the countryside with the monasteries. In 1444 Yamato lay a short ride from the capital yet ran its own affairs through temple halls and local forts.

The Sengoku wars brought Matsunaga Hisahide, a tea master turned warlord later counted among Japan's three great villains. He invaded Yamato in 1559 and drove the young Tsutsui Junkei out of Tsutsui Castle in 1565. In 1567, when Matsunaga fought the Miyoshi Triumvirs and their Tsutsui allies at Nara, the Great Buddha Hall burned down in the fighting. Junkei submitted to Oda Nobunaga through Akechi Mitsuhide in 1571 and was entrusted with all Yamato in 1576. Matsunaga rose a last time and was cornered in Shigisan Castle in 1577; he is said to have smashed his famous tea kettle Hiragumo rather than surrender it, and died there with his son. Junkei dismantled his outlying forts, moved his seat to Koriyama in 1580 and died of illness in 1584. In 1585 Toyotomi Hideyoshi moved the new lord Tsutsui Sadatsugu to Iga Ueno at 200,000 koku.

The Tokugawa divided the basin among Koriyama, Takatori, Yagyu and other small domains. The Yagyu valley produced the shogunate's swordmasters: Yagyu Munetoshi perfected the Shinkage style there, and his son Munenori taught the first three Tokugawa shoguns and made Yagyu Shinkage-ryu one of the two official sword styles. Nara remained a pilgrim town under a shogunal magistrate, and the Great Buddha sat without a hall from 1610 until a new hall was completed in 1709.
zh:
大和是京都以南的奈良盆地，也是古代大和王权的发祥地，日本的国名便来自这里。朝廷迁走后，这里的大寺社依旧势大：东大寺供奉752年开眼的大佛，兴福寺和春日大社领有广阔庄园，蓄养僧兵，门前还形成了门前町。室町时代没有一位守护能控制整个令制国，筒井、越智、箸尾、十市等武家豪族与各大寺院分据乡野。1444年的大和距京都不过一日路程，却靠寺院殿堂和地方城砦自行其是。

战国乱世把松永久秀带进了大和。他由茶人发迹为大名，后世把他列为日本三大枭雄之一。1559年他入侵大和，1565年把年轻的筒井顺庆逐出筒井城。1567年，松永氏在奈良与三好三人众及助阵的筒井军交战，大佛殿在兵火中焚毁。1571年顺庆通过明智光秀归顺织田信长，1576年受信长委任支配大和一国。1577年松永久秀最后一次反叛，被困信贵山城；据说他砸碎名器「平蜘蛛」茶釜，不愿它落入信长之手，随后与儿子一同死在城中。顺庆拆毁各处支城，1580年把本据移到郡山，1584年病逝。1585年，丰臣秀吉把新任家督筒井定次以二十万石转封伊贺上野。

德川时代，盆地被分给郡山、高取、柳生等小藩。柳生谷走出了幕府的剑术师范：柳生宗严在此打磨新阴流，其子柳生宗矩为德川家前三代将军讲剑，使柳生新阴流成为幕府公认的两大剑术流派之一。奈良作为参拜町由奈良奉行管理；大佛自1610年起长期露坐，直到1709年新的大佛殿才告落成。

en:
Ji'an, the old Luling country, fills the Jitai basin on the middle Gan, flat rice land ringed by the Luoxiao ranges on the Hunan border. Its towns made their name with porcelain, scholarship and officials. At Yonghe the Jizhou kilns fired white and purple-splashed wares in the manner of the Ding kilns from the Tang through the Song. In 1241 the prefect Jiang Wanli founded the White Egret Islet Academy on a sandbar in the Gan, where Wen Tianxiang studied before the Mongols took him and executed him at Dadu in 1283; Luling also gave the Song Ouyang Xiu and Yang Wanli. East of the city rises Mount Qingyuan, where the Chan master Qingyuan Xingsi, a disciple of the Sixth Patriarch Huineng, taught at Jingju Monastery and gave his name to the Qingyuan line of Chan. The early Ming court was thick with men of this prefecture: Xie Jin of Jishui, chief editor of the Yongle Encyclopedia, who died in prison in 1415; Yang Shiqi of Taihe, head of the Three Yang grand secretaries; and Chen Cheng of Jishui, who led five embassies to the Timurid rulers of Central Asia and wrote an account of the western lands. In 1444 Ji'an, nine counties under one prefect, passed more men into the civil service than almost any other prefecture in the empire.

The islet academy fell to ruin and was rebuilt under the Ming, moved off the flood-swept sands and brought back behind new dykes before 1600. The prefecture's war came in 1519, when Zhu Chenhao, the Prince of Ning, rose at Nanchang: Wang Yangming, the Nan-Gan commander, and Wu Wending, the Ji'an prefect, led the Luling levies north, crushed the rising and captured the prince on Poyang Lake. The Yonghe kilns kept firing into the late Ming and then closed. Under the Qing the Gan flooded the islet, and the academy was rebuilt after the great floods of 1724, 1774 and 1813.
zh:
吉安古称庐陵，地处赣江中游的吉泰盆地，是罗霄山脉环抱的一片稻米平原，西与湖南相接。这里的城镇以瓷器、书院和科举闻名。永和镇的吉州窑从唐代烧到宋代，白瓷和紫釉器物风格近于定窑。1241年，知州江万里在赣江沙洲上创办白鹭洲书院，文天祥曾在此读书，后来被元军所俘，1283年在大都就义；庐陵还走出了欧阳修、杨万里。城东的青原山上有净居寺，禅宗六祖慧能的弟子青原行思在此说法，禅宗青原一派由他得名。明初的朝堂上满是吉安府的人：吉水解缙主持编修《永乐大典》，1415年死于诏狱；泰和杨士奇是「三杨」之首；吉水陈诚五次出使中亚的帖木儿帝国，留下一部西域行记。1444年的吉安府领九县，考中科举入朝为官的人数，天下几乎没有哪个府比得上。

洲上的书院渐废，明代重修，一度迁出易遭水患的沙洲，1600年前又在新堤护卫下迁回。1519年宁王朱宸濠在南昌起兵，南赣巡抚王守仁和吉安知府伍文定率庐陵兵北上讨平，在鄱阳湖擒获朱宸濠。永和窑的窑火一直烧到明代后期才熄灭。入清以后赣江几次漫上沙洲，书院在1724年、1774年、1813年大水后三度重修。

en:
Dorpat, Tartu in Estonian, lies on the Emajõgi, the river that joins Lake Peipus to the Estonian interior and carries traffic between the Baltic and Novgorod. Yaroslav the Wise of Kiev raised a fort called Yuryev on Toome Hill around 1030, and Estonian tribes burned it in 1061. In the great siege of 1224 the Sword-Brothers of Riga stormed the hillfort; Prince Vyachko, who had come with the Novgorod and Pskov relief, died in its defence. The conquerors made the renamed Dorpat the seat of a prince-bishop, his cathedral and fortress crowning Toome Hill above the merchants' town, where the Brick Gothic church of St John rose in the fourteenth century. A Russian army sacked the lower town in 1262 without taking the hill, and in the 1280s Dorpat joined the Hanseatic League, growing into one of the richest cities of Old Livonia on the river trade to Pskov and Novgorod. In 1444 the Catholic bishop still ruled his small state, while the Livonian Order watched from neighbouring castles.

Dorpat spent the next two and a half centuries passing between the powers around it. Ivan the Terrible's gunners bombarded it into surrender in 1558 and carried the last bishop off to Moscow, ending more than three centuries of church rule; Poland-Lithuania received it by the truce of 1582, and Stephen Báthory opened a Jesuit gymnasium there. The Swedes took the town in 1625 after years of seesaw sieges, and in 1632 Gustavus Adolphus founded the Academia Gustaviana, the first university in Livonia. A Russian army forced Dorpat to surrender in 1656 and the academy fled to Reval, but the peace of 1661 gave the town back to Sweden. Peter the Great's artillery took it in 1704, and four years later the Russians blew up the fortifications, burned the town and deported its citizens inland; the treaty of 1721 assigned the empty ruins to Russia. Dorpat rose again as a provincial town: the great fire of 1775 cleared the medieval centre, the new town hall went up from 1782, and in 1802 Alexander I reopened the German-language university, which drew students and scholars from across Germany and the Baltic.
zh:
多尔帕特，爱沙尼亚语称塔尔图，地处埃马约吉河畔；这条河连接佩普西湖与爱沙尼亚内陆，船只经它往来于波罗的海和诺夫哥罗德之间。约1030年，基辅大公雅罗斯拉夫（智者）在托梅山上修筑尤里耶夫堡，1061年被爱沙尼亚诸部焚毁。1224年的大围攻中，里加的佩剑兄弟会猛攻山头要塞，率诺夫哥罗德和普斯科夫援军协守的维亚奇科亲王战死。征服者把改名多尔帕特的城镇定为采邑主教驻地，主教座堂和堡垒雄踞托梅山顶，山下是商人城，14世纪又建起砖砌哥特式的圣约翰教堂。1262年俄国军队洗劫下城却未能攻上山头；1280年代多尔帕特加入汉萨同盟，凭通往普斯科夫和诺夫哥罗德的河运贸易成为旧利沃尼亚最富庶的城市之一。1444年，天主教主教仍统治着这个小国，利沃尼亚骑士团则在邻近的城堡中监视着它。

此后两个半世纪里，多尔帕特在周边强国之间几度易手。1558年伊凡雷帝的炮兵轰开城墙，末代主教被押往莫斯科，教会三百余年的统治告终；1582年的停战协定把它划归波兰-立陶宛，斯特凡·巴托里在此开办耶稣会文理中学。经过多年拉锯围城，瑞典人于1625年拿下此城，古斯塔夫·阿道夫于1632年创办古斯塔夫学院，这是利沃尼亚的第一所大学。1656年俄军迫使城市投降，学院迁往雷瓦尔，但1661年的和约又把多尔帕特归还瑞典。1704年彼得大帝的炮兵攻下此城，四年后俄国人炸毁要塞、焚毁城市，把市民流放内地；1721年的条约把这片空地废墟划给俄国。多尔帕特作为省城重新兴起：1775年的大火清除了中世纪城心，新市政厅于1782年动工，1802年亚历山大一世重开德语教学的大学，把德意志和波罗的海各地的学生学者吸引而来。

en:
Ringed by mountains, Mino is an inland basin whose Nagara and Kiso rivers run south through Owari to Ise Bay. The Tosando highway carried its goods to Kyoto and the east, and mountain villages sold mulberry-bark washi across the country from the Nara centuries on. Its smiths were one of the five great sword traditions, their blades noted for sharpness; after floodwaters ruined the Bizen furnaces in 1590, Mino became Japan's largest sword-making province. The Toki ruled as military governors from the Kamakura age, their deputies the Saito holding Inabayama, a fort on a sheer Nagara hill rebuilt in the mid-fifteenth century. In 1444 the Toki still governed this populous 'great country' from beneath the hillfort's walls.

The Saito soon took the province outright. Saito Dosan, the self-made Kyoto soldier called the Viper of Mino, took Inabayama and in 1541 drove out his Toki lord; in 1547 he routed an Owari army under Oda Nobuhide at Kanoguchi, and in 1556 his own son Yoshitatsu killed him on the Nagara. Yoshitatsu died in 1561, and his weak heir Tatsuoki let the retainer Takenaka Shigeharu take the hillfort in 1564 with a handful of men and hold it half a year. In September 1567 Nobunaga, Dosan's son-in-law, took Inabayama in a fortnight; his general Kinoshita Tokichiro climbed the unguarded cliffs to open the gates. Nobunaga renamed it Gifu, after Qishan, the mountain from which the Zhou kings conquered China, opened free markets below and based himself there until Azuchi was completed in 1579. His guest, the Jesuit Luis Frois, called it a second Babylon.

In 1600 Nobunaga's grandson Hidenobu held Gifu for Ishida Mitsunari and lost it in a day; weeks later, on 21 October, Sekigahara in far western Mino settled the quarrel of all Japan. Sofuku-ji keeps the floorboards stained when Hidenobu's retainers killed themselves after the defeat as its 'blood ceiling', and Nobunaga's tomb is there as well. Ieyasu had the fortress dismantled in 1601 and put Okudaira Nobumasa to building Kano Castle below; under Tokugawa rule Mino passed to the domains of Ogaki and Kano, its paper finding buyers all over Japan. On the Nagara below, hereditary fishing masters had caught ayu sweetfish with trained cormorants for over a thousand years.
zh:
美浓是群山环抱的内陆国，盆地里的长良川、木曾川向南穿过尾张、注入伊势湾。古老的东山道把商货带往京都和东国，山村自奈良时代起生产的楮皮和纸行销全国。美浓锻师自成一派，位列日本刀五大传统，刀刃向以锋利著称；1590年大水毁了备前刀坊后，美浓成为日本最大的产刀之国。土岐氏自镰仓时代起担任守护，其守护代斋藤氏据守稻叶山城，这座长良川畔绝壁上的城寨在15世纪中叶经过重修。1444年，土岐氏仍在稻叶山城下统治这个人烟稠密的「大国」。

斋藤氏很快把主君的国变成了自己的国。人称「美浓的蝮蛇」、出身京都的斋藤道三以白身为稻叶山城主，1541年放逐土岐氏主君；1547年他在加纳口大败织田信秀率领的尾张军，1556年却在长良川被亲子斋藤义龙攻杀。义龙1561年病死，继承人斋藤龙兴威望扫地，1564年家臣竹中重治率十几人夺取稻叶山城、据城半年。1567年9月，娶道三之女为妻的织田信长围攻两周拿下城池，部将木下藤吉郎从无兵把守的绝壁攀入、打开城门。信长取周文王岐山定天下之意，改名岐阜，在城下开设乐市乐座的自由市场，并以此为本据，直到1579年安土城落成。在城中作客的耶稣会士路易斯·弗罗伊斯把这座城比作巴比伦。

1600年，信长之孙织田秀信据岐阜城投靠石田三成，一天就丢了城；数周后的10月21日，决定天下归属的关原之战在美浓西端打响。崇福寺保留着秀信家臣兵败自尽时染血的楼板，人称「血天井」，寺中还有信长的墓所。1601年家康下令拆毁旧城，命奥平信昌在山下另筑加纳城；德川太平之世，美浓分属大垣、加纳等藩，美浓纸行销全国。长良川上，世袭的鹈匠用驯养的鸬鹚捕捞香鱼，这门手艺已有一千多年。

en:
Luoyang sits where the Luo River crosses the western Central Plain, with the Mang Hills north of the city and the Yi River gap at Longmen to the south. After the Northern Wei moved their capital to Luoyang in 493, patrons began carving Buddhist caves into the Longmen cliffs; the great Fengxian Temple figures were completed in 675 under the Tang. By 1444 Luoyang was no longer an imperial capital. It served the Ming as the seat of Henan Prefecture, a walled administrative town on the road from Xi'an to Kaifeng, with the Longmen shrines on its southern outskirts.

The city's late Ming drama centred on the Prince of Fu's household. The Wanli Emperor tried for years to place Zhu Changxun, his third son by Noble Consort Zheng, ahead of the elder Zhu Changluo in the succession. When that effort failed, Zhu Changxun was enfeoffed at Luoyang in 1601 and took up residence there in 1614 with a large estate and rich household. Li Zicheng's rebel army stormed Luoyang in 1641, killed Zhu Changxun and the retired official Lü Weiqi, and seized the prince's grain and treasure for its campaigns. Zhu's son Zhu Yousong escaped and was installed at Nanjing in 1644 as the Hongguang Emperor, the first Southern Ming emperor. The Qing kept Luoyang as the seat of Henan Prefecture.
zh:
洛阳位于洛河穿过的中原西部，北倚邙山，南面伊水切出的龙门山口。493年北魏迁都洛阳后，供养人开始在龙门山崖开凿佛教石窟；675年唐代又完成奉先寺大像。到1444年，洛阳已失去帝都身份，作为明代河南府治，是西安通往开封道路上的一座城垣城市，南郊便是龙门石窟。

明末洛阳的变故围绕福王府展开。万历帝多年想让郑贵妃所生的第三子朱常洵越过长子朱常洛入继东宫，未能成功。1601年朱常洵受封福王，1614年就藩洛阳，府中拥有大批庄田和财货。1641年李自成军攻破洛阳，杀朱常洵和退职官员吕维祺，抄没福王府的粮食和财宝充作军饷。朱常洵之子朱由崧逃出，1644年在南京被拥立为弘光帝，即南明第一位皇帝。清代仍以洛阳为河南府治。

en:
The province follows the Hokuriku corridor from the Toyama Bay plain south-west to Kanazawa, though Kanazawa historically belonged to Kaga; the strip lies squeezed between the mountains and the sea. Etchu itself was formed when old Koshi was divided in 701. Its Muromachi governors, the Hatakeyama, preferred Kyoto to their charge and left the rice plains and the Shinano and Mino passes to deputy houses, chiefly the Jinbo and the Shiina. Kanazawa sat on a ridge between two rivers in Kaga, where the Togashi still held the governorship in 1444 while Jodo Shinshu congregations spread through the villages. The corridor belonged to its governors in name; deputies, local lords and armed temple congregations ran it in fact.

In 1488 Kaga slipped from all secular hands. While the governor Togashi Masachika was away on campaign, between 100,000 and 200,000 Shinshu monks and villagers rose, trapped him in his palace and forced him to commit seppuku; the Ikkō-ikki ran the province for nearly a century as the Peasants' Kingdom, with the Kanazawa Gobo, fortified in 1546 on the Kodatsuno ridge, as their headquarters. Etchu became a proxy war between the Takeda-backed Jinbo and the Uesugi-backed Shiina until Uesugi Kenshin conquered it in 1576. Oda Nobunaga's generals then broke the temple rule: Sakuma Morimasa burned the Kanazawa Gobo in 1580 and Oda forces took Uozu in 1582. After Nobunaga's death the spear veteran Maeda Toshiie, called Yari no Mataza, made Kanazawa his seat in 1583; Sassa Narimasa held out in Toyama until Hideyoshi's campaign of 1585, and the northern district of Niikawa passed to the Maeda in 1595.

At Sekigahara in 1600 the Maeda joined Tokugawa Ieyasu and ended with Kaga, Noto and most of Etchu, some 1.2 million koku, the largest domain in the shogunate. They spent the income on their castle town rather than on soldiers. After a great fire destroyed much of Kanazawa and the castle in 1631, Maeda Toshitsune drove a 3.3-kilometre canal from the upper Sai River to supply the castle, completed in 1632 as the Tatsumi Canal; the domain's workshops promoted lacquer and gold-lacquer work whose craftsmen served the country. Maeda Tsunanori laid out the Renchi-tei garden beside the castle in 1676, and by 1700 Kanazawa held more than 100,000 people, one of Japan's largest cities.
zh:
本省所辖的这段北陆走廊夹在群山与日本海之间，从富山湾沿岸平原向西南延伸到金泽；金泽在历史上属于加贺。越中本是701年旧越国分裂后形成的令制国。室町时代担任守护的畠山氏留恋京都，把稻米平原和通往信浓、美浓的山口交给神保、椎名等守护代。金泽坐落在加贺两河之间的小丘上，1444年仍由富樫氏担任守护，净土真宗门徒则在村落间不断扩张。名义上这条走廊属于诸位守护，实际说了算的是守护代、国人豪族和武装寺社。

1488年，加贺从一切世俗领主手中脱出。守护富樫政亲出征在外时，十至二十万净土真宗的僧俗起兵，把他困在居城，迫其切腹；一向一揆以「百姓之国」自治近百年，1546年又在小立野丘上把金泽御坊加固为大本营。越中则沦为武田支持的神保氏与上杉支持的椎名氏之间的代理战场，直到1576年上杉谦信将其平定。织田信长的将领随后击碎了寺社统治：1580年佐久间盛政烧毁金泽御坊，1582年织田军攻占鱼津。信长死后，以枪法闻名、人称「枪之又左」的前田利家于1583年入主金泽；佐佐成政据守富山，坚持到1585年丰臣秀吉来伐，最北的新川郡也于1595年归入前田氏。

1600年关原之战，前田氏加入德川家康一方，最终领有加贺、能登和越中大部分，石高约一百二十万石，是江户最大的藩。前田氏把收入花在城下町而非军备上。1631年大火焚毁金泽大片市区和城池后，前田利常命人从犀川上游开凿3.3公里的辰巳用水向城池供水，1632年完工；藩设工艺所扶持漆器与金漆工艺，工匠的产品销往全国。1676年，前田纲纪在城边营造莲池庭；到1700年，金泽人口已超过十万，是日本最大的城市之一。

en:
Hefei sits on the low saddle of country between the Huai and the Yangtze, beside Chao Lake, where goods moving between north and south changed hands: Sima Qian already names it as a mart for leather, cured fish and timber. In the Three Kingdoms wars it was Cao Wei's bulwark on the Yangtze front. In 215, with Sun Quan's army at the walls, Zhang Liao led 800 picked men out at dawn into the enemy camp, killed the Wu general Chen Wu, wounded Xu Sheng and nearly took Sun Quan himself at Xiaoyao Ford; afterwards, it was said, mothers in Jiangdong used Zhang Liao's name to quiet crying children. Renamed Luzhou under the Sui, it was the Southern Song's forward shield against the Jin, and in 1238 the prefect Du Gao beat off a Mongol assault on the city. Zhu Yuanzhang's regime made it Luzhou Prefecture in 1364, and the admiral Yu Tonghai rebuilt the walls with a brick facing. In 1444, seat of Luzhou Prefecture in South Zhili, Hefei is the administrative centre and grain market of the fertile plain south of the Huai.

The Ming centuries were mostly quiet. The city honours its most famous native, Bao Zheng, the Northern Song judge whose name stood for incorruptible justice: in 1488 the prefect Song Jian cleared a Buddhist temple off Xianghua Mound in the south moat and built the Lord Bao Academy there, and in 1539 the censor Yang Zhan made it the Lord Bao Shrine. In 1631 the prefect Yan Ergui began a wenfeng pagoda on Mount Lao in Chao Lake to improve the town's fortunes in the examinations, but work stopped at the third tier when the Chongzhen-reign rebellions overran the Huai valley. Under the Qing the prefecture passed with the division of Jiangnan Province into the new province of Anhui, whose capital remained at Anqing, and Hefei carried on as a collecting centre for the grain, beans, cotton and hemp of the surrounding plain, its craftsmen working cloth, leather, bamboo and iron.
zh:
合肥在淮河与长江之间的低矮岗地上，紧邻巢湖，南来北往的货物多在这里转手：司马迁《史记·货殖列传》已写到合肥「受南北潮」，是皮革、咸鱼、木材的集散之地。三国时它是曹魏在长江前沿的军事重镇。215年孙权兵临城下，张辽率八百勇士黎明突入吴营，斩吴将陈武、伤徐盛，在逍遥津险些生擒孙权；此后江东小儿啼哭，大人便说张辽来了，这就是「张辽止啼」。隋代改置庐州，南宋时为抗金前沿，1238年知庐州杜杲又击退攻城的蒙古军。1364年朱元璋政权改庐州路为庐州府，水师将领俞通海重修城墙，外墙包砖。1444年的合肥是南直隶庐州府首县，淮河南岸肥沃平原上的行政中心与粮食市场。

明代的庐州大体太平。城中最有名的乡人是北宋的包拯，他的名字就是清官的代称：1488年知府宋鉴拆去城南濠中香花墩上的佛寺，改建包公书院，1539年御史杨瞻将其定名包公祠。1631年，知府严尔珪为提振地方文运，在巢湖姥山岛上倡建文峰塔，塔刚修到第三层，崇祯年间的战乱蔓延到淮河流域，工程就此停下。入清以后，随着江南省分置，庐州府改属新设的安徽省，安徽省会仍驻安庆，合肥照旧收聚转运平原上出产的粮食、豆类、棉花和麻，工匠织布、制革、做竹器和铁器。

en:
Suruga, abbreviated Sunshū, occupies the Pacific coast of what is now central Shizuoka, opening onto Suruga Bay with Mount Fuji rising on its borders with Kai and Izu. A Taihō Code province ranked a 'superior country', its provincial seat lay on the Abe river, at what became Shizuoka. During the Kamakura period it was held directly by the Hōjō regents, and traffic on the Tōkaidō between Kamakura and Kyoto filled its roads; the Zen monk Enni spread tea cultivation in the Abe valley in the same age, the beginning of Suruga's tea country. From early Muromachi times the Imagawa clan held the province as shugo, and in 1444 their fifth head Imagawa Noritada kept his seat at Sunpu, schooling his warrior house in the rites and tastes of the Kyoto court.

In 1526 Imagawa Ujichika issued the house law Kanamokuroku, and his son Yoshimoto, succeeding in 1536, built the clan's golden age. Advised by the Zen monk Taigen Sessai, he held Suruga, Tōtōmi and Mikawa and was called 'the foremost bowman on the Tōkaidō'; Sunpu sheltered nobles and scholars fleeing the wars around Kyoto and was known as the capital of the east. It was in Sunpu, too, that the boy Matsudaira Motoyasu, the future Tokugawa Ieyasu, spent his youth as an Imagawa hostage. Yoshimoto's death in Oda Nobunaga's surprise attack at Okehazama in 1560 undid it all, and between 1568 and 1571 Takeda Shingen overran Suruga while Ieyasu took Tōtōmi; the Imagawa dominion collapsed.

After the Takeda fell in 1582 Suruga passed to Ieyasu, who began building Sunpu Castle in 1585; when he was moved to the Kantō in 1590 Nakamura Kazuuji took the castle. Following Sekigahara, Ieyasu recovered his old domains, settled at Sunpu in 1607 after handing the shogunate to Hidetada, and ruled there as retired shōgun until his death in the castle in 1616. Sunpu then became direct shogunal land under a castle governor, while the Tōkaidō post stations flourished. With bridges and ferries forbidden on the Ōi river, porters carried travellers across its fords, and Shimada and Kanaya grew rich on the crossing.
zh:
骏河（简称骏州）即今静冈县中部的太平洋沿岸，南面向骏河湾敞开，北方与甲斐、伊豆交界处耸立着富士山。它是《大宝律令》设立的令制国，列为上国，国府位于安倍川畔，即今静冈市一带。镰仓时代骏河由北条得宗家直辖，连接镰仓与京都的东海道商旅往来不绝；也是在镰仓时代，禅僧圆尔在安倍川流域推广茶树种植，成为骏河茶乡之始。室町时代初期起今川氏就任守护，1444年第五代当主今川范忠坐镇骏府，把京都朝廷的礼仪与风尚带进这一武家之家。

1526年今川氏亲颁布分国法《今川假名目录》；其子义元1536年继位，在禅僧太原雪斋辅佐下缔造了今川氏的全盛：领有骏河、远江、三河，号称「海道第一弓取」；骏府收容躲避战乱的京都公卿与文人，被称为「东国之都」。少年松平元康，也就是后来的德川家康，正是作为今川家的人质在骏府长大。1560年义元在桶狭间遭织田信长奇袭战死，盛景随之瓦解；1568至1571年武田信玄攻占骏河，家康夺取远江，今川的领国就此崩解。

1582年武田氏灭亡后骏河归入家康之手，他于1585年动工修筑骏府城；1590年移封关东时，由中村一氏入城。关原之战后家康收复旧领，1607年把将军位让给秀忠后退居骏府，以大御所身份在此执政，1616年病逝于骏府城。此后骏府成为幕府直辖领地，由骏府城代治理，东海道上的宿场町日趋繁荣。大井川禁止架桥和摆渡，人夫背负旅人涉过渡口，岛田宿、金谷宿便靠这处渡口致富。

en:
Guilin commands the southern end of the Hunan-Guangxi corridor, where karst peaks crowd the upper Li River. In 214 BC the Qin cut the Lingqu Canal across the low divide to link the Xiang and the Li, letting grain barges and troops pass from the Yangtze basin into the southwest, and the waterway carried traffic for centuries afterward. The peaks gave the city its other fame: the Tang poet Han Yu likened the river to a green silk girdle and the hills to jade hairpins, and in 1201 the official Wang Zhenggong, serving in Guilin, wrote the line later repeated across China, that Guilin's scenery is first under heaven. In 1370 the Hongwu Emperor enfeoffed his grandnephew Zhu Shouqian as Prince of Jingjiang, and from 1372 a walled palace city rose below Solitary Beauty Peak; fourteen princes of twelve generations lived there under the Ming. In 1444 Guilin was both the administrative seat of Guangxi and a junior imperial court set among Zhuang hill country.

The southern Ming wars reached the palace in 1650, when the Qing commander Kong Youde took Guilin and made it his residence as Prince Dingnan. Two years later Li Dingguo's army stormed the city, and Kong killed himself as the palace's wooden halls burned. The Qing placed the Guangxi provincial examination grounds in the old princely city from 1657. Guilin furnished scholars to match them: the Lingui official Chen Hongmou, held up as a model Qing official, rose to grand secretary under the Qianlong Emperor, and his great-grandson Chen Jichang, first in the provincial, metropolitan and palace examinations with the zhuangyuan of 1820, was the last man in the empire to carry off the triple first.
zh:
桂林扼守湘桂走廊南端，漓江上游岩溶峰林连绵。前214年，秦朝在低矮的分水岭上凿通灵渠，把湘江和漓江连起来，长江流域的粮船和军队得以进入西南，这条水道此后通行了千百年。群峰还给了这座城另一样名声：唐代诗人韩愈把江水比作青罗带、把山比作碧玉簪；1201年，在桂林任职的王正功写下「桂林山水甲天下」，这句诗后来传遍中国。1370年，明太祖封侄孙朱守谦为靖江王，1372年起独秀峰下建起城墙环绕的王城，明代共有十二代、十四位靖江王住在里面。1444年的桂林，既是广西的行政中心，也是一座落在壮族山居之地的藩王王城。

南明的战火在1650年打进王城：清将定南王孔有德攻占桂林，把王府作为自己的府邸。两年后李定国军攻破城池，孔有德自尽，王府的木构殿堂也随大火烧毁。清朝从1657年起把广西贡院设进这座旧王城。桂林在清代也出了两位士林名人：临桂人陈宏谋被视为清代的模范官员，乾隆年间官至东阁大学士；他的曾孙陈继昌在乡试、会试、殿试皆列第一，1820年考中状元，是科举史上最后一位三元及第者。

en:
Marienburg, Polish Malbork, lies on the lower Nogat in Pomezania, the old Prussian land above the Vistula delta. The Teutonic Order began its brick Ordensburg there around 1274 and moved its convent into the new castle in 1280; the new town received Chełmno law in 1286. In 1309 Grand Master Siegfried von Feuchtwangen moved the Order's headquarters from Venice to Marienburg, and a century of building produced the linked High, Middle and Lower Castles, the greatest Gothic brick fortress in Europe, housing at times some 3,000 brothers-in-arms. Nogat barges carried its trade to Gdańsk and the sea, the Order collected river tolls and kept its amber monopoly, and Hanseatic assemblies met in the town. In 1361 the captured Lithuanian grand duke Kęstutis was held in the castle for a time. After Grunwald in 1410 Władysław Jagiełło's army came up the Nogat and burned the town outside, but Heinrich von Plauen held the fortress through the siege. In 1444 Marienburg was still the Catholic capital of the Teutonic state, though its power had been broken on the field at Grunwald.

The Thirteen Years' War began in March 1454 with the Prussian estates joining Poland, and Marienburg changed hands for money rather than by storm: in 1457 the Order's unpaid Bohemian mercenaries sold the castle to Casimir IV for 190,000 florins, and the king entered on 7 June. Burgomaster Bartholomäus Blume led the townsmen's resistance for three more years and was executed when the town fell in 1460. The Second Peace of Thorn in 1466 placed Marienburg in Royal Prussia, and for three centuries Polish kings lodged in the castle on their way to Gdańsk. It held the Maritime Commission from 1568, a royal mint from 1584 and one of the Commonwealth's greatest arsenals, while most townspeople went over to Lutheranism. Gustavus Adolphus occupied the castle in 1626 and Charles X Gustav in 1656 during the Deluge, and in 1708 Stanisław Leszczyński sheltered there for months with his wife and mother. Prussian troops took over in 1772 and let the castle fall into neglect until restoration work began in 1817.
zh:
玛丽安堡，波兰语称马尔堡，位于诺加特河下游、维斯瓦三角洲上方的古普鲁士波梅萨尼亚。约1274年，条顿骑士团动工修筑砖砌骑士团城堡，1280年把修道院迁入，旁边的新镇则在1286年获得海乌姆诺法。1309年，大团长齐格弗里德·冯·福希特旺根把骑士团总部从威尼斯迁到这里，此后一个世纪陆续建成高堡、中堡和下堡相连的建筑群，是欧洲最大的哥特式砖砌要塞，堡内兄弟战士最多时约有三千人。诺加特河上的驳船把城堡同格但斯克和大海相连，骑士团征收河税、垄断琥珀贸易，汉萨同盟的会议也在城中召开。1361年，被俘的立陶宛大公科斯图提斯曾短暂关押于此。1410年格伦瓦尔德战役后，瓦迪斯瓦夫·雅盖沃的军队溯诺加特河而来，烧毁城外市镇，海因里希·冯·普劳恩却守住了城堡。1444年，玛丽安堡仍是条顿国家的天主教都城，只是这个国家的军威已在格伦瓦尔德战场上折损。

1454年3月，普鲁士等级投向波兰，十三年战争爆发；玛丽安堡最后因一笔买卖易主：1457年，骑士团欠饷的波希米亚佣兵以19万弗罗林的价钱把城堡卖给卡齐米日四世，国王于6月7日入城。市长巴托洛梅乌斯·布卢姆率市民继续抵抗三年，1460年城破后被处死。1466年《第二次托伦和约》把玛丽安堡划入皇家普鲁士，此后三百年间，波兰国王前往格但斯克时常驻跸城堡。堡内1568年起设有海事委员会，1584年又设皇家铸币厂，还有全联邦最大的军械库之一，市民则多数改信路德宗。古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫1626年占领城堡，卡尔十世·古斯塔夫又在1656年「大洪水」期间据有此地；1708年，斯坦尼斯瓦夫·莱什琴斯基带着妻子和母亲在堡中避难数月。1772年普鲁士军队接管，城堡长期无人照料，直到1817年修复工程才动工。

en:
Narva guards the crossing of the Narva river, where the road from Reval enters the Russian lands on the outflow of Lake Peipus. Estonian strongholds stood here before the Danish conquest of 1219, and the village of Narvia appears in the Danish Census Book of 1241. A Danish royal castle is attested in 1254, and stone Hermann Castle rose on the west bank soon after, with a Lübeck-law town huddled beneath its walls. When Denmark sold its Estonian lands to the Teutonic Order in 1346, Narva passed to the Livonian Order and became its easternmost commandery. Reval kept the little town out of the Hanseatic League, but it lived by the river trade all the same. In 1444, with only a few hundred inhabitants, it was the frontier market between Catholic Livonia and Orthodox Rus, its tolls collected under the guns of Hermann Castle.

In 1492 Ivan III of Moscow built Ivangorod fortress on the opposite bank, two castles facing each other across the water; when Moscow closed the Hanseatic kontor at Novgorod two years later, more Russian goods moved through Narva. Ivan the Terrible's gunners stormed the town on 11 May 1558, opening the Livonian War, and for twenty-three years Narva was Russia's western outlet, where English and Dutch ships loaded wax, flax and hemp; by 1570 it held some 5,000 people. Pontus De la Gardie, a French-born Swedish commander, took it by storm on 6 September 1581, driving zigzag saps up to the walls; four years later he drowned in the river below his conquest. It became the seat of Sweden's governor of Ingria, and in the 1680s the crown tried in vain to draw the Persian silk trade through its warehouses. On 30 November 1700 Charles XII routed a Russian besieging army three or four times the size of his own, but Peter the Great returned and forced Narva to surrender in August 1704; in 1708 most burghers were deported to Vologda, Kazan and Astrakhan, barely 300 of the town's 3,000 people remaining. The peace of 1721 gave the empty border town to Russia, and it recovered its old population only in the 1770s.
zh:
纳尔瓦扼守纳尔瓦河渡口：佩普西湖的河水从这里入海，从雷瓦尔通往罗斯土地的大路也在此过河。1219年丹麦征服之前，这里已有爱沙尼亚人的堡寨，1241年的《丹麦土地簿》里就记有纳尔维亚村。1254年已有丹麦王室要塞的记载，石砌的赫尔曼堡不久后矗立在河西岸，一座按吕贝克法治理的小镇缩在堡墙下。1346年丹麦把爱沙尼亚领地卖给条顿骑士团，纳尔瓦转归利沃尼亚骑士团，成为其最东端的辖区。雷瓦尔的排挤使小镇始终进不了汉萨同盟，但它照样靠河运贸易为生。1444年，居民不过数百人的纳尔瓦是天主教利沃尼亚与东正教罗斯之间的边贸市场，关税在赫尔曼堡的炮火下征收。

1492年，莫斯科的伊凡三世在对岸建起伊万哥罗德要塞，两座城堡隔河对峙；两年后莫斯科关闭诺夫哥罗德的汉萨商馆，更多俄国货物改由纳尔瓦转运。1558年5月11日，伊凡雷帝的军队攻破此城，打响利沃尼亚战争；此后23年纳尔瓦是俄国通向西方的出海口，英格兰和荷兰商船在此装载蜂蜡、亚麻和大麻，到1570年居民已有约五千。1581年9月6日，在瑞典军中效力的法国裔将领庞图斯·德拉加迪把之字形壕沟挖到墙下、强攻得手；四年后，他在自己攻下的这条河里溺水身亡。纳尔瓦后来成为瑞典英格里亚总督的驻地，1680年代王室还试图把波斯丝绸贸易引到这里的货栈，却没有成功。1700年11月30日，卡尔十二击溃兵力三四倍于己的围城俄军；但彼得大帝卷土重来，于1704年8月迫使纳尔瓦投降，1708年又把大部分市民流放到沃洛格达、喀山和阿斯特拉罕，三千居民仅余约三百。1721年的和约把这座空城划归俄国，它直到1770年代才恢复旧日人口。

en:
Kōzuke was a Tōsandō province across the upper Tone, its mountain-rimmed basins making up most of later Gunma. The Heian court ranked it among Japan's 'great countries', and imperial pastures gave it a name for strong horses; its provincial offices, temple and Sōja shrine stood near Umayabashi, a Tone bridge and post station on the site of Maebashi. The Uesugi were its military governors under the Muromachi shoguns but lived at Kamakura as Kantō deputies; in 1444 two Nagao branches at Sōja and Shiroi ran the province, a guarded corridor of horse runs between Kanto and the mountain lands.

The collapse of Uesugi power made Kōzuke a battlefield. After the Kawagoe defeat of 1546 and the fall of Hirai to Hōjō Ujiyasu in 1552, Uesugi Norimasa fled to Echigo. At Minowa, Nagano Narimasa held the west against Takeda Shingen; when Shingen's twenty thousand invested the castle in 1566, Kamiizumi Nobutsuna led a sortie and fought so well that Shingen sought his service. Nobutsuna refused. He is remembered for the sword school he created, Shinkage-ryū, which he taught in Kyoto to Yagyū Munetoshi, whose descendants taught the Tokugawa shoguns, and for the split-bamboo practice sword that let men spar at full force without fear of grave injury. Kenshin, Takeda Shingen and the Hōjō took and retook Umayabashi through the 1560s. In 1582 Nobunaga's general Takigawa Kazumasu entered the province and withdrew after the Kannagawa battle, and after the 1590 Odawara campaign Ieyasu gave the castle to his own men, Sakai Shigetada rebuilding it in 1601 as seat of the Umayabashi domain, later Maebashi.

The Tokugawa peace divided Kōzuke among Maebashi, Takasaki, Annaka and smaller domains, busy with traffic on the Nakasendō and the Mikuni Kaidō. High in the western mountains the hot springs of Kusatsu had drawn wounded samurai through the Sengoku wars; in 1595 Hideyoshi praised the waters to Ieyasu, who merely sent servants to bring some back, and under the eighth shogun Yoshimune Kusatsu water was carried all the way to Edo Castle. The Tone dealt Maebashi worse: year by year the river ate at the castle's bank, and in 1767 the Matsudaira moved their seat to Kawagoe and had Maebashi Castle pulled down two years later.
zh:
上野是东山道之国，地跨利根川上游，群山环抱的盆地构成后来群马的主体。平安朝廷将其列为「大国」，敕旨牧场又以良马闻名；国衙、国分寺和总社神社都在厩桥附近，那是利根川上设有桥梁的东山道驿家，地点即后来的前桥。室町幕府下，上杉氏身任守护，却以关东管领身份常居镰仓；1444年实际治理上野的，是分据总社、白井的长尾氏两家被官。这片养马之地夹在关东与山间诸国之间，常年有兵看护，不归单一领主紧密统辖。

上杉权威崩落后，上野沦为战场。1546年河越战败，1552年平井城落入北条氏康之手，上杉宪政逃往越后。西方的箕轮城，长野业正一直抗住武田信玄；1566年信玄以两万大军围城，上泉信纲率部出城突击，武勇之盛令信玄当面延揽，信纲没有接受。让他留名后世的是自创的新阴流剑术：他在京都把这一流派传给柳生宗严，柳生一门后来教授德川历代将军；他还被视为袋竹刀的创制者，练习者得以全力对劈而不必担心死伤。1560年代，上杉谦信、武田信玄和北条氏反复争夺厩桥；1582年织田信长部将泷川一益进入上州，神流川战败后撤退。1590年小田原征伐后，家康把城交给家臣，1601年酒井重忠将其改建，作为厩桥藩、后来前桥藩的居城。

德川太平中，上野分属前桥、高崎、安中等藩，中山道与三国街道往来繁忙。西部深山里的草津温泉在战国年间就吸引着负伤武士；1595年秀吉曾向家康推荐此汤，家康只派人取水而回，到八代将军吉宗时，草津的泉水甚至一路运进江户城。利根川对前桥却毫不留情：河水年年侵蚀城基，1767年松平氏终于把居城迁往川越，前桥城两年后拆毁。

en:
Xiangkhoang is an open plateau in the Annamite Cordillera, set high above the Mekong and the Vietnamese lowlands. Its best-known ground is the Plain of Jars, where clusters of Iron Age stone urns still stand in the upland valleys and mark old burial sites; local legend calls them jars made for a giant king's victory feast. Tai-speaking Phuan settlers founded Muang Phuan in the 13th century, with Muang Khoun as their capital, and Fa Ngum bound the principality to Lan Xang in the mid-14th century. Its princes kept their own court and sent gold and silver trees as tribute. In 1444 Chao Kam Pong had just returned to power with Lan Xang help, ruling rice lands and hill pastures that the Vietnamese court at Đông Kinh also wanted to draw into its orbit.

Control of the plateau repeatedly brought armies into the hills. After the Phuan ruler submitted to the Lê dynasty in 1469, his land was organised as Trấn Ninh; an attempt to throw out the Vietnamese garrisons brought the great invasion of 1479, when chronicles claim war and famine reduced 90,000 people to little more than 2,000. Muang Khoun recovered as a Buddhist capital, its temples using low roofs and the narrow 'waist' associated with the Xieng Khouang style. When Lan Xang split in 1707, the Phuan princes paid tribute to Luang Prabang and Vientiane, but Chao Ong Lo's failed attack on Vientiane in 1751 left them under Vientiane's supervision. The Siamese conquest of Vientiane in 1779 added Bangkok as overlord, and Siamese levies began moving Phuan households west. Chao Somphou rebuilt Muang Khoun's temples and fortifications, only to be carried prisoner to Vientiane, where he died after a second arrest in 1800. His nephew Chao Noy enlarged the army and taxes and crushed a Khmu rising in 1814. In 1821 the plateau still sent tribute to three courts: Vientiane, Bangkok and Huế.
zh:
川圹是长山山脉上的高原，地势高于湄公河流域和越南平原。当地最有名的是石缸平原，成片的铁器时代石缸立在谷地间，标示着古老墓葬；当地传说把它们说成巨人国王庆功宴上的酒缸。13世纪，说泰语的盆族迁入，建立孟潘，定都孟昆；14世纪中期，法昂把这个小邦纳入澜沧。盆族君长保留自己的朝廷，以金银花树朝贡。1444年，昭琴蓬刚在澜沧帮助下复位，统治着稻田和山地牧场；东都的后黎朝廷也想把这片高原纳入自己的势力范围。

高原的控制权反复引来军队。1469年盆族君长归顺后黎朝，其地被设为镇宁；驱逐越南驻军的尝试招来1479年大军，编年史称战火和饥荒使九万人只余二千。孟昆后来恢复为佛教都城，寺院采用低屋顶和「束腰」式的川圹风格。1707年澜沧分裂，盆族君长同时向琅勃拉邦和万象进贡，但昭翁洛1751年进攻万象失败，孟潘反受万象节制。1779年暹罗征服万象，曼谷成为新宗主，暹罗军役开始把盆族民户西迁。昭岑普重修孟昆寺院和城防，却被押往万象，1800年第二次被囚后死在那里。其侄昭内扩充军队、加重赋税，1814年镇压克木人起事。1821年，这片高原还要向万象、曼谷和顺化三个王廷输贡。

en:
Pyongyang spreads along the Taedong River, about a hundred kilometres inland from the Yellow Sea. King Jangsu of Goguryeo moved his capital here in 427, and the fortress raised in 586 was the kingdom's last capital when Goguryeo fell in 668. Under Goryeo the city was the Western Capital, Seogyeong, and more than one ruler planned to move the court there. In 1413 it became the seat of the governor of Pyongan, the north-western province named from Pyongyang and Anju; envoys to the Ming court passed this way on the road to the border crossing at Uiju. The Taedong plain fed the province and Pyongyang merchants ran the river and inland trade, for in Pyongan the local gentry lived much like commoners and a trading culture that set ability above birth grew early. In 1444, under King Sejong, Pyongyang was the administrative and market centre of the whole north-west.

The Japanese invasion of 1592 turned the city into a siege ground. In July Konishi Yukinaga's vanguard reached the Taedong; King Seonjo fled north, and the Japanese entered an abandoned Pyongyang and seized its granaries. In February 1593 a Ming army under Li Rusong stormed the walls, and the Japanese crossed the frozen river in flight that night. Later Jin troops under Amin advanced from Uiju and occupied the city in March 1627, forcing Joseon into a 'brotherly' alliance; Qing troops occupied it again during the invasion of 1636 to 1637. The Taedong Gate, ruined in the wars, was rebuilt in 1635. The same resentment of discrimination against the north-west fed Hong Gyeong-rae's rising in January 1812: his rebels took several towns, then were besieged in Jeongju, and in May government troops blew a mine under the walls and Hong died in the final assault.
zh:
平壤位于大同江畔，距黄海入海口约一百公里。427年高句丽长寿王迁都于此，586年所筑的平壤城是高句丽668年灭亡前最后的都城。高丽时代这里称西京，几代统治者都曾打算把朝廷迁来。1413年平壤成为平安道监营所在地，道名取自平壤与安州；出使明朝的使节团经此前往义州渡江。平安道的乡班与平民生活相差无几，重才能轻身份的商贾之风兴起较早，大同江平原的米粮与江运商货多经平壤商人之手。1444年朝鲜世宗在位时，平壤是整个关西的行政与商业中心。

1592年壬辰倭乱，平壤沦为围城战场。7月小西行长的先锋进抵大同江，宣祖北逃，日军进入空城平壤，夺得城中粮库。1593年2月，李如松率领的明军攻破城墙，日军当夜踏冰渡江南逃。1627年3月，阿敏的后金军从义州南下占领平壤，迫使朝鲜结成兄弟之盟；1636至1637年丙子胡乱时，平壤再遭清军占据。战乱中被毁的大同门于1635年重建。关西长期受朝廷歧视，积怨化为1812年1月洪景来的起兵：起义军连得数城后被围于定州，5月官军挖地道以火药轰塌城墙，洪景来死于最后的攻城。

en:
Amasya lies in a narrow cleft of the Yeşilırmak, the river road from central Anatolia toward the Black Sea and the eastern marches running between sheer cliffs. From the third century BC it was the capital of the kings of Pontus, and their tombs are the chambers cut in rows into the rock face above the town; the geographer Strabo, born here around 63 BC, left a description of the fortified city he grew up in. The Danishmend emirs made conquered Amasya their capital, and after the Seljuks took it in 1175 mosques and madrasas made it a seat of learning under Rum Seljuk and Ilkhanid rule. The Eretnids and the lord Hacı Şadgeldi held it before it passed to the Ottomans in 1393, when Bayezid I installed his son, the future Mehmed I, as prince-governor. After the defeat at Ankara in 1402, Mehmed held out in Amasya through the Interregnum until 1413. In 1444 it was therefore the empire's privileged princely town on the eastern military road.

Ottoman princes learned provincial government here: Mehmed II, Bayezid II and Selim I all served at Amasya, and Murad II and Selim I were born in the town. In 1486 Bayezid II raised the city's great mosque-and-hospital complex, its largest külliye, and the river orchards supplied the small sweet apples for which the district was known. Süleyman often stayed here and received the Habsburg envoy Busbecq, and in 1555 he made peace at Amasya with Shah Tahmasp, the treaty that first fixed a border between the Ottoman and Safavid empires. Between 1530 and 1545 a ritual-murder charge brought several Jews to the gallows; when the supposed Christian victim was found alive, Süleyman ordered such cases to the sultan's own court. Damaged in the Celali disorders early in the seventeenth century, Amasya afterward lived quietly as a sanjak seat beneath the rock tombs.
zh:
阿马西亚位于耶希勒河的狭窄峡谷中，安纳托利亚中部通往黑海和东部边疆的河路从陡崖之间穿过。公元前3世纪起，这里是本都诸王的都城，国王们的墓室成排凿在临河崖壁上；约公元前63年出生于此的地理学家斯特拉波，就留下过对这座他长大的设防城市的描写。达尼什曼德埃米尔征服阿马西亚后以它为都，1175年塞尔柱人取城，在罗姆塞尔柱和伊儿汗国治下，清真寺和伊斯兰学校使这里成为学术之城。埃雷特纳王朝与领主哈吉·沙德格尔迪相继据守，1393年阿马西亚并入奥斯曼，巴耶济德一世命王子、后来的穆罕默德一世出任长官。1402年安卡拉战败后，穆罕默德据守阿马西亚，撑过整个大空位期，直到1413年。因此1444年的阿马西亚是帝国东部军用大道上地位特殊的王子驻城。

奥斯曼诸王子在此学习治理地方：穆罕默德二世、巴耶济德二世和塞利姆一世都曾任阿马西亚长官，穆拉德二世和塞利姆一世也出生于此。1486年，巴耶济德二世建起宏大的清真寺兼医院建筑群，这是城中最大的库里耶；河畔果园出产个小味甜的苹果，这一带当时已以此闻名。苏莱曼一世常在此驻跸，并接见哈布斯堡使臣布斯贝克；1555年他在阿马西亚与塔赫玛斯普沙议和，这份和议第一次划定奥斯曼与萨法维两大帝国的边界。1530至1545年间，一场仪式谋杀指控把几名犹太人送上绞架，所谓的基督徒受害者后来被发现仍在人世，苏莱曼便下令此类案件归苏丹亲掌的法庭审理。17世纪初阿马西亚在杰拉里动乱中受损，此后作为桑贾克驻地，在崖墓之下过着平静日子。

en:
Shiribeshi follows the rugged Sea of Japan side of Ezo, from the Oshima Peninsula around the steep Shakotan Peninsula to Ishikari Bay. Short mountain streams such as the Shiribetsu gave the land its Ainu name, shiri pet, or 'mountain river', and Ainu villages occupied their mouths. In medieval times Watarito seafarers carried furs and dried fish from this coast to Tsugaru within the loose trading order of the Andō lords. In 1444 the country beyond the southern settlements was still Ainu land: villagers took salmon and spring herring and bartered with Japanese traders, but no Japanese town stood west of Yoichi.

War and trade moved up the coast together. When Koshamain rose in 1457, the fighting spread beyond Yoichi. Matsumae later placed trade houses at Setana, Suttsu, Iwanai, Shakotan, Yoichi and Otarunai, where Ainu exchanged furs and fish for iron, rice and sake at the annual omusha ceremony. After Shakushain's rising of 1669, the Ainu around Yoichi also submitted to the domain.

Herring made the northern posts pay. An Echigo fisherman brought hemp gill nets to these waters in 1673, and Genroku-era boats sailed north after the spring runs. From the early eighteenth century Ōmi merchants contracted the posts and shipped herring meal south on kitamaebune freighters as fertilizer for Honshu fields. Mamiya Rinzō surveyed the coast for the shogunate in 1803. Russian probes then brought a change of rule: West Ezo, including Shiribeshi, came under direct shogunal administration from Hakodate in 1807, before being returned to Matsumae in 1821.
zh:
后志位于虾夷地崎岖的日本海一侧，海岸从渡岛半岛绕过陡峻的积丹半岛，延伸到石狩湾。尻别川等山溪短促，阿伊努语称这些山溪为「尻别」，意为山之川，河口多有阿伊努村落。中世时，渡党海商在安东氏松散的贸易秩序下，把这一带的毛皮和鱼干运往津轻。1444年，南方聚落以北仍是阿伊努人的土地：村民捕鲑鱼、赶春季鲱鱼群，并与和人商人以物易物，但余市以西还没有和人城镇。

战争与贸易沿海岸一同北上。1457年科夏迈因举事，战火蔓延到余市以西。松前藩后来在濑棚、寿都、岩内、积丹、余市、小樽内设置商馆，阿伊努人每年在奥姆沙礼上以毛皮和鱼产换取铁器、米和酒。1669年夏库夏因起义后，余市一带的阿伊努人也向松前藩臣服。

鲱鱼使北方商馆获得厚利。1673年，一名越后渔民把麻制刺网带到这片海域；到元禄年间，渔船已追随春季鱼群北上。18世纪初起，近江商人承包各商馆，用北前船把鲱鱼渣南运，作为本州农田的肥料。1803年，间宫林藏奉幕府之命测量海岸。俄罗斯船只的探查随后改变了统治安排：1807年，包括后志在内的西虾夷地改由箱馆的幕府官员直辖，1821年才交还松前藩。

en:
Hamid is the rolling lake country behind the Mediterranean coast, and its chief town Burdur lies on the shore of Lake Burdur. The Byzantine Polydorion stood here when the Kınalı branch of the Oghuz Turks settled after Manzikert, and around 1300 Dündar Bey of the Hamidids took the town and built its Grand Mosque; his dynasty ruled the region chiefly from Eğirdir. In 1374, worn down by Karamanid attacks, the last effective Hamidid bey, Hüseyin, sold Beyşehir, Akşehir and his other northern lands to the Ottoman sultan Murad I for 80,000 gold coins, keeping only Isparta and Eğirdir for himself. Bayezid I took the rest, including Burdur, in 1391; Timur restored Turkish rule after Ankara in 1402, and the region came back to the Ottomans in 1423. In 1444 Burdur was a small Sunni Turkish district town of the Hamid sanjak. Ibn Battuta, who visited in 1330, found orchards and farms around the castle and an ahi guild running its markets; caravans between Konya and the Aegean carried Pisidian tragacanth this way and brought back spices, cotton and sugar from Egypt.

An Ottoman register of 1478 counted four quarters in Burdur, three Muslim and one Christian, with the mosque quarter the largest. The castle Ibn Battuta had seen beside the Grand Mosque was gradually pulled down over the years, for the town had little strategic need of it. The market around the mosque stayed the centre of local life, serving the caravans that plied between Konya and the Aegean ports.
zh:
哈米德是地中海沿岸后方起伏的湖沼地带，首府布尔杜尔位于布尔杜尔湖畔。乌古斯突厥人的克纳勒部在曼齐刻尔特战役后到此定居时，这里还是拜占庭的波吕多里翁。约1300年，哈米德贝伊国的丁达尔贝伊夺取此城，修建了大清真寺，他的王朝主要在埃尔迪尔统治这一地区。1374年，末代强势的贝伊侯赛因受不住卡拉曼人的连年攻打，以八万枚金币把贝伊谢希尔、阿克谢希尔等北部领地卖给奥斯曼苏丹穆拉德一世，自己只留下伊斯帕尔塔和埃尔迪尔。1391年，巴耶济德一世攻取包括布尔杜尔在内的余下土地；1402年安卡拉战役后帖木儿恢复了突厥人的统治，1423年此地重回奥斯曼。1444年时，布尔杜尔是哈米德桑贾克一座小小的逊尼派土耳其人城镇。1330年到访的伊本·白图泰见到城堡四周果园农田环绕，一个阿赫行会掌管着市集；往来科尼亚与爱琴海之间的商队经此运出皮西迪亚山区的黄蓍胶，带回埃及的香料、棉花和糖。

1478年的一份奥斯曼册籍记下布尔杜尔有四个居民区，三个穆斯林区、一个基督徒区，其中清真寺区最大。伊本·白图泰见过的那座城堡在大清真寺旁逐年倾圮拆除，因为这座城镇几乎没有设防的需要。清真寺周围的市集始终是本地生活的中心，接待着往来科尼亚与爱琴海港口的商队。

en:
Hama straddles the Orontes where the river leaves the Syrian steppe midway between Aleppo and Damascus, and travellers nearing the walls heard the city first: along the banks turned more than thirty wooden norias, their rim boxes lifting river water into aqueducts that fed the gardens, mosques and bathhouses. The greatest, the Noria al-Muhammadiya, raised in 1361, stood taller than any other waterwheel in the world for nearly five centuries. The old Aramaean city of Hamath passed to Muslim rule in the 630s; Nur al-Din rebuilt its Great Mosque in 1172 after the great earthquakes, and Saladin gave the town to his Ayyubid kin. Hama's most learned lord was Abu al-Fida, an Ayyubid prince who ruled from 1310 to 1332 and wrote his universal history and his survey of world geography in the city, works still read in European translations centuries later. Timur's troops sacked Hama in 1400, but in 1444 it was again a walled city of palaces, madrasas and markets on the Aleppo road, its cotton fields and gardens worked by the wheels of the river.

In 1453 a second colossal wheel, the Noria al-Ma'muriyya, was raised beside the Muhammadiya. Selim I's victory at Marj Dabiq in 1516 delivered Hama to the Ottomans, and as a district seat of the province of Tripoli the city grew rich on the caravan trade: Rustem Pasha's caravansary was built in 1556 for the merchants and their pack trains. In the eighteenth century Hama passed to the governors of Damascus; As'ad Pasha al-Azem, who governed the city until 1742, built the Azem Palace and his own great khan. By his day fourteen caravansaries handled the cotton, wool and grain on which Hama's leading families built their fortunes.
zh:
哈马城跨阿西河而建，地处阿勒颇与大马士革之间、河流离开叙利亚草原之处；走近城墙的人往往先听到这座城：河岸上转动着三十多架木制纳乌拉水车，水轮边缘的水斗把河水提进高架水渠，送入园林、清真寺和澡堂。其中最大的「穆罕默迪耶」建于1361年，在近五百年里是全世界最高的水车。古城哈马本是阿拉米人的城邦，630年代转入穆斯林统治；大地震后，努尔丁1172年重建了大清真寺，萨拉丁后来把此城封给阿尤布家族亲族。哈马最博学的君主是阿尤布王公阿布·菲达，他1310至1332年在此执政，在城里写成了通史和世界地理著作，几个世纪后还有欧洲译本可读。1400年帖木儿的军队洗劫哈马，但到1444年，它重又成为阿勒颇大道上一座城墙环绕、宫邸和经学院与市集林立的城市，河水带起的水车灌溉着棉田和园林。

1453年，第二架巨型水车「马穆里耶」在穆罕默迪耶旁竖起。1516年塞利姆一世在达比克草原获胜，哈马并入奥斯曼帝国，作为的黎波里省的县治靠商队贸易致富：1556年建起吕斯泰姆帕夏商馆，供商人和驮队落脚。18世纪，哈马改属大马士革总督；主政此城到1742年的阿萨德·帕夏·阿扎姆修建了阿扎姆宫和以他命名的大商馆。到他那时，城中十四座商栈经营棉花、羊毛和粮食，哈马的望族靠这些生意发家。

en:
Yaran is the short coastal river the Manchus called the Yalan, breaking out of the Sikhote-Alin forests into a sheltered, almost ice-free bay of the Sea of Japan. In 1444 the people on its banks were the Woji, the 'forest people' kin to the Udeghe, who took salmon at their weirs, trapped sable in the woods and dug ginseng in the hills. Their headmen still held the patents of the Ming guard once set up on the river, but no Ming clerk had come to inspect them since the Nurgan commission was withdrawn.

Nurhaci sent five hundred men to this coast in November 1614, against the Yalan and the neighbouring Xilin road; they brought back two hundred households that submitted and a thousand captives. Under the Qing the coastal clans, called Kiyakara, carried sable pelts every other year to the deputy at Sanxing and returned with the silk and cloth the court handed out as the 'forest bounty', yet the shore was kept sealed: no banner garrison, walled town or civilian field appeared there. European ships came anyway. In the summer of 1787 Lapérouse's frigates Boussole and Astrolabe surveyed this coast on their way north to latitude 51 and named De-Kastri Bay, the first European vessels to chart it.
zh:
雅兰是一条滨海小河，满语称雅兰河，它从锡霍特山脉的林海中穿出，注入日本海一处避风、几乎不封冻的海湾。1444年住在河畔的，是被称为渥集的「林中人」，与乌德盖人同源；他们在鱼梁上捕鲑鱼，在林中诱捕紫貂，在山里挖人参。头人手里还留着明朝设在河上的牙鲁卫敕书，但奴儿干都司撤回后，再没有明朝书吏前来查验。

1614年十一月，努尔哈赤发兵五百来到这段海岸，征讨雅兰和相邻的锡林二路，收降二百户、俘获千人而还。清代，被称为恰喀拉的滨海各部每两年把貂皮送到三姓副都统衙门，领回朝廷以「赏乌林」之名发给的绸缎布匹；海岸却被封禁，不设旗营、不筑城、不开民田。欧洲船只还是来了：1787年夏，拉彼鲁兹率「罗盘号」「星盘号」北上，在前往北纬51度的途中测绘这段海岸，并命名德卡斯特里湾，这是最早勘察这一带海岸的欧洲船只。

en:
Coimbra climbs a hill above the Mondego, looking over fertile grain lands and the river road between Portugal's interior and its coast. It was the Roman Aeminium, which inherited the bishopric of the ruined Conímbriga, and under Muslim rule it was Qulumriyah until Ferdinand I of León stormed it in 1064 at the end of a months-long siege; Sesnando Davides then ruled it as Count of Coimbra. Afonso Henriques made the town the first royal centre of his kingdom, and the Santa Cruz monastery founded there in 1131 held the tombs of Portugal's first two kings. On 7 January 1355 Afonso IV had his son's Galician mistress, Inês de Castro, killed at Coimbra; when Pedro I took the throne he took a bloody revenge on her killers, and legend says he had her corpse exhumed and crowned as his queen. John I created the Duchy of Coimbra for his son Peter in 1415, and in 1444 Peter governed Portugal as regent from his lands on the lower Mondego.

Peter's regency ended in civil war, and he was killed at Alfarrobeira on 20 May 1449. Coimbra's later renown came from its university, founded by Denis in Lisbon in 1290 and first brought to the city in 1308; John III moved it back permanently in 1537 and installed it in the old royal palace, which the university bought in 1597. John V built the Baroque Joanina Library between 1717 and 1728 for its books, and the later Pombaline reforms gave mathematics and natural philosophy a central place in its teaching.

On 27 September 1810 Wellington's army, drawn up on the Serra do Buçaco ridge north of the city, threw back Masséna's assaults with heavy losses, but the French turned the ridge and occupied Coimbra. On 6 October a Portuguese militia under Colonel Nicholas Trant, an Irish officer in British service, retook the city and seized the French wounded and stores left there in Masséna's wake.
zh:
科英布拉依蒙德拉古河畔的山丘而建，俯临肥沃的谷粮产地，以及连通葡萄牙内陆与海岸的河水通道。罗马时代这里称埃米尼乌姆，在科尼姆布里加被毁后承接了它的主教座；穆斯林统治时称库卢姆里亚，1064年莱昂国王费尔南多一世经数月围攻破城，塞斯南多·达维德斯随后以科英布拉伯爵身份统治此地。阿方索·恩里克斯把科英布拉作为他的王国最早的王都，1131年在此建立的圣十字修道院安葬了葡萄牙最初两代国王。1355年1月7日，阿方索四世下令在科英布拉杀死儿子的加利西亚情人伊内斯·德·卡斯特罗；佩德罗一世继位后向凶手血腥复仇，相传他还把伊内斯的遗骨掘出，加冕为王后。1415年，若昂一世为儿子佩德罗设立科英布拉公爵领，1444年，佩德罗正以蒙德拉古下游的领地为根基，出任葡萄牙摄政。

佩德罗的摄政以内战收场，1449年5月20日他在阿尔法罗贝拉战死。科英布拉后来的名声来自大学：它由迪尼什于1290年在里斯本创立，1308年首次迁来科英布拉，1537年若昂三世把它永久迁回，安置在旧王宫中，学校又在1597年买下这座宫殿。1717年至1728年，若昂五世为藏书修建了巴洛克风格的若阿宁娜图书馆，后来的蓬巴尔改革让数学和自然哲学在教学中占据重要位置。

1810年9月27日，威灵顿的军队在城北布萨科山列阵，重创马塞纳的进攻；但法军绕过山脊，占领了科英布拉。10月6日，在英军中服役的爱尔兰军官尼古拉斯·特兰特上校率领葡萄牙民兵收复该城，俘获了马塞纳后方留下的法军伤兵和物资。

en:
Tokachi is the wide coastal plain of southeastern Ezo, the island later called Hokkaido, where the Tokachi River runs out to the Pacific. Its Ainu name, Tokapchi, was explained as breast-milk, for the river's two mouths that never stopped flowing. In 1444 Ainu villages held the coast and the river terraces, living on the autumn salmon runs, sea fishing and deer and bear hunting; they traded dried salmon and furs to ships from the Japanese settlements on the Oshima Peninsula for rice and iron tools. The nearest Japanese lord, the Kakizaki house that would become the Matsumae, sat far to the southwest and scarcely touched this shore.

Under the Matsumae monopoly the Tokachi fishing ground became a licensed basho worked by a clan retainer, who exchanged Japanese goods for the Ainu catch at his trading post. The great Ainu rising under Shakushain grew from a feud between two Ainu groups into a general war on the Matsumae; when it broke out in June 1669 it ran along the Pacific coast, and Japanese residents were killed in Tokachi as well. Pressure from Russian ships probing south from the Kurils then pushed the shogunate into the north: in 1798 the shogunal official Kondo Juzo cut a steep mountain road on the coastal route out of Hakodate, and in 1799 eastern Ezo, Tokachi included, was brought under direct shogunal rule. With the scare over, it was handed back to the Matsumae in 1821.
zh:
十胜是虾夷（后改称北海道）东南沿海的广阔平原，十胜川在此注入太平洋。阿伊努语地名托卡普奇（Tokapchi）被解作乳汁之意，因这条河分两口入海、水流不绝。1444年，阿伊努人的村落占据海岸和河流阶地，以秋季鲑鱼洄游、海渔和猎鹿猎熊为生，把干鲑鱼和毛皮卖给渡岛半岛日本定居点来的船只，换回米和铁器。离他们最近的日本领主是后来成为松前氏的蛎崎氏，远在西南，几乎管不到这片海岸。

松前氏垄断虾夷贸易后，十胜渔场成为特许的「场所」，由一名松前家臣经营，在他的运上屋里用日本货物交换阿伊努人的渔获。沙牟奢允领导的阿伊努大起义起于两个部族的仇杀，后来演变为对松前氏的全面战事，1669年6月爆发后沿太平洋岸蔓延，十胜也有日本居民被杀。此后俄罗斯船只从千岛方向南下试探，幕府转而着手经营北方：1798年幕吏近藤重藏在箱馆北上的沿岸道路上凿开一段险峻山路，1799年包括十胜在内的东虾夷地收归幕府直辖。边警缓和后，十胜又在1821年交还松前氏。

en:
Kastoria lies on a promontory pushed into Lake Orestiada in western Macedonia, ringed by limestone mountains. It was the ancient Celetrum, which surrendered to the Roman consul Sulpicius Galba in 199 BC; after the earlier town was destroyed, Procopius writes that Justinian I moved its people onto the lakeside promontory they still occupy. The town walls and the oldest of Kastoria's many Byzantine churches, among them St Stephen, date from the ninth century, when it was a Byzantine fortress over the lake district. In the medieval centuries it passed from one Balkan ruler to the next: Basil II took it from the Bulgarians in 1018, Bohemond of Taranto's Normans held it in 1082-1083 until Alexios I Komnenos forced the garrison out, the Serbs of Stefan Dusan took it in 1342-1343, and the Albanian Muzaka family followed them. The Ottomans conquered the town about 1385. In 1444 Kastoria was a Greek Orthodox place of furriers, fishermen and merchants, with an old Romaniote Jewish congregation that had lived there since Bulgarian rule.

After the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople, Kastoria's Romaniote Jews were forcibly moved to the Balat quarter of the depopulated capital, but before 1500 Jews expelled from Italy, Sicily, Portugal and Spain had settled here and refilled its congregations. Fur was the town's living: the furriers dressed wolf, fox, weasel and beaver pelts, and Kastorian merchants carried them across Central Europe. Fur money paid for the town's Greek schools, the oldest in Macedonia, which opened in 1614; two more followed in 1705 and 1715. The revolutionary Rigas Feraios used Kastoria as one of his bases in 1797-1798, plotting with local merchants including Georgios Theocharis and the Emmanuel brothers. When the Austrians handed the group to the Ottomans, John Emmanuel admitted he had smuggled Feraios's call to revolt, the Thourios, into the town and sung it there many times. In 1821 Kastorians joined the Greek rising, until the Ottoman commander Mehmet Emin seized the town's notables as hostages.
zh:
卡斯托里亚位于西马其顿，坐落在伸入俄瑞斯蒂亚达湖的一座半岛上，四周石灰岩山地环抱。此地古称凯莱特隆，公元前199年向罗马执政官苏尔皮基乌斯·加尔巴投降；旧城被毁后，据普罗科匹厄斯记载，查士丁尼一世把居民迁到湖边半岛，新城便建在这座半岛上。9世纪时这里是拜占庭扼守湖区的要塞，城墙与城中众多拜占庭教堂里最古老的一批都建于此时，圣司提反堂便是其中之一。中世纪的几百年里，此城在巴尔干各势力间转手：1018年巴西尔二世从保加利亚人手中夺取，1082至1083年塔兰托的博希蒙德率诺曼人占据，阿历克塞一世·科穆宁迫降守军将其收复，1342至1343年斯特凡·杜尚的塞尔维亚人攻取此城，之后轮到阿尔巴尼亚的穆扎卡家族。1385年前后，奥斯曼人征服卡斯托里亚。1444年，这里是一座希腊东正教城镇，居民以毛皮匠、渔民和商人为主，还有一个保加利亚统治时期就已定居的古老罗马尼奥特犹太人社群。

君士坦丁堡陷落后，卡斯托里亚的罗马尼奥特犹太人被强行迁往新都的巴拉特区充实人口；但到1500年之前，被逐出意大利、西西里、葡萄牙和西班牙的犹太人来此定居，城中的犹太会众重新壮大。毛皮是这座城的生计：皮匠加工狼皮、狐皮、鼬皮和海狸皮，卡斯托里亚商人把成品贩运到中欧各地。毛皮赚来的钱供养了城里的希腊语学校，马其顿最古老的一所于1614年开办，1705年和1715年又各建一所。1797至1798年，革命家里加斯·费拉奥斯把卡斯托里亚当作据点之一，与格奥尔吉奥斯·塞奥哈里斯、埃曼努伊尔兄弟等当地商人密谋；奥地利当局把这群人交给奥斯曼人后，扬尼斯·埃曼努伊尔承认，自己曾把费拉奥斯号召起义的战歌《图里奥斯》偷运进城，还多次传唱。1821年，城中居民投身希腊起义，奥斯曼指挥官穆罕默德·埃明最后拘捕当地名流作为人质。

en:
The district runs from a rocky roadstead on the Mediterranean up to the Samarian hills. Jaffa, the port where pilgrims to Jerusalem came ashore, is among the oldest harbours in the Levant: the Bible makes it the place from which Jonah sailed, and Greek legend chained Andromeda to its sea rock. Baybars stormed and wrecked the town in March 1268, and when the Burgundian pilgrim Bertrandon de la Broquiere landed in 1432 he found only ruins and reed huts where the sultan's officers counted arrivals and took their tribute. A day's march inland stood Nablus, in a well-watered valley between Mounts Ebal and Gerizim, the Samaritans' holy mountain. The Jerusalem geographer al-Muqaddasi called it Little Damascus for its springs, its paved Great Mosque and the stream running through its markets; olive oil and soap went to Egypt, Damascus and the Hejaz, and carob jam as far as Cairo. In 1444 both coast and hills belonged to the Mamluk sultan, the one a half-ruined toll-station, the other a prosperous market town with a large Samaritan quarter.

Selim I's conquest in 1516 made Nablus the seat of one of the six sanjaks of Ottoman Palestine, while Jaffa stayed almost empty: the 1596 registers list fifteen households, and travellers of those years called the site a heap of ruins. Pilgrim hostels returned only slowly in the seventeenth century, and eighteenth-century pirates so harried the roadstead that merchants lived at Ramla and went down to the shore when a watchman signalled a ship. An Ottoman expedition of 1657 meant to tighten central rule instead planted the clans that ran the hills for two centuries, the Nimr, Jarrar and Tuqan families, whose wealth rested on olive oil, soap and the Levant's largest cotton crop; Nablus outranked Jerusalem, Jaffa and Acre as a manufacturing town. Zahir al-Umar of Acre besieged it twice in the 1770s without success. In 1775 his Egyptian enemy Abu al-Dhahab took Jaffa after forty-nine days and put its adult men to death; on 7 March 1799 Napoleon breached the same walls, sacked the town and had some 2,000 prisoners shot on the beach, after which plague swept the ruins. Muhammad Abu-Nabbut rebuilt Jaffa with the Mahmoudiya Mosque and its fountain, and after Jezzar Pasha died in 1804 the Tuqans made Nablus a power in the hills again.
zh:
这片地区从地中海边的岩港一直延伸到撒玛利亚山地。雅法是朝圣者登岸前往耶路撒冷的港口，也是黎凡特最古老的港湾之一：《圣经》里约拿从这里搭船出逃，希腊传说中安德洛墨达被锁在海边的岩礁上。1268年3月，拜巴尔攻破并摧毁此城；1432年勃艮第朝圣者贝特朗东·德·拉·布罗基耶尔上岸时，只见到处是废墟和芦苇棚屋，苏丹的官吏在那里清点登岸人数、抽取规费。往内陆走一天路程是纳布卢斯，坐落在以巴路山和基利心山之间水源丰足的谷地里，基利心山就是撒玛利亚人的圣山。耶路撒冷出身的地理学家穆卡达西称它为「小大马士革」，因为这里泉水众多、聚礼清真寺铺地齐整、溪水穿过市场；橄榄油和肥皂远销埃及、大马士革和汉志，角豆果酱甚至送到开罗。1444年，海岸与群山同属马穆鲁克苏丹：一处是半毁的收费码头，一处是繁荣的商城，城中还有一个不小的撒玛利亚人坊区。

1516年塞利姆一世征服后，纳布卢斯成为奥斯曼巴勒斯坦六个桑贾克之一的治所，雅法却几乎空无一人：1596年的税册上只有十五户，那几年路过的旅人说这里是一堆废墟。17世纪，朝圣客栈才慢慢恢复；18世纪海盗横行海路，商人索性住在拉姆拉，只在瞭望哨报来船讯时才冒险上岸。1657年，奥斯曼派来强化中央集权的远征军，结果反倒扶植起此后两百年割据山中的家族：尼姆尔、贾拉尔和图坎三大家族靠橄榄油、肥皂和黎凡特产量最大的棉花立足，纳布卢斯也因此在工商业上盖过耶路撒冷、雅法和阿卡。阿卡的扎希尔·奥马尔在1770年代两次围攻纳布卢斯，都没能攻下。1775年，他的埃及对手阿布·扎哈布围攻雅法四十九天，破城后处决成年男子；1799年3月7日，拿破仑攻破同一道城墙，纵兵洗城，把两千多名战俘押到海边枪决，瘟疫随后席卷废墟。穆罕默德·阿布·纳布特后来重建雅法，建起马哈茂迪耶清真寺和喷泉；1804年贾扎尔帕夏死后，图坎家族让纳布卢斯重新成为山中强权。

en:
Sayda, the ancient Phoenician city of Sidon, grew around two harbours on the Syrian coast, sheltered by a small island just offshore. Homer praised its glassware and its purple dye, crushed from murex shells, and a colonising party sailed from here to found Tyre. Baldwin I of Jerusalem and Sigurd of Norway took the town in 1110 and made it the seat of the Lordship of Sidon; Saladin captured it in 1187, the Ayyubids destroyed its stronghold in 1249, and the Mongols sacked it again a few years later. The Crusaders built the Sea Castle on the island, once the site of the temple of Melqart, and the Mamluks rebuilt it and joined it to the shore by a long causeway. Muslim rule was restored, but Sayda never regained its ancient size and long lay open to European sea raiders. In 1444 it was a modest fortified port living from its harbour, orchards and coastal traffic.

Sultan Selim I brought Sayda under Ottoman rule after Marj Dabiq in 1516, and it became the capital of the Sidon Eyalet. The port's revival came from Fakhr al-Din II, the Druze emir of the Ma'n dynasty appointed over Sidon-Beirut. His tie with Tuscany drove him into exile in Italy for several years, and after his return he routed the governor of Damascus at Anjar and built a domain that reached Tripoli and Latakia. He opened his ports to European merchants, set going the Mount Lebanon silk trade, restored the Sea Castle and raised palaces, caravanserais and bathhouses in Sayda; he surrendered to an imperial army in 1633 and was executed in Constantinople two years later. The separate Sidon province briefly formed during his exile was re-established in 1660, while the Ma'n and later the Shihab lords held the mountains behind the coast. Through much of the eighteenth century the Hammud family ran Sidon's customs and cotton exports and built its town palaces. Ahmad Pasha al-Jazzar moved the governor's seat to Acre in 1773, and in 1799 his garrison there withstood Napoleon's siege, leaving Sayda a busy local harbour rather than an imperial capital.
zh:
赛达就是古称西顿的腓尼基名城，在叙利亚海岸的两处港湾旁发展起来，岸边还有一座小岛。荷马称赞过这里的玻璃器，以及用骨螺榨出的泰尔紫染料；一支殖民船队还从这里出发，去建立推罗城。1110年，耶路撒冷国王鲍德温一世和挪威国王西居尔拿下此城，把它作为西顿领地的治所；1187年它落入萨拉丁之手，1249年阿尤布人摧毁要塞，没过几年蒙古人又洗劫了一遍。十字军在小岛上建起海上城堡，小岛本是腓尼基神美刻尔神庙的旧址，马穆鲁克人重建城堡，还修了一条长堤把岛与岸连起来。穆斯林统治虽然恢复，赛达却再没重现古时的规模，还长期暴露在欧洲海上袭击者面前。1444年时，它是一座不大的设防港口，靠港湾、果园和沿海航运为生。

1516年马尔吉·达比克战役后，塞利姆一世把赛达纳入奥斯曼版图，这里成为西顿埃亚莱特的首府。让港口重新兴旺的是马安家族的德鲁兹埃米尔法赫尔丁二世，他受封管辖西顿和贝鲁特，因与托斯卡纳结盟而流亡意大利数年；回来后，他在安贾尔打败大马士革总督，势力一直扩展到的黎波里和拉塔基亚。他向欧洲商人开放港口，开创了黎巴嫩山的丝绸贸易，重修海上城堡，还在赛达兴建宫殿、商栈和浴场；1633年他向帝国军队投降，两年后在君士坦丁堡被处死。他流亡期间曾短暂设立的西顿行省于1660年重建，马安家族及后来的希哈卜家族则一直控制着海岸背后的山地。18世纪大部分时间里，哈穆德家族把持西顿关税和棉花出口，在城里修造宫殿。1773年，艾哈迈德·贾扎尔帕夏把总督治所迁往阿卡；1799年他在阿卡的驻军顶住拿破仑的围攻，赛达则始终是个繁忙的地方港口，而不是帝国行省的都会。

en:
Abkhazia is the narrow Black Sea coast below the Caucasus, with Tskhumi, later Sukhumi, as its natural harbour. The Sharvashidze family, called Chachba in Abkhaz, governed the town for the Georgian crown, and Genoese merchants kept a consul there from 1354, sent out from Caffa; Armenian, Muslim and Jewish trading houses worked the port alongside them. Wine, wax, grain and slaves were shipped out and salt, cloth and luxuries brought in, and the Dadiani princes of Odishi, who held Tskhumi for long stretches, minted their coin there. In 1444 the coast was Orthodox and nominally Georgian, even as the unified kingdom's hold on the western mountains loosened.

The Sharvashidzes joined the western Georgian revolt that defeated George VIII near Chikhori in 1463, yet Abkhazia long remained under Odishi's overlordship and emerged as a separate principality only in the early seventeenth century. The Ottoman navy occupied Tskhumi in the 1570s, fortified the town as Suhum-Kale and blockaded the coast, while Islam spread only slowly among the highlanders; the princes fought the Dadiani by turns and pushed the border south to the Enguri. About 1700 Zegnak Sharvashidze divided the land among his sons, and Rostom held the family seat at Lykhny, with its tenth- or eleventh-century church of the Virgin and the princes' palace. Rebels besieged Suhum-Kale twice in the 1720s and briefly held it in 1771. Kelesh Bey, ruling from the 1780s, subdued the highland clans, built an army and fleet and made himself independent of Istanbul. When he was killed in May 1808 his elder son Aslan turned to the Ottomans, while his younger son Sefer Bey, baptized George and backed by his Mingrelian in-laws, claimed the throne as a Russian vassal. On 2 July 1810 Russian marines stormed Suhum-Kale and installed him as prince of an autonomous Abkhazia under the tsar.
zh:
阿布哈兹是高加索山脚下一条狭长的黑海海岸，天然港口茨胡米即后来的苏呼米。沙尔瓦什泽家族（阿布哈兹语称查奇巴）世代为格鲁吉亚王室镇守此城。1354年起，热那亚商人在港内派驻领事，领事从卡法派出，亚美尼亚、穆斯林和犹太商人的商行也在港中经营。酒类、蜂蜡、粮食和奴隶从这里装船外运，食盐、布匹与奢侈品则反向输入；曾长期据有茨胡米的奥季希达季阿尼王公还在这里铸币。1444年，这片海岸信奉东正教、名义上臣属格鲁吉亚，但统一王国对西部山地的控制已经松动。

沙尔瓦什泽家族参加西格鲁吉亚诸侯叛乱，1463年在奇科里附近击败格奥尔基八世；不过阿布哈兹长期接受奥季希宗主权，直到17世纪初才成为独立王公国。奥斯曼舰队在1570年代占领茨胡米，将其改筑为苏胡姆卡莱并封锁海岸，伊斯兰教在山民中却传播缓慢；王公们同达季阿尼家族时战时和，把南界推进到恩古里河。1700年前后，泽格纳克·沙尔瓦什泽把领地分给儿子们，罗斯托姆据守家族驻地利赫尼，那里有10至11世纪的圣母教堂和历代王公的宫殿。起义者1720年代两度围攻苏胡姆卡莱，1771年又短暂占领。克列什贝自1780年代执政，压服高地氏族，建立陆军和舰队，脱离伊斯坦布尔自立。他1808年5月遇刺后，长子阿斯兰倒向奥斯曼，幼子塞费尔贝受明格列里亚姻亲支持，受洗改名格奥尔基，以俄国封臣身份争位。1810年7月2日，俄国海军步兵突袭苏胡姆卡莱，立他为沙皇治下的自治阿布哈兹王公。

en:
Lauenburg guards the lower Elbe where the Stecknitz Canal branches off towards Lübeck. The Ascanians built the castle of Lowenborch here in 1181–1182, naming it from Lave, the Polabian word for the Elbe, and the settlement beneath it held city rights by 1260. When Saxony was partitioned in 1296 it became the capital of the small Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg, whose dukes long claimed the Saxon electoral vote until the Golden Bull of 1356 gave it to Saxe-Wittenberg. The Old Salt Road forded the Elbe a few kilometres upstream, and after the Stecknitz Canal opened in 1398 the salt barges from Lüneburg turned off the river at Lauenburg into the canal; tolls and river carrying made the town's living. A war with Hamburg and Lübeck ended badly, and the peace of 1420 cost the duchy Bergedorf and the Vierlande. In 1444 Lauenburg was the busy little capital of an Ascanian, Catholic river duchy.

The little duchy married high: on 29 October 1525 Christian III of Denmark married Duke Magnus I's daughter Dorothea at Lauenburg Castle, and her sister Catherine married Gustav I of Sweden in 1531. The Reformation followed these dynastic ties, and in 1585 Duke Francis II set up a Lutheran state church; a boatmen's guild founded in 1635 showed how busy the Elbe trade remained. The Thirty Years' War loaded the duchy with heavy contributions, and after the castle burned in 1616 the court moved to Ratzeburg in 1619, though Lauenburg stayed the duchy's chief town. When the Ascanian line died with Julius Francis in 1689, Hanover seized the inheritance, and the Hamburg settlement of 1693 confirmed it to the House of Hanover, whose heads wore the British crown from 1714. French troops occupied the duchy in 1803, and Napoleon annexed it to his Bouches-de-l'Elbe department in 1810. Coalition troops fought Marshal Davout's corps outside the town on 17–19 August 1813, and the peace settlement of 1815 gave Lauenburg to Denmark.
zh:
劳恩堡扼守易北河下游，施特克尼茨运河就在这里从易北河分出，通向吕贝克。1181至1182年，阿斯坎尼家族在此修筑勒文堡，名字取自波拉布语对易北河的称呼拉韦，堡下聚落在1260年已确有城市权。1296年萨克森分裂，这里成为小邦萨克森-劳恩堡公国的都城，公爵们长期自称拥有萨克森选侯票，直到1356年金玺诏书把它判给萨克森-维滕贝格。老盐路在城上游几公里处横渡易北河，1398年施特克尼茨运河通航后，吕讷堡的盐船在劳恩堡转入运河，关税和河运养起了这座城镇。对汉堡和吕贝克的战争以惨败收场，依1420年的和约，公国失去贝格多夫和四湖区。1444年的劳恩堡是阿斯坎尼家族治下一座信奉天主教、河运繁忙的小都城。

小公国靠联姻攀上高枝：1525年10月29日，丹麦的克里斯蒂安三世在劳恩堡城堡迎娶公爵马格努斯一世之女多萝西娅，她的妹妹卡塔里娜1531年嫁给瑞典国王古斯塔夫一世。宗教改革顺着这些王朝纽带进入，1585年公爵弗朗茨二世建立路德宗国家教会，1635年船工行会成立，可见易北河上的航运依旧繁忙。三十年战争的沉重摊派压垮了小公国，1616年城堡失火后宫廷于1619年迁往拉策堡，但劳恩堡仍是公国首邑。1689年尤利乌斯·弗朗茨去世，阿斯坎尼家族绝嗣，汉诺威出兵夺取遗产，1693年汉堡和议把它确认给汉诺威家族，其族长自1714年起同时身兼大不列颠国王。1803年法军占领公国，1810年拿破仑把它并入易北河口省；1813年8月17至19日，反法联军在城郊与达武元帅的部队交战，1815年的和议把劳恩堡划归丹麦。

en:
Stettin, the Polish Szczecin, commands the lower Oder where the river opens into the Baltic lagoon. It began as a West Slavic stronghold on the castle hill; Mieszko I of Poland took it in 967, and Bishop Otto of Bamberg converted its fishermen and merchants on missions in 1124 and 1128. The Griffin dukes then ruled Pomerania for more than five centuries. Barnim I granted the town Magdeburg rights in 1243, Otto I made it a ducal residence in 1309, and its Hanse merchants shipped Oder-basin grain, timber and herring to the west and brought salt and cloth back. In 1444 it was the seat of the young Joachim the Younger of Pomerania-Stettin, ruling in his own name since 1440; a trade law of 1443 ordered the duchy's goods to pass through Stettin, a staple that drew angry protests from rival Stargard.

Bogislaw X reunited Pomerania in 1478 and moved the ducal capital to Stettin in 1491; the town accepted Lutheranism in 1534, and in 1570 the peace congress held here ended the Northern Seven Years' War, while Duke John Frederick rebuilt the castle as a Renaissance residence. The town then became a fortress of the Baltic wars: the treaty of 1630 opened Pomerania to Swedish arms, the last Griffin, Bogislaw XIV, died in the castle in 1637, and from 1648 Stettin was the capital and strongest fortress of Swedish Pomerania. A Brandenburg-Danish-Luneburg army stormed it in 1677 and handed it back two years later; plague cut the population from about 6,000 in 1709 to 4,000 in 1711. Prussian troops occupied the fortress in 1713, and Frederick William I acquired it under the Peace of Stockholm in 1720, moving the Pomeranian administration from Stargard and settling Huguenot refugees in the town. Its most famous child belongs to these Prussian years: Sophie Auguste Friederike of Anhalt-Zerbst, the future Empress Catherine the Great of Russia, was born in a house on the cathedral street in 1729, the daughter of the fortress's Prussian governor. French forces took the fortress without a fight in 1806 and held it until November 1813; after 1815 Stettin became the capital of the Prussian Province of Pomerania.
zh:
斯德丁（波兰语称什切青）扼守奥得河下游，坐落在河水注入波罗的海潟湖的地方。它起于城堡山上的一座西斯拉夫人要塞；967年波兰的梅什科一世将其攻取，1124年和1128年，班贝格主教奥托两度到此，向渔民和商人传教。此后格里芬公爵家族统治波美拉尼亚五百余年。巴尔宁一世1243年授予城市马格德堡法，奥托一世1309年把这里定为公爵驻地；汉萨商人把奥得河流域的谷物、木材和鲱鱼运往西方，又运回食盐和布匹。1444年，这里是波美拉尼亚-斯德丁年轻公爵约阿希姆（小）的驻地，他1440年起亲政；1443年的贸易法规定公国货物须经斯德丁交易，这种专卖权招致对手斯塔加德的强烈抗议。

博古斯瓦夫十世1478年重新统一波美拉尼亚，1491年把公爵都城迁至斯德丁；城市1534年接受路德宗，1570年在此召开的和会结束了北方七年战争，约翰·腓特烈公爵则把城堡改建为文艺复兴式宫邸。这座城市随后成为波罗的海战争中的要塞：1630年的条约向瑞典军队敞开波美拉尼亚大门，末代格里芬公爵博古斯瓦夫十四世1637年死于城堡，1648年起斯德丁成为瑞典属波美拉尼亚的首都和最坚固的要塞。勃兰登堡、丹麦和吕讷堡联军1677年破城，两年后又将其归还；瘟疫使人口从1709年的约六千人降至1711年的四千人。普鲁士军队1713年占领要塞，腓特烈·威廉一世凭1720年《斯德哥尔摩和约》取得斯德丁，把波美拉尼亚行政机构从斯塔加德迁来，并在城中安置胡格诺难民。这座城最有名的孩子就出生在普鲁士年代：1729年，安哈尔特-采尔布斯特的索菲·奥古斯特·弗里德里克，也就是后来的俄国女皇叶卡捷琳娜大帝，出生在大教堂街的一座宅子里，她的父亲是这座要塞的普鲁士籍总督。1806年法军兵不血刃夺取要塞，统治至1813年11月；1815年后，斯德丁成为普鲁士波美拉尼亚省的首府。

en:
Chełmno Land, Kulmerland in German, is the lower-Vistula country around Toruń, called Thorn in German, the Teutonic Order's first foothold. Invited in 1226 by Duke Konrad I of Masovia to fight the pagan Prussians, the Knights chartered Toruń and Chełmno together on 28 December 1233; that charter became Kulm law, the model for hundreds of towns from Gdańsk to Königsberg. Toruń joined the Hanseatic League, shipped grain and timber down the Vistula and made gingerbread, with a town baker on record as early as 1380. Poland recovered the land after Grunwald in 1410 and lost it again by the First Peace of Thorn in 1411; in 1440 the burghers of Toruń and Chełmno formed the Prussian Confederation. In 1444 the Order ruled disaffected Polish- and German-speaking towns that refused its war taxes.

In 1454 the Confederation rose and Casimir IV incorporated Chełmno Land into Poland; Toruń's citizens dismantled the Order's castle almost brick by brick. The Second Peace of Thorn, signed in the town on 19 October 1466, ended the Thirteen Years' War and made the land Royal Prussia. Toruń became one of the Commonwealth's four largest cities, and its most famous son was born there on 19 February 1473: Nicolaus Copernicus. The town turned Protestant in 1557, the year its bakers struck a recipe pact with Nuremberg; in 1645 Władysław IV held the fruitless Colloquium Charitativum for Catholics, Lutherans and Calvinists.

Swedes held Toruń from late 1655 until a siege in 1658 returned it to John II Casimir. The Great Northern War brought Charles XII's bombardment, plague and the Treaty of Thorn of 1709 between Peter the Great and Augustus II. On 16 July 1724 the Tumult of Thorn ended with the beheading of the Protestant mayor Johann Gottfried Rösner. In the First Partition of 1772 Chełmno and the countryside went to Prussia while Toruń stayed Polish until the Prussians entered on 24 January 1793. The Treaty of Tilsit gave it to the Duchy of Warsaw in 1807, and it served briefly as the duchy's capital in 1809; the Congress of Vienna returned it to Prussia in 1815 and the great fortress of Thorn went up from 1817.
zh:
海乌姆诺地（德语称库尔默兰）地处维斯瓦河下游，以托伦（德语称托恩）为首府，是条顿骑士团在维斯瓦河这一岸最早的立足点。1226年，马佐夫舍公爵康拉德一世为征讨信奉异教的普鲁士人请来骑士团；1233年12月28日，骑士团同时为托伦与海乌姆诺颁发建城特许状，状中确立的「库尔姆法」后来成为从格但斯克到柯尼斯堡数百座城镇的范本。托伦加入汉萨同盟，沿维斯瓦河外运谷物和木材，又以姜饼闻名，1380年的记载里已有本地姜饼师傅。1410年格伦瓦德战役后此地复归波兰，1411年《第一次托伦和约》又把它交还骑士团；1440年，托伦与海乌姆诺的市民组成普鲁士联盟。1444年，这些城镇仍在骑士团名下，但城中说波兰语和德语的天主教徒已公开拒缴骑士团的战税。

1454年普鲁士联盟举事，卡齐米日四世将海乌姆诺地并入波兰，托伦市民把骑士团城堡拆得几乎一砖不剩。十三年战争以1466年10月19日在此签订的《第二次托伦和约》告终，此地成为波兰王冠治下的皇家普鲁士。托伦跻身联邦四大城市，1473年2月19日，城里最有名的人物尼古拉·哥白尼出生于此。城市1557年改宗新教，同年托伦的姜饼师傅与以姜饼闻名的纽伦堡定下互通配方之约；1645年，瓦迪斯瓦夫四世在此召开「爱心座谈会」，让天主教徒、路德宗和加尔文宗当面辩论，这场著名的辩论最终没有结果。

大洪水时代，瑞典军队于1655年底攻占托伦，1658年夏的围城战之后，城市才回到扬二世·卡齐米日手中。大北方战争又带来卡尔十二世的炮轰、瘟疫，以及1709年彼得大帝与奥古斯特二世在此签订的《托伦条约》。1724年7月16日的「托伦骚乱」以新教市长约翰·戈特弗里德·勒斯纳被斩首收场。1772年第一次瓜分时，海乌姆诺和乡村并入普鲁士，托伦却留在波兰，成为被包围的飞地，直到1793年1月24日普军入城。1807年《提尔西特条约》把它划给华沙公国，1809年还一度成为公国首都；1815年维也纳会议将其交还普鲁士，宏大的托伦要塞自1817年起动工。

en:
Norfolk is the East Anglian wool country behind the North Sea coast, with Norwich on the River Wensum and Great Yarmouth as its outport. The Normans cleared ninety-eight houses for Norwich Castle soon after the Conquest, and Bishop Herbert de Losinga began the cathedral in 1096, bringing limestone from Caen by river and a specially cut canal. Walls raised between 1280 and 1340 enclosed more ground than the City of London. Wool paid for the city's churches, friaries and merchants' houses: Norfolk sheep-walks supplied the trade, worsted took its name from Worstead village, and Great Yarmouth, a staple port from 1353, shipped cloth to continental buyers. A Hanseatic warehouse stood in Norwich. In 1444 the city was among the largest and richest in England, the main market for the East Anglian cloth trade.

Robert Kett turned a local protest against enclosure into Norfolk's largest rising in 1549. About 16,000 rebels camped on Mousehold Heath, took Norwich on 29 July and defeated the Marquess of Northampton's force before the Earl of Warwick destroyed them at Dussindale on 27 August; Kett was hanged from the castle walls on 7 December. From 1567 Flemish and Walloon Protestant weavers called the Strangers settled in the city, at times making up about a third of its people. They brought newer draperies and Norwich's first printing press. The city supported Parliament in the Civil War, but a Royalist riot in 1648 ended in the Great Blow, when the Committee House powder magazine exploded. Worsteds prospered after the Restoration, Norwich shawls became fashionable from the 1780s, and in the 1790s William Pitt called Norwich 'the Jacobin city' for its radical Dissenters.
zh:
诺福克是北海海岸后方的东盎格利亚羊毛之乡，诺里奇位于温瑟姆河畔，大雅茅斯则是它的外港。诺曼征服后不久，征服者为修建诺里奇城堡拆除了九十八所房屋；1096年，赫伯特·德·洛辛加主教动工兴建大教堂，从卡昂运来的石灰岩经河道和专门开凿的运河抵达工地。1280至1340年修筑的城墙圈起比伦敦城还大的地面。羊毛支付了教堂、修道院和商人宅邸的建造费用：诺福克牧场为织布业提供原料，精纺毛料得名于沃斯特德村，1353年成为大宗货物港的大雅茅斯把布匹运往欧洲大陆买家手中，诺里奇城里还设有汉萨商人的仓库。1444年，诺里奇是英格兰最大、最富庶的城市之一，也是东盎格利亚布匹贸易的主要市场。

1549年，罗伯特·凯特把一场反对圈地的地方抗议发展成诺福克规模最大的起义。约一万六千名起义者在茅斯霍尔德荒野扎营，7月29日占领诺里奇，击败北安普敦侯爵的军队，最后在8月27日于达辛代尔被沃里克伯爵击溃；凯特于12月7日被吊死在城堡城墙上。1567年起，被称为「异乡人」的佛兰德和瓦隆新教织工到城里定居，有时约占全城人口的三分之一。他们带来新式毛织技术和诺里奇第一台印刷机。内战中诺里奇支持议会，但1648年一场王党骚乱酿成「大爆炸」，委员会大厦的火药库被引爆。王政复辟后精纺呢绒销路兴旺，1780年代起诺里奇披肩成为时尚；1790年代，由于城中激进的不从国教者，威廉·皮特把诺里奇称为「雅各宾之城」。

en:
Derby sits at a crossing of the Derwent below the Pennine foothills, the market town of a shire rich in iron, lead and wool. The Romans kept the fort and settlement of Derventio here to supply the Peak District lead workings and to work iron and make pottery; the Vikings made Djúra-bý one of the Five Boroughs of the Danelaw; and in July 917 Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, stormed the burh and brought the district back to English Mercia.
