Yanbu al-Bahr, the harbour a few days' ride from Medina, was the nearest landing place for the holy city, where Egyptian grain, pilgrims and trade goods came ashore before going inland. When the Mamluks built up Jeddah as the main port of the Hejaz, Yanbu kept only the Medina traffic and became a quiet secondary roadstead. In 1444 the oasis and its port belonged to the Sharifate of Medina, inside the Mamluk-backed order of the Hejaz.

Ottoman sovereignty followed in 1517 and changed little; pilgrims and supply caravans kept using the harbour. Its one turn as an army base came in the Ottoman-Wahhabi war. In 1811 Tusun Pasha, the teenage son of Muhammad Ali of Egypt, seized Yanbu as the bridgehead for his march on Medina, but Abdullah bin Saud caught his column in the Wadi al-Safra and routed it in January 1812; the survivors fell back to their ships. Reinforced from Egypt, Tusun used Yanbu again for the counterstroke that retook Medina later in 1812, and the harbour supplied his army by sea until the Saudi capital Diriyah fell in 1818. In 1821 Yanbu was held by Muhammad Ali's Egyptian administration.
zh:
延布意为「泉水」，得名于平坦红海海岸背后的淡水井。早期阿拉伯地理书中的延布，通常指延布枣园：干河谷里的一片枣椰绿洲，在古莱什人前往叙利亚的商队路上；埃及朝觐队伍从亚喀巴南下麦加，也经过这片聚落。延布港离麦地那只有几天路程，是圣城最近的登陆地，埃及粮食、朝觐者和商货在此上岸，再转往内陆。马穆鲁克王朝把吉达经营成汉志首要港口后，延布只剩下通往麦地那的生意，成了冷清的次级锚地。1444年，绿洲和港口属于麦地那谢里夫国，处在马穆鲁克支持的汉志秩序之中。

1517年奥斯曼接管汉志，这里没有多少变化，朝觐者和补给商队照旧使用港口。延布唯一一次充当大军基地，是在奥斯曼—瓦哈比战争中。1811年，埃及穆罕默德·阿里十几岁的儿子图松帕夏夺取延布，作为进军麦地那的桥头堡；阿卜杜拉·本·沙特在萨夫拉谷截住他的队伍，1812年1月将其击溃，残部退回船上。得到埃及增援后，图松再以延布为基地反攻，同年晚些时候夺回麦地那；直到沙特都城德里耶耶1818年陷落，这座港口一直从海上供应他的军队。1821年，延布归穆罕默德·阿里的埃及政权管辖。

en:
Ma'din Sulaym, the Mine of the Banu Sulaym, lies on the desert road southeast of Medina toward Najd, and Arabs later called the place Mahd al-Dhahab, the golden cradle. Gold was washed here before Islam, and the Banu Sulaym were still working the deposits in the Prophet's lifetime. Under the Umayyads their gold went to the mints Caliph Abd al-Malik opened for the first Islamic dinars, and Abbasid records claim about forty tons of it between 750 and 1258. The district also carried the Darb Zubayda, the pilgrim road from Kufa to Mecca, whose wells, cisterns and stations were endowed by Zubayda, granddaughter of Caliph al-Mansur and wife of Harun al-Rashid; travellers crossing the lava plain and its wadis watered there for centuries. Sulaym clans that stayed in Arabia were absorbed from the ninth century by the incoming Banu Harb. By 1444 the mines had long been quiet, and the wells and pastures mattered as the tribal hinterland of the Sharifate of Medina.

Ottoman sovereignty reached the district with the rest of the Hejaz in 1517, and nobody reopened the old workings. The armies of the Wahhabi war then passed over it: Diriyah's men entered the Hejaz in 1803 and took Medina in 1805, Tusun Pasha retook the city in 1812, and Ibrahim Pasha's march on Najd ended with the fall of Diriyah in 1818. In 1821 the old mining district lay within the Egyptian-Ottoman frontier posts run from Medina.
zh:
曼丁苏莱姆意为「苏莱姆之子的矿」，在麦地那东南、通往内志的沙漠道路上，阿拉伯人后来称这里为马赫德宰海卜，意思是黄金的摇篮。伊斯兰教以前已有人在此淘金，先知穆罕默德在世时，苏莱姆部落仍在开采矿脉。倭马亚时代，这里的黄金运进哈里发阿卜杜勒·马利克为铸造最早的伊斯兰第纳尔开设的造币厂；阿拔斯史料记载，750年至1258年间共产金约四十吨。境内还有祖拜达道经过，那是库法通往麦加的朝觐大路，沿途水井、蓄水池和驿站都由曼苏尔哈里发的孙女、哈伦·拉希德的妻子祖拜达捐建，几个世纪里穿越熔岩原和干河谷的旅人都在此取水。留在阿拉伯的苏莱姆支派，从9世纪起逐渐被迁来的哈尔卜部落吸收。到1444年，金矿早已停工，水井和牧场只是麦地那谢里夫国的部落腹地。

1517年，这一地区随汉志并入奥斯曼版图，古矿坑再没有人重新开采。瓦哈比战争的军队随后从这里往来：德里耶耶的人马1803年进入汉志，1805年拿下麦地那；图松帕夏1812年夺回该城，易卜拉欣帕夏进军内志，1818年德里耶耶陷落。1821年，这片古矿区处在麦地那派出的埃及—奥斯曼戍所一线之内。

en:
Jeddah is the port of Mecca on the Red Sea shore, a day's travel from the Holy City. It began as a fishing hamlet, and in 647 the Caliph Uthman made it Mecca's harbour in place of the older al-Shu'ayba; thereafter most pilgrims who came to the Hajj by sea landed on its beach, and Indian merchants brought spices and textiles to its customs house. Local tradition held that Eve, the mother of mankind, was buried here, and the city's name was explained from the Arabic jaddah, 'grandmother'. The Mamluks of Egypt cut Jeddah's duties to draw the Indian trade away from Aden, and Ibn Battuta found a thriving town when he passed through around 1330; the al-Shafi'i Mosque, whose minaret went up in the thirteenth century, was already the oldest mosque in town. In 1444 the city and the coastal plain around it were held, under loose Mamluk suzerainty, by Barakat ibn Hasan, the Hashemite Sharif of Mecca, whose income rested largely on Jeddah's customs and the pilgrim fleets.

After Vasco da Gama reached the Indian Ocean the Portuguese carried the war into the Red Sea, and the Mamluk sultan Qansuh al-Ghawri ordered his amir Husain al-Kurdi to ring Jeddah with a wall and shore batteries, a work Arab sources date to 1509. It served the town in April 1517, when Selman Reis's gunners drove off the armada of Lopo Soares de Albergaria. Later that year the Ottoman conquest of Egypt made Jeddah an Ottoman port, and in 1525 the Turks rebuilt the walls with six towers and six gates; Sharif Barakat II of Mecca submitted to the sultan in the same year. A second Portuguese assault was beaten back in 1541. As the Cape route and Dutch and English ships drew the Indian trade elsewhere, Jeddah lived increasingly on the Hajj alone. In 1802 the Wahhabi forces of the First Saudi State seized Mecca and Jeddah, but in January 1813 the city opened its gates without a fight to Muhammad Ali Pasha's Egyptians under his kinsman Mustafa Bey; Muhammad Ali landed there in September and made Jeddah his base for reconquering Arabia.
zh:
吉达是红海岸边的麦加外港，距圣城只有一天路程。它本是一处渔村，647年哈里发奥斯曼把它定为麦加的港口，取代更古老的舒艾巴港；此后由海路前来朝觐的香客多在吉达登岸，印度商人也把香料和布匹运进这里的海关。当地相传人类之母夏娃就葬在城中，城名也被解释为阿拉伯语里「祖母」一词。埃及的马穆鲁克人降低吉达关税，把印度贸易从亚丁吸引过来；伊本·白图泰约在1330年路过时，见到的已是一座繁荣城镇，城里最古老的沙斐仪清真寺，其宣礼塔在13世纪便已建起。1444年，吉达及周围沿海平原处在松散的马穆鲁克宗主权之下，由麦加的哈希姆系谢里夫巴拉卡特·伊本·哈桑统治，他的收入主要靠吉达的关税和朝觐船队。

瓦斯科·达·伽马驶入印度洋后，葡萄牙人把战火烧进红海，马穆鲁克苏丹坎苏·戈里命埃米尔侯赛因·库尔迪为吉达环筑城墙和海岸炮台，阿拉伯史料把这项工程系于1509年。1517年4月，城墙派上用场：塞尔曼·雷斯的炮火击退了洛波·苏亚雷斯·德·阿尔贝加里亚的舰队。同年晚些时候奥斯曼征服埃及，吉达成为奥斯曼港口，1525年土耳其人重修城墙，设六塔六门，麦加谢里夫巴拉卡特二世也在同年向苏丹称臣。1541年，葡萄牙人的第二次进攻再被击退。随着好望角航路和荷兰、英国商船把印度贸易引走，吉达越来越只靠朝觐维持。1802年，第一沙特国的瓦哈比军队攻占麦加和吉达；1813年1月，吉达不战开城，向穆罕默德·阿里帕夏的姻亲穆斯塔法贝伊所率埃及军队投降，穆罕默德·阿里本人9月登陆，把吉达作为重新征服阿拉伯的基地。

en:
Turbah is a palm-watered oasis in the wadi of the same name, one of Arabia's longest valleys, which runs down from the Sarat highlands past Jebel Hadhn, the mountain between Hejaz and Najd, to the edge of the Najd desert. Medieval Arab geographers counted it among the districts of Mecca, and its people are the Buqum, a tribe that had held the wadi since before Islam. Springs and a stream running all year fed gardens and date groves along the banks, and local accounts put the palms at around 300,000; the unwalled farms were famed for feasting passing travellers at harvest. In 1444 the valley lies within the loose lordship of the Sharif of Mecca, backed by Mamluk power, and supplies the highland road between Mecca and the interior with dates and livestock.

In 1797 the Buqum swore allegiance to Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad, the Saudi imam of Diriyah, and Turbah became a strongpoint on the Wahhabi flank facing the Hejaz. Its defence in the Ottoman-Wahhabi war made the name of Ghaliya, widow of Hamd ibn Abdallah, the Saudi amir of Turbah, who armed her household, rallied the tribesmen and was acknowledged by the garrison as their amira. When Muhammad Ali Pasha of Egypt campaigned for the Ottomans, his son Tusun Pasha stormed the oasis in 1813 and was beaten back with heavy loss; bedouin raiders struck at Tusun's supply trains, and the Egyptian soldiers blamed the rout on Ghaliya's sorcery, for rumour said she could make her men invisible. In 1814 a second assault led by Tusun and Abidin Bey collapsed after eight days of fighting. After the Saudi defeat at Busal in 1815 a peace settlement ceded the Hejaz, and Ghaliya withdrew to Diriyah, where by the local account she died when the Egyptian army stormed the Saudi capital in 1818.
zh:
图赖拜是同名干河谷中的椰枣绿洲。图赖拜干河是阿拉伯半岛最长的河谷之一，自塞拉特高地蜿蜒而下，经汉志与内志的界山哈杜恩山麓，延伸至内志沙漠边缘。中世纪的阿拉伯地理学家把它算作麦加的属地之一，居民是伊斯兰教兴起前便定居此谷的巴古姆部落。泉眼和常年不涸的河水滋养着两岸田园与椰枣林，当地记载称椰枣树约有三十万株；不设围墙的农庄还以收获季款待过路旅客闻名。1444年的图赖拜处于麦加谢里夫松散的统治之下，背后是马穆鲁克的权势，沿麦加通往内陆的山路供应椰枣和牲畜。

1797年，巴古姆人向德拉伊耶的沙特伊玛目阿卜杜勒·阿齐兹·伊本·穆罕默德宣誓效忠，图赖拜成为瓦哈比派面向汉志一侧的要塞。让这里名传一时的是女子加利亚：她是图赖拜沙特埃米尔哈姆德·伊本·阿卜杜拉的遗孀，在奥斯曼与沙特的战争中武装家中人丁、鼓动族人上阵，被守军奉为女埃米尔。埃及的穆罕默德·阿里帕夏奉素丹之命讨伐沙特人时，其子图松帕夏1813年猛攻绿洲，损兵折将而退；贝都因袭扰者又打击图松的补给线，埃及士兵便把惨败推到加利亚的妖术上，传言她能让自己的人马隐身。1814年，图松与阿比丁·贝伊再度来攻，连打八天仍告溃败。1815年沙特人在拜苏勒战败后签订和约、放弃汉志；加利亚随后撤往德拉伊耶，按当地记载，1818年埃军攻破这座沙特首都时她死在城中。

en:
Zufra is the empty western reach of the Gulf coast, the shore later known as Al Dhafra, running from the Qatar borderlands towards Liwa. Its small anchorage of Sila looks over fishing beaches, with grazing around scattered wells inland between the sea and the dunes. Arab geographers called the whole coast from Basra towards Oman the Khatt Abd al-Qays, after the tribe whose camps reached this far west. In 1444 Hormuz commanded the shipping lanes offshore, while the mainland felt the weight of the Jabrid rulers of al-Hasa, who had taken Qatif in 1439. Fish, camels, date caravans and well-water counted for more here than any walled town.

The coast's overlords changed within a few years. In 1521 the Jabrid sultan Miqrin ibn Zamil was killed in Bahrain trying to throw back a Portuguese landing, and in 1526 Rashid ibn Mughamis al-Shabib, sheikh of the Muntafiq in Iraq, seized al-Hasa and the dynasty collapsed. In the centuries after, Manasir Bedouin moved between Qatar, Buraimi, Liwa and this shore, breeding camels, leading camel trains, working date plots and diving for pearls in summer. When the Bani Yas settled Liwa about 1700 and built up Abu Dhabi in the 1790s, Sila became the far, thinly peopled western edge of their orbit; in January 1820 Abu Dhabi's acceptance of the General Maritime Treaty with Britain drew these beaches and wells into the new coastal order.
zh:
萨夫拉是海湾沿岸空旷的西陲，即后来所称的达法拉海岸，从卡塔尔边境地带延伸向利瓦。小停泊点锡拉面向渔村滩涂，往内陆去，沙丘间散布着水井，井周有牧场。阿拉伯地理学家把从巴士拉伸向阿曼的整条海岸称作「阿卜杜勒·盖斯之线」，名字来自营地远及这片西陲的阿卜杜勒·盖斯部。1444年，外海航路归霍尔木兹掌控，大陆上则承受哈萨的贾布里德统治者的压力，他们已于1439年夺取盖提夫。在这里，鱼获、骆驼、椰枣商队和井水比任何设防城池都要紧。

海岸的宗主没几年就换了。1521年，贾布里德苏丹米克林·本·扎米勒在巴林抵御葡萄牙人登陆时战死；1526年，伊拉克蒙塔菲格部的谢赫拉希德·本·穆加米斯·谢比卜夺取哈萨，王朝灭亡。此后几个世纪，马纳西尔贝都因人在卡塔尔、布赖米、利瓦和这片海岸之间转场，养骆驼、赶驼队、种椰枣地，夏天出海采珠。巴尼·亚斯人约1700年定居利瓦、1790年代建起阿布扎比后，锡拉成为其势力范围最西端人烟稀少的边地；1820年1月阿布扎比接受与英国的《总航海条约》，这些滩涂和水井也被纳入新的海岸秩序。

en:
Dawasir is the long oasis valley of Wadi ad-Dawasir in southern Najd, called al-Aqiq by older Arab geographers. Watercourses running down from the western highlands feed its wells and palm groves before the wadi loses itself in the sands east of as-Sulayyil. The Dawasir tribe made the valley its home seat: the Al Zayed and Taghlib branches both herded camels and worked the palm gardens, and the number of its wells and fighting men kept outside rulers at a distance. In 1444 this Sunni Bedouin country was run by its own shaykhs, beyond the firm reach of any court in the Najdi towns.

A tribe this strong had to be courted rather than commanded. In 1785 Rabi ibn Zayd al-Mukharim al-Dawasir and his brother Badan travelled to Diriyah and pledged obedience to Abdulaziz ibn Muhammad, then returned with money and arms to gather fighting men around the new alliance; Rabi's palace in the oasis later housed the local Saudi garrison. Wadi ad-Dawasir became one of the southern pillars of the First Saudi State and stayed tied to Diriyah until 1818, when Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian army captured and destroyed the Saudi capital and Saudi power collapsed across Najd. The wells and palm groves then went back to the shaykhs and the tribe.
zh:
代瓦西尔的核心是内志南部狭长的绿洲干河瓦迪达瓦西，阿拉伯古籍称之为阿吉格。西部高地流下的径流补给井水和椰枣林，干河最终消失在塞利勒以东的沙海里。代瓦西尔部落把这条河谷当作根本之地：阿勒·扎伊德与塔格莱卜两大支既牧放骆驼，也耕作椰枣园；水井之众、战士之多，使外来统治者难以涉足。1444年时，这片逊尼派贝都因土地由自己的谢赫治理，内志各城镇的宫廷都够不到这里。

对这样强的部落，只能争取，不能号令。1785年，代瓦西尔人拉比·本·扎伊德·穆哈里姆与兄弟巴丹前往德拉伊耶，向阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹·本·穆罕默德宣誓归顺，又带着钱帛和武器返回，在这层新盟约下集结战士；拉比在绿洲中的宫殿后来驻扎了沙特的当地守军。瓦迪达瓦西成为第一沙特国南方的支柱之一，与德拉伊耶的联系一直维持到1818年，易卜拉欣帕夏的埃及军队在这一年攻陷并摧毁沙特都城，沙特势力在内志全面瓦解，水井和椰枣林重归谢赫和部族之手。

en:
Aflaj is a string of oasis villages spread across the southern Tuwaiq upland, about 300 kilometres southeast of Riyadh, with Layla the largest of them. The villages live from the falaj, channels that carry spring water out to palm groves, grain fields and grazing; at al-Kharaz a single natural spring feeds a web of small linked canals. Dawasir clans held the oasis as one of their southern seats in Najd, shifting their herds between the settled strip and the desert around it. In 1444 dates, grain and livestock supported a small population whose mud forts answered to local elders rather than to any court in the Najdi towns.

Arab tradition makes this the country of Layla and Majnun. The town of Layla bears the name of Layla of the Banu Amir, cousin and beloved of Qays ibn al-Mulawwah, the seventh-century poet whom his people called Majnun, the possessed, after her father married her to another; Jabal Toubad above the oasis is linked with the pair. Nizami of Ganja turned the tale into a Persian narrative poem in 1188, and the versions of Jami in 1484 and Fuzuli in 1535 carried it through the Persian- and Turkish-speaking lands, while the oasis itself kept to its springs, palms and herds.
zh:
阿夫拉季是散布在图韦克山地南段的一连串绿洲村落，在利雅得东南约300公里，莱拉是其中最大的一处。各村落依靠坎儿井和明渠引出泉水，浇灌椰枣林、粮田和牧场；海拉兹渠系便由一条天然泉水分出彼此相连的小渠。代瓦西尔各部把这片绿洲当作内志南部的根基之一，赶着畜群在定居地带与周围沙漠之间转场。1444年时，椰枣、谷物和牲畜养活着不多的人口，土筑堡垒听命于本地长老，内志各城镇的宫廷都管不到这里。

相传这里就是莱拉与玛吉努故事的故乡。莱拉镇得名于阿米尔部落的莱拉：她是7世纪诗人凯斯·伊本·穆劳瓦的表妹和心上人，她的父亲把她另嫁他人后，族人便称凯斯为「玛吉努」，意为被精灵附了体的痴人；绿洲旁的图拜德山也与这对情侣联系在一起。1188年，甘贾的尼扎米把这段故事写成波斯语叙事诗，1484年贾米、1535年富祖里又各有同名之作，把它带到波斯语和突厥语世界；而这片绿洲依旧守着泉水、椰枣和畜群。

en:
Buraydah stands on the eastern rim of the Wadi al-Rummah, the long watercourse that crosses the Qasim highlands of northern Najd. Its wells watered some of the best grazing in the peninsula, used in 1444 by the Anazzah Bedouin. Nearby Unayzah was already a watering place on the Darb Zubaydah, the pilgrim road from Kufa to Mecca laid out under Harun al-Rashid. No town yet stood here, only a well called Buraydah where camel and sheep herds drank and caravans put in between the Shammar pastures and the markets of Najd and the Hijaz.

Najdi tradition has the town begin with a purchase. In 1577 Rashid ibn Abdullah al-Duraybi, chief of the Al Abu Alian clan of the Banu Tamim, bought the Buraydah well from its Anazzah owners and built around it the seat of his family's emirs, soon the chief town of Qasim and rival to Unayzah. A wall went up against Bedouin raids, then a second under Hujaylan ibn Hamd, the emir who brought Buraydah under the First Saudi State and ruled all Qasim but Unayzah. Two armies came against the walls in the 1780s, Saadun ibn Arar of the Banu Khalid in 1782 and Thuwaini al-Saadun of the Muntafiq in 1786, and both broke off their sieges. In the Ottoman-Wahhabi war the town could not hold out. After Abdullah ibn Saud's attack on the Egyptian vanguard failed at Mawiyah in May 1817, Ibrahim Pasha took Rass that October following a three-and-a-half-month siege, Unayzah surrendered, and Buraydah submitted. Its leading men went off as hostages with the army that marched south to destroy Diriyah in 1818, and an Egyptian garrison stayed behind in Qasim.
zh:
布赖代坐落在鲁迈干河东缘，这条长河谷横亘内志北部的卡西姆高地。这里的井泉滋养着阿拉伯半岛最好的几处牧场，1444年的主人是安宰部落的贝都因人。附近的欧奈宰已是祖拜黛大道上的饮水点，这条从库法通往麦加的朝觐路铺筑于哈伦·拉希德时代。此时此地还没有城镇，只有一口名叫布赖代的水井供驼羊饮水，商队往返于舍迈尔牧场与内志、汉志的市集之间时在此歇脚。

据内志志书的传承，这座城始于一笔买卖。1577年，贝尼塔米姆部落阿布·阿里扬氏族的首领拉希德·本·阿卜杜拉·德里比从安宰人手中买下布赖代井，在井边建起本家族埃米尔的驻地，这里很快成为卡西姆首镇，与欧奈宰争雄。城镇先筑一道墙抵御贝都因袭掠，侯吉兰·本·哈姆德任埃米尔时又修了第二道；他率布赖代归附第一沙特国，统辖除欧奈宰外的整个卡西姆。1780年代，两支大军先后兵临城下：1782年贝尼哈立德的萨阿敦·本·阿拉尔、1786年蒙塔菲格的苏韦尼·萨阿敦都没能破城。奥斯曼－瓦哈卜战争中，布赖代未能幸免。1817年5月，阿卜杜拉·本·沙特在穆维叶截击埃及前锋失败，易卜拉欣帕夏围攻拉斯三个半月后于10月破城，欧奈宰投降，布赖代也归顺。城中头面人物被作为人质随军押走，那支军队在1818年南下毁灭了德拉伊耶，卡西姆则留下了埃及驻军。

en: Hafar is a line of desert wells in the broad, usually dry bed of Wadi al-Batin, the lower course of Wadi al-Rummah. After rain, its pastures are among the best in this part of northern Arabia, although the channel can fill with dangerous speed. During Caliph Uthman's reign, Abu Musa al-Asha'ari dug wells here after pilgrims complained about the dry road from Iraq to Mecca; the place became known as Hafar Abu Musa and served pilgrims leaving Basra. In 1444 Shammar, Anaza and neighboring Bedouin clans watered camels, sheep and goats there, while caravans followed the wadi track. No walled town stood at Hafar. Its value lay in wells, grazing and a reliable stopping place for groups crossing the desert.
zh: 哈费尔是巴廷干河宽阔而多半干涸的河床上的一串沙漠水井，巴廷干河也是鲁迈干河的下游河段。雨后，这一带的牧场属于阿拉伯北部最好的牧区之一，但干河河道也可能迅速涨水。哈里发奥斯曼在位时，朝觐者抱怨伊拉克通往麦加的道路缺水，阿布·穆萨·阿沙里于是在此开凿水井；这里被称为「阿布·穆萨之井」，供从巴士拉出发的朝觐者使用。1444年，舍迈尔、阿奈扎及邻近贝都因部族在此给骆驼、绵羊和山羊饮水，商队也沿干河道路前行。哈费尔没有城墙环绕的城镇，它的重要性全在水井、牧场和穿越沙漠者可以依靠的停脚处。

en:
Yabrin is a watered hollow at the northern rim of the Rub' al Khali, about 210 kilometres south of Riyadh, the last oasis on the road out of Najd towards Oman. Its wells and date palms made it a caravan crossing of long standing, and travellers counted it the southernmost habitable ground before the sands of the Empty Quarter. The old walled town was already counted a ruin in the early modern centuries, its wells kept open for passing herdsmen and caravans. In 1444 camel nomads from the southern desert watered their herds here, and no town-based ruler claimed the oasis.

The nomads who used those wells were the Al Murrah, camel breeders who ranged between eastern Arabia and the edges of the Empty Quarter, and they handed the expanding Saudis one of their rare checks. In 1776 Abdulaziz ibn Muhammad of Diriyah raided south against them, and at Mukhayriq al-Safa the Murrah drove his men into a narrow defile and killed about sixty, among them Abdullah ibn Hasan, emir of Qasim, and Hudhul ibn Nasir Al Saud. Diriyah kept pressing south anyway, and as al-Hasa and Qatar came under its influence the Yabrin wells passed into the First Saudi State's loose tribal sphere. That lasted until 1818, when Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptians destroyed Diriyah and the oasis returned to Murrah hands.
zh:
耶卜林是鲁卜哈利沙漠北缘一片有水的洼地，在利雅得以南约210公里，是内志通往阿曼的道路上最后一片绿洲。水井和椰枣林使它久为商队中转之地，旅人把它看作进入空白之地沙海前最靠南的可居之处。古城在近代几个世纪里已被视为废墟，只有水井仍为过路的牧民和商队保留。1444年，南方沙漠的骆驼游牧人在此饮畜，没有哪个以城镇为根基的统治者领有这片绿洲。

用这些水井的是穆拉部落，他们牧放骆驼，游牧于阿拉伯东部与空白之地边缘之间，也曾让扩张中的沙特人少见地受挫。1776年，德拉伊耶的阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹·本·穆罕默德南征穆拉人，在穆海里格·萨法被穆拉人逼入狭窄隘口，折兵约六十人，死者中包括盖西姆埃米尔阿卜杜拉·本·哈桑和赫祖勒·本·纳赛尔·阿勒沙特。德拉伊耶并未止步，随着哈萨和卡塔尔先后落入其势力范围，耶卜林的水井也归入第一沙特国松散的部族势力圈。这一局面维持到1818年，易卜拉欣帕夏的埃及军队摧毁德拉伊耶，绿洲重归穆拉人之手。

en:
Grane, the old al-Qurayn, is a sheltered bay at the head of the Persian Gulf, where the wells of Kazima watered caravans and pilgrims travelling from Iraq into Arabia. It was at Kazima in April 633 that Khalid ibn al-Walid, in the first battle the caliph's army fought outside Arabia, routed the Sasanian army under Hormozd, remembered as the Battle of the Chains; and Kazima was the birthplace of the poet al-Farazdaq, one of the great satirical voices of the Umayyad age, whose verses later critics said preserved a third of the Arabic language. The port afterwards served the merchants of the Bahrayn coast before fading into tribal rule under the distant sway of Hormuz. Early in the fifteenth century the Banu Jabr made themselves masters of the whole western shore of the Gulf, and in 1444 the fishing and pearling hamlets of Grane lay on the northern edge of their amirate of al-Hasa.

Visitors to al-Qurayn in the following centuries found a bare fishing village, too stony for palms or grain, fed by wheat shipped from Basra. The Portuguese took the coast with Hormuz in 1507, and Ottoman governors and the Muntafiq chiefs of Basra disputed it after them, until the Bani Khalid drove the Turkish garrisons out of eastern Arabia about 1670. In 1716 the Utub clans, the Al Sabah, Al Khalifa and Al Jalahimah, settled the bay with Bani Khalid leave and divided its rule among their sheikhs, and in 1752 Sabah I ibn Jaber became the first independent sheikh of Kuwait. The Persian siege of Basra from 1775 to 1779 sent its merchants fleeing here with the India and Aleppo trade, and Kuwait grew into the busiest boatbuilding port on the Gulf, its ships known across the Indian Ocean; the East India Company moved its Gulf shipping there in 1792.
zh:
格雷恩古称古拉因，是波斯湾顶端一处避风海湾，岸边卡济马的水井曾供从伊拉克进入阿拉伯的商队和朝觐者歇脚。633年4月，哈立德·伊本·瓦利德正是在卡济马击溃霍尔木兹率领的萨珊军队，那是哈里发军队在阿拉伯之外打的第一仗，史称链条之战；卡济马还是诗人法拉兹达格的出生地，他是倭马亚时代最伟大的讽刺诗人之一，后世评家说，若无他的诗，阿拉伯语将失去三分之一的词汇。这个港口后来为巴林沿岸的商人效劳，随后湮没于部落自治，只在名义上远奉霍尔木兹。15世纪初，巴努·贾布尔成为整个海湾西岸的主人，1444年，格雷恩这些捕鱼采珠的村落正处在他们哈萨埃米尔国的北缘。

此后几百年，旅人见到的古拉因是个不毛的渔村，地上多石，长不出椰枣和粮食，每日靠从巴士拉海运小麦糊口。1507年，葡萄牙人随征服霍尔木兹一并拿下这段海岸；之后奥斯曼总督与巴士拉的蒙塔菲克首领反复争夺，直到约1670年巴尼·哈立德部落把土耳其驻军逐出阿拉伯东部。1716年，乌图布人的萨巴赫、哈利法、贾拉希马三族经巴尼·哈立德准许在海湾定居，三分其政；1752年，萨巴赫一世·伊本·贾比尔成为科威特第一位独立的谢赫。1775至1779年波斯围攻巴士拉，商人带着通往印度和阿勒颇的贸易逃来此地，科威特也成为海湾最繁忙的造船港，所造船只闻名整个印度洋；1792年，东印度公司也把海湾航运转到这里。

en:
Masirah is a long, narrow, arid island in the Arabian Sea, sixty miles from north to south and only eight or nine wide, separated from the Omani coast by a shallow channel. Its interior is empty desert and its villages cluster in the north. Copper was mined here around 1500 BC, when the land of Magan traded across the Gulf, and shards of Indus pottery have been found at the workings. The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, written in the first century, calls it the Isle of Sarapis: three villages of fish-eating holy men who spoke Arabic, wore loincloths of palm leaves and sold fine tortoiseshell to passing merchants. Medieval dhows watered at its wells, and the geographer Yaqut al-Hamawi knew it as 'a great island in the sea of Oman, with several villages'. Its people were fishermen, boatbuilders and weavers, Ibadi Omanis sailing within the loose maritime empire of Hormuz; in 1444 the island answered to Hormuz and lived from its boats and looms.

Portuguese warships occupied Masirah in the 1500s. In 1650, when the Ya'rubi imams drove the Portuguese from Muscat, the island returned to Omani allegiance, but power stayed with its own sheikhs and headmen: their sailors built their own craft, fished the surrounding banks and sold dried fish and woven cloth on the Sharqiyah mainland. Few wars or courts disturbed it under the Busaid sultans, and Masirah remained a remote, self-sufficient island under the loose rule of Muscat.
zh:
马西拉是阿拉伯海中一座狭长干旱的岛屿，南北长约六十英里，宽仅八九英里，与阿曼本土隔着一道浅海海峡。岛的内陆是空旷的沙漠，村庄多集中在北部。约公元前1500年，岛上已有铜矿开采，当时马干的商船往来于海湾之上，矿址还出土过印度河流域的陶片。成书于1世纪的《厄立特里亚海航行记》称这里为「萨拉皮斯岛」：岛上有三个村落，住着以鱼为食的圣者，他们说阿拉伯语，腰系棕榈叶，向来往的商人出售优质玳瑁。中世纪的帆船常到岛上的水井补给淡水，地理学家雅古特·哈马维称它是「阿曼海中一座大岛，岛上有数个村庄」。岛民是渔民、造船匠和织工，这些伊巴德派的阿曼人往来于霍尔木兹松散的海洋势力范围内；1444年，马西拉名义上臣服霍尔木兹，生计全靠自家的渔船和织机。

16世纪，葡萄牙舰队占领马西拉。1650年，叶阿里卜王朝的伊玛目把葡萄牙人逐出马斯喀特，马西拉随之重归阿曼，但实权仍在岛上的谢赫和头人手中：岛民自造船只，在周围渔场捕鱼，把鱼干和布匹销往东部地区本土。在赛义德王朝治下，少有战事和权贵打扰这座岛屿，马西拉始终是马斯喀特松散统治下一座偏远、自给自足的海岛。

en: Wusta is the empty middle of Oman's southern shore, where the stony plain of Jiddat al-Harasis runs back from the sea into waterless desert. Off the coast lie the five Khuriya Muriya islands, the Isles of Zenobios to the Greek sailors of the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea. Sheltered coves at Hasik and Sadah collected frankincense from the Qara country in antiquity, and the ruins of an old town stand beside Hasik's harbor. In 1444 this was remote Mahri ground, visited by little besides incense dhows and fishing boats. In May 1503 a storm caught the first Portuguese patrol in the Indian Ocean off these islands: two ships left behind by Vasco da Gama to prey on Red Sea trade were torn from their moorings and driven onto the rocks of Al-Hallaniyah, and their commander Vicente Sodré, da Gama's uncle, drowned on his carrack Esmeralda.
zh: 中部省是阿曼南岸中段一片空旷的海岸，哈拉西斯砾石平原从海边一直伸向没有水源的内陆沙漠。海岸外的五座哈拉尼亚特群岛，成书于1世纪的《厄立特里亚海航行记》已经记载。古代，哈西克和塞代赫两处有天然遮蔽的港湾集散盖拉山地的乳香，哈西克港边留有古城废墟。1444年，这里是迈赫拉人偏远的土地，除了运乳香的帆船和渔船，少有来客。1503年5月，一场风暴在群岛外海袭击了葡萄牙人在印度洋的第一支巡逻舰队：瓦斯科·达·伽马留下袭扰红海贸易的两艘船被扯离锚地、推上哈拉尼亚岛的礁石，指挥官、达·伽马的舅父维森特·索德雷随他的克拉克帆船「埃斯梅拉达号」一同溺亡。

en:
The province covers the middle of Wadi Hadhramaut, a long valley cut through an arid plateau, whose spate floods and wells sustain palm gardens and mud-brick towns. Bedouin of the surrounding jol graze camels and goats on the plateau, and caravan roads climb from the incense ports of Shihr and Mukalla to the valley markets. Three towns lie a short ride apart. Shibam, twelve kilometres west of Say'un, is enclosed by a wall and packed with about five hundred mud-brick towers five to eleven storeys high, raised against Bedouin raiders, and the present town dates from its rebuilding in 1533. Sayun lies midway of the wadi, and Tarim, thirty-five kilometres east, is its seat of religious learning, crowded with sayyid families and scholars. The Al Kathir, a Bedouin clan turned dynasty, founded their sultanate in 1379, and in 1414 their sultan Ali bin Omar, backed by the scholars of the Hadhramaut, conquered Dhofar. In 1444 his state ran from the wadi to the Arabian Sea, and was fighting the Mahra for Shihr while the walled towns harvested dates and grain.

The Kathiri took Shihr from the Tahirids in 1462 and kept it after 1495, when Sultan Jafar bin 'Amr backed the winning Zwedi faction in the Mahri civil war. In 1501 Badr Abu Tuwairq made Sayun his capital, and under his long rule the sultanate stretched from Ain Bamabd in the west to the approaches of Dhofar in the east. In 1545 his kinsmen took Qishn with Ottoman guns, but a Portuguese fleet bombarded the town and returned it to the Mahra. Portuguese raids burned several coastal ports, while the wadi itself kept its mosques, scholars and date gardens. In the eighteenth century Yafa'i tribes from the southwestern highlands overran the valley towns, and by 1821 the Kathiri sultan held little beyond his palaces at Sayun, while rival Yafa'i houses held Shibam and the coast.
zh:
本省占据哈德拉毛干谷中段：干旱高原上裂开一条长谷，季节性洪水和井水滋养着谷中的椰枣园与土坯城镇。周围高原的贝都因人放牧骆驼和山羊，商队从希赫尔、穆卡拉等乳香港口翻山进入谷地集市。谷中三大城相距不远：赛云以西十二公里的希巴姆城墙环绕，城内挤着约五百座五至十一层高的土坯塔楼，为抵御贝都因袭扰而建，现存城建自1533年的重建；赛云地处干谷中段；东行三十五公里的塔里姆是谷地的宗教学术中心，聚居着大批圣裔家族和学者。卡西部落本是贝都因部族，1379年建立苏丹国；1414年，苏丹阿里·本·奥马尔在哈德拉毛学者支持下征服佐法尔。1444年，其国家从干谷延伸到阿拉伯海，正为争夺希赫尔与迈赫拉人交战，谷中诸城则凭城墙守护椰枣和谷物的收成。

卡西里人1462年从塔希尔王朝手中夺取希赫尔；1495年，苏丹贾法尔·本·阿慕尔在迈赫拉内战中支持获胜的兹韦迪一派，此后长期占有该港。1501年，巴德尔·艾布·图韦里格定都赛云，在他长期统治下，苏丹国疆域西起艾因巴曼卜德、东抵佐法尔边地。1545年，他的族人借奥斯曼火炮攻占基什恩，但葡萄牙舰队随即炮轰该城，把它交还迈赫拉人。葡萄牙人的袭扰焚毁了几座沿海港口，干谷里的清真寺、学者和椰枣园却安然无恙。18世纪，来自西南高原的亚法伊部落席卷谷地诸城；到1821年，卡西里苏丹的号令已不出赛云的宫殿，希巴姆与海岸都掌握在敌对的亚法伊家族手中。

en: Marib was the capital of Saba, wealthiest of the old South Arabian kingdoms, which many scholars identify with the Sheba of the Bible. Across Wadi Adhanah its kings raised the Great Dam from the eighth century BC, watering the palm groves and fields around the temples of the moon god Almaqah at Awwam and Barran while caravans carried frankincense and myrrh north into the desert. In 25 BC a Roman army under Aelius Gallus reached the city and failed to take it. Breaches scattered the oasis farmers across the centuries; the last, left unrepaired after the dam was overtopped in the 570s, is remembered in the Quran as the Flood of Arim, after which tens of thousands moved north and Marib became a small town amid its own ruins. In 1444 its people lived from date gardens and flocks under tribes loosely tied to the Zaydi imams of Sanaa, and Ottoman rule never reached the arid east; under the Qasimid imam al-Mutawakkil Isma'il (1644-1676) its pastoral clans were counted among the tribes of the imamate.
zh: 马里卜是古代南阿拉伯诸王国中最富庶的塞巴王国之都，不少学者认为塞巴就是《圣经》中的示巴。公元前8世纪起，塞巴诸王在宰奈河上筑起大马里卜水坝，灌溉月神阿穆格的阿瓦姆、巴兰两座神庙周围的椰枣园与农田，商队则载着乳香、没药向北深入沙漠。公元前25年，埃利乌斯·加卢斯率罗马军队兵临城下，却未能破城。此后数百年间水坝多次溃决，绿洲农户一次次流散；最后一次在570年代漫坝后再未修复，《古兰经》称之为「阿里姆洪水」，数万人口随后北迁，马里卜沦为栖身废墟之间的小镇。1444年，居民以椰枣园和畜群为生，所属部落松散地依附于萨那的扎伊迪派伊玛目，奥斯曼人的统治始终没有深入干旱的东部；卡西姆王朝的穆塔瓦基勒·伊斯玛仪（1644—1676年在位）时，这里的游牧部落被算作伊玛目治下的部众。

en:
Beihan, also called Bayhan al-Qasab, is the market town of Wadi Bayhan, whose seasonal floods water fields along the desert edge. In antiquity this was Qataban, one of the six kingdoms of ancient South Arabia: its kings bore the title mukarrib and ruled from Timna, where camel caravans carrying frankincense stopped on the road from Shabwa to Gaza and Petra. Strabo and Pliny both recorded the Qatabanians, whom they called the Gebbanitae, and the kingdom ended in the late first century when Hadhramaut and Himyar divided its lands. By the fifteenth century the wadi was livestock country on the inland fringe of Rasulid Yemen, run by its own tribes, among them the Fuqara, Masabin and Banu Harith. In 1444 the Rasulid sultans at Zabid and Taiz were weakened by plague and succession wars and had little hold over Beihan.

The Rasulid realm passed to the Tahirid clan in 1454. Around 1500, in the reign of Sultan Amir ibn Abd al-Wahhab, a Jewish messianic movement arose near Bayhan and organized its followers into a fighting force before the sultan's troops crushed it. Ottoman armies reached inland Yemen after 1538, but Imam al-Mansur al-Qasim raised the Qasimid revolt in 1597, and tribal forces drove the Ottomans out of Yemen by 1638. As the imamate broke apart in the following century, the tribes of Wadi Bayhan ran their own affairs.
zh:
拜汉又称拜汉·盖萨卜，是拜汉干谷的集镇，季节性洪水浇灌着沙漠边缘的田地。古时这里是卡塔班，古代南阿拉伯六国之一：国王称「穆卡里布」，定都提姆纳；运送乳香的驼队从沙布瓦前往加沙和佩特拉，途中在提姆纳歇脚。斯特拉波和老普林尼都记载过卡塔班人，称之为格巴尼特人；王国在1世纪末灭亡，土地被哈德拉毛和希木叶尔瓜分。到15世纪，干谷已成拉苏勒也门内陆边缘的畜牧之地，由富卡拉、马斯阿宾、拜尼·哈里斯等本地部落自行治理。1444年，驻在扎比德和塔伊兹的拉苏勒苏丹们饱受瘟疫和继承战争削弱，对拜汉已鞭长莫及。

1454年，拉苏勒疆域转入塔希尔家族之手。约1500年，在苏丹阿米尔·伊本·阿卜杜勒·瓦哈卜统治期间，拜汉附近兴起一场犹太弥赛亚运动，追随者被编成武装，最终遭到苏丹军队镇压。1538年后奥斯曼军队深入也门内陆，但伊玛目曼苏尔·卡西姆于1597年发动卡西姆派起事，部落武装到1638年把奥斯曼人逐出也门。此后一个世纪伊玛目国家分裂，拜汉干谷诸部自行其是。

en:
Jazan is the Red Sea anchorage of the historical al-Mikhlaf al-Sulaymani, the coastal plain and hill country between the Hijaz and Yemen, with the Farasan Islands some forty-five kilometres out to sea. The Quraysh of Mecca knew the coastal road, using it on their journeys to Yemen and Abyssinia, and caravans linked the anchorage with Abu Arish inland, once called Darb al-Naja, a pilgrim station and former capital of the Mikhlaf. The town stands on a bed of rock salt, and salt dug from the hill behind it and fish from the shallows of the wadi mouth were the place's trade. In 1444 the Sulaymani sharifs still ruled its villages and forts, and Bandar Jizan served chiefly as the modest sea outlet of Wadi Jizan.

Ottoman power reached the coast after Hadım Suleiman Pasha stormed Aden in 1538 and took Zabid in 1539, and Jazan became the port of the Abu Arish sanjak on the new Yemeni frontier. During the 1620s and 1630s the Qasimid imams drove the Ottoman garrisons out of Yemen, and the weight of affairs shifted back to Abu Arish. In 1728-29 the descendants of Sharif Khayrat bin Shubayr set up a state of their own there; under the Al Khayrat rulers Jizan remained a small fishing anchorage guarded by coastal forts.
zh:
贾赞是历史上苏莱曼米赫莱夫在红海上的泊口，这片地区地处汉志与也门之间，兼有沿海平原和山地，法尔桑群岛就在外海约四十五公里处。麦加的古莱什人走熟了这条沿海道路，往返也门和阿比西尼亚都取道于此；商队把泊地与内陆的阿布阿里什连在一起，那里旧称德尔卜·纳贾，曾是朝圣驿站和米赫莱夫的都城。城镇坐落在岩盐层上，背后山中采出的食盐和河口浅滩捕来的鱼货是当地的贸易物产。1444年，苏莱曼系谢里夫仍统治着这里的村落与堡寨，贾赞港主要只是贾赞干谷规模不大的出海口。

1538年哈迪姆·苏莱曼帕夏攻陷亚丁、1539年夺取扎比德后，奥斯曼势力抵达这段海岸，贾赞成为新征服的也门边地上阿布阿里什桑贾克的港口。1620至1630年代，卡西姆伊玛目把奥斯曼守军逐出也门，事务的重心重新转回阿布阿里什。1728—1729年，谢里夫·海拉特·本·舒拜尔的后裔在那里建立了自己的政权；在海拉特家族统治者治下，贾赞仍是一座由海岸堡寨护卫的小型渔业泊口。

en:
Al-Ahsa is the great oasis of eastern Arabia, lying some forty miles inland from the Persian Gulf, where more than thirty fresh-water springs feed a wide ring of date gardens in the desert. The cities of Hofuf and al-Mubarraz stand there, on the ground of old Hajar. In 899 the Qarmatians, a millenarian Ismaili sect, seized the oasis and made it their capital. Abu Tahir al-Jannabi led his followers out from it against Mecca in 930, threw the dead into the Zamzam well and carried the Black Stone back to Hajar; the Abbasid caliphs ransomed it only in 951. When the Persian traveller Nasir Khusraw visited in 1051, he found a city where some 30,000 Ethiopian slaves worked the fruit estates, the people paid no taxes and trade ran on lead tokens. After the Qarmatians fell, the Uyunids, Usfurids and Jarwanids ruled in turn, until the Bedouin Banu Jabr stormed the oasis in 1417. In 1444 their Jabrids ruled al-Hasa and Qatif from Hofuf, their power stretching from the Iraqi border toward Oman, and their riders guarded the pilgrim road from Iraq to Mecca.

The last decades of the house turned on Bahrain. Muqrin ibn Zamil, who held al-Hasa, Qatif and the islands, fell fighting the Portuguese there in 1521, and five years later Rashid ibn Mughamis of the Muntafiq marched in from Basra and ended the dynasty. In 1550 the people of the oasis, preferring the Ottomans of Süleyman I to a Portuguese landing, accepted an imperial garrison. The new province of Lahsa built the Qasr Ibrahim in Hofuf from 1555, a fortress enclosing a domed mosque, a prison and a bathhouse; in 1559 its governor Mustafa Pasha sailed from it to besiege Bahrain and failed. Ottoman rule never ran deep among the palm groves. The Bani Khalid rose against the garrisons, and in 1670 they expelled the last Turks and made al-Mubarraz their capital. The Wahhabi army of Diriyah took the oasis in 1795, and in 1818 the Egyptian forces of Muhammad Ali, sent against the Saudis, retook it and restored the Bani Khalid under Ottoman overlordship.
zh:
哈萨绿洲是阿拉伯东部最大的绿洲，在波斯湾以南约六十公里的内陆，三十多处清泉在沙漠中滋养出大片椰枣园，胡富夫和穆巴拉斯两座城就坐落在古城哈贾尔的故地。899年，信奉救世思想的伊斯玛仪支派卡尔马特派夺取绿洲，在此定都。930年，卡尔马特派从这里奔袭麦加，把死者投入渗渗泉，并将天房黑石劫回哈贾尔；阿拔斯王朝的哈里发直到951年才付赎金将其迎回。波斯旅行家纳赛尔·霍斯鲁1051年到访时，看到城里的果园由约三万名埃塞俄比亚奴隶耕作，居民不纳赋税，买卖用铅铸的代币。卡尔马特政权灭亡后，乌尤尼、欧斯福尔、贾尔万三个王朝相继统治，1417年贝都因巴努·贾布尔部攻陷绿洲。1444年，贾布里德政权以胡富夫为都城，领有哈萨和盖提夫，势力从伊拉克边境伸展到阿曼一带，其骑兵还护卫着从伊拉克前往麦加的朝觐道路。

这个王朝最后几十年的命运系于巴林。领有哈萨、盖提夫和巴林诸岛的穆克林·伊本·扎米勒1521年在巴林与葡萄牙人作战时阵亡；五年后，蒙塔菲克部落的拉希德·伊本·穆加米斯从巴士拉进军绿洲，终结了贾布里德王朝。1550年，绿洲居民宁可接受苏莱曼一世的奥斯曼驻军，也不愿葡萄牙人登陆；新设的拉赫萨省1555年起在胡富夫修筑易卜拉欣宫，这是一座围有穹顶清真寺、监狱和浴室的要塞。1559年，省长穆斯塔法帕夏从这里出师围攻巴林，兵败而归。奥斯曼的统治在椰枣园间始终不深，巴尼·哈立德部起兵反抗，1670年逐出最后一批土耳其人，以穆巴拉斯为都城。1795年，德拉伊耶的瓦哈比军队夺取绿洲；1818年，穆罕默德·阿里派来讨伐沙特的埃及军队将其攻占，在奥斯曼宗主权下恢复了巴尼·哈立德的统治。

en:
Chios lies only a few miles from the Anatolian shore, and its most profitable ground is the dry south, where the mastic villages tend lentisk trees. Farmers cut the bark and collected the scented resin that Genoese warehouses shipped across the Mediterranean. A Greek Orthodox majority worked the fields, vineyards and port, while Latin merchants held the castle and accounts. In 1346 Simone Vignoso's fleet took Chios for the Maona of Chios and Phocaea, a Genoese tax-and-trade company later controlled by the Giustiniani; the surrender left Greek landowners their property and worship, but the company kept the mastic, alum, salt and pitch monopolies. From 1415 it also paid tribute to the Ottoman sultan. In 1444 Chios was a company island under the Genoese flag: a thin Latin ruling class lived by the harbour and fortress, and Greek merchants, sailors and villagers supplied the cargoes.

Christopher Columbus knew the port before his Atlantic voyages, spending time on Chios on Genoese maritime business in the 1470s. The Maona's rule ended in April 1566, when Piyale Pasha brought an Ottoman fleet across the narrow water and the island surrendered. Genoese residents were carried to Constantinople, and some returned only through French mediation. Ottoman governors left much of local administration and tax farming to the Greek elite, kept a small garrison, and reserved the southern villages' mastic for the palace, which made the small island unusually valuable. In July 1770 the channel off Çeşme became the Battle of Çeşme, where the Russian fleet of Orlov and Spiridov trapped and burned the Ottoman ships anchored opposite Chios. When the Greek revolt began in 1821, the leading Chian merchants held back, unwilling to risk the protected mastic trade.
zh:
希俄斯距安纳托利亚海岸只有几海里，岛上最来钱的地方是干燥的南部，乳香村在那里照料乳香黄连木。农人割开树皮，收集带香气的树脂，再由热那亚仓库装船运往地中海各地。信奉东正教的希腊人多数耕作田地、葡萄园和港口，拉丁商人则掌握城堡和账目。1346年，西蒙·维尼奥索率舰队为热那亚的税收贸易公司「希俄斯与福西亚马奥纳」夺取希俄斯，该公司后来由朱斯蒂尼亚尼家族控制；降约保留了希腊地主的财产和信仰，但乳香、明矾、盐和沥青的专卖权归公司所有。从1415年起，公司还要向奥斯曼苏丹纳贡。1444年的希俄斯是热那亚旗帜下的公司岛：少数拉丁统治者住在港口和要塞旁，希腊商人、水手和村民则提供船上的货物。

克里斯托弗·哥伦布在远航大西洋前就熟悉这个港口，1470年代曾因热那亚海上事务在希俄斯停留。1566年4月，皮亚利帕夏率奥斯曼舰队越过窄海，希俄斯投降，马奥纳的统治结束。热那亚居民被掳往君士坦丁堡，其中一些人后来靠法国调停才返回。奥斯曼总督把大量地方行政和包税事务留给希腊精英，只设少量驻军，并把南部村庄的乳香划为宫廷专用货，这座小岛因此格外值钱。1770年7月，切什梅外海爆发切什梅海战，奥尔洛夫和斯皮里多夫的俄国舰队把停泊在希俄斯对岸的奥斯曼战船围堵焚毁。1821年希腊起事时，希俄斯的大商人选择观望，不愿拿受保护的乳香贸易冒险。

en:
Kizil-Su, the 'Red Water', was the Turkmen name for the sandy, fish-rich shore and anchorage at the head of the Balkan Gulf, near the lower Uzboy. In high-water years of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries that branch of the Amu Darya carried the waters of Sarykamysh into the Caspian. Salor Turkmens had camped along its channel since the twelfth century, and Yomut clans reached the gulf in the fourteenth; they fished the shallows, grazed sheep and camels around the wells, and carried goods between the desert and the Caspian by boat and caravan. In 1444 this was Sunni Turkmen country, touched only loosely by Timurid power from the Oxus cities.

Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks took Khwarazm in 1505, and after Ilbars drove out the Persian garrison in 1511 the shore became a remote march of the khanate of Khiva. As the Oxus turned back toward the Aral, the Uzboy failed around 1600, and its riverside fields and fishing stations shrank to wells and seasonal camps; the Yomut lived increasingly off their herds, Caspian fishing and raiding. In 1716 Peter the Great's officer Alexander Bekovich-Cherkassky landed at the anchorage, rendered its name into Russian as Krasnye Vody, raised a fort and sent two envoys to Khiva who never returned. Peter believed the dry Oxus bed nearby led to gold-bearing sands, and in 1717 Bekovich marched up it to Khiva, where the khan persuaded him to quarter his army in five towns and the Khivans destroyed the separated detachments; Bekovich was killed and the coastal forts were abandoned. Nadir Shah broke Khiva in 1740, but after his murder in 1747 the coast slipped back under uncertain Khivan overlordship. In 1821 Yomut fishing camps and camel herds still held Kizil-Su, answerable more to their own clans than to a distant khan.
zh:
克孜勒苏意为「红水」，是土库曼人对巴尔干湾湾顶一带多沙而盛产鱼的海岸与锚地的称呼，邻近乌兹博伊下游。14、15世纪的丰水年，乌浒水的这条支脉把萨雷卡梅什的水送入里海。萨洛尔土库曼人自12世纪起沿河道牧居，约穆特部在14世纪进入巴尔干湾沿岸；他们在浅滩捕鱼，沿井泉放牧绵羊和骆驼，以小舟和商队在沙漠与里海之间转运货物。1444年，这里是逊尼派土库曼人的土地，乌浒水诸城的帖木儿势力只能松散地抵达海滨。

1505年，穆罕默德·昔班尼的乌兹别克人攻取花剌子模；1511年伊尔巴思逐出波斯驻军后，这片海岸成为希瓦汗国遥远的边地。乌浒水干流转回咸海方向后，乌兹博伊约在1600年断流，河畔农田和渔站缩成井泉与季节性牧帐，约穆特人越来越依靠牧畜、里海渔捞和劫掠为生。1716年，彼得大帝的军官亚历山大·别科维奇-切尔卡斯基在这处锚地登陆，按俄语把地名译作「红水」（克拉斯诺耶沃德），筑起堡垒，又派两名使者前往希瓦，二人一去不返。彼得相信附近的乌浒水故道通向含金的沙地；1717年别科维奇沿故道进军希瓦，汗王劝他把军队分驻五城，希瓦人随即将分散的分队歼灭，别科维奇被杀，海岸诸堡也放弃了。1740年纳迪尔沙攻服希瓦，但他1747年遇刺后，海岸又回到希瓦并不牢靠的宗主权下。1821年，守着克孜勒苏的仍是约穆特人的渔帐和驼群，他们更多听命于本族，而不是远方的汗。

en:
Konjikala's old site lies in the Ahal oases, a narrow strip watered by Kopet Dag streams between the mountains and the Karakum. The caravan road from Merv toward Nisa and the Caspian followed these springs. East along the same line stood walled Abivard, one of the frontier settlements Iranian rulers used against raiders from Inner Asia. Konjikala itself was a wine-growing village in the first or second century BC. An earthquake levelled it in the first century BC, but it was rebuilt and lived by caravan traffic until the Mongols destroyed it in the thirteenth century. In 1444 this was a thinly held Timurid march. Turkmen tribes pastured flocks below the peaks, caravans watered at the oasis springs, and Konjikala survived only as a village among its own ruins.

The Safavid period kept this as a border held by tribal soldiery. After Shah Ismail died in 1524, Uzbek raids emptied Abivard. Shah Abbas later retook the frontier and planted 4,500 Afshar families on abandoned land. Nader Shah, who regarded the Abivard country as his home ground, returned from his Khiva campaign in 1740 with 4,000 freed Persian captives and settled them in Khivehabad fort near the old town. After his murder in 1747, Turkmen raids turned Abivard into ruins and carried the oases beyond Iranian control. A Khiva chronicle first mentioned the village of Askhabad beside the ancient ruins in 1811. The Qajar court still claimed the strip, but its camel-herding Turkmen auls managed their own affairs, and Konjikala remained a village.
zh:
科奇喀拉的旧址位于阿哈尔绿洲。科佩特山的溪流在山脉与卡拉库姆沙漠之间灌出一条狭长绿带，从木鹿通向尼萨和里海的商路便沿这些泉水延伸。绿带东端矗立着带城墙的阿比沃尔德，它是伊朗统治者用以抵挡内亚袭掠者的边防据点之一。科奇喀拉本身在公元前1至2世纪是种植葡萄的村落。公元前1世纪的一场地震将它夷平，但村落得到重建，靠商路维持，直到13世纪被蒙古人摧毁。1444年时，这里是帖木儿势力控制薄弱的边陲。土库曼部落在山下放牧，商队在绿洲泉边补水，科奇喀拉只剩废墟间一个村庄。

萨法维时期，这里仍是由部落兵驻守的边境。1524年伊斯玛仪沙阿死后，乌兹别克人的袭掠使阿比沃尔德人口流散。阿巴斯沙阿后来收复边地，把四千五百户阿夫沙尔人安置在荒废的土地上。纳迪尔沙阿把阿比沃尔德一带视为故土，1740年征伐希瓦后带回四千名获释的波斯俘虏，安置在旧城附近的希瓦阿巴德堡。1747年他遇刺后，土库曼人的袭掠使阿比沃尔德化为废墟，绿洲也脱离伊朗控制。1811年，一部希瓦编年史首次提到古城遗址旁的阿什哈巴德村。恺加宫廷仍声称拥有这条山麓地带，但放牧骆驼的土库曼村落自行其是，科奇喀拉始终只是一个村庄。

en:
The Shekty are one of the six Alimuly clans of the Alshyn, the great tribe of the Kazakh Junior Jüz. Their herds of horses, sheep and camels grazed the open steppe between the Mugodzhar hills and the Turgay river. Where most Kazakh clans covered 50 to 100 kilometres on their yearly round, the Shekty might cover 1,000 to 2,500, from the summer grass in the north to the winter reed-beds of the Aral shore and the lower Syr Darya, where they sold livestock at the caravan cities around Turkestan. Other herdsmen had a saying for their numbers: 'Which are more, the Shekty or the locusts?' In 1444 this country was the eastern flank of the Nogai Horde, the Manghit confederation that had broken away from Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek khanate, and its Kipchak-speaking people were Sunni Muslims ruled from movable camps.

After Abu'l-Khayr died, the Kazakhs of the sultans Kerei and Janibek took over the steppe, and their pressure later drove the Nogais across the Volga. In 1577 Haqnazar Khan seized Saraychik, the Nogais' river capital and their only real city. When the Dzungars overran the pastures in the Great Disaster of 1723, the Shekty became the chief support of Abulkhair, khan of the Junior Jüz, who swore allegiance to the Russian crown in 1731. Baraq Sultan beheaded him in 1748 over that submission; the Shekty rejected the Russian-backed Nuraly and proclaimed Batyr Kayaipuly their khan, splitting the Junior Jüz. They rode with Srym Datov against the Orenburg frontier in 1783–1797, and in 1806, together with the Tortkara, they stormed the Khivan town of Kungrad.
zh:
舍克图是哈萨克小玉兹阿尔申大部落阿利姆乌鲁六支之一，马群、羊群和骆驼牧在穆戈贾雷山与图尔盖河之间的开阔草原上。别的部落一年转场不过50到100公里，舍克图人能走1000至2500公里：夏天在北方草场，冬天赶到咸海沿岸和锡尔河下游的芦苇荡，在突厥斯坦一带的商队城市出售牲畜。别的牧人形容其人多，有句谚语：「舍克图多，还是蝗虫多？」1444年，这里是诺盖汗国的东境，这个曼格特联盟刚从阿布勒海尔的乌兹别克汗国分立；居民是说钦察语的逊尼派穆斯林，在移动的营地中受治。

阿布勒海尔死后，克列与贾尼别克两位苏丹的哈萨克人接管了草原，后来其兵锋把诺盖人赶过伏尔加河。1577年，哈克纳扎尔汗夺取诺盖人的河畔都城、也是他们唯一像样的城市萨莱奇克。1723年准噶尔入侵，即「大灾难」之年，牧场尽遭蹂躏，舍克图成为小玉兹汗阿布勒海尔的主要支柱；他于1731年向俄国宣誓臣服。1748年，巴拉克苏丹以此为由将他斩首，舍克图人拒绝俄国扶持的努拉里，拥立巴蒂尔·卡伊普为汗，小玉兹就此分裂。1783至1797年，他们随斯雷姆·达托夫攻打奥伦堡防线；1806年又与托卡拉部联手攻克希瓦治下的昆格勒城。

en:
Alty-Kuduk, the 'six wells', opens onto the north-eastern corner of the Aral Sea around Great Saryshyganak Bay. Reed beds at the lower Syr Darya meet the Aral Karakum, giving clans both shallow fishing water and desert-edge pasture for sheep and horses. No walled town guarded the shore; families moved between wells, fisheries and a caravan track that followed the Syr Darya up from Khwarazm. In 1444 the grazing circuit belonged to Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek Khanate, the nomadic power that had united the steppe clans in 1428.

After Abu'l-Khayr died in 1468 his khanate broke apart and the pastures passed to the Kazakhs, whose western clans became known as the Junior Jüz. Dzungar raids shattered the shoreline camps during the 'Great Disaster' of 1723, and in 1731 the Junior Jüz swore allegiance to the Russian crown while seeking help against further attacks. The Dzungar war of 1739-1741 again crossed these wells. In 1821 Kazakh nomads still fished the bay and moved their flocks between the same wells, with Russian suzerainty over the Junior Júz acknowledged on the northern steppe.
zh:
阿尔蒂库杜克意为「六口井」，位于咸海东北的大萨雷什加纳克湾畔。锡尔河下游的芦苇荡连接咸海卡拉库姆沙漠，使部族既能在浅水海湾捕鱼，也能在漠缘牧场放牧羊马。岸边没有城墙守护的城镇；牧民辗转于水井、渔场和一条从花剌子模沿锡尔河而上的商路之间。1444年，这条转场路线属于阿布海尔的乌兹别克汗国；他在1428年统一了草原诸部。

阿布海尔于1468年死后，汗国分裂，这些牧场转入哈萨克人手中，西部诸部后来被称为小玉兹。1723年准噶尔人的「大灾难」突袭打散沿岸牧帐；1731年，小玉兹为寻求援助以抵御后续进攻，向俄国沙皇宣誓效忠。1739—1741年的准噶尔战争又一次波及这些水井。1821年，哈萨克牧民仍在海湾捕鱼，并赶着牲畜往来于同样的井泉之间，北部草原上的小玉兹已处于俄国宗主权之下。

en:
The Tortkara are one of the six Alimuly clans of the Alshyn in the Kazakh Junior Jüz, divided among the four lineages of Orazkeldi, Oraz, Zhanshukir and Karash. Their pastures covered the upper Turgay and the eastern foothills of the Mugodzhar, where a corridor of grassland runs north to the upper Tobol; camel trains between the Aral winter camps and the summer grazing of the southern Urals followed the same line. In 1444 the country belonged to the Nogai Horde, the Manghit yurt whose beys had lately broken with the Uzbek khanate to the east, and its Kipchak-speaking people were Sunni Muslim herdsmen who built no towns and moved with the seasons.

The Kazakh khans later drove the Nogais west and opened these pastures to the Alimuly clans. The Dzungar invasion of 1723 scattered the Tortkara auls, the year the Kazakhs call the Great Disaster, and their riders served Abulkhair of the Junior Jüz at the victories on the Bulanty river in 1726 and at Anrakai in 1729. Abulkhair swore allegiance to Russia in 1731 to gain help against the Dzungars, but the war returned to this country: in February 1741 a Dzungar army campaigned through to the Tobol and the Ishim, and refugee auls fled towards the Russian forts. The clan later joined Srym Datov's rising against the Orenburg frontier in 1783–1797, and in 1806 the Tortkara fought beside the Shekty when the clans stormed the Khivan town of Kungrad.
zh:
托卡拉是哈萨克小玉兹阿尔申部落阿利姆乌鲁六支之一，内分奥拉兹凯勒德、奥拉兹、詹舒基尔、卡拉什四个支系。其牧地在图尔盖河上游与穆戈贾尔山东麓，一条草原走廊向北通到托博尔河上游，往返于咸海冬牧场与南乌拉尔夏牧场之间的驼队也走这条线。1444年，这里属于诺盖汗国，曼格特兀鲁思的伯克们不久前才脱离东边的乌兹别克汗国自立；居民是说钦察语的逊尼派穆斯林牧民，不建城郭，随季节迁徙。

后来哈萨克诸汗把诺盖人逐向西方，把这些牧场让给阿利姆乌鲁诸部。1723年准噶尔入侵，托卡拉人的阿乌尔四散，这一年哈萨克人称作「大灾难」；其骑手在小玉兹阿布勒海尔军中，参加了1726年布兰特河与1729年安拉凯两次胜仗。为换取俄国相助对抗准噶尔，阿布勒海尔于1731年向俄国宣誓臣服，但战火又烧回这一带：1741年2月，准噶尔军队一直打到托博尔河与伊希姆河，逃难的阿乌尔涌向俄国要塞。该部后来参加了1783至1797年斯雷姆·达托夫反抗奥伦堡边防当局的起义；1806年诸部联军攻克希瓦治下的昆格勒，托卡拉人与舍克图人并肩作战。

en:
Shegendyk is named for one of the five Meiram clans of the Argyn, the most numerous tribe of the Middle Jüz; the Kaksal were their leading subdivision. Their camps lay in the dry steppe between the Ishim and its tributary the Zhabay, where winter pastures, hay meadows and small ploughed plots kept Kazakh herdsmen and their sheep, horses and camels through the year. In 1444 this country belonged to Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek ulus; its people were Turkic-speaking Sunni Kazakhs, with no walled towns of their own.

After Abu'l-Khayr's death in 1468 the Argyn clans entered the new Kazakh khanate as part of the Middle Jüz. The Dzungar wars struck the northern steppe hardest, and through the worst decades of the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries these pastures stood largely empty as Kazakhs drove their herds south. The Middle Jüz khan accepted Russian subjecthood in 1740, during the Dzungar invasion of 1739-1741. The Kaksal drifted back afterwards: by the early nineteenth century they again moved between the Ishim and the Zhabay in the Atbasar steppe, whose caravan and cattle-droving roads gave the tract its name, Atbasar, the Kazakh for 'horse market'.
zh:
舍根迪克得名于舍根迪克部，它是中玉兹人数最多的阿尔根部梅拉姆五氏族之一，卡克萨尔是其主要支系。其营地位于伊希姆河与其支流扎巴伊河之间的干草原，冬牧场、干草地和小块耕地供养着哈萨克牧民和他们的羊、马、骆驼。1444年，此地属于阿布勒海尔的乌兹别克兀鲁思，居民是说突厥语、信奉逊尼派伊斯兰教的哈萨克人，没有自己的城郭。

1468年阿布勒海尔死后，阿尔根诸部加入新兴的哈萨克汗国，归入中玉兹。准噶尔战争使北部草原受害最深，在17世纪至18世纪初最艰难的几十年里，哈萨克人赶着畜群南逃，这一带的牧场几乎空无一人。1739—1741年准噶尔大举入侵期间，中玉兹汗于1740年接受俄国臣属。卡克萨尔人后来陆续北返：到19世纪初，他们重新转场于阿特巴萨尔草原的伊希姆河与扎巴伊河之间；穿过这里的商路和赶畜道给了这片土地阿特巴萨尔之名，它在哈萨克语中意为「马市」。

en:
The Narym range runs for about 120 kilometres across the southern Altai, rising to 2,533 metres and parting the Narym and Kurchum rivers on their short course to the Irtysh. Larch and fir darken its northern face while the southern slope is open feather-grass steppe; the rivers give fish and the high valleys serve as summer pasture for sheep and horses. In 1444 Naiman and Kerei clans grazed these valleys under the loose overlordship of Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Uzbek ulus, on a steppe march disputed with Moghulistan and the Oirats.

Armies found their way into these mountains in the eighteenth century. In May 1720 Major Ivan Likharev, sent up the Irtysh by Peter I after tales of gold dust on the Yarkand River, reached Lake Zaysan; his men beat off the attacks of a large Dzungar force on the Black Irtysh, but the shoaling river stopped the boats, and on the way back, on 30 August, they raised the Ust-Kamennaya fortress where the Ulba joins the Irtysh, at the point where the river breaks out of the stone mountains. Farther up these valleys, beyond the Russian fortified line, Old Believers had been hiding since the 1720s, fleeing the double tax on schismatics and forced labour in the state mines. They hunted, kept bees and traded furs to Kazakh, Altai and Chinese neighbours, and their hidden country became known as Belovodye. After the Qing destroyed the Dzungar Khanate in 1755–1758, Kazakh auls moved into the empty upper Irtysh pastures. A rescript of Catherine II in 1791 took in 205 men and 68 women of the mountain settlers as yasak-paying subjects; the next year they gathered into nine villages, among them Malonarymskaya.
zh:
纳里姆（纳雷姆）山横亘阿尔泰山西南段，长约120公里，最高峰海拔2533米，是纳雷姆河与库尔丘姆河的分水岭，两河出山后都注入额尔齐斯河。北坡覆着深色的落叶松和冷杉林，南坡是开阔的针茅草原；河中渔产丰富，高山谷地又是绵羊和马匹的夏牧场。1444年，乃蛮与克烈诸部在这些山谷游牧，名义上归阿布勒海尔汗的乌兹别克兀鲁思管辖，地处草原与蒙兀儿斯坦、卫拉特人拉锯的边地。

18世纪，军队开始进出这片山地。1720年5月，伊凡·利哈列夫少校听到叶尔羌河出砂金的传闻，奉彼得一世之命溯额尔齐斯河而上，抵达斋桑湖；他的队伍击退了黑额尔齐斯河上大队准噶尔军的进攻，河道却浅得行不了船，只得折返，并在归途的8月30日，于乌尔巴河汇入额尔齐斯河、河水冲出石山峡口之处筑起乌斯季卡缅要塞。更上游的山谷里，旧礼仪派为逃避向分裂派加倍征收的人丁税和官营矿场的劳役，从1720年代起就躲过俄国的筑垒线藏身于此。他们打猎、养蜂，用毛皮与哈萨克人、阿尔泰人和中国商民交易，把藏身之地称作「别洛沃季耶」，意为白水。1755至1758年清朝攻灭准噶尔汗国后，哈萨克阿乌尔迁入空旷的上额尔齐斯牧场。1791年，叶卡捷琳娜二世下诏接纳这些山里人中的205名男子和68名女子为缴纳雅萨克的臣民；次年他们聚成九座村落，小纳雷姆村便是其一。

en:
Shymkent and its older neighbour Sayram sit on the small rivers running into the Arys, where the irrigated oases of Transoxiana end and the pastures of the Dasht-i Qipchaq begin. Sayram, medieval Isfijab, was called the White City by the eleventh-century scholar Kashgari and lived by that border: Samanid governors ringed it with walls, the oases behind it were strung with ribat forts, seventeen hundred of them by al-Muqaddasi's count, and merchants from Bukhara and Samarkand kept caravanserais in its streets, while four gates were guarded by volunteer fighters of the faith. It was also the birthplace of Khoja Ahmed Yasavi, the Sufi saint most widely honoured across the Turkic lands, and the tombs of his parents there drew pilgrims from the whole region. By Timur's day, Rashid al-Din called it a city of forty gates that took a full day to cross; Timur gave it to his grandson Ulugh Beg, the right wing of his China-bound army wintered around it, and Moghul forces once besieged its fortress. The smaller settlement of Chimkent, later Shymkent, grew on the caravan road nearby, and Sharaf al-Din Yazdi mentions Timur finding his baggage train there. In 1444 this Sunni caravan frontier was governed from Samarkand.

Muhammad Shaybani took Sayram in 1503, but in 1512 the townsmen handed its keys to the Kazakh Qasim Khan, of whom Babur wrote that no khan of the age matched him in authority, and the border slipped from Uzbek into Kazakh hands. Dzungar armies sacked Sayram in 1684 and carried off many craftsmen, then overran the oasis again in 1723, opening a long period of raids and tribute. From 1784 the oasis belonged to Yunus Khoja's Tashkent state until Kokand's Alim Khan seized it in 1809. Kokand governors put their walls and garrison at Shymkent and built it up as the regional market, and old Sayram never caught up. In 1821 the Kazakh sultan Tentek Tore raised the clans against Kokand taxes and stormed both Sayram and Shymkent, until Kokand reinforcements retook them after several battles.
zh:
希姆肯特和更古老的邻城塞兰位于几条注入阿雷斯河的小河旁，河中灌溉绿洲到此为止，再往前便是钦察草原的牧场。塞兰在中世纪叫伊斯菲贾布，11世纪的学者喀什噶里称它为「白城」。这座城靠边境立足：萨曼王朝的长官绕城筑墙，身后的绿洲上遍布穆斯林的边防要塞里巴特，据穆卡达西统计有一千七百座；布哈拉和撒马尔罕的商人在城里开着商馆，四座城门由志愿的信仰战士把守。这里还是突厥语世界最受尊崇的苏菲圣徒霍贾·艾哈迈德·亚萨维的出生地，他父母在城中的陵墓吸引各地的朝圣者。到帖木儿的时代，拉施特丁称塞兰是一座有四十座城门的大城，横穿全城要走一整天。帖木儿把它封给孙子兀鲁伯，征明大军的右翼曾在城周过冬，蒙兀儿军队还围攻过它的城堡。希姆肯特的前身，是附近商道上发展起来的小聚落奇姆肯特，谢雷夫丁·亚兹迪在书里提到，帖木儿曾在奇姆肯特找到自己的辎重队。1444年，这条逊尼派商队边境由撒马尔罕管辖。

穆罕默德·昔班尼1503年夺取塞兰，但1512年市民把城钥交给哈萨克的哈斯木汗——巴布尔写道，当时没有哪位汗能在威望上与哈斯木相比，这片边境就此从乌兹别克政权转入哈萨克人之手。准噶尔军队1684年洗劫塞兰，掳走大批工匠，1723年再度席卷绿洲，开启了长期袭扰与称贡的局面。1784年起，这片绿洲归尤努斯·和卓的塔什干政权，直到浩罕的阿里姆汗1809年将其攻占。浩罕长官把城墙和驻军设在希姆肯特，把它经营成地区市场，古老的塞兰再没能追上。1821年，哈萨克苏丹腾特克·托列率诸部反抗浩罕赋税，连克塞兰和希姆肯特，几场战斗之后又被浩罕援军夺回。

en:
Aksary is the name of a northern Kazakh clan of the Ashamayly branch of the Kerei, one of the six tribes of the Middle Jüz. Their grazing grounds ran along the middle Ishim and the adjoining dry steppe, a country of sparse watercourses, long winters and seasonal transhumance, where wealth moved on horse, sheep and camel. In 1444 these nomads belonged to Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Uzbek confederation and were Sunni Muslims.

The Russian frontier reached the Aksary pastures in the mid-eighteenth century, after the Dzungar invasion of 1739-1741 and the Middle Jüz's submission of 1740. In the summer of 1752 an expedition of nearly two thousand dragoons and soldiers built the wooden fortress of Saint Peter at Kyzyl-Zhar, the 'red cliff' on the right bank of the Ishim. It opened a new fortified line drawn across the steppe from Omsk on the Irtysh to the Tobol: a hexagonal fort with bastions, barracks and a powder magazine. The garrison market outgrew its military purpose, for under Ablai Khan caravan routes between Russia and Central Asia converged on it, and a salt house inside the walls received envoys from Kokand. In 1782 the Middle Jüz sultan Vali took his oath of allegiance there and was confirmed as khan by Catherine II's government; the fortress was renamed Petropavlovsk in 1807. The Aksary kept their camps and herds along the Ishim through these years.
zh:
阿克萨莱是哈萨克北部一个氏族之名，属于中玉兹六大部落之一克烈部的阿沙马伊勒支系。其牧场沿伊希姆河中游及相邻干草原展开，那里水道稀疏、冬季漫长，人们按季节转场，财富就是马、羊和骆驼。1444年，这些游牧人属于阿布勒海尔汗的乌兹别克联盟，是逊尼派穆斯林。

1739—1741年准噶尔入侵、中玉兹1740年臣服之后，俄国边防线在18世纪中期推进到阿克萨莱牧场。1752年夏，一支近两千人的龙骑兵和步兵队伍在伊希姆河右岸的克孜勒扎尔（意为「红色崖岸」）修筑木结构的圣彼得要塞。它开启了一条横跨草原的新防线，从额尔齐斯河畔的鄂木斯克一直延伸到托博尔河；要塞为六边形，设有棱堡、兵营和火药库。驻军集市的作用超出了军事本身：在阿布赉汗时期，连接俄国与中亚的商路汇聚于此，城内还设了一座盐馆接待浩罕来使。1782年，中玉兹苏丹瓦里在要塞中宣誓效忠，被叶卡捷琳娜二世的政府正式承认为汗；要塞于1807年改名彼得罗巴甫洛夫斯克。这些年里，阿克萨莱人始终在伊希姆河一带保留着营地与畜群。

en:
The Altyn are one of the twelve clans of the Baiuly branch of the Alshyn in the Kazakh Junior Jüz. Their auls lay along the Irgiz and the middle Turgay, shallow rivers that carry snowmelt south through the Turgay gateway, the low pass between the Mugodzhar and the Kazakh uplands joining the Siberian steppe to the Aral lowlands; caravan tracks followed the rivers towards the markets of Turkestan and the Syr Darya. In 1444 this was the western march of Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek khanate, the Shibanid power that had reunited most of the eastern Dasht-i Qipchaq, and its Kipchak-speaking people were Sunni Muslim herdsmen with horses, sheep and camels.

When Kerei and Janibek's Kazakhs inherited the steppe after Abu'l-Khayr, the Altyn pastures passed to them; under an agreement of 1495–1496 between Burunduk Khan and Muhammad Shaybani the Kazakhs kept several northern cities of Turkestan. Their westward drive in the 1520s broke Nogai power and opened the Aral steppe to the Baiuly clans. The Dzungar invasion of 1723, the Great Disaster, drove the Junior Jüz west, and Abulkhair's oath to Russia in 1731 put the frontier on the Turgay. In Pugachev's revolt of 1773–1775 Junior Jüz horsemen raided the Orenburg line, and from 1783 the Baiuly clans made up the backbone of Srym Datov's rising: the clan elders elected him head of their steppe assembly, the pastures west of the Ural stayed shut to Kazakh herds, and the fighting stopped the Central Asian caravan trade for most of the 1790s. When the rising collapsed in 1797, Srym withdrew to Khiva.
zh:
阿尔钦是哈萨克小玉兹阿尔申大部落拜乌雷支派十二部之一，其阿乌尔分布在伊尔吉兹河与图尔盖河中游一带。两条浅河挟融雪水向南穿过图尔盖走廊，即穆戈贾雷山与哈萨克丘陵之间连接西伯利亚草原和咸海低地的低矮通道，商队沿河谷走向突厥斯坦与锡尔河的市场。1444年，这里是阿布勒海尔乌兹别克汗国的西部边地，这个昔班尼王朝的政权重新统一了钦察草原东部的大部，居民是说钦察语的逊尼派穆斯林，牧放马、羊和骆驼。

阿布勒海尔死后，克列与贾尼别克的哈萨克人接管草原，阿尔钦的牧地随之归入汗国；1495至1496年布伦杜克汗与穆罕默德·昔班尼立约，突厥斯坦北部数城仍归哈萨克。1520年代哈萨克人向西进击，打垮诺盖势力，咸海草原向拜乌雷诸部敞开。1723年准噶尔入侵，即「大灾难」，小玉兹向西奔逃；1731年阿布勒海尔向俄国宣誓臣服，边界推到图尔盖河一线。1773至1775年普加乔夫起义中，小玉兹骑手袭掠奥伦堡防线；1783年起，拜乌雷诸部构成斯雷姆·达托夫起义的主力：各部长老推举他主持草原大会，乌拉尔河以西的牧场始终不许哈萨克牧民进入，战事使通往中亚的商队贸易在1790年代大部停顿。1797年起义失败，斯雷姆退往希瓦。

en:
The Baganaly are a clan of the Naiman tribe within the Kazakh Middle Jüz. Their name comes from the bakan, the forked long pole used to raise a yurt's roof, and a forked pole is their tamga, stamped on their horses and borne on their banners; their battle cry was Bayanbay. Their pastures climb from the Turgay and Sarysu plains into the Ulytau, a low granite range of springs, lakes and birch-filled hollows called the 'land of lakes and springs'. The White Horde khans kept their headquarters in these hills: Jochi's ordo stood here, his mausoleum and that of Alash Khan rose on the slopes, and Batu rode out from the Ulytau on his campaign into the Kipchak steppe. The Golden Horde khan Tokhtamysh and the emir Edigu were later buried in the range, and in the spring of 1391 Timur, marching against Tokhtamysh, left an inscription on the rock of Altyn-Shoky. In 1444 the Baganaly pastures belonged to Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek ulus, and the Naiman clans grazed their herds between the Ulytau and the Syr Darya as Sunni Muslims.

Around 1470 the Ulytau clans passed with the rest of Abu'l-Khayr's inheritance to the Kazakhs of Kerei and Janibek, and the range remained the steppe's meeting ground. In 1730, as the Dzungars overran the eastern pastures, some forty thousand militia from all three jüz gathered in the hills, with Abulkhair holding overall command and Bokenbay Batyr leading them in the field. In 1740 the Middle Jüz accepted Russian protection; the following February a Dzungar army swept as far as the Tobol and the Ishim and carried off Sultan Abylai, who was freed only in 1743 in exchange for a hostage. Abylai later ruled all three jüz and died at Tashkent in 1781, the last Kazakh khan to reign without a foreign overlord. After him Russian outposts advanced along the pasture roads, and the khan's title kept little of its power.
zh:
巴格纳雷人是哈萨克中玉兹乃蛮部的一支。族名出自「巴坎」，即撑起毡房屋顶用的分叉长竿，分叉长竿也是他们的部族印记，烙在马身上、画在战旗上，出战时高呼的战斗口号是「巴彦拜」。他们的牧地从图尔盖河与萨雷苏河平原伸入乌勒套低山，山中多泉、多湖，洼地里长着桦林，被称作「湖泊与泉水之乡」。白帐诸汗的斡耳朵就设在这片山里：术赤的宫帐在此，他和阿拉什汗的陵墓修在山坡上，拔都也从乌勒套起兵西征钦察草原。金帐汗脱脱迷失和埃米尔也迪该后来都葬在山中；1391年春，帖木儿进兵讨伐脱脱迷失，在阿尔滕朔基（Altyn-Shoky）的岩壁上留下铭文。1444年，巴格纳雷的牧地属于阿布勒海尔的乌兹别克兀鲁思，乃蛮诸部在乌勒套与锡尔河之间放牧，信奉逊尼派伊斯兰教。

约1470年，乌勒套诸部随阿布勒海尔的遗产转归克列和贾尼别克的哈萨克人，这片山仍是草原各部会集之地。1730年准噶尔人攻入东部牧场，三玉兹约四万名民兵在山中集结，由阿布勒海尔总领、博肯拜巴图尔实际指挥。1740年中玉兹接受俄国庇护，次年2月准噶尔军便横扫至托博尔河与伊希姆河，掳走苏丹阿布赉，直到1743年以人质交换他才获释。阿布赉后来总领三玉兹，1781年在塔什干去世，是最后一位没有外来宗主的哈萨克汗。他死后，俄国要塞沿牧道步步推进，汗的名号已没有多少实权。

en:
The Tobykty are a clan of the Argyn tribe in the Kazakh Middle Jüz, counted in genealogies among the seven lineages of Momyn, one of the two founding branches of the Argyns. Their auls moved through the mountain steppe of Chingiztau, a 200-kilometre eastern ridge of the Sary-Arka; Kosoba rises to 1,305 metres, the Bakanas and smaller streams start on its slopes, and birch and aspen groves in the valleys sheltered the winter camps. In 1444 these Sunni Turkic herders kept sheep, horses and wool-bearing flocks under the loose rule of Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Uzbek ulus.

Abu'l-Khayr's death in 1468 broke up his ulus, and the Tobykty entered the confederation of the sultans Kerei and Janibek. Their eastern pastures lay open to the Dzungars: the invasion of 1723, remembered as the Years of the Great Disaster, drove the auls from these winter camps into a long flight west.
zh:
托毕克提是哈萨克中玉兹阿尔浑部的一个氏族，谱系列为莫温七支之一，莫温是阿尔浑两大始祖支系之一。他们的阿乌尔游牧于成吉思套山的山地草原；这条长约200公里的山脉是萨雷阿尔卡东缘，科索巴峰海拔1305米，巴卡纳斯等溪河发源于山坡，谷中的桦树和山杨林为冬营挡风。1444年，这些信奉逊尼派的突厥语牧户放养绵羊、马匹和毛用羊群，受阿布勒海尔汗的乌兹别克兀鲁思松散统辖。

1468年阿布勒海尔死后，兀鲁思解体，托毕克提加入克烈、贾尼别克两位苏丹的联盟。他们的东部牧场正对准噶尔方向敞开：1723年那场后世称为「大灾难年代」的入侵，把诸部从这些冬营地逐出，向西长途流亡。

en:
Dzhaman-Kuduk, the 'bad well', belongs to the dry corridor between the Syr Darya towns and the central steppe: the Moiynkum sands along the northern Karatau, the lower Sarysu, and the western edge of the Betpak-Dala. Groundwater collects in hollows between the sand ridges, giving herdsmen winter pasture for sheep and horses, while the track from Sozaq toward the Irtysh depended on wells such as this. In 1444 the route lay within Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek Khanate.

In the late 1450s the sultans Kerei and Janibek broke from Abu'l-Khayr and led about 200,000 nomads east to the Chu and Talas valleys, where they founded the Kazakh Khanate around 1465. Abu'l-Khayr marched against them in 1468 and died on campaign; the war that followed lasted until 1500 and left the central steppe in Kazakh hands. Dzungar armies crossed these waterless marches in 1723 and 1739-1741, and Kazakh forces used the desert routes to counter-attack in 1728 and 1730. In 1821 Middle Jüz clans still moved between wells and winter sands, after their khans had accepted Russian protection from 1731 onward.
zh:
朱曼意为「坏井」，地处锡尔河诸城与中部草原之间的干旱走廊：卡拉套山北麓是莫因库姆沙地，向北连接萨雷苏河下游与别特帕克达拉西缘。沙垄间的洼地可以找到地下水，为羊马提供冬牧场；从所扎克通往额尔齐斯河的道路也要依靠这一类水井。1444年，这条通道属于阿布海尔的乌兹别克汗国。

15世纪50年代末，克烈与贾尼别克脱离阿布海尔，率领约二十万部众东迁楚河和怛罗斯河谷，于1465年前后建立哈萨克汗国。1468年阿布海尔出征途中死去，随后的战争持续到1500年，中部草原转入哈萨克人手中。1723年和1739—1741年，准噶尔军队两度穿过这片缺水荒原；哈萨克人则在1728和1730年借沙漠路线发起反攻。1821年，中玉兹诸部仍往来于水井与冬牧场之间，而他们的可汗自1731年起已陆续接受俄国保护。

en:
Gurganj, later called Konye-Urgench, Old Urgench, stood on the Amu Darya channels that then ran toward Sarykamysh. For three centuries it was the capital of the Khwarazmshahs and one of the richest cities in Central Asia, its broad bazaars crowded with caravans plying between the Volga and the east. Early in the eleventh century Khwarazmshah Mamun's academy here employed Ibn Sina, known in Europe as Avicenna, and al-Biruni. When Ibn Battuta visited in the fourteenth century he called Gurganj the largest, finest and best-built of the Turkic cities; the Kutlug Timur minaret, the mausoleum of Turabek Khanum and the tombs of the shahs Il-Arslan and Tekesh rose above its quarters. In 1221 the Mongols took the city after a long siege, killed or enslaved its people and opened the river dams, drowning those hiding in the ruins, one of the bloodiest sacks of the conquest. Gurganj recovered under the Golden Horde, but Timur, who had already campaigned here four times between 1372 and 1379, returned in 1388, levelled the city, broke its canals, deported its craftsmen to Samarkand and had barley sown over the site, sparing only one mosque. In 1444, after Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbeks took the delta in 1430 or 1431, the old capital survived as a reduced frontier town among ruins, canals and Turkmen pastures.

In 1505 Muhammad Shaybani's army took it after an eleven-month siege. When Shaybani fell at Merv in 1510 Gurganj passed to the Safavids, until Ilbars seized it in 1512 and the Qizilbash were driven out of Khwarazm; the Arabshahid khans moved the capital back from Vazir to Gurganj. Bukhara conquered the khanate in 1593, and Haji Muhammad returned from Safavid exile only in 1598. Early in the next century a band of Yaik Cossacks under the ataman Nechay seized the weakened city but, lacking horses, could not get away; Arab Muhammad Khan besieged them, swore they would be spared and given mounts, and had them cut down as they marched out. As southern Khwarazm diverted the river for its own fields, the Daryaliq canals lost water, and Abu al-Ghazi moved the last inhabitants south to Yangi Urgench. The old capital became pasture scattered with the ruins of its mausoleums.
zh:
玉龙杰赤，后来又称库尼亚-乌尔根奇，意为「旧乌尔根奇」，坐落在阿姆河当时通向萨雷卡梅什的旧水道旁。它做了三个世纪花剌子模沙的都城，是中亚最富庶的城市之一，伏尔加河与东方之间的商队往来于宽阔的巴扎。11世纪初，花剌子模沙马蒙在这里办的学院曾延揽伊本·西那（欧洲称阿维森纳）和比鲁尼。14世纪伊本·白图泰到访时，称玉龙杰赤是突厥诸城之中最大、最好、建筑最精的一座，巴扎齐整、街道宽阔；库特卢格·帖木儿宣礼塔、图拉别克·哈努姆陵墓以及伊尔·阿尔斯兰、塔乞失两位沙的陵墓高耸在城区之上。1221年，蒙古人久围攻下此城，屠戮或掳走居民，又掘开阿姆河大坝，藏在废墟中的人也被洪水吞没，这是蒙古征服中最惨烈的屠城之一。玉龙杰赤在金帐汗国治下复兴，但帖木儿1372年至1379年间已四度来攻，又于1388年重返：他夷平城市、毁坏灌渠、把工匠迁往撒马尔罕，还在城址上播种大麦，只留下一座清真寺。1430年或1431年阿布勒海尔的乌兹别克人攻占三角洲；到1444年，这座旧都只是一座衰微的边镇，夹在废墟、灌渠和土库曼牧场之间。

1505年，穆罕默德·昔班尼的军队围城十一个月才将它拿下。1510年昔班尼在梅尔夫战死后，玉龙杰赤转入萨法维之手；1512年伊尔巴斯夺取此城，克孜勒巴什被逐出花剌子模，阿拉伯沙希王朝诸汗把都城从瓦济尔迁回玉龙杰赤。1593年布哈拉征服汗国，哈吉·穆罕默德流亡萨法维波斯，1598年才返回。17世纪初，首领涅恰伊带一队雅依克哥萨克袭取这座衰弱的城市，却因没有马匹无法脱身；阿拉伯·穆罕默德汗围城，发誓饶他们性命并供给坐骑，等他们一出城便将其尽数诛杀。后来南花剌子模引水浇灌自家田地，达里亚里克各渠水量日减，阿布·哈齐把最后的居民南迁到杨吉·乌尔根奇，旧都化为牧场，只剩陵墓散落在废墟之间。

en:
The province called Atakent covers the south-eastern fringe of the Kyzylkum, where the red dunes run into the salt loess of Mirzachol, the Hungry Steppe, on the left bank of the Syr Darya. It was march country: riverside meadows and scattered wells gave seasonal grazing for sheep, horses and camels, and tracks from Tashkent and Khujand bent west through the sands toward Bukhara and Khwarezm. In 1444 the nomads here belonged to Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Uzbek confederation, whose armies were pressing the walled Syr Darya towns; they took Sighnaq, the old capital of the Blue Horde, in 1446.

These clans passed to the Kazakh Khanate after Kerei and Janibek founded it in 1465. Under Qasim Khan, from 1511, Kazakh herds and patrols reached the Syr Darya pastures, and his riders watered at these desert wells during the campaigns of 1520. When khanal authority broke apart after Tauke Khan, the clans lay open to the Dzungar army that struck in the spring of 1723; Kazakhs remember the rout as the Barefooted Flight, when refugees were driven across the Syr Darya and whole bands scattered into the Kyzylkum. No walled town ever rose here, and through the wars Atakent stayed a watered crossing and grazing ground that Kazakh, Uzbek and Bukharan riders contested in turn.
zh:
名为阿塔肯特的这片地区位于克孜勒库姆东南缘，红色沙丘在锡尔河左岸接入米尔扎乔尔，即饥饿草原的盐碱黄土。这是片边地：河畔草甸和零星水井为绵羊、马匹和骆驼提供季节性牧场，从塔什干和苦盏西去布哈拉与花剌子模的道路绕沙而行。1444年，这里的游牧民属于阿布海尔汗的乌兹别克联盟，他的军队正在进逼锡尔河诸城，1446年拿下旧白帐汗国的都城瑟格纳克。

1465年克烈和贾尼别克建立哈萨克汗国后，这些部族转归哈萨克。哈斯木汗1511年即位后，哈萨克的牧群和游骑抵达锡尔河牧场，1520年出征时他的骑兵也在这些沙漠水井歇脚饮水。头克汗之后汗权瓦解，诸部失去屏障，1723年春准噶尔大军突入；哈萨克人把这场溃败称为「赤脚逃亡」，难民被驱过锡尔河，整支整支的队伍散入克孜勒库姆。这里始终没有筑起城镇，在连绵的战事里，阿塔肯特只是一处有水井的歇脚地和牧场，被哈萨克、乌兹别克和布哈拉的骑兵轮流争夺。

en:
Talas is a high valley of the western Tian Shan, shut between the Kyrgyz Ala-Too and the Talas Ala-Too, with dry steppe pasture on the upper slopes and irrigated fields and orchards along the Talas River. Arab and Tang armies fought their way through its passes at the Battle of Talas in 751, but by the fifteenth century the valley mattered chiefly for its summer pastures and the tracks linking the Chu valley, Ferghana and the Syr Darya. Kyrgyz and Moghul tribes grazed there within the loose Moghulistan confederation, and in 1444 it was a Sunni borderland where tribal herdsmen met Muslim merchants from the oasis towns.

In the 1470s the Kyrgyz clans wanted a khan of Genghisid blood and drew in Ahmad, a son of Yunus Khan who had slipped away from his father's ulus; he spent ten years breaking the Moghul nobles who resisted him, and his ulus stretched from the Talas across the Tian Shan to the Ili. His son Khalil was beaten by Mansur Khan in 1508, and many Kyrgyz were driven toward Kashgar and Turfan. For two centuries afterwards the clans fought beside Kazakh allies against Yarkand, Bukhara and the Oirats. Kubat Biy, born in this valley in 1690, led the united Kyrgyz army into Kashgaria, ruled Kashgar for the White Mountain khojas in 1755–1756, and was killed in 1761 while defending Osh against Kokand. By then the Kokand army already relied heavily on Kyrgyz cavalry, and early in the nineteenth century the Talas valley itself passed under the khanate, its chiefs trading military service for influence at the Kokand court.
zh:
塔拉斯是西天山西段的高位河谷，夹在吉尔吉斯阿拉套山与塔拉斯阿拉套山之间，高处是干旱草原牧场，塔拉斯河两岸分布着可灌溉的农田和果园。751年，阿拉伯与唐朝的军队穿过河谷山口打了怛罗斯之战；到15世纪，它的价值主要在于夏季牧场，以及连接楚河谷地、费尔干纳和锡尔河的小路。吉尔吉斯与蒙兀儿诸部当时在蒙兀儿斯坦的松散联盟内游牧，1444年的塔拉斯是一条逊尼派边地，部落牧民在此同来自绿洲城镇的穆斯林商人交易。

1470年代，吉尔吉斯诸部要立一位有黄金家族血统的汗，便迎来偷偷离开父亲兀鲁思的羽奴思汗之子艾哈迈德。他花了十年制服反抗的蒙兀儿贵族，其乌鲁斯从塔拉斯横跨天山直到伊犁。其子哈利勒1508年败于满速儿汗，许多吉尔吉斯人被赶往喀什噶尔和吐鲁番。此后两个世纪，诸部与哈萨克结盟，先后同叶尔羌、布哈拉和卫拉特作战。1690年生于这个河谷的库巴特·比，曾率领吉尔吉斯联军进入喀什噶尔，1755至1756年替白山派和卓镇守喀什城，1761年在保卫奥什、对抗浩罕时被杀。那时浩罕军队已大量征用吉尔吉斯骑兵；19世纪初，塔拉斯河谷本身也被并入浩罕汗国，各部首领以从军作战换取在浩罕宫廷的势力。

en:
The steppe between the lower Volga and the middle Yaik has almost no standing water: the Bolshoy Uzen and its sister rivers wind south out of the downs and die in the sands. The grass fattened sheep, horses and camels, and the country served the nomads as their orda, the moving inner camp of the Nogai Horde, where the Manghit clans grazed under their own beys. In 1444 they did so in loose allegiance to the fading Golden Horde, while caravans from the Volga towns to Khwarazm avoided the waterless interior and kept to the Yaik along the steppe's southern rim.

Kazakh khans pressed the Nogais west across the Volga in 1521. A century later Kho-Urluk's Torghut Oirats overran the Volga-Yaik grassland in 1628–1630 and in 1634 beat the Great Nogai Horde in a battle it never recovered from; the surviving uluses drifted off to the Kuban. Kalmyk herdsmen held the country until 1771, when the Torghuts struck camp for Dzungaria and left the steppe vacant. Pugachev's rebellion ran across this grassland in 1773–1774, and Kazakhs from beyond the Yaik swelled his Cossack ranks; after his defeat at Tsaritsyn his own followers handed him over, and he was executed in Moscow in January 1775.
zh:
伏尔加河下游与亚伊克河中游之间的草原几乎没有常年积水：大乌津河等几条河道从丘陵间蜿蜒南流，最终消失在沙地中。草色足以养肥羊、马和骆驼；省名奥尔达就是「斡耳朵」，这里正是诺盖汗国流动的内营，曼格特诸部在本部首领率领下在此放牧。1444年，他们对日渐衰微的金帐汗国只保持松散的臣属；从伏尔加河诸城前往花剌子模的商队不进缺水的腹地，而是沿草原南缘的亚伊克河行进。

1521年，哈萨克诸汗把诺盖人逼过伏尔加河以西。一个世纪后，和鄂尔勒克的土尔扈特卫拉特人在1628至1630年席卷伏尔加河与亚伊克河之间的草原，又在1634年一战击败大诺盖斡耳朵，使其再未恢复，残存各帐辗转西迁库班河。卡尔梅克牧人占有此地直到1771年，土尔扈特人拔营东归准噶尔，留下空旷的草原。1773至1774年，普加乔夫起义在这片草原上往来，亚伊克河以东的哈萨克人充实了他的哥萨克队伍；普加乔夫在察里津战败后被自己的部下交出，1775年1月在莫斯科被处决。

en:
The Utva, or Shyngyrlau, winds for 290 kilometres from the Podural plateau across grassy steppe to the lower Yaik. Its lower course is full of old channels, the water is shallow for much of the year, and the many fords made it a useful route for herds rather than an obstacle. The river freezes in November and opens again in mid-April. In 1444 it crossed the western pastures of the Nogai Horde, where Sunni Manghit clans grazed horses and sheep. Later auls of the Kazakh Little Jüz, chiefly Bayuly clans, used the same banks and crossings.

After the Orenburg line reached the Yaik in the 1730s, Cossack patrols on the far bank turned these fords into controlled points. The Yaik Cossacks themselves traced their host to late-sixteenth-century Volga raiders who crossed the river, sacked Saraychik and founded Yaitsk; by the eighteenth century fishing dues and service rights had become bitter issues. In 1772 the Cossacks killed General von Traubenberg during a rising over those grievances. Yemelyan Pugachev used the unrest to claim the title of Peter III and began his revolt at Yaitsk in 1773. Little Jüz riders raided settlements along the steppe side, and Syrym Datuly led a Kazakh detachment with the rebels in 1774. His own rising of 1783–1797 kept the same issue open: herders were barred from crossing to the Yaik's right bank.
zh:
乌特瓦河（哈萨克语称申格尔劳河）起于乌拉尔山前高原，在草原上蜿蜒290公里，注入亚伊克河下游。下游多旧河道，一年中大部分时间水浅，浅滩反倒方便牧群通行，不像天险。河水11月封冻，4月中旬解冻。1444年时，这条河流经诺盖汗国西部牧场，逊尼派曼吉特各部在此放马牧羊。后来哈萨克小玉兹的阿吾勒，主要是巴伊乌勒各部，也使用同样的河岸和渡口。

1730年代奥伦堡防线推进到亚伊克河后，对岸的哥萨克巡哨把这些浅滩变成受管控的地点。亚伊克哥萨克自称源自16世纪末的伏尔加河袭掠者：他们渡过亚伊克河，洗劫萨莱楚克，建起雅依克城；到18世纪，渔税和服役权益已积怨很深。1772年，哥萨克在一场围绕这些争端的暴动中杀死特劳本贝格将军。叶梅利扬·普加乔夫利用这场动荡，自称彼得三世，于1773年在雅依克城举事。小玉兹骑兵从草原一侧袭扰聚落，瑟雷姆·达托夫1774年率一支哈萨克支队加入义军。他在1783至1797年领导的起义仍围绕同一争端：牧民被禁止迁往亚伊克河右岸。

en:
The lower Yaik slackens into a reedy Caspian delta, and on the right bank, fifty kilometres above the sea, stood Saray-Jük, 'Little Sarai', the only walled city the Nogai Horde ever possessed. The caravan road from the Volga marts to Khwarazm and China crossed the river here, and the Florentine merchant Pegolotti listed the town in his merchants' handbook of the 1340s. Ibn Battuta, passing around 1333, found a pontoon bridge across the Yaik that put him in mind of Baghdad, and Golden Horde nobles came to the surrounding marshes to hunt and fish. The town minted its own coins and drew water through ceramic mains, and the historian Abu al-Ghazi wrote that Khans Berdibek and Janibek were enthroned and buried there. Timur's army sacked it in 1395, and by the 1440s it had been rebuilt as the seat and market of the Nogai beys, ringed by their herdsmen's winter camps. Kazakh khans later kept their headquarters here, and Qasim Khan, who carried Kazakh power to the Yaik, was buried in the city.

Volga Cossacks under the atamans Nechai and Bogdan Barbosha stormed and burned Saray-Jük in 1580, and the survivors removed to Khiva. The ruins never recovered: in 1640 Russian settlers built a small fort two kilometres upstream, and the merchant Mikhail Guryev put a wooden stockade and fish-weir at the river mouth, the seed of Guryev. The settlers paid tribute to the Kalmyk khans who now held the steppe, until a stone fortress secured the mouth. Stenka Razin seized it in 1668 during his Volga revolt, and Pugachev's ataman Ovchinnikov stormed the Guryev fortress on 25 January 1774. After the revolt was crushed the government renamed the Yaik the Ural and the Yaik Cossacks the Ural Host, while Guryev carried on as a fishing fort at the mouth of the renamed river.
zh:
下伊克，即亚伊克河下游，在注入里海前水势趋缓，三角洲上芦苇丛生。右岸距海五十公里处的萨莱楚克（意为「小萨莱」），是诺盖汗国唯一的筑墙城市。伏尔加河商埠通往花剌子模和中国的商路在此过河，佛罗伦萨商人佩戈洛蒂在1340年代编写的商旅手册里收录了此城。伊本·白图泰约1333年经过时，河上的浮桥让他想起巴格达，金帐汗国的贵族还常到城外沼泽渔猎。城中自铸钱币，陶制管道引水入户；史家阿布·哈兹记载，别儿迪别和札尼别两位汗都在此登基并安葬。1395年帖木儿的军队洗劫该城，到1440年代它已重建为诺盖首领的驻地与市集，四周环绕牧人的冬营。哈萨克诸汗后来也在此设立牙帐，把哈萨克势力带到亚伊克河的哈斯木汗即葬于城中。

1580年，哥萨克首领涅恰伊和波格丹·巴尔博沙率伏尔加河哥萨克攻陷并焚毁萨莱楚克，幸存者迁往希瓦，废墟再未复兴。1640年，俄国移民在废墟上游两公里处建起小堡，商人米哈伊尔·古里耶夫又在河口立下木栅、筑起鱼梁，这便是古里耶夫的开端。在石砌要塞落成前，移民一直向据有草原的卡尔梅克诸汗纳贡。斯捷潘·拉辛1668年伏尔加河起义时占领此地，1774年1月25日，普加乔夫的首领奥夫钦尼科夫强攻拿下古里耶夫要塞。起义被镇压后，政府把亚伊克河改称乌拉尔河、亚伊克哥萨克改称乌拉尔哥萨克军，河口的古里耶夫则作为渔业要塞留存下来。

en:
The dry heart of this province is the Saryesik-Atyrau desert along the southern shore of Lake Balkhash, where the Ili once emptied through many channels. Between the ninth and thirteenth centuries those channels watered a string of farming towns, and the northernmost was Karamergen, 'the Black Hunter', a walled rectangle with corner towers, irrigated fields, fishing in the lake and game in the tugai woods. Caravans from its gate followed the shore to the Uzun-Aral peninsula, which all but joins the two sides of Balkhash and leaves a strait little more than eight kilometres wide. When the Ili shifted course the town died of thirst and was never rebuilt, and in 1444 its walls stood empty above a dried channel while the nomad clans of Moghulistan, the future Senior Juz, pastured the surrounding steppe.

After the Kazakh Khanate formed around 1465, the southern Balkhash became Senior Juz grazing ground from winter to summer. The Dzungars swept through it in 1723, the opening blow of the catastrophe the Kazakhs call the Great Disaster, and the clans did not come back until Qing armies destroyed the Dzungar state in 1755–57 and the empty shore was reopened to their herds.
zh:
这片省份的干旱腹地，是巴尔喀什湖南岸的萨雷耶西克-阿特劳沙漠，伊犁河曾在此以众多汊道注入湖中。9至13世纪间，这些汊道滋养着一连串农业城镇，其中位置最北的是卡拉门根，突厥语意为「黑猎人」：带角楼的方形城墙、灌溉农田、湖中的渔产与吐加依林中的猎物。出城的商队沿湖岸走到乌尊-阿拉尔半岛，这座半岛几乎把巴尔喀什湖两岸连成一片，只留下一道八公里多宽的海峡。伊犁河改道后，卡拉门根干涸而废，再未复兴。1444年，城墙空立于干涸的河道之上，周围草原是东察合台游牧部落的牧场，他们就是后来的大玉兹。

1465年前后哈萨克汗国建立，巴尔喀什湖南岸成为大玉兹冬夏相继的牧地。1723年准噶尔人席卷此地，这是哈萨克人所称「大灾难」的第一波；直到1755至1757年清军攻灭准噶尔，空旷的湖岸重新向牧群开放，诸部才陆续返回。

en:
The Upper Ishim, called Esil in Kazakh, carries water north from the Kazakh uplands through steppe and forest-steppe. Its pastures supported large nomad camps, and Lake Buzykty held one of the region's rare fixed strongpoints. Bozok began as a Turkic fortified settlement in the seventh century, with three moated quarters and a wall up to eight metres thick at its base. Kipchak rulers made it a kaghan's residence in the tenth century, adding mudbrick houses, a watch tower and irrigation channels; from there they watched caravans between Siberia and Sighnaq, Sauran and Taraz. Horses, leather, metalwork, ceramics and jewellery moved along those routes. In 1444 the Esil grazings belonged to Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Uzbek ulus, and the clans of Sultans Janibek and Kerei were among the herders.

Around 1465 Janibek and Kerei led those clans away to live as free qazaqs. After Abu'l-Khayr died in 1468, the upper Esil passed to the Kazakh khans. Kasym Khan's power after 1511 stretched from the Syr Darya to the Urals, and his men took the Nogai capital Saray-Juk in 1520. Dzungar campaigns later broke across the same pastures. Erdeni Batur's 1643 invasion carried off thousands of people, Khan Jangir was killed in 1652, and the wars of 1723 to 1727, called the Years of the Great Disaster, drove the Middle Jüz from the Esil. The surviving clans gathered at Ordabasy in 1726.

To obtain Russian support, the Middle Jüz accepted Russian suzerainty in 1740. In the summer of 1752 a force of about 2,000 dragoons, foot soldiers and Cossacks built the fortress of Saint Peter at the Kyzyl-Zhar tract on the Ishim. Its wooden ramparts formed a hexagon with bastions and a chain of outer redoubts. The post became Petropavl, a market where Russian and Central Asian caravans met, a trade encouraged by Abylai Khan. In 1782 Abylai's son Vali took the oath of allegiance there and was confirmed by the Russian court as khan of the Middle Jüz.
zh:
上伊希姆在哈萨克语中称叶西尔，源出哈萨克丘陵，向北穿过草原与森林草原。河畔牧场足以容纳大型游牧营地，布祖克特湖畔则有这一带少见的固定据点博佐克。早在7世纪，西迁突厥人就在这里筑起设防聚落，三片围有壕沟的街区外，是底宽可达8米的城墙。10世纪，钦察统治者把它改为可汗驻地，建起土坯房屋、瞭望塔和灌溉渠，并监视从西伯利亚通往瑟格纳克、扫兰、塔拉兹的商队；马匹、皮革、金属器、陶器和珠宝沿这些道路往来。1444年，叶西尔牧场属于阿布勒海尔汗的乌兹别克兀鲁思，贾尼别克与克烈两位苏丹的氏族也在这里放牧。

约1465年，贾尼别克和克烈率部脱离阿布勒海尔，做自由的哈萨克人。1468年阿布勒海尔死后，叶西尔河上游归入哈萨克诸汗。1511年后，哈斯木汗的势力从锡尔河延伸到乌拉尔山，1520年又攻占诺盖都城萨莱楚克。准噶尔人的战事后来席卷同一片牧场：1643年额尔德尼·巴图尔入侵，掳走上万人口，1652年江格尔汗战死；1723至1727年的「大灾难年代」又把中玉兹逐出叶西尔。幸存者1726年在奥尔达巴锡集结。

为取得俄国支持，中玉兹于1740年接受俄国宗主权。1752年夏，约两千名龙骑兵、步兵和哥萨克在伊希姆河畔的克孜勒扎尔地段修建圣彼得要塞。木墙构成六角形防线，配有棱堡和一连串外围工事。这个据点后来发展为彼得罗巴甫尔，俄国和中亚商队在此交易，阿布莱汗也曾推动这条商路。1782年，阿布莱之子瓦里在这里宣誓效忠，并被俄国朝廷确认为中玉兹汗。

en:
Kungirot, the Qońirat of Karakalpak sources, lies on the left side of the Amu Darya delta where the wetlands end and the Ustyurt plateau begins. Its walled settlement guarded the caravan tracks that crossed the waterless plateau toward the Caspian and the Ural country: four gates pierced its clay walls, three of them named for Qongirat clans, and a khan's palace ringed by crenellated ramparts stood at the centre. The place took its name from the Turkic Qongirat clan. In 1444, as the Golden Horde broke apart, this was Nogai-Manghit pasture frontier: Sunni herders bred horses, cattle and sheep on the plain, while fishing families, craftsmen and caravan traders lived around the old fort and its delta channels.

The lower delta went its own way as the Aral polity in 1625. In 1643 Abu al-Ghazi Bahadur was crowned khan at Kungirot before he took the throne of Khiva, a sign of the weight the lower-delta clans carried in Khwarazm's wars. In November 1740 the Kazakh khan Abu al-Khair arrived and briefly installed his son Nuraly as ruler there. After 1747 the Aral polity pushed east to the lower channels of the Syr Darya, gathering Qongirat, Nogai and Qaraqalpak clans between the Amu Darya and the Zhanadarya; the brothers Toremurat and Khojamurat made it independent of Khiva in 1794 and 1795. When a Qongirat line took the khan's title at Khiva in 1804, Muhammad Rahim Khan retook the Zhanadarya lands in 1811 and captured Kungirot the next year. The town kept its caravan market and remained the seat of a semi-independent Qongirat lordship.
zh:
昆格勒，卡拉卡尔帕克语称科尼拉特（Qońirat），位于阿姆河三角洲左岸，水泽到此为止，再往前就是乌斯秋尔特高原。它的城墙聚落扼守商队穿越无水高原、前往里海和乌拉尔地区的道路：土墙开有四座城门，其中三座以昆格拉特人的分支部族命名，城中央还有一座汗宫，围着带雉堞的土墙。地名来自突厥语的昆格拉特部。1444年金帐汗国瓦解之际，这里是诺盖—曼吉特人的牧地边境：逊尼派牧人在平原上繁育马、牛、羊，渔夫、工匠和商队居民则住在旧堡垒和三角洲水道周围。

1625年，下游三角洲自成一方，即阿拉尔领地。1643年，阿布·哈齐·巴哈杜尔在昆格勒加冕称汗，随后才在希瓦登上汗位，可见下游各部的兵马在花剌子模战事中的分量。1740年11月，哈萨克汗阿布勒海尔兵临此地，一度立其子努拉里为当地统治者。1747年后，阿拉尔政权向东推进到锡尔河下游水道，把阿姆河与扎纳达里亚之间的昆格拉特、诺盖和卡拉卡尔帕克各部收拢到一处；1794年至1795年，托列穆拉特与霍贾穆拉特兄弟使其脱离希瓦自立。1804年昆格拉特王朝在希瓦称汗后，穆罕默德·拉希姆汗于1811年夺回扎纳达里亚，次年攻占昆格勒。这座城镇仍是商队市集，也是一个对希瓦半独立的昆格拉特领地的治所。

en:
Song La follows the Black River through the mountains of northwestern Đại Việt. Warm valleys planted with wet rice and tea gardens on the slopes supported a string of Tai muang, settled chiefly by Black, White and Red Tai.
