塔曼半岛是迈奥提斯海与攸克辛海之间、同刻赤隔海峡相望的一块要冲之地，水浅峡窄。莱斯沃斯岛的希腊人约在公元前600年建立赫尔莫纳萨；博斯普鲁斯诸王、可萨的图敦和拜占庭的执政官先后统治此地，10世纪它成为罗斯人的商贸城市特穆塔拉干，1068年王公格列布曾在此丈量冰封的刻赤海峡。1094年后钦察人把它与罗斯故地隔断，蒙古人之后它归入热那亚，得名马特雷加；1449年热那亚黑海殖民地宪章中，普里库班耶只有两处殖民地，它是其一。1419年，出身热那亚犹太家族的文琴佐·德·吉佐尔菲迎娶特穆塔拉干的执政者、阿迪格公主比哈汗。1444年，他们的家族同时作为卡法热那亚领事和大陆切尔克斯王公的藩属据有此城；希腊人、阿迪格人、亚美尼亚人和犹太人杂居一城，商船经海峡贩运奴隶、鱼和葡萄酒。

1453年，热那亚把黑海属地移交圣乔治银行，吉佐尔菲家族代银行治理马特雷加，直到1475年奥斯曼舰队将其攻取。扎卡里亚·德·吉佐尔菲向苏丹输诚，保住了城镇，只是家中挤满从灭亡的狄奥多罗逃来的公侯，逃往热那亚的路上又遭劫掠，1482年他不得不开口向银行请求一千枚金币的补贴。土耳其人筑起洪卡拉要塞，改称塔曼，这里的奴隶市场长期是切尔克斯海岸最繁忙的市场之一。1556年，臣属伊凡雷帝的阿迪格诸王公袭取半岛，连克塔曼和捷姆留克，1570年奥斯曼大军卷土重来。1782年7月的叛乱赶走了俄国拥立的沙辛·格来汗，土耳其驻军重回岛上，但1783年俄国兼并克里米亚汗国时连塔曼一并收入版图。1787至1791年的战争和《雅西条约》确认了这一归属，1792年8月25日首批黑海哥萨克登岸，苏沃洛夫规划新的工事，塔曼成为军法官安东·戈洛瓦季的驻地和哥萨克舰队的基地。

en:
Fezzan is the chain of oases threading south-western Libya between the sand seas of the Sahara, where dry wadi beds in the north hold wells and date palms. The Garamantes made these oases a pivot of trans-Saharan trade from the fifth century BC, sending north the gold, ivory and slaves of the Sahel; after their empire faded, Kanem and then Bornu stretched suzerainty over the wadi towns. Arab Banu Sulaym tribes drifted in during the thirteenth century, and Murzuk grew around its oasis fortress on the road from Tripoli and Ghadames to the Kawar salt mines and Bornu beyond. In 1444 the oases were ruled by local lords in the shadow of Bornu, and in the later fifteenth century they became tributaries of the Hafsid sultan in Tunis.

The Awlad Muhammad gave Fezzan its lasting dynasty. Tradition credits its founding to Muhammad al-Fasi, a sharif at the head of a caravan, whom the Murzuk lords invited to rule in the early sixteenth century as Tuareg raids worsened; from the mid-1500s the sultans of his line held Fezzan with Murzuk as their capital. The town became the greatest slave market of the central Sahara, outstripping Ghat and Ghadames by the end of the century. The Ottoman pashas of Tripoli invaded as early as 1574, but their grip stayed loose: the sultans of Murzuk kept internal rule, and Turkish garrisons appeared only on occasional marches south, as in 1679–1682 and 1718. Tripoli finally made its claim good and annexed the sultanate in 1813.
zh:
费赞是串起利比亚西南部沙海的一串绿洲，北方的干河谷中藏着水井和椰枣林。公元前5世纪起，加拉曼特人便把这些绿洲经营成跨撒哈拉贸易的枢纽，将萨赫勒的黄金、象牙和奴隶运往北方；他们的帝国衰落后，卡涅姆、继而博尔努的宗主权延伸到这些河谷城镇。13世纪，阿拉伯巴努·苏莱姆部落陆续迁入，穆尔祖克依托绿洲上的要塞兴起，正处在的黎波里、古达米斯通往卡瓦尔盐矿和远方博尔努的大道上。1444年，各绿洲由本地首领统治，仍笼罩在博尔努的阴影之下；15世纪后期，他们又向突尼斯的哈夫斯苏丹称臣纳贡。

奥拉德·穆罕默德王朝给了费赞持久的统治世系。相传创立者穆罕默德·法西是带领商队的圣裔，16世纪初图阿雷格袭扰加剧，穆尔祖克的地方首领请他出面主政；自16世纪中叶起，他的后裔以穆尔祖克为都城统治费赞。这座城成为撒哈拉中部最大的奴隶市场，到16世纪末已盖过加特和古达米斯。奥斯曼的黎波里帕夏早在1574年就攻入费赞，但控制始终松散：穆尔祖克苏丹保留内部统治，土耳其驻军只在偶尔南下时出现，如1679至1682年和1718年。的黎波里最终把宗主权落到实处，于1813年吞并了这个苏丹国。

en:
The Jufra is the chain of oases – Sokna, Hun and Waddan – that breaks the desert in the heart of Libya, where the road south from the coast at Sirte turns into Fezzan. Medieval geographers knew the district simply as the land of Waddan, its oldest town: Arab raiders first reached it under Busr ibn Artat in 642, extracting only tribute, and Uqba ibn Nafi placed a garrison there in 666–667; by the mid-thirteenth century Waddan was the northernmost point held by the kings of Kanem. The eleventh-century geographer al-Bakri described Hun as a crowded oasis of vast palm groves and many springs, a market a day's journey from Waddan on the road to Sabha. In 1444 the oases kept their own shaykhs and their Berber speech, Sokna still speaking its Eastern Berber tongue, and lived by dates, livestock and the passing caravans.

With the rise of the Awlad Muhammad in the early sixteenth century, the Jufra became the northern march of the Fezzan sultanate, whose authority at its height ran from Sokna to Murzuk. The Ottoman pashas of Tripoli passed through these oases on the marches south that began in 1574, and the Jufra shared the sultanate's loose tributary life until Tripoli made it part of its eyalet together with Fezzan in 1813.
zh:
朱夫拉是苏克纳、洪、瓦丹一线绿洲的总称，嵌在利比亚腹心的沙漠中，海岸锡尔特南往费赞的道路正是从这里折向南方。中世纪的地理学家只把这一带称作「瓦丹之地」——瓦丹是其中最古老的城镇：阿拉伯袭掠军642年在布斯尔·本·阿尔塔特率领下首次抵达，仅取贡赋而退，666至667年欧格白·本·纳菲又在此设下驻军；到13世纪中叶，瓦丹已是卡涅姆君王控制的最北据点。11世纪的地理学家白克里记载，洪是个人口稠密的绿洲，椰枣林广袤、泉水众多，是瓦丹往塞卜哈道上的商站，距瓦丹仅一日路程。1444年，各绿洲由本地谢赫治理，仍保留柏柏尔人的语言——苏克纳说的是东柏柏尔方言——居民靠椰枣、牲畜和过路商队为生。

16世纪初奥拉德·穆罕默德王朝兴起后，朱夫拉成为费赞苏丹国的北部边区，其极盛时的辖地北起苏克纳、南至穆尔祖克。1574年起，的黎波里的奥斯曼帕夏们南下征讨时屡屡取道这些绿洲；朱夫拉也随苏丹国过着松散的朝贡生活，直到1813年与费赞一道被的黎波里并入其行省。

en:
Ghadames, the Roman Cydamus, is a palm oasis on the Tripolitanian edge of the Sahara, hard by where Tunisia, Algeria and Libya meet. Lucius Cornelius Balbus captured it for Rome in 19 BC, a Severan garrison held it around 202, and a Byzantine bishopric sat there before the Arab conquest of 667. Its spring, Ain al-Faras, was shared among the townsfolk in fixed water-turns, and around it rose a walled ksar of seven Berber clans, each with its own quarter. Muslim merchants made the oasis a chief station of the trans-Saharan road, with caravans running south to Timbuktu and Ghadamsi leather famed across the Maghreb. In 1444 it was loosely tied to the Hafsid rulers of Tunis and the Djerid oases, its merchant clans managing most of their own affairs.

In the sixteenth century Ghadames passed under the Ottoman regency of Tunis, and in the eighteenth under the pashas of Tripoli, when the ksar reached its greatest prosperity. An Ottoman castle was raised, and the slave market and the caravan trains linked the Mediterranean shore with Timbuktu and the lands beyond.
zh:
古达米斯是撒哈拉边缘的的黎波里塔尼亚境内一处椰枣绿洲，毗邻突尼斯、阿尔及利亚和利比亚三地交界。公元前19年，卢修斯·科尔内利乌斯·巴尔布斯为罗马攻取此地，约202年塞维鲁王朝曾在此驻军，拜占庭时期这里设有主教区，直到667年阿拉伯人征服。绿洲中心的马泉按固定份额分给全城，泉边建起有城墙的堡寨，七个柏柏尔氏族各居一区。穆斯林商人把这里经营成跨撒哈拉大道上的主要驿站，商队南下廷巴克图，古达米斯皮革也风行整个马格里布。1444年，它在名义上臣属于突尼斯的哈夫斯王朝和杰里德绿洲，市政大半由本地商人氏族自理。

16世纪，古达米斯转入以突尼斯为中心的奥斯曼行省治下，18世纪改归的黎波里的帕夏，堡寨也在此时臻于鼎盛：奥斯曼城堡拔地而起，奴隶市场和南来北往的商队把地中海沿岸与廷巴克图乃至更南方的土地连在一起。

en:
Thubaqt, the ancient Thubactis, is often identified with the coastal oasis of Misrata, though its exact location is disputed. Misrata takes its name from a branch of the Berber Hawwara whom Ibn Khaldun found on this shore. After the Arab conquest it became a caravan station and a port, its looms famed for carpets, while palms, olives and market gardens crowded the springs. In 1444 the town and its roadstead were held with Tripoli by the Hafsid sultans of Tunis.

Spanish troops seized Tripoli in 1510, and the Knights of St John held the coast from 1530 until Turgut Reis took it for the Ottomans in 1551. Under the Karamanli dynasty, founded in 1711, Misrata grew into a principal mart of the trans-Saharan road, where caravans from Fezzan sold gold, leather and slaves; the harbor at Qasr Ahmad shipped grain and carpets to Egypt and the Levant.
zh:
图巴克特即古代的图巴克提斯，常被比定为米苏拉塔滨海绿洲，但确切位置仍有争议。米苏拉塔得名于柏柏尔豪瓦拉联盟的分支米苏拉塔部落，伊本·赫勒敦曾记载他们住在这段海岸。阿拉伯征服后，这里成为商队驿站和港口，织机以地毯闻名，泉水周围椰枣、橄榄和菜园密布。1444年，城镇和锚地与的黎波里一同处在突尼斯哈夫斯王朝苏丹治下。

1510年西班牙军队攻占的黎波里，1530年起圣约翰骑士团据守这段海岸，1551年图尔古特·雷伊斯为奥斯曼人将其夺取。1711年建立的卡拉曼利王朝治下，米苏拉塔成长为跨撒哈拉商路上的主要商市，费赞来的商队在此出售黄金、皮革和奴隶，盖斯尔·艾哈迈德港则把粮食和地毯运往埃及和黎凡特。

en:
Zuwarah is a Berber fishing town on the coast west of Tripoli, set among salt flats on the edge of the Nafusa country, whose people kept the Ibadi faith when it survived in Libya only here and in the Nafusa mountains. Al-Bakri numbered the Zuwarah among the Berber tribes of this shore, and al-Tijani, visiting in 1306 to 1309, found two villages: Little Zuwarah, near extinction after repeated attacks by European corsairs who came for salt, and Greater Zuwarah, the walled Qutayn among the palms. In 1444, some two thousand strong, it lived by salt, fish, lime and gypsum and owned only a loose allegiance to Tunis.

Leo Africanus found Qutayn's walls crumbling a century later, its people dreading the corsairs, yet under the Karamanli pashas after 1711 Zuwarah revived: treaties with the Italian republics opened the salt trade, its roadstead of Tibuda became one of the coast's busiest salt harbours, and an Ottoman-built port carried its fish and esparto to Tripoli.
zh:
祖瓦拉是的黎波里以西的柏柏尔渔镇，四周盐沼环绕，地处奈富塞山区边缘；当伊巴德派在利比亚仅存于奈富塞山与祖瓦拉时，这里的居民仍守着这一信仰。贝克里已把祖瓦拉人列为这段海岸的柏柏尔部落之一，提贾尼1306至1309年间到访时见到两座村庄：小祖瓦拉因前来取盐的欧洲海盗屡次袭击而濒临消亡，大祖瓦拉则是椰枣林中带围墙的库泰因。1444年，全镇约两千人，靠盐、鱼、石灰和石膏为生，对突尼斯只维持松散的臣属。

一个世纪后，利奥·阿非利加努斯见到库泰因城墙倾颓，居民终日担心海盗来袭。1711年以后的卡拉曼利帕夏时代，祖瓦拉重获生机：与意大利诸共和国订立的条约打开了盐的销路，蒂布达锚地成为海岸最繁忙的盐港之一，奥斯曼时期修建的新港把鱼和阿尔法草运往的黎波里。

en:
Sfax was founded in 849, when the Aghlabid emir of Kairouan had a walled town raised beside the old Byzantine watch-post of Taparura. Its deep olive groves made the city's fortune: by the tenth century the geographer Ibn Hawqal saw Sfax oil shipped to Egypt, Sicily and the Christian ports of the north, while herds were ferried to graze on the Kerkennah islands. The Normans of Sicily held the town from 1148 to 1156, when a citizens' revolt ended the occupation in the wars that soon brought in the Almohads; Hafsid rule followed from the early thirteenth century. Its merchants sailed to Genoa and Marseille as well as Damascus and Cairo. In 1444, in the long Hafsid peace of Abu 'Amr 'Uthman, Sfax was the busiest port of the Tunisian south, girdled by walls and famous for olive oil and fish.

The Ottoman–Habsburg struggle shattered that order. Hayreddin Barbarossa brought the town into the Ottoman camp in 1534; after years of Spanish domination Dragut Pasha conquered it in 1551, and the Ottoman fall of Tunis in 1574 made the new rule permanent. Andalusi exiles of the Nasrid collapse joined its merchant and scholarly families. Under the Muradid deys Sfax became a corsair port and a city of learning: its ulama founded madrasas while its captains cruised against Christian shipping, not least that of the Knights of Malta. Venice fought the fleet at Ras al-Makhbaz in 1747 and bombarded the town four times in 1785–86. Under the Husainid beys the Great Mosque received its mihrab in 1758 and its enlargement was completed in 1783; from 1776 the new Frankish suburb by the sea housed Jewish and Christian merchants, proof that oil and trade still paid for the city's wars.
zh:
849年，凯鲁万的艾格莱卜埃米尔下令在拜占庭旧哨站塔帕鲁拉旁筑起一座城墙环绕的城镇，是为斯法克斯。成片的橄榄林造就了它的富庶：到10世纪，地理学家伊本·豪盖勒已见到斯法克斯的橄榄油远销埃及、西西里和北方基督教港口，畜群则被渡海送到盖尔甘奈岛放牧。1148年西西里诺曼人占领此城，1156年市民起义终结了占领，随后的战乱把穆瓦希德人引入突尼斯；13世纪初起斯法克斯归入哈夫斯王朝。这里的商人既航行到大马士革和开罗，也航行到热那亚和马赛。1444年，在阿布·阿慕尔·奥斯曼治下的漫长太平岁月里，斯法克斯已是突尼斯南部最繁忙的港口，城墙环抱，以橄榄油和渔产闻名。

奥斯曼与哈布斯堡的争夺打破了旧秩序。1534年，「红胡子」赫伊尔丁把斯法克斯带入奥斯曼阵营；经过多年西班牙人的控制，德拉古特帕夏于1551年攻克此城，1574年奥斯曼攻陷突尼斯后，新统治就此稳固。奈斯尔王朝覆灭后出走的安达卢斯人，也加入了这里的商人和学问世家。穆拉德迪伊们治下，斯法克斯成了海盗港与学术之城：乌理玛兴办经学院，船长们出海劫掠基督教船只，尤以马耳他骑士团为对手。威尼斯舰队1747年在拉斯马克赫兹之战中来攻，又在1785至1786年间四次炮轰此城。侯赛因王朝的贝伊们给了城市新的营建：大清真寺1758年立新米哈拉布，扩建工程1783年完工；1776年起，海边新建的法兰克区住满犹太与基督教商人——橄榄油和贸易，仍在为这座城市的战争买单。

en:
El Kef crowns a cliff of the Jebel Dyr in the High Tell, the strong hill country of northwestern Tunisia. Carthaginians knew it as Sicca and the Romans as Sicca Veneria, a favoured colony and one of the chief Christian cities of Africa; Arab raiders reached it in 688, and in time the rock fortress became al-Kaf. In 1444 it was the dominant stronghold and market of the Hafsid western march, on the road from Tunis to Constantine, where the wool clipped from the flocks of the Tell was gathered and the governors sent from Tunis watched the frontier.

Ottoman rule made the rock a garrison town: its kasbah was built in 1600 to hold a permanent garrison, and ramparts were added in 1740. El Kef gave the Husainid dynasty its founder and its second bey, for Hussein ibn Ali was born there in 1675 and Ali Pasha on 30 June 1688. The armies of the Regency of Algiers fought beneath its walls in 1694 and again on 8 July 1705, and from 10 to 23 June 1756 the bey of Constantine routed the Tunisians outside the town; El Kef was taken and pillaged. The medina also holds the shrine of its patron saint, Sidi Bou Makhlouf.
zh:
卡夫雄踞在突尼斯西北上泰勒山区代尔山的崖顶。迦太基人称之为西卡，罗马人称之为西卡维内里亚，曾是受优待的殖民城，也是阿非利加最重要的基督教城市之一；688年阿拉伯攻略军兵临此地，这座崖顶要塞后来以「卡夫」（岩石）之名见称。1444年，它是哈夫斯王朝西部边疆首屈一指的要塞和集镇，地处突尼斯城通往君士坦丁的大道上，泰勒高原羊群剪下的羊毛在此集散，突尼斯城派来的长官据此监视西方边境。

奥斯曼统治把这座岩城变成驻军重镇：1600年筑起城堡，常驻守军，1740年又加修环城壁垒。侯赛因王朝的开创者与第二任贝伊都出生在卡夫——侯赛因·伊本·阿里生于1675年，阿里帕夏生于1688年6月30日。阿尔及尔摄政的军队两度兵临城下：一次在1694年，一次在1705年7月8日；1756年6月10日至23日，君士坦丁贝伊在城外击溃突尼斯军，卡夫城破遭劫。旧城中还奉有本地守护圣人西迪·布·马赫卢夫的陵寝。

en:
Bizerte is the northernmost harbour of Africa, set where a narrow channel joins the open sea to a wide inland lake. Phoenician settlers called it Hippo, 'the harbour', and the Greeks knew it as Hippo Diarrhytus, 'Hippo divided by the water', after that same canal; wheat from the plains behind it and the fish of the lake long filled its quays. Arab conquest reached the town in the seventh century and it passed with Carthage into Muslim Ifriqiya. In 1444 it was a northern port of the Hafsid sultans, its roadstead open alike to the traders and the raiders of the central Mediterranean.

By the early sixteenth century Bizerte was a nest of corsairs. On 25 April 1519 a Genoese fleet under Andrea Doria destroyed the flotilla of Kaïd Ali off Pianosa, near Elba, and broke the port's rise as a corsair base. Barbarossa took it in 1534 with La Goulette and Tunis, and the troops of Charles V took it back in 1535; the Ottomans made themselves masters of it in 1574, and it again became a lair of corsairs who preyed on the shipping of Sicily, Italy, France and Venice. On 4 and 5 July 1770 a French fleet under Rafélis de Broves bombarded Bizerte with the other Barbary ports in reprisal for the corso, sinking its vessels and freeing French captives.
zh:
比塞大是非洲最北端的港口，一条狭窄的水道把外海与宽阔的潟湖连在一起。腓尼基定居者称之为希波，意为「港湾」；希腊人因这条水道称它为希波·迪亚里托斯，意为「被水分开的希波」。城后平原的小麦和湖中的渔产长久以来堆满码头。阿拉伯征服在7世纪抵达此地，它随迦太基一起归入穆斯林的伊夫里奇亚。1444年，它是哈夫斯苏丹治下的北方港口，锚地向中部地中海的商人和劫掠者一同敞开。

到16世纪初，比塞大已成海盗巢穴。1519年4月25日，安德烈亚·多里亚率领的热那亚舰队在厄尔巴岛附近的皮亚诺萨海面歼灭卡伊德·阿里的船队，遏止了这座港口崛起为海盗基地。1534年，巴巴罗萨·海雷丁连同比塞大、拉古莱特和突尼斯城一并夺取；1535年，查理五世的军队将其攻占；1574年奥斯曼人成为这里的主人，比塞大再度成为柏柏尔海盗的据点，劫掠西西里、意大利、法国和威尼斯的商船。1770年7月4日至5日，拉费利斯·德·布罗夫率领法国舰队，为报复海盗行径炮轰比塞大及其他柏柏尔港口，击沉港内船只，解救了被俘的法国人。

en:
Touggourt — Tugurt, 'the gateway', in Berber — is the chief oasis of the Oued Righ, the old river course that runs north from the Sahara toward Biskra. A Berber town founded by the Banu Ifren, it passed under Rustamid, Hammadid and Hafsid overlordship before 1414, when Sulayman ibn Rajab founded the Berber sultanate of the Banu Djellab, who were to rule for more than four centuries. Its walled ksar rose amid the palm gardens, and as a Sunni city at the desert gate it drew to itself the pilgrim and gold caravans coming from the west, at the expense of Ibadi Ouargla. In 1444 the young sultanate, famed above all for its dates, was one of the prosperous independent principalities of the northern Sahara.

In 1552 Salah Raïs, beylerbey of Algiers, marched south with the Beni Abbès to enforce tribute: his cannon battered Touggourt for three days before the assault, when the town was sacked and its fourteen-year-old sultan carried off. The Banu Djellab returned as vassals of Algiers through the bey of Constantine. Repeated revolts brought fresh Ottoman expeditions under Yusuf Pasha in 1646, Salah Bey in 1783 and 1789, and Ahmed al-Mamluk in 1818, and in quieter years the oasis answered also to the Arab chieftains of the Zab. In 1805 Sultan Ibrahim built the great mosque in the old ksar.
zh:
图古尔特在柏柏尔语中意为「门户」，是里格古河谷（Oued Righ）的首要绿洲，这条古河道由撒哈拉向北通往比斯克拉。这座柏柏尔城镇最初由伊夫伦人建立，曾先后臣属罗斯图姆、哈马德和哈夫斯诸王朝；1414年，苏莱曼·伊本·拉杰卜建立柏柏尔人的杰拉布家族苏丹国，王朝在此延续四百余年。带城墙的堡寨坐落在椰枣林间，作为沙漠门户上的逊尼派城市，它把西来的朝圣客与黄金商队吸引到自己这边，令伊巴德派的瓦尔格拉相形见绌。1444年，这个立国方三十年、以椰枣闻名的苏丹国已是北撒哈拉富庶的独立公国之一。

1552年，阿尔及尔贝勒贝伊萨拉赫·赖斯联合贝尼·阿巴斯的军队南下索贡：火炮轰城三日，第四日发起强攻，城破后遭洗劫，年仅十四岁的苏丹也被掳走。杰拉布家族随后复位，作为阿尔及尔的附庸，经由君士坦丁的贝伊称臣。此后一次次反叛引来新的奥斯曼讨伐：1646年优素福帕夏、1783和1789年萨拉赫贝伊、1818年艾哈迈德·马穆鲁克先后兵临城下；在相对平静的年月，绿洲还要听命于扎卜地区的阿拉伯酋长。1805年，易卜拉欣苏丹在旧堡寨内建起大清真寺。

en:
The Mzab is a stony plateau, the Chebka or 'net', whose dry watercourses converge on the Oued Mzab. Its people are Zenata Berbers, and when the Fatimids overthrew the Ibadi Rustamids of Tahert in 909, the refugees first settled at Sedrata near Ouargla and then withdrew into this harsh chebka, raising walled ksour around fortress-mosques: El Atteuf in 1012, Ghardaïa in 1053, Bounoura in 1065 and Beni Isguen in 1321, with Melika completing the pentapolis. Azzaba councils of scholars governed each town, and from the fourteenth century the Mzab was a caravan crossroads for wool, dates, salt and arms, its merchants established as far as Tunis and Algiers. In 1444 the five towns formed a self-governing Ibadi confederacy under the loose suzerainty of the Zianid sultans of Tlemcen, with Ghardaïa at its head.

In the seventeenth century dissidents from Ghardaïa founded two more ksour to the north, El Guerrara and Berriane, making the seven cities of later tradition. Under the Ottoman regency of Algiers the Mzab kept its own laws in exchange for allegiance and tribute: a Mozabite amin represented the confederacy at the dey's court, while Mozabites ran much of Algiers's caravan trade and its public baths, mills and butcheries. In 1792 Salah Bey of Constantine persuaded the dey to annex the Mzab to his beylik, but the towns refused the new taxes, and Dey Hassan Pasha soon reversed the annexation and appointed a new bey at Constantine. Left to itself, the confederacy entered the nineteenth century still ruled by its scholars.
zh:
姆扎卜是一片石质高原，沟壑交错如网，故称「舍卜卡」，意为网，众多干河都汇入姆扎卜干河。居民为扎纳塔柏柏尔人。909年法蒂玛王朝攻灭伊巴德派的罗斯图姆王朝后，塔赫尔特的遗民先在瓦尔格拉附近的塞德拉塔落脚，随后退入这片严酷的石漠，在一座座要塞式清真寺周围建起带城墙的堡寨：阿塔夫（El Atteuf）建于1012年，盖尔达耶（Ghardaïa）建于1053年，布努拉建于1065年，贝尼伊斯甘（Beni Isguen）建于1321年，与迈利卡合称「五城」。每座城由贤达组成的阿扎巴会议治理；14世纪起，姆扎卜成为羊毛、椰枣、盐和武器的商队枢纽，商人远至突尼斯和阿尔及尔。1444年，五城组成自治的伊巴德派联盟，以盖尔达耶为首，仅在名义上臣属于特莱姆森的扎扬王朝苏丹。

17世纪，盖尔达耶的异议者在北方另建盖拉拉（El Guerrara）和拜尔扬（Berriane）两座堡寨，成为后世所称的七城。奥斯曼阿尔及尔行省时期，姆扎卜以称臣纳贡为代价保有自己的法律：联盟派驻一名阿明代表于德伊宫廷，姆扎卜商人则主持阿尔及尔的大部分商队贸易，经营公共浴场、磨坊和肉铺。1792年，君士坦丁的萨拉赫贝伊说动德伊把姆扎卜并入他的贝伊辖区，但各城拒绝新税，德伊哈桑帕夏很快撤销成命，另换贝伊。这个由学者治国的联盟便在自治状态下步入19世纪。

en:
The Hodna is a closed steppe basin between the Tell and the Saharan Atlas, its centre the great salt flat of the Chott el-Hodna, where nomads grazed their flocks and gathered salt. Its northern gateway is M'Sila, founded by the Fatimids in the tenth century as al-Muhammadiya and built by Ali ibn Hamdun al-Andalusi to hold the Zab: a double-walled city of canals and orchards that eclipsed ancient Tobna, where the poet Ibn Rashik was born. In 1007 Hammad ibn Buluggin, once its governor, built his capital at the Qal'a of the Banu Hammad nearby and carried off its people, and the Hilalian raids impoverished both cities. M'Sila revived in the wake of Béjaïa under the Almohads and Hafsids, and Ibn Khaldun and his brother served there in the mid-fourteenth century, but Arab tribes then overran the Hodna and the city shrank to a small market. In 1444 it lies on the marches between Tunis and Tlemcen, tributary to the Hafsids but in the hands of its tribes.

Through the Ottoman centuries M'Sila remained one of the small inland garrison towns of the Regency, held by a Turkish detachment with the support of tribal sheikhs. Its weekly market drew the nomads of the Hodna and the Ouled Naïl country, who brought salt from the chott together with wool and livestock, and in the eighteenth century a Kouloughli quarter took shape in the town. Above the plain the abandoned ruins of the Qal'a of the Banu Hammad still overlooked the old trade road from the Zab to the sea.
zh:
霍德纳是泰勒阿特拉斯山脉与撒哈拉阿特拉斯山脉之间的封闭草原盆地，中央是大片盐滩霍德纳盐沼，游牧人在此放牧、采盐。盆地的北部门户是姆西拉：它10世纪由法蒂玛王朝建立，取名穆罕默迪耶，由阿里·伊本·哈姆敦·安达卢西主持修筑以镇守扎布。这是一座双重城墙、渠水环绕、果园成片的城市，取代古城托卜纳成为一方重镇，诗人伊本·拉希克就出生在这里。1007年，曾任姆西拉总督的哈马德·伊本·布卢金在附近兴建新都贝尼·哈马德的卡拉城，把居民迁走，希拉勒部族的袭掠又使两城一同凋敝。阿尔摩哈德与哈夫斯时期，姆西拉借贝贾亚的繁荣一度复苏，14世纪中叶伊本·赫勒敦兄弟还曾在此任职，但阿拉伯诸部随后席卷霍德纳，城市缩为一座小集镇。1444年，它处在突尼斯与特莱姆森之间的边地，名义上向哈夫斯王朝纳贡，实权却在部落手里。

整个奥斯曼时期，姆西拉始终是摄政国的内陆小戍城之一，靠一支土耳其驻军和若干部落长老维持。每周的集市吸引霍德纳和乌列奈尔地方的游牧人，他们带来盐沼的盐、羊毛和牲畜；18世纪，城中还形成了一个库鲁格里人街区。平原上方，贝尼·哈马德的卡拉城自被废弃后的废墟依旧俯瞰着从扎布通向海边的古商路。

en:
Titteri is the high country south of Algiers, where Médéa lies in a fold of the Tellian Atlas between the Ouarsenis and the Blida Atlas, among grain fields and orchards. Bologhine ibn Ziri refounded the town in the tenth century, and it lay in the Sanhaja land of the Lamdiyya until the Almohads broke the old Berber confederations; a Zayyanid governor then held it for Tlemcen from the days of Yaghmoracen, and Leo Africanus found it a fertile place grown rich on trade. In 1444 the future seat of the beys was a caravan stage on the Zayyanid kingdom's southern flank, where the Tell met the road to the Sahara.

Arudj Barbarossa occupied Médéa in 1517, the year after taking Algiers, and quartered Turkish infantry and Andalusian refugee cavalry in the town. Under the Regency of Algiers, Hassan Pasha created the Beylik of Titteri in 1548, with Médéa as its seat; the beys kept house in the Dar el-Bey while a hakim governed the townspeople. As the last great market for caravans coming up from the south, exchanging Tell grain for highland and desert goods, it held a modest prosperity through the Ottoman centuries. In 1819 Mostefa Boumezrag succeeded as bey and took up residence in the Dar el-Bey.
zh:
提泰里是阿尔及尔以南的山乡，麦迪亚坐落在泰勒阿特拉斯山脉的一处洼地，介于瓦尔塞尼斯山与卜利达阿特拉斯山之间，四周遍布麦田和果园。这座城镇于10世纪由博卢金·伊本·齐里重建，本是桑哈贾人拉姆迪耶部落的土地，直到穆瓦希德王朝打碎旧的柏柏尔部落联盟；此后从亚格穆拉桑时代起，便有扎扬王朝的总督代表特莱姆森驻守此城，利奥·阿非利加努斯见到的是一座靠贸易致富的丰饶之城。1444年，这座后来的贝伊首府是扎扬王国南缘的商队驿站，泰勒山区与通往撒哈拉的道路在此相接。

奥鲁奇·巴巴罗萨1516年夺取阿尔及尔，次年占领麦迪亚，在城中驻扎土耳其步兵和流亡自西班牙的安达卢西亚骑兵。在阿尔及尔摄政国体制下，哈桑帕夏于1548年设立提泰里贝伊里克，以麦迪亚为首府；贝伊们住在达尔贝伊宫，城市民政则由哈基姆掌管。作为南方商队进入泰勒山区前最后的大市集，这里以谷物交换高原与沙漠货物，在整个奥斯曼时期维持着不算显赫却殷实的繁荣。1819年，穆斯塔法·布梅兹拉格接任贝伊，入主达尔贝伊宫。

en:
The Saoura is the wadi born where the Guir and the Zouzfana meet at Igli, carrying a long avenue of date palms between the Grand Erg Occidental and the oases of the Touat. Its first ksar, Oulad Mehdi, was founded by Mehdi ben Youssef and Ali ben Moumen, who brought date-palms from the Draa, and families from Figuig and Tamantit settled beside them in the 14th century. In 1444 the villages lived from their palms and the caravan road that ran from Sijilmasa toward the Touat, within the sphere of Tafilalt.

In 1593 the rebel marabout Abu Mahali settled at Béni Abbès, the beginning of the revolt that later carried him to Marrakesh. Long raids by the Ghenanma drove the villagers to appeal to the sultan in Fez, whose makhzen troops defeated the raiders; with the marabout Mohamed Ben-Abdeslam they then built a single strong ksar in the heart of the palm grove, called Béni Abbès, early in the 18th century.
zh:
苏奥拉（萨乌拉）是吉尔河与济兹法纳河在伊格利汇流后形成的干河，河谷中椰枣成林，夹在西部大沙漠与图瓦特绿洲群之间。最早的堡村奥拉德·迈赫迪由迈赫迪·本·优素福和阿里·本·穆明建立，椰枣苗是他们从德拉河带来的，14世纪又有来自菲吉格和塔曼提特的人家迁来。1444年，各堡村以椰枣和商路为生，处在塔菲拉勒特的势力范围内，商路从锡吉勒马萨南通图瓦特。

1593年，起兵的马拉布特阿布·马哈利在贝尼阿巴斯落脚，他的叛乱正是从此发端，后来一度攻入马拉喀什。甘南玛部落长年袭掠，村民被迫向非斯的苏丹申诉，苏丹的马赫曾军队击败了袭掠者；随后他们在马拉布特穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜勒·萨拉姆主持下，于18世纪初在椰枣林中心建起一座坚固的统一堡村，即贝尼阿巴斯。

en:
The Dahra is a wooded coastal ridge of the western Tell Atlas, near the mouth of the Chelif and the harbor of Mostaganem. Its Zenata Berber population included Maghraoua and Banu Ifren groups, and Mostaganem served the Maghraoua confederation as its seaward gate. In the eleventh century al-Bakri described a walled town sustained by fertile fields and cotton, and Yusuf ibn Tashfin built the Bordj El-Mehal fortress there in 1082. Yaghmoracen brought the region into the Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen; after a Marinid interlude in 1334-1335 it returned to Zayyanid rule under Abu Hammu Musa II. Catalan merchants kept a consulate in the port during the fourteenth century. In 1444, therefore, Mostaganem was a fortified Muslim outlet of Tlemcen, linking Mediterranean shipping with Berber villages that supplied grain, cotton and woven cloth.

The Spanish imposed a capitulation on Mostaganem in 1511, but the Ottoman corsair powers of the Algerian coast took the town in 1516, and Hayreddin Barbarossa enlarged and fortified it as a commercial and privateering rival to Spanish Oran. Inland at Mazouna, the Dahra held the seat of the western beylik until 1701. Andalusian refugees expelled from Spain settled the countryside, planted mulberries and developed silk work and other crafts, while in the early eighteenth century the hills supplied cereals, cattle, honey and wax. After Oran passed from Spain to Algiers in 1792, part of Mostaganem's population was moved to the new western capital. By 1821 the town remained a walled coastal market bordering a grain-growing Berber hinterland.
zh:
达赫拉是泰勒阿特拉斯山脉西部林木覆盖的沿海山脊，靠近谢里夫河口与穆斯塔加奈姆港。当地居民属泽纳塔柏柏尔人，包括马格拉瓦和巴努伊夫伦等支系，穆斯塔加奈姆则是马格拉瓦联盟通向海洋的门户。11世纪，巴克里记载这里是一座有城墙的城镇，依靠肥沃农田和棉花维生；优素福·伊本·塔什芬于1082年在此修建迈哈勒堡。叶格穆拉辛后来把这一地区纳入扎扬王朝的特莱姆森王国，1334—1335年经历马林王朝短暂统治后，又在阿布·哈穆·穆萨二世治下回到扎扬政权手中。14世纪时，加泰罗尼亚商人在港内设有商馆。因此在1444年，穆斯塔加奈姆是特莱姆森一座设防的穆斯林港口，把地中海航运与供应谷物、棉花和布匹的柏柏尔村落连接起来。

1511年，西班牙迫使穆斯塔加奈姆接受降约，但阿尔及尔沿海的奥斯曼海盗势力于1516年夺取此城，海雷丁·巴巴罗萨随后扩建工事，把它建成对抗西班牙属奥兰的商业与私掠港口。在达赫拉内陆，马祖纳在1701年之前一直是西部贝伊辖区的治所。被西班牙驱逐的安达卢西亚难民在乡野定居，种植桑树并发展丝织和其他手工业；18世纪初，山地还大量输出谷物、牲畜、蜂蜜和蜂蜡。1792年奥兰从西班牙转入阿尔及尔之手后，穆斯塔加奈姆的一部分居民被迁往这座新的西部首府。到1821年，穆斯塔加奈姆仍是一座有城墙的沿海集市，毗邻出产谷物的柏柏尔腹地。

en:
The Ouarsenis is the great cedar-clad massif of the Tellian Atlas between the Chelif valley and the Sersou plateau, its highest point, Sidi Amar, climbing to 1,985 metres; the Berber name means 'nothing higher'. No Roman road ever entered it, and its Zenata Berbers, Aït Ifran, Maghraoua and their kin, kept their mountain villages through Almohad and Zayyanid times. The Marinid triumph of 1337 brought Hilalian Arabs of the Ouled Ryah to the Chelif lowlands, but the highlanders stayed Berber-speaking small farmers and herders. In 1444 the Zayyanid sultans of Tlemcen claimed a loose overlordship over a massif that ran its own affairs.

Title deeds of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries record the old order of self-governing hamlets, the boccas, whose families held gardens on the lower ground and forest above, grazed their flocks and worked the fields in common labour-bands, the touiza; each hamlet kept the shrine of its saint, where the people feasted in spring and autumn. Zenata Berber lived on in the high villages long after Arabic had taken the plains.
zh:
瓦尔塞尼斯是泰勒阿特拉斯山脉的大山块，雪松林覆盖，横亘在谢利夫河谷与塞尔苏高原之间，最高峰西迪阿马尔峰海拔近两千米，柏柏尔语地名意为「无出其右者」。罗马人的道路从未深入山中，扎纳塔系的艾特伊夫伦、马格拉瓦等柏柏尔部落经历穆瓦希德与扎扬王朝的更迭，始终保有自己的山村。1337年马林王朝的征服把希拉勒系的奥拉德·里亚赫阿拉伯人带到谢利夫低地，但山里人仍是操柏柏尔语的小农和牧人。1444年，特莱姆森的扎扬苏丹对这片山乡只有松散的宗主权，山中的事由山民自己做主。

16、17世纪的地契记录着旧秩序：自治的小村布卡，各家在低地经营果园、在高处保有山林，放牧畜群，并以被称作图伊扎的集体互助共耕田地；每个村子都有本村圣徒的拱北，村民春秋两季在那里聚宴。阿拉伯语席卷低地之后，扎纳塔柏柏尔语仍在高山村落中沿用。

en:
Kasdir is the steppe and mountain edge south-east of Tlemcen, where the Ksour range, the westernmost chain of the Saharan Atlas, runs down towards the oasis country of Figuig. Spring-fed valleys held fortified ksour of Zenata Berbers, sedentary gardeners who kept their Berber tongue, while Berber and Arab nomads pastured great flocks over the grasslands between; their camels, sheep and horses served the caravan trade between the Tell and the Touat. In 1444 the Zayyanid sultan in Tlemcen claimed the country's allegiance, but so far from the city its villages and tents answered to their own elders and sheikhs.

In the seventeenth century the nomad camps drew together around the descendants of the marabout Sidi Shaykh, whose preaching, dated to about 1651, bound the date-growers of the Gurara and the Zenata villages into the confederation of the Awlad Sidi Shaykh. Their zawiyas lined the desert roads, and their caravans traded as far as the Touat and Timbuktu. Praying and trading in the name of their saint, they paid tribute at times to the Regency of Algiers and at others inclined to the Sharifian sultans of Morocco, and so held this dry borderland through the rest of the Ottoman age.
zh:
卡斯迪尔是特莱姆森东南方的草原山缘地带，撒哈拉阿特拉斯山脉最西端的古苏尔山在此向菲吉格绿洲方向迤逦而降。泉水滋养的谷地里散落着扎纳塔柏柏尔人的设防村落古苏尔，定居的园户保留着柏柏尔语；柏柏尔与阿拉伯游牧民在其间的草地上放牧大群牲畜，骆驼、绵羊和马匹服务于泰勒山区与图瓦特之间的商队贸易。1444年，特莱姆森的扎扬苏丹在此保有宗主权，但离城市如此遥远，村落和帐篷实际听命的都是本地长老与谢赫。

17世纪，各游牧群体逐渐聚集到圣徒西迪·谢赫后裔的周围：约1651年，西迪·谢赫的传道把古拉拉的枣农和扎纳塔村落结合为奥拉德·西迪·谢赫联盟。他们的扎维叶遍布沙漠商道，商队远行至图瓦特和廷巴克图。联盟以圣徒的名义聚礼和贸易，时而向阿尔及尔摄政国纳贡，时而倒向摩洛哥的谢里夫苏丹，就这样在奥斯曼时代余下的岁月里掌控着这片干旱的边地。

en:
Ouarzazate originally named a wadi and oasis basin below the High Atlas, where the road from Marrakesh through the Tizi n'Tichka pass and Aït Benhaddou descends toward the Draa, Dadès and the Sahara. In 1444 there was still no fixed urban centre, only a caravan crossing; medieval geographers knew the country as Haskoura land, where Berber clans pastured flocks in the mountains and cultivated the irrigated hollows. The ksar of Aït Benhaddou, fortified since Almoravid times, guarded the Ounila valley road.

The Saadian rise made this crossing a dynastic link. In the sixteenth century Sheikh Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Abdallah al-Wizkiti al-Warzazi held the qasba that Arabic sources call Taourirt and helped the Saadis establish control over Sous and the Draa; his daughter Lalla Masuda married Muhammad al-Shaykh, became mother of Ahmad al-Mansur, and remained influential until her death in 1591. The Aït Atta confederation coalesced in the nearby Jbel Saghro in the same century and was recorded by Marmol in 1571 as the “Ytata.” Their expansion into oases and passes brought a first major clash with the forces of Moulay Ismail in 1678. The surviving Kasbah Taourirt was built in the seventeenth century by the local Imzwarn family, while the present earthen houses at Aït Benhaddou likewise date mainly from that century, the ksour continuing to police caravan traffic through the valleys.
zh:
瓦尔扎扎特本指大阿特拉斯山南缘的干河谷与绿洲盆地。从马拉喀什经提什卡山口和阿伊特·本·哈杜南下的道路，由此通向德拉河、达德斯河谷与撒哈拉。1444年这里还没有固定城邑，只是一处商队渡口；中世纪地理学家把这一带称为哈斯库拉人的地方，柏柏尔氏族在山地放牧，在有灌溉的洼地耕作。自穆拉比特时代起已设防的阿伊特·本·哈杜村，则扼守着乌尼拉河谷道路。

萨阿德王朝兴起时，这处通道变成王朝纽带。16世纪，谢赫阿布·阿拔斯·艾哈迈德·本·阿卜杜拉·维兹基提·瓦尔扎齐据有阿拉伯文献所称的陶里尔特卡斯堡，帮助萨阿德人确立对苏斯和德拉的控制；他的女儿拉拉·穆萨嫁给穆罕默德·谢赫，是艾哈迈德·曼苏尔的母亲，直到1591年去世前仍保有影响力。同一世纪，阿伊特·阿塔联盟在附近的萨格罗山形成，1571年已被马尔莫尔以「伊塔塔」之名记载。他们向绿洲和山口扩张，1678年与穆莱·伊斯梅尔的军队发生第一次大规模冲突。现存陶里尔特卡斯堡由当地伊姆兹瓦伦家族建于17世纪，阿伊特·本·哈杜现存土坯房屋也多成于此时；这些堡寨继续控制着穿过河谷的商队交通。

en:
Oujda commands the Angad plain on the road between Fez and Tlemcen, beneath the Beni Iznassen hills. The Zenata chief Ziri ibn Atiyya founded it in 994 as a garrison town. Yusuf ibn Tashfin's Almoravids took it in 1079, and later Almohad rulers repaired its walls. In 1271 the Marinid sultan Abu Yusuf Yaqub destroyed Oujda after defeating Yaghmorasan of Tlemcen; when Marinid forces reconquered the site in 1296 they rebuilt the walls, a palace and the Great Mosque. Abu al-Hasan campaigned through it again around 1325. In 1444 it was a contested Muslim frontier market on the western approaches to the Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen, sustained by overland traffic and the flocks of its Berber hinterland, with Marinid Fez still a looming power to the west.

From the sixteenth century Oujda stood between Morocco's Sharifian dynasties and the Ottoman Regency of Algiers, and its allegiance followed the fighting around Tlemcen. Moulay Isma'il, who ruled Morocco from 1672 to 1727, made it an Alaouite stronghold, adding fortifications and garrisons to secure his eastern border. After his death succession crises loosened the court's hold on this distant march. Alaouite forces retook the town in 1795, after which Oujda was incorporated into the Moroccan realm rather than remaining a pawn of the Tlemcen frontier.
zh:
乌季达位于贝尼·伊兹纳桑山地南缘的安加德平原，控扼非斯与特莱姆森之间的道路。泽纳塔首领齐里·伊本·阿提耶于994年建立这座驻军城镇。优素福·伊本·塔什芬的穆拉比特王朝在1079年夺取此地，后来的穆瓦希德统治者又修缮城墙。1271年，马林苏丹阿布·优素福·叶尔孤白击败特莱姆森的叶格穆拉辛后摧毁乌季达；1296年马林军队再占此地，重建城墙、宫殿和大清真寺。阿布·哈桑约在1325年再度由此进军。1444年时，这里是扎扬王朝特莱姆森王国西缘反复争夺的穆斯林边境集市，依靠陆路商队和柏柏尔腹地的羊群维生，西方马林王朝治下的非斯仍是强大威胁。

16世纪起，乌季达夹在摩洛哥的谢里夫王朝与奥斯曼阿尔及尔摄政政权之间，归属随特莱姆森一带的战局变化。1672年至1727年统治摩洛哥的穆莱·伊斯梅尔把这里建成阿拉维王朝的要塞，增设工事和驻军以守护东部边界。他死后，继承危机削弱了宫廷对这片遥远边地的控制。1795年，阿拉维军队收复乌季达，此后这里并入摩洛哥王国，不再只是特莱姆森边境上任人易手的棋子。

en:
The Draa is Morocco's longest river, running 1,100 kilometres from the High Atlas to the Atlantic. Its valley is a chain of oases and walled ksour watered by irrigation canals, whose caravan stations linked the Atlas lands with the routes to Timbuktu. At its heart lay the district of Tagmadert, where a family of sharifs claiming origin at Yanbu had settled early in the fourteenth century. By the mid-fifteenth century the Marinid sultans of Fez had little hold over the south, and in 1444 the Draa oases governed their own affairs through local chiefs and Sufi brotherhoods, while caravans still passed north to Marrakesh and the Sous and south into the Sahara.

In 1510 the Tagmadert sharif Muhammad al-Qa'im was called to the Sous to lead its tribes against the Portuguese, and his sons Ahmad al-Araj and Muhammad al-Shaykh went on to found the Saadian dynasty. In the 1540s Tuareg raiders sent by Askia Ishaq I of Songhai swept through the valley when the two powers quarrelled over the salt mines of Taghaza. Muhammad al-Shaykh, who styled himself al-Drawi, 'the man of the Draa', founded the town of Tagmadert in 1550. In 1591 the Saadian army mustered in the Draa oases and marched across the desert to overthrow Songhai and take Timbuktu. Under Moulay Ismail the valley became an appanage ruled from 1701 by sons of the sultan with the title khalifa. Tagmadert never recovered from the troubles of the early nineteenth century: it was probably sacked by the Aït Atta Berbers, as Sijilmasa was in 1818, and only an irrigation canal kept its name alive.
zh:
德拉河是摩洛哥最长的河流，从大阿特拉斯山奔流1100公里注入大西洋。河谷中是一连串靠灌溉渠引水的绿洲和设防城堡村，绿洲商站把阿特拉斯山区与通往通布图的商路连接起来。河谷中心是塔格马德特地区，14世纪初便有一支自称源自延布的圣裔家族定居于此。到15世纪中期，非斯的马林王朝苏丹对南方几乎无力掌控，1444年的德拉绿洲由本地首领和苏菲教团自行其是，商队仍往返于北方的马拉喀什、苏斯与南方的撒哈拉之间。

1510年，塔格马德特的圣裔穆罕默德·卡伊姆被请往苏斯，领导各部族抵抗葡萄牙人，他的儿子艾哈迈德·阿拉杰和穆罕默德·谢赫后来开创了萨阿德王朝。1540年代，桑海与摩洛哥为塔加扎盐矿反目，桑海的阿斯基亚·伊沙克一世派图阿雷格骑手袭掠了河谷。自称「德拉人」的穆罕默德·谢赫于1550年建起塔格马德特城。1591年，萨阿德大军在德拉绿洲集结，穿越沙漠攻灭桑海、夺取通布图。穆莱·伊斯梅尔在位时，河谷成为封邑，1701年起由苏丹的众子以哈里发的头衔统辖。塔格马德特没能从19世纪初的动乱中恢复：它可能像1818年的西吉勒马萨一样遭艾特阿塔柏柏尔人洗劫，只剩一条灌溉渠还留着这个名字。

en:
Meknes grew from a string of Miknasa Berber villages, the miknāsat al-zaytūn or 'Meknes of the olives', settled on the Saïss plain around the tenth century. The Almoravids planted a fortress called Tagrart beside them, and the Nejjarine Mosque of that garrison survives. The Almohads razed the town in the twelfth century, then Caliph Muhammad al-Nasir rebuilt its walls, Grand Mosque and aqueduct at the start of the thirteenth. The Marinids took Meknes in 1244, Abu Yusuf Ya'qub added its first kasbah in 1276, and Abu al-Hasan founded the Bou Inania Madrasa in 1336; under the later Marinids the city was a favoured residence of princes and viziers. In 1444 Meknes is therefore a prosperous but secondary town of Marinid Morocco, ringed by the olive groves and grain fields of the Saïss and overshadowed by the capital at Fez a day's ride to the east.

The Saadian age passed Meknes by, its sultans spending their wealth on Marrakesh. The first 'Alawi sultan, Moulay Rashid, made his brother Moulay Isma'il governor here, and on Rashid's death in 1672 Isma'il chose Meknes as the new capital, away from the hostile ulama of Fez. For fifty-five years tens of thousands of workmen and Christian captives raised an imperial palace-city four times the size of the old medina: the Dar al-Kebira was finished in 1679, new walls and gates ringed the town, the Bab Berda'in Mosque went up in 1709, and the Heri al-Mansur granary and stables followed between 1721 and 1725, guarded by the sultan's black slave army. Isma'il died in 1727, and Meknes died as a capital with him: his sons fought over the throne, the great Bab al-Mansur gate was completed only in 1732 by Moulay Abdallah, and the Lisbon earthquake of 1755 shattered much of the palace quarter. Later 'Alawi sultans kept a residence here and were buried beside Isma'il, but by 1821 Meknes is above all the market centre of Morocco's richest farmland, its imperial grandeur slowly crumbling beyond the gates.
zh:
梅克内斯起于米克纳萨柏柏尔人的一连串村落——10世纪前后散落在赛斯平原上的「橄榄米克纳萨」。穆拉比特人在村落旁建起塔格拉尔特要塞，当年驻军所建的纳贾林清真寺历经岁月尚存。12世纪穆瓦希德人将该城夷平，13世纪初哈里发穆罕默德·纳赛尔又重修城墙、大清真寺和引水渠。马林王朝1244年攻取梅克内斯，阿布·优素福·叶尔孤白1276年添建第一座城堡，阿布·哈桑1336年创办布伊纳尼亚学院；马林王朝后期，这里是王公和维齐尔偏爱的驻地。因此1444年的梅克内斯是马林摩洛哥一座富庶却次要的城市，四周是赛斯平原的橄榄林与麦田，东边一日骑程之外的都城非斯令它相形见绌。

萨阿德时代的荣光与梅克内斯无缘，苏丹们把财富都花在马拉喀什。阿拉维王朝开国之君穆莱·拉希德让弟弟穆莱·伊斯梅尔在此担任总督，1672年拉希德死后，伊斯梅尔选梅克内斯为新都城，以避开非斯怀有敌意的乌理玛。五十五年间，数万名工匠和基督徒战俘建起一座比老麦地那大四倍的帝王宫城：大达尔宫1679年完工，新城墙与城门环绕全城，巴布·贝尔达因清真寺1709年落成，1721至1725年又建成赫里·曼苏尔粮仓与马厩，统由苏丹的黑奴禁军戍守。1727年伊斯梅尔去世，梅克内斯的都城地位也随之终结：诸子争位，宏伟的曼苏尔门迟至1732年才由穆莱·阿卜杜拉完工，1755年里斯本大地震又震毁大片宫区。此后的阿拉维苏丹仍在此保留宫殿，并葬在伊斯梅尔身旁，但到1821年，梅克内斯首先是摩洛哥最富庶农田的商贸中心，帝王气象在城门之外日渐倾颓。

en:
Tadla is the broad plain between the High and Middle Atlas, watered by the Oum Er-Rbia; its name is Amazigh for 'the sheaf', a tribute to the wheat raised here since the early Islamic conquests. The Almohads kept a fortress at the river crossing where Kasba Tadla now stands, and a son of Caliph Abd al-Mu'min governed the district from it. Under the later Marinids the march was neglected, for it lay on the road between Fez and Marrakesh: rebels sheltered in its hills and the old kasbah fell to ruin. In 1444 Tadla is thus a buffer country between the Marinid sultan in Fez and the Hintata emirs of Marrakesh, peopled by semi-nomadic Tadla tribes whose wealth lies in cattle, grain and the pastures fed by the streams off the Atlas.

Tadla gave its name to the treaty that ended the first Saadi–Wattasid war: in 1527 the two dynasties divided Morocco along the Oum Er-Rbia, the north to the Wattasids and the south to the Saadis. Fighting resumed within three years, and in 1536 the Saadis routed the Wattasid army at Wadi al-'Abid, on the southern edge of the plain, opening the road to a unified Morocco. The district returned to obscurity under Saadian rule until Moulay Isma'il, who planted guich tribal garrisons on the march, settling Guettaya, Samguet and Ait Ma'dane Arabs there and merging them with the original Tadla people into the Ait Rob'a confederation. On the Almohad ruin he raised the great rectangular Kasbah of Tadla, complete with stores, mosque and secret stairways, to command the crossing; his son Ahmad ad-Dhahabi added the houses and the bridge over the Oum Er-Rbia later credited to the Portuguese. In 1821 Tadla remains what its geography made it, Morocco's granary and cattle country, held for the 'Alawi sultan by the guich tribes encamped around the kasbah.
zh:
塔德莱是大阿特拉斯山与中阿特拉斯山之间的广阔平原，乌姆赖比阿河穿流其间；其名在柏柏尔语中意为「麦穗」，足见自伊斯兰早期征服起这里便是产麦之地。穆瓦希德王朝在今日塔德莱堡所在的渡口设有要塞，哈里发阿卜杜勒·穆明的一个儿子曾坐镇其中统辖该区。马林王朝后期，这条地处非斯与马拉喀什之间的通道无人经营：叛乱者藏身群山，旧堡渐成废墟。因此1444年的塔德莱是夹在非斯马林苏丹与马拉喀什欣塔塔埃米尔之间的缓冲地带，居民是半游牧的塔德莱诸部，财富全靠牲畜、麦禾和山间诸溪滋养的牧场。

塔德莱的名字与终结萨阿德—瓦塔斯第一次战争的和约连在一起：1527年，两朝以乌姆赖比阿河为界瓜分摩洛哥，河北归瓦塔斯、河南归萨阿德。三年后战火重燃，1536年萨阿德人在平原南缘的瓦迪阿比德击溃瓦塔斯军队，打通了统一摩洛哥之路。萨阿德时代该区重归沉寂，直到穆莱·伊斯梅尔在这条边陲通道屯驻军屯部落：他把盖塔亚、萨姆古特和艾特·迈丹三支阿拉伯人迁来，与土著塔德莱人合并为艾特·鲁巴阿同盟；又在穆瓦希德废墟上修起长方形的塔德莱大堡，内有仓廪、清真寺和暗道，扼守渡口。其子艾哈迈德·宰海比添建了民居和乌姆赖比阿河大桥——此桥后来被误传为葡萄牙人所造。1821年的塔德莱仍是其地理所塑造的模样：摩洛哥的谷仓与牧地，由城堡周围扎营的军屯部落替阿拉维苏丹把守。

en:
Dukkala is the low coastal plain between Safi and Anfa, the grain country of the Doukkala, a Berber tribal confederation that rebelled against the Almohads and was crushed by Caliph Abd al-Mu'min around 1160; he settled Hilalian Arab tribes on their land, and the Doukkala were Arabised thereafter. Al-Idrisi knew the roadstead off their shore as Mazighan, where an old tower stood above the anchorage. In 1444 the plain was held by its tribes under the fading rule of the Marinids, sowing grain with no town yet on the Mazighan shore.

In summer 1514 the Portuguese built a four-towered citadel at Mazighan, the work of the brothers Diogo and Francisco de Arruda, and the place became Mazagão. When John III gave up Safi and Azemmour in 1541, he made Mazagão the strengthened heart of Portugal's Moroccan positions, ringed from 1542 with walls able to hold several thousand settlers. It outlasted every other Portuguese fortress in the country until 1769, when Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah's army closed on it: the garrison evacuated under terms and blew up its bastions as the Moroccans entered, leaving the place al-Mahdouma, 'the Ruined'. In May 1815 the Doukkala joined the Abda in revolt and drove out their governor, in the unrest of Moulay Slimane's later years.
zh:
杜卡拉是萨菲与安法之间的沿海低地平原，住着柏柏尔人的部落联盟杜卡拉人。他们曾起兵反抗穆瓦希德王朝，约1160年被哈里发阿卜杜勒·穆敏击败，后者把希拉勒系阿拉伯部落安置在他们的土地上，杜卡拉人此后逐渐阿拉伯化。伊德里西把这一带海岸外的锚地记作马齐甘，锚地旁立着一座旧塔。1444年，在马林王朝的衰微统治下，谷物平原由杜卡拉各部落自行其是，马齐甘海岸还没有城镇。

1514年夏，葡萄牙人在马齐甘筑起一座四角带塔楼的城堡，由迪奥戈·德·阿鲁达和弗朗西斯科·德·阿鲁达兄弟主持修筑，此地得名马扎甘。若昂三世1541年放弃萨菲和艾宰穆尔后，把马扎甘经营为葡萄牙在摩洛哥各据点的核心，1542年起环筑厚墙，可容纳数千居民。它比葡萄牙在摩洛哥的其他所有要塞都撑得更久，直到1769年穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉苏丹的大军兵临城下：守军依约撤离，却在摩洛哥人入城时引爆棱堡，城市只剩残垣断壁，得名迈赫杜马，意为「被毁者」。1815年5月，杜卡拉人响应阿卜达人起事，驱逐了自己的总督，时当穆莱·苏莱曼晚年的动乱。

en:
The Haha, or Iḥaḥan, are a Shilha confederation of Masmuda Berber clans occupying the Atlantic face of the western High Atlas, from the bay of Mogador south toward the Sous. Their mountains and narrow valleys raised goats, barley, millet and honey, while argan trees covered the drier slopes. In 1444 this coast belonged to the Marrakesh-centered world of southern Morocco; Mogador itself was still an anchorage sheltered by its offshore island, taking its name from the holy man Sidi Mogdoul.

In 1506 King Manuel I of Portugal ordered Castelo Real de Mogador built on the shore, but local Regraga resistance took it in 1510. During the rest of the century Spanish, English, Dutch and French ships tested the anchorage, which served sugar and molasses exports as well as corsairs; Isaac de Razilly's French colonists landed briefly on Mogador island in 1629 and then withdrew. In 1760 the Alawid sultan Mohammed bin Abdallah entrusted Théodore Cornut and Ahmed al-Inglizi with laying out a new port, Essaouira, designed for foreign merchants and caravans from Marrakesh. Jewish trading families were encouraged to settle, and by the late eighteenth century Mogador had become Morocco's leading commercial port.
zh:
哈哈又称伊哈哈恩，是什卢赫人中的马斯穆达柏柏尔部落联盟，占据西阿特拉斯山面向大西洋的坡地，北起摩加多尔湾，南抵苏斯方向。山地和狭谷出产山羊、大麦、黍和蜂蜜，较干旱的坡地上遍布阿甘树。1444年，这段海岸属于以马拉喀什为中心的摩洛哥南部世界；摩加多尔本身还只是一处受近海岛屿屏障的锚地，其名来自圣徒西迪·莫格杜勒。

1506年，葡萄牙国王曼努埃尔一世下令在岸边修建摩加多尔王家城堡，但1510年即被当地雷格拉加兄弟会的抵抗力量夺取。此后一个世纪，西班牙、英格兰、尼德兰和法国船只反复试探这处锚地，蔗糖、糖蜜出口与海盗活动在此交织；1629年，伊萨克·德·拉齐利率领的法国殖民者曾短暂登上摩加多尔岛，随后撤离。1760年，阿拉维苏丹穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉委托泰奥多尔·科尔尼和艾哈迈德·因吉利齐规划新港索维拉，使其服务于外国商人和从马拉喀什前来的商队。苏丹还鼓励犹太商贸家族定居，到18世纪末，摩加多尔已成为摩洛哥最重要的商港。

en:
Ouargla is the great palm oasis of the Wadi Mya basin in the central Sahara, watered by underground courses and once the largest palm grove in Algeria. The Banu Wargla, a clan of Zenata Berbers who had migrated from the Tlemcen country, built the old ksar and adopted Ibadi doctrines in the eighth century. After the Fatimids destroyed Tahert in 909, Rustamid exiles made nearby Sedrata their new capital; a Hammadid raid at the end of the eleventh century then drove the people to build the present town, and Sedrata's destruction in the thirteenth century left Ouargla the sole centre of the region. A Hafsid sultan of Tunis entered the city and raised its great mosque, and Ibn Khaldun called it 'the gate of the desert', through which Mzab merchants carried their goods to the land of the blacks. In 1444 the oasis, still mostly independent under its own Ibadi lords, lived on the caravan trade in gold and slaves.

In 1552 Salah Raïs of Algiers marched beyond Touggourt against Ouargla, whose sultan fled with four thousand horsemen to El Golea, leaving the town to its merchants and marabouts; the oasis submitted and pledged tribute. Ouargla was attached to the Beylik of the East at Constantine, the Friday prayer was said in the name of the Ottoman caliph, and a makhzen tribe, the Said Atba, held the region for the regency. Its trade faded soon after, as the Sudan caravans were diverted to Touggourt, and the old 'gate of the desert' entered the eighteenth century a quiet, half-forgotten oasis.
zh:
瓦尔格拉是撒哈拉腹地米耶河（Wadi Mya）盆地中的大绿洲，靠地下暗河供水，椰枣林曾为阿尔及利亚之冠。柏柏尔扎纳塔人的一支巴努·瓦尔格拉从特莱姆森一带迁来，建起旧堡寨，并在8世纪皈依伊巴德派。909年法蒂玛王朝摧毁塔赫尔特后，罗斯图姆遗民在附近的塞德拉塔另立新都；11世纪末哈马德王朝的一次袭击迫使居民修筑今城，13世纪塞德拉塔被毁，瓦尔格拉遂成为这一带唯一的中心。突尼斯的哈夫斯苏丹曾入城并敕建大清真寺，伊本·赫勒敦称它为「沙漠之门」，姆扎卜商人带货南下黑非洲都要从此经过。1444年，绿洲仍由本地伊巴德派首领统治，大半独立，靠黄金与奴隶的商队贸易为生。

1552年，阿尔及尔的萨拉赫·赖斯越过图古尔特进兵瓦尔格拉，当地苏丹率四千骑兵逃往古莱阿（El Golea），城中只剩商人与隐士；绿洲最终称臣纳贡。瓦尔格拉被划归君士坦丁的东部贝伊辖区，周五聚礼以奥斯曼哈里发的名义诵读，麦赫赞部落赛义德·阿特巴替行省镇守此地。但它的贸易很快衰落，通往黑非洲的商队改走图古尔特，这座昔日的「沙漠之门」到18世纪已是一处安静、近乎被遗忘的绿洲。

en:
The port of Susa—Arabic Sūsa, French Sousse—covers the ruins of Hadrumetum, a Tyrian foundation older than Carthage which grew to be the second city of Roman Africa and capital of Byzacena. The Vandals sacked it in 434, the Byzantines retook and refortified it in 534, and the conquest of Uqba ibn Nafi left it in ruins. The Aghlabids built Susa beside them and made it their chief port: the Ribat, fortress and lighthouse in one, bears an inscription of 821 from the emir Ziyadat Allah I and marble plundered at the fall of Malta in 870, and in 827 their fleet sailed from this roadstead to begin the conquest of Sicily. A Sicilian-Norman fleet under George of Antioch stormed the town on 1 July 1148. In 1444 Susa was the first port of the Hafsid Sahel, its weavers famous for Sūsī silk and linen stuffs and for the ready-made shuqqa robes sold across the Mediterranean.

After Mahdia declined in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, Susa led the towns of the Sahel, with some 15,000 inhabitants. A joint Spanish-Maltese assault was beaten back with heavy loss in 1537, and with the Ottoman conquest of 1574 the town passed into the Regency of Tunis, its seamen joining the Barbary corso. In 1722 the old Ribat was restored, its sea-facing wings rebuilt. Angelo Emo's Venetian fleet bombarded Susa in 1784 and again in 1785 during a four-year campaign meant to force Hammuda Pasha to rein in his pirates; the walls held, the bey did not yield, and the bombardment settled nothing.
zh:
苏塞（阿拉伯语称苏萨）港城建在哈德鲁梅图姆的废墟之上。这座推罗人建立的古城比迦太基还要古老，后来成为罗马阿非利加的第二大城、拜扎凯纳行省的首府。汪达尔人434年洗劫此城，拜占庭人534年将其收复并重修工事，而欧格白·伊本·纳菲的征服把它夷为废墟。阿格拉布王朝在废墟旁营建苏萨，定为王朝首要军港：集要塞与灯塔于一身的里巴特修道堡中，存有821年埃米尔齐亚达特·安拉一世的铭文，870年马耳他陷落时掠来的大理石也用于堡内；827年，阿格拉布舰队从这片锚地启航，开启征服西西里之战。1148年7月1日，安条克的乔治率领西西里诺曼舰队攻破城池。1444年，苏萨是哈夫斯王朝萨赫勒地区的第一大港，织工以「苏西」丝绸、亚麻织物和远销地中海各地的成衣「舒卡」袍闻名。

15、16世纪马赫迪叶衰落后，苏萨成为萨赫勒诸城之首，居民约一万五千人。1537年，西班牙与马耳他联军的进攻被击退，损失惨重；1574年奥斯曼征服后，城市并入突尼斯摄政区，本地水手也加入柏柏尔海盗的行列。1722年，旧里巴特得到修缮，临海的两翼重建。1784年和1785年，安杰洛·埃莫率领的威尼斯舰队两度炮轰苏萨——这场持续四年的战事意在逼迫哈穆达帕夏约束海盗，然而城墙守住了，贝伊没有屈服，炮击终归徒劳。

en:
Tajarhi is the southernmost oasis of Fezzan, lying on the edge of the Idehan Murzuq dune sea where desert roads from Tripoli and Sirte divide toward the Niger River, Lake Chad and the Sudan. Kanem established its authority over Fezzan in 1258, and Bornu still held Murzuk around 1400, but later in the fifteenth century the oases moved into the Hafsid orbit. In 1444 Tajarhi had no royal court of its own; its wells, date palms and brackish pools made it a watering place for Muslim camel caravans at the threshold of the central Sahara.

By the mid-sixteenth century the Awlad Muhammad dynasty ruled from Murzuk and taxed gold, slaves, cloth and ostrich feathers moving between the Sudan and the Mediterranean. An Ottoman army under Mahmut Bey invaded Fezzan in 1574, but the settlement of about 1626 left the local dynasty in hereditary control of internal affairs under Tripoli's overlordship. Tajarhi remained the last Fezzani station before the long empty crossing toward Niger and Lake Chad. The Karamanli government of Tripoli brought Fezzan under direct rule in 1813. When George Francis Lyon passed through in 1819, he found a lush oasis of date groves and wild ducks on the brackish lakes.
zh:
泰杰尔希是费赞最南端的绿洲，位于迈尔祖格沙漠边缘；从的黎波里和苏尔特南下的道路，在此分别通向尼日尔河、乍得湖和苏丹地区。卡涅姆于1258年在费赞建立统治，约1400年时博尔努仍控制迈尔祖格，但15世纪后期诸绿洲转入哈夫斯王朝的势力范围。1444年的泰杰尔希没有自己的王庭，水井、椰枣林和咸水湖使它成为穆斯林驼队进入撒哈拉腹地前的补给地。

到16世纪中叶，奥拉德·穆罕默德王朝以迈尔祖格为都，对往来于苏丹地区与地中海之间的黄金、奴隶、布匹和鸵鸟羽毛征税。1574年，马赫穆特贝伊率奥斯曼军队入侵费赞，但约1626年达成的安排承认该王朝在臣服的黎波里的前提下世袭管理内部事务。泰杰尔希仍是费赞最后一处驿站，向南便是通往尼日尔和乍得湖的漫长无人沙路。1813年，的黎波里的卡拉曼利政权将费赞改为直接统治。1819年乔治·弗朗西斯·莱昂路过时，看到的是一片椰枣成林、咸水湖上有野鸭的丰茂绿洲。

en:
Djado is an oasis on the stony plateau of the same name, northeast of the Aïr, where the desert road from the Fezzan runs south toward the Kaouar and Bornu. Kanuri tradition credits the Sao people with founding its ksar; others trace the town to Ibadi merchants from Jadu in the Jabal Nafusa, who named it after their hometown. The oases owed allegiance to the mais of Kanem-Bornu from the reign of Dunama Dibalemi (1203–1243), though they often went their own way. In 1444 its Kanuri farmers tended date groves and salt pans, and caravans bound for Bornu watered here under the loose lordship of the Sayfawa dynasty.

In the later sixteenth century Mai Idris Alauma led an army across the desert from Fachi as far as Bilma, and Djado again acknowledged the Sayfawa. As Bornu's power faded in the eighteenth century, Tuareg raiders repeatedly fell on the oasis; its people drifted south to the Kaouar, leaving the old ksar to the sand.
zh:
贾多是同名石质高原上的绿洲，位于阿伊尔山东北方，费赞南下卡瓦尔、博尔努的沙漠商路经由此地。卡努里人的传说把这座堡寨的建立归于萨奥人，也有人认为它由的黎波里西南奈富塞山贾杜城的伊巴德派商人所建，城名也随了故乡。至少从杜纳马·迪巴勒米在位时（1203—1243年）起，这片绿洲便臣属加涅姆-博尔努，但时常自行其是。1444年，城中的卡努里人经营椰枣园和盐池，前往博尔努的商队在此补水，赛法瓦王朝的宗主权相当松散。

16世纪后期，国王伊德里斯·阿劳马率军从法奇穿越沙漠，远抵比尔马，贾多再度臣服于赛法瓦。18世纪博尔努国力衰退，图阿雷格人屡屡袭掠绿洲，居民逐渐南迁卡瓦尔，古城终被黄沙吞没。

en:
Kuumeyay is the land of the Kumeyaay, who in 1444 held the coast from modern Oceanside south beyond the bay of Ensenada and east as far as the Colorado River. The San Diego River parted the Ipai clans to the north from the Tipai to the south, while the Kamia lived in the desert valleys beyond the mountains. Thirty patrilineal clans made up autonomous bands speaking a Yuman tongue: they took fish, shellfish and sea mammals from the kelp beds, gathered acorns in the oak canyons, and their waterside villages held one of the densest native populations on the Pacific coast. At Cosoy, their village on San Diego Bay, no European had yet landed.

Juan Rodriguez Cabrillo sailed the San Salvador and Victoria into that bay on 28 September 1542, named it San Miguel and briefly met its people; Sebastian Vizcaino renamed it San Diego de Alcala early in the following century. In July 1769 the Portola expedition built a presidio on the site of Cosoy, and on 16 July Junipero Serra founded Mission San Diego de Alcala, the first mission in Alta California; Kumeyaay warriors attacked it within weeks. After the mission was moved up the San Diego River, more than six hundred Tipai rose on the night of 4 November 1775, burned it to the ground and killed Father Luis Jayme, California's first Christian martyr. Serra rebuilt it as a fortified settlement, consecrated in October 1776. The church was thrown down by an earthquake in 1803 and stood rebuilt by 1813; in 1821 the land passed from Spain with Mexican independence.
zh:
库米艾（库梅雅）是库梅雅人的土地。1444年，他们据有从今日欧申赛德向南越过恩塞纳达湾、东抵科罗拉多河的海岸。圣迭戈河把北方的伊派氏族与南方的蒂派氏族分开，卡米亚人则住在山脉以东的荒漠谷地里。三十个父系氏族组成互不统属的群体，操尤曼语支的语言：他们在海藻林中捕鱼、采贝、猎取海兽，在橡树峡谷采拾橡子，水畔村庄构成太平洋沿岸人口最稠密的原住民地区之一。他们在圣迭戈湾畔的科索伊村，此时还没有任何欧洲人登陆。

1542年9月28日，胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略率「圣萨尔瓦多号」和「维多利亚号」驶入海湾，将其命名为圣米格尔，并与当地人短暂接触；下个世纪初，塞瓦斯蒂安·比斯卡伊诺把海湾改名圣迭戈·德·阿尔卡拉。1769年7月，波尔托拉远征队在科索伊村旧址建起要塞，7月16日胡尼佩罗·塞拉创立上加利福尼亚的第一座传教所——圣迭戈·德·阿尔卡拉传教所；几周后库梅雅战士便发起进攻。传教所溯圣迭戈河迁址后，六百多名蒂派战士又在1775年11月4日夜起事，将传教所夷为平地，杀死路易斯·海梅神父——加利福尼亚的第一位基督教殉道者。塞拉把它按设防聚落重建，1776年10月重新祝圣。教堂在1803年的地震中倒塌，到1813年重建完成；1821年，这片土地随墨西哥独立脱离西班牙。

en: In the forested ridges north of Pomo country, the Yuki held Round Valley and the mountains about it, while their kin the Coast Yuki lived on the Pacific shore. They called themselves the Ukomno'om, the Valley People; the name Yuki, by which their neighbours knew them, was a Wintu word for foreigner or enemy. Their tongue and Wappo formed the Yukian language family, and they counted by eights, numbering the spaces between the fingers. Bands lived on deer, salmon and acorn mush and gathered in cone-roofed, half-sunken dance houses. In 1444, and still in 1821, neither road nor mission crossed the ranges: the valley and the coast belonged to them alone.
zh: 在波莫之地以北林木丛生的山岭间，尤基人据有圆谷及其周围的山地，同族的海岸尤基人则住在太平洋畔。他们自称乌科姆诺姆，意为「谷地之民」；邻人称呼他们的「尤基」一名，来自温图语，意为外人或敌人。他们的语言与瓦波语共同构成尤基语系，计数采用八进制，数的是手指之间的空隙。各群体以鹿肉、鲑鱼和橡子糊为食，在锥形顶、半地穴式的舞屋中聚会。1444年如此，到1821年依然如此：没有道路或传教团越过分水岭，圆谷与海岸只属于他们自己。

en:
The Tachi are Southern Valley Yokuts of the great Tulare Lake basin, living north and west of the water among reed marshes, sloughs, and the Kettleman Hills. Fed by the Kings, Kaweah, Tule, and Kern rivers, Tulare was historically the largest freshwater lake west of the Mississippi; its fish, birds, roots, islands, and seasonal floods supported an unusually large Native population. The Tachi called the lake Pa'ashi, meaning 'big water'. In 1444 their villages drew on lake fishing, hunting, and acorn gathering, while Yokuts trade carried valley produce, salt, steatite, and obsidian toward the Chumash and other neighbors and marine shells served as money.

Spanish parties first entered the southern San Joaquin Valley in the 1770s, when Pedro Fages crossed the country south of the lake; the Spaniards called the reed beds tulares, from Nahuatl tollin. In 1806 Father José María de Zalvidea rode with the Ruiz expedition in search of mission sites, and Gabriel Moraga's official valley expeditions of 1806–1808 gave the Spanish a fuller knowledge of its rivers. The 1808 party also pursued mission runaways who had taken horses, cattle, and weapons. No mission or pueblo was founded on the Tachi shore, so in 1821 Tulare Lake and its maze of tules remained Yokuts country rather than a settled colonial district.
zh:
塔奇人是南谷约库特人的一支，住在大图莱里湖流域的北岸和西岸，活动于芦苇沼泽、水道与凯特尔曼丘陵一带。图莱里湖由金斯河、卡威亚河、图莱河和克恩河补给，历史上是密西西比河以西最大的淡水湖；湖中的鱼、鸟类、根茎、岛屿和季节性洪水养育了异常众多的原住民人口。塔奇人称该湖为帕阿希，意为大水。1444年，他们的村落以湖中捕鱼、狩猎和采集橡实为生；约库特商路还把谷地物产、盐、皂石和黑曜石带向丘马什等邻人，海贝则充当货币。

西班牙人在1770年代首次进入圣华金谷南部，佩德罗·法赫斯曾从湖泊以南地区穿过；西班牙人把这种芦苇荡称为图拉尔，词源是纳瓦特尔语的托林。1806年，何塞·玛丽亚·德·萨尔维德亚神父随鲁伊斯远征队查勘传教站选址；加夫列尔·莫拉加1806—1808年的官方远征则让西班牙人更了解谷地诸河，1808年的队伍还负责追捕带走马匹、牛只和武器的传教站逃亡者。塔奇人的湖畔没有建起传教站或村镇，因此1821年时，图莱里湖和芦苇迷宫仍是约库特人的土地，而不是已被殖民定居的地区。

en: East of the Wintun plains the land rises from the Sacramento Valley into the pine-clad Sierra Nevada, cut by the Feather and American Rivers: Maidu country. In their tongue maidu means 'person'. In 1444 the Nisenan held the American and Yuba drainages, the Konkow the north fork of the Feather, and the Mountain Maidu its high forks, each valley with its own band. They lived on acorns from fire-tended oak groves, salmon taken on the upstream run and deer from the hills. Their women wove baskets so fine some need a magnifying glass; their men kept the Kuksu cult of the 'big head' dances, shared with the Pomo and Patwin. Through this era no mission rose in the foothills, and the years turned by the Bear Dance and the acorn crop.
zh: 温图人的平原以东，地势从萨克拉门托河谷攀上松林覆盖的内华达山脉，羽毛河与亚美利加河穿行其间，这就是迈杜人的土地。在他们的语言里，「迈杜」就是「人」的意思。1444年，南方支系据有亚美利加河与尤巴河流域，西北支系住在羽毛河北支流的谷地，山地迈杜人住在上游各汊流，每条河谷各有自己的群体。他们以焚烧养护的橡树林所产的橡子、洄游时捕取的鲑鱼和山中的鹿为食；妇女编织的篮子细密到有的要用放大镜才看得清，男子奉行「大头舞」的库克苏崇拜，波莫人和帕特温人也有同样的信仰。整个年代里，山麓没有建起一座传教团，岁月随熊舞和橡子收成轮转。

en: High in the Klamath Mountains, where the Klamath, Shasta and Scott Rivers cut through pine and oak, the Shastan peoples lived beneath the snow peak that bears their name. They were four kindred peoples, the greatest the Kahosadi, or Shasta proper, who called themselves 'plain speakers'; in 1444 their villages rarely held more than a family or two, and wealthy headmen settled disputes with gifts. Spring and autumn brought the salmon runs; deer were driven by fire into ambush, acorns leached into meal, and buckskin garments went downriver in exchange for abalone beads. The Karuk White Deerskin dance set the season when the salmon might be eaten.
zh: 克拉马斯山脉高处，克拉马斯河、沙斯塔河与斯科特河穿松林与橡林而过，沙斯塔语诸族住在后来以他们命名的雪峰之下。他们分为四个同源族群，最大的是沙斯塔本支，自称「言语平实之人」；1444年时村落往往只有一两户人家，富有的头人用馈赠调停纷争。春到秋鲑鱼陆续溯河，人们用火把鹿赶入埋伏，把橡子去涩磨成粉，鹿皮衣顺河而下换回鲍鱼贝珠。何时可以吃鱼，要以卡洛克人的白鹿皮舞为准。

en: Maqlaqs, meaning 'people' in Klamath, names the lake people of the upper Klamath Basin. In 1444 their bands lived at Klamath Marsh, Pelican Bay, the Link River and the Williamson and Sprague valleys, east of the Cascade Range. Winter stores of fish, wocus seeds and roots carried the villages through until the late-March c'waam runs up the Williamson, Sprague and Lost Rivers, marked by the Return of C'waam ceremony. Canoes crossed the marshes, and trails led over the mountains to trade at The Dalles with the Wasco and Wishram. In later centuries horses carried Klamath raiders south against the Achomawi of the Pit River, where captives might be taken as slaves; in 1821 the marsh villages still lay beyond the routes of European fur brigades.
zh: 马克拉克斯（Maqlaqs）在克拉马特语中意为「人」，指上克拉马特盆地的湖人。1444年，各群体住在克拉马特沼泽、鹈鹕湾、林克河以及威廉森河与斯普拉格河河谷，位于喀斯喀特山脉以东。冬天靠储鱼、沃库斯睡莲籽和根茎过活，到三月末夸姆鱼（c'waam）溯威廉森河、斯普拉格河和洛斯特河而上时，人们举行夸姆鱼回归仪式。独木舟穿行沼泽，山路越岭通往达尔斯，与沃斯科人和威什拉姆人贸易。此后几个世纪，马匹传入，克拉马特骑手南下袭击皮特河的阿乔马维人，有时把俘虏收为奴隶；到1821年，欧洲毛皮商队仍未进入这些沼泽村落。

en:
The Kalapuya were not one village but a constellation of independent bands across the Willamette Valley, among them the Tualatin and Yamhill on northern streams and the Santiam, Luckiamute and Chepenefa along central and southern tributaries. In 1444 their seasonal round moved between winter villages, root grounds, hunting camps and fishing weirs. Women dug camas in prairies kept open by regular burning; families gathered hazelnuts, berries, acorns and wapato while men took salmon, deer and elk and shaped obsidian from the eastern ranges into points. Camas, hides and dried meat moved north to Chinookan villages, where they could be exchanged for dried salmon and shell wealth.

The river mouth entered European written records when William Broughton sighted it in 1792, and William Clark entered the Willamette in April 1806 after Native guides pointed out the channel. In 1812 William Wallace and John Halsey established Wallace House, the valley's first fur post, north of the Chemeketa Kalapuya village. They traded with local people and hunted deer and elk to supply Fort Astoria. When the North West Company's Oregon districts passed under Hudson's Bay Company control in 1821, the valley had entered the maritime fur economy, but its villages and burned prairies remained Kalapuya.
zh:
卡拉普亚不是一座村落，而是散布在威拉米特谷地的一系列独立群体，图拉丁、亚姆希尔、桑蒂亚姆、勒基缪特和切佩内法等群体分别住在北部溪流与中南部支流旁。1444年，他们按季节往返于冬村、球根采地、猎营和鱼梁之间。妇女在定期烧荒保持开阔的草地上挖卡马斯球根；家人采集榛子、浆果、橡子和瓦帕托块根，男子捕捞鲑鱼、猎取鹿和麋，并用东方山地的黑曜石打制箭镞。卡马斯球根、兽皮和肉干北运到奇努克人的村落，换取干鲑鱼和贝饰。

1792年，威廉·布劳顿望见威拉米特河口，这条河才进入欧洲文字记录；1806年4月，威廉·克拉克经原住民指引进入威拉米特河。1812年，威廉·华莱士和约翰·哈尔西在切梅克塔卡拉普亚村以北建立华莱士屋，这是谷地第一个毛皮商站。他们同当地人贸易，猎取鹿和麋以供给阿斯托里亚堡。1821年西北公司的俄勒冈商区并入哈德逊湾公司时，谷地已经卷入海洋毛皮经济，但村落和烧荒草地仍属卡拉普亚人。

en:
Umatalum recalls Imatalamłáma, the people of Ímatalam, the village at the mouth of the Umatilla River. In 1444 their villages and seasonal camps followed the Umatilla into the Blue Mountain foothills and along the nearby south bank of the Columbia. Families took salmon on the river and at Wyam, the fishing and trading centre later called Celilo Falls, dug camas and other roots in spring, gathered high-country berries in late summer, and hunted deer and elk on the winter grasslands. Dried salmon, fish oil, obsidian, shells and Plains hides changed hands at Celilo and The Dalles, where Sahaptian river people met Chinookan traders from the lower Columbia.

Horses from Spanish New Mexico reached the Shoshone by 1700 and the neighbouring Nez Perce and Cayuse around 1730; Umatilla bands later kept sizable herds, while their fishing stations and root grounds remained the core of yearly life. On 19 October 1805 Lewis and Clark entered Umatilla territory, and frightened villagers hid until councils with chiefs and the presence of Sacagawea turned the meeting to friendship. In 1818 the North West Company built Fort Nez Percés upriver on Walla Walla land. When the post passed to the Hudson's Bay Company in 1821, the Umatilla mouth stood at the edge of a rapidly widening British fur trade.
zh:
乌马塔卢姆（Umatalum）接近乌马蒂拉人自称伊马塔兰拉马（Imatalamłáma），意为伊马塔兰村人；伊马塔兰村就在乌马蒂拉河汇入哥伦比亚河处。1444年，他们的村落和季节营地沿乌马蒂拉河深入蓝山山麓，也分布在邻近的哥伦比亚河南岸。家人在河上与怀阿姆捕捞鲑鱼，那里后来称塞利洛瀑布，是捕鱼和贸易中心；春天挖卡马斯等球根，夏末到高地采浆果，冬季在草地猎鹿和麋。干鲑鱼、鱼油、黑曜石、贝壳和大平原兽皮在塞利洛与达尔斯易手，萨哈普廷河民与下游的奇努克商人在此相会。

来自西属新墨西哥的马到1700年已传入肖肖尼人，约1730年又传到邻近的内兹珀斯人和卡尤塞人；后来乌马蒂拉各群体也养有大群马，但渔场和球根采地仍是年度生活的中心。1805年10月19日，刘易斯与克拉克进入乌马蒂拉地界，受惊的村民躲了起来，直到他们与酋长会谈、萨卡加维亚在场安抚，会面才转为友好。1818年，西北公司在瓦拉瓦拉人的土地上兴建内兹珀斯堡。1821年该商站转归哈德逊湾公司，乌马蒂拉河口也被卷入迅速扩大的英国毛皮贸易圈。

en:
Aqokulo, or Aqokúlo, was the self-name of the Chemakum, also called the Port Townsend Indians. Their villages lay on the northeastern Olympic Peninsula, between Discovery Bay and Hood Canal, especially on Port Townsend Bay and Port Ludlow Bay. Their Chimakuan language was closely related to Quileute, while sheltered anchorages and the Kah Tai canoe portage placed them at the entrance to Puget Sound. In 1444 they lived from the bays and salmon streams as a distinct people among Klallam and Coast Salish neighbours.

About 400 Chemakum lived on the Quimper Peninsula and along Hood Canal around 1789, when raiding and counter-raiding tied them to wars with the Klallam, Makah, Snohomish, Snoqualmie and Ditidaht. In the summer of 1790 Manuel Quimper and Gonzalo López de Haro, sent by Francisco de Eliza to chart the Strait of Juan de Fuca, became the first known Europeans to map Port Discovery, which they named Puerto Quadra. George Vancouver returned in 1792, naming Discovery Bay and Port Townshend, later Port Townsend. The surveys opened the sound's gateway to European charts, but no foreign fort or town yet stood among the Chemakum villages in 1821.
zh:
阿科库洛（Aqokulo）是切马库姆人（Chemakum）的自称，欧洲人也曾称他们为汤森港印第安人。他们的村落在奥林匹克半岛东北端，介于发现湾与胡德水道之间，尤以汤森湾和勒德洛湾为主。其奇马库安语与奎鲁特语相近，避风锚地和卡泰（Kah Tai）独木舟转运道又使他们地处普吉特湾入口。1444年，他们依托海湾和鲑鱼河流而居，是克拉勒姆人与海岸萨利什邻族之间一支独立族群。

1789年前后，约有400名切马库姆人住在昆珀半岛和胡德水道一带，当时他们正同克拉勒姆、马卡、斯诺霍米什、斯诺夸尔米、迪蒂达特等族交战。1790年夏，弗朗西斯科·德·埃利萨派曼努埃尔·昆佩尔和贡萨洛·洛佩斯·德·阿罗测绘胡安·德富卡海峡；他们是已知最早测绘发现湾的欧洲人，并将其命名为夸德拉港。1792年乔治·温哥华再来，命名发现湾和汤森港。这些勘测把普吉特湾门户绘入欧洲海图，但到1821年，切马库姆村落间仍没有外来要塞或城镇。

en:
The Kwaiailk, q̓ʷay̓áyiɬq in their own language, were the Upper Chehalis, a Southwestern Coast Salish people of the upper Chehalis River. Their autonym derives from q̓ʷayáiɬ, Mud Bay on Puget Sound, pointing to an older presence on that shore as well. Downstream, the river opened toward Grays Harbor and the Lower Chehalis. In 1444 Kwaiailk villages held the fisheries, prairies and canoe routes between the sound and the lower Columbia, a position that made them links in a trade largely handled downriver by Chinookan speakers.

Robert Gray entered Grays Harbor in 1792 and gave weapons and tools to Lower Chehalis people, but no European is recorded reaching the Upper Chehalis before the period ended. Foreign metal and manufactured goods therefore moved indirectly, passing through Chinookan and Lower Chehalis middlemen to Kwaiailk villages rather than arriving with a ship or fort. The Kwaiailk remained the connecting country between Puget Sound and southwestern Coast Salish networks, and their river crossings and trade grounds were still under Indigenous control in 1821.
zh:
夸伊艾尔克人（q̓ʷay̓áyiɬq）即上奇黑利斯人，是西南海岸萨利什人的一支，住在奇黑利斯河上游。其自称来自普吉特湾马德湾的当地名称（q̓ʷayáiɬ），说明他们早年也可能分布在那片海岸；下游则通向格雷斯港和下奇黑利斯人的地方。1444年，夸伊艾尔克村落掌握着海湾与哥伦比亚河下游之间的渔场、草原和独木舟路线，处在贸易网络的连接地带，而河海贸易多由奇努克语族群经手。

1792年，罗伯特·格雷进入格雷斯港，把武器和工具送给下奇黑利斯人，但在本时期结束前，没有欧洲人抵达上奇黑利斯的记载。外来金属器和制造品因此经奇努克人与下奇黑利斯中间商间接转入夸伊艾尔克村落，而非随船只或要塞直接到来。夸伊艾尔克仍是普吉特湾与西南海岸萨利什贸易网络之间的纽带；到1821年，他们的渡口和贸易地仍由原住民掌握。

en: Mámachatpam is the self-name of the Lower Yakama people whose villages and fishing grounds occupied the dry lower Yakima Valley east of the Cascade Range. In 1444 winter houses stood along the Yakima, Naches, Ahtanum, Toppenish and Satus watercourses, while families moved in season to salmon fisheries, camas and root grounds, and upland hunting camps. Dried salmon, hides and later horses linked the valley to Chinookan and other Columbia River traders. The first recorded western visitors were Lewis and Clark, who reached the mouth of the Yakima about 17 October 1805 and recorded the river as Tâpe têtt; the expedition did not ascend the valley. Through 1821 the Mámachatpam still governed their own villages and fishing stations.
zh: 马马查特帕姆（Mámachatpam）是下亚基马人的自称，他们的村落和渔场位于喀斯喀特山脉以东干燥的下亚基马河谷。1444年，人们在亚基马河、纳奇斯河、阿塔努姆溪、托彭尼什溪和萨图斯溪沿岸建有冬屋，并按季节前往鲑鱼渔场、卡马夏等球根植物采集地以及高地狩猎营地。鱼干、兽皮和后来的马匹把这座河谷与奇努克人及哥伦比亚河沿岸的其他交易者联系起来。有记载的最早西方来客是刘易斯与克拉克，他们在1805年10月17日前后抵达亚基马河口，把河名记为塔佩泰特（Tâpe têtt），但并未溯河进入谷地。直到1821年，马马查特帕姆仍由自己的村落和渔场首领管理。

en:
Sqeliz is the land of the Spokane, Interior Salish people of the Spokane, Little Spokane and Latah waterways. In 1444 the Lower, Middle and Upper Spokane bands kept permanent winter villages for three months of the year and moved through salmon fisheries, root grounds and upland hunting camps for the other nine. Their meeting place at the mouth of the Little Spokane drew families who caught and dried salmon, and trade in fish, hides and later horses connected them with Nez Perce, Coeur d'Alene and Columbia River peoples.

The Lewis and Clark Expedition encountered the Spokane in 1805, after which fur traders quickly entered the plateau. Under David Thompson's direction, Jaco Finlay built Spokane House during the winter of 1810–1811 at the Spokane-Little Spokane confluence, the North West Company's farthest post in the Columbia country. John Jacob Astor's Pacific Fur Company opened adjacent Fort Spokane, and Illim-Spokanee traded at both stations. The War of 1812 forced the American post into North West Company hands, and in 1821 the merger with the Hudson's Bay Company placed Spokane House within a new British fur-trading empire.
zh:
斯凯利兹是斯波坎人的土地，他们属于内陆萨利什人，活动在斯波坎河、小斯波坎河和拉塔溪一带。1444年，下、中、上三个斯波坎群体每年有三个月住在固定冬村，其余九个月按季节往返鲑鱼渔场、球根植物采集地和高地猎营。小斯波坎河口的集会地吸引各家族前来捕捞、晾晒鲑鱼；鱼、兽皮以及后来的马匹贸易，把他们与内兹珀斯、科达伦和哥伦比亚河各群联系在一起。

刘易斯与克拉克探险队在1805年遇到斯波坎人，毛皮商人随后很快进入高原。1810年至1811年冬，在戴维·汤普森指导下，雅科·芬利在斯波坎河与小斯波坎河汇流处建立斯波坎屋，这是西北公司在哥伦比亚地区最远的据点。约翰·雅各布·阿斯特的太平洋毛皮公司在旁边开设斯波坎堡，伊利姆—斯波坎尼在两处商站都做买卖。1812年战争迫使美国商站落入西北公司之手；1821年西北公司并入哈德逊湾公司，斯波坎屋也随之纳入新的不列颠毛皮贸易体系。

en:
Palus is the river country of the Palouse, a Sahaptin people of the Columbia Plateau. Their three bands lived along the Palouse, lower Clearwater and Snake rivers, and the village of Pa-luš-sa near the Palouse-Snake confluence gave its name to the whole people. In 1444 families followed the salmon runs, camas and root grounds and upland game, then gathered with Nez Perce, Yakama and Walla Walla relatives to feast, trade and race.

In October 1805 the Lewis and Clark Expedition met the Palus and their chief Kepowhan, presenting a Jefferson peace medal while recording them as a people distinct from the Nez Perce. Horses introduced through the plateau trade had already made the Palus skilled riders. In July 1818 the North West Company began Fort Nez Percés near the Snake's mouth, and that September Donald MacKenzie led a large trapping brigade into Palus and Snake country; his rich catch in July 1819 made the brigades annual. In 1821 the post and trade passed to the Hudson's Bay Company, leaving Palus villages still firmly in the fur economy but under their own leaders.
zh:
帕卢斯是哥伦比亚高原上萨哈普廷语族群帕卢斯人的河谷之地。他们分为三个群体，住在帕卢斯河、克利尔沃特河下游和斯内克河沿岸；帕卢斯河汇入斯内克河处的帕卢萨村（Pa-luš-sa），后来成为全族名称的来源。1444年，各家族随鲑鱼洄游、卡马夏等球根植物的成熟期和高地猎期迁徙，并与内兹珀斯、雅卡马和沃拉沃拉亲属聚首宴饮、贸易和赛跑。

1805年10月，刘易斯与克拉克探险队见到帕卢斯人及其首领克波汉，向他赠送杰斐逊和平纪念章，同时在日志中把帕卢斯人与内兹珀斯人明确区分开来。那时经高原贸易传入的马匹已使帕卢斯人成为熟练骑手。1818年7月，西北公司在斯内克河口附近开始修建内兹珀斯堡；同年9月，唐纳德·麦肯齐率领大型猎队进入帕卢斯与斯内克地区，1819年7月带回丰厚毛皮，使这种狩猎队成为年度行动。1821年，商站和贸易转入哈德逊湾公司之手；帕卢斯村落已深深卷入毛皮经济，却仍由自己的首领掌握。

en:
Boho'inee, also called Pohogwe or Bohogue, was the country of the Fort Hall Shoshone on the upper Snake River Plain. Their winter camps clustered in sheltered bottoms near the place later named Fort Hall; in warmer months families scattered to dig camas and other roots, hunt antelope and mountain game, fish the streams, and travel toward the Wind River country. Bannock-speaking relatives lived and intermarried among them, so the camps were often bilingual rather than parts of one centralized tribe. In 1444 the horse had not yet reached these northern Shoshone bands. People moved on foot and with dogs, built sagebrush and willow lodges, and took their leadership from local family heads.

Horses probably reached the Shoshone in the late seventeenth century, coming north through the Plains and Spanish Southwest. By the early eighteenth century mounted Bohogue bands could ride far east on bison hunts and trade horses to friendly Nez Perce and Flathead neighbors, but by the mid-eighteenth century Blackfoot pressure had pushed Shoshone hunters back toward the mountains. In the autumn of 1810 Andrew Henry's fur trappers wintered on Henry's Fork and built the rough post remembered as Fort Henry; they abandoned it in the spring, and Wilson Price Hunt's Astorians used the empty cabins in October 1811 before attempting the Snake River route. The beaver trade had thus touched the upper plain, yet in 1821 the wintering grounds around Bohogue remained in Native hands.
zh:
博霍伊内又称波霍格维或博霍格，是上斯内克河平原上「霍尔堡肖肖尼人」的地方。他们的冬营聚集在后来称为霍尔堡一带避风的河谷低地；天气转暖后，各家族分散采集卡马夏球茎和其他根块，猎取羚羊与山野猎物，在溪流捕鱼，并远行至温德河地区。说班诺克语的亲族与他们混居通婚，因此营地常有两种语言通行，并不是一个集权部落的分支。1444年时马尚未传到这些北肖肖尼群体，人们靠步行和狗驮运行李，以山艾、柳枝搭棚屋，由本地家族首领维系秩序。

马可能在十七世纪末经大平原和西班牙人控制的西南部传到肖肖尼人中间。到十八世纪初，骑马的博霍格队群已能远赴东方猎野牛，并同友好的尼米普人和弗拉塞德人交易马匹；到十八世纪中叶，黑脚人的压力已迫使肖肖尼猎手退回山地边缘。1810年秋，安德鲁·亨利带领的捕兽者在亨利支流过冬，搭起后来被称为亨利堡的简陋据点，次年春天便将其放弃；1811年10月，威尔逊·普赖斯·亨特率领的阿斯托远征队曾使用这些空屋，随后尝试沿斯内克河水路前行。海狸贸易虽已触及这片上游平原，但到1821年，博霍格周围的越冬地仍掌握在原住民手中。

en:
Kusiutta, better known as Goshute, is the desert country of a Western Shoshone-speaking people west and southwest of Great Salt Lake. Their valleys reached from the Skull, Tooele, and Deep Creek watersheds toward the Snake Valley and the ranges of eastern Nevada. In winter several families gathered in willow-framed wickiups near springs and streams; in summer small parties moved into cooler hills, harvesting pine nuts, grass seeds, roots, insects, rabbits, lizards, and snakes, and taking antelope, deer, or bighorn sheep when opportunity allowed. In 1444 there was no central Goshute chief. Authority belonged to family camps, and survival depended on an exact knowledge of scarce water and seasonal foods.

During the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries mounted Ute and Navajo raiders carried off Goshute captives for the borderlands slave trade, tying these quiet desert valleys to a wider and violent colonial economy. Unlike the Bannock and many Shoshone bands, the Kusiutta did not reshape their life around horses: animals would compete for scarce grass and water and offered little advantage in narrow canyons and steep desert ranges. While mounted hunters and fur companies transformed the plains and plateaus around them, Goshute families still traveled on foot along trails between springs. In 1821 no mission, trading post, or permanent settler occupation had yet entered the Kusiutta heartland, though its isolation was already under pressure.
zh:
戈休特人又称库休塔，是大盐湖以西和西南荒漠中说西肖肖尼语的居民。他们活动的干谷从斯卡尔谷、图埃勒谷和迪普克里克流域一直延伸到斯内克谷及内华达东部诸山脉。冬天，几个家族在泉水和溪流附近的柳骨棚屋聚居；夏天，小队迁入较凉爽的山地，采集松子、草籽、根块和昆虫，捕捉兔、蜥蜴、蛇，有机会也猎取羚羊、鹿或大角羊。1444年时，戈休特人没有统一首领，权威属于各个家族营地；生存依赖对稀缺水源和季节性食物的精确知识。

十八世纪至十九世纪初，骑马的尤特人和纳瓦霍人劫掠者会掳走戈休特人，卖到边疆奴隶市场，使这些平静的荒漠谷地被卷入更广阔而暴力的殖民地经济。同班诺克人和许多肖肖尼队群不同，库休塔人没有围绕马重塑生活：马会争夺稀缺的牧草和饮水，在狭窄峡谷和陡峭荒漠山地中也优势有限。当骑马猎手和毛皮公司改变周围的平原与高原时，戈休特家族仍沿泉间步道徒步迁徙。到1821年，尚无传教站、贸易据点或永久定居者进入库休塔人的腹地，但这种孤立已经开始承受压力。

en:
The Hwalbay, or Hualapai – 'people of the tall pines' – held a hundred-mile stretch of the pine-clad southern rim of the Grand Canyon, from the Colorado River south toward the Cerbat and Hualapai mountains. Their roots lay with the Patayan farming peoples of the river and its side canyons. Three subtribes, the Middle Mountain People of the northwest, the Plateau People of the eastern canyons and the Yavapai Fighters of the south, were divided among seven bands and some thirteen local groups of family villages camped near springs. They planted maize, beans and squash in storm-water washes, hunted deer and bighorn, gathered pine nuts, and followed trails west to the Mohave on the river and east to the Hopi mesas; the Havasupai of Cataract Canyon were their own kin, one band of the Plateau People. In 1444 no European had yet entered their canyons.

In September 1540 a party from Coronado's army led by García López de Cárdenas reached the Grand Canyon's South Rim with Hopi guides, but far to the east, and the Hwalbay canyons went unseen by outsiders for more than two centuries. The first European to enter them was the Franciscan Francisco Garcés, who in 1776 traveled inland from the Mohave villages across Hwalbay land to the Havasupai and on to the Hopi town of Oraibi, where the Hopi turned him back; his diary is the first written description of the Hwalbay. After the Quechan uprising of 1781 destroyed the Spanish missions on the lower Colorado, no friar or soldier came this way again. Horses and a few metal goods filtered in through native trade, and when Mexico inherited Spain's claims in 1821, the Hwalbay still moved freely among their springs, canyons and pine ridges.
zh:
瓦拉佩人自称瓦尔拜（Hwalbáy），意为「高大松树之人」，据有大峡谷南缘松林地带约一百英里长的一段土地，北起科罗拉多河，南抵塞尔巴特山和瓦拉佩群山。他们是科罗拉多河及其支峡古代帕塔扬农耕人群的后裔，分为三支：西北的中部山地人、东部峡谷的高原人和南方的亚瓦派战士，三支之下又分七个群体、约十三个地方小集团，各家族在泉眼附近结成小村。他们在雨后涨水的旱谷里种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎鹿和大角羊，采集松子，沿小径西行与河畔的莫哈维人往来，东去霍皮人的台地贸易；卡特拉克特峡谷的哈瓦苏佩人本是他们的亲族，原属高原人中的一支。1444年时，还没有欧洲人进入过这些峡谷。

1540年9月，科罗纳多麾下加西亚·洛佩斯·德·卡德尼亚斯率一队士兵由霍皮向导带到大峡谷南缘，但他们到达的是远在东边的一段，瓦拉佩人的峡谷此后两个多世纪仍不为外界所见。第一个走进这些峡谷的欧洲人是方济各会修士弗朗西斯科·加尔塞斯：1776年，他从莫哈维人的村落出发，穿过瓦拉佩土地到达哈瓦苏佩人处，再东行至霍皮人的奥拉伊比镇，遭霍皮人拒绝后折返；他的旅行日记是关于瓦拉佩人最早的文字记载。1781年克尚人起义摧毁了科罗拉多河下游的西班牙传教站，此后再没有修士或士兵来到这一带。马匹和少量金属器经原住民贸易渐渐流入，到1821年墨西哥继承西班牙的权利主张时，瓦拉佩人仍自由往来于自己的泉眼、峡谷和松林山脊之间。

en:
The Chiricahua Mountains rise from the arid borderlands of Arizona, New Mexico, Sonora and Chihuahua, their canyons and pine ridges forming part of Apacheria. Mogollon and Mimbres villagers had farmed and made pottery in nearby valleys before Southern Athabaskan bands became the region's mounted future. By 1444 small family groups related to the Chiricahua, including the Bedonkohe, moved through this country hunting and gathering, trading and raiding between the mountains and the valleys to the south. The Opata called the range Chiwi Kawi, meaning Turkey Mountain.

Spanish power reached the region only indirectly. Juan de Oñate's occupation of New Mexico in 1598 left the first known Spanish written record of Apache people, and by the late 1600s Chiricahua raiders were striking Sonora for horses and cattle. Mounted raids and Spanish slave-catching reprisals shaped the frontier through the 1700s; presidios and official gifts sometimes checked attacks, but never brought the Chiricahua Mountains under settled colonial rule. When New Spain gave way to Mexico in 1821, the Bedonkohe still controlled the mountain roads.
zh:
奇里卡瓦山脉耸立于亚利桑那、新墨西哥、索诺拉和奇瓦瓦之间的干旱边地，峡谷与松岭构成阿帕奇利亚的一部分。在南阿萨巴斯卡诸群体成为这里日后的骑马居民之前，莫戈永人与明布雷斯农民已在附近河谷耕种制陶。到1444年，包括贝当科赫人在内、与奇里卡瓦诸群体有关的小家族群已穿行此地，在山地和南方河谷之间狩猎采集、贸易或袭掠。奥帕塔人称这片山脉为奇维卡维，意为野火鸡山。

西班牙势力最初只是间接到达这里。胡安·德·奥尼亚特1598年占领新墨西哥时，留下了西班牙人关于阿帕奇人最早的已知文字记录；到17世纪末，奇里卡瓦袭掠者已南下索诺拉夺取马匹和牛群。18世纪，骑马袭掠与西班牙人抓捕奴隶的报复行动塑造了整条边地；要塞和官方赠礼有时能遏制攻击，却从未让奇里卡瓦山脉接受稳固的殖民统治。1821年新西班牙演变为墨西哥时，贝当科赫人仍控制着山中道路。

en:
Hopituh is the mesa country of the Hopi, descendants of the Ancestral Puebloan farmers known in Hopi as Hisatsinom. After the great Pueblo centres of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries were abandoned, villages clustered around the scarce springs on Antelope Mesa and the First, Second, and Third Mesas. Awatovi was founded after about 1300 and became the leading town on Antelope Mesa, while Old Oraibi, established before 1100, was already among the oldest continuously occupied Hopi villages. In 1444 its stone pueblos, kivas, and matrilineal clans depended on careful dry farming and springs; no European soldier or missionary had yet reached Tusayan.

Recorded Spanish contact came in 1540, when Coronado sent Pedro de Tovar west from Zuni to Awatovi. Antonio de Espejo found five Hopi villages and about 12,000 Hopi people in 1582–1583, yet Spain placed no garrison in this remote country. Franciscan friars arrived in 1629 and built a church at Awatovi. Forced labour and persecution of Hopi ceremonies helped draw the mesas into the Pueblo Revolt of 1680: friars were killed and the missions dismantled. When Awatovi accepted a rebuilt church in 1700, warriors from the other villages destroyed it in the winter of 1700–1701, killing the men and taking away the women and children. During the seventeenth century many villages had moved from the mesa feet to the heights for defence, and no Spanish mission or garrison returned before the end of Spanish rule.
zh:
霍皮图是霍皮人的台地之邦；霍皮人是古普韦布洛农民的后裔，霍皮语称这些祖先为希萨齐诺姆（Hisatsinom）。12至14世纪的大型普韦布洛中心被放弃后，村庄聚集到羚羊台地以及第一、第二、第三台地上水源稀少的泉眼周围。阿瓦托维约1300年后建立，后来成为羚羊台地最重要的村镇；1100年以前已经形成的旧奥赖比，则已是霍皮人持续居住的最古老村庄之一。1444年，这里的石砌普韦布洛、基瓦会堂和母系氏族依靠精细的旱作农业与泉水生活，欧洲士兵和传教士都还没有进入图萨扬。

有记载的西班牙接触始于1540年，科罗纳多从祖尼派佩德罗·德·托瓦尔西行抵达阿瓦托维。1582年至1583年，安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍发现五座霍皮村庄和约12000名霍皮人，但西班牙并未在这片偏远之地驻军。1629年，方济各会修士抵达并在阿瓦托维修建教堂。强迫劳役和对霍皮仪式的迫害，使各台地卷入1680年普韦布洛起义：修士被杀，传教站被拆毁。1700年阿瓦托维接纳重建的教堂后，其他村庄的战士在1700年至1701年冬季将其摧毁，杀死村中男子并带走妇女和儿童。17世纪期间，许多村庄为防御已从台地脚下迁到高处；直到西班牙统治结束，传教站和驻军都未能重返霍皮之地。

en:
Shiwinna is the provincial name for the Zuni River valley, homeland of the A:shiwi, who call the country Halona Idiwan'a, the Middle Place. During the fourteenth century their farming settlements drew together into six pueblos, among them Halona and Hawikku, above the river that runs toward the Little Colorado. They irrigated maize fields and traded salt, corn and turquoise along routes around Zuni Salt Lake. In 1444 these independent pueblo towns had no Spanish mission or garrison, guarding a gateway between the Rio Grande pueblos, Hopi mesas and the southern deserts.

In 1539 Estevanico reached Hawikku and was killed there; Marcos de Niza's report turned the pueblo into the supposed Cibola. On 7 July 1540 Coronado's expedition stormed Hawikku, met about 200 Zuni defenders, and took the town in less than an hour. Juan de Oñate visited the country in 1598, and the Franciscans established a mission at Hawikku in 1628. The Zuni burned the church and killed its priest in 1632, and Apache raiders burned it again in 1672. During the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 the Zuni withdrew to Dowa Yalanne and remained there until 1692, then consolidated around Halona, the Pueblo of Zuni. Spanish control stayed thin: only seven Spaniards were recorded living there in 1799, and the Franciscans left in 1821.
zh:
希温纳是祖尼河谷地在本省的名称。这里是祖尼人（A:shiwi）的故乡，他们称这片土地为中央之地（Halona Idiwan'a）。14世纪时，各农业聚落聚合成六座普韦布洛，哈洛纳和哈维库即在其中，俯瞰着流向小科罗拉多河的祖尼河。他们引水浇灌玉米田，并在祖尼盐湖周围的商路上贸易盐、玉米和绿松石。1444年，这些独立的普韦布洛村镇中还没有西班牙传教站或驻军，扼守着格兰德河普韦布洛、霍皮方山与南方沙漠之间的门户。

1539年，埃斯特万尼科到达哈维库并在那里被杀；马科斯·德·尼萨的报告随后把这座普韦布洛说成传说中的西博拉。1540年7月7日，科罗纳多远征队猛攻哈维库，遭遇约二百名祖尼守卫，不到一小时便夺下城镇。胡安·德·奥尼亚特1598年来到此地，方济各会则于1628年在哈维库建立传教站。1632年，祖尼人烧毁教堂并杀死神父；1672年，阿帕奇袭掠者再次焚毁教堂。1680年普韦布洛大起义中，祖尼人退守多瓦·亚兰内山，直到1692年才下山，随后集中到哈洛纳，也就是祖尼普韦布洛。西班牙人的控制始终薄弱：1799年当地记录只有七名西班牙人居住，1821年方济各会传教士撤离。

en:
Aa'ku is the mesa country of the Acoma, a Keres-speaking Pueblo people. Their sky village stood on a 365-foot rock, reached by narrow stairways and ladders cut into the stone; above were cisterns, stored maize and room to sow, while farming camps such as Acomita used the valley below. Maize, turkeys, cotton cloth, buffalo hide and turquoise sustained a life shaped by drought and raid, and Navajo and Apache pressure helped make the mesa a fortress. In 1444 the Acoma kept their independence under their own elders and warriors, trading or fighting across the surrounding Pueblo country.

Outside expeditions reached Aa'ku after Estevanico reported the pueblo in 1539, and Hernando de Alvarado, serving Coronado, saw its rock fortress in 1540. Juan de Oñate entered peacefully on 27 October 1598, but after his nephew Juan de Zaldívar was killed that December, Vicente de Zaldívar returned with seventy soldiers. The three-day Acoma War of January 1599 destroyed most of the pueblo, killed about 800 people and opened an era of tribute, forced labour and missionary rule. Survivors began rebuilding in December 1599; Spanish authorities imposed appointed governors in 1620, and in 1623 Franciscans ordered work on San Estevan del Rey, whose great walls Acoma labourers raised from adobe and sandstone. Acoma joined the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, helped drive Spanish authority from New Mexico and sheltered refugees, while Catholic and traditional rites had long since become intertwined on the mesa.
zh:
阿库是阿科马人的台地家园，阿科马人是说凯雷斯语的普韦布洛族群。他们的天空村落建在111米高的岩丘上，只能沿凿入岩体的狭窄石阶和木梯攀入；岩顶有蓄水池、储存的玉米和可耕作的土地，阿科米塔等农耕营地则利用下方河谷。玉米、火鸡、棉布、野牛皮和绿松石维系着适应干旱与袭掠的生活，纳瓦霍人和阿帕契人的压力也使这座台地成为堡垒。1444年，阿科马人仍保持独立，由本族长老与战士治理，并在周围的普韦布洛地带贸易或作战。
