The Innu kept to their summer-only custom at Mingan, coming in each year to barter furs. The post was run for a time by the North West Company, and in 1807 it passed to the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
在明根，同名河流注入海湾，河口外横着一长串裸露的石灰岩群岛。因努人称此地为埃夸尼楚（Ekuanitshit），意即「有东西被冲上岸的地方」，所指大概是常在群岛间搁浅的鲸。这里是他们夏日大聚的营地之一：在内陆猎驯鹿越冬的各家来到河口，叉鲑鱼、捕鲸和海豹、聚会交易，封冻前再溯河而去。河口与群岛都在尼塔希南的季节迁徙范围之内，1444年时岸上还没有任何欧洲人造物。

1661年，明根领地获得封授，这是法国人在这段海岸上的第一处产业，河口随之立起毛皮贸易站。1680年，路易十四把明根群岛连同安蒂科斯蒂岛封给探察过密西西比河的路易·若列；他在岛上的设防据点用武器杂货向蒙塔涅人和帕皮纳舒瓦人换取海豹皮。因努人仍只在夏天到明根，每年来站上以毛皮易物。贸易站一度由西北公司经营，1807年转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Between the broad mouths of the Manicouagan and the Betsiamites, the coast belonged to the Montagnais bands the French called the Bersimis — the Pessamit Innu, for Pessamit means 'the place of lampreys' — with the Papinachois up the Betsiamites and the Ouchestigouetch at the head of the Manicouagan. They summered at the river-mouths taking salmon, seal and lamprey, and wintered far inland on caribou. Champlain marked them on his map of 1632 as the 'Sauvages Bersiamiste'. In 1444 this was still untouched Innu country, deep in Nitassinan, its rivers known only to the people who paddled them.

Jacques Cartier noted the Manicouagan's mouth without naming it at the end of August 1535. Once the French opened the trade at Tadoussac to the west, the Bersimis became among their earliest allies, and in June 1664 the Jesuit Henri Nouvel became the first missionary to ascend the great river the Innu called Manikouaganistikou and the French the Rivière Noire. Missionaries went on working the summer gatherings for the rest of the century, and the Innu signed the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701. In 1733 Intendant Gilles Hocquart had a fur post built at Pointe-des-Bersimites. The post was later leased to the North West Company, and in 1821 it passed with that company to the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
在马尼夸根河与贝齐亚米特河两个宽阔河口之间，海岸属蒙塔涅人的几支：法人称作贝尔西米人的一支，即佩萨穆因努人——佩萨米特意为「七鳃鳗之地」；帕皮纳舒瓦人住在贝齐亚米特河上游，乌谢斯蒂古埃奇人住在马尼夸根河源头一带。他们夏天聚到河口捕鲑鱼、海豹和七鳃鳗，冬天深入内陆猎驯鹿。尚普兰1632年的地图已把他们标作「贝尔西亚米斯特人」（Sauvages Bersiamiste）。1444年时，这里仍是欧洲人未曾涉足的因努土地，深藏在尼塔希南腹地，各条河流只在因努人的独木舟下有名。

1535年8月底，卡蒂亚记下马尼夸根河口，却没有为它命名。法国人开通西边的塔杜萨克贸易后，贝尔西米人成为法人最早的盟友之一。1664年6月，耶稣会士亨利·努韦尔成为第一位溯行这条因努语称作马尼夸加尼斯蒂库、法人称作黑河的大河而上的传教士。此后整个世纪，传教士继续在各夏日聚点传教；1701年，因努人签署《蒙特利尔大和约》。1733年，新法兰西行政长官吉勒·奥卡尔在贝尔西米特角建起毛皮贸易站。贸易站后来租给西北公司，1821年随该公司并入哈德逊湾公司。

en:
Anticosti is a long, forested island set across the mouth of the St Lawrence where the gulf narrows into the Jacques Cartier and Honguedo straits. The Innu called it Notiskuan, 'where bears are hunted', and for thousands of years mainland parties crossed to it in summer to hunt bear and take salmon from its rivers, yet they never settled it the year round. In 1444 it was an empty, fog-bound hunting ground: no European had seen it, and even the people who owned it withdrew to the mainland through the long winter.

Jacques Cartier was the first European to report the island, in 1534, and on 15 August 1535, sailing past on the feast of the Assumption, he named it Île de l'Assomption. In 1680 Louis XIV granted it with the Mingan Archipelago to Louis Jolliet, explorer of the Mississippi. Jolliet raised a fortified post against Inuit raiders and settled there in the spring of 1681 with his family and servants, trading arms and goods to the Montagnais for sealskins. In 1690 William Phips's Massachusetts troops, retreating from their failed attack on Quebec, seized the fort. Jolliet died in 1700, and after a long lawsuit the island passed among his three sons, who kept it until the Treaty of Paris in 1763. It was annexed to Newfoundland that year, returned to the Province of Quebec in 1774 and attached to Newfoundland again in 1809, a distant timber-rich seigneurie whose few inhabitants lived by fishing and the fur trade.
zh:
安蒂科斯蒂是一座狭长的森林大岛，横在圣劳伦斯河口，扼守雅克·卡蒂亚海峡与翁格多海峡。因努人称它为诺蒂斯宽（Notiskuan），意即「猎熊之地」。几千年来，大陆上的人夏天渡海而来猎熊、在岛河上捕鲑鱼，却从不在岛上常年定居。1444年时，它还是一座雾霭笼罩、空无一人的猎场：欧洲人尚未见过它，连以岛为猎地的人们在漫长冬季也撤回大陆。

1534年，卡蒂亚成为第一个记载此岛的欧洲人；1535年8月15日圣母升天节，他再次绕过该岛，将它命名为圣母升天岛。1680年，路易十四把此岛连同明根群岛封给探察过密西西比河的路易·若列。若列筑起设防据点以防因纽特人袭击，1681年春携家眷和仆人定居岛上，用武器杂货向蒙塔涅人换取海豹皮。1690年，威廉·菲普斯麾下攻打魁北克失利的马萨诸塞部队在撤退途中占领了这座堡垒。若列1700年去世，经过一场漫长官司，海岛分归他的三个儿子，若列家族一直保有到1763年《巴黎条约》。该年岛屿被划归纽芬兰，1774年交还魁北克省，1809年再度并入纽芬兰。这座遥远而林木丰茂的封地上居民寥寥，皆以捕鱼和毛皮贸易为生。

en:
Pekuakami is the Innu name of the broad, shallow lake the French would call Lac Saint-Jean, set in the Laurentian highlands and draining through the Saguenay River. Its people are the Pekuakamiulnuatsh, 'the people of Pekuakami', the Innu band the French knew as the Montagnais. They followed the shoreline and the surrounding boreal forest, hunting caribou and moose, fishing through the ice and taking beaver, and in summer families gathered at river-mouth points such as Métabetchouane to meet and trade. In 1444 no European had yet seen the lake, which lay deep in the Innu country called Nitassinan, and the year still turned to the old seasonal round.

French ships were trading at Tadoussac by 1600, and the Innu became France's first allies upriver: Champlain made his alliance with them in 1603, and Montagnais warriors went with him in 1609. On 17 July 1647 the Jesuit Jean de Quen, ascending the Saguenay, became the first European to reach Pekuakami and said mass on its shore. In 1652 Governor Jean de Lauson had a fur post raised at Métabetchouane, within the king's own domain; a Jesuit mission was added there in 1676, the same year as the Chicoutimi post, but in 1697 the post was closed and its trade moved to Chicoutimi. Iroquois raiding parties reached the lake country during that century's wars, until the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701. After the British conquest the post reopened and its stone powder magazine was built between 1760 and 1778; the North West Company ran it from 1802, and in 1821 it passed, with the whole company, into Hudson's Bay Company hands.
zh:
佩夸卡米是因努语对这片宽阔浅水湖的称呼，法国人后来称它为圣让湖。湖在劳伦琴高原之间，湖水经萨格奈河流出。湖畔居民是佩夸卡米乌尔努阿奇（佩夸卡米乌尔努阿特），意即「佩夸卡米人」，属因努人的一支，法国人称之为蒙塔涅人。他们循着湖岸与周围的针叶林迁徙，猎驯鹿和驼鹿、冰下捕鱼、诱捕海狸；夏天各家聚到梅塔贝楚安等河流入湖处相会交易。1444年时还没有欧洲人见过这座湖，它深藏在因努人称作尼塔希南的土地腹地，一年仍按古老的季节节律轮转。

到1600年，法国商船已在下游的塔杜萨克贸易，因努人成为法国人溯河而上最早的盟友：尚普兰1603年与他们结盟，1609年蒙塔涅战士随他出征。1647年7月17日，耶稣会士让·德康溯萨格奈河而上，成为第一个抵达佩夸卡米的欧洲人，并在湖边做了弥撒。1652年，总督让·德洛松在梅塔贝楚安建起毛皮贸易站，此地属国王直辖的王家领地；1676年站内增设耶稣会传教所，与希库蒂米贸易站同年，但1697年贸易站关闭，生意并入希库蒂米。那个世纪的易洛魁战争中，劫掠队伍一度深入湖区，直到1701年《蒙特利尔大和约》才告平息。英国征服后贸易站重开，石砌火药库建于1760至1778年间；西北公司自1802年起经营此站，1821年随该公司一并落入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Atikamekw is the upper Saint-Maurice country that its people call Nitaskinan, a boreal world of lakes, spruce forest and family hunting grounds above the later French town of Trois-Rivières. In 1444 its people gathered at riverside places such as Wemotaci in summer, then split into small winter camps to fish under the ice, hunt moose and trap beaver. Birchbark canoes and snowshoes tied the territory together, and no European power had yet reached it.

French records first mention the Atikamekw in the early seventeenth century. As the fur trade developed, beaver pelts moved down the Saint-Maurice to the St. Lawrence, while metal tools returned upstream. French seigneurial settlement after 1634 stayed close to the river mouth, leaving the upper country to Atikamekw hunters and traders rather than habitant farms. The name Wemotaci first appears in a written source in 1724. Fur traders continued to use the Saint-Maurice through the eighteenth century, and Jean-Baptiste Perrault built the first confirmed trading post there in 1806; the Hudson's Bay Company took it over in 1821.
zh:
阿蒂卡梅库是阿蒂卡梅库人称作尼塔斯基南的土地，位于圣莫里斯河上游，是后来三河城以北一片由湖泊、针叶林和家族猎场组成的北方世界。1444年，人们夏季在韦莫塔奇等河畔地点聚集，入冬后分成小群营地，在冰下捕鱼、猎取驼鹿并诱捕河狸。桦皮舟和雪鞋把这片土地连为一体，欧洲势力当时尚未到来。

法国文献在17世纪初首次提到阿蒂卡梅库人。毛皮贸易发展后，河狸皮沿圣莫里斯河运往圣劳伦斯河，金属工具则溯流而上。1634年以后，法国人的领主拓殖仍集中在河口附近，河流上游依旧是阿蒂卡梅库猎人和商人的天地，并未出现农户定居带。韦莫塔奇一名最早见于1724年的文字记载。整个18世纪，毛皮商人持续利用圣莫里斯河；1806年，让-巴蒂斯特·佩罗在韦莫塔奇建起第一座可确认的商站，1821年该站转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Timiskaming is a long, deep lake on the Ottawa River, where the water bends from its northwestern course toward Montreal. Its Algonquin name was Temi Kami, and at the narrows called Obadjiwan, 'the strait where the current flows', Algonquin families kept a summer camp, fishing the lake and taking beaver and moose in the surrounding forest. In 1444 the country was Anishinaabe land, and the lake stood near the midpoint of the canoe route that would one day join the St. Lawrence to James Bay by way of Lake Abitibi.

In 1686 a French expedition paddled north through the lake to surprise the English posts on James Bay, becoming the first Europeans to travel the whole route. A Montreal merchants' post built on the west shore about 1679 was destroyed by the Iroquois in 1688. In 1720 French merchants founded Fort Témiscamingue at the Obadjiwan narrows, on the old Algonquin campground, and for forty years the post traded guns, brandy and ironware for furs. After the fall of New France it was reopened by independent traders, and in 1788 it passed to the North West Company, whose brigades still carried the northern furs down the Ottawa to Montreal.
zh:
蒂米斯卡明是渥太华河上一道又长又深的湖，河水在此由西北流向折而奔向蒙特利尔。湖的阿尔冈昆语名作特米卡米；在名为奥巴吉万（Obadjiwan，意为「水流湍急的狭口」）的窄道处，阿尔冈昆家族设有夏季营地，在湖中捕鱼，到周围森林猎取河狸与驼鹿。1444年，这片土地属于阿尼希纳贝人，湖的位置接近一条独木舟路线的中点——这条路线日后经由阿比蒂比湖，把圣劳伦斯河与詹姆斯湾连接起来。

1686年，一支法国远征队为奇袭詹姆斯湾上的英国商站取道此湖北上，成为首批走完全程的欧洲人。约1679年蒙特利尔商人在湖西岸建起的商栈，1688年被易洛魁人摧毁。1720年，法国商人在奥巴吉万狭口、旧日的阿尔冈昆营地处兴建蒂米斯卡明堡，四十年来以枪支、白兰地和铁器交换毛皮。新法兰西陷落后，商栈由独立商人重新经营，1788年转入西北公司之手，北方的毛皮仍由成队独木舟沿渥太华河南运蒙特利尔。

en:
Animouski is the Algonquian name the French would write as Rimouski, a river that enters the lower St. Lawrence estuary on this forested south shore, between the Bic headland and Matane. In 1444 the Wolastoqiyik, the Maliseet bands of the Wabanaki confederacy, moved with the seasons between these river mouths and the inland lakes, taking salmon, seal and moose, while Mi'kmaq parties from the east used the same coast; the Matapédia and Témiscouata portages ran from here toward Chaleur Bay and the Saint John River. No European had yet settled, but by about 1570 Basque whalers were rendering their catch on Île aux Basques off Trois-Pistoles, where they built three stone try-furnaces.

Early in the seventeenth century La Rochelle merchants ran a fur post at Matane, trading European goods with the Mi'kmaq. The French granted more than twenty seigneuries along this coast, but settlers were few: the seigneury of Rimouski was granted in 1688 and occupied only in 1696, when René Lepage moved his family over from the Île d'Orléans. At the conquest of 1760 a few dozen families lived in just four seigneuries between Rivière-du-Loup and Matane. Around 1783 a road over the Témiscouata portage opened toward British New Brunswick, yet in 1790 the whole shore still held only some 1,250 people; migrants from the older parishes then swelled the river mouths. The lighthouse on Île Verte was raised between 1806 and 1809, the first on the St. Lawrence.
zh:
阿尼莫斯基是阿尔冈昆语地名，法国人后来写作「里穆斯基」；里穆斯基河在这片森林南岸注入圣劳伦斯河口湾，海岸介于比克海岬与马塔纳之间。1444年，瓦巴纳基联盟的沃拉斯托奇人——即马勒西特诸游群——随季节往返于这些河口和内陆湖泊之间，捕鲑鱼、猎海豹与驼鹿，东方来的米克马克游群也使用同一片海岸；马塔佩迪亚和塔米斯库塔两条搬运道从这里通向沙勒尔湾和圣约翰河。欧洲人尚未定居，但约1570年时，巴斯克捕鲸人已在特鲁瓦皮斯托勒外海的巴斯克岛上熬炼鲸油，并在岛上修起三座石炉。

17世纪初，拉罗谢尔商人在马塔纳经营毛皮商站，用欧洲货与米克马克人交易。法国在这一带沿海封出二十多个领地，定居者却寥寥：里穆斯基领地1688年封出，直到1696年勒内·勒帕热率全家从奥尔良岛迁来才有人常住。1760年英国征服时，从里维耶尔迪卢到马塔纳之间只有数十户人家、四个领地。1783年前后，一条翻越塔米斯库塔搬运道、通往英属新不伦瑞克的道路开通，可1790年整条海岸仍只有约1250人；此后来自老教区的移民才让各个河口充实起来。绿岛灯塔于1806至1809年建成，是圣劳伦斯河上的第一座灯塔。

en:
Kikonteku is Kik8ntekw, 'River of the Fields' in Abenaki — the Chaudière, which runs north from the Appalachian lakes to plunge into the St. Lawrence over a churning fall opposite the rock of Quebec. In 1444 its valley and the wooded south shore belonged to that Algonquian world: Abenaki and Etchemin bands used the river as a canoe road between the St. Lawrence, the Kennebec and the Atlantic, while St. Lawrence Iroquoian villagers of Stadacona fished and farmed along the riverbank. Cartier sailed this shore on his way to Stadacona in 1535; Champlain later charted the water as the Etchemin River, and in 1629 he named the cape facing Quebec Cap de Lévy.

The seigneury of Lauzon was granted on the cape in 1636, but its first settler, Guillaume Couture, a former Jesuit interpreter, did not arrive until 1647. During Phips's attack on Quebec in October 1690, English raiders burned the Pointe-Lévy settlements until Couture, seventy-two years old, led the militia against them. On 30 June 1759 Wolfe's troops under Monckton seized the point, and for seventy days their batteries on its cliffs bombarded the city across the water. On 9 November 1775 Benedict Arnold's six hundred survivors, having marched through the Maine wilderness and descended the Chaudière, reached the point; they crossed the river four nights later and failed in their New Year's Eve assault. In 1791 the Chaudière parishes became part of Lower Canada.
zh:
基康特库（Kik8ntekw）在阿布纳基语中意为「田野之河」，即肖迪耶尔河。它从阿巴拉契亚湖群向北流，在魁北克巨岩对岸越过翻滚的瀑布注入圣劳伦斯河。1444年，河谷与林木葱郁的南岸属于阿尔冈昆人的世界：阿布纳基和埃切明游群把这条河当作独木舟通道，往来于圣劳伦斯河、肯纳贝克河与大西洋之间；圣劳伦斯易洛魁人的斯塔达科纳村民则在河畔捕鱼种田。1535年卡蒂亚驶往斯塔达科纳时经过此岸；尚普兰后来把这条水道标作「埃切明河」，1629年又将魁北克对岸的海角命名为莱维角。

1636年，莱维角上的洛宗领地获封，但第一个定居者、曾为耶稣会做翻译的纪尧姆·库蒂尔直到1647年才到来。1690年10月菲普斯攻打魁北克，英军劫掠队焚毁莱维角的定居点，七十二岁的库蒂尔率民兵将他们击退。1759年6月30日，沃尔夫麾下孟克顿的部队夺取该角，崖上炮台在此后的七十天里隔河轰城。1775年11月9日，本尼迪克特·阿诺德的六百名残兵穿过缅因荒原、顺肖迪耶尔河抵达这里；四天后他们夜渡圣劳伦斯河，新年前夜的攻城以失败告终。1791年，肖迪耶尔河畔各教区成为下加拿大省的一部分。

en:
The Masoliantekw, an Abenaki name meaning 'the water where there is plenty of food', is the river the French first called the Rivière aux Iroquois and later the Richelieu; it runs north from Lake Champlain to the St. Lawrence through fertile bottoms and the Chambly rapids. In 1444 its lower valley was part of the St. Lawrence Iroquoians' maize-and-longhouse world, and the river itself was the road between the villages of the St. Lawrence, Lake Champlain and the Mohawk country beyond, while Abenaki bands ranged the eastern bank.

Jacques Cartier sighted its mouth in 1535, but when Samuel de Champlain explored it in 1603 the St. Lawrence villages had vanished, and in 1609 he joined a Huron, Algonquin and Montagnais war party up the river into Lake Champlain, opening the long French quarrel with the Mohawk. On 19 June 1610 Champlain and the same allies destroyed a Mohawk band at the mouth in the battle of Sorel. Fort Richelieu, raised there in 1641, was burned by the Iroquois in 1647 and rebuilt by the Carignan-Salières regiment in 1665, when Fort Saint-Louis at the Chambly rapids and Fort Sainte-Thérèse were also built; Fort Saint-Jean followed in 1666. Settlers then took up the fertile banks, and after the Great Peace of Montreal of 1701 the stone Fort Chambly of 1709 to 1711 anchored a chain of strongholds that gave the valley its nickname of the valley of forts. The forts passed to Britain in August 1760; American forces took Fort Chambly on 20 October 1775 and burned it when they retreated the following spring, after which Loyalists settled along the river.
zh:
马索利安特库（Masoliantekw）是阿布纳基语河名，意为「食物丰足之水」；法国人起初称它易洛魁河，后来改名黎塞留河。河水自尚普兰湖北流，穿过肥沃的低地和尚布利急滩，注入圣劳伦斯河。1444年，下游谷地属于圣劳伦斯易洛魁人种植玉米、居住长屋的生活范围，河流本身则是圣劳伦斯各村寨、尚普兰湖与再往南的莫霍克人之间的往来通道，河东一带有阿布纳基人游猎。

1535年雅克·卡蒂埃望见它的河口；塞缪尔·德·尚普兰1603年前来探察时，圣劳伦斯易洛魁人的村寨已经消失。1609年，他随休伦人、阿尔冈昆人和蒙塔涅人（Montagnais）的战队溯河北上尚普兰湖，由此开启法国与莫霍克人的长期敌对；1610年6月19日，尚普兰与这些盟军在河口的索莱尔之战歼灭一支莫霍克队伍。1641年河口兴建黎塞留堡，1647年被易洛魁人焚毁，1665年由卡里尼昂-萨利埃团重建；同年尚布利急滩畔的圣路易堡与圣泰蕾兹堡也相继建成，圣让堡落成于1666年。移民随后到肥沃的河岸领垦，1701年《蒙特利尔大和平》之后，1709至1711年以石材重建的尚布利堡镇守着这串要塞，河谷由此得到「要塞之谷」的别称。1760年8月各堡落入英国之手；1775年10月20日美军攻占尚布利堡，次年春撤退时将其焚毁，此后效忠派沿河定居。

en:
Arendaronon was the eastern gateway of Wendake, the country between Coldwater and Orillia where tracks from the Bear and Cord ridges descended toward Lake Couchiching, the Narrows fishing grounds and Lake Simcoe. Iroquoian farmers and fishing parties had long used the lake crossings, and palisaded villages with cornfields stood on the light soils near Hawkestone. In 1444 this was still the older Huron country's exposed eastern flank, open to Algonquin neighbours and raiders from the south; the Rock People who gave the province its name entered the Wendat confederacy only around 1590 and made Cahiagué their principal town.

When Samuel de Champlain reached Cahiagué in 1615, he counted about 200 longhouses in the Rock capital. The chief Atironta was already known to the French and joined Champlain's Wendat-Algonquin war party against a Haudenosaunee village south of Lake Ontario; in 1616 he travelled to Quebec as Champlain's guest. The Jesuits founded the mission of Saint-Jean-Baptiste at Cahiagué in 1639-1640, where Antoine Daniel and Simon Le Moyne were sheltered by another Atironta during hostility toward the missionaries. As the easternmost Wendat nation, the Rock People bore the first weight of Beaver Wars raids. Epidemics and the 1649 invasion shattered their towns, and survivors fled toward Quebec or were absorbed by Haudenosaunee nations. Ojibwe bands later used the old trail and lakeshore; the British treaties of 1798, 1815 and 1818, followed by Penetanguishene Road in 1815, opened the country between Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay.
zh:
阿伦达罗嫩是温达克的东部门户，地处科尔德沃特与奥里利亚之间。熊族、绳族山岭上的小路由此通向库钦钦湖、狭窄水道渔场和锡姆科湖。易洛魁语农人和渔队很早就使用这些湖上渡口，霍克斯通附近的疏松土地上分布着带玉米田的木栅村落。1444年时，这里仍是旧休伦之地暴露的东翼，面向阿尔冈昆邻族和南方袭掠者；赋予本省名称的岩族要到约1590年才加入温达特联盟，并以卡希亚盖（Cahiagué）作为主村。

塞缪尔·德·尚普兰1615年抵达卡希亚盖时，估计这座岩族首府约有两百座长屋。首领阿蒂龙塔（Atironta）早已同法国人相识，他随尚普兰率领的温达特—阿尔冈昆战队进攻安大略湖以南的一座豪德诺索尼村落，1616年又作为尚普兰的客人前往魁北克。1639年至1640年，耶稣会在卡希亚盖建立圣让巴蒂斯特传教站；当传教士遭到敌视时，另一位承袭阿蒂龙塔之名的首领庇护了安托万·达尼埃尔和西蒙·勒穆瓦纳。作为温达特最东面的族群，岩族最先承受海狸战争的袭掠。疫病和1649年的入侵摧毁其村镇，幸存者或逃往魁北克，或被豪德诺索尼诸族吸纳。后来奥吉布瓦游群使用旧道和湖岸；1798年、1815年和1818年的英国条约，以及1815年修建的佩内唐吉申路，打开了锡姆科湖与乔治亚湾之间的土地。

en:
Tionontate is the cold south-western shore of Georgian Bay, where the Niagara Escarpment meets Nottawasaga Bay. In 1444 it was the country of the Tionontati, an Iroquoian people later called the Petun or Tobacco Nation for the tobacco they raised and traded. Eight to ten palisaded longhouse villages stood above the bay, surrounded by cornfields and linked by trails to the Wendat across Nottawasaga Bay. Their Wolf and Deer divisions hunted in the woods, fished the shore waters and carried tobacco and skins along one of the Algonquian-Iroquoian routes of the upper Great Lakes.

Samuel de Champlain explored and mapped Georgian Bay in 1615-1616 and recorded the Petun villages. Epidemics swept through after 1634, and Jesuits from nearby Huronia entered the country as French trade drew it into Wendat alliances. In March 1649 Wendat refugees crossed the frozen Nottawasaga Bay after Haudenosaunee armies overran Huronia; by the end of the year the same forces had destroyed the bulk of the Petun settlements, and the survivors fled with the Odawa, eventually becoming part of the Wyandot. Haudenosaunee war parties withdrew from the region around 1700, leaving the shore to the Anishinaabe lake routes. On 17 August 1814 American warships destroyed the British schooner Nancy in the Nottawasaga River; Lieutenant Miller Worsley escaped to Michilimackinac and returned with a small force to capture the USS Tigress and Scorpion.
zh:
提奥嫩塔特位于乔治亚湾寒冷的西南岸，尼亚加拉陡崖在这里与诺塔瓦萨加湾相接。1444年，这里是提奥嫩塔提人的土地；他们是说易洛魁语的民族，后来因种植和交易烟草而被法兰西人称为佩琴人，即烟草民族。八至十座设有栅栏的长屋村落俯瞰海湾，周围是玉米田，并有小路通往诺塔瓦萨加湾对岸的温达特人。其下的狼部与鹿部在林中狩猎、在近岸水域捕鱼，也把烟草和兽皮带上五大湖上游的阿尔冈昆—易洛魁商路。

塞缪尔·德·尚普兰在1615年至1616年探测并绘制乔治亚湾，记录了佩琴人的村落。1634年后疫病席卷此地，来自邻近休伦尼亚的耶稣会士进入该地，法兰西贸易也把他们牵入温达特同盟。1649年3月，豪德诺索尼军队攻灭休伦尼亚后，温达特难民越过冰封的诺塔瓦萨加湾；同年年底，同批军队又摧毁了大部分佩琴村落，幸存者随奥达人撤离，最终融入怀安多特人。约1700年，豪德诺索尼战队撤出这一地区，湖岸重归阿尼什纳比人的湖上通路。1814年8月17日，美国战舰在诺塔瓦萨加河击毁英国纵帆船「南希号」；米勒·沃斯利中尉逃到米希利马基诺后率小队折返，夺取了美国军舰「蒂格雷斯号」和「斯科皮恩号」。

en:
Odawa is the lake country of the Bruce Peninsula and Manitoulin Island, where the wooded Niagara Escarpment runs into Lake Huron as a chain of islands and narrow channels. In 1444 it was the homeland of the Odawa, Anishinaabe members of the Council of Three Fires. Their name came from adaawe, to trade, and birchbark canoes carried cornmeal, sunflower oil, furs and skins, mats, tobacco and medicinal roots between Georgian Bay, the North Channel and the upper Great Lakes. Manitoulin, the Odawa Manidoowaaling or spirit island, offered fishing rivers, sheltered straits and meeting places for the trading families.

In 1615 Samuel de Champlain met about 300 Odawa warriors near the mouth of the French River; the French called them the Cheveux Relevés, and in 1616 he visited their country west of the Wendat. The Odawa soon became the chief middlemen of the French fur trade, while canoes from Montreal used the Ottawa, Mattawa and French rivers and the North Channel to reach Lake Superior. The Jesuit Joseph Poncet opened a mission near Wiikwemkoong on Manitoulin in 1648, naming the island Isle de Sainte-Marie. Disease and Haudenosaunee raids shattered the settlement, and in 1650 the surviving Anishinaabe burned their villages and withdrew, many to Michilimackinac and the upper lakes. Manitoulin then remained almost uninhabited for roughly 150 years, although French traders continued through its channels. After the War of 1812, Odawa, Ojibwe and Potawatomi families began returning to the spirit island, so by 1821 the old homeland was again being reoccupied.
zh:
渥太华是布鲁斯半岛与马尼图林岛一带的湖乡，林木覆盖的尼亚加拉陡崖在这里伸入休伦湖，化成一串岛屿和狭窄水道。1444年，这里是渥太华人的故地，他们属于阿尼什纳比人的三火议会。族名来自意为贸易的词（adaawe）；桦皮独木舟载着玉米粉、葵花油、毛皮、席子、烟草和药根，往来于乔治亚湾、北海峡与五大湖上游之间。马尼图林在渥太华语中称马尼多瓦林（Manidoowaaling），即精灵之岛，岛上的渔河、避风海峡和会合点供贸易家族使用。

1615年，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰在弗伦奇河口附近见到约三百名渥太华战士，法兰西人因他们的发式称之为「高发髻人」；1616年，他又走访了温达特人以西的渥太华地域。渥太华人很快成为法兰西毛皮贸易最重要的中介，来自蒙特利尔的独木舟则经渥太华河、马塔瓦河、弗伦奇河和北海峡前往苏必利尔湖。1648年，耶稣会士约瑟夫·庞塞在马尼图林的威奎米孔附近设立传教站，把该岛命名为圣玛丽岛。疫病和豪德诺索尼人的袭击摧毁了这一定居点；1650年，幸存的阿尼什纳比人焚毁村落撤离，许多人迁往米希利马基诺和五大湖上游。此后马尼图林几乎无人居住约一百五十年，只有法兰西商人继续穿行其海峡。1812年战争结束后，渥太华、奥吉布瓦和波塔瓦托米家庭开始返回精灵之岛，到1821年，这片旧地正重新有人定居。

en:
The Piscatang country centres on Night Hawk Lake, the old Piscoutagamy, whose waters enter the Frederick House River and then the Abitibi on their way to James Bay. Cree and Ojibwe bands used its islands, rapids and surrounding Shield forest as fishing and hunting grounds and linked the lake by birchbark canoe to the Moose River routes. In 1444 no European post stood on these waters, and the seasonal rounds of Indigenous families controlled movement through the forest.

In 1785 Philip Turnor, sent inland from Moose Factory by the Hudson's Bay Company, established Frederick House to keep Canadian fur traders from diverting the region's beaver pelts away from James Bay. The Frederick House and Abitibi rivers were difficult for supply canoes, and Montreal traders pressed the post from a rival station on nearby Devil's Island. During the winter of 1812-13 the manager, two labourers and several Indigenous people were murdered there; Frederick House was not permanently staffed afterwards. It was abandoned in 1821, when the Hudson's Bay and North West companies merged and the local trade rivalry ended.
zh:
皮斯卡唐一带以夜鹰湖为中心，旧称皮斯库塔加米；湖水流入弗雷德里克豪斯河，再经阿比蒂比河通往詹姆斯湾。克里和奥吉布瓦诸部把湖岛、急流与周围的地盾森林作为捕鱼狩猎之地，并乘桦皮独木舟把湖区同穆斯河诸水道连接起来。1444年，这些水面上还没有欧洲商站，穿越森林的行动仍依照原住民家庭的季节迁徙而展开。

1785年，哈得孙湾公司从穆斯法克特里派菲利普·特纳尔深入内陆，设立弗雷德里克豪斯商站，以阻止加拿大毛皮商人把这一带的河狸皮分流，不往詹姆斯湾运送。弗雷德里克豪斯河与阿比蒂比河都不利于补给独木舟航行，蒙特利尔商人又在附近的魔鬼岛设站竞争。1812年至1813年冬，商站主管、两名劳工和数名原住民在此遇害，此后弗雷德里克豪斯便不再常驻人员。1821年哈得孙湾公司与西北公司合并，当地的贸易争夺结束，商站也于同年废弃。

en: The shallow, fish-rich lake the Cree called Kesagami, recorded also as Mesackamee, lies in swampland between the Moose and Harricana rivers, the winter hunting grounds of the Moose Cree, who canoed each summer down to the James Bay coast to fish and hunt waterfowl. In 1444 they lived by this seasonal round of fishing and hunting, long before the fur posts arrived. Their furs went to Moose Fort, the Hudson's Bay Company post opened at the mouth of the Moose in 1673. In 1777 the Company sent George Atkinson, Peter Liske, William Thomas and William Robinson up from the fort with two Cree families to defend its Abitibi trade from rivals, and they raised Mesackamee House on the shore. The post never paid and was abandoned by October 1779, leaving the lake country to the Cree traplines.
zh: 克沙加米湖（一译凯萨加米湖，旧称梅萨卡米湖）水浅鱼丰，坐落在麋河与哈里卡纳河之间的沼泽地带，是驼鹿克里人的冬季猎场；每到夏天，他们便乘独木舟顺水下到詹姆斯湾沿岸捕鱼猎禽。1444年，他们随季节迁徙渔猎，毛皮商栈还远未到来。族人的毛皮都送往麋河堡（Moose Fort）——哈得孙湾公司1673年在麋河口开设的商馆。1777年，为挡住同业竞争、保住阿比蒂比的毛皮生意，公司从商馆派来乔治·阿特金森、彼得·利斯克、威廉·托马斯和威廉·罗宾逊四人，偕两户克里人在湖畔建起梅萨卡米屋。商馆始终无利可图，1779年10月前即遭废弃，湖区重归克里人的猎道。

en:
The Shaggami country covers the boreal upland between the Night Hawk lake country, Kesagami and the upper approaches to the Moose River. In 1444 it was Cree hunting ground: families used its lakes and streams as summer fishing routes, then scattered to winter traplines for beaver, moose and caribou. No European post had yet been built in the inland behind James Bay, and trade followed Indigenous canoe rounds rather than company boundaries.

The Hudson's Bay Company opened Moose Fort on the bay in 1673. In 1686 the Chevalier de Troyes advanced by the Abitibi and Moose routes and captured it for France, renaming the post Fort St Louis; after years of changing hands, the British rebuilt on the Moose River in 1730. The inland rivalry reached Shaggami's southwestern approaches in 1785 with Frederick House, built to hold Cree trappers in the Hudson's Bay trade. The Company and the North West Company competed for their furs until the merger of 1821, after which Moose Factory supplied the inland routes.
zh:
沙加米一带是夜鹰湖地区、克沙加米与穆斯河上游之间的北方林地。1444年，这里是克里人的猎场：各家族以湖泊溪流作为夏季捕鱼通道，随后分散到冬季猎径，捕猎河狸、驼鹿和驯鹿。詹姆斯湾海岸后方的内陆还没有欧洲商站，贸易仍依照原住民的独木舟迁徙路线进行，不受公司疆界约束。

哈得孙湾公司1673年在湾边开设穆斯堡。1686年，特鲁瓦骑士沿阿比蒂比河与穆斯河路线北上，为法国夺取该堡，改名圣路易堡；几经易手后，英国人于1730年在穆斯河畔重建商站。1785年，为把克里猎人留在哈得孙湾贸易圈内，弗雷德里克豪斯商站设在沙加米猎区的西南通道上，内陆争夺随之逼近。哈得孙湾公司与西北公司持续争夺克里人的毛皮，直至1821年两家合并；此后穆斯法克特里负责向这些内陆路线供货。

en:
The Outoulibi country is the Missinaibi watershed between the Moose River and the height of land leading toward Lake Superior. Its Cree river name means 'pictured waters', after rock paintings along the banks; falls and long portages divided the canoe route into fishing, summer gathering and winter trapping grounds. In 1444 Cree families held the lakes and rapids, moving with the seasons for fish, moose, caribou and beaver, while no European post had yet been built behind the James Bay coast.

That coast changed when the Hudson's Bay Company built Moose Fort in 1673, and the Chevalier de Troyes's French expedition of 1686 made these river systems an Anglo-French fur-trade frontier. In 1775-76 Edward Jarvis crossed from the Kenogami to the Missinaibi on his way toward Lake Superior. The Company built Wapiscogamy House near the Opasatika confluence in 1777, and Philip Turnor surveyed the route to the upper lakes in 1781. William Boland added Macabanish House in 1788; it was named New Brunswick House in 1799. A North West Company post stood less than a kilometre downstream of Wapiscogamy from 1800 to 1806, and the Missinaibi Lake post was reoccupied in 1817. When the two companies merged in 1821, the rivalry along the river ended.
zh:
欧托利比一带是米西奈比河流域，位于穆斯河与通向苏必利尔湖的分水岭之间。克里语河名意为「绘有图像的水」，得自河岸岩画；瀑布和漫长搬运道把独木舟路线分隔成捕鱼、夏季聚集与冬季设猎的场所。1444年，克里诸家族据有湖泊与急流，随季节迁徙捕鱼，猎取驼鹿、驯鹿和河狸，詹姆斯湾海岸后方的内陆还没有欧洲商站。

1673年哈得孙湾公司在下游海岸建立穆斯堡，局势随之改变；1686年特鲁瓦骑士的法国远征队又使这些水系成为英法毛皮贸易的交界。1775年至1776年，爱德华·贾维斯从凯诺加米河进入米西奈比河，向苏必利尔湖方向穿行。1777年，哈得孙湾公司在奥帕萨蒂卡河汇流处附近设立瓦皮斯科加米屋，菲利普·特纳尔又于1781年测绘通往上游大湖的路线。威廉·博兰1788年增设马卡巴尼什屋，该站1799年改名新不伦瑞克屋。1800年至1806年，西北公司在瓦皮斯科加米下游不到一公里处设站；米西奈比湖商站则于1817年重新启用。1821年两家公司合并，沿河竞争随之结束。

en:
The western shore of James Bay is a drowned flat of muskeg and goose-marshes, where the Moose and Albany rivers wind out of the boreal forest to the tides. Its people, the Omushkego, are the eastern Swampy Cree — Moose Cree at the bay's head — who kept an exact seasonal round: summer fishing and berrying by canoe, autumn goose-hunting along the shore, winter trapping at inland camps. In 1444 no European sail crossed their bay, and the coastal camps lay seasons away from any European frontier.

Henry Hudson, ice-bound, wintered in the bay in 1610-11 and was cast adrift by his mutineers in June 1611. Pierre-Esprit Radisson explored the Moose River in the winter of 1670-71, and the Hudson's Bay Company raised Moose Fort in 1673 and Fort Albany in 1679. A French column under the Chevalier de Troyes marched overland from Quebec and seized all three James Bay posts in 1686. The English retook Albany in 1693 and Moose in 1696, burned the latter, and after Utrecht (1713) rebuilt Moose Fort in 1730. Henley House, pushed 160 miles up the Albany in 1743, was sacked in December 1754 by Cree under Wappisis, who was hanged at Albany on 21 June 1755; Gloucester House (1777) and Osnaburgh House (1786) then carried the trade deep into the interior.
zh:
马什凯科瓦克所在的詹姆斯湾西岸是一片被海水浸透的泥炭沼与雁沼低地，穆斯河与奥尔巴尼河在其中蜿蜒穿过北方针叶林，奔流入海。此地居民是奥马什凯戈人（Omushkego），即东部沼泽克里人——海湾南端的一支又称穆斯克里人；他们严守季节的节律：夏天划独木舟捕鱼采莓，秋天到岸边猎雁，冬天到内陆营地捕猎毛皮兽。1444年的詹姆斯湾上没有一片欧洲帆影，海岸营地离任何欧洲人的边疆都还隔着好几个季节的路程。

亨利·哈德逊的船被海冰封在湾中，于1610至1611年在此过冬，1611年6月他被哗变船员放逐，不知所终。1670至1671年冬，皮埃尔-埃斯普里·拉迪松探察了穆斯河；哈得孙湾公司1673年建起穆斯堡，1679年又设奥尔巴尼堡。1686年，德·特鲁瓦骑士率一支法军从魁北克陆路北上，一举拿下詹姆斯湾上的三座公司商栈。英军1693年夺回奥尔巴尼堡，1696年收复穆斯堡并将其焚毁；《乌得勒支和约》（1713年）之后，穆斯堡于1730年重建。1743年，公司沿奥尔巴尼河深入160英里设立亨利屋商栈；1754年12月，瓦皮西斯率克里人攻陷该栈，他本人1755年6月21日在奥尔巴尼堡被处绞。此后格洛斯特屋（1777年）与奥斯纳堡屋（1786年）相继设立，把贸易一直推进到遥远的内陆。

en:
The Winnipeg River — its Cree name means 'murky water' — runs from Lake of the Woods down to Lake Winnipeg through a chaos of rapids and portages: Portage de l'Isle, the seven white-water climbs of La Rivière Blanche, then Manitou Rapids just before the mouth. For thousands of years it had been a native canoe road, the only easy passage by bark canoe between the Great Lakes country and the inland northwest, and halfway along it the English River led over toward James Bay. In 1444 its people were Anishinaabe-speaking Nakawe bands and Cree, hunters and fishers whose camps moved with the river's seasons, and no European had yet placed a post on its banks.

The French came in the 1730s. Pierre Gaultier de La Vérendrye, building Fort St. Charles on Lake of the Woods in 1732, sent his sons down the river in 1733, and about 1739 his men raised Fort Maurepas at the Bas de la Rivière near the river's mouth. By 1775 a large Cree village stood there when Alexander Henry the elder traded through. In 1792 Toussaint Le Sieur built the North West Company's depot Fort Bas de la Rivière, and the Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Alexander before 1800. After 1810 the warehouses stacked Assiniboine pemmican for the canoe brigades bound for Athabasca. At the merger of 1821 the Company kept the North West post under the name Fort Alexander, and the river's great days faded as the trade swung to York Factory.
zh:
瓦普斯一带的温尼伯河，其克里语名意为「浑水」，它自森林湖流出，在重重急流和搬运道间奔泻，最终注入温尼伯湖：沿途有岛屿搬运道（Portage de l'Isle）、白河（La Rivière Blanche）的七连跌水，以及河口前的马尼图急流。几千年来这里就是原住民的独木舟之路，是五大湖地区与西北内陆之间唯一便于树皮独木舟通行的水道；行至半途，英格兰河（English River）又可通往詹姆斯湾。1444年，河畔居民是说阿尼什纳比语的纳卡韦（索尔托人）与克里人，他们以渔猎为生，营地随河水的季节迁徙，河岸上还没有欧洲人的商栈。

法国人在1730年代到来。皮埃尔·戈蒂埃·德·拉韦朗德里1732年在森林湖建起圣夏尔堡，1733年派儿子们顺温尼伯河下行；约1739年，其部下又在河口地带巴德拉里维耶尔（Bas de la Rivière）建起莫尔帕堡。到1775年老亚历山大·亨利来此贸易时，河口已有一座不小的克里人村庄。1792年，图桑·勒西厄尔为西北公司建起货栈巴德拉里维耶尔堡，哈得孙湾公司则在1800年前针锋相对地设立亚历山大堡。1810年后，货栈里堆满阿西尼博因河运来的肉糜饼，供开往阿萨巴斯卡的独木舟大队食用。1821年两公司合并，哈得孙湾公司保留西北公司的货栈，沿用亚历山大堡之名；随着贸易转向约克堡，温尼伯河的黄金时代也随之黯淡。

en:
Between Lake Winnipeg and Hudson Bay lies a labyrinth of taiga lakes — Playgreen and Cross among them — and the upper Nelson and Hayes rivers, the canoe road from the bay into the Saskatchewan country. Its Cree bands lived on whitefish and sturgeon, moose and woodland caribou, moving camp with the seasons, while Chipewyan hunting grounds pressed in from the north-west. In 1444 these were exclusively native waterways, where no axe had ever sounded.

On 12 June 1690 Henry Kelsey left York Factory by canoe, crossed this lake country up the Nelson — five lakes, thirty-three portages — reached the Saskatchewan, becoming the first recorded European to visit present-day Saskatchewan, and on 20 August 1691 saw bison on the prairies before returning in 1692. The Cree, armed from the bay, barred the Chipewyan from the coast until the Chipewyan woman Thanadelthur led a peace mission out from York on 27 June 1715 and reconciled the two peoples; she died of fever at the factory on 5 February 1717. The Hayes–Nelson waterway stayed the main road to the west, and in 1817 the Hudson's Bay Company built Norway House where the Nelson flows out of the lake.
zh:
温尼伯湖与哈得孙湾之间，横亘着泰加林中的湖泊迷宫——普莱格林湖、克罗斯湖等大大小小的水面——以及纳尔逊河、海斯河的上游，这里正是从海湾进入萨斯喀彻温腹地的独木舟之路。昆内比贡赫利尼的克里人部落以白鱼、鲟鱼、驼鹿和林地驯鹿为生，营地随季节迁徙；奇佩瓦恩人的猎场从西北方向逼近。1444年，这些水道完全属于原住民，从未响起过斧头的声音。

1690年6月12日，亨利·凯尔西乘独木舟离开约克堡，沿纳尔逊河穿过这片湖乡——五个湖泊、三十三处搬运道——抵达萨斯喀彻温，是有记录以来第一个抵达今萨斯喀彻温省的欧洲人；1691年8月20日，他在草原上见到美洲野牛，1692年返回。得到海湾火器的克里人把守海岸，不许奇佩瓦恩人前来交易，直到1715年6月27日，奇佩瓦恩女子塔纳德尔图尔率议和使团从约克堡出发，促成两族和解；她却在1717年2月5日染热病殁于商栈。海斯—纳尔逊水道始终是西行正路，1817年哈得孙湾公司在纳尔逊河出湖处建起挪威之家。

en:
The upper Churchill is a labyrinth of rivers, rapids and long island-strewn lakes – Missinipe, 'the great water', to the Cree – running west to Lac Île-à-la-Crosse and the Methye Portage, where the waters divide between Hudson Bay and the Arctic Ocean. These forests and caribou runs were the country of the K'ësyëhót'ı̨ne, the 'aspen-house people', a Chipewyan band of the Dene nation. They moved in small family camps between winter hunting grounds and summer fishing stations, following barren-ground caribou, taking moose in the woods and whitefish at the lake narrows. In 1444 their world ran north toward the Athabasca and Great Slave lakes.

War with the gun-armed Cree long barred the Chipewyan from the bay, until Thanadelthur, a Chipewyan woman who had escaped Cree captivity while serving the Hudson's Bay Company, helped broker a peace in 1715 and guided William Stuart's mission among her people before dying of fever on 5 February 1717. The peace opened the road to trade at Churchill. In the winter of 1776 Thomas Frobisher built the first trading post on Lac Île-à-la-Crosse, and in 1778 Peter Pond crossed the twelve-mile Methye Portage to the Clearwater, opening the rich Athabasca country; the Cree, Dene, French and Scots who met there made the lake a border market and the cradle of a Métis community. A Hudson's Bay Company post followed in 1791. Smallpox travelled the same portage road in 1781–82 and thinned the bands, and the rival companies kept the trade until their union in 1821.
zh:
丘吉尔河上游是一片由河流、急流和狭长岛屿湖泊交织成的迷宫，克里人称之为密西尼皮（Missinipe），意为「大水」；水路西至拉克罗斯湖与梅蒂转运站——那里是哈得孙湾水系与北冰洋水系的分水岭。这片森林与驯鹿迁徙之地属于德内族奇帕维安人的一支：邻族称他们为凯斯耶霍廷内（K'ësyëhót'ı̨ne），即「白杨屋人」。他们以家族小营为单位，在冬季猎场和夏季渔场之间迁徙，追逐荒地驯鹿，在林中猎驼鹿，在湖峡捕白鱼。1444年时，他们的世界向北延伸至阿萨巴斯卡湖与大奴湖。

与持枪克里人的长期交战曾使奇帕维安人无法前往海湾，直到曾被克里人掳走、后为哈得孙湾公司效力的奇帕维安女子塔纳德尔图尔在1715年促成双方议和，并为威廉·斯图尔特的使团带路深入本族之地，最终于1717年2月5日死于热病。和约打开了丘吉尔河贸易的通道。1776年冬，托马斯·弗罗比舍在拉克罗斯湖建起第一座商站；1778年，彼得·庞德越过12英里长的梅蒂转运站抵达克利尔沃特河，打开了富庶的阿萨巴斯卡地区。在湖畔相遇的克里人、德内人、法国人和苏格兰人把这里变成边境集市，也催生了一个梅蒂社群。哈得孙湾公司1791年在此设站。1781至1782年，天花沿同一条转运小路传入，使各氏族人口大减；两家公司的竞争一直持续到1821年合并。

en:
Here the Saskatchewan River breaks out of the prairies into the boreal forest, widening through Cedar Lake and the Cumberland marshes where the Carrot and Pasquia rivers join it. It is Cree country: bands fished the lakes, took moose and beaver in the woods, and hunted the bison herds on foot at the parkland edge, moving by canoe along waterways that led down to Hudson Bay. In 1444 those canoe roads had never seen a European.

Henry Kelsey paddled up from York Factory in 1690, wintered at Deering's Point on the Saskatchewan near The Pas, and in 1691 went up the Carrot River to become the first European to see bison and grizzlies on the northern plains, returning in 1692 with Cree and Assiniboine hunters. In 1741 the French answered with Fort Paskoya on Cedar Lake, built by the La Vérendryes to divert western furs from the bay to Montreal; a second post at The Pas, raised around 1752, struck Anthony Henday in 1754 as a 'hogstye', and it closed with New France in 1759. Montreal traders soon returned: Joseph Frobisher wintered on Cumberland Lake in 1772, and Samuel Hearne built Cumberland House there for the Hudson's Bay Company in 1774, the first depot of its inland advance. The North West Company built beside it in 1793, and rival houses united there in 1821.
zh:
马米基维尼一带，萨斯喀彻温河流出草原、进入北方针叶林，河面在雪松湖（Cedar Lake）与坎伯兰沼泽间展宽，卡罗特河（Carrot River）与帕斯基瓦河（Pasquia River）先后汇入。这里是克里人的土地：族人在湖中捕鱼，在林中猎驼鹿、捕海狸，又在林缘草原徒步围猎野牛，靠独木舟经各条水路往来——这些水道一直通向哈得孙湾。1444年时，这些独木舟航道上还没有欧洲人的身影。

1690年，哈得孙湾公司的亨利·凯尔西（Henry Kelsey）从约克堡（York Factory）划独木舟上行，在今帕斯（The Pas）附近的迪灵角过冬；1691年他溯卡罗特河而上，成为第一个在北部平原见到野牛和灰熊的欧洲人，1692年带着克里人和阿西尼博因猎人返回。1741年，法国人以雪松湖畔的帕斯科亚堡回应：拉韦朗德里父子建此商栈，意在把西部毛皮从哈得孙湾引向蒙特利尔；约1752年又在今帕斯建起第二座，1754年安东尼·亨德路过时斥其像个「猪圈」，1759年随新法兰西崩溃而关闭。蒙特利尔商人很快卷土重来：1772年约瑟夫·弗罗比舍在坎伯兰湖过冬，1774年塞缪尔·赫恩为哈得孙湾公司在此建起坎伯兰豪斯（Cumberland House），这是公司向内陆推进的第一座货栈。西北公司1793年贴邻设栈，两家对手于1821年在此合为一家。

en:
East of the future Prince Albert the two branches of the Saskatchewan meet in a wide, wooded valley at the edge of the aspen parkland. In Cree the people of this stretch of river were the Sīpīwininiwak, the 'river people', kin of the bands on the lower Saskatchewan; they netted sturgeon in the eddies, hunted moose in the boreal forest to the north and drove buffalo into pounds on the plains to the south and west, where Blackfoot and Gros Ventre camps held the open grass. In 1444 all these peoples still travelled on foot with dog-travois; the horse frontier had not yet reached the Saskatchewan, and the valley was a meeting ground of forest and plains nations.

French traders were on the lower river from 1739, and in 1753 Louis de la Corne carried the French posts to their western limit, building Fort de la Corne about twenty miles below the forks. Anthony Henday for the Hudson's Bay Company passed this way in 1754–55 with Cree and Assiniboine, wintered among the Blackfoot and returned down the North Saskatchewan. Free traders came back after the French withdrawal: James Findlay wintered at Nipawin in 1768, and Fort Sturgeon, the first post on the North Saskatchewan, went up in 1776. The smallpox of 1781–82 emptied camps through the valley, just as the mounted, gun-armed river Cree were becoming the eastern wing of the plains alliance with the Assiniboine. Gros Ventre raiders burned South Branch House in 1793 and Manchester House in 1794; the Hudson's Bay Company raised Carlton House downstream from Fort de la Corne in 1796, and the company's rivalry with the North West Company ran on until the union of 1821.
zh:
在今艾伯特亲王城以东，萨斯喀彻温河的北支与南支汇合于杨树林草原边缘一条宽阔的林木河谷。克里语把这一河段的人称作斯匹维尼瓦（Sīpīwininiwak），即「河人」，与下游各氏族同源：他们在河湾漩流处下网捕鲟，到北方针叶林猎驼鹿，在西、南两面的草原把野牛赶入围栏；开阔草地上则分布着黑脚人和格罗斯文特人的营地。1444年，这些部族仍靠徒步和狗拉拖架迁徙，马匹尚未传到萨斯喀彻温，河谷正是森林民族与草原民族往来交汇之地。

法国商人1739年已出现在下游；1753年，路易·德·拉科尔讷把法国商站推到其西端极限，在汇流处以下约20英里修建拉科尔讷堡。1754至1755年，为哈得孙湾公司效力的安东尼·亨迪随克里人和阿西尼博因人经过此地，到黑脚人处越冬，再沿北萨斯喀彻温河东返。法国势力退出后，自由商人重新到来：詹姆斯·芬德利1768年在尼帕温越冬，1776年北萨斯喀彻温第一座商站斯特金堡建成。1781至1782年的天花使河谷营地十室九空；此时已持枪骑马的河克里人正与阿西尼博因人结成草原同盟，据有其东翼。1793年格罗斯文特袭掠者焚毁南岔屋站，1794年又焚毁曼彻斯特屋站；1796年哈得孙湾公司在拉科尔讷堡下游建起卡尔顿屋，与西北公司的竞争一直持续到1821年两家合并。

en:
Ye Xa Yabine is Hebina, the 'Rock Mountain People' of the Nakoda. The land is the wooded Cypress Hills and the shortgrass plains around them, a high refuge of springs, pine and aspen between the South Saskatchewan and the Missouri. In 1444 it was a hunting ground rather than a fixed frontier: small foot-borne bands wintered in sheltered coulees, drove bison over jumps and dragged their lodges with dog travois. Nakoda-speaking relatives of the Assiniboine were moving northwest toward the plains, while the Hebina themselves would later appear as a southern Assiniboine division.

That division emerged around 1744, when the Mountain Stoney branched from Assiniboine bands as horses and muskets reached the plains. Mounted war parties soon moved through the hills between Blackfoot, Gros Ventre, Cree and Crow country. The fur trade touched only the northern approaches: Gros Ventre warriors burned Manchester House in 1793 and stormed South Branch House in July 1794 after European arms flowed to Cree and Assiniboine, while in 1800 the Siksika chief Old Swan allowed Peter Fidler to build Chesterfield House at the mouth of the Red Deer River. There in 1801–02 Fidler used Old Swan's own maps to chart the upper Missouri and the Rockies. The post did not hold, and when the Hudson's Bay and North West companies merged in 1821 no trading post had yet taken root among the Cypress Hills.
zh:
耶哈亚比内是纳科达人中的赫比纳人（Hebina），意为「岩山人」。这片土地是赛普里斯山及其周围的短草平原：松林、白杨林和泉水构成高地上的游猎避难地，北接南萨斯喀彻温河流域，南通密苏里河水系。1444年时，这里更像游猎之地而非固定边界；徒步的小队伍在避风冲沟过冬，把野牛逼下崖猎取，再靠狗拉拖橇搬运帐篷。与阿西尼博因人同源的纳科达先民正向西北草原移动，而赫比纳作为阿西尼博因人南支的名字要到后世才出现。

这支南支约在1744年形成，山地斯托尼人由此从阿西尼博因人中独立出来；当时马匹和火枪正传入平原，骑马战队很快穿行于黑脚、格罗斯文特、克里和克劳各方之地之间。毛皮贸易只触及此地北缘：1793年，格罗斯文特战士焚毁曼彻斯特商栈，1794年7月又突袭南支商栈，以反击欧洲武器流向克里人和阿西尼博因人；1800年，西格西卡酋长老天鹅允许彼得·菲德勒在雷德迪尔河汇入南萨斯喀彻温河处建立切斯特菲尔德商栈。1801至1802年，菲德勒在此参照老天鹅亲手绘制的地图，测绘上密苏里与落基山脉。这座商栈未能久存；到1821年哈得孙湾公司与西北公司合并时，赛普里斯山中仍没有真正扎根的商栈。

en:
Lake Athabasca is the great shallow lake of the boreal forest, fed by the Athabasca River and drained north through the Slave River to the Arctic. Its Woods Cree name, aðapaskāw, 'where the reeds grow one after another', was later attached to the whole Athabasca country and to its family of languages. In 1444 its shores belonged to Dënesųłiné bands, the people the Cree called Chipewyan, 'pointed hides', after the cut of their parkas: the Kaí-theli-ke-hot'ínne kept the western shore while the Thilanottine followed the Athabasca River. They moved between winter and summer camps, taking caribou and moose and fishing the lakes, with the Cree pressing from the southeast.

In 1715–17 the Chipewyan woman Thanadelthur, guiding Hudson's Bay Company men from Churchill, brokered a peace between her people and the Cree. The first post in the Athabasca country was Peter Pond's Pond House, built on the lower Athabasca River in 1778. Smallpox swept the lake bands in 1781–82. In 1788 Roderick Mackenzie of the North West Company founded Fort Chipewyan at Old Fort Point, moving it to the north shore in 1798; from 1790 the fort kept a library of more than 2,000 volumes, which he called the 'little Athens of the Arctic regions'. Alexander Mackenzie set out from the fort to reach the Arctic in 1789 and the Pacific in 1793. Rival Hudson's Bay posts came and went until the two companies merged in 1821, when the lake's trade centred on Fort Chipewyan.
zh:
阿亚巴斯卡维尼瓦克一带的阿萨巴斯卡湖是北方针叶林中一座广阔的浅水湖，阿萨巴斯卡河注入湖中，湖水向北经斯拉维河注入北冰洋。伍兹克里语称其为阿达帕斯卡乌（aðapaskāw），意为「芦苇一株接一株生长之地」，后来整个阿萨巴斯卡地区乃至阿萨巴斯卡语族都由此得名。1444年时，湖岸属于德内苏林各游群，即克里人口中的奇佩维安人——意为「尖皮」，得名于他们皮袍的裁制样式；卡伊特利克霍廷人据守西岸，蒂拉诺廷人则沿阿萨巴斯卡河游猎。他们在冬营与夏营之间迁徙，猎取驯鹿和驼鹿，在湖中捕鱼，东南方承受着克里人的压力。

1715至1717年，奇佩维安女子塔纳德尔图尔为从丘吉尔堡来的哈德逊湾公司人员充当向导和翻译，斡旋促成了本族与克里人的和约。阿萨巴斯卡地区的第一座商站，是彼得·庞德1778年在阿萨巴斯卡河下游建起的庞德屋。1781至1782年，天花席卷湖畔各游群。1788年，西北公司的罗德里克·麦肯齐在旧堡角建立奇佩维安堡，1798年迁往湖北岸；商站自1790年起藏书两千余册，他戏称这里是「北极地区的小雅典」。亚历山大·麦肯齐从此堡出发，1789年抵达北冰洋，1793年抵达太平洋。哈德逊湾公司的竞争商站几经兴废，直到两家公司于1821年合并，全湖贸易才统归于奇佩维安堡。

en:
Between Lake Athabasca and the Peace River stretches a maze of boreal forest, muskeg and lakes — the lower Athabasca, the Wabasca and Lesser Slave Lake. In 1444 this was Dene country: Beaver and Chipewyan bands moved through its woods after moose and woodland caribou, fishing the lakes and snaring hare in the hard winters. The name Nihithawak belongs to the Woods Cree, who call themselves Nîhithaw, 'the people'; in those years they still lived nearer Hudson Bay and dealt in furs there as middlemen.

During the 18th century Cree bands armed through the Hudson's Bay trade pushed northwest into this country. The smallpox epidemic of 1781 devastated them along with their Dene rivals, and the peace that followed made the Peace River the border between Cree and Dane-zaa. Traders followed the hunters in: the North West Company opened a post at Buffalo Bay on Lesser Slave Lake in 1802, and Cree hunters provisioned the posts with meat and pemmican. When the North West and Hudson's Bay Companies merged in 1821, the Woods Cree were fixed in the land that now bore their name.
zh:
阿萨巴斯卡湖与皮斯河之间，是一片密布着针叶林、沼泽与湖泊的土地——阿萨巴斯卡河下游、瓦巴斯卡河与小奴湖都在这里。1444年时，这里是德内人的家园：比弗人和奇佩维安人的游群在林中追逐驼鹿与林地驯鹿，在湖里捕鱼，严寒的冬季则套捕野兔。尼希塔瓦克之名属于伍兹克里人，他们自称尼希塔乌（Nîhithaw），意为「族人」；那时他们还住在更靠近哈德逊湾的地方，在毛皮生意中充当中间人。

18世纪，凭哈德逊湾贸易获得火枪的克里游群向西北迁入此地。1781年的天花使他们和德内邻族都损失惨重，随后的和约把皮斯河定为克里人与达内扎人的分界。商人随猎人而至：西北公司1802年在小奴湖的布法罗湾开设商站，克里猎手为各商站供应肉食和干肉饼。1821年西北公司与哈德逊湾公司合并时，伍兹克里人已在这片后来以他们为名的土地上扎下根来。

en:
The Peace River runs nearly 2,000 kilometres from the Rocky Mountains to the Peace–Athabasca Delta, threading prairie-bottomed valleys through the boreal forest. In 1444 its banks were the heart of the Dane-zaa, 'the real people', whom their Cree and Dakelh neighbours called the Amiskiwiyiniw and Tsattine, the 'beaver people' of the European traders; they themselves called the water Saaghii Naachii, 'big river'. They hunted bison on the river prairies and moose in the woods, and their generations-old rivalry with the Cree ran through the country to the southeast.

In the later 18th century Cree carrying trade muskets drove the Dane-zaa northwest, until the smallpox epidemic of 1781 broke the Cree pressure. The two nations then smoked a peace pipe and fixed the river as their border, Dane-zaa to the north and Cree to the south — the treaty that gave the Peace River its name. Peter Pond had visited the river in 1785, and in 1788 Charles Boyer of the North West Company built the post at the Boyer River that became Fort Vermilion. Alexander Mackenzie wintered at Fort Fork in 1792–93 and went on up the Peace to the Pacific, and in 1794 the company built Rocky Mountain Fort at the mouth of the Moberly River, the first European post on the British Columbia mainland. The Dane-zaa fed the trade with bison meat and grease until the rival companies merged in 1821.
zh:
皮斯河发源于落基山脉，奔流近两千公里注入皮斯河—阿萨巴斯卡三角洲，在北方针叶林中切出一道道铺着草原的河谷。1444年时，河两岸是达内扎人的腹心，他们自称「真正的人」，而克里人和卡尔克邻族以「阿米斯基维纽」「察廷」相称，意为「海狸人」，欧洲商人据此称他们为比弗人；他们自己则称这条河为萨吉纳奇（Saaghii Naachii），意为「大河」。他们在河畔草原猎野牛、在林间猎驼鹿，与东南方的克里人世代相争。

18世纪后期，手持贸易火枪的克里人把达内扎人逼向西北，直到1781年天花重创克里人，攻势才告瓦解。两个民族随后共吸和平烟斗，约定以河为界——达内扎人在北，克里人在南——皮斯河（和平河）由此得名。彼得·庞德1785年已到过此河；1788年，西北公司的夏尔·布瓦耶在布瓦耶河口设站，后来发展为弗米利恩堡。亚历山大·麦肯齐1792至1793年在福克堡过冬，随后溯皮斯河而上抵达太平洋；1794年，西北公司在莫伯利河口建起落基山堡，这是不列颠哥伦比亚大陆上第一座欧洲人商站。达内扎人以野牛肉和油脂供应毛皮贸易，直到两家竞争公司于1821年合并。

en:
The Siksikawa — Siksikáwa, 'the Blackfoot People' — hold the short-grass prairie of south-central Alberta between the Red Deer River and the North Saskatchewan. In 1444 they were foot hunters: bands of ten to thirty lodges followed the bison on foot, drove them into pounds and over the jumps along the foothill edge, and wintered in timbered river valleys with dogs pulling the travois. Every summer the scattered bands gathered for the Okan, their great sun ceremony. The Siksika, whose name told of moccasins blackened by prairie ash, were the northernmost of the four Blackfoot nations, standing between the woods and the open plains.

Horses and trade guns reached the Blackfoot in the first half of the 18th century, and the mounted Siksika and their allies drove the Shoshone back toward the mountains; by 1787, when the surveyor David Thompson knew their country, Blackfoot power ran from the North Saskatchewan to the Missouri. Anthony Henday of the Hudson's Bay Company wintered in the Blackfoot camps as early as 1754–1755, near the Red Deer, inviting them down to Hudson Bay, but the Siksika preferred to trade through Cree and Assiniboine middlemen and kept the mountain Kootenay away from the posts. The smallpox epidemic of 1781 swept through every band, yet the confederacy remained master of the plains: from 1795 Fort Augustus and Edmonton House, and from 1799 Rocky Mountain House, traded on its northern border, and the Siksika were still called 'Lords of the Plains' in 1821.
zh:
西西卡瓦——即黑脚语所说的锡克锡卡瓦，「黑脚人」——占据艾伯塔中南部雷德迪尔河与北萨斯喀彻温河之间的短草平原。1444年时他们还是步猎的人：十到三十座帐篷组成的队伍徒步追逐野牛，把牛群赶入围栏、逼向山麓边缘的跳崖，冬天则在林木繁茂的河谷扎营，由狗只拉动拖橇。每年夏天，分散的队伍聚集起来，举行盛大的太阳仪式「奥坎」。锡克锡卡人是黑脚四族中位置最北的一支，族名来自被草原灰烬染黑的软皮鞋底，正处在森林与开阔平原之间。

18世纪上半叶，马匹和商队火枪传到黑脚人手中，骑马的锡克锡卡人与盟友把肖肖尼人逐回山区；到1787年测量员戴维·汤普森了解这片土地时，黑脚人的势力已从北萨斯喀彻温河一直伸展到密苏里河。早在1754至1755年，哈得孙湾公司的安东尼·亨德代就随黑脚人的队伍在雷德迪尔附近过冬，劝说他们前往哈得孙湾交易，但锡克锡卡人宁愿经由克里和阿西尼博因中间商做买卖，还阻止山区的库特尼人直接接触商站。1781年的天花大流行横扫各个队伍，黑脚联盟却依旧是平原的主人：1795年起，北萨斯喀彻温河畔先后建起奥古斯都堡与埃德蒙顿屋，1799年又添了落基山屋，商站都开在他们的北境；直到1821年，锡克锡卡人仍无愧于「平原之王」的称号。

en:
Beyond the last ramparts of the Peace River canyon rise the northern Rocky Mountains, where the Finlay and Parsnip rivers gather in the Rocky Mountain Trench to form the headwaters of the Peace. In 1444 this high country belonged to the Tsek'ene, the 'people on the rocks', whom traders later rendered as Sekani. Kindred of the Dane-zaa and the Dakelh, they moved in small nomadic bands through mountains and trench, living by moose and caribou rather than fish like their lake neighbours to the west, and they cremated their dead on the trail.

Toward the end of the 18th century Plains Cree raiding pushed the Sekani deeper into the trench and the mountains. Alexander Mackenzie's canoes worked up the Parsnip in 1793 on his crossing to the Pacific. In 1805 Simon Fraser of the North West Company built two posts: Rocky Mountain Portage House below the Peace canyon and Trout Lake Fort, soon renamed Fort McLeod, on McLeod Lake, the first permanent European settlement west of the Rocky Mountains in present-day Canada. The Sekani brought furs, meat and grease to the new forts, which became the seed of the company's New Caledonia district; the Hudson's Bay Company inherited them with the merger of 1821.
zh:
越过皮斯河峡谷最后的陡岸，便是落基山北段：芬利河与帕斯尼普河在落基山地堑中汇聚，构成皮斯河源头。1444年时，这片高地属于采凯内人——「岩石上的人」，后来的商人把这个名字译作塞卡尼。作为达内扎人和卡尔克人的亲族，他们结成小股游群在山岭与地堑间迁徙，不像西边湖畔的邻族那样以鱼为主，而是靠驼鹿和驯鹿为生，并在行旅途中火化死者。

18世纪末，平原克里人的袭扰迫使塞卡尼人更深地退入地堑与群山。1793年，亚历山大·麦肯齐的独木舟正是溯帕斯尼普河而上，完成了横跨北美大陆的旅程。1805年，西北公司的西蒙·弗雷泽建起两座商站：皮斯峡谷下方的落基山运输屋，以及麦克劳德湖畔的鳟鱼湖堡（不久改称麦克劳德堡），后者是今加拿大境内落基山脉以西第一座欧洲人永久定居点。塞卡尼人把毛皮、兽肉和油脂带到新堡，这些商站后来成为公司「新喀里多尼亚」辖区的雏形；1821年两公司合并后，由哈德逊湾公司接手。

en:
The Dakelh, or Carrier people, occupy the lake country of the central interior, from the Nechako River and Stuart, Fraser and Babine Lakes to the upper Fraser. Their Athabascan tongue belongs to the Dene family, and each family's keyoh, its hunting and fishing grounds, is held under a hereditary chief. Life follows the seasonal round: salmon are taken at the runs and smoked for winter, moose and caribou are hunted through the boreal forest, and hides, dried meat and berry cakes are packed along the 'grease trails' to the coast and exchanged for eulachon oil. In 1444 these trails carry only Dakelh and coastal goods.

Alexander Mackenzie's party followed one of those trails to the Pacific in 1793. In the winter of 1805-06 James McDougall, sent by Simon Fraser, reached Stuart Lake, and in 1806 Fraser built Fort St. James on its shore, the North West Company's anchor in its New Caledonia fur district; two years later Fraser descended the river that now bears his name to its mouth. The trade grew slowly among a people whose living came chiefly from the fishery, and in 1821 the post passed with the rest of the company to the Hudson's Bay Company, becoming the centre of its New Caledonia district.
zh:
达凯尔人（Dakelh，欧洲人旧称卡列尔人）住在中部内陆的湖乡，内查科河、斯图尔特湖、弗雷泽湖、巴宾湖与弗雷泽河上游一带都在其传统地界内。他们的语言属于阿萨巴斯卡语系的德内语支；每个家族的传统狩猎与捕鱼领地（keyoh）由世袭首领掌管。生活随季节轮转：鲑鱼汛期大量捕鱼熏制过冬，在北方森林里猎取驼鹿和驯鹿，再把兽皮、肉干和果饼沿「油脂小道」驮到海岸，换回蜡鱼油。1444年，这些小道上来来往往的还只有达凯尔人与海岸部落的货物。

1793年，亚历山大·麦肯齐的队伍正是沿着其中一条小道抵达太平洋。1805至1806年冬，西蒙·弗雷泽派出的詹姆斯·麦克杜格尔到达斯图尔特湖；1806年弗雷泽在湖畔建起圣詹姆斯堡，作为西北公司新喀里多尼亚毛皮区的据点，两年后他顺后来以他命名的弗雷泽河而下，直抵河口。达凯尔人的生计以渔获为主，毛皮贸易起初进展缓慢。1821年，这座商站随西北公司一并归入哈德逊湾公司，成为新喀里多尼亚区的行政中心。

en:
The Secwepemc, the Shuswap of the early traders, hold the widest country of any people in the southern interior, a plateau land of about 145,000 square kilometres running from the Chilcotin and Cariboo plateaus down the North and South Thompson to Kamloops and across the great bend of the Columbia. Their language is Interior Salish. The bands lived by the salmon runs, the chase and trade with neighbouring peoples, and raided other bands for captives, who were mostly ransomed back for dried salmon. In 1444 the meeting of the two Thompson rivers is a Secwepemc gathering ground alone.

The first European explorers came in 1811, when David Stuart of the Pacific Fur Company wintered with the Kamloops band. In May 1812 Alexander Ross raised Fort Cumcloups at the confluence, and the North West Company answered with Fort Shuswap nearby, absorbing its rival in 1813. Kwa'lila, chief of the main village, moved his people up to the fort gates to control the trade; he was followed by his nephew and foster son Nicola, who later led an alliance of Okanagan and lower Thompson peoples. After the merger of 1821 the post, called Thompson's River Post, answered to the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
赛克维派克人（Secwepemc，早期商人旧译舒什瓦普人）据有南部内陆最广阔的地界：约14.5万平方公里的高原，从奇尔科廷高原、卡里布高原向东南沿北、南汤普森河一直延伸到坎卢普斯，并越过哥伦比亚河大拐弯。他们的语言属内陆萨利什语支。各部以鲑鱼汛期、狩猎和与邻族贸易为生，还会袭击其他部落掳人为俘，俘虏多半被其族人用干鲑鱼赎回。1444年，汤普森河两支流交汇之处还只是赛克维派克人自己的聚会之地。

1811年，太平洋毛皮公司的戴维·斯图亚特到坎卢普斯部过冬，是第一批欧洲探险者。1812年5月，亚历山大·罗斯在两河交汇处筑起库姆克鲁普斯堡，西北公司随即在附近另建舒什瓦普堡与之竞争，并于1813年吞并了对手。主村首领夸利拉率族人迁到堡门附近以控制交易；他死后由外甥兼养子尼古拉继任，尼古拉后来统领奥肯那根人与汤普森河下游诸部结成的同盟。1821年两公司合并后，这座改称汤普森河商站的据点转归哈德逊湾公司。

en:
The Tsilhqot'in, 'people of the river', make their home on the dry plateau between the Coast Mountains and the Fraser, holding most of the Chilcotin River basin and the headwaters of the Homathko and Dean. They are the southernmost of the Athabascan-speaking peoples of British Columbia, and call their country Tŝilhqot'in Nen. Before contact they had a name as a strong warrior nation whose reach ran from the Similkameen in the south to the Rockies and the Pacific coast, and they stood at the centre of a wide trade in obsidian, the glassy stone prized for arrowheads. In 1444 a band's standing rested on its warriors and its access to the obsidian trails.

European goods first reached the plateau in the 1780s and 1790s, carried inland from the British and American sea-otter ships on the coast. By 1808 the North West Company had raised posts in Dakelh country immediately to the north, and Tsilhqot'in furs then moved north both directly and through Dakelh middlemen. In 1821 a post was opened at Fort Alexandria on the Fraser, at the eastern edge of their country, which became the people's main doorway to European goods.
zh:
奇尔科廷人（Tsilhqot'in，族名意为「河上之人」）的家园在海岸山脉与弗雷泽河之间的干燥高原，据有奇尔科廷河流域大部及向西入海的霍马斯科河、迪恩河上游。他们是不列颠哥伦比亚各阿萨巴斯卡语族群中分布最南的一支，称自己的故土为「奇尔科廷嫩」（Tŝilhqot'in Nen）。接触欧洲人之前，他们以强悍善战著称，势力南起西密卡米恩、东抵落基山、西达太平洋海岸，并处在一个黑曜石贸易网络的中心——这种玻璃质岩石是打造箭头的上佳材料。1444年，一个部落的地位系于其武士的勇名和通往黑曜石产地的山路。

1780和1790年代，欧洲货物先随海岸收购海獭皮的英美船只传入内陆高原。到1808年，西北公司已在北面相邻的达凯尔人地界建起商站，奇尔科廷人的毛皮随后或直接北上交易，或经达凯尔人转手。1821年，弗雷泽河畔、奇尔科廷地界东缘的亚历山德里亚堡开设商站，成为他们获取欧洲货物的主要门户。

en:
The Syilx, known to the early traders as the Okanagan, hold the string of long lakes and dry grasslands running south from Okanagan Lake down the Okanagan River to the Columbia, together with the Similkameen country to the west, roughly 69,000 square kilometres in all. They speak an Interior Salish tongue, kin to the Secwepemc and the Nlaka'pamux. Bands wintered in villages of kekuli pit houses and moved through the year with the salmon runs, the root grounds and the deer hunt. In 1444 Okanagan Lake lay at the heart of a web of plateau trails, and no European had yet crossed the mountains to the east.

In 1811 Pacific Fur Company men coming up the Columbia met Okanagan headmen in council on 31 October and raised Fort Okanogan where the Okanagan River joins the Columbia; the Syilx promised the lonely post friendship, furs and food. The North West Company bought it with the rest of Astor's inland enterprise in 1813, and the fur brigades used the Okanagan valley as their road north to Thompson's River and New Caledonia. In 1821 the post passed to the Hudson's Bay Company when it merged with the North West Company.
zh:
锡尔克赫人（Syilx，早期商人惯称奥卡诺根人）据有从奥卡诺根湖南下、经奥卡诺根河通向哥伦比亚河的一串长湖与干草原，连同西面的西密卡米恩一带，地界约6.9万平方公里。他们的语言属内陆萨利什语支，与赛克维派克等邻族相近。各部冬天住在克库里半地穴屋组成的村落，一年中随鲑鱼汛期、根茎采集季和猎鹿之期辗转迁徙。1444年，奥卡诺根湖还是高原商路网的中心，东面的群山尚不曾有欧洲人翻越。

1811年，太平洋毛皮公司的人沿哥伦比亚河而上，在10月31日与奥卡诺根诸首领会盟，并在奥卡诺根河汇入哥伦比亚河处筑起奥卡诺根堡；锡尔克赫人应允与这座人地两生的商站修好，供给毛皮和食物。1813年，西北公司随收购阿斯特的全部内陆产业而取得此堡，毛皮运输队遂取道奥卡诺根河谷北上，往返于汤普森河商站与新喀里多尼亚。1821年，西北公司并入哈德逊湾公司，商站也随之易手。

en:
The Nisga'a take their name from a Tongass Tlingit word meaning 'people of the Nass River'. Their territory follows the Nass from its rain-soaked valley to Nass Bay and Portland Inlet, a 380-kilometre river whose lower 40 kilometres were navigable and whose salmon and oolichan runs supplied winter food. In 1444 Nisga'a clan houses occupied permanent and seasonal villages along this corridor, while canoes carried trade and diplomacy between Tsimshian and Tlingit neighbours.

Disaster struck around 1775, when Nisga'a tradition remembers an eruption of Tseax Cone sending volcanic gas and lava down to the Nass, destroying the villages of Lax Ksiluux, Lax Ksiwihlgest and Wii Lax K'abit and killing about 2,000 people. On 23 July 1793 HMS Discovery and HMS Chatham anchored in Salmon Cove on Observatory Inlet, part of Nisga'a territory; George Vancouver set up an observatory and mapped Portland Inlet before the ships left on 17 August. European navigators had placed the waterway on their charts, but through 1821 the Nass villages remained in Nisga'a hands.
zh:
尼斯加（又译尼斯迦）之名来自汤加斯特林吉特语，意为「纳斯河的人」。他们的土地沿纳斯河从多雨河谷延伸到纳斯湾和波特兰湾；河长380千米，下游40千米可通航，鲑鱼和蜡鱼渔汛是冬季食物的保障。1444年，尼斯加各氏族家族在这条走廊上的永久与季节性村落居住，独木舟维系着他们同钦西安、特林吉特邻族之间的贸易与交涉。

约1775年灾难降临：据尼斯加口传，齐阿克斯火山喷出的有毒气体和熔岩涌向纳斯河，摧毁拉克斯克西卢克斯（Lax Ksiluux）、拉克斯克西威尔盖斯特（Lax Ksiwihlgest）、维拉克斯卡比特（Wii Lax K'abit）三座村落，约两千人丧生。1793年7月23日，「发现号」与「查塔姆号」停泊在尼斯加传统领地观测湾的鲑鱼湾；乔治·温哥华架设观测仪器、测绘波特兰湾，船队于8月17日离去。欧洲航海家虽已把这些水道绘入海图，但直到1821年，纳斯各村落仍由尼斯加人掌握。

en:
The Heiltsuk country of island passages, permanent winter villages and sea harvesting centred on Milbanke Sound and the waters around later Bella Bella. Campbell Island and Lama Passage belonged to a wider central-coast world of Heiltsuk-speaking divisions; families moved seasonally from their winter villages to fish, gather herring roe and shellfish, and tend clam gardens along the shore. Rank, inherited prerogatives and ceremony ordered society, with potlatches making status visible, while Heiltsuk carvers, canoe makers and warriors were renowned among neighbouring nations. In 1444 no European ship had entered these channels.

That changed in late June 1788, when Charles Duncan brought Princess Royal into uncharted Milbanke Sound, traded for several days with the Heiltsuk and named the water after Vice Admiral Mark Milbanke. George Vancouver later sailed through the sound. During the maritime fur trade the Heiltsuk became suppliers and middlemen: their canoe makers learned to build western-style trading schooners, early access to guns strengthened their bargaining power, and European traders found them shrewd and difficult negotiators. Introduced diseases and intensified wars took a heavy toll, but through 1821 no European post had yet been built in these waters; the fort and old Bella Bella later established at McLoughlin Bay still lay ahead.
zh:
黑尔楚克（Heiltsuk，中文又作海尔楚克）人的家园岛径纵横、冬季村落临海，以米尔班克湾和后来贝拉贝拉所在的水域为中心。坎贝尔岛与拉马水道属于黑尔楚克诸部更广的中部海岸世界；各族以永久冬村为基础随季节移动，捕鱼、采集鲱鱼子和贝类，并在潮间带经营蛤蜊养殖地。等级、世代特权与仪式维系社会秩序，夸富宴公开展示身份，黑尔楚克的雕刻者、独木舟匠人和战士也受邻族敬重。1444年，还没有欧洲船只驶入这些水道。

1788年6月底，查尔斯·邓肯率「皇家公主号」进入当时尚未标上海图的米尔班克湾，与黑尔楚克人交易数日，并以海军中将马克·米尔班克之名为海湾命名。乔治·温哥华后来也驶过这里。海上毛皮贸易期间，黑尔楚克人既是供货者也是中间人：独木舟工匠学会建造西式贸易纵帆船，较早取得火器增强了谈判地位，欧洲商人则认为他们精明而难缠。传入的疫病和加剧的战事造成沉重损失，但到1821年，这些水域仍未设立欧洲商站，麦克洛克林湾后来的要塞与旧贝拉贝拉尚未出现。

en:
Kodiak (Alutiiq Qikertaq) is a mountainous island in the Gulf of Alaska, its coast cut by deep bays and fjords, and the homeland of the Koniag Sugpiaq, the Kodiak branch of the Alutiiq people. They lived in large coastal villages of semi-subterranean houses, took salmon from the rivers, hunted sea lions and seals from skin kayaks on the open water, and gathered shellfish on the tides. In 1444 the many villages were linked by kayak along the shore, trading and raiding under local chiefs, and no European had yet landed there.

Stepan Glotov, the first Russian to reach the island, wintered on Kodiak in 1762–64 under repeated attack, and the navigator Potap Zaikov charted its coast in 1778. In 1784 Grigory Shelikhov arrived with 130 men to stay: when the islanders took refuge on the sea stack of Awa'uq off Sitkalidak, his cannon killed an estimated 200 to 500 of them, and hostages secured the rest. Three Saints Bay, founded that year, was the first permanent Russian settlement in Alaska; in 1792 the post moved to St. Paul harbour, the nucleus of the future town of Kodiak, which became the emporium of Russian America. Monks from Valaam brought Orthodoxy in 1794. The Russian-American Company then conscripted the islanders for ever-longer sea-otter voyages far from home, and the archipelago's sixty-odd villages, which had held some 13,000 people at contact, shrank steadily.
zh:
科迪亚克（阿留特克语称基克尔塔克）是阿拉斯加湾中一座多山大岛，海岸被深水海湾与峡湾切开，是科尼亚格苏克皮阿克人的家园，即阿留特克人的科迪亚克支系。他们在海岸边聚成大村落，住半地穴式房屋，从河中捕捞鲑鱼，乘兽皮小艇到海上猎取海狮和海豹，在潮间带采集贝类。1444年时，众多村落靠沿岸水路往来，在地方首领治下贸易、攻掠，还没有欧洲人登上过这座岛。

第一个抵达该岛的俄国人斯捷潘·格洛托夫于1762至1764年在此过冬，期间不断遭到岛民攻击；航海者波塔普·扎伊科夫1778年测绘了海岸。1784年，格里戈里·舍利霍夫率一百三十人前来久占：岛民退守西特卡利达克岛外的海蚀柱阿瓦乌克，他下令开炮，估计有二百至五百人遇害，又以人质制服了其余各部。同年建立的三圣湾是俄罗斯人在阿拉斯加的第一个永久定居点；1792年据点迁到后来科迪亚克城所在的圣保罗港，成为俄属美洲的贸易中心。1794年，瓦拉姆修道院的修士带来东正教。此后俄美公司强征岛民远赴外海长期猎獭，群岛上六十余座村落接触之初共约一万三千人，此后不断凋敝。

en:
The coast between Prince William Sound and the Copper River delta is a tangle of glacier-carved fjords, islands and forested shore, lashed by Gulf of Alaska storms. In the island-studded sound lived the Chugach, an Alutiiq people who hunted seal, sea otter and whale from skin baidarkas and traded or fought the Eyak, Ahtna and Tlingit; at the Copper River mouths, among the richest salmon grounds on the coast, lived the small Eyak nation in a handful of villages such as Alaganik. In 1444 these were among the northernmost peoples of the Northwest Coast, living richly by fish, furs and raids, untouched by Europeans.

On 20 July 1741 the first European foot was set on Alaskan soil here, when the naturalist Georg Steller went ashore from Bering's St Peter on Kayak Island; Bering himself never landed. James Cook's ships entered the sound in May 1778 and named it, first Sandwich Sound and then Prince William. The Spaniards Arteaga and Bodega y Quadra followed in 1779, claiming Port Etches as Puerto de Santiago, and Salvador Fidalgo repeated the claim on the site of Cordova in 1790. Russians first met the Chugach on 17 August 1783, and a month later nine of their sentries lay dead; trade nonetheless followed, and in 1793 the Saints Constantine and Helen redoubt rose at Nuchek on Hinchinbrook Island, where Chugach brought dried fish and furs. The far smaller Eyak nation, pressed by Chugach and Tlingit raids, intermarriage and the newcomers' diseases, kept dwindling.
zh:
威廉王子湾与铜河口之间的海岸，是冰川刻出的峡湾、岛屿和林木海岸交织之地，常年受阿拉斯加湾风暴拍击。岛礁密布的湾中住着楚加奇人，他们是阿留特克人的一支，驾兽皮小艇「拜达卡」猎捕海豹、海獭和鲸，与埃雅克人、阿特纳人和特林吉特人或贸易或交战；铜河口是沿岸最富饶的鲑鱼场之一，小小的埃雅克部族就住在阿拉加尼克等寥寥几座村落里。1444年时，他们是西北海岸最北的族群之一，靠鱼产、毛皮和劫掠为生，欧洲人尚未涉足。

1741年7月20日，欧洲人第一次踏上阿拉斯加的土地：博物学家格奥尔格·斯特勒从白令的「圣彼得号」登上卡亚克岛，白令本人并未上岸。1778年5月，库克的船队驶入海湾并为之命名，初称桑威奇湾，后改名威廉王子湾。西班牙人阿特阿加和博德加-夸德拉1779年接踵而至，在埃奇斯港以「圣地亚哥港」之名宣布占领；萨尔瓦多·菲达尔戈1790年又在后来科尔多瓦城的原址照做一遍。俄国人1783年8月17日首次与楚加奇人相遇，一个月后九名俄军哨兵被杀；贸易仍随之展开，1793年欣钦布鲁克岛的努切克建起圣君士坦丁与圣海伦娜堡，楚加奇人到此用鱼干和毛皮交易。小得多的埃雅克部族在楚加奇人与特林吉特人的袭掠、通婚和新来者带来的疾病夹击下，人口不断流失。

en:
Sitka Sound lies on the western side of Baranof Island, called Shee in Tlingit, where rainforest mountains meet one of the richest sea-otter and fishing grounds of the Alexander Archipelago. In 1444 the Kiks.ádi clan and the Sheetʼká Ḵwáan kept plank-house villages and seasonal camps around the sound. Their large canoes supported trade and raiding along the coast, while clan chiefs and matrilineal houses controlled fishing places, stored salmon and fortified ground.

Alexander Baranov first examined the sound in 1795 while seeking sea-otter grounds, and in 1799 his Russian-American Company party built the Fort of Archangel Michael with Tlingit permission. The arrangement collapsed under demands for allegiance and labor, and in June 1802 Tlingit warriors under Shḵ'awulyéil and Kotleian burned the post. Baranov returned in 1804 with the warship Neva under Yuri Lisyansky; after bombardment and a failed assault, the Kiks.ádi slipped away from their sapling fort in October. The Russians raised New Archangel on the harbor, which became the capital of Russian America in 1808, while Tlingit clans nearby kept up a trade embargo through 1821.
zh:
锡特卡湾位于巴拉诺夫岛西岸，特林吉特人称该岛为希岛（Shee）；雨林覆盖的群山临着亚历山大群岛最丰饶的海獭与渔场之一。1444年，基克萨迪氏族和锡特卡地方群体（Sheetʼká Ḵwáan）在湾畔拥有木板房屋村落与季节性营地。大型独木舟既用于沿海贸易，也用于袭掠；氏族首领和母系大家族控制渔场、鲑鱼储备以及设防地点。

亚历山大·巴拉诺夫为寻找海獭猎场，在1795年首次考察此湾；1799年，他的俄美公司队伍在取得特林吉特长老许可后建起大天使米迦勒堡。效忠和服劳役的要求很快摧毁了这一安排，1802年6月，什卡乌列尔与科特良率领的特林吉特战士焚毁据点。1804年，巴拉诺夫带着尤里·利相斯基指挥的「涅瓦号」战舰返回；经过炮击和一次失败的强攻，基克萨迪人在10月悄悄撤离幼树堡垒。俄国人随即在港畔建立新阿尔汉格尔斯克，并于1808年将其定为俄属美洲首府；邻近的特林吉特氏族则一直以贸易禁运相抗，直至1821年。

en: In 1444 the dry lower Rio Grande valley bearing the name Cotoname was a homeland of small nomadic Cotoname-speaking bands, who hunted and gathered across southern Texas and northeastern Mexico. Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca crossed neighboring Coahuiltecan country in the early 1530s. From 1580 Luis de Carvajal's raids along the Rio Grande seized people for enslavement, and the smallpox and measles epidemic of 1636–1639 began a long demographic collapse. José de Escandón's Nuevo Santander colonization reached the lower valley in 1748; in 1757 Spanish observers identified fourteen bands in the delta. Missions, ranches and towns then overshadowed the old rancherías, and most local Coahuiltecans were absorbed into colonial society over the following decades.
zh: 1444年，得名科托纳梅的里奥格兰德河下游干旱河谷是若干说科托纳梅语的游猎小群体的家园，他们在得州南部与墨西哥东北部之间往来采集。1530年代初，阿尔瓦·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡穿过邻近的科阿韦尔特坎地区。1580年起，路易斯·德·卡瓦哈尔沿里奥格兰德掳掠人口为奴，1636—1639年的天花与麻疹疫情开启了长期人口崩溃。何塞·德·埃斯坎东开拓新桑坦德的行动在1748年推进到下游河谷；1757年，西班牙观察者在三角洲辨认出十四个群体。传教站、牧场和城镇随后压过旧有的游动营地，此后数十年间多数当地科阿韦尔特坎人被吸纳进殖民社会。

en:
The dry plains and ridges of the Bajío were Guamare country. Around 1400, pressure from the Aztec Empire to the east and the Purépecha to the south moved several local peoples to form the league called Pechichitane Altepetlatskostli, whose chiefs decided common action through a council. In 1444 the country remained outside both empires. The league was not a single people: the Guaxabanes were Guachichiles, the Xiconaques were Zacatecos, and only groups such as the Copuces were regarded as pure Guamares; the Spanish later used Ixtlachichimecas and Guamares as broad labels for them all.

After 1543, silver strikes in Zacatecas and Guanajuato drew Spanish roads, mining towns and allied native settlers into the semi-arid country, opening the long Chichimeca War. In 1563 Guamare fighters destroyed Pénjamo and attacked Comanja de Jaso, and in 1569 they struck El Robledal near Guanajuato and reached Jilotepec before Pedro de Ahumada Sámano defeated them. Spanish columns could not break the guerrilla resistance by force. By the early seventeenth century the Crown pacified the region through treaties, gifts, land grants and mission settlements, and the Guamare communities were gradually drawn into the mining society of New Spain.
zh:
巴希奥的干旱平原和丘陵是瓜马尔人的土地。约1400年，为应对东面阿兹特克帝国与南面普雷佩查的压力，若干当地族群结成佩奇奇塔内·阿尔特佩特拉斯科斯特利联盟，由各族酋长通过议事会决定共同行动。1444年，这片土地仍处在两大帝国之外。联盟并非单一族群：瓜克萨班人属于瓜奇奇尔人，西科纳克人属于萨卡特卡人，只有科普塞斯等支系被视为纯瓜马尔人；西班牙人后来则把他们泛称为伊斯特拉奇奇梅卡人或瓜马尔人。

1543年后，萨卡特卡斯和瓜纳华托发现银矿，把西班牙人的道路、矿镇和同盟土著定居者引入这片半干旱地带，漫长的奇奇梅克战争由此展开。1563年，瓜马尔战士摧毁彭哈莫并进攻科曼哈-德哈索；1569年，他们又袭击瓜纳华托附近的罗夫莱达尔，一度进抵希洛特佩克，最终被佩德罗·德·阿乌马达·萨马诺击败。西班牙军队无法以武力压服游击抵抗。到17世纪初，西班牙王室通过条约、礼物、土地授予和传教定居点安抚当地，瓜马尔社群也逐渐被纳入新西班牙的矿业社会。

en:
The Seri homeland was the arid Sonoran coast between the Encinas Desert, the inland mountains, and the Gulf of California, with Tiburón and San Esteban islands as part of its western reaches. Its nomadic bands moved between desert hunting grounds, fishing shores, and island camps; their territory stretched from the Altar Desert in the north toward the Yaqui River in the south, and leaders were chosen only for war or unusually hard seasons. In 1444 the Seri lived beyond the reach of the inland Mexican empires, taking their living from both the desert and the gulf.

Spanish expeditions touched Sonora in the sixteenth century, but no lasting settlement was planted in Seri country. The steadiest colonial contact came later through Jesuits, who tried to gather the bands into agricultural missions; the Seri rose against that pressure in 1725 and repeatedly returned to their desert rounds. When Charles III expelled the Jesuits in 1767, the mission system collapsed. By Mexican independence in 1821 the Seri had lost people and ground, but Spanish sources acknowledged that they had never been formally conquered, pacified, or evangelized.
zh:
塞里人的家园是索诺拉干旱海岸，夹在恩西纳斯沙漠、内陆山地与加利福尼亚湾之间，蒂布龙岛和圣埃斯特万岛也属于其活动范围西缘。各个游居群体往来于沙漠猎场、捕鱼海岸和岛屿营地之间，传统领地北起阿尔塔沙漠，南至亚基河一带；只有在战争或狩猎、渔获异常艰难的季节，他们才临时推举首领。1444年时，塞里人仍不受墨西哥内陆诸帝国控制，同时依靠沙漠与海湾为生。

西班牙探险队在16世纪已抵达索诺拉，但没有在塞里人的土地上建立持久定居点。后来最持续的殖民接触来自耶稣会士，他们试图把各群体集中到农业传教区；塞里人在1725年因这种压力起事，并一再回到沙漠游居生活。卡洛斯三世1767年驱逐耶稣会士后，传教体系随之瓦解。到1821年墨西哥独立时，塞里人虽人口锐减、领地收缩，但西班牙资料也承认，他们从未被正式征服、平定或改宗。

en:
Huichol is the broken southern edge of the Sierra Madre Occidental, where the Bolaños canyon cuts through the forested ridges of northern Jalisco. Wixárika families lived in scattered mountain rancherías, spoke a Uto-Aztecan language related to Nahuatl, and exchanged salt with neighbouring peoples. Peyote gathering, fire ceremonies and kinship bound their communities more tightly than any single town. In 1444 the difficult highland roads kept this country apart from the richer valley chiefdoms nearer Lake Chapala and the Pacific coast.

Nuño de Guzmán's brutal campaign through Jalisco in 1531 drove native groups into these mountains. During the Mixtón War of 1540–1541, communities of the Gran Chichimeca and Sierra Madre rose against Spanish raids, encomiendas and mining labour, and Wixárika groups withdrew deeper into the Nayar highlands. They joined their highland neighbours in revolt at El Teúl in 1592 and rose again at Nostic in 1702. The canyons allowed their villages, rites and language to endure on the rough margin of Spanish colonial rule.
zh:
维乔地处西马德雷山脉南段的破碎山地，博拉尼奥斯峡谷切开哈利斯科北部林木覆盖的山脊。维乔人自称维夏里卡，各家族散居在山间村落，使用与纳瓦特尔语相近的犹他—阿兹特克语，并同周边族群交换食盐。佩奥特仪典、火祭和亲族关系把各社区联结起来，其纽带比任何单一城镇都更牢固。1444年，崎岖的山路使这片高地与查帕拉湖和太平洋沿岸较富庶的谷地酋邦保持着距离。

1531年，努尼奥·德·古斯曼征伐哈利斯科时手段残暴，把原住民群体逼入这片山地。1540—1541年米克斯通战争期间，大奇奇梅卡和西马德雷山区的诸族群起而反抗西班牙人的劫掠、委托监护制和矿山劳役，维乔各部也退入纳亚尔高地深处。1592年，他们与山地邻族在埃尔特乌尔起事；1702年又在诺斯提克起兵。凭借峡谷天险，他们的村落、仪典和语言在西班牙殖民统治的粗糙边缘延续下来。

en:
The arid northern Bolsón de Mapimí and neighbouring basins were Toboso country. The Toboso spoke a language influenced by Tepehuan and hunted with sling and spear, moving between desert camps. They had ties with the peoples of La Junta de los Ríos farther north but lived farther south, while the Irritila of the valleys were their rivals. In 1444 the Spanish frontier had not yet reached them, and many autonomous bands shared the land.

When Antonio de Espejo passed through in 1583, the Jumano at La Junta welcomed his expedition while the Toboso fled, for their southern lands had already felt Spanish slaving raids. From the 1640s Toboso bands attacked Spanish-controlled missions and Tarahumara mines to the west. Many Toboso were later taken to missions around Monterrey, but large numbers left them and rejected Christianity; Spaniards called them ladinos because they used their knowledge of frontier life against the settlements. Raids on Tarahumara missions and ranches continued in the 1690s. The Spanish counted twelve Toboso bands in the 1680s but only four by 1693, among them the Chichitames and Sisimbles. By 1800 Toboso who remained in Mexico had been absorbed into mestizo society, although baptismal records from 1807 place some refugees at the Texas-coast mission of Nuestra Señora del Refugio.
zh:
干旱的马皮米洼地北部及周边盆地是托沃索人的土地。托沃索人使用受特佩万语影响的托沃索语，以投石索和长矛狩猎，在沙漠营地间往来。他们与北方两河汇流处的居民有联系，但住得更靠南；谷地中的伊里蒂拉诸部则是其敌手。1444年，西班牙人的边疆尚未推进到这里，许多自主游群分据这片土地。

1583年安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍经过时，两河汇流处的胡马诺人友好迎接探险队，托沃索人却四散躲避，因为他们靠南的土地已经承受过西班牙奴隶劫掠。从1640年代起，托沃索游群向西袭击西班牙人控制的传教站和塔拉乌马拉矿山。后来许多托沃索人被带到蒙特雷一带的传教站，但大批人离开并拒绝基督教；西班牙人称他们为「拉迪诺人」，因为他们把对边疆生活的了解用来对抗定居点。1690年代，他们继续袭掠塔拉乌马拉人的传教站和牧场。西班牙人在1680年代还数出十二个托沃索游群，到1693年只确认四个，其中包括奇奇塔梅斯人和西辛布雷斯人。到1800年，留在墨西哥的托沃索人已基本融入梅斯蒂索社会；1807年起的洗礼记录则显示，一些避难者出现在得克萨斯海岸的努埃斯特拉·塞尼奥拉·德尔·雷富希奥传教站。

en:
The Laguneros — the Irritila, as their name is most often recorded — lived around a chain of shallow lakes in the Bolsón de Mapimí, fed by the Nazas and Aguanaval rivers. These included the great Laguna de Mayrán, once called the Great Lake of Nueva Vizcaya, and the smaller lakes of Viesca, Tlahualilo and Álamo. They were not one people but a dozen or more bands speaking different tongues, who used Nahuatl as a common language and kept their villages on the lake shores. In 1444 they sowed nothing and kept no herds, living by fishing the lagoons, hunting and gathering mesquite, prickly pear and maguey, and moving as the waters and harvests shifted.

Expeditions out of the new silver mines pushed north after Zacatecas was founded in 1557 and Durango in 1563: fray Pedro Espinareda in 1566, Francisco Cano in 1568 and Alberto del Canto in 1577 found populous Irritila rancherías but no mines, so the lagoon country was left to missionaries. By a royal cédula of 6 April 1594 Philip II named it the Provincia de La Laguna and entrusted it to the Jesuits, whose reports from Parras describe naked, houseless fishermen so wary that the priests feared being killed and eaten. The missions never took firm root: around 1687 the Jesuits were expelled from the region, the mission villages were abandoned, and the surviving Irritila drifted back into the desert and disappeared as a distinct people.
zh:
拉古内罗斯人——其族名通常被记作伊里蒂拉人——生活在马皮米封闭盆地的一串浅湖周围，湖泊由纳萨斯河和阿瓜纳瓦尔河注入。其中有大湖马伊兰潟湖（旧称「新比斯开大湖」），另有别斯卡、特拉瓦利洛和阿拉莫等较小的湖泊。他们并非单一民族，而是十余个操不同语言的游群，彼此以纳瓦特尔语往来，村落就设在湖岸上。1444年时他们不事农耕、不养牲畜，以潟湖捕鱼、狩猎和采集豆灌木、仙人掌、龙舌兰为生，随湖水涨落和采集季节迁徙。

1557年萨卡特卡斯、1563年杜兰戈两座银矿城镇建立后，西班牙人的远征队随即北上：佩德罗·埃斯皮纳雷达修士1566年、弗朗西斯科·卡诺1568年、阿尔韦托·德尔·坎托1577年先后来到湖边，见到人烟稠密的伊里蒂拉村落，却没找到金银矿藏，湖区于是被留给传教士。1594年4月6日，腓力二世颁布王旨，将此地定名「潟湖省」，交由耶稣会经营；传教士从帕拉斯发出的报告称这些渔民居无定所、不穿衣服、警惕至极，连神父都担心被他们杀掉吃掉。传教事业始终未能扎根：1687年前后耶稣会被逐离此地，传教村遭到废弃，幸存的伊里蒂拉人退回荒漠，作为一个独立族群就此消亡。

en:
The Nyakipa occupied the southwestern corner of the wider Kiliwa country behind San Quintín Bay on the Pacific coast. They were closely related to the eastern Kiliwa and, like them, spoke a Yuman language. Life followed water and seasonal foods: pit-roasted agave was the most important staple, acorns and pine nuts drew families into the higher hills, rabbits and deer were taken in organized hunts, and the Pacific shore supplied fish and shellfish. In 1444 these autonomous bands had neither towns, agriculture, nor outside overlords.

Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo reached the San Quintín coast in 1542, but contacts remained sparse for more than two centuries. Wenceslaus Linck reached the eastern approaches to Kiliwa country in 1766, and the Portolá-Serra expedition passed through its western lands in 1769. The decisive colonial foundation came in 1775, when Dominicans Miguel Hidalgo and Manuel García established Santo Domingo northeast of San Quintín among the Kiliwa of this frontier. An inadequate water supply forced the mission to move east in 1793. Epidemics and mission congregations reduced the native population, which had already fallen sharply by Mexican independence in 1821; from that year Santo Domingo no longer had a resident priest.
zh:
尼亚基帕人（Nyakipa）占据圣金廷湾后方、广义基利瓦地区西南角的太平洋沿岸。他们与东基利瓦人关系密切，同样使用尤曼语系语言。生活随水源和季节物产移动：坑烤龙舌兰是最重要的主食，橡子和松子把各家族引向较高的山地，人们有组织地猎捕兔和鹿，太平洋岸则提供鱼和贝类。1444年，这些自治小队没有城镇、农业，也没有外来宗主。

1542年，胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略抵达圣金廷海岸，但此后两个多世纪里接触仍然稀少。文策斯劳斯·林克1766年抵达基利瓦地区东部边缘，波尔塔与塞拉的远征队1769年穿过其西部土地。决定性的殖民据点出现于1775年：多明我会士米格尔·伊达尔戈和曼努埃尔·加西亚在圣金廷东北建立圣多明各传教站，向这边疆地带的基利瓦人传教。由于供水不足，传教站于1793年东迁。疫病和传教集居使原住民人口减少，到1821年墨西哥独立时已经大幅衰落；圣多明各也从这一年起不再有常驻神父。

en:
Tizapan occupies the southeastern shore of Lake Chapala, close to the old frontier with Michoacán. The Nahuatl name means a place of chalk, and Chichimec communities farmed and fished along the lake and the La Pasión river. Because the country lay within reach of the Purépecha kingdom, its villages suffered repeated incursions from Michoacán. In 1444 it was a border lake shore, pressed between the small chiefdoms of Jalisco and the more powerful state beyond the frontier.

Spanish captains under Hernán Cortés conquered the district toward the end of 1521. Alonso de Ávalos later visited it with the friars Miguel de Bolonia and Juan de Padilla, and native and Spanish families were brought together in the colonial Estancia de Tizapán, later called San Francisco Tizapán. The new settlement kept the lake shore tied to Sayula and the royal province of Ávalos through the rest of the colonial period.
zh:
蒂萨潘位于查帕拉湖东南岸，邻近古时与米却肯交界的边地。其纳瓦特尔语名称意为「白垩之地」，奇奇梅卡诸部沿湖岸和拉帕西翁河农耕、捕鱼。由于此地处在普雷佩查王国势力可及之处，村社屡遭来自米却肯的入侵。1444年，这里是哈利斯科诸小酋邦与边界另一侧强国之间受挤压的湖滨边疆。

1521年底，埃尔南·科尔特斯麾下的西班牙队长征服了这一地区。阿隆索·德·阿瓦洛斯后来与修士米格尔·德·博洛尼亚、胡安·德·帕迪利亚到此，原住民与西班牙家庭被编入殖民时期的蒂萨潘牧场，后称圣弗朗西斯科·蒂萨潘。在整个殖民时代后期，这座新聚落同萨尤拉和阿瓦洛斯皇家省保持联系。

en:
Cuitzeo takes its name from the broad, shallow lake at the northeastern edge of the Purépecha highlands, a place whose Purépecha name meant a place of water jars. East of the lake, the obsidian quarries around Ucareo had supplied central Mexican cities for centuries before Tarascan power reached the basin; under Hiripan in the fifteenth century, Zinapécuaro and its villages were drawn into the tribute network ruled from Tzintzuntzan. Local people kept a temple to Cuerauáperi, mother goddess of the Purépecha. In 1444, fishermen, maize farmers and obsidian workers here lived on a prosperous inland frontier of the Purépecha realm.

Spanish forces reached the district around 1530, when Luis Montañez founded the settlement of Zinapécuaro; Franciscan friars took charge of evangelization there, while Cuitzeo became an encomienda and Augustinians began the monastery of Santa María Magdalena in 1550, the foundation around which the colonial town grew. Native communities were reorganized as a republic of Indians under the new government of Michoacán. Long after the conquest had turned the lake shore into a quiet agricultural district, Miguel Hidalgo's insurgent forces entered Zinapécuaro in October 1810, carrying the Mexican independence rising through this corner of Michoacán.
zh:
奎采奥得名于普雷佩查高地东北缘宽阔水浅的奎采奥湖，普雷佩查语地名意为盛水器皿之地。湖东的乌卡雷奥黑曜石矿曾在数百年间供应墨西哥中部诸城；15世纪伊里潘向外扩张时，锡纳佩夸罗及其村落被纳入以钦聪灿为中心的贡赋网络。当地人还建有祭祀普雷佩查母神库埃拉瓦佩里的神庙。1444年，渔民、玉米农和黑曜石工匠居住在此，使这里成为普雷佩查王国富庶的内陆边地。

约1530年，西班牙势力进入这一地区，路易斯·蒙塔涅斯建立锡纳佩夸罗定居点；方济各会修士负责当地传教，奎采奥则成为委托监护地，奥斯定会会士于1550年开始修建圣玛利亚·马格达莱纳修道院，殖民城镇也围绕它发展起来。土著村社在新的米却肯政府治下被整编为印第安人共和国。征服过去很久后，湖滨已成平静农业区，米格尔·伊达尔戈率领的起义军又在1810年10月进入锡纳佩夸罗，把墨西哥独立运动带到米却肯的这一角。

en:
Cutzamala lies in the hot Tierra Caliente corridor where streams descend toward the Balsas. Its Nahuatl name means a place of weasels, and a weasel-like idol was venerated here before the Purépecha conquered the town around 1410 and called it Apatzingani. They made it a southeastern frontier post looking toward central Mexico. In 1444 its Matlatzinca and Nahua farmers lived under the power of Tzintzuntzan; in the following decades the garrison faced Aztec Oztuma, and Purépecha tradition remembered the warriors of Apatzingani serving the death god Apatzi.

After the Spanish conquest an encomienda of Cutzamala is documented under Hernán Cortés in 1528. Silver from the Alba de Liste mines financed the church of the Assumption, raised with its convent from 1555 to 1565 in Plateresque style under Juan Bautista Moya. The frontier town became an insurgent base in December 1813, when José María Morelos gathered Mariano Matamoros, Hermenegildo Galeana, Nicolás Bravo and some 6,900 men with thirty cannon before marching on Valladolid. Morelos returned for Corpus Christi in May 1815 and heard Mass in the great church; Agustín de Iturbide was lodged there in 1821, as Spanish rule in Mexico came to an end.
zh:
库察马拉坐落在火地通道上，河溪顺着炎热山地流向巴尔萨斯河流域。它的纳瓦特尔语地名意为「鼬鼠之地」，当地曾供奉形似鼬鼠的偶像。约1410年，普雷佩查人征服此镇，称之为阿帕钦加尼，并把它建成面向墨西哥中部的东南边境据点。1444年，这里的马特拉钦卡和纳瓦农民已处在钦聪灿的权势之下；此后数十年间，当地驻军与阿兹特克人的奥斯图马要塞对峙，普雷佩查传统也记得阿帕钦加尼战士侍奉死神阿帕齐。

西班牙征服后，1528年的文献已记载库察马拉成为埃尔南·科尔特斯名下的委托监护地。阿尔瓦·德·利斯特诸矿出产的白银资助了圣母升天教堂，这座银匠风格建筑及修道院由胡安·包蒂斯塔·莫亚主持，在1555年至1565年间建成。1813年12月，这座边镇成为起义军基地，何塞·玛丽亚·莫雷洛斯在此会合马里亚诺·马塔莫罗斯、埃梅内希尔多·加莱阿纳、尼古拉斯·布拉沃，集结约6900人和30门火炮，随后向巴利亚多利德进军。1815年5月，莫雷洛斯回到这里过基督圣体节，并在大教堂听弥撒；1821年阿古斯丁·德·伊图尔维德也曾驻跸此镇，此时西班牙在墨西哥的统治已近终结。

en:
