1503年1月6日，哥伦布第四次航行期间，西班牙人在加勒比海岸建立圣玛丽亚·德贝伦，但原住民的抵抗迫使他们放弃殖民地。贝拉瓜公国长期实际保持独立；在涉及路易斯·科隆的仲裁后，其地于1557年并入铁拉菲尔梅。胡安·鲁伊斯·德·蒙哈拉斯随后命弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯前去征服，巴斯克斯建立圣菲和康塞普西翁，贝拉瓜斯则在1560年设为督军府。两人的反目引发加图河之战，村镇离散、矿业中断，最后由拉斐尔·德·菲格罗拉继续完成征服。圣地亚哥·德·贝拉瓜斯建于1621年10月23日，1637年迁往新址；1687年，莫伊塞斯·范克莱因和佩德罗·皮卡多率领海盗洗劫该城。1751年巴拿马检审庭撤销后，贝拉瓜斯划归铁拉菲尔梅总兵辖区实行军政。1821年12月1日，圣地亚哥宣布脱离西班牙，加入西蒙·玻利瓦尔的哥伦比亚。

en:
The Eyeish, also written Ais, were a Caddo-speaking people whose villages and bayou lands lay between the Neches and Sabine rivers, around the stream later called Eyeish Creek. In 1444 they were connected to the wider Caddo world yet stood uneasily within it: their relations with the Hasinai were often hostile, and they were also on poor terms with peoples west of the Trinity and near the Red River.

The first known Spanish encounter came in 1542, when survivors of the De Soto–Moscoso entrada reached this part of East Texas and reported large buffalo herds. More than a century and a half later, Domingo Ramón's expedition brought Franciscans to the Ais, and Antonio Margil founded Nuestra Señora de los Dolores de los Ais in 1717. French pressure forced the missionaries out in 1719 during the War of the Quadruple Alliance, but the mission was re-established near its old site in 1721, guarding El Camino Real de los Tejas and Spain's Louisiana frontier. Most Ais kept their own practices; in roughly fifty years the mission drew only about thirty converts, and the Marquess of Rubí's inspection brought its closure in 1773. Smallpox and measles cut deeply into the community. John Sibley recorded only twenty Eyeish in 1805, and in 1821 their borderland passed from Spain to newly independent Mexico.
zh:
耶伊斯人（Ais）是使用卡多语的族群，村落与河湖地带位于内奇斯河与萨宾河之间，即后来被称为艾什溪的水道一带。1444年，他们同更广大的卡多世界保持联系，却并非其中顺从的一支：他们与哈西奈人时常敌对，同特里尼蒂河以西、雷德河附近诸族关系也很紧张。

已知最早的西班牙接触发生在1542年，德·索托—莫斯科索远征队的残部进入东得克萨斯这一带，并记录下庞大的野牛群。一个半多世纪后，多明各·拉蒙的远征把方济各会士带到耶伊斯人中，安东尼奥·马吉尔于1717年创立艾什痛苦圣母传教站（Nuestra Señora de los Dolores de los Ais）。1719年四国同盟战争期间，法国压力迫使传教士撤离，但传教站1721年又在旧址附近重建，扼守特哈斯皇家大道与西班牙面对路易斯安那的边境。多数耶伊斯人仍保留自己的仪轨；约五十年间，传教站只吸引约三十人改宗，鲁维侯爵巡视后于1773年将其关闭。天花和麻疹使这个社群损失惨重。约翰·西布利1805年只记录到二十名耶伊斯人；1821年，这片边地随得克萨斯由西班牙转入独立的墨西哥之手。

en:
The lower Rio Grande country, where the Gulf coastal plain gives way to dry grassland and mesquite thorn scrub, was Konitsąąįį gokíyaa, the country of the Tú sis Ndé — the 'Great Water People', Tuintsundé — a band of the Lipan Apache. The Lipan call themselves Ndé, 'the people', speaking an Athabaskan tongue carried south from the Great Plains over generations. They lived in brush wikiups, following bison and deer and gathering mescal and mesquite. In 1444 that southern drift had barely begun: the camps along the river still belonged to older Coahuiltecan-speaking foragers, no horse had yet been seen, and no European had yet reached the country.

By 1608 the Ndé had Spanish horses, turning into mounted raiders whose range ran on both sides of the Rio Grande and deep into Coahuila; Spanish slavers hunted them in return through the 1600s. They enter the records as Lipanes in 1718, raiding the new settlement of San Antonio and its Coahuila supply trains, although two of their chiefs made peace there in 1749. The missions of San Lorenzo de la Santa Cruz and Candelaria, founded for them on the Nueces River, could not hold them: by 1767 the Lipan had left, and Comanches burned the missions that year. Smallpox had swept the bands three years earlier, and that same year the Marqués de Rubí called for their extermination. Lipan auxiliaries served with Elizondo at Acatita de Baján in 1811, and when Mexico became independent in 1821 the raiding along the Coahuila frontier had not stopped.
zh:
里奥格兰德河下游一带，海湾平原逐渐过渡为干草原和豆灌木荆棘丛，这里是科尼康伊·戈基亚——图西斯·恩德人的故土。图西斯·恩德意为「大水之人」，即图沙逊德，是利潘阿帕奇的一个游群。利潘人自称「恩德」，意为「人」，所操的阿萨巴斯卡语是一代代人从大平原南迁带来的。他们住在灌木搭成的窝棚里，追逐野牛和鹿，采集龙舌兰和豆灌木。1444年时南迁才刚刚开始：河畔营地还属于更古老的科阿韦尔特卡语游猎族群，马还没有出现，欧洲人也尚未踏上这片土地。

到1608年，恩德人已有了西班牙马，成为骑马的袭掠者，活动范围横跨里奥格兰德河两岸、深入科阿韦拉，而整个17世纪西班牙奴隶贩子也反过来围猎他们。1718年，他们以「利潘人」之名首次见于西班牙文献，袭掠新建的圣安东尼奥和从科阿韦拉出发的补给车队；1749年，两名利潘首领在圣安东尼奥议和。西班牙人在努埃塞斯河畔为他们修建圣洛伦索·德·拉圣克鲁斯和坎德拉里亚传教站，却留不住人：到1767年利潘人已离开传教站，同年科曼奇人焚毁了传教村。三年前天花曾使各族群元气大伤，同年鲁维侯爵又下令对他们斩尽杀绝。1811年，利潘辅助兵随埃利松多的部队参加了巴汉伏击；1821年墨西哥独立时，科阿韦拉边境上的袭掠仍未止息。

en:
Between the southward bend of the Nueces River and the lower Rio Grande, the South Texas plain breaks into dry thorn scrub and grassland crossed by no permanent roads. The Cacaxtles were a hunting band in this region, one of the hundreds of small autonomous peoples later lumped together as Coahuiltecan; their name comes from the kakaxtle, the netted carrying frame they bore on their backs. They lived in scattered rancherías, hunting deer and bison and gathering prickly pear, mesquite and mescal as the seasons turned. In 1444 they knew nothing of Spaniards, horses or missions, and their raiding ran only against neighbouring bands.

Pineda mapped the coast to the east in 1519, but the Cacaxtles enter history on the attack: between 1653 and 1663 they and their allies crossed the Rio Grande to raid Spanish settlements and mining camps in Coahuila and the Nuevo Reino de León. Punitive expeditions followed in 1663 and 1665, and in two battles about two hundred Cacaxtles were killed and as many taken, the captives sold to the mines of Zacatecas and Durango. The battles broke Cacaxtle power, and little was recorded of them afterward. In 1685 La Salle founded his short-lived Fort Saint-Louis on the Texas coast to the north-east, and Spanish patrols sent to hunt it down crossed Cacaxtle country, as Alonso de León did on his way to the fort's ruins in 1689. In the decades that followed Lipan and Comanche raiders operated in the region, and at Mexican independence in 1821 this was still a roadless frontier of war.
zh:
努埃塞斯河南折处与里奥格兰德河下游之间，南得克萨斯平原铺展成干旱的荆棘丛和草原，没有常年通行的道路。卡卡斯特斯人是这一带的狩猎游群，后来被笼统称为科阿韦利特卡人的数百个小型自治族群之一；他们的名字来自「卡卡斯特尔」，即背负重物时使用的网兜背架。他们住在分散的村落里，猎鹿和野牛，随季节采集仙人掌果、豆灌木和龙舌兰。1444年的卡卡斯特斯人不知道西班牙人、马和传教站为何物，袭掠的对象只有邻近的游群。

1519年皮内达测绘了东边的海岸，但卡卡斯特斯人是以袭击者的身份进入历史的：1653至1663年间，他们联合盟友渡过里奥格兰德河，袭扰科阿韦拉和新莱昂王国的西班牙村镇与矿营。西班牙人的惩罚性远征于1663年和1665年先后渡河，两战之中约两百名卡卡斯特斯人被杀、差不多同样数目的人被俘，俘虏被卖往萨卡特卡斯和杜兰戈的矿场。两战重创了卡卡斯特斯人的势力，此后有关他们的记载稀少。1685年，拉萨尔在东北方的得克萨斯海岸建立短命的圣路易堡，奉命搜寻它的西班牙巡逻队穿过卡卡斯特斯人的土地——1689年阿隆索·德·莱昂正是沿这条路找到了堡垒的废墟。此后数十年间，利潘人和科曼奇人的袭掠队伍在这一带活动；1821年墨西哥独立时，这里仍是无路可走的战争前线。

en: In 1444 the country bearing the name Borrado belonged to small mobile Quinigua-speaking bands. Their rancherías lay in the dry corridor between the Sierra Madre Oriental and Sierra de Tamaulipas, bounded by the Rio Grande and the Pilón Grande, where families hunted, gathered and fished. Alberto del Canto's Santa Lucía settlement, founded in 1577, failed under native attacks. Luis de Carvajal launched the New Kingdom of León in 1580–1582, but the colony collapsed after his Inquisition arrest. Diego de Montemayor permanently founded Monterrey in 1596, and Franciscans opened San Andrés convent in 1602. War, slave raiding and disease reduced the Borrados, whose poorly recorded Quinigua language is thought to have disappeared by the late eighteenth century.
zh: 1444年，得名博拉多的土地属于若干说奎尼瓜语的流动小群体。其临时营地分布在东马德雷山脉与塔毛利帕斯山脉之间、里奥格兰德河和皮隆格兰德河围出的干旱走廊中，人们在那里狩猎、采集和捕鱼。阿尔韦托·德尔·坎托1577年建立的圣卢西亚据点在原住民袭击下失败。路易斯·德·卡瓦哈尔于1580—1582年开创新莱昂王国，但他被宗教裁判所逮捕后，殖民地也随之崩溃。迭戈·德·蒙特马约尔于1596年永久建立蒙特雷，方济各会1602年开设圣安德烈斯修道院。战争、奴隶掳掠和疫病使博拉多人人口锐减，记载稀少的奎尼瓜语据信在18世纪末以前已经消失。

en:
Between the Sabine and Trinity rivers, in the pine woods and bayous of easternmost Texas, lived the Hasinai, a loose confederacy of Caddo-speaking peoples — the Nabedache, Hainai, Nacogdoche and others — whose name meant 'our own people'. Along the Neches and Angelina rivers they cleared fields of maize, beans and squash and dwelt in pole-framed, grass-thatched lodges, their villages gathered around earthen temple mounds served by priests. In 1444 these were among the most numerous farming peoples anywhere on the Gulf plain, their world still untouched by Europeans.

Survivors of Hernando de Soto's expedition under Luis de Moscoso crossed this country in 1542, the first white men the Hasinai saw. Henri Joutel, journeying on after La Salle's death, reached the Nabedache at the headwaters of the Neches; the French called these people the Cenis. Fear of France drew Alonso de León inland in 1690, and two missions, San Francisco de los Tejas and Santísimo Nombre de María, rose among the Nabedache, who also received Jumano traders at their western town. Smallpox swept through in the winter of 1690–91, killing some 3,300 people, and both missions were gone by 1693; a people numbering perhaps 10,000 in 1690 had fallen to about 2,000 by 1720. Missions returned with Domingo Ramón in 1716, were lost in the war scare of 1719 and restored in 1721, only to be withdrawn to San Antonio in 1731. In 1779 Antonio Gil Y'Barbo led settlers back to lay out the pueblo of Nacogdoches by the old Nacogdoche village.
zh:
在萨宾河与特里尼蒂河之间、得克萨斯最东端的松林与水网地带，居住着哈西奈联盟——纳贝达切、海奈、纳科多切等说卡多语的部族，其族名意为「我们自己的人」。他们在内奇斯河与安杰利娜河畔开辟玉米、豆类和南瓜田，住在木骨草顶的圆屋里，村落围绕祭司侍奉的土筑神庙丘分布。1444年的哈西奈人是墨西哥湾沿岸平原上人口最稠密的农耕族群之一，他们的世界此时还从未有欧洲人涉足。

1542年，埃尔南多·德·索托探险队的残部在路易斯·德·莫斯科索率领下穿过此地，哈西奈人第一次见到欧洲人。拉萨勒死后继续跋涉的亨利·茹泰勒在内奇斯河源头抵达纳贝达切人的村落，法国人把这些人称作「塞尼人」。对法国势力的警惕促使阿隆索·德·莱昂于1690年深入内陆，在纳贝达切人中间建起圣弗朗西斯科·德·洛斯特哈斯和至圣圣马利亚两座传教站；他们最西端的村镇也同来自草原的霍瓦诺商人交易。1690年至1691年冬天天花蔓延，约三千三百人病死，两座传教站到1693年均告废弃；1690年约有一万人的族群，到1720年只剩两千人左右。1716年多明戈·拉蒙重设传教站，1719年因战事恐慌撤离，1721年再度恢复，最终仍于1731年迁往圣安东尼奥。1779年，安东尼奥·希尔·伊巴尔沃率领移民回迁，在纳科多切人的旧村旁规划建立了纳科多奇斯镇。

en:
Tahontaenrat was the southwestern edge of historic Wendake, the wooded creek country north of Orr Lake where trails left the Bear towns for Petun tobacco fields and Neutral hunting grounds. Iroquoian farmers built bark longhouses, planted maize, beans and squash, and drove deer into rivers and enclosures for meat and hide. In 1444 this was still a borderland among Wendat, Petun and Neutral exchange networks rather than a fixed four-nation frontier. The Deer People, probably formed from communities on the north shore of Lake Ontario, entered the Wendat confederacy only around 1610 and made this district their home.

By the 1620s their single fortified village, Scanonaenrat, called Saint-Michel by French missionaries, was one of the strong towns of Wendake and could field hundreds of warriors. Measles in 1634, influenza in 1636-1637 and smallpox in 1639 helped reduce the combined Wendat and Tionontati population to about 10,000-12,000. In March 1649 a Haudenosaunee army armed through Dutch trade burned Saint-Ignace and Saint-Louis, and the French burned Sainte-Marie rather than leave it to the invaders. After the continued collapse, the people of Saint-Michel gave themselves up to the Iroquois and later kept their own Huron village among the Seneca. Their old clearings north of Orr Lake were left empty; Ojibwe families later travelled through them, and the Lake Simcoe-Lake Huron Purchase of 1815 brought the district under British treaty.
zh:
塔洪塔恩拉特是历史上温达克的西南边缘，地处奥尔湖以北、溪涧纵横的林地。小路从熊族村落通向佩蒂温人的烟草田和中立联盟的猎场。易洛魁语农人在这里建造树皮长屋，种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜，并把鹿赶入河道或围场以取得肉和鹿皮。1444年时，这里仍是温达特、佩蒂温与中立联盟交换网络之间的边地，还不是固定的四族联盟边界。鹿族大概由安大略湖北岸的社群聚合而成，约1610年才加入温达特联盟，并把这一地区作为家园。

到1620年代，他们唯一设防的村落斯卡诺纳恩拉特（Scanonaenrat，法国传教士称圣米歇尔）已是温达克的强镇之一，可出动数百名战士。1634年的麻疹、1636年至1637年的流感和1639年的天花，使温达特与蒂翁农塔提总人口降到约一万至一万二千。1649年3月，一支经荷兰贸易获得火器的豪德诺索尼军队焚毁圣伊尼亚斯和圣路易，法国人也烧毁圣玛丽传教站，以免其落入敌手。局势继续崩溃后，圣米歇尔的人向豪德诺索尼人投降，后来在塞尼卡人中保有自己的休伦村落。他们在奥尔湖以北开垦的旧地随之空弃，后来奥吉布瓦家族在此往来；1815年的《锡姆科湖—休伦湖购地条约》使这一地区纳入英国条约体系。

en:
The Mississagi country lies along the North Channel of Lake Huron, where a wide Ojibwe-named river drains the northern forests. The Mississaugas are an Anishinaabe and Ojibwe people; their early lands included the shores of northern Lake Huron and the river called Misi-zaagi, 'at the wide river mouth'. Canoes linked riverside camps with the interior woods and the fishing lake, and travel followed the water rather than roads. In 1444 the valley was beyond European maps, but it stood on Anishinaabe routes between the upper Great Lakes, Nipissing country, and Huronia.

French records later spelled the band as Oumisagai or Mississauga, and a French map of 1675 marked them in the upper Great Lakes. In 1649-50, Iroquois raids during the Beaver Wars destroyed the Huron-Wendat towns to the south and carried warfare through the Great Lakes routes. Around 1700 some Ojibwe moved south toward Lake Ontario, and the French applied the Mississagi river name to those bands. The river mouth itself retained its place in the fur trade: the North West Company built a post there in 1799 to check competition from the Timiskaming country, and it passed to the Hudson's Bay Company with the merger of 1821.
zh:
米西索加（密西沙吉）之地位于休伦湖北海峡沿岸，一条由奥吉布瓦语命名的宽阔河流从北方森林注入湖中。密西沙吉人是阿尼什纳比人的奥吉布瓦支系，传统土地包括休伦湖北岸以及密西沙吉河（Misi-zaagi），意为「宽大河口」。独木舟把河畔营地、内陆森林和产鱼的湖岸连接起来，人们旅行皆循水道而非道路。1444年，这片河谷还没有出现在欧洲地图上，却处在阿尼什纳比人往来五大湖上游、尼皮辛人之地与休伦尼亚的路线之间。

法国文献后来用乌米萨盖（Oumisagai）、密西索加（Mississauga）等名称记载这一支人，1675年的法国地图已在五大湖上游标出他们。1649—1650年的河狸战争中，易洛魁武装摧毁了南方的休伦-温达特村镇，战祸也沿五大湖路线蔓延。1700年前后，部分奥吉布瓦人南下安大略湖北岸，法国人便把密西沙吉河名用于那些支群。河口本身仍在毛皮贸易中占有一席之地：西北公司于1799年在此设立贸易站，以阻挡贸易流向蒂米斯卡明一带；1821年公司合并后，贸易站转入哈德逊湾公司。

en:
Kitkehaki is the Republican River country, where cold plains meet fertile bottoms along the Kansas-Nebraska line. In 1444 Caddoan-speaking Pawnee families lived in earth and grass lodges, planted corn, beans and squash, then left the valley on communal buffalo hunts. Their descendants became the Kitkehahki, the Republican Pawnee whose villages gave the river its French trader name.

In 1541 Coronado crossed Quivira into Harahey, the next Caddoan country to the north, and met Pawnee-related people who answered his summons as armed followers rather than guides to gold. Horses reached the plains later in the seventeenth century, sharpening Apache, Osage and Omaha raiding while French traders carried metal weapons up the Missouri. The Kitkehahki occupied the Republican valley intermittently from the 1770s. In 1798 Omahas acting for Chief Blackbird burned their lodges and killed about a hundred Pawnees after a calumet dispute. The band was back on the Republican by 1806, when Facundo Melgares's Spaniards arrived first with gifts and a Spanish flag; Zebulon Pike followed and persuaded the chiefs to exchange it for the United States flag. Louisiana had passed between France and Spain before its American purchase in 1803, but in 1821 the Republican valley remained Kitkehahki ground.
zh:
基特凯哈基是共和河地区，寒冷草原与肥沃低地在堪萨斯—内布拉斯加一线相接。1444年，说卡多语的波尼家族住在土屋和草屋里，种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，随后离开河谷集体猎捕野牛。他们的后裔形成基特凯哈基人，即「共和波尼人」；法国商人后来以其村名命名这条河。

1541年，科罗纳多穿过基维拉，进入北方相邻的卡多地区哈拉赫，见到与波尼人有关的居民；应召而来的是携带弓箭的随从，而不是通往黄金的向导。17世纪后期，马匹传入草原，阿帕奇人、奥塞奇人和奥马哈人的袭掠随之加剧，法国商人则沿密苏里河带来金属武器。基特凯哈基人从1770年代起断断续续占据共和河谷。1798年，奥马哈人在一次烟斗仪式争执后奉黑鸟酋长之命焚毁他们的屋舍，杀死约一百名波尼人。1806年，这支波尼人已回到共和河；法昆多·梅尔加雷斯率领西班牙人先到，带来礼物和西班牙旗，泽布伦·派克随后说服首领将其换成美国旗。路易斯安那在1803年售予美国前几经法国与西班牙转手，但到1821年，共和河谷仍是基特凯哈基人的土地。

en:
Pasai lies on the northern Sumatran coast east of Kutaraja, facing the Strait of Malacca. The fourteenth-century Malay history Hikayat Raja-raja Pasai explains its names: Merah Silu, hunting on high ground, came upon an ant as large as a cat and called the place Samudera; after he converted and ruled the coast as Sultan Malik ul Salih, his hound Si-Pasai met a deer that was not frightened of its barking but barked back, so he named his new settlement after the dog. The Muslim kingdom took shape around 1267, and a royal tomb of 1297, carved entirely in Arabic, is one of the earliest marks of Islam in the archipelago. Marco Polo spent five months there waiting out the monsoon, and Zheng He's fleets called three times. In 1345 Ibn Battuta stayed a fortnight in the wooden-walled town as the guest of a pious Shafi'i sultan, who sent him onward to China in one of his own junks; the Moroccan wrote that no Muslim ruler held land farther east. By the late fourteenth century Pasai was a wealthy emporium for gold and forest produce, and pepper spread through its hinterland early in the fifteenth, but after Majapahit attacked and made it submit, Malacca's safer harbour drew the shipping away. In 1444 Pasai was still a Muslim trading power, already living in Malacca's shadow.

The Portuguese, who knew the place as Pacem, occupied Pasai in 1521, ten years after taking Malacca. Aceh attacked in 1523 and 1524, overcame the local ruler and the Portuguese fortress, and the garrison withdrew in 1524, when Sultan Ali Mughayat Syah annexed the coast. Pasai kept no court of its own after that. Its pepper fields and Muslim trading networks became parts of Aceh Darussalam and followed Kutaraja into its wars with Johor and Portuguese Malacca.
zh:
八昔位于苏门答腊北部海岸、哥打拉贾以东，面向马六甲海峡。14世纪的马来史书《巴赛列王传》记下了国名的由来：梅拉·西卢在一片高地上打猎时，见到一只大如家猫的蚂蚁，便把那里叫作苏木都剌；他皈依伊斯兰教、称苏丹马利克·乌勒·萨利赫统治海岸后，他的猎犬西巴赛遇到一只不惧狗吠、反而回吠的鹿，他又以猎犬的名字命名新的定居点。这个穆斯林王国约1267年成形，1297年的一座王陵通篇以阿拉伯文镌刻，是伊斯兰教传入群岛最早的标志之一。马可·波罗曾在此等候五个月季风，郑和船队也三次到访。1345年，伊本·白图泰在木墙城镇做客两周，主人是一位虔诚奉行沙斐仪派教法的苏丹，还派自己的帆船送他前往中国；这位摩洛哥人写道，再往东就没有穆斯林统治者的土地了。到14世纪末，巴赛已是黄金和林产汇聚的富庶商埠，15世纪初胡椒又遍种腹地；但满者伯夷来攻、迫使它臣服后，防护更佳的马六甲港把商船渐渐吸走。1444年的巴赛仍是穆斯林贸易政权，却已生活在马六甲的阴影下。

葡萄牙人把这里称作帕塞姆，1521年，即夺取马六甲十年后，出兵占领巴赛。亚齐在1523—1524年来攻，击败当地统治者和葡萄牙要塞，守军于1524年撤离，苏丹阿里·穆加亚特·沙阿随即兼并这条海岸。巴赛此后不再有自己的宫廷，胡椒田和穆斯林贸易网络都并入亚齐达鲁萨兰，随哥打拉贾投入对柔佛和葡属马六甲的战事。

en:
Peureulak, also written Perlak, is a coastal district of east Aceh facing the Strait of Malacca. Its lowlands grew perlak, a durable timber prized for building ships and houses, and the region took its name from the tree. Arab, Persian and Gujarati ships were already calling there by the eighth century, and local tradition dates to 1 Muharram 225 AH, or 840, the proclamation of what it calls the first Muslim state in Southeast Asia. Its first sultan, Alaiddin Syed Maulana Abdul Aziz Shah, was an Arab of Quraysh descent married to a local chief's daughter, and the capital Bandar Perlak was renamed Bandar Khalifah after Nakhuda Khalifah, the shipmaster said to have first brought Muslim teachers to the bay. The sultanate is given to have lasted until 1292, when Pasai absorbed it, and in 1444 the town and its spice-growing hinterland were under Pasai, the Muslim sea power on the neighbouring coast.

Ali Mughayat Syah's campaigns from 1520 drew Peureulak into the Aceh Sultanate as Aceh conquered Pasai, Pedir and Deli. Its merchants shared in the pepper and spice traffic that brought Dutch and English ships to northern Sumatra, while Aceh fought Portuguese Malacca and Johor for the strait. After the strong seventeenth-century reigns the court weakened, and by the 1680s local lords and port chiefs governed much of the coast in the sultan's name; Bandar Khalifah itself had shrunk to a small village.
zh:
卑列拉又译佩尔拉克，是亚齐东部面向马六甲海峡的沿海地区。周围低地盛产卑列拉木，木质坚固，适于造船和建房，地区也因这种树得名。阿拉伯、波斯和古吉拉特的船只8世纪起便在此停靠；当地相传，回历225年穆哈兰月初一，即840年，这里宣告建立东南亚第一个穆斯林政权，首任苏丹阿拉丁·赛义德·毛拉纳·阿卜杜勒·阿齐兹·沙是出身古莱什的阿拉伯人，娶了当地首领的女儿；都城班达·卑列拉改名班达·哈里发，以纪念据说最早把穆斯林经师带到海湾的船主纳胡达·哈里发。苏丹国据当地说法延续到1292年，随后被八昔吞并；1444年，这座城镇和出产香料的内陆受邻近海岸的穆斯林海上强国八昔统治。

阿里·穆哈亚·赛亚自1520年起征战，亚齐先后攻灭八昔、珀迪尔和德利，把卑列拉纳入亚齐苏丹国。当地商人参与胡椒和香料贸易，荷兰和英国船只随之来到苏门答腊北部，亚齐则同葡属马六甲和柔佛争夺海峡控制权。17世纪的强盛期过去后，宫廷权力转弱，到1680年代，沿海大部分事务已由地方首领和港主以苏丹名义治理，班达·哈里发本身也缩成了一座小村。

en:
Rokan is the lowland basin of the Rokan River, which crosses eastern Sumatra to a marshy mouth on the Strait of Malacca. Fishing villages and riverside markets sent fish and forest products downstream, and their boats tied the upper valley to the commerce of Malacca. On the Left Rokan tributary stood Rokan IV Koto, a kingdom founded in 1340 by Sutan Seri Alam, and the Javanese court poem Nagarakretagama already names Rokan among the lands beyond Java. In 1444 its Muslim Malay and Minangkabau settlements lay between two greater powers, Pagaruyung in the highlands behind them and Malacca on the strait.

Pagaruyung's tie ran deeper than suzerainty. Tomé Pires, writing his Suma Oriental in 1513-1515, put Rokan between Arcat and Rupat as a Pagaruyung vassal, and in the sixteenth century the upstream kingdom of Tambusai was founded by Sultan Mahyuddin, a son of the ruler of Pagaruyung, while Rambah and other small Muslim states took shape on the same tributaries. The valley's own rulers lost it to Siak. In 1724-1726 Raja Kecil, the Johor pretender who had built a new sultanate on the Siak River, brought Rokan within his dominions. Siak later divided the lower valley into the Bangko and Tanah Putih districts, with borders running upstream toward Tambusai and Kepenuhan.
zh:
洛江（Rokan）是罗干河流域的低地，罗干河穿过苏门答腊东部，在马六甲海峡边的沼泽河口入海。渔村和河边市集把鱼产、林产顺流运出，船队也把上游河谷与马六甲的贸易连在一起。左罗干河畔有罗干四科托王国，1340年由苏丹·斯里·阿拉姆建立；爪哇宫廷史诗《爪哇史颂》已把洛江列为爪哇以外的邦国之一。1444年，这里信伊斯兰教的马来人和米南加保人聚落夹在两个强邻之间，一个是高原上的帕加鲁永，一个是海峡边的马六甲。

洛江与帕加鲁永的关系不止于宗主名分。托梅·皮莱资1513年至1515年间写《东方志》时，把洛江标在阿尔卡特与鲁帕岛之间，记为帕加鲁永的附庸；16世纪，帕加鲁永统治者之子苏丹马赫尤丁在支流上游建立坦布赛王国，兰巴等穆斯林小邦也在各条支流上成形。洛江本地的统治者最终失掉了河谷。1724年至1726年，在锡亚河畔建立新苏丹国的柔佛王位觊觎者拉惹·基希尔把洛江并入版图。锡亚后来把下游划为邦科和丹那布蒂两区，边界沿河上溯，直至坦布赛和克佩努汉一带。

en:
Indragiri is the river country behind Sumatra's eastern coast. The Sinamar, flowing out of Lake Singkarak in the Minangkabau highlands, joins the Ombilin to form the Batang Kuantan, which takes the name Indragiri as it nears the Strait of Malacca. Malay villages and trading clearings lined its banks, and Talang Mamak communities held the inland forests; its Sanskrit name means 'hill of Indra', a trace of pre-Islamic worship. By its own tradition the Kerajaan Indragiri was founded by Raja Merlang I, a prince of Melaka, and Tomé Pires wrote that it sent tribute to the Melaka of his day. In 1444 Raja Merlang II, a Muslim, reigned over a network of river chiefs rather than a compact territorial state.

Around 1473 Narasinga II succeeded, brought from Melaka by Datuk Patih and the Rakit Kulim chiefs. He built the first royal palace at Kota Lama and made the ruler reside in his own capital instead of governing through distant upriver chiefs. The fort raised there in the sixteenth century had walls four hundred metres long on each side and seven metres high, standing five hundred metres from the river; its southern enclosure holds the tombs of Indragiri's kings, Narasinga among them. In the following centuries the sultanate manoeuvred among Aceh, Johor and Siak. Sultan Ibrahim joined the 18 June 1784 attack on Dutch Melaka in Teluk Ketapang Bay and founded Rengat two years later. When his reign ended in 1815 the court moved down to Rengat, while Dutch-backed chiefs installed a Sultan Muda, a junior sultan, upriver at Peranap, splitting authority between the new river town and the old interior.
zh:
丁机宜（因德拉吉里）是苏门答腊东海岸后方的河域。锡纳马尔河出自米南加保高地的辛卡拉克湖，与翁比林河汇成库安坦河，下游临近马六甲海峡时称因德拉吉里河。马来村落和贸易林盘沿河分布，塔朗·马马克人居住在内陆森林中；其名出自梵语，意为「因陀罗之丘」，还带着前伊斯兰时代崇拜的痕迹。按本国传统，丁机宜王国由马六甲王族拉惹·默朗一世开创，托梅·皮莱士记载它向马六甲纳贡。1444年，穆斯林君主拉惹·默朗二世统治着一张由沿河酋长组成的网络，而不是一个边界紧密的国家。

约1473年，纳拉辛哈二世继位，他由拿督·帕蒂和拉基特库利姆诸酋从马六甲迎回。他在哥打拉马修建第一座王宫，使君主常驻都城，不再借重远方的上游酋长。16世纪在那里筑起的堡垒，每边城墙长400米、高7米，距河500米；南院是丁机宜历代君主的墓地，纳拉辛哈也葬在其中。此后数百年，苏丹国在亚齐、柔佛和锡亚克之间周旋。苏丹易卜拉欣参加了1784年6月18日克塔邦湾进攻荷属马六甲的战事，两年后兴建冷岳。1815年他统治结束，宫廷迁往下游的冷岳；受荷兰支持的首领们又在上游佩拉纳普立了一位副苏丹，使权力分属新河城与旧内陆。

en:
Jambi commands the lower Batang Hari, the river that carries gold, pepper and forest products from the Sumatran interior to the Strait of Malacca. At Muaro Jambi, twenty-six kilometres downriver from the city, eight excavated brick temples and eighty unexcavated mounds run seven and a half kilometres along the bank, the remains of the Melayu kingdom, which dominated Sumatran trade in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries and may have held the early seat of Srivijaya itself. Chinese records knew the port as Zhanbei; its envoys reached the Tang court in the ninth century, and Song porcelain has been dug up at the temples. The old polity fell to a Javanese attack in 1278, and the riverside settlement of Tanah Pilih, core of the later city, was founded in 1401. In 1444 Jambi is a Malay river port where Islam is taking root, still within Majapahit's distant Sumatran sphere; in 1460 Datuk Paduko Berhalo and his wife Putri Selaras Pinang Masak founded the local royal line.

Pepper made Jambi's fortune. Vines planted along the Batang Hari and Tembesi and gold, beeswax, resin and timber from the upriver forests drew Chinese junks every year, and Chinese merchants held the office of shahbandar; pepper crowded out the rice fields so thoroughly that the city depended on Javanese grain. In 1615 Pangeran Kedah took the title Sultan Abdul Kahar, Dutch and English traders opened their posts, and within a year Jambi was accounted the second-richest port in Sumatra after Aceh. It accepted Mataram's overlordship in the 1640s and broke away two decades later. Rivalry with Johor over Kuala Tungkal then brought fifteen years of war: Jambi burned Johor's capital in 1673, but in 1679 a Johorese fleet said to number three hundred ships forced the river blockade and exacted an indemnity, and the pepper trade never recovered. The VOC deposed Sultan Ingalaga in 1688 and split the realm into upper and lower river domains, reunited only in 1708; the Dutch later abandoned their factory. A capital revolt in 1811 and the civil war that followed left the sultan holding Upper Tembesi while a rival held the upper Batang Hari.
zh:
占碑控扼巴当哈里河下游，苏门答腊内陆的黄金、胡椒和林产品都经这条河运往马六甲海峡。城以下26公里的穆阿罗占碑，八座已发掘的砖寺和八十座未发掘的土冢沿河绵延7.5公里，是末罗瑜王国的遗存；该国在12至13世纪主导苏门答腊贸易，有人认为室利佛逝早期的都城也在这里。中国史籍称此港为占卑，9世纪已有占卑使节抵达唐朝宫廷，寺址还出土过宋代瓷器。1278年，古城毁于爪哇的入侵，后来占碑城的核心塔纳西利赫建于1401年。1444年的占碑是伊斯兰教开始扎根的马来河港，仍处在满者伯夷对苏门答腊的遥远势力圈内；1460年，拿督·帕杜科·贝尔哈洛与妻子普特里·塞拉拉斯·皮南马萨克开创了本地王统。

胡椒成就了占碑的财富。巴当哈里河与坦贝西河沿岸种满胡椒藤，上游森林出产黄金、蜂蜡、树脂和木材，中国帆船每年驶来购货，沙班达（港务长官）也由华人充任；胡椒挤占粮田，城中食粮只能仰仗爪哇。1615年，吉打王子称苏丹阿卜杜勒·卡哈尔，荷兰和英国商人同年开设商馆，不出一年，占碑已被视为苏门答腊仅次于亚齐的第二富港。它在1640年代接受马打兰的宗主权，二十年后又脱离。随后为争夺瓜拉通卡尔与柔佛开战，前后打了十五年：占碑1673年焚毁柔佛都城，1679年柔佛一支据称有三百艘船的舰队突破河道封锁、勒索赔款，胡椒贸易再未恢复。1688年荷兰东印度公司废黜苏丹因加拉加，把国土分为河上游与河下游两部，1708年才重新统一，荷兰人后来也放弃了商馆。1811年都城叛乱，随后的内战打到苏丹只保住坦贝西上游，巴当哈里河上游落入对手手中。

en:
Bangka lies across the Gaspar Strait from the Musi estuary, a low island of white-sand shores and metal-bearing gravels. The Kota Kapur inscription of 686, cut on its west coast, shows the reach of Srivijaya, and Majapahit later claimed the island before it fell quiet. Fei Xin, a soldier on Zheng He's voyages, called it Peng-ka Hill in the account he presented to the Ming court in 1436, and saw Chinese junks trading in the waters off the Musi. In 1444 only a few Malay and Sawang sea-people's villages cling to the coasts, loosely attached to Palembang; the island lives from the passage that carries Palembang's pepper and spices toward China, and no one yet knows its river gravels hold tin.

Islam came in with Johor and Minangkabau traders, and after passing under Banten the island was inherited by Palembang in the later seventeenth century. Tin was found in the southern rivers around 1710, and the find remade Bangka. In 1722 the Palembang court brought in miners from Johor, Siam and Champa and granted the Dutch East India Company a monopoly on tin purchases; in the 1730s Encek Wan Akub laid out Muntok as the mining port, and Chinese miners from Guangdong soon joined the Malays at the gravels. Tin ingots became the island's livelihood, and before the century ended Bangka ranked among Asia's chief tin producers. The mines then pulled it into the British invasion of Java. In 1811 Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin's men stormed the Dutch post on the island and killed its staff; a British expedition took Muntok in 1812, renamed it Minto, and the new sultan ceded Bangka to Britain. Under the Anglo-Dutch convention of 1814 the island was exchanged for Cochin in India, and Dutch officials returned in 1816 to run the mines. In 1821 Muntok is the tin emporium of the Gaspar Strait under the Dutch flag.
zh:
邦加与穆西河河口隔加斯帕海峡相望，是一座低平岛屿，沿岸多白沙滩，砂砾中含金属。西海岸686年凿刻的科塔卡普尔铭文，显示了室利佛逝势力之所及；满者伯夷后来也声称据有此岛，再后来邦加重归沉寂。随郑和下西洋的士兵费信，在1436年进呈明朝的《星槎胜览》中称它为「彭加山」，并见到中国帆船在穆西河口外的海面通商。1444年，岛上只有几处马来人与萨旺海人的村落，松散地依附巴邻旁；岛民靠那条把巴邻旁胡椒和香料运往中国的航道为生，还无人知晓河砾里藏着锡矿。

伊斯兰教随柔佛和米南加保商人传入，邦加一度归属万丹，17世纪后期由巴邻旁继承。1710年前后岛南河道发现锡矿，邦加的面貌为之一变。1722年，巴邻旁宫廷从柔佛、暹罗和占婆招募矿工，把锡的专买权授予荷兰东印度公司；18世纪30年代，恩切·温·阿库布辟建矿业港口文岛，广东华工不久也来到矿砂地，与马来人一同开采。锡锭成了全岛的生计，到18世纪末，邦加已跻身亚洲主要产锡地之列。锡矿又把它卷进英国入侵爪哇之役：1811年，苏丹马哈茂德·巴达鲁丁的部众袭取岛上的荷兰商馆，杀了馆中人员；英军1812年攻占文岛，改名明托，新任苏丹把邦加割让给英国。依1814年的英荷协定，邦加被用来交换印度的柯枝，荷兰官员1816年回返，重营锡矿。1821年的文岛，是加斯帕海峡上一座挂着荷兰旗的锡业商埠。

en:
Belitung is a granite island in the Java Sea, between the Gaspar and Karimata straits that separate Sumatra from Borneo. Its people call it Belitong, and its name is said to come from a kind of sea snail. Malay fishing villages kept to the sheltered bays, and the crop traders came for was white pepper, called sahang locally. These were old sailing waters: around 830 an Arab dhow carrying Tang ceramics went down off the coast on her way home from China. In 1444 Belitung had neither court nor walled port, and its headmen governed themselves on the edge of a commercial world run from Palembang, Java and Borneo.

When the Palembang Sultanate was proclaimed in 1659 it counted Belitung among its outer islands. The island was drawn into European war in September 1811, when Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II's followers attacked the Dutch lodge at Palembang and killed twenty-four Europeans. Britain, then holding Java, sent an expedition under Robert Rollo Gillespie, and a treaty signed in April 1812 ceded Bangka and Belitung to the British; Palembang princes kept up resistance in parts of the islands for months afterwards. In 1821 Belitung was still formally held by Britain, and most of its people still called it Belitong.
zh:
勿里洞是爪哇海中的一座花岗岩岛，地处隔开苏门答腊与婆罗洲的加斯帕尔海峡和卡里马塔海峡之间。岛上居民称它比利通，据说岛名来自一种海螺。马来渔村多设在有屏障的海湾内，商人来此收购的作物是白胡椒，当地称萨杭。这片水域早有商船往来：约830年，一艘满载唐朝瓷器的阿拉伯独桅帆船从中国返航时在勿里洞外海沉没。1444年时，勿里洞既无王廷也无城墙港口，首领们各自为政，地处巨港、爪哇与婆罗洲商业势力所及的边缘。

1659年巨港苏丹国建立后，把勿里洞算作外围属岛之一。1811年9月，苏丹马哈茂德·巴达鲁丁二世的部众袭击巨港的荷兰商馆，杀死二十四名欧洲人，勿里洞也被拖进欧洲人的战争。当时占据爪哇的英国派出罗伯特·罗洛·吉莱斯皮率军远征，1812年4月签订的条约把邦加和勿里洞割让给英国；此后几个月，巨港的王子们仍在群岛部分地区继续抵抗。到1821年，勿里洞名义上仍在英国手中，岛上多数人依旧叫它比利通。

en:
Muko-Muko lies on the wet, forested west coast of Sumatra at the southern end of the Minangkabau lands, where short rivers break through to the Indian Ocean. Its people, the Mukomuko, speak a language close to Minangkabau and follow its matrilineal clans, and the Minangkabau chronicles count their shore as the rantau, the outer coast running south from Padang. Rice fed the river-mouth villages, and their politics looked north to Inderapura, the 'Edge of Pagaruyung', formally a vassal of the kings of Pagaruyung but in practice free to run its own affairs; pepper and gold made that court rich. In 1444 Muko-Muko was the southern rim of a Minangkabau maritime world, still ordered in the old pre-Islamic manner.

After Malacca fell to the Portuguese in 1511 the eastern trade swung round to Sumatra's west coast and pepper planting spread south. Dutch reports in 1616 described Inderapura as a prosperous kingdom of some 30,000 people farming rice and pepper, and by the later 1500s the little kingdom of Anak Sungai held the shore from the Manjuto river to Air Urai, seated at Sungai Selagan, its rajas claiming descent from the kings of Pariaman. When Inderapura defied Aceh's grip on the pepper trade an Acehnese fleet sacked it in 1633, put its king Raja Puti to death and seized the pepper stocks. In 1662 Raja Adil, who held Manjuto for the sultan and claimed the succession through the female line, rose in revolt; the sultan called in the Dutch, and the treaty of 1663 gave the VOC the pepper monopoly and rights to the gold fields while Raja Adil was confirmed in Manjuto. In the eighteenth century the coast fell within British Bencoolen; East India Company men called it 'Moco Moco', posted a resident by 1745, and loaded pepper and rice in the open roadstead.
zh:
穆科穆科位于苏门答腊潮湿多林的西海岸，地处米南加保人天地的南端，数条短促河流在此注入印度洋。当地人所说的语言接近米南加保语，行米南加保式的母系氏族制；米南加保史书把这片海岸算作「朗道」，即从巴东向南延伸的外围海岸。河口村寨以种稻为生，政事上则北望因陀罗补罗，其号「帕迦鲁荣之端」，名义上是帕迦鲁荣国王的藩属，实际自行其是，靠胡椒和黄金致富。1444年的穆科穆科处在这个米南加保海洋世界的南缘，仍按伊斯兰化之前的旧俗治理。

1511年满剌加落入葡萄牙人之手后，东方贸易改走苏门答腊西岸，胡椒种植随之向南推广。1616年荷兰人的报告称因陀罗补罗户口殷盛，约有三万人种植稻米和胡椒。16世纪后期，阿纳克松盖小王国以苏拉甘河为中心，据有曼朱托河至乌拉伊水之间的海岸，其统治者自称帕里亚曼诸王的后裔。因陀罗补罗抗拒亚齐把持胡椒贸易，1633年亚齐舰队洗劫其地，处死国王罗阇·普蒂，夺走胡椒存货。1662年，替苏丹镇守曼朱托、又依母系世系主张继承权的罗阇·阿迪尔起兵，苏丹向荷兰人求援；1663年的条约把胡椒专卖权和金矿开采权交给荷兰东印度公司，罗阇·阿迪尔则得以保住曼朱托。18世纪，这片海岸纳入英属明古连范围，东印度公司的人称之为穆科穆科（Moco Moco），1745年已派驻驻扎官，在敞开的锚地装运胡椒和稻米。

en:
Pagaruyung lies in the cool Minangkabau highlands of central Sumatra, among the gold-bearing valleys above the Padang coast. Here the three luhak, the oldest Minangkabau lands, were organised by matrilineal clans: land and clan name passed through women, each nagari ran its own affairs, and the king at Suruaso near Batusangkar was more sacred overlord than governor. Tradition explains the name Minangkabau with a buffalo fight. When a neighbouring prince pressed his claim, the highlanders matched his great bull with a starving calf whose horns they had ground to points; the calf gored it to death, and menang kabau, 'the buffalo wins', became the people's name. The first named king was Adityawarman, a former Majapahit vassal who proclaimed himself king in 1347, moved his court inland as Tantric Buddhist heir of Dharmasraya, sent envoys to China and lived by the highland gold trade. In 1444 the clans still looked to the Raja of Pagaruyung, while river gold washed down to pepper ports whose coasts were going their own way.

Tomé Pires, writing his Suma Oriental in 1513-15, found power shared by three 'kings of the three seats', kings of the world, of custom and of religion, and only one of them yet a Muslim. Teachers from Aceh and Malacca carried Islam through the highlands, and by the early 1600s the court had its first sultan, remembered as Sultan Alif. Aceh had imposed its governors on the coast early in the century; the VOC opened an office at Padang in 1663 and backed a rising that drove the Acehnese from the west coast within three years. In 1684 Thomas Dias became the first European received at Pagaruyung, and reported a palace behind three gates, perhaps from hearsay, and people living by gold-panning and farming. The Padri War broke the old order: its fighters burned the royal palace on Batu Patah hill in 1804 and killed most of the royal house in 1815 on Tuanku Lintau's orders. Raffles in 1818 found the capital thrice burned and abandoned. On 10 February 1821 Sultan Tunggul Alam Bagagarsyah and nineteen chiefs accepted Dutch help against the Padri; the campaign opened that April.
zh:
帕迦鲁荣地处苏门答腊中部凉爽的米南加保高地，在巴东海岸上方出产沙金的河谷之间。这里是米南加保人最古老的三个「鲁哈克」之地，行母系氏族制：土地和族姓沿女性传承，每个村落自行议事，巴都桑卡尔附近苏鲁阿索的国王更像神圣共主，而非行政长官。相传「米南加保」之名来自一场水牛之斗。邻邦王子强索土地，高地人便拿一头挨饿的牛犊应战，牛犊双角磨得像刀尖，冲上去把大牛顶死；「menang kabau」意为「水牛获胜」，成了族名。第一位有名可考的国王是阿迪蒂亚瓦尔曼，他原是满者伯夷的藩属，1347年自立，以达摩僧耶王室密宗佛教传人的身份把王廷迁入内陆，多次遣使中国，靠高地黄金贸易致富。1444年，诸氏族仍尊帕迦鲁荣的罗阇为共主，河里的沙金顺流而下，运往沿海自行其是的胡椒港口。

托梅·皮莱资1513至1515年撰写《东方志》时，发现王权由「三席之王」分掌：世界之王、风俗之王与宗教之王，其中只有一人是穆斯林。16世纪后期，来自亚齐和满剌加的教师把伊斯兰教传入高地，到17世纪初王廷有了第一位苏丹，相传称苏丹·阿利夫。该世纪初亚齐曾向沿海强派长官；荷兰东印度公司1663年在巴东开设商馆，又支持当地人起兵，不出三年便把亚齐人逐出西海岸。1684年，托马斯·迪亚斯成为第一个获准进入帕迦鲁荣的欧洲人，他记述一座须经过三道门进入的宫殿（可能得自传闻），以及当地人以淘金务农为生。帕德里战争随后打碎了旧秩序：帕德里派武装1804年焚毁巴都帕达山上的王宫，又奉端古·林道之命于1815年处死大部分王族。1818年莱佛士见到王都时，它已三度被焚、无人居住。1821年2月10日，苏丹·东古尔·阿拉姆·巴加加尔夏与十九名首领接受荷兰援助对抗帕德里派，荷兰军队于同年4月开战。

en:
Pariaman faces the Indian Ocean on a broad rice plain at the foot of the Barisan Mountains, on the Minangkabau coast of western Sumatra. It was one of the rantau, the coastal outlets through which the highland kingdom of Pagaruyung traded, linked to the interior by river and hill paths; its own name means a safe place for merchants. Coastal chiefs sold the plain's rice together with gold, camphor and forest produce brought down from the Minangkabau valleys, and ships sailing the west-Sumatra route put in for water and stores. In 1444 the coast still stood in the shadow of Pagaruyung's Hindu-Buddhist kingship and Minangkabau adat; Islam had reached the ports but had not yet taken the villages.

The Portuguese capture of Malacca in 1511 sent more traffic round to Sumatra's western shore, and Pariaman grew into a pepper and gold port where western Indian merchants were followed by Europeans. Aceh closed over the coast next, and Sultan Iskandar Muda posted panglima at Tiku and Pariaman to watch every pepper sale. Islam in the district was shaped by Shaikh Burhanuddin, born at Sintuk near Pariaman in 1646, who studied under the Acehnese scholar Abdurrauf Singkil and founded the first important surau, a religious school, at nearby Ulakan; Minangkabau students carried his Shattari teachings inland before he died in 1704. The Painan settlement of 1663 opened this coast to the Dutch East India Company, which built a lodge at Pariaman in 1671 and a fort soon afterwards. Wars with local chiefs and rivalry with other European traders made the post unprofitable, and the Dutch abandoned it in 1770.
zh:
帕里亚曼临印度洋，坐落在巴里桑山脉脚下一片广阔的稻米平原上，地处苏门答腊西岸的米南佳保沿海。它是「兰陶」之一，即高地帕迦鲁荣王国对外通商的沿海出口，靠河道和山路与内陆相连；地名本身的意思就是商人的安全之地。沿海首领出售平原稻米，连同米南佳保各河谷运出的黄金、樟脑和山林物产，沿苏门答腊西岸航行的商船也在此补给淡水和给养。1444年，这片海岸仍受帕迦鲁荣印度教—佛教王权和米南佳保旧俗的笼罩；伊斯兰教已传入港口，却还没有进入村落。

1511年葡萄牙攻占马六甲，把更多贸易赶到苏门答腊西岸，帕里亚曼发展为胡椒和黄金港，西印度商人之后又来了欧洲人。随后亚齐收紧对海岸的控制，苏丹伊斯坎达尔·穆达在第库和帕里亚曼派驻庞利马，监视每一笔胡椒买卖。当地伊斯兰教的面貌与谢赫·布尔哈努丁有关：他1646年生于帕里亚曼附近的辛图克，师从亚齐学者阿卜杜勒·拉乌夫·辛基尔，在附近的乌拉坎建起第一座重要的经堂，作为宗教教育中心；他的米南佳保弟子把其教义传入内陆，他本人于1704年去世。1663年的帕伊南协议把这片海岸开放给荷兰东印度公司，公司1671年在帕里亚曼设立商馆，不久又修建要塞。与本地首领的战事和欧洲商人之间的竞争让商站无利可图，荷兰人遂于1770年将它放弃。

en:
The Mentawai are the rainforested islands beyond the strait off western Sumatra: Siberut, the largest, then Sipora and the North and South Pagais. Their Austronesian people, among the oldest populations in the archipelago, lived as semi-nomadic hunters and gatherers who also kept sago, banana and taro plots. Several families shared an uma longhouse; their titi tattoos marked a person's role and standing, they sharpened their teeth to the local ideal of beauty, and sikerei ritual specialists maintained the Arat Sabulungan, the body of custom that tied ancestral spirits to the forest and the sea. In 1444 the Hindu-Buddhist and Islamic currents of Sumatra had barely crossed the strait, and each island community governed itself.

Siberut appeared on a Portuguese chart in 1606 under the name Mintaon. Before any European post existed, the two Pagais sold pepper to merchants from the Minangkabau lands and Bengkulu, and in the eighteenth century the Dutch brought the islands within their East Indies sphere without placing much authority over the rainforest settlements. A British East India Company ship called at the Pagais in 1792. No mission or plantation followed, and in 1821 the uma communities still ordered most of their lives by the Arat Sabulungan, with foreign power confined to charts, trade and occasional landings.
zh:
明打威是苏门答腊西岸海峡外的雨林群岛，以最大的西比路岛为首，其南依次为锡波拉、北帕盖和南帕盖。岛上的南岛语居民是这一群岛最古老的人群之一，半游牧地以渔猎采集为生，也照料西米、香蕉和芋类地块。几户人家同住一座乌玛长屋；名为「蒂蒂」的纹身在身上标出各人的角色和身份，人们还按当地的审美锉尖牙齿，西克雷祭司则维系着阿拉特·萨布伦甘信仰，这套规矩把祖灵同森林和海洋连在一起。1444年时，苏门答腊的印度教、佛教和伊斯兰潮流几乎没有越过海峡，各岛社群自行其是。

1606年，西比路已以明塔翁之名出现在葡萄牙海图上。在欧洲人设立据点以前，北帕盖和南帕盖就把胡椒卖给米南佳保和明古鲁来的商人；18世纪，荷兰人把群岛纳入荷属东印度的势力范围，却很少向雨林聚落伸张国权。1792年，一艘英国东印度公司的船靠泊帕盖群岛。此后没有传教站，也没有种植园；到1821年，乌玛社群的大部分生活仍按阿拉特·萨布伦甘安排，外来权力只停留在海图、贸易和偶尔的登岸上。

en:
Nias is the largest island off Sumatra's western coast, and its people, the Ono Niha, call it Tanö Niha, the land of humans. Their villages stood on fortified hilltops, laid out around a stone-paved square where upright slabs and carved statues rose before the chiefs' houses. Feuding between settlements kept the walls and gates manned, and rank ran through twelve levels under the customary law called fondrakö: a man reached the highest grade, Balugu, only by giving feasts that lasted several days and slaughtering pigs by the thousand. Young men proved their courage in the fahombo, a coming-of-age leap over a stone wall two metres high. Traders from Sumatran ports called for island produce in exchange for metals and cloth, but in 1444 no foreign court ruled the interior, which remained a world of competing noble houses rather than a single kingdom.

Acehnese expansion reached the west Sumatran ports in 1513, and Acehnese fleets began raiding Nias, especially the northern beaches, to carry off captives; seven large Acehnese ships landed on the eastern coast in 1642 and left a lasting settlement. The Dutch East India Company made contracts with local villages in 1668 and built a harbour and storehouses near Gunungsitoli, but abandoned the post in 1740. From about 1750 Nias nobles themselves became major suppliers in the slave trade, handing over prisoners taken in their feuds for gold from Aceh, Padang, Batavia and Malaya and spending it on great houses, statues and weapons. When British traders returned to Gunungsitoli in 1821, the island's villages still remained under their own lords and federations.
zh:
尼亚斯是苏门答腊西岸外最大的岛屿，岛上的奥诺·尼哈人称之为塔诺·尼哈，意为「人的土地」。他们的村寨建在设防的山顶，围着石板铺就的广场，首领宅前竖立着石板和雕像。村与村之间的仇杀使寨墙寨门常年有人把守；按丰德拉科习惯法，身份地位分成十二级，一个人要升到最高的巴卢古（Balugu），必须连摆数日大宴、宰杀上千头猪。年轻人则以跳石（fahombo）证明自己成年，纵身跃过一道两米高的石墙。苏门答腊港口的商人常来岛上，用金属和布匹换取物产，但1444年时没有外来王权统治内陆，这里仍是彼此竞争的贵族家系，而不是一个统一王国。

1513年，亚齐势力扩张到苏门答腊西岸港口，亚齐船队开始袭掠尼亚斯，尤其常在北部海滩掳人；1642年，七艘亚齐大船在东海岸登陆，留下长期的定居点。1668年，荷兰东印度公司与当地村社缔约，在古农萨蒂利附近修建港口和仓库，又于1740年放弃。约从1750年起，尼亚斯贵族自身也成了奴隶贸易的重要供应者，把仇杀中俘来的人交给亚齐、巴东、巴达维亚和马来亚的商人换取黄金，再用来兴建大宅、雕像并购置兵器。1821年英国商人重返古农萨蒂利时，岛上各村仍由本地首领和联盟自理。

en:
Tanah Gayo is the broken highland along Sumatra's Barisan Mountains, centred on the basin of Lake Laut Tawar, with Takengon on its western shore. Gayo villages farmed rice and vegetables in the mountain valleys, kept buffaloes and lived in longhouses, and their language and genealogies were carried by word of mouth. The genealogies centre on the Raja of Linge, whose line Gayo tradition traces to the tenth century. The founding king, Meurah Adi Genali, is remembered as the father of Sultan Johan Syah, founder of Aceh in that tradition, and his sons are said to have left the mountains for the coasts: Meurah Johan founded Lamuri in Aceh Besar, Meurah Silu went to Pasai, where the same genealogy makes him founder of Samudera Pasai, and Sebayak Lingga went to the Karo country, while the youngest son stayed at Linge. The grave of Meurah Mege at Wih ni Rayang, on the slope of Keramil Paluh, is still tended and honoured by highland villagers. In 1444 this was an isolated frontier above Aceh's Muslim ports, reached only by steep tracks and governed in practice by Gayo chiefs.

As the Aceh Sultanate expanded through the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, the highland was drawn into its interior domains, Islam took firmer root, and rice, buffaloes and forest produce went down the tracks to the coast; when Aceh's court weakened after the seventeenth century, the upland districts stayed in the hands of local lords.
zh:
加约之地是苏门答腊巴里桑山脉间起伏崎岖的高地，以劳特塔瓦尔湖盆地为中心，塔肯贡坐落在湖西岸。加约村落在山谷里种植水稻和蔬菜、饲养水牛，住长屋，语言和谱系全靠口耳相传。谱系围绕林耶的拉阇展开，加约传说把这一系追溯到10世纪：始祖穆拉·阿迪·格纳利被认为是佐汉·沙苏丹之父，按这一传说佐汉·沙创建了亚齐；他的儿子们纷纷离开山地前往海岸，穆拉·佐汉去大亚齐建立蓝无里（Lamuri），穆拉·希鲁去八昔，同一份谱系把他算作苏木都剌·八昔的建立者，塞巴亚克·林加去了卡罗之地，小儿子留在林耶。克拉米尔·帕卢山坡威尼拉扬的穆拉·梅格墓，一直由高地村民看护和敬奉。1444年，这里是亚齐穆斯林港口上方封闭的边地，只有险峻山路可通，实际由加约首领治理。

16至17世纪亚齐苏丹国扩张，高地被纳入它的内陆领地，伊斯兰教扎根更深，稻米、水牛和山林物产沿山路运往海岸；17世纪以后亚齐宫廷衰弱，山地区域一直由地方领主掌握。

en:
Bintan is the largest of the Riau Islands, a wooded island set where the Strait of Malacca opens into the South China Sea, with the port of Tanjungpinang on its southern shore guarding the mouth of the Bintan River. Indian and Chinese ships used its roads from the early centuries of the sea trade; the Chinese ceramics dug up there include Northern Song ware, and by the twelfth century Chinese sailors called it Pirate Island, for the fleets that herded passing junks into its harbours. Its Malays and Orang Laut were the sea power on which Malacca relied after the sultanate rose around 1400. In 1444 Bintan is a Sunni Malay dependency of Malacca, sending timber, rattan and dammar to the city's shipyards and sharing in the strait's carrying trade, its raiders as feared as its merchants.

When Malacca fell to the Portuguese in 1511 Sultan Mahmud Shah made Bintan the seat of his exiled court, and for fifteen years Orang Laut fleets sailing from the island blockaded and harassed Portuguese Malacca, until a Portuguese expedition stormed the island in 1526 and razed his stronghold. Under the new Johor Sultanate the port of Bandar Riau opened, and as the sultans moved between the Johor River, Riau and Lingga, Bintan became the centre of their empire in the early eighteenth century. Riau outshone Dutch Malacca as a market for tin, pepper, spices and gambier, and was a school of Malay Islamic learning. Real power lay with the Bugis underkings, the Yam Tuan Muda. Raja Haji Fisabilillah beat off a thirteen-ship Dutch assault on Riau in January 1784 and held out through a three-month siege, but was killed that June while attacking Malacca. The Dutch then seized Bintan and expelled the Bugis; they were driven out themselves in 1787, and the sultan moved his court to Lingga the following year. Nearby Penyengat became a seat of government, and after a succession crisis the Dutch reoccupied Tanjungpinang in 1818. Raffles negotiated his Singapore treaty of 1819 partly with these island chiefs, and in 1821 Bintan lay under Dutch protection, the island half of a divided Johor.
zh:
民丹是廖内群岛第一大岛，林木葱郁，坐落在马六甲海峡通往南海的狭窄水道上，南岸的丹戎槟榔扼守民丹河口。早在海上贸易的最初几百年，印度与中国商船便在此停泊，岛上出土过大量中国瓷器，其中一些可追溯至北宋；到12世纪，中国水手因当地舰队强拉过往帆船入港而称之为「海盗岛」。岛上的马来人与海人是一支海上劲旅，1400年前后马六甲苏丹国兴起，倚仗的正是这支力量。1444年的民丹是马六甲治下的逊尼派马来人属地，向马六甲船坞输送木材、藤条与达玛树脂，也分享海峡的转运之利，而其海盗与商人一样令人生畏。

1511年马六甲陷落后，苏丹马末沙把流亡朝廷设在民丹，十五年间，海人舰队从这里出发，不断封锁、袭扰葡属马六甲，直到1526年葡萄牙远征军攻陷民丹，将他的据点夷为平地。柔佛苏丹国建立后，岛上开辟了廖内商埠；随着苏丹们在柔佛河、廖内与林加之间屡迁都城，民丹在18世纪初成为帝国的中枢。廖内经营锡、胡椒、香料与甘蜜，市面盖过荷属马六甲，当地的学者也使它成为马来伊斯兰学问的中心。实权掌握在武吉斯副王「杨端·慕达」手中：拉惹·哈吉·菲萨比拉1784年1月击退来攻廖内的十三艘荷兰战舰，又坚守了三个月的围攻，却在同年6月攻打马六甲时战死。荷军随即占领民丹、驱逐武吉斯人；1787年荷兰人自己也被赶走，苏丹次年迁都林加。邻近的喷延格特岛成为政务中心，一场继承危机之后，荷兰于1818年重新进驻丹戎槟榔。1819年莱佛士谋取新加坡，便有一部分谈判是与这些岛上首领进行的；到1821年，民丹已处在荷兰保护之下，成为分裂的柔佛的海岛半边。

en:
Pakuan was the old royal seat of the Sundanese, in the wet-rice lands between the Ciliwung and Cisadane rivers where Bogor later stood. A Sundanese king had kept court there from 669, and over the centuries the capital moved between Pakuan and Kawali in the eastern land of Galuh. In 1444 the reigning king still held court at Kawali, but Pakuan remained the dynasty's venerable old capital in the rainy highlands of western Java, its palace enclosure ringed by wet-rice fields and rain forest.

In 1482 Sri Baduga Maharaja, the King Siliwangi of Sundanese legend, was crowned, reunited Sunda with Galuh and brought the capital back to Pakuan. The Batu Tulis inscription, carved by his successor, lists his works: a wall and moat around the city, sacred mounds and pavilions, a protected forest, and a dam holding a lake to water the rice fields. Tomé Pires, the first European to see Pakuan, came in 1513 and called Daio a great city of near 50,000 people, its houses thatched with palm leaves and the king's wooden palace raised on hundreds of carved columns. A palm-leaf travel poem by Bujangga Manik, a prince of this court who left it to wander Java and Bali as a Hindu hermit, also describes the walled city. Banten pressed hard from the 1550s, and in 1579 its troops broke in through a guard's treachery, sacked the city and carried off the watu gililang, the royal throne-stone, which was set at an intersection in Banten's royal square to serve as the sultan's throne.

Pakuan then reverted to tiger-haunted forest. When a VOC party under Pieter Scipio van Oostende first reached the ruins in 1687, one of its men had been mauled by a tiger nearby two days earlier, and the report of tigers guarding the dead king's palace fed a Sundanese belief that Siliwangi and his courtiers had been changed into tigers. In 1745 Governor-General van Imhoff built a country residence on the old estate, named Buitenzorg the following year; Stamford Raffles made it his seat during the British interregnum, and in 1817 a botanical garden was laid out beside the palace.
zh:
帕库安是巽他王朝的旧都，坐落在芝利翁河与芝萨达尼河之间的水田之乡，后来茂物城即建在这片地方。669年起就有巽他国王在此临朝，此后数百年间，王都在帕库安与东部加卢的卡瓦利之间迁移。1444年在位的国王仍在卡瓦利听政，但帕库安仍是王朝尊崇的旧都：在西爪哇多雨的高地上，水田与雨林环抱着宫殿区。

1482年，巽他传说中的西里旺义王、即斯里·巴杜加·马哈拉惹登基，重新统一巽他与加卢，把王都迁回帕库安。继位者凿刻的巴都图利斯石碑（Batu Tulis）记下了他的工程：环城的城墙与壕沟、神坛与亭阁、一片受保护的山林，还有拦出湖水灌溉稻田的堤坝。第一个见到此城的欧洲人托梅·皮莱资于1513年到访，他称这座「达约」大城有近五万人口，民居多是棕榈叶顶的木屋，国王的木造宫殿立在数百根雕花柱之上。宫廷王子布姜加·马尼克弃世为印度教行者，遍游爪哇与巴厘，他写在棕榈叶上的行纪也描绘了城墙内的帕库安。1550年代起万丹不断进逼，1579年万丹军队靠一名守将叛卖破城，大肆劫掠，把国王的御座石（watu gililang）运走，安置在万丹王宫广场的路口，充作苏丹的御座。

此后帕库安沦为猛虎出没的雨林。1687年，彼得·斯基皮奥·范·奥斯滕德率荷兰东印度公司考察队最先进入废墟，两天前队中刚有人在附近被虎咬伤；那份猛虎看守废王宫殿的报告，后来演为巽他民间的说法：相传西里旺义与他的臣子都化成了猛虎。1745年，总督范·伊姆霍夫在故苑上修建乡间行宫，次年取名布伊滕佐格；英国统治爪哇期间，莱佛士把驻地设在此处，1817年行宫旁开辟了植物园。

en:
Sumedang Larang was a small Sundanese polity in the Tampomas highlands of the eastern Parahyangan, where tracks from Pakuan Pajajaran and Galuh dropped toward the Cirebon coast and the Java Sea. Its early center stood at Citebong Girang, and for centuries its rulers were local lords under the kings of Sunda and Galuh. In 1444 Sumedang was still a Hindu inland state on the edge of Pajajaran's world; Islam reached its court only three generations later.

Islam came with Prince Santri, who ruled from 1530 to 1578 and bound Sumedang to Cirebon. In 1578 his son Angkawijaya received the crown and regalia of Pajajaran, carried out of the collapsing kingdom by its former commander Jaya Perkosa, and was crowned Prabu Geusan Ulun with the blessing of forty-four Parahyangan lords; when Banten's Maulana Yusuf destroyed Pajajaran in 1579, Sumedang claimed to be the Sunda kingdom's heir, and the Babad Sumedang gives its bounds from the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean. Geusan Ulun broke with Cirebon in 1585, but squeezed between Banten, Cirebon and Mataram, his successor Rangga Gempol I submitted to Sultan Agung in 1620. He led Mataram troops in the Madura campaigns and sent rice for Agung's 1628-1629 sieges of Batavia; the Sumedang-Ukur revolt that followed was put down by 1636, and Sumedang became a Mataram regency before passing to the Dutch East India Company with Pakubuwana I's concessions. In 1808 and 1809 Daendels drove the Great Post Road through a limestone cliff west of the town; thousands of laborers died in the cutting and the regent Pangeran Kornel rode out to confront the governor-general over it. Sundanese legend adds that he drove his keris into the rock, which has been called Cadas Pangeran, the Prince's Rock.
zh:
双木丹·拉朗是帕拉扬甘东部坦波马斯山区的巽他小邦，从帕匡·帕查查兰和加卢通往井里汶海岸与爪哇海的山路经过这里。它早期的治所在西特邦吉朗，数百年间统治者都是巽他和加卢君主座下的地方领主。1444年的双木丹还是帕查查兰世界边缘的印度教内陆政权，三代人之后伊斯兰教才进入它的宫廷。

伊斯兰教随桑特里亲王而来，他1530年至1578年在位，使双木丹与井里汶结盟。1578年，他的儿子昂卡维查亚得到帕查查兰旧将查亚·佩尔科萨在王国倾覆之际带出的王冠和王权信物，经四十四名帕拉扬甘领主拥立，加冕为帕布·格乌桑·乌伦；1579年万丹的莫拉纳·优素福灭掉帕查查兰后，双木丹以巽他王统的继承者自居，《双木丹编年史》称其疆土北起爪哇海、南抵印度洋。格乌桑·乌伦1585年与井里汶反目，但其继任者朗加·根波尔一世夹在万丹、井里汶和马打兰之间，于1620年归附阿贡苏丹。他率马打兰军队参加马都拉战役，又为1628年至1629年围攻巴达维亚输送军粮；随后爆发的双木丹—乌库尔叛乱到1636年被镇压，双木丹成为马打兰摄政区，帕库布沃诺一世作出让步后转入荷兰东印度公司之手。1808年至1809年，丹德尔斯修筑大邮路，公路从镇西的石灰岩绝壁间劈开，数千役夫死在工地上，摄政库苏马迪纳塔九世（人称科内尔亲王）当面质问这位总督；巽他传说称他把克里斯短剑插进岩壁，那处石崖后来得名「查达斯·庞格尔」，意为「亲王岩」。

en:
Pekalongan lies on the flat north Javanese shore, behind mangroves and wet-rice fields. Chinese traders used the anchorage early. The Song account Lingwai Daida, completed in 1178, calls the port Pukalong, a month's fair-wind voyage from Guangzhou. It describes Javanese with short hair and colourful woven cloth, coconut wine, red and white sugar, copper coinage, pepper, cloves, sandalwood, eaglewood and white cardamom. The seventh-century Sojomerto inscription found nearby links this coast with the older kingdom of Kalingga. In 1444 Pekalongan was still a Majapahit port in name, but Chinese, Arab and Malay Muslim merchants already handled much of its shipping, and the rising Muslim port of Demak lay farther east along the coast.

In the century after Majapahit's collapse, Pekalongan followed Demak and then Pajang. Treaties and marriage alliances brought it to Mataram in the early seventeenth century. Although the Mataram court lay inland, rice, sugar and port dues made Pekalongan one of its richest appanages by the end of the century. Amangkurat I's closure of coastal ports disrupted the Muslim merchant networks that carried that wealth. The Chinese-Javanese rising of 1741–1743 swept across the north coast, and in 1743 Pakubuwana II ceded the Pasisir to the VOC. Pekalongan then passed under Company rule. In 1753 the Dutch built a fort in the town to watch the harbour and the loading of rice and sugar.
zh:
北加浪岸位于爪哇海北岸，港岸后方是红树林和连片水田。中国商人很早便来此停泊。1178年成书的《岭外代答》称这里为莆加龙，说从广州顺风航行一月可达；书中记当地人剪短发、以花布裹身，用椰子酿酒，铸造铜钱，出产红白蔗糖、胡椒、丁香、檀香、沉香和白豆蔻。邻近出土的7世纪索佐梅尔托石碑，又把这片海岸与诃陵古国联系起来。1444年，北加浪岸名义上仍是满者伯夷的港口，但华人和阿拉伯、马来穆斯林商人已掌握大量航运，海岸以东的淡目也正在兴起。

满者伯夷崩溃后的一个世纪里，北加浪岸先后从属于淡目和巴章。17世纪初，条约与联姻把它纳入马打兰。马打兰王都虽在内陆，到17世纪末，稻米、蔗糖和港口税已使北加浪岸成为它最富庶的封邑之一。阿莽古拉特一世关闭沿海港口，打断了输送这些财富的穆斯林商人网络。1741至1743年华人与爪哇人起事席卷北海岸，1743年帕库布沃诺二世把北海岸割让给荷兰东印度公司，北加浪岸随之归入公司治下。1753年，荷兰人在城中筑堡，监视港口以及稻米、蔗糖装船。

en:
Kotagede lies on open ground east of the Gajah Wong river, south-east of Yogyakarta, between Mount Merapi and the sea, on the roads that link the towns of the Mataram heartland. In 1444 it was Mentaok, a tract of hunting forest and rice villages in the fading inland domains of Majapahit, and later it passed to the kingdom of Pajang. In the 1570s the ruler of Pajang granted the forest to his courtier Ki Ageng Pemanahan for putting down a rebellion; Pemanahan and his son Danang Sutawijaya cleared it and settled, naming the place Mataram.

After Pemanahan's death Sutawijaya took the title Panembahan Senopati and made the settlement his base. Javanese tradition, in the Babad Mangkubumi, tells how he meditated on a stone in a river until a giant fish carried him to the court of Ratu Kidul, the queen who rules the spirits of the southern ocean; she pledged him her support and became the consort of his line. In 1586 he took Pajang itself, and the walled town became the first capital of the Mataram Sultanate, called Kotagede, the 'Great City': its walls ran along the Gajah Wong, whose water was diverted to fill the moats on the other three sides, and the royal mosque and cemetery went up beside the palace. Senopati died in 1601 and was entombed here. His successor Mas Jolang kept building at the court until, tradition says, a stag killed him while he hunted in his own enclosed forest; Sultan Agung, reigning from 1613, moved the capital south to Karta and then Plered. When Trunajaya's rebels sacked Plered in 1677 the court moved on to Kartasura and later Surakarta, leaving Kotagede as a pilgrimage town around Senopati's mausoleum, its ancestral ground held indivisible and guarded by both the Surakarta and Yogyakarta courts. The treaty of Giyanti in 1755 gave it to the new Sultanate of Yogyakarta, whose kraton nearby was stormed and looted by Gillespie's British troops in June 1812.
zh:
哥打格德位于日惹东南、加约旺河以东的开阔地带，在默拉皮火山与海洋之间，地当马打兰腹地各镇往来的通道。1444年时这里还叫门陶克，是满者伯夷日渐衰微的内陆疆土上一片猎场与稻米村落，后来又归属巴章王国。16世纪70年代，巴章君主把这片林地封给平定叛乱有功的廷臣基·阿贡·帕马纳汉；帕马纳汉与儿子达南·苏达威查雅拓土定居，将此地命名为马打兰。

帕马纳汉死后，苏达威查雅上帕南巴汉·塞纳帕蒂尊号，以此为基业。爪哇编年史《芒库布米》（Babad Mangkubumi）记载，塞纳帕蒂曾在河心一块石头上苦修，一条巨鱼驮他入海，觐见统御南海诸灵的女王拉杜·基杜尔；女王许以助力，并做了他王朝世代君王的配偶。1586年，他攻下巴章本土，这座设防城邑成为马打兰苏丹国的第一个首都，得名哥打格德，意为「大城」：城墙沿加约旺河而筑，河水被引入其余三面的壕沟，王宫旁建起了王室清真寺与陵寝。塞纳帕蒂1601年去世，安葬于此。继位的玛斯·佐朗继续营建宫室，据说在自己的围苑中猎鹿时被鹿撞死；1613年即位的苏丹阿贡则把首都南迁卡尔塔，再迁普莱雷德。1677年杜鲁诺佐约的起义者洗劫普莱雷德后，王廷再迁卡尔塔苏拉、后迁梭罗，哥打格德便成为围绕塞纳帕蒂陵寝的朝圣地，这片祖地被认为不可分割，由梭罗与日惹两朝共同守护。1755年《吉安蒂条约》将它划归新立的日惹苏丹国；1812年6月，吉莱斯皮率领的英军攻破并劫掠了近旁的日惹王宫。

en:
Kediri, the old Daha, lies in the upper valley of the Brantas, the river that carries the rice of inland East Java down to the sea. Airlangga founded Dahanapura in 1042, and as the capital of Panjalu it headed a kingdom that held the eastern interior until Ken Arok overthrew it in 1222. Its best-remembered king is Jayabaya of the mid-twelfth century, when Kediri's power was at its height; Javanese tradition holds him an incarnation of Vishnu and the archetype of the Ratu Adil, the just king who returns in an age of madness to put the world right, and in old age he abdicated to meditate at Menang. This was the age of the poet Mpu Sedah, whose Kakawin Bharatayuddha retells the great Bharata war in Javanese verse. Under Majapahit, Daha stayed a royal appanage held by the king's kin, and in 1444 it was a wealthy Hindu-Javanese river town of merchants, fishermen and temple estates while the empire around it slipped into factional wars.

In 1478 the prince of Daha, Girindrawardhana, rose against Trowulan and made Kediri the seat of the last Majapahit kings, until Sultan Trenggana of Demak stormed the city in 1527 and its last ruler fled to Blambangan. Demak, Pajang and Mataram held it in turn after that. In 1677 the Madurese rebel Trunajaya, fresh from sacking Mataram's capital, made Kediri his court and piled his plunder there; on 25 November 1678 a VOC army under Anthonio Hurdt, marching with Amangkurat II's troops, stormed the town, and in 1680 the king killed Trunajaya with his own hands. When Cakraningrat IV of Madura defied the Company from East Java in the 1740s, his defeat left Kediri, with the rest of the Oosthoek, under Dutch rule.
zh:
谏义里古称达哈，地处布兰塔斯河上游河谷，这条河把东爪哇内陆的稻米运往大海。1042年，埃尔朗加建达哈纳普拉城；作为潘贾卢的都城，它所统领的王国曾掌握东爪哇内陆，直到1222年被肯·阿罗克推翻。谏义里最有名的国王是12世纪中叶的查亚巴亚，当时国势正值全盛；爪哇传统认为他是毗湿奴的化身、公正之王拉杜·阿迪尔的原型，这位公正之王将在疯狂之世重回人间、拨乱反正，他晚年退位，到默南村苦修。诗人穆普·塞达写下《婆罗多战争》正是在这一时代，把婆罗多大战搬入爪哇诗章。满者伯夷时代，达哈一直是王族领有的亲王封邑；1444年时，它是一座富庶的印度教爪哇河城，商人、渔户与寺院庄园辐辏其间，而周围的帝国正陷入党争内战。

1478年，达哈王公吉林德拉瓦尔达纳起兵反对特罗武兰，使谏义里成为满者伯夷末代君主的朝廷所在地；1527年淡目的特林卡纳苏丹攻破此城，末代统治者逃往布兰邦岸，此后淡目、巴章、马打蓝相继领有其地。1677年，马都拉起义者杜鲁诺佐约洗劫马打蓝首都之后，以谏义里为王廷，将劫得的财货囤积于此；1678年11月25日，安东尼奥·赫尔特麾下的荷兰东印度公司军队会同阿莽古拉特二世的部队攻破城池，1680年国王亲手杀死了杜鲁诺佐约。1740年代，马都拉的查克拉宁格拉特四世据东爪哇与公司对抗，他败亡之后，谏义里便与整个东角一起落入荷兰统治。

en:
Madura is a long, narrow island set across the Madura Strait from Surabaya, guarding the sea approaches to northeastern Java. Its plains are drier than Java's, and the Madurese lived by farming, fishing and trade with the ports on the far side of the strait. Javanese kingdoms drew the island into their politics early: the Nagarakretagama of 1365 already names Madurese lords within the Majapahit order. In 1444 Madura still belonged to the Majapahit world, but the declining empire could not shield it from the Muslim sultanates rising on Java's north coast.

The island's princely line began in 1624, when Sultan Agung conquered Madura and installed Raden Prasena, titled Cakraningrat I, to govern the west from Sampang and Bangkalan. Half a century later a Madurese prince nearly overturned Mataram. Trunajaya of Arosbaya in Bangkalan led Madurese and Makassarese rebels across the strait in 1674, overran Java's north coast and in 1677 sacked Mataram's court at Plered; Amangkurat I died during the flight. His son called in the Dutch East India Company, whose troops drove Trunajaya out of Surabaya, stormed his capital at Kediri in 1678 and seized him the next year, and Amangkurat II put him to death in 1680.

The Cakraningrats then sided with the Dutch in the Javanese wars of succession. Cakraningrat II backed Puger, who as Pakubuwana I granted the Company East Madura by treaty in 1705. Cakraningrat IV helped retake Kartasura in 1742, only for Pakubuwana II to cede the whole island to the Company in 1743. He rose in revolt, was hunted down at Banjarmasin and exiled to the Cape of Good Hope, where he died. The Dutch then ruled through the island's four regencies and drew heavily on Madurese levies, who served in Company wars across the archipelago.
zh:
马都拉是一座狭长岛屿，与苏腊巴亚隔着马都拉海峡相望，扼守通往爪哇东北的海路。岛上平原比爪哇干燥，马都拉人以农耕、捕鱼为生，并同海峡对岸的港口通商。爪哇诸王国很早就把这座岛拉进自己的政治圈，1365年的《爪哇史颂》已提到身处满者伯夷秩序中的马都拉领主。1444年，马都拉仍属于满者伯夷世界，但日趋衰落的帝国已挡不住爪哇北岸兴起的穆斯林苏丹国。

岛上的王公世系始于1624年：阿贡苏丹征服马都拉后，封罗登·普拉塞纳为查克拉宁格拉特一世，以三邦和邦卡兰为中心治理西马都拉。半个世纪后，一位马都拉王子险些掀翻马打兰。出身邦卡兰阿罗斯巴亚（Arosbaya）的杜鲁诺佐约率马都拉人和望加锡人于1674年渡过海峡，席卷爪哇北岸，1677年洗劫马打兰在普莱雷德的宫廷，阿莽古拉特一世死于逃亡途中。新君阿莽古拉特二世向荷兰东印度公司求援，公司军队把杜鲁诺佐约逐出苏腊巴亚，1678年攻陷他设在谏义里的都城，次年将他擒获；1680年，阿莽古拉特二世亲手将他处死。

此后查克拉宁格拉特家族在爪哇继承战争中站在荷兰一方。查克拉宁格拉特二世支持普格尔，后者成为帕库布沃诺一世后，在1705年依约把东马都拉交给荷兰东印度公司。查克拉宁格拉特四世1742年协助公司夺回卡尔塔苏拉，帕库布沃诺二世却在1743年把全岛主权割让给公司。他随即起兵，在马辰被追捕擒获，流放好望角并死在那里。荷兰人随后通过岛上的四个摄政进行统治，并大量征募马都拉士兵，派往群岛各地为公司作战。

en:
Lombok lies across the narrow Lombok Strait east of Bali, with Sumbawa beyond the Alas Strait on its other side, and the cone of Mount Rinjani dominates its northern half. In 1257 Samalas, a volcano in the Rinjani massif, collapsed in one of the largest eruptions of the last several thousand years. Pyroclastic flows buried much of Lombok, destroyed Pamatan, the capital of the island's kingdom, and crossed the sea to Sumbawa; ash fell as far as Java, 340 kilometres away. The palm-leaf Babad Lombok describes the disaster, and the collapsed peak became the caldera lake of Segara Anak; Bali and Lombok may have stood depopulated for generations afterwards. The Nagarakretagama later counted the island among Majapahit's conquests as Lombok Mirah, but Majapahit's rule ran shallow, and by 1444 Lombok was divided among many small, quarrelling Sasak principalities whose people still kept their old animist rites.

The Balinese kingdom of Gelgel first conquered Lombok early in the sixteenth century and settled its western side. Islam, carried there by traders, spread widely only around 1600 through the preaching of Sunan Prapen of Gresik, son of Sunan Giri, and the new faith mingled with the old cults in the Wetu Telu way. Early in the seventeenth century Balinese princes seized the west while Makassarese invaders from Sumbawa took the east. The Dutch East India Company made its first treaty on the island in 1674 with the Sasak princess who then ruled part of it. In 1740 the Balinese kingdom of Karangasem destroyed the old Sasak kingdom of Selaparang, and by 1750 all Lombok was in Balinese hands, soon split between four rival Balinese kingdoms. In the east the lords held garrisoned forts and the Sasak village head became little more than a tax collector, and that was how the Sasak majority still lived in 1821.
zh:
龙目位于巴厘岛以东，与巴厘只隔一道狭窄的龙目海峡，东面再隔阿拉斯海峡与松巴哇相望，林贾尼火山的锥体雄踞岛的北半部。1257年，林贾尼群峰中的萨马拉斯火山崩塌，是几千年来最大规模的火山喷发之一。火山碎屑流掩埋了龙目大部，摧毁了岛上王国的都城帕马坦，还越过海峡扑上松巴哇；火山灰一直飘到三百四十公里外的爪哇。棕榈叶文献《龙目纪事》（Babad Lombok）记下了这场灾难，崩塌的峰顶后来形成塞加拉阿纳克湖；巴厘和龙目可能因此荒疏了好几代人。后来的《爪哇史颂》把此岛算作满者伯夷的征服地，称龙目米拉（Lombok Mirah），但满者伯夷的统治始终浮于表面，到1444年，龙目已分裂为众多互相争战的萨萨克小邦，百姓仍守着旧有的泛灵祭祀。

16世纪初，巴厘的格尔格尔王国首次征服龙目，并在西部定居。伊斯兰教早已随商人上岛，但直到1600年前后，才因苏南·吉里之子、爪哇锦石的苏南·普拉彭传教而广为传播，新信仰与旧俗融合为韦图特鲁（Wetu Telu）之道。17世纪初，巴厘诸王公夺取龙目西部，来自松巴哇的望加锡人则侵入东部。1674年，荷兰东印度公司与当时统治岛上一部分的萨萨克女亲王订立第一份契约。1740年，巴厘的卡朗阿森王国攻灭萨萨克古国塞拉帕朗，到1750年整个龙目都落入巴厘人手中，不久又分裂为四个互相敌对的巴厘王国。在岛的东部，巴厘王公据守设防要塞，萨萨克人的村长沦为替他们收税的人；1821年，占人口多数的萨萨克人仍过着这样的日子。

en:
Gangneung lies on Korea's eastern coast beneath the Taebaek Mountains, the chief town of the Yeongdong region, where cold and warm currents meet offshore and the fishing is rich. The country once belonged to the Ye people and was called Haseulla; Silla took it in 639 and made it a secondary capital, and Goryeo guarded its north-eastern frontier from the town it called Myeongju. In 1423 King Sejong's reorganization named the surrounding province Gangwon, from Gangneung and Wonju. In 1444 Gangneung is a small Confucian prefectural town, ranked a grand protectorate over the neighbouring hyeon, whose shoreline markets live by fishing.

Late in the fifteenth century the scholar's house Ojukheon was built here; it was the home of the painter and calligrapher Shin Saimdang and the birthplace, in 1536, of her son Yi I, the Confucian thinker known as Yulgok. Gangneung also produced the poet Heo Nanseolheon, whose collected verse was printed in Ming China after her death in 1589 and later in Japan, and her younger brother Heo Gyun, who raised a righteous army during the 1592 invasion, rose to high office in Seoul, and wrote the early Korean novel Hong Gildong jeon before he was executed in 1618. By Lake Gyeongpo stood the pavilion Gyeongpodae, counted among the eight scenic views of the Gwandong country. Every fifth lunar month the town held its dano festival, honouring the mountain god with sacrifices, shaman rites and folk plays.
zh:
江陵位于太白山脉东麓的朝鲜东海岸，是岭东地方的中心；外海寒暖流交错，鱼群繁盛。这里原为濊人居地，名为河瑟罗，639年新罗攻取后设为小京，高丽又以溟州为号，在此经略东北边防。1423年朝鲜世宗调整区划，取江陵与原州首字，命名江原道。1444年的江陵是一座儒教朝鲜的小型府城，以大都护府统辖附近属县，海岸市镇多以渔业为生。

15世纪末建成的乌竹轩，是画家、书法家申师任堂的故居，她的儿子、号栗谷的儒学家李珥也于1536年出生于此。江陵还养育了女诗人许兰雪轩，她1589年去世后，诗集经弟弟许筠刊行于明朝，后来又传到日本；许筠在壬辰倭乱中举起义兵，仕至高位，所作《洪吉童传》是朝鲜早期小说，1618年被处斩。镜浦湖畔的镜浦台，是关东八景之一。每逢农历五月，江陵举行端午祭，祭祀山神，巫祭与民间戏乐同时上演。

en:
East Timor is the mountainous eastern half of Timor, the sandalwood island at the southern end of the Moluccan trade routes. Its southern shore is wet and forested; its northern coast opens on the sheltered roadsteads of the Banda Sea. Tetum, Kemak and Galoli peoples lived in the fifty or so small kingdoms the Portuguese later called Belos, and their lords acknowledged the ruler of Wehale in the island's centre as their ritual overlord. Coastal rajas sold white sandalwood, beeswax and honey to junks from Java, Malacca and China. In 1444 no European ship had yet entered these waters, and the hill kingdoms kept their ancestor cults and their feuds to themselves.

Sandalwood brought the Portuguese. The first landing was near Pante Macassar in 1515, and Dominican friars built their post at Lifau in 1556, running a trade that did much to keep Macau prosperous. Lisbon's grip was weak, and for a century and a half the real masters were the Topasses, mestiço traders led by the da Costa and Hornay families, who held off both the Dutch at Kupang and the governors sent from Goa. A governor only reached Lifau in 1702, António Coelho Guerreiro, and his authority scarcely ran beyond the settlement. Fifteen kingdoms rose against him in the 1720s; a Portuguese army stormed their hill stronghold at Cailaco in 1726 after a six-week siege, yet the interior was never pacified. The Dutch pressed from Kupang, and a fort they backed at Maubara pulled the western kingdoms into the rivalry. In 1766 the Topasses killed Governor Dionísio Galvão at Lifau, and three years later his successor abandoned the place and founded Dili in the kingdom of Motael, the first solid European footing in the east. Dili shipped sandalwood to Macau, but the hill rajas let the groves die and the trade withered; coffee was tried from 1815 with little success. In 1821 the colony still amounted to little more than Dili, its priests, and a string of rajas loyal in name only.
zh:
东帝汶是帝汶岛多山的东半部，这座檀香木之岛处在摩鹿加商路的南端。南岸湿润多林，北岸掩着班达海的几处避风锚地。德顿、克马克、加洛利等族群生活在后来被葡萄牙人统称为贝卢的约五十个小王国里，各国首领奉岛中部韦哈莱之主为礼仪上的共主。沿海拉惹把白檀、蜂蜡和蜂蜜卖给来自爪哇、马六甲和中国的商船。1444年时，还没有欧洲船进入这片水域，山地诸邦守着祖先祭祀，也守着彼此的世仇。

引来葡萄牙人的正是檀香木：1515年首批葡萄牙人在潘特马卡萨附近登陆，1556年多明我会修士在利福设立据点，他们经营的檀香贸易是澳门富庶的重要财源。里斯本的控制力薄弱，此后一个半世纪里真正的主人是托帕塞人；这些混血商人以达科斯塔和奥尔奈两大家族为首，既抗拒盘踞古邦的荷兰人，也不买果阿派来的总督的账。直到1702年，安东尼奥·科埃略·格雷罗才作为首任总督抵达利福，其权势几乎出不了这座据点。1720年代，十五个王国起兵反抗，葡萄牙军队围攻六周，于1726年攻破他们的山地要塞凯拉科，内陆却始终未被驯服。荷兰人从古邦步步进逼，在其支持下修建的毛巴拉堡把西部诸王国也卷进两强之争。1766年，托帕塞人在利福杀死总督迪奥尼西奥·加尔旺；三年后，继任者放弃利福，在莫塔埃尔王国境内兴建帝力，这是欧洲人在岛东第一个稳固的立足点。帝力向澳门输出檀香木，山地拉惹却任檀林荒弃，贸易日渐凋敝；1815年起又试种咖啡，收效甚微。1821年时，这块殖民地仍不过是帝力一城、几名教士和一串名义效忠的拉惹。

en:
Yamdena is the largest island of the Tanimbar group, about sixty-five islands set between the Banda and Arafura seas where Austronesian and Melanesian peoples meet. Forested hills run along its eastern shore; the western coast is low and reef-fringed, and wild water buffalo roam the inland woods. Some forty villages lived by gardens, fishing and inter-island barter, and their craftsmen did fine woodcarving and goldwork while nearby Selaru wove ikat cloth. At Sangliat Dol a stone stairway climbs from the beach to a boat-shaped stone platform, raised for the canoes that carried the ancestors to the island. In 1444 no chief above the villages was obeyed here, and the spice fleets sailing between Malacca and the Moluccas passed these waters by.

Portuguese pilots sighted and possibly landed on the islands between 1522 and 1526, and Portuguese charts marked Tanimbar from the 1560s; Petrus Plancius put the group on his Insulae Moluccae map of 1594. A Dutch ship first called in 1629, and in 1639 the VOC claimed Tanimbar by right of discovery, then did nothing with it: no fort was built, no garrison posted, no treaty enforced. Through 1821 the villages of Yamdena kept their own councils, their feuds and their ancestor stones, visited now and then by a passing trader.
zh:
延德纳是塔宁巴尔群岛的第一大岛；这群约六十五个岛屿夹在班达海与阿拉弗拉海之间，南岛人与美拉尼西亚人在此相接。岛东是林木覆盖的丘陵，西岸低平、珊瑚礁环绕，野水牛在内陆林间出没。沿岸约四十个村落以园圃、渔捞和岛际易物为生，工匠擅木雕与金工，邻近的塞拉鲁岛出产扎染花布。在桑利亚特多尔，一条石阶从海滩通向一座船形石坛，为运载祖先登岛的独木舟而建。1444年时，村落之上没有更高的首领，往来马六甲与摩鹿加的香料船队也径直驶过塔宁巴尔的海面。

1522至1526年间，葡萄牙领航员望见并可能登上过这组岛屿，1560年代起的葡萄牙海图已标出塔宁巴尔，普兰修斯1594年的《摩鹿加群岛图》也将其绘入。1629年荷兰船只首次到访，1639年荷兰东印度公司凭发现权宣布领有群岛，之后便再无下文：不筑要塞，不派驻军，也没有真正执行的条约。直至1821年，延德纳各村依旧自行议事、自相攻伐、自守祖先的石坛，只有过路商人偶尔停靠。

en:
Tondo occupied the north bank of the Pasig River delta, with Maynila facing it across the water. The two bayan divided the China trade between them: Fujian junks unloaded silk, porcelain and iron at the river mouth, and Tondo's merchants carried the goods from island to island, bringing back honey, wax and gold piloncitos. Its barangays were led by datus under a paramount lakan, and the Laguna Copperplate of 900, the oldest Philippine document, already mentions Tundun among its places. Trade with Brunei and Majapahit gave the ruling families Malay and Indian titles. In 1444 the junks still came each year, and the lakan of Tondo stood first among the chiefs around Manila Bay.

Martín de Goiti sailed into the bay in 1570 and burned Maynila after a parley broke down, while Lakandula of Tondo held back. When Miguel López de Legazpi returned in 1571, Lakandula was the first chief to meet him; a Kapampangan fleet from Macabebe chose to fight instead, and on 3 June Legazpi's ships destroyed it in Bangkusay Channel and killed its chief Tarik Sulayman, the last open resistance on the bay. Tondo's datus became tribute collectors under a Spanish governor, and in 1587 a group of them plotted to throw the Spaniards out. The leaders were Magat Salamat, a son of Lakandula, and his cousin Agustín de Legazpi, grandson of the conquistador and son-in-law of Sultan Bolkiah of Brunei. A chief from Calamianes, Antonio Surabao, betrayed the plot, and the leaders were put to death in 1588. Tondo became a mission town governed from Manila, its shore still crowded with Chinese junks and traders. During the Seven Years War the British seized Manila in 1762 and held the bay until 1764.
zh:
汤都地处巴石河三角洲北岸，与南岸的马尼拉隔河相望。两座巴彦分据对华贸易：福建帆船在河口卸下丝绸、瓷器和铁器，汤都商人再把货运往一座座岛屿，换回蜂蜜、蜂蜡和皮隆西托金币。它的巴朗盖由达图统领，共尊一位拉干；900年的拉古纳铜版铭文是菲律宾现存最古的文献，其中已提到「汤敦」之名。与文莱、满者伯夷的贸易给统治家族带来马来和印度式的称号。1444年，中国商船仍年年前来，汤都的拉干在马尼拉湾诸首领中位居首座。

1570年，马丁·德·戈伊蒂驶入马尼拉湾，谈判破裂后焚毁马尼拉，汤都的拉坎杜拉则按兵未动。1571年米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮再至，拉坎杜拉是第一个出迎的首领；马卡贝贝的邦板牙舰队却选择开战，6月3日，莱加斯皮的舰队在班库赛海峡将其歼灭，击毙首领塔里克·苏莱曼，这是马尼拉湾最后一次公开抵抗。汤都的达图们沦为西班牙总督治下的包税人，1587年，其中数人密谋驱逐西班牙人。主谋是拉坎杜拉之子马加特·萨拉马特和他的表亲阿古斯丁·德·莱加斯皮，后者是征服者莱加斯皮之孙，也是文莱苏丹博尔基亚的女婿。卡拉棉群岛首领安东尼奥·苏拉豪出卖了密谋，首领们于1588年被处死。汤都此后成为受马尼拉管辖的传教城镇，岸边仍挤满中国帆船和商人。七年战争期间，英军于1762年夺取马尼拉，占据马尼拉湾直到1764年。

en:
Pangasinan curves along the eastern shore of Lingayen Gulf, and its coastal villages lived from the salt pans that gave the land its name, 'place of salt'. Up the Agno River delta lay Caboloan, 'place of bolo bamboo', whose chief town Binalatongan was said to hold more than two thousand houses, the largest settlement in the region. Ming annals called the country Fengjiashilan, and embassies from its rulers reached the Yongle Emperor in 1406 and 1408; Chinese and Japanese merchants sailed in with silk and porcelain and sailed out with gold, slaves, deerskins and civet, so that the Spaniards later called the roadstead the 'Port of Japan'. In 1444 Binalatongan still governed itself under its own ari, or king, and its people were animists whom neither Islam nor Christianity had reached.

Juan de Salcedo sailed into the gulf and landed at the Agno's mouth in 1572, after which the encomienda of Pangasinan was formed. Two years later the Chinese pirate Limahong, twice beaten back from Manila with a fleet of nearly seventy ships and four hundred Japanese soldiers in his crews, sailed north and seized the Agno delta to found a kingdom of his own; Salcedo landed behind him in March 1575 and besieged his fort for seven months, until Limahong slipped away with the last of his men and was never heard of again. Dominican friars made Binalatongan their first mission town in the Philippines, and in 1611 the colonial government merged the coastal salt villages with the inland settlements into the province of Pangasinan. In December 1660 Andres Malong, a chief of Binalatongan, drove out the Spanish and was proclaimed Ari na Pangasinan, King of Pangasinan; his kingdom fell before the spring. When word came that the British had taken Manila in 1762, Juan de la Cruz Palaris raised the country against Spain and held it until he was captured in 1765.
zh:
邦阿西楠位于林加延湾东岸，沿海村落靠盐田为生，地名本意就是「盐之地」。阿格诺河三角洲上游是「竹子之地」卡布洛安，首镇比纳拉图干（Binalatongan，今圣卡洛斯市）据说有两千多户人家，是整个邦阿西楠地区最大的聚落。明代史籍称此地为冯嘉施兰，其统治者的使者于1406年和1408年两度到永乐朝廷朝贡；中国和日本商人载来丝绸、瓷器，换走黄金、奴隶、鹿皮和灵猫香，西班牙人后来因此把这个锚地称作「日本港」。1444年，比纳拉图干仍由本地的阿里（ari，即王）统治，居民信奉泛灵信仰，伊斯兰教和基督教都还没有传来。

1572年，胡安·德·萨尔塞多驶入林加延湾，在阿格诺河口登陆，邦阿西楠随后被划为西班牙人的监护征赋地。两年后，中国海盗林凤两度攻打马尼拉受挫，带着近七十艘船、部众中还有四百名日本士兵北上，占领阿格诺河口打算自立王国；萨尔塞多1575年3月在他后方登陆，围困他的寨堡七个月，最后林凤率残部逃脱，此后再无音讯。多明我会修士把比纳拉图干建成他们在菲律宾的第一个传教城镇；1611年，殖民当局把沿海盐村与内陆聚落合并为邦阿西楠省。1660年12月，比纳拉图干首领安德烈斯·马隆驱逐西班牙人，被拥戴为「邦阿西楠之王」，他的王国没撑过第二年春天。1762年英军攻占马尼拉的消息传来，胡安·德拉克鲁斯·帕拉里斯举兵抗西，一直坚持到1765年被俘。

en:
The Bicol peninsula, called Ibalon by its people, reaches from southeastern Luzon into the Philippine and Sibuyan seas. Its barangays followed datus rather than a king or sultan, and the settlement on the Naga River handled gold from Paracale and rice from the Yraya lowlands; Chinese junks brought iron armour and firearms to exchange for them. Streams from Mount Isarog watered rice fields and abaca plots. In 1444 Bicol's datus still kept animist rites, while their villages lived from the trade passing along the river and coast.

Juan de Salcedo's soldiers crossed Bicol in 1573, and Pedro de Chavez secured the Naga settlement after fighting on the river banks. The Spanish town there became Nueva Caceres, and Franciscan friars built its churches and made the see one of the oldest diocesan centres in the Philippines. Bicol's hardwoods also fed royal shipyards, above all Pasacao, whose carpenters built vessels for the Manila trade; abaca remained the peninsula's main export. Dutch raiders burned Cagsawa's Franciscan church in 1636. When the British took Manila in 1762, the Camarines rose and Spanish troops needed two years to defeat them. The Mayon Volcano erupted on 1 February 1814, burying Cagsawa and about 2,000 people. Survivors moved to Daraga, and the church belfry rose above the ash.
zh:
比科尔半岛被当地人称作伊巴隆，从吕宋东南部伸入菲律宾海与锡布延海。岛上居民以巴朗圭为单位，首领是达图，没有更高的国王或苏丹。那牙河畔的聚落转运帕拉卡莱的黄金和伊拉亚低地的稻米，中国帆船则运来铁甲、火器交换。伊萨罗格山的溪流灌溉稻田和蕉麻地。1444年，比科尔的达图们仍奉行泛灵仪式，各村依靠河海往来贸易为生。

1573年，胡安·德·萨尔塞多的军队进入比科尔，佩德罗·德·查韦斯经过河畔战斗后控制那牙聚落。西班牙人在那里建立的城镇成为新卡塞雷斯，方济各会修士修建教堂，使这里成为菲律宾最早的教区中心之一。比科尔的硬木供养王家船厂，尤其是帕萨考，船匠在那里为马尼拉贸易建造船只；蕉麻长期是半岛的主要出口物产。1636年，荷兰袭掠者焚毁卡格萨瓦的方济各会教堂。1762年英军占领马尼拉后，甘马仁人起兵，西班牙军队用了两年才将其击败。1814年2月1日，马荣火山喷发，掩埋卡格萨瓦和约两千人。幸存者迁往达拉加，教堂钟楼露出火山灰。

en:
Panay is the broad triangular island at the western end of the Visayas, with the Panay River and shorter streams running from the central highlands to the Sibuyan Sea. The northeast coast, where the old settlement of Bamban became the Spanish town of Panay, had wide rice plains and easy landing places. Visayan datus ruled its coastal barangays before Spanish contact. Yuan Chinese records knew a Visayan trading polity in these islands as Oton, called Yachen, and islanders bartered rice, gold and sea produce for Chinese porcelain, metal gongs and bells. A later written tradition, the Maragtas, remembered the chiefs as the confederacy of Madja-as, though historians treat the story of the ten datus as legend. In 1444 Panay was an animist island of rival chiefs and productive river plains.

The Spaniards reached Panay town in 1566 and made it their second settlement after Cebu. Miguel Lopez de Legazpi moved his whole camp there in 1569 because the island could feed his men and offered more shelter from Portuguese pressure on Cebu; the expedition that conquered Luzon sailed from Panay on 8 May 1570. Juan de la Isla built a fortress at the town later that year. For two centuries Panay shipped rice and meat to Manila, while the shipyards at Arevalo built galleys for the colonial government. Panay town remained a provincial capital and in the 18th century produced suerte cloth for export, before Capiz took its place as the seat of provincial administration in 1716.
zh:
班乃岛是米沙鄢西端的三角形大岛，班乃河和较短的河川从中部高地流向锡布延海。东北海岸的班班旧址后来成为西班牙人的班乃镇，这一带有开阔的稻米平原和便于登陆的海岸。西班牙人到来前，沿海的巴朗圭由米沙鄢达图统治。元代中国记载把群岛上的米沙鄢贸易政体称为奥通，记作哑陈；岛民以米粮、黄金和海产交换中国瓷器、金属钟锣。后世文献《马拉格塔斯》把诸首领称作马迪亚斯联盟，但学界将十达图的故事视为传说。1444年的班乃仍是诸首领并立的泛灵信仰岛屿，河畔平原出产丰足。

1566年，西班牙人抵达班乃镇，把这里建为宿务之后的第二个定居点。1569年，米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮把整个营地迁来，因为岛上能够供应军粮，也比受葡萄牙威胁的宿务更安全；1570年5月8日，征服吕宋的远征军正是从班乃出发。同年晚些时候，胡安·德·拉·伊斯拉在镇上筑起要塞。此后两百年间，班乃向马尼拉运送米粮和肉类，阿雷瓦洛船场则为殖民政府建造桨帆战船。班乃镇长期担任省城，18世纪还出产供出口的苏埃尔特布，到1716年卡皮斯才取代它成为行政中心。

en:
Tagloc was the shore of the great gulf then called the Gulf of Tagloc, now Davao Gulf, where the Tagloc River enters the sea beneath Mount Apo, the highest peak in the Philippines. To the Bagobo, Matigsalug and other Lumad peoples of its foothills the mountain was Apo Sandawa, Grandfather Sandawa, the ancestor spirit for whom their shamans performed rites on the slopes. The Lumad farmed the interior valleys, while Islamized Kagan and Maguindanaon settlers clustered at the river mouth and Maguindanaon and Tausug traders sailed the gulf, carrying out wax, honey and forest produce and bringing in salt, metal goods and Chinese porcelain. In 1444 no European had yet entered these waters, and Lumad datus ruled their own valleys, though their trade already bound them to the Muslim sultanates to the west.

When Ruy López de Villalobos surveyed Mindanao's eastern coast for Spain in 1543, he gave the Gulf of Tagloc a wide berth: Moro war fleets crowded its waters, and his pilots judged a landing suicidal. No Spaniard pressed a claim there for almost three centuries. Around 1800 Datu Mama Bago, a Maguindanaon chief granted these shores for his campaigns against the Spaniards, moved east from his homeland, drew the Bagobo and neighbouring peoples to his side, and spent the following years conquering the gulf shore by shore until he ruled all of Tagloc.
zh:
塔格洛克是塔格洛克湾（即今达沃湾）的沿岸之地，塔格洛克河（今达沃河）在菲律宾最高峰阿波火山下注入湾中。在山麓的巴戈博人、马蒂格萨卢格人等卢马德族群看来，这座山是「阿波·桑达瓦」，意为「桑达瓦老翁」，是护佑他们的祖灵，由巫师在山坡上主持祭祀。卢马德人在山谷中耕作，归信伊斯兰教的卡甘人和马京达瑙人聚居河口，马京达瑙与陶苏格商人往来湾上，运出蜂蜡、蜂蜜和山林物产，运入盐、金属器和中国瓷器。1444年时还没有欧洲人进入这片水域，卢马德的达图们仍统治着各自的山谷，只是贸易早已把他们同西边的穆斯林苏丹国连在一起。

1543年，为西班牙勘测棉兰老东海岸的鲁伊·洛佩斯·德比利亚洛沃斯有意绕开塔格洛克湾：湾中密布摩洛人的战舰，引水员认定登陆无异于送死。此后近三百年，再没有西班牙人来此主张主权。1800年前后，马京达瑙的达图·马马·巴戈因对西班牙人作战有功而受封这片海岸，他从故土东迁，争取到巴戈博等邻近族群归附，随后数年逐岸攻战，最终统治了整个塔格洛克。

en:
Butuan lies at the mouth of the Agusan River on Mindanao's north-eastern coast, where gold washed out of the river gravel made its smiths famous, and its shipwrights built the balangay, the great ocean-going outriggers whose planked remains have been dug up at Libertad. A mission reached Song China as early as 1001, and the Chinese annals called the rajahnate Puduan. One rajah asked the Song for standing equal with Champa and was refused; a later envoy startled Emperor Zhenzong by arriving on the eve of a great state sacrifice with a memorial engraved on a gold tablet, white camphor, Moluccan cloves and a slave. Gold jewellery, cloves and camphor sailed from here to Champa, Majapahit, Brunei and the Bengali coast. A Chinese annal records Brunei conquering Butuan in 1304, before the port won its freedom back. In 1444 it was a rajah's town of fishermen and gold-panners, who kept the old animist rites beneath the Indian-style titles of their court.

On 31 March 1521 Rajah Siagu of Butuan was among the chiefs who met Ferdinand Magellan at Mazaua and stood at the first Catholic mass said in the Philippines. Real submission came only with the Jesuits: Father Valerio de Ledesma landed with a mission in 1596, sent to make a Spanish foothold in Mindanao against the Moro slave-raiders out of the southern seas, and the first church opened on 8 September 1597; Augustinian Recollects later carried the work on. Reinforcements from Mexico strengthened the Caraga garrison in 1635 and again in the 1670s, yet the sea-raiding never quite stopped. A Spanish census in 1818 counted 3,703 native families in Butuan.
zh:
