庆州古称徐罗伐、金城，近千年间一直是新罗的王都。668年新罗统一之后，国王与贵族大多聚居于此：瞻星台建于640年代，皇龙寺九重木塔于645年落成，8世纪大臣金大城又主持修建佛国寺与石窟庵。据《三国遗事》记载，极盛时城中有十七万八千九百三十六户，9世纪的阿拉伯地理书也把它的声名传到了波斯。935年新罗归降高丽，朝廷不复存在；改称庆州后，它在987年被高丽定为「东京」，1012年这一称号又被废止。13世纪蒙古入侵，皇龙寺大塔毁于兵火；进入朝鲜时代初期，性理学者中的排佛激进者还砸毁了南山的佛教造像。1444年的庆州是庆尚道一座安静的府城，田野街巷间散落着旧王朝的遗迹。

1592年壬辰倭乱，庆州平原沦为战场：金虎率领的本地义兵8月在露谷击败一支日军，但旧都终归陷落。朴晋的官军与义兵首领权应铢当年两度围城，用新造的飞击震天雷轰开城墙，收复庆州。1593年5月日军放火焚烧佛国寺，近两千间殿宇化为灰烬；国家修复工程于1604年启动。1601年，庆尚道监营从庆州迁往大邱，庆州再未能恢复旧日的行政地位。17、18世纪里，它是南人派和新罗旧族后裔的乡居之地，两班村落如良洞村坐落于王陵之间，行人车马从皇龙寺残破的塔址旁经过。

en:
Vidin guards a broad Danube crossing in the fertile, wine-growing north-west of Bulgaria. Roman Bononia stood here on the Danube frontier, and the medieval Bulgarian stronghold of Bdin grew around the Baba Vida citadel, raised between the tenth and fourteenth centuries. Basil II took the town only after an eight-month siege in 1003, when the local bishop betrayed it to him, and under the Second Empire the local Shishman dynasty gave Bulgaria an emperor when Michael Shishman was chosen tsar in 1323. In 1356 Ivan Stratsimir inherited the town and ruled the surrounding Vidin Tsardom as an independent Bulgarian ruler; Hungarian crusaders held it from 1365 to 1369, until Vladislav I of Wallachia drove them out. The Ottomans annexed Vidin after Bayezid's victory at Nicopolis in 1396 and made it a sanjak, and King Vladislav III's crusaders besieged it in vain in 1444.

Vidin then spent three centuries in the Ottoman-Habsburg border belt, trading wine, furs and barrelled caviar from the Danube. Austrian troops stormed it in October 1689 and deported thousands of its Muslims to Nikopol; when the Ottomans returned nine months later, only two or three hundred of the town's three thousand buildings were still standing. The frontier disorders of the 1790s raised Osman Pazvantoğlu, a former Janissary who ruled the Vidin region as his own from 1795 until his death in 1807 and built a mosque, a library and barracks in the town. His wars and the rival campaigns of other Ottoman commanders scattered the villagers of the Danube flats, and between 1812 and 1820 the authorities brought Bulgarian families back from Wallachia to resettle abandoned estates. In 1821 Vidin was a fortified Ottoman river town on a slowly reviving frontier.
zh:
维丁扼守保加利亚西北肥沃产酒之地的一处宽阔多瑙河渡口。罗马的波诺尼亚曾在此守卫多瑙河边防，中世纪保加利亚要塞布丁围绕巴巴维达城堡发展，城堡建于10至14世纪。1003年，巴西尔二世围城八个月，才靠当地主教叛卖拿下此城。第二帝国时期，本地的希什曼家族还出了一位君主：米哈伊尔·希什曼1323年被拥立为沙皇。1356年伊凡·斯拉齐米尔继承此城，以独立君主身份统治周围的维丁沙皇国；1365至1369年匈牙利十字军占据这里，最后被瓦拉几亚的弗拉迪斯拉夫一世赶走。1396年巴耶济德在尼科波尔获胜后，奥斯曼吞并维丁并设为桑贾克；1444年瓦迪斯瓦夫三世的十字军又围攻此城不克。

此后三个世纪，维丁处在奥斯曼与哈布斯堡的边界地带，输出葡萄酒、毛皮和多瑙河的桶装鱼子酱。1689年10月奥地利军队破城，把数千名穆斯林押往尼科波尔；九个月后奥斯曼人返回时，全城三千座建筑只剩两三百座尚存。1790年代的边疆动乱把前禁卫军奥斯曼·帕兹万特奥卢推上台面，他从1795年起把维丁地区当作私产统治，直到1807年死去，还在城中修建清真寺、图书馆和兵营。他的战争和其他奥斯曼军队的来回攻伐使多瑙河平原的村民离散；1812至1820年，当局招引从瓦拉几亚返回的保加利亚家庭重新垦殖废弃庄园。1821年的维丁，是缓慢恢复的边疆上一座设防的奥斯曼河城。

en:
Khara Narin Ula, the Black Narrow Mountain, is the range the Chinese call Lang Shan, the Wolf Mountains, the westernmost spine of the Yin range, covering the north-west corner of the Yellow River's Ordos Loop. Its southern face drops in cliffs to the irrigated back-loop plain, and the gentler northern slope runs out into the stony Gobi plateau. A gorge in the range, Gaoque, the High Tower pass, carried the long wall of the kings of Zhao and let Han armies march out against the Xiongnu. In 1444 no Ming garrison or magistrate remained in the back loop; Tatar, Oirat and Uriankhai herdsmen roamed the mountains and the desert pastures under the loose lordship of the Northern Yuan.

Dayan Khan's victories around 1510 brought the loop into his reunited Mongol realm, and the Ordos tumen took these lands for their grazing. They were the guardians of the Eight White Tents, the eight white gers that held the portable shrine of Genghis Khan, and from those tents, the ordo, they took their name. For a century their horsemen filed through the Lang Shan gorges on their way to raid the Ming frontier. Ligdan Khan scattered the Ordos in 1628, and the survivors submitted to Hong Taiji in 1635. The eastern range and the steppe reaching north toward the Gobi then passed to the Urad, enfeoffed as three jasak banners in 1648 and moved to the north bank of the Yellow River in 1649, a quiet Qing frontier facing the Khalkha across the desert.
zh:
哈拉纳林乌拉，蒙古语意为「黑色的窄山」，汉人称之为狼山，是阴山山脉最西端的一道山脊，屏护着黄河河套的西北角。山南是直落后套灌溉平原的峭壁，北坡平缓，逐渐没入砾石遍布的戈壁高原。山间峡谷中的高阙塞，是赵武灵王长城所经的关口，汉军也由这里出塞攻击匈奴。1444年，后套已无明朝的卫所与官吏，鞑靼、瓦剌、兀良哈牧民在狼山与北面的荒漠牧场上游牧，只在名义上尊奉北元大汗。

1510年前后，达延汗连战胜出，河套并入他重新统一的蒙古，鄂尔多斯万户以此为牧场。他们是八白室的守护者：八顶白色毡帐供奉着成吉思汗的移动灵帐，部落的名字就来自「斡耳朵」，即宫帐。此后百年间，骑兵不断穿过狼山口南下，袭扰明朝边境。1628年林丹汗西进，打散了鄂尔多斯部，余众在1635年归附皇太极。狼山东段及向北通往戈壁的草原后来归了乌喇特：1648年封授三个札萨克旗，1649年移牧黄河北岸，成为清代与大漠以北喀尔喀相望的安静边地。

en:
Jianchang follows the Anning River valley between the Dadu and Jinsha rivers, the open corridor from Sichuan into Yunnan and the Daliangshan Yi country. The Qiongdu people lived here before the Han set up Qiongdu county, and a local lord later held the Song title King of the Qiongdu. Nanzhao made the valley Jianchang Prefecture in the ninth century, Dali kept the name, and Mongol armies subdued it between 1253 and 1256. In 1275 the Yuan created Jianchang Route, seated at Jian'an near present-day Xichang. Marco Polo knew the country as Jiandu and recorded rods of gold for larger payments and half-catty pieces of molded salt used as small change. Ming forces took over in 1382. From 1394 Jianchang Guard was the seat of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission, directing five guards, eight battalions and four native offices; Chengdu lay 1,480 li to the northeast. In 1444 soldiers and native chiefs shared this frontier.

The Ming garrison order survived the dynastic change, though Qing officials gradually brought it under civilian administration. In 1728 the court made Jianchang the seat of Ningyuan Prefecture and Xichang County, replacing the old guard hierarchy with regular prefectural government. During the eighteenth century, missionaries of the Paris Foreign Missions Society brought Roman Catholicism into Ningyuan. The old name Jianchang remained in use beside the new Qing name.
zh:
建昌在大渡河与金沙江之间的安宁河谷，是四川进入云南、通向大凉山彝区的开阔走廊。汉人在此设县以前，当地住着邛都人；后来还有地方首领受宋朝封为邛都王。9世纪时，南诏把这里设为建昌府，大理国沿用其名。蒙古军1253至1256年征服此地，元朝1275年置建昌路，治所在今西昌附近的建安州。马可·波罗称这一带为建都，记载当地人用金条支付大数目的交易，又把半斤重的模制盐块当作零钱。明军1382年接管；1394年起，建昌卫成为四川行都指挥使司治所，统辖五卫、八所、四长官司，东北距成都一千四百八十里。1444年，驻军和土著首领共同维持这片边地。

明代卫所格局经历了明清易代，之后逐渐纳入文官行政。1728年，朝廷以建昌为宁远府和西昌县治所，用常规府县体系取代旧卫军建制。18世纪，巴黎外方传教会的传教士把罗马天主教传入宁远。旧名建昌仍与清代的新府名并用。

en:
Tikhvin began as the Predtechensky pogost on the Tikhvinka, where boats and portages linked the Volga basin with Lake Ladoga and the Baltic. A chronicle first notices it in 1383, when a wooden Church of the Dormition stood there, and church tradition connects that year with the image later called the Theotokos of Tikhvin: said to have been painted by Luke the Evangelist, it was believed to have appeared hovering over a lake nearby. In 1444 the place was still only a Novgorodian parish and a calling point on the portage road, where traders and craftsmen stopped between the Volga and the Baltic.

Vasily III paid for a stone Dormition Cathedral, raised in 1507-1515 to house the icon. In 1560 Ivan IV ordered the Dormition Monastery built on the river bank, with the smaller Vvedensky Convent and two trading settlements, all in a single spring and summer; by the mid-seventeenth century two log walls packed with earth and stone and nine towers ringed the grounds. In 1613 Swedish troops burned the posad, but on 25 May Leonty Artsybashev roused the townspeople, who held the monastery through the siege and then drove the Swedes out; the war ended with the Peace of Stolbovo in 1617. Tikhvin blacksmiths sold their iron abroad and the Tikhvin Fair became one of the largest in Russia. The Tikhvin water system, opened in 1811, joined the Volga to Ladoga by canal and in busy years carried as many as 6,000 vessels.
zh:
季赫温起于季赫温卡河畔的普列杰琴斯基教区聚落，附近的船只拖运路线把伏尔加河流域同拉多加湖、波罗的海连在一起。编年史在1383年首次提到它，当时那里有一座木制圣母安息教堂；教会传说把这一年与后来称作「季赫温圣母」的圣像联系起来，相传此像为福音书作者路加所绘，曾显现于附近的湖面之上。1444年时，这里还只是诺夫哥罗德的一个教区和拖运道上的停靠点，往来伏尔加河与波罗的海之间的商人和工匠在此歇脚。

瓦西里三世出资修建石造圣母安息大教堂，1507至1515年建成，用以安放这幅圣像。1560年，伊凡四世下令在河岸修建圣母安息修道院，连同较小的圣母进堂女修道院和两个工商业聚落，全部在一个春夏之内建成；到17世纪中叶，修道院四周已有两道内部填实土石的原木墙和九座塔楼。1613年，瑞典军队焚毁城镇聚落，列昂季·阿尔齐巴舍夫在5月25日唤起市民，他们退入修道院顶住围城，随后把瑞典人赶走；战争以1617年的斯托尔博沃和约结束。季赫温铁匠打造的铁器销到海外，季赫温集市也成为俄国最大的集市之一。1811年开通的季赫温水系以运河连接伏尔加河与拉多加湖，繁忙年份通行船只多达六千艘。

en:
Plovdiv spreads over seven syenite hills beside the Maritsa in the fertile Upper Thracian plain. Philip II of Macedon founded Philippopolis there in 342 BC, and under Rome the town was capital of the province of Thracia, where the Via Militaris met roads running to the Danube, the Aegean and the Black Sea; a chronicler of the Fourth Crusade called it the third city of the Byzantine Empire after Constantinople and Thessalonica. It changed hands repeatedly in the Bulgarian-Byzantine wars, Kaloyan destroyed it in 1206, and it served for a time as the seat of the Latin Duchy of Philippopolis before Ivan Asen II took it in 1230. Ottoman forces under Lala Şahin Pasha seized it in 1364 and called it Filibe. The town was the early Ottoman centre of Rumelia before Sofia took that role, while remaining chief town of its own sanjak. In November 1444, after Varna, Filibe was a securely Ottoman road and caravan town in productive Bulgarian Orthodox country.

In the Ottoman centuries Filibe became one of the richest market towns of the inland Balkans. Caravans between Edirne, Istanbul, Sofia and Belgrade lodged in its khans, and the Maritsa valley carried out the grain, livestock and crafts of the Thracian plain. Soon after the conquest the Ottomans pulled down the cathedral of St Petka and built the nine-domed Dzhumaya Friday Mosque on its site in 1363-1364, the first of the mosques, madrasas, caravanserais, bazaars and hammams that filled the town; the Imaret Mosque followed in the 1440s. From the fifteenth century to the end of the seventeenth most of its people were Muslims, though Sephardic Jews, Armenians and Bulgarian and Greek Orthodox Christians traded there too. Evliya Çelebi, visiting in the seventeenth century, counted many mosques, minarets, khans, baths and schools and ranked the city among the notable towns of Rumelia. In 1821 Filibe remained the seat of a sanjak and a rich market on the empire's main Balkan road.
zh:
普罗夫迪夫位于肥沃的上色雷斯平原，城区铺展在马里查河畔的七座正长岩丘陵上。公元前342年，马其顿王腓力二世在此兴建菲利普波利斯；罗马时代它是色雷斯行省首府，军事大道在此与通往多瑙河、爱琴海和黑海的道路相接。第四次十字军的一位编年史家称它是拜占庭帝国第三大城，仅次于君士坦丁堡和塞萨洛尼基。它在拜占庭与保加利亚的战争中多次易手，1206年被卡洛扬摧毁，一度成为十字军建立的菲利普波利斯公国都城，1230年被伊凡·阿森二世攻占。1364年，拉拉·沙欣帕夏率奥斯曼军攻占此城，改称菲利贝。它是奥斯曼人在鲁米利亚最早的统治中心，后来这一地位让给索非亚，但始终是本桑贾克的首城。1444年11月瓦尔纳战役之后，菲利贝已稳在奥斯曼治下，是丰裕的保加利亚东正教土地上的道路与商队城镇。

奥斯曼世纪里，菲利贝成为巴尔干内陆最富庶的市场城镇之一。往返埃迪尔内、伊斯坦布尔、索非亚和贝尔格莱德的商队在它的客店投宿，马里查河谷运出色雷斯的谷物、牲畜和手工业品。征服之初，奥斯曼人拆毁圣佩特卡大教堂，于1363至1364年在原址建起九穹顶的朱马亚聚礼清真寺；此后清真寺、伊斯兰学校、商队旅馆、巴扎和浴室遍布全城，1440年代又建成伊马雷特清真寺。从15世纪到17世纪末，菲利贝居民以穆斯林为多，也有塞法迪犹太人、亚美尼亚人以及保加利亚和希腊的东正教徒在此经商。17世纪埃夫利亚·切莱比到访时，数出城中众多清真寺、宣礼塔、客店、浴室和学校，把它列为鲁米利亚的名城之一。1821年，菲利贝仍是桑贾克治所，也是帝国巴尔干干道上的富庶市场。

en:
Cuenca crowns a narrow rock ridge squeezed between the gorges of the Júcar and the Huécar in the Iberian System. Muslims built the fortress of Qunka there, ringed by about a kilometre of wall, and Alfonso VIII of Castile took it only after a siege that ran from Epiphany to 21 September 1177; the garrison held the citadel into October. The Fuero of Cuenca became one of the most admired town charters in Castile, a bishopric followed in 1183, and Alfonso X granted civic rank in 1257. French masons raised the cathedral in an Anglo-Norman Gothic new to Castile, and in the fifteenth century townsmen built the hanging houses, their balconies projecting out over the Huécar gorge. Flocks and woollen cloth paid for the building boom and pushed new quarters down the river slopes. In 1444 Cuenca was a prosperous Catholic Castilian wool town, its defence still tied to the citadel on its rock.

The southern town of Belmonte, in the same province, produced two famous Castilians: Juan Pacheco, born there in 1419, who as marquis of Villena and master of Santiago dominated the court of Henry IV and helped depose him in effigy at the Farce of Ávila, and the Augustinian poet and theologian Fray Luis de León, born there in 1527, who held a chair at Salamanca and spent four years in the prisons of the Inquisition before he was cleared. Cuenca's Jewish quarter ended with the expulsion of 1492, and its last large crypto-Jewish trials ran from 1718 to 1725. Woollen cloth and tapestries made the city famous in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries until the trade collapsed in the seventeenth and emptied its streets. In the War of the Spanish Succession Anglo-Portuguese troops took Cuenca for the Habsburg claimant in June 1706, lost it in August, and Archduke Charles held it again briefly in 1710; the town's loyalty to Philip V earned it the title 'Most Faithful and Heroic'. During the Peninsular War French forces sacked Cuenca more than nine times.
zh:
昆卡雄踞在伊比利亚山脉中一道狭窄的岩脊上，胡卡尔河与韦卡尔河在两侧切出深峡。穆斯林在这里筑起约一公里长城墙环绕的昆卡要塞，卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索八世从1177年主显节起围攻，直到9月21日才破城，守军又在城寨里守到10月。《昆卡法典》后来成为卡斯蒂利亚最受推崇的城市宪章之一，1183年设主教区，1257年阿方索十世授予城市地位。法国工匠把大教堂修造成卡斯蒂利亚人还很陌生的盎格鲁-诺曼哥特式；15世纪，居民又在韦卡尔峡谷上方造起悬屋，阳台直接探出峡谷之上。牧群和毛织业为这场营建热潮出资，也把新街区推向河谷坡地。1444年的昆卡是一座富庶的天主教卡斯蒂利亚毛织城镇，防务仍系于岩脊上的城寨。

省境南部的贝尔蒙特镇出过两位卡斯蒂利亚名人：1419年出生的胡安·帕切科，他受封比列纳侯爵、出任圣地亚哥骑士团首领，长期左右恩里克四世的朝政，也是「阿维拉闹剧」废立仪式的主谋之一；1527年出生的奥斯定会诗人、神学家路易斯·德·莱昂，他在萨拉曼卡大学任教席，被宗教裁判所关押四年才洗清罪名。昆卡的犹太区随1492年的驱逐令而消亡，当地最后一轮大规模隐秘犹太教徒审判发生在1718年至1725年。15至16世纪，毛料和挂毯让昆卡闻名，17世纪产业崩溃，街区为之一空。西班牙王位继承战争中，英葡联军1706年6月替哈布斯堡觊觎者拿下昆卡，8月即告失守，卡尔大公1710年又短暂占据；昆卡因效忠费利佩五世获「至信至勇」称号。半岛战争期间，法军先后九次以上洗劫昆卡。

en:
Romsdal is the fjord country of western Norway where the Romsdalsfjord meets the steep Romsdalen valley, through which the Rauma river runs down from the mountains to the sea; the valley has always been the road between the western fjords and the inland. In the Viking age the island of Veøya, where the inner sea lanes forked, held the district's first market and probably the seat of Jarl Ragnvald of Møre, and a small stone church was raised there over a heathen site at the end of the 1100s. On 7 July 1162 the fjord itself was the scene of the battle of Sekken: King Håkon Herdebrei was killed fighting Erling Skakke, and the crown passed to the young Magnus Erlingsson. In 1444 Romsdal belonged to the Norwegian crown within the Kalmar Union, a Catholic land of free fishermen and farmers under the diocese of Nidaros, with Veøya and the fishing haven of Bud as its main settlements.

By 1604 Molde had become a timber-and-herring harbour trading with Holland and was made a loading place under Trondheim. During the Kalmar War some 300 Scottish mercenaries landed at Isfjorden in 1612 and marched inland through the valley to join the Swedes; Norwegian peasants ambushed and nearly annihilated them at Kringen. The treaty of Roskilde in 1658 carried the Swedish frontier down to the Romsdalsfjord, but the farmers refused Swedish taxes and conscription, and the treaty of Copenhagen restored the old border two years later. Molde became the governor's seat, with the governor residing at Moldegård from 1705, and on 29 June 1742 Christian VI granted the town full market-town rights despite protests from Bergen and Trondheim. In 1814 the district followed Norway into the union with Sweden.
zh:
鲁姆斯达尔是挪威西部的峡湾之乡：鲁姆斯达尔峡湾与陡峻的鲁姆斯达尔山谷相接，劳马河穿山出谷、奔流入海，这条山谷自古就是西部峡湾通往内陆的要道。维京时代，扼守内海航道分岔口的韦于亚岛形成了本区最早的市集，很可能还是默勒伯爵拉格瓦尔德的驻地；12世纪末，岛上在异教圣地建起一座小石堂。1162年7月7日，峡湾中爆发塞肯海战，国王哈康二世与厄尔林·斯卡克交战时阵亡，王冠落入年轻的马格努斯五世手中。1444年的鲁姆斯达尔属卡尔马联盟中的挪威王冠，是尼达罗斯教区治下天主教自由渔民和农民的土地，韦于亚和渔港布德是主要聚落。

1604年，靠木材和鲱鱼与荷兰通商的莫尔德成为特隆赫姆管辖的装卸港。1612年卡尔马战争期间，约三百名苏格兰雇佣兵在伊斯菲尤伦登陆，沿山谷东进去投瑞典，在克林根遭挪威农民伏击，几乎被全歼。1658年《罗斯基勒条约》把瑞典边界推到鲁姆斯达尔峡湾，农民却拒缴瑞典赋税、拒服兵役，两年后《哥本哈根条约》恢复旧界。莫尔德成为鲁姆斯达尔长官驻地，1705年起长官住进莫尔德庄园；1742年6月29日，克里斯蒂安六世不顾卑尔根和特隆赫姆反对，授予莫尔德完整市镇权。1814年，鲁姆斯达尔随挪威并入与瑞典的联盟。

en:
Narbonne first grew powerful as a Roman road junction and Mediterranean port. Founded in 118 BC as the colony of Narbo Martius, it became the capital of Gallia Narbonensis, where the Via Domitia toward Spain branched from the Via Aquitania toward the Atlantic. After centuries as a centre of Visigothic Septimania, the Frankish conquest of 759 left the archbishop and viscount sharing rule. In the twelfth century Viscountess Ermengarde kept a court frequented by troubadours, and the city's Jewish exegetical school drew scholars from across Latin Christendom. Around 1300 Narbonne had perhaps 30,000 people and was the leading cloth-working town in Languedoc, sending woollens to Spain and the Levant. The Aude then turned against the port. A flood in 1320 destroyed the river dam, the harbour began to silt, and the Black Death, Free Companies and the Black Prince's raid of 1355 further reduced the city. In 1444 Narbonne was still one of France's oldest archiepiscopal sees, but it had become a half-empty former port whose viscounts lived elsewhere.

In 1447 the viscounty was sold to Gaston IV of Foix. The dynasty soon reached a royal marriage: Germaine of Foix, daughter of Viscount John and granddaughter of Gaston, married King Ferdinand II of Aragon in 1505. Cardinal Giulio de' Medici held the archbishopric from 1515 until he was elected Pope Clement VII in 1523. The unfinished Cathedral of Saints Justus and Pastor shows the city's contracted ambitions. Begun in 1272, it has a choir vault 41 metres high, among the highest in France, but the city walls blocked the planned nave and transept and the work stopped after 1354. From the sixteenth century Narbonne dredged and rebuilt its old channel as the Canal de la Robine; wine boats used the waterway, which finally joined the Canal du Midi in 1776.
zh:
纳博讷最早凭借罗马大道交会处和地中海港口兴起。它建于公元前118年，初名纳尔博·马提乌斯殖民地，后来成为纳尔博南西斯行省首府；通往西班牙的多弥提亚大道在这里与通往大西洋的阿基坦大道分岔。西哥特统治时期，这里是塞蒂马尼亚的中心；759年法兰克人收复后，城市由大主教与子爵共同治理。12世纪，女子爵埃芒加德的宫廷常有行吟诗人出入，城中的犹太解经学校也吸引着拉丁基督教世界的学者。1300年前后，纳博讷约有三万居民，是朗格多克首屈一指的呢绒织造城镇，毛料远销西班牙和黎凡特。后来奥德河毁了这座港口：1320年洪水冲毁河坝，港湾开始淤塞，黑死病、自由佣兵和黑太子1355年的劫掠又使城市进一步衰败。1444年，纳博讷仍保有法兰西最古老的总教区之一，却已是一座半空的旧港，子爵一家也久居外地。

1447年，子爵领被卖给富瓦伯爵加斯东四世。这个家族很快通过婚姻接近王位：子爵让的女儿、加斯东的孙女热尔梅娜于1505年嫁给阿拉贡国王斐迪南二世。1515年至1523年，枢机主教朱利奥·德·美第奇担任纳博讷大主教，随后当选教皇，称克雷芒七世。未完工的圣茹斯特与圣帕斯托尔大教堂显示出这座城市收缩后的抱负。大教堂1272年动工，歌坛拱顶高达41米，属于法兰西最高的一批拱顶，但城墙挡住了规划中的正殿和耳堂，1354年之后工程便停止。16世纪起，纳博讷人疏浚并重修旧河道，建成罗比讷运河，酒船沿河道出入；1776年，这条运河终于与米迪运河连通。

en:
La Mancha is the dry southern tableland of Castile, crossed by the Guadiana and bounded by the Montes de Toledo and the Sierra Morena, a country of grain fields, sheep walks and windmills. After the Reconquista its towns and pastures went chiefly to the military Orders of Santiago and Calatrava; the masters of Calatrava made Almagro their seat, where Alfonso X held the Cortes in 1273. Alfonso X also founded Villa Real in 1255, a royal town planted inside the order's lands, and John II raised it to Ciudad Real in 1420 after its militia fought for him against the orders. The order's mines at Almadén produced cinnabar and quicksilver. In 1444 Ciudad Real was still a small royal town overshadowed by Almagro, while the plains lived from grain and sheep.

In the succession crisis after 1474 the Pachecos of Villena and the two orders backed Juana la Beltraneja and her Portuguese husband, until the 1479 Treaty of Alcáçovas confirmed Isabella and Ferdinand. Ciudad Real's own hero of that age was Hernán Pérez del Pulgar, born there in 1451 and called el de las Hazañas, 'the man of deeds': a captain in the Granada war who slipped into Granada by night with fifteen horsemen in 1490, nailed an Ave María placard to the door of the Great Mosque and set fire to the silk bazaar before fighting his way back to the camp at Santa Fe. After the Comuneros' defeat the order estates, Almadén included, passed to the Crown in 1523 and were leased to the Fuggers; Almadén quicksilver went through Seville to the American silver mines for the amalgamation process, and from 1566 convicts worked its poisonous shafts, until the Crown took the mines back in 1645. Almagro kept the Fuggers' stone warehouses and built its corral de comedias in the seventeenth century, a courtyard theatre for Golden Age plays; the conquistador Diego de Almagro is traditionally said to have been born there, and the town served as provincial capital from 1750 to 1761. Cervantes set Don Quixote's adventures among La Mancha's windmills in 1605 and 1615, and Charles III founded Spain's first mining school at Almadén in 1777. French troops took Ciudad Real in 1809 and Almadén in 1810.
zh:
拉曼查是卡斯蒂利亚南部干燥的高原，瓜迪亚纳河流贯其间，北界托莱多山，南接莫雷纳山，乡野间是粮田、牧道和风车。再征服运动之后，这里的城镇和牧场主要封给圣地亚哥和卡拉特拉瓦两个骑士团；卡拉特拉瓦的首领把治所设在阿尔马格罗，阿方索十世1273年还在那里召开议会。1255年，阿方索十世在骑士团领地之中建起王室直辖的皇家镇，1420年该镇民兵在内战中支持胡安二世，国王升其为城市，改名雷阿尔城。骑士团在阿尔马登的矿山出产辰砂和水银。1444年，雷阿尔城还是一座被阿尔马格罗盖过锋芒的小王领城镇，高原靠谷物和绵羊为生。

1474年后的继承危机中，比列纳的帕切科家族和两个骑士团支持胡安娜·贝尔特拉内哈和她的葡萄牙丈夫，直到1479年《阿尔卡索瓦斯条约》确认伊莎贝尔与费尔南多获胜。雷阿尔城为这个朝代贡献的人物是1451年出生于此的埃尔南·佩雷斯·德尔·普尔加，绰号「建功者」：他是格拉纳达战争中的卡斯蒂利亚队长，1490年率十五名骑士夜入格拉纳达，把写有「万福玛利亚」的告示钉在大清真寺门上，又放火烧了丝绸市场，才杀出城去，退回圣菲的王军大营。公社起义失败后，包括阿尔马登在内的骑士团地产于1523年并入王室，租给富格尔家族经营；阿尔马登的水银经塞维利亚运往美洲银矿，供混汞法炼银之用，1566年起苦役犯被送进有毒的矿坑，1645年矿山收归王室。阿尔马格罗留有富格尔家族的石砌仓库，17世纪又建起喜剧剧场，演出黄金世纪的戏剧；相传征服者迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗就出生在这座镇子，1750年至1761年它还做过省会。塞万提斯在1605年和1615年的《堂吉诃德》里，把主人公的冒险放在拉曼查的风车之间；1777年，卡洛斯三世在阿尔马登创办西班牙第一所矿业学院。1809年法军攻占雷阿尔城，1810年阿尔马登失守。

en:
Soria sits high on the upper Douro, on the pasture country where the kingdoms of Castile, Aragon and Navarre met. Alfonso I of Aragon, the Battler, conquered and resettled it between 1109 and 1114, and it passed to Castile in 1134. Kings kept coming back: Alfonso VIII was born here in 1155, and in 1257 the offer of the crown of the Holy Roman Empire reached Alfonso X at his court here. In 1375 the deposed James IV of Majorca died and was buried here, and that same year the future John I of Castile married Eleanor of Aragon in the same church. Its fueros put the town in the hands of twelve noble lineages, the Doce Linajes, who grew rich on wool: Soria stood at the head of several royal drovers' roads, and after the Mesta was created in 1273 it organised the summer shearing of the transhumant flocks and sent the clip through Burgos to the northern ports. Its Jewish quarter, about a thousand strong in the census of 1290, handled much of the trade. In 1369 Henry II gave the town to Bertrand du Guesclin in payment for his mercenaries, and the Frenchman's troops had to storm it. In 1444 Soria was a wealthy wool town ruled by its noble lineages, though the frontier wars that fed it were already over.

The union of Castile and Aragon in 1479 stripped Soria of its border trade, and the expulsion of the Jews in 1492 dispersed its merchant houses. The town remained a lordship of royal princes until 1539, then shrank into a quiet provincial capital of Romanesque churches and Renaissance palaces: the Hospitallers' San Juan de Duero keeps a thirteenth-century cloister mixing several styles, and Santo Domingo a carved doorway with a rare image of the Trinity. In 1808 the city raised a Numantine Volunteers battalion; on 22 November Marshal Ney's troops occupied Soria and sacked it for three days. His 20,000 men lingered while the Battle of Tudela was fought nearby, and Castaños and his army slipped out of the trap.
zh:
索里亚雄踞杜罗河上游的高原牧场，正当卡斯蒂利亚、阿拉贡与纳瓦拉三国交界处。1109年至1114年间，阿拉贡国王阿方索一世（斗士）攻占并重新移民此地，1134年并入卡斯蒂利亚。君主们一次次回到这里：1155年阿方索八世出生于此；1257年，神圣罗马帝国帝位的推举送达在此驻跸的阿方索十世；1375年，被废黜的马略卡国王海梅四世客死并安葬于此，同年，未来的卡斯蒂利亚国王胡安一世也在当地的教堂迎娶阿拉贡的莱昂诺尔。索里亚的特许状把市政交给十二支贵族世家（「十二族」），他们的财富来自羊毛：城市扼守数条皇家牧道的起点，1273年梅斯塔荣誉会成立后，由它组织转场羊群的夏季剪毛，再把羊毛经布尔戈斯运往北方各港。本地犹太社区在1290年普查中约有千人，承担了其中大部分贸易。1369年卡斯蒂利亚内战中，恩里克二世把索里亚送给贝特朗·杜·盖克兰以抵雇佣兵的军饷，这位法国统帅的部队只得强攻入城。1444年的索里亚是一座由贵族世家治理的富庶羊毛城镇，只是养肥它的边境战争已成往事。

1479年卡斯蒂利亚与阿拉贡合一，索里亚失去了边镇之利；1492年驱逐犹太人，又散去了它的商人家族。城市作为王族封邑一直保留到1539年，之后缩成一座安静的省会，城中多的是罗曼式教堂和文艺复兴式宫邸：医院骑士团的圣胡安·德·杜埃罗修道院保留着一座13世纪回廊，混用了好几种风格；圣多明我教堂的雕花门楣上则有一幅罕见的三位一体圣像。1808年，城市组建努曼西亚志愿营起兵抗法；11月22日，内伊元帅的部队进占索里亚，在城中盘踞三日、大肆劫掠。他的两万人马在索里亚逗留不去，附近正进行图德拉战役，卡斯塔尼奥斯的军队反倒因此逃出了包围圈。

en:
The highlands of Welayta fill the broken country between the Bilate and the Omo, where the rains turn the valleys into marsh and the mountain woods run with coffee. Its Omotic-speaking people, the Wolayta, were ruled by kings bearing the title kawo, in a kingdom whose own traditions reach back to about 1251 and which some scholars identify with the medieval kingdom of Damot of the remembered Kawo Motolomi. More than fifty kings across four dynasties are said to have reigned, and in 1444 the Malla kawo still held court beyond the reach of both Christian Ethiopia and the Muslim lords of the lowlands, his people keeping their old rites among coffee forests and cattle pastures.

The wars of Ahmad Gragn reached even these marshes in the sixteenth century, when Adal's men for a time occupied the country, until its waterlogged roads drove them out, as the Adal chronicler Arab Faqih himself admitted. Far more lasting were the Oromo migrations, which stripped away the kingdom's subject lands and in the upheaval replaced the Malla dynasty with the Tigre Malla line; in the seventeenth century Kawo Gazenja struck back and won a string of victories over Oromo raiders. The Wolayta kept their crown and their old beliefs in their mountains.
zh:
瓦莱提（瓦莱塔）高地占据着比拉特河与奥莫河之间的破碎地带，雨水把谷地泡成沼泽，山林间遍布咖啡。当地的瓦莱塔人说奥莫语族语言，统治者号称「卡沃」。按本国传统，瓦莱塔王国始建于约1251年，一些学者认为它就是中世纪的达莫特王国，传说中的卡沃·莫托洛米即其君主。据说四个王朝的五十多位君王相继在位；1444年，马拉王朝的卡沃仍在这片山乡发号施令，基督教的埃塞俄比亚和低地的穆斯林领主都鞭长莫及，族人在咖啡林与牧场之间守着旧有仪轨。

16世纪，艾哈迈德·格兰的战火甚至烧进了这片沼泽，阿达尔军队一度占领此地，但正如阿达尔编年史家阿拉伯·法基赫所承认的，泥泞难行的水乡最终迫使他们撤走。影响更深远的是奥罗莫人的迁徙：王国的属地大片沦丧，动荡之中马拉王朝被蒂格雷·马拉一系取代。17世纪，卡沃·加曾贾挥军反击，对奥罗莫袭掠者连获大胜。瓦莱塔人的王冠与旧信仰在这片群山中延续下来。

en:
Kaffa lies on the wet, forested southern flank of the Ethiopian Highlands. The Gojeb River bounds it to the north and the Omo to the east; near Anderaccha the Guma flows into the Gichey. Oral tradition dates the kingdom to about 1390, when Minjo replaced the earlier Mato dynasty; Bonga became the first royal center. In 1444 the sacred king, the tato, ruled the Kefficho people from these mountain forests. Hunters, leatherworkers and blacksmiths held distinct hereditary duties, while Muslim traders and Ethiopian Christians lived in the kingdom before it became a Christian state. The fertile highland valleys could yield three harvests a year, and the shade forests were an early home of Coffea arabica.

During the sixteenth century Emperor Sarsa Dengel's influence persuaded Kaffa's court to accept Christianity as the state religion, and the church of St George at Baha preserved a tabot bearing his name; the faith largely faded in later centuries. Under Gali Ginocho, who reigned from 1675 to 1710, Kaffa began a long expansion and annexed the Gimira lands of She, Benesho and Majango. Mecha Oromo invasions in the eighteenth century cost it all territory north of the Gojeb, but the forested mountain core held. Tato Shagi Sherocho, ruling from 1775 to 1795, brought Welayta and Konta under control and pushed the frontier to the Omo and Denchya rivers. Hoti Gaocho, ruler from 1798 to 1821, carried Kaffa's power to its greatest extent.
zh:
咖法（亦译卡法）在埃塞俄比亚高原南部湿润多林的山坡上，北以戈杰布河为界，东接奥莫河；安德拉恰附近，古马河汇入吉切河。口述传统把王国的开端定在约1390年，明乔取代更早的马托王朝，本加成为最早的王都。1444年，具有宗教权威、称「塔托」的国王在这些山地森林中治理卡菲乔人。猎户、皮匠和铁匠各有世袭职分，穆斯林商人和埃塞俄比亚基督徒也住在王国境内，尽管基督教要到后来才成为国教。肥沃的高地谷地一年可三熟，遮阴林则是阿拉比卡咖啡树的原生地之一。

16世纪，在埃塞俄比亚皇帝萨尔·登格尔的影响下，咖法宫廷接受基督教为国教，巴哈的圣乔治教堂保存着刻有他名字的塔博特；但这种信仰在以后几个世纪里又大致衰落。1675年至1710年在位的加利·吉诺乔开启长期扩张，吞并谢、贝内绍和马扬戈等吉米拉人的土地。18世纪梅查·奥罗莫人入侵，咖法丢失戈杰布河以北的全部属地，却守住密林山地核心。塔托·沙吉·谢罗乔1775年至1795年在位时控制瓦莱提和孔塔，把边界推到奥莫河与登奇亚河。1798年至1821年在位的霍蒂·高乔则把咖法的势力带到最大范围。

en:
Illubabor lies in the forested western Ethiopian highlands, where the headwaters of the Baro flow west towards the Nile. To the east, in the Gibe region, lay the Gonga kingdom of Ennarea. After separating from Damot in the fourteenth century, it became the strongest power in the non-Muslim south, drawing tribute from Kaffa and Bosa and sending gold, slaves and cattle to the Ethiopian emperors; a song for Yeshaq I records that tribute by the early fifteenth century. In 1444 the Hinnario court of Ennarea was tied to the Christian empire to the north but ruled through its own institutions.

The Borana Oromo conquered much of Gibe between 1578 and 1586 and formed the Sadacha federation. After they took Ennarea in 1588, Emperor Sarsa Dengel campaigned south of the Nile and brought Christianity to its elite. A Sadacha attack in 1594 cost Ennarea the land between the main Gibe and Gibe Ennarea. In the mid-seventeenth century a Kaffa royal clan seized power and Kaffa, with Sheka, broke away. Emperor Iyasu I reached Ennarea in 1704 during a civil war, but around 1710 the Sadacha overthrew Shisafotchi. He led survivors south across the Gojeb into Kaffa, where an exile kingdom was subdued by Kaffa in the early nineteenth century. Oromo settlers then turned from pastoralism to agriculture, and five kingdoms, including Limmu-Ennarea, took shape in the old Ennarean lands.
zh:
伊路巴博位于埃塞俄比亚西部林木茂密的高地，巴罗河源流从这里向西流往尼罗河。东面的吉贝地区有贡加人的伊那瑞亚王国。14世纪脱离达莫特后，它成为南方非穆斯林诸邦中最强的政权，迫使咖法和博萨纳贡，又把黄金、奴隶和牛只送往埃塞俄比亚皇帝那里；一首为耶沙克一世而作的歌在15世纪初已记载这种贡赋。1444年，伊那瑞亚的辛纳里奥宫廷同北方基督教帝国联系密切，却依照自身制度治理。

1578年至1586年，博尔纳奥罗莫人征服吉贝大部，并组成萨达查联盟。1588年他们夺取伊那瑞亚后，埃塞俄比亚皇帝萨尔·登格尔进兵青尼罗河以南，把基督教带到当地精英中间。1594年萨达查再度来攻，伊那瑞亚失去吉贝干流与吉贝·伊那瑞亚之间的土地。17世纪中叶，咖法王室夺取政权，咖法和谢卡相继独立。1704年，伊亚苏一世在一场内战中抵达伊那瑞亚，但约1710年萨达查人推翻希萨福奇。他率残部南越戈杰布河进入咖法，这个流亡王国在19世纪初被咖法征服并沦为其附庸。奥罗莫定居者随后从游牧转向农耕，旧伊那瑞亚土地上形成五个王国，利穆-伊那瑞亚便是其中之一。

en: Gambela is the hot riverine lowland between the Openo-Baro and Akobo, where streams from the Ethiopian Highlands descend toward the Upper Nile. Between the twelfth and fifteenth centuries the ancestors of the Anuak, a Luo Nilotic people, moved south and east from the Gezira between the Blue and White Niles and settled as farmers and herdsmen along the Baro and Gilo. In 1444 their scattered river villages held the country, a frontier that highland Ethiopian rulers knew chiefly as a source of slaves rather than a directly taxed province. For the rest of the period it remained a slave-raiding borderland.
zh: 甘贝拉是奥佩诺-巴罗河与阿科博河之间炎热的河畔低地，埃塞俄比亚高地的河川由此流向尼罗上游。12至15世纪，阿努亚克人的祖先——属于尼罗特卢奥人群——从青尼罗河与白尼罗河之间的杰济拉向南、向东迁徙，在巴罗河与吉洛河沿岸定居，亦农亦牧。1444年，正是他们分散的河畔村落据有这片土地；高地埃塞俄比亚政权主要把这里视为掠取奴隶的边疆，而非直接征税的省份。此后直到本时期结束，低地仍是掠奴边界。

en:
Hadiya is the fertile, well-watered plateau south of Shewa, its ridges around the highland heart of Angacha given over to grain fields, orchards and horse pastures above the Rift Valley lakes. Its people, Muslim like the lords of Zeila and Adal, were the Cushitic Hadiyya, Halaba and Kebena, with the Semitic-speaking Silte among them, and their ruler bore the title garad. The Arab geographer al-Umari in the fourteenth century already praised its cereals, fruit and herds and its strange iron currency, and reckoned it could raise forty thousand horsemen; since the bloody campaign of Amda Seyon against King Amano the Ethiopian emperors had held it as a tributary. In 1444 the country smarted from a fresh chastening: the Emperor Zara Yaqob had deposed the tribute-refusing Garad Mahiko in favour of his uncle Bamo, and Mahiko, slain in flight to Adal, had his head and limbs sent back to the imperial camp. The Hadiya princess Eleni, baptized and married to the emperor, would one day hold the regency itself; Badlay of Adal's attempt to avenge all this ended in his death at Gomit in 1445.

Hadiya was still a quiet, densely wooded tributary paying cattle to Lebna Dengel when the Portuguese priest Francisco Álvares passed through in the 1520s. When Ahmad Gragn invaded, its Muslim governor opened the country without a fight and marched at his side. In 1569 the Emperor Sarsa Dengel crushed the revolt of Garad Aze at the Battle of Hadiya, and before the century ended the Oromo had overrun the eastern marches, where the Arsi would in time claim Hadiya forebears. Early in the seventeenth century Garad Sidi Muhammad routed the troops of Emperor Susenyos, and Hadiya kept its independence behind its forests: the Portuguese Fernandez was briefly detained and turned back in 1613, and as late as 1751 the Czech traveller Remedius Prutky could still describe an independent Muslim kingdom south of Abyssinia, marching with the western border of Adal.
zh:
哈迪亚是绍阿以南肥沃湿润的高原，昂加查一带的高地丘陵上，谷田、果园和马场连成一片，俯瞰东非大裂谷的湖群。居民与泽伊拉、阿达尔的统治者同为穆斯林，包括说库希特语的哈迪亚人、哈拉巴人、克贝纳人，以及说闪米特语的西尔提人，君主号称「加拉德」。14世纪的阿拉伯地理学家欧麦里已盛赞此地五谷丰登、果木成林、牲畜成群，以铁片为通货，并估计其能出骑兵四万；自从阿姆达·塞约恩讨平国王阿马诺的抵抗、血洗其国之后，埃塞俄比亚皇帝便把它收为藩属。1444年，哈迪亚刚挨过新的惩戒：拒纳贡赋的加拉德·马希科被皇帝扎拉·雅各布废黜，改立其叔巴莫，马希科逃奔阿达尔途中被杀，首级和四肢被送回皇帝大营；被带入宫廷、受洗并嫁给皇帝的哈迪亚公主埃莱尼，日后还将亲掌摄政权。阿达尔苏丹巴德莱兴兵复仇，于1445年在戈米特兵败身亡。

16世纪20年代，葡萄牙神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯路过时，哈迪亚仍是一片林木茂密、向勒布纳·丹格尔皇帝贡纳牲畜的安静藩地。艾哈迈德·格兰入侵时，当地穆斯林长官不战而开放国境，并随军出征。1569年，萨尔萨·登格尔皇帝在哈迪亚战役镇压了加拉德·阿泽的叛乱；到该世纪末，奥罗莫人已席卷其东部边地，后来的阿尔西奥罗莫人便自称有哈迪亚人的血统。17世纪初，加拉德·西迪·穆罕默德击溃苏森约斯皇帝的军队，哈迪亚凭密林保住了独立：1613年葡萄牙人费尔南德斯被短暂扣留后遣返；迟至1751年，捷克旅人雷梅迪乌斯·普鲁特基仍能记述，在阿比西尼亚以南、与阿达尔西境接壤处存在着这样一个独立的穆斯林王国。

en:
The Arsi country is the chain of fertile highlands southeast of Shewa, between the Awash basin and the lakes of the Rift Valley. Before the sixteenth century it belonged, with neighbouring Dawaro, to the Muslim principality of Hadiya, whose Cushitic farmers kept great herds of horses and cattle and traded iron and highland produce through the Zeila union under a ruler called the garad. Restive under Christian overlordship, the Hadiya garad Mahiko refused tribute to Zara Yaqob, fled to Adal and was killed in the pursuit, while the emperor married a Hadiya princess, Eleni. In 1444 Arsi was still Hadiya country, Muslim and tributary, in the shadow of the wars between Adal and Abyssinia.

In the 1530s Ahmad Gran's army was welcomed in Hadiya as it marched against the Christian empire, and the land supplied the imam's campaigns. After Gran's overthrow the great Oromo expansion reached these highlands: by the end of the sixteenth century the Arsi clans had occupied the country and given it their name, absorbing or displacing the older Hadiya communities. Hadiya chiefs nevertheless defeated an army of the emperor Susenyos in the early 1600s and kept their frontier independent for centuries, and a Hadiya kingdom south of Abyssinia was still reported in 1751. The Arsi lived under their own elders and customs, pasturing cattle on the heights above Assela and sending coffee and other highland goods through the markets of Harar; no outside power subdued them before the nineteenth century.
zh:
阿尔西是绍阿东南方一串肥沃高地，夹在阿瓦什河流域与裂谷湖群之间。16世纪以前，这里与邻近的达瓦罗同属穆斯林小邦哈迪亚；操库希特语的农人牧养大群马匹和牛只，在称「加拉德」的首领治下通过泽拉联盟贩卖铁器和高地物产。哈迪亚加拉德马赫科不甘基督教宗主的统治，拒绝向扎拉·雅各布纳贡，逃奔阿达尔后在追兵手中丧命，皇帝则迎娶了哈迪亚公主埃莱妮。1444年的阿尔西仍是哈迪亚之地，居民信奉伊斯兰教、称臣纳贡，处在阿达尔与阿比西尼亚战争的阴影之下。

1530年代，艾哈迈德·格兰的军队进攻基督教帝国时在哈迪亚受到欢迎，当地为伊玛目的征战供给粮草。格兰败亡后，奥罗莫人大扩张波及这片高地：到16世纪末，阿尔西部落已占据此地并以自己的名字称呼它，同化或逐走了早先的哈迪亚居民。不过哈迪亚诸首领在17世纪初击败苏塞尼奥斯皇帝的军队，使这条边疆独立了数百年之久；迟至1751年，仍有记载称阿比西尼亚以南存在一个哈迪亚王国。阿尔西人在自己的长老和习俗下生活，在阿塞拉上方的高地牧场放牧牛群，把咖啡等高地货产经哈勒尔市集外销，直到19世纪都没有外来势力征服他们。

en:
South of the Blue Nile and west of Shewa stretch the fertile highlands of Damot, the country that would later be called Welega. Its people once spoke Omotic languages and kept a pagan kingdom of their own, until tradition brought the monk Tekle Haymanot to convert its ruler and the armies of Emperor Amda Seyon I annexed the land in 1316–17. Damot became a valued province of the Ethiopian realm: its gold was carried east to the markets of Zeila, Muslim merchants prized its slaves, and its spearmen and archers marched in the emperor's wars against Ifat and Adal. In 1444 Christian lords governed these highlands on the empire's remote south-western march, whose wealth was still measured in gold dust and cattle.

The Portuguese priest Francisco Álvares, visiting in the early sixteenth century, found Damot a large and plentiful land. In 1531 the armies of Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim of Adal overran it and installed Gasa Umar as governor; after the imam's death in 1543, Emperor Gelawdewos eventually restored imperial rule over the province. Sarsa Dengel later campaigned there and led Damot warriors against the Oromo at Waj in 1572, but the Oromo tide could not be held: under the luba Birmaje, between 1578 and 1586, the Boran Oromo surrounded the province, enslaving people and carrying off herds, while the Macha occupied it. Numbers of Christians fled across the Blue Nile, taking the name Damot to the Gojjam side, while the Macha settled the vacated highlands and their growing markets became the first towns of a new Welega.
zh:
青尼罗河以南、绍阿以西，横亘着达莫特的肥沃高地，即后来的沃莱加。当地居民原说奥莫语族语言，保有自己的异教王国；相传僧侣特克莱·海马诺特使其统治者皈依基督教，阿姆达·锡安一世皇帝的大军又于1316至1317年吞并此地。达莫特由此成为埃塞俄比亚的重要省份：黄金东运至泽拉的市集，奴隶深受穆斯林商人看重，当地的长矛兵和弓箭手则随皇帝出征伊法特与阿达尔。1444年，基督教诸侯统治着帝国西南边陲的这片高地，财富仍以砂金和牲畜计算。

16世纪初葡萄牙神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯到访时，见达莫特地域辽阔、物产丰足。1531年，阿达尔伊玛目艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣的大军攻陷此地，任命加萨·奥马尔为总督；伊玛目1543年战死后，格拉德沃斯皇帝最终恢复了对该省的统治。萨尔萨·登格尔后来多次到此巡战，1572年率达莫特士兵在瓦季迎击奥罗莫人，但迁徙大潮已无法阻挡：1578至1586年的比尔马杰轮值期，博兰部奥罗莫人包围全省，掳人为奴、夺取牲畜，马查人则占据此地。大批基督徒北渡青尼罗河，把达莫特之名带到戈贾姆一侧；马查人则在空出的高地上定居，日益繁荣的市集成为新沃莱加最早的城镇。

en:
West of Damot the highlands of Asosa break into forested ravines that plunge towards the White Nile basin. This is the country later called Benishangul, home to the Gumuz and other Nilo-Saharan peoples whom the Christian highlanders knew as the Shanqella and had raided for slaves since the days of Aksum; gold panned from the mountain streams was the land's other treasure. In 1444 it marked the furthest edge of Damot's reach, a borderland valued for gold dust and for the slave caravans led away by Sudanese merchants. After the founding of the sultanate of Sennar in 1504, it lay as a buffer between that Muslim state on the Nile and the Christian provinces of the Ethiopian plateau.

During the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the Berta, kinsmen of the Funj of Sennar, drifted in from the Sudan and built their villages on craggy hills to guard against slave raiders. The Emperor Susenyos led an army through the country in 1617–18, but highland rule did not hold, and in 1685 the land passed to the Funj sultanate of Sennar. From the middle of the eighteenth century Oromo groups began to filter in as Funj power ebbed, settling and mingling among the Shangul villages. When the Ottoman Egyptian armies overthrew Sennar in 1821, this ravined borderland was left in the hands of its own small hill chiefdoms.
zh:
达莫特以西，阿索萨的高地裂作林木密布的深谷，一路俯向白尼罗河盆地。这便是后来所称的本尚古勒，住着古穆兹等尼罗-撒哈拉语族群；高原上的基督徒称他们为香克拉，自阿克苏姆时代起便到此掳掠奴隶，而山溪中淘出的黄金是此地的另一宗财富。1444年，它处在达莫特势力所及的最西缘，领主们看重的是砂金，以及由苏丹商人成队贩走的奴隶。1504年森纳尔苏丹国建立后，这里成为尼罗河上这一穆斯林国家与埃塞俄比亚高原基督教行省之间的缓冲地带。

16至17世纪，与森纳尔丰吉人同源的贝尔塔人从苏丹陆续迁入，为防备掠奴者，把村舍建在峭峻的山丘上。1617至1618年，苏塞尼奥斯皇帝曾率军深入此地，但高原的统治未能维持，1685年这片土地转归森纳尔的丰吉苏丹国。18世纪中叶起，随着丰吉势力衰退，奥罗莫群体开始渗入，在尚古勒人的村落间定居杂处。1821年奥斯曼埃及的军队攻灭森纳尔时，这片沟壑纵横的边地已落入本地众多小山酋之手。

en:
Aussa is the inland delta of the Awash, whose waters lose themselves in the sands and salt lakes of the northern Afar country; its perennial pastures and gardens make the oasis a meeting ground for Afar camel-herders and caravans plying between Zeila, Harar and the Ethiopian highlands. Older Harla and Doba peoples had long mingled with the Afar here. In the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries the oasis formed the western march of the Muslim Adal sultanate, and in 1444 its clans marched with Sultan Badlay in the jihad that the Emperor Zara Yaqob broke at Gomit the following year.

In 1577, after Oromo invasions and a terrible famine had undone Harar, Imam Muhammad Gasa moved Adal's capital to the Aussa oasis, near Asaita. The amirs of Harar broke away in 1647, and the imamate, worn down by raiding, was overthrown by the local Mudaito Afar in 1672. In 1734 the Mudaito leader Data Kadafo made himself sultan and founded the dynasty that ruled Aussa into modern times; he was followed by his son and grandson, whose long reigns gave the caravan roads peace. In the last decade of the century the Debne-Wemas Afar marched on the capital with hundreds of Yemeni matchlockmen hired at Aden, slew Sultan Yusuf ibn Idjahis and sacked the town. Aussa never quite recovered its political weight, but its fair remained a perpetual market thronged with Afar and Somali caravans.
zh:
奥萨（阿法尔语称阿乌萨）是阿瓦什河的内陆三角洲，河水最终消失在阿法尔北部的沙地与盐湖之间。绿洲上常年有牧草和园地，是阿法尔驼队往来于泽伊拉、哈拉尔与埃塞俄比亚高原之间的会集之地，更早的哈拉人和多巴人也早已与当地阿法尔人融合。14、15世纪时，这片绿洲是穆斯林阿达尔苏丹国的西部边地；1444年，这里的部族随苏丹巴德莱参加对埃塞俄比亚的圣战，次年这支大军被皇帝扎拉·雅各布击败于戈米特。

1577年，在奥罗莫人入侵和大饥荒摧毁哈拉尔之后，伊玛目穆罕默德·加萨把阿达尔都城迁到奥萨绿洲，在阿萨伊塔一带立足。1647年，哈拉尔的埃米尔们分立；此后伊玛目国在各路袭扰中日渐衰弱，1672年被当地的穆代托阿法尔人攻灭。1734年，穆代托首领达塔·卡达福自立为苏丹，建立了一直延续到近代的王朝，其子其孙相继在位，长久的统治护佑了商路安宁。18世纪最后十年，德布内-韦马斯阿法尔人带着数百名在亚丁雇来的也门火绳枪手进攻都城，苏丹优素福·伊本·伊德贾希斯兵败被杀，城镇遭到洗劫。奥萨的政治分量再未完全恢复，但它的集市始终是阿法尔人与索马里人驼队长年往来的常设市场。

en: Assab is a wide, sheltered bay on the arid Danakil coast, just north of the Bab-el-Mandeb; Hellenistic sailors knew a trading post nearby as Arsinoe Epidires. In 1444 it formed the remote southern edge of the Adal sultanate's coast, far from its emirs and off the caravan routes that carried slaves and ivory westward to Zeila and Tadjoura. After the Ottomans seized Massawa in 1557 their Habesh province ended well to the north, and the bay remained in the hands of local Afar chiefs.
zh: 阿萨布是干旱的达纳基尔海岸上一处宽阔避风的海湾，就在曼德海峡以北不远处。希腊化时代的水手知道附近有个叫阿尔西诺伊·埃皮迪雷斯的商站。1444年，这里是阿达尔苏丹国海岸遥远的南端，远离它的埃米尔，也不在把奴隶和象牙输往泽伊拉、塔朱拉的商路上。1557年奥斯曼人夺取马萨瓦后，其哈贝什行省的管辖仅止于北面很远的海岸，阿萨布湾始终留在当地阿法尔酋长手中。

en:
The grain country around Mendefera is the historic Seraye highland, southernmost of the Christian plateau districts bound together in Medri Bahri. It had been part of the Aksumite world since antiquity: a cemetery in the area held second-century-BCE burials, pottery, and bronze bracelets, and later finds included crosses and Roman coins. In the fourteenth century followers of Ewostatewos founded Debre Mariam, which grew into an important monastery and school linked to Aksum. Under Zara Yaqob, the Bahr Negash at Debarwa was raised above the chiefs of Hamasien and Seraye, and the emperor confirmed the monastery's lands. In 1444 Mendefera's fertile plateau therefore stood on Medri Bahri's southern road, where Tigrinya-speaking Orthodox villagers, monks, and traders looked toward both Aksum and Massawa.

Seraye was swept into the Ethiopian-Adal war in 1535. After Imam Ahmad's men occupied the district, a local lord, Tasfa Le'ul, killed the Adal general Addole and sent his head to the emperor; Ahmad led a punitive campaign, forced the population to submit and appointed new administrators, though plague and famine later helped force his troops out. The Ottoman seizure of Massawa in 1557 turned the road through Seraye into a contested military corridor, and Bahr Negash Yeshaq was killed fighting with the Turks against Sarsa Dengel at Addi Qarro in 1578. During the seventeenth century local rule settled into hereditary highland families, above all the house of Hab Sellus. As imperial power faded in the eighteenth century, rival chiefs divided Seraye and the surrounding Medri Bahri lands.
zh:
门德费拉周围的谷物之乡，是历史上的瑟拉耶高地，也是梅德里·巴赫里诸基督教高原区域中最靠南的一处。此地早自古代便属于阿克苏姆世界：当地一处墓地有公元前2世纪的墓葬、陶器和铜镯，后世还出土过十字架与罗马钱币。14世纪，埃沃斯塔特沃斯的追随者建立德布雷·马利亚姆修道院，使它发展成与阿克苏姆相连的重要修院和学府。扎拉·雅各布在位时，驻德巴尔瓦的总督地位提高，统辖哈马西恩与瑟拉耶的首领，皇帝还确认了修院地产。因此在1444年，门德费拉的肥沃高原正位于梅德里·巴赫里的南道上，操提格雷尼亚语的正教村民、修士和商人同时通往阿克苏姆与马萨瓦。

1535年，瑟拉耶被卷入埃塞俄比亚—阿达尔战争。伊玛目艾哈迈德的军队占领此地后，本地首领特斯法·莱乌勒杀死阿达尔将领阿多勒，把他的首级送给皇帝；艾哈迈德随后发动惩罚性进军，迫使当地居民服从并另派官员，不过瘟疫和饥荒后来也迫使他的军队撤出。1557年奥斯曼人夺取马萨瓦后，穿过瑟拉耶的道路成为反复争夺的军事走廊。1578年，总督伊沙克与奥斯曼人联手对抗萨尔萨·丹格尔，战死于阿迪卡罗。17世纪，地方统治逐渐落入世袭高原家族之手，其中最显赫的是哈布·塞卢斯家族。18世纪帝国权威衰退，敌对首领分割了瑟拉耶和周围的梅德里·巴赫里土地。

en:
Enderta lies on the eastern edge of the Tigray highlands, where its historic seat Antalo, also called Hintalo, occupied a plateau beneath Amba Aradam and became a natural mountain fortress. Hereditary chiefs had ruled the district after the Solomonic restoration, but their bid for independence brought Emperor Amda Seyon north in the 1320s; in 1328 his son Bahr Seged also received the maritime lands. By the fifteenth century Enderta appeared on indigenous maps of the northern Horn. Its governor held the title bäalgada and organized salt caravans linking the Danakil and Afar flats with the highlands. In 1444, under Zara Yaqob, Antalo's cliffs thus guarded a Tigrinya Orthodox province of the Ethiopian empire, living from highland grain, livestock, and taxed desert salt.

Enderta entered the Adal wars early: Ras Robel, its lord and salt-district governor, was serving as governor of Tigray when he was killed fighting Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi's army at Sambera Kware on 7 March 1529. Antalo first appears in a written account in 1648, when a Yemeni ambassador described it as a fortified town; in 1678 Lasta chiefs marching to join a southern Tigray revolt were defeated nearby, and men of Hintalo were driven over the precipices. The Enderta noble Mikael Sehul became Ras of Tigray and regent at Gondar, and on 7 May 1769 his men killed Emperor Iyoas, opening the Era of Princes. After Mikael's defeat at Sarbakusa in May 1771, Enderta's governor Kefla Iyasus challenged him for Tigray and was killed. Kefla's son Wolde Selassie, born at Antalo in 1736, became Ras in 1790, kept Hintalo as his capital, sheltered Emperor Tekle Giyorgis in 1799 and 1800, and received Henry Salt there in 1805 to discuss British friendship and trade. He remained the dominant Christian warlord of northern Ethiopia until his death on 28 May 1816.
zh:
恩德塔位于提格雷高原东缘，其历史首府安塔洛又称欣塔洛，坐落在安巴·阿拉达姆山南的台地上，是天然的山寨要塞。所罗门王朝复兴后，这里长期由世袭首领统辖；14世纪20年代，他们谋求独立，安达·塞永一世因而北上压制，1328年又令其子巴赫里·塞格德兼管滨海地区。到15世纪，恩德塔已出现在非洲之角北部的本土地图上。当地总督拥有「巴阿尔加达」头衔，负责组织往来达纳基尔与阿法尔低地的盐队。1444年，在扎拉·雅各布皇帝治下，安塔洛的崖壁守护着埃塞俄比亚帝国这个操提格雷尼亚语的正教省份，居民依靠高原谷物、牲畜和向沙漠盐路征税为生。

恩德塔很早便被卷入阿达尔战争：其首领、盐区总督罗贝尔担任提格雷长官期间，于1529年3月7日在桑贝拉夸雷与艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的军队作战身亡。1648年，安塔洛首次见于文字记载，一名也门使节称它为设防城镇。1678年，拉斯塔首领准备会合南提格雷的叛军，在附近被击败，欣塔洛人被赶下悬崖。出身恩德塔贵族的米卡埃尔·塞胡尔成为提格雷总督和贡德尔朝廷摄政，1769年5月7日，他的部下杀死伊约阿斯皇帝，开启「王侯时代」。1771年5月米卡埃尔在萨尔巴库萨战败后，恩德塔总督凯夫莱·伊亚苏斯试图争夺提格雷，兵败被杀。凯夫莱之子沃尔德·塞拉西1736年生于安塔洛，1790年成为拉斯，仍以欣塔洛为都城；他在1799年和1800年庇护特克勒·乔治斯一世，1805年又在此会见亨利·索尔特，商谈与英国的友好和贸易。直到1816年5月28日去世前，他始终是埃塞俄比亚北部最有权势的基督教军阀。

en:
Angot, whose name means 'the Neck', is the ribbon of broken highland country running south from Lake Ashenge along the rim of the Ethiopian plateau, where the mountains fall away into the Muslim Afar lowlands. It was always a borderland: Christianity had been preached here in the last age of Aksum, and medieval emperors kept churches and garrisons above the escarpment, while the Dobe'a pastoralists of Doba grazed great herds below and traded with the Adal coast. Their chief market was Manadeley, on the highland edge overlooking the desert. In 1444 Angot obeyed the Christian Emperor Zara Yaqob, but many of its people were Muslim, and its caravans and kinship tied the province to Adal.

Early in his reign the Emperor Baeda Maryam (1468–1478) harried the Dobe'a for years until they submitted, accepted Christianity and turned to farming; he built a church of the Virgin and planted vines and orange groves in their country. When Francisco Álvares visited Manadeley in the 1520s he found a market 'like a city or seaport', thronged with merchants from Jeddah, Cairo, Tunis, Fez, Ormus and India. The Ethiopian–Adal war swept this away: Angot was overrun and governed for Adal by Ali Ankarsah, and on 29 August 1542 Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi stormed the Portuguese stockade at Wofla on the shore of Lake Ashenge and put Cristóvão da Gama to death. After the war the Yejju, converts of the imam, settled Angot under their sheikh Umar, while Raya and Wollo Oromo pressed in from the later sixteenth century. From this mixed frontier rose the Yejju Warra Sheik, Oromo ras lords who dominated the Gondar court during the age of the princes; in the early nineteenth century the mightiest of them, Ras Gugsa of Yejju, held the puppet emperors in his hand.
zh:
安戈意为「脖颈」，是从阿申盖湖向南、沿埃塞俄比亚高原边沿延伸的一条破碎高地，再往下便是穆斯林阿法尔人的低地。这里自古是边界之地：阿克苏姆末期基督教已传入，中世纪的皇帝们在崖畔建堂驻军，崖下多巴地区的多贝阿牧人放牧着大群牲畜，与阿达尔海岸通商，他们最大的市场是坐落在高原边缘、俯瞰荒漠的马纳德莱。1444年，安戈臣属于基督教皇帝扎拉·雅各布，但居民中穆斯林众多，商路和亲族都把这方边地与阿达尔连在一起。

巴埃达·马里亚姆皇帝（1468—1478年在位）即位之初连年征讨多贝阿人，最终迫使其归降、皈依基督教并转为农耕；他在当地建起圣母教堂，还种下葡萄和橙子。1520年代，弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯到访马纳德莱，看到这里的集市「如同城市或海港」，挤满了来自吉达、开罗、突尼斯、非斯、霍尔木兹和印度的商人。埃塞俄比亚—阿达尔战争把这一切击碎：安戈被攻占，由阿达尔方面的阿里·安卡尔萨管辖；1542年8月29日，艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐攻破阿申盖湖畔沃夫拉的葡萄牙人营寨，将克里斯托旺·达伽马处死。战后，被这位伊玛目改宗的耶朱人在谢赫·奥马尔率领下定居安戈，拉亚和沃洛的奥罗莫人也从16世纪后期起不断涌入。正是在这片混杂的边地上，耶朱人的「谢赫家族」瓦拉·谢赫崛起，在王子纷争时代以奥罗莫「拉斯」的身份掌控贡德尔宫廷，其中权势最盛的拉斯·古格萨在19世纪初挟制傀儡皇帝。

en:
Lasta is the mountain fastness of the Agaw, set between Wag and Bete Amhara. The Zagwe dynasty kept its court at Roha after losing Aksum and ruled Ethiopia from there between about 1150 and 1270; King Lalibela, who reigned around 1181–1221, gave his capital its eleven churches cut from the living rock, laid out like a second Jerusalem after the city in Palestine had fallen to the Muslims, and after his death Roha bore his name. Yekuno Amlak's restoration of the Solomonic line in 1270 ended Zagwe rule, but the dynasty's heirs stayed in Lasta and Wag, holding the title of Wagshum and claiming Israelite descent, and still commanded respect. In 1444, under Zara Yaqob, Lasta was an ancient Christian province governed through these Zagwe lords, and its rock churches already drew pilgrims.

In the 1520s the Portuguese Francisco Álvares visited Lalibela twice and despaired of making Europe believe the churches he had seen. Between July and September 1531 the soldiers of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi wasted the district, and the Adal chronicle claims he burned one of the rock churches; yet Portuguese who came after him found the churches had defied crowbars and even gunpowder. Lasta's proudest hour came under Susenyos: from 1629 the Agaw of the Emekina mountains rose under Melka Krestos for the old Orthodox faith, defeated the emperor's armies and forced him to abandon Catholicism in 1632. The revolt outlived him — at Libo in 1637 the rebels routed Fasilides and Melka Krestos briefly seized the throne before he was killed, and in 1638 another imperial army perished in the Lasta cold. Later Gondarine emperors campaigned there for generations, for Lasta and Wag kept resisting imperial control through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries; in the 1750s a European traveller still counted Lasta among the six provinces of Ethiopia truly deserving the name of kingdom.
zh:
拉斯塔是阿高人的险峻山地，夹在瓦格与贝特阿姆哈拉之间。扎格维王朝失去阿克苏姆后以罗哈为廷，约1150至1270年间在此统治埃塞俄比亚；拉利贝拉王（约1181—1221年在位）在都城凿出十一座整岩教堂，在耶路撒冷落入穆斯林之手后按第二座耶路撒冷的形制布局，罗哈在他死后也改以他的名字为名。1270年耶库诺·阿姆拉克恢复所罗门王朝，扎格维的统治告终，但其后裔留在拉斯塔和瓦格，保有「瓦格舒姆」头衔和以色列后裔的血统宣称，仍受朝野敬重。1444年扎拉·雅各布在位时，拉斯塔是由这些扎格维领主治理的古老基督教省份，岩凿教堂已吸引着八方朝圣者。

1520年代，葡萄牙人弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯两度到访拉利贝拉，说自己无论怎样描述这些教堂，欧洲人都不会相信。1531年7月至9月，艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的军队蹂躏此地，阿达尔编年史称他焚毁了一座岩教堂，可后来的葡萄牙人发现，这些教堂在撬棍甚至火药之下都安然无恙。拉斯塔最有声色的一页在苏西约斯时代：1629年起，埃梅基纳山区的阿高人在梅尔卡·克里斯托斯率领下为捍卫旧正教起事，屡败皇军，最终迫使皇帝在1632年放弃天主教。叛乱比皇帝更长寿——1637年叛军在利博击溃法西里德斯，梅尔卡·克里斯托斯一度登上皇位，随即被杀；1638年又一支皇军葬身于拉斯塔的严寒。此后贡德尔历代皇帝一再兴兵，而拉斯塔与瓦格在17、18世纪始终抗拒朝廷；1750年代到访的欧洲旅人仍把拉斯塔列为埃塞俄比亚六个真正配称王国的省份之一。

en:
Agawmeder, the 'Land of the Agaw', fills the rolling country between Gojjam, Lake Tana and the Sudanese lowlands, where the town of Dangila would later stand. The Agaw, a Cushitic people already named in Aksumite inscriptions of the fourth century, count among the oldest inhabitants of the Ethiopian highlands, and from their stock came the Zagwe dynasty that ruled the country until 1270, Lalibela among its kings. Under the restored Solomonic line their western lands became a frontier province: long since Christian, the Agaw kept their own tongue, grew grain on the high plateaux and pastured large herds, while slaves and gold brought up from the western lowlands changed hands at their markets. In 1444 Agaw lords held the western marches for the emperor, a country the court knew as a granary and a gateway towards the Muslim lands on the Nile.

The wars of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi reached the Agaw with Gojjam's fall after the Battle of Zari in 1531, and Adal raiders harried the province for the rest of the war. From the later sixteenth century Oromo war-bands pressed on the southern flank and crossed the Blue Nile, and the frontier knew no long peace. Susenyos passed through Dangila in 1620 while making his power felt along the west from Fazogli to Suakin, but his turn to Catholicism brought civil war, and his reign ended in revolt and abdication in 1632, when his son Fasilides restored the old faith. Order returned under the Gondarine kings: after putting down the pretender Yeshaq in 1685, Iyasu I marched the following year beyond southern Gojjam against the Agaw who had backed him, and in 1688 campaigned by way of Metekel into the Shanqella country, burning Gisa and taking captives at Gorsi; in 1704 he settled the Christianized Gawe Oromo along the north bank of the Abbay as a bulwark. Agawmeder was never a strong polity of its own, and the lords of Gojjam gradually absorbed it.
zh:
奥格（阿高默德尔）意为「阿高人之地」，位于戈贾姆、塔纳湖与苏丹低地之间的起伏地带，丹吉拉后来便兴起于此。阿高人属库希特语族，4世纪的阿克苏姆铭文中已有记载，是埃塞俄比亚高原最古老的居民之一；统治埃塞俄比亚直至1270年的扎格维王朝——拉利贝拉即在其列王之中——便出自阿高人。所罗门王朝复辟后，阿高人的西部土地成为帝国的边疆行省：居民早已信奉基督教，仍保留本族语言，在高原台地上种植谷物、牧放大群牲畜，西部低地贩来的奴隶和黄金也在此地市集转手。1444年，阿高诸侯为皇帝扼守西陲，宫廷视此地为粮仓，也是通向尼罗河畔穆斯林诸地的门户。

格兰的战火随着1531年扎里战役后戈贾姆陷落而蔓延到阿高，阿达尔骑兵在战争剩余的年月里连年蹂躏此地。16世纪后期起，奥罗莫武装从南境压来、渡过青尼罗河，边疆再无长久太平。1620年，苏塞尼奥斯在西巡、将兵威伸展于法祖格利到萨瓦金一线的途中经过丹吉拉；但他改宗天主教引发内战，统治于1632年在叛乱与退位中终结，其子法西利德斯随即恢复古老信仰。贡德尔林诸帝重建了秩序：1685年伊亚苏一世平定僭称者叶沙克，次年便进军戈贾姆以南，惩讨支持叛乱的阿高人；1688年他取道梅特克尔攻入香克拉人之地，焚毁吉萨，并在戈尔西掳走居民；1704年又将已改宗基督教的加韦部奥罗莫人安置在青尼罗河北岸，充作藩屏。奥格从未形成强有力的政权，后来被戈贾姆诸侯逐步吞并。

en:
Semien is a wall of tablelands and pinnacles north of Lake Tana, rising to Ras Dashen and cut by the Tekezé. A sixth-century record of an Aksumite inscription called its snowy peaks inaccessible and the mountains a place of exile. The high valleys later sheltered Beta Israel villages whose people followed Haymanot Judaism, farmed cold plots, and worked as weavers and smiths. In 1329 Amda Seyon campaigned in Semien, Wegera, Tselemt, and Tsegede, and Emperor Yeshaq's conquest of Semien and Dembiya between 1414 and 1429 broke the power of Jewish governors; his settlement tied inherited land to baptism. Thus in 1444, under Zara Yaqob, the Ethiopian crown claimed the province, but many Beta Israel kept their faith in fortified villages above Christian estates and the Dabareq pass.

In 1445 Zara Yaqob married Seyon Moges, daughter of the Beta Israel leader Gideon V. After a highland revolt in 1462 she was executed for alleged espionage and Jewish leaders imprisoned; from 1465 to 1472 General Markos's campaigns demolished synagogues, built churches, and forced baptism. During the Adal war they first joined Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi, then after Dawit II's death supported Gelawdewos. Sarsa Dengel later turned captured Ottoman cannon against Semien strongholds and put the leader Gershom to death. A 1614 revolt against Susenyos was crushed by 1625, ending Beta Israel autonomy; lands were seized and Judaism forbidden. In 1629 Susenyos made his son Fasilides governor with the title Aggafari. After Fasilides became emperor in 1632 and expelled the Jesuits, Jewish craftsmen served near Gondar, while Semien passed to royal princes: Yostos held it until 1676, followed by Iyasu I and their sister Eleni. Dabareq first appears in records as a late-seventeenth-century supply stop on Iyasu's northern campaigns. James Bruce passed its high market in 1770, and Ras Gebre ruled the mountain province from Amba Hay from 1771 until 1815. In 1814 Henry Salt mapped Dabareq and noted Semien wool carpets.
zh:
塞米恩是塔纳湖北侧一列台地与尖峰，耸立着拉斯达山，并被特克泽河切开。6世纪记录下来的一份阿克苏姆铭文称这里的雪峰难以接近，还把群山当作流放之地。后来，高山河谷庇护了许多贝塔以色列村落；居民奉行哈伊马诺特犹太教，在寒冷高地上耕作，并以织布和打铁闻名。1329年，安达·塞永一世征讨塞米恩、韦格拉、策莱姆特和策格德；1414年至1429年间，伊沙克皇帝征服塞米恩与登比亚，瓦解犹太首领的权力，并把土地继承权与受洗绑定。因此在1444年扎拉·雅各布在位时，埃塞俄比亚皇权已声称领有此地，但许多贝塔以色列人仍在设防山村中保持信仰，俯视低处的基督教地产和德巴尔格山口。

1445年，扎拉·雅各布娶贝塔以色列首领吉迪恩五世之女锡永·莫格斯为妻。1462年高地爆发叛乱后，她被控通敌而处死，许多犹太首领被囚禁；1465年至1472年，马科斯将军的征讨拆毁会堂、改建教堂并强迫受洗。阿达尔战争期间，他们起初投奔艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐，达维特二世死后又转而支持格拉德沃斯皇帝。萨尔萨·丹格尔后来把缴获的奥斯曼火炮用于塞米恩山寨，并处死首领革顺。1614年反苏斯尼约斯的起义到1625年被镇压，贝塔以色列的政治自治终结，土地被没收，犹太教也遭禁止。1629年，苏斯尼约斯封其子法西利德斯为塞米恩总督，称阿加法里。法西利德斯1632年继位并驱逐耶稣会士后，犹太工匠到贡德尔附近服役，塞米恩则成为皇族亲王的封邑：约斯托斯治理到1676年，其后由伊亚苏一世和他们的姐妹埃莱尼相继管辖。德巴尔格最早见于17世纪后期记载，是伊亚苏北征途中的补给站。1770年，詹姆斯·布鲁斯经过这里的高山市场；1771年至1815年，拉斯·格布雷以安巴海为要塞统治这个山地省份。1814年，亨利·索尔特把德巴尔格绘入地图，并记载了塞米恩的羊毛地毯。

en:
Dembiya is the low-lying country on the northern shore of Lake Tana, where the warm Foggora plain rises from the reed-fringed water towards the Begemder and Wogera heights; the lake itself was once called Dembea. Amhara farmers shared it with Beta Israel villages, the Falasha whose communities stretched from here towards Semien, and its dark soil grew cotton and grain for the lake markets, with the island monastery of Gelila Zakarias standing just offshore. In 1444, under Zara Yaqob, Dembiya was a settled province of the Christian empire, its peasant villages and Falasha hamlets living together under the emperor's peace.

The jihad of Ahmad Gran reached the lake: on 19 March 1537 his men burned the monastery of Gelila Zakarias, and on 21 February 1543 the emperor Galawdewos and his Portuguese allies killed Gran at Wayna Daga on the Dembiya lake shore and routed the Adalite army. Half a century later the province became the unlikely centre of a Catholic experiment. In 1607 Susenyos granted the Jesuits land at Gorgora, where Pedro Páez built a stone church between 1618 and 1621 and a royal palace rose beside it; Susenyos declared for Rome, and perhaps 100,000 people of Dembiya and Wegera are said to have accepted the Roman rite. Orthodox revolt forced his abdication in 1632, and his son Fasilides expelled the Jesuits, abandoned Gorgora, moved the court inland to found Gondar in 1636, and in 1665 ordered the Catholic 'books of the Franks' burned. During the Era of the Princes the dejazmachs of Dembiya held the lake plain and took tribute from Muslim Galabat on the Sudan road.
zh:
德姆比亚是塔纳湖北岸的低地，温暖的福格拉平原从芦苇丛生的湖边向北抬升到贝格姆德尔和沃格拉高地；塔纳湖本身旧名就叫德姆贝亚。阿姆哈拉农民与贝塔以色列人（法拉沙人）的村落共处，后者的社群从这一带一直延伸到瑟门；肥沃的黑土种植棉花和谷物供应湖畔集市，格利拉·扎卡利亚斯岛修道院就矗立在近岸水面上。1444年扎拉·雅各布在位时，德姆比亚是基督教帝国治下安居一省，农夫的村庄与法拉沙人的村落在皇帝的和平中相邻而居。

格兰的圣战很快波及湖区：1537年3月19日，他的部下焚毁格利拉·扎卡利亚斯修道院；1543年2月21日，皇帝格拉德沃斯与葡萄牙盟友在德姆比亚湖畔的韦伊纳达加击杀格兰，阿达尔大军就此崩溃。半个世纪后，这个省份意外成为一场天主教实验的中心：1607年苏西约斯把戈尔戈拉的土地赐给耶稣会士，佩德罗·佩斯1618至1621年在此建成石砌教堂，旁边又修起王宫；苏西约斯宣布皈依罗马，据说德姆比亚和沃格拉有十万人随之改奉罗马礼。正统教派的叛乱最终迫使他在1632年退位，其子法西里德斯驱逐耶稣会士、弃置戈尔戈拉，1636年把宫廷迁往内陆、兴建贡德尔，又在1665年下令焚毁「法兰克人的经书」。王子时代里，德姆比亚的德贾兹马奇们据守湖原，并向通往苏丹道上的穆斯林城镇加拉巴特收取贡赋。

en:
Mora is the dry belt between the Harar plateau and the Gulf of Tadjoura, a country of granite hills, dry riverbeds and wells where Issa and other Somali clans pastured their camels, and where caravans coming down from Harar with coffee, ivory and slaves made their first camps on the Zeila road. Such settlements as Ali Adde grew under Ifat and Adal rule, and in 1444 the whole arid border belonged to the sultan of Adal, its wells mustering the Somali lancers who filled his armies.

The emir Usman routed the raiding columns of the Emperor Baeda Maryam on this frontier in the 1470s, and for a generation the emir Mahfuz of Zeila launched his raids through these lowlands into Christian country, until Lebna Dengel's ambush destroyed his army in Fatagar and left Mahfuz dead. The sultan Abu Bakr moved his capital from Dakkar to Harar in 1520, and Ahmad Gragn rode this same road on his conquest of Abyssinia. After the long war and the Oromo incursions of the mid-sixteenth century the Adal court withdrew to Aussa in 1577; the camel clans stayed by their wells, and the Zeila road carried its coffee and ivory as before.
zh:
莫拉是哈勒尔高原与塔朱拉湾之间的干旱地带，花岗岩丘陵、干涸河床和水井散布其间；伊萨等索马里氏族在此放牧骆驼，从哈勒尔驮着咖啡、象牙和奴隶前往泽伊拉的商队，出城后第一批营地就扎在这里。阿里阿德等聚落便是在伊法特和阿达尔治下发展起来的。1444年，整条干旱边地都归阿达尔苏丹所有，各水井处集结着他军队中的索马里骑兵。

15世纪70年代，埃米尔乌斯曼在这道边境击溃了巴德·玛利亚姆皇帝的讨伐纵队；此后一代人时间里，泽伊拉的埃米尔马赫福兹不断经这些低地袭掠基督教地区，最终勒布纳·丹格尔在法塔加尔设伏歼灭其军，马赫福兹本人战死。1520年，苏丹阿布·贝克尔把都城从达卡尔迁往哈勒尔，艾哈迈德·格兰后来正是沿这条道路出征阿比西尼亚。长年大战和16世纪中叶奥罗莫人的涌入之后，阿达尔宫廷于1577年迁往奥萨；骆驼氏族仍守着各自的水井，泽伊拉商路上的咖啡与象牙也照旧往来。

en:
At the mouth of the Jubba River the Somali coast breaks into a chain of low islands and reefs running south toward Pate. Somali herders watered their stock at the wells of the hinterland, while on the islands lived Bajuni fishermen, Swahili-speaking Muslims in coral hamlets who sailed the sea lanes in lateen-rigged beden boats, taking shark and trading dried fish up and down the coast. Both answered to the Ajuran sultans of the House of Garen, whose engineers dammed the Jubba and Shabelle and ringed the country with stone wells, making theirs the only hydraulic empire in Africa. River plantations sent grain and fruit through Barawa and Mogadishu to Arabia and India. In 1444 the fishing anchorage that would become Kismayo was a quiet southern outpost of that wealthy state.

Early in the sixteenth century a Portuguese fleet under Tristão da Cunha stormed and burned nearby Barawa, yet could not hold the town and dared not attack Mogadishu; in the 1580s the coastal cities joined the Ottoman corsair Mir Ali Bey, a Somali fleet sailing with him to seize Pate, Mombasa and Kilwa before a Portuguese armada retook them. In the mid-1600s the Garen sultans fought long campaigns, the Gaal Madow wars, against Oromo pressing down to the coast, converting those they captured to Islam. The empire grew oppressive as it weakened, and at the century's end a former general, Ibrahim Adeer, overthrew its local vassals and founded the Geledi state of the Gobroon dynasty, which by 1821, under Sultan Mahamud Ibrahim, held the Jubba mouth and its fishing islands.
zh:
朱巴河河口一带的索马里海岸散落着一长串低矮岛屿与礁群，向南一直延伸到帕泰。内陆，索马里牧人依托水井放牧畜群；岛上住着巴琼尼渔民，他们是讲斯瓦希里语的穆斯林，聚居在珊瑚石小村，驾驶挂斜桁帆的「贝登」船往来海上，捕捞鲨鱼、沿海南北贩卖鱼干。两者都臣服于加伦家族的阿朱兰苏丹：其工匠在朱巴河与谢贝利河上筑坝修堰、在各地开凿石井，阿朱兰也由此成为非洲唯一的水利帝国。河畔农庄出产的谷物和果实，经巴拉韦与摩加迪沙销往阿拉伯和印度。1444年，后来发展为基斯马尤的那处渔港，还是这个富庶国家南端一处宁静的据点。

16世纪初，特里斯唐·达·库尼亚率葡萄牙舰队猛攻并焚毁了邻近的巴拉韦，却无力久占，更不敢进犯摩加迪沙；1580年代，沿岸各城响应奥斯曼私掠首领米尔·阿里·贝伊，一支索马里舰队与他联手夺取帕泰、蒙巴萨和基尔瓦，直到葡萄牙大舰队反攻夺回。17世纪中叶，加伦王朝对南下压迫海岸的奥罗莫人连年用兵，史称「加尔·马多战争」，被俘虏者尽数改宗伊斯兰教。帝国在衰弱中渐趋苛暴，世纪之末，出身将领的易卜拉欣·阿代尔推翻其地方封臣，建立格布龙家族的格勒迪国家；到1821年马赫穆德·易卜拉欣苏丹在位时，朱巴河口与这片渔岛都已在格勒迪治下。

en:
Merca is an old roadstead on the Banaadir coast, southwest of Mogadishu. The first-century Periplus of the Erythraean Sea already knew a trading emporium here, Essina. By the twelfth century al-Idrisi placed the Hawiye along this shore, and Ibn Sa'id called Merca their capital, ranking it with Mogadishu and Barawa as one of the three chief Muslim cities of the East African coast. In the fifteenth century it was an administrative centre of the Ajuran Sultanate, governed by the sultan's naa'ibs, to whom local tradition credits the pillar tombs around the town. The Ming treasure fleets counted the port, recorded as Molugan, among their African calls, and it was also the birthplace of the saint Sheikh Hussein, who carried Islam into Bale. In 1444 Merca was a prosperous Ajuran haven, shipping the produce of the Shabelle lowlands to Arabia.

Tristão da Cunha's Portuguese burned Barawa in 1507, and later fleets bombarded Mogadishu, but Merca itself was never stormed, and its merchants kept the Indian Ocean trade. As Ajuran power crumbled at the end of the seventeenth century, a warlord called Amir seized Merca and expelled its Ajuran lords; his following, the El Amir, ruled for thirty-four years until the Bimaal drove them out in their turn. The Bimaal made the town their stronghold and kept it independent even after the Geledi Sultanate arose inland at Afgooye.
zh:
马尔卡是贝纳迪尔海岸一座古老的锚地港口，位于摩加迪沙西南。公元1世纪的《厄立特里亚海航行记》已记载这一带有商埠埃西纳。12世纪时，伊德里西记述哈维耶人居住在这片海岸；伊本·赛义德更称马尔卡为哈维耶人的都会，把它与摩加迪沙、巴拉韦并列为东非海岸三座最重要的穆斯林城市。15世纪时，它是阿朱兰苏丹国的行政中心之一，由苏丹的总督纳伊卜治理，当地传说把城外的柱墓归于他们所建。明代郑和船队也曾抵达此港，将其记作「木鲁旰」；这里还是圣徒谢赫·侯赛因的出生地，他后来把伊斯兰教传入巴莱。1444年的马尔卡是阿朱兰治下一座殷实港口，把谢贝利河下游的物产运往阿拉伯。

1507年，特里斯唐·达·库尼亚麾下的葡萄牙人焚毁巴拉韦，后来的舰队又炮轰摩加迪沙，但马尔卡本身始终未遭攻破，商人得以继续印度洋贸易。17世纪末阿朱兰国势瓦解，一个名叫埃米尔的首领率众夺取马尔卡，赶走了阿朱兰统治者；他的部众「埃米尔人」统治此地三十四年，最终又被比马尔人逐出。比马尔人以马尔卡为据点，即便盖莱迪苏丹国在后方的阿弗戈耶兴起之后，仍长期自主掌控这座港口。

en:
Afgooye stands on the lower Shebelle River, where roads from Mogadishu and the Benadir ports meet routes into the grain-growing interior. Its medieval core was Lama Jiidle, meaning 'two roads', the seat of the Silcis, who governed the district under Ajuran overlordship. Their officials took a daily measure of grain from Geledi households and dues from herdsmen watering stock at the river. In 1444 the riverine farms, camel caravans and subject clans around Lama Jiidle made it a useful administrative and tribute centre rather than a great stone city.

Late in the 17th century, after Ajuran power weakened, Ibrahim Adeer led the Geledi revolt against Silcis ruler Umar Abrone and founded the Gobroon dynasty. Afgooye, as the town came to be called, became the capital of the Geledi Sultanate. Gobroon authority reached across the country between the Shebelle and Jubba rivers and to parts of the Benadir coast, and its markets drew ivory, leopard skins and aloe from inland caravans in exchange for cloth, sugar, dates and firearms. By the early 19th century the walled town had five gates, mosques and palaces, with weavers, potters and jewellers serving the caravan trade.
zh:
阿夫戈耶（通行译名阿夫哥耶）坐落在谢贝利河下游，摩加迪沙和贝纳迪尔诸港通往内陆产粮区的道路在此交会。其中世纪核心是意为「两条路」的拉马吉德莱，希尔西斯人以此为中心，在阿朱兰宗主权下治理这片地区。他们的官吏向格勒迪各户逐日征收谷物，又向到河边饮水放牧的牧民收费。1444年时，河畔农田、骆驼商队和纳贡诸族使拉马吉德莱成为实用的行政与贡赋中心，而不是一座巨石筑成的大城。

17世纪末阿朱兰势力衰微，易卜拉欣·阿代尔率领格勒迪人起兵，推翻希尔西斯统治者奥马尔·阿夫罗内，建立戈布伦王朝。改称阿夫戈耶的城镇成为格勒迪苏丹国都城。戈布伦的势力跨越谢贝利河与朱巴河之间的土地，远及贝纳迪尔海岸的一部分；市场吸引内陆商队带来象牙、豹皮和芦荟，换走布匹、糖、椰枣和火器。到19世纪初，这座有城墙的城镇设有五座城门，拥有清真寺和宫殿，织工、陶匠与珠宝匠为商路贸易服务。

en:
Bardera stands on the Jubba where the river bends through high, fertile ground, its banks and farms thick with tall palms — hence its Somali name Baardheere, 'the tall palm'. In 1444 it was one of the foremost inland cities of the Ajuran Sultanate, Africa's hydraulic empire: Ajuran dams and wells commanded the Jubba, its granaries supplied the Benadir ports, and Ajuran roads carried its merchants down to Barawa and Mogadishu. Its madrasas made Bardera a seat of Islamic learning as well as a market for grain, ivory and cloth.

In the 1500s Portuguese fleets sacked the coastal cities and burned Barawa, but the Ajurans kept their hold on the river and Bardera's trade went on. At the end of the seventeenth century the Ajuran empire broke apart, and the Geledi sultans of the Gobroon dynasty inherited the Jubba; under them Bardera kept its citadel and became the chief ivory market of the southern Horn, linking interior caravans to the Benadir. In 1819 a local sheikh raised a puritanical revival, forbidding tobacco, folk dances, the ivory trade and the sight of unveiled women, and gathered a reformist community within the citadel whose fame outgrew the town before 1821.
zh:
巴尔代雷坐落在朱巴河穿过高腴之地的河段，河岸与农田长满高大的棕榈，索马里语名巴尔代雷（Baardheere）即「高棕榈」之意。1444年时，它是阿朱兰苏丹国——非洲的水利帝国——最重要的内陆城市之一：阿朱兰人的水坝和水井控制着朱巴河，这里的粮仓供给贝纳迪尔诸港，阿朱兰人修筑的道路把商人送往巴拉韦和摩加迪沙。城里的经学堂使巴尔代雷既是伊斯兰学术之地，也是谷物、象牙和布匹的集市。

16世纪，葡萄牙舰队洗劫沿海诸城，焚毁巴拉韦，但阿朱兰人守住了河道，巴尔代雷的贸易得以维持。17世纪末阿朱兰帝国瓦解，戈布伦家族的盖莱迪苏丹接管朱巴河流域；在其治下，巴尔代雷保留了城堡，成为非洲之角南部首要的象牙市场，把内陆商队与贝纳迪尔海岸连在一起。1819年，当地一位谢赫发起清教式复兴，禁止烟草、民间歌舞、象牙贸易和妇女不戴面纱露面，并在城堡内聚集起一个改革派社群，到1821年前其声势已超出这座城。

en:
Werder, in Somali Wardheer, is the well-country of the eastern Ogaden: the dry Doollo plain of red and white sand between the Haud and the grazing lands of the Darod clans. Its people in the 15th century were Sunni Somalis, above all the Marehan, who counted their wealth in camels and sheep and followed their own clan chiefs rather than any city sultan. Their wells made the district a node on the tracks between the upper Shebelle and the northern markets, and in 1444 the plains lay beyond the direct reach of the Adal court on the Harar plateau, a Somali pastoral country loosely bound to the Muslim world of the interior.

When Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi summoned the Somali clans to his jihad, the Marraihan, as the chronicler Arab Faqih calls the Marehan, answered under their chief Hirabu and fought in the conquest of Abyssinia. To the south the Ajuran Sultanate, whose power ran up the Shebelle to Qalafo, set the wider order of the interior until its decline in the 17th century. From that century onward the caravan trails across the Ogaden also carried slaves taken among the Arsi and other southern peoples toward Berbera and the Red Sea, together with the livestock and hides that remained the country's real wealth; no garrison sat over Wardheer's wells, which belonged to the clans that could hold them.
zh:
韦尔德（索马里语名Wardheer）是东欧加登的水井之地：处在豪德与达鲁德诸族牧地之间的多洛干旱平原，红白沙地之上河道常年干涸。15世纪时这里的居民是逊尼派索马里人，以马雷汉人为主，他们以骆驼和羊群计富，听从本族酋长，而非任何城里的苏丹。各处水井使这一地区成为上谢贝利河与北方市场之间商路的节点；1444年，驻在哈勒尔高原的阿达尔朝廷号令难及这片平原，它是一块索马里游牧之地，与内陆穆斯林世界只保持着松散的联系。

艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐号召索马里诸族参加圣战时，编年史家阿拉伯·法基赫笔下的「马拉伊汉」人——即马雷汉人——在酋长希拉布率领下起兵响应，参加了征服阿比西尼亚的战争。南面的阿朱兰苏丹国势力沿谢贝利河上溯至卡拉福，在17世纪衰落之前一直主导着内陆大局。也是从17世纪起，穿过欧加登的商路除了牲畜和兽皮这两宗本地真正的财富，还把掳自阿尔西等南方民族的奴隶运往柏培拉和红海；韦尔德的水井之上不设驻军，它们属于守得住水井的氏族。

en:
Afder, in Somali Afdheer, is the southern grazing country of the Ogaden, the semi-arid plains beyond the upper Ganale Dorya River, which here separates Somali rangeland from the Oromo country to the west. Darod Somali clans—the Ogaden and the Absame families—move camels and small stock between its wells, and in the 15th century these lands lay within the wide sphere of the Habr Maqdi, a Somali confederacy of the Bartire and Yabarre whose chieftains are remembered as holding the grazing grounds from the Bakool country as far as Afder between the 14th and 18th centuries. They were Sunnis, trading livestock toward Harar and the Shebelle valley, and in 1444 the plains formed the quiet southern wing of the Muslim frontier below the embattled provinces of Bale and Dawaro.

When Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi raised his jihad the Habr Maqdi answered with the largest of the Somali contingents. In the wars' wake Oromo migrants spread over the flat plains of Bale to the north, but the Afder grazing grounds stayed in Somali hands under the Maqdi chieftainship, which endured here into the 18th century. The Bartire kept up their long-standing tie with the emirs of Harar after the emirate broke away in 1647, and Harari caravans crossed Afder buying livestock, hides and ivory for the Red Sea markets.
zh:
阿夫德（索马里语名Afdheer）是欧加登南部的牧地，即加纳莱·多里亚河上游以外的半干旱平原；这条河在此把索马里牧场同西面的奥罗莫地区分开。达鲁德系索马里氏族——欧加登人和阿布萨梅诸部——赶着骆驼和小家畜往来于各处水井之间。15世纪时，这些土地处在哈卜尔·马克迪联盟的广阔势力范围内：它由巴尔蒂雷和亚巴雷两支索马里人组成，相传14至18世纪间，其酋长的辖地从巴科勒一直延伸到阿夫德的牧场。他们是逊尼派穆斯林，赶着牲畜同哈勒尔和谢贝利河谷贸易；1444年，在战事不断的巴勒和达瓦罗两省以南，这片平原构成穆斯林边疆平静的南翼。

艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐发动圣战时，哈卜尔·马克迪以索马里诸部中最大的一支兵力响应。战乱之后，奥罗莫移民散布到北面巴勒的平坦原野，阿夫德的牧场则始终在索马里人手中，马克迪酋长的势力在此延续到18世纪。1647年哈勒尔酋长国独立后，巴尔蒂雷人保持着他们与哈勒尔埃米尔之间由来已久的联系，哈勒尔商队穿过阿夫德收购牲畜、兽皮和象牙，运往红海市场。

en:
Beledweyne is the crossing of the middle Shebelle valley in Hiran, where the river divides the town and pastoral roads from the Ogaden meet caravan routes running south toward Mogadishu. In 1444 it lay within the Ajuran Sultanate, whose wells, river controls and tribute system bound Hawiye pastoralists to the riverine farms. Livestock, hides and access to water mattered more here than the trade of a coastal city.

As Ajuran rule weakened, the Darandoolle and other Hiraab clans challenged its governors. According to a regional tradition, the Ajuran forbade them to water their herds by day, and the Darandoolle killed an Ajuran imam at the well of Ceel Cawl. The Gaaljecel, Baadicade and Xawaadle united in the upper and middle Shebelle valley to drive the Ajuran out. By 1700 Hiraab power stretched from this riverine corridor toward Mudug and the Benadir coast, leaving the Beledweyne crossing to the pastoral clans and caravan traffic of the new order.
zh:
贝兰德文（通行译名贝莱德文）是希兰地区谢贝利河中游的渡口，河流将城镇分开，来自欧加登的牧道与南下摩加迪沙的商路在此相接。1444年，这里属于阿朱兰苏丹国；阿朱兰人的水井、河道控制和贡赋制度，把哈维耶游牧民与河畔农田联系在一起。此地的重要性在牲畜、兽皮和用水权，而不在海港城市那种贸易。

阿朱兰统治衰微后，达兰多莱和其他希拉布氏族起而对抗其总督。据当地传说，阿朱兰人禁止他们白天饮牲畜，达兰多莱人便在塞尔考勒井杀死了一名阿朱兰伊玛目。加勒杰勒、巴迪卡德和哈瓦德莱则在谢贝利河中上游联手驱逐阿朱兰人。到1700年，希拉布势力已从这条河谷走廊延伸到穆杜格和贝纳迪尔海岸，贝兰德文渡口也转入新秩序下的游牧氏族与商队交通之中。

en:
Gedo is the upper Jubba country around the Dawa confluence, with Luuq set in a horseshoe bend of the Ganane, as the upper Jubba is called here. Digil and Mirifle clans farmed and pastured stock along its rivers, while Luuq was already one of the older market settlements on the road from the Benadir coast into southern Ethiopia. In 1444 Ajuran governors kept those caravan roads open; Bender-Luuq merchants drew coffee, gold, slaves and ivory from the interior and sent goods onward toward Bardera and the coastal ports.

In the Geledi period, the Gasaaragude dynasty ruled the upper Jubba within the Geledi federation and made Luuq its military centre, where troops trained, weapons were made and prisoners were held. The town's merchants used weights, credit and written contracts, exchanging Benadir cotton cloth for cattle among Arsi and Borana Oromo, then trading the cattle to hunters for ivory. In 1811 Captain Thomas Smee reported a heavily fortified town with more than two thousand stone houses, mosques, roads, palaces and castles at its centre.
zh:
盖多是达瓦河汇流处一带的朱巴河上游地区，卢格坐落在当地所称加纳内河的马蹄形河弯中。迪吉尔与米里弗莱诸氏族沿河畔农耕牧畜，卢格则早已是贝纳迪尔海岸通往埃塞俄比亚南部道路上的古老集市之一。1444年，阿朱兰总督维持着这些商路畅通；本德尔-卢格商人从内陆取得咖啡、黄金、奴隶和象牙，再把货物运往巴尔代雷和沿海港口。

格勒迪时期，加萨拉古德王朝在格勒迪联盟内统治朱巴河上游，并以卢格为军事中心，军队在此训练、武器在此制造、囚犯也关押于此。城中商人使用度量衡、信贷和书面契约，把贝纳迪尔棉布卖给阿尔西与博兰纳的奥罗莫人换取牛只，再用牛向猎人交换象牙。1811年，托马斯·斯米船长报告称，这座设防坚固的城镇有两千多所石屋，并有清真寺、道路、宫殿和位于城中心的堡楼。

en:
Warsheikh is a coastal town about seventy kilometres north of Mogadishu. Somali tradition identifies it with Sarapion, the harbour listed in the first-century Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, though modern scholars place that ancient port somewhere between here and Mogadishu. By the later Middle Ages it was an early centre of Islam, trade and learning, and one of the chief towns of the Sultanate of Mogadishu, whose Fakhr al-Din dynasty minted its own coin and traded as far as Egypt, Arabia and China. Like the rest of the Banaadir, the town lay within the hegemony of the Ajuran Sultanate. In 1444, under the sultan in Mogadishu, Warsheikh lived by its anchorage and by the livestock driven down from its arid hinterland.

The Portuguese sacked the Swahili cities farther south and burned Barawa in 1507, but never forced themselves on Mogadishu and its ports, so Warsheikh kept its place in the city's Indian Ocean commerce. That order ended in the late seventeenth century, when Ajuran rule collapsed before the revolt of the Hiraab clans: the Yacquubi imams took Mogadishu, and Warsheikh passed to their new Hiraab Imamate, ruled locally by Abgaal chiefs.
zh:
瓦尔希赫是摩加迪沙以北约七十公里处的一座滨海城镇。索马里传统把它认作公元1世纪《厄立特里亚海航行记》所记的古港萨拉皮翁，但学者多把这座古港推定在瓦尔希赫与摩加迪沙之间一带。到中世纪后期，它已是伊斯兰教、商贸与学术的早期中心，也是摩加迪沙苏丹国的首要城镇之一；当时的法赫尔丁王朝自铸钱币，商路远达埃及、阿拉伯和中国。与贝纳迪尔其他地方一样，该镇处在阿朱兰苏丹国的霸权之下。1444年，瓦尔希赫归属摩加迪沙的苏丹，靠港湾贸易和干旱腹地赶来的牲畜为生。

葡萄牙人劫掠了更南方的斯瓦希里诸城，又于1507年焚毁巴拉韦，却始终未能染指摩加迪沙及其属港，瓦尔希赫因此得以保住它在摩加迪沙印度洋贸易中的位置。这一秩序在17世纪末终结：阿朱兰统治在希拉布诸部的反抗中崩溃，雅库比家族的伊玛目们夺取摩加迪沙，瓦尔希赫随之归入新建的希拉布伊玛目国，由当地的阿布加尔酋长治理。

en:
Hobyo is an ancient Somali anchorage on the arid Mudug coast, founded in the 13th century as a coastal outpost of the Ajuran Sultanate. Its market drew livestock and grain from the interior into the Indian Ocean coastal trade. At the height of Ajuran power the sultanate's reach ran from Hobyo in the north to Kismayo in the south, so in 1444 the Sunni Somali port was a northern gateway of a centralized Muslim state, watched over by nearby coastal settlements such as Mareeg.

In the late 17th century the Hiraab clans rose against Ajuran rule, heavy taxation and neglect of Islamic law feeding the revolt. By 1700 their imamate controlled a wide belt from the Shabelle valley through the dry lands of Mudug to the coast around Hobyo, and it remained independent in 1821. The hinterland supplied sorghum, beans, camels, cattle, sheep and goats; Hobyo exported livestock, hides, aromatic woods and raisins, took in rice, foodstuffs and clothing, and provisioned ships sailing down the Somali coast.
zh:
霍比奥是干旱的穆杜格海岸上一座古老的索马里锚地，13世纪作为阿朱兰苏丹国的沿海据点建立。内陆的牲畜和谷物汇集到这里的市场，再进入印度洋沿岸贸易。阿朱兰强盛时，势力北起霍比奥、南至基斯马尤；因此在1444年，这座逊尼派索马里港口是这个集权穆斯林国家的北方门户，与马雷格等邻近沿海聚落彼此呼应。

17世纪末，希拉布诸部起兵反抗阿朱兰统治，沉重赋税和统治者对伊斯兰教法的疏失推动了叛乱。到1700年，他们的教长国已控制从谢贝利河谷穿过穆杜格旱地、直达霍比奥附近海岸的广阔地带，至1821年仍保持独立。内陆供应高粱、豆类、骆驼、牛、绵羊和山羊；霍比奥输出牲畜、兽皮、香木和葡萄干，输入稻米、食品和布匹，也为沿索马里海岸南下的船只补给。

en:
Galkayo is a stretch of wells and grazing grounds in the arid Mudug plains, the border country where the Darod clans pressing from the north met the Hawiye of the south, both watering camels, sheep and cattle there in the dry season and feuding over wells in bad years. There was no town yet in 1444, but the land looked toward Hobyo on the coast, an ancient harbour which the Ajuran empire had founded as one of its northern outposts in the 13th century; Ajuran governors and Somali caravan traders drew the herds and hides of Mudug into the Indian Ocean commerce. The people were Sunni Muslims, and the sultanate's hold over these dry marches was loose, resting on kinship and trade rather than garrisons.

In the late 17th century the Hiraab, a Hawiye confederation, rose against the Ajuran and built their own imamate, which through the 18th century ruled from the Shabelle valley and the Benaadir coast up to the arid lands of Mudug. Hobyo prospered under the new order: it shipped out livestock, hides, aromatic woods and raisins, imported rice and clothes, and drew merchants seeking textiles, precious metals and pearls. It also provisioned vessels sailing down the coast to Mogadishu. Around Galkayo the change of dynasties mattered less than the old rivalry of Darod and Hawiye over pasture and water, which outlasted the imamate itself. As late as 1821 the place remained a nomads' rendezvous rather than a city.
zh:
加勒卡约是干旱的穆杜格平原上一片有水井和牧场的地方，北来的达鲁德氏族与南方的哈维耶人在此交界：旱季双方都到这里饮骆驼、羊和牛，年景坏时便为水井争斗。1444年时这里还没有城镇，但这片土地在经济上朝向海边的霍比奥——那是阿朱兰帝国13世纪建立的北方港口据点之一，阿朱兰的官吏和索马里商队把穆杜格的畜群和兽皮纳入印度洋贸易。当地居民都是逊尼派穆斯林，苏丹国对这片干旱边地的控制松散，靠的是姻亲关系和贸易而非驻军。

17世纪末，哈维耶人的希拉布联盟起兵推翻阿朱兰统治，建立自己的伊玛目政权，整个18世纪其治下从谢贝利河谷、贝纳迪尔海岸一直延伸到穆杜格的干旱地带。霍比奥在新秩序下繁荣起来：输出牲畜、兽皮、香木和葡萄干，输入大米和衣物，吸引商人前来购买纺织品、贵金属和珍珠，也为沿海岸南下摩加迪沙的船只补给给养。加勒卡约一带对王朝更迭感受不深，真正贯穿始终的是达鲁德与哈维耶之间争夺牧场和水源的旧怨，比伊玛目政权本身还要长久。直到1821年，这里仍是游牧者的会聚之地，而不是一座城市。

en:
El Buur, or Ceelbuur, lies in the dry inland heart of Galguduud, where tracks from Hiran, the Ogaden, Mudug and Warsheikh meet around wells and low hills. The Murusade branch of the Hawiye had settled there by at least the 13th century. In 1444 the town served the Ajuran Sultanate as a local commercial hub.

As Ajuran rule collapsed, the Habar Gidir and Duduble fought the Ajuran out of Galguduud and Mudug. By 1700 those lands lay within the Hiraab Imamate's inland arc, which stretched from the Shebelle valley through the arid country toward Mudug and the coast between Mogadishu and Hobyo. El Buur then remained a Murusade caravan market, linking pastoral herdsmen with the Benadir ports.
zh:
埃勒布尔（Ceelbuur）位于加勒古杜德干旱的内陆中心，希兰、欧加登、穆杜格和瓦尔谢赫方向的道路在水井与低丘间交会。哈维耶人的穆鲁萨德支系至迟在13世纪已定居于此。1444年，这座城镇是阿朱兰苏丹国的地方商业中心。

阿朱兰统治崩溃时，哈巴尔·吉迪尔人与杜杜布莱人经过苦战，把阿朱兰势力逐出加勒古杜德和穆杜格。到1700年，这些土地已纳入希拉布伊玛目国的内陆势力圈，其范围从谢贝利河谷穿过干旱地带，延伸至穆杜格以及摩加迪沙与霍比奥之间的海岸。此后埃勒布尔仍是穆鲁萨德人的商队集市，连接游牧牧民与贝纳迪尔诸港。

en:
Bosaso, historically Bender Qassim, lies on the Bari coast at the mouth of the Baalade valley. The author of the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea knew this shore as Mosylon, famed for its frankincense. The present anchorage takes its name from Qasim, a trader said to have settled here in the fourteenth century; his favourite camel was called Boosaas. The Kaptallah were its first settlers, and for centuries the Dishiishe and other Harti clans of the Darod family held the coast, shipping frankincense, dates, skins and livestock to Arabian ports. In 1444 it was a chain of small Muslim fishing and trading roads under its own clan elders, within the loose orbit of Adal.

In 1520 the ships of the Portuguese embassy to Abyssinia watered along this coast between Cape Guardafui and Mount Felis, buying goats and taking aboard white gum for caulking their hulls; Francisco Álvares found a sterile land where thick cloth served as money and a local ruler reigned subject to Adel. In the following centuries the Majeerteen, another Harti clan, built up a kingdom on the Guardafui peninsula: oral tradition places its first rulers in the late fifteenth or sixteenth century, and by the late eighteenth century it was a centralised sultanate with a strong seafaring tradition. Bender Qassim remained a Dishiishe harbour within that Harti maritime world, its dhows carrying the frankincense of the interior hills to Arabian and Indian ports.
zh:
