Chiloé is the large green island at the heart of a rainy archipelago, separated from the mainland by the Chacao Channel. The Piuchén and Pirulil highlands run through it, forests and swamps cover the wetter west, and calmer eastern and northern coves open onto the Sea of Chiloé. In 1444 Chono canoe parties hunted, fished and gathered shellfish, while Huilliche and Cunco communities grew potatoes, maize and beans and kept llamas. Their dalca boats linked coves and smaller islands. The later name Chiloé comes from Huilliche and means the place of the chelles gull; the island's life already belonged more to sea routes than to mainland chiefdoms.

Alonso de Camargo sighted the coast in 1540, Francisco de Ulloa entered the Chacao Channel and explored the islands in 1553, and García Hurtado de Mendoza claimed the archipelago for the Spanish Crown in 1558. Conquest began in 1567 with the foundation of Castro; the island was originally named New Galicia. In 1600 the Dutch corsair Baltazar de Cordes and local Huilliches captured Castro, but a Spanish counterattack forced him to withdraw northward. Jesuits reached the islands at the turn of the seventeenth century and built a circuit of chapels; seventy-nine stood there by their expulsion in 1767, and Franciscans took over the mission in 1771. A Huilliche revolt against Spanish encomenderos began in early February 1712 and was crushed within a week, leaving several hundred Huilliches and several dozen Spaniards dead. During the Spanish American wars of independence Chiloé remained a remote royalist enclave: a patriot expedition failed in 1820, and in 1821 the islands still remained under the Crown.
zh:
奇洛埃是这片多雨群岛中心的苍翠大岛，北隔查考海峡与大陆相望。皮乌琴和皮鲁利尔山地纵贯全岛，湿润西部遍布森林沼泽，东面与北面较平静的小湾朝向奇洛埃海。1444年，乔诺人的独木舟队伍在此狩猎、捕鱼、采集贝类，韦利切和昆科社群则种植马铃薯、玉米和菜豆，并饲养美洲驼。他们的「达尔卡」舟往来于各个海湾和小岛之间。后来的奇洛埃一名出自韦利切语，意为「切莱斯鸥之地」；这里的生活也更依赖海路，而非大陆上的酋邦。

阿隆索·德·卡马戈1540年望见海岸，弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚1553年进入查考海峡并巡弋群岛，加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨则于1558年为西班牙王冠宣布占有。1567年，卡斯特罗建立，征服由此展开；岛屿最初被命名为新加利西亚。1600年，荷兰私掠船长巴尔塔萨尔·德·科德斯与当地韦利切人攻占卡斯特罗，但西班牙军队随即反击，迫使他向北撤退。耶稣会士在17世纪初抵达群岛，沿巡回传教路线建立小堂；到1767年被驱逐时已有79座，方济各会士于1771年接掌传教事务。1712年2月初，韦利切人起兵反抗西班牙委托监护主，起义一周内便遭战斗与屠杀镇压，数百名韦利切人和数十名西班牙人死亡。西属美洲独立战争期间，奇洛埃仍是偏远的保王据点；1820年独立派远征失败，到1821年群岛仍在西班牙王权统治下。

en:
Aysén is the glacier-carved threshold of Chilean Patagonia. The Guaitecas and Chonos islands guard its rainy coast, channels run south toward the Taitao Peninsula and Ofqui Isthmus, and the Andes, icefields and eastern grasslands rise behind them. In 1444 the channels between about 44° and 48° south belonged to Chono groups. They moved by canoe, men fishing and hunting sea lions while women gathered seaweed and shellfish; they kept dogs, wove rough dog-hair cloth, and in places planted small potato crops. South of Taitao lived Kawésqar canoe people, later called Alacaluf by outsiders, while Aónik'enk or Tehuelche hunters followed game on the open mainland. No town or outside chiefdom controlled these crossings.

Magellan's passage through the strait in 1520 led Spanish geography to associate the broken coast with Trapananda and the Lands of December, but the first recorded encounter with the Chonos came on Francisco de Ulloa's voyage of 1553, which reached the archipelago and Taitao. Between 1557 and 1679 the Spanish launched twelve religious expeditions; Jesuits from Castro visited the Guaitecas in 1612 at a Chono leader's invitation, building chapels and preparing local assistants, while raids from Chiloé also carried canoe people into servitude. In 1710, 166 Chonos of all ages came to Calbuco seeking peace and baptism; later about 600 were gathered on Guar Island, where a Jesuit mission was formed in 1717, though timber-cutters and settled life led most back to nomadism. The wreck of HMS Wager in the Guayaneco Islands in 1741 drew new Spanish attention. Mateo Abraham Evrard went to Wager Island in 1743, and Ferdinand VI ordered Fort San Fernando de Tenquehuén on Taitao in 1749, only for the post to be dismantled. Authorities later emptied parts of the archipelago to deny corsairs native support, and in 1821 Aysén still had no permanent Spanish town, only seasonal sea-lion and sea-otter hunters and cypress cutters from Chiloé.
zh:
艾森是智利巴塔哥尼亚由冰川塑造的门户。瓜伊特卡斯群岛与乔诺斯群岛屏障般横亘在多雨海岸外，水道向南通向泰陶半岛和奥夫基地峡，后方则耸立着安第斯山、冰原与东部草原。1444年，南纬约44度至48度间的水道属于各个乔诺人群。他们乘独木舟不断迁徙，男子捕鱼、捕猎海狮，妇女采集海藻和贝类；他们养狗，用狗毛织成粗布，也会在一些地点粗放种植马铃薯。泰陶半岛以南是卡韦斯卡尔独木舟人群，后来被外人称作阿拉卡卢夫；开阔大陆上则有阿奥尼肯克人，即特维尔切猎人追逐草原猎物。没有任何城镇或外来酋邦控制这些水道。

麦哲伦1520年穿过海峡后，西班牙地理学把这片破碎海岸与「特拉帕南达」和「十二月之地」的名称联系起来，但首次有记录地接触乔诺人，是弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚1553年抵达乔诺斯群岛和泰陶半岛的航行。1557年至1679年间，西班牙人组织了十二次宗教探险；1612年，卡斯特罗的耶稣会士应一位乔诺首领邀请前往瓜伊特卡斯，修建小堂并培养本地助手，而来自奇洛埃的掳掠也把一些独木舟居民带入奴役。1710年，166名各年龄段的乔诺人来到卡尔布科，请求和平与受洗；后来约六百人被安置到瓜尔岛，耶稣会1717年在那里设立传教站，但伐木者侵扰和定居生活使多数人重新回到游牧生活。1741年，英国军舰「韦杰号」在瓜亚内科群岛失事，使西班牙重新关注此地。马特奥·亚伯拉罕·埃夫拉尔1743年前往韦格岛，费尔南多六世1749年下令在泰陶半岛修建圣费尔南多·德·滕克文堡，该据点后来却被拆除。西班牙当局随后清空部分群岛，使私掠船得不到当地人支援；1821年的艾森仍没有西班牙常设城镇，只有来自奇洛埃、季节性捕猎海狮与海獭并采伐柏树的营地。

en:
The Chubut rises in the eastern foothills of the Andes and winds east across dry Patagonian tablelands; its Tehuelche name, chupat, means transparent. In 1444 the shallow river, its floodable bottomlands and the nearby Río Chico were seasonal country for nomadic Tehuelche bands. They hunted guanaco and rhea, camped in skin tents and used the valley as a corridor between winter lowlands, summer uplands and the Atlantic coast.

Magellan's ships sighted this coast in 1520. On 24 February 1535 Simón de Alcazaba, Charles V's governor of Nueva León, founded Puerto de los Leones near Camarones. He then marched inland to the Río Chico, where Tehuelche guides led his men for ten days toward a rumoured gold city; the party found only desolate steppe. Alcazaba was killed in a mutiny in May. The mutineers left on 17 June, leaving exiles who survived there until the end of the year. Missionaries later crossed parts of Chubut, while horses and Mapuche trade reshaped Tehuelche life in the eighteenth century, but the river valley remained without a permanent Spanish town through 1821.
zh:
丘布特河发源于安第斯山东麓，蜿蜒向东穿过干旱的巴塔哥尼亚台地；特维尔切语称其为「丘帕特」，意思是透明。1444年，水浅的河道、会受洪水漫润的低地与邻近的奇科河，是特维尔切游牧群体的季节性天地。他们猎捕原驼和美洲鸵，在兽皮帐篷中扎营，把河谷当作冬季低地、夏季高地与大西洋海岸之间的通道。

1520年，麦哲伦的船队望见这片海岸。1535年2月24日，查理五世任命的新莱昂总督西蒙·德·阿尔卡萨瓦在卡马罗内斯附近建立莱昂港。随后他率军深入奇科河，特维尔切向导带他们走了十天，去寻找传说中的金城，却只见到荒凉草原。阿尔卡萨瓦在5月的哗变中被杀。哗变者于6月17日离开，留下的流放者存活至年底。后来传教士曾穿过丘布特部分地区，马匹和马普切贸易则在18世纪改变了特维尔切人的生活，但直到1821年，丘布特河谷仍没有永久性的西班牙城镇。

en:
Behind the harbours of Deseado and San Julián, stony canyons and semi-arid mesas rise from the Atlantic steppe toward the Chilean cordillera. In 1444 Teush was the country of the Teushen or Tehues, foot nomads placed between the Puelche to the north and the Aónikenk Tehuelche to the south. They lived by hunting guanaco and rhea, gathering seasonal foods and moving in small camps; their language was a close relative of Tehuelche.

Magellan's winter at San Julián in 1520 opened this coast to Europeans, but the interior remained beyond Spanish control. Thomas Cavendish named Port Desire in 1586 and met arrow resistance; Flores de León crossed the region in 1621 and Nicolás Mascardi in 1671–72, without founding lasting reductions. In 1780 Spanish colonists established Floridablanca near San Julián. The Aónikenk leader Julián Grande showed them a freshwater valley, and settlers exchanged goods for guanaco meat, but Charles III ordered the costly Patagonian establishments abandoned in 1783 and Floridablanca was dismantled in 1784. In 1821 the Teushen still held the inland hunting tracks.
zh:
德塞阿多港与圣胡利安港后方，石质峡谷和半干旱台地从大西洋草原向智利方向的安第斯山抬升。1444年，托伊施是特乌申人（又称特乌斯人）的土地；这些徒步游猎者北邻普埃尔切人，南接阿奥尼肯克特维尔切人。他们以猎捕原驼和美洲鸵、采集季节性食物为生，结成小型营地不断迁徙，所用语言与特维尔切语相近。

1520年麦哲伦在圣胡利安过冬，欧洲人由此认识这片海岸，但内陆仍不受西班牙控制。1586年，托马斯·卡文迪什将此地命名为德塞阿多港，并遭到弓箭抵抗；1621年弗洛雷斯·德·莱昂、1671至1672年尼古拉斯·马斯卡尔迪先后穿行这一地区，却未能建立持久的传教居留地。1780年，西班牙殖民者在圣胡利安附近建立佛罗里达布兰卡。特维尔切首领大胡利安为他们指出一处淡水谷地，殖民者也用货物交换原驼肉，但查理三世在1783年下令放弃耗费巨大的巴塔哥尼亚据点，佛罗里达布兰卡于1784年拆除。1821年时，特乌申人仍掌握着内陆猎道。

en:
Mendoza lies on the arid eastern foot of the Andes, where snowmelt rivers create irrigated oases between the mountains and the Pampas. In 1444 Huarpe farmers of the Agrelo heritage watered maize, beans, squash and quinoa in the northern and central valleys, while Puelche hunter-gatherers moved between the Barrancas and Diamante rivers. Inca power had not yet arrived; local tradition places Túpac Yupanqui's advance near Coquimbo only around 1470.

Francisco de Villagra's Chile-bound expedition wintered at Huentota in 1551 with 185 men and 500 horses and explored as far as the Diamante. Pedro del Castillo founded Mendoza del Nuevo Valle de La Rioja on 2 March 1561, naming it for Governor García Hurtado de Mendoza; the first settlement had 47 Spanish householders, 30 encomenderos and about 2,500 indigenous tributaries. Juan Jufré moved it two arquebus shots southwest on 28 March 1562 and briefly renamed it City of the Resurrection in the Province of the Huarpes, but Mendoza remained its name. As seat of the Cuyo corregimiento under Chile, the town built San Carlos fort in 1771 and San Juan Nepomuceno in 1772 against Mapuche expansion, then passed to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776. River works in 1788 expanded irrigated farming. The intendancy of Cuyo was restored in 1813 with Mendoza as its capital, and José de San Martín took charge in 1814. At El Plumerillo his powder works, foundry and cloth shops equipped the Army of the Andes, some 4,000 soldiers and 1,000 auxiliaries with 10,000 mules, which crossed into Chile in January 1817. The Cuyo government was dissolved on 1 March 1820; Tomás Godoy Cruz became Mendoza's governor on 3 July.
zh:
门多萨位于安第斯山东麓的干旱地带，融水河流在山地与潘帕斯之间滋养出灌溉绿洲。1444年，具有阿格雷洛文化传统的瓦尔佩农人在北部和中部谷地开渠，种植玉米、菜豆、南瓜和藜麦；普埃尔切狩猎采集者则在巴兰卡斯河与迪亚曼特河之间活动。印加势力此时尚未到达，当地传说把图帕克·尤潘基推进到科金博附近的时间放在约1470年。

1551年，弗朗西斯科·德·比亚格拉前往智利的队伍带着185名士兵和500匹马在温托塔过冬，并探索到迪亚曼特河一带。1561年3月2日，佩德罗·德尔·卡斯蒂略建立「新拉里奥哈谷地之门多萨」，以智利都督加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨命名；最初的居民点有47户西班牙人、30名委托监护主和约2500名纳贡原住民。1562年3月28日，胡安·胡弗雷把城向西南迁移两个火绳枪射程的距离，一度改名为「瓦尔佩省复活城」，但门多萨之名最终保留下来。作为智利治下库约裁判区的首府，这座城市于1771年修建圣卡洛斯堡，1772年修建圣胡安·内波穆塞诺堡，以抵御马普切人的扩张；1776年又转入拉普拉塔总督辖区。1788年的河渠工程扩大了灌溉农业。1813年，库约监督区恢复，以门多萨为首府，何塞·德·圣马丁于1814年接掌此地。他在埃尔普卢梅里略设火药厂、铸炮厂和被服工场，为安第斯军团装备约4000名士兵、1000名辅助人员和10000匹骡子，大军于1817年1月翻山进入智利。1820年3月1日，库约政府解散；托马斯·戈多伊·克鲁斯于7月3日成为门多萨省长。

en:
Matará takes its name from the Mataraes, a people linked to the Tonocoté who occupied the dry plains south of the Bermejo River between the 61st and 63rd meridians west. In 1444 their villages shared the western Chaco frontier with Vilela bands moving between the Bermejo and Salado rivers. Thorn forest, floodlands and seasonal lagoons supplied fish, game, carob and small cultivated fields, while tracks joined the Bermejo plains to Tonocoté lands around Santiago del Estero. No outside overlord yet ruled the Mataraes.

Spanish penetration turned this indigenous place into an encomienda. In 1584 Matará and nearby Guacara were assigned to settlers from Talavera de Esteco; after Alonso de Vera y Aragón founded Concepción in 1585 he claimed both villages, about seven leagues or 50 kilometres west of his new city, and the jurisdictional quarrel was carried to the Spanish king. Matará labor sustained Concepción. A census in 1622 recorded 638 Matará and Nogosna people in the encomienda. In 1631 a coalition of tribes destroyed Matará and killed much of Concepción's garrison; the survivors withdrew toward Corrientes, and Concepción's cabildo was dissolved in 1645. Some Mataraes later settled around Santiago del Estero. By 1821 no Spanish town remained at the old encomienda, while the surrounding bush stayed in Chaco hands.
zh:
马塔拉得名于马塔拉人；他们被视为与托诺科特人有关的族群，居住在贝尔梅霍河以南、西经61度至63度之间的干燥平原。1444年，他们的村落与活动在贝尔梅霍河、萨拉多河之间的维莱拉群体共同分享西查科边疆。刺林、河泛地和季节湖提供鱼、猎物、角豆和小块农田，小路则把贝尔梅霍平原与圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗一带的托诺科特土地连接起来。此时还没有外来领主统治马塔拉人。

西班牙人深入后，这个原住民地方变成委托监护地。1584年，马塔拉和附近的瓜卡拉被交给塔莱韦拉-德埃斯特科的殖民者；阿隆索·德·贝拉-阿拉贡1585年建立康塞普西翁后，宣称这两座位于新城以西约七里格、即五十公里处的村镇归自己管辖，司法争端最后上诉到西班牙国王。马塔拉的劳役支撑着康塞普西翁。1622年的人口清点记载，该监护区有六百三十八名马塔拉人和诺戈斯人。1631年，诸部族联军摧毁马塔拉，歼灭康塞普西翁的大部分驻军；幸存者退往科连特斯，康塞普西翁市议会也于1645年解散。后来一些马塔拉人在圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗一带定居。到1821年，旧监护地已无西班牙城镇存留，周围丛林仍掌握在查科诸族手中。

en:
Santa Tecla names a stretch of rolling pampa around the Rio Negro and Piraízinho, on the old line between the Guarani mission country, the River Plate garrisons, and the overland route toward Montevideo. In 1444 these grasslands were above all Charrua and Guenoa country; bands hunted the open camps and moved between waterholes and ridgeways, while Guarani-speaking travellers from the Uruguay valley crossed the same ground. No European fort had yet been planted there.

The Jesuit reduction of Santo André dos Guenoas was established in the region in 1683, and feral cattle later made the ridges a target of Spanish and Portuguese raiders. In January 1774 Juan José de Vértiz, governor of Buenos Aires, ordered the engineer Bernardo Lecocq to build a pentagonal Fort Santa Tecla, blocking Portuguese routes toward the missions and the Banda Oriental. Rafael Pinto Bandeira's guerrillas and Rio Pardo dragoons captured and dismantled it in 1776 after a long siege. The 1777 Treaty of San Ildefonso returned the border post to Spain, but in 1801 the Spanish abandoned and destroyed it during the War of the Oranges, leaving the district under Portuguese control. A military camp at the Cerros de Bagé in July 1811 became the nucleus of Bagé, and a chapel dedicated to Saint Sebastian was built there in 1820. By 1821 this was frontier cattle country around the memory of a demolished fort.
zh:
圣特克拉指内格罗河与皮拉伊齐纽河一带起伏的潘帕草原，旧处瓜拉尼传教区、拉普拉塔驻军和通往蒙得维的亚的陆路之间。1444年，这片草地主要是查鲁亚人与格诺阿人的土地；人群在开阔原野狩猎，在水源和山脊路之间移动，乌拉圭河谷讲瓜拉尼语的旅人也会经过这里。那时欧洲人尚未在此修建要塞。

1683年，耶稣会在这一地区建立圣安德烈-杜斯格诺阿斯归化村；后来野牧牛群使这些山脊成为西班牙和葡萄牙掠牛者争夺的目标。1774年1月，布宜诺斯艾利斯总督胡安·何塞·德·贝尔蒂斯下令工程师贝尔纳多·勒科克修建五边形的圣特克拉要塞，以阻断葡萄牙人通往传教区和东岸的道路。1776年，拉斐尔·平托·班德拉的游击队与里奥帕尔多龙骑兵经长期围攻攻占并拆除要塞。1777年的《圣伊尔德方索条约》使这个边堡重归西班牙，但1801年橘子战争期间，西班牙人撤离并摧毁它，地区落入葡萄牙控制。1811年7月，巴热丘陵的一座军营成为巴热的雏形；1820年，当地建起献给圣塞巴斯蒂昂的小教堂。到1821年，这里已是一座被毁要塞记忆环绕的边境牧地。

en:
Griqualand is a later political name. The dry grassland between the Vaal and Orange rivers, around the future Kimberley, was first Khoe-San country; hunter-foragers and herders knew its pans, springs and game routes, and stone tools at nearby Wildebeest Kuil recall that presence. Setswana-speaking farmers and cattle keepers later moved into the wider region from the north, organizing villages under chiefs and councils, but the Kimberley ridge itself had no recorded permanent town. In 1444 the mixed, Afrikaans-speaking Griqua community had not yet formed, and rivers, pans and springs rather than a colonial frontier governed movement.

During the eighteenth century, mounted Baster and Oorlam groups moved beyond the Cape and along the Orange River corridor. In 1801 William Anderson and Cornelius Kramer of the London Missionary Society opened a station at Leeuwenkuil among Chaguriqua Khoe and mixed Baster families; around 1805 it was moved to a higher, equally dry spring called Klaarwater. In 1813 the missionary John Campbell promoted the name Griqua in place of Baster, and Klaarwater became Griquatown, the core of Waterboer's Land under Andries Waterboer and Adam Kok II. Robert and Mary Moffat were staying there on their way to Kuruman when their daughter Mary was born in 1821, by which time the spring station linked Cape missionaries, Griqua horsemen and Tswana lands to the north.
zh:
格里夸兰是后世才有的政治名称。法尔河与奥兰治河之间、未来金伯利周围的干旱草原，最初是科伊桑人的土地；猎民和牧人熟悉盐盘、泉水和猎物通道，附近的怀尔德比斯特奎尔（Wildebeest Kuil）发现的石器仍显示他们曾在此活动。说茨瓦纳语的农民和牧牛者后来从北方迁入更广阔的区域，以酋长和议事会组织村落，但金伯利所在的山脊本身没有留下固定城镇的记载。1444年时，操南非荷兰语的混血格里夸共同体尚未形成；决定人们如何移动的是河流、盐盘和泉水，而不是殖民边疆。

18世纪，骑马的巴斯特人和奥拉姆人越过开普边疆，沿奥兰治河走廊移动。1801年，伦敦传道会的威廉·安德森和科内利斯·克拉默在莱乌恩奎尔（Leeuwenkuil）设立传教站，周围是查古里克瓦科伊人和混血巴斯特家庭；约1805年，传教站迁至一处更高、同样缺水的泉水，命名为克拉尔瓦特（Klaarwater）。1813年，传教士约翰·坎贝尔推动以「格里夸」取代「巴斯特」一名，克拉尔瓦特随后成为格里夸镇，也是安德里斯·沃特布尔和亚当·科克二世治下「沃特布尔之地」的核心。1821年，罗伯特·莫法特与妻子玛丽前往库鲁曼途中暂住于此，女儿玛丽在当地出生；此时这座泉水传教站已经把开普传教士、格里夸骑兵和北方茨瓦纳土地连接起来。

en:
Corumbá lies on the right bank of the Paraguay River where the seasonally flooded Pantanal plains stretch west toward Bolivia. Its lagoons were the country of the Guató, the canoe people, who lived in small family bands aboard dugout canoes and took fish and birds with the bow, while the Paiaguá ranged the river itself. In 1444 no European had yet entered this maze of floodland; its only roads were the waterways linking the Paraguay with the camps of the Mato Grosso plateau.

The first Spanish town, Santiago de Xerez, was founded in 1593, but it and the nearby Jesuit settlements were destroyed by bandeirantes raiding upstream from São Paulo; a Portuguese post at Camapuã followed in 1650. To secure the river against Spain, the governor of Mato Grosso, Luís de Albuquerque, had Forte Coimbra built from 13 September 1775, and in 1778 Sergeant-Major Marcelino Rois Camponês founded the Vila de Nossa Senhora da Conceição de Albuquerque, the settlement that would become Corumbá, on the last deep-water reach below the Serra de Albuquerque. In 1821 it was still a small garrison port serving the river traffic of Cuiabá and Cáceres.
zh:
科伦巴位于巴拉圭河右岸，季节性泛滥的潘塔纳尔平原从这里向西一直延伸到玻利维亚。潟湖之间是瓜托人的天地，他们被称为独木舟人，以小家族为单位住在挖空树干做成的独木舟上，靠弓箭捕鱼射鸟为生；帕亚瓜人则游弋于巴拉圭河上。1444年时还没有欧洲人进入这片水网之地，唯一的道路是连通巴拉圭河与马托格罗索高原各处营地的水道。

西班牙人1593年最早在这里建立圣地亚哥-德赫雷斯城，但这座城镇和附近的耶稣会定居点都被从圣保罗溯河而上劫掠的旗队探险者摧毁；葡萄牙人1650年在卡马庞设立据点。为防范西班牙、控制河道，马托格罗索都督路易斯·德·阿尔布克尔克下令自1775年9月13日起修建科英布拉堡，1778年军士长马塞利诺·罗伊斯·坎波内斯又在阿尔布克尔克山以下最后一段深水河道旁建立「圣母受孕德阿尔布克尔克镇」，即后来的科伦巴。1821年时，这里仍是一座小小的驻防河港，为库亚巴和卡塞雷斯的河运服务。

en:
The steep hills above a bay of the Paraguay River, near the southern waters of the Pantanal, had no Spanish garrison in 1444. This was Mbayá and Guaná country: river people, hunters and mobile bands knew the crossings and seasonal floods, and the bluffs later chosen for a fort offered refuge in a land without towns. For more than two and a half centuries after contact, no colonial power could turn that river gateway into a secure frontier.

On 17 October 1791 the Viceroy of the Río de la Plata ordered a post built to check Portuguese advance and Mbayá raids. José Antonio Zavala y Delgadillo founded Fuerte Borbón on 25 September 1792, inviting Mbayá chiefs to the ceremony; José de Isasi became its first commander. The garrison of about a hundred men depended on convoys from Concepción and Charcas, and mistrust soon returned. Mbayá attacks in 1796 prompted a bloody reprisal at Concepción, and during the 1801 Spanish-Portuguese war an attempt against upstream Coimbra failed. In 1810 troops from Borbón fought Manuel Belgrano's expedition; after the post was abandoned it passed briefly through Mbayá and Portuguese hands before being returned. Around 1817 Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia strengthened it with a long stone wall, keeping the northern river gate of independent Paraguay.
zh:
1444年，巴拉圭河一处河湾上方、临近潘塔纳尔南缘的陡峭丘陵还没有西班牙驻军。这里是姆巴亚人和瓜纳人的土地：河畔居民、猎人和移动群体熟悉渡口与季节洪水，日后被选为要塞的高地也为这片没有城镇的土地提供了天然依托。欧洲人到来后的两个半世纪里，没有哪个殖民强权能把这座河上门户变成安全边界。

1791年10月17日，拉普拉塔总督下令设立据点，以阻挡葡萄牙推进和姆巴亚人袭掠。1792年9月25日，何塞·安东尼奥·萨瓦拉-德尔加迪略建立波旁堡，并邀请姆巴亚酋长出席建堡仪式，何塞·德·伊萨西任首任指挥官。约一百人的驻军依赖康塞普西翁和查尔卡斯运来的补给，双方的互不信任很快重现。1796年姆巴亚人袭击康塞普西翁，引发当地血腥报复；1801年西葡战争期间，西班牙人溯流攻打科英布拉堡的行动也告失败。1810年，波旁堡军队参加了对抗曼努埃尔·贝尔格拉诺远征的战斗；据点弃守后一度落入姆巴亚人和葡萄牙人之手，后因葡萄牙撤退而归还。约1817年，加斯帕尔·罗德里格斯·德·弗朗西亚加修一道长石墙，把这里维持为独立巴拉圭的北方河门。

en:
The Paraguay River banks and islands northwest of Asunción were Payaguá country in 1444. These Guaycuruan people, who called themselves Evueví or people of the river, moved in large dugouts between the Pantanal and downstream waters, fishing, hunting, gathering and raiding Guarani fields on the eastern shore. Behind them stretched the dry Chaco; on the water they were the power Spanish crews would later call river pirates.

After Asunción was founded in 1537, Payaguá canoes made the Paraguay unsafe for Spanish traffic. In 1613 the colony declared a 'war of fire and blood' against them and their Mbayá allies, but seventeenth-century yerba mate traffic often moved overland to avoid river raids. Policy changed after 1730, when officials sought trade and accommodation, and southern bands settled near Asunción around 1750. In 1786 Father Juan Francisco Amancio González y Escobar founded Reducción Melodía on this bank, naming it for Governor Pedro Melo de Portugal. The priest's departure left the reduction abandoned, and the place was remembered as Amancio Cué. By 1821 this frontier had a name and a river crossing, but no town strong enough to command the Chaco.
zh:
1444年，亚松森西北方的巴拉圭河岸与岛屿是帕亚瓜人的土地。他们自称埃武埃维，意为河上人，属瓜伊库鲁族群，划着大型独木舟在潘塔纳尔与下游水道之间往来，以渔猎、采集和袭击东岸瓜拉尼人的农田为生。他们身后是干旱的查科；在水上，他们正是后来西班牙船员口中的河流海盗。

1537年亚松森建立后，帕亚瓜人的独木舟使巴拉圭河对西班牙交通充满危险。1613年，殖民地对他们和姆巴亚盟友宣布「火与血之战」，但17世纪的马黛茶贸易仍常改走陆路，以避开河上袭掠。1730年后政策转向贸易与安抚，约1750年，南部帕亚瓜人开始在亚松森附近定居。1786年，神父胡安·弗朗西斯科·阿曼西奥·冈萨雷斯·伊·埃斯科瓦尔在这一岸建立摩罗蒂亚（梅洛迪亚）传教村，以总督佩德罗·梅洛·德·葡萄牙的姓氏命名。神父离开后，传教村遭到废弃，旧址被称为阿曼西奥库埃。到1821年，这条边疆在这里有了名字和渡口，却仍没有一座足以控制查科的城镇。

en:
The grasslands and riverine forests east of the upper Uruguay, around the future São Borja, were Guarani country in 1444. Canoes and trails linked scattered villages along the river crossings, but no Spanish town or Jesuit reduction yet stood on this bank. The Uruguay was still an indigenous highway rather than an imperial boundary, and the peoples later gathered into the Seven Peoples of the Missions moved through its open campos and gallery woods beyond the reach of Spain or Portugal.

After bandeirantes had destroyed earlier Jesuit reductions in Guaíra and Tape, Spanish Jesuits returned to the region from 1682. Francisco Garcia founded São Francisco de Borja with 195 Guarani brought from São Tomé; it was the first of the Seven Peoples and held 2,814 people by 1707. Cattle herds, stone churches and planned plaza villages made the missions prosperous, but the Treaty of Madrid of 1750 assigned their east bank to Portugal in exchange for Colônia do Sacramento and ordered the Guarani moved west. Under Sepé Tiaraju they refused, opening the Guarani War of 1753–1756. At Caiboaté on 10 February 1756, 3,000 Spanish and Portuguese troops killed 1,511 Guarani at a cost of four European dead and occupied the seven reductions. The Treaty of El Pardo annulled the transfer in 1761 and returned the district to Spain, while the Jesuit expulsions of 1759 and 1767 had emptied the mission system by 1768. In 1801 a Portuguese force of only forty men under Manuel dos Santos Pedroso and José Borges do Canto seized the Seven Peoples, and São Borja was raised to a town on 13 October 1817.
zh:
乌拉圭河上游东岸、后来圣博尔哈所在的草原与河畔林地，在1444年属于瓜拉尼人。独木舟和小路连接着渡口附近散布的村落，但此时河岸还没有西班牙城镇，也没有耶稣会传道村。乌拉圭河仍是原住民的通道，而非帝国边界；后来被集中到传教士城（七传道区）的人群，正活动在开阔草原与林泽之间，不受西班牙或葡萄牙管辖。

旗兵摧毁瓜伊拉和塔佩等地较早的耶稣会传道村后，西班牙耶稣会士从1682年起重返这一地区。弗朗西斯科·加西亚带着从圣多梅迁出的一百九十五名瓜拉尼人建立圣方济各·德·博尔哈；它是七传道区中的第一个，到1707年已有二千八百一十四人。牛群、石砌教堂和按广场规划的村落使传道区繁盛起来，但1750年的《马德里条约》把乌拉圭河东岸划给葡萄牙，以交换科洛尼亚-德尔萨克拉门托，并命令瓜拉尼人西迁。他们在塞佩·蒂亚拉茹领导下拒绝，1753—1756年瓜拉尼战争爆发。1756年2月10日的凯博阿特之战中，三千名西葡军队杀死一千五百一十一名瓜拉尼人，己方仅死四人，随后占领七座传道村。1761年《埃尔帕多条约》废除这次转让，地区归还西班牙；而1759年和1767年耶稣会先后遭葡萄牙、西班牙驱逐，到1768年传道体系已经瓦解。1801年，曼努埃尔·多斯桑托斯·佩德罗索和若泽·博尔热斯·多坎托率领仅四十人的葡萄牙部队夺取七传道区；1817年10月13日，圣博尔哈升格为镇。

en:
Barra guards the meeting of the Rio Grande and São Francisco, where seasonally flooded river flats and gallery forests cut through the northeastern sertão. In 1444 the confluence was Xakriabá country; these Akwé-speaking Ge people also occupied stretches of the Tocantins valley, moving between riverine woods, hunting grounds and inland trails.

In 1670 Dias d'Ávila's Casa da Torre, one of Bahia's powerful cattle and landholding houses, opened a corral on the Rio Grande ravines. Franciscans raised a chapel in 1680, and cattle pens, ferries and boat traffic on the São Francisco turned the spot into an interior river station. In 1752 the settlement was raised to a town as Vila de São Francisco do Rio Grande.
zh:
巴拉扼守格兰德河汇入圣弗朗西斯科河之处，季节性河滩与走廊林穿过东北部内陆荒原。1444年，这个河口是舍克里厄巴人的土地；他们属于说阿克温语的热依人，也活动于托坎廷斯河谷，往来利用河畔林地、猎场和内陆小径。

1670年，迪亚斯·达维拉的卡萨达托雷在格兰德河坡地设立牧栏，这是巴伊亚最有势力的畜牧与地产家族之一。方济各会于1680年建起礼拜堂，牛栏、渡口和圣弗朗西斯科河上的船运逐渐把这里变成内陆水路驿站。1752年，定居点升格为城镇，称圣弗朗西斯科-杜里奥格兰德镇。

en:
Parnaíba takes in the river's delta, where the great river splits into the Igaraçu and a web of mangrove channels before the Atlantic. In 1444 the shores were the country of the Tremembé, who fished the shoals and crossed the river mouths in canoes; the river's Tupi name means muddy-water river. Portuguese vessels reconnoitred the coast in the sixteenth century, and Jesuits began work among the Indians in 1607, but no town yet stood among the dunes.

Cattle changed all that. As ranchers occupied the Parnaíba valley, the baptized Indian Mandu Ladino rose in 1712 and led Tupi and Cariri bands through the sertões of Piauí, Maranhão and Ceará, burning fazendas. An expedition of 1716 was raised with Tabajara allies from the Serra da Ibiapaba; Mandu Ladino was mortally wounded and drowned in the Parnaíba, and the conflict lasted until 1719. In 1758 Domingos Dias da Silva set up a charqueada and founded Porto das Barcas, and in 1762 Governor João Pereira Caldas installed the Vila de São João da Parnaíba, which became an entrepôt for dried beef and leather and took the name Parnaíba in 1801. In 1821 its quays still handled the cattle products of the Piauí sertão.
zh:
巴纳伊巴一带是大河入海的三角洲，大河在注入大西洋前汊出伊加拉苏河和一片红树林水道。1444年，两岸是特雷门贝人的地盘，他们在浅滩捕鱼，划独木舟穿行河口；大河的图皮语名字意为「浑水河」。16世纪有葡萄牙船只侦察这段海岸，耶稣会士从1607年起向印第安人传教，但沙丘之间还没有城镇。

改变一切的是牛。牧人占据巴纳伊巴河谷后，受洗的印第安人曼杜·拉迪诺于1712年起事，率领图皮人和卡里里人转战皮奥伊、马拉尼翁和塞阿拉的荒原，焚毁牧场。1716年，一支得到伊比亚帕巴山塔巴哈拉人助战的讨伐队集结；曼杜·拉迪诺受伤后溺死在巴纳伊巴河中，冲突持续到1719年。1758年，多明戈斯·迪亚斯·达席尔瓦开设腌肉作坊、建立巴尔卡斯港；1762年，若昂·佩雷拉·卡尔达斯都督设立圣若昂达巴纳伊巴镇，这里成为腌肉和皮革的贸易站，1801年改名巴纳伊巴。1821年时，码头上装卸的仍是皮奥伊荒原出产的牛肉制品和皮革。

en:
Santa Catarina is the long island guarding a chain of Atlantic anchorages on the southern Brazilian coast, with mainland bays and the Serra do Mar behind it. In 1444 the Carijó, a Tupi-Guarani people, knew the island as Meiembipe, the mountain beside the channel. Their villages combined maize and manioc gardens with fishing and shellfish gathering, and canoes crossed the sheltered strait later used by ships bound for the River Plate.

Portuguese navigators named the island Ilha dos Patos around 1514 and Ilha de Santa Catarina in 1526, but permanent settlement began only in 1673, when Francisco Dias Velho brought settlers to the shore; a chapel dedicated to Nossa Senhora do Desterro followed in 1678. The crown made the community a parish in 1714 and a town in 1726, then created the island captaincy by an 11 August 1738 charter and appointed José da Silva Paes its governor. From 1739 the forts of Santa Cruz de Anhatomirim, São José da Ponta Grossa and Santo Antônio de Ratones secured the northern anchorage. From 1748 onward about six thousand Azorean and Madeiran settlers reached the coast, expanding farms and cotton and linen production. In February 1777 Pedro de Cevallos's Spanish expedition seized the island, but the Treaty of San Ildefonso on 1 October 1777 returned it to Portugal. By 1821 Desterro was an Azorean fishing, provisioning and garrison port on the road to the River Plate.
zh:
圣卡塔琳娜是一座狭长岛屿，扼守巴西南部大西洋上的一串锚地，岛后是大陆海湾和马尔山。1444年，图皮-瓜拉尼人的一支卡里若人把此岛称为梅因比佩，意为水道旁的山。他们的村落既种玉米和木薯，也捕鱼、采集贝类；独木舟往来于遮蔽良好的海峡，后来这条水路也服务于前往拉普拉塔河的船只。

约1514年，葡萄牙航海者把此岛命名为鸭岛，1526年改称圣卡塔琳娜岛，但永久定居到1673年才开始：弗朗西斯科·迪亚斯·维略率领移民登岸，1678年又建起献给流亡圣母的小教堂。王室先后在1714年将此地设为堂区、1726年升为镇，1738年8月11日颁布敕令设立岛都督辖区，并任命若泽·达席尔瓦·派斯为总督。1739年起，阿尼亚托米林圣十字、蓬塔格罗萨圣若泽和拉托内斯圣安多尼等要塞锁住北方锚地。1748年起，约六千名亚速尔和马德拉移民抵达海岸，扩展农庄并发展棉花与麻布生产。1777年2月，佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯的西班牙远征队夺取岛屿，但1777年10月1日的《圣伊尔德方索条约》又将其归还葡萄牙。到1821年，德斯泰罗已是亚速尔渔民的补给港和驻军港，扼守通往拉普拉塔河的航路。

en:
The Cuiabá country lies around the Cuiabá and Coxipó rivers, where tropical forest gives way to scrubland and seasonal floodplains. Its Bororo name is commonly explained as the place of the ikuia, a fishing arrow; Coxiponé people lived along the riverbanks when European power was still far away. In 1444 their villages, fishing grounds and forest trails belonged to no Portuguese captaincy, while the rivers feeding the Paraguay linked the region to wider indigenous networks.

Manoel de Campos Bicudo passed through in 1673 and 1682 and founded the short-lived São Gonçalo Beira-Rio. Pascoal Moreira Cabral reached the abandoned site in 1718; after a clash with Coxiponé warriors, his party found gold, and the founding act of Cuiabá was recorded at Forquilha on 8 April 1719. A richer strike was made in October 1722 by enslaved Indians working for Miguel Sutil, drawing miners to the Prainha stream. Rodrigo César de Menezes raised the settlement to Vila Real do Senhor Bom Jesus de Cuiabá on 1 January 1727. The gold soon proved thinner than hoped. The Captaincy of Mato Grosso was created in 1748, and after Antônio Rolim de Moura arrived in 1751 he established Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade as its capital. Cuiabá remained a riverside mining and supply town until it received city rank on 17 September 1818.
zh:
库亚巴一带位于库亚巴河与科希波河沿岸，热带雨林在此过渡为灌丛草原和季节性洼地。博罗罗语常把它解释为使用「伊库亚」渔箭的地方；1444年时，欧洲人的势力还远在大西洋沿岸，科希波内人住在河畔，村落、渔场和林中小径都不属于任何葡萄牙都督辖区，汇入巴拉圭河的水路则把这里接入更广的原住民交流网络。

曼努埃尔·德·坎波斯·比库多曾在1673年和1682年经过此地，建立起短暂存在的圣贡萨洛·贝拉-里奥。1718年，帕斯科阿尔·莫雷拉·卡布拉尔抵达这个废弃地点；他的队伍与科希波内武士交战后发现黄金，1719年4月8日在福基利亚登记了库亚巴的建置文书。1722年10月，为米格尔·苏蒂尔劳作的被奴役印第安人在普赖尼亚溪找到更富的矿脉，淘金人随即涌来。1727年1月1日，罗德里戈·塞萨尔·德·梅内塞斯将定居点升格为维拉·雷亚尔·杜·塞尼奥尔·邦热苏斯·德·库亚巴。金矿不久便证明不如预期丰厚。马托格罗索都督辖区于1748年设立，安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1751年到任后，把维拉贝拉达桑蒂西马特林达德建为首府。库亚巴此后长期是河畔采矿与补给城镇，1818年9月17日才升格为市。

en:
Rio Branco covers the upper valley of the Branco, where the Uraricoera and Tacutu meet before the river runs south toward the Negro. Carib-speaking Macushi lived along its savanna streams and gallery woods, while Arawak-speaking Wapishana held country to the east. High water opened the lower Branco to canoes from the Negro, and in 1444 the valley remained in Indigenous hands, its villages linked by river travel, fishing, manioc fields and regional trade.

Carmelite missionaries began work here in 1725, and Portuguese raiders and troops pushed up the Branco in the 1730s, seeking captives and forest products while securing a frontier against Dutch, English and Spanish rivals. The Portuguese built São Joaquim Fort at the Uraricoera-Tacutu confluence in 1775-1778, then placed mission villages along the rivers. In 1789 Manuel da Gama Lôbo d'Almada introduced cattle and horses, and the São Bento, São José and São Marcos ranches followed between 1793 and 1799. An English incursion in 1810-1811 was driven back from the valley.
zh:
里奥布朗库位于布朗库河上游，乌拉里奎拉河与塔库图河在此汇合，河水随后向南流入内格罗河。说加勒比语的马库希人居住在稀树草原的水道与林泽间，说阿拉瓦克语的瓦皮沙纳人则生活在东面土地。涨水时，独木舟可从内格罗河驶入布朗库河下游。1444年，河谷仍掌握在原住民手中，村落依靠河运、渔猎、木薯田和区域贸易往来。

1725年，加尔默罗会传教士开始在此传教；1730年代，葡萄牙劫掠队和军队沿布朗库河而上，掳掠人口、搜集林产品，并把这里作为对抗荷兰、英格兰和西班牙竞争者的边疆。1775—1778年，葡萄牙人在乌拉里奎拉河与塔库图河交汇处修建圣若阿金堡垒，随后在沿河设置传教村。1789年，曼努埃尔·达·加马·洛博·德·阿尔马达引入牛和马，圣本图、圣若泽和圣马科斯牧场随后在1793—1799年间建立。1810—1811年，一支进入河谷的英格兰武装被击退。

en:
Marajó is the great fluviomarine island between the Amazon mouth, the Pará channels and the Atlantic. Its indigenous name was Marinatambal. Seasonal floods shaped life on the island: for centuries river peoples had raised villages on artificial earthen mounds called tesos, planted manioc, fished the maze of channels and made decorated Marajoara pottery. In 1444 the Aruã phase of that long mound-building tradition was still underway, and the island's fishermen and canoe-warriors controlled the approaches between river and sea.

European ships entering the Amazon estuary in the sixteenth century brought trade, raids and epidemic disease, severely weakening the island's indigenous populations. On 23 December 1665 the Portuguese crown granted the island as the captaincy of Ilha Grande de Joanes, named for the Joanes people, to António de Sousa Macedo; his proxy took possession in 1667. The grant commanded strategic channels at the Amazon mouth, while natural grasslands supported cattle and hide production for Belém and the Atlantic trade. In 1696 Luís Gonçalo de Sousa Macedo gave lands near the Arari River to Capuchin friars for missions and settlement, and religious cattle ranches became a feature of the island. The crown bought the captaincy back on 29 April 1754 and placed Marajó under Grão-Pará, tightening royal control over the Amazon entrance on the eve of the Jesuit expulsion.
zh:
马拉若是横亘在亚马逊河口、帕拉河水道与大西洋之间的巨大河海岛屿，印第安人原称马里纳坦巴尔。季节性洪水塑造了岛上生活：多个世纪以来，河畔民族把村落建在名为特索的人工土丘上，种植木薯，在迷宫般的水道中捕鱼，并制作纹饰精美的马拉若陶。1444年，这一悠久筑丘传统的阿鲁昂阶段仍在延续，岛上渔民和独木舟战士控制着河海之间的通道。

16世纪，进入亚马逊河口的欧洲船只带来贸易、袭掠和传染病，使岛上印第安人口遭受重创。1665年12月23日，葡萄牙王室把全岛封赐为大若阿内斯岛都督领，名称来自若阿内斯人，受封者是安东尼奥·德索萨·马塞多；其代理人于1667年正式接管。这片封地扼守亚马逊河口的战略水道，天然草场则为贝伦和大西洋贸易提供牛只与皮革。1696年，路易斯·贡萨洛·德索萨·马塞多把阿拉里河附近土地赠予嘉布遣会修士，用于传教和定居，教会牧场由此成为岛上一景。1754年4月29日，王室购回都督领，将马拉若并入格劳帕拉管辖，在驱逐耶稣会前夕加强了对亚马逊入口的王室控制。

en:
Santo Antônio da Manga covers a stretch of the left bank of the São Francisco, between the mouths of the Urucuia and Paracatu and the Ribeirão da Conceição. In 1444 the river, its wooded islands and the surrounding sertão were Kaiapó country; an island later called São Romão held an indigenous village whose people lived by the river before Portuguese backwoodsmen and slave-raiding bands entered the middle São Francisco.

The Portuguese arraial of Santo Antônio da Manga was founded on 23 October 1668 on that left bank. The island opposite became a battleground between fugitives, runaway slaves, remnants of earlier expeditions and colonial patrols, and tradition placed the destruction of the Kaiapó village there on a feast of Saint Romanus before 1712. In 1736 the settlement was a centre of the Motins do Sertão, when backcountry men led by Pedro Cardoso rose against colonial taxation, half a century before the Minas conspiracy. As the first river port and judicial seat on the middle São Francisco, the arraial shipped gold, coin and precious stones brought from Goiás and Mato Grosso toward the coast.
zh:
圣安东尼奥-达曼加位于圣弗朗西斯科河左岸，地当乌鲁库亚河、帕拉卡图河与孔塞桑溪之间。1444年时，大河、林木覆盖的岛屿和周围腹地都是卡亚波人的土地；后来被称为圣罗芒的岛上曾有印第安村落，居民傍水而居，直到葡萄牙腹地开拓者和捕奴队进入圣弗朗西斯科河中游。

1668年10月23日，葡萄牙人在河左岸建立圣安东尼奥-达曼加村。对岸岛屿后来成为逃犯、逃亡奴隶、旧远征队残部与殖民巡逻队交战之地；相传在1712年以前的一个圣罗芒日，卡亚波人的村落就在那里被摧毁。1736年，此地成为「腹地暴动」的中心之一，佩德罗·卡多佐率领腹地居民反抗殖民征税，比米纳斯密谋早了半个世纪。作为圣弗朗西斯科河中游最早的河港和司法驻地，这个村落把来自戈亚斯和马托格罗索的黄金、钱币与宝石运往沿海。

en:
The open plateau between the Serra da Canastra and the Rio Grande was remembered in colonial records as the country of the Araxás. Their lands commanded crossings and camping grounds on the routes from São Paulo towards the Goiás and Minas interior, alternating gallery forest with high grassland. In 1444 their villages remained independent, bound by kinship and intertribal diplomacy; no Portuguese farm, parish or military road had yet fixed this far western borderland of the future Minas Gerais.

European accounts place the Araxás in the region from the late sixteenth century, but sustained colonial pressure came much later. In 1749 they asked the governor of Goiás for Jesuit missionaries and settlement under the protection of the Paulista frontier leader Antônio Pires de Campos. A new village was laid out on the Rio Claro near its mouth into the Rio das Velhas in 1750–1751; while Pires de Campos was campaigning north, Caiapó warriors attacked, killed the Araxá men and carried off the surviving women and children, so that official letters reported the group destroyed by early 1751. Bandeira warfare then opened the plateau to cattle ranches, whose owners began to settle around 1770. In 1791 the farming settlement was organized as the parish of São Domingos de Araxá, carrying the indigenous name into the Portuguese province that existed by 1821.
zh:
卡纳斯特拉山脉与格兰德河之间的开阔高原，在殖民记录中被称为阿拉斯人的土地。他们的土地控制着从圣保罗通往戈亚斯和米纳斯内陆道路上的渡口与营地，景观在林带河谷和高原草场之间交替。1444年时，阿拉斯人的村落仍保持自主，依靠亲属关系和部族间往来维系；在后来的米纳斯吉拉斯极西边地，还没有葡萄牙人的农庄、堂区或军用道路。

欧洲记载从16世纪后期起已提到这一地区的阿拉斯人，但持续的殖民压力要晚得多。1749年，他们请求戈亚斯总督派遣耶稣会士，并在圣保罗边地首领安东尼奥·皮雷斯·德·坎波斯保护下建立定居村。1750—1751年，新村落设在克拉鲁河汇入旧河处附近；皮雷斯·德·坎波斯北征期间，卡亚波战士发动袭击，杀死阿拉斯男子并掳走幸存妇孺，官员信函因此在1751年初报告这一部群已覆灭。随后远征战争把高原开放给牧牛场，牧场主约在1770年开始定居。1791年，农业聚落被编为圣多明我-迪阿拉沙堂区，使这个原住民地名延续到1821年已存在的葡萄牙行省之中。

en:
Ofaie takes its name from the Ofaié, a Macro-Jê people of the Paraná bend in what is now eastern Mato Grosso do Sul. They lived along the great river about the mouth of the Sucuriú and at the headwaters of the Ivinhema and Vacaria, in small bands that hunted and planted fields in the gallery forest; their number before the colonists came was later put at perhaps five thousand. Eastward lay the sertão of the São Paulo backlands, and the cerrado stretched on every side. In 1444 this was a world of rivers and villages untouched by Europeans.

Europeans first crossed these waters in numbers after gold was found on the Cuiabá River in 1718. From the 1720s great canoe convoys called monções left Porto Feliz at high water, descended the Tietê into the Paraná and paddled past the Sucuriú mouth on the 3,500-kilometre road to the mines. The Ofaié watched the fleets go by year after year. In 1821 no Portuguese town or fort yet stood on the Sucuriú, and the passing convoys, already past their greatest days, were the people's only regular link with the world beyond their rivers.
zh:
奥法耶得名于奥法耶人，他们是住在巴拉那河大拐弯一带的大热依语族群，地在今南马托格罗索州东部。奥法耶人聚居在苏库里乌河口附近的大河两岸以及伊维涅马河、瓦卡里亚河的源头，以小群体游猎、在长廊林间开垦为生；据估殖民者到来之前他们约有五千人。东边是圣保罗腹地的荒原，四周绵延着塞拉多稀树草原。1444年，这里还是一片欧洲人未曾涉足的河流与村落世界。

1718年库亚巴河发现黄金后，欧洲人才成批经过这片水域。从1720年代起，名为「季风船队」的独木舟队趁水涨时从波尔图费利斯出发，沿铁特河驶入巴拉那河，经过苏库里乌河口，走上去金矿的3500公里水路。奥法耶人看着船队年年经过。1821年时，苏库里乌河畔仍没有葡萄牙人的城镇或要塞，已过鼎盛期的过往船队是他们与河流之外世界唯一的固定往来。

en:
The hills and water meadows of the Rio das Mortes, the River of Deaths, were Macro-Jê country on the southern approaches to the Minas interior long before the gold rush. Its streams, crossings and tracks between the Serra do Lenheiro and Serra de São José served Indigenous villages whose occupants moved between hunting, planting and interregional exchange. In 1444 there was no Portuguese royal road or mining camp in the valley; its place in the route from Paraty to the future Ouro Preto still lay in the future.

Around 1700 the Taubaté bandeirante Tomé Portes del-Rei led a Paulista party to the Rio das Mortes and opened the first lasting camps; after his death around 1702, Antônio Garcia da Cunha and other miners developed the Arraial de Nossa Senhora do Pilar. The district was drawn into the War of the Emboabas of 1707–1709, when Paulista claimants fought newcomers for control of its gold-bearing streams. Royal administration followed quickly: in 1713 the settlements were raised into the town of São João del-Rei, named for John V of Portugal, and in 1714 it became seat of the Rio das Mortes judicial district. On the Estrada Real, the town combined gold with ranching, supply trade and African slave labour; Pilar, Carmo, Mercês and Rosário churches gave it a dense baroque skyline. Even after mining declined in the later eighteenth century, it remained an administrative and market centre, and in 1789 the Minas conspiracy reached the households and militias of its comarca.
zh:
圣若昂-德尔雷伊一带死亡河（Rio das Mortes）的丘陵与水草甸，位于通往米纳斯内陆的南缘，早在淘金潮以前就是大热依语族人群的土地。莱涅罗山和圣若泽山之间的溪流、渡口与小路服务着原住民村落，居民在狩猎、种植和区域交换之间往来。1444年时，河谷中还没有葡萄牙皇家大道或淘金营地；它日后连接帕拉蒂与未来欧鲁普雷图的道路地位也尚未出现。

约1700年，来自陶巴特的圣保罗远征者托梅·波尔特斯·德尔雷伊率队抵达死亡河，开辟了最早的持久营地；他约于1702年死后，安东尼奥·加西亚·达·库尼亚和其他矿工发展出圣母皮拉尔营地。1707—1709年恩博阿巴斯战争期间，这一地区被卷入战事，圣保罗拓殖者与新来者为控制含金溪谷交战。王室行政很快跟进：1713年，各聚居点升格为圣若昂-德尔雷伊镇，以葡萄牙国王若昂五世命名，1714年成为死亡河司法辖区驻地。凭借皇家大道上的位置，此镇把黄金生产、牧牛、补给贸易和非洲奴隶劳动结合起来；皮拉尔、卡尔莫、梅尔塞斯和罗萨里奥诸堂构成密集的巴洛克天际线。即使18世纪后期采金衰落，它仍是行政与市场中心，1789年米纳斯密谋也牵连到这个司法辖区的家族与民兵。

en:
Castro occupies the open Campos Gerais grasslands of Paraná, where the Iapó River cuts through forested sandstone country later known for the Guartelá Canyon. In 1444 its fords and pastures were used by Guarapiaba people, a Tupi group recorded along the Iapó, while Kaingang bands moved through the surrounding forest edge. Native paths followed the dry ground between southern grasslands and the plateaus to the north, but there was as yet no Portuguese ranch, chapel or ferry toll on the river.

Paulista cattlemen reached the Campos Gerais around the turn of the eighteenth century; the Capão Alto land grant is dated to 1704. Pouso do Iapó became a watering place and overnight camp on the Caminho de Sorocaba, used by tropeiros driving cattle from Viamão to the great fair at Sorocaba. Families from Sorocaba, Santos and Itu took up ranches, a wattle-and-daub chapel was built in 1751, and Carmelite friars put up a new church in 1769. Lieutenant-Colonel Afonso Botelho de Sam Payo visited on 15 March 1771, after which the settlement became the parish of Sant'Ana do Iapó; its boundaries were confirmed in 1775. On 24 September 1788 it was separated from Curitiba and raised to a town as Vila Nova de Castro, named for the Portuguese overseas minister Martinho de Melo e Castro. In 1821 cattle, ranching and the long mule and cattle road still defined the town.
zh:
卡斯特鲁地处巴拉那的坎波斯吉拉斯草原，亚波河在这里切过林覆砂岩地带，后来以瓜尔特拉峡谷闻名。1444年时，亚波河畔的瓜拉皮亚巴人（属图皮语族群）使用这里的渡口和牧场，卡因冈游群则在周围森林边缘活动。原住民小路沿干燥地面连接南方草原与北方高原，但河畔还没有葡萄牙牧场、小教堂或渡税卡。

18世纪初，圣保罗牧人进入坎波斯吉拉斯，卡庞阿尔托授地的时间可追溯到1704年。亚波宿地随后成为索罗卡巴路上的饮水点和夜营处，赶畜人从维亚芒驱赶牛群前往索罗卡巴大集市，索罗卡巴、桑托斯和伊图的家族也到此经营牧场。1751年，当地建起一座泥栅小教堂；1769年，加尔默罗会修士另建新教堂。1771年3月15日，中校阿方索·博特略·德·桑帕约到此巡视，聚落随后成为圣安娜-杜亚波教区，教区边界在1775年得到确认。1788年9月24日，此地从库里蒂巴划出，升格为新卡斯特鲁镇，名称来自葡萄牙海外部大臣马蒂尼奥·德·梅洛·埃卡斯特罗。到1821年，牧牛、牧场和那条漫长的赶畜道路仍决定着这座城镇的面貌。

en:
Inland beyond the Serra do Mar, the plateau broke into wide natural clearings in the Atlantic forest, grassy flats the paulistas called simply campinas. Indian peoples speaking Tupi-Guarani and Jê languages farmed mandioca, maize and beans along the watercourses and hunted the woods between. In 1444 native trails crossed this country; for more than two centuries after the first ships reached Brazil no European road ran through it.

Between 1721 and 1730 bandeirantes from the Piratininga plateau opened the Caminho dos Goiases, a trail to the new goldfields of Minas Gerais and Goiás, and the sertanista Fernão de Camargo set up a tropeiros' stopping post in a grassy clearing called Campinas do Mato Grosso. Sesmarias were granted from 1728. The chapel the settlers had asked for was marked out on 22 September 1773, and on 27 May 1774 Francisco Barreto Leme do Prado was named founder of the new nucleus; on 14 July 1774 its first mass was said and the Freguesia de Nossa Senhora da Conceição das Campinas came into being. On 14 December 1797 the settlement was detached from Jundiaí as the vila of São Carlos, later called Campinas. From the 1790s the provision farms gave way to sugarcane, encouraged by the roads built under the governor Morgado de Mateus, and Campinas became one corner of the paulista 'sugar quadrilateral' with Sorocaba, Piracicaba, Mogi-Guaçu and Jundiaí.
zh:
越过马尔山深入内陆，高原上的大西洋森林间展开大片天然草甸，圣保罗人径直称之为「坎皮纳斯」，意即草原。操图皮-瓜拉尼语和热语的印第安族群沿水道种植木薯、玉米和豆类，在林间狩猎。1444年，土著小道穿行于这片土地；首批船只抵达巴西之后的两百多年里，没有一条欧洲人开辟的道路经过此地。

1721至1730年间，皮拉蒂宁加高原的旗队开辟了通往米纳斯吉拉斯和戈亚斯新金矿区的「戈亚斯之路」，内陆开拓者费尔南·德·卡马戈在一处名叫「马托格罗索草原」的草甸上设了赶骡人歇脚点。1728年起王室开始在此分封授地。1773年9月22日，居民请愿修建的小堂划定地界；1774年5月27日，弗朗西斯科·巴雷托·莱梅·杜·普拉多被任命为新聚落的创立者，同年7月14日首场弥撒举行，「坎皮纳斯圣母无染原罪堂区」正式成立。1797年12月14日，聚落脱离容迪亚伊设镇，定名圣卡洛斯，后改称坎皮纳斯。1790年代起，在莫尔加多·德·马特乌斯总督修筑的道路网带动下，自给农庄逐渐让位于甘蔗种植，坎皮纳斯与索罗卡巴、皮拉西卡巴、莫日瓜苏和容迪亚伊一道，成为圣保罗「蔗糖四边形」的一角。

en:
Araraquara covers the open Campos de Aracoara on the central São Paulo tablelands, a country of grasslands, low hills and gallery forest. In 1444 it belonged to the Guaianás, a Macro-Jê people whose southern farming groups are counted among the ancestors of the Kaingang. They kept gardens while also hunting, fishing and gathering across the campos, and knew the sunlit ridge and plateau as Aracoara, the dwelling place of daylight. No Portuguese ranch or chapel yet stood between the Guaianá villages and the Tietê valley.

Portuguese occupation came late. Pedro José Neto, born in 1760, moved to Itu in 1787 and, after being sentenced to exile by the Itu justices, fled with his sons into the Campos de Araraquara. They built a small chapel dedicated to Saint Benedict and established cattle claims across the surrounding grasslands. On 22 August 1817 the parish of São Bento de Araraquara was created under Piracicaba, and on 30 October the settlement was raised to a district. Its early estates planted sugarcane, maize, tobacco and cotton, and raised pigs and cattle. In 1821 Araraquara was therefore only four years old as a settled parish, where São Paulo ranching expansion met the old Guaianá country.
zh:
阿拉拉夸拉位于圣保罗中部高原的阿拉科阿拉草原，四周是草地、低丘和河岸林。1444年时，这里属于瓜亚纳人；他们是大热语系族群，其中南方农耕支系被视为卡因冈人的祖先之一。瓜亚纳人既经营田园，也在草原上狩猎、捕鱼和采集，并把日照下的山脊与高原称作阿拉科阿拉，意为「日光栖居之处」。那时在瓜亚纳村落与铁特河谷之间，还没有葡萄牙牧场或小教堂。

葡萄牙人的占据来得很晚。佩德罗·若泽·内图1760年出生，1787年迁居伊图，后来被伊图法庭判处流放，便带着儿子逃入阿拉拉夸拉草原。他们建起一座供奉圣本托的小教堂，并在周围草原上取得多处牧地。1817年8月22日，隶属皮拉西卡巴的圣本托-迪阿拉拉夸拉教区设立；10月30日，聚落又被升为辖区。早期庄园种植甘蔗、玉米、烟草和棉花，也饲养猪和牛。因此到1821年，作为定居教区的阿拉拉夸拉只有四年历史，是圣保罗牧牛扩张与瓜亚纳故土相接的边地。

en:
Serro occupies a cold, broken section of the Serra do Espinhaço near the headwaters of the Jequitinhonha. The Tupi-Guarani name Ivituruí described a windy, cold hill, and in 1444 these ridges, creeks and upland camps belonged to indigenous peoples rather than to any Portuguese captaincy. No mines, roads or colonial town yet marked the country later called Serro Frio.

An expedition led by Antônio Soares Ferreira reached the area in 1701 and found gold along the Quatro Vinténs and Lucas streams. The camp was formally recorded in 1702 as Arraial do Ribeirão das Minas de Santo Antônio do Bom Retiro do Serro do Frio, and in 1714 Governor Brás Baltasar da Silveira raised it to a town as Vila do Príncipe. In 1720 it became seat of the great Serro Frio comarca, governing the north and northeast of Minas, including the future diamond camp at Tejuco. A crown foundry was ordered in 1725, forcing regional gold through official controls, while diamonds discovered around Milho Verde, São Gonçalo do Rio das Pedras and Tejuco encouraged still stricter surveillance and smuggling. By the early nineteenth century mining had declined in favour of cattle and subsistence farming; when Auguste de Saint-Hilaire visited in 1817, Vila do Príncipe had about 700 houses and 2,500 to 3,000 people, with churches rising above its amphitheatre of slopes.
zh:
塞鲁位于埃斯皮尼亚苏山脉一段寒冷崎岖的山地，靠近热基蒂尼奥尼亚河源头。图皮-瓜拉尼语称这里为伊维图鲁伊，意为多风的寒冷山丘。1444年时，这些山脊、溪流和高地营地属于印第安人，而不属于任何葡萄牙都督辖区；后来被称为塞鲁弗里乌的地方还没有矿山、道路或殖民城镇。

1701年，安东尼奥·苏亚雷斯·费雷拉率领远征队抵达此地，在夸特罗温滕斯溪和卢卡斯溪一带发现黄金。1702年，矿区被正式登记为「圣安多尼邦雷蒂鲁杜塞鲁弗里乌矿溪村」；1714年，总督布拉斯·巴尔塔萨·达西尔韦拉将其升格为镇，命名为太子镇。1720年，这里成为塞鲁弗里乌大辖区的治所，管辖米纳斯北部和东北部，包括后来的特茹科钻石营地。1725年，王室下令设立熔铸厂，把地区黄金纳入官方管制；米尔霍韦尔德、圣贡萨洛杜里奥达什佩德拉斯和特茹科一带发现钻石后，监视进一步加强，走私也随之盛行。19世纪初矿业衰落，养牛和自给农业取而代之。1817年奥古斯特·德·圣伊莱尔到访时，太子镇约有700栋房屋、2500至3000人，几座教堂耸立在层叠山坡上。

en:
The future Vila Rica, now Ouro Preto, began as steep Macro-Jê country beneath Itacolomi Peak in the Serra do Espinhaço. Indigenous villagers used the Tripuí and other mountain streams long before prospectors learned that their dark, iron-stained gravel contained exceptionally rich gold. In 1444 there was no royal road, smelter or mining arraial in these valleys; the ridges, campsites and watercourses belonged to peoples who had never encountered Portuguese tax collectors or Paulista bandeirantes.

Gold was found in the mountain streams in 1695–1696 by parties including Antônio Dias de Oliveira, Father João de Faria Fialho and Tomás Lopes de Camargo, and the rush quickly overran the valleys. The War of the Emboabas of 1707–1709 pitted Paulista pioneers against outsiders, after which the crown tightened its hold: the camps were united as Vila Rica in 1711, and the town became a judicial seat in 1714. In 1720 protests against the new foundry-house monopoly, the ban on circulating gold dust and the royal fifth brought on the Vila Rica Revolt of 28 June–19 July; the Count of Assumar crushed it and executed Filipe dos Santos, while Minas Gerais became a separate captaincy with Vila Rica as its capital. Officially recorded exports alone reached about 800 tons of gold during the eighteenth century, supporting roughly 40,000 people by 1730 and about 80,000 by mid-century. Wealth raised baroque churches and the Casa da Ópera, opened on 6 June 1770, and drew artists and poets such as Aleijadinho, Manoel da Costa Ataíde, Cláudio Manuel da Costa and Tomás António Gonzaga. As gold output declined, the derrama tax crisis fed the Inconfidência Mineira of 1788–1789; Tiradentes was arrested in 1789 and hanged on 21 April 1792. In 1821 Vila Rica remained the mountain capital of Minas Gerais.
zh:
后来的里卡镇（Vila Rica，即今欧鲁普雷图），原是埃斯皮尼亚苏山脉中伊塔科洛米峰下的大热依语族人群山地。特里普伊等山溪早为原住民村落所用，要到很久以后，探矿者才发现溪中发黑、裹着氧化铁的砾石含有极富的黄金。1444年时，这些山谷里还没有皇家大道、熔铸厂或淘金营地；山脊、营地与水道属于从未遇见葡萄牙税吏或圣保罗远征队的人群。

1695—1696年，安东尼奥·迪亚斯·德·奥利维拉、神父若昂·德·法里亚·菲亚略和托马斯·洛佩斯·德·卡马戈等人的队伍在山溪中发现黄金，淘金潮随即涌入山谷。1707—1709年的恩博阿巴斯战争使圣保罗拓殖者与外来者兵戎相见，战后王室加强控制：各营地于1711年合并为里卡镇，1714年成为司法辖区驻地。1720年，新设熔铸厂垄断、禁止金砂流通和征收五分之一金税引发6月28日至7月19日的里卡镇暴动；阿苏马尔伯爵将其镇压并处决费利佩·多斯桑托斯，米纳斯吉拉斯也在同年分设为独立都督辖区，以里卡镇为首府。仅官方登记的18世纪黄金出口就约达800吨，支撑起1730年约4万人、18世纪中叶约8万人的城市。财富带来大量巴洛克教堂和1770年6月6日开幕的歌剧院，也吸引阿列哈迪尼奥、曼努埃尔·达·科斯塔·阿塔伊德、克劳迪奥·曼努埃尔·达科斯塔、托马斯·安东尼奥·贡萨加等艺术家与诗人。随着黄金产量下降，「德拉马」摊派税危机催生1788—1789年的米纳斯密谋；蒂拉登特斯1789年被捕，1792年4月21日被处以绞刑。1821年时，里卡镇仍是米纳斯吉拉斯的山中首府。

en:
The Guaporé, called Iténez on its Spanish bank, rises in the Parecis plateau and flows west through flooded savanna and gallery forest to join the Mamoré. On its lower course, Chapacuran villagers—Chapacura, Itenes, Torá and others—cleared gardens above the annual floods, while Jê-related groups occupied the Branco, Mequens and Corumbiara valleys. They grew maize and peanuts, fished with arrows and fish poisons, and travelled the river by canoe. In 1444 the Guaporé was a native road rather than an imperial frontier: its villages controlled the crossings, fishing grounds and routes linking the river with the Mamoré and Madeira.

Spanish Jesuit missions and Portuguese gold seekers later turned the waterway into a contested border. Portugal created the captaincy of Mato Grosso in 1748, and Antônio Rolim de Moura founded Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade on the upper Guaporé in 1752. A small post, the Presídio de Nossa Senhora da Conceição, was built on the lower river in 1769 but proved too weak to secure it. Luís de Albuquerque therefore began the stone Real Forte Príncipe da Beira in April 1775; its foundation stone was laid on 20 June 1776, and work continued to 1783. Built largely with Indigenous and enslaved African labour, the fortress guarded the Guaporé-Mamoré-Madeira route and faced Spanish claims after the treaties of Madrid in 1750 and San Ildefonso in 1777. By 1821 it was a remote, fever-ridden garrison on the edge of the Portuguese Amazon.
zh:
瓜波雷河在西班牙语一侧称伊特内斯河，发源于帕雷西斯高原，向西穿过泛滥热带草原与河岸林，汇入马莫雷河。下游沿岸有查帕库拉人、伊特内斯人、托拉人等查帕库兰语族群；布兰库河、梅肯斯河和科伦比阿拉河流域则住着与热语族群相近的人群。他们在洪水线以上开辟田园，种植玉米和花生，用箭和鱼药捕鱼，并以独木舟往来河面。1444年时，瓜波雷还不是帝国边界，而是原住民自己的水路；沿岸村落掌握着渡口、渔场和通往马莫雷河、马代拉河的航路。

后来，西班牙耶稣会传教站和寻找黄金的葡萄牙人把这条水道变成相争的边地。葡萄牙于1748年设立马托格罗索都督辖区，安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1752年在上瓜波雷建立维拉贝拉-达桑蒂西马特林达迪。1769年，葡萄牙人在下瓜波雷修筑圣母受孕哨所，却不足以稳固航道。路易斯·德·阿尔布克尔克遂于1775年4月动工兴建石砌的贝拉亲王皇家堡垒，1776年6月20日安放基石，工程持续到1783年。堡垒主要由原住民和非洲奴工劳动建成，守护瓜波雷—马莫雷—马代拉航路，与1750年《马德里条约》和1777年《圣伊尔德方索条约》后仍反复争执的西班牙势力隔河相望。到1821年，这里已是葡萄牙亚马孙边缘一处偏远、瘴疠流行的驻军地。

en:
Cerejeiras lies about 45 kilometres north of the Guaporé, on rolling ground in southern Rondônia where the Corumbiara, Mequens and neighbouring streams drain south toward the border river. In 1444 its gardens and hunting grounds belonged to Jê-related peoples of those tributary valleys, while Chapacuran villagers lived closer to the Guaporé itself. They planted maize and peanuts, gathered Brazil nuts in season, fished with arrows and poisons, and used canoes on the main rivers. No European post yet stood between their villages and the river crossings.

The Spaniard Ñuflo de Chávez crossed the Guaporé valley in 1541-42, and Portuguese bandeirantes entered the region around 1650. After gold was found on the river's right bank, the Portuguese Crown created the captaincy of Mato Grosso in 1748. Local history records a camp made by Antônio Rolim de Moura on this stretch of the Guaporé in 1750; fugitive slaves from Vila Bela later occupied it, and the place became a supply point for traffic descending the river. Work on the stone Príncipe da Beira fortress downstream began in 1775 and continued to 1783, securing the main waterway rather than turning Cerejeiras's inland country into a town. In 1821 it remained a thinly travelled corridor between the Mato Grosso mines and the Madeira route.
zh:
塞雷热拉斯位于瓜波雷河以北约45公里，地处龙多尼亚南缘缓丘，科伦比亚拉河、梅肯斯河及邻近溪流由此南注界河。1444年，这里的田园和猎场属于这些支流河谷中与热语族群相近的人群，靠近瓜波雷干流处则住着查帕库兰语村民。他们种植玉米和花生，按季采集巴西坚果，用箭和鱼药捕鱼，并在主要河道上使用独木舟。那时在他们的村落与各渡口之间，还没有欧洲人的常设据点。

西班牙人努夫洛·德·查韦斯于1541年至1542年穿过瓜波雷河谷，葡萄牙旗队约在1650年进入这一带。瓜波雷右岸发现黄金后，葡萄牙王室于1748年设立马托格罗索都督辖区。当地史记载，安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1750年曾在这段瓜波雷河畔扎营；后来从维拉贝拉逃出的奴工占据此地，使它成为顺河下航者的补给点。下游石砌的贝拉亲王堡1775年开工、1783年仍在营建，锁住的是干流航道，并未把塞雷热拉斯的内陆林地变成城镇。1821年时，这里仍是马托格罗索金矿区与马代拉航路之间一条人烟稀少的走廊。

en:
Vila Bela lies on the upper Guaporé, where streams from the Parecis plateau gather before the river runs west toward the Bolivian plains. Gallery forest, cerrado and the ridges of the Serra de Ricardo Franco divide the country. In 1444 this was Nambikwara land: mobile Sararé, Kabixi and other bands moved between the Guaporé and Juruena headwaters, hunting, gathering and shifting camp through forest and savanna, while Chiquitano peoples held the plains and hills farther west. The river supplied fish and crossings, but no Portuguese tax house, town or permanent garrison yet controlled the valley.

Gold seekers reached the upper Guaporé in 1733-34, and in 1742 Manuel Félix de Lima descended the Guaporé, Madeira and Amazon to Belém, opening a long supply route. Diamonds were found in Mato Grosso in 1747, and the Portuguese Crown created the Captaincy of Mato Grosso on 9 May 1748. Its first governor, Antônio Rolim de Moura, arrived in 1751 and installed Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade as his capital on 19 March 1752. A mining-tax office followed, while Rolim expelled Spanish missionaries, made Indigenous alliances, opened roads toward Maranhão and Bahia, and promoted sugar cultivation. The treaties of Madrid in 1750 and San Ildefonso in 1777 framed the rivalry with Spain. On 28 February 1821 Mato Grosso became a province; after Governor Magessi was deposed on 20 August, Vila Bela raised its own junta alongside the junta in Cuiabá.
zh:
维拉贝拉位于上瓜波雷：帕雷西斯高原的溪流在此汇合，瓜波雷河随后西向玻利维亚平原。河岸林、热带稀树草原与里卡多·佛朗哥山的山脊把这片土地分隔开来。1444年时，这里是南比夸拉人的土地，萨拉拉、卡比希等游群在瓜波雷河与茹鲁埃纳河源头之间迁徙，在森林和草原间狩猎、采集、移营；更西的平原和丘陵则属于奇基托斯人。河流提供鱼获与渡口，但谷中还没有葡萄牙税务所、城镇或常设驻军。

1733年至1734年，寻金者进入上瓜波雷；1742年，曼努埃尔·费利克斯·德·利马顺瓜波雷河、马代拉河和亚马孙河下航至贝伦，开辟了一条漫长补给线。1747年马托格罗索发现钻石，葡萄牙王室遂于1748年5月9日设立马托格罗索都督辖区。首任都督安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1751年到任，1752年3月19日把维拉贝拉-达桑蒂西马特林达迪定为辖区首府。此地随后设立矿税机构，罗林驱逐西班牙传教士、与原住民结盟、开辟通往马拉尼昂和巴伊亚的道路，并推动甘蔗种植；1750年《马德里条约》和1777年《圣伊尔德方索条约》则界定着葡萄牙与西班牙的争夺框架。1821年2月28日，马托格罗索改为省；8月20日都督马热西被推翻后，维拉贝拉与库亚巴各自成立政务会。

en:
The future Cáceres lies on the upper Paraguay at the edge of the Pantanal, where seasonal floods turn grassland and riverine woods into a maze of channels. Guató people moved through these waters as canoe builders, fishermen and archers, living mainly in small family groups rather than large villages. In 1444 the Paraguay was their road between fishing grounds and temporary camps, and no Portuguese or Spanish frontier post yet stood on the bank.

On 6 October 1778 the dragoon officer Antônio Pinto Rego e Carvalho founded Vila Maria do Paraguai by order of Luís de Albuquerque de Melo Pereira e Cáceres, governor of Mato Grosso. The post was meant to check Spanish and indigenous raids, protect river navigation, and connect Vila Bela and Cuiabá with São Paulo by way of the Paraguay. Its first settlers included scattered couples and sixty Indians brought from the Castilian mission of Chiquitos; houses, a church and a council-and-prison building were laid out near a chapel dedicated to Saint Louis. By 1809 Vila Maria held a Royal Warehouse of arms, tools, food and boat equipment, serving the captaincy as a small military river port.
zh:
后来的卡塞雷斯位于巴拉圭河上游、潘塔纳尔沼泽边缘；季节性洪水会把草原与河畔林地变成纵横水网。瓜托人擅长造船、捕鱼和射箭，多以小型家族群体活动，而不是聚居成大型村落。1444年时，巴拉圭河是他们往来渔场和临时营地的通路，河岸上还没有葡萄牙或西班牙的边防据点。

1778年10月6日，龙骑兵军官安东尼奥·平托·雷戈·埃·卡瓦略奉马托格罗索总督路易斯·德·阿尔布克尔克·德·梅洛·佩雷拉·埃·卡塞雷斯之命，建立巴拉圭河畔玛丽亚镇。这个据点用来抵御西班牙人和原住民的袭扰、保护河运，并经巴拉圭河把维拉贝拉、库亚巴与圣保罗联系起来。最早的居民包括分散的夫妇，以及从西班牙人管辖的奇基托斯传教区招来的六十名印第安人；住宅区、教堂、议会兼监狱围绕圣路易小堂规划。到1809年，玛丽亚镇设有皇家仓库，储存武器、工具、粮食和船只装备，是都督辖区的一座小型军用河港。

en:
Diamantino lies on the broken southern foothills of the Parecis plateau, where the Diamantino and Ouro streams descend toward the Paraguay while other valleys feed the Arinos and the Amazon. Pareci, or Haliti, Arino and neighbouring peoples moved through this cerrado and riverine-forest country, using the waterways to hunt, fish and keep distant communities in contact. In 1444 the gravel of the Ouro had not yet drawn Portuguese miners, and the plateau remained an indigenous borderland between the Amazon and Paraguay worlds.

On 18 September 1728 Gabriel Antunes Maciel found gold in the Ribeirão do Ouro and reported the strike to Cuiabá, creating the Arraial do Ouro, later called Félix. Precious stones then drew the Portuguese crown's attention: it imposed a strict monopoly, closed workings and stationed the Destacamento Diamantino do Paraguai against clandestine prospectors. The settlement nevertheless endured as a supply centre, with paranista boatmen carrying local trade north to Pará along the Arinos. On 9 August 1811 the parish of Our Lady of the Conception of Alto Paraguai Diamantino was created, its mistaken name reflecting the explorers' belief that they were near the Paraguay's headwaters. A royal charter raised Diamantino to vila status on 23 November 1820.
zh:
迪亚曼蒂努位于帕雷西斯高原崎岖的南缘，迪亚曼蒂努河与金溪的水流朝巴拉圭河方向下行，另一些谷地则汇入阿里努斯河并通向亚马孙流域。帕雷西人（自称哈利蒂人）、阿里努人及邻近族群穿行在这片塞拉多草原与河畔林地之间，借水道狩猎、捕鱼，并维系分散社群的联系。1444年时，金溪的砂砾还没有引来葡萄牙淘金者，高原仍是亚马孙世界与巴拉圭世界之间的原住民边地。

1728年9月18日，加布里埃尔·安图内斯·马西埃尔在金溪发现黄金并向库亚巴议会报告，金溪营地由此形成，后来又称费利克斯。宝石随后引起葡萄牙王室注意：王室实行严格专卖、封闭矿场，并设置迪亚曼蒂努·杜·巴拉圭支队缉拿私采者。尽管如此，定居点仍作为补给中心延续下来，「巴拉尼斯塔」船工沿阿里努斯河把本地贸易向北送往帕拉。1811年8月9日，上巴拉圭·迪亚曼蒂努圣母受孕教区设立；这个名字来自探险者的地理误判，他们以为自己已靠近巴拉圭河源头。1820年11月23日，王室特许状将迪亚曼蒂努升格为镇。

en:
The Rio das Mortes, also called the Manso, rises in the Serra de São Lourenço and runs roughly 1,200 kilometres through the Mato Grosso cerrado before joining the Araguaia. In 1444 its valley formed the northern edge of the wide Bororo world, whose villages and hunting grounds reached from the Paraguay eastward toward the Araguaia. The river gave fish, crossing places and seasonal camps, while its banks were known to Bororo travellers and neighbouring peoples; no Portuguese miner or slaver had yet mapped them.

Around 1660 slaving bandeiras began crossing this country. In 1673 Bartolomeu Bueno da Silva and Antônio Pires de Campos, then still young, claimed to have seen the gold-rich land of Araés and the Serra dos Martírios while accompanying their fathers; forty years later the story sent expeditions into the interior. Bartolomeu marched out in July 1722 with 300 men and returned on 21 October 1725 with only sixteen, finding Goiás gold rather than the legendary place. In 1745 Amaro Leite Moreira's party struck gold in northern Mato Grosso and raised a small camp named Araés, soon renamed Santo Antônio do Amarante. Poor communications with Cuiabá, failing deposits and indigenous attacks forced its abandonment in 1789. Other placer camps along the Rio das Mortes were also deserted after the easy gold ended, leaving the valley without a Portuguese town in 1821.
zh:
莫尔蒂斯河又称曼苏河，发源于圣洛伦索山，穿过马托格罗索的塞拉多草原约1200千米后注入阿拉瓜亚河。1444年时，河谷构成广阔博罗罗人地域的北缘；他们的村落与猎场西起巴拉圭河一带，东抵阿拉瓜亚河。河流提供鱼产、渡口和季节性营地，博罗罗旅行者与邻近族群熟悉河岸，葡萄牙淘金者或奴隶贩子还不曾测绘这里。

1660年前后，捕奴旗队开始进入这片地方。1673年，尚在年少的巴托洛梅乌·布埃诺·达·席尔瓦和安东尼奥·皮雷斯·德·坎波斯随父亲的远征队出行，声称见到盛产黄金的阿赖埃斯和马蒂里奥斯山；四十年后，这段说法把多支探险队引向内陆。1722年7月，巴托洛梅乌率三百人出发，1725年10月21日只剩十六人归来；他们没有找到传说之地，却在戈亚斯发现黄金。1745年，阿马罗·莱特·莫雷拉的队伍在马托格罗索北部找到金矿，建起名为阿赖埃斯的小营地，不久改称圣安东尼奥·杜·阿马兰蒂。由于与库亚巴交通困难、矿脉衰竭且不断遭到原住民攻击，村民在1789年弃村。莫尔蒂斯河沿岸其他砂金营地也在易采黄金耗尽后荒废，到1821年，河谷中仍没有葡萄牙人城镇。

en:
Iporá is the western Goiás cerrado, the headwater country of the Rio Claro and the Caiapó, whose streams run south to the Paranaíba; Iporá itself is a later Tupi name meaning 'clear waters'. In 1444 this was Xavante land, held by Jê-speaking hunters and gardeners whose villages lay between the Araguaia and the Tocantins, with the Ofaié beyond the southern rivers. No mule road or mining camp had yet entered it.

The frontier arrived in the 1730s, when the São Paulo entrepreneurs Joaquim and Felisberto Caldeira Brant worked gold strikes across western Goiás. In 1748 a troop of dragoons was posted on the right bank of the Rio Claro at the Arraial de Pilões, guarding the brothers' diamond workings; the garrison raised a barracks, the parish church of Senhor Jesus do Bom Fim and the ranchos of the garimpeiros. Diamonds proved thin, and Pilões lived on as the trading post on the overland road between Vila Boa and Cuiabá. The surrounding sertão stayed in Xavante hands through the colonial wars, until Tristão da Cunha's 'pacification' campaigns of 1794-1798 broke the villages.
zh:
伊波拉是戈亚斯西部的塞拉多，克拉鲁河与卡亚波河发源于此，溪水南流汇入巴拉那伊巴河；「伊波拉」是后来的图皮语地名，意为「清水」。1444年，这里是沙万特人的土地：这些说热依语的猎手和农人把村落散建在阿拉瓜亚河与托坎廷斯河之间，河南更远则是奥法耶人的地盘。此时还没有一条骡道或采矿营地进入此地。

边疆在1730年代到来：圣保罗商人若阿金·卡尔德拉·布兰特与费利斯贝托·卡尔德拉·布兰特兄弟在西戈亚斯各地开采金矿。1748年，一队龙骑兵驻守克拉鲁河右岸的皮隆伊斯营地，护卫兄弟二人的钻石开采；驻军建起营房、善终耶稣教区教堂和矿工棚屋。钻石储量微薄，皮隆伊斯便靠博阿镇与库亚巴之间陆上通道的商站维持。周围腹地在殖民冲突中始终留在沙万特人手中，直到1794至1798年特里斯坦·达库尼亚的「绥靖」征讨打散了各村落。

en:
Vila Boa huddles in the Serra Dourada, on the Rio Vermelho, a headwater running west to the Araguaia. The cerrado around it was the country of the Goiá, a Jê-speaking nation whose name the whole inland region came to bear. They planted maize and manioc in forest gardens and hunted the savanna, their streams already yielding the alluvial gold the bandeirantes would one day seize. In 1444 the Portuguese had yet to reach this inland country, and the Serra Dourada held Goiá villages.

Gold gave the town its birth. Bartolomeu Bueno da Silva, the second Anhanguera — 'old devil' in Tupi — had first crossed the sertão with his father in 1682; setting out again from São Paulo in 1722, he searched for nearly three years and struck rich gravels in the Rio Vermelho in 1725. Named captain-major of the mines in 1726, he laid out the Arraial de Sant'Anna in 1727; a royal order in 1736 called for its elevation, and Vila Boa de Goiás was formally established in 1739. The Captaincy of Goiás was created on 9 May 1748, with Vila Boa its capital; its first governor, Dom Marcos de Noronha, took office on 8 November 1749. Its early government built the Casa de Fundição, the royal gold foundry, in 1750 and the Palácio Conde dos Arcos in 1751. The Casa de Câmara e Cadeia rose in 1761. As gold ran out late in the century, Governor Luís da Cunha Meneses, in office from 1778 to 1783, planted avenues and aligned the streets, leaving the shrinking town the quiet grid of adobe houses and baroque churches that suited its turn to ranching. On 28 February 1821 the captaincy became a province, with Vila Boa still its seat.
zh:
博阿镇（Vila Boa de Goiás，今戈亚斯城）深藏在多拉达山中，傍着西流注入阿拉瓜亚河的红河。四周的塞拉多本是热依语族群戈亚人的家园，后来整个内陆地区都因他们得名。戈亚人在林地里种玉米和木薯，在草原上狩猎，河溪里的沙金后来正是旗手们要夺取之物。1444年，葡萄牙人尚未抵达这片内陆，多拉达山中有戈亚人的村落。

黄金催生了这座城镇。第二位「阿年古埃拉」（图皮语意为「老魔鬼」）巴托洛梅乌·布埃诺·达席尔瓦1682年就随父亲穿过这片腹地；1722年他再从圣保罗出发，寻觅近三年，于1725年在红河挖到富矿。1726年他被任命为矿区总兵，1727年辟建圣安娜营地；1736年王室下令设镇，1739年戈亚斯的博阿镇正式成立。1748年5月9日戈亚斯都督府设立，博阿镇即为首府；首任都督多姆·马科斯·德·诺罗尼亚于1749年11月8日就任。都督府初年于1750年建成王家铸金局、1751年建成阿科斯伯爵宫。市政暨监狱大厦建于1761年。18世纪末金沙渐尽，1778至1783年在任的都督路易斯·达库尼亚·梅内塞斯沿街植树、裁齐道路，让这座收缩中的小城变成土屋与巴洛克教堂组成的宁静棋盘，与它转向畜牧的命运相称。1821年2月28日都督府改为行省，博阿镇仍为省会。

en:
Arraial dos Couros is the high cerrado on the eastern rim of the Goiás plateau, around the Lagoa Feia, whose streams feed the Paranã and where the Itiquira river leaps off the plateau edge. In 1444 this was Jê country: Caiapó and Xavante bands moved through the gallery woods and grasslands between the Paranã headwaters and the São Francisco, and no Portuguese road had yet climbed onto the plateau.

It became a road before it became a town. In February 1736 the crown planted a toll and customs post, the Registro da Lagoa Feia, to tax the gold moving from the Goiás mines toward Bahia and Minas Gerais. Settlers soon drifted up from the Arraial de Santo Antônio do Itiquira, a Paranã-valley camp thinned by killing fevers; with muleteers who camped in leather shelters on the cool upland they formed the Arraial dos Couros in 1749, the 'leather camp', perhaps named for the wild hides traded there. Attached to the comarca of Santa Luzia, it became the chief station on the Bahia road, where tropeiros traded leather and cattle for mining tools and salt. Through 1821 it remained a rough waystation on the long haul between the mines and the coast.
zh:
阿拉亚尔-杜斯科鲁斯（Arraial dos Couros，意为「皮革营地」，即今福莫萨）坐落在戈亚斯高原东缘的高地，费亚湖一带的溪流汇入帕拉南河，伊蒂基拉河在高原边缘纵身跌落。1444年，这里是热依语族群的土地：卡亚波人与沙万特人的队伍穿行于帕拉南河源与圣弗朗西斯科河之间的林带和草原，葡萄牙人的道路还没有登上高原。

这里先成通衢，后有村镇。1736年2月，葡萄牙王室设立费亚湖税卡（Registro da Lagoa Feia），对从戈亚斯金矿区运往巴伊亚和米纳斯吉拉斯的黄金抽税。不久，帕拉南河谷中被热病掏空的圣安东尼奥-杜伊蒂基拉营地居民陆续迁来，与在凉爽高地支起皮帐歇脚的骡夫汇合，于1749年聚成阿拉亚尔-杜斯科鲁斯——「皮革营地」，可能得名于当地贩卖的野皮。它在行政上隶属圣卢齐亚区，逐渐成为巴伊亚商路上的首要驿站，骡队在这里用皮革和牲畜换取矿具与食盐。直到1821年，它始终是矿区与海岸之间漫长驮路上一座粗粝的驿站。

en:
Conceição lies in the high cerrado of the Tocantins-Araguaia basin, above the valley later called São João da Palma. In 1444 this was Jê country: small communities opened gardens in woodland clearings, hunted the grasslands, and shifted camp with the seasons, while the rivers and ridges kept Portuguese expeditions still far to the south and east.

Gold-seekers moving north from Goiás reached the district in the mid-eighteenth century. In 1741 Manoel Paes Andrade settled near a placer mine and had enslaved workers build a house and a church dedicated to Our Lady of the Conception. The Contagem de Conceição became a fiscal post for traffic to the northern mines, and in 1755 the settlement was raised to a parish. Gold washing, cattle ranching, and the slow rhythm of a remote mining parish marked its life until 1821.
zh:
康塞桑位于托坎廷斯-阿拉瓜亚流域的高位塞拉多，俯临后来被称为圣若昂-达帕尔马的河谷。1444年，这里是热依族群的土地：小型社群在林中空地开辟园圃，在草原狩猎，并随季节迁移营地；河流与山脊使葡萄牙远征队仍远在南方和东方之外。

18世纪中叶，从戈亚斯北上的淘金者进入这一地区。1741年，曼努埃尔·派斯·安德拉德在一处砂金矿附近定居，驱使被奴役者修建住宅和献给无玷始胎圣母的教堂。康塞桑税务站成为往来北方矿区的征税点，1755年定居点升格为堂区。直到1821年，砂金淘洗、牧牛和偏远采矿堂区的缓慢节奏，构成了这里的生活。

en:
Pontal takes its name from a point of land on the left bank of the Tocantins, in country later drawn into the mining frontier of northern Goiás. In 1444 the river and surrounding cerrado were Jê land. The Akwẽ-Xerente and related Central Jê peoples kept villages along the Tocantins, hunting, fishing, planting seasonal gardens, and moving across ground that no Portuguese expedition had yet secured.

The gold rush from Goiás reached this stretch after Natividade was founded in 1734. The Arraial de Bom Jesus do Pontal grew as a mining camp. The Presídio da Matança watched nearby trails and river traffic, while gold moved by canoe and pack train. By the late eighteenth century the placers were thinning, cattle and crops mattered more, and the Porto Real crossing drew trade away. In 1821 the old arraial remained a small settlement beside the rising river port.
zh:
蓬塔尔得名于托坎廷斯河左岸的一块尖角地，后来被卷入北戈亚斯的淘金边疆。1444年，托坎廷斯河与周围的塞拉多仍是热依人的土地。谢伦特人（Akwẽ）及相近的中央热依族群在河畔建立村落，狩猎、捕鱼、开辟季节园圃，并在尚未被葡萄牙远征队控制的土地上往来。

纳蒂维达于1734年建立后，戈亚斯的淘金潮推进到这一河段，邦热苏斯-杜蓬塔尔成为一处淘金营地。马唐萨要塞监视附近道路与河上交通，黄金则靠独木舟和驮队运出。18世纪末，砂金日渐稀少，牧牛和农耕变得更加重要，波尔图雷亚尔渡口又吸走贸易。到1821年，旧营地仍是崛起河港旁的一座小聚落。

en:
Natividade lies beneath the Serra da Natividade, in the southeastern Tocantins cerrado where highland streams drain toward the Tocantins basin. In 1444 it was Xavante country. Central Jê villagers kept seasonal gardens and hunting grounds and controlled the trails between ridges and river valleys, long before the Goiás gold frontier entered their lands.

That frontier advanced between 1724 and 1734. In the latter year Antônio Ferraz de Araújo founded the Arraial de São Luiz atop the serra, naming it for Governor Dom Luís de Mascarenhas; devotion to Our Lady of the Nativity later gave the town its present name. Enslaved workers washed gold from its streams, mule caravans carried the metal toward Salvador, and Natividade became one of Goiás's largest mining camps, surpassed only by Pirenópolis. Later in the eighteenth century enslaved builders began the soapstone church of Nossa Senhora do Rosário dos Pretos, still unfinished when Pohl saw it in 1819. A royal charter in 1809 made the camp provisional seat of the new Comarca do Norte. By 1821 cattle were replacing the exhausted placers.
zh:
纳蒂维达位于纳蒂维达山脚下，地处托坎廷斯东南部的塞拉多，山地溪流汇入托坎廷斯流域。1444年，这里是沙万特人的土地。中央热依村民经营季节园圃和猎场，控制着山脊与河谷之间的小路；那时戈亚斯淘金边疆尚未进入他们的土地。

1724年至1734年间，这条淘金边疆向前推进。1734年，安东尼奥·费拉斯·德·阿劳若在山顶建立圣路易斯营地，以总督唐·路易斯·德·马斯卡伦哈斯命名；后来对圣诞圣母的敬奉使城镇改用今名。被奴役者在溪流中淘金，骡队把黄金运往萨尔瓦多，纳蒂维达也成为戈亚斯最大的采矿营地之一，仅次于皮雷诺波利斯。18世纪后期，被奴役的工匠开始建造皂石教堂黑人玫瑰圣母堂；1819年波尔见到它时，工程仍未完工。1809年的王室敕令设立北方司法区，营地成为临时驻地。到1821年，牧牛正取代枯竭的砂金矿。

en:
In 1444 the land between the lower São Francisco and the Sergipe river was held by Tupinambá tribes, whose coastal villages grew manioc and gathered crabs in the mangroves — the river's Old Tupi name Siriîype means 'river of crabs'. By the early sixteenth century French brazilwood smugglers were already bartering with its people. The Portuguese Crown counted the coast as part of the Captaincy of Bahia, but the Tupinambá kept settlers out for decades, rising against slaving expeditions until the campaigns of the 1580s broke their resistance.

Conquest came only in 1590, when Cristóvão de Barros defeated the river tribes and founded São Cristóvão on New Year's Day, seat of the new Captaincy of Sergipe d'El-Rey. Sugar mills worked by enslaved Africans spread through the Cotinguiba valley, while cattle ranches and leather works occupied the drier interior, and French buccaneers raided the coast for its prized hardwood. Dutch troops sacked and burned São Cristóvão in 1637, and the land remained under Dutch Brazil until the Portuguese recovered it in 1645. Sergipe became a separate captaincy in 1696, was reannexed to Bahia in 1763, and on 8 July 1820 João VI restored its autonomy, with São Cristóvão the seat of the reborn captaincy.
zh:
1444年，圣弗朗西斯科河下游与塞尔希培河之间的土地属于图皮南巴诸部落，他们的滨海村落种植木薯、在红树林中捕蟹——塞尔希培河的古图皮语名「西里伊佩」意为「蟹河」。到16世纪初，走私巴西木的法国商人已来此与土著以物易物。葡萄牙王室把这片海岸算作巴伊亚都督辖区的一部分，但图皮南巴人数十年间将殖民者拒之门外，并起兵反抗掳奴远征，直到1580年代的历次战役才被压服。

征服迟至1590年才到来：克里斯托旺·德·巴罗斯击败沿河诸部，于元旦建立圣克里斯托旺，作为新设「王家塞尔希培」都督辖区的首府。使用非洲奴隶劳作的糖坊遍布科廷吉巴河谷，干旱内陆则兴起牧场和皮革业，法国海盗还为掠夺珍贵硬木频频袭扰海岸。1637年，荷兰军队洗劫并焚毁圣克里斯托旺，此后这片土地处于荷兰巴西治下，直到1645年被葡萄牙收复。塞尔希培1696年成为独立都督辖区，1763年被重新并入巴伊亚，1820年7月8日若昂六世恢复其自治，圣克里斯托旺仍是重生都督辖区的首府。

en:
Jeremoabo lies in the dry sertão of northern Bahia, where caatinga scrub and the stony Raso da Catarina are crossed by the Vaza-Barris River. In 1444 this was Tupinambá country; its later recorded Tupi name, Yuru'mún-yba, referred to a pumpkin plant and belonged to the language of the villagers who kept clearings, hunting grounds and trails through the backlands.

Cattle ranches tied to Garcia d'Ávila's Casa da Torre entered the region in the seventeenth century. In the 1660s the priests Jacob Roland and João de Barros founded the Geremoabo mission to catechize and protect the local people. By 1698 Geremoabo had the standing of a julgado.
zh:
热雷莫阿布位于巴伊亚北部干旱的内陆荒原，卡廷加灌丛和多石的卡塔里纳裸地被瓦扎巴里斯河切过。1444年，这里是图皮南巴人的土地；后来记载下来的图皮语名尤鲁蒙伊巴（Yuru'mún-yba）意为南瓜植株，来自这片腹地中经营垦地、猎场和小径的村民所说的语言。

17世纪，与加西亚·达维拉的卡萨达托雷相连的牧场进入这一地区。1660年代，神父雅各布·罗兰和若昂·德巴罗斯建立热雷莫阿布传教站，向当地人传教并提供保护。到1698年，热雷莫阿布已具备司法辖区地位。

en:
Inhambupe lies inland of the Bay of All Saints, among the rolling agreste woods that separate the sugar coast from the dry sertão. The river threading the district bears a Tupi name, 'among the waters of the inhambu', a forest tinamou, but in 1444 its valleys belong to Tapuia bands, the non-Tupi, Jê-speaking hunters and gatherers whom the coastal peoples lumped together as Tapuia, 'strangers'. They moved between riverside camps, taking game and wild fruits, with no European yet within a thousand leagues.

From the late 1500s cattle herds moved up these valleys: the Casa da Torre, the ranching empire founded near Salvador by Garcia d'Ávila, drove cattle along the royal road into the sertão to supply beef and leather to the coastal sugar mills, and its vaqueiros mixed with, or enslaved, the Tapuia as they went. Jesuits had already settled at Água Fria in 1562, and the whole district long depended on that town for justice and worship. A hermitage of the Holy Spirit formed the nucleus of Inhambupe, and in 1718 the parish of Divino Espírito Santo do Inhambupe de Cima was created; by 1757 it ran three filial chapels, and in the 1780s tobacco spread alongside the cattle lands. The governor of Bahia, Fernando José de Portugal, authorized a town in 1798, and the Vila do Inhambupe was installed in 1801.
zh:
伊尼扬布皮位于万圣湾内陆，地处沿海蔗区与干旱腹地之间的阿格雷斯特疏林丘陵间。贯穿此地的河流有一个图皮语名字，意为「在伊尼扬布鸟——一种林栖鸟——出没的水畔」；1444年时，河谷属于塔普亚诸部，即沿海民族笼统称为「塔普亚」（意为外族人）的非图皮、操热语的狩猎采集者。他们在河畔营地间迁徙，猎取野味、采集野果，此时欧洲人远在千里之外。

16世纪末起，牛群沿这些河谷上行：加西亚·德阿维拉在萨尔瓦多附近建立的牧业世家「塔楼庄园」沿王家大道把牛赶入腹地，为沿海糖坊供应牛肉和皮革，牧人一路与塔普亚人通婚，或将其掠为奴隶。早在1562年，耶稣会已在阿瓜弗里亚落脚，整个地区的司法与宗教事务长期隶属该镇。一座圣灵小圣堂成为伊尼扬布皮的核心，1718年「上伊尼扬布皮圣灵教区」正式设立，到1757年已下辖三座附属小教堂，1780年代烟草种植随牧场一同扩张。1798年，巴伊亚总督费尔南多·若泽·德·葡萄牙批准设镇，伊尼扬布皮镇于1801年正式建立。

en:
Pambu names a stretch of the northern Bahian sertão, where caatinga backlands reach the islands and banks of the lower-middle São Francisco. In 1444 this country was held by the various Indigenous groups the Portuguese later called Tapuia; its camps, hunting grounds and river crossings would also be remembered through the Tumbalalá, a people historically connected with the Kariri and Procá and with the old aldeia of Pambu.

The bandeira of Belchior Dias founded the settlement of Pambu as an Indigenous aldeia, and in the seventeenth century cattle ranges and river missions drew the Rodelas sertão into Bahia's colonial frontier. In 1809 a new ranch chapel, Bom Jesus da Boa Morte, became another nucleus in the same thinly peopled borderland.
zh:
帕姆布指巴伊亚北部内陆荒原的一片土地，卡廷加旱地在这里延伸至圣弗朗西斯科河中下游的岛洲与河岸。1444年，这片地方由后来被葡萄牙人统称为塔普亚人的多个原住民族群占据；他们的营地、猎场和渡口，也通过通巴拉拉人留存于记忆中——通巴拉拉人在历史上与卡里里人、普罗卡人及旧帕姆布传教村联系在一起。

贝尔希奥尔·迪亚斯的远征队建立帕姆布定居点，把它作为原住民传教村；17世纪，牧牛场和河畔传教站使罗德拉斯腹地被纳入巴伊亚殖民边疆。1809年，新的邦热苏斯-达博阿莫尔特牧场礼拜堂形成，成为这个人烟稀少的边地中的又一个定居核心。

en:
Rio de Contas takes its name from the upper valleys of the Contas Pequeno, the old name of the Brumado, where the cool ridges of the Chapada Diamantina rise above the Bahian sertão. In 1444 only Indians know these mountains. Pataxó bands, peoples of the Macro-Jê family, ranged between the Contas and the Pardo, hunting the gallery forests and camping above the valley mists.

Cattle came first: in the seventeenth century the Bahian sertanista Antônio Guedes de Brito drove herds into these high valleys, and around mid-century freed and runaway Africans founded a quilombo, Pouso dos Crioulos, on the Brumado. An expedition from the coast reached it in 1690, when it was already a halting place on the trail from Minas Gerais to Salvador. Then in 1710 the São Paulo bandeirante Sebastião Pinheiro Raposo struck alluvial gold in the Brumado and its streams, and a rush of Portuguese, Paulistas and Pernambucans threw up the camps of Mato Grosso and Livramento; Mato Grosso became the first parish of the alto sertão in 1718. A royal charter of 27 November 1723 created the Vila de Nossa Senhora do Livramento das Minas do Rio de Contas, installed in 1724 by Pedro Barbosa Leal; a royal road to Jacobina followed in 1725 and a crown foundry to collect the royal fifth in 1726. Fever in the riverside seat moved the viceroy to order its transfer in 1745, and in July 1746 the planned Vila Nova was laid out at Pouso dos Crioulos. Enslaved miners worked its gold until the washings petered out early in the next century, when the town fell back on stock-raising, crops and the traffic of the royal road.
zh:
里奥孔塔斯得名于孔塔斯河上游谷地——该河旧称小孔塔斯河，即今布鲁马杜河——迪亚曼蒂纳高原的清凉山脊在此耸立于巴伊亚腹地之上。1444年时，只有印第安人熟悉这片群山：属大热语族的帕塔肖诸部游猎于孔塔斯河与帕尔多河之间的长廊林中，在谷雾之上扎营。

先来的是牛群：17世纪，巴伊亚腹地开拓者安东尼奥·格德斯·德·布里托把牧群赶进这些高山谷地；约在17世纪中叶，获得自由的黑奴与逃亡者在布鲁马杜河畔建起一处逃亡者聚落，名叫「克里奥尔人驿站」。1690年，一支沿海远征队抵达该地，当时它已是米纳斯吉拉斯通往萨尔瓦多商路上的宿营地。1710年，圣保罗旗兵塞巴斯蒂昂·皮涅罗·拉波索在布鲁马杜河及其支流淘得沙金，葡萄牙人、圣保罗人和伯南布哥人蜂拥而至，建起马托格罗索与利夫拉门托两处淘金营地；马托格罗索于1718年成为巴伊亚高地的第一个教区。1723年11月27日的王旨敕设「孔塔斯河金矿圣母利夫拉门托镇」，1724年由佩德罗·巴尔博扎·莱阿尔主持建镇，1725年修通通往雅科比纳的王家大道，1726年又设王室熔金所以征收五一税。因河畔镇址热病流行，副王于1745年下令迁治，1746年7月按规划在克里奥尔人驿站建成新镇。黑奴矿工在此淘采黄金，直到19世纪初砂金渐竭，城镇转而依靠畜牧、农耕和王家大道上的往来商旅。

en:
Paratinga occupies a crossing on the middle São Francisco, where the river cuts through caatinga and gives access to overland trails through western Bahia. In 1444 the banks were Indigenous country; Tuxá people are thought to have predominated around Paratinga, while other peoples of the middle river used its islands, fishing grounds and inland trails. No permanent Portuguese settlement yet existed.

Portuguese expeditions passed through between 1543 and 1550, when Duarte Coelho Pereira visited the region, and the bandeirante Belchior Dias Moreia crossed it in 1602. Permanent colonization followed in the seventeenth century after Antônio Guedes de Brito received vast sesmarias and formed the Casa da Ponte, the second-largest latifundium in colonial Brazil; its expansion destroyed much of the middle-river Indigenous population and enslaved survivors. On the Santo Antônio do Urubu de Cima ranch, a chapel of Saint Anthony built in 1680 became the nucleus of Urubu, whose inhabitants included Luso-Brazilians, Indigenous people and Africans. By 1714 it had 362 households and 3,425 people, and on 11 April 1718 it became a parish. Cattle herds rested there between Bahia and Minas Gerais; John V ordered a town in 1746, and Vila de Santo Antônio do Urubu was installed on 27 September 1749. In the later eighteenth century it was the second-largest slave market in the Jacobina comarca, receiving 601 enslaved people, and in 1819 the Casa da Ponte lands were registered and divided into six districts.
zh:
帕拉廷加位于圣弗朗西斯科河中游一处渡口，河流穿过卡廷加旱地，并连通穿越巴伊亚西部的陆路。1444年，两岸仍是原住民的土地；一般认为帕拉廷加一带以图沙人（Tuxá）为主，中游的其他族群也使用河岛、渔场和内陆小径，葡萄牙人的永久定居尚未出现。

1543至1550年间，佩南布科受赠船长杜阿尔特·科埃略·佩雷拉曾到这一地区探险，远征者贝尔希奥尔·迪亚斯·莫雷亚又于1602年经过。17世纪，安东尼奥·格德斯·德布里托获得大片授地，组成殖民巴西第二大地产蓬特庄园，永久殖民才真正展开；庄园的扩张摧毁了圣弗朗西斯科河中游的大部分原住民社群，幸存者则被奴役。在圣安东尼奥-杜乌鲁布德西马牧场，1680年所建的圣安东尼小堂成为乌鲁布村的核心，居民包括葡裔巴西人、原住民和非洲人。1714年，这里有362户、3425人，1718年4月11日升为教区。往返巴伊亚与米纳斯吉拉斯的牛群在此歇脚；若昂五世1746年下令设镇，圣安东尼奥-杜乌鲁布镇于1749年9月27日正式建立。18世纪后期，它是雅科比纳司法区第二大奴隶市场，登记接收601名被奴役者；1819年，蓬特庄园的土地被登记并划分为六个行政区。

en:
Campo Largo was the old name of a broad ranching country on the Rio Grande in the far west of Bahia. In 1444 its grasslands and gallery woods were Acroá country, part of the Macro-Jê linguistic world; Acroá was later also recorded around the headwaters of the Parnaíba and Paranaíba. No Portuguese town yet stood on the river plains.

The Rio Grande lands were later included in the Casa da Ponte land grant. In the first half of the eighteenth century, adventurers from Pernambuco settled on the riverbank and raised cattle and crops. A great flood drove them to the Alto do Umbuxeiro, where the church of Nossa Senhora Santana do Campo became the nucleus of the Campo Largo settlement. On 3 June 1820 a royal charter of John VI created the Comarca do Rio de São Francisco, seated at Vila da Barra and explicitly including Campo Largo.
zh:
坎普拉古是巴伊亚极西部格兰德河畔一片广阔牧地的旧称。1444年，这里的草原和走廊林属于阿克罗阿人，是大热依语世界的一部分；阿克罗阿语后来也在帕纳伊巴河与巴拉那伊巴河源头一带有记录。此时河畔平原还没有葡萄牙人的城镇。

格兰德河沿岸土地后来被划入蓬特庄园的授地。18世纪上半叶，来自伯南布哥的冒险者在河畔定居，经营畜牧和农业。一场大洪水迫使他们迁往温布谢罗高地，圣安娜-杜坎波教堂在那里成为坎普拉古居民点的核心。1820年6月3日，若昂六世颁布王室敕令，设立圣弗朗西斯科河司法区，治所设在巴拉镇，并明确把坎普拉古纳入辖区。

en:
Luziânia is the south-eastern Goiás plateau, the campo around the Rio São Bartolomeu where the cerrado begins its long fall toward the Paranaíba and the mines of Minas. In 1444 it held no towns at all: Caiapó and Xavante bands of the Jê family moved through its grasslands and gallery forest, and the creek beds later to be turned over for gold ran untouched.

Gold found the place late and fast. On 13 December 1746 the Paulista bandeirante Antônio Bueno de Azevedo, pushing northwest from Paracatu, spotted nuggets in a creek and raised a cross the next morning, dedicating the diggings to Saint Lucy. The Arraial de Santa Luzia drew more than ten thousand people within a year, and the first mass was said there in 1746 by Father Luiz da Gama Mendonça before some six thousand miners. In April 1758 thousands of enslaved Africans began the Saia Velha cut, a 42-kilometre canal finished in two years to carry water to the washings, and on 6 December 1758 the arraial became an ecclesiastical comarca.
