By the end of the century the gold was spent, its people drifting out to cattle ranches and farms, leaving the eighteenth-century church of Nossa Senhora do Rosário above a quiet pastoral town on the Minas road.
zh:
卢齐亚纳（卢齐阿尼亚，殖民时期称圣卢齐亚）位于戈亚斯高原东南、圣巴托洛梅乌河一带的原野上，塞拉多由此向巴拉那伊巴河和米纳斯金矿区缓缓倾斜。1444年，这里没有一座城镇：热依语族的卡亚波人与沙万特人游猎于草原和林带之间，后来要被翻遍淘金的河床，当时还无人扰动。

黄金来得晚，却来得猛。1746年12月13日，圣保罗旗手安东尼奥·布埃诺·德阿泽维多从帕拉卡图向西北探矿，在一处溪床中发现金块，次日清晨竖起十字架，把矿区献给圣卢齐亚。圣卢齐亚营地在一年内聚起上万人；同年，路易斯·达伽马·门多萨神父主礼首场弥撒，在场矿工约六千人。1758年4月，数千名非洲黑奴开工开凿「旧裙」水渠，这条42公里长的水道历时两年修成，引水淘矿；同年12月6日，营地升为教务区。18世纪末金沙耗尽，人口散向牧场和农庄，只留下18世纪的玫瑰圣母教堂，守着米纳斯大道旁一座安静的牧歌小镇。

en:
Coxim stands at the meeting of the Coxim and Taquari rivers, where the wooded cerrado breaks into the flooded plains of the Pantanal. Its first lords were Caiapó and Bororó bands; in the Bororó tongue cojim means fish, and the rivers teemed with them. In 1444 this was still Caiapó and Bororó country, known only to its own hunters and fishermen.

The place entered colonial history in 1719, when the Lemes brothers fled São Paulo and reached the new gold diggings on the Cuiabá by way of Coxim. Sesmarias were granted along the Taquari in 1727, and in 1729 Domingos Gomes Biliago and his companions founded the Arraial do Biliago on the river bank to succour the monções, the great canoe convoys from Porto Feliz: after a thirteen-kilometre portage at Camapuã they launched into the Coxim and Taquari and entered the Pantanal. Those waters were Paiaguá country, and the canoe warriors all but annihilated convoy after convoy, killing 400 men in 1730 and leaving but four survivors in 1733, until a punitive expedition destroyed one of their towns in 1734. The arraial never prospered, and in 1821 Coxim was a mere riverside waystation on a route already past its prime.
zh:
科欣位于科欣河与塔夸里河交汇处，塞拉多稀树草原在此化作潘塔纳尔的泛滥平原。这里最早的主人是卡亚波人和博罗罗人；博罗罗语中「科欣」（cojim）意为鱼，而河中正盛产鱼。1444年，这里还是卡亚波人与博罗罗人的土地，只有他们自己的猎人和渔民往来其间。

1719年，莱梅斯兄弟逃离圣保罗，经科欣抵达库亚巴河畔新发现的金矿，此地由此进入殖民史。1727年，塔夸里河沿岸的土地被分赐为份地；1729年，多明戈斯·戈麦斯·比利亚戈和同伴在河畔建立比利亚戈村，接济季风船队——这些从波尔图费利斯出发的独木舟大船队在卡马庞经过13公里陆上搬运后，转入科欣河和塔夸里河进入潘塔纳尔。那一带水域是帕亚瓜人的天下，这些独木舟战士几乎接连歼灭船队：1730年杀死四百人，1733年一队仅四人生还，直到1734年讨伐队摧毁了他们的一座城镇。村庄始终没有兴旺起来，1821年时，科欣只是河畔一处小小的中途站，所在的航路也已过了鼎盛期。

en:
Alagoas takes its name from the string of coastal lagoons between Pernambuco and the lower São Francisco. In 1444 their shores were held by the Caeté, a Tupi-Guarani people who fished the lagoons and grew manioc, while older Jê groups had been pushed inland toward the sertão. Amerigo Vespucci's voyage mapped this coast in 1501, naming the São Francisco on 4 October, and French brazilwood traders were soon anchoring at the Porto do Francês. The land then formed the southern fringe of the Captaincy of Pernambuco.

Penedo arose at the wide São Francisco estuary as settlement pushed south with the sugar frontier. After the Caetés killed the shipwrecked bishop Pero Sardinha in 1556, a punitive expedition nearly destroyed them, and in 1570 Cristóvão Lins founded Porto Calvo with five engenhos. Dutch raiders burned the towns from 1630; Domingos Fernandes Calabar, the mameluco who guided them, was hanged at Porto Calvo in 1635, and the Portuguese drove the Dutch out in September 1645. In the palm forests behind the coast, runaway slaves had built the quilombo of Palmares, an African-style kingdom ruled by Ganga Zumba and then his nephew Zumbi; in January 1694 three columns of paulistas and local troops led by Domingos Jorge Velho overran its last stronghold, and Zumbi was killed on 20 November 1695. The comarca of Alagoas was created in 1711 and held nearly fifty sugar mills by 1730; cotton spread from the 1770s, and on 16 September 1817 João VI raised Alagoas to an independent captaincy, with Penedo and Porto Calvo its chief towns.
zh:
阿拉戈斯得名于伯南布哥与圣弗朗西斯科河下游之间成串的海岸潟湖。1444年，潟湖沿岸是图皮-瓜拉尼人的一支卡埃特人的地盘，他们在潟湖捕鱼、种植木薯，更早的热依诸族则被逐往内陆旱源。1501年，阿梅里戈·韦斯普奇的远航测绘这段海岸，于10月4日命名圣弗朗西斯科河；不久，走私巴西木的法国商人便在「法国人港」停泊。当时这片土地还是伯南布哥都督辖区的南部边缘。

随着蔗糖拓殖向南推进，佩内杜在宽阔的圣弗朗西斯科河口兴起。1556年，卡埃特人杀死遇海难的主教佩罗·萨尔迪尼亚，惩罚性远征几将他们灭族；1570年，克里斯托旺·林斯建立波尔图卡尔沃和五座糖坊。荷兰袭掠者从1630年起焚毁城镇，为其引路的马梅卢科人多明戈斯·费尔南德斯·卡拉巴尔1635年在波尔图卡尔沃被处绞，葡萄牙人1645年9月将荷兰人逐出。在海岸后方的棕榈林中，逃亡奴隶建起帕尔马雷斯逃奴堡——按非洲模式组织的王国，先后由冈加·尊巴和其侄祖比统治。1694年1月，多明戈斯·若热·韦柳率领圣保罗旗兵与当地联军三路并进，踏平其最后据点，祖比于1695年11月20日战死。1711年设立阿拉戈斯司法区，到1730年已有近五十座糖坊；棉花自1770年代推广；1817年9月16日，若昂六世将阿拉戈斯升为独立都督辖区，佩内杜与波尔图卡尔沃是其首要城镇。

en:
The Borborema is the broad plateau that parts the coastal forests of Paraíba and Pernambuco from the dry sertão: its eastern escarpment catches the Atlantic rains and gives birth to more than a hundred rivers, among them the Paraíba do Norte and the Pajeú, while the westward slope fades into drought-prone caatinga. In 1444 these highlands belonged to the non-Tupi peoples the Portuguese later called tapuias — Cariri, Tarairiú and Ariú bands who farmed the moist mountain hollows and hunted the scrub, and whom the coastal Tupi held for ancient enemies.

Cattle were the first European wedge into the highlands: vaqueiros drove herds up from the coast during the seventeenth century, and missions followed the ranches. The French Capuchin Martin of Nantes worked among the Cariri from 1672, and around 1676 João Duarte do Sacramento founded the Mission of Our Lady of the Mountains among the Ararobá; the Xukuru joined it in the 1690s, and it grew into Cimbres, chartered as a town on 3 April 1762. Native resistance ran on far longer: the cycle of raids and punitive columns remembered as the Barbarians' War stretched from the mid-seventeenth century into the eighteenth, as Cariri, Tarairiú and Janduí war bands fought the cattle grants eating into the sertão. In 1697 Captain Teodósio de Oliveira Ledo settled Ariú families at Campina Grande, which with Cimbres became one of the market towns of the agreste, living on cattle and, from the later eighteenth century, on cotton.
zh:
博尔博雷马是一片宽阔高原，隔开帕拉伊巴、伯南布哥的沿海林地与干旱旱源：东麓截住大西洋雨水，北帕拉伊巴河、帕热乌河等一百多条河流发源于此，西坡则渐入易旱的卡廷加灌丛。1444年，这片高地属于后来被葡萄牙人泛称为塔普亚人的非图皮族群——卡里里、塔莱里乌和阿里乌等部落在湿润的山谷耕作、在灌丛中狩猎，沿海图皮人视他们为世仇。

牛群是欧洲人插入高地的第一个楔子：17世纪，牧牛人从沿海把畜群赶入高原，传教士也随牧场而来。法国嘉布遣会士南特的马丁1672年起在卡里里人中间传教；约1676年，若昂·杜阿尔特·多萨克拉门托在阿拉罗巴人中间建立「山中圣母」传教站，舒库鲁人1690年代并入，传教站后来发展为辛布雷斯，1762年4月3日正式设镇。土著的抵抗延续了更久：袭扰与讨伐交相循环的「野蛮人战争」从17世纪中叶一直拖到18世纪，卡里里、塔莱里乌和扬杜伊战士抗击不断蚕食旱源的牧地封授。1697年，特奥多西奥·德·奥利维拉·莱多上尉率阿里乌人在大坎皮纳定居；大坎皮纳与辛布雷斯后来同为阿格雷斯特过渡带的集镇，以畜牧为生，18世纪后期又以棉花为业。

en:
Pastos Bons lies on the chapadas of the upper Itapecuru, the dry southeastern edge of Maranhão where cerrado grasslands meet caatinga scrub. In 1444 it was Timbira country: Jê-speaking villages of the southern Maranhão interior, with Sakamekra groups nearby, moved through gallery woods, savannah and seasonal lagoons. Europeans had not yet reached this interior, and the good pastures later praised by ranchers had not yet been measured into colonial land grants.

Piauí cattlemen entering from the southeast founded Pastos Bons in 1744. The trail-and-ranch frontier supplied Maranhão's coastal towns with cattle and hides. In 1755 Portuguese law declared Indians free, while the General Trading Company of Grão-Pará and Maranhão brought thousands of enslaved Africans into the wider colony to sustain cotton, rice and other exports. By 1770 ranchers from the sertões of Pastos Bons were confirming rural grants along the upper streams.
zh:
帕斯图斯邦斯位于伊塔佩库鲁河上游台地，是马拉尼昂东南的干燥边缘，塞拉多草原与卡廷加灌丛在此相接。1444年，这里是廷比拉人的土地：马拉尼昂南部内陆的热依语村群与邻近的萨卡梅克拉人，在林缘林地、稀树草原和季节性湖泊之间迁徙。欧洲人尚未抵达这片内陆，后来受牧牛人称赞的优良牧场也还没有被划成殖民授地。

1744年，从东南进入的皮奥伊牧牛人建立帕斯图斯邦斯。这条由小径和牧场组成的边疆向马拉尼昂沿海城镇供应牛只和皮革。1755年，葡萄牙法律宣布印第安人自由；同年，大帕拉与马拉尼昂总贸易公司成立，却向整个殖民地运入数以千计的非洲奴隶，以维持棉花、水稻等出口。到1770年，帕斯图斯邦斯腹地的牧场主已在上游溪流旁确认乡郊授地。

en:
Timon occupies the Maranhão bank of the middle Parnaíba, opposite the lands that became Piauí. In 1444 the river, seasonal floodplain woods and overland trails belonged to Timbira and Gamela Indians, native groups of the eastern Maranhão interior's Jê-speaking world. There was no Portuguese town or customs point: canoes and fords linked village networks, while the cattle roads and royal highway that would fix the site still lay in the future.

After the Portuguese took São Luís from France in 1615, expeditions pushed toward the Itapecuru and enslaved or displaced nearby Timbira and Gamela communities. Cattle raising, deliberately pushed inland by Portuguese land grants so that the coast could keep producing sugar, reached the Parnaíba sertão in the seventeenth century; the Fazenda Cabrobó settlement that became Oeiras took shape in the 1670s and became Vila da Mocha in 1712. Piauí became a separate captaincy in 1718. During the eighteenth century a royal road linked Vila da Mocha with Aldeias Altas, later Caxias, and Passagem de Santo Antônio, thirteen kilometres above the future town, remained the only settlement until 1779.
zh:
蒂蒙位于帕纳伊巴河中游的马拉尼昂一岸，对岸就是后来成为皮奥伊的土地。1444年，河流、季节性洪泛林地和陆上小径都属于廷比拉人与加梅拉人，他们是马拉尼昂东部内陆热依语世界的原住民。这里还没有葡萄牙人的城镇或税卡：独木舟和浅滩连接着村社网络，后来真正固定这处地点的牧牛道与王家大道尚未出现。

1615年葡萄牙从法国手中夺取圣路易斯后，探险队向伊塔佩库鲁河推进，把附近的廷比拉和加梅拉村社掳为奴隶，或逐离故土。葡萄牙授地制度刻意把养牛业推向内陆，好让沿海继续种蔗，牧牛边疆遂在17世纪抵达帕纳伊巴河腹地；后来发展为奥埃拉斯的卡布罗博牧场在1670年代成形，1712年成为莫沙镇。1718年皮奥伊成为独立辖区。18世纪，一条王家大道连接莫沙镇与后来改称卡希亚斯的阿尔德亚斯阿尔塔斯；位于未来城镇上游十三公里的圣安东尼渡口，到1779年仍是唯一聚落。

en:
Parnaguá lies in the southern Piauí cerrado beside the Lagoa de Parnaguá, the largest lake in the state; its Tupi name joins paranã, a great river, and kûá, a cove. In 1444 the camps and fields about the lagoon belonged to Pimenteira, Xerente and Acroá bands of the Ge stock, far from any European frontier.

From 1676 the governor of Pernambuco, Pedro de Almeida, granted the country as sesmarias, and the cattle fazendas that sprang up were long harried by Macoá and Rodelleiro raiders; it was these attacks that brought the founding of a fortified settlement at Parnaguá in 1698. The povoação already stood on the western shore of the lagoon in 1751, became a freguesia in 1755, and was created a vila by royal charter of 19 June 1761, installed on 3 June 1762 in the presence of the ouvidor-geral Luís José Duarte Freire. Its independence was short: on 25 June 1816 a provincial law suppressed the vila and attached its territory to Corrente, so that in 1821 Parnaguá was no more than a district of its neighbour.
zh:
帕纳瓜位于皮奥伊南部的塞拉多草原，傍着全州最大的帕纳瓜湖；其名来自图皮语，由「大河」（paranã）和「河湾」（kûá）拼成。1444年，湖周的营地和田地属于热依语群的皮门泰拉人、谢伦特人和阿克罗阿人，离任何欧洲人的边境都很遥远。

从1676年起，伯南布哥总督佩德罗·德·阿尔梅达把这片土地分赐为份地，建起的牧牛场长期遭到马夸人和「持盾人」罗德莱罗人袭扰；正是这些袭击促成1698年在帕纳瓜设防建镇。1751年湖西岸已有聚落，1755年设堂区，1761年6月19日王室诏令升为市镇，1762年6月3日在都督辖区总督察官路易斯·若泽·杜阿尔特·弗莱雷主持下正式开镇。它的独立为时不长：1816年6月25日省法令撤销该市镇，辖区并入科伦蒂，因此1821年时帕纳瓜不过是邻镇治下的一个区。

en:
Grajaú lies in south-central Maranhão on the river of the same name, a Tupi name explained as 'river of the Carajás'. In 1444 its gallery woods and crossing places belonged to Timbira and Piocobjé Indians, Jê-speaking peoples of the southern Maranhão interior. The east-bank chapada later called Porto da Chapada held no Portuguese town or land grant; canoes and overland trails served native villages rather than colonial ranches.

Permanent Portuguese occupation came only on 11 March 1811, when Ensign Antônio Francisco dos Reis founded a settlement at Manoel Valentim Fernandes's Fazenda Chapada, also called Porto da Chapada, on the east bank. Cattle and horse ranches had pushed into the region, and the river linked the new post to markets in Maranhão and neighbouring sertões. The west bank remained Timbira and Piocobjé country, and in 1814 those Indians destroyed the settlement, then numbering forty people; only six survived because they were away. Survivors returned in 1816 and named the place São Paulo do Norte, keeping a small military detachment. In 1817 the governor established the nearby Colônia Leopoldina at Estrião Grande, placing forty line soldiers under Francisco José Pinto Magalhães to guard the frontier. By 1821 Grajaú remained a fortified river-trade outpost rather than a chartered vila.
zh:
格拉雅乌位于马拉尼昂中南部的格拉雅乌河畔；这个图皮语地名被解释为「卡拉雅人之河」。1444年，河畔林地与渡口属于廷比拉人和皮奥科贝人，他们是马拉尼昂南部内陆的热依语族群。东岸后来称为沙帕达港的台地上还没有葡萄牙城镇或授地，独木舟与陆上小径服务于原住民村社，而不是殖民牧场。

葡萄牙人的永久占据迟至1811年3月11日才开始：少尉安东尼奥·弗朗西斯科·多斯·雷斯在东岸曼努埃尔·瓦伦丁·费尔南德斯的沙帕达牧场（又称沙帕达港）建立聚落。牧牛和养马边疆已经推进到此，河流也把新据点与马拉尼昂市场及周围腹地连接起来。西岸仍是廷比拉人和皮奥科贝人的土地；1814年，这些印第安人摧毁了这座已有四十人的聚落，只有六人因外出而幸存。1816年，幸存者重返此地，命名为北圣保罗，并保留一支小型驻军。1817年，总督在附近的埃斯特里昂格兰德设立莱奥波尔迪纳殖民点，由弗朗西斯科·若泽·平托·马加良斯率领四十名线列步兵守卫边疆。到1821年，格拉雅乌仍是一座有军队护卫的河贸据点，还不是特许镇。

en:
Alcântara faces São Luís across the Bay of São Marcos, its mangrove shores and tidal channels lying between the mouths of the Mearim, Pindaré and Turiaçu. In 1444 the land held a cluster of Tupinambá villages, the principal one called Tapuitapera. Canoes moved between the bay and river mouths, while mangroves and flooded channels shaped the villages' coastal world, and no European power yet contested the shore that later became the Captaincy of Cumã.

Daniel de La Touche's French expedition made contact with these villages after founding Saint-Louis in 1612 and built the first chapel at Tapuitapera. Portuguese occupation followed between 1616 and 1618, after French rule in Maranhão collapsed, and Tapuitapera became seat of the Captaincy of Cumã, first granted to Antônio Coelho de Carvalho and his grandson Francisco. The Dutch invasion of 1641 forced the Portuguese out and the settlement was abandoned, but after the reconquest it was raised in 1648 to the Vila de Santo Antônio de Alcântara, with a town hall, pillory and parish church; sugar mills and cotton cultivation returned. The Crown reincorporated the donated captaincy by royal charter around 1754. In the late eighteenth century cotton exports and enslaved African labour made Alcântara one of Maranhão's richest plantation towns, its planters and merchants facing São Luís across the bay.
zh:
阿尔坎塔拉隔着圣马科斯湾与圣路易斯相望，红树林海岸和潮汐水道位于梅阿林河、平达雷河与图里亚苏河河口之间。1444年，这里分布着一串图皮南巴村落，主村名为塔普伊塔佩拉。独木舟在海湾与河口之间往来，红树林和潮水沟渠构成村社的海岸世界，欧洲势力还未争夺这片后来成为库芒辖区的土地。

1612年，达尼埃尔·德·拉图什率领的法国远征队在建立圣路易后与这些村落接触，并在塔普伊塔佩拉建起第一座小教堂。法国在马拉尼昂的统治崩溃后，葡萄牙人于1616年至1618年间占领此地；塔普伊塔佩拉成为库芒辖区治所，最初封给安东尼奥·科埃略·德·卡瓦略及其孙子弗朗西斯科。1641年荷兰入侵迫使葡萄牙人撤离，聚落也遭废弃；收复后，它于1648年升格为圣安多尼·德·阿尔坎塔拉镇，设有市政厅、鞭刑柱和教区教堂，糖坊与棉花种植也重新恢复。约1754年，王室通过特许状收回这座赠领辖区。18世纪末，棉花出口和被奴役非洲劳工使阿尔坎塔拉成为马拉尼昂最富庶的种植园城镇之一，种植园主和商人隔湾与圣路易斯相望。

en:
Tucuruí lies on the lower Tocantins, above the river's final approach to the Pará and Amazon delta. In Tupi the name joins tukura, a grasshopper, with oby, green, and in 1444 the forests, rapids and river crossings were used by Asurini do Tocantins, Paracanã and Gavião peoples. Their camps and trails linked the lower and middle Tocantins long before Portuguese troops tried to secure the river.

French and Portuguese expeditions probed the waterway from the sixteenth century, but permanent occupation came only in the eighteenth. In 1779 Governor Telo de Meneses founded the military settlement of Vila de São Bernardo da Pederneira, responding to the growth of the Itapocu confederation; it was renamed Alcobaça in 1780. Construction of the Fort of Nossa Senhora da Fachina, later Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, followed in 1782 with indigenous and enslaved labour. The post watched Tocantins traffic, checked gold smuggled from Goiás and Mato Grosso, and served as a base against the region's quilombos; expeditions against runaway slaves and for indigenous captives also left from Baião and Cametá. Between 1809 and 1814 Alcobaça was nominally attached to the short-lived captaincy of São João das Duas Barras during the dispute over control of Tocantins navigation.
zh:
图库鲁伊位于托坎廷斯河下游，扼守河道进入帕拉河和亚马逊三角洲前的水段。其名在图皮语中由意为蚱蜢的图库拉（tukura）和意为绿色的奥比（oby）组成。1444年时，托坎廷斯阿苏里尼人、帕拉卡南人和加维翁人在森林、急流和渡口间活动；早在葡萄牙军队试图控制托坎廷斯河以前，他们的营地和小路就已连接着河流下游与中游。

16世纪起，法国和葡萄牙远征队先后探查这条水道，但永久性占据要到18世纪才出现。1779年，总督特卢·德梅内塞斯针对伊塔波库联盟的壮大建立军镇圣贝尔纳多-达佩德内拉，1780年改名为阿尔科巴萨。1782年，当局使用印第安人和奴隶劳力修建法希纳圣母堡，后改称拿撒勒圣母堡。据点负责监视托坎廷斯河航运，查禁从戈亚斯和马托格罗索顺河走私的黄金，并作为镇压当地逃奴堡的基地；讨伐逃亡奴隶和抓捕印第安人的远征也从这里及巴扬、卡梅塔出发。1809年至1814年，在争夺托坎廷斯河航行权期间，阿尔科巴萨名义上被划入短暂存在的双河圣若昂都督领。

en:
Para takes its name from the broad tidal Pará channel south of Marajó, and its capital Portel lies in the same forested world of islands, igarapés and seasonal floodwaters. In 1444 Tupinambá and other indigenous canoe peoples used the riverbanks and rainforest clearings for fishing, planting, travel and trade between the Amazon and Tocantins systems. No Portuguese mission or military post yet marked the route later controlled from Portel.

Portel's recorded history began in the mid-seventeenth century with Arucará, a Jesuit aldeia founded by Father António Vieira for Nhengaíba people brought from the Ilha Grande de Joanes. The settlement fitted the Portuguese strategy of occupying Amazon channels also claimed by Spain and turning river navigation into effective possession. On 24 January 1758 Mendonça Furtado, president of the captaincy of Grão-Pará, installed the municipal senate and elevated the old mission settlement to Vila de Portel during the crown's reorganization of Amazonian government. In 1786 Munduruku resistance reached the town and killed several Luso-Brazilian residents, a sharp reminder that Portuguese control still depended on contested river lanes.
zh:
帕拉因马拉若岛南侧宽阔的感潮水道帕拉河得名，首府波特尔正位于这片由岛屿、溪流和季节性洪水林组成的森林水网中。1444年时，图皮南巴人和其他以独木舟为生的印第安族群在河岸与雨林开垦地捕鱼、种植、往来，并在亚马逊水系和托坎廷斯水系之间贸易；当时还没有葡萄牙传教站或军事据点标记这条后来由波特尔控制的航路。

波特尔有记载的历史始于17世纪中叶：安东尼奥·维埃拉神父建立阿鲁卡拉耶稣会传教村，安置从大若阿内斯岛迁来的年加伊巴人。这个聚落符合葡萄牙王室的战略，即占据同样被西班牙声索的亚马逊水道，把航行控制转化为实际占有。1758年1月24日，格劳帕拉都督府主席门东萨·富尔塔多设立市参议会，在王室重整亚马逊行政的过程中把旧传教村升格为波特尔镇。1786年，蒙杜鲁库人的抵抗波及该镇，杀死若干葡裔巴西居民，也清楚表明葡萄牙人的控制仍依赖那些充满争夺的河道。

en:
Santarém occupies the bluffs at the Tapajós mouth, where the clear tributary meets the sediment-laden Amazon. From about the tenth century, the Santarém or Tapajonic culture raised riverside agricultural towns here; its Tupi-related Tapajó people kept populous villages, maize fields and ceramics at the crossroads of river routes. In 1444 the confluence had no European post. Canoes linked its fishing and farming communities with upstream and downriver peoples, and the Tapajós gateway remained under Indigenous authority.

Francisco de Orellana's Spanish party entered this stretch in mid-1542 and was met by Tapajó war canoes led by Chief Chipayo. Pedro Teixeira called at the Tupuliçus settlement near the mouth in 1626 and opened trade. On 22 June 1661 the Jesuit João Filipe Bettendorff founded Aldeia dos Tapajós and built the Chapel of Our Lady of Conception. Work on the Tapajós fortress began in 1693 and ended in 1697, giving the Portuguese mission a fortified nucleus on the lower Amazon. The last Tapajó and Urucucú at the mouth were forcibly moved to the Cumaru mission in 1698, and in 1758 the settlement was raised to a town and renamed Santarém.
zh:
圣塔伦位于塔帕若斯河河口的高岸上，清澈的支流在此与挟带泥沙的亚马孙河交汇。约从10世纪起，圣塔伦文化（又称塔帕若尼卡文化）在此发展出滨河农业城镇；与图皮语有关的塔帕若斯人在河运要冲拥有人口稠密的村落、玉米田和陶器。1444年，河口还没有欧洲人的据点。独木舟把渔耕社区与上下游各族群连接起来，塔帕若斯门户仍掌握在原住民手中。

1542年中，弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷利亚纳的西班牙队伍进入这段河道，遭到酋长奇帕约率领的塔帕若斯作战独木舟拦截。1626年，佩德罗·特谢拉在河口附近的图普利苏斯聚落停靠并开启贸易。1661年6月22日，耶稣会士若昂·菲利佩·贝滕多夫建立塔帕若斯村，并修建圣母受孕小堂。塔帕若斯堡垒1693年动工、1697年完工，使这座葡萄牙传教站成为下亚马孙设有防御的核心。1698年，河口最后的塔帕若斯人和乌鲁库库人被强行迁往库马鲁传教站；1758年，该聚落升格为镇并得名圣塔伦。

en:
Pirara lies in the Rupununi, the open savanna enclosed by forest at the head of the Essequibo. In the rains its rivers spill over the flat grassland and linger as shallow lakes, and a short carry across the Pirara watershed joins the Essequibo to the Takutu and, beyond it, the Amazon. In 1444 this was the country of the Macushi, Carib-speakers who hunted the grassland, fished the floodwaters and grew cassava on the ridges, with the Arawak-speaking Wapishana their neighbours to the south. The Rupununi, or Raponani, took its name from the whistling duck of its lagoons, and the canoe-and-portage road through Pirara was the highway between two great river systems.

It was this road that fed the dream of El Dorado. In 1595 Walter Raleigh, ascending the Orinoco no farther than Angostura, heard that the golden city of Manoa stood on a vast inland lake, and in 1596 his lieutenant Lawrence Kemys learned from Carib guides that twenty days up the Essequibo and a day's portage led to a great water the Caribs called Parime. Some explorers later proposed that seasonal flooding of the Rupununi savanna had been mistaken for a lake. In 1598 Jodocus Hondius engraved the lake and city on his map of Guiana, and for two centuries Europeans sought them there. From 1616 the Dutch fort at Kyk-Over-Al drew the interior's trade down the Essequibo, while on the far side of the watershed the Portuguese built up the Rio Branco; in 1789 Manuel da Gama Lobo d'Almada brought cattle and horses into those grasslands, and ranching edged up towards the divide. Yet no fort or mission ever stood on the savanna itself, and in 1821 Pirara was still Macushi country, crossed by trade paths and by the remembered road to a lake that no one ever found.
zh:
皮拉拉地处鲁普努尼——埃塞奎博河源头一带、被林海环抱的开阔热带草原。雨季时河水漫过平坦的草地，积成大片浅水湖；只要在皮拉拉分水岭上走一小段陆运，就能从埃塞奎博河水系进入塔库图河，进而通往亚马孙河。1444年，这里是马库希人的家园：这些说加勒比语的居民在草原上狩猎、在洪水中捕鱼、在高地上种植木薯，南边与说阿拉瓦克语的瓦皮沙纳人为邻。鲁普努尼土名拉波纳尼，名字取自河洲间的啸鸭；这条穿皮拉拉而过的独木舟加陆运之路，是沟通两大水系的通衢。

正是这条通衢滋养了黄金国的传说。1595年沃尔特·雷利溯奥里诺科河而上，最远只到安戈斯图拉，却听说金城马诺阿坐落在一个巨大的内陆湖畔。1596年，他再派副官劳伦斯·凯米斯前来，凯米斯从加勒比向导口中得知：沿埃塞奎博河上行二十天，再陆运一天，便有一片大水，加勒比人称之为帕里梅。后来有探险者认为，季节性泛滥的鲁普努尼草原可能被误认成了湖泊。1598年，约道库斯·洪迪乌斯把大湖和金城刻进他的圭亚那地图，此后两个世纪里欧洲人一直在这片草原上搜寻它们。从1616年起，荷兰人的基克-奥弗阿尔堡把内陆物产沿河引向海岸；分水岭另一侧的葡萄牙人则经营着里奥布兰科，1789年曼努埃尔·达·伽马·洛博·达尔马达把牛马引入这片草原，牧场也随之向分水岭方向推进。但草原上始终没有立起一座要塞或传教站：直到1821年，皮拉拉仍是马库希人的土地，往来的只有商道，和那条通向一座从未被找到的大湖的旧路。

en:
Wadai is a country of hills, wells, millet fields, and cattle pastures in the highlands between the Lake Chad basin and Darfur. The land around Ouara, later remembered for its ruined palace, mosque, and city wall, was Maba, or Bargo, country in 1444. Maba clans combined farming with pastoralism, while Tunjur power from Darfur was reaching over the older local chiefdoms. Islam was a court influence more than a common faith, and many villagers still followed traditional religions.

In 1635 Abd al-Karim rallied the Maba under an Islamic banner, overthrew the Tunjur king Daud, married his daughter, and founded the Kolak dynasty at Ouara. The new state spent much of the seventeenth century as a tributary of Darfur, until its late-century ruler Ya'qub Arus refused tribute and defeated a Darfuri invasion. Wadai's power grew sharply under Muhammad Sabun from 1804: in 1805 it conquered Bagirmi and carried off thousands of captives, and about 1809 a caravan route through Ennedi and Kufra to Benghazi opened the northern trade. Sabun minted coins and imported chain mail, firearms, and military advisers, but his death around 1815 opened a succession crisis along the Ouara wells.
zh:
瓦达伊位于乍得湖盆地与达尔富尔之间的高地，是一片由丘陵、水井、粟田和牧场组成的土地。1444年，后来以宫殿、清真寺和城墙遗址闻名的瓦拉（Ouara）周围还是马巴人（又称巴尔古人）的地方。马巴诸氏族兼营农耕和畜牧，来自达尔富尔的通朱尔势力正逐步控制旧日的地方酋长国；伊斯兰教更多影响宫廷，许多村民仍信奉传统宗教。

1635年，阿卜杜勒·卡里姆以伊斯兰教为号召集结马巴人，推翻通朱尔国王达乌德，娶其女儿为妻，并在瓦拉建立科拉克王朝。新国家在17世纪大部分时间向达尔富尔纳贡，直到17世纪末的统治者雅库布·阿鲁斯拒绝进贡并击退达尔富尔入侵。1804年穆罕默德·萨本即位后，瓦达伊势力迅速扩张：1805年征服巴吉尔米，掳走数千人；约1809年，经恩内迪、库夫拉通往班加西的商路打开了北方贸易。萨本铸造钱币，进口锁子甲、火器并聘请军事顾问，但他约在1815年去世后，瓦拉诸井旁也陷入继承危机。

en:
Barcelos covers a stretch of the middle Negro, a black-water river broken by islands and flooded forests on the canoe route between the Branco and the Amazon. Manau communities held its right-bank landing later called Mariuá; they fished, planted manioc and moved among riverside villages, with Baré, Baniwa and other Negro peoples nearby. In 1444 this remained a world of river chiefs and traders, untouched by Portuguese missions or frontier forts.

In 1728 Carmelite friar Matias de São Boaventura reached Mariuá from the Japurá and founded the Mission of Our Lady of Conception beside the Manau village of chief Camandri; Baré, Baniwa, Passé and Uerequena people later gathered there. Francisco Xavier de Mendonça Furtado arrived in 1754 to carry out the Portuguese-Spanish boundary settlement and remained for two years directing works. The crown created the captaincy of São José do Rio Negro in 1755, and on 6 May 1758 Mariuá became a town renamed Barcelos, with Joaquim de Melo e Póvoas as its first governor. The seat moved to Barra in 1791, later returned, and was fixed at Barra, the future Manaus, in 1808; in 1806 most of Barcelos's public buildings, except the palace, offices and church, had been demolished.
zh:
巴塞卢斯地处内格罗河中游，深色河道上岛洲密布、洪泛林绵延，是布朗库河与亚马孙河之间的独木舟水路。马瑙人的社群据有后来称为马里瓦的右岸登陆地；他们捕鱼、种植木薯，往来于滨河村落，附近还有巴雷人、巴尼瓦人等内格罗河族群。1444年，这里仍是河上酋长与商贩的世界，葡萄牙传教站和边疆堡垒都尚未出现。

1728年，加尔默罗会修士马蒂亚斯·德·圣博阿文图拉从雅普拉河来到马里瓦，在酋长卡曼德里的马瑙人村落旁建立圣母受孕传教站；巴雷人、巴尼瓦人、帕塞人和韦雷凯纳人后来也聚居于此。1754年，弗朗西斯科·沙维尔·德·门东萨·富尔塔多为执行葡萄牙与西班牙的划界安排抵达，并停留两年督办工程。1755年，葡萄牙王室设立内格罗河圣若泽都督区；1758年5月6日，马里瓦升格为镇并改名巴塞卢斯，若阿金·德·梅洛·埃·波沃阿什出任首任都督。治所1791年迁往巴拉，后来一度迁回，最终在1808年固定于后来的马瑙斯；1806年，除宫殿、公署和教堂外，巴塞卢斯的大部分公共建筑已奉命拆除。

en:
Manaus commands the mouth of the Negro, where the black river enters the Solimões and canoe routes from the upper Amazon meet the downstream road. Manaó and Baré villages occupied its banks and islands, living by fishing, manioc fields and trade along the Negro's tributaries. In 1444 there was no fort at the future Lugar da Barra, only a strategic confluence controlled by river chiefs and traders.

Orellana entered and named the Negro on 3 June 1542. In 1669 Francisco da Mota Falcão began the stone-and-clay Fort of São José da Barra do Rio Negro, completed by his son Manoel da Mota Siqueira to deter Dutch and Spanish rivals; missionaries built the Chapel of Our Lady of Conception beside it in 1695. From 1723 to 1728 the Manaó fought Portuguese slaving and conquest, and their captured leader Ajuricaba threw himself into the Amazon while being taken in chains to Belém for trial. The captaincy of São José do Rio Negro was created in 1755 with its seat at Mariuá, moved to Barra in 1791, returned to Barcelos in 1799, and was fixed at Barra on 29 March 1808. In 1821 the settlement was still formally Lugar da Barra, but its fort and administrative seat guarded the upper Amazon gateway.
zh:
马瑙斯扼守内格罗河口，深色的内格罗河在此注入索利蒙伊斯河，来自上亚马孙的独木舟水路与下游通道相接。马瑙人和巴雷人的村落占据河岸与岛洲，以渔猎、木薯种植和内格罗河各支流贸易为生。1444年，后来的巴拉地方还没有堡垒，只有河上酋长与商贩控制的战略汇流点。

1542年6月3日，弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷利亚纳的探险队进入并命名内格罗河。1669年，弗朗西斯科·达·莫塔·法尔康开始用石材和黏土修筑内格罗河河口圣若泽堡垒，后由其子曼努埃尔·达·莫塔·西凯拉完工，用以威慑荷兰和西班牙竞争者；1695年，传教士在堡旁修建圣母受孕小堂。1723—1728年，马瑙人为反抗奴役和征服同葡萄牙作战，领袖阿茹里卡巴被俘并锁送贝伦受审，途中投入亚马孙河而死。1755年设立内格罗河圣若泽都督区，治所原在马里瓦；1791年迁至巴拉，1799年迁回巴塞卢斯，1808年3月29日最终定于巴拉。1821年，这里在名义上仍只是巴拉地方，但堡垒和都督区治所已使它扼守住上亚马孙门户。

en:
Muturu commanded the channels where the Xingu River meets the Amazon, a world of floodplain gardens, islands and canoe routes. In 1444 Tupinambá-speaking villages held the banks, fishing, farming and exchanging forest produce with peoples farther along the great river. No European garrison had yet secured the mouth, though its canoes and anchorage already made it useful to anyone entering the Amazon from the sea.

Dutch and English traders entered the delta after 1599, and the Dutch post here was called both Orange and Muturu. It traded for annatto and other inland goods while sugar and tobacco were planted nearby. In 1623 Portuguese forces under Luís Aranha de Vasconcelos and Bento Maciel Parente, supported by more than a thousand native bowmen, took the fort in a two-hour fight and demolished it. Capuchins later formed a native settlement at Muturu, traditionally dated to 1639; it became Porto de Moz, which Portuguese administration raised to town status in 1758.
zh:
莫图鲁扼守欣古河汇入亚马孙河的河汊，周围是泛滥平原田园、岛屿与独木舟航道。1444年，图皮南巴语村社控制两岸，居民捕鱼、耕作，并沿河与更远的族群交换林产品。欧洲人尚未在河口建立常驻要塞，但这里的独木舟航道和锚地，已使它成为从海上进入亚马孙河的要地。

1599年后，荷兰与英国商人进入三角洲，荷兰人在此设立的据点兼有奥兰治和莫图鲁两个名字，收购胭脂树红等内陆物产，并在附近种植甘蔗和烟草。1623年，路易斯·阿拉尼亚·德·瓦斯康塞洛斯与本托·马西埃尔·帕伦特率领葡萄牙军队，在一千多名原住民弓箭手支援下，经两小时战斗夺取并拆毁要塞。后来嘉布遣会在莫图鲁建立原住民村，传统上定为1639年；此地发展为莫兹港，葡萄牙行政当局1758年将其升为城镇。

en:
The Suriname River flows from the rainforest and rapids of the interior toward the coastal plain. In 1444 Arawak villages occupied the lower banks, including the place later recorded as Torarica, while Kalina (Carib) groups fished, grew cassava and commanded crossings and portages. Their dugouts linked river villages to the shore, and smaller Cariban-speaking peoples moved through the forests and savanna upstream. Europeans did not yet know the waterway; Dutch mariners would record it as the Surinamo in 1598.

English colonists sent by Francis Willoughby entered Suriname in 1650, and the 1662 royal charter made the Arawak village of Torarica capital of Willoughbyland before Paramaribo outstripped it by 1665. After Abraham Crijnssen's Dutch force took the colony in 1667, plantations pushed up the river. In 1664 David Cohen Nassy led Sephardic refugees from Brazil and Cayenne to the savanna later called Jodensavanne; its first synagogue rose between 1665 and 1671 and a brick one in 1685. Around 1700 about 500 Jewish planters there held roughly 9,000 enslaved people. Kalina warriors attacked the settlement late in 1678, enslaved people rebelled on the Machado plantation in 1690, and French sailors raided it in 1712. Many who escaped slavery fled upstream, and the 1757 Tempati revolt strengthened the Ndyuka. On 10 October 1760 the Dutch recognized Ndyuka freedom and territorial autonomy; a treaty with the Saramaka followed on 19 September 1762. Jodensavanne meanwhile declined to about twenty-two Jewish residents by 1790. British forces held the wider colony from 1799 to 1802 and again from 1804 to 1816, while the treaty peoples kept their own lands far upriver.
zh:
苏里南河从内陆雨林和急流流向海岸平原。1444年，阿拉瓦克人的村落占据下游河岸，后来被记作托拉里卡的地方便是其中之一；卡利纳（加勒比）人捕鱼、种植木薯，并控制渡口和陆路转运道。他们的独木舟把河畔村落与海岸连接起来，更上游的雨林和草原上还有较小的加勒比语族群活动。欧洲人此时还不知道这条水道，荷兰水手要到1598年才把它记作苏里纳莫。

1650年，弗朗西斯·威洛比派来的英国殖民者进入苏里南；1662年的王室特许状把阿拉瓦克村落托拉里卡定为威洛比兰首府，但到1665年前后，帕拉马里博已超过它。1667年亚伯拉罕·克莱因森率领荷兰军队夺取殖民地后，种植园继续向河上游推进。1664年，大卫·科恩·纳西率领来自巴西和卡宴的塞法迪犹太难民来到后来称为尤登萨瓦内的草原；第一座会堂建于1665—1671年间，砖造会堂则在1685年落成。1700年前后，当地约500名犹太种植园主占有约9000名奴隶。1678年末，卡利纳战士袭击此地；1690年，马查多种植园的奴隶起义；法国水手又在1712年来袭。许多逃奴沿河上游出走，1757年滕帕蒂起义壮大了恩迪乌卡人。1760年10月10日，荷兰承认恩迪乌卡人的自由和领地自治；1762年9月19日，又与萨拉马卡人签订类似条约。与此同时，尤登萨瓦内日渐衰落，到1790年只剩约22名犹太居民。英军在1799—1802年、1804—1816年两度控制整个殖民地，而远水上游的缔约族群仍保有自己的土地。

en:
Oiapoque is the forested lower course and estuary where the river once called Japoc or the Vicente Pinzón reaches the Atlantic. In 1444 Waiãpi, Galibi and Palikur families lived along the main stream and the Uaçá affluents, combining floodplain farming, fishing and travel by canoe. The river mouth was not yet an imperial border, but a coastal gateway watched and used by the peoples of the Guiana coast.

Vicente Yáñez Pinzón reached the river early in 1500. Charles Leigh's English expedition arrived in May 1604 and left a small settlement called Oliveleighe, but mutiny and a Carib raid forced the last settlers away in May 1606. Robert Harcourt claimed Guiana for England at the Wiapoco in 1609, yet the English posts had faded by 1623; the Walloon organizer Jessé de Forest died on the river during a Dutch reconnaissance on 22 October 1624. The 1713 Treaty of Utrecht made the Japoc or Vincent Pinson the Franco-Portuguese limit, but rival readings of which river that name meant kept the frontier in dispute. In 1808-1809 Luso-Brazilian and British forces moved through this coast against Cayenne.
zh:
奥亚波基是森林密布的奥亚波克河下游与河口一带，这条河旧称亚波克河或维森特·平松河，最终注入大西洋。1444年，瓦亚皮人、加利比人和帕利库尔人的家族居住在干流与瓦萨河支流沿岸，兼营泛滥平原农业、渔业和独木舟运输。此时河口尚不是帝国边界，而是圭亚那沿海族群掌握和使用的入海门户。

1500年初，维森特·亚涅斯·平松抵达这条河。1604年5月，查尔斯·利率领英国远征队到此，留下一个名为奥利弗莱的小型殖民点，但哗变和加勒比人的袭击迫使最后的定居者在1606年5月撤离。罗伯特·哈考特1609年在维亚波科宣布圭亚那归英国所有，到1623年英国据点已消失；1624年10月22日，瓦隆人组织者杰西·德·福雷斯特在一次荷兰侦察途中死于河畔。1713年《乌得勒支和约》把亚波克河或维森特·平松河定为法葡边界，但双方对该名指哪条河解释不同，边界争议延续。1808至1809年，葡属巴西与英国军队沿海岸进军，进攻卡宴。

en:
The Eastern Llanos meet the Unare River lowlands around the future Zaraza, where plains tracks joined routes toward eastern Venezuela. In 1444 this was Carib-speaking country; peoples later recorded nearby as Palenque and Cumanagoto kept maize, manioc and sweet-potato fields, hunted in the gallery woods and sometimes palisaded their villages. At the Unare's confluence with Quebrada Honda, the ground later called El Batey was a crossroads, but no Spanish town yet stood there.

European penetration began in the 1640s. Miguel de Urbés, a lieutenant of Joan Orpí, established San Miguel de la Nueva Tarragona del Batey near the confluence in 1645, and Governor Gregorio de Castellar authorized the short-lived settlement on 22 April 1646. The place later revived as ranch country after Carlos del Peral bought the García lands in 1740 and formed the Chaguaramal del Batey estate. In May 1760 the Andalusian Capuchin Anselmo Isidro de Ardales founded nearby Santo Tomás de Tucupío for Palenque and Cumanagoto people. A parish was authorized in 1779, and Bishop Mariano Martí's 1783 visit counted 119 houses in the settlement, 117 more nearby and 1,607 people around estates producing cotton, rice, maize, plantains, wheat and cassava. During the independence war Chaguaramal supported the Crown until Pedro Zaraza's republican troops occupied it in 1816; the town was burned. On 2 December 1817 Miguel de la Torre's royalists defeated Zaraza nearby at La Hogaza.
zh:
萨拉萨所在之地位于东亚诺斯草原与乌纳雷河低地相接处，草原小路在此汇通往委内瑞拉东部的道路。1444年，这里属于加勒比语族群的活动范围；后来在附近留下记载的帕伦克人和库马纳戈托人种植玉米、木薯和甘薯，在林带中狩猎，聚落有时还会设置木栅防卫。乌纳雷河与翁达溪交汇处的巴特伊已是道路要冲，但还没有西班牙城镇。

欧洲势力在1640年代进入这里。霍安·奥尔皮的副官米格尔·德·乌尔韦斯于1645年在两水交汇处附近设立圣米格尔·德拉新塔拉戈纳·德尔巴特伊，总督格雷戈里奥·德·卡斯特利亚尔于1646年4月22日批准这个存在不久的定居点。1740年，卡洛斯·德尔佩拉尔购有加西亚土地，建立查瓜拉马尔·德尔巴特伊牧场，该地才重新作为牧畜区发展。1760年5月，安达卢西亚嘉布遣会修士安塞尔莫·伊西德罗·德·阿达莱斯在附近为帕伦克人和库马纳戈托人建立图库皮奥的圣多马村。1779年，堂区获准设立；马里亚诺·马蒂主教1783年巡访时，统计到镇内119栋房屋、附近另有117栋，周围共有1607人，庄园出产棉花、稻米、玉米、香蕉、小麦和木薯。独立战争期间，查瓜拉马尔支持王室，1816年被佩德罗·萨拉萨的共和军占领，城镇遭到焚毁。1817年12月2日，米格尔·德拉托雷率领保王军在附近的拉奥加萨击败萨拉萨。

en:
Chichas is the rugged southern country of the Chicha people, where the Potosí highlands fall into the arid valleys around Tupiza, Talina and the Angostura River. Communities kept towns and mountain pastures along ancient caravan routes, while Tupiza was later remembered as a principal Chicha centre. In 1444 the land still stood on the southern edge of the Pacajes highland world, guarding the road from Upper Peru toward Tarija, the Puna de Atacama and the Chilean and Argentine frontiers.

Inca forces under Túpac Inca Yupanqui conquered the Chicha valleys around 1478 and integrated them into Qullasuyu; the state also transplanted some Chichas as mitimaes to frontier districts in what are now Argentina and Chile. Diego de Almagro's expedition reached Tupiza in 1535 and used the Chicha settlements as a supply base until January 1536 before pushing on toward Chile. The region entered the Viceroyalty of Peru in 1542, and on 2 January 1566 Judge Juan de Matienzo listed Chicha towns such as Ayavisca, Turqui and Talina along the Inca road, showing their place in the colonial tribute and transport system. In 1776 the southern Chichas lands were transferred to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. Their most famous battle came on 7 November 1810 at Suipacha, near Tupiza: forces sent from Buenos Aires under Balcarce, Castelli and Eustoquio Díaz Vélez, together with the Chicha leader Pedro Arraya, won the first patriot victory in Upper Peru. Control of the road and valleys remained contested when the wars reached 1821.
zh:
奇查斯是奇查人崎岖多山的南部故土，波托西高原在这里降入图皮萨、塔林纳和安戈斯图拉河一带的干旱谷地。当地群落沿古老商路经营城镇和高山牧场，图皮萨后来被铭记为奇查人的主要中心之一。1444年，这片土地仍位于帕卡赫斯高原世界的南缘，扼守着上秘鲁通往塔里哈、阿塔卡马高原以及智利、阿根廷边疆的道路。

图帕克·印卡·尤潘基麾下的印加军队约在1478年征服奇查谷地，将其纳入科利亚苏尤；国家还把一些奇查人作为米蒂马埃斯迁移到今阿根廷和智利境内的边疆区。迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗的远征队于1535年抵达图皮萨，在1536年1月前以奇查聚落为补给基地，随后继续前往智利。1542年，这一地区被划入秘鲁总督辖区；1566年1月2日，法官胡安·德·马廷索在信中沿印加道路列出阿亚维斯卡、图尔基、塔林纳等奇查城镇，显示它们已处于殖民贡赋和交通体系之中。1776年，南奇查斯土地被改属新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区。1810年11月7日，苏伊帕查战役在图皮萨附近爆发：巴尔卡斯、卡斯特利、埃乌斯托基奥·迪亚斯·贝莱斯率领的布宜诺斯艾利斯援军，与奇查人首领佩德罗·阿腊亚协同作战，赢得爱国者在上秘鲁的第一场胜利。战争进入1821年时，这条道路和周边谷地仍处在争夺之中。

en:
Choquechaca, 'silver bridge' in Quechua, is the cold high country of the Chayanta, some 4,000 metres up in the mountains north of Potosi, where Aymara-speaking ayllus herded llamas and worked small veins of metal. In 1444 these valleys still lay beyond the Inca frontier: Tupac Inca Yupanqui's late-fifteenth-century campaigns made Chayanta part of Collasuyu, its warriors marched in the Inca armies, and Guarani Chiriguanos kept raiding in from the eastern lowlands. Under Spanish rule the district became one of the great silverfields of Upper Peru, for the mines of Aullagas and Hankonasa were ranked with those of Porco and Potosi. Around them grew the mining town of Colquechaca, whose camps at more than 4,000 metres were fed by the forced mita labour of the surrounding communities.

In 1776 Chayanta passed with the Audiencia of Charcas to the new Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata. In 1778 Tomas Katari, a cacique of Macha, walked to Buenos Aires to protest that a Spaniard had stolen his office and his people's tribute; on his return the corregidor's men jailed him, and armed communities freed him by force. The rising he led overran the province, and when a patrol took him near Aullagas and murdered him at the Chataquilla pass on 15 January 1781, his brothers Damaso and Nicolas carried the revolt on to Challapata and Chuquisaca, alongside the Andean rebellions of Tupac Amaru at Cuzco and Tupac Katari at La Paz. Royalist troops crushed the movement and executed its leaders. After 1809 the mining province changed hands again and again: Manuel Belgrano's defeat at Ayohuma on 14 November 1813 left Upper Peru to the royalist armies, though irregular bands in these mountains kept fighting as the wars entered 1821.
zh:
卓奎查卡（今译科尔克查卡，克丘亚语意为「银桥」）地处波托西北方海拔约4000米的查扬塔高寒山区，艾马拉语村社在此放牧美洲驼、开采零星矿脉。1444年时这些山谷还在印加边界之外：15世纪末图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的远征把查扬塔并入科利亚苏尤，当地战士被编入印加军队，瓜拉尼人的奇里瓜诺分支则不断从东部低地前来袭扰。西班牙统治时期，这里成为上秘鲁最重要的银矿区之一，奥亚加斯和安科纳萨的银矿被认为可与波尔科、波托西比肩。矿场周围形成科尔克查卡镇，海拔4000多米的营地靠周边村社的米塔徭役劳力维持。

1776年，查扬塔随查尔卡斯检审庭划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区。1778年，马查村酋长托马斯·卡塔里为抗议西班牙人篡夺其酋长职位、侵吞村社贡赋，步行前往布宜诺斯艾利斯申诉，回乡后却被省督手下逮捕，武装村社将他武力救出。他领导的起义席卷全省；当巡逻队在奥亚加斯附近再次抓获他，并于1781年1月15日在查塔基利亚山口将他杀害后，其弟达马索和尼古拉斯把起义推进到查亚帕塔和丘基萨卡，与库斯科的图帕克·阿马鲁二世、拉帕斯的图帕克·卡塔里大起义遥相呼应。起义最终被保王军镇压，领袖被处死。1809年以后的独立战争中，这片矿区反复易手：1813年11月14日贝尔格拉诺在阿约乌马战败，上秘鲁重归保王军，而山间的非正规武装一直坚持战斗到1821年战争末期。

en:
The broken highlands north of Potosi, cold valleys and plains between La Paz, Oruro and Cochabamba, were the homeland of the Charcas, who called themselves Qhara Qhara, a warrior people speaking Aymara. Their confederation kept its capital at Sacaca, and in 1444 it lived under its own lords, free of Inca rule. That freedom ended in the 1470s, when Tupac Inca Yupanqui's armies subdued the country after heavy fighting and made it a province of Collasuyu; the chief Copacatiraca helped persuade his people to submit. The Incas prized the Charcas as soldiers, and Wayna Capac recruited them in great numbers for his northern campaigns.

When Gonzalo Pizarro entered the country in 1538, the Charca lord Consara made friends with the Spaniards and showed them the silver deposits of Porco, opening the way to the riches of Potosi. The colonial corregimiento of Charcas then supplied the mita levies that kept the Cerro Rico working. From the 1580s its mining camps were drawn into the long feud between the Basque Vascongados and the creole Vicunas, and in 1617 Jose Alonso de Ibanez led an uprising at Potosi that ended with his execution. In 1776 the district passed to the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata and in 1782 into the new intendancy system. During the wars after 1809 royalist and patriot armies repeatedly marched its roads between Oruro, Cochabamba and Potosi, and as the war entered 1821 these highlands were still held by royalist troops.
zh:
波托西北方这片崎岖高地处在拉帕斯、奥鲁罗和科恰班巴之间，由寒冷的山谷与高原组成，是自称卡拉卡拉（Qhara Qhara）的查尔卡人的故土——这个善战的艾马拉语族群以萨卡卡为联盟首府。1444年时，他们在自己的酋长治理下生活，还不受印加统治。1470年代，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的大军经激战后征服此地，把它设为科利亚苏尤的一个省；首领科帕卡蒂拉卡曾劝说族人归附。印加人极为看重查尔卡士兵，瓦伊纳·卡帕克曾把他们大量征往北方战场。

1538年贡萨洛·皮萨罗进入这里时，查尔卡首领孔萨拉与西班牙人交好，向他们指明波尔科的银矿，为征服打开了通往波托西财富的道路。殖民时期的查尔卡斯辖区随后承担米塔徭役，持续为波托西里科山输送劳力。1580年代起，各矿营卷入巴斯克人的「巴斯孔加多斯」与克里奥尔人的「比库尼亚斯」之间长达数十年的仇杀；1617年，何塞·阿隆索·德·伊瓦涅斯在波托西率众起事，事败被处死。1776年这一地区划归拉普拉塔总督辖区，1782年又被纳入新的行政区制度。1809年以后的独立战争中，保王军与爱国军反复在奥鲁罗、科恰班巴与波托西之间的道路上行军，直到1821年战争进入末期，这片高地仍握在保王军手中。

en:
The Chachapoyas, called the 'warriors of the clouds', lived in the misty eastern Andes above the Utcubamba River, terracing cloud-forest slopes and building circular stone houses. At Kuelap their masons girdled a limestone ridge with walls rising in places to nineteen metres, creating a stronghold and ceremonial centre above the valley. Chachapoya was the Inca name for these people, perhaps meaning 'people of the cloud forest'; their country was divided among local chiefs rather than ruled from one court. In 1444 it remained independent, a fortified highland farming country between the Andes and the Amazon.

Tupac Inca Yupanqui conquered Chachapoyas around 1470, campaigning through Pías, Cajamarquilla, Raimipampa and Levanto, where the Incas built a military bastion. The new order remained fragile: two revolts broke out under Huayna Capac, many Chachapoyas were deported as mitmas and foreign colonists were settled in their valleys. The civil war between Huascar and Atahualpa left the land divided when Alonso de Alvarado arrived in 1535, finding epidemic and factional violence. He founded San Juan de la Frontera de los Chachapoyas on 5 September 1538, and the settlement was moved to its present site around 1545. Encomiendas and reductions concentrated the survivors, Kuelap was abandoned around 1570 and the Ipapuy uprising of 1549 was crushed. On 6 June 1821 patriots defeated a royalist force from Moyobamba at Higos Urco and swore local independence.
zh:
查查波亚人被称为「云中武士」，居住在乌特库班巴河上游云雾缭绕的东安第斯山区，在云雾林坡地上开垦梯田、建造圆形石屋。他们在库埃拉普的石灰岩山脊上筑起城墙，部分墙段高达19米，形成俯瞰河谷的要塞与礼仪中心。「查查波亚」是印加人对他们的称呼，可能意为「云雾林之人」；这片土地由众多地方首领分治，而不是由一个统一王廷统治。1444年，它仍是安第斯山脉与亚马孙雨林之间一片独立的高地农区，凭要塞自保。

约1470年，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基经皮亚斯、卡哈马基利亚、莱米班巴和莱万托征服查查波亚，并在莱万托修建军事据点。新秩序并不稳固：瓦伊纳·卡帕克在位时爆发两次叛乱，许多查查波亚人被作为米特马迁往帝国别处，外来垦殖者则被安置进他们的谷地。瓦斯卡尔与阿塔瓦尔帕的内战使这里陷入分裂；1535年阿隆索·德·阿尔瓦拉多到来时，当地正遭受疫病和派系冲突。1538年9月5日，他建立圣胡安·德拉弗龙特拉·德·洛斯查查波亚斯，居民点约在1545年迁到今址。监护征赋制和集居村镇把幸存者集中起来，库埃拉普约在1570年废弃，1549年的伊帕普伊起义也遭镇压。1821年6月6日，爱国者在伊戈斯乌尔科击败来自莫约班巴的保王军，并宣誓当地独立。

en:
The Ucayali takes shape where the Tambo and Urubamba rivers meet, then winds north through seasonally flooded rainforest below the Andean foothills. By the fifteenth century, Pano-speaking Shipibo, Conibo and Shetebo communities lived along its banks, oxbow lakes and tributaries, while Piro or Yine people of the Maipurean language family occupied upper-river and Urubamba reaches. Canoes, fishing, riverside gardens and hunting tied the villages to the water and kept them apart from highland states. In 1444 Inca armies and governors had not subdued the lowland forest; Ucayali was a network of autonomous river settlements, not a provincial capital.

Recorded missionary penetration began only in the mid-seventeenth century, first by Franciscans and later by Jesuits, and the mission villages founded between the Ucayali and the Perené remained fragile. In 1742 Juan Santos Atahualpa, a Cuzco-born leader who claimed to be Atahualpa returned, led the forest peoples in revolt. Asháninka, Yanesha, Shipibo, Piro and Quechua fighters destroyed or forced the evacuation of 23 missions. The 1752 raid on Andamarca showed the limits of Spanish power, and the Crown largely abandoned attempts to reconquer the central jungle. On 15 July 1802 a royal cédula created the General Command of Maynas, formally bringing Ucayali under a viceregal frontier government and ordering garrisons toward Portuguese Brazil. When independence was proclaimed on the Pacific in 1821, that authority still scarcely reached most river villages.
zh:
乌卡亚利河由坦博河与乌鲁班巴河汇合而成，随后在安第斯山麓以东穿过季节性泛滥的雨林北流。到15世纪，说帕诺语的希皮博、科尼博和谢特博群体已生活在它的河岸、牛轭湖和支流旁；属于马伊普雷语族的皮罗（又称伊内）人则占据上游及乌鲁班巴河一带。独木舟、渔猎和河畔园地把这些村落同河流联系在一起，也使它们同高地国家保持距离。1444年，印加军队和官员尚未征服低地雨林；乌卡亚利是一片由自治河畔聚落组成的网络，而不是某个行省治城。

有记载的传教进入迟至17世纪中叶才开始，方济各会先来，耶稣会随后；他们在乌卡亚利河与佩雷内河之间建立的传教村落始终脆弱。1742年，出身库斯科、自称阿塔瓦尔帕转世的胡安·桑托斯·阿塔瓦尔帕率领丛林诸族起义。阿沙宁卡、亚内沙、希皮博、皮罗和克丘亚战士摧毁或迫使西班牙人撤离了23座传教站。1752年起义者突袭安塔马尔卡，暴露出西班牙力量的极限；王室此后基本放弃重新征服中央丛林，只在西侧防守。1802年7月15日，国王诏令设立迈纳斯军政区，正式把乌卡亚利划入一个总督辖区边地政府，并命令在朝向葡属巴西的边界布置驻军。1821年太平洋沿岸宣布独立时，这种权力仍几乎没有触及大多数河畔村落。

en:
The future site of Yurimaguas lies in the lowland rainforest where the lower Huallaga meets the Paranapura and Shanusi rivers. In 1444 there was no town of that name. Shawi or Chayahuita people canoed the Paranapura, Cahuapanas, Sillay, Supayacu and Shanusi, while Muniche communities lived on the lower Paranapura. Their villages lived from fishing, hunting, riverside gardens and canoe-borne exchange beyond the reach of the Inca Empire. The Yurimagua people, whose migrants would later give the place its name, still lived far to the east between the Napo and Negro rivers.

Alonso de Mercadillo and Diego Núñez became the first Spaniards known to cross Chayahuita territory in 1538 and 1539. The Jesuit Mainas missions began in 1638, and in 1654 Chayahuita, Jebero and Muniche people were gathered into a mission where epidemics took a heavy toll. In 1686 the Bohemian Jesuit Samuel Fritz began working among the eastern Yurimagua, Omagua and neighboring peoples, founding reductions between the Napo and Negro. Repeated attacks by Brazilian Bandeirantes from the 1690s led him to lead survivors westward, and on 8 December 1709 he founded Santa María de las Nieves de Yurimaguas at the Shanusi–Paranapura confluence, the origin of the present town. After the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 many people abandoned the missions, while Franciscans took over part of the network. In 1802 the territory was placed in the General Command of Maynas; when Peruvian independence came in 1821, this river port remained on the edge of the viceregal frontier.
zh:
后来尤里马瓜斯所在之地，是瓦亚加河下游与帕拉纳普拉河、沙努西河交汇处的低地雨林。1444年，这里还没有同名城镇。沙维（查亚维塔）人在帕拉纳普拉河、卡瓦帕纳斯河、锡亚伊河、苏帕亚库河和沙努西河上往来行舟，穆尼切人群体则住在帕拉纳普拉河下游。各村落以渔猎、河畔园地和独木舟交换为生，远在印加帝国势力之外。后来把名称带给这座城镇的尤里马瓜人，当时仍生活在东方遥远的纳波河与内格罗河之间。

1538年和1539年，阿隆索·德·梅尔卡迪略与迭戈·努涅斯成为已知最早穿过查亚维塔地区的西班牙人。耶稣会的迈纳斯传教事业始于1638年；1654年，查亚维塔人、赫贝罗人和穆尼切人被集中到一处传教村，疫病使人口损失惨重。1686年，波希米亚耶稣会士萨穆埃尔·弗里茨开始到东方的尤里马瓜、奥马瓜及邻近族群中传教，在纳波河与内格罗河之间建立集居村。自1690年代起，巴西捕奴旗队不断袭击，他带领幸存者西迁，并于1709年12月8日在沙努西河与帕拉纳普拉河汇合处建立圣玛利亚·德·拉斯·涅韦斯·德·尤里马瓜斯，这便是今城的起源。1767年耶稣会被驱逐后，许多原住民离开传教村，方济各会接管了部分网络。1802年，该地划入迈纳斯军政区；1821年秘鲁独立时，这座河港仍处在总督辖区边疆的边缘。

en:
Quillacas is the high Aymara country around the southern approaches to Lake Poopó, where the Oruro and Potosí plateaux merge into arid caravan country. After the decline of Tiwanaku, the Quillacas emerged with the Carangas among the Aymara lordships, holding pastures, lake shores and mountain roads between the Pacajes world and the southern deserts. In 1444 their communities were still living in the last decades of that independent highland order, as Inca power pressed into Qullasuyu.

During the later fifteenth-century conquests, Quillaca became a huamani, one of the twenty-eight provinces of Inca Qullasuyu. Spanish rule then placed the land within Upper Peru, and Potosí's silver rush after 1545 gave its people a harsh place in the colonial order: by 1581 Potosí had the church of San Sebastián for Quillacas mitayos. Even beyond mining, the plateau remained a corridor between Oruro, Potosí, Chichas and Atacama. A colonial church and sanctuary stood at Quillacas itself.
zh:
基亚卡斯是波波湖南缘一带的艾马拉高原故土，奥鲁罗与波托西高原在这里相接，并伸向干旱的商队地带。蒂亚瓦纳科衰落之后，基亚卡人与卡兰加人同属艾马拉诸领地，占据着帕卡赫斯世界与南部荒漠之间的牧场、湖岸和山路。1444年，印加势力正向科利亚苏尤推进，而他们的群落仍生活在这个独立高原秩序的最后数十年间。

在15世纪后期的征服中，基亚卡斯成为一个「瓦马尼」，即印加科利亚苏尤二十八省之一。西班牙统治随后把这片土地划入上秘鲁，1545年以后的波托西采银潮又使这里的人在殖民秩序中承受了严酷位置：到1581年，波托西已有为基亚卡斯米塔劳工设置的圣塞瓦斯蒂安教堂。除矿业外，这片高原仍是奥鲁罗、波托西、奇查斯和阿塔卡马之间的通道。基亚卡斯当地还建有殖民时期的教堂和圣所。

en:
Macaya was the old Colla stopping place that became Azángaro; Spanish local histories place it six kilometres east of the present town on the cold plains north-west of Lake Titicaca. Caravans used the road between Cuzco and Alto Perú, and barter at the pascana gave it the name Aswan Q'atu, the great market. Colla farmers kept llamas and raised potatoes and quinoa on the high plain. In 1444 Macaya was a chief place of the Colla lords of Omasuyos, while Pachacuti's armies were about to enter the Collao.

The Colla–Inca War of 1445–1450 brought the market and its road under Cuzco. Local tradition connects the name aswan qharis, 'the strongest men', with the inhabitants' bloody resistance to Pachacuti. Captain Manuel Ortiz Aguilar reached Macaya in November 1535; a priest reported a cat-like idol with eyes of precious stones, and Dominicans established the doctrine of Our Lady of the Rosary. Water shortage and continuing native worship led the settlement to move, and on 5 July 1586 the Viceroy Count of Villar authorized Diego Chuquihuanca to found Spanish Azángaro; the first stone of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción was laid on 22 August. In 1776 the district passed to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. During the 1780–1783 Andean rising Azángaro became a rebel centre. Pedro Vilca Apaza, born there in 1741, led the siege of Sorata with Andrés Túpac Amaru and was executed in the town on 8 April 1782. Its colonial church of San Bernardo was famed for its gilded interior.
zh:
马卡亚是后来成为阿桑加罗的旧科拉驿站；西班牙地方史把它定位在今镇以东6公里、的的喀喀湖西北的寒冷平原。商队取道库斯科与上秘鲁之间的道路，驿站中的物物交换使它得到「阿苏万卡图」之称，意为大市场。科拉农民在高原上牧养大羊驼，种植马铃薯和藜麦。1444年，马卡亚是奥马苏约斯科拉首领的要地，而帕查库特克的军队即将进入科亚奥。

1445—1450年的科拉—印加战争使这个市场和道路归入库斯科治下。当地传统把「阿苏万卡里」（最强壮的人）这一称呼与居民对帕查库特克的浴血抵抗联系起来。1535年11月，曼努埃尔·奥尔蒂斯·阿吉拉尔上尉抵达马卡亚；一名神父报告那里有一尊眼睛嵌着宝石的猫形偶像，多明我会士随后建立玫瑰圣母传教区。由于缺水且本地崇拜仍在延续，聚落后来迁移；1586年7月5日，比利亚尔伯爵总督授权迭戈·丘基万卡建立西班牙式阿桑加罗，8月22日安放圣母升天堂的第一块基石。1776年，此地划归拉普拉塔总督辖区。1780—1783年的安第斯起义中，阿桑加罗成为起义中心。1741年出生于此的佩德罗·比尔卡·阿帕萨与安德烈斯·图帕克·阿马鲁一同指挥索拉塔围城战，1782年4月8日在镇中被处决。当地的圣贝尔纳多殖民教堂则以镀金内堂闻名。

en:
Matamba was an Mbundu kingdom in the wooded savanna east of Ndongo, in the Baixa de Cassanje country of Angola's Malanje Province. Its rulers, like the lords of Ndongo, bore the title of ngola, and its village communities lived in the orbit of the Mbundu powers and the great kingdom of Kongo. In 1444 no European had yet reached this far inland: the Portuguese would not found Luanda until 1575, and Matamba's name first appears in writing in 1530, when its ruler sent tribute to Afonso I of Kongo. Kongo's overlordship was never more than symbolic, and Matamba's closest ties were always with Ndongo.

War arrived with the Portuguese. A Matamba army helped Ndongo rout the invaders at the Lukala in 1590, but in 1618–21 Portuguese columns and their Imbangala allies ravaged the country, and thousands of its people were shipped to Spanish America as slaves. In 1629 Queen Njinga of Ndongo, driven out of her own kingdom, defeated Matamba's queen Mwongo Matamba and from 1631 made the town of Matamba the capital of a joined Ndongo–Matamba state. She allied with the Dutch when they seized Luanda in 1641 and crushed a Portuguese army at the battle of Kombi in 1647; after the Dutch withdrawal she made peace in 1657 and received Italian Capuchins, who baptized thousands. Njinga died in 1663, and in 1681 her successor Francisco beat off a Portuguese invasion at Katole on 4 September but fell in the battle; his sister Verónica I, who ruled until 1721, accepted only nominal vassalage by the treaty of 1683. Another Portuguese invasion in 1744 ended in a similar face-saving treaty for Queen Ana II, and Matamba kept its real independence to the end of the era.
zh:
马坦巴是姆本杜人的王国，位于恩东戈以东的林木稀树草原，即今安哥拉马兰热省的卡桑热低地一带。其统治者和恩东戈君主一样称恩戈拉，诸村落处在姆本杜诸政权与刚果王国的势力圈中。1444年还没有欧洲人深入到这片内陆：葡萄牙人要到1575年才建立罗安达，而马坦巴之名最早见于文字是1530年，其君主向刚果国王阿方索一世进贡。刚果的宗主权始终只是名义上的，马坦巴最紧密的关系一直在恩东戈一边。

战争随葡萄牙人而来。1590年，马坦巴出兵助恩东戈在卢卡拉击溃入侵者；但1618至1621年间，葡萄牙军队与其姆班加拉盟军蹂躏此地，数以千计的居民被掳往西属美洲为奴。1629年，被逐出本国的恩东戈女王恩津加击败马坦巴女王姆翁戈·马坦巴，1631年起以马坦巴城为都，把它与恩东戈合并为一国。1641年荷兰人夺取罗安达，她立刻与之结盟，1647年在科姆比之战大败葡军；荷兰人撤走后，她于1657年议和，接纳意大利嘉布遣会传教士，数千臣民受洗。恩津加1663年去世，1681年9月4日继位者弗朗西斯科在卡托莱击退葡萄牙入侵，本人却战死阵中；其妹韦罗妮卡一世统治至1721年，依1683年条约仅接受名义上的臣属。1744年葡萄牙再度入侵，女王阿娜二世同样以一纸保全颜面的条约了结，直至本时期结束马坦巴都保持着实际独立。

en:
Mbata was the eastern march of the Kingdom of Kongo and, in the country's memory, its oldest partner. Its king Nsaku Lau gave his daughter in marriage to Nimi a Nzima of Mpemba Kasi around 1375, and from that union came Lukeni lua Nimi, the first manikongo; in memory of it the mwene Mbata held the title Nkaka andi Mwene Kongo, 'grandfather of the king of Kongo', his office passing by matrilineal inheritance rather than royal appointment. From Mbanza Mbata, on the plateau above the Inkisi near the later Angola border, the province led Kongo's eastward drive into the cloth-weaving lands of Kongo dia Nlaza. In 1444 its princes still spoke for Kongo in dealings with the interior, and its markets sent grain and raffia cloth west to the capital.

After the conversion of the court the Portuguese knew Mbata as the Duchy of Bambata, and Mbanza Mbata, rebuilt from the late sixteenth century, received a stone church in the seventeenth. Yet the grandfather's power had shrunk to honour by 1620, when Mbata was remembered only through its ancient title. In 1665 António I fell at Mbwila, and for forty years Kongo tore itself apart between the Kimpanzu and Kinlaza; São Salvador was sacked in 1678 and rival kings held out in mountain strongholds in the eastern provinces. Only with the restoration of the kingship in the early eighteenth century did Mbata's roads and markets know peace again.
zh:
姆巴塔是刚果王国的东疆，在这个国家的记忆中也是最古老的盟友。约1375年，姆巴塔王恩萨库·劳将女儿嫁给姆潘巴·卡西的首领尼米·阿·恩齐马，二人生下的卢基尼·卢阿·尼米便是第一位马尼刚果；为纪念这桩联姻，姆巴塔长官保有「恩卡卡·安迪·姆韦内刚果」之号，意为「刚果王的祖父」，其职位按母系世代相承，而非由国王任命。从因基西河上游、靠近后来安哥拉边界的高原首府姆班扎姆巴塔出发，姆巴塔率领刚果向东进入「刚果·迪亚·恩拉扎」的织布之乡。1444年，姆巴塔的王公仍代表刚果与内陆交涉，市集上的谷物和拉菲草布源源西运，输往王都。

王室皈依基督教后，葡萄牙人称姆巴塔为班巴塔公国；16世纪末起重建的姆班扎姆巴塔在17世纪建起一座石砌教堂。然而到1620年，「祖父」的实权已只剩荣名，人们提到姆巴塔时只余那个古老头衔。1665年安东尼奥一世殒命姆布维拉，此后四十年间刚果在金潘祖与金拉扎两派之间自相残杀，圣萨尔瓦多于1678年遭洗劫，争位的国王们在东部诸省的山寨中负隅固守。直到18世纪初王权重立，姆巴塔的商路与市集才重归太平。

en: Buhera, or VuHera, is the country of the Hera Shona around Gombe Hill and the upper Save River, where the VaHera of the Museyamwa totem lived under the Nyashanu chiefly line. In 1444 its grazing lands and elephant country formed part of the southern tributary world of Mutapa, between declining Great Zimbabwe and the gold-bearing Manyika highlands, with ivory moving toward Sofala. Portuguese fairs took root in Manyika in the late sixteenth century, but Changamire Dombo's Rozvi armies overran that kingdom in the 1690s and drew the Hera hill chiefs into the Rozvi order; Hera genealogies also remembered marriage ties with Rozvi rulers. The Changamire succession war of 1768 and the drought of 1795-1800 weakened central power.
zh: 布海拉（VuHera）意为赫拉人的土地，是贡贝山与萨韦河上游一带赫拉绍纳人的家园；穆塞亚姆瓦图腾的瓦赫拉人在尼亚沙努酋长谱系下居住于此。1444年时，这里的牧场和猎象之地属于穆塔帕南部纳贡网络的一部分，处在衰落中的大津巴布韦与产金马尼卡高地之间，象牙则流向索法拉。16世纪后期，葡萄牙商站在马尼卡扎根，但昌加米雷·敦布的罗兹维军队在17世纪90年代征服马尼卡，也把赫拉山地酋长纳入罗兹维秩序；赫拉人的谱系还保留着与罗兹维统治者联姻的记忆。1768年的昌加米雷继承战争和1795年至1800年的旱灾削弱了中央权力。

en:
Manyika was the gold-bearing highland country of the Manyika Shona, lying between Mutapa's southern province of Guruuswa and the coast-facing kingdom of Uteve. Its rulers bore the title Chikanga, and gold washed from its streams joined ivory on the Sofala road long before the Portuguese reached the interior. In 1444 local Manyika chiefs still controlled their hill valleys and mining camps, although the expansion of Mutapa and the trade rivalries of Sofala were already drawing them into highland politics.

Around 1500, during Chikuyo's reign, the Barue king Makombe sent his son Chikanga into the highlands; he occupied Manyika and checked Uteve, making the kingdom a Mutapa vassal. After Portugal took Sofala in 1506, control over the route to Manyika's gold became a recurring cause of war, and in the late sixteenth century the Mwenemutapa allowed a Portuguese feira in the kingdom. Manyika broke away during Mutapa's early-seventeenth-century civil wars, but a Portuguese army conquered it in 1632. In 1695 Changamire Dombo's Rozvi forces invaded, temporarily closed its fairs and installed their own Chikanga, possibly the exiled Mwenemutapa Nyakunembire, founder of the Mutasa dynasty. Manyika remained under Rozvi suzerainty until the mid-eighteenth century, when it again became effectively independent.
zh:
马尼卡是马尼卡绍纳人的产金高地，位于穆塔帕南方省古鲁乌斯瓦与面向海岸的乌泰韦王国之间。当地统治者称奇坎加，河川中淘出的黄金早在葡萄牙人深入内陆以前，就与象牙一起沿索法拉商路外运。1444年时，马尼卡本地酋长仍控制着山谷和采金营地，但穆塔帕的扩张以及索法拉的贸易争夺，已经把他们卷入高原政治。

约1500年，在奇库约在位期间，巴鲁埃王马孔贝派儿子奇坎加进入高地，占据马尼卡并阻挡乌泰韦，使这个王国成为穆塔帕属国。1506年葡萄牙夺取索法拉后，通往马尼卡黄金的道路一再成为战争焦点；16世纪后期，姆韦尼穆塔帕允许葡萄牙人在王国境内开设商站。17世纪初，马尼卡趁穆塔帕内战脱离，但葡萄牙军队又在1632年征服此地。1695年，昌加米雷·敦布的罗兹维军队入侵，一度关闭商站，并改立自己的奇坎加，可能就是流亡的姆韦尼穆塔帕尼亚库嫩比雷，即穆塔萨王朝的开创者。马尼卡此后臣服于罗兹维，直到18世纪中叶才再度实际独立。

en:
Madanda was the Shona-speaking country of the Madanda, later counted among the five main Ndau groups, lying on the inland approaches between Sofala and the Manyika highlands. Its villages kept cattle and cultivated while elephant herds supplied ivory for the coastal trade in cloth and beads. In 1444 the country stood on the south-eastern edge of the expanding Mutapa world, close enough to Sofala to share its Swahili commercial network but still governed through local chiefs.

Mutapa traditions remembered Matope's armies overrunning Teve and Madanda as the empire pushed toward the coast. In the early sixteenth century the Sachiteve declared Uteve independent with Changamire II's help, conquered Madanda and installed his younger brother as its first Sedanda. Control of the road from Portuguese Sofala to the gold of Manyika then drew Madanda into the Mutapa-Teve wars that continued into the 1540s. In the 1640s a Portuguese settler who had helped the Sachiteve keep power received northern Uteve as a prazo, bringing armed European clients close to Madanda. A Portuguese coup against Uteve failed in the 1690s amid the Rozvi rise, allowing the reduced kingdom to regain its sovereignty.
zh:
马丹达是说绍纳语的马丹达人之地，后来被列为恩达人五大支系之一，位于索法拉与马尼卡高地之间的内陆通道上。当地村落务农养牛，象群提供象牙，用以在海岸贸易中交换布匹和珠子。1444年时，这里处在穆塔帕扩张世界的东南边缘，既近索法拉、能接入斯瓦希里贸易网络，又仍由本地酋长治理。

穆塔帕传说记得，马托佩的军队在向海岸推进时征服了特维和马丹达。16世纪初，萨奇特韦借昌加米雷二世之助宣布乌泰维脱离穆塔帕，随后征服马丹达，并立自己的弟弟为第一代塞丹达。从葡萄牙控制的索法拉通往马尼卡黄金的道路至关重要，马丹达因此被卷入穆塔帕与特维的战争，战祸一直延续到16世纪40年代。17世纪40年代，一名协助萨奇特韦保住权位的葡萄牙拓殖者获得乌泰维北部作为普拉佐，也把武装的欧洲依附者带到马丹达附近。17世纪90年代罗兹维兴起时，葡萄牙人推翻萨奇特韦的图谋失败，旧王国虽然疆域缩小，却恢复了独立。

en:
Djerba is a 514-square-kilometre island in the Gulf of Gabès, the largest island off North Africa. Its sheltered roadsteads, olive groves, gardens and small market ports gave it a place in Mediterranean trade long before the Ottomans reached the Maghreb. Arab forces took the island in 665, and Ibadi Islam became one of its enduring marks; Djerba was often semi-independent, passing uneasily between the Aghlabids, Rustamids, Fatimids and later Berber dynasties. A Norman force stormed it in 1135 and carried off many women and children to Sicily, before the Hafsids brought it into their Ifriqiyan state. In 1444 Djerba belonged to the Hafsid rulers of Tunis, where Ibadi villagers, Jewish communities, olive pressers and sailors made it a distinctive and outward-looking island.

The Ottoman-Spanish struggle over collapsing Hafsid Tunisia reached Djerba in the 1530s. A Christian coalition of Spanish, Papal, Genoese, Maltese and Neapolitan forces seized the island and built a fortress early in 1560, but Piali Pasha's Ottoman fleet attacked in May and destroyed much of the allied force, with Dragut Pasha joining the fighting and thousands of men killed or carried into captivity. Ottoman rule over Tunisia was secured only after the fall of Tunis and La Goulette in 1574. The island then shared in the rule of pashas and deys, the Muradid beys from 1628 to 1702, and the Husainid beys after 1705. Djerban merchants and sailors remained active across the Ottoman Mediterranean, and Hammuda Pasha's long rule from 1782 to 1814 gave Tunisia broad autonomy under the Husainids. In 1821 the island remained tied to Tunis, olive oil, shipping and its old Ibadi religious life.
zh:
杰尔巴是加贝斯湾中一座面积514平方公里的岛屿，也是北非近海最大的岛屿。早在奥斯曼势力抵达马格里布之前，岛上隐蔽的锚地、橄榄园、园圃和小型商港就已使它进入地中海贸易网络。665年，阿拉伯军队攻占杰尔巴，伊巴德派伊斯兰教此后成为这里的持久印记；岛屿长期保持半独立状态，在艾格莱卜王朝、鲁斯塔姆王朝、法蒂玛王朝及后来的柏柏尔王朝之间艰难易手。1135年，诺曼军队攻陷杰尔巴，把许多妇孺掳往西西里，后来哈夫斯王朝将它并入伊夫里奇亚。1444年，杰尔巴臣服于突尼斯的哈夫斯统治者；岛上的伊巴德派村民、犹太居民、榨油匠和水手，使这里成为一座特色鲜明、面向海洋的岛屿。

16世纪30年代，奥斯曼与西班牙争夺衰落的哈夫斯突尼斯，战火烧到杰尔巴。1560年初，由西班牙、教皇国、热那亚、马耳他和那不勒斯组成的基督教联军夺取岛屿并修筑堡垒，但皮雅利帕夏的奥斯曼舰队在5月发起攻击，摧毁大量联军舰船，德拉古特帕夏也参战，数千人战死或被俘。直到1574年突尼斯与拉古莱特陷落，奥斯曼对突尼斯的统治才稳固下来。此后，杰尔巴先后经历帕夏与德伊统治、1628年至1702年的穆拉德贝伊政权，以及1705年后的侯赛因贝伊王朝。杰尔巴商人和水手仍活跃于奥斯曼地中海各地；1782年至1814年哈穆达帕夏长期执政，使侯赛因王朝治下的突尼斯拥有广泛自治。1821年，这座岛屿仍同突尼斯、橄榄油、航运和古老的伊巴德派宗教生活紧密相连。

en:
Ingolstadt guards a Danube crossing on the road from Munich to Nuremberg. First recorded on 6 February 806 as the Carolingian royal estate Ingoldesstat, it became a planned Wittelsbach walled town and from 1392 the capital of the small Duchy of Bavaria-Ingolstadt. Duke Louis VII ringed it with walls of eighty-seven towers and began the New Castle and the Church of Our Lady. Upstream, Neuburg commanded the next Danube crossing: on 4 October 1443 Louis VIII took it after a four-month siege and handed over his own father, Louis VII, to Henry XVI of Bavaria-Landshut. In 1444 Ingolstadt was a Catholic ducal residence and a salt and wine market, its ruling line already broken; when Louis VII died in prison in 1447 the duchy passed to Landshut.

Louis IX founded Bavaria's first university here on 13 March 1472. The town's most famous document followed on 23 April 1516, when Dukes William IV and Louis X issued the Bavarian state ordinance containing the beer-purity rule since called the Reinheitsgebot. After the Landshut succession war Neuburg became the seat of the new Wittelsbach principality of Palatinate-Neuburg in 1505, and Count Palatine Ottheinrich introduced Lutheran teaching there in 1542; Ingolstadt became the Catholic answer, its state fortress built from 1537 to about 1565, its Jesuit college opened in 1549 and Johann Eck teaching at the university. In April 1632 Gustavus Adolphus failed to storm the fortress, the first in Germany to hold out through a whole Swedish siege; a cannon shot killed the king's horse under him, and the town had the animal preserved and showed the Schwedenschimmel for centuries. Tilly, wounded earlier against the Swedes, died here on 30 April 1632, and Swedish troops occupied Neuburg again and again until 1634. Adam Weishaupt, a professor at the university, founded the Order of the Illuminati in Ingolstadt on 1 May 1776, and Mary Shelley set Victor Frankenstein and his anatomy studies in the same town. The French razed the fortress after entering in July 1799 and moved the university to Landshut; Palatinate-Neuburg was absorbed into Bavarian administration in 1808.
zh:
英戈尔施塔特扼守多瑙河渡口，位于慕尼黑通往纽伦堡的大道上。806年2月6日，它首次以加洛林王室领地「英戈尔德施塔特」之名见于记载，后来成为维特尔斯巴赫家族规划营建的城墙城镇，1392年起是小巴伐利亚-英戈尔施塔特公国的都城。路德维希七世公爵为它修起有87座塔楼的城墙，又动工兴建新宫和圣母教堂。上游的诺伊堡控制着多瑙河上的下一处渡口：1443年10月4日，路德维希八世经四个月围城拿下该城，还把自己的父亲路德维希七世交给巴伐利亚-兰茨胡特的亨利十六世。1444年的英戈尔施塔特是天主教公爵驻地和盐、酒贸易城市，统治家族却已崩坏；路德维希七世1447年死于囚中后，公国并入兰茨胡特。

1472年3月13日，路德维希九世在此创办巴伐利亚第一所大学。本城最出名的一份文件在1516年4月23日颁布：威廉四世与路德维希十世发布巴伐利亚邦法，其中关于啤酒原料的规定后来被称为《纯酿法》。兰茨胡特继承战争结束后，诺伊堡于1505年成为维特尔斯巴赫新邦国普法尔茨-诺伊堡的驻地，行宫伯爵奥特海因里希1542年在此引入路德宗；英戈尔施塔特则成为天主教一方的回应：国家要塞1537年至约1565年修筑，耶稣会学院1549年开办，约翰·埃克在大学任教。1632年4月，古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫未能攻下这座要塞，它也是第一座顶住瑞典人全程围攻的德意志要塞；一发炮弹击毙了国王胯下的战马，城里人将马剥制后长期展出，称为「瑞典灰马」。此前与瑞典人作战受伤的蒂利于1632年4月30日在此死去，1634年前瑞典军队又反复占领诺伊堡。大学教授亚当·魏斯豪普特1776年5月1日在英戈尔施塔特创立光明会，玛丽·雪莱后来也把学生维克多·弗兰肯斯坦和他的解剖学业安排在这座城市。1799年7月法军入城后拆除要塞，大学迁往兰茨胡特；普法尔茨-诺伊堡于1808年并入巴伐利亚行政体系。

en:
Straubing holds the Danube crossing at the centre of the Gäuboden, the broad grain plain between Regensburg and Passau. The Romans kept the military post of Sorviodurum here, and Bavarian settlers later gathered round St Peter's. In 1218 Duke Louis I of Wittelsbach laid out a new town beside the old settlement, and after the Wittelsbach partitions the local dukes kept their seat here as dukes of Bavaria-Straubing; the same line also ruled the wealthy counties of Holland, Hainaut and Zeeland far down the Rhine. Their male line died with Duke John III in 1425, and the imperial award of 1429 assigned Straubing to Bavaria-Munich. Six years later Duke Ernest, unwilling to accept his son Albert's match with a barber's daughter, had Agnes Bernauer condemned for witchcraft and drowned in the Danube; the Bernauer Chapel he later raised in St Peter's churchyard was his penance. In 1444 Catholic Straubing served Munich as a Danube market and toll town, with the tall city tower and the Gothic basilica of St Jacob above its quays, while glass huts such as Rabenstein, already firing in 1421, drew on the woods toward the Bavarian Forest.

The town enlarged its walls in the 1470s and stayed a Bavarian administrative centre, seat of a ducal revenue office from 1507. It was among the first towns in Lower Bavaria to accept the Reformation, but the dukes forced it back to Catholicism and brought in Capuchins and, in 1631, Jesuits. Two years later the Swedes of Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar took it, and plague and the passage of armies killed about 1,800 of its 4,000 people. Austrian troops occupied Straubing in 1704 and came back to besiege it twice in the 1740s, and a fire swept the northern quarters in 1780. Napoleonic secularization closed the old ducal offices, but with the grain of the Gäuboden and Danube shipping Straubing stayed the chief market between Regensburg and Passau.
zh:
施特劳宾扼守多瑙河渡口，地处雷根斯堡与帕绍之间广阔的高博登粮仓中心。罗马人曾在此设有军事据点索尔维奥杜鲁姆，巴伐利亚人后来在圣彼得教堂一带定居。1218年，维特尔斯巴赫家族的路易一世公爵在旧聚落旁营建新城；维特尔斯巴赫家族分封后，本地公爵以巴伐利亚-施特劳宾之名在此开府，同一支公爵还远在莱茵河下游领有富庶的荷兰、埃诺和泽兰伯国。1425年末代公爵约翰三世去世，男嗣断绝，1429年皇帝的仲裁把施特劳宾判给巴伐利亚-慕尼黑。六年后，恩斯特公爵容不下儿子阿尔布雷希特与理发师之女的婚事，以巫术罪将阿格妮丝·贝尔瑙尔沉入多瑙河；他后来在圣彼得教堂墓园修建贝尔瑙尔小堂，以此赎罪。1444年，信奉天主教的施特劳宾是慕尼黑治下的多瑙河市集与税关，高耸的城市塔和哥特式圣雅各布宗座圣殿俯瞰码头，拉本施泰因等玻璃作坊1421年已在通往巴伐利亚森林的林地中开炉烧造。

1470年代城市扩建城墙，此后长期是巴伐利亚的行政中心，1507年起设有公爵税务公署。它是下巴伐利亚最早接受宗教改革的城市之一，但公爵们把它拉回天主教，先后引入嘉布遣会，又在1631年引入耶稣会。两年后萨克森-魏玛的伯恩哈德率领瑞典军队攻占此城，瘟疫和军队往来使全城四千居民中约一千八百人丧生。1704年奥地利军队占领施特劳宾，1740年代又两度围城，1780年大火席卷城北街区。拿破仑时代的世俗化裁撤了旧的公爵官署，但凭高博登的粮食和多瑙河航运，施特劳宾仍是雷根斯堡与帕绍之间最大的市集。

en:
Regensburg occupies the northernmost bend of the Danube, where the Regen and Naab enter the river. The Roman fortress Castra Regina became the core of a town that the Agilolfing dukes made their Bavarian capital, and bishops and monasteries kept large church estates within and around the walls. The Stone Bridge, built from 1135 to 1146, mattered more than any charter: for centuries it was the only Danube crossing between Ulm and Vienna, carrying traffic between northern Europe and Venice. Merchants and goldsmiths grew rich, mills used the current pressed through its piers, and the city became a Free Imperial City in 1245. By 1444 the eastern routes had shifted, debt had mounted, and Catholic Regensburg maintained a narrow self-rule between Bavaria and its own bishop.

The later city is best read through its assemblies and sieges. In 1519, after Emperor Maximilian I died, the council expelled about 500 Jews, destroyed the synagogue and much of the Jewish quarter, and removed or reused gravestones from the cemetery. The city adopted the Reformation in 1542 even though the Catholic bishopric and three imperial abbeys kept their own votes in imperial affairs. Swedish troops stormed Regensburg in 1633 and blew a span of the Stone Bridge; imperial and Bavarian forces retook it the next year. From 1663 the Imperial Diet sat there without dissolving, called first to discuss the Ottoman threat and later attended by roughly seventy foreign envoys. Princes of Thurn und Taxis served as the emperor's principal commissioners. French troops stormed the town in 1809, and Napoleon was wounded in the fighting; Regensburg passed to Bavaria in 1810.
zh:
雷根斯堡位于多瑙河最北的河湾，雷根河与纳布河在此汇入。罗马要塞卡斯特拉雷吉纳构成城市核心，阿吉洛尔芬公爵曾把这里作为巴伐利亚都城；主教和修道院又在城墙内外保有大片教会领地。1135至1146年建成的石桥比任何特许状都更关键：此后几百年间，它是乌尔姆与维也纳之间唯一的多瑙河渡河处，承载北欧与威尼斯之间的人流货运。商人和金匠借此致富，水磨利用桥墩束紧的水流作业，城市则在1245年成为帝国自由城市。到1444年，东方商路已经改道，城债日增，信奉天主教的雷根斯堡在巴伐利亚与本城主教之间维持着狭小的自治。

后来的雷根斯堡，可以从帝国会议和攻城战来看。1519年皇帝马克西米利安一世去世后，市议会驱逐约五百名犹太人，拆毁犹太会堂和大片犹太区，墓地的许多墓碑也被移走或再用。1542年城市接受宗教改革，但天主教主教区和三座帝国修道院仍在帝国事务中保有自己的席位。1633年瑞典军队攻陷雷根斯堡并炸断石桥一跨，皇帝与巴伐利亚联军次年收复城市。自1663年起，帝国议会在此持续召开而不解散；它最初为讨论奥斯曼威胁而召集，后来约有七十名外国使节常驻。图恩与塔克西斯亲王作为皇帝首席专员驻在城中。1809年法军强攻城市，拿破仑在战斗中受伤；1810年雷根斯堡并入巴伐利亚。

en:
Osterode began as a Teutonic watchtower on the islands where the Drwęca runs into its lake, in the Sasin lands of the Order's Oberland. Around 1270 the Knights raised a wooden tower and named it after Osterode am Harz, the home country of many of their Welf commanders. In 1329 Komtur Luther von Braunschweig, himself later grand master, granted Kulm town rights, and between 1349 and 1370 the commandery's granite-and-brick castle rose beside the old wooden fort. Kęstutis burned castle and town in 1381. The fields of this very commandery were where Grunwald was fought in July 1410: Polish troops cut down fugitive knights under the town walls, the knight Claus von Doringe handed castle and town to Władysław Jagiełło, and the king brought the body of the slain Grand Master Jungingen there before the Order retook the place a few months later. Osterode joined the Prussian Confederation in 1440, and in 1444 it was a commandery town grown restive under Order rule.

The peace of 1466 made it a Polish fief held by the Order, a standing it kept until 1657. Sigismund the Old's army took it in the war of 1519, and after the secularisation of 1525 the last komtur, Count Quirin Schlick, stayed on as the duchy's first captain; a Latin school opened in 1592. Gustavus Adolphus lodged in the town while the Swedes held it in 1628 and 1629. From 1633 John Christian of Brzeg, one of the last Silesian Piasts, governed Osterode by grant of the Polish king and died there in 1639, his wife buried in the town church. Tatar and Swedish raids laid it waste in 1656, plague came in 1708 and 1711, and Russian troops were quartered there for four years during the Seven Years' War. The fire of 1788 destroyed the old castle and most of the houses. In the spring of 1807, soon after the refugee King Frederick William III and Queen Louise had passed through, Napoleon himself lived in the castle from 21 February to 1 April, directing the East Prussian campaign; a medal struck for his stay and a painting of the burghers' homage are kept at Versailles.
zh:
奥斯特罗德起于德雷文察河注入湖泊处一片岛屿上的条顿哨塔，地处骑士团上普鲁士辖区的萨辛人之地。1270年前后骑士团筑起木塔，以许多出身韦尔夫家族的指挥官的故乡哈茨山奥斯特罗德命名。1329年，后来官至大团长的长官路德·冯·布伦瑞克授予库尔姆城市法；1349至1370年，长官辖区的花岗岩砖石城堡在旧木堡旁建成。1381年科斯图提斯焚毁了城堡和城镇。1410年7月的格伦瓦德战役就打在这片长官辖区的土地上：波兰军队在城墙下追杀逃散的骑士，骑士克劳斯·冯·多林根把城堡和城镇献给瓦迪斯瓦夫·雅盖沃，国王还把战死的大团长容金根的遗体运到这里；数月后骑士团夺回此城。1440年奥斯特罗德加入普鲁士联盟，1444年时已是一座对骑士团心怀不满的长官驻地。

1466年的和约把它定为骑士团领有、向波兰称臣的封邑，这一地位维持到1657年。1519年的战争中，「老国王」齐格蒙特一世的军队攻占此城；1525年世俗化后，末任长官奎林·施利克伯爵留任公国首任行政官，1592年城里开设了拉丁语学校。1628至1629年瑞典占领期间，古斯塔夫·阿道夫曾在此下榻。1633年起，经波兰国王同意，西里西亚末代皮亚特公爵之一、布热格的扬·赫雷斯特安以受封方式治理奥斯特罗德，1639年死于此地，他的妻子葬在城中教堂。1656年鞑靼人和瑞典军队先后把城镇劫掠一空，瘟疫在1708和1711年两度袭来，七年战争中俄军又在此驻留四年。1788年的大火烧毁了旧城堡和大半房屋。1807年春，出逃途中的弗里德里希·威廉三世与路易丝王后刚经过这里，拿破仑本人便在2月21日至4月1日住进城堡指挥东普鲁士战役；为他此行铸造的「拿破仑在奥斯特罗德」奖章和一幅市民献降图，都藏在凡尔赛宫的藏品中。

en:
Tarnow lies at the meeting of the Biala and the Dunajec, on the old road from Krakow into Ruthenia. A Slavic gord stood on St Martin's Mount from the mid-ninth century, and the name first appears in a papal document of 1124. In 1327 the knight Spycimir of the Leliwa clan bought the village, and in 1330 Wladyslaw the Elbow-high granted it Magdeburg rights; Spycimir raised his castle on the hill, and Tarnow stayed with his descendants, the Tarnowski magnates, for more than two centuries. They ringed the town with walls in the mid-fifteenth century and in 1467 piped water into the market square, where German settlers and craftsmen swelled the guilds. In 1444 Tarnow was a busy private town in Sandomierz Voivodeship, its river trade and workshops enriching one of the great families of the Crown.

The town's golden age belonged to Jan Amor Tarnowski, born there in 1488. He became Grand Crown Hetman, led the Crown army to victory over the Moldavians at Obertyn in 1531, had fought the Moors in Portuguese Africa and been made a knight of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, and became the first Imperial count in his family. In 1528 his castle sheltered the exiled Hungarian king Janos Szapolyai. The town below held up to twelve guilds, a school, a synagogue and a Calvinist prayer house among its Catholic churches. After the hetman died in 1561 the Italian sculptor Jan Maria Padovano built his tomb in the cathedral, a Renaissance monument almost fourteen metres high in St Anne's Chapel, finished in 1573; he also remodelled the town hall, whose twenty-eight niches carried portraits of the family. In 1570 Tarnow passed by marriage to the Ostrogski family, and after 1588 through several hands until the Sanguszko family bought it in 1723. Swedish troops sacked it in October 1655 during the Deluge, and the population fell from 2,000 to 768. With the First Partition of 1772 it went to Austria, becoming a Galician county seat and, in 1783, a bishop's see.
zh:
塔尔努夫位于比亚瓦河注入杜纳耶茨河之处，地处克拉科夫通往罗斯的古道上。9世纪中叶，圣马丁山上已矗立斯拉夫人的堡寨，塔尔努夫之名最早见于1124年的教皇文书。1327年，莱利瓦氏族的骑士斯皮齐米尔买下这座村落，1330年瓦迪斯瓦夫一世（矮子）授予它马格德堡法；斯皮齐米尔在山丘上筑起城堡，塔尔努夫此后二百多年一直属于他的后裔塔尔诺夫斯基世家。他们在15世纪中叶环筑城墙，1467年把自来水管铺进集市广场，德意志移民和工匠充实了各个行会。1444年的塔尔努夫是桑多梅日省一座繁忙的贵族私城，河运与作坊养富了波兰王国的一个世家大族。

城市的全盛时代属于1488年出生于此的扬·阿莫尔·塔尔诺夫斯基。他官至王军大盖特曼，1531年率王军在奥伯廷击败摩尔达维亚人，此前曾随葡萄牙人到非洲与摩尔人作战，并在耶路撒冷受封为圣墓骑士，后来成为家族中的第一位神圣罗马帝国伯爵。1528年，他的城堡接待流亡的匈牙利国王绍波尧伊·亚诺什。山下的城市有多达十二个行会，除天主教教堂外，还办有学校、犹太会堂和加尔文宗祈祷所。盖特曼1561年去世后，意大利雕塑家扬·马里亚·帕多瓦诺在大教堂的圣安娜礼拜堂为他修筑陵墓，这座近十四米高的文艺复兴式纪念碑1573年完工；他还改建市政厅，厅上二十八个壁龛安放着家族成员的肖像。1570年，塔尔努夫随联姻转入奥斯特罗格斯基家族，1588年后几经易主，1723年由桑古什科家族购得。大洪水时代，瑞典军队于1655年10月洗劫城市，人口从两千降至768人。1772年第一次瓜分中它归属奥地利，成为加利西亚的县治，1783年又成为主教驻地。

en:
Nowy Sącz sits in the Dunajec valley at the foot of the Beskids, where the road from Kraków climbs towards the Hungarian border. It was founded on 8 November 1292 by Wenceslaus II of Bohemia on the site of the village of Kamienica, at the request of its owner Bishop Paweł of Przemanków, and it was the only Polish town the Bohemian king ever chartered; it took its name from older Stary Sącz nearby. Granted Magdeburg rights, it grew rich on the Hungarian carrying trade, and in 1329 it struck a reciprocal staple treaty with Kraków, whose merchants had to halt here on their way south. Casimir the Great ringed it with walls and built a royal castle, the seat of a castellan and starosta on the southern frontier, and many royal meetings were held there; in 1409 Władysław Jagiełło and Vytautas met in the castle to plan their war on the Teutonic Order. In the fifteenth century the town's forges produced steel, its weavers woollen cloth, and its painters nearly rivalled those of Kraków. In 1444 Nowy Sącz was a royal city of the Kraków Voivodeship, still peopled largely by descendants of German colonists.

In 1448 Bishop Zbigniew Oleśnicki raised the parish church to a collegiate, and the town won the staple right in 1554. It became a centre of the Reformation, hosting a school and congregation of the Polish Brethren from 1556 to 1616. A great fire devastated it in 1611, and in the Deluge the Swedes seized and sacked it in late 1655. On 13 December 1655 the burghers, led by the Wąsowicz brothers with a detachment of Gabriel Wojniłłowicz's troops, drove the garrison out, one of the first towns of the Commonwealth to free itself; the Swedes abandoned the siege of Jasna Góra thirteen days later, and John II Casimir sent the town his thanks in January 1656. In 1683 John III Sobieski met his queen Maria Kazimiera at nearby Stary Sącz on his way back from Vienna. The Great Northern War and the Bar Confederation brought fresh destruction and the burning of the castle. In 1770, ahead of the First Partition, Austrian troops annexed the Sącz lands, which became part of Galicia.
zh:
新松奇坐落在贝斯基德山麓的杜纳耶茨河谷，是克拉科夫通往匈牙利边境道路的要冲。1292年11月8日，波希米亚国王瓦茨拉夫二世应卡缅尼察村的主人、克拉科夫主教普热梅努夫的帕韦尔请求，在该村旧址颁令建城，这也是这位国王在波兰建立的唯一一座城市，城名则取自附近更古老的旧松奇。城市获授马格德堡法，靠转运匈牙利货物致富，1329年与克拉科夫订立对等的货栈条约，规定克拉科夫商人南下匈牙利必须在此停驻。卡齐米日大帝为它修筑城墙和王家城堡，城堡是镇守南部边境的城主与行政长官驻地，历代君主多次在此会面，1409年瓦迪斯瓦夫·雅盖沃和维托尔德便在堡中筹划对条顿骑士团的战争。15世纪，城中锻炉出产钢材，织工织造毛呢，绘画几乎可与克拉科夫比肩。1444年的新松奇是克拉科夫省的一座王家城市，居民多为早期德意志移民的后裔。

1448年，兹比格涅夫·奥莱希尼茨基主教把当地教堂升格为协同教堂；1554年城市取得货栈特权。宗教改革时期，这里是波兰兄弟会的一个中心，1556至1616年间办有该会的学校和会堂。1611年一场大火重创全城；「大洪水」中瑞典人于1655年底攻占并洗劫城市。同年12月13日，市民在翁索维奇兄弟率领下，由加布里埃尔·沃伊尼沃维奇率部配合，驱逐了瑞典守军，是共和国最早自行解放的城市之一；瑞典人十三天后解除了对光明山的围攻，1656年1月扬·卡齐米日国王致信向全城致谢。1683年，扬三世·索别斯基在维也纳之捷后回国途中，在附近的旧松奇与王后玛丽亚·卡齐米埃拉团聚。大北方战争和巴尔联盟战争又带来破坏，城堡也遭焚毁。1770年，在第一次瓜分之前，奥地利军队即已吞并松奇地区，此地后来成为加利西亚的一部分。

en:
Lwów grew up below the High Castle on the roads that carried Black Sea and Crimean goods into central Europe. Daniel of Galicia is counted its founder, naming the stronghold for his son Leo; it is first documented in 1256 and became the capital of Galicia-Volhynia around 1272. Casimir III of Poland took the city in 1349 and granted Magdeburg rights in 1356, walling a new market town governed by German burghers while Ruthenian, Armenian and Jewish communities kept their own quarters; the Armenians had their own archbishop there by about 1280. From 1434 Lwów was the capital of the Ruthenian Voivodeship. In 1444 it was a royal city of the Polish Crown, whose merchants forwarded furs, wax and eastern goods to Kraków and the German towns.

Fires in 1527 and 1556 destroyed most of Gothic Lwów, and the rebuilt centre took on its Renaissance face around the Market Square, with the Black House, the Korniakt Palace and the Boim family chapel rising there in the next two generations. The Orthodox Dormition Church served the Ruthenian townspeople, its brotherhood ran a school, and Ivan Fedorovych, a printer who had fled Moscow, worked in the city. In 1648 Bohdan Khmelnytsky's Cossacks stormed the High Castle and withdrew only for a ransom, and the town's repeated defence won it the motto Semper fidelis, always faithful. John II Casimir made his Lwów Oath in the Latin cathedral in 1656, an Ottoman siege failed in 1672, and John III Sobieski defeated another Ottoman and Crimean army outside the walls in 1675. Lwów fell to a foreign army for the first time since the Middle Ages in 1704, when Charles XII of Sweden took and looted it. The First Partition of 1772 gave the city to the Habsburgs as Lemberg, capital of the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria; its old walls were dismantled from 1777, and a university opened in 1784.
zh:
利沃夫在高堡脚下兴起，地当黑海、克里米亚通往中欧的商路。传统上认为它由加利西亚王公丹尼尔兴建，并以其子列夫命名；现存最早的文字记载在1256年，约1272年成为加利西亚-沃里尼亚的都城。波兰国王卡齐米日三世1349年攻取此城，1356年授予马格德堡法，筑起一座由德意志市民治理的有墙市场新城，鲁塞尼亚人、亚美尼亚人和犹太人则各居自己的街区；约1280年，亚美尼亚人已在此设有自己的大主教。1434年起，利沃夫成为鲁塞尼亚省首府。1444年时，它是波兰王国的王室城市，商人把毛皮、蜂蜡和东方货物转销克拉科夫与德意志诸城。

1527年和1556年的大火烧毁了哥特式利沃夫的大部分城区，重建后的市中心在集市广场周围显出文艺复兴面貌，黑屋、科尔尼亚克特宫和博伊姆家族礼拜堂都在这一时期建起。东正教圣母安息教堂服务于鲁塞尼亚市民，附设的兄弟会开办学校，从莫斯科逃出的印刷匠伊万·费多罗维奇也曾在此工作。1648年，博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基的哥萨克攻下高堡，拿到赎金才撤兵；城市在连番围攻中坚守，得到「始终忠诚」的铭言。1656年，扬二世·卡齐米日在拉丁主教座堂发表利沃夫誓愿；1672年奥斯曼军队攻城不克；1675年，扬三世·索别斯基又在城外击败一支奥斯曼与克里米亚联军。1704年，卡尔十二世的瑞典军队攻破并劫掠利沃夫，这是中世纪以来它第一次落入外国军队手中。1772年第一次瓜分后，城市以「伦贝格」之名归属哈布斯堡，成为加利西亚和洛多梅里亚王国的首府；旧城墙自1777年起拆除，大学则于1784年开办。

en:
Rowne lies on the Ustia River, on the old road that carried traffic between Kyiv, Volodymyr and western Volhynia. The Kraków Chapter Annals first mention it in 1283, as a settlement of Galicia–Volhynia near which Leszek the Black of Poland defeated a Lithuanian army; Ukrainian tradition names Prince Volodymyr Vasylkovych as its founder. In 1434 Svidrigailo, prince of Volhynia, granted the place to the Lutsk boyar family of Dychko. In 1444 it is still a small Orthodox Ruthenian settlement, worth holding only because its road and river crossing tied the older Volhynian towns together.

Later in the century the Dychko family sold Rowne to Prince Semen Nesvizh. His widow Maria called herself princess of Rowne and made the place her residence: in 1481 she built an oak castle on a river island, and in 1492 she obtained Magdeburg rights for the town from King Casimir IV; a later royal privilege added an annual fair. In the sixteenth century Rowne passed to the Ostrogski, and after the Union of Lublin in 1569 it was a private town under the Polish Crown. Tatars burned the castle and churches early in the seventeenth century, Khmelnytsky's uprising devastated the place in 1648, and plague and fire long delayed recovery. Charles XII's Swedes sacked it in 1706. The Lubomirski, who acquired it in the 1720s, demolished what remained of the stronghold and built a palatial residence on the site. The Second Partition assigned Rowne to Russia in 1793, and four years later it became a county town of the Volhynian Governorate.
zh:
罗夫诺位于乌斯季亚河畔，在基辅通往沃洛德米尔和沃里尼亚西部的旧道上。克拉科夫主教区编年史1283年首次提到它，当时是加利西亚-沃里尼亚的一处定居点，波兰王公莱谢克二世就在附近击败一支立陶宛军队；乌克兰文史料则称其由沃里尼亚王公弗拉基米尔·瓦西里科维奇建立。1434年，沃里尼亚王公斯维特里盖拉把罗夫诺赐给卢茨克波雅尔迪奇科家族。1444年时，它仍是一座小型东正教鲁塞尼亚定居点，价值只在连接沃里尼亚诸城的道路和河流渡口。
