该世纪后期，迪奇科家族把罗夫诺卖给谢苗·涅斯维茨基王公。谢苗的遗孀玛丽亚自称罗夫诺女王公，把这里经营成自己的驻地：1481年她在河中小岛上修建橡木城堡，1492年又从波兰国王卡齐米日四世手中为城镇取得马格德堡权利，后来的王室敕许又添了一年一次的集市。16世纪，罗夫诺转入奥斯特罗兹基家族，1569年卢布林联合后成为波兰王冠领治下的贵族私城。17世纪初鞑靼人烧毁城堡和教堂，1648年赫梅利尼茨基起义又使此地遭到重创，瘟疫和火灾令恢复迟迟无望。1706年，卡尔十二世的瑞典军洗劫此城。1720年代取得罗夫诺的卢博米尔斯基家族拆除残存要塞，原地建起宫殿宅邸。1793年第二次瓜分波兰时罗夫诺划归俄国，四年后成为沃里尼亚省的县城。

en:
Notec covers the Noteć meadows and marshes around Nakło, the crossing where the upper river gives way to its lower course toward the Warta and Oder. The Pomeranian stronghold of Nakieł guarded this wet frontier against the Piast state; Palatine Sieciech took it by siege in 1090, and Bolesław III Wrymouth secured it for good in 1113. Ladislaus the Short granted Magdeburg town rights in 1299, and Casimir the Great built a brick Gothic castle there after 1357. In 1393 Władysław Jagiełło enfeoffed Warcisław VII of Szczecin with the stronghold while organising a land blockade of the Teutonic Order. In 1444 Nakło was a small Polish frontier town, and the Noteć pastures fattened the cattle that were the province's trade.

For centuries the lower marshes also marked the edge of Greater Poland toward Brandenburg's Neumark. The First Partition of 1772 carried Nakło to Prussia with the newly organised Netze District, and Prussian engineers set about remaking the wetland. They began the Bydgoszcz Canal from the Noteć near the town in 1773 and opened it on 14 June 1774; by way of the Brda it joined the Vistula to the Noteć, Warta and Oder, so grain and timber could travel to Szczecin without the Baltic sea route. Napoleon's victories brought Nakło to the Duchy of Warsaw in 1807, but the Congress of Vienna returned it to Prussia in 1815 within the Grand Duchy of Posen.
zh:
诺泰奇省涵盖纳克沃周围诺泰奇河的草甸与沼泽，诺泰奇河在此从上游转入下游，流向瓦尔塔河和奥得河。波莫瑞人的纳基乌要塞镇守这片湿润边疆，抵御皮雅斯特波兰；宫相谢切赫1090年经围攻夺取要塞，博莱斯瓦夫三世1113年才把它稳固纳入波兰。1299年，瓦迪斯瓦夫一世授予马格德堡城市权；1357年后，卡齐米日大帝在此修建砖砌哥特式城堡。1393年，瓦迪斯瓦夫·雅盖沃把要塞封给什切青公爵瓦尔季斯瓦夫七世，以配合对条顿骑士团的陆上封锁。1444年时，纳克沃是一座波兰边陲小镇，诺泰奇河畔牧场养肥的牛群就是本省的外销货物。

几个世纪里，下游沼泽也是大波兰与勃兰登堡新马克之间的边界。1772年第一次瓜分波兰后，纳克沃随新设的诺泰奇区归入普鲁士，普鲁士工程师着手改造这片湿地。他们1773年从镇旁的诺泰奇河开凿比得哥什运河，1774年6月14日通航；运河经布尔达河把维斯瓦河与诺泰奇河、瓦尔塔河、奥得河连成一条水路，粮食和木材可以运往什切青，不必绕行波罗的海。拿破仑的胜利在1807年使纳克沃归入华沙公国，但1815年维也纳会议又把它交还普鲁士，隶属于波森大公国。

en:
The Altmark is the flat country west of the middle Elbe, with Stendal its chief town and Tangermünde holding the Elbe crossing. The name, the 'Old March', states what it was: the oldest ground of the Margraviate of Brandenburg. When the Slav rising of 983 overran the Northern March, Saxon lords kept only this western strip; in 1134 Emperor Lothair enfeoffed Albert the Bear with it, and from it Albert built the margraviate founded in 1157. The towns made their money on the crossing, cloth and Hanse trade. Stendal, founded by Albert about 1160, kept its own ships sailing to the Baltic and the North Sea, and its 'Stendal silver' coinage passed widely for its quality; the brick merchants' hall first recorded in 1188 was counted among the largest north of the Alps. In 1444 it was a Catholic, Saxon-speaking core province of the Hohenzollern electorate: Stendal Cathedral was rising above the roofs, the Uenglingen Gate had just gone up, and Tangermünde still housed a court of the electors.

Emperor Charles IV kept a second residence at Tangermünde from 1373, rebuilding the castle above the Elbe and meaning to make the town the centre of his middle-German lands; the first Hohenzollern electors lived there too, until a rising against the beer tax in 1488 moved John Cicero to take the court permanently to Cölln on the Spree. Stendal had joined the Hanse in 1358, and in the same year as the tax revolt it took in the first printer of the Mark, Joachim Westfal. Lutheran teaching became the official religion in 1539. The town's most famous son was born there in 1717: Johann Joachim Winckelmann, who went from Stendal's Latin school to write the first ordered history of ancient art and so gave the subject its modern shape. After Jena, French troops occupied the country; the Treaty of Tilsit assigned the Altmark to the Kingdom of Westphalia in 1807, and when it returned to Prussia in 1815 it went to the new Province of Saxony, not to Brandenburg.
zh:
阿尔特马克是易北河中游以西的平坦乡野，首城施滕达尔之外，唐格明德扼守着易北河渡口。「旧边区」这个名字说明了它的身份：勃兰登堡边疆伯国最古老的根基。983年斯拉夫人起义席卷北方边区后，萨克森领主只保住了西侧这一条；1134年皇帝洛泰尔把它封给阿尔布雷希特·大熊，阿尔布雷希特正是从这片土地建起1157年立国的勃兰登堡边疆伯国。各城靠渡口、呢绒和汉萨贸易谋生。施滕达尔约1160年由阿尔布雷希特建城，自有商船航行于波罗的海与北海，所铸「施滕达尔银币」因成色好而通行甚广；1188年初见记载的砖石商人会堂，被认为是阿尔卑斯山以北最大的同类建筑之一。1444年，这片操萨克森语、信奉天主教的土地是霍亨索伦选侯国的古老核心：施滕达尔大教堂正拔地而起，于恩林根门刚刚竣工，唐格明德还住着选侯的宫廷。

1373年起，皇帝查理四世在唐格明德经营第二驻地，扩建易北河畔的城堡，打算把此城建成他德意志中部领地的中心；最早几代霍亨索伦选侯也住在这里，直到1488年市民反抗啤酒税，选侯约翰·西塞罗把宫廷最终迁到施普雷河畔的克尔恩。施滕达尔1358年加入汉萨，又在抗税暴动的同一年迎来边区第一位印刷匠约阿希姆·韦斯特法尔。1539年，路德宗成为官方信仰。城中最著名的儿子1717年出生于此：约翰·约阿希姆·温克尔曼，他从施滕达尔拉丁学校走出去，写出第一部系统的古代艺术史，为这门学问奠定了近代形态。耶拿战败后法军占领此地，1807年《提尔西特和约》把阿尔特马克划给威斯特伐利亚王国；1815年它回归普鲁士时没有归入勃兰登堡，而被划入新设立的萨克森省。

en:
Vogtland is the wooded hill country where Thuringia, Saxony, Franconia and Bohemia meet. Its name comes from the Vogte, imperial advocates installed under Frederick Barbarossa to govern the eastern imperial forests from castles like the Osterburg at Weida. The chief town is Plauen, first documented in 1122 on the White Elster; the Teutonic Order opened a commandry there in 1214. Henry of Plauen accepted Bohemian suzerainty in 1327, and in 1356 Charles IV made the lordship a hereditary fief of the Bohemian crown. Hussites under Prokop stormed the castle in 1430, killed hundreds and burned the town. In 1444 Plauen was a Catholic market town on a fought-over frontier, its rebuilt castle held by Burgrave Henry I with Bohemia and the Wettin lands pressing in.

Henry II, remembered as the Tyrant, quarrelled with George of Podebrady, who put him under the imperial ban in 1466; Duke Albrecht's Saxon troops, sent to enforce it, took Plauen, and the Leipzig partition of 1485 assigned Vogtland to the Ernestine Wettins. The Reformation followed quickly: Georg Eulner and Georg Raute preached Luther's teaching in the Johanniskirche from 1521 and introduced it in Plauen in 1524. Ferdinand I re-enfeoffed Henry IV in 1547, but his sons pledged the lordship to Elector August of Saxony in 1559, who secured Plauen and its offices in 1566. Cotton gave the town its living: an ordinance of 1600 recognised the veil-weavers' guild, and their fine cotton head-veils sold across the Empire; Johann Friedrich Schildt opened a larger cotton works in 1702 and a calico works followed in 1753, the start of the Plauen textile trade. Georg Samuel Doerffel, a clergyman and astronomer born in Plauen in 1643, was the first to show that the great comet of 1680 travelled in one parabolic orbit. War kept passing through: Holk's and Wallenstein's troops plundered the town in 1632, plague killed about half its people in 1634 and another great fire came in 1635; after a spell with Saxe-Zeitz the castle was rebuilt in 1670-1675, and Plauen returned to Electoral Saxony in 1718. Rival armies occupied it by turns in the Seven Years' War and again during the Napoleonic wars after 1806.
zh:
福格特兰是图林根、萨克森、法兰克与波希米亚交界处的林野丘陵，地名来自「福格特」，即腓特烈一世·巴巴罗萨时期受任管理东部皇家森林的帝国长官，他们以魏达的奥斯特堡等城堡为据点统治此地。首府普劳恩坐落在白埃尔斯特河畔，最早见于1122年文献，条顿骑士团1214年在此设立据点。1327年，普劳恩的海因里希接受波希米亚宗主权，1356年查理四世把这块领地封为波希米亚王冠的世袭封地。1430年，普罗科普率领的胡斯军攻下城堡，杀死数百人并焚毁全城，重建十分缓慢。因此1444年时，普劳恩是一座地处争夺前沿的天主教商业城镇，修复后的城堡由城堡伯爵海因里希一世据守，波希米亚和韦廷领地从两侧逼近。

城堡伯爵海因里希二世在史书中被称为「暴君」，他与波杰布拉德的伊日反目，后者1466年对他下达帝国夺爵令；阿尔布雷希特公爵的萨克森军队奉命执行，攻占普劳恩，1485年莱比锡分封又把福格特兰划给韦廷家族恩斯特系。新教随即传入：格奥尔格·奥伊勒纳和格奥尔格·劳特自1521年起在圣约翰教堂宣讲路德的教义，1524年将宗教改革引入普劳恩。城堡伯爵家族一度复辟，斐迪南一世1547年重新册封海因里希四世，但他的儿子们1559年把领地抵押给萨克森选侯奥古斯特，后者1566年取得普劳恩及邻近官署。棉花是这座城的生计：1600年市议会的规例承认头巾织工行会，他们织的精细棉纱头巾销往整个帝国；约翰·弗里德里希·席尔特1702年开办规模更大的棉织工场，1753年又出现印花棉布厂，这便是普劳恩纺织业的开端。1643年生于普劳恩的牧师兼天文学家格奥尔格·萨穆埃尔·德费尔最先证明，1680年的大彗星沿同一条抛物线轨道运行。战争仍反复经过此地：1632年霍尔克和华伦斯坦的军队劫掠城镇，1634年瘟疫夺去约半数居民生命，1635年又遭大火；普劳恩一度划归萨克森-蔡茨，城堡于1670至1675年重建，1718年复归萨克森选侯国。七年战争期间交战各方轮番占领，萨克森1806年成为王国后，拿破仑战争中法国、反法同盟和俄国军队又接踵过境。

en:
Głogów (German Glogau) guards a crossing of the Oder where the Barycz joins it, on the roads from Greater Poland and Saxony into Silesia. A Piast stronghold from the late 10th century, it won its place in Polish memory on 24 August 1109, when King Henry V of Germany came against it with an imperial army and a Bohemian contingent while Bolesław III Wrymouth's forces were marching from Pomerania. The chronicler Gallus records that the besiegers tied Polish hostages to their siege engines as shields; the townspeople held out and the emperor gave up the siege. Frederick Barbarossa took and burned the town in 1157. In 1251 Konrad I made it the seat of his Duchy of Głogów and granted Magdeburg rights two years later, and brewing, clothmaking and river trade filled the new walls. From 1331 the Silesian dukes held the town of the Bohemian Crown. In 1444 a Silesian Piast still reigned there, behind some of the strongest fortifications in Lower Silesia.

In 1462 the town hosted the meeting of Casimir IV Jagiellon and George of Poděbrady, sealed with a Polish-Bohemian alliance. The last Piast, Jan II the Mad, was driven out by Matthias Corvinus in 1488, and from 1491 to 1506 Głogów was held by the future Polish kings John Albert and Sigismund the Old; with the line extinct the duchy passed to the Bohemian Crown in 1506 and to the Habsburgs in 1526. Two scholars were born in the town: Jan of Głogów, born about 1445, an astronomer and philosopher at the University of Kraków, and Andreas Gryphius, born in 1616, the leading German poet and playwright of the Baroque. A printing press was at work by about 1606. In the Thirty Years' War the fortress changed hands with every campaign: Protestant troops in 1632, Imperials in 1633, Swedes in 1642, Habsburgs again in 1648. In March 1741 a Prussian night attack under Leopold of Anhalt-Dessau delivered Glogau to Frederick the Great. French troops took it after Jena in 1806, Napoleon visited three times, and a garrison of some 9,000 endured a year-long allied siege before capitulating on 10 April 1814, when only 1,800 remained. The Congress of Vienna confirmed the town to Prussia.
zh:
格沃古夫（德语名格洛高）扼守奥得河上的渡口，巴里奇河在此汇入，大波兰和萨克森方向进入西里西亚的道路都经此过河。10世纪末这里已是皮雅斯特家族的堡寨。1109年8月24日是它载入波兰记忆的一天：德意志国王亨利五世率帝国军和波希米亚军前来围城，博莱斯瓦夫三世（歪嘴）的军队当时正从波莫瑞赶回。据编年史家加卢斯记载，攻城者把波兰人质绑在攻城器械上当挡箭牌，市民仍坚守不降，亨利五世最终撤围。1157年，腓特烈·巴巴罗萨攻下并焚毁了这座城。1251年，康拉德一世以它为格沃古夫公国都城，两年后授予马格德堡法，酿酒、织布和河运贸易让新筑的城墙内富庶起来。1331年起，西里西亚诸公爵以波希米亚王冠为宗主。1444年，坐在这里的仍是一位西里西亚皮雅斯特公爵，城防是下西里西亚最坚固的之一。

1462年，波兰国王卡齐米日四世·雅盖隆契克与波希米亚国王波杰布拉德的伊日在此会盟，结成波希米亚—波兰同盟。末代皮雅斯特公爵扬二世（狂人）1488年被马加什·科尔温驱逐；1491至1506年，格沃古夫由后来的波兰国王扬·奥尔布拉赫特和齐格蒙特一世（老者）相继持有，血脉绝嗣后公国于1506年并入波希米亚王冠领地，1526年归于哈布斯堡家族。城里还走出两位学者：约1445年出生的格沃古夫的扬，后来在克拉科夫大学讲授天文学和哲学；1616年出生的安德烈亚斯·格吕菲乌斯，是德语巴洛克时代最重要的诗人和剧作家。约1606年城中已办起印刷所。三十年战争期间，这座要塞随战局几度易手：1632年归新教军队，1633年被帝国军夺回，1642年落入瑞典之手，1648年再归哈布斯堡。1741年3月，安哈尔特-德绍的利奥波德率普军夜袭，把格洛高交到腓特烈大帝手中。1806年耶拿战役后法军占城，拿破仑曾三次到访；约九千人的法波守军在联军长达一年的围攻中苦守，1814年4月10日投降时只剩一千八百人。维也纳会议确认格洛高归普鲁士。

en:
Eger, called Cheb in Czech, lies on the Ohře on the road from Nuremberg to Prague. The Hohenstaufen turned the Slavic border stronghold into the centre of the Egerland: Frederick Barbarossa took the land in 1146 and built an imperial palace around 1180, whose chapel and Black Tower survive above the town. Eger became a town in 1179 and struck regional coinage from 1235. Wenceslaus II married Judith of Habsburg there in 1285. Its place under the Bohemian crown came through a pledge. After Mühldorf in 1322, the Emperor Louis IV pledged Eger to King John of Bohemia, and the pledge was never redeemed. Wenceslaus IV concluded the Eger Landfried there with south-west German free cities in 1389. In 1444 about 7,300 people lived in this largely German-speaking Catholic town; its merchants and brewers kept a strong measure of self-government.

The hills east of the town produced the best-known money in these parts. In 1516 Count Stephen Schlick founded Sankt Joachimsthal, later Jáchymov, on a rich silver vein; the Joachimsthaler, minted from 1519, supplied the name for the thaler and later the dollar. Ferdinand I brought minting under the crown in 1528, and by 1535 Jáchymov was the second-largest town in the Bohemian kingdom. The crown stripped the Schlicks of their rights there in 1547. Eger itself turned Lutheran and was forcibly re-Catholicised after the White Mountain. On 25 February 1634 Albrecht von Wallenstein was killed in the Pachelbel house on the square while several of his officers were killed in the castle. Swedish troops struck the town in 1631 and 1647. The Habsburgs made Eger a free royal town in 1723, ending its long autonomy.
zh:
埃格尔（捷克语称海布）位于奥赫热河畔，正处在纽伦堡通往布拉格的大道上。霍恩施陶芬王朝把这座斯拉夫人边寨建成埃格尔兰的中心：巴巴罗萨1146年取得此地，约1180年修建帝国行宫，行宫礼拜堂和黑塔现存于城内高地上。1179年埃格尔升为城市，1235年起开始为整个地区铸造钱币。1285年，瓦茨拉夫二世在此迎娶鲁道夫一世之女茱蒂丝。它归入波希米亚王冠是因为一笔抵押：1322年米尔多夫战役后，皇帝路易四世把埃格尔抵押给国王约翰，抵押始终没有赎回。1389年，瓦茨拉夫四世又在此与西南德意志自由城市缔结埃格尔地方和约。1444年，这座约有7300人的城市以德语居民和天主教徒为主，商人和酿酒商在波希米亚王冠治下保留着很强的自治权。

城东山里产出了这一带最有名的钱币。1516年，斯特凡·什利克伯爵在一条富银矿脉上建立圣约阿希姆斯塔尔，也就是后来的亚希莫夫；1519年起铸造的约阿希姆斯塔尔银币，把名称传给了塔勒和后来的元。斐迪南一世1528年把铸币权收归王室；到1535年，亚希莫夫已是波希米亚王国第二大城，1547年王室又褫夺什利克家族在此的权利。埃格尔本城改宗路德宗，白山战役后被强制重新天主教化。1634年2月25日，阿尔布雷希特·冯·华伦斯坦在广场边的帕赫尔贝尔宅被杀，他的几名部将同时在城堡丧命。瑞典军队1631年和1647年两度进攻。1723年，哈布斯堡将埃格尔改为自由王家城市，结束了它长期自治的地位。

en:
České Budějovice, Budweis to its German-speaking burghers, lies where the Malše enters the Vltava. A village stood there in 1251, and in 1265 King Ottokar II founded a fortified royal city on the site, entrusting the plan to his knight Hirzo as a crown check on the powerful Vítkovec lords of the Rožmberk house. Three gates, a broad market square and craftsmen's streets gave the crown a firm base in southern Bohemia, while silver found nearby added to the town's revenues. Budějovice stayed Catholic during the Hussite Wars. Jan Žižka's Taborites passed nearby in 1420 on their campaign against the Rožmberks, but no assault followed. In 1444 it was a Catholic royal town set in a largely Hussite countryside, with many German-speaking burghers among its Czech inhabitants.

Confessional politics kept the town on the crown's side. In 1467 Catholic burghers murdered Burgomaster Ondřej Puklice ze Vztuh for supporting George of Poděbrady. Silver, beer, salt and fish-pond revenues later paid for the Black Tower, raised beside the square from 1547 to 1577. During the Bohemian revolt, Mansfeld's Protestant army besieged Budějovice until Bucquoy defeated him at Záblatí on 10 June 1619 and the siege was lifted; the townsmen then paid Bucquoy to destroy rebel-held Rudolfov, by then one of Bohemia's leading silver-mining districts. In the 1630s Budějovice served for twenty-two months as a temporary seat of government, and the St Wenceslas Crown and other crown jewels were kept in St Nicholas Church under Wallenstein's guard. A fire in July 1641 destroyed more than half the town. Later rebuilding added the Samson Fountain in 1727 and Martinelli's town hall, and in 1785 St Nicholas became the cathedral of the new diocese.
zh:
布杰约维采位于马尔谢河汇入伏尔塔瓦河之处，操德语的市民称它为布德韦斯。1251年当地已有一座村庄；1265年，国王奥托卡二世在此营建设防王城，命骑士希尔佐主持规划，作为王权制衡罗日姆贝克家族等维特科夫采大领主的据点。三座城门、宽阔的集市广场和工匠街巷使王权在南波希米亚有了稳固根基，附近发现的银矿也增加了城市收入。胡斯战争期间，布杰约维采坚持天主教。1420年，扬·杰什卡的塔博尔军征讨罗日姆贝克家族时从附近经过，却没有攻城。1444年，它是胡斯派乡野中的一座天主教王城，捷克居民中还有许多操德语的市民。

宗派政治使这座城市长期站在王权一边。1467年，天主派市民杀害支持波杰布拉德的伊日的市长翁德热伊·普克利采。后来，银矿、啤酒、盐和鱼塘的收入支撑广场旁的黑塔在1547至1577年间建成。捷克等级起义期间，曼斯菲尔德的新教军围攻布杰约维采，直到比夸于1619年6月10日在扎布拉蒂将其击败，围城才告解除；市民又出资请比夸摧毁叛军控制的鲁道夫夫，那里当时已是波希米亚主要银矿产区之一。1630年代，布杰约维采有二十二个月充当临时政府驻地，圣瓦茨拉夫王冠和其他加冕珍宝藏在圣尼古拉教堂，由华伦斯坦的士兵看守。1641年7月的大火烧毁大半个城市。后来的重建增建了1727年的参孙喷泉和马丁内利设计的市政厅；1785年，圣尼古拉教堂成为新教区的主教座堂。

en:
The Sternberg was the Brandenburg countryside behind the Oder crossing at Frankfurt; its Land is first on record early in the fourteenth century. The crossing itself grew from a merchant settlement on a sandy island where several long-distance roads met, which held market and staple rights from Henry I of Silesia in 1225. Margrave John I issued Frankfurt's charter in July 1253 under Berlin town law, and two days later granted the town an exclusive staple right over the surrounding country. Boats carried its cloth and other goods between Breslau and Stettin, and Frankfurt sat with the Hanseatic towns by 1430. When Sigismund pawned the Neumark to the Teutonic Knights in 1402, the Sternberg lands were expressly excluded and stayed with Brandenburg. Hussite raiders burned the Guben suburb and the Carthusian monastery on 6 April 1432 but failed to storm the walls a week later. In 1444 this was a Catholic cloth and market district under the Hohenzollern elector.

In 1506 Elector Joachim I opened the Brandenburg University in Frankfurt, the first university of the electorate: about 950 scholars came in its opening year, among them the young Ulrich von Hutten, more than at any German university before it. Its theologians faced Luther at a disputation in January 1518, when theses written by Konrad Wimpina for the indulgence preacher Johann Tetzel were approved against him, and many students drifted off to Wittenberg; the town also left the Hanse that same year at the elector's wish. In 1535 the Sternberg passed to the junior Brandenburg-Küstrin line, returning to the electorate in 1571. Gustavus Adolphus's Swedes stormed and plundered Frankfurt in 1631 during the Thirty Years' War, and the population fell from about 12,000 to 2,366. The writer Heinrich von Kleist, author of Michael Kohlhaas and The Prince of Homburg, was born here in 1777. In 1759 the Russians occupied the river suburb and levied heavy contributions, and on 12 August Frederick II suffered his worst defeat at Kunersdorf, just beyond the Oder, against the Russian and Austrian armies. The university was moved to Breslau in 1811, five years before Frankfurt became the seat of a Prussian administrative region.
zh:
施滕贝格是奥得河畔法兰克福渡口后方的勃兰登堡乡野，其领地之名最早见于14世纪初的文献。渡口本身起于河沙岛上的商人聚落，数条远途商路在此交会；1225年，西里西亚公爵亨里克一世授予它市场权和堆货权。1253年7月，藩侯约翰一世依照柏林城市法为法兰克福颁发建城特许，两天后又授予它周边地区的独占堆货权。往来布雷斯劳与斯德丁的船只载着这里的布料和其他商货，到1430年法兰克福已列名汉萨城邦。西吉斯蒙德1402年把诺伊马克抵押给条顿骑士团时，施滕贝格领地被明确排除在外，继续留在勃兰登堡手中。1432年4月6日，胡斯派袭掠者烧毁古本郊区和加尔都西会修道院，一周后攻城又告失败。1444年，这里是霍亨索伦选帝侯治下一个信奉天主教的布料与市集地区。

1506年，选帝侯约阿希姆一世在法兰克福创办勃兰登堡大学，这是选侯国的第一所大学；开学第一年约有950名学者到来，年轻时的乌尔里希·冯·胡滕也在其中，人数超过此前任何一所德意志大学。1518年1月，大学举行辩论会，本校神学家为赎罪券修士约翰·台彻尔代写的反题获得通过，路德被判定为已遭驳倒，许多学生随后转往维滕贝格；同年，法兰克福应选帝侯之请正式退出汉萨同盟。1535年，施滕贝格划归幼支的勃兰登堡-屈斯特林，1571年重新并回选侯国。三十年战争中，古斯塔夫·阿道夫的瑞典军队1631年攻破并劫掠法兰克福，居民从约一万二千人减至2366人。1777年，作家海因里希·冯·克莱斯特出生于此，《米夏埃尔·科尔哈斯》和《洪堡亲王》都出自他手。1759年，俄军先占领堤坝郊区、勒索巨额摊派；8月12日，腓特烈二世又在奥得河对岸的库讷斯多夫被俄奥联军击败，这是他平生损失最重的一役。1811年大学迁往布雷斯劳，五年后法兰克福成为普鲁士一个行政专区的治所。

en:
Hradec Králové, the capital of Hradecko and Königgrätz to German speakers, takes its name from a castle above the Elbe and Orlice that became a dower seat of the Bohemian queens. Around 1300 Wenceslas II assigned the town to the queens, and Elizabeth Richeza of Poland and Elizabeth of Pomerania both kept court there. By the next century it ranked after Prague among Bohemian towns and had the Cathedral of the Holy Spirit on its main square. Its later fame came from war. The Hussites took it in 1420, and Jan Žižka made it the base of his East Bohemian brotherhood. On 20 April 1423 he defeated Čeněk of Wartenberg's Catholic nobles at Hořice from a wagon fort on high ground, occupied Hradec in July, and dismantled the old queens' castle. After Žižka died at Přibyslav in 1424, the priest Ambrož brought his body back for burial in the Holy Spirit; the remains were later moved to Čáslav, and Žižka's followers called themselves the Orphans. In 1444 Hradec was the strongest Hussite town in eastern Bohemia.

George of Poděbrady confirmed the town's privileges, but its part in the 1547 rising against Ferdinand I cost Hradec its estates and self-government. Martin Cejp, a later burgomaster, paved the streets and raised the White Tower during a partial recovery. The Swedes took Hradec in 1639 and returned several times during the Thirty Years War, leaving the suburbs wasted and the town much reduced. Fighting returned in the War of the Austrian Succession, and in 1766 Joseph II ordered a modern fortress on the rivers. Finished in 1789, it covered 320 hectares, levelled a nearby hill and changed the courses of both the Elbe and the Orlice, yet no enemy attacked it before 1821.
zh:
赫拉德茨克的首府赫拉德茨－克拉洛韦（德语名柯尼希格雷茨）得名于拉贝河与奥尔利采河汇流处的城堡，这座城堡后来成为波希米亚王后的寡居封地。1300年前后瓦茨拉夫二世把城镇封给王后，波兰的伊丽莎白·瑞什卡和波美拉尼亚的伊丽莎白都曾在此设朝。到下一世纪，它已是仅次于布拉格的波希米亚城市，大广场上立着圣灵教堂。它更大的名声来自战争。1420年胡斯派占领城市，扬·杰什卡把这里作为东波希米亚兄弟会的基地。1423年4月20日，他在霍日采依托高地车垒击败瓦滕贝格的切涅克率领的天主教贵族，7月进占赫拉德茨，拆毁历代王后的旧城堡。1424年杰什卡病死于普日比斯拉夫城下后，神甫安布罗日把遗体运回圣灵教堂安葬，遗骨后来迁往恰斯拉夫；杰什卡的追随者此后自称孤儿派。1444年，赫拉德茨是东波希米亚最强大的胡斯派城市。

波杰布拉德的伊日确认过城市特权，但1547年赫拉德茨参与反抗斐迪南一世，失败后被没收地产、剥夺自治。后来的市长马丁·采伊普在城市部分恢复时铺筑街道、建起白塔。三十年战争中，瑞典军1639年攻占赫拉德茨，随后又数次返回，郊区荒废，城市人口大减。奥地利王位继承战争时战祸再至，1766年约瑟夫二世下令在两河间修建现代化要塞。要塞1789年完工，占地320公顷，施工时推平附近山丘、改移拉贝河与奥尔利采河河道，但到1821年还没有敌军进攻过它。

en:
The middle Weser around Hoya runs through a flat country of marsh and sandy geest above the floodplain. At the end of the twelfth century the counts of Hoya raised a castle on an island in the river, the family first appearing in 1202 as vassals of the archbishop of Bremen; the castle and its ferry let them take toll of the Weser traffic. Buying Nienburg in 1215 opened long quarrels with the bishops of Minden, and in 1345 the county split into a lower line seated at Hoya and an upper line at Nienburg. From 1351 to 1359 the counts fought the Hoya Feud against Bremen and beat its troops on the Aller in 1358. In 1444 they still held their own small territory astride the Weser, and Nienburg was their largest town.

The lower line died out in 1497 and the Nienburg counts reunited the county, but debt and Welf pressure told: Brunswick-Lüneburg occupied Hoya in 1512, and after that the counts held it only as a Welf fief. Count Jobst II professed the Lutheran teaching as early as 1523 and sent a reformer to Nienburg two years later. When Otto VIII died at Hoya castle on 25 February 1582 the county passed to the Welf dukes, the greater part in time to the Celle line. In 1625 and 1626 Christian IV of Denmark and Tilly's imperial army fought over the Weser crossing, their cannonballs wrecking the counts' old residence, and on 12 December 1626 the town surrendered to the Danes. Hoya later belonged to the Electorate of Hanover and from 1815 to the Kingdom of Hanover.
zh:
霍亚一带的威悉河中游，是洪泛平原上沼泽与沙岗交错的低地。12世纪末，霍亚伯爵在河心岛上筑起城堡，这一家族1202年作为不莱梅大主教的封臣首见记载；凭城堡和渡头，他们得以向威悉河上的往来船只抽税。1215年购得尼恩堡后，他们与明登主教结下长年纷争；1345年伯爵领一分为二，幼支驻霍亚，长支驻尼恩堡。1351至1359年，伯爵们与不莱梅进行「霍亚仇争」，1358年在阿勒尔河击败不莱梅军队。1444年，他们仍保有这片横跨威悉河的小领地，尼恩堡是最大的城镇。

1497年幼支绝嗣，尼恩堡支系统一了伯爵领，但债务和韦尔夫家族的压力日甚：不伦瑞克-吕讷堡1512年占领霍亚，此后伯爵只能以韦尔夫封臣的身份守着领地。约布斯特二世早在1523年便信奉路德的教义，两年后派一名改革者前往尼恩堡。1582年2月25日，奥托八世在霍亚城堡去世，伯爵领归于韦尔夫诸公爵，大部落入策勒支系之手。1625至1626年，丹麦国王克里斯蒂安四世与蒂利的帝国军队争夺这处威悉河渡口，炮弹毁了伯爵们的旧宫，1626年12月12日霍亚向丹麦军队投降。霍亚后来隶属汉诺威选帝侯国，1815年起隶属汉诺威王国。

en:
Paderborn is the cathedral city of eastern Westphalia, set where the river Pader wells out of more than two hundred springs at the foot of its minster and runs a few kilometres to the Lippe. Charlemagne built a palace on the springs during the Saxon wars and held his first imperial diet there in 777; in 799 Pope Leo III, fleeing rebellion in Rome, spent three months with Charlemagne at the palace, and the two settled the imperial coronation in Rome in 800. The bishopric founded that year grew into an imperial prince-bishopric, whose bishops ruled the market towns and abbeys between Paderborn and Warburg and held Neuhaus Castle west of the city from 1371. In 836 the relics of Saint Liborius were brought from Le Mans to the minster crypt, the origin of the July Liborius festival and the town's tie with Le Mans. In 1444 the see was held by Dietrich III of Moers, archbishop of Cologne as well; his debts and the Soest Feud of 1444-1449 were already drawing fighting into this Catholic corner of Westphalia.

The minster cloister carries the city's best-known image, the sixteenth-century Window of Three Hares: three hares chase in a circle, each with two ears though only three are drawn. Lutheran preaching arrived in 1526, and under a Lutheran bishop much of the bishopric turned Protestant; the chapter called in the Jesuits in 1580, and Bishop Dietrich IV von Fürstenberg led the Catholic restoration, forced the city to submit in 1604 and founded Westphalia's first university in 1614. The Thirty Years' War undid much of it: Christian of Brunswick sacked the city in 1622, Hessian troops held the land from 1632 to 1636 and Wrangel stormed it in 1646; Paderborn was taken or besieged sixteen times, and war and plague cost the bishopric about a third of its people. Baroque building resumed under Ferdinand II von Fürstenberg after 1661; in 1804 Friedrich Sertürner, a Paderborn pharmacist's apprentice, first isolated morphine from opium. Prussian troops occupied it in 1802, secularisation came in 1803, and after the Westphalian interlude of 1807-1813 the land returned to Prussia.
zh:
帕德博恩是威斯特伐利亚东部的主教座堂城市。帕德河从座堂脚下的两百多处泉眼中涌出，西行几公里便注入利珀河，城市也因这些泉源得名。萨克森战争期间，查理大帝在泉边修建行宫，777年在此召开第一次帝国会议；799年，躲避罗马叛乱的教宗利奥三世逃到行宫，与查理大帝同住三个月，两人谈定了800年在罗马举行的皇帝加冕。同年设立的主教区后来成为神圣罗马帝国的采邑主教区，主教们统治着帕德博恩与瓦尔堡之间的集镇、修道院和乡村庄园，1371年起又把城西的新豪斯城堡作为治所。836年，圣利博留斯的遗骨从勒芒迁来，安葬在座堂地下，两座城市也因遗骨结缘，帕德博恩每年7月举办利博里节纪念这位圣人。1444年，主教迪特里希三世·冯·默尔斯同时兼任科隆大主教；他负债累累，1444年爆发的索斯特封邑冲突又把战火烧进这片天主教的威斯特伐利亚土地。

座堂回廊里保存着全城最有名的图像，即16世纪的「三兔窗」：三只兔子绕圈追逐，每只都有两只耳朵，画面上却一共只画了三只耳朵。1526年路德宗讲道传入，在一位路德宗主教治下，主教区大部分改宗新教；座堂参事会1580年召来耶稣会，迪特里希四世·冯·菲尔斯滕贝格主教随后完成天主教复兴，1604年迫使城市屈服，又于1614年创办威斯特伐利亚第一所大学。三十年战争一度打断这一进程：不伦瑞克的克里斯蒂安1622年纵兵劫掠，黑森军队1632至1636年占领此地，弗兰格尔1646年破城；帕德博恩先后十六次被攻占或围困，战争与瘟疫使采邑主教区损失约三分之一人口。1661年后，斐迪南二世·冯·菲尔斯滕贝格大兴土木，建起巴洛克式的塔楼和立面。1804年，帕德博恩本地的药剂学徒弗里德里希·瑟图纳首次从鸦片中分离出吗啡。1802年普鲁士军队占领主教区，1803年世俗化完成；1807至1813年此地归属威斯特伐利亚王国，此后复归普鲁士。

en:
Meppen sits at the mouth of the Hase, which then reached the Ems in three branches; its Old Saxon name means 'at the mouths'. The Emperor Louis the Pious gave the missionary settlement here to Corvey Abbey in 834, and Otto the Great granted it minting and toll rights in 945 and market rights a year later. In 1252 the place passed with the Emsland lands of Countess Jutta to the bishop of Münster and became part of the Niederstift, the northern half of the prince-bishopric. Bishop Adolf granted town rights and leave to fortify in 1360, and the lords of Langen administered it for the see from 1392. In 1444 Meppen was a small walled market town, where the shipping of the Ems met the overland roads at its river crossing.

Jesuits opened a college in 1613, and their school and mission did much to keep the Emsland Catholic through the Reformation. The walls and bastions were strengthened until 1660, but the fortress was demolished in 1762, near the end of the Seven Years' War. Secularisation in 1803 made Meppen the capital of the new Duchy of Arenberg-Meppen, given to the Duke of Arenberg in exchange for his lands west of the Rhine. French annexation followed in 1811, and after Napoleon's fall the Congress of Vienna assigned the town to the Kingdom of Hanover in 1815.
zh:
梅彭位于哈瑟河注入埃姆斯河之处，当时哈瑟河分为三汊，古萨克森语地名意为「河口」。834年，虔诚者路易把这里的传教站赠予科尔维修道院；945年奥托大帝授予铸币权与关税权，次年又授予市集权。1252年，随着费希塔-拉文斯贝格女伯爵尤塔的埃姆斯兰领地易手，梅彭归入明斯特主教区，成为主教区北半部「下主教区」的一部分。1360年主教阿道夫授予城市权和筑城权，1392年起朗根家族代主教治理此地。1444年，梅彭是一座有城墙的小集镇，埃姆斯河的航运与陆路在它的渡口相汇。

1613年，耶稣会士在此开办学校，他们的学堂和传教使埃姆斯兰在宗教改革年代保持了天主教信仰。城墙和棱堡一直加固到1660年，但七年战争末期的1762年，要塞遭到拆毁。1803年世俗化中，梅彭成为新设的阿伦贝格-梅彭公国首府，封给阿伦贝格公爵，以交换他在莱茵河以西丧失的领地。1811年法国吞并此地；拿破仑失败后，维也纳会议在1815年把梅彭划归汉诺威王国。

en:
Loon was the Flemish countryside of the Prince-Bishopric of Liège, spread between the fertile villages of Hesbaye, the Kempen heaths and the towns along the Maas. Its counts first kept court at Borgloon, whose early castle gave the county its name. Count Gerard moved the court to Kuringen, later part of Hasselt, after Liège soldiers burned Borgloon in 1179, yet the old town stayed among Loon's recognized 'Good Cities'. All ten Dutch-speaking Good Cities of the principality, including Hasselt, Maaseik and Borgloon, lay in this quartier. When the comital line ended, Prince-Bishop Engelbert III of the Marck occupied Loon in 1362 and annexed it four years later. In 1444 John of Heinsberg ruled it as a Catholic part of the Prince-Bishopric, while Loon kept its own estates, towns and customs.

Burgundy put that self-government to the test in the Liège wars. After the Liégeois revolted against Louis de Bourbon, the bishop backed by Philip the Good, Charles the Bold routed their army at Brustem, near Sint-Truiden, on 28 October 1467; Burgundian troops burned Liège the following year. Brustem had been a fortified Loon place, and the campaigns drew the county's southern towns directly into the fighting. Charles's death in 1477 let Liège recover its autonomy. In 1492 the Peace of Donchery ended the war between Bishop John of Horne and the House of the Marck, and Liège proclaimed its neutrality. Loon therefore stayed outside the Seventeen Provinces and the Burgundian Netherlands until French revolutionary armies dissolved the old quartier in 1795 and placed it in Meuse-Inférieure.
zh:
隆恩是列日采邑主教区内的佛兰德人地区，地跨哈斯拜的肥沃村野、肯彭荒原和马斯河畔城镇。历代伯爵最初驻在博尔赫隆，伯国也因这座早期城堡得名。1179年列日士兵焚毁博尔赫隆后，赫拉德伯爵把宫廷迁往库林根，也就是后来哈瑟尔特的一部分，但旧城仍是隆恩受承认的「良城」之一。主教区全部十座讲荷兰语的良城，包括哈瑟尔特、马塞克和博尔赫隆，都坐落在这个分区。伯爵血脉断绝后，采邑主教恩格尔贝特三世·范·德·马克于1362年占领隆恩，四年后正式吞并。1444年，约翰·范·海因斯贝格以采邑主教身份统治这片天主教土地，隆恩则保留自己的等级会议、城镇和旧俗。

列日战争中，勃艮第逼到了这套自治面前。列日人起兵反对好人菲利普支持的采邑主教路易·德·波旁，1467年10月28日，大胆的查理在圣特赖登附近的布鲁斯特姆击溃列日军；次年，勃艮第军队焚毁列日本城。布鲁斯特姆本是隆恩设防据点，战祸也直接卷入党区南部城镇。1477年查理战死后，列日恢复自主。1492年，《栋什里和约》结束约翰·范·霍恩主教与马克家族的战争，列日宣布中立。隆恩没有并入十七省和勃艮第尼德兰；1795年，法国革命军队废除旧分区，把它划入下默兹省。

en:
Cleves straddled the Lower Rhine, and its dukes lived in the Schwanenburg, the Swan Castle, on a steep bluff above the town. Its massive tower, the Schwanenturm, is tied in legend to the Knight of the Swan, the tale Richard Wagner later made into Lohengrin. Count Dietrich granted the settlement town rights in 1242, and a Marian collegiate foundation moved from Monterberg helped the four-part medieval town grow. When the native comital line died out, Adolf of the Mark inherited Cleves in 1368 and reunited it with the County of Mark in 1398. In 1397 he captured William II of Jülich-Berg at Kleverhamm in a fight over the Kaiserswerth Rhine toll, and in 1417 Sigismund raised him to duke at Constance. In 1444 the town of Soest placed itself under his protection against Cologne, and the Soest Feud began; the Catholic Rhenish duchy lived on Rhine tolls, market towns and cloth traffic.

Adolf's son John I closed the feud by making Cologne renounce its feudal claim. A marriage treaty, the Klever Union, then joined the dynasties: John III married Maria of Jülich-Berg, and the United Duchies of Jülich, Cleves and Berg took shape in 1521. Their daughter Anne married Henry VIII of England in 1540; Henry had Holbein paint her portrait before the wedding, but the marriage was annulled after six months and she lived out her life in England as the king's 'beloved sister'. The dukes stayed Catholic while letting Wesel and Duisburg shelter Protestant communities. When the dynasty died out in 1609, the Treaty of Xanten in 1614 assigned Cleves provisionally to Brandenburg, a settlement confirmed only in 1666. From 1647 Johann Moritz of Nassau-Siegen, called the Brazilian after governing Dutch Brazil, ruled the duchy for more than thirty years: he rebuilt the Schwanenburg in baroque style, put up the Prinzenhof and laid out gardens that made Cleve a Brandenburg residence. French troops took the town in October 1794, and after two decades of French and Berg rule Cleves returned to Prussia in 1815.
zh:
克莱沃据有莱茵河下游两岸，公爵们住在高踞镇旁陡崖上的天鹅堡。堡中巍峨的高塔「天鹅塔」相传与天鹅骑士的故事有关，瓦格纳后来把这个传说写成《罗恩格林》。1242年，迪特里希伯爵向聚落颁发城市权，从蒙特贝格迁来的圣母修道院又推动这座由四部分组成的中世纪城镇成长。旧伯爵家族绝嗣后，马克的阿道夫1368年继承克莱沃，1398年把马克伯国并回。1397年，双方为凯泽斯韦尔特的莱茵河关税开战，阿道夫在克莱弗哈姆俘获于利希-贝格的威廉二世；1417年，西吉斯蒙德在康斯坦茨立他为公爵。1444年，索斯特为对抗科隆而投入阿道夫麾下，索斯特仇争随之爆发；这个信天主教的莱茵公国靠莱茵河关税、市集城镇和布匹贸易为生。

阿道夫之子约翰一世结束了这场仇争，迫使科隆放弃封主权。后来的婚约《克莱沃联盟》把两大家族连在一起：约翰三世娶于利希-贝格的玛丽亚，1521年于利希、克莱沃和贝格组成联合公国。他们的女儿安妮1540年嫁给英格兰国王亨利八世；婚前亨利曾让荷尔拜因为她画像，但婚姻仅维持半年即告无效，她以国王「亲爱的姊妹」之名在英格兰终老。历代公爵仍奉天主教，同时听任韦瑟尔和杜伊斯堡庇护新教社群。王朝1609年绝嗣后，1614年《克桑滕条约》先把克莱沃分给勃兰登堡，归属直到1666年才最终确认。1647年起，曾治理荷属巴西、人称「巴西人」的约翰·莫里茨·冯·拿骚-锡根统治这里三十多年：他把天鹅堡改建为巴洛克风格，修建亲王宫，辟造园林，使克莱沃成为勃兰登堡的一处驻地。1794年10月法军攻占该城，在法国和贝格治下度过二十年后，克莱沃于1815年回归普鲁士。

en:
Perugia crowns a high ridge above the upper Tiber, its oldest quarters ringed by the Etruscan walls of Perusia, one of the twelve cities of the Etruscan League. The medieval commune was a Guelph power, fighting Assisi, Siena and Arezzo and opening its gates to popes driven out of Rome; five papal conclaves met in the city, and the university founded in 1308 drew law students from all over Italy. When an aqueduct at last carried water to the hilltop in the 1270s, Nicola and Giovanni Pisano carved the marble reliefs of the Fontana Maggiore to mark it. The commune also bred soldiers. The condottiero Braccio da Montone made himself lord in 1416, briefly held Rome, and was killed besieging L'Aquila in 1424. In 1444 Perugia governed itself under the covert rule of Braccio I Baglioni, the dead condottiero's nephew, while nominally belonging to the Church.

The Baglioni carried Perugia into its Renaissance, building palaces and roads and drawing painters to the city: Pinturicchio worked there, the young Raphael painted in and near it, and Perugino, Raphael's teacher, covered the walls of the money-changers' Sala del Cambio with frescoes between 1498 and 1500. Patronage and blood feud ran side by side. On the night of 14 July 1500 rival branches of the family killed one another in the streets and palaces in the 'Red Wedding'. In 1520 Pope Leo X lured Giampaolo Baglioni to Rome and had him beheaded. The Salt War against Paul III put an end to Perugian self-rule: papal troops under Pier Luigi Farnese took the city on 3 June 1540, and Antonio da Sangallo the Younger's Rocca Paolina rose over the levelled Baglioni quarter, raised to overawe the citizens. French troops arrived in 1797 and Perugia became the capital of the short-lived Tiberina Republic in February 1798; Napoleon attached the region to his empire as the Department of Trasimène in 1809, and papal rule returned in 1814.
zh:
佩鲁贾雄踞台伯河上游的高山脊上，老城外围着佩鲁西亚的伊特鲁里亚城墙，佩鲁西亚本是伊特鲁里亚联盟十二城之一。中世纪的公社是圭尔夫派强权，连年与阿西西、锡耶纳、阿雷佐交战，又收留被逐出罗马的教宗，先后有五次教宗选举秘密会议在此召开；1308年创办的大学吸引着全意大利攻读法律的学生。1270年代输水道终于把水引上山岭，尼古拉·皮萨诺和乔瓦尼·皮萨诺父子为马焦雷喷泉雕刻了大理石浮雕，以庆其成。公社还出军人。雇佣军队长弗泰布拉乔1416年成为城主，一度占领罗马，1424年在拉奎拉围城战中毙命。1444年的佩鲁贾在这位已故队长的外甥布拉乔一世·巴廖尼的隐性统治下自治，名义上仍是教会的城市。

巴廖尼家族把佩鲁贾带入它的文艺复兴盛期，修筑宫殿和道路，把画家引来此地：平图里乔在城中作画，年轻的拉斐尔在城内外留下作品，拉斐尔的老师佩鲁吉诺则在1498至1500年间为钱商行会的坎比奥厅绘满湿壁画。庇护与仇杀并行。1500年7月14日夜，家族的两支旁系在街头和宅第中互相屠戮，史称「红色婚礼」。1520年，良十世把詹保罗·巴廖尼诱往罗马斩首。对抗保禄三世的食盐战争终结了佩鲁贾的自治：皮埃尔·路易吉·法尔内塞率领的教宗军队1540年6月3日破城，小安东尼奥·达·桑加罗设计的保利纳堡垒在被夷平的巴廖尼宅第上筑起，用意是震慑市民。1797年法军入城，1798年2月佩鲁贾成为短命的台伯里纳共和国首都；1809年拿破仑把这一带并入帝国的特拉西梅诺省，1814年教宗统治复辟。

en:
Urbino sits on a steep ridge of the Marche, on the old road between the Apennine passes and the Adriatic, its houses climbing to a fortress the Montefeltro held for nearly three centuries. The family made themselves lords in 1234 and led the Ghibellines of the Marche through their long feud with the Malatesta of Rimini. In 1443 Pope Eugene IV raised the town to a duchy for Oddantonio da Montefeltro; within a year his own subjects murdered the young duke, and in 1444 his half-brother Federico, a condottiere already known across Italy, seized power. His thirty-eight-year rule turned a rough hill fortress into one of the most polished courts of the Renaissance.

Mercenary wars paid for it all. Federico had Luciano Laurana rebuild the Palazzo Ducale, kept a team of scribes at work on one of Italy's greatest libraries, and gathered Piero della Francesca and Pedro Berruguete at his court; Pope Sixtus IV confirmed his ducal title in 1474. When Federico died in 1482 the court kept its lustre: Raphael was born in the town in 1483, the son of the court painter Giovanni Santi, and Baldassare Castiglione set The Book of the Courtier among the men and women of Duke Guidobaldo's palace. Cesare Borgia drove Guidobaldo out in 1502, the university was founded in 1506, and in 1508 the duchy passed to the Della Rovere, who moved the court to Pesaro in 1523. Urbino then lived by its crafts: its potters made the istoriato maiolica painted with biblical and classical scenes, and masters such as Nicola da Urbino and Francesco Xanto Avelli signed dishes sent to princes across Italy. The last duke, Francesco Maria II, signed the devolution of his state to the Papacy in 1625, and when he died in 1631 Pope Urban VIII incorporated it into the Papal States. Cardinal Giovanni Francesco Albani, born in the city, was elected pope as Clement XI and spent on his hometown, and from 1717 to 1718 it sheltered the exiled British pretender James Stuart. The earthquake of 1789 brought down the cathedral dome, French troops occupied Urbino in 1798 and withdrew in 1799, and Giuseppe Valadier's new Duomo was consecrated in 1809.
zh:
乌尔比诺坐落在马尔凯地区一道陡峭的山梁上，扼守亚平宁山口通往亚得里亚海的古道，房屋顺着山坡一直延伸到蒙特费尔特罗家族据守近三百年的要塞。1234年，这个家族成为城市领主，此后作为马尔凯吉伯林派的领袖，同里米尼的马拉泰斯塔家族长期相争。1443年，教皇尤金四世将乌尔比诺升为公国，封奥丹托尼奥·达·蒙特费尔特罗为公爵；不出一年，年轻的公爵便被自己的臣民杀死，1444年，他的异母兄、早已闻名全意大利的雇佣军首领费代里科夺取政权。他三十八年的统治，把一座粗陋山城变成文艺复兴最精致的宫廷之一。

这一切靠的是雇佣军战争的收入。费代里科请卢恰诺·劳拉纳重建公爵宫，雇一群抄书人建起意大利首屈一指的图书馆，皮耶罗·德拉·弗朗切斯卡和佩德罗·贝鲁格特齐聚宫中作画；1474年教皇西克斯图斯四世确认他的公爵头衔。他1482年去世后，宫廷声望不坠：拉斐尔1483年生于城中，父亲是宫廷画师乔万尼·桑蒂；巴尔达萨雷·卡斯蒂廖内的《廷臣论》就把对话安排在圭多巴尔多公爵宫中的男女之间。1502年切萨雷·波吉亚驱逐圭多巴尔多，大学1506年创立；1508年公国传入德拉·罗韦雷家族，1523年宫廷迁往佩萨罗。此后乌尔比诺靠手艺立足：陶工烧制马约利卡锡釉彩陶，盘面上画满圣经与古典故事，尼古拉·达·乌尔比诺等名家在盘底签名，作品送往意大利各邦君主的宫廷。末代公爵弗朗切斯科·马里亚二世1625年签署文书把国家交还教廷，1631年他去世后，教皇乌尔班八世将公国并入教皇国。出生于此的枢机主教乔万尼·弗朗切斯科·阿尔巴尼后来当选教皇，称克莱门特十一世，斥资整修故乡；1717至1718年，流亡的英国王位觊觎者詹姆斯·斯图亚特曾在此驻留。1789年大地震震塌大教堂穹顶，1798年法军占领乌尔比诺、1799年撤出，朱塞佩·瓦拉迪耶设计的新大教堂于1809年祝圣。

en:
Arezzo sits in a basin where the roads from the Val di Chiana, the Casentino and the Valdarno meet before the Apennine passes. It was one of the twelve cities of Etruria, and Roman Arretium was the third-largest city of Augustan Italy: its moulded red-gloss tableware was shipped across the Roman world, and Gaius Maecenas, the friend and minister of Augustus whose name became the word for a patron of poets, came of an old Aretine Etruscan family. The bronze Chimera dug up outside the walls in the sixteenth century, now in Florence, was cast by its craftsmen. The medieval commune, generally Ghibelline, fought Guelph Florence for the upper Arno and lost at Campaldino on 11 June 1289; Bishop Guglielmino degli Ubertini died in the field, and Dante Alighieri, then twenty-four, rode in the Florentine cavalry. After a final revival under Bishop Guido Tarlati in the 1320s, the French soldier Enguerrand de Coucy sold his occupation of the city to Florence in 1384. In 1444 Arezzo is a subject fortress on Florence's eastern frontier.

The city's famous sons worked in books and music. Around 1025 the Benedictine monk Guido of Arezzo taught singers at the cathedral the staff notation explained in his Micrologus. Petrarch was born here in 1304, the son of a Florentine in exile. Giorgio Vasari, born in Arezzo in 1511, wrote the Lives of the painters, sculptors and architects of Italy. Between 1452 and 1466 Piero della Francesca painted the Legend of the True Cross on the walls of San Francesco, and San Domenico holds Cimabue's large painted crucifix.

Arezzo rose against Florentine rule in 1529, and around 1560 the Medici built the bastioned Fortezza above the town to keep it quiet. In the course of the 1700s the malarial marshes of the neighbouring Val di Chiana were drained and put under the plough. In 1799 the city became a centre of the Viva Maria, the rising of peasants and priests against the French, named for the Marian hymn the insurgents sang; under Napoleon it belonged to the French department of the Arno, and the Accademia Petrarca was founded there in 1810.
zh:
阿雷佐坐落在一处盆地，瓦尔迪基亚纳、卡森蒂诺和瓦尔达诺的道路在此会合，再通向亚平宁山口。它曾是伊特鲁里亚十二城之一；罗马时代的阿雷提乌姆是奥古斯都时期意大利第三大城，模制的红釉餐具远销罗马世界，奥古斯都的友臣、以庇护诗人闻名的盖乌斯·梅塞纳斯就出身当地古老的伊特鲁里亚世家。16世纪在城墙外出土的青铜奇美拉像便出自这里的工匠之手，后来被运往佛罗伦萨。中世纪的城市公社多站在吉伯林派一边，为争夺阿尔诺上游同归尔夫派的佛罗伦萨交战，1289年6月11日在坎帕尔迪诺战败：主教圭利尔米诺·德利·乌贝尔蒂尼战死，时年二十四岁的但丁也在佛罗伦萨骑兵阵中。圭多·塔尔拉蒂主教1320年代让城市重振一时，此后法国军人昂盖朗·德·库西于1384年把占领下的阿雷佐卖给佛罗伦萨。1444年，这里是佛罗伦萨东部边境上一座受其统治的要塞。

这座城市的名人多与书籍和音乐有关。约1025年，本笃会修士阿雷佐的圭多在大教堂教唱诗班识谱，他在《Micrologus》中阐述的线谱记谱法通行于中世纪欧洲。1304年，彼特拉克出生于此，父亲是被放逐的佛罗伦萨人。1511年生于阿雷佐的乔尔乔·瓦萨里写下《艺苑名人传》，为意大利的画家、雕塑家和建筑师立传。1452至1466年，皮耶罗·德拉·弗兰切斯卡在圣方济各堂绘制《真十字架传奇》湿壁画，圣多明我堂则藏有契马布埃的大型彩绘十字架。

1529年阿雷佐起兵反抗佛罗伦萨统治，约1560年美第奇家族在城镇上方修起棱堡式要塞，以弹压全城。18世纪，邻近的瓦尔迪基亚纳瘴气沼泽被排干，改成耕地。1799年，阿雷佐成为「玛利亚万岁」反法起事的中心，起兵者多为农民和教士，唱着圣母颂歌进军，运动也以此得名；拿破仑时期城市被划入法国的阿诺省，彼特拉克学院于1810年在此创立。

en:
Novara lies in the grain country of the western Po plain, between the Agogna and Terdoppio streams, where the road from Turin to Milan meets routes climbing to the Alpine passes. Roman Novaria was a municipium on the Vercelli road, and its cross-street plan still marks the centre; Magnus Maximus destroyed the town in 386 and Attila's Huns sacked it in 452. It revived as a free commune of the Lombard League, and three hundred Novarese and Vercellese fought in the league ranks at Legnano in 1176. The theologian Peter Lombard, later bishop of Paris and author of the Sentences, was born at Lumellogno, now part of the city. By 1200 Novara had accepted Milan's protection, and the Visconti and Sforza dukes built and held its castle. In 1444 it was a grain-growing town of Filippo Maria Visconti's Milanese state.

The Italian Wars twice made the Novarese the setting of Ludovico Sforza's ruin. In 1495 the French Duke of Orléans took the city and was in turn besieged there by Ludovico's army. On 8 April 1500 the duke's Swiss mercenaries refused to fight the Swiss in French pay; he slipped out among their columns in disguise, was given up by two companions, and was locked in a cage in the Château de Loches, where he died in 1508. In 1513 another French siege collapsed when Swiss in Massimiliano Sforza's pay scattered the besiegers. Savoyard troops occupied the town in 1706, but the Peace of Utrecht left it with Habsburg Milan; Charles Emmanuel III took it in 1734 and it passed to Savoy the next year. Under Napoleon Novara headed the Department of the Agogna, and on 8 April 1821 Sardinian and Austrian regulars defeated Piedmontese liberals outside the walls.
zh:
诺瓦拉位于波河平原西部的粮乡，在阿戈尼亚河与泰尔多皮奥河之间，都灵通往米兰的大道在此与通向阿尔卑斯山隘的道路相接。罗马时代的诺瓦里亚是韦尔切利大道上的自治城，十字相交的街道格局保留在老城中心；386年马格努斯·马克西穆斯摧毁此城，452年阿提拉的匈人又将它洗劫。后来它作为伦巴第联盟的自由公社复兴，1176年三百名诺瓦拉人和韦尔切利人加入联盟军队参加莱尼亚诺战役。神学家彼得·伦巴德出生在城边的卢梅洛尼奥（今属诺瓦拉市区），他后来担任巴黎主教，所著《箴言四书》是中世纪神学的标准教本。1200年前后诺瓦拉接受米兰的庇护，维斯孔蒂与斯福尔扎两姓公爵先后修筑并据守城中的城堡。1444年，它是菲利波·马里亚·维斯孔蒂的米兰公国境内一座盛产谷物的城镇。

意大利战争中，诺瓦拉一带两度成为卢多维科·斯福尔扎覆灭的现场。1495年，法兰西奥尔良公爵占领此城，反被卢多维科的大军围困。1500年4月8日，公爵麾下的瑞士雇佣兵拒绝与法军中的瑞士同胞交战；他化装混在瑞士队伍里出城，被两名随从交出，关进法国洛什城堡的牢笼，1508年死于该处。1513年，为马西米利亚诺·斯福尔扎效力的瑞士军队击溃围城法军，又一次围城告吹。1706年萨伏依军队占领诺瓦拉，但《乌得勒支和约》把它留在哈布斯堡治下的米兰；卡洛·埃马努埃莱三世1734年攻取此城，次年它并入萨伏依。拿破仑时期诺瓦拉成为阿戈尼亚省省会，1821年4月8日，撒丁与奥地利的正规军在城外击败皮埃蒙特立宪派。

en:
Lucca sits on the Serchio, where a fertile plain opens between the Ligurian hills and Tuscany. The Roman colony of 180 BC left its rectangular street plan, and the curve of the old amphitheatre still sets the shape of Piazza dell'Anfiteatro. Medieval pilgrims on the Via Francigena stopped to venerate the Holy Face, an eight-foot wooden crucifix said to have come to the city in 742. The merchants who made Lucca counted on a smaller luxury: silk. From the 11th century its weavers produced Lucca cloth with gold and silver threads, and the city's banking houses kept offices as far away as Bruges, where the Arnolfini family traded.

Soldiers mattered as much as merchants in Lucca's politics. Castruccio Castracani took power after a Pisan occupation, defeated a Florentine army at Altopascio in 1325, and received the title duke of Lucca; Machiavelli later made his career the subject of a political biography. The last lord of the republic was Paolo Guinigi, who ruled from 1400 to 1430. The cathedral holds the marble tomb Jacopo della Quercia carved for Guinigi's wife Ilaria del Carretto, while the tall brick Guinigi Tower recalls the family's houses inside the city. A Florentine siege in 1429 failed when Francesco Sforza brought Milanese cavalry to its relief, and the Lucchese expelled the Guinigi the next year. In 1444 Lucca was therefore a small Catholic free republic, surrounded by stronger neighbours but paying its way with silk, credit and careful diplomacy.

That diplomacy was backed by one of the largest Renaissance city walls in Italy. Work on the bastioned ring, more than four kilometres around with eleven bastions, continued from 1544 to 1648. Florence and later the grand duchy of Tuscany were the danger its builders had in mind, yet no besieging army ever reached the walls; Lucca's wars with Modena were fought away in the Garfagnana. The popular republic narrowed into an oligarchy in 1628, but the silk looms kept working. French and Austrian troops contested the city in 1799 and 1800, a democratic charter followed in 1801, and in 1805 Napoleon made his sister Elisa princess of Lucca and Piombino. The ramparts met their only emergency in 1812, when a flooding Serchio forced the Lucchese to bolt and mattress the gates; the Congress of Vienna then assigned Lucca to Maria Luisa of Bourbon, who took possession in 1815.
zh:
卢卡位于塞尔基奥河畔，利古里亚丘陵与托斯卡纳之间的肥沃平原在此展开。公元前180年这里成为罗马殖民城，方整的街道格局保留了罗马营城痕迹，古竞技场的弧形外墙也仍决定着圆形竞技场广场的轮廓。中世纪时，取道法兰契杰纳路前往罗马的朝圣者会在这里瞻仰圣容苦像；这座约二点四米高的木雕苦像据说于742年运抵卢卡。让卢卡商人真正立足的则是丝绸。从11世纪起，当地织工生产织入金线、银线的卢卡绸，商人银行家还把商行开到遥远的布鲁日，阿尔诺尔菲尼家族便在那里经商。

在卢卡政治中，军人和商人同样重要。卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼在比萨占领之后掌权，1325年在阿尔托帕肖击败佛罗伦萨军队，受封卢卡公爵；马基雅维利后来以他的生平写成一部政治传记。共和国最后一位僭主是保罗·圭尼吉，1400至1430年统治卢卡。大教堂中保存着雅各布·德拉·奎尔恰为圭尼吉之妻伊拉里娅·德尔·卡雷托雕刻的大理石墓，城内高耸的砖砌圭尼吉塔则提醒人这一家族曾在城中拥有宅邸。1429年佛罗伦萨围攻卢卡，弗朗切斯科·斯福尔扎率米兰骑兵解围，卢卡人次年驱逐圭尼吉家族。因此到1444年，卢卡是一个天主教自由小共和国，强邻环伺，却靠丝绸、信贷和谨慎外交维持自身。

这种谨慎外交背后，是意大利规模最大的文艺复兴城墙之一。棱堡城墙周长四公里多，设有十一座棱堡，1544年动工，1648年完工。筑城者担心的是佛罗伦萨以及后来的托斯卡纳大公国，但围城军队从未抵达城下；卢卡与摩德纳的战争也都在加尔法尼亚纳山区进行。1628年，平民共和国收缩为寡头政体，丝织机却没有停转。1799至1800年，法军和奥军争夺卢卡；1801年这里颁布民主约法，1805年拿破仑封妹妹埃莉萨为卢卡与皮翁比诺公主。1812年，城墙唯一一次应急用在塞尔基奥河洪水期间，卢卡人锁死城门并垫上床垫；维也纳和会随后把卢卡交给波旁家族的玛丽亚·路易莎，她于1815年入城。

en:
Montferrat is a country of vineyard hills between the Po and the Ligurian Apennines, and its marquesses were famous in Christendom before they were ever powerful. The Aleramics married into the royal houses of Jerusalem and Byzantium. Conrad of Montferrat organised the defence of Tyre against Saladin in 1187 and was elected king of Jerusalem in 1192, only to be stabbed by Assassins days after his election; his kinsman Boniface I led the Fourth Crusade and wore the crown of Thessalonica. Their seat was Chivasso. When the Aleramic line ran out in 1305, Montferrat passed to Theodore Palaiologos, son of the Byzantine emperor, and a Greek dynasty ruled for two centuries under pressure from Milan and Savoy. John Jacob lost Chivasso to Amadeus VIII of Savoy, moved his capital to Casale in 1434 and accepted Savoyard protection. In 1444 Montferrat survived as a small imperial marquisate of the Palaiologoi, its wine hills ringed by greater neighbours.

The last Greek marquess, John George, died without male heirs in 1533, and in 1536 Charles V granted the fief to Federico II Gonzaga of Mantua, husband of the Palaeologan heiress. The Gonzaga gave Casale a large new citadel, and French troops held the town until the Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis in 1559; in 1574 Montferrat was raised to a duchy. The Gonzaga succession then made these hills a battlefield: Savoy invaded in 1613, and during the Mantuan succession war the Spanish commander Ambrogio Spinola besieged Casale and died there in September 1630 without taking it. The fortress held out until French relief and the Peace of Cherasco ended the war in 1631, when western Montferrat was detached for Savoy; in 1708, when the Gonzaga lost Mantua, the rest passed to the House of Savoy. It shared Piedmont's fate in the Napoleonic wars and returned with the Kingdom of Sardinia in 1814.
zh:
蒙费拉托是波河与利古里亚亚平宁山脉之间一片葡萄园丘陵，这里的侯爵在权势壮大之前便已闻名基督教世界。阿莱拉莫家族与耶路撒冷和拜占庭的王室联姻：1187年，蒙费拉托的科拉多在推罗组织防御、挡住萨拉丁，1192年当选耶路撒冷国王，当选几天后便被阿萨辛派刺死；他的族人博尼法乔一世率领第四次十字军，戴上了塞萨洛尼基的王冠。家族的都城是基瓦索。1305年阿莱拉莫家族绝嗣，蒙费拉托传给拜占庭皇帝之子特奥多罗·帕里奥洛加斯，希腊王朝在米兰和萨伏依的压力下统治了两百年。吉安·贾科莫把基瓦索丢给萨伏依公爵阿梅迪奥八世，1434年迁都卡萨莱，并接受萨伏依保护。1444年，蒙费拉托是帕里奥洛加斯王朝治下的帝国小侯国，产酒的丘陵被强邻环伺。

末代希腊裔侯爵乔瓦尼·乔治1533年去世，没有男嗣；1536年查理五世把封地赐给曼托瓦的费代里科二世·贡扎加，他娶了帕里奥洛加斯家族的女继承人。贡扎加家族为卡萨莱建起一座宏大的新城塞，法军曾占据此城，直到1559年《卡托-康布雷西和约》才撤出；1574年蒙费拉托升格为公国。此后贡扎加家族的继承问题让这片丘陵变成战场：1613年萨伏依出兵来攻，曼托瓦继承战争中，西班牙名将安布罗焦·斯皮诺拉围攻卡萨莱，1630年9月死在围城军营里，城却始终没有攻下。要塞坚守到法国援军抵达、1631年《凯拉斯科和约》结束战争，和约把蒙费拉托西部割给萨伏依；1708年贡扎加家族失去曼托瓦，余下的土地也并入萨伏依王室。拿破仑战争中它随皮埃蒙特一同易手，1814年随撒丁王国归还。

en:
Syracuse occupies Ortygia island and the great harbour on Sicily's southeastern corner. Corinthian settlers founded it in 733 BC, and at the height of its power the city rivalled Athens; it was the birthplace of Archimedes, who held the Romans at bay with his engines in the siege of 212 BC until the town was stormed and a soldier cut him down in the street. Its cathedral stands inside the fifth-century BC Temple of Athena, whose Doric columns still frame the walls. Constans II made the town his Byzantine capital in 663 and was murdered in his bath there five years later; the Arabs took it in 878 after a long siege, and Robert Guiscard's Normans recovered it in 1085, though Palermo kept the royal capital. From 1302 it belonged to the queens of Sicily, whose Camera reginale gave the city wide autonomy under the Crown of Aragon. In 1444 Syracuse was an Aragonese market town and fortress, smaller than Palermo or Messina, guarding the sea lanes toward Malta and the Levant.

Charles V had Ortygia rebuilt as a royal fortress. The Hospitallers, freshly expelled from Rhodes, wintered there in 1529 hoping to stay, but the emperor refused them the city and enfeoffed them with Malta instead. After Germaine de Foix died in 1536 he suppressed the Camera reginale and put the city under a military governor; in 1565 the viceroy of Sicily gathered his fleet in the great harbour for the relief of Malta. Caravaggio reached Syracuse in 1608 after his break with the Hospitallers in Malta and painted the Burial of Saint Lucy for the church of Santa Lucia. On 11 January 1693 a great earthquake followed by a wave wrecked Ortygia and killed some four thousand people; the rebuilding gave the old centre its late Baroque form. A Spanish occupation in 1718 ended with a British naval victory off Capo Passero, before Sicily passed to the Habsburgs and then to the Bourbon kings of Naples. During the Napoleonic wars the Royal Navy used the harbour as a base from 1807, and in 1816 Syracuse joined the Bourbon Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
zh:
锡拉库扎（通行译名为锡拉库萨）据守西西里东南角的奥尔蒂贾岛与大港。公元前733年科林斯殖民者在此建城，强盛之时势力比肩雅典；阿基米德出生于此，公元前212年罗马围城时，他凭机械装置久挫敌军，城破之后一名罗马士兵在街头将他杀死。城中的主教座堂就嵌在公元前5世纪的雅典娜神庙之内，多立克石柱还夹在教堂墙体之间。663年君士坦斯二世定此为拜占庭都城，五年后他在城中的浴室遇刺；阿拉伯人经长期围城于878年攻陷此城，1085年罗贝尔·吉斯卡尔的诺曼人将其收复，但西西里都城设在巴勒莫。1302年起，这里成为西西里王后的领地，王后府在阿拉贡王权下给了城市很大自治。1444年，锡拉库扎是阿拉贡治下的集镇兼要塞，规模不及巴勒莫或墨西拿，扼守着通往马耳他和黎凡特的海路。

查理五世把奥尔蒂贾改建成王室要塞。刚被逐出罗得岛的医院骑士团1529年在此过冬，希望留驻，但皇帝拒绝把此城交给他们，转而将马耳他封给骑士团。末代王后热尔梅娜·德·富瓦1536年去世后，他废除王后府，改派军事总督治理；1565年，西西里副王在大港集结舰队，前往救援马耳他。1608年，与马耳他骑士团决裂后出逃的卡拉瓦乔来到这里，为圣路济亚教堂绘成《埋葬圣路济亚》。1693年1月11日，大地震和接踵而至的海啸摧毁奥尔蒂贾，约四千人丧生，重建后的老城有了晚期巴洛克面貌。1718年西班牙一度占领此地，最终英国舰队在帕塞罗角外海取胜，此后西西里先转归哈布斯堡，再落入那不勒斯波旁王室。拿破仑战争期间，皇家海军从1807年起以这个港湾为基地；1816年，锡拉库扎并入波旁王朝的两西西里王国。

en:
Salerno curves around its Tyrrhenian gulf at the Campanian end of the road into Lucania. The Roman colony of Salernum guarded that route, but the city's medieval fame came from two powers close to the waterfront: its princes and its physicians. Lombard rulers made it capital of the independent Principality of Salerno in 839, and around the year 1000 Prince Guaimar IV drew Amalfi, Sorrento, Gaeta and Apulia into a short-lived Salernitan dominion; the city's coins proclaimed it 'Opulenta Salernum', wealthy Salerno. The Schola Medica Salernitana was already active in the ninth century and became western Europe's leading source of medical learning, combining Greek, Latin and Arabic practice at a time when women also treated patients and wrote medical texts there. Robert Guiscard took the city in 1077, built its cathedral and palace, and kept Saint Matthew's relics in the cathedral crypt. Salerno's defiance of Henry VI in 1194 followed the city's part in handing Empress Constance to King Tancred; imperial troops sacked it after the siege. In 1444 it was a city of the Kingdom of Naples, while the Sanseverino princes held much of its hinterland from fortified estates strong enough to rival the crown.

During the Italian Wars the Sanseverino and other local lords moved between the French Angevin and Aragonese causes. Ferrante Sanseverino, the last Prince of Salerno, broke with the Spanish viceregal government and the Inquisition and died in exile at Orange in 1568; his fall stripped the city of the princely court that had sustained much of its patronage. A storm scattered Hayreddin Barbarossa's fleet as it moved against Salerno in 1544. Revolutionaries declared the city part of the Parthenopean Republic in 1799, though Bourbon rule returned within months. Under Napoleonic Naples, Joachim Murat reorganized public education and suppressed the Schola Medica Salernitana on 29 November 1811, ending the institution that had taught physicians there for more than eight centuries.
zh:
萨莱诺环抱第勒尼安海上的萨莱诺湾，位于坎帕尼亚通往卢卡尼亚道路的一端。罗马殖民城萨莱努姆曾把守这条道路，但中世纪的名声主要来自近水的两股力量：诸侯和医生。839年，伦巴第统治者把这里定为独立的萨莱诺亲王国都城；约1000年时，亲王瓜伊马尔四世一度将阿马尔菲、索伦托、加埃塔和普利亚纳入萨莱诺势力，本地钱币上铸有「富饶的萨莱诺」字样。萨莱诺医学校在9世纪已经活动，后来成为西欧最重要的医学知识来源，兼采希腊、拉丁和阿拉伯医术；当时也有女性在这里治病并撰写医书。1077年，罗贝尔·吉斯卡尔攻占城市，修建主教座堂和宫殿，并把圣马太遗骨安放在主教座堂地下圣堂。萨莱诺曾参与把皇后康斯坦茨交给坦克雷迪国王，1194年又抵抗亨利六世，城破后遭帝国军队洗劫。1444年，萨莱诺是那不勒斯王国的城市，后方大片土地却掌握在圣塞韦里诺诸侯手中；他们的要塞和领地足以同王权抗衡。

意大利战争期间，圣塞韦里诺家族和其他本地领主在法国安茹阵营与阿拉贡阵营之间摇摆。末代萨莱诺亲王费兰泰·圣塞韦里诺同西班牙副王政府和宗教裁判所决裂，最终流亡，1568年死于奥朗日；他的败落使供养城市艺文活动的亲王府随之消失。1544年，赫伊尔丁·巴巴罗萨的舰队进逼萨莱诺时被风暴吹散。1799年，革命者宣布萨莱诺加入帕尔瑟诺佩共和国，但波旁统治数月后便恢复。拿破仑体系下的那不勒斯时期，若阿尚·缪拉整顿公共教育，并于1811年11月29日下令关闭萨莱诺医学校，终结了这所在当地延续八百多年的医学机构。

en:
Cosenza lies in the Crati valley, where the Busento joins the Crati on the road down through northern Calabria. Ancient Consentia was the chief town of the Bruttii and later a station on the Roman road to Rhegium. The river junction carries its most enduring story: the historian Jordanes says that Alaric, king of the Visigoths, died near Cosenza after sacking Rome in 410, and that his slaves diverted the Busento to bury him, his horse and Roman treasure beneath the waters; the tomb has never been identified. Norman and Hohenstaufen rulers strengthened the castle and cathedral, and Frederick II promoted the annual Maddalena fair while keeping the town under direct royal authority. Louis III of Anjou, heir to Naples, held court in the castle from 1432 and was buried in the cathedral after his death in 1434. In 1444, two years after Alfonso V of Aragon took Naples, Cosenza was an autonomous Catholic town set among grain fields, pastures and vineyards such as Donnici.

Spanish troops under Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba occupied Cosenza in 1500, and the town later became a governor's seat for Calabria Citeriore. Its strongest claim to fame was intellectual: Aulo Giano Parrasio founded an academy in 1511, and Bernardino Telesio later used it to argue that natural knowledge should rest on observation rather than inherited authority. The circle became the Accademia Cosentina and gave Cosenza the name 'Athens of Calabria'. War and geology struck harder than princes did. The earthquakes of 27-28 March 1638 destroyed more than a hundred villages in the upper Crati, Savuto and neighbouring valleys, with an estimated ten to thirty thousand dead. Cosenza supported the Parthenopean Republic briefly in 1799 before Fabrizio Ruffo's Sanfedist forces restored Bourbon rule. French administrators after 1806 abolished feudal jurisdiction and made the town capital of northern Calabria, while royalist bands kept up resistance in the Sila highlands.
zh:
科森扎位于克拉蒂河谷，布森托河在此汇入克拉蒂河，南通北卡拉布里亚的道路也经过这里。古城孔森蒂亚是布鲁提人的主城，后来成为罗马通往雷吉乌姆大道上的驿站。两河合流处留下了本地最持久的传闻：史学家约达尼斯称，西哥特国王阿拉里克410年洗劫罗马后死在科森扎附近，奴隶们引开布森托河水，把他、他的战马和来自罗马的财宝葬在河床之下；墓穴始终没有被确认。诺曼和霍亨斯陶芬君主加固城堡与主教座堂，腓特烈二世推动一年一度的马达莱纳集市，同时把城市置于王室直接管辖下。那不勒斯继承人安茹的路易三世自1432年起在城堡中开府，1434年死后葬入主教座堂。1444年，也就是阿拉贡的阿方索五世取得那不勒斯两年后，科森扎是一座享有自治权的天主教城市，周围分布着粮田、牧场和多尼采等地的葡萄园。

1500年，贡萨洛·费尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦率西班牙军队占领科森扎，城市后来成为近卡拉布里亚的长官驻地。这里最出名的是学术：1511年，奥洛·贾诺·帕拉西奥创立学会，贝尔纳迪诺·特莱西奥后来借此主张，认识自然应依靠观察，而不是承袭权威。这个团体成为科森扎学会，也为科森扎赢得「卡拉布里亚的雅典」之称。诸侯的影响之外，战争和地质变动留下的痕迹更重。1638年3月27日至28日的地震摧毁上克拉蒂谷、萨武托谷及邻近山谷的一百多个村庄，估计有一万至三万人死亡。1799年，科森扎短暂支持帕尔瑟诺佩共和国，随后法布里齐奥·鲁福的圣信派军队恢复波旁统治。1806年后的法国行政当局废除封建司法，把科森扎设为北卡拉布里亚省城，保王派武装则在西拉高地继续抵抗。

en:
Capitanata is northern Apulia: the Ofanto river, the broad Tavoliere plain called the granary of Italy, and the Gargano ridge pushing into the Adriatic. Frederick II kept a palace and court at Foggia, where the scholar Michael Scot served him, and in 1250 he died at Castel Fiorentino on the edge of the plain. At Lucera he settled thousands of Muslims expelled from Sicily, and the town, Lucaera Saracenorum, remained the last Muslim city in Italy until 1300, when Charles II of Naples sacked it and sold some 10,000 of its people into slavery; the cathedral rose on the site of its main mosque. Higher on the Gargano, the grotto of Monte Sant'Angelo, where the archangel Michael was said to have appeared around 490, drew pilgrims and kings. In 1444 the province belonged to the Aragonese kings of Naples and lived by the transumanza: flocks from the Abruzzo mountains came down the tratturi to winter on the Tavoliere and to Foggia's sheep fairs, and livestock was its wealth.

In 1447 Alfonso V built a customs palace at Foggia to tax the drovers, and the sheep duty became one of the crown's steadiest revenues. War reached the plain on 28 April 1503, when Gonzalo Fernandez de Cordoba dug his arquebusiers in behind a ditch at Cerignola and shattered the French cavalry, killing the duke of Nemours; the fight is counted among the first in Europe decided by firearms. Earthquakes struck Foggia in 1456 and again in 1731, when about a third of the town was destroyed. The provincial administration settled at Lucera in 1579 and stayed there until 1806, when French-backed reforms abolished feudal jurisdiction, split Molise away and moved the provincial seat back to Foggia. Under Bourbon rule the former pastures of the Tavoliere were meanwhile turned over to grain.
zh:
卡皮塔纳塔位于普利亚北部，由奥凡托河、号称「意大利粮仓」的塔沃列雷大平原和伸入亚得里亚海的加加诺山脊组成。腓特烈二世在福贾建有宫殿和宫廷，学者迈克尔·斯科特曾在此侍奉，1250年他在平原边缘的菲奥伦蒂诺堡去世。他把数千名被逐出西西里的穆斯林安置在卢切拉，这座被称作「撒拉森人的卢切拉」的城市因而成为意大利最后的穆斯林地，直到1300年那不勒斯国王查理二世攻破城池，约万人被卖为奴，大教堂就建在主清真寺旧址上。加加诺山上的蒙特圣安杰洛岩洞，相传大天使米迦勒约在490年显现，历代吸引朝圣者和国王前来。1444年，此地归阿拉贡系那不勒斯国王所有，靠转场牧业为生：阿布鲁佐山区的羊群沿牧道南下，到塔沃列雷过冬、赶福贾的羊群市集，牲畜便是这里的财富。

1447年，阿方索五世在福贾修建海关宫向牧羊人征税，羊税成为王室最稳定的收入之一。1503年4月28日，战火打到平原上：贡萨洛·费尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦在切里尼奥拉让火枪手据壕据守，击溃法国骑兵，击毙法军主帅内穆尔公爵，这一战被视为欧洲最早由火器决定胜负的战役之一。福贾先后在1456年和1731年遭地震，后一次约三分之一城区被毁。省级机构1579年固定设在卢切拉，直到1806年法国支持下的改革废除封建司法权、把莫利塞分出，并将省治迁回福贾。此前在波旁王朝治下，塔沃列雷的牧场上已渐渐改种谷物。

en:
Cagliari commands Sardinia's southern shore, where a sheltered bay, the salt lagoons of Santa Gilla and the wheat fields of the Campidano meet. Phoenicians founded Caralis there, the seat of Rome's praetor and its chief naval station on the island; after the Saracen raids the people withdrew to Santa Igia, capital of the native Giudicato of Cagliari. In 1215 the Pisan Lamberto Visconti seized the hill above the harbour, and Pisan merchants raised the walled Castel di Castro, entered through the San Pancrazio tower (1305) and the Elephant tower (1307), both built by the Sardinian architect Giovanni Capula. In 1258 Pisa destroyed Santa Igia and sowed salt over the ruins. The town, called the key of the Mediterranean, held out against the Crown of Aragon until the war of 1323-1326: the Infante Alfonso built a rival fortress at Bonaria, his fleet defeated the Pisans in December 1325, and the Castello passed to him. It became the capital of the Kingdom of Sardinia and the seat of its viceroy, and from 1333 native Sardinians were barred from the Catalan Castello. In 1444 the harbour ships Campidano grain, Iglesiente silver and lagoon salt to Barcelona.

Under the Spanish Habsburgs the bastioned walls made Cagliari a stronghold of the western Mediterranean. The Elephant tower served as a prison, with severed heads hung over its gate; after Viceroy Camarassa was murdered in the city in 1668, the head of the implicated Marquis Cea was displayed there for years. A university opened in 1607. An Anglo-Dutch fleet ended Spanish rule in 1708, and after Austrian rule, a Spanish return under Cardinal Alberoni in 1717 and the Treaty of The Hague, the House of Savoy took the island on 20 February 1720. In 1793 the Cagliaritani beat off French revolutionary troops landed on the Poetto beach, and when their claims were refused they drove out the Piedmontese on 28 April 1794, a date later kept as Sardinia's national day. From 1798 to 1814 the Royal Palace housed the Savoyard court expelled from Turin, so that through the Napoleonic wars Cagliari was the kingdom's working capital. In 1821 it remained the viceregal capital of the Kingdom of Sardinia.
zh:
卡利亚里扼守撒丁岛南岸，避风海湾、圣吉拉咸水潟湖与坎皮达诺的粮田在此相接。腓尼基人在此建立卡拉利斯，罗马时代是岛上裁判官驻地和主要军港；萨拉森海盗袭扰后，居民退守本土卡利亚里吉乌帝卡提的都城圣伊贾。1215年，比萨人兰贝托·维斯孔蒂夺下港口上方的山丘，比萨商人筑起城墙环绕的卡斯泰尔迪卡斯特罗城，1305年的圣潘克拉齐奥塔和1307年的大象塔扼守着入口，两座塔都出自撒丁建筑师乔瓦尼·卡普拉之手。1258年比萨毁掉圣伊贾，在废墟上撒盐。这座被称为「地中海之钥」的城池抵抗阿拉贡直到1323至1326年的战争：阿方索王子在博纳里亚另筑要塞对峙，他的舰队1325年12月击败比萨舰队，城堡区随即易手。卡利亚里成为撒丁王国的都城和总督驻地，1333年起本地撒丁人被禁止进入卡塔兰人居住的城堡区。1444年，港中的船把坎皮达诺的小麦、伊格莱西安特的白银和潟湖盐运往巴塞罗那。

西班牙哈布斯堡时期，棱堡城墙使卡利亚里成为西地中海的坚固要塞。大象塔被当作监狱，首级悬在城门上示众；1668年总督卡马拉萨在城中遇刺后，卷入此案的切亚侯爵的头在塔上挂了好几年。大学于1607年开办。1708年，英荷联合舰队结束了西班牙的统治；经过奥地利统治、1717年枢机主教阿尔贝罗尼支持下的西班牙短暂收复和《海牙条约》，萨伏依王朝于1720年2月20日接管全岛。1793年，卡利亚里军民击退在波埃托海滩登陆的法国革命军；犒赏落空后，市民于1794年4月28日赶走皮埃蒙特人，这一天后来被定为撒丁岛的民族节日。1798至1814年，被逐出都灵的萨伏依宫廷避居在城里的王宫，拿破仑战争期间卡利亚里实际充当着王国的施政都城。1821年，这里仍是撒丁王国的总督都城。

en:
Urgell is the inland plain of western Catalonia around Tàrrega, crossed by the valleys of the Ondara, Sió and Corb. It was one of the chief Catalan counties from Frankish times, with its comital court at Balaguer from 1130. Tàrrega grew after Count Ramon Berenguer I took its castle in the eleventh century, at a crossing of roads where fairs, markets and goldsmiths made it a busy trading town. The Black Death emptied the place, and on 26 July 1348 about 800 Jews were killed there. The county ended over a succession quarrel. When Martin I of Aragon died without an heir, Count James II claimed the crown, rejected Ferdinand of Antequera elected at Caspe in 1412, and took up arms. He surrendered at Balaguer on 31 October 1413, spent twenty years in prison and died at Xàtiva in 1433, remembered in Catalan as James the Unlucky; his county passed to the Crown of Aragon. In 1444 Tàrrega was a Catholic, Catalan-speaking market town one generation after the annexation.

The Catalan Civil War of 1462-1472 split the surrounding countryside, setting John II and the Remença peasants against the Catalan institutions. The peasants' dues dispute ended only when Ferdinand II issued the Sentencia de Guadalupe on 21 April 1486, allowing redemption from the mals usos in return for payments. From the sixteenth century Tàrrega settled into a quieter rural life under wealthy local families. After the War of the Spanish Succession, Philip V rewarded Cervera, east of Tàrrega, for taking the Bourbon side. In 1717 he founded a royal and pontifical university there, while the six other universities of the Principality were closed and their faculties transferred to Cervera; its great Baroque building went up between 1718 and 1740. The Napoleonic wars reached the district's roads in October 1811, as Spanish and French columns skirmished around Cervera, Tàrrega and Bellpuig; on 14 October the Spaniards took 178 prisoners near Bellpuig.
zh:
乌尔赫尔是加泰罗尼亚西部以塔雷加为中心的内陆平原，翁达拉河、西奥河和科尔布河的谷地穿行其间。自法兰克时代起，它就是加泰罗尼亚首要伯国之一，1130年起伯爵宫廷设在巴拉格尔。11世纪拉蒙·贝伦格尔一世夺取塔雷加城堡后，城镇在一处道路口发展起来，集市、市场和金银匠把它做成繁忙的商业镇。黑死病使这里人口流散，1348年7月26日又有约800名犹太人在镇上遇害。伯国的终结源于一场继承之争。阿拉贡的马丁一世无嗣而终，伯爵海梅二世要求继承王位，拒不接受1412年卡斯佩会议选出的安特克拉的斐迪南，举兵相向。1413年10月31日他在巴拉格尔投降，随后被囚二十年，1433年死于哈蒂瓦，加泰罗尼亚人称他「不幸者海梅」，伯国并入阿拉贡王室。1444年的塔雷加是一座讲加泰罗尼亚语的天主教集镇，被吞并才过去一代人。

1462年至1472年的加泰罗尼亚内战分裂了周边乡野，胡安二世与雷门萨农民同加泰罗尼亚政权机构兵戎相见。农民的负担之争直到1486年4月21日斐迪南二世颁布《瓜达卢佩仲裁判决》才了结，农民支付赎金即可摆脱「恶习」。16世纪以后，塔雷加在本地富户支配下过上更安静的乡间生活。西班牙王位继承战争后，腓力五世奖赏站在波旁一边、位于塔雷加以东的塞尔韦拉。1717年，他在那里设立皇家与宗座大学，同时关闭亲王国原有的另外六所大学，把院系迁往塞尔韦拉；宏大的巴洛克式校舍建于1718年至1740年。1811年10月，拿破仑战争打到这一带的道路，西班牙与法国部队在塞尔韦拉、塔雷加和贝尔普奇之间接战，10月14日西军在贝尔普奇附近俘虏法军178人。

en:
Tarragona stands on a coastal hill beside the Francolí, amid the vineyards of the Camp de Tarragona. As Roman Tarraco it was the Scipio brothers' main base against Carthage and later capital of Hispania Tarraconensis; the geographer Mela called it the richest town on the coast. Its wine went to Rome, Augustus wintered there after his Cantabrian campaign, and the Pont del Diable, a Roman aqueduct, carried the city's water. It had shrunk to a frontier settlement when the counts of Barcelona took it in 1117. The archiepiscopal see was restored in 1118, and from 1129 to 1173 a Norman-led principality organised its resettlement before full incorporation into the Crown of Aragon; the archbishop remained Catalonia's leading churchman, while the Camp's vines and the harbour kept the city alive. In 1444 Tarragona was a Catholic, Catalan-speaking Aragonese port and primatial see, its Roman amphitheatre and circus standing among the medieval houses.

The walls were tested in every Catalan war. During the Catalan Civil War the town council joined the Generalitat and repaired the walls while Archbishop Pere Ximénez de Urrea supported John II. John besieged Tarragona from 17 October 1462, and after relief by sea failed Damià de Montserrat's garrison capitulated on 31 October, with the royal army kept outside the town. Catalan and French forces blockaded the royalist port in 1641 and attacked again in 1644, taking it neither time. Allied armies captured it in 1705 during the War of the Spanish Succession and held it until the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713; after Barcelona fell, Philip V's Nueva Planta decrees of 1716 abolished Catalonia's old institutions. In the Peninsular War Louis-Gabriel Suchet's French army besieged the port from 4 May to 28 June 1811 and stormed the upper town, despite Juan de Contreras's defence and a British squadron under Edward Codrington that cannonaded the besiegers and ran reinforcements in by sea. A second allied siege failed in June 1813, and the French withdrew from Tarragona later that year.
zh:
塔拉戈纳坐落在弗兰科利河旁的滨海高岗，四围是塔拉戈纳原野的葡萄园。罗马时代的塔拉科曾是西庇阿兄弟对抗迦太基的主要据点，后来成为塔拉科西班牙行省的首府，地理学家梅拉称它是沿海最富庶的城镇。这里的酒运往罗马，奥古斯都在坎塔布里亚战役后到此过冬，罗马人修的水道桥「魔鬼桥」为城市输水。1117年巴塞罗那伯爵攻取这里时，它已衰为边境据点。总主教区于1118年恢复，1129年至1173年，一个由诺曼人主导的亲王国主持重新垦殖，其后该地完全并入阿拉贡联合王国；总主教仍是加泰罗尼亚地位最高的神职人员，原野上的葡萄园和港口维持着城市生计。1444年的塔拉戈纳是阿拉贡治下一座讲加泰罗尼亚语的天主教港口和首席主教驻地，罗马时代的圆形剧场和竞技场就立在中世纪屋舍之间。

此后每一场加泰罗尼亚的战争都要考验塔拉戈纳的城墙。加泰罗尼亚内战时，市政会加入总议会一边修补城墙，总主教佩罗·希门尼斯·德·乌雷亚则支持胡安二世。1462年10月17日胡安二世围城，海上援军失败后，达米亚·德·蒙特塞拉特所部于10月31日投降，条件是国王的军队不得入城。1641年加泰罗尼亚与法国军队封锁这座保王港口，1644年再度进攻，两次都没有攻下。西班牙王位继承战争中，同盟国军队1705年攻占塔拉戈纳，据守至1713年《乌得勒支条约》；巴塞罗那陷落后，腓力五世1716年颁布《新基本法令》，废除加泰罗尼亚旧有制度。半岛战争期间，路易-加布里埃尔·絮歇的法军从1811年5月4日围城至6月28日，尽管胡安·德·孔特雷拉斯坚守、爱德华·科德林顿的英国舰队一边炮击围城军一边从海上运入援军，上城仍被强攻拿下。1813年6月同盟国第二次围城失败，法军在同年稍后撤出塔拉戈纳。

en:
Rioja occupies the upper Ebro valley, where the kingdoms of Castile, Navarre and Aragon met along the Way of Saint James. Its chief town, Logroño, stands at the Ebro ford that gave it its name; after Alfonso VI granted the town its fuero in 1095, the pilgrim bridge made it a busy stage on the road to Compostela. The valley changed hands more than once, and after the townspeople held out against John II of Aragon, John II of Castile made Logroño a city in 1431 and added the titles 'very noble and very loyal' in July 1444. By then Rioja Alta was wine country: monasteries and pilgrim hospitals had planted vines for centuries, wine went to other regions from the late 1200s, and the upper valley made wine its specialty. Inland, the twin monasteries of San Millan de la Cogolla kept some of the earliest words written in a Romance vernacular and in Basque, and the first named Spanish poet, Gonzalo de Berceo, was a cleric there in the thirteenth century. On the pilgrim road, the cathedral of Santo Domingo de la Calzada keeps a live white rooster and hen, recalling the story of a hanged pilgrim whom the saint saved while the magistrate's roasted birds began to crow.

In 1521, during the Franco-Navarrese invasion, Andre de Foix besieged Logroño for a week and broke off on 11 June, the feast of St Barnabas, still kept as the city's festival; Charles V added three fleurs-de-lis to its arms in 1523. In January 1609 the Spanish Inquisition opened the Basque witch trials here: around 7,000 people were investigated, and six were burned at the auto-da-fe on 1 November 1610, before the inquisitor Alonso de Salazar Frias found no proof of witchcraft and the remaining cases were quashed in 1614. Wine kept its hold on the valley: growers adopted a quality symbol in 1560, the town banned carts from passing beside the cellars in 1635, quality rules were set down in 1650, and the Royal Society of Rioja Growers met in 1790 with delegates from fifty-two towns to press for better roads to market.
zh:
里奥哈占据埃布罗河上游谷地，卡斯蒂利亚、纳瓦拉和阿拉贡三个王国的势力在这里相接，圣雅各之路也穿过谷中。首府洛格罗尼奥坐落在埃布罗河的渡口上，地名据说便来自意为「渡口」的凯尔特语词；1095年阿方索六世向它颁发特许状，河上的朝圣桥使它成为前往孔波斯特拉路上的繁忙一站。谷地在邻邦诸王之间几度易手，洛格罗尼奥市民顶住阿拉贡国王胡安二世的进攻后，卡斯蒂利亚国王胡安二世于1431年升它为城市，又在1444年7月加上「极高贵、极忠诚」的称号。这时的里奥哈上区已是葡萄酒之乡：修道院和朝圣客栈种了几百年葡萄，13世纪末起葡萄酒便销往外地，上游谷地也以酿酒为业。内地圣米良-德拉科戈利亚的苏索、尤索两座修道院，保存着用罗曼语方言和巴斯克语写下的最早一批词句；有姓名可考的第一位卡斯蒂利亚语诗人贡萨洛·德·贝尔塞奥，13世纪就在苏索当修士。圣雅各路旁的圣多明各-德拉卡尔萨达大教堂养着一只白公鸡和一只白母鸡，纪念圣人救活被绞死的朝圣者、法官盘中烤鸡当场啼鸣的传说。

1521年法国—纳瓦拉联军入侵时，安德烈·德·富瓦围攻洛格罗尼奥一周，于6月11日圣巴纳伯节撤围，这个日子后来成为洛格罗尼奥的城庆；1523年，查理五世在城徽上加了三朵鸢尾花饰。1609年1月，西班牙宗教裁判所在这里开庭，兴起巴斯克女巫审判：苏加拉穆尔迪一案前后追查约七千人，1610年11月1日的火刑宣判中有六人被烧死，受命复查的裁判官阿隆索·德·萨拉查·弗里亚斯找不到巫术实据，其余案件于1614年全部撤销。葡萄酒始终是谷地的主业：1560年酿酒者选定品质标记，1635年市政当局禁止马车在酒窖旁通行，1650年订立成文的品质规矩，1790年里奥哈葡萄种植者皇家学会集合五十二个城镇的代表开会，争取修路通商。

en:
Teruel stands high on Aragon's southern frontier, 915 metres above the sea, guarding the road that drops toward Valencia. Alfonso II of Aragon captured the Muslim outpost of Tirwal and on 1 October 1171 founded the town, granting fueros to draw settlers to the exposed border. Its coat of arms recalls the foundation story: settlers looking for omens found a bull lowing on a height with a star shining above it, and a bull and a star figure on the town's arms. The citizens served in the conquest of Valencia and in the wars of the Union, and Peter IV raised Teruel to the rank of city in 1347 for its service against the rebel towns. Jewish weavers and a large Mudéjar population shaped its markets, while the ore of the Sierra Menera had been worked since the days of al-Andalus. Brick Mudéjar towers rose above the roofs: Santa María de Mediavilla took its tower in 1257 and was rebuilt with three Mudéjar naves by the Muslim master builder Juzaff, until the Aragonese antipope Benedict XIII raised it to a collegiate church in 1423. In 1444 Teruel was a Catholic royal town whose craftsmen sold wool cloth and green-glazed pottery.

A romance of 1217, the Lovers of Teruel, carried the town's name through Spain: two young lovers died for love, and the citizens had them buried side by side in San Pedro; in 1560 their mummies were moved to the carved tombs where they now rest, and Juan Pérez de Montalbán's play spread the story in print in 1635. The old frontier fueros, printed in 1531, clashed increasingly with royal law after Philip II's reforms of 1565, and after the 1591 disturbances in Zaragoza they were abolished in 1598. Martín de Montalbán raised the cathedral's octagonal lantern in 1538, and the collegiate church became Teruel Cathedral with the new diocese in 1587. The expulsion of the Moriscos in 1610 struck the town directly, when hundreds left Teruel and nearby Bezas for the coast and took much of the old tile-making craft with them. In the War of the Spanish Succession Aragon sided with Archduke Charles; defeat at Almansa brought the Nueva Planta decrees of 1707 and an end to its autonomous courts.
zh:
特鲁埃尔位于阿拉贡南部高地边疆，海拔915米，扼守通往瓦伦西亚的下坡路。阿拉贡国王阿方索二世攻占穆斯林前哨蒂尔瓦尔后，于1171年10月1日建立此城，授予特许状以吸引人到空旷的边境定居。城徽来自建城的传说：迁徙者寻找征兆时，看见一头公牛在高处鸣叫，上方有一颗明星闪耀；城徽上的公牛与星便来自这个故事。居民先后参加征服瓦伦西亚和联盟战争，佩德罗四世因他们讨伐叛城有功，于1347年将特鲁埃尔升为城市。犹太织工和人数众多的穆德哈尔人塑造了本地市场，梅内拉山脉的铁矿自安达卢斯时代便已开采。砖造穆德哈尔高塔高出全城屋顶：圣马利亚·德·梅迪亚维亚教堂1257年建成高塔，穆斯林工匠大师胡萨夫又把它改建成三座穆德哈尔式中殿，阿拉贡籍的对立教宗本笃十三世于1423年将其升为协同教堂。1444年的特鲁埃尔是一座天主教王家城镇，工匠以毛呢和绿釉陶器为业。

1217年的一段恋情把特鲁埃尔的名字传遍西班牙，即「特鲁埃尔恋人」：一对年轻恋人相继殉情，市民将他们并排葬在圣佩德罗教堂；1560年，两人的干尸被移入雕刻精美的合葬棺墓，胡安·佩雷斯·德·蒙塔尔万的剧本又在1635年把故事印行传开。古老的边境特许状于1531年印行，腓力二世1565年改革后与王法冲突日深，1591年萨拉戈萨骚乱后于1598年被废止。1538年，马丁·德·蒙塔尔万为教堂增建八角采光塔，1587年新教区设立，协同教堂成为特鲁埃尔主教座堂。1610年驱逐莫里斯科人直接打击了这座城，数百人从特鲁埃尔和邻近的贝萨斯前往海岸，古老的瓷砖手艺也随他们大损。西班牙王位继承战争中，阿拉贡支持查理大公；阿尔曼萨战败后，1707年的《新基本法令》废除了其自治法院。

en:
Forcalquier holds a hill between the Lure and Luberon ranges in Haute-Provence, west of the Durance. One reading of its name is 'lime kiln', and a castle crowned the butte above the settlement by the eleventh century; in 1060 the exiled bishop of Sisteron made its church a concathedral. In the twelfth century the town was the capital of its own county, whose lords held Sisteron, Gap, Embrun, Manosque and Apt and took the title of counts of Forcalquier. The county ended in a marriage. In 1209 Garsende of Sabran, heiress of Forcalquier, wed Alfonso II of Provence; she later ruled Provence as regent for her son, patronised the troubadours and wrote verse of her own as the trobairitz Garsenda de Proensa. Local tradition has it that her son's four daughters were raised at the castle of Saint-Maime in the county and married the kings of France and England, the King of the Romans and the king of Naples. The union did not end civic freedoms. A charter of 1206 traded tax privileges for militia service, and the charter of 1385 gave the town a very wide measure of self-rule. In 1444 Forcalquier was an Occitan-speaking Catholic town of Provence held by René of Anjou, its Romanesque Cordeliers convent and the castle above its streets.

When Louis XI claimed Provence in 1481 Forcalquier resisted his army for three weeks before it was stormed and sacked on 21 July. The town bought off its last feudal dues in 1521. Protestant teaching arrived early. By 1559 a Protestant consul sat in the town; Huguenot troops took it on 12 June 1562 and gutted the cathedral and the Cordeliers' church, and Catholic soldiers retaliated against the townspeople. The Peace of Saint-Germain-en-Laye in 1570 named Forcalquier, with Mérindol, one of two Protestant surety places in Provence, which made it a target, besieged in 1576, 1580 and 1585 and invested by the dukes of Épernon and La Valette in 1587 and 1588. The town rallied to Henry IV in 1589, and the old castle was razed on his order in 1601. Plague killed some 2,000 inhabitants in 1630. The cathedral was sacked again under the Terror in 1794, the Consulate made Forcalquier a subprefecture, and the last ramparts were taken down between 1806 and 1813.
zh:
福卡勒基耶（通行译名福卡尔基耶）地处上普罗旺斯迪朗斯河以西，坐落在吕尔山与吕贝龙山之间的山丘上。地名的一种解释是「石灰窑」，到11世纪一座城堡已立在聚落上方的山岗；1060年，流亡的锡斯特龙主教把城中教堂升为共主教座堂。12世纪时，这座城市是独立的福卡勒基耶伯国的都城，伯爵们领有锡斯特龙、加普、昂布兰、马诺斯克和阿普特，自称福卡勒基耶伯爵。伯国终结于一场婚姻。1209年，福卡勒基耶女继承人萨布朗的加尔桑德嫁给普罗旺斯的阿方索二世；她后来为儿子摄政，统治普罗旺斯，资助行吟诗人，自己也以女诗人「普罗旺斯的加尔桑达」之名写诗。当地相传，她儿子的四个女儿在伯国境内的圣迈姆堡长大，后来分别嫁给法兰西国王、英格兰国王、罗马人的国王和那不勒斯国王。合邦之后，城市的自由并未终结。1206年的特许状以免服民团换取免税特权，1385年的特许状又给了城市相当大的自治权。1444年的福卡勒基耶是安茹的勒内治下一座讲奥克语的天主教城镇，罗马式的科德利埃修道院和山岗上的城堡俯瞰着街道。

1481年路易十一取得普罗旺斯时，福卡勒基耶抵抗法军三周，7月21日城破后遭洗劫。1521年，城市赎买了最后的封建赋税。新教思想很早就传到这里。1559年已有新教徒出任执政官；1562年6月12日胡格诺派军队攻占城市，捣毁主教座堂和科德利埃教堂，天主教军队随后报复城中居民。1570年《圣日耳曼昂莱和约》把福卡勒基耶与梅朗多勒列为普罗旺斯的两个新教担保地，这也使它成为围攻的目标，1576年、1580年和1585年三度被围，1587年和1588年埃佩尔农公爵与拉瓦莱特公爵又先后来攻。1589年城市归顺亨利四世，旧城堡奉他的命令于1601年拆毁。1630年瘟疫夺去约两千人的生命。1794年恐怖统治时期主教座堂再遭洗劫，执政府时期福卡勒基耶成为副省会，最后的城墙在1806年至1813年间拆除。

en:
Albenga lies on the western Italian Riviera, where the Alps drop to a narrow coastal plain and the Centa river runs into the Gulf of Genoa. Its Roman name was Albingaunum, and it had been the capital of the Ingauni, Ligurian sailor-traders whose coast stretched from Finale to Sanremo; during the Second Punic War Hannibal's brother Mago used the town as a naval base and sailed from it to sack Genoa in 205 BC. Rome broke their sea power twenty-four years later, and in 13 BC the Via Julia Augusta linked the town with Gaul and Spain. The fifth-century baptistery stands in the old centre beside the paired towers of the commune and the cathedral of San Michele, raised against one another in the rivalry of town and church; noble families built so many towers that Albenga was called the city of a hundred spires. A free commune from 1098, it sent its own ships to the First Crusade and long rivalled Genoa, until a convention of 1251 forced it under Genoese rule, and Visconti and French lordships came and went before it returned to Genoa. In 1444 Albenga was Genoa's chief city on the western Riviera, its Centa-mouth harbour shipping the timber and wool of the Ligurian hinterland.

The Italian Wars made the Centa plain an army road, and Saracen raids kept the walls in repair. In 1552 Andrea Doria anchored offshore with forty-eight galleys, and when the Centa flooded in 1564 and swept away houses and ramparts, Bishop Luca Fieschi spent his fortune on the rebuilding. The town changed hands repeatedly in the wars of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and in July 1746 its militia defeated a Piedmontese force at nearby Zuccarello and captured its commander the Marchese Del Carretto. French troops entered on 4 April 1794; three days later Napoleon Bonaparte, new to the command of the Army of Italy, met Masséna here and planned the campaign from the Palazzo Rolandi-Ricci. Under the Ligurian Republic Albenga became capital of the Centa jurisdiction; after the Congress of Vienna assigned it to the Kingdom of Sardinia, it became a provincial capital in 1818.
zh:
阿尔本加位于利古里亚西海岸，阿尔卑斯山在这一带逼近海面，只留下一片狭窄平原，琴塔河在此注入热那亚湾。罗马时代它称阿尔宾高努姆，曾是因高尼人的首府；这些利古里亚人以航海贸易为生，海岸领地从菲纳莱延伸到圣雷莫。第二次布匿战争中，汉尼拔的弟弟马戈以这里为海军基地，公元前205年从这里出发洗劫了热那亚；二十四年后罗马击溃他们的海上力量，公元前13年修成的尤利亚·奥古斯塔大道把城镇与高卢、西班牙连在一起。老城中心立着5世纪的洗礼堂，旁边是公社塔楼与圣米凯莱主教座堂的塔楼，两塔并立，对应市民与教会的争衡；贵族家族争相修塔，阿尔本加因而有「百塔之城」的别称。1098年它成为自由公社，自备船只参加第一次十字军东征，长期与热那亚争雄，1251年的协约迫使它接受热那亚统治，此后维斯孔蒂家族与法国人相继入主，才重归热那亚。1444年，它是热那亚在利古里亚西海岸的首要城市，琴塔河口的港口运出利古里亚内陆的木材和羊毛。

意大利战争把琴塔平原变成大军往来的通道，撒拉森海盗的袭掠则让城墙一再修缮。1552年，安德烈亚·多里亚率四十八艘桨帆船停泊在外海；1564年琴塔河洪水冲走房屋和城墙，主教卢卡·菲耶斯基倾尽家产主持重建。17、18世纪的战争中该城几度易手，1746年7月，城中民兵在附近的祖卡雷洛击败一支皮埃蒙特军队，生俘指挥官德尔卡雷托侯爵。1794年4月4日法军入城，三天后新任意大利军团司令拿破仑·波拿巴在此与马塞纳会面，在罗兰迪-里奇宫中筹划战役。利古里亚共和国时期，阿尔本加成为琴塔辖区首府；维也纳和会把它划归撒丁王国后，它于1818年成为省府。

en:
The Uckermark is the fertile lakeland of the Uecker and the Ucker lakes, named after the Slavic Ukrani, whose gords at Drense and by the later Prenzlau guarded the routes through it. Pomeranian dukes opened the country to Christian missions and Low German settlers, and their trading place at Prenzlau was described in 1188 as a fortified settlement with a market, an inn and one of Pomerania's three mints; Duke Barnim I gave it German town law in 1234. The town stood on the busy Magdeburg-Stettin road, and Wolfram von Eschenbach names 'Ukerlant' and its 'Ukersee' in Parzival. By 1250 Prenzlau had walls, four parish churches and a monastery, and ranked with Berlin, Stendal and Frankfurt an der Oder among the largest towns of the March. The Treaty of Landin handed the whole Uckerland to Brandenburg in that same year, and after two centuries of war with Pomerania and Mecklenburg, Prenzlau returned to Hohenzollern rule in 1426 and the Peace of Wittstock secured the region for the elector in 1442. In 1444 it was a still-Catholic Brandenburg frontier province of rich farms and long-distance trade.

The Thirty Years' War reached it in 1626 and plague in 1630. When Gustavus Adolphus fell at Lützen, his body was carried north and lay for three days that December in Prenzlau's St Mary's, the first brick hall church built east of the Elbe. At the peace nearly two in five of the region's 222 villages lay destroyed or empty. In 1701 Dorothee Elisabeth Tretschlaff was executed there, the last person put to death for witchcraft in Brandenburg. Dutch settlers and a French Huguenot community founded in Prenzlau in 1687 brought new crafts, the Finow Canal, opened in the south in 1746, carried the region's timber and grain, and the Uckermark became the granary of Berlin.
