In 1444 the lake fisheries and the dry plains around them belonged to older fishing and herding peoples, while from the north a Nilotic section of the Ateker confederation was moving into the basin with its zebu herds. These newcomers, the Turkana, were already at war with the kinsmen they had split from, and would prove the stronger.

Over the following generations the Turkana pushed southwards, defeating the peoples they met with better tactics, weapons and organization and taking the young of conquered groups into their own ranks; by the 1600s they and their allies held the whole basin. Wealth was counted in the grey zebu bulls from which the Turkana take their proud name for themselves, and power was guided by the diviners, the ngimurok. On the margins of their hard country they fought sporadic actions against Arab, Swahili and Abyssinian slave-raiders and ivory traders. Thus in 1821 the Turkana remained the unchallenged masters of the lake and its plains, in a land no European had yet seen.
zh:
图尔卡纳是骄阳炙烤的盆地，旁倚一汪碧绿色的大湖——当地人称之为阿纳姆·卡阿拉科尔，意为「多鱼之海」。这是东非大裂谷中一座没有出口的碱性内流湖，湖水靠北方奥莫河从埃塞俄比亚高地、南方特克韦尔河与凯里奥河补给，只能借蒸发排去水量；湖岸散布着黑色火山岩与沙丘，中央岛上的火山口还吐着蒸汽。1444年时，湖上的渔场和周围干旱平原的主人还是更早的渔猎与游牧部族，而一支属于阿特克尔联盟的尼罗特人正赶着瘤牛群从北方进入盆地。这些新来者就是图尔卡纳人，他们已与分裂出去的同族交战，并将成为胜者。

此后几代人之间，图尔卡纳人凭更出色的战术、武器和编组向南推进，击败所到之处的各部，又把被征服者中的年轻人纳入自己的队伍；到17世纪，他们和盟友已据有整个盆地。财富以灰色的瘤牛公牛来衡量，图尔卡纳人也以「灰牛之民」自居；权柄则听命于占卜师恩吉姆罗克。在这片严酷土地的边缘，他们不时与阿拉伯、斯瓦希里和阿比西尼亚的捕奴者、象牙商人交战。到1821年，图尔卡纳人仍是湖泊与平原无可争议的主人，他们的土地也仍未有欧洲人踏足。

en: Kuria land is the rolling grass country east of Lake Victoria, from the Migori river in the east to the Mara river and its estuary in the west, where modern Kenya and Tanzania meet. By 1444 its Bantu people, the AbaKuria, grazed cattle on the plains and tilled the wetter valleys in many independent clans, speaking a tongue close to that of their kinsmen the Gusii highlanders; between them and the lake ran a narrow Luo corridor, and their other neighbours were the Suba and Ikoma, while the grasslands far to the south-east belonged to Maa-speaking herdsmen. Cattle were the measure of all wealth, paid over as bride-price and slain in the sacrifices of the old religion, and young men were bound into warrior age-sets to guard the herds.
zh: 库里亚之地是维多利亚湖以东起伏的草原，东起米戈里河，西抵马拉河及其河口，正落在今日肯尼亚与坦桑尼亚相接之处。到1444年，住在这里的阿巴库里亚人是一支班图人，在平原牧牛、在较湿润的谷地耕作，分成众多互不统属的氏族，讲与近亲古西山地人相近的语言；他们与大湖之间隔着一条卢奥人的走廊，其他邻人是苏巴人和伊科马人，东南远方的草原则属于讲马阿语的牧人。牛是衡量一切财富的尺度，既用作聘礼，也在传统信仰的祭祀中宰杀；年轻男子按年龄结为武士团守护牛群。

en:
The Shamba of the Usambara Mountains call their wet highland home Shambaai, 'where bananas thrive', in contrast to the dry nyika plains below. By 1444 Shambaa clans lived in separate hill villages, clearing forest and watering banana groves through irrigation channels. They exchanged local iron tools, salt from the plains and shell ornaments reaching them from the coast. Elders settled disputes and marriage alliances linked neighbouring hills, but no single ruler governed the whole range.

Maasai raids and the arrival of refugee pastoralists in the early eighteenth century made common defence more urgent. In the first half of that century Mbegha, a hunter from the Ngulu hills, helped Vugha against dangerous game, married into leading clans, and bound the mountain villages into the Kilindi dynasty through kinship and diplomacy. His grandson Kinyashi Muanga Ike strengthened its military authority. Around 1815 Kimweri ye Nyumbai became ruler at Vugha, and in 1821 the mountain kingdom remained a growing power whose influence was reaching toward the Pangani valley and the coastal towns.
zh:
乌桑巴拉山区的珊巴人把湿润高地称为尚巴伊，意思是「香蕉繁盛之地」，与山下干旱的尼伊卡平原相对。1444年时，珊巴各氏族分居在不同山村，开垦森林，用灌溉渠滋养香蕉林。他们以本地铁器、平原出产的盐和来自海岸的贝饰互通有无。争端由长者调解，婚姻联盟把相邻山丘联系起来，但整个山区还没有统一的统治者。

18世纪初，马赛人的袭扰和避难牧人的到来使共同防御变得迫切。18世纪上半叶，来自恩古鲁山地的猎人姆贝加帮助武加除去危害人畜的野兽，又与主要氏族联姻，凭借亲属关系和外交把各山村纳入基林迪王朝。他的孙子基尼亚希·穆安加·伊凯强化了王朝的军事权威。约1815年，金韦里·耶·尼乌姆巴伊在武加继位；1821年时，这个山地王国仍在扩张，势力正向潘加尼河谷和沿海城镇延伸。

en: Gogo is the dry Ugogo plateau, the uncertain-rain country between the coastal hinterland and Tanzania's western plateau. In 1444 scattered Bantu-speaking homesteads combined cultivation and hunting with cattle keeping where pasture and waterholes permitted, their affairs resting with local elders and headmen. The road from Bagamoyo to Tabora later crossed this country. After the long-distance ivory trade expanded in the early nineteenth century, Nyamwezi caravans passed through Ugogo toward the coast. By 1821 Gogo communities stood on one of East Africa's rising inland routes, where provisions, cattle and local permission to pass had become matters no caravan could ignore.
zh: 戈戈地处干旱的乌戈戈高原，雨量无常，夹在沿海腹地与坦桑尼亚西部高原之间。1444年时，说班图语的居民以分散家户生活，在牧场和水坑允许的地方兼营农耕、狩猎与养牛，事务由当地长者和头人主持。后来，从巴加莫约通往塔波拉的道路穿过这片土地。19世纪初长途象牙贸易扩大后，尼亚姆韦齐商队经乌戈戈前往海岸。到1821年，戈戈诸社群已位于东非一条正在兴起的内陆商路上，商队不能不考虑这里的补给、牛群和通行许可。

en: Nyatura is the Singida plateau country of the Arimi, whose name means farmers and whose Bantu speech is Kinyaturu. In 1444 Airwana, Vahi and Anyinganyi clans farmed the plateau, kept cattle where pasture allowed, and managed their affairs through village and lineage elders rather than a single king. Kinyaturu's Cushitic influence and the people's joking partnerships with the Nyiramba and Iraqw show long contact between farmers and pastoral neighbours.
zh: 尼亚图拉是阿里米人的辛吉达高原之乡；「阿里米」意为农人，他们的班图语称基尼亚图鲁语。1444年时，艾尔瓦纳、瓦希和安宁加尼等氏族在高原耕作，在牧场允许的地方养牛，由村落和世系长者而不是单一国王处理事务。基尼亚图鲁语中的库希特语影响，以及他们与尼伊拉姆巴人、伊拉库人的戏谑伙伴关系，显示农耕者与邻近牧人早有长期往来。

en:
Zigua is the hinterland country of the Zigua people, lying behind the Swahili coast between the Pangani and Ruvu rivers. By 1444 its Bantu-speaking farming clans lived in palisaded villages and, on the Ruvu, in island settlements reached by light bridges. Their matriclans held the land, while elders settled disputes through gifts and bloodwealth. Near the shore, Kaole and the small markets around Bagamoyo and Pangani linked hinterland produce with Indian Ocean exchange, but no Zigua king ruled all the villages.

For centuries authority remained local, measured by a leader's raids, gifts and ability to protect his people. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries Bagamoyo grew from a small fishing and farming market into a caravan stopping place, and Muslim families settling there in the late eighteenth century traded salt and taxed traffic with the hinterland. Maasai and Baraguyu cattle raids intensified in the early nineteenth century, while Zigua leaders exchanged ivory, animals and slaves for coastal imports.
zh:
兹古阿是兹古阿人的腹地家园，位于斯瓦希里海岸后方、潘加尼河与鲁伏河之间。1444年时，说班图语的农耕氏族住在栅栏围护的村落里，鲁伏河上还有靠轻便木桥出入的岛上聚落。土地归母系氏族所有，长者通过赠礼和偿命财调解争端。近海的考莱以及巴加莫约、潘加尼周围的小市场把腹地物产带入印度洋交换，但没有一个兹古阿国王统治全部村落。

此后数百年间，权威仍限于地方，取决于首领能否组织袭掠、分配礼物并保护部众。17至18世纪，巴加莫约从渔农小市场发展为商队停驻地；18世纪末定居当地的穆斯林家族经营食盐贸易，并对通往腹地的往来征税。19世纪初，马赛人和巴拉古尤人的夺牛袭扰加剧，兹古阿首领则以象牙、牲畜和奴隶交换海岸输入品。

en:
Shaga is an older name for the mountain country documented as Uchaga, Dschagga or Chagga on Kilimanjaro's southern slopes. Bantu farmers had been settling there since about the eleventh century, terracing wet ridges, watering banana groves with mountain channels and keeping cattle above the hot plains. In 1444 the land was still divided among autonomous clan villages and highland mitaa, rather than the later Umangi kingdoms. Families venerated ancestors and Ruwa, the sun deity whose shrines stood in the high forest, while food, pottery and iron linked the mountain with Taveta, Taita and Pare.

The small Chagga kingdoms hardened during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Late in the eighteenth century Mangi Horombo, called Orombo in English sources, ruled from Keni, raided east into Mwika and raised large stone-walled enclosures; his power overshadowed Vunjo even while Queen Mashina preserved the small but wealthy state of Mamba. Around the same time trade from the coast began to reach up the Pangani basin. After 1810 Rengua of Machame used an iron spear to overawe rival clans in the Kikafu valley and became the first Mangi of Machame; his killing of Kibosho initiates at Kimbushi opened a long feud. As rival rulers sought weapons after 1800, Pare, Taveta and Taita smiths supplied increasing quantities of iron, tying spears, cattle and caravan goods to mountain politics.
zh:
沙嘎（查加，Uchaga/Dschagga/Chagga）是乞力马扎罗山南坡山地之国的旧称。约从11世纪起，班图农民陆续在此定居，在湿润山脊修筑梯田，引山水浇灌香蕉林，并在炎热平原上方牧牛。1444年时，这里仍由自治的氏族村落和高地社区分治，尚未形成后来的「乌曼吉」诸王国。各户敬奉祖先与太阳神鲁瓦，高山森林中设有神龛；粮食、陶器和铁器则把山地与塔韦塔、泰塔、帕雷联系起来。

17至18世纪，查加人的小王国逐渐成形。18世纪末，凯尼的曼吉·霍龙博（又称奥龙博）据地称强，向东袭掠姆维卡，建起大型石墙围寨，权势压过温乔；女王玛希娜则保住了狭小而富庶的曼巴邦。大约同一时期，海岸贸易开始沿潘加尼河盆地深入山地。1810年后，马查姆的伦瓜凭借铁矛震慑基卡富河谷的敌对氏族，成为第一位马查姆曼吉；他在金布希杀害基博绍成年礼成员，开启了长期世仇。1800年以后，诸首领争相寻求武器，帕雷、塔韦塔和泰塔铁匠供应更多铁器，使长矛、牲畜与商队货物都卷入山地政治。

en:
The Kikuyu country is the cool, fertile highland between the snowy pyramid of Mount Kenya, which they call Kirinyaga, and the long wall of the Aberdares, reaching towards the Ngong hills and Ol Donyo Sabuk. Bantu farmers of the Thagicu branch reached the northern slopes of the mountain around the third century, and by the thirteenth century their descendants had formed a settled core at Murang'a, mingling with the older hunter-gatherers of the forests. By 1444 the Agĩkũyũ were a nation of nine clans without a king, ruled by councils of elders: they tilled millet and the njahi bean in valleys that gave two harvests a year, kept the rites of Ngai at the sacred fig trees with their faces turned to Kirinyaga, and named the years by initiation sets, companies of youths circumcised together who were formed into regiments and handed power to a new ruling generation roughly every thirty-five years.

The centuries that followed were an age of steady growth: by purchase, blood-brotherhood, intermarriage and adoption the Kikuyu drew forest hunter-gatherers into their clans and opened new ridges, and in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries a great southward movement carried them from Murang'a into the Kiambu country. With the Maasai of the southern and northern plains they both traded and fought, while Kamba caravans brought the goods of the dry country to their markets. Arab and Swahili slavers moving up from the coast touched only the southern edge of the nation and were killed if they pushed farther; the Kikuyu kept no slaves and answered to no outside power. In the early nineteenth century the ruling generation was the Ndemi, whose rule began around 1792, and the whole highland still lay in Kikuyu hands.
zh:
基库尤之地是凉爽肥沃的高地，夹在雪锥般的肯尼亚山——他们称之为基里尼亚加——与阿伯德尔山脉的长墙之间，一直延伸到恩贡丘陵和奥尔东约奥萨布克山。属塔吉库分支的班图农民约在3世纪抵达肯尼亚山北坡，到13世纪，他们的后裔已在穆兰卡形成定居核心，并与林中更古老的采集狩猎者融合。1444年时，阿基库尤是一个没有国王、由九大氏族组成的族群，靠长老议事会治理：他们在谷地种植粟和恩贾希豆，一年两熟；在神圣的榕树下祭祀天神恩盖，脸朝基里尼亚加；他们还以成年礼年龄组纪年——一同割礼的青年编成连队，约每三十五年把统治权移交给新一代。

此后几个世纪是稳步扩张的时代：基库尤人靠购买土地、结血盟、通婚和收养，把林中的采集狩猎者纳入自己的氏族，开辟出新的山脊；18至19世纪，一场大南迁把他们从穆兰卡带到基安布地方。对南北两线平原上的马赛人，他们既通商也交战；坎巴人的商队把干旱地区的货物带进他们的市集。从海岸北上的阿拉伯与斯瓦希里捕奴商队只能擦着族群的南缘行走，再深入便会被处死；基库尤人不蓄奴隶，也不服从任何外来强权。19世纪初，当政的是恩代米一代，这一统治世代约始于1792年，而整片高地仍完全掌握在基库尤人手中。

en: Buzinza is the land of the Zinza, a Bantu people of the south-western corner of Lake Victoria. They fish the lake, farm bananas and grain on the shore and the offshore islands, and graze cattle on the grasslands behind. Hereditary smith-clans smelted local iron in charcoal furnaces, forging hoes, spears and knives, and weaving supplied a second trade good; Zinza iron, dried fish and cloth went to the Haya chiefdoms to the north and into Karagwe to the west. Their language ties them most closely to peoples on the northern, Ugandan side of the lake.
zh: 布津扎是津扎人的土地。津扎人是生活在维多利亚湖西南角的班图人，在湖中捕鱼，在湖岸和近岸岛屿上种植香蕉与谷物，在岸后草原放牧。世袭的铁匠氏族用木炭炉冶炼当地铁矿，打造锄头、长矛和刀，纺织是另一项营生；津扎的铁器、鱼干和布匹销往北方的哈亚诸酋长国，也输入西边的卡拉圭。津扎语表明他们与湖北岸乌干达一侧的各族关系最近。

en:
Busoga is the green, water-girt country east of the Victoria Nile, with Lake Kyoga to the north, the Mpologoma to the east and the broad reach of Lake Victoria to the south; fishing villages such as Bukaleba lined its shore. Its Soga people farmed bananas and millet, herded cattle on the ridges and drew much of their living from the lakes, smoking fish for the inland trade. They had no single king: clan chiefs with their own totems ruled their separate hills and answered to no overlord, though Bunyoro beyond the Nile was honoured as the wellspring of royalty. In 1444 the chiefdoms were still wholly independent.

The 16th century brought new dynasties. Mukama Namutukula, a prince of Bunyoro's Bito house, crossed Lake Kyoga with his following, and his sons founded the northern chiefdoms: Bulamogi dated to about 1550 under Zibondo Lamogi, Bukono existed before 1656 and Bugabula was founded around 1730. Bito principalities thus stood beside older clan chiefdoms. In the 17th and 18th centuries the rising kabakas of Buganda, Kimbugwe, Katerega and Mutebi, conquered stretches of Busoga, and the chiefs of the southern shore became Ganda clients. Rival Soga factions called in Bunyoro or Buganda by turns, paying cattle, goats and sometimes slaves to the stronger court, where succession disputes were arbitrated; in 1821 the chiefdoms still had no common ruler.
zh:
布索加是一片被水环绕的青翠之地，位于维多利亚尼罗河以东：北临基奥加湖，东界姆波洛戈马河，南接浩瀚的维多利亚湖，湖畔分布着布卡莱巴这样的渔村。索加人种植香蕉和黍子，在山脊放牧，生计很大程度上仰仗湖泊，把鱼熏干后输往内陆。他们没有共主：各有图腾的氏族酋长统治各自的丘陵，不奉任何宗主，只把尼罗河对岸的布尼奥罗奉为王权之源。1444年时，这些酋邦仍然完全独立。

16世纪，新的王朝到来。布尼奥罗比托王室的王子姆卡马·纳穆图库拉率部众渡过基奥加湖，他的子孙在北方建立了多个酋邦：齐邦多·拉莫吉约在1550年建立布拉莫吉，布科诺在1656年以前已经存在，布加布拉则建于1730年前后，比托系公国与更古老的氏族酋邦并立。17至18世纪，日益强盛的布干达卡巴卡金布圭、卡特雷加和穆特比征服了布索加的大片土地，南湖沿岸的酋长沦为布干达的附庸。敌对的索加派系轮番向布尼奥罗或布干达求援，向更强的一方进贡牛、羊乃至奴隶，酋长继承之争也要到强国王廷上裁断；到1821年，这些酋邦仍没有共同的统治者。

en:
Karagwe, also called Bunyambo after its people the Abanyambo, is the high grassland between Rwanda and Lake Victoria. Its kings, titled Omugabe, belonged to the Hinda clan and claimed descent from Ruhinda, son of Wamara, the Chwezi ruler of Kitara; tradition places the founding of the line around 1450, and Bweranyange became the royal capital. Hima cattle-owning families stood above the farming clans, lending out stock to bind cultivators as clients, and the kings fought a long struggle to bring the mediums of the Kubandwa cult under court control. The land's other renown was iron: closed hereditary smith-clans smelted the ore with charcoal, and their hoes and weapons sold across the lake region. In 1444 the Hinda kingdom was newly settled on its hills, a stratified cattle-and-iron state on the western edge of Lake Victoria.

In the following generations Karagwe took its place in the chain of interlacustrine kingdoms, each clan serving the court at Bweranyange in its appointed role. Long overshadowed by Bunyoro, it turned against its northern overlord late in the eighteenth century: the Omugabe Ntare VI, who reigned from about 1775 to 1795, destroyed the Nyoro host and was remembered as Kitabanyoro, the Nyoro-slayer. Ruhinda VI ruled across the turn of the century, and about 1820 Ndagara I came to the throne.
zh:
卡拉圭又称布尼扬博，得名于境内的尼扬博人，是卢旺达与维多利亚湖之间的高原草地。这里的国王称奥穆加贝，出自欣达氏族，自称是基塔拉的齐韦兹统治者瓦马拉之子鲁欣达的后裔；传说王统开创于1450年前后，都城设在布韦拉尼扬盖。拥有牛群的希马牧人家族高居于农耕氏族之上，以出借牲畜把农人束缚为依附者，历代国王又经过长期经营，把主宰本地宗教的库班德瓦神媒置于宫廷控制之下。卡拉圭的另一项名声是铁：封闭的世袭铁匠氏族以木炭炼铁，打出的锄头和武器销往大湖各处。1444年的欣达王国刚刚在这片丘陵上立足，是维多利亚湖西缘一个等级森严、以牛群和铁器立国的政权。

此后的几代人里，卡拉圭跻身环大湖诸王国之列，各氏族按分工在布韦拉尼扬盖的宫廷当差。它长期受布尼奥罗压制，18世纪末转而进攻北方的宗主：约1775至1795年在位的奥穆加贝恩塔雷六世击溃尼奥罗军队，被称作基塔巴尼奥罗，意为「屠戮尼奥罗人者」。鲁欣达六世在世纪之交执政，约1820年恩达加拉一世即位。

en:
Buganda covers the green hills and swamps north of Lake Victoria, the Ganda name for which is Nalubaale. Bantu farmers making Urewe pottery had settled there by the sixth century, and the kingdom probably took shape between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries around the small counties of Kyadondo, Busiro and Mawokota. In 1444 the fifth kabaka, Kiggala, ruled from Kitala Hill, the capital he had established about 1434. His power still depended on powerful clan heads and hill chiefs, whose villages drew tribute from productive banana gardens and dressed court and household in beaten barkcloth.

A Bunyoro invasion in the sixteenth century killed Kabaka Nakinge, but Buganda kept its independence and then expanded as Bunyoro weakened. Under Kimbugwe, Katerega and Mutebi in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, its armies took Buddu and parts of Busoga and Karagwe, made Kooki tributary and replaced conquered rulers with royal appointees. Blue beads served as state currency under Kyabaggu from about 1750 to 1780, and ivory discs circulated under Junju around 1790 to 1800. The office of katikkiro, or chief minister, took shape around 1800. In that same year Kamanya sent a hundred canoes to Jinja, had them carried overland through Busoga and reassembled, and struck the Lango from an unexpected quarter while another army moved by land. By 1821 appointed chiefs, dry-season campaigns and war-canoe logistics had made Buganda one of the most formidable powers on the Great Lakes.
zh:
布干达位于维多利亚湖以北的青翠丘陵与沼泽之间，干达人称该湖为纳卢巴莱。早在6世纪，制作乌雷韦陶器的班图农民已在此定居；王国大约在12至14世纪成形，最初只统有基亚东多、布西罗和马沃科塔等小郡。1444年，第五任卡巴卡基加拉以基塔拉山为王都，这座都邑是他约1434年建立的。他的权力仍依赖强势的氏族首领和山丘酋长；村社靠丰饶的香蕉园征收贡赋，宫廷与家户则穿着捶制的树皮布。

16世纪，布尼奥罗的入侵杀死卡巴卡纳金格，但布干达保住了独立，并趁布尼奥罗衰落开始扩张。17至18世纪，在金布格韦、卡泰雷加和穆特比统治下，军队夺取布杜以及布索加、卡拉圭的部分土地，迫使库基纳贡，并以国王任命的官员取代被征服者的首领。约1750年至1780年基亚巴古在位时，蓝珠成为国家通货；约1790年至1800年君朱在位时，象牙圆片也进入流通。首席大臣「卡蒂基罗」之职约在1800年成形。同年，卡曼亚把一百艘独木舟运到金贾，再经布索加陆运、重新组装，从意想不到的方向攻击兰戈人，另一支军队则由陆路推进。到1821年，任命制酋长、旱季征战和战船运输体系已使布干达成为大湖地区最可畏的强权之一。

en:
This is the southern Bunyoro country around Mugenyi, whose name preserves Bigo bya Mugenyi, the great earthwork on the Katonga River. Around 1444 its outer ditch and bank ran for more than six kilometres, joining the Katonga to the Kakinga swamps and enclosing over 300 hectares around four central enclosures. Excavations have found roulette-decorated pottery, iron arrowheads and a grain knife, showing an Iron Age elite able to organize labour, hold cattle, and redistribute goods while Kibiro salt moved through Bunyoro's exchange networks.

After the Babiito kings founded the later Kingdom of Bunyoro in the late sixteenth century, their princes carried royal influence toward Busoga, Kiziba, Buzinza, and the lands beyond the Rwenzoris. Duhaga ruled Bunyoro from about 1731 to 1782, but by the end of the century internal division and Buganda's seizure of Kooki and Buddu had weakened the monarchy. Nyamutukura Kyebambe III came to the throne in 1786 and still ruled in 1821; his realm remained rich from salt, iron, and ivory, but its southern earthworks lay on a frontier increasingly pressed by Buganda.
zh:
这是穆根伊周围的布尼奥罗南部地区，穆根伊之名保存着卡通加河畔大型土垒遗址比戈·比亚·穆根伊的记忆。1444年前后，这里的外壕与土堤长逾六公里，把卡通加河与卡金卡沼泽连接起来，围住三百多公顷土地和四座中央围场。考古发现了绳纹陶、铁箭镞和收割谷物用的铁刀，说明当时已有能够组织劳役、畜养牛群、再分配货物的铁器时代精英；基比罗盐也在布尼奥罗的交换网络中流通。

16世纪末，巴比托诸王建立后来的布尼奥罗王国后，王族王子把王权影响带向布索加、基济巴、布津扎和鲁文佐里山以外地区。杜哈加约1731—1782年统治布尼奥罗；到18世纪末，内部分裂以及布干达夺取科基和布杜，削弱了王权。尼亚穆图库拉·基埃班贝三世1786年即位，1821年仍在位；他的王国仍靠盐、铁和象牙致富，但南部土垒已处在日益受布干达压力的边境上。

en:
Nkore, called Ankole only after the colonial conquest, is the rolling grass country east of Lake Edward between Buganda, Bunyoro, Karagwe and Rwanda. Its pastures were so rich that cattle could be watered almost all year round, and the land was known as Kaaro Karungi, 'the good land': Bahima herdsmen tended the long-horned Ankole cattle and stood above the Bairu millet-farmers, while the mugabe ruled through cattle-clientage, war-bands called emitwe and the sacred royal drum Bagyendanwa. Tradition made Ruhinda, founder of the Hinda dynasty, a king within living memory, and his son Nkuba firmed up the new kingship from its core at Isingiro. In 1444 Nkore was still a small kingdom in the shadow of Bunyoro.

For two and a half centuries it stayed a minor power, at times owning Bunyoro's overlordship. Ntare IV, who reigned from 1699 to 1727, turned the tables: invaded by the Bunyoro army of Cwamali, he took shelter in the Nyamistindo caves and on Kantsyore Island in the Kagera, then counter-attacked, killed Cwamali and earned the name Kiitabanyoro, 'slayer of the Banyoro', pushing his border north to the Katonga and seizing Kabula. Macwa, who followed him, kept the peace from 1727 to 1755, but his death threw the throne into disputed succession. Wars with Rwanda and cattle-raids on every frontier filled the later reigns, and in 1821 the Hinda kings still held their pastures as their own.
zh:
安科莱（旧称恩科莱，殖民征服之后才改称安科莱）是爱德华湖以东、夹在布干达、布尼奥罗、卡拉圭与卢旺达之间的起伏草原之国。这里牧场肥美，牛群几乎一年到头都能饮水，土地因此得名「卡鲁昆吉」，意为「好地方」：巴希马牧人放牧长角安科莱牛，地位高于种黍子的巴伊鲁农人；姆加贝国王以牛群封臣、名为埃米特韦的战团和神圣王鼓巴吉丹瓦维治国。按口述传统，欣达王朝的开国君鲁欣达距当时不过一代人之久，他的儿子恩库巴在伊辛吉罗的核心之地巩固了新生王权。1444年时，恩科莱还是布尼奥罗阴影下的一个小王国。

此后两个半世纪里，它始终是个小国，有时还向布尼奥罗称臣。1699至1727年在位的恩塔雷四世扭转了局面：布尼奥罗的茨瓦马利率军来犯，他先避入尼亚米斯廷多洞穴和卡盖拉河中的坎乔雷岛，随后反攻，杀死茨瓦马利，赢得「基塔巴尼奥罗」（意为诛杀尼奥罗人者）的称号，并把北界推进到卡通加河、夺取卡布拉。继他之后的马克瓦在1727至1755年间维持了和平，他一死，王位便陷入继承纷争。其后诸王的岁月充斥着与卢旺达的战事和各条边境上的掠牛之争；到1821年，欣达诸王仍然独立自主地守着自己的牧场。

en:
Nduga is the hilly country of central Rwanda around the old Gitarama, reaching south toward Nyanza, a land of banana groves and cattle pastures watered by the Nyabarongo. It was once the kingdom of the Ababanda clan, whose king ruled from the hill of Rwesero with the royal drum Nyabahinda as his emblem, while Twa hunters and Hutu farmers shared the hills with incoming cattle-keeping clans. In 1444 Nduga was still its own master: the Nyiginya kingdom to its north-east was then little more than the 'Rwanda of Gasabo' around Lake Muhazi, one chiefdom among several.

Nduga kept its freedom through the first Rwandan wars of expansion. The Ababanda king Mashira retook his realm with shelter from Bugesera, and the mwami Mibambwe Mutabazi had to accept the restoration. Mibambwe then gave Mashira his daughter Nyirantobwa in marriage and, travelling through Nduga as a guest, was feasted at Nyamagana near Nyanza; in the middle of the festivities he seized his host and put Mashira and all his sons to death, and the Ababanda army was destroyed to the last man. With its royal line extinguished, Nduga was annexed in the Rwandan expansion of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, and its hills became part of the kingdom's central provinces.
zh:
恩杜加地处卢旺达中部丘陵，即旧吉塔拉马一带，向南延伸到尼安扎附近，尼亚巴隆戈河滋养着这里的香蕉园和牧牛场。它曾是阿班达氏族的王国，国王在鲁韦塞罗山发号施令，以圣鼓尼亚巴欣达为权力象征；山丘上住着特瓦猎人、胡图农民，还有陆续迁入的牧牛氏族。1444年的恩杜加仍是自主之邦，东北方的尼金亚王国还只是以穆哈齐湖周边的「加萨博卢旺达」为中心的一个酋长国，与恩杜加、布格塞拉等小国并立。

恩杜加一度顶住了卢旺达扩张的最初攻势：阿班达国王马希拉在布格塞拉避难后收复故国，姆瓦米·米班布韦·穆塔巴齐不得不承认阿班达王朝复辟。后来米班布韦把女儿尼兰托布瓦嫁给马希拉，又以过客身份做客恩杜加，在尼安扎附近的尼亚马加纳赴宴；宴席之间他突然拿下主人，将马希拉和他所有的儿子处死，阿班达军队也被全歼。王统既绝，恩杜加在16至17世纪卢旺达的扩张中被兼并，这片丘陵此后成为王国中部疆土的一部分。

en:
Bafuriru is the highland country above the northern end of Lake Tanganyika, where the mountains of Uvira drop to the Ruzizi plain on the border with Rwanda and Burundi. Clans tracing their origin to the Lwindi country, at the mouth of the Ulindi on the Lualaba, settled the valleys of Mulenge, Luvungi and Lemera between the tenth and fourteenth centuries; they kept cattle, worked the fields, and won a name for pottery and basketwork. By 1444 the Bahamba clan was building these settlements into the Hamba kingdom, a small highland state more centralised than most of its neighbours, while the Ruzizi plain below served mainly as pasture and hunting ground.

In the seventeenth century the related Vira people arrived through Maniema and the Itombwe mountains and spread along the lakeside slopes from Mount Munanira above Uvira, dividing the highlands with the Bafuliru. Tradition names the mwami Kahamba Kalingishi as the founder who united the Bafuliru clans in Lemera and established their royal line, though oral accounts differ widely on his dates. From the 1600s Bafuliru hunters and herders also began to descend into the Ruzizi plain, the frontier march with the kingdoms of Rwanda and Burundi.
zh:
巴夫里鲁位于坦噶尼喀湖北端的高地，乌维拉山区在此俯临与卢旺达、布隆迪交界的鲁济济平原。当地诸氏族自称源自卢阿拉巴河上乌林迪河口的卢温迪，于10至14世纪间陆续定居穆伦盖、卢温吉和莱梅拉的河谷；他们牧牛耕种，并以制陶和编篮闻名。到1444年，巴汉巴氏族正把这些聚落组建成汉巴王国，一个比多数邻邦都集权的山地小国，而山下的鲁济济平原主要还是牧场和猎场。

17世纪，与他们相近的维拉人经马涅马和伊通布韦山区迁来，以乌维拉上方的穆纳尼拉山为中心散布到沿湖山坡，与巴夫里鲁人分据高地。相传姆瓦米·卡汉巴·卡林吉希是在莱梅拉统一各氏族、开创巴夫里鲁王统的建国者，但口述传统对他的年代说法不一。从17世纪起，巴夫里鲁的猎人和牧人也开始下山进入鲁济济平原，那里正是与卢旺达、布隆迪两王国相邻的边陲。

en: Bushubi is the highland country of the Washubi around Ngara, in the hills of north-western Tanzania between Rwanda, Burundi and the Zinza lands to the east. The Shubi lived by hunting before turning mainly to farming, growing grain and keeping cattle on the well-watered ridges. In 1444 it was still a country of autonomous hill villages, bound to the neighbouring Buha and Buhaya worlds by a Bantu language close to Kinyarwanda and Kirundi. The Shubi kings, titled mwami, are remembered by the royal names Magina, Kibogora, Nsoro and Kinanaira, repeated down the remembered line of reigns.
zh: 布苏毕是瓦苏比人的山地，位于坦桑尼亚西北部恩加拉一带，处在卢旺达、布隆迪与东方津扎之地之间。苏比人原先以狩猎为生，后来主要转为农耕，在水源充足的山梁上种植谷物、牧养牛群。1444年，这里还是自治山村并立的地方，居民的班图语接近卢旺达语和布隆迪语，与相邻的布哈、布哈亚世界声息相通。苏比人的国王称姆瓦米，留下了马吉纳、基博戈拉、恩索罗、基纳奈拉等王名，在历代君王中循环沿用。

en:
Nkoma is the ridge country of the Nkoma massif, overlooking the Kumoso plain in what is now Rutana Province, southeastern Burundi. In 1444 it was not a royal capital. Bantu farmers, Twa hunter-foragers, and cattle-keeping families lived in scattered hill homesteads under local leaders, their farms, herds, and forges tying the ridge to both the Buha and Burundian worlds.

Later oral tradition made Nkoma the first royal stage in the rise of Ntare Rushatsi, the founder remembered in the southern Burundian cycle that also connected his following to Buha. As the Burundian kingdom coalesced during the seventeenth century, its mwami drew neighbouring hill communities into a loose monarchy. From about 1795 the wars of Ntare IV carried Burundian power back toward the smaller polities of Buha, so that in 1821 Nkoma stood on an eastern frontier being drawn toward the royal court.
zh:
恩科马是恩科马山地的山脊地带，俯瞰今布隆迪东南部鲁塔纳省境内的库莫索平原。1444年时，这里并不是王都。班图农民、特瓦族狩猎采集者和牧牛家族散居在各处山梁庄园中，受本地首领管辖；农田、牛群和锻炉把这座山脊同布哈与布隆迪两边的世界联系起来。

后来的口述传统把恩科马视为恩塔雷·鲁沙齐崛起过程中的第一个王权舞台；布隆迪南部传统谱系记住了这位开国者，也把他的追随者同布哈联系在一起。17世纪布隆迪王国逐渐聚合，姆瓦米把相邻的山地共同体纳入一个松散王权。约1795年起，恩塔雷四世的战争再次把布隆迪势力推向布哈诸小邦；到1821年，恩科马已处在东部边境上，日益被吸向王室权力中心。

en:
Buyogoma is the high eastern plateau between the Ruvubu valley and the Moso plains, on the western edge of Buha. In 1444 its Ha farmers, the Abaha, lived in dispersed homesteads and spoke Kiha, a Bantu language close to Kirundi. Sorghum and millet fields, goats and cattle sustained the villages and the tribute owed to local rulers, while ancestor spirits and the high god Imana shaped religious life.

The plateau remained a western march of Buha's small kingships rather than a town-centered state. By 1796 Ntare Rugamba's Burundian armies had opened a period of royal expansion, and Buyogoma was held by the Buha mwami Ruhaga. Rugamba coveted its grain and open pasture and went to war with Buha. In 1821 the plateau had yet to be incorporated into Burundi, caught between the old Ha court and the growing power of Burundi.
zh:
布约戈马是鲁武布河谷与莫索平原之间的东部高原，位于布哈西缘。1444年，这里的哈人农民（阿巴哈人）散居在各家庄园里，使用与基隆迪语相近的班图语基哈语。高粱和粟米田、山羊和牛群维持着村落生计，也供应本地统治者索取的贡赋；祖先神灵和至高神伊马纳则支配着人们的宗教生活。

这片高原长期是布哈诸小王国的西部边地，而不是以城镇为中心的国家。到1796年，恩塔雷·鲁加姆巴的布隆迪军队已经开启王室扩张阶段，布约戈马由布哈姆瓦米鲁哈加掌握。鲁加姆巴觊觎这里的谷物和开阔牧场，向布哈开战。1821年时，高原尚未并入布隆迪，夹在旧布哈王庭与崛起的布隆迪强权之间。

en:
Ruguru, also called Luguru or Nkanda-Luguru, was one of the small Ha polities of Buha, covering the country around later Basanza, Murufyiti, and Makere in what is now Kasulu District. In 1444 Kiha-speaking clans lived in scattered homesteads on fertile grassland and open woodland under elders called muteko. Women cultivated millet and other food crops, men hunted and gathered honey, and Ha smelters forged hoes, knives, and arrows that could be exchanged for cattle, skins, and Uvinza salt.

The spread of shifting cultivation in the seventeenth century strengthened these village economies, but around 1800 cattle-keeping dynasties reshaped Buha during its succession wars. Their ubugabire patron-client system raised a mwami and watwale officials above the old clan heads, who retained duties over land and ritual while tribute in grain, salt, milk, honey, and cattle flowed toward the new courts. Nkanda-Luguru thus entered 1821 as one of Buha's six chiefdoms, its older Ha clan order being folded into a cattle aristocracy.
zh:
卢古鲁又称恩坎达-卢古鲁，是布哈的哈人小政权之一，地域包括今卡苏卢县境内后来的巴桑扎、穆鲁菲蒂和马凯雷一带。1444年，说基哈语的氏族散居在肥沃草地与开阔疏林中，由称穆特科的长老统领。妇女种植粟米等粮食，男子狩猎并采集蜂蜜；哈人铁匠锻打锄头、刀和箭，用这些器物交换牛、兽皮和乌温扎盐。

17世纪迁移耕作扩展，巩固了这些村落经济；约1800年，牧牛王朝趁布哈继承战争重塑了当地秩序。他们带来的乌布加比雷保护—依附关系把姆瓦米和称瓦特瓦莱的官员抬到旧氏族首领之上，旧首领仍保留土地分配和仪式职责，而谷物、盐、奶、蜂蜜和牛等贡赋流向新王庭。恩坎达-卢古鲁因此作为布哈六个酋邦之一进入1821年，旧的哈人氏族秩序正被纳入一个牧牛贵族体系。

en: Hehe is the high southern plateau later called Uhehe, around Iringa and the grazing lands above the Great Ruaha. In 1444 it was not a single kingdom. Bantu farming communities kept cattle and goats where pasture allowed, and local traditions name the Hafiwa, iron-working Vanyategeta, Vanyakilwa, Vasavila and Vadongwe among the groups settled in its hills and valleys. Small chiefs raided one another for cattle, made marriage alliances and broke them when advantage shifted. In 1821 Uhehe remained a patchwork of rival agricultural chiefdoms and pastoral homesteads, with no court that could speak for all the people later known as the Hehe.
zh: 赫赫是后来被称为乌赫赫的南方高原，位于伊林加一带和大鲁阿哈河上游牧地之上。1444年时，这里还不是统一王国。说班图语的农耕社群在牧场允许的地方饲养牛和山羊；当地传统提到，山丘与谷地中分布着哈菲瓦人、擅长冶铁的瓦尼亚特盖塔人、瓦尼亚基尔瓦人、瓦萨维拉人和瓦东圭人。小首领们互相夺牛，缔结婚姻联盟，又会随利害变化而毁约。1821年的乌赫赫仍是彼此竞争的农业酋邦和牧人家户拼成的地带，没有一个宫廷能代表后来所称的赫赫全体。

en:
Pubungo, remembered in Luo tradition as Pubungu, was a Nile crossing and short-grass livestock frontier usually identified near later Pakwach on the Albert Nile. In 1444 it was not a walled capital. Earlier Madi-, Okebo- and Lendu-speaking communities shared the river banks and surrounding savanna with incoming Luo clans, fishing, growing sorghum and millet, and keeping sheep, goats, and cattle. Bunyoro's influence reached the southern approaches, but authority still rested mainly with village and kin elders.

Luo tradition later remembered Pubungu as the dispersal point where the migrants divided, some remaining near the Nile while others moved west or south into Bunyoro. From the late seventeenth century, Luo chiefdoms emerged under rulers called rwodi, and during the eighteenth century they adopted royal drums and other regalia from Bunyoro, redistributing tribute and organizing large communal hunts. In 1821 the country remained a fluid cattle frontier between the Bito monarchy and the small Luo chiefdoms later known as Acholi, linked by trade, marriage, and raiding.
zh:
普布恩戈在卢奥传统中称普本古（Pubungu），地处阿尔伯特尼罗河上的渡口和短草畜牧边境，通常比定在后来帕夸奇附近。1444年时，这里并不是有城墙的都城。较早的马迪、奥凯博和伦杜语共同体与迁入的卢奥氏族共居河岸和周围稀树草原，以捕鱼、种植高粱和粟米、饲养绵羊、山羊和牛为生。布尼奥罗的势力抵达其南缘，但权力主要仍掌握在村落和氏族长老手中。

卢奥传统后来把普本古记住为族群分散点：迁徙者在此分路，一些人留在尼罗河畔，另一些人向西或向南进入布尼奥罗。17世纪末起，卢奥酋邦在称为鲁奥迪（rwodi）的统治者下兴起；18世纪，他们借鉴布尼奥罗的王鼓和其他王权器物，再分配贡物并组织大型围猎。1821年，这里仍是比托王朝与后来被称为阿乔利人的卢奥小酋邦之间流动的牧牛边境，联系各方的是贸易、婚姻和袭掠，而不是固定边界。

en:
Lango is the grassland and wetland country north of Lake Kyoga, where Lake Kwania and papyrus swamps lie on the approaches to Bunyoro. The people later called Lango were connected with the Ateker world of the Karamojong and Teso, though their speech would take a Luo form close to Acholi. Farming, hunting, cattle and the worship of Jok and ancestral spirits shaped their clan life.

From about 1780, ancestral Lango groups split from the Jie section of the Karamojong cluster and moved west with Teso-related peoples, halting for a time around Mount Otuke before entering the Kyoga lowlands. By 1821 Lango clans were taking shape on the wetland frontier, still without a permanent king or central chief. Cultivators gained land rights by first breaking unused ground. Wartime leaders commanded fighters drawn from several clans, but their authority ended when peace returned, and village elders resumed their authority over land, marriage disputes, sacrifices and tribute.
zh:
兰戈是基奥加湖北方的草原与湿地之乡，夸尼亚湖和纸莎草沼泽位于通向布尼奥罗的方向。后来被称为兰戈的人群与卡拉莫琼人和特索人所属的阿特克尔世界相连，但其语言后来发展成与阿乔利语相近的卢奥形态。农耕、狩猎、牧牛，以及对乔克神和祖灵的崇拜，构成氏族生活的核心。

约1780年起，兰戈先民从卡拉莫琼群体中的杰人支系分出，与和特索有关的人群一同西迁，曾在奥图凯山一带停留，随后进入基奥加低地。到1821年，兰戈各氏族已在湿地边疆逐渐成形，却仍没有常设国王或中央首领。最先开垦未用土地的耕作者获得土地权利。战时首领可以统率多个氏族的战士，但和平恢复后其权威便告终止，村落长老重新掌管土地、婚姻争端、祭祀和贡纳事务。

en: Muhambwe is the country of the Wahambwe, the Kibondo branch of the Ha peoples in the Buha highlands east of Lake Tanganyika. Bantu-speaking farmers and cattle keepers occupied its ridges before 1444. Its people spoke Kiha, a language close to Kirundi and Kinyarwanda, and combined cultivation with herding, hunting and trade in food and cattle. Around 1800 related Ha clans were drawn together under chiefly authority; they included the Wayungu of Kakonko and the Wanyaheru of the Heru highlands. Muhambwe was recognized alongside Heru, Bushingo, Ruguru and Buyungu as one of the small Ha states.
zh: 穆罕布韦是瓦汉布韦人的土地，他们是坦噶尼喀湖以东布哈高地哈人的基邦多支系。1444年以前，讲班图语的农民和牧人已在此地丘陵定居。居民讲与基隆迪语和卢旺达语相近的基哈语，生活依靠农耕、牧牛、狩猎，并以粮食和牲畜交易。1800年前后，彼此关联的哈人氏族聚合于首领权威之下，其中包括卡孔科的瓦永古人和赫鲁高地的瓦尼亚赫鲁人。穆罕布韦与赫鲁、布欣戈、鲁古鲁、布永古一同被承认为哈人的小邦之一。

en:
Rukwa takes its name from the long, enclosed alkaline lake in the trough between Lake Tanganyika and Lake Nyasa, whose shoreline shifts with the rains. Above its western side rises the open Ufipa Plateau, where Fipa, Wanda and Nyika clans farmed, kept cattle, hunted and guarded the techniques of iron smelting. The smith dynasty of Milanzi, called 'the eternal village', stood above neighbouring clans and traded iron for woven cloth, while village headmen and local chiefs governed a mosaic of plateau settlements.

During the seventeenth century Milanzi became the central Fipa chiefdom, but around 1700 it was succeeded by Nkansi and Lyangalile. Twa rulers formed a territorial aristocracy, while the older Milanzi dynasty retained ritual authority and the right to install a new chief. In the following century Nkansi maintained a court of titled officials and a queen mother, appointed district officers, and left villages under elected headmen. Iron, grain, cattle and cloth moved between the courts, villages and lake approaches, giving the thinly wooded plateau a more ordered political life than its open borders suggest.
zh:
鲁夸得名于坦噶尼喀湖与尼亚萨湖之间凹陷地带中的狭长内流咸水湖，湖面会随降雨涨落。湖西隆起开阔的乌菲帕高原，菲帕、旺达和尼伊卡氏族在此农耕、牧牛、狩猎，并守护冶铁技术。被称为「永恒之村」的米兰齐铁匠王朝凌驾邻近氏族，以铁器交换织物；村落头人和地方首领则分治高原上星罗棋布的聚落。

17世纪时，米兰齐成为菲帕人的中心酋邦，但约在1700年由恩坎西和利扬加利莱继承。特瓦统治者形成领地上的贵族阶层，古老的米兰齐王朝则保留宗教权威，以及为新首领举行授职仪式的权力。此后一个世纪里，恩坎西设有多名有头衔官员和王太后组成的宫廷，任命地方官吏，村落则由选举产生的头人管理。铁器、粮食、牲畜和布匹在宫廷、村落与通往湖区的道路间流通，使这片林木稀疏的高原拥有比其开放边界所显示的更为有序的政治生活。

en:
Mayumba is the southern Gabonese coast of long sandspits and the Banio and Ndogo lagoons, where the Bantu expansion left Lumbu and Vili villagers, peoples akin to the Bakongo. They fished, gathered oysters and boiled sea salt to sell to the Punu of the interior, exchanging ivory and raffia cloth along the beaches. In 1444 this was a chain of small Lumbu and Vili chiefdoms on the northern edge of the Kongo world; later Dutch records would name Mayumba itself among the tiny coastal states that 'made war on each other' before the rise of Loango, and Portuguese sails first appeared offshore in the 1470s.

In the later sixteenth century the founder of Loango conquered rivals including Kilongo, and at Loango's seventeenth-century height its reach ran north to Cape St Catherine, bringing the lagoon villages under the king at Bwali and his Vili governors. Just up the shore, Setté Cama was already a busy timber-and-ivory port, and Mayumba shared in the same traffic: Dutch and English ships anchored offshore and paid the royal trade official, the mafouk. From the late 1600s captives brought down from the interior by Vili merchants joined ivory and raffia cloth among the exports. Through the eighteenth century the lagoon mouths remained small, thronged markets on the far northern edge of the Loango world.
zh:
马永巴所在的加蓬南部海岸是一列长沙嘴，巴尼奥、恩多戈等潟湖横亘其间。班图人迁徙后，伦布人和维利人的村落分布于此，他们与巴刚果人同源。村民捕鱼、采蚝、熬煮海盐，卖给内地的蓬古人，又在海滩上交换象牙和拉菲亚布。1444年的这里是刚果世界北缘一连串伦布、维利小酋邦；后来荷兰人的记载把马永巴本身列为卢安果兴起之前「彼此攻战」的海岸小国之一，到1470年代，葡萄牙人的帆影才第一次出现在外海。

16世纪后期，卢安果的创建者征服了基隆古等对手；17世纪卢安果鼎盛时，势力北达圣凯瑟琳角，潟湖村落归布瓦利的国王和他任命的维利长官管辖。沿海岸北上，塞泰卡马已是繁忙的木材与象牙港，马永巴也参与同样的贸易：荷兰和英国船只停泊外海，向王室贸易官马富克缴费。17世纪末以后，维利商人从内陆贩来的俘虏与象牙、拉菲亚布并列为出口货物。整个18世纪，这些潟湖口始终是卢安果世界北疆上拥挤繁忙的小市场。

en:
Ngoyo was the kingdom of the Woyo, a Bakongo people, on the coast immediately north of the Congo River, around the bay that later became Cabinda; its capital was Mbanza Ngoyo. Because its dynasties claimed the earliest roots in the soil, its chiefs bore the title nfumu nsi, 'lords of the earth', and with Vungu and Kakongo it had formed one of the small confederations out of which the Kingdom of Kongo itself grew. In 1444 it sat in Kongo's northern shadow, its people shipping ivory, raffia cloth and red tukula dyewood along a coast Portuguese ships had not yet reached.

Diogo Cão's voyage opened the coast in 1482–83, and Ngoyo appears in the titles of the Manikongo Afonso I by 1535, but its later history was shaped above all by Soyo, the militant Kongo province at the river mouth. In the 1630s a Soyo army installed the ruler's son at Mbanza Ngoyo, and in the 1680s the prince of Soyo, António II Baretto da Silva, invaded again while English merchants tried in vain to defend Ngoyo's interests. By 1700 Cabinda had become the leading slave port north of Luanda, and the kingdom lived chiefly by selling captives brought up from the interior. In 1783 Ngoyo and Kakongo joined forces to attack a Portuguese fort, but the assault was beaten off; the costly kingship attracted fewer and fewer claimants, and from that time the old kingdom steadily fragmented.
zh:
恩戈约是沃约人的王国。沃约人属巴刚果一支，住在刚果河正北的海岸，即后来卡宾达湾一带，都城为姆班扎·恩戈约。其王族自称是这片土地最早的主人，首领因此号称恩富姆·恩西，意为「大地之主」；它与温古、卡刚果曾同属一个小邦联，而刚果王国正是从这些邦联中兴起的。1444年，恩戈约处在刚果的北方阴影之下，居民沿葡萄牙船只尚未到达的海岸贩运象牙、拉菲亚布和红色的图库拉染木。

迪奥戈·卡奥的航行在1482至1483年间打开了这片海岸，到1535年，恩戈约已列在马尼刚果阿方索一世的名号之中；但塑造它后来历史的，主要是刚果河口那个好战的刚果省份索约。1630年代，索约军队把索约统治者的儿子扶上姆班扎·恩戈约的王位；1680年代，索约亲王安东尼奥二世·巴雷托·达席尔瓦再度入侵，英国商人想维护恩戈约的利益，却未能成功。到1700年，卡宾达已成为罗安达以北最大的奴隶港，恩戈约主要靠出售从内陆贩来的俘虏为生。1783年，恩戈约与卡刚果联手攻打一座葡萄牙要塞，但进攻被击退；王位的负担越来越重，问津者日少，自那时起这个古老王国便一步步走向瓦解。

en:
Soyo was the coastal province of the Kingdom of Kongo, reaching south from the mouth of the Congo River towards the Loze and some 100 kilometres inland. Its governor bore the title mwene Soyo, 'lord of Soyo', and was usually a royal kinsman serving a limited term. In 1444 it was Kongo's window on the Atlantic, still unknown to European sailors.

Diogo Cão entered the estuary in 1482 and planted a stone pillar dedicated to St George on its point. In 1491 the lord of Soyo, baptised Manuel, became the first Kongo ruler to accept Christianity. Portuguese traders settled at the river port of Mpinda, shipping ivory, copper and slaves; a royal inquest of 1548 found up to 4,000 captives a year passing through to São Tomé and then Brazil. Álvaro II made its ruler Miguel a count in the early 1590s. From 1641 Count Daniel da Silva insisted that Soyo's nobles chose their own lord, and Garcia II's armies broke against the fortified forest of Nfinda Ngula in 1641, 1643, 1645 and 1656. On 18 October 1670 Soyo routed a Portuguese army at Kitombo. Its rulers, later styled princes, stopped taking part in Kongo's royal elections after 1708.
zh:
索约是刚果王国的沿海省份，从刚果河口向南延伸到洛热河，深入内陆约一百公里。这里的长官称「索约之主」，通常由国王的亲族出任，任期有限。1444年，索约是刚果面向大西洋的门户，欧洲航海者尚未到过这里。

1482年，迪奥戈·康驶入河口，在岬角上立起献给圣乔治的石柱。1491年，受洗名为曼努埃尔的索约之主成为第一个皈依基督教的刚果统治者。葡萄牙商人在河港姆平达定居，经营象牙、铜和奴隶，1548年刚果王室的调查显示，每年多达四千名奴隶从这里被运往圣多美，再转往巴西。16世纪90年代初，阿尔瓦罗二世封索约统治者米格尔为伯爵。1641年起，达尼埃尔·达席尔瓦伯爵坚持索约领主应由本地贵族推选，加西亚二世在1641、1643、1645和1656年四度出兵，都在设防的恩芬达恩古拉森林前败退。1670年10月18日，索约在基通博大败葡萄牙军队。其统治者后来改称亲王，1708年后不再参与刚果国王的推选。

en:
Songo is the forest-and-savanna country east of Okango, the district that Portuguese records often spell Okanga. Its Kikongo-speaking villagers farmed the inland valleys and wove palm-fibre cloth that travelled west toward the Mbanza-Kongo markets. The older lands around Okanga, Kundi and Mbata were remembered as part of the Seven Kingdoms of Kongo dia Nlaza, whose chiefs were drawn only gradually into the kingdom founded around 1390. In 1444 Songo therefore stood on Kongo's loosely governed eastern approaches: its headmen answered to greater lords and tribute demands, while its shrines, village councils and looms remained local affairs.

After Diogo Cão reached the Kongo coast in 1483, priests and soldiers accompanied his return mission and baptised the Manikongo Nzinga a Nkuwu in 1491; Afonso I's victory in 1509 made Catholicism the court religion, though inland families kept older rites. The new Portuguese market at Luanda, founded in 1575, drew heavily on this region's textiles, and in 1611 and 1612 fiscal official Pero Sardinha reported an average of 45,000 Songo cloths arriving there each year. The Jaga raids of 1568 opened decades of border instability, and after António I was killed at Mbwila on 29 October 1665, Kongo split between the Kinlaza and Kimpanzu houses. São Salvador was sacked in 1678 and captives flowed to Atlantic ports until the crown was restored in the early eighteenth century, leaving Songo largely in the hands of local chiefs and merchant clans.
zh:
松戈是奥坎加（Okanga）以东的林莽与稀树草原地带。这里的居民说刚果语，在河谷间耕作，并用棕榈纤维织布；布匹沿商路西行，送往姆班扎刚果的市场。奥坎加、昆迪和姆巴塔一带有更古老的「刚果迪亚恩拉扎七王国」传统，各地酋长后来才逐渐被纳入约1390年建立的刚果王国。1444年的松戈处在刚果王国控制松散的东缘：村社首领向更强大的统治者纳贡应役，但神龛、村落议事和织机仍由本地人掌握。

1483年，迪奥戈·康抵达刚果海岸；他后来的使团带来神父和士兵，马尼刚果恩津加·恩库武于1491年受洗。阿方索一世1509年获胜后，天主教成为宫廷宗教，但内陆家族仍保留旧有仪式。1575年葡萄牙人建立罗安达市场后，这里的纺织品大量西运；财政官佩罗·萨尔迪尼亚在1611和1612年报告，平均每年有四万五千匹松戈布运抵罗安达。1568年的贾加人袭掠开启了长期边患，1665年10月29日安东尼奥一世又战死于姆布维拉，刚果随后分裂为金拉扎与金潘祖两派。圣萨尔瓦多在1678年遭洗劫，人口被掳往大西洋港口；十八世纪初王权恢复后，松戈大半仍由地方酋长和商业氏族实际控制。

en:
Kasanje is the Baixa de Cassanje, the wooded savanna between the Kwanza and the upper Kwango. In 1444 its Mbundu villages were far beyond the reach of Europe: Luanda did not exist and no Portuguese factor had yet crossed the Kwanza. The kingdom that would give this province its name had not yet been founded either. It grew out of an Imbangala war band, one of the mercenary companies whose kilombo camps, initiation rites and war clubs the English sailor Andrew Battell witnessed while living south of the Kwanza in about 1600.

In 1618 the band led by Kasanje helped Portuguese forces sack Ndongo's capital, then broke away, ravaged Matamba and in about 1620 settled its followers on the upper Kwango as a new state. Its elected ruler bore the title kinguri, chosen from the three founding clans, and wars with Queen Njinga's Matamba, especially in 1634–35, and with neighbouring chiefdoms widened its reach; by the 1650s six languages were spoken within its borders. Portuguese merchants operated there from that decade, and between the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries the Feira de Cassange became the main market between Luanda and the Lundas, where slaves and ivory from the interior met cloth and firearms. In 1689 the Portuguese chronicler Cadornega put its population at 300,000, 100,000 of them able to bear arms, figures perhaps exaggerated but evidence of the kingdom's scale. The slave caravans sustained the kinguri and the Feira through the eighteenth century, even as the first Ovimbundu rival routes began to appear.
zh:
卡桑吉地处宽扎河与宽果河上游之间的林木稀树草原卡桑热低地。1444年，这里的姆本杜村落远在欧洲人势力之外：罗安达尚未建立，也没有任何葡萄牙商队越过宽扎河。日后赋予本省名字的王国同样还不存在——它诞生于一支因班加拉武装。约1600年，英国水手安德鲁·巴特尔在宽扎河以南生活时，记下了这类雇佣军团的基隆博营地、入会仪式和战棍。

1618年，卡桑吉率领的战团协助葡萄牙军队洗劫恩东戈王都，随后脱离葡方，蹂躏马坦巴，约1620年在宽果河上游安顿部众，建立新的国家。其君称「金古里」，由三个开国氏族中选出；与恩津加女王的马坦巴交战（尤以1634至1635年为烈），又不断征伐周边小邦，到1650年代境内已通行六种语言。葡萄牙商人从1650年代起在此活动，17世纪末至18世纪初兴起的卡桑吉集市成为罗安达与隆达之间最大的市场：内地贩来的奴隶和象牙在此换取布匹和火器。1689年，葡萄牙编年史家卡多内加估计其人口有三十万，其中十万可执兵器，数字或有夸张，却也可见王国的规模。整个18世纪，奴隶商路供养着金古里的王权与这座集市，尽管奥文本杜人的竞争商路这时已开始出现。

en:
The Shinje are a Lunda-related people of the rolling savanna and gallery forests east of the upper Kwango. Their villages lay on a frontier shared by Yaka farmers to the north, Ruund lands around the Kalanyi to the east and Lwena country to the south. In 1444 headmen still governed millet fields, fishing camps and oil-palm groves, and the Kasanje state remembered by later Portuguese sources had not yet been formed. Local paths already carried ivory, salt and captives toward the wider Kwango and Kasai basins.

In 1620 a Mbangala war band under Kasanje settled the upper Kwango and built the kingdom that bore his name, turning the western approaches to Shinje into a market for Portuguese slave traders. Lunda power expanded from Musumba during the following century, and Lunda caravans linked the Shinje country with the Atlantic traffic in slaves and ivory. In the 1650s Kasanje fought Matamba and other neighbours; by the later eighteenth century rivalry for captives and tribute still kept Shinje a borderland between Kasanje and the Mwata Yamvo's empire.
zh:
欣杰人是与隆达有关的族群，住在宽果河上游以东起伏的稀树草原和廊林之间。他们的村社处在一条交汇地带：北面是雅卡农人，东面是卡兰伊河一带的鲁恩德之地，南面是卢埃纳人的乡土。1444年，这里仍由各村首领管理粟田、渔场和油棕林，后世葡萄牙资料所载的卡桑吉国家尚未形成；本地小路已把象牙、盐和俘虏运往更广阔的宽果河、开赛河流域。

1620年，卡桑吉率领一支姆班加拉战团在宽果河上游定居，建立以他名字命名的王国，欣杰西侧通道也随之成为面向葡萄牙奴隶商人的市集。此后一个世纪，隆达势力从穆松巴向外扩张，隆达商队把欣杰同大西洋的奴隶与象牙贸易连接起来。17世纪50年代，卡桑吉同马坦巴等邻邦交战；到18世纪后期，对俘虏和贡赋的争夺仍使欣杰处在卡桑吉与姆瓦塔·扬沃帝国之间的边疆。

en:
Malem is the narrow corridor of woodland and plateau between the Ndongo highlands and the Baixa de Cassanje, where the paths from the Kwanza valley turn east towards the Kwango. In 1444 its Mbundu villages answered to local sobas within the loose orbit of the ngola of Ndongo; nothing European had yet reached them, for the Portuguese were a century and more away from the Kwanza.

The Imbangala band of Kasanje, hired for the Portuguese sack of Ndongo in 1618, broke from Portuguese service and ravaged Matamba before settling on the upper Kwango around 1620. The corridor was Kasanje's western approach, and in time the chief caravan track between the Portuguese presidio country of Ambaca and the Feira de Cassange: pombeiro traders led their carriers through it with slaves and ivory bound for Luanda, and through the eighteenth century its villages lived by feeding and supplying the trade or by fleeing its raiding parties.
zh:
马勒姆是恩东戈高地与卡桑热低地之间一条林木覆盖的高原走廊，宽扎河谷东赴宽果河的道路在此转向。1444年，这里的姆本杜村落由本地索巴管辖，处在恩东戈恩戈拉松散的势力圈内；欧洲事物尚未抵达——葡萄牙人进入宽扎河流域还要等一个多世纪。

1618年，受雇随葡萄牙洗劫恩东戈的卡桑吉因班加拉战团脱离葡军，蹂躏马坦巴，约1620年在宽果河上游定居立国。这条走廊是卡桑吉的西部门户，久而久之又成为葡属要塞区安巴卡与卡桑吉集市之间的主要商道：庞贝罗商人驱赶脚夫经此把奴隶和象牙运往罗安达，整个18世纪，沿途村落或靠供应商队为生，或为躲避掳掠而逃亡。

en:
Yaka is the middle Kwango country between the Kwango and Wamba rivers, a belt of forest, savanna, fishing streams and hunting grounds. In 1444 its villages were ruled by local chiefs and clan elders, with kinship and inheritance carrying strong matrilineal ties. Farmers cleared the upland soils, hunters took game with dogs, and carvers made masks, figures and slit drums for ceremonies that linked the living to the ancestors. The lands lay beyond the direct provincial government of Mbanza-Kongo, yet Bakongo already knew their eastern neighbours as formidable fighters.

In 1568 raiders from the eastern border overran Mbata and drove Álvaro I from Mbanza-Kongo; the Portuguese called armed bands from several peoples Jaga. About 600 Portuguese matchlockmen helped restore Álvaro, and the raiders were pushed out of Kongo by the mid-1570s, though they remained a power on the frontier. During the seventeenth century Lunda-led lineages moving west married local Kongo women, adopted Kiyaka and merged with older clans to form the historic Yaka kingdom. Yaka companies later hired into Kongo's dynastic wars, while captives were drawn toward Atlantic markets; after the 1665–1709 civil war, this armed frontier remained only loosely tied to the restored Manikongo.
zh:
雅卡位于宽果河与万巴河之间的宽果河中游地带，林莽、稀树草原、渔场和猎场交错。1444年时，这里的村落由地方酋长和氏族长老掌管，亲属与继承带有浓厚的母系色彩。人们在高地焚荒耕作，带猎犬猎取野兽，工匠雕刻面具、人像和缝鼓，用于沟通生者与祖先的仪式。此地不受姆班扎刚果的行省机构直接管辖，但西边的刚果人早已知道，这些东邻是强悍善战的人。

1568年，来自东部边境的武装群体冲垮姆巴塔，把阿尔瓦罗一世赶出姆班扎刚果；葡萄牙人用贾加一名称呼多个族群的武装。约六百名葡萄牙火枪手帮助阿尔瓦罗复位，到1570年代中期，入侵者被逐出刚果，却仍是边境上的一股强大势力。十七世纪，西迁的隆达谱系首领与本地刚果氏族通婚，采用基亚卡语，逐渐融合成历史上的雅卡王国。后来的刚果王朝战争中常有雅卡佣兵，战俘也被输往大西洋市场；1665至1709年内战之后，这条武装边地与复位的马尼刚果之间始终只有松散联系。

en:
Nunu is the watery forest country where the Kasai meets the Fimi below Lake Mai-Ndombe, with Mushie as its riverine meeting place. Its BaNunu inhabitants farmed the banks, fished the flooded channels and built the canoes that carried warriors, tolls and fine cloth along the Lukenie, Kasai, Kwilu and Wamba. Oral king lists place the formation of Mwene Muji just after 1400 under rulers titled Ntote; in 1444 it was a young river power. At its height it dominated Lower Kasai trade and may have extended into parts of the later Kuba lands. Its authority rested more on canoe landings, river navies and market villages than on broad territorial conquest.

Filippo Pigafetta's account of 1591 gave the outside world its first written name for Monemugi, though geographers long misplaced the polity far toward East Africa. In the late sixteenth century its river power and cloth trade were still known as far west as Kongo's eastern province of Mbata. The early seventeenth century broke that unity: Boma, Yaka and Bozanga split away, while around 1625 Shyaam a-Mbul united the Kuba chiefdoms to the southeast and founded the Bushoong-led Kuba federation. As Kuba power grew along the Kasai in the eighteenth century, Nunu remained a world of fishermen, canoe-men and forest markets, paying allegiance where river power demanded and preserving older local rites beneath the rival claims of Mwene Muji and Kuba.
zh:
努努是迈恩东贝湖下游、开赛河与菲米河相会的水网森林，穆希是这里的河运交会地。巴努努人在河岸耕作，在泛水河道捕鱼，并制造独木舟；战船、商税和精致布匹沿卢凯尼河、开赛河、奎卢河与万巴河往来。口传王表把姆韦内·穆吉的形成放在1400年之后不久，统治者称「恩托特」。1444年，它还是一个年轻的水上政权；鼎盛时它控制下开赛贸易，势力可能扩及后来库巴地区的一部分。它的权威更多依赖舟船码头、河上水军和集市村落，而不是广阔的陆地领土。

1591年，菲利波·皮加费塔的记述让外部世界第一次以「莫内穆吉」之名知道这个政体，但地理学家曾长期把它误放到东非。十六世纪末，它的水上势力和布匹贸易仍为远在西方的刚果东部省份姆巴塔所知。十七世纪初，统一走向瓦解，博马、雅卡和博赞加相继分立；约1625年，希亚姆·阿-姆布尔在东南统一库巴诸酋长国，建立由布雄人主导的库巴联邦。十八世纪库巴沿开赛河扩张时，努努仍是渔夫、舟师和森林集市的世界：哪里的水上强权征索贡赋，他们便向哪里臣服，同时在姆韦内·穆吉与库巴的争夺之间保留着更古老的地方仪式。

en:
Kumbana takes its name from the title Mwata Kumbana, but in 1444 that office did not yet exist. The country between the Lutshiko and Loange rivers, southeast of later Kikwit, was a forest-and-savanna borderland of small Bantu villages, fishing waters and fields. Decentralized Pende groups would enter the region during their seventeenth-century migrations, before Lunda power followed from Musumba. Tracks from the rivers already pointed toward the Kwilu, Kwango and Kasai, but no paramount chief yet ruled the land.

About 1650 Mukelenge Mutombo, a Lunda leader from Musumba, settled at the confluence of the Loange and Lutshiko, dislodged Pende newcomers and founded a chiefdom under the title Mwatha Kombana, meaning 'one who gives generously'; positional succession made the title outlive its first holder. His Shakatwala clansmen continued westward to Mwe Nzila. By the eighteenth century Mwene Putu Kasongo's Yaka state controlled the route from Ambriz through the Kiamfu's capital to Kombana. Slaves and ivory moved along it, while Kombana's Lunda elite adopted the Gipende language and customs yet kept authority delegated from the Mwata Yamvo.
zh:
库巴纳得名于姆瓦塔·库巴纳头衔，但在1444年，这个职位尚未出现。卢奇科河与洛安盖河之间、后来基奎特东南的这片土地，是林莽与稀树草原交错的边疆，散布着班图人的小村庄、渔场和田地。17世纪，分散而无统一王权的巴彭德人迁入此地，随后隆达势力才从穆松巴跟进。河畔小路已通往奎卢河、宽果河和开赛河方向，却还没有高居各村之上的统治者。

约1650年，来自穆松巴的隆达首领穆凯伦盖·穆通博在洛安盖河与卢奇科河汇流处定居，逐走新来的巴彭德人，建立酋长国，并采用姆瓦塔·孔巴纳头衔，意为「慷慨施予者」；通过职位继承制，这个头衔在首任统治者之后延续下来。他的沙卡特瓦拉族人继续向西，建立姆韦·恩齐拉。到18世纪，姆韦内·普图·卡松戈的雅卡国家控制着从安布里什经基阿姆富都城通往孔巴纳的商路，奴隶和象牙沿此往来；孔巴纳的隆达上层改习吉彭德语和风俗，却仍承认自己的权力来自姆瓦塔·扬沃。

en:
Munene is the river corridor above the Kasai-Tshikapa confluence, where falls and rapids forced canoe traffic to unload and cross the bank. In 1444 the country was not yet the later Lunda chiefdom remembered as Mai Munene. Tufia, Tupokoto, Kete and Bashilange villagers farmed the savanna edges, fished the Kasai and Tshikapa, hunted in gallery forest and traded at the portages; village heads and custodians of the land held authority where the river passage mattered. Kuba power still belonged to the future, for the Kuba federation would only be united in the seventeenth century.

The Lunda reach came after 1700, with the push up the Tshikapa valley around the middle of the eighteenth century. A commander named Mujinga had already failed against the Tufia before the leader Mai Munene subdued them and brought some Tupokoto, Kete and Bashilange communities under his rule. His attempt to conquer the Pende failed when their chief Kombo defeated his forces and preserved Pende autonomy. Mai's seat near the great Kasai falls became the capital of a state bearing his own title; across the Loange another Lunda-founded chiefdom, Mwaka Kumbana, completed the pair described in regional tradition. The fallside market soon drew caravans from the Kwango, exchanging captives and forest produce for cloth, beads and other goods brought from Angolan markets. Strong Luba influence later touched the court, yet in 1821 Mai Munene remained an interior river market ruled by its own chiefs rather than a European post.
zh:
穆内内是开赛河与奇卡帕河汇流处上游的河运走廊；瀑布和急流迫使独木舟在此卸货，行人货物必须上岸转运。1444年时，后来以「迈伊穆内内」为名的隆达系酋长国尚未建立。图菲亚、图波科托、克特和巴希兰格人的村社在稀树草原边缘耕作，在开赛河与奇卡帕河捕鱼，在走廊森林中狩猎，并在转运点交换物产。掌握河津要地的，是各村首领和守护土地权威的仪式长老。库巴强权也还属于未来，因为库巴联邦要到十七世纪才完成联合。

隆达势力在1700年以后抵达此地，这次沿奇卡帕河谷的推进约在十八世纪中叶。将领穆金加先已败于图菲亚人，随后首领迈伊穆内内征服图菲亚，并把部分图波科托、克特和巴希兰格社群置于治下。他试图征服彭德人，却被彭德首领孔博率军击败，彭德人保住了自治。迈伊在开赛大瀑布附近设立驻地，这个地点后来成为以其称号命名的酋长国都城；在洛安热河彼岸，另有一个隆达人建立的姆瓦卡·昆巴纳酋长国，与它并称口传中的两个小邦。瀑布市场很快吸引来自宽果河的商队，他们用布匹、珠子和安哥拉市场转来的货物，交换人口与森林物产。后来宫廷又受到强烈卢巴影响，但直到1821年，迈伊穆内内仍是由本地酋长统治的内陆河市，而不是欧洲人的据点。

en:
Kuba is the river country between the Sankuru and Kasai, near the Lulua bend. In 1444 Bushong-speaking villagers, Kete, Leele and other neighbouring peoples lived under separate chiefs rather than a single crown. Its homesteads drew wealth from the rivers, farms and raffia palm groves: men wove plain raffia cloth, while women embroidered geometric patterns and cut the stitches into a velvet-like pile for ceremonial skirts, headdresses and tribute cloths.

About 1625 Shyaam a-Mbul a Ngoong, a leader tradition connects with the Pende and Kongo kingdoms to the west, returned to the Sankuru country, took power in a chiefdom and drew the separate communities under one government. The new kingdom was ruled from Mushenge by a Bushoong king, the nyim, advised by a court council representing its peoples. Maize, tobacco, cassava and beans added to its prosperity, and Kuba nobles patronized carved figures and elaborate raffia textiles. Early in the eighteenth century Kuete M'bogi extended Kuba power south along the Kasai; Koto Nche continued that expansion later in the same century, leaving the inland kingdom wealthy and comparatively sheltered from the Atlantic slave trade reaching the coast.
zh:
库巴是桑库鲁河与开赛河之间、邻近卢卢阿河河曲的河间之地。1444年，使用布雄语的村民以及克特人、利利人等邻近族群分属各自首领，还没有一个共戴的王权。村落依靠河汊、农田和酒椰棕榈林积累财富：男子织造素面酒椰布，妇女绣出几何纹样，并把线脚剪短成天鹅绒般的绒面，用来制作仪式裙、头饰和贡赋布。

约1625年，曾与西方彭德和刚果两王国有所渊源的首领希亚姆·姆布尔·恩贡（Shyaam a-Mbul a Ngoong）回到桑库鲁一带，夺取一个酋邦的权力，并把分散社群纳入同一政府。新王国以穆申盖为中心，由布雄氏族的国王统治，代表各族群的宫廷会议参与议政。玉米、烟草、木薯和菜豆的传播增加了当地财富，库巴贵族开始赞助雕像和精美的酒椰织物。18世纪初，库埃特·姆博吉把库巴势力沿开赛河向南扩展；科托·恩切在同一世纪继续扩张，使这个内陆王国富足起来，也比沿海王国更少受到大西洋奴隶贸易的直接冲击。

en:
The Songye country is rolling savanna between the Sankuru and its tributary the Lubilash in the west and the upper Lualaba in the east, cut through by the Lomami. Its Bantu-speaking people lived in farming villages grouped into some forty chiefdoms, each under a sacred chief advised by a council of elders; the western groups called themselves Kalebwe or Yembe, while those east of the Lomami called themselves Songye. Their smiths smelted local iron and forged axes prized across the Luba world, and hunters and farmers carried dried meat, palm oil and grain to the river markets. Their speech was close to Luba, and in 1444 the chiefs of the upper Sankuru looked to the Luba-speaking kings of Kalundwe, their powerful kinsmen to the south.

For centuries the Songye kept their loose chiefdoms while the Luba empire to the south-east grew into the dominant power of the region. Early in the 19th century, among the headwaters of the Congo, the Luba set up Buki, a client 'fire kingdom' built on the scattered Songye chiefdoms and straddling both banks of the river, whose ruler received the sacred royal embers and guarded Luba's northern frontier. The bond lasted only a reign, for the fire was held to die with the king who had given it.
zh:
松吉耶之地是一片起伏的稀树草原，西起桑库鲁河及其支流卢比拉什河，东抵卢阿拉巴河上游，洛马米河纵贯其间。说班图语的居民以农耕村落为单位，分属约四十个酋邦，各有一位神圣酋长，由长老议事会辅佐；洛马米河以西的群体自称卡莱布韦或延贝，河东的群体才自称松吉耶。当地铁匠用本地铁砂锻斧，斧头在卢巴各部远近闻名，猎户和农户把肉干、棕榈油和谷物运往沿河集市。他们的语言与卢巴语相近，1444年时，桑库鲁河上游的酋长们都仰仗南方同族的强国——卡隆兑的卢巴语国王。

此后几百年间，松吉耶人保持着松散的酋邦，而东南方的卢巴王国逐渐成为这一带的霸主。19世纪初，卢巴人在刚果河源头一带众多分散的松吉耶酋邦之间设立了附庸「火王国」布基，地跨大河两岸；其统治者从卢巴国王手中接过神圣的王廷火种，为卢巴镇守北境。这种纽带只维系一代——按卢巴礼制，赐予火种的国王一死，火便随之熄灭，封邑的名分也就此终结。

en:
Mpasu is the high savanna and gallery-forest country of the Basala Mpasu, better known as Salampasu, east of the Kasai and around the western headwaters of the Lulua. In 1444 they were not subjects of Musumba: their patrilineal villages had no king, and successful hunter-raiders held authority through personal prestige. The mungongo warrior societies crossed clan lines, while women worked the fields and men treated hunting and warfare as honoured callings. To the south lay the small Ruund communes, with Kete, Lwalwa and Mbala groups sharing the broken country to the north and west.

After the Lunda kingdom took shape around 1665, the Sala Mpasu became its first major military test. Nawej, ruler from about 1695, invaded their country and built a fortress there but could not subdue its loose alliances; a Kanyok attack forced him to withdraw, and Kanyok forces killed him. In the 1720s Lunda armies under Mai pushed across the Kasai, while Luba and Lulua pressure also tightened from the north. Mpasu communities answered with their graded mungongo initiations, the fibre idangani, wooden kasangu and copper-covered mukinka masks marking warrior rank and helping the villages defend their autonomy.
zh:
姆帕苏是巴萨拉·姆帕苏人（更常称萨兰帕苏人）的高地稀树草原与廊林之地，位于开赛河以东、卢卢阿河西源一带。1444年，他们并非穆松巴的属民：各父系村庄没有国王，靠狩猎和战功树立声望的首领凭个人威望行事。蒙贡戈战士会社跨越氏族界限，妇女耕作农田，男子则以狩猎和作战为荣。南面是当时仍分散的鲁恩德村社，北面和西面的破碎地带则杂居着凯特、卢卢瓦和姆巴拉等群体。

隆达王国约1665年成形后，萨拉·姆帕苏成为它第一场重大战争的考验。约1695年即位的纳韦吉入侵此地，修筑要塞，却无法征服这些松散联盟；卡尼奥克人的进攻迫使他撤兵，纳韦吉也死于卡尼奥克军队之手。18世纪20年代，马伊率领隆达军队越过开赛河，卢巴和卢卢阿自北方施加的压力也同时增强。姆帕苏各村社则以分级的蒙贡戈入会式回应：纤维制的伊丹加尼面具、木制卡桑古面具和包铜穆金卡面具标示战士等级，帮助这些小村庄维系自治。

en:
The savanna between the upper Kasai and the Lualaba is the heartland of the Lunda, or Ruund, a Bantu people of millet fields, fishing camps and oil-palm groves. In the mid-fifteenth century they still lived in small village communes along the Kalanyi River under their own headmen, honouring the high god Nzambi through the spirits of their ancestors, and the outside world valued their country chiefly for its ivory. Kalundwe to the east, Lwena and Kanongesha to the west were then still independent neighbours.

Lunda tradition traces the kingdom to the marriage of Queen Lueji to Tshibinda Ilunga, a prince from the Luba country, whose son became the first Mwata Yamvo around 1665; Nawej reigned from about 1695. The Mwata Yamvo held court at Musumba, a fenced capital of earthen walls, a moat and paved courtyards. In the 1730s-1750s Lunda armies overran the surrounding country, defeated peoples were resettled at Musumba, and cadet dynasties came to rule at Kanongesha and as far afield as Kazembe on the Luapula. Lunda caravans carried ivory and captives west to Portuguese traders on the Atlantic coast and east to Arab and Swahili merchants, the traffic on which the empire's wealth rested down to the nineteenth century.
zh:
开赛河上游与卢阿拉巴河之间的稀树草原，是隆达人（又称鲁恩德人）的故土。这个班图语族群种粟、捕鱼、采收油棕，15世纪中叶仍以卡兰伊河沿岸的村社为单位，各有首领，通过祖先之灵敬奉至高神恩赞比；外界看重这片土地，主要是为了这里出产的象牙。当时东面的卡隆韦，西面的卢埃纳和卡农盖沙，都还是各自独立的邻族。

隆达传说把王国的开端归于女王卢埃吉嫁给来自卢巴之地的王子奇宾达·伊隆加，他们的儿子约在1665年成为第一位姆瓦塔·扬沃；纳韦吉约从1695年起在位。姆瓦塔·扬沃在穆松巴设朝，这座王都围有土墙和壕沟，内有铺砌的庭院。18世纪30至50年代，隆达军队征服四周，被击败的部族被迁置到穆松巴，支系王公则被封往卡农盖沙，远至卢阿普拉河畔的卡申贝。隆达商队把象牙和俘虏向西运到大西洋沿岸卖给葡萄牙商人，向东卖给阿拉伯和斯瓦西里商人，帝国的财富正是建立在这条商路之上。

en:
Lwena is the river-cut savanna between the western Ruund country and the routes leading toward the upper Zambezi, home of the people more widely called Luvale and in Angola also Lwena or Luena. In 1444 they were close kin of the Lunda but lived under their own matrilineal village headmen, with no paramount chief. Men fished and hunted in the Yanga hunters' association, and elephant ivory from the woodland drew paths toward Chokwe and Lunda neighbours.

Luvale tradition traces the split from the Lunda to Queen Lueji's marriage with the Luba prince Tshibinda Ilunga, after which her brothers Chinguli and Chinyama led their followers southwest. About 1747 Chinyama cha Mukwamayi founded the Kakenge chieftainship near the Lumbala stream in Angola. During the eighteenth century the Lwena became the first Upper Zambezi people to receive Ovimbundu traders from Angola. They bought guns, cloth and jewelry with captives, raided neighbouring peoples for fresh supplies and levied payments on caravans, turning their local chiefs into increasingly powerful brokers on the Atlantic ivory and slave routes.
zh:
卢文纳是鲁恩德故地以西、通向上赞比西道路之间的河川稀树草原，居民更常见的称呼是卢瓦勒人，在安哥拉也称卢文纳或卢埃纳。1444年，他们与隆达人血缘相近，却由各自母系村庄的首领治理，没有共主。男子捕鱼并在扬加猎手会中狩猎；林地象牙把小路引向绍奎和隆达邻人之地。

卢瓦勒传说把他们同隆达的分裂追溯到女王卢埃吉嫁给卢巴王子奇宾达·伊隆加，此后她的兄弟钦古利和奇尼亚马率部众西南方迁去。约1747年，奇尼亚马·查·姆克瓦马伊在安哥拉的伦巴拉溪附近建立卡肯盖酋长国。18世纪，卢文纳人成为上赞比西一带最早接待来自安哥拉的奥文本杜商人的族群。他们用俘虏购买枪支、布匹和珠宝，又袭掠邻族补充货源，并向商队征收费用；各地酋长由此成为大西洋象牙与奴隶商路上日益重要的中间人。

en:
The Chokwe country is the rolling miombo woodland on the watershed between the Kasai and the upper Zambezi, where Angola, Congo and Zambia now meet. The Chokwe are a Bantu people whose own traditions bring them south with the Lunda migrations. They lived by shifting cultivation, hunting and fishing, the village year turning on the rains and the long dry season; they were carvers as well, of masks and ancestor figures charged with the power of spirits and the chase, and their smiths forged the local iron into hoes and spears.

In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the twelve Chokwe clans were drawn into the Lunda Empire and took service with its nobles, but disputes over tribute ended in a breakaway. The seceded clans prospered on their hunting grounds and resources, ivory above all, and grew richer than the neighbouring peoples. The slave trade of the eighteenth century divided them as well: some Chokwe were carried off to the coasts while others kept slaves of their own. By the close of the eighteenth century the breakaway clans had made themselves the rising power of these borderlands, richer and more cohesive than the tribute-empire could safely ignore.
zh:
绍奎人的土地是开赛河与赞比西河上游分水岭上连绵的米翁博林地，地处今安哥拉、刚果与赞比亚三国交界一带。绍奎人是班图人的一支，口述传统称他们随隆达南迁而来。他们以轮作、狩猎和捕鱼为生，村落的岁时随雨季和漫长旱季轮转；他们也善雕刻，面具和祖先像被赋予神灵与狩猎之力；铁匠把当地的铁锻成锄头和长矛。

17至18世纪，绍奎十二氏族被纳入隆达帝国，为隆达贵族服役；围绕贡赋的一连串争执最终使他们脱离隆达寡头。独立出去的氏族凭借猎场和物产致富，尤以象牙为重，比四邻各族更为殷实。18世纪的奴隶贸易也撕裂着绍奎社会：一部分绍奎人被掳走、贩卖到海岸，另一些人则自己蓄奴。到18世纪末，这些脱离宗主的氏族已成为边地上崛起的力量，其富庶和凝聚力令那个贡赋帝国无法再等闲视之。

en:
Ishindi is the floodplain of the upper Zambezi and the woodlands around it, the headwater country between the Lwena lands and the Kaonde plateau. Before the Lunda came it belonged to the Mbwela, scattered Bantu villagers who fished the plain, planted the raised banks and hunted the woodland, with little rank beyond their own headmen. In 1444 there was no court in the land, only the Mbwela fishing and farming villages on the floodplain; the rising Lunda empire still lay far to the north, beyond the horizons of the upper river.

The Lunda reached the upper Zambezi in the eighteenth century. Among the chiefs sent out from the musumba of the Mwata Yamvo was Ishindi, the paramount's firstborn son, charged with extending the dynasty to the south-west. His columns overcame the Mbwela and fixed the chiefdom's capital at Zambezi, bringing the floodplain into the Lunda commonwealth as a tributary land. The Lunda brought cassava and iron hoes, and under their rule the upper river joined the long-distance traffic that carried ivory and slaves back to the musumba.
zh:
伊辛迪位于赞比西河上游洪泛平原及其周围林地，是卢韦纳之地与卡翁德高原之间的河源之国。隆达人到来之前，这里属于姆布维拉人：散居的班图村民在平原捕鱼，在高起的河岸种植，在林地狩猎，除本村头人之外几乎没有别的等级。1444年，这片土地上没有宫廷，只有洪泛平原上姆布维拉人的渔村和农村；正在兴起的隆达帝国还远在北方，不在上游河民的视野之内。

18世纪，隆达人到达赞比西河上游。在姆瓦塔·亚姆沃从穆松巴派出的扩张首领中，有宗主的长子伊辛迪，受命向西南扩展王统。他的队伍征服姆布维拉人，把酋长国的都城设在赞比西，洪泛平原作为纳贡之地并入隆达共同体。隆达人带来了木薯和铁锄，在他们治下，这条上游河流也加入了把象牙和奴隶输往穆松巴的长途贸易。

en:
West of the Upemba Depression the wooded savanna runs toward the Kasai, the country of Luba-speaking farmers and cattle-keepers whose sacred kings held court at Kalundwe. They grew grain, herded on the open ridges and worked iron after the manner of Upemba, ruling through ancestor cults and the ritual of the royal fire. The Kanyok country to the north-west may once have formed part of the larger kingdom of Kalundwe. In 1444 Kalundwe lay as a buffer between the Luba kings in the Upemba marshes and the growing Lunda empire to the south-west, courted and coveted by both.

Oral tradition tells how, early in the 18th century, the Kanyok ruler Shimat Citend, or his son Cibend Kadwo, refused tribute and led the Kanyok out of Kalundwe's rule; Kanyok armies then invaded Lunda and killed the Mwata Yamvo Nawej, whose father, Lunda tradition said, had himself come from Kalundwe. After 1700 the Luba empire expanded on every side, and Kalundwe and Kanyok became the wall between Luba and Lunda. Early in the 19th century the Luba kings sent army after army west to make both buffer kingdoms their tributaries, and every attempt failed; Kalundwe kept its sacred court and its freedom between the two empires.
zh:
乌彭巴洼地以西，林地稀树草原向开赛河方向缓缓抬升，这里是卡隆兑——一群说卢巴语、种谷养牛者的国度，他们的神圣国王在卡隆兑设廷。当地人种植谷物，在开阔的山脊上放牧，按乌彭巴传下来的法子冶铁，借祖先崇拜和王廷圣火之礼维系统治。西北方的卡尼奥克之地可能曾是较大的卡隆兑王国的一部分。1444年时，卡隆兑夹在乌彭巴沼泽的卢巴诸王与西南方兴起的隆达帝国之间，是两边都想拉拢、也都想吞并的缓冲国。

口述传统说，18世纪初，卡尼奥克首领希马特·奇特登（一说他的儿子齐本德·卡德沃）拒绝纳贡，率卡尼奥克脱离卡隆兑的统治；卡尼奥克军队随后攻入隆达，杀死了姆瓦塔·亚姆沃纳韦吉——按隆达传说，纳韦吉的父亲正是从卡隆兑出走的。1700年以后，卢巴帝国四面扩张，卡隆兑与卡尼奥克成了横在卢巴与隆达之间的一道墙。19世纪初，卢巴国王一再派军西征，要把这两个缓冲王国都降为附庸，却每次都告失败；卡隆兑得以在两大帝国之间保住自己的神圣王廷和独立。

en:
Luba lies among the lakes, marshes and grasslands of the Upemba Depression. Iron-working farmers had settled there by the fifth century, and over the following centuries Luba villagers combined farming, fishing and metalwork, drying fish for the savanna trade and sending iron and salt outward in exchange for copper, beads and cowries. Chiefs who guarded the channels and lake crossings collected tribute in fish, game and harvests. In 1444 the villages of the future Luba kingdom were already bound by these markets, ancestor spirits and sacred lords of the land, though a single royal authority was still taking shape.

During the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, Luba authority hardened around the mulopwe, a sacred ruler whose court balanced royal power with a council of elders and regional chiefs. Control of southern salt and iron workings helped consolidate the kingdom in the eighteenth century, while marriage alliances tied conquered lineages to the ruling house. Lunda power to the southeast limited regular contact with Portuguese traders from Angola. Around 1800 the Kanyok rejected Luba authority and drove back an invasion, while Ilunga Sungu extended Luba influence eastward; when he died in 1810, his royal court became a kitenta, a sacred village where his spirit continued to guard the state.
zh:
卢巴位于乌朋巴洼地的湖泊、沼泽与草原之间。早在5世纪，掌握冶铁技术的农民已在此定居；此后数个世纪里，卢巴村落兼营农耕、渔猎和金属加工，把鱼干输往草原，又以铁器和食盐交换铜料、珠子与宝螺。控制水道和湖泊渡口的首领向村落征收渔猎与谷物贡赋。1444年，日后卢巴王国的各村已由这些市场、祖先神灵和掌管土地的神圣首领联系在一起，但统一王权仍在成形。

16至17世纪，卢巴的权力围绕神圣国王「姆洛普韦」稳固下来，王宫以王族和长老、地方首领组成的会议平衡王权。18世纪，对南方盐矿和铁矿的控制帮助王国完成整合，联姻也把被征服的世系纳入统治家族。东南方的隆达势力限制了安哥拉葡萄牙商人与卢巴的经常往来。约1800年，卡尼奥克人摆脱卢巴统治并击退其入侵，而伊隆加·松古则向东扩张卢巴势力；他于1810年去世后，其王宫成为「基滕塔」，也就是继续供奉其神灵、守护国家的神圣村落。

en:
Upemba is the marshy bowl of the upper Lualaba, where lakes Kisale and Upemba break into channels, floating reed beds and fishing villages. Luba-speaking farmers and ironworkers had settled the lakeshores by about 800, growing sorghum and millet and trading dried fish, salt and iron tools for copper brought from the southern copperlands. By 1444 the lakeshore communities around Lake Kisale, where Kikondja stands, lived by fishing, farming and metalworking; local lords held authority over groups of villages.

Oral traditions tell of Nkongolo and Kalala Ilunga in the origins of the Luba kingdom, whose founding date remains disputed. During the seventeenth century it grew from a lake-basin power into an empire built on sacred kingship, tribute and councils. Kikondja, Kalundwe and Kanyok were among the neighbouring Luba states brought within this expanding order. The lake villagers continued to supply dried fish and salt to savanna markets, while smiths drew in copper and charcoal and regional trade carried beads and cowries from the Indian Ocean. By the eighteenth century the rulers at Kikondja had become part of the wider Luba political world rather than an isolated lake chiefdom.
zh:
乌彭巴是卢阿拉巴河上游的沼泽盆地，基萨莱湖与乌彭巴湖在此分出条条水道、浮动芦洲和渔村。约800年时，说卢巴语的农民和冶铁者已在湖岸定居，种植高粱和粟，用干鱼、盐和铁制工具交换南方铜矿产区的铜。到1444年，基孔贾所在的基萨莱湖沿岸社群以渔业、农耕和金属加工为生，地方领主管辖着一组组村落。

口述传统将卢巴王国的起源与恩孔戈洛、卡拉拉·伊隆加联系起来，其建国年代则众说纷纭。17世纪，卢巴由湖区政权扩张为以神圣王权、贡赋和议事会维系的帝国。基孔贾、卡隆兑和卡尼奥克等邻近卢巴邦国先后被纳入这一扩张秩序。湖岸村落继续向草原市场供应干鱼和盐，铁匠则输入铜和木炭，区域贸易又把来自印度洋的珠子和海贝带到此地。到18世纪，基孔贾统治者已成为更广阔卢巴政治世界的一部分，而不再是孤立的湖区小邦。

en:
Hemba is the country of rolling savanna bounded by the Lukuga River in the north and the Luvua in the south, where the Lualaba flows north past Kongolo. In 1444 these valleys formed the eastern march of the Luba kingdom then taking shape in the Upemba depression, and their villages answered to local chiefs rather than to any single king.

The Hemba moved east into the Lualaba valley from the Luba empire, probably after 1600. They traded salt for iron hoes from the Luba heartland and wore raphia cloth made by the Songye and brought through Luba middlemen. Around 1800 the expansion of King Ilunga Sungu made the southern Hemba tributaries of Luba, governed through a 'fire king' who stood in place of the Luba sovereign. On Ilunga Sungu's death the Hemba broke away, and his successor Kumwimbe Ngombe had to fight several campaigns to recover the eastern lands. He set up a client kingdom joining the Hemba villages of the Lukushi River valley, which held the smaller states of the region under Luba dominance for decades afterward.
zh:
亨巴北界卢库加河、南至卢武阿河，卢阿拉巴河向北流经孔戈洛，是一片起伏的稀树草原。1444年，这些河谷是正在乌彭巴洼地兴起的卢巴王国的东陲，各村落听命于本地头人，并没有共同的君王。

亨巴人约在1600年以后从卢巴帝国东迁至卢阿拉巴河谷。他们用盐换取卢巴腹地的铁锄，穿着松格人织成、经卢巴中间商转来的酒椰布。1800年前后，国王伊隆加·松古向外扩张，南部的亨巴人沦为卢巴属民，由一位代表卢巴君主的「火王」管辖。伊隆加·松古死后亨巴人脱离控制，继位的库姆温贝·恩贡贝几经征战才收复东方疆土。他把卢库希河流域的亨巴各村组成一个附庸王国，在此后数十年间借此维持卢巴对当地各小邦的支配。

en:
Luapula takes its name from the river that drains the Bangweulu wetlands, runs west and north through a broad floodplain, and enters Lake Mweru. In 1444 this was Shila country, a chain of farming villages, fishing camps and river crossings between the wetlands, the Mweru fisheries and the copper-bearing lands to the west. Its people grew grain on the fertile valley soils, dried fish for trade, and occupied one of the natural corridors linking the Luba and Lunda worlds with the peoples east of the river.

Around 1740 a Luba-Lunda following under the Kazembe line moved east under Kanyembo Mpemba, crossed the Luapula at Matanda and conquered the Shila, placing Luba and Lunda titleholders over the valley. The new kingdom grew rich from Mweru and Mofwe fisheries, farm produce and Katangan copper, and its rulers could field large armies by the late eighteenth century. Portuguese expeditions reached the court in 1796 and 1798, when Francisco José de Lacerda e Almeida died there after waiting for trade talks, and the pombeiros Pedro João Baptista and Amaro José followed in 1802. None secured the Angola-to-Mozambique route Lisbon wanted, while Swahili and inland traders continued to exchange cloth and beads for copper and ivory.
zh:
卢阿普拉得名于同名河流；河水从班韦乌卢沼泽流出，先向西再向北穿过广阔洪泛平原，最终注入姆韦鲁湖。1444年，这里是希拉人的土地，村落、渔场和渡口串联在沼泽、姆韦鲁渔场与西方含铜地带之间。当地人在肥沃谷地种植谷物，把鱼干用于贸易，也据守着一条天然走廊，连接卢巴、隆达世界与河东各族。

约1740年，卡曾贝一系的卢巴-隆达部众在坎延博·姆彭巴率领下东进，在马坦达渡过卢阿普拉河，征服希拉人，并以卢巴、隆达贵族统治谷地。新王国凭姆韦鲁湖和莫夫韦潟湖的渔业、农产品与加丹加铜矿致富，到18世纪末已能出动大军。葡萄牙使团先后于1796年和1798年抵达宫廷，方济各·若泽·德·拉塞尔达-埃·阿尔梅达在等待通商谈判时客死此地；商贩佩德罗·若昂·巴普蒂斯塔和阿马罗·若泽又于1802年前来。他们都未能为里斯本取得连通安哥拉与莫桑比克的商路，斯瓦希里商人和内陆商人则继续以布匹、珠子交换铜和象牙。

en:
Lualaba is the upper course of the Congo's greatest feeder. Its headwaters rise near Musofi and Lubumbashi, beside the Zambian Copperbelt, and the river runs north through Shaba toward the Upemba marshes. In 1444 Luba-speaking farmers, fishers and smiths occupied the upper valley and its crossings. They worked iron, dried fish, evaporated salt and bartered these goods for copper from the southern workings.

The Luba state that coalesced around 1585 drew the upper valley into its widening network of sacred kingship, tribute and councils, and Luba power reached its height in the eighteenth century. Around 1740 the Luba-Lunda followers of the Kazembe line crossed the Luapula to the east; by the late eighteenth century their tributary claims stretched back west to the Lualaba, which separated Kazembe's lands from Mwata Yamvo's Lunda power and other Luba kingdoms. Salt, copper, iron and fish moved along this contested border, giving local chiefs their place in the court's hierarchy. The Portuguese embassies of 1798 and 1802 found Kazembe wealthy and ceremonially powerful, but they never won control of the inland routes running toward this river.
zh:
卢阿拉巴是刚果河最大支流的上游。其源头在赞比亚铜带旁的穆索菲和卢本巴希附近，河水向北穿过沙巴，流向乌彭巴沼泽。1444年，说卢巴语的农民、渔民和铁匠居住在上游河谷及各渡口一带。他们冶铁、晒鱼、煮盐，用这些物产交换南方矿区的铜。

约1585年凝聚成形的卢巴国家，以神圣王权、贡赋和议事会把上游河谷纳入日益扩大的网络，卢巴势力在18世纪达到鼎盛。约1740年，卡曾贝一系的卢巴-隆达部众东渡卢阿普拉河；到18世纪后期，他们的贡赋势力已向西伸至卢阿拉巴河，此河也成为卡曾贝与姆瓦塔·亚姆武的隆达政权及其他卢巴王国之间的分界。盐、铜、铁和鱼沿这条争夺中的边界流通，使地方首领在王庭秩序中占有一席之地。1798年和1802年的葡萄牙使节看到卡曾贝富庶而礼仪森严，却始终未能控制通向这条河的内陆商路。

en:
In 1444 the plateau later called Ulubemba, between the Luapula, upper Chambeshi and Lake Bangweulu, was a patchwork of small Bantu farming villages and wooded clearings. Its people kept goats and sheep, worked millet fields, and looked to village heads rather than a paramount court. The Bemba rulers who would give the country its name were still tied to the Luba world west of the Luapula, where their royal Abena Ng'andu clan carried the crocodile as its totem.

Bemba traditions recall a sixteenth- or seventeenth-century movement led by Nkole and Chiti, sons connected with the Luba ruler Mukulumpe. After crossing the Luapula before 1740, the migrants settled successively near Lakes Mweru and Bangweulu and along the Chambeshi; an omen at the Milando River fixed Ng'wena as their first capital. By the late eighteenth century the twenty-second Chitimukulu, Mukuka wa Malekano, was driving the Lungu from the Kasama country and enfeoffing his brother Chitundu as Mwamba I of Ituna. Under Chitimukulu Chilyamafwa expansion continued until 1808, when Bemba arms pushed the Mambwe toward Mpanda and created a new vassal kingdom there. From 1810 the long rule of Chileshe Chepela carried Bemba power deeper into the surrounding plateau.
zh:
1444年，卢阿普拉河、尚贝西河上游与班韦乌卢湖之间后来被称为乌卢本巴的高原，还只是一片片林地开垦地和小班图农耕村落。人们饲养山羊和绵羊，种植黍类，听从村落头人而不是最高王庭。后来为这片土地命名的本巴统治者当时仍与卢阿普拉河以西的卢巴世界相连，王族阿本纳·恩甘杜氏族以鳄鱼为图腾。

本巴口述传统称，恩科莱与奇蒂在16或17世纪率领部众离开卢巴，二人均与卢巴统治者穆库伦佩有关。他们在1740年前渡过卢阿普拉河，先后在姆韦鲁湖、班韦乌卢湖附近和尚贝西河流域停留；米兰多河畔的征兆最终使他们定恩圭纳为第一个都城。18世纪末，第二十二代奇蒂穆库卢穆库卡·瓦·马莱卡诺把伦古人赶出卡萨马一带，并把新得的伊图纳封给弟弟奇通杜，即姆万巴一世。奇蒂穆库卢奇利亚马富瓦在位时，扩张持续到1808年，本巴军队把曼布韦人逼向姆潘达并在那里设立藩属。1810年起，奇莱谢·切佩拉长期统治，继续把本巴势力推向周围高原。

en:
Tabwa is the plateau and broken hill country behind the southwestern shore of Lake Tanganyika, between the Marungu heights, the Luapula-Mweru basin and the Bemba plateau. In 1444 its Bantu-speaking villagers lived more through autonomous clan settlements than through a single kingdom. They farmed, fished and kept the lake and river catches by smoking them, while smiths and traders exchanged iron, salt and dried fish across the neighboring hills. Matrilineal clans, above all the Zimba leopard clan, supplied the ruling lines of village chiefs, whose authority was tied to ancestral shrines, new-moon ceremonies and the arbitration of paths and fishing grounds.

During the eighteenth century some Tabwa groups moved southeast toward the upper Luapula, where contact with the Bemba shaped the Shila dialect. Around 1740 the Kazembe kingdom took shape to the west after the Luba-Lunda crossing of the Luapula; its copper, ivory, salt and fish trade soon reached toward the Tanganyika routes, turning Tabwa chiefs into brokers between lake traders, Bemba speakers and the Kazembe court rather than subjects of a single province. Bemba power expanded under Chitimukulu Mukuka wa Malekano in the late eighteenth century and again under Chilyamafwa until 1808, driving Lungu communities westward. By 1821 the older village chiefdoms remained, but their holders now had to balance Kazembe tribute, Bemba expansion and the first inland caravan trade.
zh:
塔布瓦位于坦噶尼喀湖西南岸后方的高原丘陵，处在马伦古山地、卢阿普拉—姆韦鲁盆地与本巴高原之间。1444年，这里的说班图语村民并非生活在统一王国之下，而是分属各个自治氏族聚落。他们务农、捕鱼，用熏制方法保存湖鱼和河鱼，铁匠与商人则在邻近山地间交换铁器、盐和鱼干。母系氏族，尤其是以豹为图腾的津巴氏族，提供了各村首领的统绪；首领权威依托祖先祭坛、新月仪式，以及对道路和渔场纠纷的仲裁。

18世纪，一部分塔布瓦人向东南迁到卢阿普拉上游，与本巴人的接触塑造了希拉方言。约1740年，卢巴-隆达人渡过卢阿普拉河后在西方形成卡曾贝王国；其铜、象牙、盐和鱼贸易很快伸向通往坦噶尼喀湖的商路，使塔布瓦首领成为湖区商人、说本巴语者和卡曾贝王庭之间的居间者，而不是某一个王庭直辖的臣民。18世纪末，奇蒂穆库卢·穆库卡·瓦·马莱卡诺统治下的本巴势力开始扩张，奇利亚马夫瓦又将扩张延续到1808年，隆古社群被迫西迁。到1821年，旧有的村落酋长领仍然存在，但其首领已必须在卡曾贝贡赋、本巴扩张和早期内陆商队贸易之间周旋。

en:
In 1444 the high plateau later called Ilamba, or Lambaland, on the border between central Zambia and Katanga was Lamba country. Lamba-speaking Bantu villages occupied woodland clearings and the country around Lake Kashiba, exchanging the copper and ivory of the mineral-rich plateau through regional networks. No outside source records a single royal capital; authority rested with local chiefs and clan heads rather than a court on the scale of the Lunda states.

The Lambas enter written history through Portuguese travel notes. On 21 September 1798 Francisco de Lacerda recorded that Lamba copper and ivory reached Kazembe's Lunda and Nsenga middlemen near Zumbo on the Zambezi. His entry shows that before 1821 Lamba villages were already tied to a long inland route linking the copper-bearing country of Katanga and the Copperbelt with Zambezi traders.
zh:
1444年，赞比亚中部与加丹加边境高原上后来被称为伊兰巴或兰巴兰的地方，已是兰巴人的土地。说兰巴语的班图村落散布在林间开垦地和卡希巴湖周围，把矿产丰沛高原上的铜与象牙投入区域交换网络。外来记载没有提到统一王都；与隆达诸强国不同，这里的权威属于地方酋长和氏族头人。

兰巴人最早因葡萄牙旅行记录而进入文字史。1798年9月21日，弗朗西斯科·德·拉塞尔达记载，兰巴人的铜和象牙流入卡曾贝的隆达人及赞比西河上祖博附近的恩森加中间商手中。这条材料说明，在1821年以前，兰巴村落已经连接在加丹加、铜带省产铜地与赞比西商人之间的内陆商路上。

en: Kusu is the Lomami River country of Maniema, around Kibombo and Kailo, lying between the Luba lands to the south and the forests of the Lega. The Bakusu speak a Bantu language of the Anamongo group and are close kin of the Tetela. Kusu carvers made chiefly thrones resembling those of the Luba, nkisi ritual figures like those of the Songye and ancestor statues of the Hemba type, while the women made pottery and baskets for daily use.
zh: 库苏位于马涅马的洛马米河流域，以基邦博和凯洛为中心，南接卢巴之地，东邻莱加人的森林。巴库苏人操阿纳蒙戈族群的一支班图语，与特特拉人是近亲。库苏工匠雕制的酋长宝座与卢巴人的相似，恩基西神像近于松格人的样式，祖先像则类似亨巴人的作品；妇女制作日用陶器和篮筐。

en: Lenje country lies around the wooded plateau and fishing waters of the Lukanga Swamp. The date of the Lenje people's arrival is unknown, but they are believed to have lived in central Zambia at least by the seventeenth century. Lenje-speaking villagers farmed seasonal clearings and supplemented their living by hunting and fishing, a loose society whose boundaries shifted between neighbouring peoples. Early in the eighteenth century, Portuguese traders from Tete made Zumbo a Zambezi trading fair, sending ivory routes up the lower Luangwa and as far as Lake Bangweulu. Those routes ran along the southeastern flank of Lenje country, so that by 1821 its hunting grounds were linked to the Zambezi trade even though no foreign court ruled the swamp.
zh: 伦吉人的土地位于卢坎加沼泽周围的林质高原和渔区。伦吉人何时迁来并无确切纪年，但有人认为他们至迟在17世纪已生活在赞比亚中部。说伦吉语的村民耕作季节性开垦地，并以狩猎和渔捞补足生计；他们的社会组织松散，与邻族之间的文化边界也不固定。18世纪初，来自太特的葡萄牙商人把祖博经营成赞比西河商站，象牙商路沿卢安瓜河下游一直延伸到班韦乌卢湖。这些商路经过伦吉土地东南缘，使当地猎场到1821年已与赞比西贸易相连，但并没有外邦王庭统治这片沼泽。

en:
Kanongesha is the high, well-watered woodland at the head of the Zambezi, around what later became Mwinilunga, where the rivers set off on their long course to the Indian Ocean while the copper-bearing country runs north toward Katanga and the salt pans of the Lualaba. Its first known people were the Mbwela, Bantu hunters and farmers with no chief above the village, smelting iron and living off the dense miombo. In 1444 this was still the Mbwelas' frontier, with no lord ruling these upper valleys.
