路德宗传教士17世纪才来到伊纳里。第一座教堂1646年落成，王室又把北方贸易收拢到伊纳里冬季集市。索丹屈莱的木教堂由卡尔十一世出资，1688年动工、次年在基蒂宁河畔一块萨米人献出的土地上建成；它是芬兰保存下来的最古老柱状木教堂之一，后来管辖着异常广大的腹地。1754年至1760年，皮尔帕耶尔维湖畔又建起一座木教堂。芬兰人定居始于1758年，一名农户在伊瓦洛河畔领了土地，他的农庄发展成屈莱村（Kyro），是伊瓦洛的前身。1809年，古凯米拉普兰税区随芬兰从瑞典转入俄国统治。

en:
The wooded highlands later called Kainuu were the southernmost reach of Kemi Lappmark: beside the great lakes Kitkajärvi and Kuusamojärvi stood the Sámi winter villages of Kitka and Maanselkä, the southernmost of Kemi Lappmark's eight villages. Their people wintered in the villages, moved to the rivers in spring and the lakes in summer, and lived mainly from wild reindeer and fish, selling furs to Bothnian-coast Finns and White Sea Karelians. In 1444 the frontier existed only on parchment: the Swedish claim went no further than gathering tribute, while Russia taxed the same country as masterless land.

The Treaty of Teusina drew the Swedish-Russian border east of the lakes in 1595, and from the 1670s, after Stockholm promised Lappland settlers fifteen years free of tax, Finnish farmers from Kainuu and the Torne and Kemi valleys moved in with their slash-and-burn clearances. The Sámi summoned the newcomers to court for illegal settlement but could not stop them; nearly two hundred farmers had arrived by 1685. Kuusamo became a parish of its own in 1675, its first church went up in 1680 under the priest Gabriel Tuderus, and a tally of 1713 found seventy-nine Finnish families against ten Sámi ones; by the 1760s no Sámi household remained, the people leaving only graves, hearth-stones and Sámi place names. The settlers farmed, burned tar and herded reindeer, and the lakeside tracks carried furs between the Gulf of Bothnia and the White Sea. In 1775 the district passed from Lappmark to the new province of Oulu; after a run of failed harvests and a smallpox epidemic around the turn of the century, about three thousand people lived here when Finland passed to Russia in 1809.
zh:
后来称作凯努的森林高地是凯米拉普兰的最南缘：基特卡湖和库萨莫湖畔坐落着基特卡、曼塞尔凯两个萨米人的冬季村落，是凯米拉普兰八个村落中最南的两个。村民在村里过冬，春天迁至河畔、夏天移往湖边，主要以捕猎野驯鹿和捕鱼为生，把毛皮卖给波的尼亚湾沿岸的芬兰人和白海的卡累利阿人。1444年，边界只存在于纸面上：瑞典的宗主权不外乎征收贡赋，俄国也把同一片土地当作无主之地收税。

1595年《特乌西纳和约》把瑞典与俄国的边界划到湖群以东；1670年代，斯德哥尔摩承诺给拉普兰移民十五年免税之后，凯努以及托尔讷河、凯米河谷的芬兰农民刀耕火种而来。萨米人把新来者告上法庭，指控他们非法占地，却无力阻止；到1685年迁来的农民已近二百人。库萨莫1675年成为独立教区，第一座教堂1680年落成，首任牧师加布里埃尔·图德鲁斯主持教务；1713年的清查记下七十九户芬兰移民、十户萨米人家，到1760年代已无一户萨米人，只留下坟茔、火塘遗址和萨米语地名。移民务农、烧焦油、养驯鹿，湖边的小路把毛皮在波的尼亚湾和白海之间转运。1775年此地从拉普兰划归新设的奥卢省；世纪之交连年歉收又逢天花，到1809年芬兰并入俄国时，这里约有三千居民。

en:
Around Fofa, the mountain kingdom of Yamma, known to Amharic speakers as Janjero, fills the angle formed by the Omo and the Jimma Gibe; Mount Bor Ama, Mount Azulu and Mount Toba mark its skyline. Its people are the Yem, speakers of the Omotic language Yemsa. A victory song for Yeshaq I records Yamma among the lands south of the Abay that sent horses as tribute to the Ethiopian emperor. In 1444 a small Yem court still ruled this river-girt pocket, tied to the highlands by tribute but preserving its own ritual kingship.

In 1614 the Portuguese priest António Fernandes entered Yamma while searching for a southern route to Malindi. He found the king seated on a carpet atop a railed wooden tower about six yards high, while courtiers stood below; the ruler gave audience, settled disputes and dispatched business there, clad in a white silk Indian garment. Long after that visit, Yamma remained a small Yem polity wedged between Jimma to the west and Garo to the south, keeping its separate court through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
zh:
富法一带的山间小国亚马，在阿姆哈拉语中称詹吉罗，位于奥莫河与吉马吉贝河形成的角地，博尔阿马山、阿祖卢山和托巴山标示着它的天际线。居民是说奥莫语族耶姆萨语的耶姆人。耶沙克一世的一首凯歌记载，亚马是阿巴伊河以南向埃塞俄比亚皇帝进贡马匹的地方之一。1444年，耶姆人的小朝廷仍统治着这块河流环抱的山地，虽以贡赋与高地相连，却保留自身的仪式性王权。

1614年，葡萄牙神父安东尼奥·费尔南德斯为寻找通往马林迪的南方路线进入亚马。他看到国王坐在约六码高、围有栏杆的木塔顶端的地毯上，廷臣都立于下方；国王身着白色印度丝衣，在塔上接见来使、裁决争讼并处理政务。这次到访之后很久，亚马仍是西临吉马、南接加罗的耶姆小国，在17和18世纪保住自己的朝廷。

en:
The Göta älv was medieval Sweden's only road to the North Sea: Bohuslän on the north bank belonged to Norway and Halland on the south to Denmark, so the river mouth carried the whole foreign trade of the Västergötland plains. Älvsborg castle rose on the Klippan rock to guard it, first mentioned in 1366, with Lindholmen fortress on the opposite bank and the market town of Lödöse upstream, where merchants loaded for Hanseatic ports. The rebel Engelbrekt stormed the castle in vain in 1434; two years later the marshal Karl Knutsson talked its German castellan into surrendering, and in 1439 a Norwegian army gave up a ten-week siege. In 1444, with the Kalmar Union restored, Älvsborg was a frontier royal castle, the Swedish crown's sole outlet to the western sea, ringed by rival lands.

Later Norwegian attacks were beaten off by Tord Bonde, but in 1502 Crown Prince Christian of Denmark took the castle and burned it, and the Danes held it again from 1519 until the end of the Swedish War of Liberation. Gustav I rebuilt Älvsborg as a Renaissance fortress and founded a town beside it in 1547. The Danes came back in the Northern Seven Years' War, razed the town and kept the castle until the Treaty of Stettin in 1570, when Sweden paid the First Älvsborg Ransom of 150,000 riksdaler, raised by taxing a tenth of every peasant's property and a twelfth of the townsmen's. Captured once more in the Kalmar War of 1612, the fortress was redeemed at Knäred in 1613 with a second ransom of about a million riksdaler; the Danes stayed on as security until the last payment in 1619. Gustavus Adolphus founded Gothenburg downriver in 1621, and Dutch engineers laid out its canals. Halland and Bohuslän passed to Sweden in 1645 and 1658, turning the old frontier into an inland border. The medieval castle, exposed to cannon from the Sjöbergen hills, was demolished in 1673 and replaced by the island fortress of Nya Älvsborg. In 1731 the Swedish East India Company based its China trade in Gothenburg, and Indiamen loaded for Canton in the same roadstead the castle had watched for three centuries.
zh:
约塔河是中世纪瑞典通往北海的唯一水道：北岸的布胡斯兰属于挪威，南岸的哈兰属于丹麦，西约塔兰平原的全部外贸都要从河口出入。河口的克利潘岩上矗立着埃尔夫斯堡要塞，1366年初见于记载，对岸是林霍尔门堡，上游的集镇勒德瑟则是商人装货前往汉萨港口的地方。义军首领恩厄尔布雷克特1434年猛攻不克，两年后政务元帅卡尔·克努特松说服德意志籍守将献城，1439年一支挪威军队围攻十周也只能撤走。1444年卡尔马联盟重归一统，埃尔夫斯堡是一座边塞王城，是瑞典王冠唯一的西海出口，四周尽是敌手的土地。

挪威人后来的进攻都被托德·邦德击退，但1502年丹麦王储克里斯蒂安攻陷城堡并付之一炬，1519年丹麦人再度占据，一直守到瑞典解放战争结束。古斯塔夫一世把埃尔夫斯堡改建为文艺复兴式要塞，1547年又在堡旁设镇。北方七年战争中丹麦人卷土重来，荡平市镇、占据城堡，直到1570年《斯德丁条约》才以十五万里克斯达勒的「第一次埃尔夫斯堡赎金」归还，这笔钱靠对农民征收十分之一财产、对市民征收十二分之一凑齐。1612年卡尔马战争中要塞再度失守，1613年《克奈勒德和约》规定了约一百万里克斯达勒的第二次赎金，丹麦人留驻作抵押，直到1619年最后一笔款项付清。古斯塔夫二世1621年在下游建立哥德堡，由荷兰工匠规划运河。哈兰1645年、布胡斯兰1658年相继并入瑞典，旧日边塞就此成为内地。中世纪旧堡抵挡不住邻近舍贝里山（Sjöbergen）方向的炮火，1673年被拆除，由岛上的新埃尔夫斯堡要塞接替。1731年，瑞典东印度公司把对华贸易的基地设在哥德堡，前往广州的商船就在这座城堡看守了三百年的锚地上装货。

en:
Dal is the forest-and-lake country west of Lake Vänern, hard against the Norwegian marches; its farmers and woodsmen lived scattered along lake landings and forest tracks, paying the dues of a poor border province. Above the Dalbergsån outlet stood Dalaborg, raised in 1304 by Dukes Erik and Valdemar, sons of Magnus Ladulås, to watch lake traffic and the roads into Norway. In 1388 the Swedish council met at the castle and acknowledged Queen Margaret of Denmark and Norway as regent of Sweden, nine years before the Kalmar Union joined the three Nordic crowns. Dalaborg's royal years ended early: Engelbrekt's rebels burned it in 1434. In 1444 only its moat and cellars remained above Vänern, and the region, still called Dal in the law of 1442, had no town.

Armies crossed these woods whenever Sweden fought Denmark-Norway: 281 Dalsland farms went up in flames in 1568 during the Nordic Seven Years' War, and the campaigns of 1611–1612, 1644–1645 and 1675–1679 swept the same forest roads. The province got its first and only chartered town late, when Queen Christina's regency founded Åmål on a Vänern shore road on 1 April 1643, largely to stop peasants selling timber straight across the Norwegian border. Smuggling continued regardless, and Åmål itself stood in the path of every later war: nearly destroyed in 1645, attacked in 1676 and 1679 and briefly held by the Danes in 1788. Fire also gutted parts of the little timber town in 1777 and 1809. The name Dalsland appears in writing only from 1508; before that the country was simply Dal.
zh:
达勒是维纳恩湖以西林湖相间的地方，紧挨着挪威边境；农户和林居者散居在湖岸码头与林间小路旁，缴纳的是一个贫穷边区的赋税。达尔贝里河入湖口上曾矗立着达拉堡，1304年由马格努斯·拉杜洛斯之子埃里克公爵与瓦尔德马公爵修建，用以监视湖上交通和入挪道路。1388年，瑞典政务会议在堡中承认丹麦、挪威的玛格丽特女王为瑞典摄政，九年后三个北欧王国便在卡尔马结成联盟。达拉堡的王堡岁月结束得很早：1434年，恩厄尔布雷克特的起义军将它付之一炬。1444年，维纳恩湖畔只剩壕沟与地窖，按1442年地方法仍称「达尔」的这片地区没有一座城镇。

每逢瑞典与丹麦—挪威交战，军队就会穿过这片林地：北方七年战争期间，1568年有281座达尔斯兰农场被烧毁，1611—1612年、1644—1645年和1675—1679年的战事又扫过同样的林间道路。这片地区很晚才有第一座、也是唯一一座特状城镇：1643年4月1日，克里斯蒂娜女王的摄政政府在维纳恩湖畔的路旁设立奥莫尔，主要为的是阻止农民把木材直接卖到挪威那边。走私并未因此断绝，而奥莫尔本身正挡在后来每一场战争的路上：1645年几乎被毁，1676年和1679年连遭进攻，1788年又被丹麦人短时占领。1777年和1809年，火灾两度烧毁这座木材小城的部分城区。达尔斯兰一名到1508年才见于文字，此前这里只称达尔。

en:
Eastern Scania runs from the open Österlen coast up through the forests of Göinge to the Småland border. Gladsaxehus at Gladsax controlled one of the chief Danish fiefs in this country; after Ide Pedersdatter Falk, its last private holder, died, Queen Margaret turned Gladsax län into a crown fief. Farther inland, peasants on the stony Göinge soils combined cattle farming with smithwork and woodworking, while dense woods gave cover on the road into Sweden. In 1444 the whole district was Danish, governed from Gladsax and kept under arms against raiders crossing the forest frontier.

That frontier determined the history of the province. During the Kalmar War, Swedish troops fell back through Göinge after fighting at Vittsjö on 11 February 1612, and raiders burned the nearby town of Vä. Christian IV answered in 1614 by founding Kristianstad as a planned Renaissance fortress town and moving the town rights of Vä and Åhus there; only an arsenal was built of the planned royal castle. Roskilde ceded eastern Scania to Sweden in 1658 after a skirmish at Sibbarp, but the Göinge woods did not accept the change quietly. Pro-Danish snapphanar used them as guerrilla country in 1658-1660 and again during the Scanian War of 1676-1679, with local captains such as Lille Mads raiding Swedish garrisons. Swedish forces answered with executions, breaking wheels and forced oaths; a Danish incursion in 1710 ended at Hästveda.
zh:
东斯科讷从开阔的厄斯特伦海岸伸入约因厄森林，直抵斯莫兰边境。格拉德萨克斯的格拉德萨克斯城堡统辖着丹麦在这里最重要的封邑之一；末代私人领主伊德·佩德斯达特·法尔克死后，玛格丽特女王把格拉德萨克西兰收为王室封邑。更往内陆，约因厄土地多石，农民在养牛之外兼做锻铁和木工，密林也掩护着通往瑞典的道路。1444年，整个地区属丹麦，由格拉德萨克斯管辖，并因森林边境另一侧的袭掠者而保持军备。

这条边境决定了此地后来的历史。卡尔马战争期间，瑞典军在1612年2月11日的维特舍战斗后经约因厄撤退，袭掠者焚毁了附近的韦镇。克里斯蒂安四世的回应是在1614年建立按文艺复兴规划布置的设防城克里斯蒂安斯塔德，把韦镇和奥胡斯的城市权迁到那里；计划中的王室城堡最终只建成一座军械库。西巴普小规模交兵后，罗斯基勒和约于1658年将东斯科讷割让瑞典，但约因厄森林并未平静接受。1658至1660年以及1676至1679年斯科讷战争期间，亲丹麦的自由射手把这里当作游击区，「小个子马兹」等本地头目不断袭击瑞典驻军。瑞典军方以处决、轮刑和强制宣誓回应；1710年丹麦军的一次入侵也在海斯特韦达告终。

en:
Tiohärad, the 'ten hundreds', was the inland law-district of south-western Småland, where the three forest folklands of Finnveden, Värend and Njudung came together. Its roads converged on Växjö, on the shore of the lake of the same name; the town's name means 'road lake', since the winter way to its market crossed the frozen water. A diocese under the patronage of Saint Sigfrid was created there about 1170, and Magnus Eriksson granted the town its charter in 1342. Just to the north, on Lake Helgasjön, Bishop Lars Mikaelson built the first stone house at Kronoberg in 1444. In that year Tiohärad was Catholic Sweden's forest borderland facing Danish Blekinge and Halland; free farmers and foresters lived off cattle, timber and the Växjö markets, which drew merchants even from Danish towns.

The border castle and the market town drew most of this region's wars. Danish forces burned that new house in 1470 and it was rebuilt and fortified after peace in 1472; Gustav Vasa seized Kronoberg at the Reformation. In 1542 the Småland yeoman Nils Dacke raised the countryside against the king's taxes and the Lutheran seizure of church plate; from that summer until after New Year his peasants held Växjö and made Kronoberg their base. It was the most widespread civil war Sweden had known, one that came close to toppling Gustav Vasa; royal armies invaded from both Östergötland and Västergötland and ended it when Dacke was shot in August 1543. Danish troops took and burned Kronoberg in 1570, it was rebuilt with at least fifty guns by the 1580s, and Danish forces burned it again in January 1612 during the Kalmar War. When the 1658 Peace of Roskilde pushed the frontier away to the Sound, the castle lost its purpose and became a ruin; fire cleared old Växjö later that year, and the town was rebuilt on a regular grid.
zh:
蒂约海拉德意为「十个海拉德」，是斯莫兰西南部的内陆法区，芬韦德恩、韦伦德和尼乌东三个林区民间地区在此相接。道路汇向同名湖畔的韦克舍；城名意为「道路湖」，因为冬季赶集的路要从结冰的湖面穿过。约1170年，这里设立以圣西弗里德为主保圣人的教区，1342年马格努斯·埃里克松授予韦克舍城市特许状。1444年，就在城北海尔加湖畔，主教拉尔斯·米凯尔松在克鲁努贝里建起第一座石屋。这一年的蒂约海拉德是瑞典面向丹麦属布莱金厄和哈兰的天主教森林边地，自由农和林民靠畜牧、木材和韦克舍市集为生，连丹麦城镇的商人都远道前来赶集。

边境城堡和集镇卷入了这一带的大部分战事。1470年丹麦军队烧毁这座新建石屋，1472年议和后重建加固；宗教改革时古斯塔夫·瓦萨没收了克鲁努贝里。1542年，斯莫兰自耕农尼尔斯·达克举兵反抗国王重税和路德宗没收教会银器，当年夏至新年之后农民军占领韦克舍，并以克鲁努贝里为据点。这是瑞典史上规模最大的内战，险些推翻古斯塔夫·瓦萨；王室军队从东约特兰和西约特兰两路攻入，1543年8月达克中枪身亡，起义才告平息。丹麦军队1570年攻占并烧毁克鲁努贝里，城堡重建后到1580年代已配备至少五十门火炮，1612年1月卡尔马战争中再度被丹麦人焚毁。1658年《罗斯基勒条约》把边界远推到厄勒海峡，城堡失去用途，沦为废墟；同年晚些时候大火烧过韦克舍旧城，城市随后按整齐网格重建。

en:
Abarquh lies on the high desert plain midway between Yazd and Shiraz, where the roads from Shiraz, Isfahan and Yazd met. In the tenth century Ibn Hawqal found a prosperous, walled town with a citadel, which shipped cotton cloth across the treeless country and brought its food in from elsewhere; he also noted a 'lofty hill of ashes' nearby, said to be the remains of the fire where Nimrod tried to burn Abraham. The octagonal Gonbad-e Ali mausoleum was built in 1056 or 1057 for the Firuzanid amir Hazarasp, and Seljuk and Ilkhanid rule left the four-iwan Friday mosque and a mint: coins struck here by the Ilkhanids, Injuids, Mozaffarids, Timurids and Aq Qoyunlu all survive. Hamdallah Mustawfi in 1340 called the town small but prosperous, its grain and cotton fed by qanats, and marvelled at its ancient cypress, already the most famous tree in Iran. The same tree, the Sarv-e Abarkuh, is piously said to have been planted by Zoroaster himself. In 1444 Timurid power was slackening, and the town lay between that empire and the rising Qara Qoyunlu.

Safavid Abarquh was crown domain, farmed out to high officials; the early-seventeenth-century Tadhkirat al-Muluk valued the district at 711 tomans and assigned its revenue to the commander of the musketeers. Hotak Afghans sacked the town in 1722, in the invasion that brought down the Safavids, and in 1793 or 1794 Lotf Ali Khan Zand briefly held its citadel in his losing war with the Qajars. Four adobe ice-houses, built to keep winter ice through the summer, went up in the Qajar period, by which time the caravans that had fed Abarquh for a thousand years had mostly taken other roads.
zh:
阿巴尔古位于亚兹德与设拉子之间的高原荒漠，设拉子、伊斯法罕、亚兹德三条道路在此会合。10世纪时，伊本·豪盖勒见到一座有城墙和城堡的繁荣城镇：此地不生树木，城镇外销棉布，粮食则从外地运入；他还记下城郊一座「高耸的灰烬山」，相传是宁录试图烧死先知易卜拉欣的火堆遗迹。八角形的贡巴德·阿里陵墓建于1056或1057年，墓主是菲鲁赞家族的埃米尔哈扎拉斯普；塞尔柱和伊儿汗时期留下了四伊万聚礼清真寺和一座铸币厂，伊儿汗、因朱、穆扎法尔、帖木儿、白羊诸朝都有在此铸造的钱币存世。1340年，哈姆杜拉·穆斯图菲称此城小而富庶，坎儿井浇灌着谷物与棉花；他已叹赏城中古柏是波斯最有名的树，这棵阿巴尔古巨柏相传为琐罗亚斯德亲手所植。1444年，帖木儿的控制力正在衰退，城镇夹在旧帝国与崛起的黑羊王朝之间。

萨法维时期，阿巴尔古是王室直辖领地，分封给朝中高官；17世纪初的《王臣备忘录》把该区税入估值711托曼，拨归火枪兵统领。1722年，推翻萨法维王朝的阿富汗霍塔克人洗劫此城；1793或1794年，卢图夫·阿里汗·赞德在与卡扎尔人的败战中曾短暂据守城堡。四座土坯冰库建于卡扎尔时代，用以把冬冰存到盛夏；那时，养活阿巴尔古千年之久的商队已大多改走他路。

en:
Syrmia is the broad grain plain between the Danube and the Sava, with the wooded Fruška Gora ridge running along its Danube side. Its capital, Mitrovica, stands on the Sava beside the ruins of Sirmium, the Roman capital of Pannonia where ten emperors were born in the city or nearby. Hungary took the region in 1180; the Serbian king Stefan Dragutin ruled a realm here from 1282 to 1316, and by 1437 local records describe most of the plain as settled by Serbs. In 1444 Syrmia is an Orthodox, grain-growing march of the Hungarian crown, its estates in the hands of frontier lords while Ottoman armies move up the Balkans. After Serbia fell in 1459, Hungarian kings kept titular Serbian despots at Kupinik, and Nicholas of Ilok, one of the richest magnates in Hungary and its titular king of Bosnia from 1471, ruled the eastern plain from his castle at Ilok; his son Lawrence held the lands until 1524.

Ottoman troops entered Syrmia in 1521, took Mitrovica in 1526, and by 1538 the whole plain had become the Sanjak of Syrmia. The wars of the next two centuries were fought on its fields. On 19 August 1691 Ludwig Wilhelm of Baden, the imperial general nicknamed 'Turkish Louis', destroyed an Ottoman army at Slankamen; the grand vizier Köprülü Mustafa was killed in the rout, and the Peace of Karlowitz, signed on 26 January 1699 at Sremski Karlovci, gave western Syrmia to the Habsburgs. Austrian troops finally secured Mitrovica in the campaign of 1717, confirmed by the Treaty of Passarowitz the next year, and after 1745 the country was divided between Syrmia County and the Military Frontier. Serbian religious life gathered around the Fruška Gora monasteries: Krušedol, founded between 1509 and 1514 by the metropolitan Maksim Branković, was the mausoleum of the last Branković despots, and Ottoman raiders burned it during the 1716 campaign, though it was rebuilt. Back in 1663 Evliya Çelebi had counted fifteen hundred houses in Mitrovica, with mosques, madrasas, baths, caravanserais and four hundred shops; in 1807 the peasants of the Ruma and Ilok estates rose at Voganj in Tican's Rebellion.
zh:
叙尔米亚（通行称斯雷姆）是多瑙河与萨瓦河之间广阔的谷物平原，多瑙河一侧横卧着林木覆盖的弗鲁什卡山。首府米特罗维察（今斯雷姆斯卡米特罗维察）位于萨瓦河畔，紧挨着罗马时代潘诺尼亚首府西尔米乌姆的遗址，有十位罗马皇帝出生在这座城或其附近。1180年匈牙利取得这一地区，塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·德拉古廷1282年至1316年在此立国；到1437年，当地材料已记载平原上的居民以塞尔维亚人为主。1444年，叙尔米亚是匈牙利王冠治下一片信奉东正教、盛产谷物的边地，领地握在边境领主手中，奥斯曼军队则沿巴尔干北上。1459年塞尔维亚陷落后，匈牙利国王仍在库皮尼克维持名义上的塞尔维亚专制公；伊洛克的尼古拉是匈牙利最富有的大贵族之一，1471年起兼领名义上的波斯尼亚国王，以伊洛克城堡为中心统治东部平原，其子洛夫罗保有这片土地直到1524年。

奥斯曼军队1521年攻入斯雷姆，1526年拿下米特罗维察，到1538年整片平原成为斯雷姆桑贾克。此后两个世纪的战争多在这片平原上进行。1691年8月19日，绰号「土耳其人路易」的帝国将领、巴登的路德维希·威廉在斯兰卡门歼灭奥斯曼大军，大维齐尔科普鲁律·穆斯塔法死于溃军之中；1699年1月26日在斯雷姆斯基卡尔洛夫奇签订的《卡洛维茨和约》把西斯雷姆交给哈布斯堡。奥地利军队在1717年战役中最终拿下米特罗维察，次年由《波扎雷瓦茨和约》确认；1745年以后，此地被分划为斯雷姆县和军事边屯区。塞尔维亚人的宗教生活围绕弗鲁什卡山的修道院展开：1509年至1514年由都主教马克西姆·布兰科维奇创建的克鲁舍多尔修道院，是末代布兰科维奇专制公一族的陵寝，1716年战事中被奥斯曼袭掠者焚毁，日后又予重建。早在1663年，爱维亚·切莱比就记载米特罗维察有一千五百栋房屋，以及清真寺、伊斯兰学校、浴场、商队旅馆和四百家店铺；1807年，鲁马和伊洛克领地上的农民在沃甘起事，即蒂昌起义。

en:
Durrës lies on a flat Adriatic bay facing southern Italy. Founded as Epidamnus and known in Roman times as Dyrrachium, it was the western end of the Via Egnatia, the road across the Balkans to Thessalonica and Constantinople. Its Roman amphitheatre could hold about twenty thousand spectators, and the late antique walls were built under Emperor Anastasius I, a native of the city; Anna Komnene later wrote that four horsemen could ride abreast along them. The walls were repaired after the earthquake of 1273 and strengthened again after Venice took the city from Gjergj Thopia in 1392. The coastal salt pans gave the port another source of wealth, and Jewish merchants worked the salt trade here in the thirteenth century. In 1444 Venice held the town as Durazzo: Venetian galleys used the harbour, Albanian villagers farmed the coastal plain, and the citadel watched the sea lane between Vlorë and Lezhë.

Mehmed II besieged Durazzo in 1466 during his campaign against Skanderbeg's Albanian resistance, but the Venetian garrison held out. Ottoman forces took the city in 1501 and kept its castle as the main strongpoint on this part of the coast. The harbour shrank during the first Ottoman centuries, and Evliya Çelebi found only about 150 houses and a mosque named after Bayezid II when he visited in 1670-71. Salt brought merchants back. Around 1699 roughly a hundred Turkish and Greek merchants were shipping wax, cloth, leather and grain to Venice, even when Constantinople formally banned the trade. France, England, the Netherlands and Austria opened consulates in 1700. Grain and olive oil still dominated exchanges with Venice in 1769; after Napoleon extinguished the Venetian Republic in 1797, Durrës sent more of its cargoes through Austrian Trieste. In 1821 it remained an Ottoman coastal fortress whose living came chiefly from salt, grain and shipping.
zh:
都拉斯位于亚得里亚海一处平坦海湾，与意大利南部隔海相望。它初名埃庇达诺斯，罗马时代称都拉基乌姆，是埃格纳提亚大道的西端，这条大道横穿巴尔干，通往帖撒罗尼迦和君士坦丁堡。当地的罗马竞技场可容纳约两万名观众；古城墙则出自出生于此的皇帝阿纳斯塔修斯一世之手，安娜·科穆宁娜后来记载，四名骑兵可以在墙顶并行。1273年地震后城墙得到修缮，威尼斯1392年从杰尔吉·托皮亚手中取得城市后又加以加固。沿海盐田是港口的另一项财富来源，13世纪已有犹太商人在此经营盐业。1444年，威尼斯以「杜拉佐」之名统治这座设防港口：威尼斯桨帆船使用海港，阿尔巴尼亚村民耕种沿岸平原，城堡监视发罗拉与莱什之间的海路。

1466年，穆罕默德二世在镇压斯坎德培领导的阿尔巴尼亚抵抗时围攻杜拉佐，但威尼斯守军守住了城市。1501年奥斯曼军队攻占都拉斯，把城堡作为这段海岸的主要据点。港口在奥斯曼统治最初几个世纪趋于缩小，埃夫利亚·切莱比1670至1671年到访时，只见到约一百五十栋房屋和一座以巴耶济德二世命名的清真寺。盐业让商人重新回来。约1699年，约有一百名土耳其和希腊商人把蜂蜡、布匹、皮革和谷物运往威尼斯，哪怕君士坦丁堡正式禁止这种贸易。1700年，法国、英国、尼德兰和奥地利开设领事馆。1769年，对威尼斯贸易仍以谷物和橄榄油为主；1797年拿破仑灭亡威尼斯共和国后，都拉斯把更多货物送往奥地利的里雅斯特。1821年，它仍是奥斯曼的沿海要塞，生计主要依靠盐、谷物和航运。

en:
Lezhë, the ancient Lissus, guards the mouth of the Drin on the Adriatic, a walled town on a low hill between the sea and the sheep-rearing uplands of northern Albania. It was a stronghold of the Illyrian Labeatae: Philip V of Macedon seized its citadel in 211 BC, and the Illyrian king Gentius struck his own coinage there before the Roman conquest. After centuries of Byzantine and Slav rule, the Dukagjini family handed the town, called Alessio by the Italians, to Venice in 1386. So it stood in 1444, a Venetian walled town whose surrounding hills were held by Catholic and Orthodox Albanian clans.

On 2 March 1444, with the Republic's leave, Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeg assembled the Albanian nobles, Kastrioti, Arianiti, Muzaka, Thopia, Dukagjini and the rest, in the church of Saint Nicholas, and was proclaimed chief of the League of Lezhë against the Ottomans; historians count the assembly as the first common Albanian state. Skanderbeg's men even besieged Lezhë during his war with Venice of 1447–1448, until the peace of 4 October 1448 reconciled him with the Republic. He died on 17 January 1468 and was buried in Saint Nicholas', which became the shrine of the Albanian cause. The Ottomans took the town in 1478 during the great siege of Shkodra and turned the cathedral into the Selimiye Mosque; Venice held it again only for 1501–1506. As Leş it then served the Sanjak of Shkodra until 1757, when the region passed to the semi-autonomous Bushati pashas of Shkodra, its masters in 1821.
zh:
莱什古称利苏斯，扼守亚得里亚海滨的德林河口，是一座低山上的筑城城镇，面朝大海，背靠阿尔巴尼亚北部牧羊的高地。它曾是伊利里亚人拉贝阿特部族的重镇：马其顿的腓力五世于公元前211年夺取其卫城，伊利里亚国王真提乌斯落入罗马之手前还曾在此自铸钱币。历经拜占庭与斯拉夫人的数百年统治，杜卡吉尼家族1386年把这座意大利人称作阿莱西奥的城镇交给威尼斯。1444年时局面便是如此：城墙之内属威尼斯，周围山地掌握在天主教和东正教的阿尔巴尼亚部族手中。

1444年3月2日，经威尼斯准许，乔治·卡斯特里奥蒂·斯坎德培在圣尼古拉教堂召集阿尔巴尼亚贵族，卡斯特里奥蒂、阿里亚尼蒂、穆扎卡、托皮亚、杜卡吉尼等家族齐聚，被推举为莱什联盟的领袖，共抗奥斯曼；史家把这次集会视为第一个统一的阿尔巴尼亚政权。1447至1448年斯坎德培与威尼斯交战期间，他的军队连莱什城也围攻过，直到1448年10月4日双方议和。1468年1月17日斯坎德培病逝，安葬于圣尼古拉教堂，这座教堂此后成为阿尔巴尼亚人心中的圣地。1478年，奥斯曼人在围攻斯库台期间拿下莱什，把大教堂改为塞利米耶清真寺；威尼斯只在1501至1506年短暂重据此城。此后它以莱什之名隶属斯库台桑扎克，1757年转入斯库台半独立的布沙蒂帕夏家族治下，1821年时仍受其统治。

en:
This province takes its name from Braničevo, a land of pastures and fords between the Danube, the Great Morava and the Homolje and Kučaj highlands. Its medieval fortress rose near the Roman city of Viminacium on the Mlava and guarded the Via Militaris, the road that carried armies and goods between the Danube and Constantinople; Byzantine emperors kept it as a Danubian base against Hungary, and the armies of the Second and Third Crusades marched past. From the late thirteenth century the region belonged to Serbian rulers. Farther up the Morava system, Kruševac was founded by Prince Lazar in 1371 as his fortified capital. Beside the citadel he built the Lazarica church between 1375 and 1378, the palace church that became the model for the churches of the Morava school; Lazar's army gathered in the town before Kosovo in 1389, where he was killed and later venerated as a saint. Ottoman troops held Kruševac in 1413 and 1427 and Hungarian forces in 1437, but Đurađ Branković recovered it in 1444, when the stock routes and fortresses of the province again belonged to the hard-pressed Serbian Despotate.

Ottoman armies returned in 1454; Serbian troops inflicted heavy losses at the Battle of Kruševac, but Mehmed II sent reinforcements and the town fell the same year. It became Alacahisar, the seat of an Ottoman sanjak, and the Lazarica was desecrated and turned into a stable. The Austrians occupied Kruševac from 1688 to 1690 and again from 1717 to 1739 in the Habsburg-Ottoman wars. The uprisings after 1804 transformed the Serbian lands farther north, while in 1821 Kruševac remained an Ottoman district and garrison town.
zh:
这片地区以布兰尼切夫得名，地当多瑙河、大摩拉瓦河与霍莫列、库查伊山地之间，遍布牧场和渡口。中世纪要塞建在姆拉瓦河畔罗马城市维米纳基乌姆遗址近旁，扼守连通多瑙河与君士坦丁堡的军用大道，军队和商货都走这条路；拜占庭皇帝以它为多瑙河上对抗匈牙利的基地，第二次和第三次十字军的队伍也都取道于此。13世纪后期起，此地归塞尔维亚统治者所有。在摩拉瓦水系更上游，克鲁舍瓦茨由拉扎尔公1371年兴建，作为他设防的都城。他在城堡旁于1375年至1378年修建拉扎里察教堂，这座宫廷教堂后来成为摩拉瓦派教堂的范本；拉扎尔的军队1389年出征科索沃前在此集结，他本人战殁于科索沃，后被东正教会尊为圣徒。奥斯曼军队1413年、1427年两据克鲁舍瓦茨，匈牙利人1437年又占据该城，久拉吉·布兰科维奇1444年将其收复；这一年，省内的牲畜商路和各处要塞重新归入处境艰难的塞尔维亚专制公国。

1454年奥斯曼大军再度来攻，塞尔维亚军队在克鲁舍瓦茨之战中重创敌军，但穆罕默德二世增兵反攻，城市同年陷落。克鲁舍瓦茨改称阿拉贾希萨尔，成为奥斯曼桑贾克的治所，拉扎里察教堂遭亵渎，被当作马厩。哈布斯堡与奥斯曼的战争中，奥地利人1688年至1690年、1717年至1739年两度占领该城。1804年后的起义改变了更北面的塞尔维亚土地，而1821年的克鲁舍瓦茨仍是奥斯曼的地区行政和驻军城镇。

en:
Hyuga faces the Pacific along southeastern Kyushu, where coastal plains give way to mountain valleys and fast rivers. The Kyoto court knew the province early for its horses; under the eighth-century codes it also included the lands that became Satsuma and Osumi, until those districts separated in 702 and 713. The provincial temple and presumed seat of government stood near Saito. By 1444 that older order had little force in the south. The Tsuchimochi held Obi on a hill above the Sakatani River, the Ito were pressing down from central Hyuga, and the Shimazu of southern Kyushu saw the same valley as the approach to their border. Downstream lay Aburatsu, the port that gave the castle its value.

Obi remained the prize in the Ito-Shimazu rivalry for more than a century. The Shimazu installed Niiro Tadatsugu there in 1458, and Ito Sukekuni was killed attacking the castle in 1484. Ito Yoshisuke opened another long siege in 1544; even mediation by Ashikaga Yoshiteru in 1560 did not settle the border, and the Ito took Obi two years later. Their defeat at Kizakiwara in 1572 opened Hyuga to a Shimazu recovery: Obi fell in 1576, and an Otomo army was destroyed at Mimigawa in 1578. Ito Suketaka guided Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Kyushu campaign in 1587 and returned to Obi as castellan the next year, then kept his domain after serving the eastern side at Sekigahara. In the Edo peace, Obi cedar was floated down the Sakatani to Aburatsu for shipment. Earthquake repairs completed the stone walls and moat in 1691 and the palace in 1693; in 1821 the Ito still ruled their small timber domain from the castle.
zh:
日向位于九州东南，面朝太平洋，沿海平原向内接入山谷与急流。京都朝廷很早就知道这里出产良马；8世纪律令制下，日向曾辖有后来成为萨摩和大隅的土地，两地分别在702年和713年分出，国分寺与推定国府则在西都一带。到1444年，这种旧国衙秩序在南部已没有多少约束力。土持氏据有酒谷川边丘陵上的饫肥，伊东氏从中部日向南压，萨摩的岛津氏则把这条谷地视为北部边防。酒谷川下游就是油津港，也正因如此，饫肥城成了各方争夺的要地。

饫肥在伊东氏与岛津氏之间争了一百多年。1458年，岛津氏派新纳忠续入城；1484年，伊东祐国攻城时战死。伊东义祐1544年再启长期围攻，1560年足利义辉出面调停也未划清边界，伊东氏两年后仍夺下饫肥。1572年木崎原之战后局势逆转，岛津氏1576年收复饫肥，1578年又在耳川击溃大友军。伊东祐兵为1587年丰臣秀吉九州征伐引路，次年回到饫肥任城主，关原之战时从属东军，保住了藩领。江户承平时期，饫肥杉顺酒谷川运到油津出海。地震后的修缮在1691年完成石垣与护城河，1693年建成御殿；1821年，伊东氏仍在饫肥城统治这个不大的木材之藩。

en:
Higo occupies central Kyushu, rising from coastal plains toward the volcanic cone of Mount Aso and the forested Kuma valley. The Kikuchi were its Muromachi military governors, but they shared the province with strong neighbours: the Aso family drew power from the great shrine around Mount Aso, while the Sagara were rooted in the southern mountains. In 1444 Higo therefore belonged to no single lord. Kikuchi armies and marriages could alter the balance in Kyushu, yet the hill town that became Kumamoto had not yet acquired its famous castle.

Kumamoto's rise came out of the wars of unification. Ideta Hidenobu built Chiba Castle there between 1469 and 1487, and Kanokogi Chikakazu added a fort called Kumamoto between 1521 and 1531. As the Kikuchi weakened, the Otomo and Shimazu intervened in Higo's succession quarrels. After Toyotomi Hideyoshi conquered Kyushu in 1587, Sassa Narimasa entered the castle, but a forced land survey brought out the local warriors in revolt and Sassa was ordered to kill himself the next year. His lands passed to Katō Kiyomasa, one of Hideyoshi's Seven Spears of Shizugatake, while the Christian general Konishi Yukinaga held central and southern Higo. Konishi was executed after Sekigahara in 1600, and Kiyomasa united a 520,000-koku domain. He rebuilt Kumamoto from 1591, completed its keep around 1600, and gave the castle its present written name in 1607; its curved musha-gaeshi walls, turrets and gates were built to break any assault. After the Katō were attainted in 1632, Hosokawa Tadatoshi entered with 540,000 koku. The swordsman Miyamoto Musashi spent his final years under the Hosokawa and completed The Book of Five Rings there, and in 1821 Kumamoto remained one of the greatest castle towns in Tokugawa Japan.
zh:
肥后位于九州中部，地势从沿海平原抬向阿苏火山与林木幽深的球磨谷地。菊池氏是室町幕府任命的守护，但肥后并非他们独占之地：阿苏氏依托阿苏山一带的大社掌权，相良氏扎根南部山地。1444年，这里仍是多家势力并立的领国。菊池氏的军队和姻亲关系足以影响九州局势，但后来成为熊本的那片丘陵还没有那座名城。

熊本的崛起与统一战争连在一起。1469年至1487年，出田秀信在当地筑起千叶城；1521年至1531年，鹿子木亲员又修筑隈本城。菊池氏衰落后，大友氏与岛津氏先后介入肥后的继嗣纷争。1587年丰臣秀吉平定九州，佐佐成政进入熊本，却因强行检地激起国人反抗，次年被勒令切腹。他的领地转封给秀吉「贱岳七本枪」之一的加藤清正，信奉基督教的武将小西行长则领有肥后中部和南部。1600年关原之战后，小西被处死，清正合并成52万石的熊本藩。他1591年开始改建熊本城，约1600年建成天守，1607年定下「熊本」这个写法；弧形的「武者返」石垣、橹和城门都用于阻击攻城者。1632年加藤氏被改易，细川忠利以54万石入封。剑术家宫本武藏在细川氏庇护下度过晚年，在肥后完成《五轮书》；1821年，熊本仍是德川日本最重要的城下町之一。

en:
Hizen faces the seas of western Kyushu, covering the lands that became Saga and most of Nagasaki, a coast of sheltered harbours and the seafaring Matsuura districts cut off from inland Kyushu by hills. It was formed from the old Land of Hi at the end of the seventh century and kept provincial ranches and old trading ports, Hirado above all. In 1444 the Shoni, heirs of the Kamakura government's command in Kyushu, still carried weight, but no lord ruled all Hizen. The Muromachi deputy Shibukawa and local houses such as the Chiba of Saga, the Matsuura of Hirado and the Omura and Arima of the southern peninsulas held their own lands, and Nagasaki was only a small anchorage in Hirado's shadow.

The Portuguese at first traded at Hirado, but after attacks on foreigners there they turned to Omura Sumitada, baptised in 1563 as Dom Bartolomeu, the first Japanese daimyo to become a Christian. He gave them the harbour of Yokoseura and then opened Nagasaki to them in 1570; in 1580 he ceded the port to the Jesuits outright. The Tensho embassy sent by the Christian lords of Kyushu sailed from this coast for Rome in 1582. After his Kyushu campaign of 1587, Hideyoshi took Nagasaki under direct rule and ran the invasion of Korea from his headquarters at Nagoya in Hizen, and in 1597 twenty-six Christians were crucified at Nagasaki.

The Shimabara Rebellion of 1637-1638, raised by tax-burdened peasants and persecuted Kirishitan, ended with the storming of Hara Castle after a siege of several months; in 1641 the Dutch factory was moved to Dejima, through which nearly all of Japan's European trade then passed. Hizen also became Japan's porcelain country. After porcelain stone was found near Arita around the turn of the seventeenth century, Korean potters brought over in the Korean wars opened kilns there, and Imari and Kakiemon ware, with the finer Nabeshima ware made for the lords of Saga, went by way of Imari harbour to the Dutch at Nagasaki and on to Europe. The Nabeshima held most of the province from their castle town of Saga, while Nagasaki remained shogunal land.
zh:
肥前面向九州西部的大海，疆域相当于后来的佐贺和长崎大部，海岸曲折多避风良港，熟悉海路的松浦诸郡被丘陵与九州内陆隔开。它在7世纪末由旧肥国分置，境内有官营牧场和平户等老牌港口。1444年，继承镰仓幕府镇西职能的少贰氏仍有声望，却没有一位领主能统制整个肥前。室町幕府派出的涩川氏与佐贺千叶氏、平户松浦氏以及南部半岛的大村氏、有马氏等地方武家各据一方，长崎还只是平户阴影下的一个小港湾。

葡萄牙人最初在平户贸易，当地发生袭击外国人的事件后，他们转投大村纯忠。纯忠1563年受洗，教名巴尔多禄茂，是第一位成为基督徒的日本大名。他先向葡萄牙人开放横濑浦，又在1570年开放长崎，1580年更把长崎永久交给耶稣会。九州基督教大名派遣的天正遣欧使节1582年从这片海岸启程前往罗马。1587年丰臣秀吉平定九州后，把长崎收为直辖领，并在肥前名护屋设立大本营指挥侵朝；1597年，二十六名基督徒在长崎被钉上十字架。

1637至1638年，不堪重税的农民和受迫害的吉利支丹掀起岛原之乱，原城被围数月后遭攻破；1641年荷兰商馆迁到出岛，日本对欧洲的贸易此后几乎都经此进行。肥前还成了日本的瓷器产地。17世纪初有田附近发现瓷土，从朝鲜之役带回的朝鲜陶工在当地开窑，伊万里烧、柿右卫门和供佐贺藩主烧制的锅岛烧，经伊万里港运到长崎的荷兰人手中，再转销欧洲。锅岛氏以佐贺城下町为据点领有肥前大部，长崎则一直是幕府天领。

en:
Iwami faces the Sea of Japan west of Izumo, where narrow river valleys open into fishing harbours along the San'indō coast. Hamada was its provincial seat, while the Masuda, a warrior house of Genji descent, kept estates around Masuda and the western inlets. The Yamana held the provincial governorship in 1444, but local lords managed much of the hill country. Boats supplied fish from offshore banks, farmers worked the small valley fields, and the Ōuchi of neighbouring Suō already kept a close eye on local shipping and ores. The silver at Ōmori was not yet mined on a large scale.

Kamiya Jutei, a Hakata merchant backed by the Ōuchi, opened deep workings at Ōmori in 1526. Seven years later craftsmen introduced haifuki cupellation, allowing the mine to turn large amounts of ore into refined silver. Warlords treated Ōmori as a prize: the Ōuchi built Yamabuki Castle above the workings, the Amago of Izumo seized the mines, lost them and came back, and their men beat Mōri forces in the fighting of 1556 and 1559. Only after Amago Haruhisa's death did a 1562 truce leave the mountain to Mōri Motonari.

Tokugawa Ieyasu took Iwami Ginzan for the shogunate after Sekigahara, and Ōkubo Nagayasu became its first mining commissioner in 1601. In the early seventeenth century the mine produced about 38 tons of silver a year, close to a fifth of Japan's output; Sekishū chōgin ingots circulated in western Japan and went out on Chinese, Portuguese and Dutch ships. Guards escorted bars over the Chūgoku mountains to Onomichi and the Kyoto guild. Output fell after the 1670s, and the commissioner's post became a district magistracy. During the famine of 1731, the magistrate Ido Heizaemon opened granaries and promoted sweet potatoes, which earned him the name 'potato magistrate'.
zh:
石见位于出云以西，北临日本海，中国山地的河谷在山阴道沿岸通向一座座渔港。滨田是国府所在地，源氏出身的益田氏在益田一带和西部港湾保有领地。1444年，山名氏担任守护，山地却多由本地豪族自理。渔船出海捕捞，村民在狭小水田间耕作，邻接周防的大内氏也已留意这里的船运和矿产；大森的银矿还没有大规模开采。

1526年，博多商人神屋寿祯得到大内氏资助，在大森开出深入矿脉的坑道。1533年，工匠引入灰吹炼银法，矿石可以大量提炼成纯银。大森随即成为武将争夺的目标：大内氏在矿区上方修筑山吹城，出云尼子氏夺取银山、又在失守后反攻，并在1556年和1559年的战事中击败毛利军。直到尼子晴久死后，1562年的云艺和议才把这座山留给毛利元就。

关原之战后，德川家康把石见银山收为幕府直辖，1601年任命大久保长安为第一任银山奉行。17世纪初，这里年产银约38吨，接近日本全国产量的五分之一；石州丁银通行西日本，也随中国、葡萄牙和荷兰商船流出日本。役人护送银锭翻越中国山地到尾道，再转交京都的银座。1670年代后产量下降，银山奉行改设为代官。1731年饥荒时，代官井户平左卫门开仓放粮、推广甘薯，被领民称作「芋代官」。

en:
Bizen, or Bishū, was the easternmost province formed from the old kingdom of Kibi on the San'yō coast. Its rice fields and salt pans faced the Seto Inland Sea, while coastal ships carried goods toward the capital. The hill country supplied iron, and from Heian times smiths at Osafune and Fukuoka, including the Osafune and Ichimonji schools, made Bizen blades prized by warriors. The kilns at Imbe produced hard, unglazed Bizen ware, which tea masters later favoured for utensils. The Akamatsu of Harima long held the shugo post, but after their fall in 1441 the Yamana moved into Bizen. In 1444 the province was rich in grain and steel, with its new rulers not yet secure.

During the Sengoku wars the Urakami deputies displaced the Akamatsu, only to be overthrown by their vassal Ukita Naoie. Naoie made Okayama his seat and ruled Bizen with Mimasaka and parts of Bitchū. His son Hideie, one of Toyotomi Hideyoshi's five elders, completed the black-lacquered keep in 1597; gilded roof tiles gave it the name Golden Crow Castle. Hideie chose the losing side at Sekigahara in 1600, was attainted, and spent his later years exiled on Hachijōjima. After Kobayakawa Hideaki held Okayama for two years and died without an heir, the castle passed to the Ikeda, who governed Bizen from Okayama until the nineteenth century.

The Ikeda turned the domain to civil works. Under Lord Ikeda Tsunamasa, Tsuda Nagatada cut flood channels and opened new fields, and between 1687 and 1700 the domain laid out Kōraku-en beside Okayama Castle. Cotton spread over reclaimed coastal land, and works joined the island of Kojima to the mainland. The Ikeda also granted privileges to Bizen kiln families at Imbe, whose tea bowls, water jars and flower vessels kept the province's pottery in demand among tea circles.
zh:
备前简称备州，是古代吉备国分出的三国中最东的一国，位于山阳道沿海。稻田和盐田面向濑户内海，沿岸船只把货物运往畿内。山地出产铁，从平安时代起，长船、福冈的刀工，包括长船派和一文字派，打造出深受武将重视的备前刀。伊部窑场烧制坚硬无釉的备前烧，茶人后来很爱用它做茶器。播磨赤松氏长期担任守护，1441年赤松氏败亡后，山名氏进入备前。1444年的备前粮铁丰足，新主人的统治还不稳固。

战国乱世中，守护代浦上氏取代赤松氏，却被自家家臣宇喜多直家推翻。直家以冈山为本据，领有备前、美作和备中一部。其子宇喜多秀家是丰臣五大老之一，1597年建成漆黑的天守；瓦片贴金，使它得到「金乌城」之名。1600年关原之战，秀家加入战败一方，被剥夺领地，晚年流放八丈岛。小早川秀秋领有冈山两年后无嗣而终，冈山城随后转入池田氏手中，池田氏从冈山统治备前，直到19世纪。

池田氏把藩政转向土木营缮。藩主池田纲政命家臣津田永忠开凿排洪水道、开垦新田，又在1687至1700年间于冈山城边建成后乐园。沿海新田广泛种棉，儿岛也通过工程与陆地相连。池田氏还授予伊部备前烧窑户特权，他们烧制的茶碗、水罐和花器，让备前陶器继续受到茶人欢迎。

en:
Tango is the mountainous peninsula north of Kyoto, reaching into the Sea of Japan between Wakasa and Tajima. Its chief town, Miyazu, lies on a sheltered bay where the pine-covered sandbar of Ama-no-Hashidate cuts across the water, counted among the three famous views of Japan. Kono Shrine was the province's ichinomiya, and boats from Kumihama, Miyazu and Maizuru worked the offshore fishing banks and carried sea products toward the capital. The Isshiki, who had taken the shugo post from the Yamana in 1392, still held Tango in 1444.

In 1579 Oda Nobunaga's armies ended Isshiki rule and granted Tango to Hosokawa Fujitaka, better known as Yūsai, a general learned in poetry and court tradition. He built Tanabe Castle at Maizuru on the old governors' site. During the Sekigahara campaign of 1600, Yūsai burned Miyazu and held Tanabe with a small garrison against about 15,000 western soldiers for fifty days. Before the final assault he sent the secret Kokinshū texts transmitted in his school to Emperor Go-Yōzei; the court intervened, and the garrison was allowed to leave the castle.

His son Tadaoki was transferred to Kyushu, and Kyōgoku Takatomo received the whole province at 123,000 koku. After his death in 1622 it split into the Miyazu, Tanabe and Mineyama domains; the Miyazu line lost its domain through bad administration in 1666, the Tanabe house moved to Toyooka two years later, and only Mineyama stayed with the Kyōgoku. The shogun kept Kumihama as direct land. In the mid-Edo period Mineyama brought craftsmen from Nishijin to teach silk-crepe weaving, and Tango chirimen became the peninsula's best-known product.
zh:
丹后是京都以北的多山半岛，夹在若狭与但马之间伸入日本海。首府宫津位于避风湾内，青松覆盖的天桥立横过水面，是日本三景之一。笼神社是丹后一之宫，久美浜、宫津和舞鹤的船只在近海渔场捕鱼，也把海产运往京都。一色氏1392年从山名氏手中接过守护一职，到1444年仍领有丹后。

1579年，织田信长的军队终结一色氏统治，把丹后封给精通和歌与朝廷典故的武将细川藤孝（幽斋）。他在舞鹤的旧守护所修筑田边城。1600年关原之战时，幽斋烧掉宫津城，以少量守军在田边城抵御约一万五千西军达五十天。总攻之前，他把本门秘传的《古今集》授书献给后阳成天皇；朝廷出面调停，守军获准开城撤离。

幽斋之子忠兴被转封九州后，京极高知领有丹后一国，石高十二万三千石。1622年高知死后，领地分成宫津、田边、峰山三藩；宫津一支1666年因恶政被改易，田边一支两年后转封丰冈，只有峰山藩留在京极氏手中。幕府直辖久美浜。江户中期，峰山藩从西阵请来织工传授绉绸织法，丹后绉绸成了这座半岛最出名的物产。

en:
Iyo, or Yoshū, occupies northwestern Shikoku, with bays and islands opening onto the Seto Inland Sea. The Geiyo Islands break the route toward Honshu, while Dōgo's hot springs behind Matsuyama were already known in the early chronicles and Ōyamazumi Shrine on Ōmishima served sailors and warriors. The old Kōno house held the governor's title and kept Yuzuki Castle beside Dōgo from 1335, but its fleets came from the Murakami sea lords of Innoshima, Kurushima and Noshima. They collected passage money in the island channels and attacked ships that refused to pay. In 1444 the Kōno spoke for Iyo in name, houses such as the Utsunomiya and Saionji held the southern valleys, and the Murakami ships decided who could use the sea roads.

Kōno succession disputes, Ōuchi pressure on the Geiyo Islands and Chōsokabe attacks from Tosa after 1581 left the house leaning on Mōri support. Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Shikoku campaign reached Yuzuki in 1585; after about a month the castle surrendered, and the last Kōno lord, Michinao, died at Takehara two years later. Kobayakawa Takakage briefly held Iyo before the province was divided into several Tokugawa domains. Work began on Matsuyama Castle on Mount Katsuyama in 1602, and in 1614 Tokugawa Ieyasu granted Uwajima in the south, rated at 100,000 koku, to Date Hidemune, eldest son of Date Masamune.

The mountains behind Niihama brought a different kind of wealth after the Sumitomo opened the Besshi copper mine in 1691. Its output reached a pre-modern peak in 1698, and Besshi became one of Japan's three great copper mines. The copper supplied the shogunate's coinage and the export trade through Nagasaki for the rest of the Tokugawa period.
zh:
伊予别称予州，位于四国西北部，曲折的海湾和岛屿面向濑户内海。艺予诸岛散落在通往本州的航线上，松山后方的道后温泉在早期史书里已有名气，大三岛上的大山祇神社则受水手和武人奉祀。古老的河野氏拥有守护头衔，1335年起在道后旁以汤筑城为居城，但舰队掌握在因岛、来岛、能岛的村上水军手中。他们在岛屿海峡征收通航钱，拒绝缴纳的船只就会遭到攻击。1444年，河野氏只是名义上号令伊予，宇都宫氏、西园寺氏等家族占据南部山谷，谁能通过海路则要由村上的船队决定。

河野氏的家督纷争、大内氏对艺予诸岛的压迫，以及1581年后长宗我部氏从土佐发起的进攻，使河野氏日益依赖毛利氏的援助。1585年，丰臣秀吉的四国征伐军抵达汤筑城，围城约一个月后城池开城；末代当主河野通直获免，两年后在竹原去世。小早川隆景一度领有伊予，随后该地在江户时代被分成数个藩。松山城于1602年在胜山动工；1614年，德川家康把南部十万石的宇和岛封给伊达政宗的长子伊达秀宗。

新居滨后方的山地则带来另一种财富。1691年，住友家开坑别子铜山，1698年产量达到近代以前的高峰，别子也成为日本三大铜山之一。江户时代余下的岁月里，这里的铜支撑着幕府铸币，也经长崎港投入海外贸易。

en:
Kii wraps around the south-western side of the Kii Peninsula, where forested mountains fall to the Kii Channel and the Kumano Sea. Its hills supplied timber and ship stores, Kumano mariners sailed its coasts into the Inland Sea trade, and pilgrims took the Kumano roads toward the Kumano shrines and the mountain monastery of Koya-san; another Shingon house, Negoro-ji, kept armed followers of its own. After the Northern and Southern courts were reconciled the Hatakeyama held the office of provincial shugo, but the monasteries, local gentry and armed seafaring communes left them little power. In 1444 the Hatakeyama governed Kii chiefly in name.

No Sengoku lord found the province easy. At Ota the Saika communes under Suzuki Magoichi hired themselves out as matchlock mercenaries, famed for their gunners and gunsmiths; up in the hills Negoro-ji kept some ten thousand soldier-monks, many armed with muskets, on estates rated at 720,000 koku, a match for a great daimyo. Both sent help to the Ishiyama Hongan-ji while Oda Nobunaga besieged it, and Nobunaga marched on Ota himself in 1577. The Jesuit Luis Frois described Kii's self-governing communes as little republics no lord had been able to destroy. In 1584 Saika and Negoro raided toward Osaka while Toyotomi Hideyoshi was locked in war with Tokugawa Ieyasu; he marched against them the next year and burned Negoro-ji on 23 March 1585, then flooded Ota Castle into surrender after about a month. He ordered a sword hunt and had Wakayama Castle built as the province's new centre.

After Sekigahara in 1600 Asano Yoshinaga was enfeoffed at Kii; in 1619 the Asano moved to Hiroshima and Tokugawa Yorinobu, Ieyasu's tenth son, took Wakayama with 555,000 koku. His Kii Tokugawa house became one of the three collateral houses allowed to supply a shogun, and Kii produced one in 1716, when its lord Yoshimune went to Edo as the eighth shogun and carried through the Kyoho reforms.
zh:
纪伊占据纪伊半岛西南侧，多林的山地直落纪伊水道与熊野滩。山地出产木材和船用物料，熊野水军驾船沿海航行，卷入濑户内海的贸易；巡礼者沿熊野古道前往熊野三山和高野山的山岳道场，另一座真言宗寺院根来寺也蓄有自己的武装。南北朝合一后，畠山氏担任纪伊守护，但大寺社、国人豪族和武装的海上共同体留给他们的权力所剩无几。1444年的畠山氏对纪伊的统治，大半只停留在名义上。

战国时代没有哪位大名能轻易拿下纪伊。以铃木孙市为首的杂贺众据守太田一带，以铁炮雇佣兵为业，枪手和造枪工匠都很出名；山中的根来寺领有七十二万石的寺领，养着约万名僧兵，其中不少是铁炮手，实力堪比大藩。织田信长围攻石山本愿寺时，两方都出兵相助，信长本人也在1577年亲征太田。耶稣会士路易斯·弗洛伊斯把纪伊这些自治共同体比作无人能灭的小共和国。1584年，趁丰臣秀吉与德川家康交战，杂贺、根来势力进逼大阪；秀吉次年挥军来攻，1585年3月23日火烧根来寺，又筑堤水攻太田城约一个月，迫其投降。他随后在纪伊推行刀狩，并新建和歌山城作为统治中心。

1600年关原之战后，浅野幸长受封纪伊；1619年浅野氏转封广岛，德川家康第十子德川赖宣以五十五万五千石入主和歌山。纪州德川家列为德川御三家之一，有资格继嗣将军；1716年纪伊真的出了一位将军，藩主德川吉宗入主江户，是为第八代将军，推行享保改革。

en:
Shinano, also called Shinshū, filled the mountainous middle of Honshū between Kantō and the Japan Sea coast, its high ranges split into the Matsumoto, Ina and Zenkō-ji basins. The Tōsandō road, later the Nakasendō, threaded these valleys, and the high pastures of Kiso bred the small, sturdy horses prized by warlords. Two sanctuaries drew travellers: Suwa Taisha, the province's chief shrine, in the south, and Zenkō-ji in the north, where pilgrims prayed before a hidden Amida under the saying that everyone ought to visit once; the temple's monzen town grew into Nagano. In 1444 no lord ruled the whole province. The Ogasawara held the shugo title, while the Murakami, Takanashi and Suwa kept their own basins and the Kiso held the mountain road, none strong enough to overawe the rest.

The fighting that made Shinano known began when Takeda Shingen of Kai, who seized his own clan in 1541, destroyed the Suwa in 1542 and drove the Ogasawara out of Fukashi Castle by 1550, carrying Zenkō-ji's hidden Buddha off to his capital at Kōfu. The displaced northern lords turned to Uesugi Kenshin of Echigo, and from 1553 to 1564 the two fought five battles on the Kawanakajima flatland between the Chikuma and Sai rivers without either ever holding it for good. After the Takeda fell in 1582, Nobunaga divided Shinano among his generals and the Tokugawa later took the greater part; at Ueda in 1600 the Sanada pinned Hidetada's 38,000 men with 2,000 defenders long enough that Ieyasu's son missed the battle of Sekigahara. Under Tokugawa rule the province held nineteen domains. Ishikawa Kazumasa raised Matsumoto's black keep after 1590, Nakasendō post towns served the Kiso valley whose cypress went to the Owari lords of Nagoya, and new irrigation canals opened fresh fields, until the 1783 eruption of Mount Asama helped bring on the Tenmei famine.
zh:
信浓（简称信州）位于本州中部的山岳地带，隔在关东与日本海沿岸之间，群山之间分布着松本、伊那和善光寺平等盆地。东山道（后来的中山道）沿山谷穿行，木曾的高山牧场出产军阀看重的矮壮良马。国内两处圣地吸引行旅：南方的一之宫诹访大社，北方的善光寺；善光寺供奉秘佛阿弥陀如来，「一生一度上善光」的说法吸引各方参拜者，门前町后来发展为长野。1444年，没有一家能统治全信浓：小笠原氏保有守护头衔，村上、高梨、诹访诸氏各据盆地，木曾氏控扼山路，谁也压服不了谁。

让信浓留名的大战起于甲斐的武田信玄。他1541年夺取家督，1542年攻灭诹访，到1550年把小笠原氏逐出深志城，还把善光寺的秘佛运到自己的居城甲府。失领的北信豪族投奔越后的上杉谦信，1553至1564年间，两大对手在千曲川与犀川之间的川中岛五次交战，谁也没能长久占有这块平地。1582年武田氏灭亡后，信长把信浓分给诸将，大部分后来落入德川之手；1600年，真田氏在上田城以两千守军拖住德川秀忠的三万八千人，使家康之子没能赶上关原之战。德川治下，信浓分为十九个藩；石川数正1590年后筑起松本城的黑漆天守，中山道宿场町沿路兴起，木曾谷的桧林供应名古屋的尾张藩，灌溉渠又开出新田，直到1783年浅间山喷发，加重了天明大饥馑。

en:
Sagami faces Sagami Bay on the Tōkaidō, where coastal plains and the Ashigara passes join Kanto to Suruga and the road to Kyoto. Samukawa Shrine was its ichinomiya, but the province is remembered for Kamakura: Minamoto no Yoritomo entered it in 1180 and built Japan's first samurai government there, and the Hōjō regents ruled from it until 1333. Tsurugaoka Hachimangū, the Zen temples Kenchō-ji and Engaku-ji and the bronze Great Buddha of Kōtoku-in date from those years. In 1333 Nitta Yoshisada took the town by wading past the Inamuragasaki headland at low tide, and the last Hōjō regents and hundreds of their kinsmen killed themselves at Tōshō-ji. The Ashikaga kept a Kamakura government over the east until its kubō Ashikaga Mochiuji turned against the Uesugi and the Muromachi shogunate; Kamakura fell in 1439 and Mochiuji killed himself. In 1444 Sagami was formally back in Ashikaga hands, its old military capital much weakened.

In 1455 the last Kamakura kubō, Ashikaga Shigeuji, moved his seat to Koga in Shimōsa, and Kamakura emptied. Early in the sixteenth century Ise Moritoki, later called Hōjō Sōun, seized Odawara east of Kamakura, and five Later Hōjō lords made it the strongest fortress in the Kanto. A tsunami swept away the Kōtoku-in Buddha's hall in 1498, leaving the bronze statue in the open, and fighting in 1526 left Kamakura all but burned; the clan rebuilt Tsurugaoka Hachimangū after its wars with the Satomi. Odawara threw back Uesugi Kenshin's siege of 1561 and weathered Takeda Shingen's demonstration before its walls in 1569, but in 1590 Toyotomi Hideyoshi's host surrounded it. After three months the Later Hōjō surrendered almost without a battle, and their Kanto domains passed to Tokugawa Ieyasu.

Ōkubo Tadayo rebuilt the castle on a smaller scale for the Tokugawa, and Odawara became a fudai castle town and the largest of the fifty-three Tōkaidō post stations; at Uraga on the Miura peninsula officials checked ships entering Edo Bay. Kamakura drew pilgrims and sightseers from Edo to its temples and the open-air Buddha. In 1703 the Genroku earthquake wrecked Odawara; the Hōei earthquake and Mount Fuji's eruption followed in 1707.
zh:
相模是东海道上面朝相模湾的令制国，沿海平原和足柄隘口把关东同骏河、同通往京都的东海道连在一起。寒川神社是国内一之宫，真正让这一国扬名的是镰仓：1180年源赖朝进入镰仓，在此建立日本第一个武家政权，北条执权从这里统治天下，直到1333年。鹤冈八幡宫，建长寺、圆觉寺等禅宗大寺，以及高德院的青铜镰仓大佛，都是那个时代留下的。1333年，新田义贞趁退潮绕过稻村崎攻入镰仓，末代北条执权与数百族人在东胜寺自尽。足利氏的镰仓府继续统辖关东，但1438年镰仓公方足利持氏与上杉氏、室町幕府兵戎相见，1439年镰仓城破，持氏自尽。1444年的相模名义上重归足利氏，这座旧武家都城却已大为衰弱。

镰仓的衰落再未扭转。1455年，末代镰仓公方足利成氏把治所迁往下总国古河，镰仓人口渐空。16世纪初，后来世称北条早云的伊势盛时夺取镰仓以东的小城小田原，后北条氏五代领主把它经营成关东最强的城池。1498年大海啸卷走供奉高德院大佛的佛殿，大佛便一直露天而坐；1526年的战火又几乎把镰仓焚毁。后北条氏在与里见氏交战后重建鹤冈八幡宫，旧都居民也多被迁往小田原。小田原顶住了1561年上杉谦信的围攻，1569年武田信玄兵临城下的示威也无功而返；但1590年丰臣秀吉率西方大军压境，围城三个月后后北条氏几乎未经激战便开城投降，关东领地转封给德川家康。

大久保忠世为德川氏按较小的规模重修了小田原城。江户时代，这里成为谱代大名的城下町，也是东海道五十三次最东端、规模最大的宿场；三浦半岛端头的浦贺设有官员盘查进出江户湾的船只。镰仓归于平静，各座寺院和露天大佛吸引江户的参拜客与游人前来。1703年元禄大地震摧毁小田原，1707年宝永地震和富士山喷发又接踵而至。

en:
Shimōsa lay across the lower Tone and Edo River lowlands north of the Boso Peninsula, covering most of later northern Chiba and southwestern Ibaraki. Formed in the seventh century when the old land of Fusa was divided, it kept its provincial capital near Ichikawa and Katori Shrine as its chief sanctuary. The Chiba, who had backed Minamoto no Yoritomo, held the governorship for generations, but by the Muromachi age they shared the province with the Yuki and other houses. In 1444 the Chiba, still seated around Inohana on the coast, were the leading family of a fragmented land of river plains, hemp fields and fishing shores.

The province's fate was settled on the Konodai heights: the Later Hōjō of Odawara defeated Ashikaga Yoshiaki and the Satomi there in 1538 and beat the Satomi again in 1564, pulling the Chiba and the smaller Hara and Takagi houses into their orbit. When Odawara fell to Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1590, Chiba Shigetane surrendered Sakura to Honda Tadakatsu and Sakai Ietsugu, and the Chiba lost the dominion their house had held since the Kamakura age. The Tokugawa split Shimōsa between vassal fiefs and direct shogunal land, and Doi Toshikatsu rebuilt Sakura Castle from 1610 to 1617 to guard the eastern road into Edo; the Hotta were its best-known later lords.

At Narita, the Shinshō-ji temple drew pilgrims longer than any castle. It was founded in 940, when the Shingon priest Kanchō brought a Fudō image said to have been carved by Kūkai and performed fire rites for the court army that put down Taira no Masakado's revolt. Ieyasu credited its abbot with turning him to Buddhism and charged the lords of Sakura with the temple's upkeep, and after the main hall was rebuilt in 1655 the kabuki actor Ichikawa Danjūrō I made the Narita Fudō famous with a play in 1703; commoners from Edo then took to the road to pray there in crowds.
zh:
下总位于房总半岛以北的利根川下游与江户川低地，辖境大体是后来的千叶县北部和茨城县西南部。7世纪旧总国分为上下两国时设立，国衙在市川附近，香取神宫为国内一宫。曾支持源赖朝的千叶氏世袭守护之职，到室町时代已须与结城氏等豪族分享权力。1444年，本据仍在沿海亥鼻一带的千叶氏是国内最有势力的家族，而这片河川平原、麻地和渔业海岸已被各家领地分割。

下总的归属在国府台高地决出：1538年，小田原的后北条氏在此击败足利义明和里见氏，1564年再破里见氏，千叶、原、高城诸家随之进入后北条氏的势力圈。1590年小田原落入丰臣秀吉之手后，千叶重胤把佐仓交给本多忠胜和酒井家次，千叶氏丧失了镰仓以来的旧领。德川氏把下总分为家臣藩领与幕府直辖地，土井利胜于1610至1617年重建佐仓城，扼守通往江户的东路；堀田氏是后来最知名的藩主。

成田的新胜寺吸引参拜者的时间比任何城池都久。这座真言宗寺院建于940年，僧人宽朝携一尊相传为空海所刻的不动明王像，随朝廷讨伐军修护摩法事，平定了平将门之乱，因而就地建寺。家康自称因该寺住持而归依佛门，并令佐仓藩负责寺院营缮；本堂1655年重建后，歌舞伎名优初代市川团十郎1703年以一出戏让成田不动声名远播，江户平民此后成群上路参拜。

en:
Shimotsuke filled the inland Tochigi basin beyond northern Kantō and took its present name in 713. Its Nara-period capital stood near Tochigi, where the great Shimotsuke Yakushi-ji was founded, while Futarasan Shrine at Utsunomiya served as the province's chief shrine. Around 1063 a castle went up south of that shrine, where the Ōshū and Nikkō highways met, and the Utsunomiya clan, descendants of Fujiwara, held it for five centuries; the Ashikaga shōguns took their name from an estate here, and the Nasu held lands in the north. The old Ashikaga Gakkō, revived by Uesugi Norizane in 1432, taught the Confucian classics and medicine under Zen monks and drew some three thousand students by the next century; Francis Xavier called it the greatest academy in the Kantō lands. In 1444 Utsunomiya Castle nevertheless commanded the rich Kinugawa grain fields while the province stayed a mosaic of rival warrior houses.

Pressed by the Later Hōjō, Takeda and Uesugi, the Utsunomiya held their castle through the Sengoku wars and joined Toyotomi Hideyoshi at Odawara in 1590, only to be dispossessed in 1597 when their reported revenues far exceeded their grant. After Sekigahara the province passed through several lords until Honda Masazumi, one of the first rōjū, entered Utsunomiya in 1619 at 155,000 koku, ringed the castle with water moats and rebuilt the post town for the traffic climbing to Nikkō. He fell three years later: Shōgun Hidetada planned to lodge at the castle after visiting Ieyasu's tomb at Nikkō, but heard that Masazumi had fitted a dropping ceiling to crush him, and never entered; Masazumi lost his domain and was exiled to Dewa. Fudai lords then followed in quick succession, the Toda returning in 1774.

That traffic climbed to Nikkō itself. After Ieyasu died in 1616 his remains were entombed at the Nikkō Tōshō-gū, built the next year by Tōdō Takatora and lavishly enlarged under his grandson Iemitsu, with the carved Yōmeimon gate and the stable relief of the three wise monkeys. Shogunal processions of daimyō retinues travelled the Nikkō Kaidō up from Edo for the memorial rites, between cedars planted along the road.
zh:
下野占据关东以北的栃木盆地，713年定今名。奈良时代的国衙在后来的栃木市一带，宏伟的下野药师寺建于此；宇都宫的二荒山神社为国内一宫。约1063年，神社南侧、奥州街道与日光街道交会处筑起城池，藤原后裔宇都宫氏在此盘踞五百年；足利将军家的名字就来自国内的足利庄，那须氏则领有北方。古老的足利学校1432年由上杉宪实复兴，以禅僧为师讲授儒家经典与中国医药，到下一个世纪已有学生约三千人，方济各·沙勿略称它为关东最负盛名的学府。1444年，宇都宫城控制着鬼怒川沿岸的富饶粮田，国内却仍是诸武家割据的拼图。

战国时代，下野受到后北条、武田和上杉的逼迫，宇都宫氏据城撑过战乱，1590年参加小田原征伐，却在1597年因申报收入远超恩准石高而被改易。关原之后藩主几度更替，1619年，幕府最早的老中之一本多正纯以15万5千石入封宇都宫，绕城开凿多重水濠，又为前往日光的人流重整宿场。三年后他倒台：将军秀忠参拜日光的家康陵墓后原定在宇都宫城宿泊，有人告发正纯在殿中装设可落下的天井，要压死将军；秀忠没有入城，正纯被夺封流放至出羽。此后谱代大名更替频繁，户田氏于1774年再封宇都宫。

参拜的人流最终登上日光。家康1616年死后葬于日光东照宫，神社次年由藤堂高虎主持建成，其孙家光时又大加扩建，留下雕饰繁丽的阳明门和神厩上的三猿雕刻。为举行祭典，将军的参拜行列沿日光街道从江户北上，路旁是为这条路栽种的杉树。

en:
The coastal plain below the Ōu range faces the Sea of Japan and, across the water, the island of Ezo. In 733 the Nara court built Akita Castle here as a base for subduing the Emishi, and the anchorage at Tsuchizaki became the port through which dealings with the Ainu passed; from the Kamakura age the Andō clan, installed at Tsugaru by the Hōjō, ran this northern trade. Fish from the offshore grounds and goods from Ezo made the family, and in 1444 the Andō were lords of the whole coast. The Sengoku wars cost them Tsugaru, which the Nanbu took: Andō Chikasue fell back on Akita, made it his seat and took the place's name for his clan, and under Toyotomi Hideyoshi his heir Akita Sanesue held the country round the city at 50,000 koku.

After Sekigahara the Satake of Hitachi paid for the side they had taken. Once lords of an entire province rated at 540,000 koku, they were moved to Akita in 1602 with their large old retinue, while Sanesue was transferred the other way to Shishido in Hitachi. Their new domain's rating was left unset until 1664, when it came to 205,800 koku, though the land yielded close to twice as much; even so the swollen household ran chronic debts, and a quarrel over paper money set off the Satake Disturbance in 1754. Its eighth lord, Satake Yoshiatsu, who styled himself Shōzan, spent on painting instead: between 1773 and 1780 he and his retainer Odano Naotake founded the Akita school, using Western shadows and perspective on Japanese plants, birds and insects. Naotake had studied in Edo under Hiraga Gennai, who was first invited to Akita to advise on the domain's copper mines, whose metal went out through Nagasaki. In 1807, when Russian raiders struck Ezo, the domain sent troops to garrison Hakodate; they were kept there forty days.
zh:
羽后地处奥羽山脉之下，沿海平原隔日本海与虾夷相望。733年，奈良朝廷在此修筑秋田城，作为制服虾夷的前沿据点；土崎泊地成为港口，与阿伊努人的往来都经此出入。镰仓时代，奉北条之命驻在津轻的安東氏掌管着这道北方生意，渔场的鱼获和虾夷来的货物养起了这一家，1444年安東氏正是整片海岸的主人。战国乱世中，南部氏夺走津轻，安東爱季退回秋田、以此为居城并取姓秋田；到丰臣秀吉时，其子秋田实季领有秋田周边五万石。

关原之战后，常陆佐竹氏为自己在变局中的立场付出了代价。这个曾领有常陆一国五十四万石的家族，1602年被转封秋田，庞大的旧臣团随行，实季则被对调往常陆宍户。新领国的表高一直没有核定，直到1664年才定为二十万五千八百石，而实际收成接近两倍；即便如此，臃肿的家臣团仍年年举债，1754年围绕藩札的争端又引发佐竹骚动。八代藩主佐竹义敦号曙山，把钱花在了绘画上：1773至1780年间，他与家臣小田野直武开创秋田兰画，用西洋的阴影和透视画日本的花鸟草虫。直武曾在江户师从平贺源内，源内最初受请来秋田，是为指导藩内的铜矿，所产之铜经长崎输出。1807年俄国船寇犯虾夷，藩中派兵守备箱馆，只驻了四十天。

en:
Oshima is the mild southern peninsula of Ezo and the only part of the island where Japanese had settled in force by the fifteenth century. Migrants from Tsugaru built fortified houses along the coast, later counted as the Twelve Houses of Dōnan, from Shinoridate on Hakodate Bay to Hanazawa at Kaminokuni. Their lords served the Andō family, deputies for the northern seas. Matsumae, Esashi and Usukeshi, later called Hakodate, shipped herring, salmon, kelp and furs south and brought back iron, rice and cloth. In 1444 the Andō banner still flew over the stockades, while the country beyond them belonged to the Ainu.

A knife quarrel opened the war that brought the Matsumae to power. In 1456, at Shinori, a Japanese blacksmith killed an Ainu customer during a dispute over a ritual knife. When Koshamain united the eastern Ainu two years later, ten of the twelve fortified houses fell. Takeda Nobuhiro counterattacked from Hanazawa and killed Koshamain and his son at Nanaehama in 1458, giving his Kakizaki kinsmen control of Katsuyama. Ainu forces under the brothers Shoya and Koji took the Matsumae stronghold in 1513, but Kakizaki Mitsuhiro occupied it the following year.

The clan converted military footholds into a trade monopoly. Toyotomi Hideyoshi confirmed Kakizaki Yoshihiro as lord of Ezo in 1593, after which he took the name Matsumae and built Fukuyama Hall at Matsumae between 1600 and 1606. Tokugawa Ieyasu's black-seal patent of 1604 granted the house exclusive trade with the Ainu. The shogunate took Ezo under direct rule in 1807, moved the Matsumae lord to Yanagawa in Mutsu, and held the Russian captain Golovnin at Matsumae from 1811 to 1813. The clan received its domain back in 1821.
zh:
渡岛是虾夷地南端气候温和的半岛，也是15世纪和人成规模定居的唯一区域。来自津轻的移民在沿海筑馆，后来合称「道南十二馆」，东起箱馆湾的志苔馆，西至上之国的花泽馆，馆主都奉统辖北方海域的安东氏。松前、江差、宇须岸（后来称箱馆）把鲱鱼、鲑鱼、昆布和毛皮南运，换回铁器、米和布匹。1444年，十二馆的栅栏内仍挂着安东氏旗帜，栅栏之外则是阿伊努人的土地。

一场小刀争端开启了松前氏崛起的战争。1456年，在志苔一地，一名和人铁匠因祭祀小刀的价钱和质量争执，杀死了阿伊努顾客。两年后，科夏迈因联合东部阿伊努人进攻，十二馆陷落十馆。武田信广从花泽馆反击，1458年在七重滨击杀科夏迈因父子，让蛎崎族人掌握了胜山。1513年，庶野、訇时兄弟率领阿伊努人攻陷松前大馆，但蛎崎光广在次年入主该城。

松前氏把军事据点变成贸易垄断。1593年，丰臣秀吉承认蛎崎庆广为虾夷岛主，他随后改称松前，并于1600至1606年在松前修筑福山馆。1604年，德川家康颁发黑印状，授予松前氏与阿伊努人贸易的独占权。1807年，幕府将虾夷地收归直辖，把松前藩主移封陆奥梁川；俄国舰长戈洛夫宁于1811至1813年被囚禁在松前。1821年，松前氏才重新领有此地。

en:
Yongping was a Ming prefecture on the coastal plain between the Yan Mountains and the Bohai Sea. Its seat stood at Lulong, while the prefecture's eastern end narrowed into the Liaoxi Corridor, the strip of dry land that carried troops, grain carts and merchants between Beijing and Liaodong. In 1381 Xu Da built Shanhai Pass where the eastern Great Wall meets the coast. By 1444 the walled pass and the prefectural towns behind it held the shortest road from Liaodong and the Jurchen lands into the Beijing region, and Yongping formed part of Northern Zhili.

The tower above Shanhai Pass bears the inscription 'First Pass Under Heaven'. In the late sixteenth century Qi Jiguang strengthened its walls, watchtowers and outworks after his campaigns against the wokou. Hong Taiji avoided a direct assault in 1629 and turned through narrow passes in the Yan Mountains instead; Later Jin troops reached the Yongping plain and took Lulong early in 1630 before Sun Chengzong's counterattack recovered Yongping and neighbouring cities. The coastal road still settled the issue in 1644. Wu Sangui withdrew his Ningyuan garrison into Shanhai Pass and submitted to the Qing regent Dorgon, and on 27 May their combined forces defeated Li Zicheng outside the walls before the Qing army moved on Beijing. Under Qing rule Lulong remained the seat of Yongping Prefecture, while the old Shanhai garrison became Linyu County.
zh:
永平是明代府份，府治卢龙，位于燕山与渤海之间的滨海平原。府境东端收窄成辽西走廊，北京通往辽东的军队、粮车和商旅多沿这条干地行进。1381年，徐达在明长城东端临海处修筑山海关。到1444年，关城和后方的永平诸城控制着辽东、女真之地进入京师附近最近的陆路，永平府当时隶属北直隶。

山海关城楼匾额题有「天下第一关」。16世纪后期，戚继光在抗倭之后主持加固这里的城墙、敌台和外围工事。1629年，皇太极没有正面强攻，而是绕道燕山诸口；后金军进入永平平原，于1630年初攻占卢龙，随后孙承宗组织反攻，收复永平及附近诸城。1644年，滨海大路仍决定了胜负：吴三桂率宁远守军退入山海关，归降清朝摄政王多尔衮，5月27日两军在关城外合力击败李自成，清军随即进向北京。清代卢龙仍为永平府治，旧山海卫改设临榆县。

en:
Zhending stands on the grain plain north of the Hutuo River, where the passes of the Taihang range open onto the North China Plain and the road from Beijing runs south into Henan. Its most famous native was Zhao Yun, the Shu Han general of the Three Kingdoms: born a man of Changshan Zhending, in the Romance of the Three Kingdoms he opens a fight with the cry 'I am Zhao Zilong of Changshan'. After the An Lushan rebellion the city became the seat of the Chengde military governors. Its Longxing Temple was founded under the Sui in 586; in 971 Song Taizu ordered it rebuilt on a grand scale, and the monks cast a 21.3-metre bronze thousand-armed Guanyin for its Dabei Pavilion, with Tang and Song pagodas of other monasteries standing around the city. Jin troops took Zhending in 1126 and carried off the Song prefect Li Miao, who refused to submit and was killed. In 1399 the Prince of Yan, marching on the throne in the Jingnan campaign, caught the imperial general Geng Bingwen outside the walls with 130,000 men, beheaded 30,000 of them and seized his senior commanders; Geng shut himself in, and the prince raised the three-day siege and moved on. In 1444 Zhending was a major prefectural city guarding Beijing's southern road, its monasteries fed by the grain of the surrounding plain.

The earthen ramparts were enlarged in 1449 to a circumference of twenty-four li, and brick facing, begun in 1571, was finished in 1576; each of the four gates received an inner wall, a barbican and a crescent outer wall, a triple defence few Chinese cities could show. In 1669 the Zhili governor moved his seat to Baoding, and Zhending ceased to be a provincial capital. The Kangxi Emperor granted a name plaque to Longxing Temple in 1710. In 1723 the county and prefecture were renamed Zhengding, because the sound of their old name clashed with the Yongzheng Emperor's personal name.
zh:
真定位于滹沱河北岸的粮田平野，太行山诸口在这里通向华北平原，北京南下河南的大道也经此而过。真定最出名的同乡是三国蜀汉名将赵云：他是常山真定人，《三国演义》里临阵通名，一句「吾乃常山赵子龙」。安史之乱后，这里是成德军节度使的驻地。隆兴寺始建于隋代586年，971年宋太祖下令大事扩建，为大悲宝阁铸起21.3米高的铜质千手千眼观音，城内外还散布着其他寺院的唐宋佛塔。1126年金军攻占真定，俘去宋知府李邈，他拒不屈降，被杀。1399年靖难之役中，燕王朱棣在城外咬住率十三万大军北征的耿炳文，斩首三万余级，生擒其大将；耿炳文退入城中固守，燕王攻城三日不克，解围而去。1444年的真定是拱卫北京南路的重要府城，周围平原的粮食供养着城内众多寺院。

1449年，土城扩建为周长二十四里的城垣；1571年开始包砖，1576年完工，四座城门各设里城、瓮城和月城三道城垣，这样的三重规制在全国也不多见。1669年，直隶巡抚移驻保定，真定失去了省级治所的地位。1710年，康熙帝为隆兴寺赐额。1723年，因旧名读音触犯雍正帝名讳，真定县、真定府改称正定。

en:
Haizhou lies on the open Jiangsu coast where the Shandong hills run down to the sea, a shore of tidal flats, salterns and offshore islands. In 212 BC the First Emperor raised a stone marker on the Qu headland and named it the Eastern Gate of Qin. The Yuntai peaks then stood out at sea as islands; their highest summit, called Cangwu in Tang and Song times, was later renamed Huaguoshan, the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit, and is the place most commonly taken as the original of Sun Wukong's enchanted island in Journey to the West. South of the department town rise the Kongwang Hills, whose cliffs carry late Han carvings of the Buddha and Laozi cut in the second century, among the oldest Buddhist images in China. The early Ming folded Qushan county into Haizhou and placed the department under Huai'an Prefecture, with only Ganyu county attached. In 1444 it is a remote corner of salt and fish: fishermen work the shallows off Lian Island, and the northern Huai salterns with the salt office at Banpu draw merchants to the coast.

The Qing kept the department as it was until 1668, when the great Tancheng earthquake convulsed the shore: the Ganyu flats were heaved upward and the sea withdrew some thirty li, and the waters around Yuntai grew steadily shallower. In 1724 the Yongzheng Emperor raised Haizhou to a department directly under Jiangsu, adding Shuyang to Ganyu. The salt office at Banpu brought the town its best-remembered resident. In 1782 the nineteen-year-old Li Ruzhen followed his elder brother, a salt-tax official, to the town and studied under the scholar Ling Tingkan; after nearly twenty years and three drafts he completed Flowers in the Mirror in 1818, whose voyagers sail to imagined kingdoms beyond the eastern sea.
zh:
海州在江苏北部开阔的海岸上，山东丘陵在这里没入海中，沿岸尽是滩涂、盐田和离岸岛屿。公元前212年，秦始皇在朐县临海处立石，称这里为「秦东门」。那时云台群峰还是海上的岛屿，主峰唐宋时名叫苍梧山，后来改名花果山，被较普遍地看作《西游记》里孙悟空那座仙山的原型。州城之南的孔望山，崖壁上留有东汉晚期雕造的老子与佛像石刻，成于2世纪，是中国最早的佛教造像之一。明初省朐山县入海州，划归淮安府，唯领赣榆一县。1444年的海州是一处偏远的盐渔角落：渔民在连岛外的浅海劳作，淮北盐场和板浦盐课司把商人招到海边。

入清以后海州建制照旧，直到1668年郯城大地震撼动海岸：赣榆滩涂隆起，海水后退约三十里，云台山四周的海域日渐淤浅。1724年，雍正皇帝升海州为直隶州，除赣榆外又划来沭阳县。板浦的盐务还成全了一部奇书：1782年，十九岁的李汝珍随任盐课司大使的兄长来到板浦，师事学者凌廷堪，近二十年里三易其稿，于1818年写成《镜花缘》，让远航者遍历东海之外一个个想象中的国度。

en:
Huangzhou Prefecture lay along the north bank of the middle Yangtze, where river plains meet the southern edge of the Dabie Mountains. Its Ming seat at Huanggang stood beside the river, while Qizhou and the eastern counties covered lowlands between Huguang, Anhui and Jiangxi. Late Yuan warfare had emptied many valleys, and settlers from northern Jiangxi reopened much of the farmland in the Hongwu reign. In 1444 Huangzhou was a grain district and river corridor under Huguang administration: boats used its Yangtze landings, and overland routes ran on toward Anhui and Jiangxi.

A reddish riverside rock outside the prefectural city gave Huangzhou its best-known literary name. While exiled here under the Northern Song, Su Shi visited the rock and wrote the two Red Cliff rhapsodies, and in the late Kangxi reign the Huangzhou prefect Guo Chaozuo renamed the place Dongpo Chibi after Su's art name. The prefecture's later scholarly fame came from Qizhou, where Li Shizhen was born in 1518. He spent twenty-seven years on the Compendium of Materia Medica, which recorded 1,892 medicinal entries, 11,000 prescriptions and more than a thousand illustrations, with notes on plants, animals and minerals. The draft was finished in 1578 but was not printed until Nanjing publishers issued it in 1596. Qing rule kept the seat of Huangzhou Prefecture at Huanggang.
zh:
黄州府位于长江中游北岸，滨江平原与大别山东南缘相接。明代府治黄冈城临江而立，蕲州和东部诸县覆盖湖广、安徽、江西之间的低地。元末战乱使许多河谷人烟稀少，洪武年间来自江西北部的移民重新开垦了大量农田。1444年，黄州是湖广管辖下的谷物产区和滨江通道：船只使用这里的长江码头，陆路又通向安徽和江西。

府城外一块红色临江石矶给黄州留下了最知名的文名。北宋年间，苏轼谪居黄州时游此地，写下前后《赤壁赋》；清代康熙末年，黄州知府郭朝祚取苏轼的号，将这里改称东坡赤壁。黄州府后来的学问声名来自蕲州，1518年李时珍出生于此。他用二十七年撰成《本草纲目》，收录一千八百九十二条药物资料、一万一千余首药方和一千一百余幅插图，并考述植物、动物与矿物。书稿1578年完成，直到1596年才由南京书坊刊行。清代仍以黄冈为黄州府治。

en:
Fengxiang lies at the western end of the Guanzhong plain, where the Wei valley narrows between the Qinling range and the Long hills. Baoji to its south guards the Chencang road into Sichuan, and Longzhou to the west opens the road into Gansu, so armies passing between Guanzhong, Shu and the upper Wei have always come this way. The old city of Yong was a capital of the state of Qin for nearly three centuries, and Qin kings kept their ancestral temples and tombs there. In 757 the Tang made it Fengxiang Prefecture and for a time ranked it the Western Capital while imperial armies fought to take Chang'an back from An Lushan's rebels; from 907 to 924 Li Maozhen held it as the capital of his state of Qi. In 1061 the young Su Shi took his first office here as assistant prefect. He dredged the old Phoenix-Drinking Pool into the East Lake, planted willows and lotus along its banks and built pavilions and bridges, and after a long drought broke in spring rain he put up the Joyful Rain Pavilion and wrote the essay that made it famous. The Ming set up Fengxiang Prefecture in 1369, governing one department and seven counties, and in 1429 the Prince of Zheng, Zhu Zhanjun, took up residence here; reassigned to Huaiqing in 1443, he left for his new fief the next year.

The town lived by the wheat of the western plain and by its liquor: the distilleries at Liulin sold a strong spirit already praised in Tang times, the drink that later took the name Xifeng. The early Qing peace broke in 1674, when the Shaanxi commander Wang Fuchen joined the Three Feudatories' revolt, seized Lanzhou and turned neighbouring Pingliang and the Longyou marches into a campaigning ground, until he surrendered to the Kangxi Emperor's armies in 1676. The Qing rated Fengxiang a busy and populous post and made it the seat of the Feng-Bin intendant; its roads kept carrying the grain and wine of the western plain between the Wei valley and the western passes.
zh:
凤翔在关中平原西端，渭河谷地在这里被秦岭与陇山夹窄。南翼的宝鸡扼守入蜀的陈仓道，西边的陇州敞开通往甘肃的大路，关中、蜀地与渭水上游之间的兵马往来，都要经过这里。雍城做了秦国近三百年的都城，秦君的宗庙与陵寝也在那里。757年唐朝于此置凤翔府，在官军收复长安、平定安史之乱期间一度号为西京；907至924年，李茂贞又以这里为岐国都城。1061年，初入仕途的苏轼到任凤翔府签书判官；他把古饮凤池疏浚成东湖，沿堤种柳栽莲、修筑亭桥，久旱之后一场春雨降下，他建起喜雨亭，写下传名的《喜雨亭记》。明朝1369年置凤翔府，领一州七县；1429年郑王朱瞻埈在此就藩，1443年改封怀庆，次年才前往新封地。

凤翔靠西原的麦子和酒过活：柳林镇烧坊卖的烈酒唐代就有人称道，所产之酒后来得名西凤酒。清初的太平日子在1674年被打破，陕西提督王辅臣响应三藩之乱起兵，攻破兰州，邻近的平凉与陇右尽成战场，1676年他向康熙的大军投降。清代把凤翔考定为冲、繁缺分，凤邠道也驻节于此，往来大道照旧转运着西原的粮食与酒，穿行在渭河谷地与西边的关隘之间。

en:
Tongren guards the Jin River gap in the Wuling Mountains, where Guizhou meets Hunan and Sichuan. Local records explain its older name, Tongren or 'copper men': a Yuan fisherman was said to have found three bronze Confucian, Buddhist and Daoist images in the river beside Copper Rock, where the Greater and Lesser Rivers meet. The valleys were then native chief country, but a quarrel over cinnabar drew in the Ming court. After the Sizhou and Sinan chiefs went to war over the mines, the Yongle emperor abolished their commissions in 1413, created Guizhou Province, and set up Tongren Prefecture. Dawanshan, already known for cinnabar and mercury, was attached to it in 1414. Nearby Fanjing Mountain was also a Buddhist centre by the early Ming. In 1444 Tongren was a young prefectural and garrison town on the edge of the Miao hills.

The Ming abolished the Tongren chief office and placed the town under Tongren County in 1598. During the She-An rising in 1622, An Bangyan's army captured the prefectural city, and Sun Keshu, vice intendant of the Si-Shi circuit, died defending it. Qing forces fought the Red Miao in the same hills in 1703 and built Zhengda post with an assistant prefect under Tongren; Songtao Subprefecture was created farther north in 1730. In 1795 Shi Liudeng launched a Miao rising at Datang in Songtao and besieged Zhengda, Ganao and the Songtao seat. Songtao was promoted to an independent subprefecture two years later.
zh:
铜仁位于武陵山区的锦江峡谷，扼守贵州、湖南、四川交界的山路。地方志解释了它的旧名「铜人」：相传元代有渔人在大小江汇流处的铜岩旁入水，找到铜铸的儒、释、道三像，长官司便以此为名，后来才改「人」为「仁」。这一带原是土司地，真正把明朝朝廷引来的是朱砂之争。思州、思南两土司为争夺矿地相攻，永乐帝在永乐十一年（1413年）废除两宣慰司，设贵州行省和铜仁府。永乐十二年（1414年），以朱砂、水银闻名的大万山划入铜仁；近处的梵净山在明初也已是佛教名山。1444年的铜仁，是苗疆边缘一座设治未久的府城和军镇。

万历二十六年（1598年），明朝废铜仁长官司，在同城改设铜仁县。天启二年（1622年）奢安之乱中，安邦彦的军队攻破铜仁府城，分巡思石道副使孙克恕战死。康熙四十三年（1703年），清军在同一带山地征讨红苗，随后设正大营和铜仁府同知；雍正八年（1730年）又在北边设松桃厅。乾隆六十年（1795年），石柳邓在松桃大塘发动苗民起事，围攻正大营、嘎脑营和松桃厅城。嘉庆二年（1797年），松桃升为直隶厅。

en:
Hulan lies on the lower Hulan river, just above where it runs into the Songhua, in the fattest grazing belt of the northern plain. The Jin called the water the Hulahun and kept a stockaded village here under their supreme capital at Huining; the Ming recorded it as the Hulawen, the river from which the Hūlun took their name. Along its banks pastured the 'river Jurchen' of the Haixi, the Sibe among them: they raised horses and cattle, scratched fields of grain and sent sable and ponies to the Kaiyuan fairs. From the Zhengtong years their kin drifted south, carrying the Hūlun name to the four tribes of Hada, Ula, Hoifa and Yehe, which Nurhaci broke one by one between 1601 and 1619. In 1444 the Hulan country was still their stockaded pasture, with no walled town in it.

The Later Jin gathered the country with the rest of the Haixi lands, and the early Qing kept it a sealed hunting reserve, eight guard posts set along the river in 1683. A walled city came only in 1734, approved by the Yongzheng Emperor under the military governor of Heilongjiang. The post road from Maoxing reached it the next year and five hundred banner soldiers moved in from Qiqihar and Boduna; a flotilla stationed at the river mouth carried grain, and the Hengji granary filled for the garrisons of Qiqihar, Mergen and Aigun. In 1737 four hundred manor bondsmen came up from Shengjing to work forty official manors. The cattle and goods markets at the city and its five stations were the first taxed markets in Heilongjiang, and Hulan became the granary of the northern frontier.
zh:
呼兰在呼兰河下游，南距河水汇入松花江处不远，是北部平原最肥沃的一片牧场。金代称这条水为活剌浑水，河畔的胡剌温屯归上京会宁府管辖；明代典籍作忽剌温江，「扈伦」之名便得自这条江。沿江牧放的是海西女真中的「江夷」，锡伯部也在其中：他们养马放牛，粗放种谷，把貂皮和马匹送往开原边市。自正统年间起，部众不断南迁，把忽剌温之名带往哈达、乌拉、辉发、叶赫四部；1601至1619年，努尔哈赤将四部次第攻灭。1444年的呼兰河两岸，仍是他们栅栏围起的牧场，境内没有一座城。

明末，这里随海西旧地一并归入后金，清初则长期封禁为猎场，1683年起沿河设卡伦八处。城池直到1734年才获准兴筑，谕旨出自雍正皇帝，归黑龙江将军管辖。次年茂兴至呼兰的驿道开通，又从齐齐哈尔、伯都讷移来旗兵五百；河口设水师营转运粮食，城内建起恒积仓，常年供给齐齐哈尔、墨尔根和瑷珲三城驻军。1737年，自奉天移来庄丁四百名，设官庄四十所。呼兰城与所属五站的牲畜、杂货市集，是黑龙江最早征税的市集，呼兰也成了北边的粮仓。

en:
These wooded hills between the upper Hun and the middle Sungari, where modern Liaoning meets Jilin, are the country the Ming called Jianzhou. Its people came south from the Ilan Tumen land at the confluence of the Mudan and Sungari: the Ming enrolled the Odoli, Huligai and Tuowen clans as frontier guards, gave Ahacu of the Huligai the Jianzhou Guard in 1403, and after years of pressure from Koreans and Wild Jurchens the guard was rebuilt in these hills in 1438, later splitting into a Left and a Right Guard. In 1444 the Jianzhou already ploughed as well as hunted, and their wealth passed through the Ming markets at Fushun and Kaiyuan, where cured ginseng and sable and squirrel pelts from these forests were exchanged for iron ploughshares, cloth and grain.

Jurchen raiding drew joint Ming and Korean expeditions in 1467 and 1478 that killed the chiefs and burned the stockades, and the guards did not recover for a century. Their recovery was the work of Nurhaci of the Aisin Gioro. He had served as a young man in the household of the Ming general Li Chengliang at Fushun, where he learned Chinese and read the Romance of the Three Kingdoms and Water Margin, and in 1582 a Ming attack on Fort Gure, guided by the rival chief Nikan Wailan, killed his grandfather and his father. In 1583 he set out to avenge them with the thirteen suits of armour his father had left him and marched on Tulun; by 1588 he was master of all the Jianzhou. In 1599 he ordered a Manchu script adapted from the Mongolian alphabet, and in 1616, at Hetu Ala in these hills, he proclaimed the Later Jin. Under the Qing the old guard country stayed the dynasty's ancestral homeland, worked by ginseng diggers and huntsmen whose tribute pelts and roots travelled to the capital.
zh:
这片林海丘陵夹在浑河上游与松花江中游之间，地当今辽宁、吉林两省相接处，明朝称之为建州。这里的人是从牡丹江与松花江汇流处的三姓故地南迁而来：斡朵里、胡里改、托温三部被明朝编为边地卫所，1403年胡里改酋阿哈出受任建州卫长官；在朝鲜和北方「野人」女真的多年挤压下，1438年建州卫在这片丘陵重建，后来又分置左卫、右卫。1444年的建州人已兼事农耕与狩猎，财货走的是抚顺、开原的马市，山里制好的人参和紫貂、灰鼠皮，在这里换来铁犁铧、布匹和粮食。

女真的抄掠引来明朝与朝鲜的夹击，1467年和1478年两次联合进剿，斩杀酋长、焚毁城寨，诸卫此后一百年没能恢复。复兴建州的是爱新觉罗家的努尔哈赤。他年轻时在驻守抚顺的明将李成梁麾下为军，通汉文，读过《三国演义》和《水浒传》；1582年，明军在敌酋尼堪外兰引导下攻打古勒城，他的祖父和父亲都死在乱中。1583年，他以父亲留下的十三副遗甲起兵报仇，攻打图伦城，到1588年已成为全部建州之主。1599年，他命人参照蒙古文创制满文；1616年，他在这片丘陵间的赫图阿拉称汗，建立后金。入清以后，建州旧地始终是王朝的发祥之地，刨夫和猎夫穿行山林，贡参和贡皮运往京师。

en:
Taining is the grassland around Baichungtze on the middle Tao'er, which crosses the western Songnen plain to join the Nen. Four Liao emperors, Shengzong, Xingzong, Daozong and Tianzuo, kept their spring travelling palace at Changchunzhou here, carrying the court out to the Nen marshes, where the emperor fished the opening rivers, hunted swan geese on the lakes and feasted the tribal chiefs who came to pay court. The stamped-earth ruins of Changchunzhou lie south of Baicheng. The Jin held the place as Taizhou and the Yuan ran it as Taining circuit, the name the Ming guard inherited. The guard was founded in 1389 under Azhashili, a descendant of Genghis Khan's youngest brother Temuge, the first of the three Uriankhai guards. In 1444 its clans were already drifting south, hard pressed by Ming expeditions and the Oirat in turn.

Between 1446 and 1448 Esen's Oirats overran the three guards and the Taining clans scattered. What survived was absorbed in the mid-16th century by the Inner Khalkha, while the Tao'er valley passed to the southward-moving Nun Khorchin. In 1636 Hong Taiji enrolled the country in the Khorchin right-wing banners, which later joined the assembly of the Jirim league. The Tao'er saw no more wars after that: a jasak ruled from felt camps moved with the seasons, herds covered the plain, and neither walled town nor county office was raised here through the rest of the period.
zh:
泰宁的中心是洮儿河中游的白城子一带，洮儿河横贯松嫩平原西缘，东注嫩江。辽圣宗、兴宗、道宗、天祚帝四代皇帝都把春捺钵的行宫设在长春州，行在移到嫩江畔的泡沼，皇帝在开江河上捕鱼，到湖面猎天鹅，并设宴款待入朝的各部酋长。长春州的夯土故城就在白城子以南。金朝沿置泰州，元朝设泰宁路，后来的明卫便因路得名。1389年，明朝置兀良哈三卫之首的泰宁卫，以成吉思汗幼弟铁木哥斡赤斤的后裔阿札失里统领。到1444年，在明军出塞和瓦剌逼压的交替冲击下，部众已经陆续南徙。

1446至1448年间，也先的瓦剌大军横扫三卫，泰宁部众溃散。16世纪中叶，残部被内喀尔喀吞并，洮儿河谷则转入南下的嫩科尔沁之手。1636年，皇太极把这片地方编入科尔沁右翼诸旗，后来随诸旗参加哲里木盟会盟。这以后洮儿河上下再无战事：札萨克在随季节迁移的毡帐里理政，畜群布满原野，直到本时期结束，这里也没有筑过城、设过州县。

en:
Ju Ud, 'a hundred willows', is the broad basin where the Xar Moron and Laoha meet to form the Western Liao, grassland ringed by the last ridges of the Greater Khingan. Two Liao capitals stood in this country. The Upper Capital Linhuang was founded by Abaoji in 918 in what is now the Bairin Left Banner: an imperial city in the north and a walled Chinese town in the south, where Uyghur merchants kept their own quarter and envoys from the Western Xia stayed at a state hostel. The Central Capital Dading was raised in 1007 on the upper Laoha. Jin armies sacked Linhuang in 1120, and Mongol forces ruined what remained in 1214. The Ming later garrisoned Daning, but after the Yongle Emperor pulled the frontier armies south the basin became pasture of the loosely ruled Uriankhai guards. In 1444 herds grazed among overgrown walls, and the clans later known as the Bairin, Ongniud and Aohan drifted with the wars of Taisun Khan and Esen.

Ligdan Khan, the last Mongol ruler recognised as great khan, built his capital here. His Chagaan Baishin, the White City, rose on the ruins of Liao Qingzhou in what is now the Ar Horqin country, and the Mahakala image installed in it made his seat the Buddhist centre of the Mongols while he held the five Inner Khalkha tribes, the Bairin, Jarud and their kin. In 1632 Hong Taiji crossed the Khingan against him with a host said to number 100,000; Ligdan fled west with his Chakhars and died of smallpox in 1634 at Sira Tala in Gansu. His son Ejei submitted in 1635 and was said to have handed over the Yuan dynasty's imperial seal, and the next year Hong Taiji proclaimed the Qing. In 1639 the princes of eight tribes and eleven banners, among them the Keshiketeng, Bairin, Ar Khorchin, Ongniud and Aohan, assembled at Jaguun Uda in the Ongniud Left Banner, the meeting that gave the Ju Ud League its name. Chinese farmers followed the peace northward: the Qing opened the Ulanhad hall below the 'red cliff' in 1774, and in 1778 it became Chifeng County, a Chinese market town planted in Mongol pasture.
zh:
昭乌达，蒙古语意为「百柳」，是西拉木伦河与老哈河汇为西辽河的宽阔盆地，四周环着大兴安岭余脉。辽代两座京城都建在这片土地上。上京临潢府由耶律阿保机建于918年，遗址在今巴林左旗：北城是皇城，南城是汉城，回鹘商贩在南城里有专属营地，西夏使者则在驿馆安顿。中京大定府于1007年筑城于老哈河上游。1120年金军攻陷上京，1214年蒙古军又把残存城郭摧毁殆尽。明初曾设大宁卫屯守，永乐撤卫后，盆地改由受羁縻的兀良哈诸卫游牧。1444年，牧群在荒废的城墙间游走，后来的巴林、翁牛特、敖汉诸部正随着脱脱不花汗与也先的战事聚散迁徙。

末代得到公认的蒙古大汗林丹汗把都城建在这里。他在辽庆州旧址筑起瓦察尔图察汉城，即白城，遗址在今阿鲁科尔沁旗；城中供奉的玛哈噶拉神像使这里成为蒙古的佛教中心，他也据此节制巴林、扎鲁特等内喀尔喀五部。1632年，皇太极率号称十万的大军越过大兴安岭来攻，林丹汗带察哈尔部众西逃，1634年在甘肃大草滩（西拉塔拉）死于天花。其子额哲于1635年归附，相传将元朝传国玉玺献给皇太极；次年皇太极改国号为清。1639年，克什克腾、巴林、阿鲁科尔沁、翁牛特、敖汉等八部十一旗的王公在翁牛特左翼旗境内的扎滚乌达会盟，盟名即此而来。关内汉民随着和平北上垦荒：1774年，清廷在褐色孤峰下置乌兰哈达厅，1778年改设赤峰县，蒙古牧场中长出了一座汉人集镇。

en:
Anding is the pasture country between the Qilian range and the Qaidam salt wastes, with the Sugan lakes lying in its open steppe. Its herdsmen were Sarïgh Yogïr, or Yellow Uyghurs, Vajrayana Buddhists descended from the old Ganzhou Uyghurs. The Ming named their loose commandery the Anding Guard after Buyan Temür, a former Yuan prince of Anding, submitted in 1375.
