In 1444 this was a forested Orthodox Ruthenian march of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania: boyars held timber castles among the rivers, patrols watched the tracks from the steppe, and settlers used the pockets of drier ground for grain and livestock.

The two castles carried most of the border fighting. Crimean Tatars sacked Ovruch in 1483 and destroyed its castle in 1506; the rebuilt works had a stone wall, deep moat, four gates and six towers. Kyiv voivode Fryderyk Pronski rebuilt Chernobyl Castle in 1548. After the Union of Lublin in 1569 the country passed to the Polish Crown, with Ovruch as a county seat in Kyiv Voivodeship; Władysław IV granted it Magdeburg law in 1641. During the Khmelnytsky rising of 1648 Ivan Holota raised more than six thousand Cossacks at Ovruch, and Chernobyl also served briefly as a regiment town before the Truce of Andrusovo returned both places to Poland in 1667. Haiduks burned Chernobyl Castle in 1747 and 1751, and the region rose again in the Koliyivshchyna of 1768. By the time the Second Partition assigned it to Russia in 1793, Chernobyl had another claim to notice: Rabbi Menachem Nachum Twersky, a disciple of the Baal Shem Tov, had founded the Hasidic dynasty that made the small town a Jewish religious centre.
zh:
奥夫鲁赤是普里皮亚季河上游的林地与沼泽，首城为奥夫鲁奇，东边的河畔还有切尔诺贝利。奥夫鲁奇古称弗鲁奇，本是德列夫利安人的要塞，后来成为留里克·罗斯季斯拉维奇王公的驻地；1190年，他把木构的圣瓦西里教堂改成石堂。1240年蒙古军洗劫此城，1356年立陶宛的统治推进到此。切尔诺贝利则在1193年作为王公猎苑首次出现。1444年时，这里是立陶宛大公国一片森林密布的东正教鲁塞尼亚边地：波雅尔在河网间守着木堡，巡逻队监视来自草原的小路，定居者在较干燥的地块种植谷物、牧养牲畜。

边防战事主要压在两座城堡上。1483年克里米亚鞑靼人洗劫奥夫鲁奇，1506年又摧毁其城堡；重建后的要塞设有石墙、深壕、四座城门和六座塔楼。1548年，基辅总督弗里德里赫·普龙斯基重建切尔诺贝利城堡。1569年卢布林联合后，这片土地划归波兰王国，奥夫鲁奇成为基辅省的县治，瓦迪斯瓦夫四世于1641年赐其马格德堡法。1648年赫梅利尼茨基起义期间，伊万·戈洛塔在奥夫鲁奇拉起六千多名哥萨克，切尔诺贝利也曾短暂成为团城；1667年安德鲁索沃停战协定把两地都归还波兰。1747年和1751年，盖达马克人焚毁切尔诺贝利城堡，1768年科利伊夫希纳起义又在此爆发。1793年第二次瓜分把它划给俄罗斯时，切尔诺贝利已有另一项名气：巴尔·谢姆·托夫的弟子梅纳赫姆·纳胡姆·特韦尔斯基在此创立哈西德拉比世系，使这座小镇成为犹太教宗教中心。

en:
Kashin grew around a tight loop of the Kashinka, a Volga tributary whose bends made the kremlin almost an island; only a narrow isthmus joined it to the mainland, and a deep ditch, rampart and palisade closed that approach. The chronicles first name it in 1238 among the towns ruined in the Mongol invasion, and a nine-day siege in 1287 showed the value of the position. In 1319 Mikhail of Tver left Kashin to his youngest son Vasily, who founded the Dormition Monastery for his mother Anna. She was veiled and buried there after her death in 1368. The local princes used Moscow against Tver and held a briefly separate principality after 1375, but their line ended in 1382 and the second Kashin line returned to Tver in 1426. In 1444 Kashin was the strongest northeastern town of the Tver realm, a fortified market with its own coinage and a trade in white lead paint.

The walls withstood Dmitry Shemyaka in 1452, and Kashin passed to Moscow with Tver in 1485. Ivan III allotted it in 1504 to his son Yuri of Dmitrov, who built the town's first stone cathedral; Yuri was imprisoned under Elena Glinskaya in 1534 and the appanage was abolished. Poles sacked Kashin in 1609. Anna's relics drew pilgrims after the Church glorified her as a saint in 1650, though the dispute over liturgical reforms led to her veneration being withdrawn in 1677. Plague struck in 1654 and fire gutted the town in 1676, but Kashin rebuilt as a market for some of Russia's best white lead, with blacksmiths, potters, icon painters and fairs. It became an uyezd seat in 1775. In 1812 its merchants armed and supplied the local levy themselves; flax and army contracts moving through the Vyshny Volochyok waterway had made many of them rich.
zh:
卡申围着伏尔加河支流卡申卡河的一道窄河湾发展起来。河湾几乎把克里姆林围成孤岛，只有一道狭窄地峡与陆地相连，深壕、土墙和木栅封住入口。编年史在1238年首次提到它，将其列为蒙古入侵中被毁的城镇；1287年一场九天围攻也显出这块地形的价值。1319年，特维尔王公米哈伊尔的遗嘱把卡申留给幼子瓦西里，瓦西里为母亲安娜修建圣母安息修道院。安娜后来在此出家，1368年死后葬在院中。本地王公借莫斯科对抗特维尔，1375年后一度维持独立公国，但王统在1382年断绝，第二系卡申王公也在1426年重归特维尔。1444年，卡申是特维尔疆域东北部最强的城镇，既是设防市场，也自铸钱币，并以铅白粉生意闻名。

1452年，城墙顶住德米特里·舍米亚卡；1485年卡申随特维尔归入莫斯科。1504年，伊凡三世把它封给儿子德米特罗夫王公尤里，尤里建起城中第一座石造大教堂；1534年尤里被叶莲娜·格林斯卡娅下令囚禁，封邑随后废除。1609年波兰人洗劫卡申。1650年教会将安娜封圣，她的圣物引来朝圣者，但礼仪改革之争又使对她的敬奉在1677年被取消。1654年瘟疫来袭，1676年大火几乎烧光全城；卡申仍重建为商镇，出售俄国一流的铅白粉，并有铁匠、陶匠、圣像画师和集市。1775年它成为县城。1812年，城中商人自行武装并供应本城民团；亚麻和军需合同经上沃洛乔克水系转运，已让许多商人致富。

en:
Zubtsov occupies the high ground at the mouth of the Vazuza, where that river enters the Volga and a crossing watched one branch of the Varangian route to the Greeks. The chronicles first name it in 1216, when Mstislav Udatny of Novgorod took the settlement from Prince Yaroslav Vsevolodovich. It became the southwestern fortress of the Principality of Tver, and in 1318 or 1319 Mikhail of Tver's will made it the seat of an appanage for his son Aleksandr. Aleksandr later held the Tver table itself before the Horde executed him in 1339. In 1444 Zubtsov was still a small Tver appanage town on the Volga, with walls covering the roads toward Rzhev, Mozhaysk and Moscow.

The childless death of its last appanage prince around 1460 returned Zubtsov to the Tver grand prince, and Ivan III annexed it with Tver in 1485. Polish raiders ruined the town during the Time of Troubles. Its later livelihood came from the river: when the Vyshny Volochyok waterway was rebuilt in the early nineteenth century, barges from Rzhev were handled here on their way toward Tver, Moscow and the Baltic link to St Petersburg. The fairs sold flax and linseed above all, with cattle, hides and pottery as side trades. Catherine II's government made it an uyezd town in 1776, gave it a red coat of arms with a fortress wall in 1780, and the Neoclassical cathedral was completed in 1801.
zh:
祖布佐夫位于瓦祖扎河注入伏尔加河的河口高地上，控制着「从瓦良格人到希腊人」商路一条支线的渡口。1216年，诺夫哥罗德王公姆斯季斯拉夫·乌达特尼从雅罗斯拉夫·弗谢沃洛多维奇手中夺取此地，编年史首次写下它的名字。它后来成为特维尔公国西南边境要塞；1318或1319年，特维尔王公米哈伊尔的遗嘱把祖布佐夫封给儿子亚历山大，作为封邑中心。亚历山大后来一度坐上特维尔大公之位，1339年在金帐汗国被处死。1444年，祖布佐夫仍是特维尔封邑下的伏尔加河畔小城，城墙监视着通往勒热夫、莫扎伊斯克和莫斯科的道路。

约1460年，末代封邑王公无嗣而终，祖布佐夫重归特维尔大公；1485年，伊凡三世吞并特维尔时将它一并纳入莫斯科。大动乱年代，波兰袭掠者摧毁了这座城。它后来的生计靠河流：19世纪初上沃洛乔克水系整修后，来自勒热夫的驳船在此换装，经特维尔、莫斯科和波罗的海水路运往圣彼得堡。集市上最大宗的货物是亚麻和亚麻籽，也买卖牲畜、皮张和陶器。1776年，叶卡捷琳娜二世政府将它设为县城；1780年赐下红底城墙城徽；新古典主义大教堂则在1801年建成。

en:
Mologa stood where the river of that name runs into the Volga, a landing that existed by the 12th century and passed from Rostov to the princes of Yaroslavl. When Prince David of Yaroslavl died in 1321, his son Mikhail Davidovich took the lands along the Mologa as his share and made the town the seat of an independent principality; local tradition recorded that he carried with him his father's blessing, the Tikhvin icon of the Mother of God, which became the chief shrine of Mologa's Afanasyevsky Monastery. Under him an international barter fair opened at Kholopiy Gorodok, about fifty kilometres up the Mologa, drawing Russian and eastern merchants to the upper Volga. His son Fyodor Mikhailovich marched with his retinue on Dmitry Donskoy's wars, fought on the right wing at Kulikovo in 1380, and was buried in Mologa's cathedral when he died a monk in 1408. His descendants split the appanage into the Mologa, Prozorovsk and Sitsk principalities. In 1444 Mologa was a tiny princely seat under the loose lordship of Yaroslavl, living by the river traffic and the old fair.

In 1463 the last prince of Yaroslavl sold his rights to Ivan III, and Mologa's ruling houses entered Moscow's service, later known there as the Princes Prozorovsky and Shakhovskoy. Late in the 15th century the Kholopiy Gorodok fair was moved into the town, and Mologa became one of Russia's busiest markets for eastern trade; Sigismund von Herberstein saw its fortress on his travels. After the Troubles it lived on as a free trading sloboda on the Volga, and in the early 19th century the new Tikhvinskaya water system made the old landing a staging point between the Volga and the Baltic.
zh:
莫洛加城坐落在莫洛加河注入伏尔加河处，12世纪时已有这个河埠，先后从属于罗斯托夫公国和雅罗斯拉夫尔公国。1321年雅罗斯拉夫尔公达维德死后，其子米哈伊尔·达维多维奇分得莫洛加河沿岸的土地，以此城为中心建立独立公国；相传他就封时带去了父亲的祝福、季赫温圣母像，圣像后来成为莫洛加阿法纳西耶夫修道院的主保圣物。他在位时，莫洛加河上游约五十公里处的霍洛皮戈罗多克兴起以物易物的国际集市，把罗斯和东方的客商引到伏尔加河上游。其子费奥多尔·米哈伊洛维奇率亲兵随德米特里·顿斯科伊征战，1380年在库利科沃战役中位列右翼，1408年出家后去世，葬于莫洛加的大教堂。他死后，封邑被后裔分成莫洛加、普罗佐罗夫斯克和西茨克三个小公国。1444年的莫洛加是雅罗斯拉夫尔松散宗主权下的一座小公城，靠河运和旧集市为生。

1463年末代雅罗斯拉夫尔公把统治权卖给伊凡三世，莫洛加的统治家族转入莫斯科效力，后来在莫斯科被称为普罗佐罗夫斯基王公和沙霍夫斯科伊王公。15世纪末，霍洛皮戈罗多克的集市迁入城内，莫洛加成为俄罗斯对东方贸易最繁忙的商埠之一；西格蒙德·冯·赫伯施泰因在行记中记下了这里的要塞。混乱时代之后，它作为伏尔加河上的自由商镇（斯洛博达）再度兴旺；19世纪初，新修的季赫温水运系统又让这个老河埠成为伏尔加河与波罗的海之间的中转码头。

en:
Mozhaysk stands on the upper Moskva River 110 kilometres west of Moscow, on the road that runs on to Smolensk and Lithuania; every army marching on the capital from the west had to pass its hill. A fortress above the Mozhayka River is documented from the thirteenth century and held out against Algirdas of Lithuania in 1341 and 1370. Moscow took the town in 1303, and sixty of its boyars died with Dmitry Donskoy at Kulikovo in 1380. The appanage prince Andrei Dmitrievich, a son of Donskoy, struck his own coin and brought the monk Ferapont Belozersky to found the Luzhetsky Monastery. Mozhaysk's fame, though, rested on Saint Nicholas: a fourteenth-century wooden statue showed the saint holding a sword in one hand and the town in the other, and legend said he had shown himself on the walls during a siege and frightened the attackers off. In 1444 Andrei's son Ivan ruled the shrine town as its appanage prince, having sided with his uncle Yuri of Zvenigorod against Vasily II in Moscow's dynastic war.

Ivan helped capture and blind Vasily II in 1446 and lost his seat when Moscow absorbed the appanage in 1493. Ivan IV kept his headquarters in Mozhaysk through much of the Livonian War, receiving Swedish and Danish envoys there, and the Danish treaty of August 1562 bears the town's name. In the Time of Troubles it swore to Władysław Vasa and was sacked when the Poles withdrew, yet in 1617 and 1618 its garrison blocked Władysław's march on Moscow; the Deulino truce that ended the fighting specifically required the Poles to give back the seized icon of Saint Nicholas. A stone kremlin went up in 1624-1626 to replace Smolensk, lost to the commonwealth, and Dmitry Pozharsky, the liberator of Moscow, served there as voivode in 1632. The walls were already being taken down in 1812, when the Borodino field twelve kilometres away made Mozhaysk a hospital and supply base. Napoleon entered on 28 August, Platov's rearguard fought him in the suburbs, and the French retreat burned much of the town.
zh:
莫扎伊斯克位于莫斯科河上游、莫斯科以西110公里，城在通往斯摩棱斯克和立陶宛的大道旁，从西面进军莫斯科的军队都要绕过它的山丘。莫扎伊卡河畔高地上13世纪便有要塞，1341年和1370年两度顶住立陶宛大公阿尔吉尔达斯的围攻。莫斯科1303年夺取该城，1380年库里科沃一役有60名莫扎伊斯克波雅尔随德米特里·顿斯科伊战死。封邑王公安德烈·德米特里耶维奇是顿斯科伊之子，在任时自铸钱币，并请修士费拉蓬特·别洛泽尔斯基建立卢热茨基修道院。不过莫扎伊斯克的名声主要系于圣徒尼古拉：14世纪的一尊木雕中，他一手持剑、一手托着城池；相传城池被围时，尼古拉显圣于城墙之上，围军惊惧退走。1444年，安德烈之子伊万以封邑王公的身份统治这座圣城，而他已站在叔父兹韦尼哥罗德的尤里一边，卷入同瓦西里二世的王朝战争。

伊万1446年参与俘获并弄瞎瓦西里二世，1493年封邑被莫斯科吞并，他也丢掉了地盘。利沃尼亚战争的大部分时间里，伊凡雷帝把莫扎伊斯克当作行辕，在此接见瑞典和丹麦使节，1562年8月的丹麦对俄条约便以该城命名。动乱时代中，城市向瓦迪斯瓦夫宣誓，波兰人撤离时又将它洗劫；但1617和1618年，守军挡住瓦迪斯瓦夫进军莫斯科的道路，结束战事的《杰乌利诺停战协定》还专门写明波兰须归还掠走的圣尼古拉像。1624至1626年，旧木寨址上建起一座石砌克里姆林宫，以替代沦于波兰的斯摩棱斯克；解放莫斯科的德米特里·波扎尔斯基1632年出任这里的督军。1812年城墙已在拆除，而12公里外的博罗季诺战场使莫扎伊斯克成了俄军的医院和辎重基地。拿破仑于8月28日入城，普拉托夫的后卫军在城郊迎战，法军撤退时又烧毁大片城区。

en:
Kolomna sits where the Moskva River runs into the Oka, southeast of Moscow: grain, cattle and timber coming up the Oka had to pass it, and so did every Tatar raid aimed at the capital. Moscow made it its first conquest when Prince Daniil took it from Ryazan in 1301, and Dmitry Donskoy mustered his host on these meadows before riding to Kulikovo in 1380. During Vasily II's dynastic war the town served the grand prince as a temporary capital in 1433 after Yuri of Zvenigorod seized Moscow. Its market ranked among the richest in the principality, while the raid of Khan Ulugh Muhammad of Kazan in 1440 showed how open it lay. In 1444 Kolomna was Muscovy's main southern stronghold and river market, fortified only in wood.

Vasily III replaced those timber walls with the red-brick Kolomna Kremlin between 1525 and 1531, after the Crimeans had burned the town, and no enemy ever stormed the new walls. Ivan IV, aged sixteen, camped under them with his army in 1546 until a Crimean invasion turned back, and in July 1552 he held the council here that sent a 150,000-strong army against Kazan; the Brusensky Monastery was founded in thanks for that victory. In the Time of Troubles Bolotnikov's rebels took the outer posad in 1606 but could not take the kremlin, and in 1612 it became the last town held for Marina Mnishek, wife of the false tsars, who tried to rule from here with the Cossack ataman Zarutsky; legend later said she turned into a crow and flew out of the tower that bears her name. When Patriarch Nikon reformed the liturgy, Bishop Pavel of Kolomna rejected the new service books and became one of the most honoured martyrs of the Old Belief. With the wars over, Kolomna lived by the river: its merchants carried grain, honey, wax, hemp, wool and hides to Moscow and other cities, and twenty-five malt houses supplied the capital's brewers.
zh:
科洛姆纳位于莫斯科河汇入奥卡河之处、莫斯科东南方向：奥卡河运来的粮食、牲畜和木材要经过这里，鞑靼人奔袭莫斯科也多取道于此。1301年，莫斯科王公丹尼尔从梁赞手中夺取该城，这是莫斯科公国兼并的第一座城镇；1380年，德米特里·顿斯科伊在城外河滩集结大军，随后开赴库里科沃。瓦西里二世王朝战争期间，兹韦尼哥罗德的尤里攻占莫斯科后，该城于1433年成为大公的临时都城。城中市集在公国里首屈一指，而1440年喀山汗兀鲁·穆罕默德的袭扰表明它依然门户洞开。1444年时，科洛姆纳是莫斯科南方首要要塞和河港，却只有木构城防。

克里米亚军焚城之后，瓦西里三世在1525至1531年以红砖砌成科洛姆纳克里姆林宫，新城墙此后从未被强攻突破。1546年，年仅16岁的伊凡四世率军扎营墙下，直到来犯的克里米亚军队掉头退走；1552年7月，他又在此召开军事会议，定下以15万大军出征喀山的计划，城中的布鲁先斯基修道院便是为答谢喀山大捷而建。动乱时代中，博洛特尼科夫起义军1606年攻占城外工商区，却拿不下克里姆林宫；1612年，这里成为伪皇之妻玛琳娜·姆尼舍克控制的最后一座城，她与哥萨克首领扎鲁茨基据此发号施令，后来民间传说她化作一只乌鸦，从以她得名的马林娜塔中飞出。牧首尼康改革礼拜仪式时，科洛姆纳主教帕维尔拒绝新的礼仪经书，成为旧信仰派最受尊崇的殉道者之一。战火平息后，科洛姆纳靠河水谋生：商人把粮食、蜂蜜、蜂蜡、大麻、羊毛和兽皮运往莫斯科等城，25座麦芽坊则为京城的酒坊供料。

en:
Between the Koloksha River and Lake Pleshcheyevo lies a rolling stretch of Zalesye holding two towns founded in the same year, 1152, by Yuri Dolgoruky. Yuryev, later called Yuryev-Polsky, received an almost circular earth-and-timber detinets above the river; its white-stone Cathedral of St George, raised from 1230 under Prince Svyatoslav, was among the last great churches built before the Mongol invasion. Pereslavl-Zalessky stood on the Trubezh at the lake, laid out as a future capital of the northeastern lands with earthen ramparts nearly 2.5 kilometres around, and Alexander Nevsky was born there in 1221. It passed to Moscow by bequest in 1302. Yuryev, sacked by the Mongols in 1238, followed in 1340, and both towns were raided again in 1382 and 1408. In 1444 they were Orthodox Muscovite fortresses over farming country and roads northwest of Vladimir.

In the 1460s the dome of St George's collapsed and broke many of its carved stones; Vasili Yermolin rebuilt the cathedral in 1471 in a simpler shape. From the fifteenth century Pereslavl was bound to send the Moscow court the small whitefish netted in Lake Pleshcheyevo, a duty remembered on the town's coat of arms. During the Time of Troubles Polish-Lithuanian forces destroyed Pereslavl's old fortress in 1608 and burned Yuryev. The towns recovered with traffic along the Great Stromyn Road linking the Suzdal lands with Moscow, and Yuryev rebuilt its Monastery of Archangel Michael, its gate church dated 1670. Between 1688 and 1693 Peter the Great had boats built and drilled on Lake Pleshcheyevo as his 'fun flotilla', the first school of the Russian navy.
zh:
科洛克沙河与普列谢耶沃湖之间是扎列西耶的一片起伏乡野，尤里·多尔戈鲁基1152年同一年在这里建起两座城镇。尤里耶夫后称尤里耶夫-波利斯基，在河畔筑起近乎圆形的土木要塞；斯维亚托斯拉夫王公时自1230年起修建的白石圣乔治主教座堂，是蒙古入侵前最后建成的一批宏大教堂之一。佩列斯拉夫尔-扎列斯基位于湖畔的特鲁别日河口，按东北罗斯未来都城的规模规划，土筑城墙周长近2.5公里，亚历山大·涅夫斯基1221年就出生在这里。1302年，它依遗嘱归属莫斯科。尤里耶夫1238年遭蒙古人洗劫，1340年并入莫斯科，两城1382年和1408年又两度受袭。1444年时，它们是莫斯科治下信奉东正教的要塞，拱卫着弗拉基米尔西北的农田与道路。

1460年代，圣乔治座堂穹顶坍塌，许多石雕被砸坏，瓦西里·叶尔莫林1471年重建，形制已比原样简朴。从15世纪起，佩列斯拉夫尔须向莫斯科宫廷进贡普列谢耶沃湖出产的小白鱼，这项义务也画上了城徽。动荡时期，波兰立陶宛军队1608年摧毁佩列斯拉夫尔旧要塞，又焚毁尤里耶夫。城市后来沿着连接苏兹达尔土地与莫斯科的大斯特罗梅恩路复苏，尤里耶夫重建了米哈伊尔·阿尔汉格尔斯克修道院，门堂建于1670年。1688年至1693年，彼得大帝在普列谢耶沃湖造船练兵，编为「游戏舰队」，这里成了俄罗斯海军最初的训练场。

en:
Starodub-on-the-Klyazma lay in the Opolye, the rolling grain country beyond the forests, on a bend of the Klyazma. Local tradition credits Yury Dolgorukiy with founding it in 1152, and settlers from the south named it after Starodub in Severia. After the Mongol invasion of 1238, Ivan, the youngest son of Vsevolod the Big Nest, made the town his seat. His descendants ruled one of the smallest Russian principalities, pressed between Moscow and Nizhny Novgorod. Dmitry Donskoy annexed it in the late 1370s, and the princely family moved to Moscow. Its branches included the Gagarins, Khilkovs, Romodanovskys and Pozharskys; Dmitry Pozharsky, who raised the Second Volunteer Army with Kuzma Minin in 1612, came from that line. In 1444 Starodub was an old appanage seat and small Muscovite market town in grain country.

Ivan IV kept Starodub in the zemshchina when he formed the Oprichnina in 1565. Its life ended in March 1609, when Alexander Jozef Lisowski's Polish raiders burned it during the Time of Troubles. No new town rose on the ashes, and its earthen ramparts remained above the village later called Klyazminsky Gorodok. The district's old ties to the Pozharsky princes survived in the surrounding land. Local trade and administration moved twelve kilometres downriver to Kovrov, which Catherine II made a town and uyezd centre in 1778.
zh:
克利亚济马河畔的斯塔罗杜布位于奥波利耶，也就是林海之外起伏的产粮地带，城址在克利亚济马河一道弯旁。当地相传尤里·多尔戈鲁基1152年建城，南来移民以故乡谢韦尔斯基的斯塔罗杜布为它命名。1238年蒙古入侵后，弗谢沃洛德·大窝最小的儿子伊万把这里设为驻地。他的后裔统治着俄罗斯最小的公国之一，夹在莫斯科和下诺夫哥罗德之间。14世纪70年代末，德米特里·顿斯科伊吞并该城，斯塔罗杜布王公家族迁往莫斯科，支系包括加加林、希尔科夫、罗莫达诺夫斯基和波扎尔斯基等家族；1612年与库兹马·米宁组建第二民军的德米特里·波扎尔斯基，就出自这一系。1444年，斯塔罗杜布是旧日封邑都城，也是产粮区里一座莫斯科治下的小集镇。

1565年伊凡四世设立特辖区时，斯塔罗杜布被留在领主区。1609年3月，亚历山大·尤泽夫·利索夫斯基率领的波兰袭掠者乘动乱时期攻入城中，将它焚毁。废墟上没有再建新城，只有古老土墙留在后来称作克利亚济明斯基戈罗多克的村庄旁。周边土地仍保留着与波扎尔斯基王公家族的旧联系。地方贸易和行政中心转到下游十二公里的科夫罗夫，叶卡捷琳娜二世1778年将科夫罗夫升格为县城。

en:
Pronsk occupies a high cape on the left bank of the Pronya, near the mouth of the Pralya and above a crossing on the roads north from the steppe. The Nikon Chronicle first names it in 1131. Its appanage princes were kinsmen, and often rivals, of the rulers of Ryazan. Mongol troops stormed the town in December 1237, and in August 1378 its retinue fought beside Muscovite forces on the Vozha, where Mamai's commander Begich was routed. In 1444 Pronsk was a Ryazan fortress at the forest-steppe edge, its kremlin watching the approach to Pereyaslavl-Ryazansky.

The appanage passed to Ryazan in the 1460s and 1470s, and the town came under Moscow with the rest of the principality in 1520. In 1536 the Italian fortification engineer Petrok Maly built a new earthen fortress there, a work adapted to cannon fire and close to the bastion-style defences then appearing in Muscovy. Ivan the Terrible placed Pronsk in the zemshchina when he divided the realm in 1565. The small town remained a garrison point on Moscow's southern frontier.
zh:
普龙斯克位于普龙尼亚河左岸高岬，靠近普拉利亚河河口，俯守草原道路北上的渡口。《尼康编年史》1131年首次提到它。本地采邑王公与梁赞统治者同族，也常相争。1237年12月蒙古军攻破此城；1378年8月，普龙斯克卫队在沃扎河与莫斯科军队并肩作战，马迈的将领别吉奇兵败。1444年，普龙斯克是梁赞在森林草原边缘的要塞，克里姆林监视着通往佩列亚斯拉夫尔-梁赞斯基的道路。

15世纪六七十年代，采邑归入梁赞；1520年又随梁赞转入莫斯科。1536年，意大利筑城工程师彼得罗克·马雷在此修建新的土筑要塞，形制适应火炮，接近当时莫斯科逐渐采用的棱堡式防御。1565年伊凡雷帝划分特辖区和普通区时，普龙斯克划入普通区。这座小城仍是莫斯科南侧边防线上的驻防城。

en:
Solvychegodsk, whose name means 'salt on the Vychegda', grew up beside a salt lake on the lower Vychegda, in country Novgorod used as a fur hinterland and a route toward the Pechora. The early posad was called Usolye, the salt place, and in 1444 its people boiled brine, trapped sable and squirrel and carried both south through Ustyug.

The salt pans made the Stroganovs. Fyodor Stroganov, a salt boiler, settled in Usolye in the fifteenth century, and in 1517 Grand Prince Vasily III granted his son Anikey and Anikey's brothers the right to hold Vychegodsk Usolye and boil salt for the crown; Anikey's salterns became the base of the richest merchant house in the tsardom. In 1558 Ivan the Terrible granted the family great lands beyond the Kama, and in 1581 Stroganov money and men sent the Cossack Yermak into Siberia; during the Time of Troubles the family paid for Pozharsky's army that retook Moscow. The town had no such protection of its own: Lisowczycy raiders sacked it in January 1613, and in the summer of 1648 its people rose against the triple collection of old taxes after Moscow's Salt Riot. Later in the seventeenth century Solvychegodsk lived by finer work, painting Usolye enamel and the small, finely drawn icons of the Stroganov school, and the family paid for the Cathedral of the Presentation, built in 1688-1696, one of the northern churches in their baroque style.
zh:
索里维切戈茨斯克（通译索利维切戈茨克）意为「维切格达河上的盐」，兴起于维切格达河下游一座盐湖旁。这片地方本是诺夫哥罗德的毛皮腹地，也是前往伯朝拉的通道；早期城郊因盐湖得名乌索利耶，即「盐地」。1444年，这里的居民煮盐、猎取紫貂和松鼠，把盐和毛皮经乌斯秋格南运。

盐场造就了斯特罗加诺夫家族。煮盐户费奥多尔·斯特罗加诺夫15世纪定居乌索利耶；1517年，大公瓦西里三世特许他的儿子阿尼克和诸子领有维切格达乌索利耶、为大公煮盐，阿尼克的盐釜撑起了全俄最富有商人家族的家业。1558年，伊凡雷帝把卡马河以外的大片土地赐给该家族；1581年，斯特罗加诺夫家出钱出人，派哥萨克首领叶尔马克出征西伯利亚；动乱时期又出资供养波扎尔斯基收复莫斯科的军队。城镇自己却没有这样的庇护：1613年1月利索夫奇基轻骑将它洗劫，1648年夏莫斯科盐税暴动后旧税按三倍追征，市民也起而反抗。17世纪后期，索里维切戈茨斯克靠更精细的手艺立足，烧制乌索利耶珐琅，绘制工笔细密的斯特罗加诺夫画派圣像；斯特罗加诺夫家族还出资修建圣母进堂大教堂，教堂建于1688—1696年，是该家族巴洛克风格的北方教堂之一。

en:
Mezen covers the lower course of its river and the shore of Mezen Bay on the White Sea, a coast of fishermen, seal hunters and river pilots. Finnic hunters lived along the river before Novgorod merchants worked their way to the White Sea and used the Mezen, the Pyoza and portages over to the Tsilma as a route toward the Pechora fur grounds. In 1444 Novgorod's hold on the lower river was still light: no Russian town stood there yet, only fisheries, seal grounds and summer camps serving boats travelling between the Dvina and the Pechora.

The first permanent settlement, Okladnikova Sloboda, appears in records in 1545; local tradition traces its first Russian settlers to a Novgorod boyar named Okladnikov and his sons. It and the adjoining Kuznetsova Sloboda became the market of the Mezen valley, holding yearly fairs while most households lived by fishing and seal hunting. Its remoteness made it a place of exile. Avvakum, the archpriest who led the Old Believers against Patriarch Nikon's reforms, was kept there with his family in 1664-1666, between his Siberian exile and his final imprisonment at Pustozersk, where he was burned in 1682. The disgraced boyar Artamon Matveyev, once Alexis I's chief minister, was held there in 1680-1682. In 1780 Catherine II joined the two slobody into the town of Mezen.
zh:
梅津涵盖梅津河下游和白海梅津湾沿岸，居民多是渔民、猎海豹人和引船员。芬兰各族先在河畔渔猎，后来诺夫哥罗德商人抵达白海，沿梅津河、皮奥扎河，再经连水陆路转入齐尔马河，前往伯朝拉毛皮地带。1444年，诺夫哥罗德对河下游的控制还很松散：那里没有俄罗斯城镇，只有渔场、海豹猎场和夏季营地，供往来德维纳河与伯朝拉的船只停靠。

1545年，第一个永久定居点奥克拉德尼科瓦斯洛博达见于记载；当地传说把最早的俄罗斯居民追溯到诺夫哥罗德波雅尔奥克拉德尼科夫和他的儿子们。它和相邻的库兹涅佐瓦斯洛博达成为梅津河谷的市集，年年开集，多数人家则靠捕鱼和猎海豹为生。偏远使这里成为流放地：领导旧礼仪派反对牧首尼康改革的大司祭阿瓦库姆，1664—1666年带着全家被关押于此，这介于他的西伯利亚流放和普斯托泽尔斯克终身囚禁之间，1682年他在普斯托泽尔斯克被火刑处死。曾担任阿列克谢一世首席大臣的失势波雅尔阿尔塔蒙·马特维耶夫，1680—1682年也被关押在这里。1780年，叶卡捷琳娜二世把两处斯洛博达合并为梅津城。

en:
Onega occupies the mouth of the Onega River, a few kilometres from Onega Bay on the White Sea. In 1444 there was no town here, only the Pomor pogost of Ust-Onega, belonging to Novgorod. Boats coming downriver brought furs from the forest interior, while Pomor fishermen and sea hunters worked the cold coast and exchanged fish, salt and ship provisions. The river mouth and the short passage to the bay mattered more than any fortification: it was a place where inland cargoes changed to sea-going craft.

Ust-Onega passed to Moscow with Novgorod in 1478, and Polish-Lithuanian raiders sacked the pogost in 1613. The coast's most striking religious house grew on Kiy Island offshore. In 1632 the future Patriarch Nikon was caught in a storm while sailing from Solovki and put a wooden cross on the island after reaching land; as patriarch he founded the Krestny Monastery there in 1656. Its granite cathedral and monastic buildings were set among the rocks, and Nikon sent a large cypress cross made in Palestine. By the late seventeenth century Ust-Onega had also become one of four Russian ports allowed to ship goods to Britain under the Russia Company. English capital then turned the river into a timber estate: Pyotr Shuvalov opened sawmills in 1756, and William Gom added shipyards, ropeworks and a loading station on Kiy Island. Catherine II chartered the settlement as Oneg in 1780, and the new seaport began exporting timber the next year.
zh:
奥涅加位于奥涅加河河口，距白海奥涅加湾仅数公里。1444年这里还没有城市，只有隶属于诺夫哥罗德的波莫尔村镇乌斯季-奥涅加。沿河而下的船只运来内陆森林中的毛皮，波莫尔渔民和海猎者则在寒冷海岸活动，交易鱼、盐和船上给养。真正使这里立足的是河口与通往海湾的短程航路：内陆货物要在这里换成海船，而不是某座要塞。

1478年，乌斯季-奥涅加随诺夫哥罗德并入莫斯科；1613年，波兰-立陶宛袭掠者洗劫了这座村镇。海岸一带最引人注目的修道院坐落在外海的基伊岛。1632年，后来成为牧首的尼孔从索洛韦茨基出行时遭遇风暴，登岛后立下木十字架；他担任牧首后，于1656年在岛上创建十字修道院。修道院的花岗岩大教堂和房舍依岩石修建，尼孔还送来一具在巴勒斯坦订制的大型柏木十字架。到17世纪末，乌斯季-奥涅加已成为俄罗斯公司体制下获准向英国输出货物的四个俄罗斯港口之一。英国资本随后把这条河变成木材产区：彼得·舒瓦洛夫于1756年开设锯木厂，威廉·戈姆又增建船坞、缆绳厂和基伊岛上的装货站。1780年，叶卡捷琳娜二世颁令将聚落设为奥涅格城，新海港在次年开始输出木材。

en:
Velsk stands where the Vel flows into the Vaga, on ground so low that floods drove the settlement up to a higher bank in the sixteenth century. It first appears in writing in 1137, in a charter of the Novgorod prince Sviatoslav Olgovich, as a point for collecting church dues, and a chronicle of 1397 already calls the district the volost of Vel. In 1444 the Velsk pogost was a Novgorodian fur outpost on the Vaga, on a frontier Moscow was pressing hard.

Moscow took it in 1462, in the long contest with Novgorod, and made it a posad in 1550. Velsk grew on Vaga boat traffic and, in the following century, on the road between Moscow and Arkhangelsk, then Russia's chief northern harbour; its merchants held regular fairs, the largest of them the St Athanasius fair. Tar was the trade the town put on its arms: the charter of 1780 set a barrel brimming with pitch on a gold field, in token that the townsmen carried on a notable trade in it. In the nineteenth century the same woods supplied resin and turpentine, and Velsk became a centre of linen weaving.
zh:
韦利斯克位于韦利河汇入瓦加河之处，地势低洼，16世纪时洪水逼人迁到了较高的河岸。它最早见于1137年诺夫哥罗德王公斯维亚托斯拉夫·奥利戈维奇的宪章，是征收教会贡赋的一个地点；1397年的编年史已把这一带称作韦利乡。1444年，韦利斯克乡是诺夫哥罗德人在瓦加河上的毛皮据点，而莫斯科正沿这条边境步步紧逼。

1462年，在与诺夫哥罗德的长期争夺中，莫斯科取得韦利斯克，1550年把它设为城郊。它先靠瓦加河水运发展，下一个世纪又得益于莫斯科通往阿尔汉格尔斯克的大路，那时阿尔汉格尔斯克是俄国最主要的北方海港；商人定期办集，其中以圣亚大纳西集市最大。焦油贸易被搬上了城徽：1780年的特许状在金地上绘一只盛满焦油的桶，「以表示本市居民以此项贸易著称」。19世纪，同一片林地出产的树脂和松节油也成了生意，韦利斯克又成为亚麻织造中心。

en:
Vyshny Volochyok, the Upper Portage, sits on the Valdai watershed between the Tvertsa, which runs to the Volga and the Caspian, and the Tsna, which carries water through the Msta to Lake Ladoga and the Baltic. Cargoes coming up the Volga were unloaded here, hauled over the low divide, and reloaded for Novgorod, and the place lived by that drag, worked by boatmen, carters, and haulers. An account of Metropolitan Isidore's journey to the Council of Florence mentions the portage in 1437, and the first universally accepted chronicle notice is of 1471. In 1444 it was therefore a working Novgorodian crossing in the forest trade, not yet a town.

After Moscow took Novgorod a relay post stood at the portage. The Nikolsky pogost of the sixteenth century is marked as Volock on Western maps of Muscovy, but the seventy-three taxable households of a 1546 survey had fallen to forty-five by 1582, a decline Russian writers connect with Ivan IV's march on Novgorod in 1569; Polish troops destroyed the settlement in the Time of Troubles. Peter the Great began the Tveretsky Canal in 1703, and the man who made it work was Mikhail Serdyukov, a self-taught hydraulic engineer born in Mongolia and brought to Russia as a boy, where a clerk ransomed him for ten roubles and had him baptized. He dammed the Tsna to form Russia's first reservoir, added the Tsninsky Canal in 1719-1722, and released stored water in pulses to float great barge caravans, and grain for St Petersburg went through the Vyshny Volochyok Waterway from then on. The settlement received town rights in 1770. Catherine II inspected the locks in 1785, praised the engineering, and had granite obelisks raised to Serdyukov.
zh:
上沃洛乔克意为「上游拖船道」，坐落在瓦尔代高地的分水岭上：特维尔察河流入伏尔加河与里海，茨纳河经姆斯塔河通向拉多加湖和波罗的海。沿伏尔加河而来的货物在此卸下，拖过低矮的分水岭，再装船运往诺夫哥罗德，整个地方就靠这道拖运道过活，干活的是船工、车夫和纤夫。都主教伊西多尔前往佛罗伦萨会议的行记在1437年提到这条拖运道，普遍认可的编年史首次记载则是1471年。因此1444年时，它还是诺夫哥罗德森林商路上一处干活的转运点，尚未成镇。

莫斯科吞并诺夫哥罗德后，拖运道上设了驿栈。16世纪的尼科利斯克教区聚落被西方的莫斯科维亚地图标为沃洛克，但1546年调查中的七十三户纳税人家，到1582年只剩四十五户，俄国史家把这一衰落与1569年伊凡四世讨伐诺夫哥罗德的行军联系起来；动乱时期波兰军队又摧毁了聚落。彼得大帝1703年开建特维尔察运河，真正让运河运转起来的是自学成才的水利工程师米哈伊尔·谢尔久科夫：他生在蒙古，幼年被带到俄国，一名文书花十卢布把他赎下并为他施洗。他在茨纳河上筑坝，造出俄国第一座水库，又在1719至1722年修成茨纳运河，以蓄水、放水的办法放大批驳船队通过，运往圣彼得堡的粮食就走上沃洛乔克水系。1770年，这里获得城市权。叶卡捷琳娜二世1785年视察船闸，称赞这套工程，下令为谢尔久科夫立起花岗岩方尖碑。

en:
Ustyuzhna stands at the mouth of the Izhina where it joins the Mologa, in a district called the Iron Field for the bog iron dug from its marshes. The Uglich chronicle first names the place in 1252, as Ustyug Zhelezny, or Iron Ustyug, and the river road through it was the shortest way from Novgorod into the Northern Dvina basin. In 1444 it was an Orthodox town of Beloozero whose smiths already worked local bog iron for northern markets, before the arms boom that made the town's name.

Ivan the Terrible knew the place: he granted its customs charter in 1544 and visited it in person. By the later 1500s Ustyuzhna held about 6,000 people and seventy-seven recorded smithy owners, against thirty at Tula. Its smiths made salt-pan iron, ploughshares, nails, small cannon called volkoneyki and tens of thousands of cannonballs. Plague, the Livonian War and the ruin of Novgorod left nearly seventy percent of its households empty by 1597. In the Time of Troubles a militia of Ustyuzhna and Beloozero townsmen was cut down at Batnevka on 5 January 1609, mown like grass; the survivors shut the gates and from 3 to 8 February beat off Polish cavalry and German mercenary infantry, and the town was never taken. Through the seventeenth century Ustyuzhna ranked second only to Tula among Russian arms centres. In 1630 its smiths forged the grilles for the Spasskaya and other Kremlin tower gates in Moscow, and in 1694 the Church of Our Lady of Kazan went up, a Stroganov-pattern stone church among the town's growing row of stone churches. Peter the Great ran the Izhina arms works here in 1702-1714, casting cannon and forging muskets and shot, until Ural ore displaced bog iron and the works closed in 1714.
zh:
乌斯秋日纳位于伊日纳河汇入莫洛加河之处，当地沼泽出产沼铁矿，这片地区因而得名「铁原」。1252年，《乌格利奇编年史》首次提到此地，称作乌斯秋格·热列兹内，即「铁乌斯秋格」；穿过这里的水路是诺夫哥罗德前往北德维纳河流域的最捷路线。1444年，它是别洛奥泽罗治下的东正教城镇，铁匠已用当地沼铁打造器物供应北方市场，而让此地出名的军械繁荣还在后面。

伊凡雷帝知道这座城镇：1544年为它颁发关税特许状，还亲自到访。到16世纪后期，乌斯秋日纳约有六千居民，登记在册的铁匠铺主有七十七人，图拉则只有三十人。工匠打造煮盐用铁、犁铧、铁钉、名为「沃尔科涅伊卡」的小炮，还有数以万计的炮弹。瘟疫、利沃尼亚战争和诺夫哥罗德的衰败，使近七成院宅到1597年已无人居住。动乱时期，乌斯秋日纳和别洛奥泽罗民军1609年1月5日在巴特涅夫卡被「像草一样砍倒」；幸存者闭门据守，在2月3日至8日击退波兰骑兵和德意志雇佣步兵，城镇始终未陷。整个17世纪，乌斯秋日纳是仅次于图拉的俄国军械中心。1630年，这里的铁匠为莫斯科克里姆林宫斯帕斯门等塔楼锻打格栅；1694年，喀山圣母教堂落成，是镇上日渐增多的石造教堂中一座斯特罗加诺夫式样的教堂。1702—1714年，彼得大帝设立的伊日纳兵工厂在此铸造火炮、打造火枪和炮弹，后来乌拉尔铁矿取代沼铁，工厂于1714年停办。

en:
Totma lies on the Sukhona, the river road that carried northern furs and salt toward the Northern Dvina and the White Sea. A charter of Prince Svyatoslav Olgovich lists the pogost of Todma in 1137, though its Finno-Ugric name and older traces point to a Merya settlement before Novgorodian traders used the bank. Salt boilers were at work by the thirteenth century, and in the fifteenth century villagers of Uglitskaya and Galitskaya sank deep brine wells, a technique that produced the salt settlement of Usolye Totemskoye. Spaso-Prilutsky and other Vologda monasteries long controlled many of the pans, while furs from forests beyond the Sukhona crossed the same landing stages. In 1444 Totma was a chain of wooden salt-boiling hamlets in Muscovy's northern borderlands, halfway between Vologda and Veliky Ustyug.

Kazan Tatars ravaged the district in 1539-41, and an ostrog fortress was raised on the high Sukhona hill afterward. Feodosy Sumorin founded the Spaso-Sumorin Monastery in 1554, and the house became a major holder of the salt trade. In the seventeenth century five hundred to a thousand vessels could pass in a year and eight large pans boiled about 200,000 poods of salt. Peter I visited three times; local legend has him lifting a brine bucket. When St Petersburg and the Baltic drew trade away, Totma's merchants looked east. In the later eighteenth century the Kholodilov, Panov and Cherepanov families equipped about twenty Pacific expeditions, more than the merchants of Moscow, Vologda and Veliky Ustyug combined; over the next half-century those voyages brought back roughly a fifth of the furs taken in America. Their money built the tall, cartouche-covered churches called Totma baroque, and in 1785 the town received arms of a black fox on a gold field. Ivan Kuskov, born in Totma, sailed that route to California and founded Fort Ross in 1812.
zh:
托季马位于苏霍纳河畔，北方的盐和毛皮沿这条河路前往北德维纳河与白海。1137年，王公斯维亚托斯拉夫·奥尔戈维奇的宪章列有「托德马」乡；但这个芬兰—乌戈尔语地名和更早遗迹说明，在诺夫哥罗德商人利用这段河岸之前，这里已有梅里亚人聚落。13世纪时两岸已在煮盐，15世纪，乌格利茨卡亚和加利茨卡亚的村民开凿深井汲取卤水，靠这项技术兴起了盐业聚落乌索列·托季姆斯科耶。斯帕索-普里卢茨基等沃洛格达修道院长期控制许多盐锅，苏霍纳河彼岸密林的毛皮也经过同一批码头外运。1444年，托季马是莫斯科北方边疆一串煮盐木寨村落，位于沃洛格达和大乌斯秋格之间的半路上。

1539至1541年，喀山鞑靼人蹂躏这一带，事后人们在苏霍纳河高地上筑起木栅要塞。1554年，费奥多西·苏莫林创办斯帕索-苏莫林修道院，修道院后来掌握了大部分盐业。17世纪时，每年可有五百至一千艘船经过，八口大盐锅年产约二十万普特盐。彼得一世曾三次到访，当地传说还说他亲手提过一桶卤水。圣彼得堡和波罗的海商路吸走贸易后，托季马商人把目光转向东方。18世纪后期，霍洛季洛夫、帕诺夫和切列帕诺夫等家族装备约二十支太平洋探险队，数量超过莫斯科、沃洛格达和大乌斯秋格商人的总和；此后半个世纪里，这些航行运回约占美洲所产毛皮五分之一的货物。他们的财富建起饰有高大涡卷铭牌的教堂，即后来所说的「托季马巴洛克」。1785年，托季马获得金底黑狐城徽。本地人伊万·库斯科夫沿这条海路远航到加利福尼亚，于1812年创建罗斯堡。

en:
Sol-Galitskaya, 'the salt of Galich', grew up around brine springs in the southern-taiga forest of the upper Kostroma, Merya hunting-ground before Novgorod boatmen pushed up the river. Its salt pans first appear in Ivan Kalita's will, and by the 14th century they ranked among the greatest saltworks of the Russian North, supplying Russia and much of Scandinavia; the place held town rank from 1389. It came to the Moscow princes with the Galich principality, but the pans passed to the family of Dmitry Shemyaka and paid for his long civil war against Vasily II. In 1444 Sol-Galitskaya was the richest town of Shemyaka's Galich appanage, lying on Muscovy's forest frontier.

Vasily II took Galich and the salt town in 1450. Early in the next century an earthen-and-timber kremlin rose on the left bank, six timber towers behind a moat fed by the Kostroma, and in 1532 it survived a three-day siege by Kazan Tatars. Local tradition says the attackers broke off at the sight of a monk on a white horse riding through their ranks, whom the townspeople recognised from their icon as St Macarius of Unzha; the defenders poured boiling water and pitch from twenty-bucket iron cauldrons forged from local bog ore by the same smiths who made the salt-pans, and one of the cauldrons is kept in the town museum. Raids by Tatars and Cheremis continued nonetheless. Six monasteries, led by the Trinity Lavra of St Sergius, boiled the brine in the 16th century, and the Kostroma-Sukhona water road carried the salt north to Arkhangelsk. A Polish band sacked the town in the Time of Troubles, and after the fire of 1649 its merchants rebuilt half a dozen churches in brick; salt and lime made the following century its most prosperous, and its coat of arms bears three piles of salt on a golden field. Another fire in 1808 destroyed the wooden town, and it was rebuilt again.
zh:
索利加利奇意为「加利奇之盐」，兴起于科斯特罗马河上游南泰加林中的盐泉旁；斯拉夫人溯河而来以前，这里是梅里亚人的猎场，最早进入林区的是诺夫哥罗德船民。盐场首见于伊凡·卡利塔的遗嘱，到14世纪已是俄罗斯北方最大的盐产地之一，食盐销往罗斯各地和斯堪的纳维亚大部，1389年取得城镇地位。它随加利奇公国归入莫斯科诸王公领地，盐场后来落入德米特里·舍米亚卡家族之手，为他同瓦西里二世的长期内战提供军费。1444年的索利加利奇是舍米亚卡加利奇封地上最富庶的城镇，坐落在莫斯科公国的林海边陲。

1450年，瓦西里二世攻下加利奇和这座盐城。16世纪初，河左岸筑起土木克里姆林，六道木塔外有科斯特罗马河引水围成的壕沟；1532年，它顶住了喀山鞑靼人三天的围攻。相传攻城者看见一名骑白马的修士在阵中往来驰骋，惊以为异象而撤围，城里人据圣像认出他是温扎的马卡里；守军把沸水和滚油从能装二十桶的大铁锅里浇下，铁锅由平时打制盐锅的本地工匠用沼泽铁铸成，其中一口现藏当地的方志博物馆。鞑靼人与切列米斯人的袭扰仍未断绝。16世纪，以圣三一谢尔盖修道院为首的六座修道院在此煮盐，食盐经科斯特罗马—苏霍纳河水路北运阿尔汉格尔斯克。大动乱年代中一股波兰匪帮洗劫了此城，1649年大火后商人用砖石重建了六七座教堂；食盐和石灰让随后一百年成为它最富庶的时期，城徽绘着金底上的三堆食盐。1808年大火再度烧毁这座木城，它又一次被重建。

en:
South of Kazan the Volga runs below soft bluffs and grain fields, the southern reach of the Kazan khanate's Gornaya storona. In the tenth century the Bulgars built Oshel here, a trading town with its own citadel; the ruins, the Bogdashkino hillfort, cover 770,000 square metres. In 1220 Prince Svyatoslav, brother of the grand prince of Vladimir Yuri Vsevolodovich, stormed and burned Oshel, and the site was abandoned for good in the Mongol sweep of 1236. A Tatar riverside landing called Tetyush took its place; one account traces the name to the Bulgar tribe temtyuzi, and local legend to a Khan Tetyush who fled the burning of Great Bulgar and settled the bluff. In 1444 it was a small Muslim landing of the Kazan khanate, living by grain, fishing and the Volga traffic passing below it.

Anthony Jenkinson, sailing to the Caspian in 1558, marked the place on his chart as Petowse, twenty leagues below the mouth of the Kama. Between 1574 and 1578 the Russians raised the Tetyushskaya zastava on the height and tied it into the Karlinsky abatis line guarding the Volga bank from the steppe. When Simbirsk was founded in 1648 the frontier and its garrison moved south, though Stenka Razin's rebels were still fought here in the revolt's Volga campaign of 1670. Tetyushi then became a merchants' and fishermen's town with its own wharf, shipping grain and Volga fish. It went to Kazan Governorate in 1708, and Catherine II gave it a coat of arms and town status in 1781.
zh:
喀山以南，伏尔加河在平缓崖岸和片片粮田之间流过，是喀山汗国「山那边」的南段。10世纪时，保加尔人在这里建起贸易城镇奥舍利，城中有自己的内堡，遗址博格达什基诺城址占地达七十七万平方米。1220年，弗拉基米尔大公尤里·弗谢沃洛多维奇之弟斯维亚托斯拉夫王公率军攻破并焚毁此城，1236年蒙古人扫荡过后，废墟彻底荒废。取而代之的鞑靼人河埠叫捷秋希：一说其名来自保加尔的捷姆秋济部落，当地传说则称，一位名叫捷秋希的汗在大保加尔城破后逃出，在这段崖岸上落脚建城。1444年，它是喀山汗国一座穆斯林小聚落，靠种粮、捕鱼和崖下往来的伏尔加河商船为生。

1558年，安东尼·詹金森沿伏尔加河前往里海，在海图上把此地标作佩托斯，位于卡马河口以下二十里格。1574至1578年间，俄罗斯人在高地上修起捷秋希哨所，把它接入防备草原的卡林鹿砦线，扼守伏尔加河岸。1648年辛比尔斯克筑城，防线和守军随之南移；1670年，斯坚卡·拉辛起义的伏尔加之役仍在这里打过一仗。捷秋希此后成为商人和渔夫的城镇，自有码头，运出谷物和伏尔加河鱼。1708年它划入喀山省，1781年叶卡捷琳娜二世赐给城徽、升格为城。

en:
Ar-Chally carries the Tatar name Yar Çallı for a stretch of the left bank of the Kama around the mouth of the little Chelny River, the site of later Naberezhnye Chelny. In 1444 no documented town stood here, only grain fields and pasture under the Muslim Kazan Khanate, whose boats worked the river below the bank.

After Ivan the Terrible conquered Kazan in 1552, the shore became a Muscovite frontier. In 1626 Russian peasants who moved in from nearby Yelabuga founded Chalninsky Pochinok, the first settlement of modern times on the site; it grew into the village of Mysovye Chelny, while neighbouring Berezhnye Chelny kept the old Tatar name. Neither village was fortified, but their ferries, fisheries and ploughed clearings kept people on the lower Kama through the rest of the period.
zh:
阿尔查利沿用鞑靼旧名亚尔·恰勒（Yar Çallı），指小切尔纳河口一带的卡马河左岸，也就是后来卡马河畔切尔内的所在。1444年这里没有文献可考的城镇，只有穆斯林喀山汗国治下的谷地农田和牧场，汗国的船只在下方河道往来。

1552年伊凡雷帝征服喀山后，这片河岸成为莫斯科的边疆。1626年，从邻近的叶拉布加迁来的俄国农民建立查尔宁斯基新村，这是当地近世第一个居民点，后来发展成梅索维耶·切尔内村；邻近的别列日涅耶·切尔内则保留了旧鞑靼地名。两个村子都没有设防，但渡口、渔场和开垦的耕地使下卡马河岸在此后的年代里一直有人居住。

en:
The Izh cuts through the wooded southern country of the Udmurts, the 'meadow people' of the Kama tributaries. Their hillforts above the river bends, two of them on the Karlutka stream, were raised between the third and fifth centuries; they tilled the clearings, kept bees and hunted, and their stronghold on the Izh was called in their own tongue Izhkar. Like the rest of the Arsk land these basins had paid tribute to Volga Bulgaria and afterwards to the Golden Horde, and in 1444 they belonged to the khanate of Kazan, drawing grain, honey and pelts from its Udmurt villages.

After the fall of Kazan the Udmurt country became Russian, and in 1582 Ivan IV granted the lower Izh lands to Bagish Yaushev, a Tatar morza; his family held them until 1733, when they sold to the diplomat Alexey Tevkelev. Iron was to make the place. In 1757 Count Pyotr Shuvalov won leave to build three ironworks in the Kama country, and his engineer Alexey Moskvin chose the Izh, with its forest, water power and empty state land. The works started in 1760, its dam ponded the river into one of the largest factory ponds in the empire, and in 1763 the first wrought iron came from Goroblagodat pig iron; Shuvalov's iron bands went to rebuilding the Moscow Kremlin and to building sites in Saint Petersburg. After Shuvalov's death Catherine II took the works into the Crown for his debts. In the summer of 1774 Pugachev's rebels seized it, executed its forty-two managers and partly burned the plant, and the bonded smiths joined his march on Kazan; production did not resume until the end of 1775.

Then it became an arsenal. In 1800 Paul I ordered a Urals arms factory against Napoleonic France, and the engineer Andrey Deryabin chose the Izh works. Alexander I approved, and in June 1807 Deryabin founded the arms factory there, staffing it with serfs and recruits and hiring master armorers from Sweden and Denmark; by 1808 more than six thousand people lived at the plant, which passed from the mining to the war department that same year.
zh:
伊日河穿过乌德穆尔特人的南方林野，他们是卡马河诸支流上的「草地之人」。河湾高地上的寨堡早在3至5世纪便已出现，卡尔卢特卡溪畔就有两座；他们耕种林间隙地、养蜂、狩猎，用本族语言把伊日河畔的据点称作伊热卡尔。与阿尔斯克之地的其余部分一样，这些盆地先后向伏尔加保加利亚和金帐汗国纳贡，1444年归属喀山汗国，汗国从乌德穆尔特村庄征取谷物、蜂蜜和毛皮。

喀山陷落后，乌德穆尔特之地并入俄罗斯。1582年，伊凡四世把伊日河下游的土地封给鞑靼穆尔扎巴吉什·亚乌舍夫；其家族保有到1733年，卖给了外交官阿列克谢·捷夫克列夫。这片地方日后靠铁矿安身立命。1757年，彼得·舒瓦洛夫伯爵获准在卡马地区修建三座铁厂，采矿工程师阿列克谢·莫斯克文选中伊日河，林地、水力和无人认领的官地一应俱全。工厂1760年动工，水坝把伊日河拦成帝国最大的工厂池塘之一；1763年用戈罗布拉戈达特运来的生铁炼出第一批熟铁，舒瓦洛夫的铁条还运往莫斯科，用于重建克里姆林宫和圣彼得堡的工地。舒瓦洛夫死后，叶卡捷琳娜二世以抵债为由把工厂收归官有。1774年夏，普加乔夫的起义者夺取工厂，处死四十二名管理人员，焚毁部分厂房，厂中的农奴和工匠加入进军喀山的队伍；直到1775年底生产才恢复。

铁厂接着变成了兵工厂。1800年，帕维尔一世下令在乌拉尔修建兵工厂，防备拿破仑法国；奉命择址的工程师安德烈·杰里亚宾选中了伊日铁厂。亚历山大一世批准后，1807年6月杰里亚宾在旧铁厂创办兵工厂，以农奴和新兵充作工人，又从瑞典、丹麦聘来军械匠；到1808年，这座工厂聚落已有六千余人，工厂也在这一年由矿业衙门划归陆军衙门。

en:
Bolgar stood on the high Volga bank about thirty kilometres below the Kama confluence, beside the Aga Bazaar, the busiest trading ground in Volga Bulgaria. Arab geographers called it the harbour of the northern trade: from the late eighth century to the eleventh, eastern silver and goods reached Rus mainly by this landing. Merchants from China, Baghdad, Damascus, Spain and Scandinavia came to its annual fair and kept their own streets in the town. Bolgar's own jewellers, tanners, blacksmiths and armourers sold leather, honey and mail coats. In 922 Ahmad ibn Fadlan, secretary of the Abbasid embassy sent to the ruler Almış, recorded the court's acceptance of Islam.

Batu Khan's army sacked Bolgar in 1236, but under the Golden Horde the town grew back larger than before: Berke, the first Muslim khan of the Horde, made it the centre of the old Bulgar lands, and builders raised the cathedral mosque, the mausolea and stone caravanserais. Bulat-Timur burned it in 1361, and a Muscovite and Nizhny Novgorod army briefly installed its own customs officer in the 1370s before the Tatars retook it. It recovered, until the Muscovite commander Fyodor Paletsky, called Pyostry, destroyed it in 1431 and the inhabitants left for good. In 1444 Bolgar was a vast, revered ruin inside the new Kazan Khanate; the living market had moved to Kazan, which the Tatars called Bolgar-al-Jadid, the new Bolgar, while Tatar Muslims still came to pray among the stone mausolea and the Black Chamber.

After Ivan the Terrible took Kazan in 1552, Russian commoners settled beneath the old earthen walls, and in the eighteenth century an Orthodox Dormition monastery rose on the site, though Tatar pilgrims kept coming to the ruins. Peter I visited in 1722 and issued an ukase ordering the monuments preserved, the first such law in Russia. Catherine II came in 1767, saw the two surviving minarets and was angered that ancient stonework had been quarried for building material. In 1781 the village of Spassk on the Bezdna became the district town of the same name; by 1821 a small Volga town trans-shipping agricultural goods stood beside the abandoned medieval capital.
zh:
保加尔坐落在卡马河汇流处下游约30公里的伏尔加河高岸上，旁边是伏尔加保加利亚最繁忙的集市阿加巴扎尔。阿拉伯地理学家把这座城称作穆斯林东方与北方贸易的港口：8世纪末到11世纪，东方的白银和货物主要经这个码头输入罗斯。中国、巴格达、大马士革、西班牙和斯堪的纳维亚的商人每年赶来赴会，外商在城里各有自己的街巷。本地的珠宝匠、鞣皮匠、铁匠和甲胄匠出售皮革、蜂蜜和锁子甲。922年，阿拔斯哈里发派往统治者阿尔穆什的使团秘书艾哈迈德·伊本·法德兰，记下了保加尔宫廷接受伊斯兰教的经过。

1236年拔都的军队洗劫保加尔，但金帐汗国时期城市比从前更大：金帐汗国第一位信奉伊斯兰教的可汗别儿哥以这里为旧保加尔土地的中心，工匠们建起聚礼清真寺、陵墓和石头商队客栈。1361年布拉特·帖木儿焚毁此城；14世纪70年代，莫斯科与下诺夫哥罗德的联军曾短暂占领它，派驻自己的税关官员，鞑靼人很快夺回城市。保加尔得到恢复，直到1431年莫斯科将领费奥多尔·帕列茨基（又称佩斯特雷）将它摧毁，居民再没有回来。1444年，保加尔是新兴喀山汗国境内一片广阔而受尊崇的废墟；活着的市场已迁到喀山，鞑靼人把喀山称作「新保加尔」，而穆斯林仍到石陵和黑殿之间祈祷。

1552年伊凡雷帝攻占喀山后，俄罗斯平民在旧土墙下定居；18世纪，遗址上建起东正教圣母安息修道院，鞑靼朝圣者仍不断来到废墟。1722年彼得一世到访，颁布保护古迹的诏令，这是俄国第一部文物保护法令。1767年叶卡捷琳娜二世前来，见到残存的两座宣礼塔，得知古建筑被拆作石材后十分愤怒。1781年，别兹德纳河畔的斯帕斯村成为同名县城；到1821年，它已是伏尔加河上一个转运农产品的小市镇，旁边就是这座废弃的中世纪都城。

en:
Aqaba sits at the narrow head of the Red Sea gulf that bears its name, where the roads from Egypt, Syria and Arabia reach the water. The Romans knew the port as Aela, terminus of the Via Traiana Nova and later a bishopric. During the Tabuk campaign of 630 Muhammad himself came to Aila and the city made terms and paid tribute; the walled Arab town that replaced it had four gates and twenty-four towers, grew rich on the spice road to India, and is mentioned in the Arabian Nights, before the earthquake of 1068 left it in ruins. The Crusaders built the fortress of Elyn and garrisoned Pharaoh's Island seven kilometres offshore; a squadron of Saladin retook the town in 1170, and Raynald of Châtillon raided it in his turn without winning it back. By 1444 old Ayla had shrunk to a Bedouin fishing haven beside its ruins, though the Mamluk sultans kept a fortified khan there for the Egyptian pilgrim caravan crossing from Sinai, and the pass above the site gave the place its later name, al-Aqaba.

The standing fortress was built by the Mamluk sultan al-Ashraf Qansuh al-Ghuri, whose inscription runs along the gatehouse, on the site of khans going back to the 13th century. In 1517 it passed with the rest of the Mamluk lands to the Ottomans, and Sultan Murad III rebuilt much of it in 1587 for the Mecca road. The port did not recover: for the rest of Ottoman times al-Aqaba remained a simple fishing village, its harbour serving pilgrim dhows and little else while Bedouin pastured their flocks along the arid coast.
zh:
亚喀巴坐落在同名红海海湾的狭口，埃及、叙利亚和阿拉伯的道路都在这里入海。罗马时代，这座港口称埃拉，是新图拉真大道的终点，后来还设有主教区。630年塔布克之战期间，穆罕默德亲自抵达艾伊拉，城邦求和纳贡；取代旧城而建的阿拉伯城墙环绕、开四座城门、立二十四座望楼，靠通往印度的香料商路致富，《一千零一夜》里也提到它，直到1068年的大地震把城震成废墟。十字军建起埃林要塞，还在七公里外的法老岛上驻军；1170年萨拉丁的一支舰队收复此地，沙蒂永的雷纳德后来虽来劫掠，法兰克人却再没能夺回。到1444年，古艾伊拉已缩成贝都因人傍着废墟而居的渔港，不过马穆鲁克苏丹在此保留了一座设防客栈，供从西奈过来的埃及朝觐驼队落脚；城旁那道山隘给了它后来的名字亚喀巴。

现存要塞由马穆鲁克苏丹阿什拉夫·甘萨赫·古里下令修建，门楼里留着他的铭文，地基上还叠着13世纪以来的几座客栈。1517年，它随马穆鲁克的全部疆土并入奥斯曼；1587年，穆拉德三世又把它大加重修，以护卫麦加路。港口并未因此复兴，此后整个奥斯曼时期，亚喀巴始终是个简陋渔村，港湾里只有朝觐帆船往来，贝都因部落则在干旱的海岸边放牧。

en:
Al-Wajh is a roadstead on the barren Red Sea coast of north-western Arabia, the seaward outlet of the oasis country behind it. Medieval Arab geographers called it the port of Hegra, and some scholars place at this bay Leuke Kome, the Nabataean 'White Village' that Strabo and the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea describe as a Red Sea market with a road running inland to Petra. The town's name points to fresh water: the spring in Wadi al-Zarib was a main watering place on the Egyptian Hajj road as early as Abbasid and Fatimid times, and after 1268 it was counted a reliable source. Pilgrim caravans coming down the coast from Aqaba filled their skins here before turning inland for Medina; fishermen beached their boats below the low cliffs, and Bedouin of the hinterland bartered at the quay. In 1444 the anchorage and its wells lay at the remote edge of the Mamluk sultanate, whose authority there went little further than the safe-conduct owed to the pilgrim caravan.

With the rest of the Hijaz coast, al-Wajh passed to the Ottomans in 1517, and their captains used the harbour as an anchorage on the northern Red Sea. In 1617, under Sultan Ahmed I, the fort of al-Zarib was raised beside the wells, a four-towered stone stronghold with two cisterns, one link in the chain of castles guarding the Egyptian pilgrims and the grain they stored for the journey home. Eleven old wells cluster around the fort in the wadi bed, and vaulted rainwater cisterns helped the town through dry years. Outside the garrison and the caravan season the port saw little change, and through the Ottoman centuries it remained a fishing and watering town, its houses clustered beneath the fort above the bay.
zh:
沃季赫（中文维基作「沃季」）是阿拉伯西北干旱红海岸上的一处锚地，也是身后绿洲地带的出海口。中世纪阿拉伯地理学家称它为黑格拉港；也有人认为，斯特拉波和《厄立特里亚海航行记》里记载的纳巴泰商镇「白村」莱夫凯科梅就在这处海湾，有条道路从那里通向内陆的佩特拉。城名与淡水有关：扎里卜干谷的泉眼早在阿拔斯和法蒂玛时代就是埃及朝觐路上的主要水源地，1268年后更被认定为可靠水源。从亚喀巴沿海岸南下的朝圣驼队在此装满水囊，再折向内陆前往麦地那；渔民在低矮崖壁下停泊小船，内陆的贝都因人到码头以物易物。1444年，这处锚地和水井处在马穆鲁克苏丹国遥远的边陲，苏丹在当地的权威大体只体现在对朝圣驼队的护送上。

1517年，沃季赫随汉志海岸其他地方一起并入奥斯曼，海军将领把这座港湾当作红海北部的锚泊地。1617年艾哈迈德一世在位时，扎里卜堡在水井旁建成，这座石砌要塞四角有楼、内有两座蓄水池，是拱卫埃及朝圣者、看护他们归途口粮的一系列城堡之一。干谷河床中，十一口老井环列在古堡周围，拱顶地下蓄水池则帮居民熬过干旱的年份。除驻防和驼队过境的季节外，港口没有多少变化；整个奥斯曼时期，这里始终是个渔镇兼补水站，屋舍簇拥在俯临海湾的古堡脚下。

en: Azraq is the only permanent freshwater oasis in some twelve thousand square kilometres of desert, lying on the old caravan tracks between the Hauran uplands, Karak and inner Arabia. Its pools drew Nabataean herdsmen and traders; Roman troops raised a basalt fort there around the third century, which Byzantine and Umayyad garrisons went on using. The black-stone Qasr al-Azraq took its present form in 1237, when the Ayyubid emir Izz al-Din Aybak rebuilt and enlarged it. Under Mamluk rule the wells, marshes and grazing around the castle were the wandering country of the Al Fadl and neighbouring Bedouin, hereditary amirs of the desert tribes, who sold caravans animals and guides and taxed or plundered them when terms failed. In 1444 Azraq was less a town than a fortified watering place where a caravan or a raiding party could fill its skins. An Ottoman garrison occupied the castle in the sixteenth century, yet the Bedouin remained the stronger power around the wells; through 1821 Azraq counted only as a muster point on the Wadi Sirhan road.
zh: 阿兹拉克是约一万二千平方公里沙漠里唯一常年有水的淡水绿洲，位于豪兰高地、卡拉克与阿拉伯半岛内陆之间的古老商道旁。水塘早为纳巴泰牧人和商人所用；3世纪前后，罗马军队在这里筑起玄武岩堡垒，此后拜占庭和倭马亚驻军继续使用。1237年，阿尤布埃米尔伊兹丁·艾贝克改建并扩建城堡，黑色石砌的阿兹拉克堡才有了现存形制。马穆鲁克时期，城堡周围的水井、沼泽和牧场是法德勒及邻近贝都因部落的游牧地；这些部落世代担任沙漠诸部的埃米尔，向商队出售牲畜和向导，谈不拢时就抽税或劫掠。1444年的阿兹拉克算不上城镇，更像一处设防的饮水地，商队和袭掠队伍都能在此灌满水囊。16世纪，奥斯曼驻军进驻城堡，但水井一带真正说了算的仍是贝都因人；直到1821年，阿兹拉克始终只是锡尔汉谷地道路上的集结点。

en:
Suwayda stands on the volcanic Jabal Hauran, where the black basalt grain lands of the Hauran climb towards the Syrian Desert. Nabataeans founded it as Suada, and in 149 it took the name Dionysias, after Dionysus, in an old vine and wine country where the Greek god and the Nabataean Dushara came to be worshipped in the same temple. When Yaqut al-Hamawi passed through in the 1220s he found a mere Hauran village among Roman ruins. Under the Mamluks the district sent grain to Damascus, watched the Gaza post road and sold provisions to the Hajj caravans mustering at nearby Bosra. Beyond the ploughland the steppe belonged to the Al Mira Bedouin. During Timur's invasion in 1400 they seized the Hauran grain revenues, and a Mamluk raid on their camp around Suwayda the next year carried off thousands of camels. In 1444 Suwayda was a small village and a tribal camp on the last edge of settled cultivation.

Ottoman tax registers of 1596 found only five households and five bachelors there, under the name Majdal Sawda, paying on wheat, barley, goats and beehives. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the mountain was largely left to itself. Bedouin levied tribute on its villages, and the Damascus pilgrimage assembled at Muzayrib instead of Bosra. Then the Druze arrived. A first party led by the Alam al-Din family came in 1685, and after the Druze defeat at the Battle of Ain Dara in 1711 a much larger migration left Mount Lebanon for the Jabal Hauran, reoccupying its well-watered, defensible ruined villages. The Hamdan chiefs led the newcomers, and by 1812 Suwayda was a Druze village, the centre of the mountain that took the name Jabal al-Druze. Its people lived by mountain vines and grain, livestock fairs and the carrying trade between Damascus, Bosra and the desert.
zh:
苏韦达位于火山质的豪兰山上，豪兰黑色玄武岩地带的粮田从这里向叙利亚沙漠抬升。纳巴泰人初建时称苏阿达；149年，这座城因当地久产葡萄美酒而以酒神狄奥尼索斯之名改称狄奥尼西亚斯，希腊酒神后来还和纳巴泰本地神祇合奉在同一座神庙。13世纪20年代雅古特·哈马维路过时，这里只剩一座豪兰村庄，散处在罗马遗迹之间。马穆鲁克时期，本区向大马士革供应粮食，扼守加沙驿道，还把补给卖给在邻近布斯拉集结的朝觐商队。耕地之外的草原则属于阿尔·米拉贝都因人：1400年帖木儿入侵时他们夺取豪兰粮税，次年马穆鲁克军队袭击他们在苏韦达一带的营地，掳走数千头骆驼。1444年的苏韦达，是定居农业最边缘的一座小村和部落营地。

1596年的奥斯曼税册里，它以迈季代勒·索达之名只登记了五户人家和五名单身男子，税项是小麦、大麦、山羊和蜂箱。17至18世纪，山地基本处于放任状态，贝都因人向村庄索贡，大马士革的朝觐队伍也改在穆宰里卜集结，不再去布斯拉。德鲁兹人随后到来。1685年，阿拉姆丁家族率领第一批人迁入；1711年德鲁兹人在艾因·达拉战役战败后，更大批离开黎巴嫩山进入豪兰山，重新占据水源充足、地势险要的荒废村庄。新来者由哈姆丹家族首领统领，到1812年苏韦达已是一座德鲁兹村庄，成为后来得名德鲁兹山的山地中心。居民靠山地葡萄和谷物、牲畜集市，以及大马士革、布斯拉与沙漠之间的运输贸易为生。

en:
Al Jawf is the oasis basin at the southern end of Wadi Sirhan, north of the An Nafud. Its old walled settlement, Dumat al-Jandal, stood where South Arabian incense roads forked toward Mesopotamia and Syria. Wells and palm gardens drew caravans into the basin, and the Marid citadel watched over them from a rise. The fortress's name means 'the rebellious', from its reputation for defying besiegers; a third-century attack by Zenobia of Palmyra failed to take it. The walled town also held a mosque attributed to Umar ibn al-Khattab. Khalid ibn al-Walid captured Dumat for the early caliphate in 630. In 1444 Anizah camps and neighboring clans moved camels, sheep and goats between Wadi Sirhan, the oasis wells and desert pasture; the old town served as a refuge and meeting place for Bedouin groups more powerful than any settled court.

The Ruwallah, a warrior branch of the Anizah confederation, took shape in the sixteenth century or shortly afterward and made Al Jawf and Wadi Sirhan their central range, able to move south toward Al Qasim and north toward Damascus. Al-Dari ibn Mishhur of the Sha'lan house, born about 1766, became their emir in 1797. As the first Saudi state collapsed, disorder spread through the Jawf and Wadi Sirhan settlements; Al-Dari brought the Ruwallah in from the pastures, placed the towns and villages under his control, and levied an annual khuwwa payment in exchange for protection. By 1821 the Ruwallah camel camps controlled the wells and the tribute collected around them.
zh:
焦夫是内夫得沙漠以北、西勒汉干河南端的绿洲盆地。古城杜马特·詹达勒有城墙环绕，正处在南阿拉伯香料路分向两河流域和叙利亚的位置。水井与椰枣园把商队引入盆地，高地上的马里德堡俯瞰着水源和道路。堡名意为「叛逆者」，得自它屡次抵御围攻的名声；3世纪时，巴尔米拉的芝诺比阿来攻也未能夺下这座要塞。城里还有一座相传与欧麦尔·本·哈塔卜有关的清真寺。630年，哈立德·伊本·瓦利德为早期哈里发国家夺取杜马特。1444年，阿尼扎营地和邻近部族赶着骆驼、绵羊和山羊，在西勒汉干河、绿洲水井和沙漠牧场之间迁移；古城是这些贝都因群体的避难所与会集点，他们的力量胜过任何定居宫廷。

鲁瓦拉是阿尼扎联盟中的战牧分支，在16世纪或稍后成形，以焦夫和西勒汉干河为核心活动范围，南可抵达盖西姆，北能抵达大马士革。沙兰家族的德里伊·本·米什胡尔约生于1766年，1797年成为首领。第一沙特王国崩溃前后，焦夫和西勒汉干河聚落陷入混乱；德里伊率鲁瓦拉人从牧地进入，控制城镇村庄，并以保护为名每年征收「胡瓦」。到1821年，鲁瓦拉人的骆驼营地已经掌握水井和周围聚落缴纳的贡赋。

en:
Al-Kariatan, Arabic for 'the two villages', takes its name from two old settlements on the Wadi al-Rummah: al-Qaryah, with its stone cistern, on the southern bank a few miles east of Unayzah, and al-Askara north of the town. The geographer al-Asfahani called them Qaryata Ibn Amir, the two villages of Ibn Amir. Both stood beside the Basra pilgrim road, on which the Hajj caravans of Iraq and eastern Arabia made for Medina and Mecca. In 1444 no walled town guarded this stretch. The trains rested at its wells and cisterns, while Anazzah Bedouin pastured camels and horses over the open steppe between Qasim and the Hijaz foothills.

The wars of later years marched down that same road. In 1786 the army of Thuwaini al-Saadun of Basra followed it west to besiege Buraydah before falling back. Ibrahim Pasha came the other way in 1817, crossing these plains at Mawiyah on his march to Rass and Buraydah before turning south to take Diriyah the next year. With the Saudi state gone, Egyptian garrisons returned to the road, and the Anazzah grazed the steppe as before.
zh:
卡里亚坦在阿拉伯语中意为「双村」，得名于鲁迈干河畔的两处古老聚落：卡里亚在河南岸、欧奈宰以东几英里，村中留有石砌蓄水池；阿斯凯拉在欧奈宰以北。地理学家伊斯法哈尼称它们为「伊本·阿米尔双村」。两村都在巴士拉朝觐道旁，伊拉克和阿拉伯东部的朝觐驼队经此前往麦地那和麦加。1444年，这一路段没有设防城镇把守，驼队在井泉和蓄水池边歇脚，安宰部落的贝都因人则在卡西姆与汉志山麓之间的开阔草原上放牧驼马。

后来的战争也走这条大路。1786年，巴士拉的苏韦尼·萨阿敦率部沿此路西进，围攻布赖代不克而退。1817年，易卜拉欣帕夏反向而来，取道穆维叶穿过这片原野，连克拉斯拉斯和布赖代，再于次年南下攻克德拉伊耶。沙特国家败亡后，埃及驻军重新驻守这条道路，安宰人仍在草原上放牧。

en:
Sudair is the chain of palm-and-wheat valleys cut into the northern flank of the Tuwaiq escarpment, a little over a hundred miles north of Riyadh. Medieval geographers knew its main watercourse as Wadi al-Faqi and peopled it with clans of the Banu Tamim. Awdat Sudair was settled as early as the first Islamic century, and in the tenth century al-Hamdani wrote of al-Hait, a market town later identified with Hautat Sudair, and of Rawdat Sudair as a palm oasis held by a fortress. In 1417 al-Majma'ah was founded on the heights commanding the valley's eastern approaches. In 1444 Sudair was a string of self-governing farming villages, Hautat Sudair among their busiest markets; wells and stone flood-dams watered fields of dates, wheat and barley, while Bedouin tribes held the desert beyond.

The seventeenth century produced Rumaizan bin Ghashsham, the poet-ruler of Rawdat Sudair. He sought the favour of Sharif Zayd ibn Muhsin of Mecca against local rivals and built the al-Sab'in dam, a stone wall holding the wadi's floodwater for his town's fields while the surplus ran on downstream. The House of Saud entered Sudair between 1757 and 1774 as much by letters as by arms. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab debated with its scholars, and Abdullah al-Muways long opposed him; only in 1774 did every town accept Diriyah's rule. In 1782 the Al Madi of Rawdat Sudair called in Sa'dun ibn Uray'ir of the Banu Khalid and retook their town, until Saud bin Abdulaziz recovered it and expelled them; a Saudi emir for Sudair then sat at Jalajil or al-Majma'ah. When Ibrahim Pasha invaded in 1818, Shaqra fell in the first weeks of the year and Rashwan Agha's cavalry swept through Jalajil carrying off horses and wheat. The Sudair towns submitted before Diriyah surrendered that September, and the old local families kept their place under Egyptian guns.
zh:
苏代尔是图韦格崖北缘一线种枣植麦的河谷，在利雅得以北一百多英里。中古地理学家称其主河谷为法基河谷，居民多属贝尼塔米姆的各支派；阿沃代早在伊斯兰历第一个世纪就有人定居，10世纪的哈姆达尼提到一座设有市集的城镇海里特，后世地方志把它比定为豪泰，又把守有堡垒的椰枣绿洲称作劳代。1417年，迈季迈阿在扼守河谷东口的高地上建城。1444年的苏代尔是一串各自为政的农耕村落，豪泰是其中最热闹的市集之一；水井和石砌拦洪坝浇灌着椰枣、小麦和大麦，四周沙漠则在贝都因部落手中。

17世纪，劳代出了一位诗人埃米尔鲁迈赞·本·甘沙姆。他与麦加谢里夫扎伊德·本·穆赫辛结交，以对付本地争雄的对手，又主持修建萨比因坝，这道石坝把河谷洪水蓄下来浇灌本镇农田，多余的水放往下游。1757至1774年间，沙特家族进入苏代尔，书信论战与用兵并行：穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜勒·瓦哈卜与当地学者辩论，阿卜杜拉·穆韦斯长期反对，直到1774年所有城镇才接受德拉伊耶的统治。1782年，劳代的马迪家族请来贝尼哈立德的萨阿敦·本·欧赖伊尔夺回本镇，沙特·本·阿卜杜勒阿齐兹随即将其收复、逐走马迪家族，此后苏代尔的沙特埃米尔驻在吉拉吉勒或迈季迈阿。1818年易卜拉欣帕夏入侵，年初舍格拉陷落，鲁什万阿加的骑兵横扫吉拉吉勒，掠走马匹和小麦；同年9月德拉伊耶投降之前，苏代尔各镇已先后归附，旧的地方望族在埃及人的枪炮下保住了地位。

en:
Al-Yamamah is the Kharj oasis, a belt of springs and palm groves southeast of Riyadh on the southern fringe of the old Yamama farmlands. The wider Yamama was once the grain country of central Arabia: Arab geographers describe its dates, wheat and meat feeding Mecca, its settled Banu Hanifa farmers, and fortresses set among silver and gold mines. It holds one of the best-remembered battlefields of early Islam, where in December 632 Khalid ibn al-Walid crushed the followers of Musaylima, the self-proclaimed prophet of the Banu Hanifa; Musaylima and most of his men died making a last stand in a walled garden called the Garden of Death. By the fifteenth century that old settled country had shrunk to pockets along the Tuwaiq. In 1444 the fortified villages of al-Yamama and Dalam guarded the wells and tracks between Najd and al-Hasa, and the Sunni villagers and herdsmen followed local Arab chiefs.

In 1581 Sharif Hasan ibn Abi Numayy of Mecca marched east, seized Kharj, Sulaymiyya and al-Yamama, installed his own chiefs in their forts and rode back west. Saudi raids out of Diriyah reached Dalam from the middle of the century, and the Kharj towns threw off Saudi allegiance more than once. Their leading chief, Zayd ibn Zamil al-Dilami, was killed fighting in 1784, and in 1785 Saud ibn Abdulaziz stormed Dalam and brought all the oasis towns into the Saudi reform state. They kept that tie until 1818, when Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian army destroyed Diriyah and broke Saudi rule over Najd.
zh:
亚玛玛以海尔季（Kharj）绿洲为中心，这片泉水与椰枣林连成的绿洲在利雅得东南，地处古叶麻麦农区的南缘。叶麻麦曾是阿拉伯半岛中部的粮仓：阿拉伯地理学家记载，这里的椰枣、小麦和肉食供应麦加，定居的巴努·哈尼法人耕作其间，堡垒之间还分布着金银矿。这里也有早期伊斯兰教最知名的战场之一：632年12月，哈立德·本·瓦利德在此击溃巴努·哈尼法自称先知者穆赛利迈的追随者，穆赛利迈率众退守一座有围墙的园圃，与部下大多战死，那座园圃后来被称为死亡园圃。到15世纪，旧日的定居区已收缩为图韦克山沿线的若干片绿洲。1444年时，亚玛玛、德莱姆等设防村落守着水井和内志通往哈萨的道路，逊尼派村民与牧民听从本地阿拉伯酋长。

1581年，麦加谢里夫哈桑·本·艾比·努迈伊东征，夺取海尔季、苏莱米耶和亚玛玛，在堡垒中安插自己的首领后西返。从18世纪中叶起，德拉伊耶沙特人的袭扰抵达德莱姆，海尔季各镇又不止一次摆脱沙特的控制。各镇的首领扎伊德·本·扎米勒·迪勒米于1784年战死，1785年沙特·本·阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹攻克德莱姆，把绿洲各镇全部带入沙特改革派政权。它们与德拉伊耶的联系维持到1818年，易卜拉欣帕夏的埃及军队在这一年摧毁德拉伊耶，瓦解了沙特人在内志的统治。

en:
Taif stands on a high, mountain-girt plateau seventy-five kilometres east of Mecca, around the Wadi Wajj. Its cool air and springs made it the 'Garden of the Hejaz': wheat fields, vineyards and orchards of grapes, pomegranates and peaches ringed the walled town, and medieval Arab writers reported that most of the fresh fruit eaten in Mecca came from here, along with wool, ghee and livestock from the tribes of its outskirts. Its people are the Thaqif, who raised the great wall that encircled the town and gave it its name, Taif, and guarded the temple of the goddess al-Lat, 'the lady of Taif'. After Muhammad's victory at Hunayn in 630 the town beat off a Muslim siege, but in 631 the Thaqif submitted and the idol was broken. Arab geographers noted that whenever the rulers of Mecca could no longer bear the heat they Withdrew to Taif, and in 1444 it serves as the summer seat of the Hashemite sharifs under Mamluk suzerainty.

On 17 July 1517 the Sharif of Mecca surrendered the keys of the two holy cities to Sultan Selim I, and Taif passed under Ottoman rule with the rest of the Hejaz. In 1802 the Wahhabi commander Uthman al-Mudhayfi, fresh from routing Sharif Ghalib's army, besieged the hill town; Ghalib slipped away to Mecca and the Saudis entered, leaving much of Taif in ruins. Muhammad Ali Pasha's Egyptian army recovered it in 1813. The Swiss traveller Burckhardt came the same year and left an eyewitness record. Three gates and several towers stood on walls that were in places only eighteen inches thick; Uthman had built the wall and ditch, and Sharif Ghalib the castle. Many houses were still in ruin, including the badly damaged tomb of Abdallah ibn Abbas, the Prophet's cousin and ancestor of the Abbasids, while the survivors, still mostly Thaqif, lived by the coffee caravans running between Yemen and Mecca. In early 1814 Abidin Bey's beaten column was besieged in Taif until a relieving army broke through.
zh:
塔伊夫位于麦加以东七十五公里、群山环抱的高原上，城跨瓦季干河。凉爽的气候和泉眼为它赢得「汉志花园」之名：城墙外是麦田、葡萄园和出产葡萄、石榴、桃子的果园，中世纪的阿拉伯作家记载，麦加人吃的鲜果大多产于此地，城郊部落还供应羊毛、酥油和牲畜。居民是塞基夫人，他们筑起绕城的高墙，城名「塔伊夫」便来自「环绕」之意，城中还守护着女神拉特的神庙，拉特号称「塔伊夫之女主」。630年穆罕默德在侯乃尼之战取胜后围攻塔伊夫不克，631年塞基夫人归顺，神像被捣毁。阿拉伯地理学家记下旧例：麦加的统治者受不住酷暑便移驾塔伊夫；1444年的塔伊夫正是马穆鲁克宗主权下哈希姆谢里夫家族的避暑之地。

1517年7月17日，麦加谢里夫把两圣城的钥匙交给素丹塞利姆一世，塔伊夫随整个汉志归入奥斯曼统治。1802年，瓦哈比将领奥斯曼·穆宰菲在击溃谢里夫加里卜的军队后进围这座山城，加里卜脱身逃往麦加，沙特人入城，塔伊夫大半化为废墟。穆罕默德·阿里帕夏的埃及军队1813年收复塔伊夫。同年瑞士旅行家布尔克哈特到此，留下亲历记录：城墙设三座城门和若干塔楼，有些地方仅四十五厘米厚；城墙与壕沟为奥斯曼·穆宰菲所修，城堡则为谢里夫加里卜所建；许多房屋仍是废墟，其中包括先知堂弟、阿拔斯家族先祖阿卜杜拉·伊本·阿拔斯严重受损的陵墓；幸存居民仍以塞基夫人为主，靠也门至麦加的咖啡驼队为生。1814年初，阿比丁·贝伊败退的部队被困在塔伊夫，直到援军前来解围。

en:
Al Qunfudhah is a Red Sea roadstead on the Tihama coast, more than three hundred kilometres south of Jeddah, founded in 1311 where the old coastal caravan road between Yemen and Syria runs into the sea. Its harbour took in large ships with the incense, spices and coffee of Yemen and India, and pilgrims from southern Arabia, India and Southeast Asia boarded here for Jeddah on the way to Mecca; caravans striking inland from the quayside made the town a market and storehouse for the lowlands south of the holy city. In 1444 the port belongs to the loose Hejaz realm of the Sharif of Mecca under Mamluk protection, living off the pilgrim road and marking the southern edge of the Sharifate.

After 1517 al-Qunfudhah followed the Sharif into the Ottoman order and became the forward base for Ottoman and Sharifian expeditions against the tribes of Asir to the south. In 1803 an Asiri force in Saudi pay under Amir Abd al-Wahhab besieged and took the town, the first battle in the First Saudi state's conquest of the Hejaz. In March 1814 an Egyptian expedition of forty ships seized the harbour, but held it for only eight days. Tami bin Shu'ayb, the Saudi amir of Asir, came back with 8,000 men, cut the wells three hours' march from the walls and stormed the camp; the garrison was driven into the sea and the survivors got away to Jeddah. Muhammad Ali Pasha retook the port after his victory at Busal in 1815. Bakhroush bin Alass, the defiant Zahran sheikh, was captured and put to death at Qunfudhah, while Tami was sent on to Cairo and Istanbul and executed there.
zh:
贡费宰是提哈马海岸上的红海港湾，在吉达以南三百多公里，1311年兴起于也门与叙利亚之间古老沿海商路的入海处。港口可供大船停泊，运来也门和印度的熏香、香料与咖啡；阿拉伯半岛南部、印度和东南亚的朝觐者在此登船，经吉达前往麦加。驼队从码头出发深入内陆，使这座城镇成为圣城以南低地的市场与补给地。1444年的贡费宰属于马穆鲁克保护下麦加谢里夫松散的汉志领地，靠朝觐商路为生，也是谢里夫领地的南界。

1517年后，贡费宰随麦加谢里夫进入奥斯曼秩序，成为奥斯曼和谢里夫向南征讨阿西尔部落的前进基地。1803年，效力沙特的阿西尔军队在埃米尔阿卜杜勒·瓦哈卜率领下围城攻克贡费宰，这是第一沙特国征服汉志的第一战。1814年3月，一支四十艘船的埃及远征军夺取港口，却只占据了八天：沙特任命的阿西尔埃米尔塔米·本·舒艾卜率八千人回师，切断距城墙三小时路程的水井后猛攻营地，守军被赶入大海，残部逃回吉达。1815年穆罕默德·阿里帕夏在拜苏勒取胜后重占此港；桀骜的扎赫拉尼部落谢赫巴赫鲁什被俘后在贡费宰处死，塔米则被押往开罗和伊斯坦布尔，最终在那里被处决。

en:
Zabid stands on the Tihama, the hot coastal plain between the Red Sea and the Yemeni highlands, astride the caravan road that joined Mecca with Aden. Around 820 the Abbasid emir Muhammad ibn Ziyad laid it out beside the old village of al-Husayb and made it his capital. Two mosques made its name, the Great Mosque and the al-Asha'ir, which tradition traces to the Prophet's companion Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and counts as the fifth mosque built in Islam; students came to Zabid for Qur'anic and legal learning. Under the Sunni Rasulid sultans it was the coastal capital and winter seat even after their summer court moved to Taiz. The fourteenth-century writer al-Khazraji counted 230 to 240 mosques there, al-Firuzabadi composed his great dictionary al-Qamus in its schools, and Red Sea customs dues filled the treasury. In 1444 the last Rasulid, al-Mas'ud Abu al-Qasim, still held the city, but his slave soldiers had rebelled and the Tahir clan was swallowing his kingdom — Lahij fell in 1443.

The Tahirids took Aden in 1454 and the last Rasulid withdrew to Mecca; Zabid stayed the winter seat and gained new madrasas, while its trade slipped to Hodeidah and the coffee port of Mocha. In 1516–17 a Mamluk army from Egypt, armed with muskets and cannon, killed the Tahirid sultan az-Zafir Amir II and garrisoned Zabid, which passed to the Ottomans with Egypt itself; from 1539 it was the headquarters of the Yemen Eyalet. The Zaydi imams of the highlands wore the Turks down: after al-Mutahhar's revolt in 1567 Zabid was for a time the only Ottoman-held town in Yemen, and the war al-Mansur al-Qasim began in 1597 took Sanaa in 1628 and Zabid in 1634. Coffee now went out through Mocha, whose caravans bought beans at Bayt al-Faqih, and the old learned city shrank into a country town. Wahhabi raiders held the Tihama ports after 1803 until the imam's men retook them in 1818. In 1821 Zabid was a quiet country town under the Qasimid imams.
zh:
扎比德位于帖哈麦——红海与也门高地之间炎热的沿海平原，扼守连接麦加和亚丁的商道。约820年，阿拔斯王朝埃米尔穆罕默德·伊本·齐亚德在古村侯赛卜旁营建此城，定为都城。两座清真寺成就了它的声名：聚礼清真寺和阿沙伊尔清真寺，相传后者为先知门弟子艾布·穆萨·艾什尔里所建，是伊斯兰教史上第五座清真寺；各地学生来扎比德学习古兰经和教法。逊尼派拉苏尔王朝的苏丹们把夏季王廷迁往塔伊兹，仍以这里为沿海都城和冬都。14世纪作家海兹拉吉清点城中有230至240座清真寺，辞书学家菲鲁扎巴迪在城中的学塾编成巨著《辞洋》，红海商路的关税也填满了苏丹的府库。1444年，末代拉苏尔苏丹麦斯欧德·阿布·卡西姆仍据有该城，但他的奴隶士兵已经叛乱，塔希尔家族正蚕食他的国土，拉赫季于1443年陷落。

1454年，塔希尔家族攻下亚丁，末代拉苏尔苏丹退往麦加；扎比德仍为冬都，城中新建了不少经学院，贸易却渐渐流向荷台达和咖啡港穆哈。1516至1517年，一支埃及马穆鲁克军队带着火枪和火炮攻入也门，杀死塔希尔苏丹扎菲尔·埃米尔二世，在扎比德驻军；埃及本土陷落后，这支驻军随之归于奥斯曼。1539年起，扎比德成为奥斯曼也门行省的治所。高地的宰德派伊玛目一步步拖垮土耳其人：1567年穆塔希尔起事后，扎比德一度是土耳其人在也门唯一据守的城市；曼苏尔·卡西姆1597年开启的战争，于1628年夺取萨那、1634年夺取扎比德。也门咖啡改从穆哈出海，驼队在拜特法基赫等市集收购咖啡豆，这座学术老城缩成一座乡间市镇。1803年后瓦哈比骑兵占据帖哈麦各港，直到1818年伊玛目的军队将其收复。1821年的扎比德，是卡西姆伊玛目治下一座宁静的乡间城镇。

en:
Taiz climbs the southern slopes below Mount Sabir, more than 1,400 metres up on the road between the Yemeni highlands and the Red Sea plain and the port of Mokha. The first Qahira Castle was built under the Sulayhids in the first half of the twelfth century, and Turan-Shah, Saladin's elder brother, raised the hill citadel after his conquest of Yemen in 1173 and made Taiz the capital of Yemen in 1175. The Rasulids kept it their capital after Sultan al-Muzaffar moved the court from Sanaa in 1288, drawn by the city's nearness to Aden, and their sultans built palaces, madrasas and mosques among the orchards below the fortress. Taiz became a centre of Shafi'i learning, and Ibn Battuta, visiting in 1332, found three quarters spread below the citadel: the court quarter, the garrison town of 'Udayna, and al-Mahalib with its principal market. In 1397 Sultan al-Ashraf Ismail built the Ashrafiyya as mosque, madrasa, Sufi lodge and Rasulid burial place. In 1444, with the Rasulid state failing, Taiz remained its political centre among the gardens on the roads to Aden and Zabid.

By the late fifteenth century Yemeni Sufis drank coffee to stay awake for night prayer, and the mufti of Aden, Jamal al-Din, adopted the drink around 1454; coffee bushes spread across the western highland terraces, and caravans carried the beans down to Mokha. Taiz changed masters with the rest of Lower Yemen: the Tahirids inherited Rasulid rule in 1454, Zaydi forces took the city in 1517, and Ottoman troops secured it in 1547. When al-Mutahhar rebelled, Osman Pasha besieged Qahira Castle in 1569 without taking it, and Sinan Pasha later recovered the city for the empire. Imam al-Mansur al-Qasim opened the Qasimid revolt in 1597, and the Ottomans left Yemen by 1638. Under the Qasimid imams, Mokha reached the height of its coffee trade in the first quarter of the eighteenth century, with English, Dutch and French factories and thousands of Banyan merchants buying the beans the caravans brought down from the hills.
zh:
塔伊兹位于萨比尔山南坡，海拔一千四百多米，地处也门高原通往红海平原和摩卡港的道路上。开罗城堡始建于12世纪上半叶的苏莱赫王朝；1173年，萨拉丁之兄图兰沙阿征服也门后在山顶修筑要塞，并于1175年把塔伊兹定为也门都城。拉苏勒王朝继续在此建都：1288年，穆扎法尔苏丹看中这里靠近亚丁，把宫廷从萨那迁来。历代苏丹在要塞下方的果园间兴修宫殿、宗教学校和清真寺，塔伊兹成为沙斐仪派学术中心。伊本·白图泰1332年到访时，看到要塞下方分为三区：王城区、驻军的欧代纳，以及设有大市场的马哈利卜。1397年，苏丹阿什拉夫·伊斯玛仪修建阿什拉菲耶，兼具清真寺、宗教学校、苏菲道堂和拉苏勒王室墓地之用。1444年，拉苏勒国家虽已衰弱，塔伊兹仍是其政治中心，坐落在通往亚丁和扎比德道路旁的园林之间。

15世纪末，也门的苏菲派已饮用咖啡，以便在夜祷时保持清醒；亚丁的穆夫提贾马勒丁约在1454年开始接受这种饮品，咖啡树随之在西部高原的梯田上推广，商队把咖啡豆运下高原送往摩卡。塔伊兹随下也门几经易手：1454年塔希尔家族接掌拉苏勒政权，1517年宰德派军队攻占该城，1547年奥斯曼军队将其控制。穆塔希尔反叛后，奥斯曼帕夏1569年围攻开罗城堡却未能破城，后来由锡南帕夏为帝国收复。伊玛目曼苏尔·卡西姆1597年发动卡西姆派起事，奥斯曼人到1638年全部撤离也门。卡西姆伊玛目治下，摩卡的咖啡贸易在18世纪头二十五年达到顶点，英国、荷兰和法国商馆并立，数千名巴尼亚商人收购商队从高原运下的咖啡豆。

en:
Dhamar spreads across the broad Jahran plain of the Yemeni highlands, about 2,400 metres up and a hundred kilometres south of Sanaa, where the road from the highland capital forks for Ibb, Taiz and Aden. The town is named after the Himyarite king Dhamar Ali Yahbur; bronze statues of the king and his son dug up at Nakhlat al-Hamra show that this well-watered plateau was royal country in the centuries before Islam, and its tribes were among the first in Yemen to accept the faith in the 630s. Unlike the walled towns of the mountains, Dhamar had no ramparts and trusted in its markets: its Wednesday market drew grain, sheep and the Arabian horses bred on the surrounding pastures, while the western hills produced onyx for jambiyyah hilts and a coffee prized as the al-Fadli variety. In 1444 it was the northern market town of the Rasulid sultans who ruled from Taiz, facing the Zaydi imams of the Sanaa highlands.

The Tahirids took the Rasulid lands in 1454, and eight years later the defeated Zaydi claimant al-Mansur an-Nasir was seized by tribesmen east of Dhamar and handed to his rival. The Zaydi imam al-Mutawakkil Yahya Sharaf ad-Din, who had ruled from Sanaa since 1506, built the Shamsiyya madrasa in the city in 1541–1543, for centuries one of the chief schools of Zaydi learning. Ottoman troops under Özdemir Pasha took Sanaa in 1547, and Dhamar became a centre of the risings against them in 1567 and 1597. The Qasimid imams fought on from the western mountains and drove the Ottomans out of Yemen between 1628 and the 1630s; west of the city, at Dawran, the Qasimid imam al-Mutawakkil Ismail later kept his capital, walling the mountain to its summit and ringing it with stone towers and a great mosque. In the eighteenth century Dhamar sank with the Qasimid state as its tribes slipped from the imams' control.
zh:
扎玛尔铺展在也门高地开阔的贾赫兰平原上，海拔约2400米，北距萨那一百公里，萨那通往伊卜、塔伊兹和亚丁的大路在此分岔。城名来自希木叶尔国王扎玛尔·阿里·叶哈布尔；奈赫拉哈姆拉出土的国王父子铜像表明，这片水草丰足的高原在伊斯兰时代之前就是王家之地，7世纪30年代当地部落又是也门最早接受伊斯兰教的人群之一。和山区的设防城镇不同，扎玛尔没有城墙，凭市集立足：周三市集汇集粮食、牲畜和周围牧场繁育的阿拉伯马，西部山地还出产能做詹比亚弯刀柄的玛瑙，以及称作法迪里的优质咖啡。1444年，它是塔伊兹的拉苏里素丹治下最靠北的集镇，与萨那高原的扎伊迪派伊玛目对峙。

1454年塔希尔王朝接管拉苏里的领地；八年后，败逃的扎伊迪派候选人曼苏尔·纳赛尔在扎玛尔以东被部落人擒获，送交其对手。自1506年起以萨那为治所的扎伊迪派伊玛目穆泰瓦基勒·叶海亚·谢拉夫丁，于1541至1543年在城中修建沙姆西耶学校，此后数百年间它一直是扎伊迪派的主要学府之一。1547年厄兹代米尔帕夏率奥斯曼军攻占萨那，扎玛尔又在1567年和1597年两度成为起义的中心。卡西姆家族的伊玛目们在西部山区坚持作战，于1628年至1630年代把奥斯曼人逐出也门；城西的道兰后来成为卡西姆伊玛目穆泰瓦基勒·伊斯玛仪的都城，他下令沿山筑墙直至山顶，四周环以巨石塔楼，并在山上建起大清真寺。18世纪，随着各部落脱离伊玛目的控制，扎玛尔与卡西姆国家一同衰败。

en:
Saada is a walled mountain town in a high basin of the Sarawat, about 1,800 metres up in northern Yemen, where caravan roads from Sanaa run on toward the Hejaz and Najran. The tribes of the basin invited the Hasanid theologian Yahya ibn al-Husayn up from Medina in 897 to settle their feuds; he founded the city as al-Hadi ila'l-Haqq and built its Friday mosque, the oldest Shia mosque in Arabia, and his tomb became a place of Zaydi pilgrimage. His Rassid line, and later its Qasimid branch, gave Yemen its Zaydi imams down the centuries. When the imam died of plague in 1436 the highlands split between rival claimants, and in 1444 al-Mansur an-Nasir held Saada as one of them, while the Sunni Rasulid sultans of the coast were losing their grip on the lowlands. The town's tanneries and markets supplied the caravans, and the mountain basin kept its Zaydi learning and its tribal arms.

The Ottomans took the Yemeni lowlands in 1538 and garrisoned Sanaa, but al-Mansur al-Qasim raised the highlands against them in 1597; his son al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad drove the last Turkish troops out of Yemen by 1636. The Qasimids then ruled the strongest Yemeni state for a century, their treasury fed by dues on coffee shipped from Mocha while Yemeni coffee spread through the Ottoman lands and on to Europe. In the eighteenth century succession quarrels and tribal revolts broke the imams' hold, and by 1821 Saada was again governed by its own clans, too strong in its mountains for Sanaa to command.
zh:
萨达是塞拉特山脉中一座带城墙的山城，坐落在也门北部海拔约1800米的高山盆地里，萨那通往汉志和奈季兰的商路经过这里。897年，盆地诸部落把哈桑家族的神学家叶海亚·本·侯赛因从麦地那请来调停仇杀；他建城称伊玛目，号「导于真者」哈迪，又修建聚礼清真寺，这是阿拉伯半岛最古老的什叶派清真寺，他的陵墓后来成为扎伊迪派的朝谒之地。他的拉西家族及后来的卡西姆支系，在此后数百年里世世代代出任也门的扎伊迪伊玛目。1436年伊玛目死于瘟疫，高地在几位竞争者之间分裂；1444年，曼苏尔·纳绥尔据萨达自立，是竞争者之一，沿海的逊尼派拉苏勒苏丹则已掌控不住低地。城内的制革作坊和市集供应往来商队，高山盆地保存着扎伊迪学问和部落武力。

奥斯曼人1538年占领也门低地并在萨那驻军，曼苏尔·卡西姆却于1597年在高地举事；其子穆艾亚德·穆罕默德到1636年把最后一支土耳其军队赶出也门。卡西姆王朝随后统治了一个世纪也门最强盛的国家，国库靠穆哈港咖啡出口的关税充实，也门咖啡也经奥斯曼各地传到欧洲。18世纪，继承纷争和部落叛乱瓦解了伊玛目的控制；到1821年，萨达又由各氏族自行治理，凭山地之险，萨那难以驾驭。

en:
Al-Shihr is the old port of Hadhramaut, a walled town on a sandy beach cut in two by the al-Misyal wadi, facing an open roadstead with no docks, where boats took cargo out to the ships. It stood at the seaward end of the incense road: frankincense from inland wadis, fish oil and the ambergris called ʿanbar Shiḥrī sailed to India and China, and geographers called its coast the bilad al-kundur, the Land of Incense. Upstream kilns at Yadhghat sent pottery out through it. From 980 it shared the coast with Sharma, founded by Persian exiles a day's sail away. In 1432 the Mahri Ba Dujana clan took it from the Rasulids of Yemen, beat back their counterattack, and in 1445 repelled the new Kathiri sultanate inland. In 1444 it was therefore an independent Mahri port, whose Sunni Arab merchants and sailors lived by frankincense and the carrying trade of the Arabian Sea.

The fight for the roadstead ran on for two centuries. In 1456 Sultan Muhammad bin Sa'd sailed against Aden with nine ships, was wrecked and captured by the Tahirids, who then marched overland and sacked the town. Sa'd bin Faris restored Ba Dujana rule in 1478, and ten years later the Mahris and their Socotran allies threw a Kathiri garrison out of Shihr. In 1495, during a Mahri civil war, the Kathiri sultan Jafar bin Amr won the battle of Tabala and made Shihr his seaport. Portuguese fleets raided in 1523, 1532 and 1533; in 1530 Ottoman officers left cannons and gunners, who helped drive off a squadron, but on 7 April 1548 Portuguese siege guns breached the fort and the Kathiri garrison was killed to a man, handing the town to Sa'd bin Afrar of Mahra. Shore graves are said to hold men killed in those attacks. Shihr later reverted to the Kathiri sultans and remained the outlet of inland Hadhramaut, its boats carrying merchants and emigrants to East Africa and India; Hadhrami settlers there were called Shihiris, after the port they sailed from. Carsten Niebuhr visited in the eighteenth century, and in 1821 Shihr remained a Kathiri town of frankincense and fish.
zh:
希赫尔是哈德拉毛的古港，这座有城墙的城镇坐落在沙滩岸上，被米斯亚勒旱谷一分为二，只有开阔的锚地、没有码头，货物全靠小船驳运出海。它地处乳香之路的出海一端：内陆干谷出产的乳香、鱼油和名为「希赫尔龙涎香」的龙涎香运往印度和中国，地理学家把这一带海岸称作「乳香之地」，上游亚德加特窑场的陶器也从这里外销。980年起，它与波斯流亡者在一天航程外所建的港口沙尔马并存。1432年，马赫里人的巴杜贾纳家族从也门的拉苏勒王朝手中夺取希赫尔，击退其反攻，又在1445年挡住内陆新生卡西里苏丹国的进攻。1444年，希赫尔是一个独立的马赫里港口，逊尼派阿拉伯商人和水手靠乳香与阿拉伯海的转运贸易为生。

争夺锚地的战争又持续了两个世纪。1456年，苏丹穆罕默德·本·萨德率九艘战船远征亚丁，舰队在风暴中覆没，他本人被塔希尔王朝俘获，塔希尔大军随即沿陆地而来，洗劫了希赫尔。1478年，萨德·本·法里斯恢复巴杜贾纳家族的统治；十年后，马赫里人联合索科特拉盟友把卡西里驻军赶出城去。1495年马赫里内战期间，卡西里苏丹贾法尔·本·阿慕尔赢得塔巴拉之战，把希赫尔变成自己的出海口。葡萄牙舰队又在1523、1532和1533年来袭；1530年，奥斯曼军官给苏丹留下火炮和炮手，帮助击退一支分舰队，但1548年4月7日，葡萄牙人的攻城炮轰破要塞，卡西里守军尽数被杀，城池交给马赫拉的萨德·本·阿夫拉尔。相传沿岸的坟墓里就葬着这些葡萄牙人攻势中的死者。希赫尔后来重归卡西里苏丹，继续充当哈德拉毛内陆的出海口，船只载着商民和移民驶往东非和印度，定居非洲海岸的哈德拉毛人因从这个港口出海而被称为希赫里人。18世纪丹麦旅行家卡斯滕·尼布尔曾到访此地，到1821年，它仍是一座靠乳香和鱼产过活的卡西里城镇。

en:
Al Ghaydah is an Arabian Sea roadstead on the eastern Mahra coast, between Qishn and the Dhofar frontier. The shore is dry desert cut by coastal wadis, though the summer monsoon reaches it, and belongs to Mahri fishermen, herdsmen and frankincense traders, whose tongue, Mahri, is a surviving South Arabian language older than Arabic. In the Al Kida quarter stands the mud-built Al-Hasni mosque, put up by Abdallah ibn Muhammad al-Hasni in 730-731. In 1444 the highland dynasties of Yemen held little direct power here. The Mahri ports obeyed their own seafaring clans, the strongest of whom took Shihr from the Rasulids in 1432 and held it against them and the new Kathiri state. Al Ghaydah itself lived by fish, livestock and the coastal carrying trade.

The wider Mahra shore stayed under its own sultans, the Banu Afrar of Qishn, who also held Socotra, while the eastern ports grew slowly. In 1777-1778 the old Al-Hasni mosque received its first recorded renewal, one of the few dates in the life of a town otherwise kept going by fish, herds and coastal traffic.
zh:
盖达是迈赫拉东部海岸濒临阿拉伯海的锚地，处在基什恩与佐法尔边地之间。沿岸是干河切割的干旱荒漠，夏季季风仍能吹到；居民是说迈赫拉语的渔民、牧人和乳香商人，迈赫拉语是早于阿拉伯语的南阿拉伯语言。城中阿勒·基达街区的哈斯尼清真寺由阿卜杜拉·伊本·穆罕默德·哈斯尼以泥土建于730至731年，寺以他得名。1444年，也门高原诸王朝对这里几乎没有直接统治：迈赫拉各港听命于本土航海部族，其中最强的一支1432年从拉苏里王朝手中夺取希赫尔，随后顶住了他们和新兴卡西里国的争夺。盖达本镇靠渔业、畜牧和沿海转运为生。

迈赫拉长岸此后数百年由本土苏丹统治，即领有索科特拉岛的基什恩巴努·阿夫拉尔家族，东部各港发展缓慢。1777至1778年，古老的哈斯尼清真寺完成有记载的首次重修；对这座靠渔场、牧群和沿海往来维持的城镇，这是少数有确切年份的大事。

en:
Baraimi is the desert-edge oasis country of Al Dhahirah, running from the Buraimi oasis to the market town of Ibri. The oasis was known in older times as Tawam, nine villages set among the palms, where wells and aflaj channels watered gardens, date groves and livestock pasture. Traders gathered at Buraimi and beside Ibri's old market before taking the inland roads toward the Omani coast, and the wells made the oases a resting place between inner Arabia and the seaward side of the Hajar. In 1444 the district lay within the domains of the Nabhani kings.

Two forts guarded the roads in the Ya'rubi century. Ibri Fort, beside the old market and attributed to the Nabahna, was completed by Sheikh Khater bin Amer bin Rashid Al-Yaqoubi. In 1718 Imam Sultan bin Saif Al-Yarubi raised Al-Sulaif Fort above Wadi Al-Salif, its seven towers set on the eastern road into Ibri.
zh:
布赖米是扎希拉地区沙漠边缘的绿洲地带，范围从布赖米绿洲延伸到集镇伊卜里。这片绿洲旧称图瓦姆，由椰枣林间的九座村庄组成；水井和法拉吉沟渠滋养菜园、椰枣林和牧场。商人在布赖米和伊卜里老市场旁聚齐，再沿内陆道路前往阿曼海岸，水井也使这些绿洲成为阿拉伯内陆与哈贾尔山靠海一侧之间的歇脚地。1444年，这一地区处在纳卜汉诸王的领地内。

叶阿里卜时代，两座堡垒看守着这里的道路。老市场旁的伊卜里堡传由纳卜汉人始建，由谢赫哈提尔·本·阿米尔·本·拉希德·雅各比建成。1718年，伊玛目苏丹·本·赛义夫·叶阿里卜在苏莱夫干谷上方筑起苏莱夫堡，七座塔楼设在通往伊卜里的东路上。

en:
Ash Sharqiyah is Oman's eastern shore on the Gulf of Oman, looking toward India and East Africa, with the walled city of Qalhat and the smaller roadstead of Sur.
