Qalhat became the second city of the Kingdom of Hormuz and one of the busiest emporia on the Indian Ocean; its merchants shipped horses, dates, incense, pearls and spices to East Africa, India and China. The mamluk commander Baha al-Din Ayaz seized the throne of Hormuz and governed from Qalhat, and after his death about 1312 his widow Bibi Maryam ruled both Qalhat and Hormuz. She built the congregational mosque that Ibn Battuta praised for its fine bazaars and qashani-tiled walls, and her domed tomb stood at the edge of the city. Marco Polo knew the port as Calatu, and Zheng He's Ming fleets marked it on their sailing charts. Sur was already an old roadstead for the East Africa run, settled in that trade since the sixth century. By 1444 Muscat was overtaking Qalhat, but the old city remained Hormuz's anchor on its Arabian shore.

Earthquakes shook Qalhat in the 1490s, and the Portuguese under Afonso de Albuquerque sacked it in 1508, burning the Great Mosque and the principal houses while Bibi Maryam's mausoleum was left standing. Another earthquake late in the sixteenth century turned the old city into ruins, and Muscat and Sur carried the coasting trade instead. After Nasir bin Murshid founded the Yarubid imamate in 1624, Omani forces drove the Portuguese out of Sur; its yards then grew known for the wooden sambuk and ghanjah dhows that sailed to India, Zanzibar and as far as China and worked the pearl banks. The coast passed to the Al Bu Said dynasty with Ahmad bin Said's election in 1744, and the court moved to Muscat in 1783. In 1821 Sur's shipyards were still at work, while Qalhat was a field of ruins above the shore.
zh:
东部区在阿曼东岸，濒临阿曼湾，与印度和东非隔海相望；岸上有城墙环绕的盖勒哈特和较小的苏尔锚地。盖勒哈特是忽里模子王国的第二都城，也是印度洋上最繁忙的商港之一，商人把马匹、椰枣、乳香、珍珠和香料运往东非、印度和中国。马木鲁克将领巴哈丁·阿亚兹夺取忽里模子王位后驻在盖勒哈特；约1312年他死后，王妃比比·玛丽亚姆同时掌管盖勒哈特和忽里模子。她修建的聚礼清真寺获伊本·白图泰称道，说巴扎齐整、寺壁满铺瓷砖；她的穹顶陵墓立在城边。《马可·波罗行纪》所述的加剌秃就是此港，郑和船队的《郑和航海图》则标作加剌哈。苏尔早自6世纪就是经营东非航路的老锚地。1444年，马斯喀特虽已开始盖过盖勒哈特，这座旧城仍是忽里模子在阿拉伯海岸的依托。

15世纪90年代，几场地震动摇了盖勒哈特。1508年，阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克麾下的葡萄牙人趁灾后重建攻陷并洗劫全城，焚毁大清真寺和主要宅第，只有比比·玛丽亚姆的陵墓留存。16世纪末又一场地震后，古城沦为废墟，沿海贸易改由马斯喀特和苏尔承接。纳绥尔·本·穆尔希德1624年建立雅鲁卜伊玛目政权后，阿曼军队把葡萄牙人逐出苏尔；这里的船坞以建造桑布克（sambuk）和甘贾（ganjah）两种木帆船闻名，船只能远航印度、桑给巴尔乃至中国，并兼采珍珠。1744年艾哈迈德·本·赛义德被推举为伊玛目，海岸归入布·赛义德王朝，宫廷又于1783年迁往马斯喀特。1821年，苏尔的船坞仍在开工，盖勒哈特只剩海岸高处的一片废墟。

en:
Ibra is an old oasis town below the eastern flank of the Hajar, on the inland roads linking Muscat with the Sharqiyah country and the deep interior. Springs and aflaj channels feed its grain fields and date gardens, and its bazaars and mosques made it both a market for the surrounding tribes and a seat of religious learning; the town is old enough to predate Islam. Its two quarters, Al Alaya and Al Sifala, answered to the Maskari and Harthi tribal confederations. In 1444, when Ibra lay inside the loose domains of the Nabhani kings, its shaikhs and their alliances mattered more than any distant court.

After the Ya'rubi imams united Oman in 1624, Ibra kept its standing. Scholars taught religion and Arabic at the Jami al-Qanater in Al Sifala, and the walled merchant village of Al-Munaysfah ran its market behind towers and forts. The town was pulled into dynasty politics when Sultan bin Saif died in 1679: his son Bil'arab took the imamate as a hereditary title over the claims of his brother Saif bin Sultan. Saif ruled after 1692 and spent on aflaj and farming in the oases, but the death of another imam in 1718 set rival claimants and their tribal backers against one another, and Oman fell into years of civil war.
zh:
伊卜拉是哈贾尔山东麓的古老绿洲城镇，地处连接马斯喀特、东部地区与阿曼腹地的内陆道路上。泉水和法拉吉沟渠滋养粮田与椰枣园，集市和清真寺使它既是周边部落赶集的市场，也是宗教学问之地；这座城镇的历史早于伊斯兰教。阿莱耶、西法莱两个街区分别听命于马斯卡里和哈尔斯部落联盟。1444年伊卜拉虽处在纳卜汉诸王松散的领地内，真正管用的却是各部谢赫和他们之间的盟约，远方王廷反倒隔了一层。

1624年叶阿里卜伊玛目统一阿曼后，伊卜拉仍保持着自己的地位。学者在西法莱的盖纳提尔清真寺讲授宗教学问和阿拉伯语，穆奈济法筑墙的商村在塔楼和堡寨围护下经营市场。1679年苏丹·本·赛义夫去世，伊卜拉被卷进王朝政治：其子比勒阿拉布不顾兄弟赛义夫·本·苏丹的争位要求，把伊玛目权位变成世袭头衔。赛义夫1692年后掌权，在各绿洲兴修法拉吉、经营农业；1718年又一位伊玛目去世，对立继承人各自带着部落支持者开战，阿曼就此陷入多年内战。

en:
At al-Qurna the Tigris and Euphrates meet and run on together as the Shatt al-Arab. All around the confluence the land dissolves into the reed sea the Ottomans called Cezayir-i Arab, the Arab islands. Island villages of arched reed houses rose from the water; their people poled narrow canoes between rice fields and date palms, herded buffalo, and paid tax only to whoever could reach them. Local tradition at Qurna pointed to an ancient tree as the Tree of Knowledge and set the Garden of Eden in this stretch of marsh. In 1444 the waterways belonged to the Musha'sha', a confederation of Arab tribes forged by the Shia theologian Muhammad ibn Falah, who gave himself out as the earthly representative of Ali and the Mahdi. From 1436 he preached his millenarian creed among the border tribes; his warriors took Huwayzah in 1441 and made it their centre, and from the marshes they became the real masters of Basra, whose nominal princes did no more than reign.

Shah Ismail broke the Musha'sha' on his Iraqi campaign of 1508, after which they served as governors under Persian suzerainty; they revived in 1588 when Mubarak ibn Abd al-Muttalib made himself master of all Arabistan. On the lower river the Ottomans drew Basra to their side in the 1530s and tightened their hold ten years later, but the delta kept its own ways. Portuguese gunboats escorted shipping to the port for a generation and helped its pasha beat off a Persian attack in 1624, while the marsh chieftains answered neither to Baghdad nor to Istanbul until the Ottomans retook Basra in 1668. The city fell to the Safavids again around the turn of the eighteenth century and was soon recovered, and in 1775 Karim Khan Zand sat down before it for a four-year siege. Through every change of masters, grain, dates and the spices of India moved up these waters, and the reed villages of the Qurna marshes went on as before.
zh:
在古尔奈，底格里斯河与幼发拉底河汇合，此后合称阿拉伯河。汇流处四周，陆地化成芦苇的海洋，奥斯曼人称之为杰扎伊尔-阿拉伯，即「阿拉伯群岛」。一座座拱形芦苇屋组成的岛村浮在水上，居民撑着狭长小舟穿行于稻田与椰枣林之间，牧放水牛，谁的手伸得到这里，他们才向谁纳税。古尔奈当地的传说指着一棵古树称之为知善恶树，把伊甸园摆在这片沼泽之间。1444年，这些水道属于穆沙沙：一个由什叶派神学家穆罕默德·伊本·法拉赫凝聚起来的阿拉伯部落联盟，他自称是阿里和马赫迪在世间的代表。他从1436年起向边境诸部宣讲末世信条，部众1441年夺取胡韦扎并以之为中心，又从沼泽出发成为巴士拉真正的主人，城里名义上的埃米尔不过垂拱而已。

沙阿伊斯玛仪1508年远征伊拉克，击溃穆沙沙，此后他们作为波斯宗主权下的总督存续；1588年穆巴拉克·伊本·阿卜杜勒·穆塔利卜称雄整个阿拉伯斯坦，势力一度复兴。下游方向，奥斯曼人在1530年代把巴士拉拉到自己一边，十年后又收紧控制，但三角洲自有一套行事方式。葡萄牙炮舰为港口护航约三十年，1624年还帮助巴士拉帕夏击退波斯的进攻；沼泽酋长们既不听命于巴格达，也不听命于伊斯坦布尔，直到1668年奥斯曼再克巴士拉。18世纪初这座城又被萨法维夺走，奥斯曼人不久将其夺回；1775年，卡里姆汗·赞德兵临城下，围城四年。尽管统治者一再更换，谷物、椰枣和印度香料始终沿这些水道北上，古尔奈沼泽里的芦苇村落也一如既往。

en:
Shushtar stands where the Karun breaks through the last Zagros foothills into the Khuzestan plain, and the river gave the city both its walls and its trade. Shapur I is said to have set the Roman soldiers captured with the emperor Valerian in 260 to building the Band-e Kaisar, 'Caesar's dam', a five-hundred-metre weir and the first bridge-dam in Iran. Together with the Band-e Mizan and the Gargar canal it drove tunnels, water-wheels and mills cut into the rock, and the canals ringed the city with water and fed the orchard plain between them called Mianab; the riverbank Salasel Castle commanded the whole works. Sugar-cane was planted here as early as the third century. Under the caliphs Shushtar headed one of the seven kuwar of Khuzestan, and its looms were the most celebrated in the province: in 933 they were charged with the kiswah, the embroidered covering of the Kaaba, and the tiraz brocade and harir silk listed by the geographers were still recorded by Hafiz-i Abru around 1430. In 1444 it was the leading Persian-speaking city of eastern Khuzestan under its local lords, its wealth and walls coveted by the Arab Musha'sha, who marched against it from Hoveyzeh repeatedly later in the century.

Shah Ismail I's army brought Shushtar under the Safavids in 1508, and the shahs left eastern Khuzestan to local houses such as the Ra'nashi; after the troubles of Tahmasp's minority the long reign of Shah Abbas gave the city security. In the mid-seventeenth century the Georgian ghulam Vakhushti Khan governed it and repaired its waterworks, years remembered for cheap bread and easy living. The old fortress walls were pulled down at the end of the Safavid age, and in 1733-34 the townsmen joined the revolt of Mohammad Khan Baluch and turned out their governor; Nader Shah retook the city, had the Band-e Mizan rebuilt and settled Afshar tribesmen in the villages around. Karim Khan Zand repaired the dam once more, though by then the Ne'mati and Heydari factions were tearing the city apart, and Shushtar remained the seat of the governors of Khuzestan through the Qajar years.
zh:
舒什塔尔位于卡伦河冲出扎格罗斯山余脉、进入胡齐斯坦平原的地方，城防和百工都系于卡伦河。相传260年沙普尔一世命随罗马皇帝瓦勒良被俘的罗马士兵修筑凯撒坝，这座五百米长的堰坝是伊朗第一座桥坝结合的工程。它与米赞坝、加尔加渠（Gargar）联动，驱动一套凿入岩壁的隧道、水车和水磨，渠水环城而过，两渠之间开出果园连绵的米扬阿布（Mianab）平原；河畔的萨拉塞尔堡（Salasel）是统管整套水工的要塞。早在3世纪，这里已开始种植甘蔗。哈里发时代，舒什塔尔是胡齐斯坦七个区之一的治所，织机之盛甲于全省：933年受命织造克尔白的罩幕吉斯瓦，被视为极大的恩宠；地理学家们列举的提袍锦缎和哈里尔丝绸，到1430年前后仍见载于哈菲兹·阿布鲁的行纪。1444年，它是东胡齐斯坦波斯语居民的首邑，由本地世家统治，财富与城墙令霍韦伊泽的阿拉伯穆沙沙垂涎，此后数十年间一再兵临城下。

1508年，沙阿伊斯玛仪一世的军队把舒什塔尔纳入萨法维版图，历代沙阿把东胡齐斯坦交给拉纳西等本地家族；塔赫玛斯普幼年的动荡过去后，阿拔斯大王的长期治世为城市带来安定。17世纪中叶，格鲁吉亚出身的古拉姆瓦胡什季汗出任长官、整修水利，后人回忆那时物价低廉、生活安逸。古城墙在萨法维时代末期被毁。1733至1734年，市民响应穆罕默德汗·俾路支叛乱，驱逐了长官；纳迪尔沙收复城市后下令重修米赞坝，把阿夫沙尔部人安置在四乡。卡利姆汗·桑德时再次修坝，但那时奈阿麦提与海达里两派的党争已把城市撕裂；进入卡扎尔时代后，舒什塔尔仍是历代胡齐斯坦长官的驻节之城。

en:
Hoveyzeh lies on the Karkheh at the desert edge, west of the Karun. The town was founded, it is said, under Shapur II and rebuilt in 974-991 by the Arab chief Dubays ibn Afif al-Asadi; when Ibn Battuta passed through in the fourteenth century he found a small town of Persian speakers. In 1441 it fell to Muhammad ibn Falah, an Iraqi-born sayyid who preached that he was the earthly deputy of Ali and the Mahdi, and the Arab tribes of the border marshes flocked to his Musha'sha movement. In 1444, then, Hoveyzeh was the rough capital of a warlike Shia confederation: its lords levied the wheat and cotton of the Karkheh plain and raided towards Basra, while the town itself was still built largely of reed and palm.

Sayyed Muhsin, who ruled from 1465 to 1500, carried the confederation's arms from Basra as far as Kohgiluyeh and raised its first brick fortress, the Mohseniyya, on the site of the old reed stronghold. Shah Ismail I ended that independence in 1508: two sons of Muhsin were put to death and the sayyid Fayyaz with his followers was slaughtered in the town, though a surviving heir was soon restored as a tribute-paying vali of the Safavids. The later valis long remained nearly independent and deep in the politics of Basra; Ottoman troops overran the lowland briefly in the 1570s, and Shah Abbas I twice marched against the overmighty Mobarak before deposing the vali Mansur in 1620. Ali Khan's tribal rising in 1650 brought the governor of Lorestan to the walls, and after his restoration and the succession wars that followed, Hoveyzeh in the 1690s could still make its weight felt in Basra. Nader Shah put an end to the dynasty in 1736, and through the eighteenth century the Banu Ka'b Arabs increasingly overshadowed the old sayyids of the marsh-edge town.
zh:
霍韦伊泽位于卡伦河以西、沙漠边缘的卡尔黑河上。城镇相传始建于萨珊的沙普尔二世时代，974至991年由阿拉伯酋长杜贝斯·伊本·阿菲夫·阿萨迪重建；14世纪伊本·白图泰路过时，见到的只是一座波斯语居民的小城。1441年，自称阿里和马赫迪世间代理人的伊拉克圣裔穆罕默德·伊本·法拉赫夺取霍韦伊泽，边境沼泽地带的阿拉伯部落纷纷投附他的穆沙沙运动。于是在1444年，霍韦伊泽是一个尚武的什叶派部落联盟的粗陋都城：统治者向卡尔黑河平原征取小麦和棉花，向巴士拉方向四出攻略，而城邑本身还多是芦苇和椰枣木搭成的屋舍。

1465至1500年在位的赛义德·穆欣把联盟的兵锋从巴士拉一直推进到科吉卢耶，并用砖筑起第一座要塞穆欣尼耶堡，取代旧日的芦苇营寨。1508年沙阿伊斯玛仪一世终结了它的独立：穆欣的两个儿子被处死，赛义德·法亚兹及其追随者在城中遭屠戮，仅存的继承人不久才以纳贡称臣的萨法维瓦利身份复位。此后历代瓦利长期近乎自立，深度插手巴士拉政局：1570年代奥斯曼军队一度攻占低地，阿拔斯一世两度出兵制服坐大的穆巴拉克，又在1620年废黜瓦利曼苏尔。1650年阿里汗治下爆发部落叛乱，洛雷斯坦长官兵临城下；阿里汗复位和随后的继承混战过去后，1690年代的霍韦伊泽仍能左右巴士拉的局势。1736年纳迪尔沙终结了这个王朝，整个18世纪，巴努卡卜阿拉伯人渐渐压过了这座沼泽边城镇的旧圣裔家族。

en:
Qazaniya is the chief village of a wide frontier country east of Baghdad: the Diyala plain and the low hills running to the Persian border around Mandali and Balad Ruz. Under the Sasanians and the early caliphs this plain was Baghdad's breadbasket, watered by the great Nahrawan canal, but the canal was breached during a civil war in 938 and by the thirteenth century it had silted up and its villages stood abandoned. Mandali, the medieval Bandanijin, was later known for its scattered palm villages, its market, amir and qadi, and had once been a seat of the Kurdish Annazid emirs on the edge of the Lur country. Arab, Kurdish and Turkmen villages shared the wells and the caravan road linking Baghdad with Kermanshah. In 1444 the land belonged to the Qara Qoyunlu, who governed it loosely from Baghdad.

It passed first to the Aq Qoyunlu and then, in 1508, to Shah Ismail's Safavids. After the Ottoman victory at Chaldiran in 1514 the hills became a marcher country: the Kurdish Baban emirs of Shahrizor allied with the sultan and harried the Safavid flank, and the Ottoman conquest of Baghdad in 1534 brought the frontier under the Porte. Murad IV retook Iraq in 1638 and the Treaty of Zuhab the next year fixed the border. The Ottomans recognised the Baban family's hereditary rights in 1678, and from the 1720s to the 1740s the emirs fought Iran for the sultan from their northern hills, while the Mandali lowland stayed a district of the Baghdad pashas. Pilgrim and merchant caravans between Baghdad and the Persian plateau kept the border towns alive throughout the Ottoman centuries.
zh:
盖赞尼耶是巴格达以东一片广阔边地的首村：灌溉便利的迪亚拉平原，以及曼代利、拜勒德鲁兹一带绵延到波斯边境的低丘。萨珊王朝和早期哈里发时代，这片平原靠纳赫拉万大渠灌溉，是巴格达的粮仓；938年内战中渠堤被掘开，到13世纪水渠已经淤积，沿岸村庄尽数荒废。曼代利中世纪称本迪尼金，后来以零散的椰枣村落和自有市场、埃米尔、卡迪为人所知，还曾是库尔德安纳兹王朝埃米尔在卢尔地区边缘的驻地。阿拉伯、库尔德和土库曼村庄共用各处水井，以及连接巴格达与克尔曼沙赫的商路。1444年，这片土地归属黑羊王朝，由巴格达方面松散管辖。

这里先归白羊王朝，1508年又为沙阿·伊斯玛仪的萨法维王朝所有。1514年奥斯曼在查尔迪兰获胜后，山地成了边疆缓冲：沙赫拉祖尔的库尔德巴班埃米尔与苏丹结盟，袭扰萨法维侧翼，1534年奥斯曼攻克巴格达，边地随之归入帝国。1638年穆拉德四世重新征服伊拉克，次年《祖哈布条约》划定边界。奥斯曼1678年承认巴班家族的世袭权利，1720至1740年代，巴班埃米尔在北部山地替苏丹与波斯作战，曼代利低地则始终是巴格达帕夏治下的一个区。往返于巴格达与波斯高原之间的朝圣者和商队取道这片边地，使边境市镇在整个奥斯曼时期维持着生计。

en:
Mardin climbs a rocky ridge looking straight over the Mesopotamian plain, and its name goes back to a Syriac word for fortress. From 1103 it was the capital of the Mardin branch of the Artuqids, Turkmen princes who lined the citadel hill with mosques and madrasas, among them the Sultan Isa complex completed in 1385. The Christians of the ridge had older institutions still: three kilometres east of the city stood the Saffron Monastery, the seat of the Syriac Orthodox patriarchs after Michael the Great was enthroned there in 1166, and Timur's troops sacked it along with the city in the 1390s. The last Artuqid surrendered to Qara Yusuf of the Qara Qoyunlu in 1409, and the citadel passed to the rival Aq Qoyunlu in 1432. In 1444 Mardin was a contested but wealthy frontier city, where Kurdish, Arab and Turkoman villagers shared the hills with Armenian, Syriac and Jewish townspeople, and the unfinished Kasimiye medrese looked over the lower town.

A Qara Qoyunlu army came against Mardin in 1451 and could not take it back, and under Uzun Hasan and his son Ya'qub the city struck Aq Qoyunlu coin. Shah Ismail captured city and citadel for the Safavids in 1507, and a Venetian who came that year counted more Armenian Christians and Jews than Muslims. After Chaldiran the Ottomans took the town in 1515 but the castle held out, and Biyikli Mehmed Pasha secured it only in 1517. Direct Ottoman government then brought long quiet: the old madrasas were repaired, wool and mountain produce kept the markets busy, and travellers late in the eighteenth century still found Muslims, Armenians and Syriacs speaking Arabic and Kurdish beneath the Artuqid skyline.
zh:
马尔丁城建在一道岩石山脊上，低头便是美索不达米亚平原；它的名字来自一个意为「堡垒」的叙利亚语词。1103年起，这里是阿尔图克王朝马尔丁支系的都城，这些土库曼王公在城堡山一带修起一连串清真寺和伊斯兰学校，1385年完工的苏丹伊萨建筑群就是其中之一。山脊上的基督徒还有更古老的所在：城东三公里处是扎法兰修道院，意思是藏红花修道院，1166年牧首米哈伊尔大帝在那里登位，此后成为叙利亚正教会牧首的驻地；帖木儿的军队1390年代攻城时，修道院也遭洗劫。末代阿尔图克王公1409年向黑羊王朝的卡拉·优素福投降，城堡1432年转入敌对的白羊王朝之手。1444年的马尔丁是一座反复易手却依旧富庶的边城，库尔德、阿拉伯和土库曼村民与亚美尼亚、叙利亚和犹太市民共居山地，尚未完工的卡瑟米耶伊斯兰学校俯临下城。

1451年，黑羊王朝的军队来攻，没能夺回马尔丁；乌尊·哈桑和他的儿子叶尔孤白在位时，城里还铸造白羊钱币。1507年，沙阿·伊斯玛仪为萨法维王朝连城市带城堡一起攻下，同年到来的一名威尼斯人数过，城里的亚美尼亚基督徒和犹太人比穆斯林还多。恰尔德兰战役后，奥斯曼人1515年取得城区，城堡却坚守不降，比耶克勒·穆罕默德帕夏直到1517年才把它拿下。此后奥斯曼中央直接派官治理，带来长期安定：旧伊斯兰学校得到修缮，羊毛和山货让市集照常繁忙；18世纪末的旅人仍能看到穆斯林、亚美尼亚人和叙利亚人在阿尔图克时代的天际线下说阿拉伯语和库尔德语。

en:
Erbil stands on a great oval tell in the plain east of Mosul, its citadel rising between twenty-five and thirty-two metres above the fields. The mound is one of the oldest continuously occupied towns: it was the Assyrian city of Arba'ilu, whose Ishtar was one of the chief goddesses of Assyria, and Alexander's victory at Gaugamela in 331 BC was won a short way to the west. Long the seat of a metropolitan of the Church of the East, Erbil passed in the tenth century to Kurdish Hadhabani lords and then to the Turcoman Begtegenids. Its most famous ruler was Muzaffar al-Din Gökböri, one of Saladin's leading generals and husband of Saladin's sister Rabia Khatun; his Old Turkic name means 'Blue-wolf'. He commanded in the wars against the Crusaders and was the first Muslim ruler to celebrate the Prophet's birthday in public. He gave Erbil a lower town with hospitals and madrasas and raised the tall Mudhafaria minaret of its congregational mosque; the historians Ibn Khallikan and Ibn al-Mustawfi were born in the town. When he died without an heir the Abbasid caliph took Erbil after a siege, the Mongols forced the citadel itself after a six-month siege in 1259, and Timur's army wrecked the town in 1397. In 1444 Erbil, much reduced, was held by the Qara Qoyunlu and lived by its cloth market on the Mosul-Tabriz road.

Later in the fifteenth century Uzun Hasan's Aq Qoyunlu broke the Qara Qoyunlu and took Erbil, and their succession wars of the 1490s let the Safavids overrun these lands. After Chaldiran in 1514 the town passed to the Kurdish Soran emirs of Rawanduz. Sultan Suleiman's campaign of 1534, confirmed by the Peace of Amasya in 1555, bound the Kurdish emirates of Shahrizor to Istanbul without replacing them, and Erbil was counted among the borderland sanjaks. The long Ottoman-Persian wars of the next two centuries changed its garrison more than once. In the eighteenth century the Baban princes of Sulaymaniya extended their power over Erbil; in 1821 they still held it, with their Soran rivals pressing at the gates.
zh:
埃尔比勒矗立于摩苏尔以东平原上一座巨大的椭圆形土丘，城堡高出周围田野25至32米。这座土丘是已知持续有人居住最久的城镇之一：亚述时代这里是阿尔巴伊鲁城，当地的伊什塔尔是亚述主神之一，公元前331年亚历山大取胜的高加米拉战场就在此城以西不远处。埃尔比勒长期是东方教会都主教的驻地，10世纪转入库尔德哈扎巴尼王公之手，后来归土库曼人的贝克特吉尼德王朝。它最有名的统治者是穆扎法尔丁·格克伯里：萨拉丁麾下主要将领之一，娶了萨拉丁的妹妹拉比娅·哈屯，名字在古突厥语里意为「蓝狼」。他率部参加过对十字军的多场大战，又是第一位公开庆祝先知诞辰的穆斯林统治者；他为埃尔比勒建起城下街区，开办医院和经学院，还为清真大寺修起高耸的穆扎法里耶宣礼塔。史学家伊本·赫利坎与伊本·穆斯塔菲都出生于此。他死后无嗣，阿拔斯哈里发以围城取得此城；1259年蒙古人围城六个月攻陷城堡，1397年帖木儿的军队又摧毁了城镇。1444年的埃尔比勒已大为衰落，为黑羊王朝所据，靠摩苏尔至大不里士商道上的布匹集市为生。

15世纪后期，乌尊·哈桑的白羊王朝击溃黑羊王朝，取得埃尔比勒；1490年代白羊陷入继承内战，萨法维人趁机席卷这一带。1514年恰尔德兰战役后，城池转入罗万杜兹的库尔德索兰埃米尔之手。苏莱曼苏丹1534年的战役经1555年《阿马西亚和约》确认，把沙赫拉佐尔的库尔德埃米尔国绑定到伊斯坦布尔而不取代它们，埃尔比勒被列为边疆诸桑贾克之一。此后两个世纪的奥斯曼－波斯战争使这里数易守兵。18世纪，苏莱曼尼亚的巴拜王公把势力伸入埃尔比勒；1821年他们仍据有此城，索兰对手则已兵临城下。

en:
Sulaimaniyah is the Shahrizor, a broad fertile plain ringed by the Azmar and Goizha mountains and watered by tributaries of the Tanjaro, whose high pastures fattened the sheep that were the country's wealth. The plain was the Zamua of Assyrian annals and later a Sasanian border province with its own Christian bishopric. In Islamic times its Annazid and Ayyubid princes were Kurds; Yaqut al-Hamawi found the whole country in Kurdish hands, paying little heed to the sultan, and the old town of Sharazur was the first seat of the Ardalan princes. In 1444 the plain was held under the Qara Qoyunlu, and its Kurdish clans grazed their flocks between the ruins of older towns and the strongholds in the hills.

Later in the fifteenth century the Aq Qoyunlu overran the plain. After Chaldiran in 1514 the clans of Shahrizor joined the Kurdish alliance Idris Bitlisi built for the Ottomans against the Safavids, and Sultan Suleiman's campaign of 1534 made Shahrizor an eyalet governed almost entirely by its own Kurdish lords. The Baban clan rose to lead them: their rule was recognised as hereditary in 1678, and in 1694 Sulayman Beg routed the army of Ardalan. From their fortress of Qala Cholan the Baban princes played the Ottomans and Nader Shah off against each other through the wars of the 1720s and 1730s. In 1784 Ibrahim Pasha Baban laid out a new capital on the plain, with covered qaysariyyas and bazaars, named it Sulaymaniya after the Sulayman who had beaten Ardalan, and summoned villagers and merchants to people its quarters; Jewish tradition adds that he brought a Jewish community from Qaradagh. Within a generation the Baban court had made the young city a centre of Sorani Kurdish poetry, where the first Sorani poets, among them Nali, found patronage.
zh:
苏莱曼尼亚所在的沙赫拉佐尔是一片肥沃开阔的平原，阿兹马尔山与戈伊扎山环绕四周，坦杰罗河支流穿行其间，高山牧场把羊群养得膘肥体壮，羊毛便是这地方的财富。这里在亚述编年史中称作扎穆亚，后来是萨珊的边疆行省，设有自己的基督教主教区。伊斯兰时代，统治此地的安纳兹与阿尤布王公都是库尔德人；雅古特·哈马维发现整个地区都在库尔德人手中，从不把苏丹放在眼里，古城沙赫拉佐尔还是阿达兰王公最早的驻地。1444年，平原为黑羊王朝所据，库尔德氏族在旧城废墟与山间要塞之间牧放羊群。

15世纪后期，白羊王朝席卷平原。1514年恰尔德兰战役后，沙赫拉佐尔诸氏族加入伊德里斯·比特利西为奥斯曼组建、对抗萨法维的库尔德联盟；苏莱曼苏丹1534年的战役把沙赫拉佐尔变为一省，几乎完全由本地库尔德王公治理。巴拜氏族兴起并成为诸族之首：其统治于1678年获得世袭承认，1694年苏莱曼贝伊又击溃阿达兰的军队。1720至1730年代的战争中，巴拜王公以卡拉乔兰堡为据点，在奥斯曼与纳迪尔沙之间左右周旋。1784年，易卜拉欣帕夏·巴拜在平原上营建新都，建起穹顶市场和大巴扎，以击败阿达兰的那位苏莱曼之名将城命名为苏莱曼尼亚，又招募乡民和商贾充实各坊；据犹太传统，他还从卡拉达格迁来一个犹太人社群。不出一代人，巴拜宫廷已使这座新城成为索拉尼库尔德语诗歌的中心，纳里等最早一代索拉尼语诗人都在那里得到庇护。

en:
Hisn Kayfa occupies a defensible stretch of the Tigris, where a walled citadel rises on the rock above a river crossing on the Diyarbakır-Mosul road. Roman and Byzantine garrisons held the cliff against Sasanian Persia. The Artuqids made the town their capital in 1102 and turned a frontier fortress into a caravan city: they bridged the Tigris between 1147 and 1172, and the lower town held bazaars, caravanserais, madrasas, baths and the Small and Great palaces. Ayyubid forces took over in 1232. Mongol troops sacked the town in 1260, but the local governor submitted and a branch of the Ayyubids kept the citadel. In 1444 a Sunni Ayyubid emir still ruled a Kurdish river district from the cliff, holding a crossing, toll road and grazing country between Diyarbakır, Mosul and Bitlis.

Uzun Hasan accepted the emir's submission in 1455. A rebellion five years later brought his Aq Qoyunlu army to the Tigris, and the town fell in 1462 after six months. He placed his son Zeynel Bey in command there. Zeynel was killed fighting Mehmed II's Ottoman army at Otlukbeli in 1473, and his brick tomb was built above the river soon afterward. The Ayyubid emirs returned in 1482, while the Safavids made Hisn Kayfa part of Diyarbakır province in 1504. Ottoman forces took it in 1515 and kept Ayyubid governors in office until 1524. Caravan routes later moved away, and repeated Ottoman-Iranian wars reduced the old river market to a small garrison town.
zh:
哈桑凯伊夫坐落在底格里斯河一处易守难攻的河湾，岩壁上的城堡俯视迪亚巴克尔至摩苏尔商路上的渡口。罗马和拜占庭守军曾凭此崖对抗萨珊波斯。1102年，阿尔图格王朝把这里定为都城，将边境要塞经营成商队城市：1147至1172年间，他们在底格里斯河上修建桥梁，下城分布着巴扎、商队客栈、经学院、浴场以及小王宫和大王宫。1232年阿尤布军队接管此地。1260年蒙古军队洗劫城镇，但地方统治者很快称臣，阿尤布一支仍守住城堡。1444年，一位逊尼派阿尤布埃米尔仍在崖上统治库尔德河区，掌握迪亚巴克尔、摩苏尔和比特利斯之间的渡口、收费道路和牧场。

1455年，乌尊·哈桑接受这位埃米尔臣服。五年后当地反叛，他率白羊军队进抵底格里斯河畔，围城六个月后于1462年夺取城镇，并命儿子泽伊内尔贝伊驻守。1473年，泽伊内尔在奥特卢克贝利与穆罕默德二世的奥斯曼军队作战时身亡，战后不久河畔建起他的砖砌陵墓。1482年阿尤布埃米尔恢复统治；1504年萨法维王朝将哈桑凯伊夫划入迪亚巴克尔省。奥斯曼军队1515年攻占此地，仍留任阿尤布地方长官，直到1524年才改派官员。后来商路改道，反复的奥斯曼—伊朗战争又削弱了河畔老市场，使它变成一座小型驻军城镇。

en:
Bitlis fills a steep valley on the Bitlis River, southwest of Lake Van and high on the Armenian plateau. Its citadel commands the Baghesh Pass, the road carrying caravans and armies down toward northern Mesopotamia. Arab forces took the town in 641, and the Zurarid emirs made this toll-road capital a rich market before Marwanid, Seljuk, Ayyubid and Ilkhanid rulers followed one another through the fortress. In the fourteenth century the Kurdish Ruzaki family held Bitlis as Kara Koyunlu vassals, their influence reaching Ahlat, Mush and Hınıs. In 1444 a Sunni Kurdish emir controlled the castle with wide practical autonomy. Armenians made up much of the town, and the monasteries tolerated by its Kurdish rulers kept workshops busy copying manuscripts through the fifteenth century.

The pass made Bitlis a prize after the Kara Koyunlu collapse: the Aq Qoyunlu needed three sieges in the 1470s to take it, and the Motikan recovered the town in 1494-1495. Shah Ismail later imposed a Safavid governor, but the emir Sheref changed sides as Ottoman armies entered the region. A three-month Ottoman siege in 1531-1532 failed; Sheref was killed in 1533, and his son submitted. After 1535 the Ottomans removed Bitlis's hereditary government, attached it first to Diyarbakır and later Van, and separated Mush and Hınıs. A register in 1540 counted 26 quarters and about 7,030 inhabitants. The Ruzakids returned as hereditary governors late in the century, and Sharaf Khan, Bitlis's Kurdish emir, completed the Persian Sharafnama in 1597, a principal chronicle of Kurdish dynasties. A Jesuit mission opened in 1685, and John Macdonald Kinneir recorded about 12,000 townspeople in 1813-1814.
zh:
比特利斯位于凡湖西南、亚美尼亚高原上的比特利斯河深谷。城堡控扼巴格什山口，商队和军队沿这条路下行进入北美索不达米亚。641年阿拉伯军队攻占城镇，祖拉里德埃米尔以这座收费商路上的都城建立富庶市场，此后马尔万、塞尔柱、阿尤布和伊儿汗的统治者相继进入这座要塞。14世纪，库尔德鲁扎基家族作为黑羊王朝附庸据有比特利斯，势力延伸到阿赫拉特、穆什和赫讷斯。1444年，一位逊尼派库尔德埃米尔以很大的实际自主权控制城堡。亚美尼亚人占城镇人口的很大一部分；库尔德统治者容许的修道院中，手抄本作坊在15世纪持续繁忙。

黑羊王朝崩溃后，山口使比特利斯成为各方争夺的要地：白羊王朝在1470年代三次围攻才将它夺取，莫蒂坎人又在1494至1495年收复城镇。后来沙阿·伊斯梅尔设置萨法维总督，埃米尔谢里夫却在奥斯曼军队进入该地区时改换阵营。1531至1532年，奥斯曼围城三个月未能得手；谢里夫1533年战死，其子臣服。1535年后，奥斯曼取消比特利斯的世袭统治，先将它隶属迪亚巴克尔，后改属凡城，并把穆什和赫讷斯分出。1540年的人口册记录了26个街区和约7030名居民。16世纪末，鲁扎基家族重新成为世袭地方长官；比特利斯库尔德埃米尔沙拉夫汗于1597年完成波斯文《沙拉夫本纪》，这是记载库尔德王朝的重要编年史。1685年耶稣会在此开设传教站；1813至1814年，约翰·麦克唐纳·金尼尔记录城镇约有12000人。

en:
Homs sits on the Orontes, where the roads from the desert, Damascus, Hama and the Mediterranean ports meet, its citadel on a tell above the river. In Roman times it was Emesa, centre of the sun cult of El-Gabal; in the third century it gave Rome the empress Julia Domna, wife of Septimius Severus, and the emperor Elagabalus, who carried the god's conical black stone to Rome. Khalid ibn al-Walid, the conqueror of Byzantine Syria, died here in 642, and Baybars later raised a mosque around his domed tomb, which drew pilgrims. Facing the Crusader County of Tripoli, Homs became a Muslim frontier fortress: Mamluk armies beat the Mongols outside its walls in 1260 and again in 1281, then lost there in 1299. Mamluk rule reduced it to the chief town of the smallest province in Syria, often attached to Damascus. Ibn Battuta praised its markets and Friday mosque, but Timur's army plundered Homs in 1400, and Bedouin raids wore it down through the next century. In 1444 it was a diminished but strategically placed market town.

The city passed under Ottoman rule without resistance in 1516, and from 1579 it was the seat of a sanjak attached to the province of Tripoli. By the end of the century it held roughly 24,000 people and wove silk and woollen cloth; its alaja, muslin shot with gold thread, went to Istanbul, and sheep coming from Aleppo met camels moving north from Damascus in its livestock markets. Tribal disorder returned in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries: Bedouin raiders sacked its markets more than once, the Ottomans tore the gates off the city walls, and around 1708 Hamad al-Abbas of the Mawali confederation captured the governor of Homs and held him to ransom. A French visitor in the later eighteenth century found the walls and citadel still in repair but the city inside decaying, a large ruined village dependent on Damascus. In 1821 Homs remained a caravan and weaving centre, but a minor one in Ottoman Syria.
zh:
霍姆斯位于阿西河畔，沙漠、大马士革、哈马和地中海港口之间的道路在此相会，城堡坐落在河畔的土丘上。罗马时代它叫埃梅萨，是拜日神埃勒伽巴尔的中心；3世纪时，这里出了塞普蒂米乌斯·塞维鲁的皇后尤利亚·多姆娜，还出了皇帝埃拉伽巴路斯，后者把该神的黑色锥形圣石运到了罗马。征服拜占庭叙利亚的哈立德·本·瓦利德642年死在这里，后来拜巴尔在他带穹顶的墓旁建起清真寺，吸引前来拜谒的人。面对十字军的黎波里伯国，霍姆斯成为穆斯林的边地要塞：1260年和1281年，马穆鲁克军队两次在城外击败蒙古人，1299年却在此战败。马穆鲁克统治下，它沦为叙利亚最小行省的治所，还常被并入大马士革辖区。伊本·白图泰称赞过这里的市场和聚礼清真寺，但1400年帖木儿的军队洗劫了霍姆斯，此后一个世纪贝都因人的袭扰不断消磨这座城。1444年，它是一座衰落却据守要冲的集镇。

1516年，霍姆斯未作抵抗就转入奥斯曼统治；1579年起，它成为隶属的黎波里行省的一个桑贾克治所。到16世纪末，城中约有二万四千人，织造丝绸和毛料；名为阿拉贾的嵌金织物远销伊斯坦布尔，牲畜市场上，来自阿勒颇的羊群与从大马士革北上的骆驼在此成交。17至18世纪部落动乱卷土重来：贝都因袭掠者多次洗劫市场，奥斯曼人拆去城墙的城门，约1708年，莫瓦利联盟的哈马德·阿巴斯俘虏霍姆斯总督，扣作人质勒索赎金。18世纪后期一名法国游客见到城墙和城堡尚且完好，城里却已衰败，像一个依附大马士革的大废墟村。1821年，霍姆斯仍是商队和纺织业的中心，却是奥斯曼叙利亚的次要城市。

en:
Ayntab holds the pass where the Marash highlands fall away toward Aleppo, a fortress town on the Sajur river twelve kilometres south of ancient Doliche. Doliche had been the greater place until earthquakes in the fourteenth century ruined it; Abulfeda found Ayntab busy with fine bazaars while Doliche lay in ruins. Rulers fought over the new fortress for generations, as Mongols, Mamluks and the Turkoman Dulkadirids took it in turn: Timur besieged it in 1400 and the Black Sheep ruler Kara Yusuf in 1420. Even so it kept a name for learning. Badr al-Din al-Ayni, an Ayntab-born judge and historian in Mamluk Cairo, called it 'little Bukhara' for the scholars who taught there, and he left an eyewitness account of a Dulkadir siege in 1390. In 1444 Ayntab was the southern marcher fortress of the Dulkadir beylik, where Turkmen pastoralists brought their wool and flocks to market and Aleppo merchants passed through on the mountain road.

The Dulkadir prince Sehsuvar turned the town into a battlefield in his revolt against the Mamluks. They stormed it, he retook it within a month, and he fought on until his capture and execution in 1473. His brother Alauddevle succeeded him and left Ayntab its two best-known landmarks. He began the great mosque in the town centre in 1479 and completed the citadel works two years later, with the Mamluk sultan Qaitbay's name carved over the gate after the sultan's tour of the northern frontier. When the Ottomans overthrew the Dulkadirids and put Alauddevle to death in 1515, the Mamluk governor Yunus Beg read the war correctly. On 20 August 1516 he handed Selim I the keys of the citadel without a fight, four days before the Ottoman army destroyed the Mamluks at Marj Dabiq. The last Dulkadir prince was executed a few years later and his lands became an Ottoman province. Once Suleiman's Iranian wars had made the Aleppo road safe the bazaars grew rich, and when Evliya Celebi passed through he counted 3,900 shops and two covered bedestens. Ayntab stayed a sanjak of the Dulkadir province until 1818, when it was attached to Aleppo, the city its merchants had always served.
zh:
加济安泰普（安泰普）扼守马拉什山地降向阿勒颇的山口，是萨茹尔河畔的一座要塞城镇，在古城多利切以南十二公里。多利切本是这一带更大的聚落，14世纪的地震把它毁成废墟；地理学家阿布·菲达记述，多利切残败之时，安泰普已是市集繁荣的城镇。一代代统治者为这座新要塞反复厮杀，蒙古人、马穆鲁克人和土库曼杜勒卡迪尔人轮番占据：帖木儿1400年围城，黑羊王朝的卡拉·优素福1420年来攻。即便如此，它仍以学问闻名。在马穆鲁克开罗做到法官和史家的安泰普人巴德尔丁·阿伊尼，因这里执教的学者众多而称之为「小布哈拉」，他还为1390年杜勒卡迪尔人的一次围城留下了亲历记述。1444年的安泰普是杜勒卡迪尔贝伊国南边的边镇要塞，土库曼牧人把羊毛和畜群赶进市集，阿勒颇商人则经山道往来。

杜勒卡迪尔王公谢赫苏瓦尔反叛马穆鲁克时，把这座城镇变成了战场。马穆鲁克军队一度攻破城池，他不出一个月便夺回，继续作战，直至1473年被俘处决。继位的弟弟阿拉丁·博兹库尔特为安泰普留下两处最知名的地标：他1479年在城中心动工修建大清真寺，又在两年后完成城堡工程，城门上方刻着马穆鲁克苏丹凯特贝巡视北部边境后留下的名字。1515年奥斯曼攻灭杜勒卡迪尔、处死阿拉丁，马穆鲁克守将尤努斯贝格看清了战局：1516年8月20日，他不战而降，把城堡钥匙交给塞利姆一世，四天后奥斯曼军便在达比克草原歼灭马穆鲁克大军。末代杜勒卡迪尔王公几年后被处死，其领地成为奥斯曼一省。苏莱曼的波斯战争保障了阿勒颇商路，市集随之富庶起来；埃夫利亚·切莱比路过时数出3900家店铺和两座有顶贝德斯坦。安泰普一直是杜勒卡迪尔省的一个桑贾克，1818年改隶阿勒颇，商人的商路本就一直通往这座城市。

en:
Shamakhi lies in the south-eastern foothills of the Greater Caucasus, on the caravan road between the Caucasus lowlands and the Caspian. From the eighth to the fifteenth century it was the capital of the Shirvanshahs and a great market of the Silk Road: silk, cotton and the patterned carpets of Shirvan passed through its caravanserais, and the soumak rug weave may take its name from the city. The Juma Mosque, founded in the eighth century, survived eight of the city's eleven great earthquakes. The Persian poet Khaqani, born in Shirvan around 1120, spent his career at the Shamakhi court writing qasidas for the Shirvanshahs, and the Franciscan William of Rubruck passed through on his way back from Karakorum. A ruinous earthquake in 1192 made the shah move his court to Baku, though Shamakhi kept the kingdom's trade. In 1444 it was the chief inland city of the Sunni Shirvanshah Khalilullah I.

The Venetian Giosafat Barbaro, visiting in 1476, found four or five thousand houses and workshops making silk and cotton. In 1500 the Safavid leader Ismail I defeated and killed the Shirvanshah Farrukh Yasar, and Shah Tahmasp I later made Shirvan a Safavid province with Shamakhi as its seat. When the English merchant Anthony Jenkinson reached it overland from Moscow, he found it much decayed and settled largely by Armenians. The Ottomans took Shamakhi in 1578 and held it for a generation before it returned to Iran. In the 1640s Evliya Çelebi counted about 7,000 houses, seventy mosques and forty caravanserais, and noted that most of the people were Sunnis who said their prayers secretly under Shia rule. On 25 November 1667 an earthquake destroyed a third of the city and killed some 80,000 people. In 1721 Lezgin tribesmen under Haji Davud sacked Shamakhi, killed its Shia inhabitants and seized the goods of Russian merchants, a pretext for Peter the Great's Persian war. Nader Shah later destroyed the city and moved its people 26 kilometres west to a new Shamakhi, but the old site was rebuilt. The Treaty of Gulistan in 1813 left it to Russia.
zh:
沙马基（今通译沙马赫）坐落在大高加索山脉东南麓，地处高加索低地通往里海的商道上。8至15世纪，这里是希尔万沙王朝的都城，也是丝绸之路上最繁忙的商埠之一，丝绸、棉布和带传统纹样的希尔凡地毯在各处商栈周转，苏马克（Soumak）织毯的名字据说就来自这座城市。城中的聚礼清真寺始建于8世纪，沙马基先后经历十一次大地震，它熬过了其中八次。波斯诗人哈卡尼（Khaqani）约1120年生于希尔凡，长期在沙马基宫廷为希尔万沙撰写颂诗；方济各会修士鲁布鲁克从哈拉和林返程时也曾路过此城。1192年的大地震迫使希尔万沙把宫廷迁往巴库，但沙马基仍是王国的贸易中心。1444年时，它是逊尼派希尔万沙卡哈利路拉一世治下最重要的内陆城市。

1476年到访的威尼斯人巴尔巴罗看到，城中有四五千户人家和织绸、织棉的作坊。1500年，萨非王朝的伊斯玛仪一世击败并杀死希尔万沙法鲁赫·亚萨尔，后来塔赫玛斯普一世把希尔凡改为萨非行省，以沙马基为省会。英国商人詹金森经莫斯科陆路抵达时，发现城市已衰败不少，居民多为亚美尼亚人。奥斯曼军队1578年攻占沙马基，统治了一代人时间才重归伊朗。1640年代，埃夫利亚·切莱比在城中数到约七千户、七十座清真寺和四十处商栈，还记下居民多为逊尼派，在什叶派治下只敢私下做礼拜。1667年11月25日的地震摧毁三分之一城区，约八万人遇难。1721年，列兹金人在哈吉·达乌德率领下洗劫沙马基，屠杀什叶派居民、抢夺俄国商人财物，彼得大帝随即以此为借口发动波斯战争。纳迪尔沙后来毁城，把居民迁到以西26公里处另建新城，但旧城原址最终又重建起来。1813年《古利斯坦条约》把沙马基划归俄罗斯。

en:
Mianeh, Miyana in the local Turkish speech and Miyanaj to the Arab geographers, guards the Qaflankuh defile, through which the road from Zanjan climbs into Azerbaijan; it has always been the first Azerbaijani town a traveller meets coming off the Iranian plateau. Ibn Hawqal numbered it among the prosperous towns of the region, and the nearby district of Khunj, later renamed Kaghazkonan, 'the paper-makers', worked paper for centuries, its workshops supplying Tabriz and the Ilkhanid foundation of Rab'-e Rashidi there. Hamdallah Mustawfi, writing after the Mongol storms, found the town reduced to a large village that yielded grain, cotton, grapes and rice to the value of 25,700 dinars, its people fair-skinned and Turkic in their ways. In 1444 Mianeh was a small posting town in the Qara Qoyunlu realm.

Under the Safavids the great highway was furnished with staging posts, among them the caravanserai at Jamalabad in Kaghazkonan and the Shahrchay bridge known as 23 Pol, built in the manner of the bridges of Isfahan. The road carried the Safavid court, its armies and its caravans between Qazvin and Tabriz, and every war over Azerbaijan brought troops through the defile. On Emanuel Bowen's map of Iran of 1747 the town appears as Miana.
zh:
米亚内在当地突厥语中称米扬纳，阿拉伯地理书称米亚纳季，扼守加夫兰库赫山口，从赞詹方向来的道路经此攀上阿塞拜疆高原，旅人离开伊朗高原后遇到的第一座阿塞拜疆城镇就是它。伊本·豪加勒曾把它列入这一带的富庶城镇；邻近的洪季地区后来改名「卡加兹科南」（意为造纸者），作坊供应大不里士和当地伊儿汗国的拉卜额·拉施迪城。蒙古浩劫之后，哈姆杜拉·穆斯塔菲见到的城镇已缩成一座大村庄，出产谷物、棉花、葡萄和稻米，岁入2.57万第纳尔，居民肤色白皙、风习近突厥。1444年，它是黑羊王朝境内的一座驿站小镇。

萨法维时期，这条大道沿途遍设驿站，卡加兹科南贾马勒阿巴德的商队客栈、仿伊斯法罕诸桥样式修建、被称作「二十三桥」的沙赫尔恰伊桥都落成于此时。萨法维宫廷、军队和商队沿这条路往返于加兹温与大不里士之间，阿塞拜疆的每一场战事也都会把军队引进山口。1747年伊曼纽尔·鲍恩绘制的伊朗地图上，这座城镇标注为米亚纳（Miana）。

en:
Kartli is the old Georgian heartland along the upper Mtkvari, on the busiest corridor between the Black Sea slopes and eastern Georgia. Gori stands where the Liakhvi joins the river, and its hill fortress, Goris-Tsikhe, commanded the main road between eastern and western Georgia; King David IV founded the town below it early in the twelfth century and settled Armenian refugees there. Ten kilometres east, Uplistsikhe is a whole town cut into the cliff above the Mtkvari, with pagan halls and Christian basilicas side by side; it was largely abandoned after the Mongol raids and afterwards served only as a refuge in invasions. Gori's markets served caravans, vineyards and the silk-working villages of the lowlands. In 1444 town and citadel still belonged to the Kingdom of Georgia, whose crown was losing its nobles to faction.

Uzun Hasan's Aq Qoyunlu army took and sacked Gori in 1477, and although Constantine II recovered the town, by 1484 Kartli was a separate kingdom. Safavid campaigns under Shah Tahmasp I gave Iran garrisons in Kartli, and the Peace of Amasya in 1555 assigned the country to the Safavid sphere. Ottoman troops held the Gori citadel through the war of 1578-1590, until Simon I stormed it in 1599. Shah Abbas I put a Persian garrison back in 1614. In 1625 Giorgi Saakadze, the 'Grand Mouravi' and former mouravi of Tbilisi, led the lords of Kartli and Kakheti in revolt: he killed the Safavid commander Qarachaqay Khan in the Persian camp and the Georgians annihilated the shah's army at Martqopi, only to be beaten at Marabda a few months later. From 1632 the Safavid appointee Rostom Khan, a Bagrationi prince converted to Islam, rebuilt the fortress and palace, ran the kingdom on Persian lines and allowed a measure of religious tolerance. Ottoman and then Persian occupation between 1723 and the 1740s left Gori damaged, before Teimuraz II recovered the town. Erekle II united Kartli with Kakheti in 1762, accepted Russian protection in 1783, and lost the kingdom to Russian annexation in 1801.
zh:
卡特利是库拉河上游古老的格鲁吉亚腹地，处在黑海坡地通往格鲁吉亚东部最繁忙的走廊上。戈里位于利亚赫维河汇入库拉河处，山顶要塞戈里斯齐赫扼守格鲁吉亚东西大道；12世纪初大卫四世在山下建城，安置亚美尼亚难民。城东10公里，乌普利斯齐赫是一整座凿在库拉河崖壁上的城镇，异教厅堂和基督教巴西利卡并排而立；它在蒙古入侵后大半废弃，之后每逢外敌来犯只充作避难之所。戈里的市场服务商队、葡萄园和低地的丝织村庄。1444年，城和堡垒仍属格鲁吉亚王国，而王权正败在贵族党争手里。

1477年，乌尊·哈桑的白羊王朝军队攻占并洗劫戈里；君士坦丁二世虽予收复，到1484年卡特利已成了独立王国。萨法维塔赫玛斯普一世的征战使伊朗在卡特利驻扎军队，1555年《阿马西亚和约》又把该国划入萨法维势力范围。1578至1590年战争中，奥斯曼军队占据戈里堡垒，直到1599年西莫内一世强攻收复。1614年阿拔斯一世重新派驻波斯守军。1625年，曾任第比利斯长官、人称「大穆拉维」的格奥尔基·萨卡泽率领卡特利和卡赫季贵族起事，在波斯大营中斩杀统帅，格鲁吉亚军队先在营地袭击中歼灭一支波斯大军，几个月后却战败。1632年起，改宗伊斯兰教的巴格拉季昂王公罗斯托姆汗受萨法维任命统治卡特利，他修复要塞和宫殿，按波斯方式治理国家，也允许一定程度的宗教宽容。1723年至1740年代奥斯曼和波斯先后占领，戈里残破，最后由泰穆拉兹二世收复。1762年伊拉克略二世把卡特利与卡赫季合并，1783年接受俄国保护，王国却在1801年被俄国兼并。

en:
Bayazid sits in a high basin of pastureland beneath Mount Ararat, where the road from Tabriz crosses into Anatolia. Its fortress climbs the rock above the town: as Daroynk it was an Armenian royal treasury that a Sasanian army failed to storm in the fourth century, Bagratid princes rebuilt its baileys one above another, and King Gagik I Artsruni made it a bishop's seat around 922. The Seljuks of Alp Arslan took it in 1064 and the Mongols in 1231. In 1374 Bayazit Han, a Jalayirid prince and governor of Ani, raised a new fortress against Qara Qoyunlu raids and gave the place his own name; Timur held it in 1386, and the Qara Qoyunlu controlled it again from 1406. In 1444 Bayazid was a mountain garrison on the Turkmen frontier, where Armenian villagers and Kurdish pastoralists grazed large wool flocks on the summer pastures and paid dues to Jahan Shah's lords.

The stronghold passed to Uzun Hasan's Aq Qoyunlu and, after Shah Ismail's victory at Sharur, to the Safavids. On 20 August 1514 Selim I's army camped on the Bayazid plain on its way to Chaldiran and the fortress opened its gates, though the frontier swung back and forth for two generations. The Ottomans took it for good in the Caucasian war of 1578 and made Bayazid a sanjak of the new province of Van; local lords resettled its deserted villages, until Nader Shah's army swept through in 1744 and the Porte took to appointing the governors itself. One of them left the town its greatest monument: Çolak Abdi Pasha of the Kurdish Cildirogullari began the palace on the eastern terrace in 1685, and İshak Pasha, whose name it bears, finished its mosque, medrese, baths and harem in 1784; Armenian and Georgian craftsmen built it in a mix of Anatolian, Persian and Mesopotamian styles. In 1805 the French envoy Amédée Jaubert, sent by Napoleon to the court at Tehran, was held prisoner there for months. In 1821 Abbas Mirza's Qajar army occupied Bayazid, at the opening of the last Ottoman–Persian war fought on this frontier.
zh:
巴耶基德（又译巴耶济德）位于阿拉拉特山下的高山牧场盆地，大不里士通往安纳托利亚的道路经此穿过。要塞踞于镇旁山岩之上：它古称达鲁因克，曾是亚美尼亚王室宝库，4世纪萨珊军队强攻不克；巴格拉季德王公把堡场一层层修上岩壁，加吉克一世·阿尔茨鲁尼约922年在此设立主教座。1064年阿尔普·阿斯兰的塞尔柱人攻取要塞，1231年蒙古人继至。1374年，曾任阿尼总督的札剌亦儿王族巴耶济德汗为抵御黑羊王朝袭扰另筑新堡，地名也得自他本人；帖木儿1386年一度占据，1406年起重归黑羊王朝。1444年的巴耶基德是土库曼边境上的山城军镇，亚美尼亚村民和库尔德牧民在高山夏牧场上放养大批毛用绵羊，向贾汉沙赫的领主纳贡。

要塞后来归入乌尊·哈桑的白羊王朝，沙鲁尔之战后又转属萨非王朝。1514年8月20日，塞利姆一世进军查尔迪兰途中在巴耶基德平原扎营，要塞开城归附，但此后两代人时间里边界反复拉锯。1578年的高加索战争中，奥斯曼人最终拿下此地，把巴耶基德设为凡城新省下辖的桑贾克；当地领主招民充实荒废的村庄，直到1744年纳迪尔沙赫的军队横扫而过，伊斯坦布尔遂改为直接委任长官。一位长官给小城留下了最宏大的建筑：库尔德吉尔德罗奥卢家族的乔拉克·阿卜迪帕夏1685年在城东台地上动工修建宫殿，以自己名字命名宫殿的伊沙克帕夏于1784年建成清真寺、经学院、浴场和后宫；亚美尼亚和格鲁吉亚工匠参与营造，建筑混合了安纳托利亚、波斯和北美索不达米亚的风格。1805年，拿破仑派往德黑兰宫廷的法国使节阿梅代·若贝尔被关在宫中数月。1821年，阿拔斯·米尔扎的恺加军队占领巴耶基德，这是这条边境上最后一场奥斯曼—波斯战争的开端。

en:
Oltu, the Georgian Oltisi, occupies a high valley of the Oltu River in Tao, where the roads fork toward Erzurum, Kars and the Black Sea. Its castle covers the top of a rocky outcrop, its walls and round towers raised in two main building periods between the seventh and eleventh centuries; in the north tower stand the ruins of a Georgian hexaconch church from the ninth or tenth century, whose foundations reused a seventh-century Greek-Armenian inscription. The pastures around grazed cattle, horses and sheep rather than feeding a large town. In 1444 the valley belonged to the Orthodox Jaqeli principality of Samtskhe, but Qara Qoyunlu raids that reached Akhaltsikhe showed how exposed this western march had become.

The Jaqelis broke from Georgia in the later fifteenth century, and Oltu's fate was settled in the Ottoman-Safavid border wars. After the Georgian defeat at Sokhoista in 1545 and the Ottoman campaign of 1578, the old Samtskhe lands became the Childir Eyalet, first governed by the converted Georgian prince Manuchar, or Mustafa Pasha. By the mid-seventeenth century Oltu was one of its sanjaks, a frontier district on the caravan route between eastern Anatolia and the Caucasus, supplying livestock, timber and minerals. The Safavid capture of Akhaltsikhe in 1635 and its return under the Peace of Zuhab in 1639 shook the district without ending Ottoman rule. In 1665 Arslan Mehmed Pasha, the Jaqeli governor of Childir, built Oltu's domed Arslan Pasha Mosque. Local craftsmen carved Oltu stone, the polished black 'black amber', into prayer beads and small ornaments. In 1821 Oltu remained an Ottoman sanjak beneath its old castle.
zh:
奥尔图，格鲁吉亚语称奥勒图西，位于陶地区奥勒图河上游的高谷，通往埃尔祖鲁姆、卡尔斯和黑海方向的道路在此分岔。城堡坐落在一座岩顶，围墙和圆塔是7至11世纪间两次主要营建的产物；北塔里残存着9或10世纪一座格鲁吉亚教堂的遗迹，教堂地基里还嵌着一块移作他用的7世纪希腊语—亚美尼亚语双语刻石。周围牧场放牧牛、马和羊群，养不起一座大型低地城镇。1444年，谷地属于信奉东正教、由贾凯利家族统治的萨姆茨赫，但黑羊王朝军队已能深入阿哈尔齐赫，足以说明这条西部边地何等暴露。

贾凯利家族在15世纪后期脱离格鲁吉亚，奥尔图的去留在奥斯曼—萨法维边境战争中落定。1545年格鲁吉亚人在索霍伊斯塔战败，1578年奥斯曼远征后，旧萨姆茨赫土地被组建为切尔德尔行省，首任总督是改宗伊斯兰教的格鲁吉亚王公马努查尔，即穆斯塔法帕夏。到17世纪中期，奥尔图已列为该行省的桑贾克之一，这个边地辖区坐落在安纳托利亚东部通往高加索的商路上，向外界供应牲畜、木材和矿产。1635年萨法维攻占阿哈尔齐赫，1639年《祖哈布和约》又将其归还，全区为之动荡，奥斯曼的统治却没有中断。1665年，切尔德尔的贾凯利裔总督阿尔斯兰·穆罕默德帕夏修建了带穹顶的阿尔斯兰帕夏清真寺。当地工匠还雕刻奥尔图石，这种光亮漆黑的石料又称「黑琥珀」，被做成念珠和小型饰物。1821年，古堡之下的奥尔图仍是奥斯曼的桑贾克。

en:
Khoy lies on a fertile, wall-girt plain between Lake Urmia and the Armenian highlands, where the silk-road branch from Tabriz into Anatolia passes through; its salt mines gave the town its name. Alp Arslan used it as his forward base on the march that ended at Manzikert in 1071, and a Georgian army of Queen Tamar took it in 1210. The Khwarazmshah Jalal al-Din held Khoy briefly at the end of the 1220s and left it to his wife Malika, while the Kurdish Donboli tribe, who would one day rule the town, pastured their flocks in the Hakkari highlands to the west. In 1444 Khoy is a Qara Qoyunlu frontier town, where caravans trade wool, salt and timber on the road west.

The town passed with Azerbaijan to the Aq Qoyunlu and then the Safavids, and on 23 August 1514 the Ottoman-Safavid war reached Khoy. On the Chaldiran plain north of Khoy, Sultan Selim's artillery and janissaries destroyed Shah Ismail's cavalry; the shah was wounded and nearly taken, and his wives were carried off to the Ottomans, while the Kurdish chiefs of the borderlands switched their allegiance to the Sultan. Under Shah Tahmasp I the Donboli chief Haji Beg governed the merged frontier district of Khoy and Sokmanabad, until the governor of Van had him murdered in 1548 and his tribesmen were killed or driven across the border. The Donboli came back after Shah Abbas's reconquest of 1603 and rebuilt a ruined Khoy with tax remissions. In 1724 an Ottoman army besieged the town for 57 days and, after storming it, put its 3,000 Qizilbash defenders to the sword. Nader Shah retook Khoy in 1737. After his death the Donboli khans ruled an independent state from the town: Ahmad Khan held Tabriz, kept Erivan and Nakhchivan as vassals and laid out the terraced Dalgoshay garden in 1777. The Qajars ended it on 17 September 1799, when Crown Prince Abbas Mirza defeated the Donbolis outside Khoy and annexed the khanate; the great covered bazaar was rebuilt afterwards, and ramparts drawn up by the French general Gardane girdled the town.
zh:
霍伊坐落在乌尔米耶湖与亚美尼亚高原之间一片肥沃的平原上，城有墙垣围护，大不里士通往安纳托利亚的丝绸之路支路穿城而过，城名据说就来自当地的盐矿。1071年，阿尔普·阿尔斯兰进军曼齐刻尔特时以霍伊为前进基地；1210年塔玛尔女王的格鲁吉亚军队攻占此城。1220年代末，花剌子模沙札兰丁短暂据有此地，把它留给王后玛利卡；日后统治此城的库尔德登贝利部，当时还在西边的哈卡里高地放牧。1444年的霍伊是黑羊王朝的边城，商队在城墙下的西行路上买卖羊毛、食盐和木材。

霍伊随阿塞拜疆先后转入白羊王朝和萨法维王朝之手，1514年8月23日，奥斯曼与萨法维的大战打到了城边。在霍伊以北的查尔迪兰平原，塞利姆苏丹的大炮和耶尼切里歼灭了伊斯玛仪沙的骑兵，沙本人负伤险些被俘，妻妾也被掳往奥斯曼，边境上的库尔德首领纷纷转投苏丹。塔赫玛斯普一世在位时，登贝利首领哈吉贝格统辖霍伊与塞克曼阿巴德合并而成的边防区，1548年凡城总督将他杀害，其族人或遭屠戮，或被逐过边境。1603年阿拔斯沙收复阿塞拜疆后，登贝利人陆续归来，靠减免赋税把已成废墟的霍伊重建起来。1724年，奥斯曼军队围城57天后破城，将3000名红头军尽数诛杀。纳迪尔沙1737年收复霍伊。他死后，登贝利诸汗以此城为都，统治一个独立的政权：艾哈迈德汗占据大不里士，使埃里温、纳希切万称臣，又在1777年下令修建层叠而上的德尔古沙花园。1799年9月17日，王储阿巴斯·米尔扎在霍伊城外击败登贝利人，恺加王朝兼并汗国；宏大的有顶巴扎此后重建，法国将领加尔达纳设计的城墙也环绕全城。

en:
Shaki lies high on the southern slopes of the Greater Caucasus, among walnut forests, silkworm farms and mountain streams, on the old road from Georgia to the Caspian. A city here was already one of the largest of Caucasian Albania in the first century, and its people took Christianity early from Armenia. After Timur's campaigns the local Oirat lord Sidi Ahmed Orlat held the country, and in 1444 it passed to the Kara-Keshish-oghlu, a Muslim dynasty of Armenian origin. Under them this mountain country lived by the silk of its mulberry groves, the fine raw silk of Shaki becoming its chief export. The town was then also called Nukha.

The local rulers stayed on as Safavid vassals after Ismail I's conquest, until Shah Tahmasp I removed the last of them in 1551 and installed a Qizilbash governor; Ottoman armies occupied Shaki in 1578–1603 and again in 1724–35. In 1743 Haji Chelebi, claiming descent from the old ruling line, killed Nader Shah's governor and proclaimed the Shaki khanate. When Nader's army came for him he shut himself in the Gelesen-Geresen fortress and held out for four months. A flood of the Kish river swept the old town away in 1772, and its people rebuilt Shaki on the higher ground of Nukha, raising a citadel and the khans' summer palace, completed in 1797 under Muhammad Husayn Khan Mushtaq. Armenian and Muslim merchants kept the old trade in silkworms and silk thread. The Treaty of Kyurekchay in 1805 placed the khanate under Russia; Selim Khan was deposed the next year and khan rule was ended in 1819.
zh:
沙基（今译舍基）坐落在大高加索山脉南坡的高地，胡桃林、蚕场与山溪之间，地处格鲁吉亚通往里海的古老山道上。1世纪时，这里已是高加索阿尔巴尼亚最大的城市之一，居民很早便经亚美尼亚接受基督教。帖木儿征战之后，本地奥拉特部首领西迪·艾哈迈德·奥拉特割据于此；1444年，政权转入亚美尼亚裔穆斯林王朝卡拉-凯希什-奥格卢之手。在他们治下，这片山地靠桑蚕之利为生，优质的沙基生丝是首要出口货。当时城镇也叫努哈。

伊斯玛仪一世征服后，本地统治者作为萨非王朝的附庸继续在位，直到1551年塔赫玛斯普一世废掉末代君主，改派克孜勒巴什总督；奥斯曼军队曾两度占领沙基，分别是1578—1603年和1724—1735年。1743年，自称出自旧统治家族的哈吉·切莱比杀死纳迪尔沙任命的总督，建立沙基汗国。纳迪尔沙的军队前来讨伐时，他退守格莱亚尔桑-格莱尔桑要塞，坚守四个月。1772年基什河暴涨，旧城被洪水冲毁，居民在地势更高的努哈重建沙基，筑起要塞和汗王的夏宫；夏宫于1797年在穆罕默德·侯赛因汗·穆什塔克治下落成。养蚕与蚕丝贸易始终是当地亚美尼亚和穆斯林商人的生计。1805年《库列克恰伊条约》使汗国臣属俄罗斯，谢里姆汗次年被废，汗国统治1819年终结。

en:
Lakia is the high Lak country along the Kazikumukh Koysu, with Kumukh, also called Gazi-Kumukh, as its fortress-capital. The Laks were among the first Muslims of Dagestan: their Friday mosque was completed in 778, and the prefix Gazi, added to the town's name by the fourteenth century, marked it as a base for spreading Islam. For centuries Kumukh combined a seat of Muslim learning, a mountain bazaar and the shamkhal's fortress, and in the fifteenth century it was Dagestan's foremost political centre. In 1444 the shamkhal ruling there held the Sunni Lak valleys and reached down toward the Kumyk coastal plain, and caravans and war parties moving between the Caspian and the interior passed beneath its walls.

The shamkhal's domains were divided among his sons in 1574, and the old state broke apart in the 1640s; in the following decades Kumukh became the capital of the Lak-ruled Gazikumukh Khanate. Nader Shah's Iranians took the town in 1734, but in 1741 Murtazali-khan led the Dagestani army against them in Andalal, and Lak singers turned the four-day battle into the Song of the Hero Murtazali. From 1789 the state was called the Kura-Gazikumukh Khanate, and between 1812 and 1820 it split into Gazikumukh and Kura. Kumukh's bazaar drew Avars, Dargins and Lezgins, and its smiths sold weapons and copper vessels. In December 1819 Surkhay Khan II fell on the Russian fort at Chirag, and of its garrison of four hundred only seventy survived. General Madatov answered by storming Khosrekh, the aul that barred the road into Lakia: fourteen cannons bombarded it for an hour, the assault drove the defenders back to the mosque, and twelve hundred highlanders were killed or wounded. On 14 June 1820 Madatov entered Kumukh, put Aslan Khan of Kura on the throne and drove Surkhay into exile through Avaria to Persia.
zh:
拉奇亚是加齐库穆赫河沿岸的拉克人高地，以要塞都城库穆赫（又称加齐库穆赫）为中心。拉克人是达吉斯坦最早的穆斯林之一：城中的聚礼清真寺于778年建成，到14世纪，城名前冠以「加齐」二字，标明这里是传播伊斯兰教的据点。数百年来，库穆赫集伊斯兰学府、山地集市和沙姆哈尔要塞于一身，15世纪更是达吉斯坦最重要的政治中心。1444年，在此执政的沙姆哈尔统治着逊尼派拉克诸山谷，势力伸向库梅克滨海平原；往来里海与内陆的商队和军队，都要从库穆赫城墙下经过。

1574年，沙姆哈尔的领地被儿子们瓜分，旧政权在1640年代解体；随后数十年，库穆赫成为拉克人统治的加齐库穆赫汗国都城。1734年纳迪尔沙阿的伊朗军队攻占此城，但1741年穆尔塔扎利率领达吉斯坦联军在安达拉尔迎击，两军恶战四昼夜，拉克民间诗歌把这场战斗唱成《英雄穆尔塔扎利之歌》。1789年起该国正式称库拉-加齐库穆赫汗国，1812至1820年间分裂为加齐库穆赫和库拉两国。库穆赫集市吸引阿瓦尔人、达尔金人和列兹金人，铁匠打造的武器和铜器向外出售。1819年12月，苏尔哈伊汗二世突袭俄军驻守的奇拉格要塞，四百名守军仅七十人生还。马达托夫将军随即强攻扼守入山通道的霍斯列赫村：十四门大炮轰击一小时，进攻部队把守军一步步逼到清真寺，山民死伤一千二百人。1820年6月14日，马达托夫进入库穆赫，立库拉的阿斯兰汗为统治者，苏尔哈伊则经阿瓦尔流亡波斯。

en:
Aksaray stands on the Melendiz river beneath Mount Hasan, the 3,268-metre volcano visible from its walls, on the old caravan road from Konya to Persia. The Greeks knew it as Garsaoura, then Archelais and Colonia, and Byzantine emperors mustered their armies here. The Seljuk sultan Kılıç Arslan II rebuilt the town in 1170 and raised a palace in it, from which it took the name Aksaray, 'white palace', and often held court there. In 1229 Kayqubad I built Sultan Han forty kilometres west of the town, the largest caravanserai in Anatolia, guarding the road through his realm. The Mongols raided in 1277 and killed or carried off 6,000 of its people, but Ibn Battuta in the next century found 'a beautiful city, surrounded by waterways and gardens, with a water supply coming right to the houses', and a new class of Muslim merchants running its trade. It then passed between the Eretnids and the Karamanids, who held it after 1402, so that in 1444 Aksaray was a Karamanid frontier town on the road to Ankara, its skyline marked by the Seljuk leaning minaret of 1236 and the Karamanid grand mosque of 1408.

In 1468, after long and destructive fighting, Mehmed II's armies made Aksaray permanently Ottoman. Part of its population was resettled in conquered Istanbul, and the quarter assigned to them took the name Aksaray. The Ottoman registers of 1530 list thirty-seven neighbourhoods and perhaps 5,000 to 6,000 people, the town forming a district attached to the sanjak of Nigde. Its caravanserais kept serving the road between Konya and Ankara, while salt from nearby Lake Tuz, the chief salt source of inland Anatolia, filled its market.
zh:
阿克萨赖在梅伦迪兹河畔，城墙边就能望见海拔3268米的哈桑火山，城在科尼亚通往波斯的古商道上。希腊人先后称此地为加尔绍拉、阿基劳斯和科洛尼亚，拜占庭皇帝曾在此集结军队。鲁姆苏丹基利杰·阿尔斯兰二世1170年重建此城并修筑宫殿，阿克萨赖的名字便来自这座宫殿，意为「白色宫殿」，苏丹也常在此驻跸。1229年，凯库巴德一世在城西四十公里处修建苏丹汗，这是安纳托利亚最大的商队商馆，扼守穿过其国土的商路。1277年蒙古人袭城，杀掠六千人；但下个世纪伊本·白图泰见到的仍是「一座美丽城市，水道与花园环绕，清水一直通到每户人家」，城中还形成了新一代穆斯林商人群体。此后它在埃尔特纳侯国与卡拉曼侯国之间反复易手，1402年后归于卡拉曼人。1444年，阿克萨赖是卡拉曼通往安卡拉大道上的边境城镇，1236年的塞尔柱斜塔和1408年的卡拉曼大清真寺矗立在城中。

1468年，经过长期而惨烈的争夺，穆罕默德二世的军队将阿克萨赖永久纳入奥斯曼版图。城中一部分居民被迁往新征服的伊斯坦布尔，划给他们的街区就叫阿克萨赖。1530年的奥斯曼册籍记载，全城有三十七个街区、约五六千居民，是尼代桑贾克下属的一个辖区。城中的商馆继续接待往来科尼亚与安卡拉的商队，附近图兹湖的盐是安纳托利亚内陆主要的食盐来源，也供应着这里的集市。

en:
Denizli occupies a well-watered plateau six or seven kilometres south of the ruins of Laodicea on the Lycus, the Hellenistic and Roman city that grew rich on the black-wool trade and was one of the Seven Churches of Asia. Earthquakes and the Byzantine-Seljuk wars wrecked its aqueducts, and from the eleventh century the people drifted south to the springs, which the Turks called Ladik; the later name Tonguzlu, 'place of boars', was softened to Denizli to shed the pig connotation. In the thirteenth century the emir Seyfettin Karasungur gave the new town its citadel and built the Akhan caravanserai on the road below. The Inanjid beys made Ladik their capital from 1261 until Germiyan absorbed it in 1368; Bayezid I took it in 1391, Timur wintered here after the battle of Ankara and left the region to Germiyan, and the last Germiyanid bequest brought it to the Ottomans in 1429. Ibn Battuta found seven Friday mosques, gardens and perennial streams, with Greek artisans working for Turkish lords, and he hired a mounted escort because brigands roamed the plain. In 1444 Denizli was an Ottoman Sunni Turkish market town on the road from the Aegean coast into inner Anatolia, and the weavers of nearby Buldan were already known for their stout cloth; a later legend claimed that Osman Gazi himself had worn clothes made from the red shawls of Lazikiye.

The Ottoman centuries passed mostly without fighting reaching the town. In the seventeenth century Evliya Çelebi measured a square fortress on flat ground with four gates, named for the painters, saddle-makers, new mosque and vineyard, and about fifty watchmen; the real town lay outside, forty-four quarters of 3,600 houses, with fifty-seven mosques, seven madrasas, six baths and seventeen dervish lodges, and rich and poor alike kept houses among the vines. Buldan drew merchants to its hard-wearing wool and cotton, and Katip Çelebi noted its weekly market in the Cihannüma. The earthquake of 1702–1703 killed some 12,000 people and left the old quarter by the citadel uninhabitable; the survivors rebuilt the town uphill around the springs, and the cloth trade moved with them.
zh:
代尼兹利位于一片水源丰沛的高原上，北面六七公里处是吕科斯河畔老底嘉的遗址。这座希腊化和罗马城市靠黑羊毛贸易致富，也是《启示录》中亚西亚七教会之一。地震和拜占庭与塞尔柱之间的战争毁了它的引水渠，居民从11世纪起陆续南迁到泉水旁，突厥人把新聚落称作拉迪克；后来的名字通古兹卢意为「野猪之地」，为避忌讳才改成读音相近的代尼兹利。13世纪，埃米尔赛义夫丁·卡拉松古尔为新城修建城堡，又在坡下的道路旁修建了阿克汉商队驿站。1261年起因詹奥卢贝伊以拉迪克为都，1368年其地并入格尔米扬；巴耶济德一世1391年取城，帖木儿在安卡拉战役后曾在此过冬，随后把此地交还格尔米扬，1429年末代贝伊的遗赠使它最终归入奥斯曼。伊本·白图泰见到七座聚礼清真寺、花园和长流泉水，希腊工匠在突厥领主手下做工；他还雇了骑兵护送，因为平原上盗匪出没。1444年时，代尼兹利是爱琴海沿岸通往安纳托利亚内陆道路上一座奥斯曼逊尼派土耳其人商业城镇，附近布尔丹的织工已以结实的布料闻名；后世传说称，奥斯曼加齐本人就穿过用拉济基耶红披肩裁成的衣裳。

奥斯曼统治的几个世纪里，战火大多没有烧到这座城镇。17世纪，埃夫利亚·切莱比记下一座平地上的方形堡垒，开有四门，分别以画家、鞍工、新清真寺和葡萄园命名，守军约五十人；真正的城区在堡外，四十四个居民区、三千六百所房屋，有五十七座大小清真寺、七所经学院、六座浴室和十七所托钵僧道堂，富户和平民都在葡萄园间筑屋而居。布尔丹结实耐穿的毛棉布吸引着四方商人，卡蒂普·切莱比在《世界志》中也记下当地每周开市。1702—1703年的地震造成约一万两千人丧生，城堡旁的旧城区无法居住，幸存者把城建到高处的泉水周围，布匹生意也随他们一同迁去。

en:
Aydın stands inland from the Aegean in the lower valley of the Büyük Menderes, the ancient Maeander. Its old city of Tralles was the birthplace of Anthemius, architect of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople. Emperor Andronikos II rebuilt and repopulated Tralles in 1278 as a barrier on the Turkish frontier, but the Menteşe took it in 1284 and called it Güzelhisar. It later passed to the Aydınid dynasty founded by Mehmed Bey around 1307. The dynasty's best-known ruler was his son Umur, a naval ghazi who used Smyrna as a base after the city fell to his house, raided Negroponte in 1332-1333 and sent fleets to help John VI Kantakouzenos in the Byzantine civil war. A Latin coalition answered with the Smyrniote crusades; Umur was killed when Smyrna fell in 1348. The principality passed to the Ottomans, was restored by Timur in 1402, and then fell again after Murad II defeated Cüneyd Bey in 1425. In 1444 Aydın was an Ottoman sanjak set among the fig orchards, olive groves and grain fields of the Maeander valley.

The Aegean wars moved elsewhere, and Aydın drew its income from the valley. Figs, olive oil and grain travelled down the valley roads toward the ports around Smyrna and Ephesus. In the eighteenth century the Cihanoğlu family of Koçarlı exploited weak provincial government and became the district's real lords. The family built its baroque mosque and attached religious complex in Aydın in 1756-1757, then raised watchtowers in the 1760s to overlook the roads and estates across the valley. The Ottoman government reasserted itself early in the nineteenth century. In 1811 Aydın became the seat of an eyalet whose governors oversaw a broad southwestern district including İzmir, Saruhan, Menteşe, Antalya and Isparta.
zh:
艾登位于爱琴海沿岸后方的大门德雷斯河（古称迈安德河）下游谷地。旧城特拉勒斯是君士坦丁堡圣索菲亚大教堂建筑师安提莫斯的故乡。1278年，皇帝安德洛尼卡二世重建城市、迁来居民，想把它作为土耳其边境上的屏障；但门泰谢侯国仍在1284年攻下此城，称它为格泽尔希萨尔。后来城市转入艾登王朝，穆罕默德贝伊约在1307年建立这个侯国。王朝最有名的统治者是他的儿子乌穆尔。这位海上加齐以士麦那为基地，1332至1333年袭掠内格罗蓬特，又在拜占庭内战中派出舰队支援约翰六世·坎塔库泽努斯。拉丁联军以士麦那十字军回应，乌穆尔在1348年士麦那陷落时战死。侯国先并入奥斯曼，1402年由帖木儿恢复，穆拉德二世1425年击灭居内伊德贝伊后再度并入。1444年，艾登是奥斯曼的桑贾克，坐落在迈安德河谷的无花果林、橄榄园和粮田之间。

爱琴海的战事转移到别处后，艾登的收入来自谷地。无花果、橄榄油和粮食沿河谷道路运往士麦那和以弗所一带的港口。18世纪，科恰勒的吉汉奥卢家族利用奥斯曼地方政府的衰弱，成为这片地区真正的主人。1756至1757年，他们在艾登修建巴洛克式清真寺和附属宗教建筑群；1760年代又建起多座瞭望塔，监视谷地里的道路和庄园。19世纪初，奥斯曼政府重新收紧控制。1811年，艾登成为艾雷特治所，总督管辖伊兹密尔、萨鲁汗、门泰谢、安塔利亚和伊斯帕尔塔等广阔的西南地区。

en:
Divriği lies high in the Anti-Taurus on the Çaltı River, where the road from Sivas crosses toward the upper Euphrates. A steep citadel above the upper town watches the mountain route. In the ninth century the site was Tephrike, founded around 850 by Karbeas as the fortress-capital of the Paulicians, an Armenian Christian sect sometimes supported by the Muslim emir of Malatya; Byzantine forces retook it under Basil I. After Manzikert the Mengücekid Turks made the district into a small highland beylik. Their most striking buildings stand below the citadel: Ahmadshah built the Great Mosque in 1228, and Turan Malik, daughter of Fakhr al-Din Bahramshah, founded the adjoining house of healing. The architect Khurramshah ibn Mughith al-Khilati came from Ahlat, and the carved portals became the town's chief landmark. Süleyman Shah's castle above the complex dates to 1224. Bayezid I took the fortress in 1398 and handed it back to the Mamluks in 1401. In 1444 a Mamluk garrison held Divriği for Cairo, while Dulkadir Turcomans pastured flocks in the surrounding hills.

After Selim I's victory at Marj Dabiq in 1516, Divriği joined the Ottoman realm and was organized as a sanjak under the governor-general at Sivas. Wool and other highland goods changed hands on the caravan road to Harput, Arapgir and Zara. From the seventeenth century, armed bands based in the Tunceli mountains preyed on that traffic for about two centuries; when raiders reached Divriği, villagers withdrew behind the walls of the upper town and into the castle. The Mengücekid mosque and hospital were restored several times under Ottoman rule and formed the principal buildings inside those walls.
zh:
迪夫里伊位于安提托罗斯山地高处的恰勒特河畔，锡瓦斯通往幼发拉底河上游的道路经过此地。上城上方山势陡峭，城堡监视着山间通道。9世纪时，这里称特夫里凯，约850年由保罗派首领卡尔比亚斯建立，作为这个亚美尼亚基督教派别的要塞都城；马拉蒂亚的穆斯林埃米尔也曾支持保罗派。巴西尔一世在位时，拜占庭军队夺回此地。曼齐刻特战役后，门居杰克土耳其人在此建立山地小侯国。他们留下的最醒目建筑在城堡下方：艾哈迈德沙赫1228年修建大清真寺，法赫尔丁·巴赫拉姆沙赫的女儿图兰·梅莱克出资修建相邻的疗愈院；建筑师胡拉姆沙赫·本·穆吉斯·赫拉提来自阿赫拉特，精雕的大门成为城市地标。苏莱曼沙赫建于1224年的城堡耸立在这些建筑上方。巴耶济德一世1398年夺取要塞，1401年又把它交还给马穆鲁克。1444年，马穆鲁克驻军替开罗据守迪夫里伊，杜勒卡迪尔土库曼人在周围山地放牧。

1516年塞利姆一世在迈尔季·达比克击败马穆鲁克后，迪夫里伊并入奥斯曼，被编为桑贾克，隶属锡瓦斯总督。羊毛和其他高原物产在通往哈尔普特、阿拉珀吉尔和扎拉的商道上交易。17世纪起，盘踞通杰利山地的武装团伙袭扰这条商路约两百年；盗匪抵达迪夫里伊时，乡民便退入有城墙的上城和城堡。门居杰克时代的清真寺和医院在奥斯曼时期经过多次修缮，构成那些城墙内最主要的建筑群。

en:
Karahisar, the Karahisar-i Sahip of Ottoman registers and modern Afyonkarahisar, is a market town on the Akarçay plain beneath a volcanic rock crowned by a fortress, where the roads between Ankara, Konya, Kütahya and the Aegean lowlands meet. Byzantines knew the place as Akroinon. In 740 Leo III defeated an Arab siege army there; its commander Abdallah al-Battal later entered Turkish folk epic as the hero Battal Gazi, and the victorious city was renamed Nicopolis. Turkish lords took firm hold around 1210 and called it Kara Hisar, the black castle, after the rock rising some 200 metres above the houses. In 1275 the sons of the Seljuk vizier Sahip Ata founded their beylik at the foot of the rock, which gave the town the second half of its Ottoman name, and Germiyan absorbed it in the 1340s. The Ottomans took it under Bayezid I, lost it after Timur's victory at Ankara in 1402, and received it for good in 1429, when Yakub II of Germiyan bequeathed his lands. In 1444 Karahisar was a fortified Sunni Turkish sanjak town of pasture and caravan traffic, with the Seljuk Grand Mosque at the foot of the citadel.

Ottoman rule brought builders and schools. In 1472 the vizier Gedik Ahmed Pasha founded the open-court Stone Madrasa, counted by the sixteenth century among the higher-ranked Ottoman madrasas, and a Mevlevi lodge established by a follower of Rumi made Karahisar one of Anatolia's Mevlevi centres. Near the Grand Mosque and the bedesten rose the seventeenth-century Stone Han, with rooms for merchants and storage for caravan goods. Two products carried the district's name abroad: white marble from its quarries and poppy grown for opium. Documents of 1684 already pair the name Afyonkarahisar with Karahisar-i Sahip, and the poppy fields later made opium the district's most famous crop. Above the bazaars the rock fortress commanded the crossing of the western Anatolian roads.
zh:
卡拉希萨尔在奥斯曼册籍中称卡拉希萨尔-伊·萨希普，即今阿菲永卡拉希萨尔，是阿卡尔恰伊平原上的商镇，火山岩山顶筑有城堡，安卡拉、科尼亚、屈塔希亚与爱琴海低地之间的道路在城下相接。拜占庭时代这里叫阿克罗伊农。740年，利奥三世在此击溃围城的阿拉伯军队，敌军统帅阿卜杜拉·巴塔勒后来进入土耳其民间史诗，成为英雄巴尔塔勒·加齐，获胜后的城市也被改名尼科波利斯。约1210年，突厥统治者稳固占据此地，按高出城区约200米的黑色岩山称之为卡拉希萨尔，即「黑堡」。1275年，塞尔柱维齐尔萨希普·阿塔的儿子们在岩山下建立贝伊国，城镇奥斯曼语名字的后半截便来自这位萨希普；14世纪40年代其地并入格尔米扬。它在巴耶济德一世时归入奥斯曼，1402年帖木儿安卡拉获胜后得而复失，1429年格尔米扬的亚库布二世以遗赠交出土地，才最终归奥斯曼所有。1444年时，卡拉希萨尔是一座设防的逊尼派土耳其人桑贾克城镇，经营畜牧与商队贸易，城堡脚下坐落着塞尔柱时代的大清真寺。

奥斯曼统治带来了建筑和学校。1472年，维齐尔格迪克·艾哈迈德帕夏创办敞院式的石建伊斯兰学校，到16世纪它已跻身等级较高的奥斯曼经学院之列；鲁米一名弟子建立的梅夫拉维道堂，则使卡拉希萨尔成为安纳托利亚的梅夫拉维中心之一。17世纪，大清真寺和贝德斯坦附近建起石商队旅馆，供商人住宿、存放商队货物。两种物产把此地的名字带到外地：采石场出产的白色大理石，以及为制取鸦片而种植的罂粟。1684年的文献已把阿菲永卡拉希萨尔与卡拉希萨尔-伊·萨希普两个名字并用，罂粟田后来使鸦片成为这一带最出名的作物。集市上方，岩山城堡控扼着安纳托利亚西部诸路的会合点。

en:
Sultanönü is the older Turkish name for the country around Eskişehir, the Byzantine Dorylaeum. The town lies on the Porsuk River, where the road from Bursa climbs into the central Anatolian plateau through grain fields and pasture. Armies learned the ground early: on 1 July 1097, Kilij Arslan I nearly destroyed Bohemond of Taranto's crusader camp near Dorylaeum before other Christian columns reached the fight and defeated him.

South of the town, at Seyitgazi, a domed tomb and mosque were built in 1207 and 1208 over the grave of Battal Gazi, the Muslim warrior-saint of the Arab raids into Anatolia. Ümmühan Hatun, mother of the Seljuk sultan Alaeddin Keykubad I, founded the complex, which the Ottomans enlarged into a lodge, kitchens and stopping place for pilgrims and caravans. Eskişehir itself came to Osman Gazi in 1289, was lost for a time to the Karamanids, and returned to Ottoman rule under Murad I. In 1444 it was a grain market on the Ankara road.

The eastern road kept bringing soldiers and merchants through the district. During the Celali troubles, the rebel Deli Hasan held Eskişehir for a time in 1601. Its best-known local product was meerschaum, the soft white stone dug from the nearby hills and carved into pipes for Istanbul and European buyers. Grain, livestock, caravans and military convoys sustained the market town around that trade.
zh:
苏丹诺努是埃斯基谢希尔一带的旧突厥语名称，埃斯基谢希尔在拜占庭时代称多里莱乌姆。城在波尔苏克河畔，从布尔萨通往安纳托利亚高原内部的道路经过这里，两侧是粮田和牧场。军人很早就熟悉这片地形：1097年7月1日，基利杰·阿尔斯兰一世在多里莱乌姆附近几乎击溃塔兰托的博希蒙德所部十字军营地，其他基督徒援军赶到后才扭转战局并将他击败。

城南的塞伊特加齐建有圆顶圣墓和清真寺，位置在巴塔勒·加齐墓上。巴塔勒·加齐是阿拉伯人攻入安纳托利亚时期闻名的武圣；1207至1208年，塞尔柱苏丹阿拉丁·凯库巴德一世的母亲于姆哈顿主持修建这组建筑，奥斯曼时期又扩建成道堂、厨房，并接待朝圣者和商队。埃斯基谢希尔于1289年归奥斯曼·加齐所有，一度被卡拉曼侯国夺去，穆拉德一世时重回奥斯曼统治。1444年，它是安卡拉大道上的粮食集市。

东方大道继续把士兵和商人带到这一地区。杰拉里之乱期间，叛首德利·哈桑于1601年一度占据埃斯基谢希尔。当地最有名的物产是海泡石，匠人从附近丘陵采出白色软石，雕成烟斗卖给伊斯坦布尔和欧洲商人。粮食、牲畜、商队和军需车队，便围绕这门手艺维持着集镇的生计。

en:
Kangırı, ancient Gangra, holds a rocky height on the northern edge of the central Anatolian plateau, above the Acıçay and Tatlıçay streams that drain toward the Kızılırmak. Strabo described the place as both a residence of the kings of Paphlagonia and a garrison town. Its castle kept that value after the Danishmend Turks took it following Manzikert: the crusaders of 1101 could not storm it, and the Byzantine emperor John II Komnenos fought his way in during 1134 only to lose the town after his army withdrew.

Kangırı entered Ottoman lands under Murad I, but Timur returned it to its old lords after his victory in 1402; the Ottomans later recovered the fortress without the date being clearly recorded. In 1444 it was the seat of a district governor in the province of Anatolia, with sheep and goats pastured on the surrounding steppe and wool sold in the market below the citadel. Greek writers had already connected the old name Gangra with the Paphlagonian word for a goat, though the story may be no more than ancient wordplay.

The Ottoman period brought few sieges. As a sanjak centre, Kangırı lived mainly from its flocks, and Süleyman I commissioned its principal mosque, the Great Mosque, built by Sadık Kalfa in Mimar Sinan's period. The smaller Ali Bey Mosque carries an inscription from 1609. A garrison stayed in the old Paphlagonian fortress, while most houses, shops and wool stalls clustered beneath its walls.
zh:
堪基利古称甘格拉，位于安纳托利亚高原北缘的岩地上，阿哲恰伊河与塔特勒恰伊河从附近流向克孜勒河。斯特拉波曾把这里称作帕夫拉戈尼亚国王的居所，也是一座驻军城镇。达尼什曼德突厥人在曼齐刻特战役后夺取此地后，城堡的价值更加明显：1101年的十字军无法攻破它；1134年，拜占庭皇帝约翰二世率军苦战入城，但大军一撤，城镇便又失守。

堪基利在穆拉德一世时期进入奥斯曼版图，帖木儿1402年获胜后又把它交还给旧日领主，奥斯曼人后来收复这座要塞，只是具体年份没有清楚记载。1444年，这里是安纳托利亚省一个县长官的驻地，绵羊和山羊放牧在周围草原，羊毛在城堡下的集市出售。希腊作家曾把古名甘格拉与帕夫拉戈尼亚语中的「山羊」联系起来，不过这也许只是古人的文字附会。

奥斯曼时代，这里没有多少围城故事。作为桑贾克治所，堪基利主要靠畜群为生；苏莱曼一世敕建城中最重要的大清真寺，由萨德克·卡尔法在米马尔·希南所处的时代修成。较小的阿里贝伊清真寺留有1609年铭文。旧帕夫拉戈尼亚要塞里仍驻有守军，而多数房屋、店铺和羊毛摊都聚在城墙下方。

en:
Kırşehir, the Byzantine Mocissus, is a steppe town on the central Anatolian plateau where the roads from Konya and Ankara turn toward Tokat and Sivas. Seljuk Turks took it in the 1070s and named it Kır Şehri, the steppe city. Its name in those years came from its guilds and schools rather than any fortress. Ahi Evran, the Sufi who organised Anatolia's craftsmen into the Ahi brotherhood of thirty-two trades, with the tanners first among them, was killed here by the Mongols in 1261. The local emir Caca Bey built his medrese in 1272, a school where the lectures were given in Turkish, and the Turkish Sufi poet Aşık Pasha died here in 1332. Bayezid I's campaign of 1398 brought the Kırşehir country under Ottoman rule, so in 1444 it was a modest Turkish Muslim market town, its wool and leather carried off by passing caravans.

Those caravans crossed the Kızılırmak at Kesikköprü, a Seljuk stone bridge built in 1248 on the Kırşehir-Konya road. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries highwaymen held the approaches so firmly that travellers knew the crossing as the Cut Bridge.
zh:
克尔谢希尔古称莫西苏斯，是安纳托利亚高原草原上的城镇，科尼亚和安卡拉通往托卡特、锡瓦斯的道路在这里转弯。塞尔柱突厥人1070年代取城，命名为克尔谢希尔，意为「草原之城」。那些年里，它的名气来自行会和学校，而不是什么要塞。把安纳托利亚工匠组进阿赫兄弟会的苏菲阿赫·埃夫兰，1261年在此被蒙古人所杀；兄弟会统管三十二个行当，以制革匠为首。当地埃米尔卡卡贝1272年修建伊斯兰学校，校内以土耳其语授课，土耳其语苏菲诗人阿什克·帕夏1332年在此去世。巴耶济德一世1398年的远征把克尔谢希尔一带收入奥斯曼版图，因此1444年的这里是一座不大的土耳其穆斯林市镇，羊毛和皮革由过往商队运走。

商队在克西克桥渡过克孜勒河，这座塞尔柱石桥建于1248年，位于克尔谢希尔至科尼亚的道路上。17至18世纪，路匪牢牢把持桥头各路，旅人便把这个渡口称作「断桥」。

en:
Tokat stands where the Tokat Suyu runs into the Yeşilırmak, at the meeting of the Black Sea roads into central and eastern Anatolia, and the whole town lies under its citadel: twenty-eight towers run along a bare rock above the river. The fortress served the Ottomans as a prison for rebels and disgraced officials, and a persistent local tradition makes the Wallachian prince Vlad the Impaler one of its inmates when he was kept as a hostage in the 1440s. The Danishmend Gazi took the rock in 1074, the Rum Seljuks took the town in 1175, and Eretna and Kadı Burhaneddin held it in turn; when Kadı Burhaneddin died in 1398 the townsmen let Bayezid I in. Timur besieged the citadel in 1402 without success, and Tokat stayed in Mehmed I's hands through the Interregnum, becoming the first capital of the province of Rum. The earthquake of 1418-19 shook it badly, yet in 1444 its fortress, caravan market, copper shops and weavers still made it the chief administrative town on the empire's north-eastern road.

The register of 1455 counted 46 quarters and 3,079 households. In August 1472 Aq Qoyunlu troops under Bektaşoğlu Ömer Bey fought their way in, sacked the town and burned it; the register of 1485 found only 1,781 households. Tokat beat off a Safavid siege in 1505, though partisans of Nur Ali Halife soon opened the gates for a moment and had the Friday sermon read in Shah Ismail's name. Bayezid II added the Hatuniye mosque and medrese, and the households climbed back to 2,568 by 1574. The Celali disorders and the Great Flight then wasted the countryside around it, and Abaza Mehmed Pasha's rebels held the town briefly in 1623. On 17 August 1668 the strongest earthquake recorded in Turkey, of magnitude 8.0, shattered part of the citadel and walls, and the fire of 1679-80 destroyed much of what had been rebuilt.
zh:
托卡特位于托卡特河汇入耶希勒河之处，黑海通往安纳托利亚中部和东部的道路在此会合，全城都在要塞的俯临之下：二十八座塔楼顺着河上一座秃石山的山脊排成一圈。奥斯曼人把这座堡垒用来关押叛乱者和获罪官员，当地相传瓦拉几亚亲王「穿刺公」弗拉德15世纪40年代作为人质时就曾囚在其中。达尼什曼德·加齐1074年夺取此山，罗姆塞尔柱人1175年取城，其后埃雷特纳和卡迪·布尔汉丁相继统治；1398年卡迪·布尔汉丁死后，市民开门迎入巴耶济德一世。1402年帖木儿围攻要塞不克，整个大空位期托卡特都在穆罕默德一世手中，并成为鲁姆行省的第一个首府。1418至1419年的大地震破坏惨重，但到1444年，要塞、商队市场、铜器作坊和织户仍撑着它作为帝国东北大道首要行政城镇的地位。

1455年的地籍调查记载全城46个街区、3079户。1472年8月，贝克塔什奥卢·厄梅尔贝伊率白羊王朝军队攻入城内，洗劫后放火烧城；1485年再查时只剩1781户。1505年托卡特击退萨法维围攻，但努尔·阿里·哈利法的支持者很快一度开门献城，以伊斯玛仪沙的名义诵读周五呼图白。巴耶济德二世增建哈通尼耶清真寺和伊斯兰学校，到1574年户数回升至2568户。此后杰拉里动乱和「大逃亡」使周边乡村凋敝，1623年阿巴扎·穆罕默德帕夏的叛军又短暂占据托卡特。1668年8月17日，土耳其有记录以来最强烈的8.0级大地震震毁部分要塞和城墙，1679至1680年的大火又烧毁了大片重建起来的城区。

en:
Al-Sharqiyya, the eastern province, covers the Nile Delta's flank toward Sinai and the Levant. Its old fortress and caravan station at Bilbeis guarded the road from Cairo to the desert, and Fatimid administrators grouped the surrounding kura districts into an eastern province. Al-Kamil founded Mansura on the Damietta branch in 1219; after the Ayyubid repulse of the Fifth Crusade it received its name, 'the Victorious.' In 1250 Louis IX of France was captured in the same watery country after the Mansura campaign, and in 1260 Sultan Qutuz was assassinated at Salihiyya while returning from Ain Jalut. In 1444 Mamluk lords thus held a province of grain villages, river crossings and eastern marches, watchful for bedouin unrest and armies coming from Syria.

The Ottoman conquest of 1517 placed Sharqiyya under Cairo's new governors, but Mamluk households gradually recovered local power. Ali Bey al-Kabir, the Mamluk strongman who ruled Ottoman Egypt from 1767, stopped the tribute to Istanbul in 1769 and sent armies into the Hejaz and Syria before his fall in 1772. When the French invaded in 1798, Napoleon had the old works at Bilbeis repaired, and on 11 August the desert edge at Salihiyya saw the battle that opened the route toward Syria. French rule lasted only until 1801, when Ottoman and British intervention forced the evacuation; the returning Ottoman order then had to contend with years of Mamluk rivalry and the rising authority of Muhammad Ali in Cairo.
zh:
东部省位于尼罗河三角洲朝向西奈和黎凡特的一侧。古城贝勒比斯是要塞与商队驿站，扼守从开罗通往沙漠的道路；法蒂玛王朝的官员把周边的库拉行政区整合为东部大区。1219年，卡米勒在杜姆亚特河畔建立曼苏拉；艾优卜王朝击退第五次十字军后，这座城得到「胜利之城」的名字。1250年，法王路易九世在曼苏拉战役后的水网地带被俘；1260年，苏丹古图兹在艾因贾鲁特返程途中于萨利希耶遇刺。因此到1444年，马穆鲁克贵族掌握的是一片遍布粮村、渡口与东边通道的土地，既要防范贝都因人骚动，也要警戒从叙利亚方向来的军队。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，东部省归开罗新任总督管辖，但马穆鲁克家族逐渐夺回地方权力。1767年起主政奥斯曼埃及的马穆鲁克强人阿里贝伊·卡比尔于1769年停止向伊斯坦布尔纳贡，并派军进攻汉志和叙利亚，最终在1772年倒台。1798年法国入侵时，拿破仑下令修缮贝勒比斯旧工事；8月11日，沙漠边缘的萨利希耶爆发战役，打开了通往叙利亚的道路。法国统治只维持到1801年，奥斯曼与英国的干预迫使其撤军；恢复后的奥斯曼秩序随后又要应付连年的马穆鲁克内争，以及开罗的穆罕默德·阿里不断上升的权势。

en:
Al-Buhayra means 'the lake district,' a fitting name for the wetlands and farmlands of the western Nile Delta between Alexandria and Cairo. Its capital Damanhur, whose Coptic and pharaonic name meant 'town of Horus,' stood on the old Butic Canal and became a provincial seat under the Fatimids in the eleventh century. During the Middle Ages it prospered as a caravan town on the post road linking Cairo with Alexandria. An earthquake badly damaged it in 1302, and the Mamluk sultan Barquq later restored its fortifications as protection against Bedouin raids. In 1444 grain, river traffic and overland trade therefore moved through a marshy frontier province watched from Damanhur.

Egypt became an Ottoman province after the conquest of 1517, yet Mamluk emirs kept many offices and tax districts, and Buhayra's road between Cairo and Alexandria lost none of its importance. On 13 July 1798 that road and river line brought fighting to Shubra Khit: marching on Cairo, Napoleon formed infantry squares against Murad Bey's Mamluk cavalry while French and Ottoman flotillas clashed on the Nile. The Mamluks were unable to break the squares. Damanhur rose against the French in 1799; the revolt was crushed with great severity, with about 1,500 people killed. Anglo-Ottoman forces expelled the French in 1801, and in 1805 Muhammad Ali seized power in Cairo, opening a new era of central rule over the Delta.
zh:
布海拉意为「湖泊之地」，正适合形容尼罗河三角洲西部、亚历山大与开罗之间的湿地和农田。首府达曼胡尔的科普特与法老时代名称意为「荷鲁斯之城」，古城坐落于古布提克运河畔，11世纪法蒂玛王朝时成为行省治所。中世纪时，它作为开罗至亚历山大驿道上的商队城镇而繁荣。1302年的地震使城市损失惨重，马穆鲁克苏丹贝尔古格后来修复防御工事，以抵御贝都因人袭扰。1444年，粮食、河运和陆路贸易都要穿过这片沼泽纵横的边地，达曼胡尔则监视着四方通道。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，埃及成为帝国行省，但马穆鲁克埃米尔仍保留许多官职和税区，布海拉境内连接开罗与亚历山大的道路依旧重要。1798年7月13日，战火烧到舒卜拉希特的道路与河道：拿破仑向开罗进军时列出步兵方阵，抵挡穆拉德贝伊的马穆鲁克骑兵，法国与奥斯曼的小型舰队也在尼罗河上交战，马穆鲁克人无法冲破方阵。1799年，达曼胡尔起兵反抗法国，起义遭到严酷镇压，约一千五百人被杀。1801年，英国与奥斯曼军队将法国人逐出埃及；1805年，穆罕默德·阿里在开罗掌权，三角洲随之进入新的集权统治时代。

en: Atfih stands on the Nile's east bank, on the road and river route from Cairo into Upper Egypt. The Greeks knew the old town as Aphroditopolis, and its Ptolemaic tombs held the sacred cows of the goddess Hesat. In Mamluk records the surrounding district was called al-A'mal al-Itfihiyya, with its seat at al-Atfihiyya. In 1444 it was a Mamluk administrative district south of Cairo. Floods and raids by pastoral tribes destroyed its seat, al-Atfihiyya, and the district lost much of its importance; the narrow floodplain and limited farmland may also have contributed to its decline. Under Muhammad Ali after 1805, Giza became the seat of an independent district and Atfih was attached to it.
zh: 艾特菲赫位于尼罗河东岸，扼守从开罗通往上埃及的道路与河路。古希腊人称旧城为阿芙洛狄忒波利斯，当地托勒密时期墓葬曾安葬女神赫萨特的神牛。马穆鲁克文献称这一行政区为「伊塔菲哈辖区」，治所在艾特菲希亚。1444年，它是开罗以南的马穆鲁克行政区。洪水与游牧部落袭扰摧毁了治所艾特菲希亚，辖区的重要性大为下降；狭窄的泛滥平原与有限的耕地也可能促成了衰落。1805年后穆罕默德·阿里执政时，吉萨成为独立行政区的治所，艾特菲赫改隶其下。

en:
Esna, ancient Latopolis, lies on the Nile's west bank about 55 kilometres south of Luxor. The Ptolemaic and Roman temple of Khnum stood in the town centre, gradually buried by centuries of river silt, while the river crossing and markets made Esna a gathering point for villagers and desert traders. Badr al-Jamali founded the first Fatimid congregational mosque in 1081-1084, and its minaret, raised in 1081, still marked the Islamic town. In 1444 the Mamluk sultan governed a Sunni Egyptian river market whose livestock, crops and craft goods moved north by Nile boat and south toward the desert roads.

After the Ottoman conquest of 1517, imperial governors ruled in name while Mamluk beys long kept provincial power. In the 18th century Hassan Bey al-Jiddawi built Wekalet al-Jiddawi, an Esna caravanserai with about forty shops and upper chambers lodging merchants from Upper Egypt and the Sudan; gum arabic, ostrich feathers, textiles, oils, animals and crafts changed hands there. French troops campaigning in the Sa'id cleared part of the buried Khnum temple, while Hassan Bey resisted them at Bir Anbar on 2 April 1799. Following the French withdrawal in 1801 and Muhammad Ali's rise in 1805, Esna was brought back under a stronger Cairo administration.
zh:
伊斯纳古称拉托波利斯，位于卢克索以南约55公里的尼罗河西岸。托勒密和罗马时期的库努姆神庙坐落于城中心，后来在数百年河泥堆积中逐渐被埋；河渡与市集则使伊斯纳成为周边村民和沙漠商人的汇集地。拜德尔·贾马利于1081—1084年兴建法蒂玛时代第一座聚礼清真寺，1081年建成的宣礼塔长期标示着这座伊斯兰城镇。1444年，马穆鲁克苏丹统治着这座逊尼派埃及河港，牲畜、谷物和手工制品或由尼罗河北运，或沿沙漠商路南行。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，总督名义上治理此地，马穆鲁克贝伊却长期掌握地方实权。18世纪，哈桑贝伊·吉达维在伊斯纳修建杰达维商馆，约有四十间店铺，楼上房舍供来自上埃及和苏丹的商人住宿；阿拉伯胶、鸵鸟羽、纺织品、油、牲畜和手工制品都在此交易。法军征战赛义德期间，士兵清理了被埋的库努姆神庙的一部分，哈桑贝伊则于1799年4月2日在比尔安巴尔抵抗法军。1801年法军撤出、1805年穆罕默德·阿里崛起后，伊斯纳重新被更强有力的开罗政府管辖。

en:
Girga stands on the west bank of the Nile in one of Upper Egypt's broad floodplains. As Qus lost trade after the late fourteenth century, Girga rose to become the leading town of the Sa'id, with Mamluk officials, river merchants and Coptic communities sharing its markets and churches. In 1444 it was therefore a substantial provincial centre rather than a mere village: taxes and grain from the surrounding Nile villages were gathered there, and the town's Coptic see gave it an enduring place in southern Egyptian Christian life.

After the Ottoman conquest of 1517, Jirja became one of Egypt's sub-provinces, and Ottoman registers named it among the governorates through which Cairo ruled the south. In 1791 the Coptic scholar and theologian Yousab El Abah was appointed bishop of Girga and Akhmim and defended the Non-Chalcedonian position against Roman overtures. On 29 December 1798 General Desaix's French army reached Girga, then called the capital of Upper Egypt, and waited twenty days for an ammunition flotilla while Murad Bey sought help from the Hijaz, Nubia and the Red Sea coast. Local resistance continued, and the Battle of Girga took place on 7 April 1799. French rule ended in 1801, and after Muhammad Ali took power in 1805 the old southern governorate was drawn into his reformed Egyptian state.
zh:
吉尔贾位于尼罗河西岸一片开阔的冲积平原上。14世纪末古斯商路衰落后，吉尔贾崛起为赛义德的首要城镇，马穆鲁克官员、河运商人与科普特社群共用这里的市集和教堂。因此到1444年，它已是相当重要的地方中心，而不只是普通村落：周边尼罗河村庄缴纳的税赋和谷物汇集于此，当地的科普特主教区也使它在南部埃及基督教生活中长期占有一席之地。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，吉尔贾成为埃及的次级行政区之一，奥斯曼册籍也把它列为开罗统治南方的辖区。1791年，科普特学者、神学家优萨卜·艾卜哈被任命为吉尔贾和艾赫米姆主教，并在罗马教廷寻求教会合一时为非迦克墩立场辩护。1798年12月29日，德塞将军率领法军抵达当时被称为上埃及首府的吉尔贾，在此等候弹药船队二十天；穆拉德贝伊则向汉志、努比亚和红海沿岸求援。当地抵抗持续不断，1799年4月7日爆发了吉尔贾战役。1801年法国统治结束，1805年穆罕默德·阿里掌权后，这个古老南部辖区被纳入他改革后的埃及国家。

en: Farafra is the least populous and most isolated of Egypt's western oases, lying in a 980-square-kilometre depression midway between Bahariya and Dakhla. Its ancient Egyptian name meant 'land of cattle', while medieval Arabs called the springs there al-Farfarun. In Ptolemaic times the oasis was administered from Oxyrhynchus, and the mud-brick fort of Qasr al-Farafra was built to protect desert caravans. In 1444 Farafra was a scant watering place on the Mamluks' distant desert frontier, useful mainly for herds and traffic between oases. It shared the formal fate of the Western Desert when Ottoman conquest ended Mamluk rule in 1517, but Cairo's governors left few recorded marks on its isolated springs.
zh: 费拉菲拉是埃及西部诸绿洲中人口最少、也最孤立的一处，位于拜哈里耶和达赫莱之间、面积980平方公里的洼地。它的古埃及语名称意为「牛之地」，中世纪阿拉伯人则称当地泉群为费尔费伦。托勒密时期，这片绿洲由俄克喜林库斯管辖；盖斯尔·费拉菲拉的土坯堡垒最初是为保护沙漠商队而建。1444年，费拉菲拉只是马穆鲁克遥远沙漠边疆上一处稀少水源，价值主要在于牧放牲畜和维系绿洲间交通。1517年奥斯曼征服结束马穆鲁克统治后，它随整个西部沙漠改换宗主权，但开罗总督在这些偏远泉眼旁留下的记载很少。

en:
Ghurian lies west of Herat on the Hari Rud, its irrigated fields strung along the highway that runs from Mashhad into the Herat basin. The older town beside it, Pushang, was called the oldest city in Khorasan, said to have been founded by Shapur I. Arab governors held it for the Abbasids, and from their house came Tahir ibn Husayn, founder of the Tahirid dynasty. Ibn Hawqal in the tenth century found a walled city half the size of Herat with three gates, and its grapes and watermelons were still famous four hundred years later. The Mongols wrecked it, the Kurt rulers rebuilt it, Timur destroyed it again in 1381, and under Shah Rukh the town was restored; the congregational mosque raised in the Timurid age stood there, and the old city had become known as Ghurian.
