In 1444 it was the western gate and granary of Herat, watering its fields from the Hari Rud and sending grapes and melons to the city's bazaars.

Because the road from Iran to Herat runs through these fields, Ghurian was the first prize of every army moving on the city. Jahan Shah's Qara Qoyunlu passed this way in 1458; the Uzbeks of Muhammad Shaybani took it in 1507, Shah Isma'il retook it three years later, and Shah Tahmasp recovered it again in 1528, the long Safavid-Uzbek frontier wars finally ruining old Pushang. In 1716 the Abdali Afghans of Herat rose and ruled the district as their own until Nader Shah retook it in 1732; in 1747 it passed with Herat to Ahmad Shah Durrani. When Herat became an independent principality Ghurian was one of its four provinces, tossed from chief to chief by the border wars: Eshaq Khan Qara'i of Torbat-e Heydarieh took it in 1804, Firuz al-Din of Herat and the Hazara Banyad Khan each held it briefly, and after the Iranians seized it in 1818 it went to Mohammad Khan Qara'i, who still held it in 1821.
zh:
古里扬位于哈烈以西的哈里河畔，引水灌溉的田野沿着马什哈德通往哈烈盆地的大道铺开。紧邻它的普尚格旧城被称作呼罗珊最古老的城市，相传为沙普尔一世所建。阿拉伯总督曾替阿拔斯王朝镇守此城，塔希尔王朝的建立者塔希尔·伊本·侯赛因就出自这个总督家族。10世纪伊本·豪卡勒见到的普尚格有城墙环护，规模相当于半个哈烈，三门并峙；四百年后，这里的葡萄和甜瓜仍负盛名。蒙古人毁城，卡尔特王公加以重建，帖木儿1381年再度将其摧毁，到沙哈鲁时代城又恢复过来，帖木儿时期修建的聚礼清真寺就矗立在城中，旧城也以古里扬之名为人所知。1444年，它是哈烈的西部门户和粮仓，引哈里河水浇灌田地，把葡萄和甜瓜运往大城的巴扎。

伊朗通往哈烈的大路正穿过这片田野，所以每支进军哈烈的军队都先取古里扬。1458年贾汉沙的黑羊王朝军队经此而过；1507年穆罕默德·昔班尼的乌兹别克人夺城，三年后伊斯玛仪一世将其收复，1528年塔赫玛斯普一世又再度克复，萨法维与乌兹别克漫长的边境战争最终毁掉了普尚格旧城。1716年哈烈的阿布达里阿富汗人起事，割据此地自立，直到1732年纳迪尔沙将其收复；1747年它随哈烈归入艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼。哈烈成为独立公国后，古里扬是其四个行省之一，在边境战乱中被豪强你争我夺：1804年托尔巴特海达里耶的伊萨克汗·卡雷夺城，哈烈的菲鲁兹丁与哈扎拉首领巴尼亚德汗曾各自短暂据有，1818年伊朗军队取城后，它落入穆罕默德汗·卡雷之手，1821年仍由他占据。

en:
Sarakhs is the last oasis of the Hari Rud before the Karakum Desert, the midway halt between Merv and Mashhad on the caravan road into Transoxiana. In Samanid and Seljuk times it was a learned city: its libraries and madrasas drew scholars, Greek and Sanskrit works were rendered into Arabic there, and the Hanafi jurist Abu Bakr al-Sarakhsi, whose legal manuals were studied for centuries, taught in the town. Under the Seljuks its builders ran a famous school of architects, and the tombs of that age stand around the oasis: the shrine of the Sufi Abul Fazl, called Sarakhs Baba, and the Yarty Gumbez mausoleum raised eight kilometres to the south in 1089. The Mongols sacked the city in 1221 and burned its manuscripts; it was rebuilt under the Ilkhans and the Timurids but never regained its old size. In 1444 Sarakhs was a Timurid caravan town guarding the road to Merv.

Jahan Shah's Qara Qoyunlu ravaged the oasis on their march through Khorasan in 1458. In March 1459 Abu Sa'id Mirza of Samarkand met the rival Timurid princes of Khorasan and Merv, Ala al-Dawla, Ibrahim and Sultan Sanjar, in a battle between Merv and Sarakhs and routed them. The Uzbeks took Sarakhs in 1507, and Shah Isma'il recovered it after his victory at Merv in 1510; thereafter it remained a small Safavid border station between Khorasan and the Turkmen desert.
zh:
萨拉赫斯是哈里河进入卡拉库姆沙漠前的最后一片绿洲，也是梅尔夫与马什哈德之间、通往河中地区商道上的中途驿站。萨曼王朝和塞尔柱时期，它是一座学术名城：图书馆与伊斯兰学校吸引各地学者，希腊文和梵文典籍在此译成阿拉伯文，哈乃斐派法学家艾布·伯克尔·萨拉赫西曾在此讲学，他的法学教科书被沿用数百年。塞尔柱时期，城中的工匠办起著名的建筑师学派，那一时代的陵墓还散布在绿洲上：苏非艾布·法兹勒的圣陵，他被人称作萨拉赫斯·巴巴；以及1089年建于城南八公里的亚尔蒂·贡贝兹陵。1221年蒙古人洗劫此城，焚毁典籍；伊儿汗国和帖木儿时期虽予重建，却再未恢复旧观。1444年，萨拉赫斯是帖木儿治下戍守梅尔夫大道的商队城镇。

1458年，贾汉沙的黑羊王朝军队穿越呼罗珊时蹂躏这片绿洲。1459年3月，撒马尔罕的阿布·萨义德在梅尔夫与萨拉赫斯之间迎战呼罗珊和梅尔夫的敌对帖木儿宗王阿拉乌丁、易卜拉欣和苏丹·桑贾尔，将三人击败。1507年乌兹别克人取城，1510年伊斯玛仪一世在梅尔夫获胜后将其收复；此后它一直是呼罗珊与土库曼沙漠之间一座小型的萨法维边境驿站。

en:
Nishapur lies on a fertile plain below the Binalud Mountains, on the old road from central Persia into Transoxiana. Shapur I founded it in the third century as the capital of Abarshahr; it later became the Tahirid capital and, in 1037, the first Seljuk capital, ranking with Merv, Herat and Balkh among the four great cities of Khorasan. Caravans carried its silk, while the mines in the nearby hills supplied high-quality turquoise for at least two thousand years. Omar Khayyam, born here in 1048, was a mathematician and astronomer who helped design the Jalali calendar and left the quatrains later collected as the Rubaiyat. Attar of Nishapur, who lived here from the twelfth century into the early thirteenth, wrote The Conference of the Birds and shaped the Sufi poetry that influenced Rumi. In 1221 Tolui's Mongols sacked the city over ten days. The rebuilt town found new life northwest of the old ruins, and Ibn Battuta saw orchards and markets there and called it 'Little Damascus'. Earthquakes further reduced it before it submitted to Timur in 1381. In 1444 it was a smaller Sunni, Persian-speaking Timurid market town under Shah Rukh, still known for turquoise and silk.

Rival Timurid princes entered Nishapur only weeks after Shah Rukh died in 1447. During the rule of Sultan Husayn Bayqara in Herat, its Friday mosque was built in 1493. Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks took the city in 1507; Shah Ismail killed Shaybani at Merv in 1510, but Uzbek and Safavid border wars continued for decades. Shah Abbas recovered Nishapur in 1592, built a royal caravanserai there and had tax cuts inscribed on the Friday mosque in 1612. After Nader Shah died in 1747, Bayat chieftains held the city as a local khanate. Ahmad Shah Durrani took it with heavy artillery in spring 1751, and the Qajars added it to their realm in 1800.
zh:
尼沙布尔坐落在比纳卢德山下的肥沃平原，处在波斯中部通往河中地区的旧道上。3世纪时，沙普尔一世建此城作为阿巴尔沙赫尔首府；它后来成为塔希尔王朝都城，并于1037年成为塞尔柱人的第一个都城，与木鹿、赫拉特、巴里赫并称呼罗珊四大城。商队贩运这里的丝绸，附近山场至少两千年来出产上等绿松石。1048年出生于此的奥马尔·海亚姆是数学家、天文学家，曾参与制定贾拉利历，也留下后来结集为《鲁拜集》的四行诗。12世纪至13世纪初住在城中的阿塔写成《百鸟朝凤》，他的苏非诗影响了鲁米。1221年，拖雷麾下的蒙古军连攻十日洗劫此城。新城在旧墟西北恢复，伊本·白图泰见到果园和市集，称之为「小大马士革」。地震继续损耗城市，1381年尼沙布尔向帖木儿投降。1444年，它是沙哈鲁治下一座规模较小的逊尼派波斯语帖木儿商城，仍以绿松石和丝绸闻名。

1447年沙哈鲁死后仅数周，争夺王位的帖木儿宗王便进入尼沙布尔。忽辛·拜哈拉在赫拉特执政期间，城中聚礼清真寺于1493年建成。1507年，穆罕默德·昔班尼的乌兹别克人攻下这里；1510年伊斯玛仪在木鹿击杀昔班尼，乌兹别克与萨法维的边境战争却又延续数十年。1592年，阿拔斯沙阿收复尼沙布尔，随后在此修建皇家商队客栈，并于1612年把减税敕令刻在聚礼清真寺上。1747年纳迪尔沙阿死后，巴亚特部首领以尼沙布尔割据为汗国；1751年春，艾哈迈德沙阿·杜兰尼以重炮破城，恺加王朝在1800年将其并入版图。

en:
Jask is a sheltered harbour on a small Makran peninsula, near where the Strait of Hormuz opens into the Gulf of Oman. The Jagin river brings fresh water from the Bashagird hills, and the roadstead gave coasting craft a stop between the Persian Gulf, Gujarat and the Indus delta. Medieval geographers called it Jashk or Ras al-Jask; after 1330 Tahmtan ibn Turanshah governed there with the title Sultan Qutb al-Din. The arid country behind the port belonged to Makran amirs, Baloch chiefs who ignored distant overlords whenever no army could reach the coast. In 1444 Jask was a Sunni fishing and trading anchorage on the edge of the Timurid world, where ships took water and shelter.

In 1515 Shah Ismail I made an agreement with the Portuguese at Hormuz for action against the Makran amirs, whose raids then reached Jask. Shah Abbas I secured the coast only after suppressing Malik Shams al-Din's revolts in 1608 and 1613. English factors soon chose Jask for their first Iranian station: an East India Company ship from India arrived in 1616, and the factory opened in 1619. In December 1620 Rui Freire de Andrade's Portuguese fleet blocked two Company ships under Andrew Shilling and John Weddell; the fighting continued into January 1621 and was the first clash between European fleets in the Persian Gulf. Portuguese and Hormuzi forces later plundered Jask and its factory. The English later made Bandar Abbas their main Iranian port.
zh:
贾斯克是莫克兰海岸一座小半岛上的避风港湾，位于霍尔木兹海峡通入阿曼湾的出口附近。贾金河从巴沙格尔德山带来淡水，港外锚地可供沿岸船只在波斯湾、古吉拉特和印度河三角洲之间停靠。中世纪地理学家称它为贾什克或贾斯角；1330年之后，塔赫姆坦·本·图兰沙以苏丹·库特卜丁的称号统治此地。港后干旱原野归莫克兰诸埃米尔掌控，这些俾路支首领在没有军队抵达海岸时便不听远主号令。1444年，贾斯克是帖木儿世界边缘一座逊尼派渔业与贸易锚地，船只在此取水避风。

1515年，伊斯玛仪一世与盘踞霍尔木兹的葡萄牙人达成协议，请他们对付势力已抵达贾斯克的莫克兰埃米尔。阿拔斯一世在平定马利克·沙姆斯丁1608年和1613年的叛乱后，才真正控制海岸。英国商务员很快选定贾斯克作为他们在伊朗的第一个据点：东印度公司一艘船1616年自印度抵达，商馆于1619年开设。1620年12月，葡萄牙舰队封锁公司的两艘船只；战斗持续到1621年1月，是波斯湾内欧洲舰队之间的第一次交战。后来，葡萄牙和霍尔木兹武装洗劫贾斯克城与商馆。英国人随后把在伊朗的主要贸易转到阿巴斯港。

en:
Fasa sits in the wide plain of south-eastern Fars on the caravan road from Shiraz to Kerman, with Jahrom to its south. In the tenth century it ranked with the greatest towns of Fars, almost the equal of Shiraz. Its markets sold multicoloured, sometimes brocaded silks, fine carpets and safflower, and its brick Friday mosque was larger than the one in Shiraz. A Buyid civil war wrecked the town in 989-990, and in 1050 Alp Arslan swept down on it by night and carried off three million dinars' worth of plunder and three thousand captives; after the Shabankara tribesmen sacked it in their turn and the atabeg Chavli rebuilt it, Fasa never regained its old size. In 1444 it is a quiet Sunni Persian town under the Timurid governor of Fars in Shiraz, living on its orchards, its grain and the silk caravans passing through.

The armies that overran Fars reached Fasa in turn. The Qara Qoyunlu took Shiraz in 1452-1453, the Aq Qoyunlu overthrew them in 1467-1468, and Shah Ismail's Safavids took the province in 1504. Under Safavid rule Fasa gained its grand bazaar, congregational mosque and baths as its people turned to Shi'ism. Karim Khan Zand, ruling from Shiraz, settled the Chahar Lang Bakhtiari on farmland near the town in 1762-1763, and early in the nineteenth century the traveller Zayn al-Abedin Shirvani still found a pleasant township of some two thousand houses ringed by thirty villages, before famine, plague and disorder in the Qajar years wore it down. Jahrom, to the south among the palm groves, is the older town: its foundation is attributed to the Achaemenid king Artaxerxes I, and it was the birthplace of Barbod, the chief musician at the court of the Sasanian king Khosrow II Parviz. Its date palms, planted in Safavid and Zand times, made its name, and Qajar governors laid out its bazaar and caravanserais.
zh:
法萨坐落在法尔斯东南部的广阔平原上，地处设拉子通往克尔曼的商路，南面是贾赫罗姆。10世纪时它还名列法尔斯最大的城市之一，规模几乎与设拉子相当。市集上出售色彩绚丽、间或织锦的丝绸、精美地毯和红花，砖砌的聚礼清真寺比设拉子的那座还要大。989至990年白益王朝内战将它摧毁，1050年阿尔普·阿尔斯兰趁夜突袭，掠走价值300万第纳尔的财物和3000名俘虏；沙班卡拉部族随后又洗劫此城，虽经阿塔贝格·乔夫利重建，法萨再未恢复旧观。1444年，它是设拉子的法尔斯帖木儿长官治下一座安静的逊尼派波斯城镇，靠果园、麦作和过境的丝绸商队为生。

席卷法尔斯的军队也先后到达法萨：黑羊王朝1452至1453年攻取设拉子，白羊王朝1467至1468年取而代之，1504年伊斯玛仪沙的萨法维王朝又拿下全省。萨法维时期，法萨建起大巴扎、聚礼清真寺和公共浴场，居民也改宗什叶派。以设拉子为都的卡里姆汗·赞德在1762至1763年把巴赫蒂亚里人的四朗部安置在城边，拨给田地；19世纪初，旅行家扎因·阿比丁·希尔瓦尼见到的仍是一座约有两千户人家、四周环绕三十个村庄的宜人小镇，此后饥荒、瘟疫和动荡在恺加年间使它日益凋敝。南边椰枣林中的贾赫罗姆历史更久，据说建城者是阿契美尼德国王阿尔塔薛西斯一世，它也是在萨珊国王霍斯劳二世（帕尔维兹）宫廷中掌乐的乐师巴尔巴德的故乡。萨法维和赞德时期栽种的椰枣为它赢得声名，恺加的统治者又为它修建了巴扎和商队客栈。

en:
Darab, the ancient Darabgerd or 'Darius-town', lies in the warm south-eastern corner of Fars on the road towards Kerman, with Neyriz and the salt lake of Bakhtegan to its north. Legend ascribes its foundation to Darius I, and Ferdowsi names the city in the Shahnameh. Beside the old citadel of Kalah-i Darab, earthen ramparts run in a great ring about an isolated rock, and a giant bas-relief on a nearby cliff shows the triumph of the Sasanian king Shapur I over the Roman emperor Valerian, whom he had captured in 260. Ardashir I had made himself master of the town before he founded the Sasanian dynasty. Darab surrendered to the Arab army together with Fasa in 644 and kept its trade in textiles, jasmine oil and mumiya, a medicinal mineral balm. Seljuk raids in the eleventh century drove the people first to the Rombeh stronghold and then down to the present site. In 1444 Darab is a weathered district town under the Timurid governors in Shiraz, and Neyriz to the north still keeps its formidable castle and the Friday mosque dedicated in 951.

Darab changed masters with the rest of Fars: the Qara Qoyunlu came in 1452-1453, the Aq Qoyunlu in 1467-1468, and Shah Ismail's Safavids in 1504. Safavid kings made the district crown land, and it throve again, counted among the five vizier's seats of Fars, a standing it kept through the Zand eighteenth century. Qajar times brought strife instead: Turkic and Arab tribes pressed in around the town, and the campaigns fought against them battered the countryside until Darab fell far behind Shiraz.
zh:
达拉卜古称达拉卜吉德，意为「大流士之城」，坐落在法尔斯东南端通往克尔曼的暖热道上，北面是内里兹和巴赫泰甘盐湖。相传此城为大流士一世所建，菲尔多西的《列王纪》也提到它的名字。旧要塞卡拉伊·达拉卜旁边，夯土城墙围绕一块孤立的巨岩弯成巨大的圆环；附近崖壁上的巨型摩崖浮雕，刻的是萨珊国王沙普尔一世战胜260年俘获的罗马皇帝瓦勒良的凯旋场面。阿尔达希尔一世建立萨珊王朝之前，已先在此城立足。644年，达拉卜与法萨一同向阿拉伯军队归降，仍以织物、茉莉油和一种叫莫米雅的药用矿物香膏为贸易物产。11世纪塞尔柱人的袭扰迫使居民先退守龙贝要塞，再迁到今址。1444年，达拉卜是设拉子帖木儿长官治下一座历经战火的区城，北边的内里兹仍保有坚固要塞和951年落成的聚礼清真寺。

达拉卜随整个法尔斯一同易主：黑羊王朝1452至1453年来攻，白羊王朝1467至1468年继之，1504年又落入伊斯玛仪沙的萨法维王朝之手。萨法维国王把这一地区划为王室直领，此地再度兴旺，位列法尔斯五个维齐尔驻地之一，整个赞德王朝的18世纪都保有这一地位。卡扎尔时期带来的却是战乱：突厥和阿拉伯部落进逼城周，官府对部落连年用兵，乡野残破，达拉卜远远落在了设拉子之后。

en:
Kazerun holds the fertile plain between Shiraz and the Persian Gulf ports, on the caravan road down to Bushehr. Above the plain stand the ruins of Bishapur, one of the Sasanian Empire's capitals. Shapur I founded it in 266 after taking the Roman emperor Valerian at Edessa, and Roman captives laid it out on a Greek street grid that no other Iranian city followed; Hormizd I and Bahram I were born there, Valerian lived out his captivity in a palace built for him and by some accounts died in the city, where Shapur himself died in 270. Arab rule, a Shabankara sack in 1101 and an earthquake left Bishapur derelict and its people drifted down to Kazerun, which kept the old faith into the tenth century. The atabeg Chawoli curbed the Shabankara and rebuilt Kazerun in 1108, and the Mongols sacked the town in 1263.

Kazerun's own fame came from a Sufi order. Shaykh Abu Ishaq Kazeruni (c. 963-1035) founded the Kazeruniyeh, whose merchant-brothers kept hostels and carried its teaching and trade from India and China to Anatolia, collecting seafarers' vows from every ship that weathered the China Sea; Ibn Battuta saw the practice himself, and Shah Rukh prayed at the founder's tomb. In 1444 Kazerun was a wealthy Sunni market town, living on the gulf caravans and on pilgrims visiting its shrines.

Shah Ismail saw the order as a rival and marched on Kazerun in person: he slew its Sufi elders and installed an Afshar tribal family as governors, beginning with Khwaja Pir Budaq, and the town became a Safavid minting centre. In 1733 Nader Shah arrived in pursuit of the rebel Mohammad Khan Baloch and afterwards made Khwaja Ali Qoli Khan governor, who rebuilt the town and laid out the Bagh-e Nazar garden. His riflemen joined Karim Khan Zand in 1753 and, after Karim Khan's defeat at Kamarej the next year, helped him defeat Azad Khan Afghan. The family later backed Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar: in 1790 they tried to trap Lotf Ali Khan Zand, who escaped over the Qebleh hills to Dashtestan, returned to storm Kazerun and blinded their ruler Reza Qoli Khan.
zh:
卡泽伦占据设拉子与波斯湾港口之间的肥沃平原，地处通往布什尔的商道上。平原上方耸立着比沙普尔城址，它曾是萨珊帝国的都城之一。沙普尔一世266年在埃德萨俘获罗马皇帝瓦勒良之后下令建城，罗马战俘按希腊式棋盘格布局施工，这种规划在伊朗城市中再无第二例；霍尔木兹德一世和巴赫拉姆一世都出生在这里，瓦勒良在专为他修建的宫殿中度过囚徒岁月，据一些记载也死于此城，沙普尔本人则于270年在这里去世。阿拉伯人的统治、1101年沙班卡拉部落的焚城和一场地震使比沙普尔沦为废墟，居民陆续迁往山下的卡泽伦，卡泽伦直到10世纪仍信奉旧教。阿塔贝格·乔夫利1108年制服沙班卡拉人、重建卡泽伦，1263年蒙古人又洗劫了此城。

卡泽伦自己的声名来自一个苏菲教团。谢赫阿布·伊沙克·卡泽鲁尼（约963至1035年）创立卡泽鲁尼耶教团，教团的商人兄弟经营客店，把教义和生意从印度、中国一直带到安纳托利亚，凡平安渡过中国海的船只都要缴付许愿的布施；伊本·白图泰曾亲见这种做法，沙哈鲁也曾到创始人墓前礼拜。1444年的卡泽伦是一座富庶的逊尼派商业城镇，靠往来海湾的商队和前往圣陵的香客为生。

伊斯玛仪一世把教团视为敌手，亲自进兵卡泽伦，诛杀苏菲长老，改以阿夫沙尔部落的家族为总督，首任是赫瓦贾·皮尔·布达格，卡泽伦在整个萨非时期都是铸币中心之一。1733年，纳迪尔沙为追剿叛酋穆罕默德汗·俾路支抵达此地，事后任命赫瓦贾·阿里·库里汗为总督；后者招抚流民、修缮城池，还修建了纳扎尔花园。他手下的火枪队1753年加入卡里姆汗·赞德的军队，次年卡里姆汗在卡马雷季战败后，又助他击败阿扎德汗·阿富汗。这个家族后来倒向阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔：1790年他们设计围捕卢特夫·阿里汗·赞德，后者越过基卜勒山逃到达什特斯坦，随后回师攻破卡泽伦，刺瞎了他们的统治者礼萨·库里汗。

en:
Siraf, also called Shilaw, lies on a narrow strip of coast pressed between the mountains and the Persian Gulf. In the 9th and 10th centuries it was the richest port on the Iranian shore. Cargoes from India, East Africa and China came ashore here: spices, ivory, ebony, sandalwood, camphor, ambergris, pearls and precious stones. Ships bound for China left Basra, called at Siraf and crossed to Muscat and the Malabar Coast, and Abu Zayd Hasan, who described this run around 900, was himself a Sirafi merchant. Captains built multi-storey houses of teak imported from East Africa, and contemporaries reckoned a fine one might cost 30,000 dinars; the congregational mosque, begun in the first half of the 9th century, was one of the earliest in Iran. Istakhri ranked Siraf second only to Shiraz among the cities of Fars. An earthquake in 977 wrecked much of the city, and al-Maqdisi, who had called it a den of usury and extravagance, read the disaster as divine punishment. Pirates from Qays then harried its shipping and Gulf traffic sailed direct to Basra; by the 13th century Yaqut al-Hamawi found a small ruined place whose name had worn down to Shilaw. In 1444 it was a minor Fars anchorage, used by small craft crossing to Qatif and Arabia.

European travellers could still find the port: António Tenreiro called at 'Chilaão' in 1528, and Gasparo Balbi at 'Silaú' in 1590. Later visitors found only a fishing harbour at Taheri beside the old ruins, which James Morier described in 1812.
zh:
希拉夫（又译希劳）夹在高山与波斯湾之间的狭窄海岸上。9至10世纪，它是伊朗沿岸最富庶的港口，印度、东非和中国的货物在此上岸：香料、象牙、乌木、檀香、樟脑、龙涎香、珍珠和宝石。开往中国的商船从巴士拉出发，先泊希拉夫，再渡海前往马斯喀特和马拉巴尔海岸；约900年记述这条航线的阿布·扎伊德·哈桑本人就是希拉夫商人。船主们用从东非运来的柚木建造多层豪宅，时人估计一座好宅第要花三万第纳尔；9世纪上半叶动工的聚礼清真寺是伊朗最早的清真寺之一。在伊斯塔赫里的笔下，希拉夫是法尔斯仅次于设拉子的第二大城。977年的大地震毁坏了大半个城市，先前斥这里充斥高利贷与奢靡的穆卡达西，把这场灾祸看作天谴。盖斯岛的海盗随后不断袭掠商船，海湾航运改由巴士拉直航；到13世纪，雅古特·哈马维见到的只是一个残破小地方，名字也讹成了希劳。1444年，它是法尔斯治下的小锚地，只有小船从这里渡海前往卡提夫和阿拉伯半岛。

欧洲旅人仍找得到这座港口：安东尼奥·特内雷罗1528年到过「希劳」，加斯帕罗·巴尔比1590年称它为「西劳」。更晚的来访者只在塔赫里见到一座渔港，挨着古城废墟，詹姆斯·莫里尔1812年记述过那些遗址。

en:
Tabas is the chief oasis at the western edge of the Great Salt Desert, where roads from Yazd, Qumis, Kerman and Quhistan meet; al-Baladhuri called it 'the Gate of Khurasan'. Its palm groves gave it its early Islamic name, Tabas al-Tamr, 'Tabas of the Dates'. Tenth- and eleventh-century geographers describe a walled town fed by underground wells, with hot baths and lemon and orange groves planted around it. In the late eleventh century it joined the network of the Nizari Ismailis, who ran a chain of fortresses across Persia from Alamut and appointed their own governors over Quhistan; a Seljuk army under Ahmad Sanjar besieged Tabas in 1102. The Mongols spared the oasis and left its local rulers in charge of Tabas, Tun and Gonabad. In 1444 it was a small Sunni Timurid frontier oasis, valued because its water let caravans cross the desert.

Uzbek tribes occupied Khorasan in 1507. After Nader Shah was killed in 1747, the Zangu'i Arabs ruled Tabas and the neighbouring oasis of Tun as an independent state. In July 1754 they met an Afghan army under Ahmad Shah Durrani at Kakhk: the governor Ali Murad Khan was killed and his force destroyed in one of the bloodiest battles fought in Persia, and both oases fell. Durrani troops returned and sacked Tun and Tabas the next year after taking Nishapur. In Ahmad Shah's Khorasan campaign of 1769 and 1770, a Tabas chief, Ali Mardan Khan, led reinforcements toward Mashhad and was defeated and slain near Gonabad.
zh:
塔巴斯是大盐漠西缘的主要绿洲，亚兹德、库米斯、克尔曼和古希斯坦的道路在此汇合，拜拉祖里称之为「呼罗珊之门」。大片椰枣林使它在伊斯兰时代早期得名塔巴斯·塔米尔，意为「椰枣的塔巴斯」。10至11世纪的地理学家记述，此城城垣环绕，地下水井供水，城中有热水浴场，周围遍植柠檬和柑橘。11世纪末，塔巴斯并入尼扎里派伊斯玛仪人的据点网络；该派以阿剌模忒为中心在波斯据有一连串山堡，并向古希斯坦派任自己的长官。1102年，艾哈迈德·桑贾尔率塞尔柱军队围攻塔巴斯。蒙古人入侵波斯时放过这片绿洲，当地统治者继续管辖塔巴斯、图恩和古纳巴德。1444年，它是帖木儿帝国一座小型逊尼派边地绿洲，价值在于有了这里的水，商队才能穿越大漠。

1507年乌兹别克诸部占领呼罗珊。1747年纳迪尔沙遇刺后，赞古伊阿拉伯人以塔巴斯和邻近的图恩为中心建立独立政权。1754年7月，他们在卡赫克迎战艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼的阿富汗大军：长官阿里·穆拉德汗战死，所部被歼，是波斯史上最惨烈的战事之一，两座绿洲随即陷落。次年杜兰尼军队攻日内沙布尔后回师，洗劫图恩和塔巴斯。1769至1770年艾哈迈德沙再征呼罗珊，塔巴斯首领阿里·马尔丹汗率援军驰援马什哈德，在古纳巴德附近兵败被杀。

en:
Kashan sits on the western rim of the Dasht-e Kavir under the Karkas mountains, on the road between Qom and Isfahan. People lived at nearby Tepe Sialk as early as the sixth millennium BC, but the walled town grew under Buyid and Seljuk rule between the ninth and twelfth centuries, its houses of sun-dried brick and its fields fed by canals and qanats. The Persian word for glazed tile, kashi, comes from the town's name, and Yaqut al-Hamawi noted its green-glazed bowls sent abroad and a population entirely Twelver Shia, which earned Kashan the name Dar al-Muminin, 'abode of the faithful'. A Khwarazmshah army stormed it in 1197; when Hulagu's Mongols arrived in the 1250s the town was partly spared, by one account through Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's intercession. The astronomer Ghiyath al-Din Jamshid al-Kashi was born here around 1380 and did his best work at Ulugh Beg's Samarkand, computing pi to sixteen decimal places before his death in 1429. In 1444 Kashan was a Shia weaving town living from silk, with Timurid power fraying around it.

The Safavids made Kashan a retreat of the court. Ismail I and Tahmasp I granted the town tax exemptions, and Abbas I kept a residence there, laid out the Fin Garden completed in 1590 a few kilometres outside the walls, and opened an official mint. Its gold-brocaded silks and velvet were sold in Europe, and European travellers ranked its bazaars with those of London. As Shia orthodoxy hardened, the heterodox Nuqtavi circles were suppressed harshly. The shrine of Abu Lu'lu'a drew Shia pilgrims as well: by a Safavid-era legend, the Persian craftsman who killed Caliph Umar in 644 fled to Kashan and was buried there.

The Hotak Afghans overran Kashan in their invasion of 1722, and the rest of the century brought Nader Shah's wars and Zand faction-fighting. The earthquake of 1778 levelled the town, destroyed the buildings of Abbas I and killed some 8,000 people. Rebuilt under the Zands and Qajars, with a fresh building wave under Fath Ali Shah, Kashan kept its looms working into the nineteenth century, even as cheap European cloth undercut its workshops.
zh:
卡尚坐落在卡维尔盐漠西缘、卡尔卡斯山下，地处库姆通往伊斯法罕的大道。邻近的锡亚尔克台地公元前六千纪已有人居住，城垣环绕的卡尚则是9至12世纪白益王朝和塞尔柱时期发展起来的，土坯为屋，明渠和坎儿井浇灌田园。波斯语把琉璃砖称作「卡希」，名字便来自卡尚；雅古特·哈马维记载，当地绿釉碗远销外地，居民全是十二伊玛目派，卡尚因而得到「信士之城」（Dar al-Muminin）的称号。1197年花剌子模军队攻破此城；13世纪50年代旭烈兀的蒙古人抵达时，卡尚得以免遭大劫，一说赖纳西尔丁·图西说情。天文学家吉亚斯丁·贾姆希德·阿尔-卡西约1380年生于卡尚，后在撒马尔罕的兀鲁伯宫廷把圆周率算到小数点后十六位，1429年去世。1444年的卡尚是一座以丝绸为生的什叶派织城，帖木儿王朝的控制力正在它四周松动。

萨法维王朝把卡尚作为宫廷的休憩之地。伊斯玛仪一世和塔赫玛斯普一世赐予免税特权，阿拔斯一世在此驻跸，在城外几公里处修起1590年完工的菲恩花园，又开设官营铸币厂。金线锦缎和天鹅绒销往欧洲，欧洲旅人把卡尚的巴扎与伦敦的市集相提并论。什叶派正统收紧后，异端的努克塔维派遭到残酷镇压。阿布·卢厄卢阿圣祠也吸引什叶派信众：相传这个波斯工匠644年刺杀哈里发欧麦尔后逃到卡尚，最终葬于此地，这一说法在萨法维时期已经流传。

1722年阿富汗霍塔克人攻陷卡尚，随后的一个世纪里，这里又经历纳迪尔沙的征战和赞德王朝的内讧。1778年的大地震将全城夷平，阿拔斯时代的建筑尽毁，约八千人罹难。城市在赞德和卡扎尔时期重建，法塔赫·阿里沙时又掀起营建热潮。卡尚的织机一直运转到19世纪，廉价的欧洲布匹也在此时开始压过本地作坊。

en:
Tun was one of the two chief cities of medieval Quhistan, paired with Qa'en, on the desert road between central Iran and Mashhad. Its walled old city opened through five gates. Nasir Khusraw in the eleventh century called Toon a large city, and Marco Polo named the whole south Khorasan district after the pair together. Quhistan was the southern base of the Nizari Ismailis, who kept a string of fortresses here under governors appointed from Alamut. Mongol troops sacked and destroyed Tun in 1239, yet the town recovered and held its rank among the region's main markets. In 1444 it was a Sunni Muslim city of the Timurid Empire, watching over the arid caravan route that ran from Yazd and Tabas toward Nishapur and Mashhad.

Uzbek tribes overran Khorasan in 1507, and after Nader Shah died in 1747 Tun passed into the Zangu'i Arab state centred on Tabas. Ahmad Shah Durrani's Afghans took the town for the first time in early 1751, on their invasion of Afsharid Khorasan. It submitted again in the summer of 1754, after the Tabas army was cut to pieces at Kakhk, and the year after that, once Nishapur had fallen, Durrani troops turned back and sacked the oasis.
zh:
图恩是中世纪古希斯坦两座首要城市之一，与加延并称，坐落在伊朗中部通往马什哈德的沙漠商路上。古城环有城墙，开五座城门。11世纪纳赛尔·霍斯鲁称图恩为大城，马可·波罗记载南呼罗珊时也以这两座城合称整个地区。古希斯坦是尼扎里派伊斯玛仪人的南方重地，他们在这一带据有一连串山堡，长官由阿剌模忒委派。1239年蒙古军队洗劫并摧毁图恩，但此城后来恢复，仍位列这一地区的主要市场。1444年，它是帖木儿帝国的逊尼派城市，扼守亚兹德、塔巴斯通往内沙布尔和马什哈德的干旱商路。

1507年乌兹别克诸部席卷呼罗珊。1747年纳迪尔沙死后，图恩并入以塔巴斯为中心的赞古伊阿拉伯人政权。1751年初，艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼的阿富汗军队入侵阿夫沙尔王朝治下的呼罗珊，首次攻占此城。1754年夏，塔巴斯军队在卡赫克被歼，图恩再度投降；次年内沙布尔陷落后，杜兰尼军队回师洗劫了这片绿洲。

en:
Saveh, rendered Sava or Sawei in Chinese sources, is a well-watered oasis in Jibal, the upland also called Iraq-e Ajam, where the road out of Ray divides toward Hamadan, Qazvin, Qom, Isfahan and Kashan. The town mattered most under the Seljuks, when rulers and atabegs kept winter quarters here; in 1118 the Seljuk princes Mahmud II and his uncle Sanjar fought a battle outside its walls. Its Friday mosque preserves a free-standing brick minaret of 1110 or 1111, inscribed with the name of its patron Abu Shuja Muhammad ibn Malikshah. Medieval readers also knew Saveh through an old story: Marco Polo called the city Saba in his Travels and recorded the local tradition that the Three Magi had set out from here and lay buried in three great tombs, side by side, their bodies still whole. Shia memory kept a grimmer event: in 816 the caravan of Fatima Masumeh was attacked here, and she was carried poisoned to Qom to die. The Mongols burned Saveh's celebrated libraries, and Timur's forces sacked the town again. In 1444 it was a Sunni, Persian-speaking market town on the western edge of Shah Rukh's Iranian lands, answering to his grandson Sultan Muhammad ibn Baysunghur at Ray.

For half a century after 1447 Qara Qoyunlu, Aq Qoyunlu and Timurid armies disputed the oasis. Safavid rule gave the Friday mosque its present skyline: in 1516 or 1517 a master builder from Qom raised a tiled outer shell over the old dome, and the qibla iwan followed in 1539 or 1540 as Saveh was brought into Twelver Shia Iran. Glazed pottery had been a local craft since Seljuk times and outlasted the fall of rival Ray, and Saveh kilims were woven from the Safavid period on. In the summer of 1725 Afghan Hotak troops beat Tahmasp Mirza outside the walls and took the town by siege; Nader Shah's victories reopened the road, but the Qajar choice of Tehran as capital drew traffic and influence northward.
zh:
萨瓦（中文资料又译萨韦）是吉巴勒、又称阿贾姆伊拉克的高原上一座水源充足的绿洲，雷伊出来的道路在此分向哈马丹、加兹温、库姆、伊斯法罕和卡尚。萨瓦在塞尔柱时代最为繁盛，统治者和阿塔贝格在此设冬宫；1118年，塞尔柱宗王马哈茂德二世还与叔父桑扎尔在城外交战。聚礼清真寺现存一座独立砖造宣礼塔，建于1110或1111年，铭文刻着施主阿布·舒贾·穆罕默德·伊本·马利克沙的名字。中世纪的人还因一个古老传说知道萨瓦：马可·波罗在游记里称此城为萨巴，记下当地说法，三位博士从这里出发去朝拜圣婴，死后并排葬在三座大墓中，遗体仍须发完好。什叶派信众记得的则是另一桩惨事：816年法蒂玛·玛苏玛的商队在此遇袭，她中毒后被送往库姆，在那里去世。蒙古人焚毁了萨瓦著名的藏书，帖木儿军又再度洗劫城市。1444年的萨瓦是沙哈鲁伊朗领地西缘一座说波斯语的逊尼派集镇，听命于驻在雷伊的皇孙苏丹·穆罕默德·伊本·拜宋豁儿。

1447年后的半个世纪里，黑羊、白羊和帖木儿军队反复争夺这座绿洲。萨法维时代，聚礼清真寺有了现存的面貌：1516或1517年，一位库米匠师给旧穹顶加上瓷砖外壳；1539或1540年又建成礼拜方向的拱门，萨瓦也被纳入十二伊玛目派的伊朗。彩釉陶器自塞尔柱时代起便是本地名产，在对手雷伊衰败后仍延续不辍；萨法维时代起，当地还织造萨瓦基利姆毯。1725年夏，阿富汗霍塔克军在城外击败塔赫玛斯普·米尔扎，再经围攻夺取萨瓦；纳迪尔沙阿的胜利使道路重新通行，但卡扎尔王朝定都德黑兰，把商路和势力都引向北方。

en:
Soltaniyeh stands on a high cold plain east of Zanjan, next to the older town of Abhar, on the Ilkhanid summer pastures beside the road from Tabriz to central Iran. Arghun Khan pitched his camp here, and his son Öljaitü built the place up from 1302 into an imperial capital, celebrating its completion in 1313. His wall ran 30,000 paces around the city, and at its centre he raised an octagonal mausoleum with a double-shelled brick dome nearly 25 metres across and about 50 metres high, one of the largest brick domes in the world and the model for the later domes of Khoja Ahmed Yasavi's tomb and the Taj Mahal. Baptised a Christian as a boy and later a Shia, Öljaitü meant the shrine to receive the bodies of Ali and Husayn until the ulama persuaded him otherwise. Allama al-Hilli taught Shia doctrine in the Ghiyathiyya madrasa, Dominican and Franciscan friars were numerous enough for the pope to erect an archbishopric here in 1318, and caravans carried the city's silk and pearls as far as Venice. The capital did not long outlive its founder: after Abu Sa'id died in 1335 the city shrank, Timur stormed it, and his son Miran Shah had Öljaitü's body removed and the tomb demolished; when Clavijo came in 1404, workmen were already pulling the mausoleum down. In 1444 Soltaniyeh belonged in name to Shah Rukh's Timurid realm, and three years later Jahan Shah of the Qara Qoyunlu made it his first prize in Iran.

Venetian envoys later in the century counted only 6,000 or 7,000 inhabitants. Under the Safavids it served as a halting place on the road from Tabriz to the shahs' summer pastures; Chardin stopped there, and the Ottoman wars of Shah Abbas's time battered what was left. The Qajars used it last: the town lay on the Tehran–Tabriz road to the crown prince's seat, and Fath-Ali Shah spent sixteen summers there reviewing troops and receiving envoys. In 1812, during the Russian war, he began a palace on a mound north of town from the stone of the Ilkhanid ruins. Around it the old capital had gone back to grassland, and the stripped brick dome stood over an empty plain.
zh:
苏丹尼耶位于赞詹以东高寒的平原上，毗邻更古老的阿卜哈尔城，大不里士通往伊朗中部的大道经过这里，沿途草原本是伊儿汗诸汗的夏营地。阿鲁浑汗曾在此扎营，其子完者都从1302年起把它营建成帝国都城，1313年大庆竣工。城墙周长3万步，城中央是他为自己修建的八角形陵墓：双层砖壳穹顶直径近25米、高约50米，是世界上最大的砖穹顶之一，后来霍贾·艾哈迈德·亚萨维陵和泰姬陵的穹顶都取法于它。完者都幼年曾受洗为基督徒，后来改宗什叶派，本想把阿里和侯赛因的遗骸迁来安葬，被宗教学者劝止。阿拉玛·希里在吉亚西耶经学院讲授什叶派教义；多明我会和方济各会的修士在此信众甚多，教皇1318年专门设立苏丹尼耶总教区；商队把城中的丝绸和珍珠一直运到威尼斯。这座都城的兴盛几乎随它的建造者一同结束：1335年不赛因死后城市萎缩，帖木儿攻破此城，其子米兰沙又命人掘走完者都的遗骸、拆毁陵墓；1404年克拉维约路过时，工匠正在拆除陵庙。1444年的苏丹尼耶名义上属沙哈鲁的帖木儿帝国，三年后黑羊王朝的贾汉沙把它作为征服伊朗的第一块战利品。

15世纪后期，路过的威尼斯使节数出居民只剩六七千人。萨法维时期，苏丹尼耶是大不里士通往国王夏牧场路上的宿站，夏尔丹曾在此停留，阿拔斯时代对奥斯曼的战争又摧残了残存的城郭。最后经营它的是卡扎尔王朝：它处在德黑兰至大不里士、通往王储驻地的大道上，法塔赫-阿里沙有十六个夏天在这里阅兵、接见使节。1812年对俄战争期间，他在城北的高地上动工修建行宫，石料就取自伊儿汗故城的废墟。故城周围重新变成牧场，剥去装饰的砖穹顶立在空旷的平原上。

en:
Rasht lies on the damp Caspian plain between the Goharrud and Zarjoub rivers, a day's ride from the lagoon port of Anzali. Rain feeds the mulberry woods around it, and one old reading of its name derives the word from reshtan, to spin thread, after the silk that has always been its trade. Arab records already call it Dar al-Marz, the 'abode of the border', in 682, and medieval geographers describe a large market village set in rain-forest and enriched by the raw silk of the country round it. West of the Sefid Rud, the rain-soaked half of Gilan called Bia-pas was ruled by the Eshaqvand, Shafi'i Sunni sayyids who held their court at Fuman; Timur's cavalry never mastered these marshes. In 1444 the sayyids still governed in their own fashion, and Rasht on the plain was their market town, where Gilani merchants gathered the silk that went out by ship from Anzali.

Shah Abbas ended the local sayyid dynasties in 1592 and three years later made Rasht the capital of Gilan and the seat of the raw-silk trade. Persian, Armenian, Russian and Greek merchants crowded in, the open ditches were covered and the bazaar paved, and women's coloured silk-thread needlework, rashti-duzi, became a craft of the town. Disaster filled the century that followed: the Cossack Stenka Razin sacked it in 1669, an earthquake levelled it in 1714, and Peter the Great's troops held it from 1722 until the Treaty of Resht returned it to Iran in 1732. The town was built again, and under the Qajars camel-loads of silk cocoons went out through Anzali to Russia; Russian, British and Ottoman consuls all kept houses in Rasht.
zh:
拉什特坐落在潮湿的里海平原上，夹在戈哈拉德河与扎尔朱卜河之间，距潟湖港口安扎利只有一天路程。雨水滋养着四乡的桑林，关于城名有一种古老的解释，说它来自动词「拉丝坦」，意为纺线，取自这里世代经营的蚕丝。682年的阿拉伯文献已称它为「达尔·马尔兹」（边境之地），中世纪地理书把它记成雨林中一座靠生丝致富的大集镇。萨菲德河以西湿润的半边吉兰称「比阿普斯」，由奉逊尼派沙斐仪教法的伊沙克万德圣裔统治，王庭设在富曼，帖木儿的骑兵始终没能征服这片沼泽。1444年，圣裔们仍按自己的方式理政，平原上的拉什特是他们的市镇，吉兰商人在此收丝，运往安扎利装船出海。

阿拔斯一世1592年灭掉地方圣裔王朝，三年后把拉什特定为吉兰省会和生丝贸易中心。波斯、亚美尼亚、俄罗斯和希腊商人涌来，露天沟渠被覆盖，市集铺了路面，妇人用彩色丝线绣成的「拉什特绣」也成了城中名产。随后的一百年灾祸接连不断：哥萨克首领斯坚卡·拉辛1669年洗劫此城，1714年地震将它夷平，1722年彼得大帝的军队进驻，直到1732年《拉什特条约》才把它归还伊朗。城市再度重建，卡扎尔时期，一驮驮蚕茧经安扎利运往俄罗斯，俄国、英国和奥斯曼都在城里设有领事馆。

en:
Astara lies where the forested Talysh mountains meet the Caspian, on the coastal road between Gilan, Baku and the Caucasus. The Hudud al-'Alam of 982 already names it as Astarab, and in the fourteenth century it became the seat of the Ispahbads of Gilan, a small Talysh principality whose old stronghold of Shandan stood just north of the Astara river; the poet Qasim-i Anvar called Astara the seat of the sipahbad Jalal al-Din Husayn. In 1444 the local dynasty still held this wet, wooded frontier between Ardabil and Shirvan.

From the sixteenth to the eighteenth century the Talysh khans of Astara ruled this coast, autonomous or tributary to Gilan and Ardabil. In 1668–69 Stenka Razin's Cossack flotilla swept these waters and looted the ports between Baku and Rasht. The Talysh khanate formed after Nader Shah's death in 1747 first kept its capital here, until Gara Khan moved it north to Lankaran. The khanate accepted Russian protection in 1802, yet Persian troops retook Lankaran in 1809; General Kotlyarevsky stormed its citadel on 1 January 1813, and the Treaty of Gulistan later that year drew the border along the Astara river and cut the town in two.
zh:
阿斯塔拉位于林木茂密的塔雷什山与里海相接之处，扼守吉兰、巴库与高加索之间的沿海道路。982年成书的《世界境域志》已以「阿斯塔拉布」之名提到它；14世纪时，这里成为塔雷什人小王朝吉兰伊斯帕赫巴德的驻地，旧堡尚丹就在阿斯塔拉河以北不远。诗人卡西姆·安瓦尔曾称阿斯塔拉为长官贾拉鲁丁·侯赛因的治所。1444年时，这个本地王朝仍在阿尔达比勒与希尔凡之间潮湿多林的边地上维持统治。

16到18世纪，阿斯塔拉的塔雷什诸汗统治这段海岸，或自行其政，或向吉兰和阿尔达比勒的长官称臣纳贡。1668—1669年，斯捷潘·拉辛的哥萨克船队席卷这一带海域，洗劫巴库到拉什特之间的港口。1747年纳迪尔沙死后形成的塔雷什汗国最初以此地为都，加拉汗随即将都城北迁连科兰。汗国1802年接受俄罗斯保护，波斯军队却在1809年夺回连科兰；1813年1月1日科特利亚列夫斯基强攻拿下连科兰要塞，同年《古利斯坦条约》沿阿斯塔拉河划定边界，城镇就此分成两半。

en:
Sari lies on the humid Caspian plain where Alborz forests slope down toward the shore. Its lemon and orange groves suggested the old name Saru, the 'yellow city', and some geographers identify the site with Zadracarta, the greatest city of Hyrcania. Farrukhan the Great of the Dabuyid dynasty rebuilt it in the seventh century and named it for his son Saruyeh. Sari then served the rulers of Tabaristan, the forested mountain country that kept caliphal armies at a distance and sheltered Alid sayyids. Mir-i Buzurg, one of those Twelver Shia sayyids, founded the Marashi dynasty in 1359 and ruled from Sari, Amol and Vatashan. Timur's army sacked and burned the city during its 1392-93 campaign. In 1444 Sari was again a Marashi seat, its bazaars and gardens lying on the road that climbed from the silk-producing Caspian lowlands to Rey.

The Marashis held Mazandaran until 1596, when Shah Abbas I brought the province directly under Safavid rule. His mother came from nearby Behshahr, and in 1611-12 he began Farahabad north of Sari as a winter capital, linked to the older city by a stone causeway. The hill palace looked toward the Caspian and the Alborz; Reza Abbasi painted its murals, a German craftsman made goldwork for it, and Persian gardens were laid out around the court. Georgians, Circassians and Armenians were settled in the province to promote silk and wine production. Pietro della Valle visited in 1618 and compared Farahabad's walls with those of Rome and Constantinople, and Abbas died there in 1629. Stenka Razin's Cossacks sacked the palace city in 1668, and Russian troops occupied the coast in 1723. After Nader Shah's death opened years of khan wars, Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar proclaimed Sari his capital in 1782 and had its goldsmiths make a crown; he moved the court to Tehran four years later.
zh:
萨里位于湿润的里海平原，厄尔布尔士山林从城后伸向海岸。城郊的柠檬和柑橘林使人把它与古称萨鲁的「黄色之城」联系起来，也有地理学家认为这里就是希尔卡尼亚最大城市扎德拉卡尔塔。7世纪，达布亚王朝的法鲁汉大帝重建此城，以儿子萨鲁耶的名字命名。此后萨里成为塔巴里斯坦统治者的都城；这片山林和低地长期挡住哈里发的军队，也收留了阿里派圣裔。1359年，十二伊玛目派圣裔米尔·布祖尔格建立马拉什王朝，以萨里、阿莫勒和瓦塔善为治所。1392至1393年，帖木儿的军队攻陷并焚毁萨里。1444年，萨里重又成为马拉什圣裔的治所，巴扎和花园位于出产丝绸的里海低地通往雷伊、翻越厄尔布尔士山的道路旁。

马拉什王朝保有马赞德兰，直到1596年沙阿·阿拔斯一世把该省直接纳入萨法维版图。他的母亲来自附近的贝赫沙赫尔。1611至1612年，他在萨里以北动工修建冬都法拉哈巴德，并用一条石砌堤道把它和萨里相连。山丘上的宫殿可眺望里海与厄尔布尔士山，礼萨·阿巴西为宫殿绘制壁画，一名德意志工匠制作金饰，宫廷周围布置了波斯式花园。格鲁吉亚人、切尔克斯人和亚美尼亚人被迁入马赞德兰，以推动丝绸和酒类贸易。1618年彼得罗·德拉·瓦莱到访，曾把法拉哈巴德城墙的周长比作罗马和君士坦丁堡；1629年，阿拔斯在这里去世。1668年，斯捷潘·拉辛率领的哥萨克洗劫这座离宫城，1723年俄国军队又占领海岸。纳迪尔沙死后，各路汗王混战多年，阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔于1782年宣布以萨里为都，命城中金匠打造王冠，四年后把宫廷迁往德黑兰。

en:
Malamir sits in a high basin of the Bakhtiari Zagros, three days’ climb through the mountains from Shushtar. Elamite kings and the later Elymaean princes cut rock reliefs above the valley, six of them in the gorge of Kul-e Farah and others at Eshkaft-e Salman. Islamic geographers knew the town as Idaj, seat of the Hazaraspid atabegs of Greater Lur; their citadel crowned the town and gave it its Luri name Mal al-Amir, ‘the amir’s estate’, which survives as Malamir. When Ibn Battuta passed through in the fourteenth century it was still a royal city in the mountains. In 1444 it lay under the loose lordship of the Lur rulers of the Zagros, overshadowed by the Bakhtiari clans, the Astarki, Janaki and their kin, whose first arrival in the valleys is recorded in 1413. Local memory held that when atabak rule ended in 1453 the townspeople abandoned the crumbling houses for tents and flocks.

The Safavids made Greater Lur into Bakhtiari country: in 1566 Shah Tahmasp named the Astarki chief Tajmir first ilkhan of the Bakhtiyari, and his successor Jahangir Khan divided the tribes into the Haft Lang and Chahar Lang, the two confederations that shaped all their later history. The plain of ruined Malamir became winter pasture, its wool worked into Bakhtiari carpets and felt, and dead chieftains were carried to Shahsavar and buried beneath carved stone lions. Nader Shah marched repeatedly against the rebel Ali Murad Khan, executed him and deported Chahar Lang clansmen to Khorasan; they fought well before Kandahar and made their way back to the Zagros after his murder in 1747. In 1750-52 Ali Mardan Khan Bakhtiari contended with Karim Khan Zand for the mastery of western Iran, and when Karim Khan prevailed in 1764 he disarmed the tribes and transplanted thousands of Haft Lang families to Qom and Varamin. Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar harried them again in 1785.
zh:
马拉米尔位于巴赫蒂亚尔扎格罗斯群山中的一处高盆，从舒什塔尔出发要在山里攀行三天。埃兰国王和后来的埃利迈斯王公在谷顶凿下岩刻，库勒法拉赫峡谷存六幅，埃什卡夫特萨勒曼另有若干。伊斯兰地理学家把这座城称作伊达季，它是大洛雷斯坦哈扎尔阿思普阿塔贝格的都城，城堡高踞城上；卢尔语称此地为「马拉·阿米尔」，意为「埃米尔的庄园」，省读便是马拉米尔。14世纪伊本·白图泰路过时，它仍是群山之中的王都。1444年，它只在扎格罗斯卢尔诸王的松散治下，声势已被1413年起陆续迁入山谷的阿斯塔基、贾纳基等巴赫蒂亚尔氏族盖过。当地人记得，1453年阿塔贝格统治终结后，居民抛下倾颓屋舍，住进帐篷、放牧畜群。

萨法维王朝把大洛雷斯坦变成了巴赫蒂亚尔人的土地：1566年塔赫玛斯普一世任命阿斯塔基部首领塔季米尔为巴赫蒂亚尔第一位伊尔汗，继任者贾汉吉尔汗把诸部编为哈夫特朗与查哈朗两大联盟，此后数百年的部落史都围绕二者展开。马拉米尔荒城周围的平原成了冬牧场，出产的羊毛织成巴赫蒂亚尔地毯和毛毡；死去的首领被送到沙赫萨瓦尔，葬在雕凿的石狮之下。纳迪尔沙屡次征讨反叛的阿里穆拉德汗，将他处死，把查哈朗部众流放呼罗珊；这些人在坎大哈城下苦战立功，1747年纳迪尔沙遇刺后才辗转返回扎格罗斯。1750至1752年，巴赫蒂亚尔首领阿里马尔丹汗与卡利姆汗·桑德争夺西伊朗霸权；1764年卡利姆汗取胜，解除部落武装，把数千户哈夫特朗人迁往库姆和瓦拉明。1785年阿迦·穆罕默德·卡扎尔再度攻掠。

en:
Termez stands on the Amu Darya at one of the river's chief crossings, where the roads from Bukhara and Samarkand pass south to Balkh and India. It was already an ancient city when the Arabs reached the Oxus: most scholars now place Alexandria on the Oxus here, and under the Kushan kings it was a Buddhist centre, whose monasteries at Kara-tepe and Fayaz-tepe drew the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang in the seventh century; he counted about ten monasteries and a thousand monks. The city also gave Islamic learning two famous sons, the hadith compiler al-Tirmidhi and the Sufi master al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, whose tomb drew pilgrims. Genghis Khan's army took Old Termez in 1220 after a two-day siege and put the people to the sword; the rebuilt town rose two miles back from the river, where Ibn Battuta in the fourteenth century found canals and bazaars, grapes and quinces of excellent flavour, and bathhouses that kept jars of milk for washing hair.

In 1444 the city belonged to the Timurids, its sayyid families claiming descent from Muhammad, and Shah Rukh was enlarging al-Hakim's shrine.

In 1449 Ulugh Beg gathered his troops here before marching on Balkh against his rebel son Abd al-Latif. Shaybani Khan's Uzbeks took Termez in 1506, and in 1571-72 Abdullah Khan II of Bukhara had to storm it after a siege when Padishah Muhammad Sultan refused to submit. Outside the city lay Kyr Kyz, a ninth-century caravanserai or summer palace; its name, Forty Girls, comes from a tale of a princess and her forty companions who died defending the country against invaders. By the later eighteenth century Termez had emptied to the villages of Salavat and Pattakesar, set among the old ruins.
zh:
铁尔梅兹位于阿姆河畔，扼守河上一处主要渡口，布哈拉、撒马尔罕南下巴尔赫和印度的道路都从这里过河。阿拉伯人抵达阿姆河时，它已是一座古城：学界多把乌浒河畔亚历山大城的故址定在此处；贵霜诸王治下，它是佛教中心，城郊卡拉特佩和法雅兹特佩的寺院在7世纪引来中国僧人玄奘，他记下这里约有十座寺院、上千名僧人。这座城还走出两位伊斯兰学术名人：汇集圣训的提尔密济，以及圣陵受人参拜的苏菲学者哈基姆·提尔米兹。1220年，成吉思汗的军队围城两天后攻破旧铁尔梅兹，屠戮居民；新城在离河两英里处重建，14世纪伊本·白图泰见到这里水渠纵横、市肆相连，葡萄和榅桲味道极美，连澡堂都备着成罐的牛奶供人洗头。

1444年，铁尔梅兹属于帖木儿王朝，城中的赛义德家族自称是穆罕默德后裔，沙哈鲁当时正在扩建哈基姆圣陵。

1449年，乌鲁伯格在此集结大军，随后进军巴尔赫，讨伐举兵反叛的儿子阿卜杜勒·拉蒂夫。昔班尼汗的乌兹别克军1506年攻取铁尔梅兹；1571—1572年，帕迪沙·穆罕默德苏丹据城抗命，布哈拉的阿卜杜拉汗二世围城才将其降服。城外有克尔克兹，突厥语意为「四十姑娘」，是一座9世纪的商队客栈或夏宫，名字来自一则传说：一位公主和她的四十名女伴抵御入侵者，战死在这片土地上。到18世纪后期，城池已经荒废，居民散入旧遗址间的萨拉瓦特和帕塔凯萨尔等村。

en:
Kish, the town later called Shahrisabz, lies in the Kashkadarya valley about eighty kilometres south of Samarkand. It was old even by Sogdian standards, and is the likely site of Nautaca, where Alexander the Great wintered and met Roxana in 328-327 BC. After the Arab conquest the Kashkadarya valley became the centre of the revolt of al-Muqanna, the Veiled One, whose followers, the Men in White Clothes, fought the caliph's armies through the eighth century. The pastures around Kish later passed to the Barlas tribe, and in 1336 Timur was born at Khoja-Ilgar outside the walls. He ruled from Samarkand but spent treasure on his birthplace: in 1380 craftsmen carried off from conquered Khwarezm began the Ak-Saray, the White Palace, meant to outdo all his other buildings; its two gate-towers rose sixty-five metres, and above the entry ran the inscription 'If you challenge our power, look at our buildings'. Ulugh Beg built the blue-domed Kok Gumbaz Friday mosque in 1437 in honour of his father Shah Rukh. In 1444 Kish remained in the Timurid realm, governed from Samarkand.

Near the mosque stood the Dorus-Saodat complex, with the tomb of Jahangir, Timur's eldest son, beside a mosque said to hold the grave of the imam Amir Kulal, teacher of Timur's house. Timur's own body was carried to Samarkand for burial in 1405. Abdullah Khan II of Bukhara stormed Kish in 1556 and attached it to the new Karshi province. In the mid-eighteenth century the Uzbek Kenagas tribe turned the district into a semi-independent beylik; the Manghits took Bukhara in 1785, but the mountain lords of Shahrisabz and Kitab kept their walled towns and much of their autonomy within the khanate.
zh:
基希后来改称沙赫里萨布兹，坐落在撒马尔罕以南约80公里的卡什卡河谷。以粟特的标准看，它也算得上古城，学界多认为古城那乌塔卡就在此处；公元前328至前327年，亚历山大在此过冬，并结识了罗克珊娜。阿拉伯征服后，卡什卡河谷成为一场反阿拉伯起义的中心，首领是阿拉伯语所称的「蒙面者」，他的追随者「白衣人」在8世纪与哈里发的军队长年作战。基希周围的牧场后来归巴鲁剌思部所有，1336年帖木儿出生在城外的霍贾伊尔加尔。他虽以撒马尔罕为都，却把大量钱财花在出生地：1380年，从被征服的花剌子模掳来的工匠开始营建阿克萨赖宫，即「白宫」，规格要压过他所建的一切；两座门塔高65米，入口上方刻着铭文：「若要质疑我们的力量，就看看我们的建筑。」1437年，乌鲁伯格为纪念父亲沙哈鲁，建起蓝顶的库克贡巴兹聚礼清真寺。1444年，基希仍在帖木儿王朝境内，由撒马尔罕方面统辖。

清真寺附近是多尔·萨阿达特建筑群，里面葬着帖木儿的长子贾汉吉尔，旁边一座清真寺相传葬有这个家族的导师、伊玛目阿米尔·库拉尔。帖木儿本人1405年死后，被送往撒马尔罕安葬。1556年，布哈拉的阿卜杜拉汗二世攻下基希，把它并入新设的卡尔希省。18世纪中叶，乌兹别克克纳加斯部把这一地区经营成半独立的伯克领地；1785年曼吉特王朝取得布哈拉，但沙赫里萨布兹和基塔布的山地首领据守城寨，在汗国内保住了很大自治权。

en:
Saidabad, the later name of Sirjan, lies on a high plain west of Kerman, on the Kerman-Shiraz road where tracks branch south toward the Persian Gulf. Under the Abbasid caliphs Sirjan shared the status of capital of Kerman with the city of Kerman, and medieval geographers praised it highly: Ibn Hawqal and al-Muqaddasi called it the greatest city of the province, wider than Shiraz, with eight gates, two bazaars and tall walls, and a congregational mosque whose minaret was fitted by Adud al-Dawla with a curious wooden mechanism that partly turned. Its water ran from two qanats dug by Amr and Tahir, sons of Layth al-Saffar, and sugarcane, fruit and wealthy houses filled the town. The last Sasanian king, Yazdgerd III, lodged in its palace while fleeing the Arab conquest in the 640s. Nearby Sang Castle went back to Sasanian times, and an inscription there dated 1387 names the Muzaffarid ruler Imad al-Din Ahmad. In 1444 the district was a Persian-speaking Timurid frontier land, its flocks, wool and caravans linking the Kerman plateau with Fars and the Gulf.

The medieval town later shifted its site three times. Under the Qajars the settlement at Saidabad became the nucleus of the city of Sirjan, and a new bazaar served the caravan trade that returned to the old road.
zh:
赛伊达巴德是锡尔詹后来的名字，位于克尔曼以西的高原，地处克尔曼通往设拉子的大道，另有小路南通波斯湾。阿拔斯哈里发时期，锡尔甘与克尔曼城同为克尔曼地区的首府。中世纪地理学家对它称赞有加：伊本·豪盖勒和穆卡达西称它是全省最大的城市，比设拉子还开阔，有八座城门、两座巴扎和高耸的城墙；聚礼清真寺的宣礼塔上，阿杜德·道莱装了精巧的木制机关，有一部分能够转动。城里的水来自两条坎儿井，是萨法尔人莱伊斯的两个儿子阿慕尔和塔希尔开凿的；蔗糖、水果和富商宅邸充满城中。末代萨珊国王伊嗣俟三世在640年代躲避阿拉伯人时，曾在城中的宫殿落脚。附近的石堡始于萨珊时期，堡中一方1387年的铭文提到穆扎法尔王朝的伊马德丁·艾哈迈德。1444年，这片地区是帖木儿王朝治下说波斯语的边疆，羊群、羊毛和商队把克尔曼高原同法尔斯和波斯湾连在一起。

这座中世纪城市后来三次迁址。卡扎尔时期，赛伊达巴德的定居点成为锡尔詹城的核心，一座新巴扎为重回老路的商旅服务。

en:
Ifugao is the steepest country of the Cordillera, where rivers cut south through folded mountains toward the Magat and lowlanders seldom went. Its people call themselves the people of the hill, and in 1444 they farmed the slopes around villages such as Kiyyangan, growing taro, trading gold and beeswax down to the plains, and following wealthy kadangyan clans rather than kings. They set carved wooden bulol guardians in their granaries and chanted the hudhud epics at their feasts. No outside power had entered these mountains, and the Ifugao answered to no state.

The Spaniards who overran the coasts of Luzon found the Cordillera a harder country. Expeditions pushed up the Magat valley between 1591 and 1594 and brought back the first Spanish accounts of the Ygolote highlanders, and the loss of the lowlands drove the Ifugao deeper into the range. Between 1600 and 1700 they gave up taro for wet rice and carved the great terraced mountainsides, field walls climbing ridge after ridge, the largest earthworks in the Cordillera; the new fields fed a growing population and bound the villages together against the lowland government. Punitive columns in the 1770s and 1790s tried to force highlanders into reduccion settlements while forts watched the Magat below, but in 1821 the terraces and the villages that built them remained outside Spanish control.
zh:
伊富高是中科迪勒拉山最险峻的地方，河谷向南穿过层叠群山通向马加特河，低地人很少进去。他们自称「山上之民」。1444年，伊富高人在基扬甘等村落周围的坡地上种植芋薯，把黄金和蜂蜡运下平原交易；他们没有国王，由富有的卡丹阳氏族统领，谷仓里供着木雕的布洛尔守护神，宴会上传唱胡德胡德史诗。还没有外来政权进入这些大山，伊富高人不属于任何国家。

征服吕宋海岸的西班牙人发现，中科迪勒拉是一块更难啃的土地。1591至1594年，远征队沿马加特河谷上行，首次留下西班牙人对「伊戈洛特」山民的记载；低地失陷，把伊富高人更深地赶入群山。1600至1700年间，他们弃芋种稻，在山坡上凿出大片梯田，田埂顺着一道道山脊层层攀高，是中科迪勒拉规模最大的土方工程；新稻田养活了增长的人口，也把各村凝聚起来，对抗低地的殖民政权。1770和1790年代，西班牙又派出讨伐队，企图把山民强行迁入归并村，并在下游马加特河畔筑堡监视，但直到1821年，这些梯田和修筑它们的村落仍不在西班牙人治下。

en:
Laguna de Bay is the great freshwater lake southeast of Manila Bay, and its southern shore was Tagalog rice country. Boats carried the harvest across the lake and down the Pasig River to the markets of Tondo, and barangays such as Bay, Pila and Lumban fed the chiefs of Tondo and Maynila. The oldest document in the Philippines, the Laguna Copperplate of 900, was written here: it acquits a debtor before Jayadewa, Lord of Pailah, the place now called Pila. Later tradition makes Bay and its neighbours the domain of a chief named Gat Pangil. In 1444 the lakeside datus stood within the orbit of the lakan of Tondo.

Juan de Salcedo overran the district in 1571 with a hundred Spanish-Mexican soldiers, and Martín de Goiti received about 8,000 tribute-payers there, one of the largest encomiendas of the early conquest. The Franciscan Juan de Plasencia arrived in 1578, laid out Bay, Majayjay, Pila and Lumban as parish towns, baptised their people and wrote the Doctrina Cristiana, the first book printed in the Philippines. Twice the lakeside hills sheltered Chinese rebels from Manila: fugitives of the 1603 Sangley rising were run to ground in the San Pablo highlands, and in 1639 another band fortified the ridges above Cavinti and Lumban before surrendering at Pagsanjan the next year. Bay remained the provincial capital until 1688, when the seat moved to Pagsanjan. During the British occupation of Manila, Captain Thomas Backhouse's men sacked Pagsanjan hunting for the silver cargo of the galleon Filipina, but Francisco de San Juan carried the hoard through to Simón de Anda in Pampanga.
zh:
内湖湾是马尼拉湾东南的大淡水湖，湖南岸是他加禄人的稻米之乡。米船穿过湖面、沿巴石河下行，把收成运往汤都的市场，巴彦、皮拉、隆班等巴朗盖供养着汤都和马尼拉的首领。菲律宾最古的文献、900年的拉古纳铜版铭文就出自此地：铭文记载一名债务人在帕伊拉（今皮拉）领主阇耶提婆面前免除债务。后世传说把巴彦一带归在首领加特·邦吉尔名下。1444年，湖岸诸达图都处在汤都拉干的势力圈内。

1571年，胡安·德·萨尔塞多率一百名西属墨西哥士兵征服此地，马丁·德·戈伊蒂受封约八千名纳贡者，是征服初期最大的监护征赋区之一。方济各会士胡安·德·普拉森西亚1578年来此，把巴彦、马海海、皮拉、隆班建成堂区城镇，为居民施洗，并写成菲律宾最早付印的书籍《基督教义》。湖岸山地两次收容从马尼拉逃出的华人起事者：1603年「生理人」起事的残部被追剿至圣巴勃罗山区；1639年另一支队伍据守卡文蒂和隆班上方的山脊，次年在百胜滩投降。巴彦作为府治直到1688年，之后府治迁往百胜滩。英军占领马尼拉期间，托马斯·巴克豪斯上尉的部队洗劫百胜滩，搜求大帆船「菲律宾人号」上的白银，弗朗西斯科·德·圣胡安却把这批财宝送到了邦板牙的西蒙·德·安达手中。

en:
Mindoro faces Luzon across a narrow sea, and Chinese records knew it as Ma-i or Mait. The Song annals name it in 972, and Zhao Rugua's Zhu Fan Zhi of 1225 describes its trade in detail. When a junk entered the anchorage it registered at the official plaza and gave the local chiefs white parasols as gifts; island traders then carried the porcelain, iron pots and coloured beads away to other islands and came back in September or October with beeswax, cotton, pearls and tortoiseshell, and the Chinese author says none ever broke their bargain. The same account speaks of bronze Buddha images among the islanders. Mangyan clans farmed the interior, while the southern anchorages of Mangarin and Caminawit drew junks and Malay prahus. In 1444 Muslim settlers tied to Brunei and Maynila held stretches of the coast, Lubang to the north paid tribute to Rajah Sulayman, and the Mangyan kept to the highlands.

Spaniards first explored Mindoro in 1570 and found enough gold to call it Mina de Oro, 'gold mine', a name later compressed into Mindoro. In 1572 Juan de Salcedo sailed its west coast and burned the Muslim village on Lubang. The coastal villages were granted as encomiendas, but war and the slave trade emptied much of the island, and refugees crossed to Batangas. In 1602 Moro fleets sacked the Spanish towns and built a fort at Mamburao. Iranun raiders returned in force in 1757 with 74 prahus and carried islanders off to the slave market of Jolo, until a Spanish expedition of 1,200 men destroyed the Mamburao fort in 1766. Caminawit later became the seat of the southern presidencia.
zh:
民都洛与吕宋隔海相望，在中国载籍中称麻逸。《宋史》在972年已记其国，1225年赵汝适的《诸蕃志》更详述了它的贸易情形：中国帆船驶入锚地后，先在官市前登记，向当地首领赠送白伞；岛上商人随即把瓷器、铁锅和彩珠携往其他岛屿，到九、十月间带着蜂蜡、棉布、珍珠和玳瑁回来，书中说他们从不爽约。同书还提到岛民家中有铜佛像。芒扬人诸部在内地农耕，南部的曼加林、卡米纳维特锚地吸引着中国帆船和马来快船。1444年，与文莱和马尼拉有联系的穆斯林居民已占据沿海多处，北方的卢邦岛向拉惹·苏莱曼纳贡，芒扬人退居山地。

1570年西班牙人首次探查民都洛，因发现黄金而称之为「金矿」（Mina de Oro），后缩读为民都洛。1572年胡安·德·萨尔塞多沿西岸航行，焚毁卢邦岛上的穆斯林聚落。沿岸村落被封作监护征赋区，但战乱和奴隶贸易使岛上大半人口流失，难民渡海逃往八打雁。1602年，摩洛舰队洗劫西班牙人城镇，并在曼布劳修筑堡垒。1757年伊拉农人集结七十四艘快船大举重来，把岛民掳往霍洛的奴隶市场；1766年一支一千二百人的西班牙远征军摧毁了曼布劳堡垒。卡米纳维特后来成为南部行政长官的驻所。

en:
Buglas was the old Hiligaynon name of Negros, a long island lying across the Tañon Strait from Cebu; the word was understood to mean 'cut off', as though the island had once broken from a larger land. Dark-skinned Ata foragers of the Negrito peoples ranged its interior mountains, while Visayan villages lined the coasts. The shore settlement that became Silay was called Carobcob, 'to scratch', for the way its people raked tuway clams out of the sand at low tide. The western coast stood under the nominal sway of the Kedatuan of Madja-as in Panay, and the east looked to the rajahs of Cebu. Local legend tells of Princess Kansilay, who led her village against pirate raiders sword in hand and was killed in the fight; a kansilay tree grew from her grave and gave the later town its name. In 1444 the islanders sailed the Visayan seas in large outrigger boats and kept their old Visayan rites.

Legazpi's men reached the island in April 1565 and, seeing the Ata, named it Negros. Carobcob was granted as an encomienda in 1571 to Cristobal Nuñez Paroja, one of the seventeen soldiers who had come with Legazpi. Moro slave-raiders harried the coasts from the late 1500s, and the Spanish commander on the island answered with flight rather than resistance: in 1760 the people of Silay left their shore village and rebuilt it behind a palisade between the Matagoy and Panaogao rivers, at the place later called Estaca after the stockade. Negros was governed from Oton in Panay until 1734, when it became a military district with its capital at Ilog, later moved to Himamaylan. By 1818 the island counted about 200 Spanish-Filipino families, and Silay alone was a town of more than 200 houses.
zh:
布格拉斯是米沙鄢语对内格罗斯岛的旧称。这座长形大岛与宿务隔着塔尼翁海峡相望，旧名意为「割断」，仿佛它曾从一块更大的陆地断裂开来。肤色黝黑的阿塔人属于尼格利陀族群，在中部山地游猎，米沙鄢人的渔村则沿海岸散布。日后发展为锡莱的滨海聚落原名卡罗布科布，意为「刨挖」，得名于居民趁退潮在沙滩上刨挖蛤蜊的生计。西岸名义上臣属班乃岛的马加斯，东岸则受宿务诸位拉惹影响。当地相传，坎西莱公主曾持剑率领村民抵御海盗，战死之后坟头长出一棵坎西莱树，后来的城镇便以此为名。1444年，岛民驾着大型舷外支架船往来于米沙鄢诸海，奉行米沙鄢旧俗。

1565年4月，莱加斯皮的部下抵达此岛，因见到阿塔人而称之为内格罗斯。1571年，卡罗布科布被封作监护征赋区，受封者是随莱加斯皮远征的十七名士兵之一。16世纪末叶起，摩洛掳奴船队不断袭扰海岸，岛上的西班牙长官采取先躲避、不抵抗的方针：1760年锡莱居民离开海边旧村，在马塔戈伊河与帕纳奥高河之间树起木栅、另建新村，那一带也因这座栅寨得名埃斯塔卡。内格罗斯长期由班乃的奥通管辖，1734年成为军区，以伊洛格为首府，后来迁往希马马兰。到1818年，全岛约有二百个西班牙—菲裔家庭，仅锡莱一镇便有二百余栋房屋。

en:
Cebu, called Sugbu by its Visayan people, is a narrow island in the central Philippines, its east-coast harbour looking across the strait toward Bohol. The Zhufan Zhi of 1225 may describe the island as Suwu, a sea country whose beeswax, tortoiseshell, cotton, agarwood and sea produce drew Chinese porcelain, silk, salt, rice and trade gold. By the 15th century the harbour was a line of coastal houses around the rajah's palace and an open square at Singhapala. Its rulers used Sanskrit titles, and Visayan oral legend traces the dynasty to Sri Lumay, a half-Tamil, half-Malay prince from Sumatra. In 1444 Cebu was an Indianized rajahnate whose chiefs lived by the port traffic and had to defend it against raiders from Mindanao.

Ferdinand Magellan's ships entered Sugbu on 7 April 1521. Rajah Humabon welcomed the Spaniards and was baptized, but Magellan was killed on 27 April while fighting Lapulapu on Mactan, and the surviving fleet sailed away. Miguel Lopez de Legazpi returned on 27 April 1565, scattered Visayan boats with cannon and forced Rajah Tupas to terms. The wooden work begun on 8 May became Fort San Pedro, the core of the first permanent Spanish settlement in the Philippines. In a burned house a Spanish soldier found the Sto. Nino image given to Humabon's queen in 1521, and a church was later raised on the spot. Legazpi moved the colonial government to Manila in 1571, yet Cebu stayed the main Spanish town in the Visayas, with its own Chinese Parian and diocese. Raids from the Muslim south led the garrison to replace the wooden fort with stone; its gate bears the date 1738.
zh:
宿务，米沙鄢人称作苏格布，是菲律宾中部一座狭长岛屿，东岸港湾隔着海峡面向保和。1225年《诸蕃志》记载的束务国可能就是这里；岛上输出蜂蜡、玳瑁、棉布、沉香和海产，引来中国瓷器、丝绸、盐、米和贸易用黄金。到15世纪，港湾沿岸屋舍连绵，拉者宫殿和广场所在的辛格帕拉是统治中心。统治者使用梵语头衔，米沙鄢口述传说把王朝追溯为来自苏门答腊的半泰米尔、半马来王子斯里·卢迈的后裔。1444年的宿务是一个印度化拉让国，首领们依靠港市贸易为生，也要防备棉兰老来的袭掠者。

1521年4月7日，麦哲伦的船队驶入苏格布。拉者·胡玛邦欢迎西班牙人并接受洗礼，但麦哲伦在4月27日进攻马克坦岛时被拉普拉普所杀，幸存船队随后离去。1565年4月27日，米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮重返此地，用火炮驱散米沙鄢战船，并迫使拉者·图帕斯议和。5月8日动工的木构工事后来成为圣佩德罗堡，也是菲律宾第一个永久西班牙人定居点的核心。一名西班牙士兵在焚毁的屋舍中发现了1521年麦哲伦赠给胡玛邦王后的圣婴像，后来人们在发现地建起教堂。1571年莱加斯皮把殖民政府迁往马尼拉，但宿务仍是西班牙人在米沙鄢的首要城镇，拥有华人涧内和主教区。为防备南方穆斯林袭掠，守军把木堡改建为石堡；堡门所刻年份为1738年。

en:
Leyte lies between Samar and Mindanao, its eastern shore opening on Leyte Gulf and its western valleys shelving to the Camotes Sea. The Spaniards who came in the 1500s heard the island called Tandaya, after one of its lords; Warays lived in the east and other Visayan peoples in the west, in datu settlements such as Carigara and Mairete, the latter once ruled by Datu Ete. They farmed rice and millet on the coastal flats, fished and built boats in the sheltered gulfs, and shared the anito rites of the rest of the Visayas. In 1444 Leyte had no kingdom and no foreign flag, only rival datus, their balangay crews, and the island traffic south to Mindanao and north to Luzon.

Magellan's fleet reached little Limasawa, off Leyte's south coast, on 28 March 1521. Two rulers were there hunting with their balangays, Rajah Kolambu of Butuan and Rajah Siaui, and they feasted the crew for several days. On Easter Sunday, 31 March, Father Valderrama said the first mass in the islands at Mazaua, and Magellan had a cross raised on the island's highest hill before Kolambu piloted the ships on to Cebu. In 1543 Ruy Lopez de Villalobos gave Leyte and Samar the name Las Islas Filipinas, in honour of the prince who became Philip II. The datu Bankaw welcomed Legazpi at Carigara in 1565 with a blood pact and baptism, but in 1621 the old convert turned back to the old gods and, with his son Pagali, a babaylan priest, raised a diwata temple and six towns in revolt. Juan de Alcarazo sailed from Cebu with forty ships, burned the temple and crushed the rising in 1622, setting Bankaw's head on a stake. Jesuits had opened a mission at Carigara in 1595, and Palo, Ormoc and Alangalang followed, yet Spanish rule stayed light: Leyte and Samar became a single province in 1735 with Carigara as capital, and after they split in 1768 the 1818 census found only fifty-six Spanish families among more than sixteen thousand native households.
zh:
莱特位于萨马与棉兰老之间，东岸敞开为莱特湾，西部山谷缓斜入卡莫特斯海。16世纪到来的西班牙人听到此岛叫坦达亚，名字来自岛上的一位首领；瓦瑞人居于岛东，其他米沙鄢族群居于岛西，住在卡里加拉、迈雷特等达图聚落中，迈雷特曾由达图埃特统治。他们在沿海平原种稻粟，在避风海湾捕鱼、造船，奉行整个米沙鄢共同的阿尼托祭祀。1444年的莱特上既无王国，也无外邦旗帜，只有相互争雄的达图、他们的巴朗盖船队，以及南往棉兰老、北通吕宋的岛际航路。

1521年3月28日，麦哲伦船队抵达莱特南岸外的小岛利马萨瓦。岛上有两位首领正率巴朗盖船队行猎，即武端的拉惹科兰布和拉惹西亚乌伊，他们设宴款待船员数日。3月31日复活节，巴尔德拉马神父在马萨瓦主持菲律宾第一场弥撒，麦哲伦又命人在岛上最高的山丘竖起十字架，随后由科兰布领航前往宿务。1543年，鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·维拉洛沃斯把莱特和萨马命名为「菲律宾群岛」，以纪念后来成为腓力二世的王子。1565年，达图班考在卡里加拉歃血欢迎黎牙实比并受洗；但到1621年，这位老基督徒重奉旧神，与任巫师的儿子帕加利筑起迪瓦塔神庙，煽动六座城镇起事。胡安·德·阿尔卡拉索率四十艘船从宿务赶来，烧毁神庙，于1622年平定叛乱，班考的头颅被悬于竹竿示众。耶稣会早在1595年就在卡里加拉开教，帕洛、奥尔莫克、阿兰加兰相继设堂，但西班牙人的统治始终稀薄：1735年莱特与萨马合为一省，以卡里加拉为首府；1768年两省分置后，1818年普查在一万六千余户本地人之外，只数出五十六户西班牙裔家庭。

en:
Zamboanga guards the western tip of Mindanao, where the peninsula ends in a roadstead facing Basilan and the Sulu Sea. Its Sinama name, Samboangan, means a mooring place. The river valleys behind the coast were Subanen country; the Subanen had farmed them since the twelfth century and kept to their old spirits, while Sama and Yakan boat-dwellers fished the islands offshore. By the 1400s the Islamised Tausug of Sulu, then founding their sultanate, were the rising sea power of these straits and claimed suzerainty over the coast. In 1444 Zamboanga was still more anchorage than town: raiders and traders from Mindanao, Sulu and Borneo put in for wood and water.

Spain built its foothold here as a barrier to the Moro raiding fleets sailing out of Sulu and Maguindanao. A first post at La Caldera, used from 1569, was withdrawn to Cebu in 1599. On 23 June 1635 the Jesuit engineer Melchor de Vera laid the cornerstone of Fort San José at his order's request, a date counted as the city's founding; Spaniards, Mexicans and Peruvians worked beside labourers brought from Cebu, Bohol, Panay and Cavite, and the camp's mixed Spanish and Visayan speech grew into the Chavacano creole. The Dutch attacked the fort in 1646, and in 1662 the garrison was recalled to Manila against Koxinga, after which the Jesuits rebuilt the ruined works in 1669.

In 1718–1719 Juan Sicarra raised the present fortress and renamed it for Our Lady of the Pillar of Zaragoza. A year later King Dalasi of Bulig stormed it with three thousand Moro raiders and was beaten off, and a British naval bombardment of January 1798 was likewise repulsed. In 1734 a carved relief of the Virgin was set over the east gate; local tradition holds that she appeared there to a sentry, and the gate became an open-air shrine. In 1821 the fort was commanded for a year by Juan Fermín de San Martín, the Uruguayan elder brother of the liberator José de San Martín.
zh:
三宝颜扼守棉兰老岛西端，半岛尽头的锚地正对巴西兰岛和苏禄海。萨马语原名三宝安岸（Samboangan）意为抛锚之地。海岸后方的河谷是苏巴农人的乡土，他们自12世纪起在此耕作，信奉古老的祖灵；萨马人和雅坎人等船民则在外海岛屿以渔为生。到15世纪，正在创建苏丹国的苏禄陶苏格人已经伊斯兰化，是这片海峡崛起的海上强权，向海岸索取宗主权。1444年的三宝颜还只是锚地、不成城镇，棉兰老、苏禄和婆罗洲的劫掠者与商船在此停泊，补充柴水。

西班牙人在此立足，为的是阻挡从苏禄和马京达瑙出海的摩洛劫掠船队。1569年他们先在拉卡尔德拉设点，1599年撤回宿务。1635年6月23日，耶稣会士工程师梅尔乔·德·贝拉应修会之请为圣何塞堡奠基，这一天被算作三宝颜的建城之日；西班牙人、墨西哥人和秘鲁人，连同从宿务、保和、班乃和甲米地征来的劳工一同施工，营中西班牙语与米沙鄢语混杂，逐渐形成查瓦卡诺克里奥尔语。荷兰人1646年来攻，1662年驻军为防备国姓爷被召回马尼拉，1669年耶稣会士重修了被毁的工事。

1718至1719年，胡安·西卡拉筑起现存的要塞，以萨拉戈萨的皮拉尔圣母为之改名。次年，布利格王达拉西率三千摩洛劫掠者猛攻，被守军击退；1798年1月英国舰队的炮击同样无功而返。1734年，东门上方安放了圣母浮雕，当地人相传圣母曾在那里向一名哨兵显现，这座门就此成为露天祭坛。1821年，要塞由乌拉圭人胡安·费尔明·德·圣马丁出任了一年司令官，他是解放者何塞·德·圣马丁的兄长。

en:
Caraga is the rain-drenched eastern shoulder of Mindanao, a coast of river mouths and offshore islands facing the Pacific. Its people were the Kalagan, 'the spirited ones' from kalag, spirit or soul, in their own tongue; they kept the anito cult, dwelt in datu-led villages called banwa, and lived by shore fishing and farms of rice, abaca and coconut. In 1444 their chiefs ruled unchallenged, though the coast was already caught up in the commerce and wars of neighbouring Butuan, whose balangay fleets and goldsmiths traded with China and Champa and whose gold drew raiding fleets all the way from Ternate in the Moluccas.

The first Europeans to meet these shores were Magellan's men: at Limasawa in 1521 Antonio Pigafetta encountered Rajah Siawi of the Surigaonon, tattooed and loaded with gold ornaments, noted the balangay warships under him and recorded the coast as 'Calagan'. Ruy López de Villalobos attacked Surigao in 1543 and was fought off, and Spanish arms made no headway until an expedition took Tandag in 1609 and organised the district of Caraga. Recollect friars opened the permanent mission at Tandag in 1622 and named the land provincia de gente animosa, the province of spirited folk, after the Kalagan name. Parties of soldiers and settler families were shipped from Mexico in 1635 and again in 1670 and 1672 to hold the coast against Moro raiders, and the census of 1818 counted 2,475 native families and 25 Spanish households in Surigao.
zh:
卡拉加是棉兰老岛雨水丰沛的东翼，海岸河口纵横、岛礁散布，面向太平洋。住在这里的是卡拉甘人，族名出自kalag（魂灵、胆气），意为「有胆气的人」。他们信奉阿尼托泛灵信仰，住在达图统领的村社（banwa）里，靠海捕鱼，种植稻、蕉麻和椰子。1444年，酋长们仍是这片海岸无可争议的主人，但海岸早已被卷入西邻武端的商路与战事：武端的巴兰盖船队和金匠与中国、占城通商，它的黄金还招来摩鹿加特尔纳特的渡海袭掠。

最早见到这片海岸的欧洲人是麦哲伦的船队。1521年，皮加费塔在利马萨瓦见到文身披金的苏里高人拉惹·西亚威，记下他乘坐的巴兰盖战船，并把这一带记作「卡拉甘」。1543年鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·比利亚洛沃斯进攻苏里高，被当地人击退；西班牙人的武力长期无所作为，直到1609年远征军攻下坦达格、设立卡拉加区。1622年重整奥斯定会传教士在坦达格开设常驻传教站，并依照卡拉甘的族名把这里命名为「勇者之地」（provincia de gente animosa）。1635年及1670、1672年，西班牙从墨西哥分批运来士兵和移民户驻守海岸、抵御摩洛袭掠者；1818年的户口册载，苏里高有2,475户本地家庭和25户西班牙家庭。

en:
Taytay guards the northern neck of Palawan, where Malampaya Sound opens between the South China and Sulu seas. Chinese records of the thirteenth century counted these islands among Sandao, vassals of the trading polity of Ma-i on Mindoro. Before the Spaniards came, Taytay was the seat of a small kingdom whose king, Antonio Pigafetta later heard, was followed wherever he went by ten scribes. Its people fished the sound, farmed along its shores and kept the animist rites of anito, and in 1444 they answered to their own king.

In 1521 the survivors of Magellan's expedition, fleeing his death at Mactan, put in at Taytay and held the king and his queen hostage for provisions before sailing on to the Moluccas; the court paid, and sent more food than the strangers had asked. Spanish rule followed a century later: the town was formally founded in 1623 and given to Augustinian Recollect missionaries, who began the stone fortress of Fuerza de Santa Isabel in 1667 and finished its walls only in 1738. Its guns covered the anchorage against Moro raiders from the Sulu archipelago, whose war fleets repeatedly struck the settlements of northern Palawan, Cuyo and the Calamianes. In 1818 Taytay became capital of the province of Calamianes, covering all of Paragua, as the Spaniards then called Palawan.
zh:
泰泰扼守巴拉望岛北端的颈部，马拉帕亚湾在此连通南海与苏禄海。13世纪的中国载籍把这一带岛屿记作三屿，是民都洛岛上商贸政权麻逸的属国。西班牙人到来之前，泰泰是一个小王国的都城；安东尼奥·皮加费塔后来听人说，那里的国王无论走到何处都有十名书吏随行。岛民在海湾捕鱼、沿岸耕种，奉行泛灵的阿尼托信仰；1444年时，他们听命于自己的国王。

1521年，麦哲伦在麦克坦丧命后，残部逃到泰泰，扣押国王与王后勒索粮食，随后继续驶往摩鹿加；王廷交了赎金，送来的食物比这些陌生人索要的还多。一个世纪后西班牙人才建立统治：城镇于1623年正式设立，交给重整奥斯定会传教士；他们1667年动工修建圣伊莎贝尔石堡，城墙直到1738年才完工。要塞炮火覆盖锚地，抵御从苏禄群岛而来的摩洛掠奴者，他们的战船屡次袭扰巴拉望北部、库约和卡拉棉群岛的聚落。1818年，泰泰成为卡拉棉省省会，管辖西班牙人当时称作拉帕瓜的整个巴拉望。

en:
Ise opens on the deep bight of Ise Bay, its shore a string of fishing harbours and salt fields, and the Tokaido crosses its north on the road between Kyoto and the east. In the cedar country south of the Kushida River stands the Ise Grand Shrine, holiest site of the imperial cult and reputed home of Yata no Kagami, the sacred mirror; its halls are rebuilt every twenty years, with offerings from every province. During the Southern Court wars the courtier Kitabatake Akiyoshi came south as provincial governor, and his family made themselves lords of the five southern districts, ruling from Kiriyama Castle above the Taki valley. In 1444 his descendant Kitabatake Noritomo held Kiriyama as governor-lord of southern Ise.

The house peaked under Harutomo and his son Tomonori, a swordsman trained by Tsukahara Bokuden, their reach extending into Shima and the border marches. In 1568 Oda Nobunaga's armies entered northern Ise and the local lords submitted; in the eighth month of 1569 he besieged Tomonori in Okawachi Castle himself, until Ashikaga Yoshiaki mediated a peace whose price was Nobunaga's second son Nobukatsu, adopted as the Kitabatake heir. Nobukatsu took the succession in 1575, and in the eleventh month of 1576 his soldiers killed Tomonori and his sons at several places in a single night, the Mitsuse bloodbath that ended the governor's line.

Under the Tokugawa the province was split among several domains, the greatest being Tsu, granted in 1608 to the castle-builder Todo Takatora and rated in time at 323,000 koku. Pilgrimage did more for Ise than any lord: in the Tokugawa peace one Japanese in ten is thought to have walked to the Grand Shrine, and in 1625 the shrine counted 3.62 million pilgrims in fifty days, crowding Yamada and the northern Tokaido post stations. The province also bred traders. Matsusaka was a commercial centre from the Sengoku years, and in 1673 Mitsui Takatoshi, son of a Matsusaka shopkeeper, opened the Echigoya draper's in Edo's Nihonbashi, selling over the counter for cash at fixed prices instead of visiting clients for orders. In 1683 the shogunate licensed him to run exchange shops, moving daimyo tax money between Osaka and Edo, and the Mitsui money house grew from that trade.
zh:
伊势面向水深湾阔的伊势湾，沿岸渔村、盐田相连，东海道自北境穿过，连接京都与东国。内陆栉田川以南杉林幽深，伊势神宫坐落其间：这是朝廷祭祀最神圣的所在，相传藏着神器八咫镜；神殿每隔二十年依式年迁宫之制重建，各国都要送来奉纳。南北朝争乱时，公卿北畠显能以国司身份南下，北畠家便成为南伊势五郡的主人，居城是多气山谷上方的雾山城。1444年，其后人北畠教具在雾山城以国司兼领主的身份统治南伊势。

晴具、具教父子两代是北畠家最强盛之时，势力伸入志摩和周边边境，具教还曾随名剑客冢原卜传习剑，自己也以剑术闻名。1568年织田信长的大军攻入北伊势，当地豪族相继臣服；1569年8月，信长亲围具教于大河内城，最后由将军足利义昭斡旋议和，条件是信长次子信雄做北畠家的养子。信雄1575年继承家督，1576年11月便派兵在一夜之间分数处袭杀具教及其诸子，史称三濑之变，国司名门就此断绝。

德川时代，伊势被分为数藩，最大的是1608年封给筑城名家藤堂高虎的津藩，石高后来达三十二万三千石。让伊势繁盛的却是参拜客：太平年月里，据说每十个日本人就有一人步行前往伊势神宫，1625年神宫记下五十天内三百六十二万人参诣，门前町山田和北境的东海道宿场人头攒动。伊势也出商人：松阪自战国年间就是商业集镇，1673年，松阪商家之子三井高利在江户日本桥开出越后屋吴服店，不再登门接订单，而在店里按固定价格现钱售货；1683年他又获准经营两替店，为大名在大阪和江户之间调拨税款，三井的钱庄生意就是从这笔银两替买卖做起的。

en:
Mikawa, or Sanshū, lay on the Tōkaidō east of Owari, its coast indented by Mikawa and Atsumi bays and the Yahagi river crossing its rice plains. The province had long been split informally into east and west around the Yasaku, and the murder of its shugo Isshiki Yoshitsura on Shōgun Yoshinori's orders in 1440, followed by the grant of the office to the Hosokawa, threw it into civil war. In 1444 rival governors, ikki bands and local houses fought over the lowlands. Among the small lords gaining ground were the Matsudaira of the Kamo hills in the west, pushing south under Matsudaira Nobumitsu.

That obscure house produced the Tokugawa. Matsudaira Kiyoyasu held Okazaki and came close to taking the whole province before a retainer killed him in his Owari camp in 1535, an event remembered as the Moriyama collapse. His grandson Takechiyo, the future Tokugawa Ieyasu, was born in Okazaki Castle in January 1543; at five he was seized on the road by Oda Nobuhide while being delivered as a hostage to the Imagawa, and he grew up at Sunpu before reclaiming Okazaki after Imagawa Yoshimoto fell at Okehazama in 1560. He broke the armed True Pure Land leagues of the Mikawa Ikkō-ikki of 1563–64, fighting in the front line at Azukizaka in 1564 where several bullets struck his armour without piercing it, and in 1566 he won imperial leave to take the name Tokugawa. After he moved east to Hamamatsu and later to the Kantō, Okazaki passed through other hands until the new shogunate enfeoffed Honda Yasushige there at 50,000 koku in 1602, first of a line of fudai lords. Mikawa then supplied the shogunate in quieter ways: the Tōkaidō stations carried daimyō retinues over the Yahagi bridge, the regime concentrated its gunpowder works in the province, and from the mid-seventeenth century the Hatchō breweries west of Okazaki aged the dark soybean miso sold to Edo's warrior houses.
zh:
三河（简称三州）位于尾张以东的东海道上，海岸凹入为三河湾与渥美湾，矢作川流过平原上的稻田。国内长期以矢作川一线分东西，1440年守护一色义贯被将军足利义教下令杀害、守护之职转授细川氏，三河就此陷入内战。1444年，新旧守护、国人一揆与在地豪族在平原上混战；西部加茂郡的松平氏只是其中一家小领主，在松平信光带领下向南扩张。

正是这个不起眼的家门生出了德川家。松平清康据有冈崎，几乎拿下整个三河，1535年却在尾张阵中被家臣刺杀，史称森山崩。其孙竹千代（后来的德川家康）1543年1月生于冈崎城，五岁时在被送往今川氏为质的途中遭织田信秀劫持，后来在骏府长大，直到1560年今川义元战死桶狭间才夺回冈崎。1563至1564年，他打垮三河一向一揆的真宗门徒武装，1564年在小豆坂之战中亲临前线，身中数弹而铠甲未穿；1566年获朝廷敕许改姓德川。他后来东移滨松、再入关东，冈崎几经转手，幕府于1602年封本多康重五万石入城，开谱代大名世袭之先。此后三河以另一种方式支撑幕府：东海道宿场迎送跨过矢作桥的大名行列，国内集中了火药工场，17世纪中叶起，冈崎城西的八丁作坊陈酿深色豆味噌，卖给江户的武家。

en:
Roxburghshire is the middle march of Scotland, where the Teviot runs into the Tweed under Roxburgh Castle. David I made Roxburgh a royal burgh and a southern seat of his court, and planted two of the border's greatest abbeys at Kelso and Jedburgh. Few castles changed hands so often. It went to England with the captive William the Lion in 1174, and under Edward I Bruce's sister Mary spent four years in a cage hung outside its walls. Sir James Douglas retook it on a February night in 1314, his men in black cloaks mistaken for grazing cattle, and Bruce ordered the whole fortress pulled down. The English rebuilt it under Edward III and kept it after Neville's Cross in 1346; two later Scottish sieges failed, and in 1444 an English garrison still held the Tweed crossing. Up the Jed water, Jedburgh lived by its abbey, its horse and cattle fairs and the reiving trade under Douglas wardens. Border speech named 'Jethart justice' after the town: a man was hanged first and tried afterwards.

In 1460 James II brought his artillery to Roxburgh and was killed when one of his own bombards burst; his queen, Mary of Guelders, pressed the storm, and the Scots razed castle and town so completely that Roxburgh was never rebuilt, and Jedburgh became the county town. English armies burned Kelso, Melrose and Jedburgh abbeys in the Rough Wooing, although the Scots won at Ancrum Moor in 1545 and the fort the English had thrown up on the castle mound was demolished when the war ended. Mary, Queen of Scots, lay ill at Jedburgh in 1566. After the Union of the Crowns the reivers were curbed and the wool and knitting trades spread up the dales; Floors Castle, seat of the Dukes of Roxburghe, rose facing the castle mound in 1721–26, and Prince Charles's army passed through on 6 November 1745. In 1787 James Hutton examined the tilted rock beds capped by red sandstone near Jedburgh, one of the unconformities on which he built his case for an immensely old earth.
zh:
罗克斯堡郡是苏格兰的中部边疆，蒂维厄特河在罗克斯堡城堡下注入特威德河。大卫一世把罗克斯堡建成皇家自治镇和南方的王家居城，又在凯尔索和杰德堡建起边境上最宏大的两座修道院。没有几座城堡像它这样频繁易主。1174年，它随被俘的狮子王威廉交给英格兰；爱德华一世据守期间，布鲁斯的妹妹玛丽被关在吊于城墙外的木笼里四年。1314年2月的一个夜晚，詹姆斯·道格拉斯率身披黑袍的部下奇袭得手，守军把他们错当成吃草的牛群，布鲁斯随后下令把整座城堡拆毁。英格兰人在爱德华三世时将其重建，1346年内维尔十字之战后持续占据；之后苏格兰人两次围攻均告失败，1444年特威德河渡口仍在英格兰守军手中。杰德沃特河上游的杰德堡靠着修道院、马市牛市和边境劫掠为生，守臣出自道格拉斯家。边境俗语把先绞后审称作「杰德哈特式审判」，名字就来自这座镇子。

1460年，詹姆斯二世携炮兵围攻罗克斯堡，他自己的一门攻城炮炸裂，碎片将他打死；王后海尔德的玛丽继续督战破城，苏格兰人把城堡和城镇彻底夷平，罗克斯堡再未重建，郡治改设杰德堡。「粗暴求婚」战争中，英军焚毁凯尔索、梅尔罗斯和杰德堡的修道院，尽管苏格兰人1545年在安克勒姆荒原取胜，城堡土丘上的英军要塞也在战后拆除。1566年，苏格兰女王玛丽在杰德堡重病。两国王位合并后，边境流寇遭到整肃，羊毛和针织业沿河谷传播开来；1721至1726年，罗克斯堡公爵的弗洛斯城堡在城堡土丘对岸建成，1745年11月6日查理王子的军队穿镇而过。1787年，詹姆斯·赫顿在杰德堡附近考察上覆红砂岩的倾斜岩层，正是这类不整合面支撑了他关于地球极为古老的论证。

en:
Dumfries commands the lowest crossing of the Nith above the Solway Firth, port and market of Scotland's West March. William the Lion made it a royal burgh in 1186. Lincluden Abbey stood on the bank above the town, and eight miles to the south Sweetheart Abbey was founded in 1273 by Dervorguilla of Galloway, who carried her dead husband John Balliol's embalmed heart in a casket of ivory and silver and was buried with it; their son reigned in Scotland as John Balliol. Further south the Maxwells' moated, three-cornered Caerlaverock guarded the Nith mouth: in July 1300 sixty men held it for days against the army Edward I led north in person, until hunger forced surrender, and the heralds in the English host turned the siege into a roll of arms in French verse. In the Greyfriars' church at Dumfries Robert Bruce stabbed the Red Comyn on 10 February 1306, and his follower Kirkpatrick went in to 'mak siccar', to make sure; the killing put Bruce on the road to Bannockburn. Beyond the Dee, Archibald the Grim raised Threave Castle for the Douglases in the 1370s, and in 1444 his widowed daughter-in-law Princess Margaret ruled the Galloway lordship from its tower. The marches lived by wool, cattle and raiding.

James II ended Douglas power with his own knife, stabbing the eighth earl at Stirling on 22 February 1452; the rising that followed collapsed near Langholm on 1 May 1455, and Threave surrendered. In November 1542 the English routed a Scottish army on Solway Moss beside the Esk, a defeat said to have hastened the death of James V. Caerlaverock held for the Catholic earls of Nithsdale until a Covenanter army took it after thirteen weeks in 1640, and the Maxwells never lived there again. Late in 1745 the Young Pretender kept his headquarters in Dumfries for three days and mulcted the town of £1,000 on his retreat north. Robert Burns farmed at Ellisland from 1788, moved into Dumfries in 1791 and died there in 1796; in 1788, the year Burns took the farm, William Symington tried a steam engine in a boat on nearby Dalswinton Loch.
zh:
邓弗里斯扼守尼思河注入索尔韦湾前的最后渡口，是苏格兰西部边疆的港口与集镇。狮子王威廉1186年将其升为皇家自治镇。林克卢登修道院立在镇北河畔；再往南八英里，甜心修道院1273年由加洛韦的德沃尔吉拉创建，她把亡夫约翰·巴利奥尔经防腐处理的心脏盛在象牙白银匣中随身携带，死后与之合葬，修道院的拉丁名意为「甜心」；他们的儿子后来登上苏格兰王位，即国王约翰·巴利奥尔。更南边，马克斯韦尔家环水而建的三角形城堡扼守尼思河口：1300年7月，六十名守军在此抵挡爱德华一世亲率的大军多日，粮尽才降，英军中的传令官把这场围城写成法文韵文的纹章名册。1306年2月10日，罗伯特·布鲁斯在邓弗里斯的灰衣修士会教堂刺死「红科明」，随从柯克帕特里克进屋补刀，说是要「确保万无一失」，这桩血案把布鲁斯推上班诺克本的道路。迪河对岸，「冷面的」阿奇博尔德在14世纪70年代为道格拉斯家筑起特利维城堡；1444年，他守寡的儿媳玛格丽特公主仍在主塔里统治加洛韦领地。边疆上下以羊毛、牲畜和劫掠为生。

詹姆斯二世亲手了结道格拉斯家的权势：1452年2月22日他在斯特灵刺死第八代伯爵，随后的叛乱于1455年5月1日在兰霍姆附近溃败，特利维城堡开城投降。1542年11月，英军在埃斯克河畔的索维莫斯击溃苏格兰军，据说这场败仗加速了詹姆斯五世之死。三角水堡为天主教的尼思河谷伯爵们坚守到1640年，盟约派军队围攻十三周才将它拿下，马克斯韦尔家再没搬回堡中。1745年末，小王位觊觎者在邓弗里斯设了三天司令部，北撤时向镇上勒索了一千英镑。罗伯特·彭斯1788年起在埃利斯兰务农，1791年迁居邓弗里斯，1796年在此去世；同在1788年，威廉·赛明顿在附近的达斯温顿湖上试航了装有蒸汽机的小船。

en:
Argyll (Gaelic Earra-Ghàidheal, the 'coast of the Gaels') is the sea-loch coast and inner isles of western Scotland, the old country of Dál Riata. Its kings were enthroned on the rock of Dunadd, and from Iona, founded in 563, Columba's monks took Christianity to the Picts. Kintyre and Lorn fell under Norse rule and came back to Scotland only with the Treaty of Perth in 1266. Power then lay with the MacDonald Lords of the Isles, Norse-Gaelic heirs of Somerled who ruled from Finlaggan on Islay with fleets of galleys and answered to no king in practice; the Campbells rose beside them as hereditary sheriffs and the crown's men, building the first castle at Inveraray on Loch Fyne around 1432. In 1444 Sir Duncan Campbell of Lochawe held Loch Awe and the sea roads for the king from his tower-houses, though the Gaelic west still looked to Islay rather than Edinburgh, and cattle, timber and herring moved through the sea lochs.

Colin Campbell became the first Earl of Argyll in 1457. The Lordship of the Isles ended in 1493, when James IV seized John MacDonald's lands and titles, and the Campbells afterwards led the crown's expansion into the Hebrides; they embraced the Reformation and under James VI subdued the Catholic MacDonald lands of Islay and Jura. Civil war struck savagely in December 1644, when Montrose and Alasdair MacColla burned Inveraray, and on 2 February 1645 destroyed Argyll's army beneath Inverlochy Castle. On 13 February 1692 government troops under Campbell of Glenlyon killed about thirty MacDonalds of Glencoe who had fed and sheltered them for a fortnight, and Glencoe fed Jacobite anger for two generations. The Campbells became dukes in 1701. From 1744 the third duke rebuilt Inveraray as a planned town with a new castle by the Adam family, and in 1753 the Bonawe furnace on Loch Etive began smelting imported ore with Highland charcoal, turning the local oakwoods into cannon and tools.
zh:
阿盖尔（盖尔语Earra-Ghàidheal，意为「盖尔人的海岸」）是苏格兰西部的峡湾海岸与内群岛，古达尔里阿达王国的故地。国王在杜纳德堡的岩石上登基，563年创立的艾奥纳修道院里，哥伦巴的修士把基督教传给皮克特人。金泰尔和洛恩曾受诺斯人统治，直到1266年《珀斯条约》才归还苏格兰。此后实权在麦克唐纳家族的群岛之主手中：他们是萨默莱德的诺斯与盖尔后裔，率桨帆船队坐镇艾拉岛的芬拉根（Finlaggan），实际上不奉王命；坎贝尔家族则作为世袭郡长和王庭的代理人崛起，约1432年在法恩湖畔建起第一座因弗雷里堡。1444年，洛赫奥的邓肯·坎贝尔爵士凭塔楼扼守洛赫奥与各条海路为王庭效力，但盖尔语的西方更听命于艾拉岛而非爱丁堡，牛只、木材和鲱鱼在重重峡湾间往来。

科林·坎贝尔1457年成为第一代阿盖尔伯爵。1493年，詹姆斯四世剥夺约翰·麦克唐纳的土地与头衔，群岛之主时代结束，坎贝尔家族此后替王庭向赫布里底扩张；他们皈依新教，奉詹姆斯六世之命平定了艾拉、朱拉两岛信奉天主教的麦克唐纳领地。内战来得惨烈：1644年12月，蒙特罗斯与阿拉斯代尔·麦科拉焚毁因弗雷里，1645年2月2日又在因弗洛希堡下歼灭阿盖尔的军队。1692年2月13日，格伦里昂的坎贝尔率领的政府军杀害了供他们食宿两周的格伦科麦克唐纳族人约三十名，格伦科之事滋养了此后两代人的詹姆斯党怒火。坎贝尔家族1701年受封公爵。1744年起，第三代公爵把因弗雷里重建成规划新城，并由亚当家族修建新堡；1753年，埃蒂夫湖畔的博诺铁炉开炉，用高地木炭冶炼进口矿石，把当地的栎树林化作大炮和工具。

en:
The Inner Hebrides run from Skye through Mull to Islay on Scotland's western sea lanes. Norse-Scottish seafaring lords grew out of Somerled's twelfth-century realm, and the 1266 Treaty of Perth brought the islands from Norway to Scotland. Their seat was Finlaggan on Islay: on Eilean Mor in the loch stood the Lord's residence, and the smaller Isle of the Council held his meeting of chiefs, whose galleys linked Ireland with the Highlands. On Skye, Dunvegan Castle on a rock in its sea loch was already the seat of the MacLeod chiefs, and it kept the Fairy Flag, a torn square of eastern silk which tradition called a fairy's gift or a relic brought home from the Crusades, and which unfurled in battle was said to multiply the clan's fighting men. MacDonalds held Sleat in the south of the island. In 1444 these Catholic, Gaelic-speaking islands were the core of the maritime power of Alexander MacDonald, Lord of the Isles and Earl of Ross, not a distant edge of Scotland.

Alexander's son John signed the secret Treaty of Ardtornish with Edward IV of England in 1462; when it came to light James III stripped him of most of his power in 1476, and his own son Angus defeated him at the Bloody Bay off Mull in 1481. James IV ended the lordship altogether in 1493, and the isles became a patchwork of MacLean, MacLeod, MacDonald and MacKinnon estates held under the Crown. Islanders joined the Jacobite risings of 1715 and 1745. After Culloden the old clan order was recast as landed estates. Flora MacDonald, who helped Charles Edward Stuart escape through Skye in 1746, later lived on the island, where Samuel Johnson and James Boswell visited her in 1773; she was buried at Kilmuir. Cattle, fishing, kelp and Easdale slate tied the islands to southern markets, until the kelp trade collapsed after 1815.
zh:
内赫布里底群岛沿苏格兰西侧海路，从斯凯岛经马尔岛延伸到艾莱岛。12世纪萨默雷德的海上王国孕育出诺斯与苏格兰混血的航海领主，1266年《珀斯条约》又把群岛从挪威移交苏格兰。领主的统治中心在艾莱岛的芬拉冈：湖中的大岛上建有领主宅邸，旁边较小的「议事岛」召开氏族首领会议，他们的桨帆船把爱尔兰和高地之间的海路连成一气。斯凯岛上，邓韦根城堡立在海湾的礁石上，已是麦克劳德首领的世代驻地；堡中收藏着「仙旗」，那是一块残破的东方丝绸，相传为仙女所赠，或十字军从圣地带回的圣物，据说战斗中展开能让氏族战士凭空倍增。岛南的斯莱特归麦克唐纳家族。1444年，这些信奉天主教、使用盖尔语的岛屿是群岛领主兼罗斯伯爵亚历山大·麦克唐纳海洋势力的核心，而不是苏格兰偏远的边地。

亚历山大之子约翰1462年与英格兰国王爱德华四世秘密签订《阿德托尼什条约》；事情败露后，詹姆斯三世于1476年剥夺他的大部分权力，1481年他的亲生子安加斯又在马尔岛近海的血腥湾战役中将他击败。1493年詹姆斯四世彻底废除群岛领地，群岛此后成为麦克莱恩、麦克劳德、麦克唐纳和麦金农等家族在王权威名下交错的封地。岛民参加了1715年和1745年的詹姆斯党起事；卡洛登之后，旧氏族秩序被改造成地产制度。弗洛拉·麦克唐纳1746年帮助查理·爱德华·斯图亚特经斯凯岛脱身，后来长住岛上，1773年塞缪尔·约翰逊和詹姆斯·鲍斯韦尔曾登门拜访，她去世后葬在基尔缪尔。牲畜、渔业、海藻灰和伊斯代尔石板把群岛与南方市场连在一起，直到1815年后海藻灰贸易崩溃。

en:
Mann, the Isle of Man, lies in the middle of the Irish Sea, within sailing reach of England, Scotland, Ireland and Wales. Norse Vikings made it the seat of the Kingdom of Mann and the Isles, whose rulers established Tynwald, by tradition founded in 979 and the oldest continuous parliament in the British Isles; its twenty-four Keys sat as the island's court, and laws were proclaimed outdoors from the mound at St John's. The 1266 Treaty of Perth transferred the island from Norway to Scotland, but Mann changed hands repeatedly in the Scottish wars, and English rule became lasting only after 1346. Castletown grew beneath Castle Rushen, guarding its southern harbour, and the three running legs of the Manx coat of arms appeared in the thirteenth century. In 1405 Henry IV granted John Stanley the title King of Mann. In 1444 Catholic, Manx-speaking islanders lived by farming and fishing under the Stanley family, whose English feudal lordship left Tynwald and local customs in being.

The Stanleys kept Mann through the fifteenth century, and early in the sixteenth their royal-sounding title became Lord of Mann.
