马拉加坐落在希布拉尔法罗山与瓜达尔梅迪纳河之间的广阔地中海海湾。约公元前770年，推罗的腓尼基商人在此建立马拉卡，罗马时代的马拉加靠鱼酱和港口贸易富庶起来。穆斯林统治时期，带城墙的城区从港口一路铺到阿尔卡萨瓦要塞和希布拉尔法罗城堡。10世纪的编年史家拉齐已经盛赞这里的葡萄园和葡萄干；伊本·白图泰约1325年路过时，看到的是天下无双的葡萄、无花果、杏仁和石榴，以及精美的鎏金陶器。纳斯里德王朝治下，它是格拉纳达首要的西部海港和王国第二大城：热那亚商人把丝绸、葡萄干、据说远销中国的拉亚无花果，还有葡萄酒、刀具、皮革和光泽陶器装上船，往来于地中海与大西洋之间的航路。1444年城中约有一万五千人，码头和热那亚人的货栈使它成为这个穆斯林王国最富庶的港口。

1487年，天主教君主的军队兵临城下，打了格拉纳达战争中最艰难的一仗。经过约四个月的强攻、炮击和饥馑，马拉加在8月投降，这次围城还第一次使用了专门运送伤兵的车辆。城市陷落使格拉纳达失去主要海上门户，幸存者几乎全部被罚为奴或押走，只有以商人阿里·杜尔杜克斯为首的二十五户获准作为穆德哈尔人留下；随后伊比利亚半岛各地的基督教定居者迁入此城，马拉加则继续经安特克拉和科尔多瓦同内陆贸易。它不甘受卡斯蒂利亚海军上将管辖，1516年起兵反抗，直到1530年才彻底摆脱，到1625年居民已有约三万六千人。1704年8月24日，城外海面爆发西班牙王位继承战争中规模最大的舰队交战，胜负未决的马拉加海战，此时距同一支英荷舰队夺取直布罗陀才过去三周。

en:
Albacete lies on Los Llanos, the wide wheat plains where La Mancha opens towards Murcia and the Valencian coast. Its Muslim village of Al-Basit, Arabic for 'the plain', sat below the fortified hill of Chinchilla, whose castle commanded the roads across the flat country. Castilian troops took it in 1241, and for two centuries the hamlet remained in Chinchilla's shadow, becoming a separate villa of the lords of Villena only with its town charter in 1375. In 1444 it was a small grain town on the road linking the Castilian Meseta with Murcia and Valencia, and Chinchilla's castle still overshadowed it.

Knife-making took root in the fifteenth century, inherited from Muslim smiths; by the seventeenth, workshops along the Calle Zapateros made knives, daggers, swords, scissors and the folding navaja, and the eighteenth was the trade's golden age, when Albacete blades sold across Spain and abroad. The town had held an annual fair since its charter, and the Catholic Monarchs added a weekly market in 1476. On 25 April 1707, on the plains at Almansa east of the town, the Duke of Berwick, illegitimate son of James II of England, led Philip V's Bourbon army against an allied force under the Earl of Galway, a French Huguenot exile in English service, prompting the joke that the English were commanded by a Frenchman and the French by an Englishman. Berwick's victory opened Valencia to the Bourbons, and Frederick the Great later called it the best-fought battle of the century. Philip V made the Albacete fair tax-free in 1710, and in 1783 a permanent fairground opened, a pan-shaped ring of stalls built in thirty-three days; the fair became one of the great stock fairs of inland Spain. During the Peninsular War French troops sacked the town and later blew up the keep of Chinchilla's castle.
zh:
阿尔瓦塞特位于利亚诺斯平原，拉曼查的广阔麦田在这里向穆尔西亚和巴伦西亚海岸方向展开。穆斯林村庄阿尔-巴西特（阿拉伯语意为「平原」）坐落在钦奇利亚设防山丘下方，山上的城堡扼守着穿越旷野的道路。1241年卡斯蒂利亚军队攻取此地，此后两百年间村落一直掩在钦奇利亚的阴影里，直到1375年凭市镇特许状成为比列纳领主治下的独立市镇。1444年，它是卡斯蒂利亚高原通往穆尔西亚和巴伦西亚路上的一座谷物小镇，仍处在钦奇利亚城堡的俯瞰之下。

制刀业在15世纪从穆斯林工匠手中接续而来；到17世纪，鞋匠街一带的作坊已在打制刀具、匕首、剑、剪刀和名叫纳瓦哈的折叠刀，18世纪更是这门手艺的黄金年代，阿尔瓦塞特出产的刀剑行销西班牙内外。小镇自立镇起便有年市，天主教双王又在1476年赐它每周开市。1707年4月25日，城东阿尔曼萨的平原上打响了西班牙王位继承战争中具有决定意义的一仗：费利佩五世的波旁军由英王詹姆斯二世的私生子贝里克公爵指挥，对面的联军主帅却是流亡英国的法国胡格诺派加尔韦伯爵，当时有人打趣说，这是唯一一场英军由法国人率领、法军由英国人率领的战斗。贝里克获胜，为波旁王朝打开巴伦西亚的大门，后来腓特烈大帝还称赞这是本世纪指挥得最好的一仗。费利佩五世1710年赐这里的集市免税特权；1783年，一座煎锅形的环形集市场在33天内建成开市，阿尔瓦塞特年市也成为西班牙内陆最有名的牲畜集市之一。半岛战争期间，法军洗劫城镇，后来又炸毁钦奇利亚城堡的主塔。

en:
Huelva sits on the sheltered ría where the Odiel and Tinto flow into the Gulf of Cádiz, with low copper-bearing hills a short way upstream. As Phoenician Onoba it shipped copper and silver, purple dye and salted fish, and Roman Onoba kept a mint on the same estuary; the Rio Tinto diggings upriver were already a major mining district under Roman rule. Muslim Walba passed to Castile when Alfonso X took the town in 1262, and for the rest of the Middle Ages it was mostly a noble lordship on the Portuguese border. In 1444 it was a Catholic Castilian fishing and trading harbour, while the little ports strung along the same estuary, Palos and Moguer among them, already made their living from the Atlantic.

Palos held the sailors who knew the Guinea run, and in the Castilian-Portuguese war of 1475-1479 they used that knowledge to raid Portuguese shipping, until the Treaty of Alcáçovas in 1479 left the Atlantic and African routes to Portugal apart from the Canaries. Columbus spent months at the Franciscan monastery of La Rábida and won over the Pinzón brothers, the leading shipmasters of Palos, who helped him raise crews and money. On 3 August 1492 the Pinta, Niña and Santa María put out from Palos with about ninety men. The Santa María was wrecked in the Caribbean, and the two caravels returned to the same roadstead on 15 March 1493. The youngest Pinzón, Vicente Yáñez, who had captained the Niña, sighted the Brazilian coast in 1500. When the Casa de Contratación opened at Seville in 1503 the Atlantic trade moved up the river, Palos emptied, and Huelva grew on sardine and tuna fishing.

The 1755 Lisbon earthquake wrecked much of the town. In 1810 French troops under the Duke of Aremberg attacked Huelva and Moguer, but the harbour stayed open and went on landing men and supplies for Cádiz, which the French had under siege.
zh:
韦尔瓦位于奥迭尔河与廷托河注入加的斯湾的避风河口，上游不远就是产铜的低缓丘陵。腓尼基时代的奥诺巴输出铜、银、紫染料和咸鱼，罗马时代的奥诺巴还在同一河口设有铸币厂，廷托河矿区在罗马治下已是重要的铜银矿区。穆斯林称此地为韦勒巴，1262年阿方索十世攻占后它归入卡斯蒂利亚，整个中世纪后期基本是葡萄牙边境上的一处贵族领地。1444年，这里是卡斯蒂利亚天主教徒的渔业与贸易港口；同一河口还串着帕洛斯、莫格尔这些小港，它们的生计早已系于大西洋。

帕洛斯有的是熟悉几内亚航路的水手。1475年至1479年卡斯蒂利亚与葡萄牙交战，他们凭着这套本事劫掠葡萄牙船只，直到1479年《阿尔卡索瓦斯条约》把大西洋和非洲航路划归葡萄牙，只把加那利群岛留给卡斯蒂利亚。哥伦布在拉维达的方济各会修道院盘桓数月，说动了帕洛斯首屈一指的船主平松兄弟，由他们帮着招募水手、筹措费用。1492年8月3日，「平塔号」「尼尼亚号」和「圣马利亚号」率约九十人从帕洛斯起航；「圣马利亚号」在加勒比海域失事，两艘卡拉维尔船于1493年3月15日返回同一锚地。曾任「尼尼亚号」船长的平松家幼子比森特·亚涅斯，1500年又望见了巴西海岸。1503年塞维利亚设立贸易署，大西洋贸易随之移往上游，帕洛斯为之一空，韦尔瓦则靠沙丁鱼和金枪鱼渔业发展起来。

1755年里斯本大地震摧毁了城中大片房屋。1810年，阿朗贝格公爵麾下法军进攻韦尔瓦和莫格尔，但港口始终未失，继续为遭法军围困的加的斯运送兵员和补给。

en:
Xàtiva climbs a hill above the Albaida river, and its castle was held to be the strongest in the Kingdom of Valencia. Roman Saetabis sold fine linen across the Mediterranean, and Catullus names its linen handkerchiefs among the presents his friends brought back from Spain. Under Muslim rule Shāṭiba learned paper-making from Arab craftsmen and became one of the first paper towns in western Europe; the geographer al-Idrisi praised its mills and its schools in the twelfth century. James I of Aragon took the city in May 1244 after an earlier siege had failed, kept its mosque and made it seat of the governorship beyond the Júcar; its fair was licensed in 1250 and Peter IV granted city status in 1347. As the second city of the kingdom, dealing in paper and linen, it was the birthplace of the House of Borgia: Alfonso de Borja, the future Pope Callixtus III, was born here in 1378, and his nephew Rodrigo de Borja, the future Alexander VI, around 1431. In 1444 Xàtiva was a walled royal city of some 8,000 people.

The Germanías revolt turned the city into a battlefield: the agermanat leader Vicent Peris made it his stronghold and held out until he was killed in 1522. The painter José de Ribera, called Lo Spagnoletto, was born here in 1591. The Morisco expulsion of 1609-1614 emptied more than a hundred villages of its governorship and cost it nearly half its people, and the plagues of the seventeenth century thinned them further. In the War of the Spanish Succession Xàtiva declared for the Habsburg claimant, and after the Bourbon victory at Almansa d'Asfeld's army laid siege; the English garrison in the castle marched out on 12 June 1707. The town was then looted and put to the torch; tradition says it burned for a year, and its people were deported to La Mancha. Philip V renamed the blackened ruins the Colonia de San Felipe and dissolved the ancient governorship, and the fire gave Xativans their nickname of socarrats, the scorched ones. The Cortes of Cádiz gave the city its old name back in 1811.
zh:
沙蒂瓦坐落在阿尔瓦伊达河畔的山丘上，城中城堡号称巴伦西亚王国最坚固的要塞。罗马时代的萨埃塔比斯出产上等亚麻布，行销地中海各地；卡图卢斯就写到朋友从西班牙带回的萨埃塔比斯亚麻手帕。穆斯林治下的沙提巴从阿拉伯工匠那里学会造纸，是西欧最早的造纸城镇之一，12世纪的地理学家伊德里西称赞过它的磨坊和学堂。阿拉贡的海梅一世早先一次围攻无功而返，1244年5月终于拿下此城；他保留了城里的清真寺，把沙蒂瓦设为胡卡尔河外辖区的首府，1250年准许开设集市，1347年佩德罗四世授予城市称号。作为王国第二大城，它靠纸张和亚麻立足，也是博尔吉亚家族的桑梓：未来的教皇加里斯都三世阿方索·德·博尔哈1378年出生于此，他的外甥罗德里戈·德·博尔哈，即后来的亚历山大六世，生于1431年前后。1444年的沙蒂瓦城墙环绕，约有八千居民。

兄弟会起义把这座城变成了战场：起义领袖维森特·佩里斯以沙蒂瓦为据点坚守，1522年被杀。画家何塞·德·里韦拉（绰号「小西班牙人」）1591年出生于此。1609至1614年驱逐摩里斯科人，使辖区内一百多处村落荒无人烟，人口损失近半，17世纪的瘟疫又使人口进一步减少。西班牙王位继承战争中，沙蒂瓦支持哈布斯堡觊觎者，波旁军队在阿尔曼萨获胜后，达斯费尔德率军围城，城堡里的英国守军1707年6月12日开出城外。城市随即遭到洗劫和纵火，相传大火烧了一年，居民被流放至拉曼查；腓力五世把这片焦黑的废墟命名为圣费利佩新殖民地，废除了古老的辖区，而这场大火也给沙蒂瓦人送来了「烧焦的人」（socarrats）的绰号。1811年，加的斯议会恢复了城市的旧名。

en:
Castelló lies on the flat coastal plain north of Valencia, the Plana crossed and watered by the Mijares, and the wheat of its irrigated fields made the district one of the granaries of the Kingdom of Valencia. Its people began on the Magdalena height, in the Muslim hill-fort of Fadrell, which capitulated to James I of Aragon in 1233. After the Mudéjar revolt of 1247 the Muslim population was expelled, and on 8 September 1251 the king authorised Ximén Pérez d'Arenós to bring the settlement down from the hill onto the plain; local tradition dates the move to the third Sunday of Lent 1252. The new town was ringed with moats, walls and towers, and its grain and fruit were loaded at the Grau, its beach landing on the shore. In 1366 a farmer called Perot de Granyana found a buried image of the Virgin, Our Lady of Lledó, who became the town's patron. During the succession crisis of 1410-1412 Castelló withstood the governor Bellera and, on 24 April 1412, defeated an attacking army at its gates, leaving more than five hundred assailants dead; two months later the Compromise of Caspe gave the crown to Ferdinand of Trastámara. In 1444 Castelló was a small royal town living off its fields and its beach trade.

In the Germanías revolt Castelló rose against Charles I and was one of the guildsmen's last strongholds until the Duke of Segorbe took and sacked it in 1521. The Crown afterwards kept clipping its old privileges; in 1616 its justicia and jurats were carried off to Valencia as prisoners. Plague ran through the town from 1647 to 1653. In the War of the Spanish Succession Castelló backed the Habsburg claimant, and in May 1707 Berwick entered it, exacted a forced payment of 8,840 Valencian pounds and had the medieval walls demolished. The Nueva Planta decree of that year abolished the Valencian furs, and in February 1708 a Castilian-style town council took over. A hemp industry grew up from 1747, and the last stretches of wall were cleared in 1796 to let the town spread.
zh:
卡斯特略位于巴伦西亚北面平坦的沿海平原上，米哈雷斯河纵贯并灌溉着这片名叫「普拉纳」的平原，灌溉田里的小麦使这一带成为巴伦西亚王国的粮仓之一。居民最初住在马格达莱纳高地上的穆斯林山堡法德雷尔，1233年山堡向阿拉贡的海梅一世投降。1247年穆德哈尔起义后，当地穆斯林遭到驱逐；1251年9月8日国王特许希门·佩雷斯·德·阿雷诺斯把定居点从山上迁到平原，相传迁城在1252年大斋期第三个星期日完成。新城外有壕沟、城墙和塔楼，粮食和果品在海滨滩岸格劳装船外运。1366年，农夫佩罗特·德·格拉尼亚纳挖出一尊被掩埋的圣母像，即利多圣母，后来成为城镇的主保。1410至1412年王位空缺期间，卡斯特略抵挡住总督贝列拉，1412年4月24日又在城下击败来犯军队，攻方死者逾五百；两个月后卡斯佩妥协把王冠交给特拉斯塔马拉家族的费尔南多。1444年的卡斯特略是一座靠田地和滨海贸易为生的皇家小镇。

兄弟会起义中卡斯特略起兵反对卡洛斯一世，是起义行会最后的据点之一，1521年被塞戈尔韦公爵攻破洗劫。此后王室不断裁削它的旧有特权，1616年甚至把市政法官和陪审官作为囚犯押往巴伦西亚。1647至1653年瘟疫肆虐。西班牙王位继承战争中它支持哈布斯堡觊觎者，1707年5月贝里克入城，强征8840巴伦西亚镑，并下令拆毁中世纪城墙；同年颁布的《新基本法令》废除巴伦西亚地方特许状，1708年2月按卡斯蒂利亚模式组建的新市府开始运作。1747年起大麻产业兴起，1796年残存的城墙也被拆除，好让城镇向外扩展。

en:
Ávila lies on the high meseta beside the Adaja, over 1,100 metres up and the highest city in Castile. It was a Visigothic bishopric, then a Muslim frontier fortress and an almost deserted no man's land, until Raymond of Burgundy repopulated it for Alfonso VI after 1088. Its walls, begun then and rebuilt through the twelfth century, ring the old town: about 2,500 metres of rampart with 88 semicircular towers and nine gates, one of the most complete medieval circuits in Europe. The cathedral was built into the wall, and its apse forms one of the towers. Frontier council militias raided as far south as Seville and Córdoba; by the late thirteenth century the town held one of Castile's largest Jewish communities, a vote in the Cortes, great herds on its pastures and a cloth industry that never matched Flemish or Italian wares. In 1444 Ávila was a quiet walled town of herdsmen and weavers, its frontier days long past.

On 5 June 1465 rebel nobles staged the ceremony later called the Farce of Ávila on open ground outside the walls. They set a wooden statue of Henry IV on a platform, dressed in mourning and wearing the crown, with his sword and staff beside it; after reading their charges they stripped the effigy of crown, sword and staff in turn and threw it to the ground, then proclaimed the king's half-brother Alfonso, not yet eleven. The Jewish quarter ended with the expulsion of 1492. When the Comuneros rose in 1520 their Holy Junta met first at Ávila, on 1 August, and drafted its perpetual-law project inside the cathedral. The town's most famous child is Teresa de Jesús, born here in 1515: in 1562 she founded San José, the first convent of her Discalced Carmelites, and she was canonized in 1622. Its walls and its mystics gave Ávila the name of the 'City of Stones and Saints'. French troops under Marshal Lefebvre sacked it from 4 to 7 January 1809 and looted its churches.
zh:
阿维拉位于阿达哈河畔的高原台地，海拔逾1100米，是卡斯蒂利亚地势最高的城市。这里先是西哥特人的主教驻地，穆斯林时期成为边塞要塞，后来沦为几近荒弃的无人地带，直到1088年后勃艮第的雷蒙奉阿方索六世之命重新移民屯垦。环城城墙此时动工，12世纪又经历重修，环抱着老城：墙身周长约2500米，立着88座半圆形塔楼，开有九座城门，是欧洲最完整的中世纪城墙之一。大教堂直接修进墙体，它的半圆形后殿就是墙上一座塔楼。边塞年代，市政民兵曾南下远掠塞维利亚和科尔多瓦；到13世纪末，阿维拉拥有卡斯蒂利亚最大的犹太社区之一、议会中的一票、四野的大群牛羊，还有一门始终敌不过佛兰德和意大利货的呢绒业。1444年的阿维拉是一座安静的城墙之城，居民以牧人和织工为主，边塞岁月早已远去。

1465年6月5日，叛乱贵族在城外举行后来被称作「阿维拉闹剧」的仪式。他们把恩里克四世的木像安在高台上，木像身着丧服、头戴王冠，旁边摆着国王的剑和权杖；宣读罪状之后，众人依次摘去塑像的王冠、剑和杖，将它掀翻在地，随即拥立国王尚未满十一岁的异母弟阿方索。1492年的驱逐令终结了犹太区。1520年公社起义爆发，起事者的「神圣委员会」于8月1日首先在阿维拉集会，在大教堂内起草《永久法律草案》。阿维拉最有名的孩子是1515年出生于此的特雷莎·德·赫苏斯：1562年她创立圣何塞修道院，即赤脚加尔默罗会的第一座修院，1622年被封圣。城墙与圣徒为阿维拉赢来「石头与圣徒之城」的称号。1809年1月4日至7日，勒菲弗尔元帅麾下的法军洗劫全城，抢掠各教堂。

en:
Palencia stands on the Carrión River in Tierra de Campos, the wheat country medieval writers called the Campos Góticos. The Vaccaei knew the settlement as Pallantia, and under the Visigoths it held a Christian bishopric that vanished after the Muslim conquest until Sancho III of Navarre restored it in 1035. Its schools became the first university in Castile: the studium Alfonso VIII and Bishop Tello Téllez de Meneses founded between 1208 and 1212 was confirmed by Pope Honorius III in 1221, and Domingo de Guzmán, later Saint Dominic, read the arts there for six years and theology for four. The Gothic cathedral was begun in 1321, and the road to Santiago crossed the north of the province past the Romanesque San Martín at Frómista and the pilgrim town of Carrión de los Condes. In 1444 Palencia was an episcopal city under one of Castile's richest dioceses, ringed by the wheat fields that paid for it.

Most of Palencia's Jews chose exile in Portugal in 1492, and their synagogue was a slaughterhouse by 1495. The city threw itself into the Comunero revolt of 1520: Antonio de Acuña, the fighting bishop of Zamora, raised troops at Dueñas and the city ran a war council, until the royal victory at Villalar on 23 April 1521; in 1524 it bought its pardon for 925,000 maravedís, which paid for repairs to the episcopal tower and palace. The province also produced the poet and courtier Íñigo López de Mendoza, Marqués de Santillana, born at Carrión de los Condes in 1398, and the painters Pedro Berruguete and his son Alonso, the leading sculptor of the Spanish Renaissance, both from Paredes de Nava. After the decline of the 17th century, engineers began the Canal of Castile at Calahorra de Ribas on 16 July 1753 and joined its branches in August 1791, to carry Tierra de Campos wheat to the northern ports. French troops were quartered on the city in 1808; the rising of 5 June brought battalions two days later, and the town escaped sack only through the council's and bishop's pleas.
zh:
帕伦西亚位于卡尔皮翁河畔，地处田野坎波斯的广阔小麦平原，中世纪作家称这片平原为「哥特田野」。瓦凯伊人曾称此地为帕兰提亚，西哥特时代这里设有基督教主教座，穆斯林征服后一度中断，直到1035年纳瓦拉的桑乔三世恢复主教区。当地的学堂发展成卡斯蒂利亚的第一所大学：阿方索八世与特略·特列斯·德·梅内塞斯主教在1208年至1212年间创办学堂，教皇洪诺留三世1221年予以批准；日后创立多明我会的多明戈·德·古斯曼曾在此攻读六年艺学、四年神学。宏大的哥特式主教座堂1321年动工，通往圣地亚哥德孔波斯特拉的朝圣路穿过省境北部，沿途有弗罗米斯塔的罗曼式圣马丁教堂和朝圣重镇卡里翁德洛斯孔德斯。1444年的帕伦西亚是一座主教城市，隶属于卡斯蒂利亚最富有的教区之一，供养它的是四周的麦田。

1492年，城中大多数犹太人不愿受洗，选择流亡葡萄牙；到1495年，他们的会堂已经被当作屠宰场。1520年，帕伦西亚全力投入公社起义：善战的萨莫拉主教安东尼奥·德·阿库尼亚在杜埃尼亚斯募兵，城中自设战争议事会，直到王军1521年4月23日在维拉拉尔取胜；1524年，城市缴纳92.5万马拉维迪才换来赦免，这笔钱用于修缮主教塔楼和宫邸。这片地方也出过文人和艺术家：诗人兼廷臣、桑蒂利亚纳侯爵伊尼戈·洛佩斯·德·门多萨1398年生于卡里翁德洛斯孔德斯，帕雷德斯德纳瓦则出了西班牙-佛兰德斯画派的佩德罗·贝鲁格特，以及他的儿子、西班牙文艺复兴最重要的雕塑家阿隆索·贝鲁格特。17世纪的衰落之后，工程师们1753年7月16日在卡拉奥拉德里瓦斯开工修建卡斯蒂利亚运河，各支段于1791年8月合流，把田野坎波斯的小麦运往北方港口。1808年法军驻扎城中；6月5日的起义在两天后招来法军营队，全靠市政当局和主教出面求情，城市才免遭洗劫。

en:
Zamora sits on a rocky bluff above the Duero, and for three centuries it was the great fortress of the Christian north, the 'well-walled city', la bien cercada, of the romances. Alfonso III of León repopulated it in 893 with Mozarab builders from Toledo, and its walls held the frontier until Almanzor sacked the city in 981 and again in 997. Ferdinand I rebuilt the fortifications in 1055 and left the city to his daughter Urraca. In 1072 her brother Sancho II of Castile, besieging the walls with El Cid at his side, was lured out and killed by the Zamoran noble Bellido Dolfos; the Portillo de la Traición, the Treason Gate, takes its name from the deed. Castile passed to the deposed Alfonso VI, and on 5 October 1143 Alfonso VII concluded here the Treaty of Zamora, recognising Afonso Henriques as king of Portugal. Bishops and princes ringed the city with Romanesque churches, twenty-four in all, more than any other city in Europe. Zamora cast one of the seventeen votes in the Cortes of Castile and even spoke there for all Galicia. In 1444 it was a Leonese-speaking city of grain and wine on the road into Portugal.

That road turned the district into a battlefield in the War of the Castilian Succession, when Afonso V's Portuguese held nearby Toro; the battle fought there on 1 March 1476 left Isabella and Ferdinand the political masters of Castile. The long sieges gave Spanish the saying that Zamora was not won in an hour. In 1492 the expelled Jews crossed here into Portugal, some 30,000 passing by way of Miranda do Douro; the crown gave their Great Synagogue to the city as a church and a hospital for the poor, and the busy frontier made Zamora a smugglers' town. On 6 January 1809 the townsmen fought the French at the Villagodio bridge before giving ground, and the French occupation lasted until the campaign that ended at Salamanca in 1812.
zh:
萨莫拉雄踞杜罗河畔的岩石高岗，在三百年里是基督教北方最坚固的要塞，即歌谣里「城墙环绕之城」（la bien cercada）。893年，莱昂国王阿方索三世把托莱多的莫萨拉布工匠迁来定居，城防一直支撑着边境战事，直到981年和997年两度遭曼苏尔洗劫。费尔南多一世1055年重修城防，把城市留给女儿乌拉卡。1072年，她的兄长卡斯蒂利亚国王桑乔二世在熙德陪同下围城，被萨莫拉贵族贝利多·多尔福斯诱出杀害，「叛国门」即因此事得名。卡斯蒂利亚王位随之落入被废的阿方索六世之手；1143年10月5日，阿方索七世在此缔结《萨莫拉条约》，承认阿丰索·恩里克斯为葡萄牙国王。主教和王公在城中建起24座罗曼式教堂，数量为欧洲城市之最。萨莫拉在卡斯蒂利亚议会十七张表决票中占其一，甚至代表整个加利西亚发言。1444年，它是通往葡萄牙大道上一座说莱昂语、产粮产酒的城市。

卡斯蒂利亚王位继承战争中，这条大道把这一带变成战场：阿丰索五世的葡萄牙军队占据附近的托罗，1476年3月1日的托罗之战在政治上让伊莎贝尔和费尔南多成为卡斯蒂利亚的主人。长年的围城还给西班牙语留下一句谚语：萨莫拉不是一个时辰打下来的。1492年，被逐的犹太人经此进入葡萄牙，约三万人取道米兰达杜罗过境；王室把他们的大会堂赐给城里，改作教堂和济贫医院，繁忙的边境也使萨莫拉成了走私客的城镇。1809年1月6日，市民在比亚戈迪奥桥迎战法军后撤退，法国人的占领一直持续到1812年以萨拉曼卡之战告终的那场战役。

en:
Lugo stands inland on a hill above the upper Miño, the oldest town in Galicia. The Romans founded Lucus Augusti in the age of Augustus as the seat of one of the three judicial districts of Gallaecia, in busy gold-mining country, and between about 260 and 325 they girdled it with a wall two kilometres round whose full circuit of gates and towers still rings the old town. The Suevi made it an archbishop's see in 460; after the Visigothic conquest of 585 it withered, and when Alfonso I entered unopposed in 741 Bishop Odoario found it half in ruins and rebuilt it. The Galician army gathered here in 842 to enthrone Ramiro I, and in 1088 Alfonso VI made the bishop lord of the city. Lugo lay on the Camino Primitivo, the early pilgrim road to Santiago: pilgrims entered by the Porta Miña to visit the cathedral begun in 1129, where the host was perpetually exposed, a rare privilege. In 1312 the townspeople drove out their bishop, and the crown prince Philip built a fortress there against him four years later. In 1444 Lugo was an old, church-ruled Castilian town inside its Roman walls, overshadowed by Santiago and the feuding Galician nobles.

When the Great Irmandiño War broke out in 1467 Lugo sent representatives to the brotherhood, and baronial strongholds went down across the region before the lords crushed the rising in 1469. Early in the sixteenth century Charles V could still name Lugo one of the capitals of the Kingdom of Galicia, but the city then declined while Santiago prospered. In 1669 the Kingdom of Galicia instituted its annual offering to the Sacrament in the cathedral, honouring the city's perpetual host. The eighteenth century brought the St Froilán cattle fairs, confirmed by royal privilege in 1754, which sold horses and mules to León and Castile; the Lisbon earthquake of 1755 cracked the cathedral's vault and the altarpiece was dismantled. War returned on 9 January 1809, when Soult's vanguard clashed with Moore's retreating British army at Conturiz outside the walls and the French occupied Lugo, until a Galician rising and the defeat at Puentesampayo drove them out that summer.
zh:
卢戈地处内陆，坐落在上米尼奥河畔的一座山丘上，是加利西亚最古老的城镇。罗马人在奥古斯都时代建立卢库斯·奥古斯塔，作为加拉西亚三个司法辖区之一的治所，地处繁忙的金矿区，约260至325年间环以两公里长的城墙，整道墙垣连同各门和塔楼完整地围在老城四周。460年苏维汇人将卢戈升为大主教驻地；585年西哥特征服后城市凋敝，741年阿方索一世兵不血刃入城时，奥多阿里奥主教见城池半毁，着手重建。842年，加利西亚军队在此集结，拥立拉米罗一世；1088年阿方索六世把城市封给主教。卢戈在通往圣地亚哥的原始朝圣路上，朝圣者经米尼亚门前往1129年动工的主教座堂，城中的教士团享有永久供奉圣体这一少见的特权。1312年市民驱逐主教，四年后王子费利佩为对抗主教在此修筑城堡。1444年的卢戈是一座围在罗马城墙内、由教会统治的卡斯蒂利亚古城，声势为圣地亚哥和混战不休的加利西亚贵族所掩。

1467年伊尔曼迪尼奥战争爆发，卢戈派出代表加入兄弟会，在领主们1469年镇压起义之前，这一带的贵族堡垒纷纷被拆毁。16世纪初，卡洛斯一世还能把卢戈列为加利西亚王国的首府之一，但城市此后陷入长期衰落，圣地亚哥则日益繁荣。1669年，加利西亚王国在主教座堂设立一年一度向圣体奉献的仪式，致敬此城永久供奉的圣体。18世纪，圣弗罗伊兰牛市带来复苏，集市1754年获王家特许，马匹和骡子远销莱昂和卡斯蒂利亚；1755年里斯本大地震震裂主教座堂的拱顶，大祭坛被拆除。1809年1月9日，苏尔特的先头部队在城外孔图里斯与撤退中的穆尔所部英军交战，法军随即占领卢戈，直到当年夏天加利西亚起义和蓬特桑帕约之战才把他们逐出该省。

en:
Pontevedra sits at the head of its ria, where the Lérez runs into the sea among the Rías Baixas. It takes its name from an old Roman bridge over the river, and its quays grew up beside the Burgo bridge on the Portuguese road to Santiago, whose arches are carved with pilgrim scallop shells. Fishing and shipbuilding made the town: in 1229 the crown gave its townsmen the monopoly of sardine oil and fish curing across Galicia, and its yards built the fleet that Payo Gómez Chariño, a son of Pontevedra, led to help Ferdinand III take Seville in 1248. By the fifteenth century it was the leading town of Galicia, with the busiest harbour on the coast; the French chronicler Froissart called it the good city. In 1444 it was a thriving Castilian port, living off the catch, the yards and the sea trade.

The crown made Pontevedra Galicia's sole port for loading and unloading cargo, and in 1467 Henry IV granted it the thirty-day free fair, the Feira Franca, for which the walls were extended. Townsmen had joined the first of the Galician brotherhoods in the rias of Pontevedra and Arousa in 1451, and the town sent its men to the Great Irmandiño War of 1467-1469 against the Galician nobles. The yards are traditionally said to have built Columbus's carrack Santa María, 'La Gallega'. The mariners' brotherhood, the oldest sea guild in Spain, paid for the basilica of Santa María la Mayor, whose plateresque facade was finished in 1541. Then the Lérez began to silt up so that large ships could no longer reach the quays, and war and plague cut the population by half. In October 1719 a British expedition under Lord Cobham held the town for ten days. In 1809 a French army occupied the coast until the Galician División del Miño, mustered around Pontevedra, checked it at Puentesampayo on 7-9 June and drove the French out of Galicia.
zh:
蓬特韦德拉位于下海湾地区莱雷斯河入海的河口顶端，城名来自河上一座古罗马桥。码头沿布尔戈桥发展起来，此桥在通往圣地亚哥的葡萄牙朝圣道上，桥拱上刻着朝圣用的扇贝壳。这座城镇靠渔业和造船立足：1229年，王室把全加利西亚沙丁鱼油和咸鱼加工的专营权授予镇民，船坞打造的舰队由本镇子弟帕约·戈麦斯·查里尼奥率领，1248年协助费尔南多三世攻取塞维利亚。到15世纪，它已是加利西亚首屈一指的城镇，港口为全海岸最繁忙，法国编年史家傅华萨称它为「良城」。1444年的它是卡斯蒂利亚治下一座兴旺的港口，靠渔获、船坞和海贸为生。

王室把加利西亚唯一的货物装卸港资格授予蓬特韦德拉；1467年恩里克四世又准其举办为期三十天的自由集市，为此扩建了城墙。早在1451年，镇民就加入了蓬特韦德拉湾与阿罗萨湾一带加利西亚的第一个兄弟会，后来又投身1467至1469年反抗加利西亚贵族的伊尔曼迪尼奥大战。相传哥伦布的克拉克帆船「圣马利亚号」（又名「加利西亚人号」）就出自这里的船坞。西班牙最古老的海员行会出资修建大圣马利亚圣殿，银匠式立面于1541年完工。后来莱雷斯河日渐淤塞，大船无法再驶到码头，战乱和瘟疫又使人口减半。1719年10月，科巴姆勋爵率领的英国远征军占领此城十天。1809年法军占据沿海，在蓬特韦德拉一带编组的加利西亚「米尼奥师」于6月7日至9日在蓬特桑帕约阻击得手，把法国人逐出了加利西亚。

en:
Aveiro sits behind the sandbars of a shallow Atlantic lagoon, at the mouth of the Vouga, where salt pans, fishing grounds and coastal sea lanes meet. The Romans already worked the salt here, and the will Countess Mumadona Dias left in 959 named her lands Alauario et Salinas, the 'bird preserve and salt pans'. John I had walls raised on the advice of his son Peter, the town's lord, and in 1434 Edward I granted an annual duty-free fair, the Feira de Março. In 1444 Aveiro was a walled Catholic salt town and small port held by Peter, Duke of Coimbra and regent of Portugal; its households lived from salt, fish and the coasting trade.

Royal favour came to Aveiro above all through Afonso V's daughter Joanna. She ruled Portugal as regent in 1471 while her father campaigned in Morocco, then entered the Dominican Convent of Jesus in the town and stayed until her death on 12 May 1490, venerated in Portugal as the Holy Princess, Santa Joana Princesa. Manuel I granted the first charter on 4 August 1515, and in 1547 John III created the Duchy of Aveiro for John of Lencastre. Between the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries the lagoon's outlet to the ocean shifted and closed. The port died, the waters stagnated and many fishermen emigrated, and the Misericórdia church was built in those hard years. In 1759 Duke José Mascarenhas was condemned and executed in the Távora affair; the ducal title was extinguished, Joseph I raised Aveiro to city rank, and for a time it was called Nova Bragança. An artificial channel cut through the bar in 1808 gave the lagoon a sea entrance again and brought trade back.
zh:
阿威罗在大西洋浅水潟湖的沙洲背后、沃加河入海处，盐田、渔场和沿海航路在此相接。罗马人已在这里煮盐，959年穆马多娜·迪亚斯伯爵夫人的遗嘱把她的领地记作「鸟类栖地与盐田」（Alauario et Salinas）。若昂一世听取领有此地的儿子佩德罗的建议修筑城墙，1434年杜阿尔特一世又恩准一年一度的免税集市，即后来的三月集市。1444年的阿威罗是一座有城墙的天主教盐业小镇和小港，属科英布拉公爵、葡萄牙摄政佩德罗，居民靠盐、鱼和沿海航运为生。

让王室眷顾阿威罗的，主要是阿方索五世的女儿若阿纳。1471年父亲在摩洛哥作战期间，她以公主身份摄政，随后进入城中的多明我会耶稣修道院，一直住到1490年5月12日去世，葡萄牙人敬称她「圣公主」若阿纳。1515年8月4日曼努埃尔一世颁下第一道特许状，1547年若昂三世为若昂·德·伦卡斯特尔设立阿威罗公爵衔。16世纪末至17世纪初，潟湖入海的水口移动后封闭，港口荒废，积水污浊，许多渔民外迁，仁慈堂教堂就建于这艰难的年月。1759年，公爵若泽·马斯卡雷尼亚斯在塔沃拉事件中被定罪处决，公爵衔遭革除，若泽一世把阿威罗升为城市，还一度改称新布拉干萨。1808年，人们凿开沙洲开出人工水道，潟湖重获入海口，贸易也跟着恢复。

en:
Calatayud commands the Jalón gap, the pass linking the Castilian meseta with the Ebro valley and carrying the road from Zaragoza to Castile. Four kilometres to the north stand the ruins of Augusta Bilbilis, capital of the Celtiberian Lusones and a town already famous for its metalwork; it was the birthplace of the poet Martial about AD 40, who praised its hills and the sulphur springs twenty-four kilometres away, the spas still used at Alhama de Aragón. After Bilbilis declined, the Muslims founded the present town around 716 beside the castle of Ayyub, Qal'at Ayyub in Arabic, from which Calatayud takes its name. Alfonso I of Aragon stormed it on 24 June 1120, consecrated the chief mosque as Santa María and granted fueros to the settlers, and from 1131 the town ruled a wide community of villages. In 1444 it was a prosperous Catholic Aragonese market town on the Castile road, with one of the largest Jewish quarters in the kingdom below the old castle and brick Mudéjar towers rebuilt after the war between Aragon and Castile.

The Jewish aljama, almost as large as Zaragoza's, ended with the expulsion of 1492. Santa María stayed a collegiate church: the town council tried once more to unite its three chapters and win a bishopric in 1592, without success. The Jesuits opened a college late in the sixteenth century, and Baltasar Gracián, born at nearby Belmonte in 1601, taught humanities there in 1627; he later wrote The Art of Worldly Wisdom and the allegorical novel El Criticón. After the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 their church became San Juan el Real in 1771. Calatayud followed Aragon into the Austrian cause in the War of the Spanish Succession, and came under Bourbon rule after the defeat at Almansa and the Nueva Planta decrees. French troops clashed here in November 1808 and held the town through most of the Peninsular War, until Pedro Villacampa drove them out on 2 October 1812.
zh:
卡拉塔尤德扼守哈隆河谷山口，这里是卡斯蒂利亚高原通往埃布罗河谷的孔道，萨拉戈萨至卡斯蒂利亚的大路从这里穿过。城北四公里是奥古斯塔·比尔比利斯遗址，原为凯尔特伊比利亚卢松人的都城，古时便以金属工艺闻名；约公元40年，诗人马提亚尔出生于此，他在诗中称赞故乡的山野和二十四公里外的硫磺温泉，那里就是后来的阿拉马-德阿拉贡温泉。比尔比利斯衰落后，穆斯林约在716年依阿尤布城堡建起新城，阿拉伯语称「阿尤布堡」，卡拉塔尤德的名字便来自这座城堡。1120年6月24日，阿拉贡国王阿方索一世破城，将大清真寺祝圣为圣马利亚教堂，向居民授予特许状；1131年起，这座城镇统辖广阔的村庄共同体。1444年的卡拉塔尤德是一座繁荣的天主教阿拉贡集镇，位于通往卡斯蒂利亚的大路上，旧城堡下有王国最大的犹太区之一，阿拉贡与卡斯蒂利亚战争后重建的砖造穆德哈尔塔楼矗立城中。

规模几乎仅次于萨拉戈萨的犹太社区在1492年驱逐令后终结。圣马利亚始终只是协同教堂：市政会1592年再次试图合并三个教士团、争取设立主教区，仍未成功。耶稣会在16世纪末创办学院，1601年出生于附近贝尔蒙特的巴尔塔萨尔·格拉西安于1627年在此讲授人文学，他后来写成《智慧书》和寓言小说《批评家》。1767年耶稣会被逐后，其教堂于1771年改为圣胡安·埃尔雷亚尔堂。西班牙王位继承战争中，卡拉塔尤德随阿拉贡支持奥地利阵营，阿尔曼萨之战和《新基本法令》后转入波旁统治。1808年11月法军曾在此交战，半岛战争大部分时间占据城镇，直到1812年10月2日佩德罗·比利亚坎帕将其收复。

en:
Ourense lies inland in a warm valley of the upper Miño, and two things have always defined it: hot water and a bridge. The Burgas springs, channelled since Roman times, run at 60 to 68 degrees; one reading of the town's Roman name Auriense makes it the city of gold, for the gold panned in the Miño. The Romans founded the town to guard the crossing on the road from Braga to Astorga, and the piers of the great bridge over the river are still Roman work. Suevic kings are said to have kept a court here, and after the Moorish capture in 716 and the later raids of Norse fleets and Al-Mansur, the town was rebuilt and resettled in the eleventh century. In 1122 Teresa of Portugal made the bishops lords of the city, and they ruled it for five centuries from Castelo Ramiro, their fortress on the hill, while they consolidated the bridge and drew wealth from the Ribeiro vineyards downstream. The Romanesque cathedral, consecrated in 1188, keeps the Pórtico del Paraíso and the much-venerated Santo Cristo. In 1444 Ourense was a quiet Castilian cathedral town on the Sanabrés road to Santiago.

In 1386 John of Gaunt occupied Ourense and had himself proclaimed king of Castile there by right of his wife, until the Treaty of Bayonne ended his claim two years later; in 1501 Philip the Handsome and Juana met Cardinal Cisneros in the city. During the Irmandiño rising of 1468, rebels stormed the baronial castles of the district and partly pulled down the Count of Lemos's fortress at Castro Caldelas, whose lords later made the villagers rebuild it. The Catholic Monarchs had the bishops' own Castelo Ramiro demolished, and the Jewish quarter was emptied in the expulsion of 1492. Ribeiro wine went down the Miño to the sea and on to England and the Indies, and the old bridge took its present form around 1660. In 1809 French troops overran the district and General Loison burned Castro Caldelas in reprisal for the guerrilla war, before the Galician rising and the victory at Puentesampayo drove the French out that June.
zh:
奥伦塞深居内陆，坐落在上米尼奥河一处温暖的河谷，两样东西自古决定了它的面貌：热水和桥梁。布尔加斯温泉自罗马时代起就被引作浴用，水温高达60至68摄氏度；关于城名的一种解释是罗马名Auriense，意为「金城」，因米尼奥河里可以淘金。罗马人在此建城，扼守布拉加至阿斯托加大道上的渡口，跨河大桥的桥墩仍是罗马旧物。据说苏维汇国王曾在此设宫廷；716年城市被穆斯林攻占，后来又屡遭诺曼舰队和曼苏尔蹂躏，11世纪才得以重建和重新安置。1122年，葡萄牙的特蕾莎把城市管辖权授予主教，此后主教们从山上的卡拉米罗堡统治此城五百年，同时主持加固大桥、从下游的里贝罗葡萄园取得财富。现存罗曼式主教座堂1188年祝圣，堂内有天堂门廊和备受敬奉的圣基督像。1444年的奥伦塞，是萨纳夫雷斯圣地亚哥朝圣道上一座宁静的卡斯蒂利亚主教城。

1386年，冈特的约翰占领奥伦塞，凭妻子的权利在此自立为卡斯蒂利亚国王，两年后《巴约讷条约》终结了他的继承权；1501年，美男子费利佩与胡安娜在此会见希斯内罗斯枢机。1468年伊尔曼迪尼奥起义期间，起事者攻打全区的贵族城堡，拆毁了莱莫斯伯爵在卡斯特罗卡尔德拉斯要塞的一部分，领主回来后又强迫村民将其重建。天主教双王后来下令拆毁主教名下的卡拉米罗堡，1492年犹太区也随驱逐令人去屋空。里贝罗葡萄酒顺米尼奥河运到海边，再远销英格兰和西印度，古桥则在1660年前后完成最后一次大修。1809年法军席卷此地，卢瓦松将军为报复游击战焚毁卡斯特罗卡尔德拉斯，直到当年6月加利西亚起义和蓬特桑帕约之战才把法国人赶走。

en:
Menorca is the smaller and more northerly of the two Gymnesian Islands, a dry country of farms and fishing anchorages. Its prehistoric people left boat-shaped navetes, taules and talaiot towers, which still dot its fields. After James I of Aragon took Mallorca, the Muslim island became his tributary in 1231 and kept its own rulers until Alfonso III invaded in January 1287; much of the population was then enslaved and Catalans settled the island, which in 1343 passed with the Kingdom of Mallorca to the Crown of Aragon. In 1444 it was a thinly peopled Catalan Catholic land, governed from western Ciutadella with Mahón at its eastern end. Mahón's inlet runs five kilometres inland, among the finest natural harbours in the western Mediterranean, on the sea lanes between Iberia, Sardinia and North Africa; mayonnaise is said to take its name from the town.

The sixteenth century brought the island its worst raids. In 1535, after the Spanish capture of Tunis, Hayreddin Barbarossa sacked Mahón and carried off about 600 captives to Algiers. In July 1558 an Ottoman fleet burned Ciutadella and took thousands of its people; the year is still remembered as Any de sa Desgràcia, the Year of Misfortune. Philip II then set his engineer Giovanni Battista Calvi to build Fort Sant Felip across the harbour mouth.

That harbour made Menorca a naval prize in the wars of the next century. An Anglo-Dutch force took the island in 1708 and the Treaty of Utrecht assigned it to Britain five years later. The British moved the capital from Ciutadella to Mahón, opened a Royal Navy dockyard there in 1715 and enlarged Sant Felip into a Mediterranean base. In May 1756 a French fleet beat off Admiral John Byng's relief squadron off the island and the fort surrendered; Byng was court-martialled and shot in 1757 for failing to do his utmost. France returned Menorca in 1763, a Franco-Spanish siege of nearly five months took it in 1782, and the Peace of Paris gave it back to Spain.
zh:
梅诺卡是吉姆内西亚两岛中较小、也更靠北的一座，气候干燥，乡间分布着农庄和渔船锚地。史前岛民留下船形石墓、石桌祭台和圆形石塔，仍散布岛上田野。阿拉贡国王海梅一世攻占马略卡后，这座穆斯林岛屿于1231年称臣纳贡，仍保留自己的统治者；1287年1月阿方索三世发兵入侵，投降之后居民多被鬻为奴隶，加泰罗尼亚移民迁来填补，1343年该岛随马略卡王国并入阿拉贡。1444年的梅诺卡人烟稀少，是操加泰罗尼亚语的天主教之地，岛西的休达德拉为统治中心，岛东端是马翁。马翁港湾深入陆地五公里，是西地中海最好的天然良港之一，扼伊比利亚、撒丁岛与北非之间的海路；据说西文里蛋黄酱一词就得名于马翁。

16世纪是梅诺卡遭劫最重的时期。1535年西班牙攻占突尼斯后，海雷丁·巴尔巴罗萨洗劫马翁，把约六百名俘虏押往阿尔及尔。1558年7月，奥斯曼舰队焚毁休达德拉，掳走数千居民，梅诺卡人把这一年称作「不幸之年」。腓力二世随后命工程师乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·卡尔维主持修筑，在马翁港入口建起圣费利佩堡。

正是这座港湾，让梅诺卡在18世纪的战争中成了各国争夺的海军据点。1708年英荷联军攻占该岛，五年后《乌得勒支条约》把它划归英国。英国人把首府从休达德拉迁往马翁，1715年在港内开设皇家海军船坞，把圣费利佩堡扩建成地中海基地。1756年5月，法国舰队在岛外击退约翰·拜恩率领的救援舰队，堡垒随后投降；拜恩经军事法庭审判，1757年以未尽全力为由被枪决。法国1763年归还梅诺卡，1782年法西联军近五个月的围攻再下该岛，《巴黎条约》又把它交还西班牙。

en:
Ibiza and Formentera, the Pine Islands, are the Balearics closest to the Iberian coast, 150 kilometres from Valencia. Phoenician settlers founded a port here in 654 BC, and Punic Ebusus traded salt, dye, fish sauce and wool; its people honoured the goddess Tanit at the Es Cuieram cave, and in 205 BC the fleeing Carthaginian general Mago called there for men and supplies. Muslim Yabisah looked across the water to Dénia, its nearest market. The Norwegian king Sigurd the Crusader sacked the island in 1110 on his way to Jerusalem, and a Sicilian Norman fleet sacked it again in 1159. In August 1235 Guillem de Montgrí, Archbishop of Tarragona, took Ibiza for James I of Aragon; most of the Muslim population was deported and settlers came from the Girona country. In 1444 it was a Catalan Catholic island run from the walled Vila above the harbour, and the southern salt pans filled the island council's treasury.

Salt was the island's fortune. Seawater was trapped in shallow pools along the southern shore, evaporated, and carried to ships beside the pans, and the Universitat, the island council created in 1299, lived on the trade. Repeated Barbary and Ottoman raids moved Philip II to rebuild the defences in Renaissance form: Giovanni Battista Calvi laid out bastions around the Vila from 1555, and Giacomo Fratín revised the works after 1575, giving Ibiza Town its walled upper city, Dalt Vila.

The island kept its own government until the War of the Spanish Succession. Its elite split, but Ibiza held to the Austrian claimant until Bourbon troops completed the conquest of the Balearics in July 1715. Philip V's Nueva Planta decree that November abolished the Universitat and gave the salt pans to the Crown, so the island's old income flowed to Madrid; the replacement town council was not settled until 1724.
zh:
伊维萨与福门特拉合称松树群岛，是巴利阿里群岛中最靠近伊比利亚海岸的两座，距瓦伦西亚仅一百五十公里。公元前654年，腓尼基商人在此建港，布匿时代的埃布苏斯经营盐、染料、鱼酱和羊毛；岛民在埃斯库埃拉姆洞供奉塔尼特女神，公元前205年败逃的迦太基将领马戈还曾到此征集人马和给养。穆斯林统治时城镇称亚比萨，与隔海相望的德尼亚往来最密。1110年，率军前往耶路撒冷的挪威国王西居尔洗劫该岛，1159年西西里的诺曼舰队又劫掠一次。1235年8月，塔拉戈纳大主教吉列姆·德·蒙特格里替阿拉贡国王海梅一世攻占伊维萨，穆斯林居民多被驱逐，移民主要来自赫罗纳一带。1444年的伊维萨是操加泰罗尼亚语的天主教岛屿，由港湾上方城墙环绕的维拉城治理，南岸盐田的收入供岛务机构开支。

盐是这座岛的财源。海水引入南岸的浅池晒成盐，再从盐田旁装船运走，设立于1299年的岛务自治会就靠这笔收入维持。柏柏尔与奥斯曼海盗反复袭扰，促使腓力二世按文艺复兴样式重修防务：1555年起，乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·卡尔维沿维拉城设计棱堡，1575年后贾科莫·弗拉廷又改造工事，伊维萨城便有了城墙环绕的上维拉。

岛上的自治一直维持到西班牙王位继承战争。岛上精英虽有分歧，伊维萨仍支持奥地利阵营，直到1715年7月波旁军队完成对巴利阿里群岛的征服。同年11月，腓力五世颁布《新基本法令》，废除岛务自治会，把盐田收归王室，岛屿旧日的收入改由马德里支配；取代自治会的市政议会直到1724年才确立。

en:
Tétouan lies in the Martil valley a short way inland from the Mediterranean, below the ridges of the Rif. The Marinids rebuilt it as a fortified citadel in 1307, but in 1399 Henry III of Castile razed the town because its corsairs preyed on Castilian shipping, and in 1436 a detachment sent from Portuguese Ceuta under Duarte de Menezes raided it again as it struggled to recover. In 1444 Tétouan was a half-ruined settlement of the Kingdom of Fez, its valley given over to grain fields and orchards.

In the late fifteenth century Ali al-Mandri, a captain of Boabdil, led Andalusians to rebuild Tétouan: they raised the walls, filled them with houses and bought the protection of the Wattasid sultan. Muslim and Jewish refugees from Andalusia also settled in the town. From the 1530s Tétouan was one of the chief corsair ports of the western Mediterranean, where Christian captives awaited ransom in the underground mazmorras whose fame reached even Cervantes; a Castilian fleet destroyed the harbour in 1565. Ruled in the 17th century by the wealthy al-Naksi family, the town was taken by Sultan Moulay Ismail only after fierce resistance, and an Alaouite governor later gave it a generation of stability, building the Meshwar palace and the Pasha mosque.
zh:
得土安位于距地中海不远的马尔蒂勒河谷，背靠里夫群山。马林王朝1307年将它重建为设防城堡，但1399年卡斯蒂利亚国王恩里克三世因城中海盗劫掠卡斯蒂利亚商船而把它夷为平地；1436年，葡萄牙据守的休达又派杜阿尔特·德·梅内塞斯率军趁其元气未愈再度洗劫。1444年的得土安是非斯王国一处半毁的聚落，河谷间散布着谷田和果园。

15世纪末，博阿布迪尔的将领阿里·曼德里率安达卢西亚人重建得土安：他们先筑起城墙，再在城内营建宅院，并向瓦塔斯苏丹纳金求得庇护。来自安达卢西亚的穆斯林与犹太难民也在城中定居。自1530年代起，得土安成为西地中海最主要的海盗港之一，基督徒俘虏被关在名为「马兹莫拉」的地下洞窟里等待赎金，其苦名甚至传到了塞万提斯耳中；1565年，一支卡斯蒂利亚舰队摧毁了它的港口。17世纪时此城由富有的纳克西家族治理，穆莱·伊斯梅尔苏丹经过激烈抵抗才将它攻下，此后一位阿拉维总督带来一代人的安定，梅什瓦尔宫和帕夏清真寺都建于这一时期。

en:
Mers El Kébir, the Great Harbour, is a sheltered roadstead a few miles northwest of Oran. The Almohads developed it as a naval arsenal in the twelfth century, and in the thirteenth it passed to the Zayyanid rulers of Tlemcen. In 1444, under a Sunni Muslim and Berber-Arab court, it was one of the seaward gates of that inland kingdom: shipping could anchor beneath the hills while merchants moved cloth and other goods between the port, Oran and the route to Tlemcen. Its value lay less in a large town than in a defensible harbor facing the straits and the Iberian coast.

By about 1492 the anchorage had become a corsair base, drawing Christian expeditions. A Portuguese force was defeated there in 1501, and the Spanish took Mers El Kébir in 1505, calling it Mazalquivir. Although a Zayyanid army defeated Spanish troops outside the port in 1507, the fortress served as the base for the conquest of neighboring Oran in 1509. Spain held the twin presidios until Mustafa Bouchelaghem, bey of Mascara, forced Mers El Kébir to capitulate on 3 April 1708. A Spanish armada recovered both ports in 1732 after the Battle of Aïn-el-Turk. In 1792 Madrid yielded them to the Dey of Algiers, and by 1821 Mers El Kébir belonged to the western beylik of Ottoman Algiers.
zh:
凯比尔港意为「大港」，是奥兰西北数英里处一处有天然屏障的锚地。穆瓦希德王朝在12世纪把这里建成海军军械库，13世纪时它转归特莱姆森的扎扬王朝统治者。1444年，在逊尼派穆斯林、柏柏尔—阿拉伯宫廷治下，这里是这个内陆王国通向海洋的门户之一：船只可在山麓下停泊，商人则把布料等货物在港口、奥兰和通往特莱姆森的道路间转运。它的重要性不在于大城，而在于这座面向海峡与伊比利亚海岸、易守难攻的港湾。

约到1492年，这片锚地已成为私掠海盗基地，引来基督教远征。1501年，一支葡萄牙军队在此战败；1505年，西班牙人夺取凯比尔港，称之为马萨尔基维尔。尽管扎扬军队1507年在港外击败西班牙部队，这座要塞仍在1509年成为西班牙征服邻近奥兰的基地。西班牙长期据守这对要塞，直到1708年4月3日，穆阿斯凯尔贝伊穆斯塔法·布歇拉格姆迫使凯比尔港投降。1732年，西班牙舰队在艾因图尔克战役后夺回两港。1792年，西班牙宫廷把它们交给阿尔及尔德伊；到1821年，凯比尔港已属于奥斯曼阿尔及尔的西部贝伊辖区。

en:
Salé faces the Atlantic at the mouth of the Bou Regreg, across from the citadel of Rabat. The Romans knew the older settlement upstream as Sala Colonia, but the town proper was founded in the 11th century by Andalusian families led by the Banu 'Ashara. Almohad caliph Yaqub al-Mansur built its Great Mosque in 1196. In September 1260 a Castilian fleet sent by Alfonso X sacked the town during Eid al-Fitr and carried off its people; the Marinid sultan Abu Yusuf Yaqub retook it after a fourteen-day siege and rebuilt the walls, raising the sea-gate of Bab el-Mrisa. In 1444 Salé was the chief Atlantic port of the Marinid Kingdom of Fez, with the Madrasa of Abu al-Hasan and streets crowded with merchants and jurists.

The expulsion of the Moriscos from Spain transformed the town. From 1609 thousands of refugees settled by the estuary, among them some 3,000 wealthy Hornacheros from Extremadura who held the kasbah across the river and took to the sea as corsairs; the Dutch renegade Jan Janszoon, known as Murad Reis, commanded their fleet as grand admiral from 1624. In April 1627 the Hornacheros expelled the Saadi governor and proclaimed the independent Republic of Bou Regreg, ruled by an annually elected Diwan. Spain bombarded Salé in May 1628 and a French fleet under Isaac de Razilly in July 1629, yet the 'Salé Rovers' remained the dread of Atlantic shipping. The Dila'iya brotherhood made the city its vassal in 1641, and in June 1668 Sultan Moulay al-Rashid ended the republic for the Alaouite dynasty.
zh:
塞拉位于大西洋畔的阿布·赖格赖格河口，与拉巴特要塞隔河相望。罗马人把上游更古老的聚落称作萨拉殖民地，塞拉城本身则是11世纪由巴努·阿沙拉等安达卢西亚家族建立的。穆瓦希德王朝哈里发雅各布·曼苏尔1196年敕建了塞拉大清真寺。1260年9月，阿方索十世派出的卡斯蒂利亚舰队趁开斋节突袭劫掠，掳走大量居民；马林苏丹阿布·优素福·叶尔孤白经十四天围城收复城市、重修城墙，海上城门迈里萨门即建于此时。1444年的塞拉是马林王朝治下非斯王国首要的大西洋商港，阿布·哈桑经学院坐落城中，商旅与法学家往来辐辏。

西班牙驱逐摩里斯科人彻底改变了这座城市。1609年起，数千名难民来到河口定居，其中约三千人是来自埃斯特雷马杜拉的奥尔纳乔斯富户，他们据有对岸的城堡，以海上劫掠为生；荷兰叛教者扬·扬松（穆拉德·雷斯）1624年起出任他们的舰队大统领。1627年4月，奥尔纳乔斯人驱逐萨阿德王朝总督，宣布建立独立的阿布·赖格赖格共和国，由每年改选的迪万议事会治理。西班牙1628年5月炮轰塞拉，1629年7月艾萨克·德·拉齐利率法国舰队再度来攻，都没能消灭「塞拉海盗」，他们始终是大西洋航路上最令人畏惧的名字。1641年迪拉兄弟会迫使此城臣服，1668年6月穆莱·拉希德苏丹为阿拉维王朝终结了这个共和国。

en:
Anfa stood on a rise of the Chaouia coast, the Atlantic harbour that al-Idrisi counted among the chief ports of the Maghreb al-Aqsa, enriched by its trade with al-Andalus. It grew up under the Barghawata, and when the Almohads broke that Berber kingdom they settled Hilalian Arabs across the Tamesna, turning it into the Arabised Chaouia. Marinid sultans kept the town prosperous: Abu Inan Faris founded a madrasa there between 1348 and 1358, and Ibn al-Khatib visited from Granada. By 1444, with the Marinid state collapsing, Anfa ran its own affairs, a wealthy merchant town whose corsairs raided as far as the mouth of the Tagus.

Its pirates drew Portuguese revenge: in 1468 a fleet sent by Afonso V and commanded by the Infante Ferdinand stormed the city and left it in ruins, and for three generations only Salé corsairs and local tribes used its anchorage. Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah rebuilt it from 1760, girdling the new town with walls and a fortified sqala, placing it under a pasha and naming it Dar al-Bayda, the White House, Casa Branca to the Portuguese. Under the later Alaouites it stayed a small grain port of the Chaouia, overshadowed by Mazagan and Mogador.
zh:
安法坐落在沙维耶海岸的一处高地上，伊德里西曾把这座大西洋港口列为马格里布最西端的主要港口之一，它因与安达卢西亚通商而富庶。安法兴起于巴尔加瓦塔王国时代；穆瓦希德王朝攻灭这个柏柏尔王国后，把希拉勒系阿拉伯部落迁入塔马斯纳一带，此地逐渐阿拉伯化，改称沙维耶。马林王朝时期城市保持繁荣，阿布·伊南·法里斯在1348至1358年间于此兴建伊斯兰学校，格拉纳达的伊本·哈提卜也曾到访。1444年马林国家土崩瓦解，安法人自行其是，既是富商云集之城，也是海盗巢穴，寇掠范围远至塔霍河口。

海盗招来了葡萄牙的报复：1468年，阿方索五世派出、由费尔南多亲王统率的舰队攻破安法，将城市夷为废墟。此后近一个世纪，只有萨累的海盗和当地部落间或使用这片锚地。穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉苏丹于1760年起重建新城，环筑城墙与炮台斯卡拉，派帕夏治理，并取名达尔贝达，意为「白房子」，葡语作卡萨布兰卡（Casa Branca）。在其后的阿拉维王朝治下，它始终是沙维耶平原一座小小的谷物港，声势不及马扎甘和摩加多尔。

en:
Tenerife is the largest Canary Island, with Teide rising above its high ravines and pine-covered ridges. The Guanches had herded goats and sheep, farmed coastal plots and fished there for many centuries. By the fifteenth century the island was split into chiefdoms called menceyatos, each under a mencey; traditional accounts traced the division to the descendants of its last common ruler, and Taoro in the fertile north was the strongest. European ships knew the island and raided its coasts, but no foreign garrison held ground there. In 1444 all nine chiefdoms were independent, and the pastures, cave shelters and mountain shrines around Teide were still outside the Castilian conquest reshaping the smaller Canaries.

Diego García de Herrera made a symbolic Castilian claim in 1464 and built a short-lived tower in Anaga. The Catholic Monarchs granted the conquest to Alonso Fernández de Lugo in December 1493. He landed near the future Santa Cruz in April 1494 with about 2,000 infantry and 200 cavalry, but the Guanches defeated him at Acentejo on 31 May by using the steep broken ground. On 14-15 November they lost the open battle of Aguere near La Laguna; another defeat at Acentejo followed, and the remaining menceys submitted by September 1496. Lugo then founded San Cristóbal de La Laguna as the island's first capital. Sugar cane, Malvasia vines and cochineal later tied its estates to Atlantic trade, while Santa Cruz became a centre for corsair expeditions. The 1706 Trevejo eruption buried the north-coast port of Garachico. On 22 July 1797 Horatio Nelson launched an amphibious attack on Santa Cruz; Spanish fire wounded his right arm, which was partly amputated, and the survivors withdrew under a truce on 25 July.
zh:
特内里费是加那利群岛最大的岛屿，泰德峰耸立于高耸沟壑和松林覆盖的山脊之间。许多世纪以来，关切人在这里牧放山羊和绵羊，在沿海地块耕作，也捕鱼采贝。15世纪时，全岛分为若干称为门塞亚托的酋邦，各由门塞统治；传统说法把这种分治归于末代共主的后裔，北部沃土上的塔奥罗最为强大。欧洲船只已经知道此岛，也曾上岸袭扰，却没有外来驻军守住土地。1444年，九个酋邦全部独立，泰德峰周围的牧场、岩洞居所和山间圣所仍在卡斯蒂利亚征服范围之外，而较小的加那利岛屿已被这场征服改变。

迭戈·加西亚·德·埃雷拉1464年代表卡斯蒂利亚作象征性占领，并在阿纳加修建一座短命塔楼。1493年12月，天主教双王把征服权授予阿隆索·费尔南德斯·德·卢戈。1494年4月，他率约两千步兵和两百骑兵，在后来的圣克鲁斯附近登陆；5月31日，关切人凭崎岖地形在阿森特霍将其击败。11月14日至15日，他们在拉古纳附近的阿格雷平原作战失利，随后又在阿森特霍战败，残余门塞到1496年9月相继臣服。卢戈建立圣克里斯托瓦尔-德拉拉古纳，作为岛上第一个首府。甘蔗、玛尔维萨葡萄和胭脂虫后来把岛上庄园接入大西洋贸易，圣克鲁斯则发展为海盗活动中心。1706年，特雷韦霍火山喷发，掩埋了北岸港口加拉奇科。1797年7月22日，霍雷肖·纳尔逊向圣克鲁斯发动两栖进攻；西班牙守军的火力击伤他的右臂，手臂随后被部分截去，残部于7月25日在停火协议下撤退。

en:
Kairouan rises in the inland plains, fifty kilometres west of Susa, where the Arab general Uqba ibn Nafi pitched his camp around 670 and raised the Great Mosque that bears his name. Under the Aghlabids it was the capital of Ifriqiya, rich enough to be set beside Basra and Kufa: jurists such as Sahnun taught Maliki law in the mosque's university, and the great Aghlabid cisterns were built beyond the walls. The Fatimids withdrew to Mahdia, the Zirids brought a second bloom, and when the Hilali bedouin sacked the city in 1057 it sank into two centuries of ruin and its scholars drifted to Tunis. The Hafsids began its revival in the thirteenth century, repairing the Great Mosque in 1248 and again in 1293–1294. In 1444 Kairouan was a city of pilgrims and grain merchants rising slowly from its ruins under the Hafsid sultans, the first holy city of the Maghreb; its historian Ibn Naji had died only a few years before.

The Muradid beys took up the work early: the Great Mosque was repaired in 1618, and outside the walls Hammuda Pasha rebuilt the zawiya of Sidi Sahab around 1662, madrasa and minaret included, over the tomb of Abu Zama'a al-Balawi, companion and barber of the Prophet; his grandson Mohamed Bey remade the mausoleum dome in 1681–1685, and pilgrim caravans from across the Maghreb gathered there before setting out for Mecca. Hussein ibn Ali, founder of the Husainid line, restored the city walls and founded a madrasa, but Kairouan became his last refuge: defeated by his nephew Ali Pasha at Smendja on 4 September 1735, he was besieged here, taken beneath the ramparts and beheaded on 13 May 1740. Under his dynasty the old holy city at last recovered a respected place in the life of Tunisia.
zh:
凯鲁万矗立在内陆平原上，东距苏萨五十公里。约670年，阿拉伯名将欧格白·伊本·纳菲在此扎营建城，筑起以他之名命名的大清真寺。阿格拉布王朝时期，它是伊夫里奇亚的都城，富庶可比巴士拉与库法：塞赫农等法学家在寺中大学讲授马立克学派教法，城外还修起宏大的阿格拉布蓄水池。法蒂玛王朝迁都马赫迪叶，齐尔王朝带来二度繁荣；1057年希拉尔贝都因人洗劫全城，凯鲁万就此荒废两个世纪，学者纷纷转往突尼斯城。13世纪哈夫斯王朝开启复兴，1248年、1293至1294年两度重修大清真寺。1444年，在哈夫斯苏丹治下，凯鲁万是一座缓慢走出废墟的圣城，朝圣者与粮商云集，位列马格里布第一圣城，为它修史的伊本·纳吉几年前刚刚去世。

穆拉德王朝的贝伊们早早接过修缮之役：1618年整建大清真寺；城外，哈穆达帕夏贝伊约1662年重修西迪·萨哈布道堂，连经学院带宣礼塔一并兴建，堂下安葬着先知的伙伴兼理发师阿布·宰迈阿·拜莱维；其孙穆罕默德贝伊又于1681至1685年重建圣墓穹顶，全马格里布的朝觐商队都在此会集，再启程前往麦加。侯赛因王朝开创者侯赛因·伊本·阿里修复城墙、创办经学院，凯鲁万却成了他最后的避难所：1735年9月4日，他在斯门贾被侄子阿里帕夏击败，退守此城，最终于1740年5月13日在城墙下被俘斩首。在他的王朝治下，这座古老圣城终于在突尼斯的生活中重获尊崇的地位。

en:
Sabha is the great oasis of central Fezzan, set on the desert road that runs from the Tripolitanian coast through Hun and Waddan to Murzuk and the lands of Bornu. Springs feed its palms and the villages of the Wadi al-Bawanis, and the mound above the town holds the remains of a fortress first raised in Garamantian times, more than 2,500 years ago. Al-Bakri, writing in the eleventh century, already marked Sabha as a station five days' march south of Hun, where caravans changed guides and laid in dates before the long crossing. Kanem and Bornu successively claimed the oases between the thirteenth and fifteenth centuries, and Arab tribes pastured their flocks around them. In 1444 Sabha was a caravan town under the lords of Fezzan, its wealth counted in slaves and ivory carried north and in the horses and cloth carried south.

The Awlad Muhammad made it a town of their sultanate, and the Ottoman march south soon reached it. Mahmut Bey, the officer who led Ottoman expeditions through Fezzan as far as Kawar and Lake Chad, fell in 1583 suppressing a Bornu-backed revolt, but Ottoman control stayed as loose here as at Murzuk, asserted only by occasional expeditions in 1679–1682, 1690 and 1718. In 1622–1626 Ahmad ibn Huwaydi al-Kharmani, a local chief who claimed Garamantian descent, rebuilt the old fortress on its hill, the castle later known as Fort Elena. When the pashas of Tripoli finally made themselves masters of the sultanate in 1813, Sabha's caravans and fortress passed to them.
zh:
塞卜哈是费赞中部的大绿洲，位于从的黎波里塔尼亚海岸经洪、瓦丹通往穆尔祖克和博尔努的沙漠大道上。泉水滋养着椰枣林和布瓦尼斯河谷的村庄，城边的山冈上留存着一座要塞的遗迹，最早建于2500多年前的加拉曼特时代。11世纪的白克里已把塞卜哈记作洪以南五日路程的驿站，商队在此更换向导、备足椰枣，然后踏上漫长的穿越之旅。13至15世纪，卡涅姆和博尔努先后宣称领有这些绿洲，阿拉伯部落则在四周放牧。1444年，塞卜哈是费赞首领治下的商队之城，财富以源源北上的奴隶、象牙和南下的马匹、布匹计。

奥拉德·穆罕默德王朝把塞卜哈纳入自己的苏丹国，奥斯曼人的南征也很快波及于此。军官马哈茂德贝伊率远征军穿过费赞，远达卡瓦尔和乍得湖一带，1583年在镇压一场博尔努支持的叛乱时阵亡；但奥斯曼在此的控制和穆尔祖克一样松散，只靠1679至1682年、1690年和1718年的数次远征维持。1622至1626年，自称加拉曼特人后裔的本地首领艾哈迈德·本·胡韦迪·海尔马尼在山冈上重建古堡，即后来的埃莱娜堡。1813年的黎波里帕夏最终成为苏丹国的主人，塞卜哈的商队和堡垒一并归于他们。

en: Demnate is a Berber market town in the fertile Tassaout valley on the northern foot of the High Atlas, about 100 kilometres east of Marrakesh. Local tradition places its foundation around 998, when the Inoultan and Infedouak clans made it a meeting place for trade and common defense; in Tachelhit its name means fertile lands. A Jewish community settled there in the early twelfth century and became known for wine, leatherwork and crafts. In 1444 Demnate was a market town of the Moroccan realm, where Atlas and southern caravans exchanged wool, hides, dates, olive oil, leather and grain. Through the Saadian and Alawid periods it remained a provisioning stop on the tracks leading from Marrakesh toward the Draa and Tafilalt.
zh: 代姆纳特是大阿特拉斯山北麓、塔萨沃特河谷肥土地上的柏柏尔集镇，位于马拉喀什以东约100公里。当地传统称城镇约建于998年，由伊努尔坦和因费杜瓦克氏族辟为交易与共同防御的集会地；其名在塔切拉特语中意为肥沃之地。12世纪初，一个犹太社区在此定居，以酿酒、皮革制作和手工业闻名。1444年，代姆纳特是摩洛哥政权治下的集镇，阿特拉斯山民与南方商队在此交换羊毛、兽皮、椰枣、橄榄油、皮革和谷物。萨阿德与阿拉维王朝时期，它始终是从马拉喀什通往德拉和塔菲拉勒特道路上的补给市场。

en:
Texcoco, the Acolhua capital on the eastern shore of Lake Texcoco, became the second city of the Aztec world after the Triple Alliance was formed with Tenochtitlan and Tlacopan in 1428. Its ruler Nezahualcoyotl had returned from exile to defeat the Tepanecs of Azcapotzalco, and by 1444 his court drew poets, priests and scholars. The city held royal archives and music rooms, took two-fifths of the alliance's tribute, and its aqueducts and gardens climbed toward the sacred hill of Texcotzingo.

Nezahualcoyotl ruled until 1472 and was succeeded by his son Nezahualpilli. When Hernán Cortés reached the lake in 1519, Cacamatzin ruled Texcoco; the city then became the Spanish base for the siege of Tenochtitlan, and the brigantines used on the lake were launched there in 1521. After the conquest the Franciscans Juan de Tecto, Juan de Ayora and Pedro de Gante began Christian instruction. Gante learned Nahuatl, wrote a Nahuatl catechism and opened a school where Latin, Spanish, carpentry, sewing and weaving were taught. Charles V recognized Texcoco as a city in 1551, but over the colonial centuries it was overshadowed by nearby Mexico City and lived increasingly from fishing, agriculture and lake-shore estates.
zh:
特斯科科是特斯科科湖东岸的阿科瓦人都城。1428年，它与特诺奇蒂特兰和特拉科潘结成三方同盟，随后成为阿兹特克世界的第二大城。统治者内萨瓦尔科约特尔曾流亡在外，归国后击败阿斯卡波特萨尔科的特帕内克人；到1444年，他的宫廷已吸引诗人、祭司和学者。城中设有王室档案库和乐厅，按盟约分得五分之二贡物，水渠与园林还沿特斯科钦科圣山层层而上。

内萨瓦尔科约特尔统治到1472年，其子内萨瓦尔皮利继位。埃尔南·科尔特斯1519年抵达湖畔时，特斯科科的统治者是卡卡马辛；这座城市随后成为西班牙人围攻特诺奇蒂特兰的基地，用于湖上作战的双桅船也于1521年在此下水。征服后，方济各会士胡安·德·托克托、胡安·德·阿约拉和佩德罗·德·甘特开始传教。甘特学会纳瓦语，编写纳瓦语教义问答，并开办学校，教授拉丁语、西班牙语、木工、缝纫和编织。查理五世1551年正式承认特斯科科为城市，但在整个殖民时期，它日渐被邻近的墨西哥城掩盖，主要依靠渔业、农业和湖畔庄园维持。

en:
Tlacopan, later called Tacuba, was a Tepanec city-state on the fertile western shore of Lake Texcoco. It had once been subject to Azcapotzalco, but in 1428 it joined Tenochtitlan and Texcoco in the Triple Alliance after Azcapotzalco's overthrow. In 1444 it was the alliance's junior partner, receiving only one-fifth of the tribute from joint campaigns while the Mexico-Tacuba causeway tied it directly to the island capital of Tenochtitlan.

On 30 June 1520, Cortés and his retreating men fled along that causeway toward Tlacopan during La Noche Triste; when the Spanish returned in 1521, the siege of Tenochtitlan ended the Triple Alliance. The last native ruler, Tetlepanquetzal, was tortured under suspicion of hiding treasure, and in 1526 a Spanish decree made Isabel Moctezuma, daughter of Moctezuma II, titular ruler of an encomienda whose households paid fowl, eggs, maize, tortillas and cacao. Franciscans built the church of San Gabriel over the old ceremonial centre, the Carmelites founded San Joaquín in 1689, and by 1632 sixty haciendas had spread through the district, supplying Mexico City with food, lumber and sandstone.
zh:
特拉科潘后来又称塔库巴，是特斯科科湖肥沃西岸的特帕内克城邦。它原臣属于阿斯卡波特萨尔科，但在1428年与特诺奇蒂特兰、特斯科科联合推翻旧主，加入三方同盟。1444年，它是同盟中较弱的一方，只分得联合作战所获贡物的五分之一；墨西哥城—塔库巴堤道则把它与岛上都城特诺奇蒂特兰直接相连。

1520年6月30日「悲痛之夜」，科尔特斯及其残部沿这条堤道逃向特拉科潘；1521年西班牙人卷土重来，特诺奇蒂特兰围城战终结了三方同盟。最后一位本土统治者特特莱潘克察尔因被怀疑藏匿财宝而受刑。1526年，一道西班牙敕令立蒙特祖马二世之女伊莎贝尔·蒙特祖马为恩孔米恩达的名义统治者，辖下民户缴纳禽鸟、禽蛋、玉米、薄饼和可可豆。方济各会在旧祭祀中心上建起圣加百列教堂，加尔默罗会1689年创立圣华金修院；到1632年，这一地区已有六十处庄园，为墨西哥城供应食物、木材和砂岩。

en:
Malinalco lies in the rugged hills south of Toluca, on routes between the high plateau and the warmer country toward Cuernavaca and Guerrero. Culhua, Matlatzinca, Ocuilteco and Otomi communities settled its valleys, and by 1444 Matlatzinca elites dominated a populous city-state with an old ceremonial centre on the Cerro de los Ídolos. It fought wars with Cuauhnahuac and kept commercial ties with the Basin of Mexico and Puebla-Tlaxcala, while still remaining outside the Mexica Empire.

Axayácatl conquered Malinalco in 1476, turning it into a tributary province that supplied maguey mantles, grain and stone. Around 1486-1490 Ahuízotl sent stonecarvers from Tenochtitlan and forced local labour to build the Cuauhcalli, a sanctuary for Eagle and Jaguar warriors cut into the Cerro de los Ídolos; it was still unfinished when the Spanish arrived. After La Noche Triste the people of Malinalco rose against the newcomers, and Andrés de Tapia subdued them together with Ocuilán. The encomienda first passed to Cristóbal Rodríguez de Ávalos and then to the Crown. Franciscans and Dominicans began evangelization before the Augustinians were assigned the town in 1533; they built the monastery of the Divino Salvador with stone from the unfinished sanctuary. The Jalmolonga hacienda, later worked by the Jesuits to support their Mexico City college, passed after the Jesuit expulsion to Manuel Romero de Terreros, Count of Regla. On 8 January 1813 José María Morelos passed through and signed orders concerning native agricultural customs and church funds raised for the war in Spain.
zh:
马利纳尔科位于托卢卡以南的崎岖山地，处在中部高原通往夸尔纳瓦卡和格雷罗暖地的道路上。库尔瓦、马特拉钦卡、奥奎尔特克和奥托米社群先后定居于这片谷地；到1444年，马特拉钦卡上层统治着一座人口稠密的城邦，并在偶像山上保有古老祭祀中心。它曾与夸尔纳瓦克交战，也同墨西哥盆地及普埃布拉—特拉斯卡拉谷地保持商业联系，当时尚未并入墨西哥帝国。

阿萨亚卡特尔1476年征服马利纳尔科，把它变为缴纳龙舌兰布、粮食和石材的贡赋行省。约1486—1490年，阿维索特尔从特诺奇蒂特兰派来石匠，并征调当地劳役，在偶像山岩体内开凿「鹰屋」，作为鹰战士与豹战士的圣所；西班牙人到来时工程仍未完成。「悲痛之夜」后，马利纳尔科人起兵抵抗，安德烈斯·德·塔皮亚将他们与奥基兰人一同平定。恩孔米恩达先授予克里斯托瓦尔·罗德里格斯·德·阿瓦洛斯，后收归王室。方济各会和多明我会最先传教，奥斯定会1533年受命接管，并利用未完工圣所的石料修建圣救主修院。哈尔莫隆加庄园后来由耶稣会经营，用以资助其在墨西哥城的学院；耶稣会被驱逐后，庄园落入雷格拉伯爵曼努埃尔·罗梅罗·德·特雷罗斯之手。1813年1月8日，何塞·马里亚·莫雷洛斯经过此地，签署了涉及原住民农业惯例和教会为西班牙战事筹款的命令。

en:
Acámbaro stands on the Lerma at the northeastern edge of the Purépecha state. Chupícuaro farming villages had occupied the country long before; in the fifteenth century Otomi lineages allied with the Uacúsecha were settled here to guard the frontier, and Purépecha lords then posted their own officials over the region. The Purépecha name Ak'amparhu recalled both the sacred maguey and a woman named Ak'amba, while the Otomi knew the place as Mauadá. In 1444 Otomi farmers and frontier warriors lived among maguey and maize lands by the Lerma, holding the road from Tzintzuntzan toward the Bajío.

On 19 September 1526 the cacique Nicolás de San Luis Montañés formally founded San Francisco de Acámbaro, the first Spanish-ordered town in what is now Guanajuato. Franciscans began evangelization and built the Hospital Temple; their Mudéjar aqueduct, begun in 1527 under Antonio de Bermul, carried water from Tócuaro, and the stone bridge over the Lerma followed in 1750. The native head town became an important republic of Indians, while the province was administered with Yuririapúndaro under the mayor of Celaya. On 22 October 1810 Miguel Hidalgo declared Acámbaro the military quarters of the Grand Army of America and was named Generalísimo of the Americas; more than 80,000 insurgents paraded that day, whereas only 800 had answered the Grito de Dolores a month earlier.
zh:
阿坎巴罗位于莱尔马河畔，地处普雷佩查国家东北缘。丘皮库阿罗农民的村落早已在此生息；15世纪，与瓦库塞查结盟的奥托米氏族被安置到这里守卫边境，普雷佩查贵族随后又派来官员控制这一地区。普雷佩查语地名阿坎帕鲁（Ak'amparhu）既关联神圣的龙舌兰，也纪念一位名叫阿坎巴（Ak'amba）的女性；奥托米语则称此地为马瓦达（Mauadá）。1444年，奥托米农民和边境战士生活在莱尔马河畔的龙舌兰与玉米地之间，为钦聪灿扼守通向巴希奥的道路。

1526年9月19日，酋长尼古拉斯·德·圣路易斯·蒙塔涅斯正式建立圣方济各·德·阿坎巴罗，这是今瓜纳华托境内第一座按西班牙殖民秩序建立的城镇。方济各会开始传教并修建医院教堂；安东尼奥·德·贝尔穆尔主持的穆德哈尔风格输水道于1527年动工，把托夸罗的泉水引来，莱尔马河上的石桥则在1750年建成。土著首镇后来成为重要的印第安人共和国，阿坎巴罗省与尤里里亚彭达罗一同归塞拉亚长官管辖。1810年10月22日，米格尔·伊达尔戈在此宣布阿坎巴罗为「美洲大军」的军营，并受任「美洲大元帅」；当天有超过8万名起义者列队受阅，而一个月前在多洛雷斯响应呼声起事的还只有800人。

en: Ihuatzio, the Purépecha 'place of coyotes', lies on the southeastern shore of Lake Pátzcuaro below Cerro Tariaqueri. Nahua speakers occupied it from 900 to 1200 and called it Coyoacán; during the Purépecha florescence after 1200, it became one of three royal lordships, with Hiripan holding Ihuatzio while Pátzcuaro and Tzintzuntzan had their own lords. In 1444 power was already shifting to Tzintzuntzan, yet Ihuatzio remained a walled ceremonial center of raised roads, three yácatas, temples to Curicaueri and Xaratanga, and a circular observatory overlooking lake farms and fishing villages. The conquest ended its court life after 1530, but Ihuatzio survived as an indigenous community; in 1593 it was still counted among the principal subject towns governed through native Tzintzuntzan.
zh: 伊瓦齐奥在普雷佩查语中意为「郊狼之地」，位于帕茨夸罗湖东南岸、塔里亚克里山下方。900年至1200年间，纳瓦语族群居住于此，称它为科约阿坎；1200年以后普雷佩查文化进入鼎盛期，伊瓦齐奥与帕茨夸罗、钦聪灿并列为三个王家庄园，伊里潘在此镇守，另外两处则各有领主。1444年，王权虽已开始转向钦聪灿，伊瓦齐奥仍是有围墙的礼仪中心，高台道路、三座亚卡塔金字塔、库里考埃里与沙拉坦加神庙和圆形观象台俯临湖滨农田与渔村。征服在1530年后终结了这里的王廷生活，但伊瓦齐奥作为土著村社存续；1593年，它仍是通过土著钦聪灿政府管辖的主要附属村镇之一。

en:
Puruarán lies in the hot southern lowlands of Michoacán, well-watered country that slopes toward the Balsas River; its Purépecha name means 'place of the steaming springs'. It was the granary of the Purépecha kingdom: according to the Relación de Michoacán, the cazonci granted the lands running from Puruarán south to Guerrero to the lord of Tacámbaro, and the maize grown here supplied the royal heartland around Lake Pátzcuaro. In 1444 the district was governed through that local lord on the Purépecha southern frontier, the country beyond the Balsas still held by peoples the cazonci could not subdue.

Cristóbal de Olid's Spaniards reached Tzintzuntzan in 1522 and the last cazonci, Tangáxuan II, submitted. When Nuño de Guzmán marched west in 1530 the king was tortured and burned alive, and the hot country was parcelled into encomiendas and later into sugar-cane haciendas. Friars made the parish of San José a base for carrying the Gospel through the Tierra Caliente, and the cult of the Señor del Huerto venerated there had its feast confirmed by papal bull in 1721. During the independence wars the Rayón brothers made Puruarán their headquarters in 1810. On 5 January 1814 Agustín de Iturbide's royalists routed Morelos's rearguard at the bridge of Puruarán and captured Mariano Matamoros, who was executed a month later; in July 1815 Morelos's itinerant Congress took refuge at the hacienda here.
zh:
普鲁阿兰位于米却肯南部炎热的低地，泉水众多，地势向巴尔萨斯河倾斜，其普雷佩查语地名意为「沸腾泉水之地」。这里曾是普雷佩查王国的粮仓：据《米却肯纪事》记载，钦聪灿的卡松西把从普鲁阿兰向南直至格雷罗的土地封给塔坎巴罗的首领，此地出产的玉米供应帕茨库罗湖一带的王畿。1444年，这片地方由那位地方首领管辖，处在普雷佩查的南部边境，巴尔萨斯河对岸仍是卡松西无法征服的族群。

1522年，克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德率领西班牙人抵达钦聪灿，末代卡松西唐加西安二世投降。1530年努尼奥·德·古斯曼西征时将他酷刑后烧死，炎热低地随后被划为委托监护地，日后又辟为甘蔗庄园。修士们以圣何塞堂区为据点，向整个铁拉卡连特传教；1721年教廷颁布诏书，确立当地「菜园基督」圣像的节庆。独立战争中，拉永兄弟1810年以普鲁阿兰为兵营。1814年1月5日，阿古斯丁·德·伊图尔维德的保王军在普鲁阿兰桥击溃莫雷洛斯的后卫，俘获马里亚诺·马塔莫罗斯，后者一个月后被处死；1815年7月，莫雷洛斯辗转各地的国会曾在当地庄园驻留。

en:
Amaxocotlan, later called Mascota, was a Tecos chief's town in the pine-covered western Sierra of Jalisco. Its Nahuatl name describes a place of deer and snakes, and its hunters and farmers lived between high mountain valleys and the Pacific slope. In 1444 the cacicazgo centered here reached over Talpa, El Tuito and coastal Chacala, giving the hill town influence beyond the mountains toward the sea.

Francisco Cortés de San Buenaventura reached Amaxacotlán Mazacotla early in 1525, sent north from Colima by Hernán Cortés; the Spaniards also called the country Valle de los Venados or Valle de Banderas. In 1530 Nuño de Guzmán subjected Mascota during his harsh western campaign, after the district had been granted in encomienda to Pedro Gómez and Martín Monje. Most of the land later passed under Augustinian administration, with the religious steward living near Mal Paso.
zh:
阿马索科特兰后称马斯科塔，是哈利斯科西部松树林山地中特科斯人酋长大镇。其纳瓦特尔语名称意为「鹿与蛇之地」，猎人和农人在高山谷地与太平洋坡地之间生活。1444年，以此地为中心的酋邦统辖塔尔帕、埃尔图伊托和滨海的查卡拉，使这座山镇的影响力越过群山通向海洋。

1525年初，弗朗西斯科·科尔特斯·德·圣布埃纳文图拉受埃尔南·科尔特斯派遣，从科利马北上，抵达阿马萨克特兰·马萨克特拉；西班牙人还把这一带称为「鹿谷」或「巴耶德班德拉斯」。1530年，努尼奥·德·古斯曼在残酷的西征中征服马斯科塔，此前该地区已被委托给佩德罗·戈麦斯和马丁·蒙赫。后来大部分土地归入奥斯定会管理，宗教事务管家住在马尔帕索附近。

en:
Tohono means 'desert people', and the western O'odham bands reached from the Gila and Colorado rivers toward the Gulf of California. The coastal people of this province were the Hia C-eḍ or Areneños, whose camps lay around the volcanic Pinacate hills and the Gran Desierto de Altar. They moved with scarce rainwater and springs, hunted and gathered in the dunes, fished along the gulf, and carried shell and other desert goods to the Cocopah and other Yuman peoples near the Colorado Delta. In 1444 this was still a roadless nomadic frontier, loosely linked to the wider Piman world to the east.

Spanish knowledge of the dune country came through Eusebio Kino, who explored the Pinacate region in 1698 and returned in later years. Missions and presidios took root farther east in the Pimería Alta, where revolt flared in 1695 and again in 1751; Charles III's expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767 then removed the order that had done most to open the frontier. Those upheavals touched Sonoyta and the river valleys more than the sand sea, and the coastal Tohono bands remained largely beyond mission control when Mexican independence reached Sonora in 1821.
zh:
「托霍诺」意为沙漠之人，西部奥奥德姆群体的活动范围从希拉河、科罗拉多河延伸到加利福尼亚湾。这片沿海地带的居民是希亚塞德·奥奥德姆人，西班牙人又称阿雷尼奥人或皮纳卡特人，营地散布在火山地貌的皮纳卡特山地与阿尔塔大沙漠周围。他们随着稀少的雨水和泉眼迁徙，在沙丘间狩猎采集，在海湾捕鱼，并把贝壳和其他沙漠物产带到科罗拉多河三角洲，与科科帕人及其他尤曼人群体交易。1444年时，这里仍是没有道路的游居边陲，只与东方更广阔的皮马人群世界保持松散联系。

西班牙人对这片沙丘地带的了解主要来自耶稣会士基诺：他在1698年探查皮纳卡特地区，此后数年间又曾重返。传教站和要塞真正扎根于更东边的皮梅里亚阿尔塔，1695年和1751年两度爆发起事；卡洛斯三世1767年驱逐耶稣会，又使最主要开拓这边疆的修会撤出。这些变动更多影响索诺伊塔和河谷地带，而非沙海本身。因此到1821年墨西哥独立的消息传至索诺拉时，沿海的托霍诺群体大体仍在传教控制之外。

en:
Tzapotzingo was one of three Totorame-speaking lordships on the Nayarit coastal plain, alongside Aztatlán and Senticpac. Its subject towns included Tepehuacan, Guaristemba, Mecatlan and Xalxocotan; Mecatlan stood near the shoreline later chosen for San Blas. Farming families grew maize, beans and chile, while fishing, shrimping and salt-making linked the coast with the Cora and Huichol mountains. By the fifteenth century the old Aztatlán network had given way to rival chiefdoms. In 1444 Tzapotzingo was still independent, bordering the inland sphere of Xalisco but not ruled from Tenochtitlan.

Francisco Cortés de San Buenaventura reached Nayarit in 1526 and received peaceful submissions, but Nuño de Guzmán began the definitive conquest in 1530; on 18 November 1531 he founded Villa del Espíritu Santo, the Spanish nucleus that became Tepic. During the Mixtón War of 1540-1542, Francisco Pantecatl, cacique of Tzapotzingo, recounted the Huasamota valley ceremony where prophets called on the peoples of Nueva Galicia to expel the Spaniards, before Viceroy Antonio de Mendoza crushed the rising. In 1768 José de Gálvez made San Blas a royal naval port and shipyard for Sonora and California, and Juan Pérez sailed north from there in 1774. The insurgent priest José María Mercado took Tepic and San Blas in 1810 and died in the royalist counterattack the following January. San Blas adhered to the Plan de Iguala on 25 July 1821.
zh:
察波钦戈是纳亚里特沿海平原上三个讲托托拉姆语的酋邦之一，与阿斯特兰和森蒂克帕克并列。它的属村包括特佩瓦坎、瓜里斯滕巴、梅卡特兰和哈尔尔索科坦；梅卡特兰靠近后来选定圣布拉斯港的海岸。农家种植玉米、豆类和辣椒，渔业、捕虾和制盐又把海岸同科拉人、惠乔尔人的山地连接起来。到15世纪，旧阿斯特兰网络已经分裂为彼此竞争的酋邦。1444年，察波钦戈仍然独立，毗邻内陆的哈利斯科势力范围，但并不受特诺奇蒂特兰统治。

1526年，弗朗西斯科·科尔特斯·德·圣布埃纳文图拉抵达纳亚里特并接受一些酋邦和平归降；努尼奥·德·古斯曼则在1530年开始决定性征服，并于1531年11月18日建立圣灵镇，这个西班牙据点后来发展为特皮克。1540至1542年米克特战争期间，察波钦戈酋长弗朗西斯科·潘特卡特记述了瓦萨莫塔谷的仪式：先知在那里号召新加利西亚各族驱逐西班牙人，随后安东尼奥·德·门多萨总督镇压了起义。1768年，何塞·德·加尔韦斯把圣布拉斯建成皇家军港和船厂，作为前往索诺拉和加利福尼亚的基地，胡安·佩雷斯于1774年由此北航。1810年，起义神父何塞·马里亚·梅尔卡多夺取特皮克和圣布拉斯，次年1月在保王派反攻中身亡。1821年7月25日，圣布拉斯宣布加入伊瓜拉计划。

en:
Sayula lies in a broad inland basin south of Lake Chapala, where shallow briny lagoons yield salt. Its people were the Tecos, Nahuatl speakers who called their town Tzaulan, 'the place where flies abound'. In 1444 it was a chiefdom within the Tecos kingdom of Colimán, and its salt and saltpeter drew traders along the western Mexican routes. The salt beds were a prize rich enough to lure the Purépecha cazonci's armies before the century was out, yet the Tecos kept their independence.

Between 1480 and 1510 the Tecos under Colímotl defeated the Purépecha in the Saltpeter War, fighting them at Zacoalco, and the caciques of Sayula, Zapotlán and Amula paid him tribute. Alonso de Ávalos, a cousin of Cortés, reached Tzaulan in 1523 and made the town the seat of his encomienda and capital of the Provincia de Ávalos under the Viceroyalty of New Spain. Franciscans founded the Convent of San Francisco in 1573 and an Indian hospital in 1578, and the Saturday market made Sayula one of the twelve towns entitled to deputies before the merchants' tribunal of the Guadalajara consulado, handling salt, soap, cloth and knives. In 1742 clay pipes carried spring water to the central stone fountain. News of Hidalgo's rising reached the town in October 1810; the Spanish merchants fled, and José Antonio Torres entered on 28 October with 5,000 men. The local priest José Guadalupe Montenegro, whose conspiracy had been uncovered back in 1793, rode out to join the insurgents.
zh:
萨尤拉位于查帕拉湖以南一片开阔的内陆盆地，水浅味咸的潟湖出产食盐。住在这里的是说纳瓦特尔语的特科斯人，他们把自己的镇子叫作察乌兰（Tzaulan），意为「苍蝇成群之地」。1444年，萨尤拉是特科斯科利曼王国治下的一个酋邦，所产食盐和硝石吸引商队往来于西墨西哥的商路。这些盐滩富庶得足以在本世纪末引来普雷佩查卡松西的大军，但特科斯人守住了独立。

1480至1510年间，特科斯人在科利莫特尔率领下打赢硝石战争，在萨科阿尔科与普雷佩查人交战并将其击败，萨尤拉、萨波特兰和阿穆拉的酋长都向他纳贡。科尔特斯的表亲阿隆索·德·阿瓦洛斯1523年抵达察乌兰，把镇子设为自己委托监护地的治所和新西班牙阿瓦洛斯省的省会。方济各会1573年建立圣方济各修道院，1578年又开设印第安人医院；每周六的集市使萨尤拉成为获准向瓜达拉哈拉商会商事法庭选派代表的十二座城镇之一，经营食盐、肥皂、布匹和刀具。1742年，陶土管道把泉水引入市中心的石砌喷泉。1810年10月，伊达尔戈起义的消息传到镇上，西班牙商人争相出逃，何塞·安东尼奥·托雷斯于10月28日率五千人入城；早在1793年密谋就已败露的本地神父何塞·瓜达卢佩·蒙特内格罗，也策马投奔起义军。

en:
Tecomán lies on the hot coastal plain of Colima, where the mountains drop to lagoons and the Pacific; its Tecos people, Nahuatl speakers, made the valley the heartland of their kingdom, with the ruler's seat at Caxitlán. In 1444 Colimán was the strongest power on the western coast. Its fishermen worked the coastal lagoons and its salt pans sent salt inland, while across the eastern hills the Purépecha cazonci cast a jealous eye on the same shore. Within a generation his armies would march on these saltpeter beds, only to be thrown back.

The Tecos under Colímotl defeated the Purépecha in the Saltpeter War of 1480–1510 and made Colima the leading power of the region. They also fended off the first Spanish expeditions: Juan Rodríguez de Villafuerte was ambushed at Trojes, Juan Álvarez Chico fell in a mountain defile, and Cristóbal de Olid was beaten at the Paso de Alima near Tecomán, until Gonzalo de Sandoval feigned a retreat and broke them at Alima in 1523. On 25 July 1523 Sandoval founded the Villa de Colima at Caxitlán, the first Spanish town council in western New Spain, and the Indian town of Santiago de Tecomán was laid two leagues away, with a hospital of Saint James recorded from about 1550. The Spanish town was moved to its present inland site on 20 January 1527, and Caxitlán slowly declined until a fire in October 1800 destroyed its parish church. In 1812 the insurgent captains Pedro and Manuel Regalado took Tecomán and Caxitlán and sacked the royal salt works of San Pantaleón.
zh:
特科曼位于科利马炎热的沿海平原，群山在此俯临潟湖与太平洋；居住于此的特科斯人说纳瓦特尔语，他们把这片河谷经营成王国的腹地，首领的驻地设在卡希特兰。1444年，科利曼是西部海岸最强大的势力：渔民在沿岸潟湖中捕捞，盐田所产的食盐输往内陆，而东山之外的普雷佩查卡松西正觊觎着同一段海岸。不出一代人的时间，他的军队就会为这些硝石滩杀来，却被击退。

1480至1510年的硝石战争中，科利莫特尔率领特科斯人击败普雷佩查，使科利马成为这一地区的首强。他们还接连击退最早的几支西班牙远征军：胡安·罗德里格斯·德·比亚富埃尔特在特罗赫斯中伏，胡安·阿尔瓦雷斯·奇科战死山隘，克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德在特科曼附近的阿利马山口落败，直到贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔佯退设伏，于1523年在阿利马将其击溃。1523年7月25日，桑多瓦尔在卡希特兰建立科利马镇，这是新西班牙西部第一个西班牙市镇议会；两里格外另设印第安人城镇圣地亚哥·德·特科曼，约1550年起已有供奉圣地亚哥的医院。1527年1月20日，西班牙人的城镇迁往今日内陆城址，卡希特兰日渐衰败，1800年10月的一场大火又烧毁了它的堂区教堂。1812年，起义军首领佩德罗·雷加拉多与曼努埃尔·雷加拉多兄弟攻占特科曼和卡希特兰，洗劫了王家的圣潘塔莱昂盐场。

en:
Yohualtepec was the Nahuatl name for a mountain frontier where Guerrero's La Montaña meets the Mixteca and the edge of Puebla. Along the Tlapanec River valley, Tlapanec communities had traded with Mixtec groups since Huamuxtitlán was settled around 1200; Mixtec and Nahua communities also shared the broken country, and some accounts tied Huamuxtitlán to the Mixtec head town of Alcozauca. In 1444 its paths linked Coixtlahuaca and Tlapa, but the Triple Alliance had not yet turned them into an imperial tribute road.

In the second half of the fifteenth century, Triple Alliance armies under Nezahualcoyotl subdued the Tlapanec settlements and made Huamuxtitlán a strongpoint. The surrounding district became part of the tribute province of Yohualtepec, mostly in Oaxaca but reaching into Puebla and Guerrero; the Codex Mendoza records forty gold disks, each the size of a communion wafer. After the Spanish conquest Bernardino Vázquez de Tapia received Huamuxtitlán as an encomienda in 1531. Augustinians founded the convent of Santa María de la Asunción in 1534, using stone from the old temple, and the mountain parishes remained within New Spain until 1821.
zh:
约瓦尔特佩克是纳瓦特尔语对一片山地边区的称呼，位于格雷罗拉蒙塔尼亚、米斯特卡和普埃布拉边缘交会之处。特拉帕内克河沿岸，特拉帕内克人约从1200年起在瓦穆斯特特兰定居，并同米斯特克人贸易；崎岖山地中还混居着米斯特克人和纳瓦人，也有记载把瓦穆斯特特兰与米斯特克首领城镇阿尔科绍卡联系起来。1444年，这里的山路连接科伊斯特拉瓦坎和特拉帕，但三方同盟尚未把它变成帝国贡道。

15世纪后半叶，内萨瓦尔科约特尔麾下的三方同盟军队征服特拉帕内克聚落，把瓦穆斯特特兰建成堡垒。周边地区后来成为约瓦尔特佩克贡赋省的一部分，其大部在瓦哈卡，另有小片土地伸入普埃布拉和格雷罗；《门多萨手抄本》记载该省缴纳四十个圣饼大小的金盘。西班牙征服后，贝尔纳迪诺·巴斯克斯·德·塔皮亚于1531年获得瓦穆斯特特兰监护权。1534年，奥斯定会修士建立圣母升天修道院，并拆用旧神庙石料；这些山区教区此后一直属于新西班牙，直到1821年。

en:
Teotitlan, 'between the houses of the gods' in Nahuatl, guarded the mouth of the Oaxacan Canada, the steep corridor joining the Puebla highlands to the tropical lowlands. The town itself was Nahua, home of the Nonoalca, set amid Mazatec and Cuicatec villagers, and towns such as Huautla and Nanahuatipam stood subject to it. Three priest-lords governed, the chief called Teuctlamacaz, serving Cihuacoatl and a local form of Xipe Totec, and its workshops wove cloth carried as far as Guatemala. A report drawn up in 1581 remembered Teotitlan as an independent republic allied to Moctezuma but paying no tribute when the Spaniards arrived.

Another account relates that, late in the fifteenth century under Axayacatl, the town rebelled against Tenochtitlan and was stormed; its old Cuicatec inhabitants were killed and Mexica settlers took their place. Under the viceroys it became Teotitlan del Camino, named for the royal road that ran from Tehuacan and Puebla down to Antequera, the gateway post through which travellers entered the Canada. A district seat under the Intendancy of Oaxaca, it entered independent Mexico in 1821.
zh:
特奥蒂特兰在纳瓦语中意为「众神之屋之间」，扼守瓦哈卡卡尼亚达峡谷的入口，这条险峻通道连接普埃布拉高原与热带低地。城本身是纳瓦人诺诺阿尔卡人的居所，周围是马萨特克人与奎卡特克人的村寨，瓦乌特兰、纳纳瓦蒂潘等镇都受它统属。三位祭司首领治理此城，为首者称特乌克拉马卡斯，供奉西瓦科亚特尔和当地化身的希佩托特克；织坊出产的布匹远销至危地马拉。1581年的一份记述回忆，西班牙人到来时特奥蒂特兰是独立的共和国，与蒙特苏马结盟而不纳贡。

另一种说法称，15世纪末阿萨亚卡特尔在位时期，特奥蒂特兰起兵反叛特诺奇蒂特兰，城陷后旧有的奎卡特克居民遭屠戮，墨西加移民取而代之。总督时期，它得名特奥蒂特兰-德尔卡米诺，即「大道上的特奥蒂特兰」，成为从特瓦坎、普埃布拉通往安特克拉的王家大道上的门户驿站，旅人由此进入卡尼亚达峡谷。它作为瓦哈卡行政区下的区治，于1821年并入独立后的墨西哥。

en:
The mountains around Xocotla, on the rainy eastern slope of Citlaltepetl, were the country of the Cuauhtochca Totonacs, who had come down from the Puebla sierra and grouped their villages, among them the old Tetlalpa, into the chiefdom of Cuauhtochco. They burned incense before their gods with offerings of flowers and birds, and their priests taught the village children, while the snows of the great volcano looked over maize lands and cloud-forest hamlets on the road between the central plateau and the Gulf coast. In 1444 these valleys still answered to their own lords, though the armies of Moctezuma I were already closing on the region.

About 1454 a son of Netzahualcoyotl, leading the forces of the Triple Alliance, conquered the Cuauhtochco country and bound it under heavy tribute. In 1520 the mountain towns rose and killed more than a hundred passing Spaniards, and in November 1521, after the fall of Tenochtitlan, Gonzalo de Sandoval marched through and subdued them; under the encomienda the survivors paid tribute in cotton and cacao. In 1597 fifteen Spanish families were settled here as San Juan Coscomatepec, and some of their kin later helped to found the nearby city of Cordoba. In October 1813, during the insurgency, Nicolas Bravo and six hundred men broke a royalist siege of the town that had lasted thirty-three days. It joined independent Mexico in 1821.
zh:
索科特拉群山位于奥里萨巴山多雨的东坡，是夸赫托奇科托托纳克人的故土。他们从普埃布拉山地迁来，把特拉拉尔帕等旧村落并入名为夸赫托奇科的酋长国；他们焚香祭神，以鲜花和飞鸟为供，祭司兼任村塾的教师。大火山的雪线俯视着玉米地和云雾林中的村寨，一条连接中央高原与墨西哥湾沿岸的道路穿境而过。1444年，这些山谷仍听命于本地首领，而蒙特苏马一世的军队已在步步逼近。

约1454年，内萨瓦尔科约特尔之子率领三国同盟的军队征服夸赫托奇科之地，科以沉重贡赋。1520年，山区诸镇起事，杀死一百多名路过的西班牙人；1521年11月特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔进军此地将其平定，在委托监护制下改以棉花和可可纳贡。1597年，十五户西班牙家庭在此定居，建立圣胡安·科斯科马特佩克，后来其中几户人家还参与了邻近科尔多瓦城的创建。1813年10月独立战争期间，尼古拉斯·布拉沃率六百名起义军打破了王党军对该镇长达三十三天的围困。1821年，此地并入独立后的墨西哥。

en:
Mitla guards the upper Tlacolula valley, the eastern arm of the central valleys of Oaxaca. The Zapotecs knew it as Lyobaa, the 'place of rest', and as Monte Albán lost power it grew into the chief religious centre of the Zapotec world, a gateway between the living and the dead. Mixtec rulers took the town around 1000, but its Zapotec priests kept their authority, and in 1444 it is a largely autonomous holy city under the kings of Zaachila, its palace walls faced with precise stone mosaic fretwork found nowhere else in Mexico.

The high priest, called the Uija-tào, still held the sanctuary when the Spaniards reached the valley in 1521, and the friar Motolinía described its temples within a generation. Later in the sixteenth century Bishop Bernardo de Albuquerque had the ancient palaces dismantled, determined to break their hold on the faithful; the church of San Pablo was raised on one of the sacred quadrangles, its monolithic lintels and dressed stone taken from Zapotec halls. Diego García de Palacio described the ruins in 1576. The new pueblo of San Pablo Villa de Mitla grew up around the church on the road from Antequera to Tehuantepec, while the greca mosaics of the abandoned palaces survived as the most famous work of Zapotec stonemasons.
zh:
米特拉扼守着瓦哈卡中央谷地东支特拉科卢拉谷的上游。萨波特克人称它为略奥瓦，意为「安息之地」；阿尔班山失势后，这里成为萨波特克世界最重要的宗教中心，被视为生者与死者之间的门户。约1000年，米斯特克君主夺取此城，萨波特克祭司却仍保有权威。1444年，它是萨奇拉诸王治下一座高度自治的圣城，宫殿墙面镶嵌着墨西哥其他地方见不到的、精密拼合的石刻回纹。

1521年西班牙人进入谷地时，称作乌伊哈-塔奥的大祭司仍主持着圣所，修士莫托利尼亚在一代人之后就记述了这里的庙宇。16世纪后期，主教贝尔纳多·德·阿尔武尔克尔克下令拆毁古宫殿，决意斩断旧信仰对信徒的维系；圣巴勃罗教堂建在一处神圣庭院之上，整块巨石的横梁和修凿的石料都取自萨波特克殿堂。迭戈·加西亚·德·帕拉西奥1576年留下了对废墟的记载。新的圣巴勃罗·米特拉村在教堂周围形成，坐落于安特克拉通往特万特佩克的大道旁；废弃宫殿里的回纹镶嵌石幸存下来，成为萨波特克石匠最负盛名的杰作。

en:
The Tzotzil, whose name means the 'people of the bat', occupy the cold pine-clad ridges and valleys of Los Altos, the highlands of Chiapas. Their ancestors had settled there by the early centuries of the first millennium, and on the eve of the conquest their country was divided among at least seven small lordships: Zinacantán was the strongest, with Chamula, Huixtán and others beside it, each lord enthroned in a fortified hilltop town. They wove cotton, worked amber, drew salt from wells near Ixtapa and sent quetzal feathers and amber north to Tenochtitlan. In 1444 the highland towns were free, quarrelsome and rich by the measure of the sierra.

In December 1522 Cuzcácuatl, lord of Zinacantán, travelled to the Spanish town of Espíritu Santo on the Gulf coast to offer an alliance, and at Easter 1524 Luis Marín's expedition, guided and fed by Zinacantec warriors, subdued the rival lordships; the people of Chamula and Huixtán abandoned their towns and fled into the mountains rather than serve. Encomiendas soon parcelled the survivors out, and on 31 March 1528 Diego de Mazariegos founded Villa Real de Chiapa, raised in 1536 to Ciudad Real de Chiapa, the seat of Spanish power over the highland towns; in 1543 Bartolomé de las Casas arrived there as first bishop of Chiapa. Heavy tribute and a new Indian cult at Cancuc brought thirty-two Tzeltal, Tzotzil and Ch'ol towns out in revolt in June 1712, the rebels calling themselves 'soldiers of the Virgin'; royal troops retook Cancuc on 21 November and crushed the rising with great severity.
zh:
索西人的族名原意是「蝙蝠人」，世居恰帕斯中部高寒的松林山脊与谷地之间。他们的祖先早在公元后最初几个世纪已到此定居；西班牙征服前夕，这片土地分裂为至少七个小邦，齐纳坎坦最强，另有查穆拉、维斯坦等，各邦君主坐镇筑垒的山头城镇。他们织棉布、制琥珀，从伊斯塔帕附近的盐井取盐，又把格查尔鸟羽毛和琥珀北销特诺奇蒂特兰。1444年，这些高原城镇自由、好斗，以山地的标准算得上富庶。

1522年12月，齐纳坎坦首领库斯卡夸特尔远赴墨西哥湾沿岸的西班牙人城镇圣灵镇求盟；1524年复活节，路易斯·马林的远征队靠齐纳坎坦战士引路供粮，征服了敌对各邦，查穆拉和维斯坦的居民则弃城逃入深山，不愿臣服。幸存者很快被编进监护征赋制分给征服者。1528年3月31日，迭戈·德·马萨列戈斯建立恰帕皇家镇，1536年升格为恰帕王城，成为西班牙人统辖高原诸城的中心；1543年，巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯到此就任恰帕首任主教。沉重的贡赋与坎库克兴起的印第安人新崇拜，终于在1712年6月激起三十二个特塞尔塔尔、索西和乔尔人城镇起事，起义者自称「圣母的士兵」；王家军队于11月21日攻陷坎库克，残酷镇压了暴动。

en:
On the high north-western shelf of the Cuchumatanes, above the river frontier with Chiapas, lies the Jacaltenango plateau, the Huista country of the Jakaltek Maya, who call themselves Popti'. Their chief town Xajlaj — Jacaltenango, 'the place of the great white rock slabs' — stood where trails from the Petén lowlands met the paths climbing from the Pacific coast, and its market drew the scattered villages around. The natural wall of the sierra kept the highland empires at arm's length, though local tradition remembers K'iche' war parties pushing this far during the reign of K'iq'ab the Great (1425–1475). In 1444 the Jakaltek towns kept their own lords and their own Q'anjob'alan tongue.

The conquest was quick but the new rule stayed distant: in 1529 Jacaltenango, together with San Mateo Ixtatán and Santa Eulalia, was granted in encomienda to Gonzalo de Ovalle, one of Alvarado's companions, and a town of some two thousand Indians became his estate.
