Dominicans carried out the first reducción there in 1549; the Mercedarians later traded their lowland doctrines for the Cuchumatanes, formed their Guatemalan province in 1565 and raised the convent of Nuestra Señora de la Purificación in 1567. Beyond the doctrines the forest frontier remained dangerous, as independent Lacandones raided all through the seventeenth century and forced the Spanish to garrison the northern towns. By about 1690 the chronicler Fuentes y Guzmán found Jacaltenango shrunk to eight hundred people, 'an ancient and principal place, the court of some cacique'; in 1754 the Bourbon reforms took the doctrine from the Mercedarians and handed it to the secular clergy.
zh:
哈卡尔特克人自称波普蒂人，居住在库丘马塔内斯山西北缘的高台地上，脚下就是与恰帕斯分界的河谷。他们的首镇哈伊拉赫——即西班牙人所称的哈卡尔特南戈，意为「巨大白石板之地」——正处在佩滕低地山道与太平洋沿岸上山路的交汇处，集市吸引着周围分散的村落。群山这道天然屏障把高原帝国挡在远处，不过当地相传，在基卡布大王（1425—1475年在位）的时代，基切人的战阵也曾推进到这里。1444年，哈卡尔特克诸城仍奉自己的首领、说自己的坎霍瓦尔兰语。

征服来得很快，统治却很疏阔：1529年，哈卡尔特南戈连同圣马特奥-伊斯塔坦、圣欧拉利娅一起被作为监护地封给阿尔瓦拉多的部将贡萨洛·德·奥瓦列，这座约有两千印第安人的城镇成了他的私产。1549年，多明我会在此完成第一次集村归化；后来仁慈圣母会用低地教区换得库丘马塔内斯的教区，1565年其危地马拉会省成立，1567年建起净礼圣母修道院。教区之外，林缘始终不太平：整个17世纪，独立的拉坎东人不断入袭，西班牙人被迫在北部诸城驻军。到1690年前后，编年史家富恩特斯-古斯曼见到的哈卡尔特南戈已缩至八百人，是「古老而首要之地，曾为某位酋长的宫廷」；1754年，波旁改革把这一教区从仁慈圣母会手中收归世俗教士。

en:
Q'umarkaj, called Utatlán in Nahuatl, was founded around 1400 on a defensible plateau beside the older K'iche' center of Pismachi'. Temples to Tohil, Awilix, Jakawitz and Q'uq'umatz stood around its main plaza, with the palaces of the Kaweq, Nijaib and other ruling lineages nearby. By 1444 K'iq'ab ruled there at the head of the K'iche'-Kaqchikel alliance. His highland wars had brought Rabinal, Cobán and Quetzaltenango under Q'umarkaj, while Kaqchikel support helped carry K'iche' power east to the Motagua River and south toward the Pacific cacao lands around Escuintla. The capital was then near the height of its power, drawing tribute and military service from subject peoples and allied clans.

The long expansion ended in 1470, when two sons of K'iq'ab rose during a great assembly, killed Kaqchikel warriors and Kaweq nobles, and forced the king to surrender power to rebel lords. The new government turned on the Kaqchikel, who withdrew to Iximché; after K'iq'ab died in 1475, a K'iche' attack under Tepepul ended in disaster, and Tekum was later killed fighting the Tz'utujil by Lake Atitlán. In March 1524, after Pedro de Alvarado defeated a K'iche' army in the Quetzaltenango valley and Tecún Umán fell there, the city's lords invited the Spanish to Q'umarkaj. Alvarado suspected a trap, seized the two principal rulers in his camp, burned them alive and destroyed the city. The Spanish then founded nearby Santa Cruz del Quiché, where Dominicans reused ruined stones in churches and a cathedral while former Q'umarkaj lords were reduced to peasant status. In 1638 Santa Cruz formed part of the Dominican doctrine based at Sacapulas, until the Bourbon reform of 1754 transferred the Indian parishes to secular clergy; the district remained in Spanish Guatemala until independence in 1821.
zh:
库马尔卡赫在纳瓦特尔语中称乌塔特兰，约1400年建在一座易守难攻的高原上，紧邻更古老的基切中心皮斯马奇。主广场周围矗立着托希尔、阿维利什、贾卡维茨和库库马茨的神庙，卡韦克、尼哈伊布等统治氏族的宫殿就在近旁。到1444年，基克阿布已在此以基切—卡克奇克尔同盟首领的身份统治。他的高地战争使拉比纳尔、科万和克萨尔特南戈臣服于库马尔卡赫；在卡克奇克尔人支持下，基切势力东抵莫塔瓜河，向南延伸到埃斯昆特拉一带的太平洋可可产地。此时的库马尔卡赫正接近权力顶峰，向被征服民族和同盟氏族征取贡赋与兵役。

长期扩张在1470年告终：基克阿布的两个儿子在一次大集会期间举事，杀死许多卡克奇克尔战士和卡韦克贵族，迫使国王向叛党首领让权。新掌权者转而敌视卡克奇克尔人，后者退往伊希姆契；1475年基克阿布死后，特佩普尔率军进攻伊希姆契却惨败，后来特库姆又在阿蒂特兰湖畔与楚图希尔人作战时身亡。1524年3月，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多在克萨尔特南戈谷地击败基切军队，特昆·乌曼也在该役战死后，库马尔卡赫的首领邀请西班牙人入城。阿尔瓦拉多担心中计，在营中擒获两名最高首领，将他们活活烧死并摧毁城市。西班牙人随后在附近建立圣克鲁斯-德尔基切，多明我会拆用遗址石材修建教堂和大教堂，昔日库马尔卡赫贵族则被降为农民。1638年，圣克鲁斯属于以萨卡普拉斯为中心的多明我会传教区；1754年波旁改革将印第安教区转交世俗教士。这一地区此后仍属西属危地马拉，直到1821年独立。

en:
The Kobox, or Kob'ox and also written Couoh, were a Maya people related to the Itzá, set across the broad forested karst corridor between the Yucatán plain and the Petén lakes. Another Maya people, the Kejache, lived in the northern part of this corridor. Kindred Maya groups had moved south from Mayapán around 1300. In 1444, as the northern league broke apart, the woods here held fortified villages and refugee kin groups linked by overland and canoe trade between the Yucatec chiefdoms and the independent Itzá power around Lake Petén Itzá.

Hernán Cortés crossed this country in 1525 on his way to Honduras and found Kejache towns built on defensible ground, some with palisades, walls, and moats. Alonso Dávila crossed the northern part in 1531. By about 1600 the Kejache numbered perhaps 7,000 in ten to twenty settlements, receiving Yucatec refugees and acting as middlemen between Spanish Yucatán and the still-independent Petén Maya. Missions were established at Ichbalche and Tzuktok along a road pushed south from Campeche. Martín de Ursúa y Arizmendi's expedition then used the Yucatán route to capture Nojpetén in 1697, ending the independent Itzá and Kob'ox world; many survivors withdrew deeper into the Lacandón forest.
zh:
科博赫人（Kob'ox，又写作Couoh）是与伊察人有亲缘关系的玛雅群体，活动在尤卡坦平原与佩滕湖群之间广阔的石灰岩森林走廊。另一支玛雅群体克哈切人居住在这条通道的北部。约1300年起，与他们相近的玛雅群体陆续从马亚潘南迁。1444年，北方联盟正走向瓦解，这片森林中分布着设防村社和避难亲族，陆路与独木舟贸易把尤卡坦诸政权同佩滕伊察湖畔仍保持独立的伊察势力连接起来。

1525年，埃尔南·科尔特斯前往洪都拉斯时穿过此地，发现克哈切人的城镇建在易守难攻之处，有些还设有木栅、城墙和壕沟。1531年，阿隆索·达维拉穿过其北部。到1600年前后，克哈切人约有七千，分布在十至二十个定居点中；他们接纳尤卡坦难民，并在西班牙统治下的尤卡坦与仍独立的佩滕玛雅人之间充当中介。沿从坎佩切向南开辟的道路，西班牙人在伊奇巴尔切和楚克托克建立传教站。1697年，马丁·德·乌尔苏亚·阿里斯门迪的远征军沿尤卡坦路线攻占诺赫佩滕，独立的伊察与科博赫世界终结，许多幸存者退入拉坎东森林深处。

en:
Moran names the wet Caribbean slope between Chetumal, the Petén lakes and the Polochic-Izabal lowlands. Rivers such as the New, Belize, Sibun and Macal cut through forest and the Maya Mountains, carrying canoes between the coast, Lamanai and Tipu. Tipu became the chief town of Dzuluinicob, a Postclassic Maya province whose material culture was closer to Petén than to northern Yucatán and which may have grown after Mayapan's fall. In 1444 its Putún-connected Maya towns kept cacao orchards and river trade on the frontier between Chactemal and the Itza, untouched by Spanish conquest.

Cortés crossed the Mopan and Manche lowlands in 1525. The Pacheco entrada of 1543–1544 is thought to have brought Dzuluinicob under the new Bacalar district, where Franciscans made Lamanai and Tipu mission towns. After decades of tribute demands, famine and flight, Tipu rose in 1638; within a few years Spanish power collapsed across Dzuluinicob, and Bacalar lost most of its Maya population. Tipu stayed autonomous until 1695, served Spanish operations against the Itza in 1696, and after Nojpetén fell in 1697 its people were forcibly removed to Lake Petén Itzá in 1707. English Baymen meanwhile turned the Belize River into a logwood and mahogany frontier; treaties of 1783 and 1786 regularised their holdings, and their victory off St George's Caye on 10 September 1798 ended the last Spanish effort to dislodge them.
zh:
莫兰指查克特马尔、佩滕湖区与波洛奇克—伊萨瓦尔低地之间这片加勒比湿润坡地。纽河、伯利兹河、西本河、马卡尔河等河流穿过雨林和玛雅山，独木舟沿水路往来于海岸、拉马奈与蒂普之间。蒂普是后古典期马雅政区祖卢伊尼科布（Dzuluinicob）的首要城镇，该政区的物质文化更接近佩滕而非北尤卡坦，可能是在马亚潘瓦解后兴起。1444年，这里与普屯人有关的马雅村镇经营可可园和河上贸易，处在查克特马尔与伊察之间的边地上，尚未遭到西班牙征服。

1525年，科尔特斯穿过莫潘与曼切低地。1543—1544年帕切科家族的远征据信使祖卢伊尼科布并入新设的巴卡拉尔辖区，方济各会随后把拉马奈和蒂普变成传教城镇。在数十年贡赋、饥荒和逃亡之后，蒂普于1638年起事；数年间，西班牙权力在整个祖卢伊尼科布崩溃，巴卡拉尔也失去大部分马雅人口。蒂普一直保持自治到1695年，1696年被西班牙用作进攻伊察人的前沿据点；1697年诺赫佩滕陷落后，蒂普居民于1707年被强行迁往佩滕湖畔。与此同时，英国「湾民」把伯利兹河变成染木和桃花心木边疆；1783年和1786年的条约确认了他们的采伐权，1798年9月10日，他们在圣乔治岛外海取胜，终结了西班牙驱逐他们的最后尝试。

en:
The Xiu province had its capital at Maní, a town founded by the Xiu lineage between 1224 and 1247 as their power shifted from Uxmal. The family had once held first place in the League of Mayapan, but by 1300 the Cocom and their Canul guards controlled the city, and many Xiu were expelled around 1400. From 1441 to 1461 Ah Xupan Xiu led the war that destroyed Mayapan and overthrew the Cocom royal house. In 1444 Maní was therefore becoming the center of the strongest western Yucatec polity, with Na, Ku, Dzul, Tun and other lineages settled within the Xiu province.

The old feud with the Cocom shaped the Spanish conquest. In 1535 a Xiu party that had received Cocom permission to sacrifice at the sacred cenote of Chichén Itzá was deceived and ambushed. During Montejo's final campaign of 1541-42, the Xiu lord of Maní submitted and converted to Catholicism, and his example encouraged the western provinces to accept Spanish rule. On 12 July 1562, after a clandestine shrine was uncovered, the Franciscan Diego de Landa held an auto de fe beside the monastery of San Miguel Arcángel in Maní, burning many Maya codices and cult images; torture and coercion speeded mass conversion. Landa was recalled to face investigation, was absolved, and returned as bishop of Yucatán in 1572, while Maní remained a colonial head town under its Franciscan monastery.
zh:
休人辖区以马尼为首府。1224年至1247年间，休家族在势力从乌斯马尔转移的过程中建立此城。该家族曾在玛雅潘联盟中居于首位，但到1300年前后，玛雅潘已由科科姆人和他们的卡努尔戍卫控制，约1400年又有大批休人被逐。1441年至1461年，阿·苏潘·休领导战争摧毁玛雅潘，推翻科科姆王室。因此到1444年，马尼正成为西尤卡坦最强大政权的中心，纳、库、祖尔、通等家族也居住在休人辖区内。

与科科姆人的旧怨深刻影响了西班牙征服。1535年，一队休人获科科姆人允许，前往奇琴伊察圣井举行祭祀，却遭到诱骗和伏击。1541—1542年蒙特霍最后一次征伐期间，马尼的休人首领归附并改宗天主教，他的先例促使西部各辖区接受西班牙统治。1562年7月12日，一处秘密祭坛被发现后，方济各会士迭戈·德·兰达在马尼的圣米格尔修道院旁举行信仰判决，焚毁大量玛雅抄本和神像；酷刑与胁迫加速了集体改宗。兰达后来被召回受审，获释后于1572年以尤卡坦主教身份返回，马尼则在方济各会修道院旁继续作为殖民时期的首镇。

en:
Chikinchel, also called Chauacá after its principal town, was the salt country of northeastern Yucatán: lagoons, marshes, hunting grounds, and a long northern shore between Ah Kin Chel, Cupul, Tases, and Ekab. As Mayapán collapsed between 1441 and 1461, this coast became one of the Maya kuchkabalob, though it was never a tightly united province. In 1444 the rival towns of Chauaca, Sinsimato, and Dzonotaké guarded the peninsula's richest salt workings from outsiders, while leading men kept to healthier villages along the coast.

In 1517 Francisco Hernández de Córdoba's expedition reached the estuary later called Río Lagartos while searching for fresh water. On 28 May 1543 the Montejo conquest government founded Valladolid at Chauac-Há in Chikinchel, laid out the Spanish town, and granted encomiendas to forty-five conquistadors. Mosquitoes, humidity, and marsh fever made the site unbearable, and on 24 March 1545 the villa was moved to Zací, a Cupul town farther inland. The Spanish settlement stayed in Chikinchel for less than two years, but the encomiendas assigned at its founding tied Chauacá's salt beds and hunting lands to colonial eastern Yucatán.
zh:
奇金切尔又称乔阿卡，后者是其主要城镇的名字。这里是尤卡坦东北部的盐乡，潟湖、沼泽、猎场和漫长北岸夹在阿金切尔、库普尔、塔塞斯和埃卡布之间。1441年至1461年马亚潘崩溃时，这片海岸成为玛雅库奇卡巴尔辖区之一，但从未形成紧密统一的政权。1444年，乔阿卡、辛西马托和佐诺塔凯等彼此竞争的城镇把守着半岛最富饶的盐场，不许外来者染指；首领们则多住在海岸一带较宜居住的村落里。

1517年，弗朗西斯科·埃尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦的探险队为寻找淡水，抵达后来被称为里奥拉加托斯的河口。1543年5月28日，蒙特霍征服政权在奇金切尔的乔阿克-阿建立巴利亚多利德，规划西班牙城镇，并向四十五名征服者分配监护征赋权。蚊虫、湿热和沼泽热病使这里难以居住，1545年3月24日，这座城镇迁往更内陆的库普尔城镇萨西。西班牙人在奇金切尔设城不到两年，但建城时分封的监护征赋权已把乔阿卡的盐场和猎地纳入殖民时期尤卡坦东部的秩序。

en:
In 1444 Ulva was the river country of the Ulwa, the southern Sumu people. Settlements followed the Río Grande de Matagalpa and Río Escondido, including the Tuma, Siquia and Mico tributaries that run from the central highlands toward Caribbean lagoons. Ulwa families fished, hunted, cleared riverside fields and travelled by dugout canoe, their territory forming a network of basins rather than a fixed frontier. Miskito communities lived to the north, Matagalpa-speaking highlanders to the west, and Kukra and Rama groups nearer the southern bays; no European post yet interrupted that river world.

Christopher Columbus's fourth voyage passed the Mosquito Shore in 1502, but outside power reached these rivers only indirectly. In the early seventeenth century Dutch and English privateers began using the Escondido and Bluefields anchorages, while British contacts after the 1630s gave Miskito allies firearms. Miskito raiders penetrated the interior to seize Ulwa and Mayangna captives, selling men toward Jamaica and incorporating many women, a trade that pulled Ulwa communities toward more isolated headwaters. Spanish missionaries and colonial officials reached the western basins in the eighteenth century, yet alliances shifted from village to village. Yarrince, an Ulwa leader from Olama, first cooperated with the British and then accepted Spanish rank as a captain-governor; he was imprisoned in 1780 and died the same year in Guatemala. The 1786 Convention of London removed British settlers without making Spanish rule firm, and after Miskito forces drove the Spanish out in 1800, the Ulwa river basins were still effectively their own in 1821.
zh:
1444年的乌尔瓦是乌尔瓦人的河网之地。乌尔瓦人是南部苏穆语人群，村落沿马塔加尔帕大河与埃斯孔迪多河展开，也分布在图马河、西基亚河和米科河等从中部高地流向加勒比潟湖的支流。乌尔瓦家庭捕鱼、狩猎、清理河畔田地，并乘独木舟往来；他们的疆域不是固定边界，而是一串相连的河流盆地。北方是米斯基托社群，西方是说马塔加尔帕语的高地人，南部港湾附近则有库克拉人和拉马人；当时还没有欧洲据点切入这个河上世界。

1502年，哥伦布第四次航行经过莫斯基托海岸，但外部势力并未直接深入这些河川。17世纪初，荷兰和英格兰私掠者开始利用埃斯孔迪多河与布卢菲尔兹锚地；1630年代以后同英国人的接触使米斯基托同盟者获得火器。米斯基托袭掠者深入内陆捉拿乌尔瓦人和马扬格纳人，把男子卖向牙买加，又把许多女子并入本社群，这种奴隶贸易迫使乌尔瓦社群向更偏远的河源退却。18世纪，西班牙传教士和殖民官吏进入西部河流盆地，但各村庄的同盟反复变化。奥拉马的乌尔瓦首领亚林塞先同英国人合作，后来又接受西班牙授予的军政长官职衔；他在1780年入狱，同年死于危地马拉。1786年《伦敦公约》撤走英国移民，却没有稳固西班牙统治；1800年米斯基托军队驱逐西班牙人后，到1821年，乌尔瓦各河流盆地实际上仍掌握在本地人手中。

en:
Xicaque is the Spanish exonym for the Tolupan country on the central Honduran coast. Its beaches, lagoons and river mouths ran from the Ulúa toward Puerto Castilla, with the forested ridges of Yoro and the Sulaco headwaters rising inland. In 1444 Tolupan-speaking villages and mobile bands cultivated bitter manioc and maize, hunted and fished, and used dugout canoes to carry maize and the cochineal cactus between Tela Bay, the rivers and the interior. Local headmen led their own settlements; there was no single capital, and no European fleet had yet anchored off the shore.

On 3 May 1524 Cristóbal de Olid established one of the earliest Spanish settlements in Honduras beside the native town of Tehuacán in Tela Bay, whose local leader the Spanish called Cucumba. The date was the feast of the Cross, and a nearby promontory became known as Triunfo de la Cruz; within months the small municipality was dissolved and the district placed under Trujillo. Spanish control remained light, and independent Tolupan groups still formed part of the forest frontier later called Taguzgalpa. At the end of the sixteenth century buccaneers haunted Tela Bay, hunting Spanish schooners carrying precious metals from Trujillo and Puerto Caballos; Franciscan reducciones began early in the next century, and in 1609 some Tolupans had settled as far inland as the Guayape and Guayambre valleys. After the British deported Black Caribs to Roatán in 1797, Garifuna families spread along the coast and founded Triunfo de la Cruz and San Juan near Tela in 1808. In 1821 the shore remained a mixed Tolupan, Garifuna and thinly settled Spanish frontier.
zh:
希卡克是西班牙人对托卢潘人土地的他称，位于洪都拉斯中北部海岸。海滩、潟湖和河口从乌卢阿河一带延伸向卡斯蒂利亚港，内陆则是约罗的林脊和苏拉克河源头。1444年，说托卢潘语的村社和流动群体种植苦木薯与玉米，兼营狩猎和渔捞，并乘独木舟把玉米和胭脂虫仙人掌运到特拉湾、各河流与内陆之间。各地由本地首领分别管辖，没有统一都城，也还没有欧洲船队在海岸外停泊。

1524年5月3日，克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德在特拉湾的原住民城镇特瓦坎旁建立洪都拉斯最早的西班牙据点之一；西班牙人把当地首领称作库库姆巴。这一天是十字架节日，附近海岬后来得名特里温福·德拉鲁斯。仅数月后，这个小小的市政建制便被撤销，地区划归特鲁希略管辖。西班牙人的控制始终薄弱，独立的托卢潘群体仍属于后来被称作塔古斯加尔帕的森林前沿。16世纪末，巴克尼尔海盗出没特拉湾，猎捕从特鲁希略和卡瓦略斯港运载贵金属的西班牙纵帆船；下一世纪初方济各会开始建立集居传教区，1609年已有部分托卢潘人深入瓜亚佩河与瓜亚姆布雷河谷居住。1797年英国把黑加勒比人流放到罗阿坦岛后，加里富纳家庭沿海岸扩散，并于1808年在特拉附近建立特里温福·德拉鲁斯和圣胡安社区。1821年时，这片海岸仍是托卢潘人、加里富纳人和稀疏西班牙移民共处的边疆。

en:
Tzul covers the rainforest and foothills between Lake Petén Itzá, the Lacandón forest and the Guatemalan highlands, the country Spanish records called Tute. Its rivers linked the Itza lake world with Cahabón, Cobán and the Sierra de los Cuchumatanes; maize fields stood beside cacao, vanilla, achiote and cotton groves. The Tute and Lakandon Ch'ol were forest nations in Kan Ek's outer orbit, sometimes tributary, often dangerous to highland travellers and missionaries. In 1444 their forest country lay between Nojpetén and the Guatemalan highlands.

Cortés crossed neighbouring Manche Ch'ol country in 1525, and Pedro Ramírez de Quiñones led the first Spanish expedition against the Lakandon in 1559. The Ch'ol later withdrew from Lakam-Tun to the hidden town of Sac Balam around 1586 and kept their independence there into the 1690s. Franciscans Antonio Margil and Melchor López were expelled in 1694, and the great Guatemalan campaign of 1695 opened the forest, baptised more than six hundred families around new Dolores settlements and occupied Sac Balam. After Nojpetén fell on 13 March 1697, the Tute fled before the troops and joined the postwar rising; Spanish prisoners named them among the killers of soldiers and looters of missionary goods. When Kan Ek' was carried to Guatemala in 1699, the Tute were counted among five fugitive Petén kingdoms, led by men named Chachulté, Chaues, Buenavista, Chatoco and Ixmucuyl. In 1712 the surviving Lakandon Ch'ol were forcibly removed toward Huehuetenango; the Tute then vanished from colonial records as a separate people.
zh:
楚尔（Tzul）位于佩滕湖、拉坎东丛林与危地马拉高地之间，是一片雨林与山麓交错地带，西班牙文献称之为图特。各条河川把伊察人的湖区世界同卡瓦翁、科万和库丘马塔内斯山脉连接起来；玉米地旁分布着可可、香荚兰、胭脂树和棉花种植园。图特人与拉坎东乔尔人是卡内克势力外圈的森林族群，有时纳贡，也常令高地商旅和传教士视为畏途。1444年，他们居住的森林地带位于诺赫佩滕与危地马拉高地之间。

1525年，科尔特斯穿过相邻的曼切乔尔地区；1559年，佩德罗·拉米雷斯·德·基尼奥内斯率领第一支征讨拉坎东人的西班牙远征队。1586年前后，乔尔人放弃拉坎-通，退入隐秘新城萨克巴兰，并在那里把独立维持到1690年代。1694年，方济各会士安东尼奥·马希尔和梅尔乔·洛佩斯被驱逐；1695年，危地马拉发动大规模进军，打开森林，在新建的多洛雷斯聚居点为六百多个家庭施洗，并占领萨克巴兰。1697年3月13日诺赫佩滕陷落后，图特人在军队逼近时逃散，并加入战后的起事；西班牙俘虏指称他们参与杀害士兵、劫掠传教士器物。1699年卡内克被押往危地马拉，图特人被列为五个继续逃亡的佩滕小王国之一，其首领名为查丘尔特、查韦斯、布埃纳维斯塔、查托科和伊什穆奎尔。1712年，幸存的拉坎东乔尔人被强行迁往韦韦特南戈一带；图特人随后也不再作为独立群体见于殖民记录。

en:
The land called Guaymi takes in the island-studded waters of Almirante Bay and Chiriquí Lagoon, backed by wet rain-forest highlands. In 1444 the Atlantic Ngäbe lived here in dispersed villages led by chiefs and powerful families; their wider country crossed the isthmus, but they had no single empire or capital. They called themselves Ngäbe, meaning 'people' in Ngäbere, while Guaymí was a later outsider name derived from Buglere.

Christopher Columbus reached these waters on 6 October 1502 while searching for a passage to the Pacific, and a leader named or titled Quibían helped drive the expedition off. Spanish footholds remained fragile: Urracá forced Captain Diego de Albites to make peace in 1522, escaped after being seized and sent to Nombre de Dios, and died a free man in 1531. Castillo de Austria, planted on Almirante Bay in 1560, was abandoned within a year, as was Artieda del Nuevo Reino de Navarra on the Cricamola in 1577–1578. During the following centuries English pirates and Miskito raiders used the lagoons. Pablo Presbere's 1709 rising reached Colón Island, and Spanish records report that a Miskito attack in 1758 destroyed the Tojar community, killing or enslaving about two thousand people. Afro-Caribbean traders settled on Bastimentos in 1817. When the isthmus left Spanish rule in 1821, the Ngäbe remained in their mountains rather than submitting to Gran Colombia.
zh:
称为瓜伊米的土地，包括岛礁散布的阿尔米兰特湾和奇里基潟湖，后方是潮湿的雨林山地。1444年，靠大西洋的恩戈贝人住在分散村落中，由酋长和望族统领；他们的活动范围横越地峡，却没有统一帝国或都城。他们自称恩戈贝，在恩戈贝雷语中意为「人」；瓜伊米则是后来外来者根据布格雷语取的名字。

1502年10月6日，哥伦布在寻找通往太平洋的水道时抵达这片海域，名为或称号为基维安的首领将远征者击退。西班牙人的据点始终脆弱：乌拉卡在1522年迫使迭戈·德·阿尔比特斯队长议和，后来他被押往农布雷-德迪奥斯又逃脱，1531年以自由之身去世。1560年设在阿尔米兰特湾的奥地利堡不足一年即遭放弃，1577年在克里卡莫拉河畔建立的新纳瓦拉王国阿尔铁达也于次年废弃。此后两个世纪，英国海盗和米斯基托袭掠者利用潟湖活动。巴勃罗·普雷斯贝雷1709年的起义波及科隆岛；西班牙记载称，1758年米斯基托人摧毁托哈尔社群，约有两千人被杀或沦为奴隶。1817年，非裔加勒比商人到巴斯蒂门托斯岛定居。1821年地峡脱离西班牙统治时，恩戈贝人仍留在山中，没有向大哥伦比亚屈服。

en:
The green shores of the Gulf of Urabá, where the muddy Atrato pours into the southern Caribbean, were Guna land in 1444. Calling themselves Dule, 'the people', these Chibchan-speakers lived in autonomous villages along the gulf and the lower Atrato, farming maize and yuca, fishing the mangrove lagoons and hunting in the rainforest behind. Their country lay at the neck of the continent, where the Darién isthmus begins, and dugouts carried them between river and sea. No paramount chief ruled them, and no European sail had yet been seen in those waters.

Rodrigo de Bastidas explored the gulf in 1501, the first Spaniard to do so, and on 20 January 1510 Alonso de Ojeda founded San Sebastián de Urabá on its eastern shore near the later town of Necoclí, the first attempted Spanish settlement on the American mainland. The Guna met it with poisoned arrows and wounded Ojeda himself; famine and siege did the rest. Ojeda sailed away, leaving the young Francisco Pizarro in command; by the time reinforcements arrived, only 42 of the original 300 settlers remained. Before the year ended the survivors crossed to the western shore to found Santa María del Darién, and San Sebastián vanished from the maps. No lasting Spanish town ever took root on the gulf: through the rest of the colonial period its coasts remained a neglected frontier of scattered Indian villages, while Guna bands, pressed by Spaniards and warring neighbours, gradually moved off westward towards the San Blas shore.
zh:
1444年，乌拉瓦湾翠绿的海岸是库纳人的土地——浑浊的阿特拉托河在此注入加勒比海的南缘。他们自称杜雷，意为「人」，说奇布查语，在海湾沿岸与阿特拉托河下游的自治村落里种植玉米、木薯，在红树林潟湖中捕鱼，到后方的雨林狩猎。此地正当大陆的咽喉、达连地峡的起点，独木舟载着他们往来于河海之间。他们没有至高的首领，那片水域上也还没有出现过欧洲人的帆影。

1501年，罗德里戈·德·巴斯蒂达斯最先勘察这个海湾；1510年1月20日，阿隆索·德·奥赫达在东岸、后来内科克利所在之处建立圣塞瓦斯蒂安·德·乌拉瓦，这是欧洲人在美洲大陆的第一个定居尝试。库纳人以毒箭相迎，连奥赫达本人也受了伤，饥馑与围攻完成了余下的事。奥赫达乘船离去，把残局交给年轻的弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗；等到援军抵达，最初的三百名定居者只剩四十二人。未到年底，幸存者渡海前往西岸另建圣玛利亚·拉安提瓜·德尔达连，圣塞瓦斯蒂安从地图上消失。整个殖民时代，海湾始终没有长出稳固的西班牙城镇，沿岸长期是一条只有印第安村落零星散布的荒僻边地；在西班牙人和敌对邻族的逼迫下，一部分库纳人陆续西迁，朝圣布拉斯海岸而去。

en:
Talamanca is the rainy Caribbean slope below the Talamanca mountains, running south from Tariaca toward the Changuinola and Sixaola rivers. In 1444 Bribri and Cabécar communities shared these forests with Térraba, Viceita, Terbi and other Viceitic-speaking peoples. Autonomous villages and chiefdoms, not a single empire, governed the country; the Cabécar polity was strongest on Costa Rica's Atlantic side. Mountain terrain and dispersed nations later made the Spaniards call the region rebellious Talamanca.

Christopher Columbus reached Cariay on 25 September 1502, anchoring off Quiribrí, now Isla Uvita, during his fourth voyage, but the wet mountains long prevented occupation. Cabécar leaders Guaycorá and Sumamará burned Santiago de Talamanca in 1610. From 1660 Cartago sent expeditions into the region; some communities submitted two years later for help against English pirates and Miskito raiders, then rebelled against attacks on polygamy and shamanic practice. Slave raiding followed under Juan López de la Flor in 1665, and in 1666 Juan de Vida Martell burned villages and crops and seized more than a hundred people. Franciscans made converts after 1670, but on 29 September 1709 Pablo Presbere led peoples from Chirripó to Almirante Bay in revolt and fourteen mission churches burned. The rising was crushed and Presbere died in 1710, yet Spanish forces withdrew, leaving Talamanca an indigenous refuge; fresh attempts after 1740 had little clear result. When Spanish rule ended in 1821, Bribri and Cabécar lords still held most of the mountains.
zh:
塔拉曼卡位于塔拉曼卡山脉下方的潮湿加勒比坡地，北起塔里亚卡，南至昌吉诺拉河与锡克绍拉河一带。1444年，布里布里人和卡韦卡尔人，与特拉瓦人、维塞塔人、特尔维人及其他维塞伊语族群共居山林。这里没有统一帝国，而是由自治村落和酋长领地分治；卡韦卡尔人的政体是哥斯达黎加大西洋岸最强大的势力。山地地形和分散的诸族群，后来使西班牙人把这里称为反叛的塔拉曼卡。

1502年9月25日，哥伦布第四次航行时抵达卡里亚伊，停泊在基里布里岛（今乌维塔岛）外，但潮湿山地长期阻碍西班牙人占领。1610年，卡韦卡尔首领瓜伊科拉和苏马马拉焚毁圣地亚哥·德·塔拉曼卡。1660年起，卡塔戈不断派远征队进入这一地区；1662年，一些部落为抵御英国海盗和米斯基托袭掠者而接受臣服，却因传教士禁止多偶制和萨满习俗再起反抗。1665年，胡安·洛佩斯·德·拉·弗洛尔转而捕人为奴；1666年，胡安·德·维达·马特尔烧毁村落和庄稼，掳走一百多人。1670年后，方济各会传教士取得一些皈依者，但1709年9月29日，巴勃罗·普雷斯贝雷率领从奇里波到阿尔米兰特湾的诸族群起义，焚毁十四座传教教堂。起义次年遭镇压，普雷斯贝雷丧生，西班牙人却撤出军队，使塔拉曼卡成为原住民避难地；1740年后新的传教和军事行动仍成效不定。1821年西班牙统治终结时，布里布里和卡韦卡尔首领仍控制着大部分山地。

en:
Cuauhtochco was a small lordship in the broken country above Veracruz's Gulf plain, guarding routes between the coast, Puebla and the Mexican highlands. Its land had once formed part of Totonacapan, but a Teochichimeca group with Tlaxcalan connections founded the señorío in 1327. Its chief places were Cuauhtochco itself, later Santiago Huatusco near modern Carrillo Puerto, Otlaquiquixtla on the site of present Huatusco de Chicuéllar, and Tototlán. In 1444 the lordship was still independent, with fewer than five thousand people but a strategic hold on traffic moving inland from the Gulf.

Moctezuma Ilhuicamina conquered Cuauhtochco in 1457, and the town became a Nahuatl-speaking Mexica garrison. After Tenochtitlan fell, Gonzalo de Sandoval stormed the garrison in November 1521. Under Spanish rule it became the corregimiento of Santiago Cuauhtochco; severe depopulation allowed its old pyramid to stand almost forgotten. In the Atoyac lowlands, Indian and African labour on estates and sugar trapiches mixed with Spanish settlement, while the administrative centre shifted toward San Antonio Otlaquiquixtla, called San Antonio Huatusco from 1670. In 1778 the district was placed in the province of Córdoba within the Veracruz intendancy. During the independence war, enslaved people and sugar workers around Atoyac rose after Hidalgo's call, and in 1812 Mariano Mota established an insurgent centre on Cerro del Chiquihuite. In 1813 the Congress of Chilpancingo named Huatusco the insurgent capital of Veracruz.
zh:
夸赫托奇科是韦拉克鲁斯湾平原上方崎岖山地中的一个小领主国，扼守着海岸、普埃布拉与墨西哥高地之间的道路。这里原属托托纳克潘的一部分，但1327年，一支与特拉斯卡拉有关联的特奥奇奇梅卡人群建立了这个领主国。主要据点包括夸赫托奇科本地（即后来今卡里略港附近的圣地亚哥·瓦图斯科）、位于今瓦图斯科—德奇库埃利亚尔的奥特拉基基斯特兰，以及托托特兰。1444年时，该领主国仍然独立，人口不足五千，却控制着从海湾进入内陆的交通要冲。

1457年，蒙特苏马·伊尔维卡米纳征服夸赫托奇科，此地后来成为说纳瓦特尔语的墨西加驻军要塞。特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔于1521年11月攻占这座要塞。西班牙统治时期，这里成为圣地亚哥·夸赫托奇科科雷希米恩托；人口急剧减少，使古老金字塔几乎被遗忘。阿托亚克低地的庄园和蔗糖作坊役使原住民与非洲劳力，并形成印第安人、非洲人和西班牙人混居的社会；行政中心后来转向圣安东尼奥·奥特拉基基斯特兰，1670年起称圣安东尼奥·瓦图斯科。1778年，该地区被划入韦拉克鲁斯都督区下的科尔多瓦省。独立战争期间，阿托亚克一带的奴隶和蔗糖工人响应伊达尔戈号召起事；1812年，马里亚诺·莫塔在奇基维特山建立起义中心。1813年，奇尔潘辛戈议会将瓦图斯科命名为韦拉克鲁斯的起义首都。

en:
The Sinú river runs from forested highlands to the Caribbean beside the wetlands of the San Jorge, and in 1444 its valley was Zenú country. Zenú farmers grew maize and cotton on raised fields laced with drainage canals dug over centuries, while their craftsmen made pottery and hammered the gold dust the river washed down from the hills; Spanish chroniclers later described Finzenú, seat of the great female chief and capital of the Zenú lands, Yapel the potters' town and Mexión the weavers' town. Around the Gulf of Morrosquillo people fished and traded salt, and the burial mounds of their ancestors held the gold that would soon undo them.

Disease and warfare devastated the chiefdoms between 1510 and 1535. After Cartagena was founded in 1533, Pedro de Heredia's men marched up the Sinú to dig gold from the royal tombs. Survivors were gathered into encomienda pueblos such as San Andrés de Mexión, refounded in 1600, whose people rowed timber, maize and manatee oil downriver to Cartagena until direct Crown rule replaced the encomienda in 1720. In 1773 the King set aside 83,000 hectares at San Andrés de Sotavento as a Zenú reserve, and in 1777 Antonio de la Torre y Miranda founded Montería, which became the market town of the cattle ranches spreading along the river. After Bolívar's victory at Boyacá in 1819 the Sinú lands entered the republic of Gran Colombia, while the reserve kept Zenú communities alive.
zh:
锡努河（省名「西努」即由此而来）从林木茂密的高地流入加勒比海，与圣豪尔赫河的湿地相连，1444年时它的河谷是塞努人的家园。塞努农人在台地上种植玉米和棉花，田间是数百年来开挖的排灌渠网；工匠制陶、锻金，金砂就由河水从山中带下来。后来的西班牙编年史家记下了芬塞努——女大酋长的居所、塞努诸邦的都城，以及制陶之城亚佩尔和纺织之城梅希翁。莫罗斯基约湾一带的居民捕鱼、贩盐，而祖先墓丘中埋藏的黄金不久便给他们招来大祸。

1510至1535年间，疾病和战争重创了这些酋邦。卡塔赫纳1533年建立后，佩德罗·德·埃雷迪亚的部下沿锡努河而上，掘开王陵取金。幸存者被并入监护征赋制下的村镇，1600年重建的圣安德烈斯-德梅希翁便是其中之一；村民把木材、玉米和海牛脂运往卡塔赫纳，直到1720年王室直接管辖取代监护制。1773年，国王在圣安德烈斯-德索塔文托划出8.3万公顷土地作为塞努人保留地；1777年，安东尼奥·德拉托雷·米兰达建立蒙特里亚，后来成为沿河散布的牧牛场的集镇。玻利瓦尔1819年赢得博亚卡战役后，锡努河流域并入大哥伦比亚共和国，而保留地让塞努人的社群延续下来。

en:
Here the Cauca and the San Jorge pour into the Magdalena through a maze of ciénagas and caños, the wettest country of the lower river. Its people were the Maguey, a Chimila people whose tongue was kin to Carib but who had the name of being peaceable: they grew cassava and maize on the levees, fished the lagoons and hunted the flooded forest, in villages long blended with the Zenú of the lower Cauca and with the Malibú. Maguey, Yati, Tacaloa and Guazo were the river chiefdoms of this water world when, in 1444, no European had yet entered the Magdalena.

Diego de Carvajal founded the Spanish town of Magangué in 1610, but it long remained a quiet riverside settlement, and on 28 October 1776 Antonio de la Torre y Miranda refounded it as Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria de Magangué, peopling the surrounding caños with new villages. The wars of independence reached these waterways in 1815, when royalists took the town; five years later José María Córdova captured Magangué and made it the headquarters of his general staff on the lower Magdalena.
zh:
考卡河与圣豪尔赫河在这里经由一片湖沼与河汊组成的水网注入马格达莱纳河，是下游地势最湿润的地方。住在这里的是马圭人——奇米拉人的一支，语言与加勒比语相近，却以性情温顺闻名。他们在天然堤岸上种植木薯和玉米，在潟湖里捕鱼、在水淹林中狩猎，村落很早就与下考卡的塞努人以及马利布人融合。1444年欧洲人尚未进入马格达莱纳河时，马圭、亚蒂、塔卡洛阿、瓜索便是这片水乡的诸个酋邦。

1610年，迭戈·德·卡瓦哈尔建立西班牙城镇马甘格，但它长期只是个安静的河畔聚落。1776年10月28日，安东尼奥·德·拉托雷·米兰达将其重建，定名坎德拉里亚圣母马甘格，并在周围河汊设立新的村落。独立战争在1815年波及这片水道，保王派攻占了镇子；五年后，何塞·马里亚·科尔多瓦夺取马甘格，把它作为自己在下马格达莱纳的总司令部。

en:
Between the snow-capped Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and the forested Serranía del Perijá lies the hot valley of the Cesar river, cut off from the sea and watered by the Ariguaní and the Guatapurí – 'cold water' in the Chimila tongue. In 1444 it belonged to the Chimila, a Chibcha people whose lands ran west to the Ciénaga de Zapatosa and the Magdalena, while the Yukpa of the Perijá hills belonged to their confederation. Their two districts, Upar and Pocabuy, obeyed a supreme sacred chief; the people of Upar farmed the riverbanks, kept bees, made pottery and played flutes at their festivals.

Raiders from Santa Marta forced their way into the valley in the 1530s, and on 6 January 1550 Hernando de Santana and Juan de Castellanos founded the Ciudad de los Santos Reyes del Valle de Upar, the future Valledupar, on the Guatapurí. Encomiendas parcelled out the Chimila, and many fled death, disease and enslavement into the mountains as the valley turned into cattle ranges. Through the eighteenth century Spanish haciendas kept pressing on their villages, and during the wars of independence the Chimila abandoned the reduction towns and slipped back into the forests of the Ariguaní; meanwhile, on 4 February 1813, Valledupar rose against the Spanish Crown.
zh:
圣玛尔塔内华达山脉与林木茂密的佩里哈山脉之间，是炎热的塞萨尔河谷。它与海洋相隔，阿利瓜尼河与瓜塔普里河穿行其间——「瓜塔普里」在奇米拉语中意为「冷水」。1444年，这里属于奇米拉人：这支奇布查语民族的土地向西直到萨帕托萨沼泽和马格达莱纳河，佩里哈山中的尤克帕人也属于他们的部落联盟。全境分为乌帕尔和波卡布伊两大区，尊一位具有神圣地位的大酋长；乌帕尔人在河畔耕作、养蜂、制陶，在节庆上吹奏长笛。

1530年代，从圣玛尔塔出发的征服者强行进入谷地。1550年1月6日，埃尔南多·德·桑塔纳与胡安·德·卡斯特利亚诺斯在瓜塔普里河畔建立「乌帕尔谷地圣王城」，即后来的巴耶杜帕尔。监护征赋制把奇米拉人层层瓜分，许多人为躲避死亡、疾病和奴役逃入深山，谷地随之变成牧牛场。整个18世纪，西班牙大庄园不断侵占他们的村落；独立战争期间，奇米拉人离开归化集镇，退回阿利瓜尼河丛林。与此同时，1813年2月4日，巴耶杜帕尔起兵反抗西班牙王权。

en:
The rain-soaked forests of the Catatumbo basin were the country of the Barí, whom Spanish-speakers later called Motilones. In 1444 their autonomous communities occupied the river lands between the eastern Andes and the Maracaibo lowlands, speaking a Chibchan language and combining forest fields with hunting and fishing. Large roundhouses gathered each community, and the name imposed by Europeans had not yet reached the rivers.

In 1530 Barí warriors ambushed the gold-bearing expedition of Ambrosius Ehinger, the Welser agent, in the Bobalí highlands and scattered its treasure. Spanish expeditions and Capuchin missionaries met prolonged resistance from 1530 to 1730; the friars then learned Barí, began catechism, and drew some families into mission villages. From 1772 the government of Maracaibo established peaceful relations with at least twenty-one communities, and metal tools, cacao planting and trade routes encouraged settlement around the missions. During the wars of independence the Capuchins supported the Spanish king; after patriots defeated them in 1813, most Barí abandoned the villages and returned to the forest. The bishop of Mérida removed Capuchin jurisdiction over the five remaining settlements in 1817, leaving the region thinly controlled when independence arrived in 1821.
zh:
多雨的卡塔通博河流域丛林是巴雷人的土地，说西班牙语的人后来称他们为莫蒂洛内斯（莫蒂隆人）。1444年，他们的自治社群占据东安第斯山脉与马拉开波低地之间的河间地带，使用一种奇布查语系语言，以林地农作、狩猎和捕鱼为生。各社群聚居在大型圆形长屋中，欧洲人后来强加的名字此时还未传到这些河畔。

1530年，巴雷战士在博巴利高地伏击韦尔塞家族代理人安布罗修斯·埃因格携带黄金的远征队，夺走并散失了其财宝。1530年至1730年间，西班牙远征队和嘉布遣会传教士持续遭到顽强抵抗；此后修士学习巴雷语、开始传教，并把一些家庭引入传教村。1772年起，马拉开波政府同至少21个社群建立和平关系，金属工具、可可种植和商路促使人们在传教点附近定居。独立战争期间，嘉布遣会支持西班牙国王；1813年爱国者击败他们后，大多数巴雷人放弃村庄回到丛林。1817年，梅里达主教撤销嘉布遣会对仅剩五处定居点的管辖权，因此到1821年独立到来时，这片地区仍只受到薄弱控制。

en: Moniquirá, recorded in the sixteenth century as Ubaza, lies on the wooded Eastern Cordillera slopes drained by the Moniquirá, Pómeca and Suárez rivers. Before the conquest it was a Muisca community under the cacique Susa, set on the north-western edge of the Altiplano Cundiboyacense; in 1444 its Chibcha-speaking people farmed maize and other crops in temperate and cold lands linked to highland trade in salt and cloth. Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada passed through Ubaza on 16 March 1537. In 1755 the visitador Andrés Verdugo y Oquendo sold the indigenous town, and its people were attached to Chitaraque; a parish was founded there in 1788.
zh: 莫尼基拉在16世纪的文献中称乌瓦萨，坐落在东部山脉被莫尼基拉河、波梅卡河和苏亚雷斯河穿过的林坡上。征服时代以前，这里是臣服于酋长苏萨的穆伊斯卡社群，位于昆迪博亚卡高原西北缘；1444年，说奇布查语的居民在温带和寒冷地带种植玉米等作物，并与高原上的盐和织物贸易相连。1537年3月16日，贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达途经乌瓦萨。1755年，巡视官安德烈斯·贝尔杜戈·伊·奥肯多出售这座印第安村镇，居民被并入奇塔拉克；1788年，这里建立堂区。

en:
From the cloud-forested Pacific littoral, where the Telembí and Patía run out through mangrove swamps, the land climbs to the cold Atriz Valley at the foot of the Galeras volcano, home of the Quillacingas, while the wider highland region took its name from the Pastos. Related Barbacoas and Awá bands lived along the coastal rivers. These peoples farmed maize and potatoes in scattered villages and panned gold, answering to no empire: in 1444 the Inca frontier still lay far to the south, and only on the eve of the Spanish arrival did Inca armies reach and subdue these mountains.

Sebastián de Belalcázar first founded a town here in 1537, and Lorenzo de Aldana moved it into the Atriz Valley in 1539 as San Juan de Pasto, which received its coat of arms from the crown in 1559 and became the administrative and religious centre of the southern highlands. Down on the coastal rivers Francisco de la Parada founded a settlement in 1600, and Pedro Martín Navarro formalised it in 1612 as Santa María del Puerto de los Barbacoas; its goldfields, worked by African slaves, belonged to Popayán families and made Barbacoas the richest mining town of the region. No place in New Granada defended the king more stubbornly. In September 1811 troops of the short-lived Quito junta entered Pasto, but royalists retook it in 1812–13, and in 1814 Antonio Nariño's patriot army was defeated outside the town. Even after Boyacá, Pasto fought on under Agustín Agualongo; at the close of 1821 it was still unconquered, the last great royalist stronghold of southern New Granada.
zh:
从云雾笼罩的太平洋沿岸——特莱姆比河与帕蒂亚河穿过红树林沼泽入海——地势一路抬升到加莱拉斯火山脚下寒冷的阿特里斯河谷，那里是基利亚辛加人的家园，而整个高原地区因帕斯托斯人得名。与他们亲缘相近的巴尔巴夸斯人、阿瓦人则住在沿海各条河流上。这些族群在分散的村落里种植玉米和马铃薯，从河里淘金，不臣服于任何帝国：1444年，印加的边界还远在南方，直到西班牙人到来的前夜，印加军队才推进并征服这片群山。

塞瓦斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔1537年首先在此建城，1539年洛伦索·德·阿尔达纳把城镇迁入阿特里斯河谷，定名圣胡安·德·帕斯托；王室1559年颁赐城徽，这里遂成为南部高原的行政与宗教中心。在沿海河流地带，弗朗西斯科·德·拉·帕拉达1600年建立定居点，佩德罗·马丁·纳瓦罗1612年将其正式定名为圣玛利亚·德尔普埃尔托·德·洛斯·巴尔巴夸斯；当地金矿区由黑奴开采，矿权归于波帕扬的豪族，使巴尔巴夸斯成为全区最富庶的矿业城镇。在整个新格拉纳达，没有哪个地方比这里更顽固地捍卫国王：1811年9月，短命的基多洪达的军队一度进入帕斯托，但保王派在1812至1813年间夺回该地，1814年安东尼奥·纳里尼奥的爱国军又在城外被击败。即便在博亚卡战役之后，帕斯托仍在阿古斯丁·阿瓜隆戈率领下继续作战；直到1821年末，它依旧未被攻克，是新格拉纳达南部最后一座保王堡垒。

en:
The Putumayo rises in the Nudo de los Pastos and cuts through forested gorges toward the Amazon. In 1444 its upper basin was divided among autonomous peoples: Cofán communities in the southwest, Kamëntšá in the northwest, Siona and other Tucano-speaking groups along the central and southern waters, and Witoto-speaking peoples toward the east. Long navigable stretches carried canoes and trade between these riverside communities, while Inca armies had not yet crossed the Andean foothills.

In 1492 the Inca Huayna Cápac crossed Cofán territory, subdued part of the Kamëntšá lands and placed a Quechua-speaking population in the Sibundoy valley, the community later known as the Inga. Inca power collapsed after 1533, Spanish expeditions entered Putumayo from 1542, and from 1547 successive Catholic missions administered much of this fragile frontier. Popayán remained its link to Spanish government, but distance, forest and the great river left the Cofán, Kamëntšá, Siona and Witoto communities with room to preserve their own authority. By 1821 the former mission country remained tied to Popayán rather than formed into a compact, closely governed province.
zh:
普图马约河发源于帕斯托斯山结，穿过森林峡谷奔向亚马逊河。1444年，其上游流域分属各个自治族群：西南部是科方人，西北部是卡门查人，中部和南部水道居住着西奥纳人和其他图卡诺语族群，东部则是维托托语族群。漫长的可通航河段让独木舟和贸易往来于河畔社群之间，而印加军队此时尚未越过安第斯山麓。

1492年，印加君主瓦伊纳·卡帕克穿过科方土地，征服卡门查人的部分领地，并在锡本多伊谷地安置一支说克丘亚语的居民，即后来所称的因加人。1533年后印加政权崩溃，西班牙远征队从1542年起进入普图马约，1547年起又由接连而来的天主教传教团管理这条脆弱边疆的大部分事务。波帕扬始终是它与西班牙政府之间的联系节点，但遥远距离、雨林和大河使科方、卡门查、西奥纳和维托托社群仍有空间维持自身权威。到1821年，这片旧日传教地仍依附波帕扬，并未形成一个紧密而受严密治理的行省。

en:
The Chichitames were a desert band of the Bolsón de Mapimí, the closed basin between the sierras of Nueva Vizcaya into which the Nazas flows. They were one of the kindred nomad peoples the Spanish grouped together as Tobosos, hereditary enemies of the lake-dwelling Irritila to their south. They had no fields or towns: they hunted with sling and lance, gathered mesquite and mescal, moved their rancherías between waterholes and raided the richer valleys to the south and west. In 1444 no road entered the bolsón: no Spaniard existed in their world, the silver at Mapimí lay untouched, and the desert answered to no lord.

Antonio de Espejo's expedition crossed the country in 1583 and the Chichitames' Toboso kin simply vanished into the desert. Silver brought the Spaniards in force: on 25 July 1598 Antón Martín de Zapata and the Jesuit Juan Agustín de Espinoza founded Santiago de Mapimí at the foot of the Sierra de la India, whose mines became one of the richest districts of New Spain. Slave-raiding drove the desert bands to war, and they had taken to horses within a generation; Mapimí was swept by risings in 1616-17, 1654-61, 1683-87, 1703-11 and 1715, answered by a presidio and campaigns of extermination. Where twelve bands had been counted in the 1680s, by 1693 only four remained: the Osatayogliglas, Guazapayogliglas, Sisimbles and Chichitames. By 1800 the survivors had dissolved into the mestizo frontier population; in 1811 Hidalgo passed through Mapimí as a prisoner, carried north to Chihuahua to be shot.
zh:
奇奇塔梅斯人是马皮米盆地的一个沙漠游群——这个封闭盆地位于新比斯开的群山之间，纳萨斯河流入其中。他们与几个亲缘游牧族群同被西班牙人归为托博索人，世代与南方湖畔而居的伊里蒂拉人为敌。他们没有田地和城镇：以投石器和长矛狩猎，采集豆灌木和龙舌兰，在水源地之间迁徙营地，不时向南、向西劫掠更富庶的山谷。1444年时没有一条道路通向盆地内部：他们的世界里没有西班牙人，马皮米的银矿还埋在地下，荒漠不奉任何君主。

1583年安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍的探险队穿过此地，奇奇塔梅斯人的托博索同族直接遁入沙漠。是银子把西班牙人成批引来：1598年7月25日，安顿·马丁·德·萨帕塔与耶稣会士胡安·阿古斯丁·德·埃斯皮诺萨在印度山脚下建立圣地亚哥·德·马皮米，这里的矿区后来成为新西班牙最富庶的矿区之一。奴隶猎捕把荒漠各族群逼上战争之路，他们只用一代人的时间就学会了骑马；起义在1616—1617年、1654—1661年、1683—1687年、1703—1711年和1715年反复席卷马皮米，西班牙人则以要塞和剿灭战役回应。1680年代这里还能数出十二个游群，到1693年只剩四个：奥萨塔约格利格拉斯、瓜萨帕约格利格拉斯、西辛布雷斯和奇奇塔梅斯。到1800年，幸存者已融入边境上的混血社会；1811年，伊达尔戈作为囚犯经过马皮米，被押往奇瓦瓦处决。

en:
Between the snowy volcanoes of the Cordillera Central and the hot valley of the upper Magdalena lay the country of the Pijao, a constellation of chiefdoms rather than a state: the Coyaima and Natagaima on the river plains, the mountain communities higher up, all joined in loose federations. They grew the tobacco they called tenú, rolled it into cigars and carried its trade far down the Magdalena, and they had the name of fierce raiders among all their neighbours. In 1444 the Spaniards had not yet arrived, and the valleys of the Saldaña, the Amoya and the Coello belonged entirely to the Pijao.

The conquistadors who pushed in from Mariquita and Neiva met eighty years of guerrilla war. Diego Bocanegra built his Fuerte de Palenque and Santiago de la Frontera in the Amoya country in 1572 and won the alliance of the chief Tala, but he was driven out before long; the Pijao commander Chequera answered every new settlement with raids, and Medina de las Torres, founded at Chaparral in 1586, was destroyed in its turn. The war ended only under Juan de Borja y Armendia, president of the Audiencia of Santafé, who played on the rivalries among the Pijao peoples and, after hard fighting near Chaparral, founded Natagaima on 8 September around 1608, calling it 'the complement of the pacification', and Nuestra Señora del Carmen de Coyaima the same year. The survivors were gathered into resguardos; Coyaima, its foundation formally recorded in 1621, became a market where the produce of the cold highlands met that of the warm valley, and the village was moved to the Saldaña bank in 1778. Natagaima, repeatedly swept by Magdalena floods, was relocated to its final site in 1801.
zh:
在中部山脉的雪峰与马格达莱纳河上游的炎热河谷之间，是皮豪斯（皮哈奥人）的土地。这不是一个国家，而是一串酋邦：平原上有科亚伊马、纳塔盖马等部，更高的山里则是山地诸部，彼此结成松散的联盟。他们种植称作「特努」的烟草，卷成雪茄，把生意一直做到马格达莱纳河下游，在四邻眼中是出名的凶悍劫掠者。1444年，西班牙人尚未到来，萨尔达尼亚河、阿莫亚河和科埃约河的河谷完全属于皮哈奥人。

从马里基塔和内瓦深入的征服者撞上的是一场长达八十年的游击战争。1572年，迭戈·博卡内格拉在阿莫亚一带修建帕伦克堡和圣地亚哥-德拉弗龙特拉堡，争取到酋长塔拉的联盟，后来仍被赶走；皮哈奥统帅切克拉对每一处新据点还以袭击，1586年建于查帕拉尔的梅迪纳-德拉斯托雷斯也被摧毁。战争直到圣菲王家检审庭主席胡安·德·博尔哈·阿门迪亚任内才结束：他利用皮哈奥各部之间的仇隙，在查帕拉尔附近苦战之后，于1608年9月8日前后建立纳塔盖马，称之为「绥靖的收尾」，同年又建立卡门圣母科亚伊马。幸存者被编入保留地；科亚伊马于1621年正式登记定名，成为寒冷高原物产与炎热河谷物产交易的市集，1778年村落迁至萨尔达尼亚河畔。纳塔盖马则屡遭马格达莱纳河洪水冲毁，1801年才迁到今日的位置。

en:
Achaguas takes its name from the Achagua, the most numerous indigenous people of the Orinoco llanos. Until the eighteenth century their villages spread through the Casanare, Meta and Apure basins, forming a trade network in which strings of quiripa shells served as money; later accounts put their population at more than 30,000 on the eve of European contact. In 1444 the wet savannas and river woods around the future town were Achagua country, with no mission or Spanish settlement.

On 4 December 1774 the Capuchin friar Alonso de Castro founded Santa Bárbara de la Isla de los Achaguas, gathering Achagua, Taparita and Otomaco people with three wealthy Spanish families. During the Venezuelan independence wars, these plains saw the clash of Las Queseras del Medio on 2 April 1819, when José Antonio Páez's llanero cavalry met royalist horse. Páez's feigned retreat, sudden countercharge and the cry '¡Vuelvan, caras!' made the action famous in the memory of the llanero war.
zh:
阿查瓜斯得名于阿查瓜人——奥里诺科亚诺斯草原上人数最多的原住民。直到18世纪，他们的村落仍分布在卡萨纳雷河、梅塔河与阿普雷河流域，组成贸易网络，并用成串的基里帕贝壳充当货币；后世记载称，欧洲人到来前夕他们的人口超过三万。1444年，未来城镇周围的湿草原与河边林地属于阿查瓜人的土地，还没有传教站或西班牙人居民点。

1774年12月4日，嘉布遣会修士阿隆索·德·卡斯特罗建立圣巴巴拉·德·拉·伊斯拉·德·洛斯·阿查瓜斯，把阿查瓜人、塔帕里塔人、奥托马科人和三户富裕的西班牙家庭聚居于一处。委内瑞拉独立战争期间，1819年4月2日，何塞·安东尼奥·派斯的亚诺斯骑兵在拉斯克塞拉斯德尔梅迪奥与保王派骑兵交战。派斯佯装撤退后突然反身冲锋，那声「转身！」使这次战斗成为草原战争中的著名记忆。

en:
The valley of the Turbio was known to its villagers as Variquicimeto, the 'ash-coloured river'. In 1444 its maize lands and hunting grounds belonged to the Caquetío and their neighbours the Gayón, Ayamán and Jirajara, Arawakan-speaking peoples who kept up a lively traffic in cotton, salt and dye along the routes from the Caribbean coast to the inland plains. No strangers yet ruled the valley.

Gold at Buría drew the captain Juan de Villegas from El Tocuyo, and in 1552 he founded Nueva Segovia de Buría on the edge of the valley. Unhealthy ground and indigenous attacks drove the settlers in 1556 to a new site at El Carabalí, named Nueva Segovia de Barquisimeto. This was the town the rebel conquistador Lope de Aguirre burned on his march through Venezuela in 1561, and at Barquisimeto his own men turned on him and killed him on 27 October that year. Rebuilt at the meeting of the Turbio and Claro, the town was moved once more to escape harsh winds and settled for good in 1563 on the plateau north of the Turbio, its native name Variquicimeto worn down by Spanish tongues to Barquisimeto. Through the colonial years it served as an agricultural market and road junction between central and western Venezuela. Barquisimeto joined the independence rising of 1811, and its deputy José Ángel Álamo signed the Independence Act on 5 July; patriot and royalist armies fought the battle of Los Horcones nearby in 1813.
zh:
图尔维奥河谷的土著地名叫巴里基西梅托，意为「灰色的河」。1444年，这里的玉米地和猎场属于卡克蒂奥人及其邻族加永人、阿亚曼人和希拉哈拉人，他们都说阿拉瓦克语，沿连接加勒比海岸与内陆平原的道路买卖棉花、盐和染料，往来兴旺。此时还没有外来者统治这片谷地。

布里亚的金矿把西班牙队长胡安·德·维列加斯从埃尔托库约引来，1552年他在谷地边缘建起「布里亚的新塞戈维亚」。水土恶劣加上土著袭击，迫使殖民者1556年迁到埃尔卡拉瓦利新址，改名「巴里基西梅托的新塞戈维亚」。1561年，起兵反叛西班牙国王的征服者洛普·德·阿基尔在转战委内瑞拉途中烧毁此城，同年10月27日，他在巴基西梅托被自己的部下杀死。城镇在图尔维奥河与克拉罗河汇流处重建，又因风害再次迁址，1563年终于在图尔维奥河北岸的台地定居下来，土著地名巴里基西梅托也在西班牙人口中讹变为巴基西梅托。整个殖民时期，这里是连接委内瑞拉中部与西部的农业集镇和道路枢纽。1811年巴基西梅托加入独立起义，代表何塞·安赫尔·阿拉莫在7月5日签署独立法案；1813年爱国军与保王军又在城外接战，是为洛斯奥尔科内斯之战。

en:
The forested folds of the Serranía del Perijá, whose eastern streams run down to the Catatumbo and Lake Maracaibo, were the land of the Yukpa, a Carib-speaking people who lived in autonomous clan villages high above the hot plains, clearing maize and manioc fields on the mountain flanks and hunting in the cloud forest. Spanish settlers later called them Motilones, 'the shaved heads', a name they shared loosely with the Barí beyond the ridges. In 1444 no road or tribute reached these valleys: the Yukpa held their mountains on their own terms.

That independence held for nearly three centuries. Spanish expeditions probed the mountains for gold and captives but won no lasting foothold, and the first Spanish town below the sierra, Concepción, founded at the Palmar's mouth in 1717, was destroyed by its indigenous neighbours three years later. Juan de Chourio, a Navarrese holding a royal licence of 1722, brought Canary Islander and Maracaibo settler families into the foothills and from 1724 built La Villa de Perijá on the Palmar, moving it in 1729 to the healthier site it still occupies. The Motilones burned Concepción again in 1752, and it was rebuilt for the last time that same year. Capuchin missionaries and cattle ranches then crept up the valleys, but even in 1821 the high sierra remained Yukpa country.
zh:
佩里哈山林木幽深，东坡的溪流向东汇入卡塔通博河与马拉开波湖，这里是尤克帕人的家园。他们说加勒比语，在炎热平原之上的高山中以氏族聚村而居，在山坡上刀耕火种玉米和木薯，在云雾林里狩猎。后来的西班牙移民称他们为莫蒂隆人，意为「剃光头的人」，山那边的巴里人也被笼统地叫这个名字。1444年，没有道路和赋税能伸进这些山谷：尤克帕人完全按自己的方式据守着大山。

这份独立维持了近三百年。西班牙远征队为寻找黄金、掳掠人口多次进山，却始终没能站住脚；山脚下第一座西班牙城镇康塞普西翁1717年建于帕尔马河口，三年后便被邻近的土著摧毁。1722年，纳瓦拉人胡安·德·乔里奥取得王室特许，带着加那利群岛和马拉开波的移民家庭进入山麓，1724年起在帕尔马河畔建起佩里哈镇，1729年又迁至更宜居住的现址。1752年莫蒂隆人再次焚毁康塞普西翁，该镇同年最后一次重建。此后嘉布遣会传教士和牧牛场才慢慢沿山谷推进，但直到1821年，高山之上仍是尤克帕人的地盘。

en:
Wayuu lies toward the southeastern shore of Lake Maracaibo, where the lowlands meet the Venezuelan Andes. In 1444 indigenous communities lived around the southern lake, fishing, hunting and gathering; peoples of Arawakan and Cariban origins inhabited the region. European settlements had not yet appeared on its shores.

In 1592 Gonzalo Piña Ludueña established Gibraltar on the lake shore. It became Mérida's chief lake port and a gathering point for cacao shipped to Spain and other colonies. Jesuits helped develop the crop, while enslaved Africans worked in the Gibraltar area. The port's prosperity drew pirates: Henry Morgan plundered it in 1669, and Michel de Grammont raided it in 1678 before advancing inland toward Trujillo. Repeated attacks had brought Gibraltar close to ruin by 1680.
zh:
瓦尤位于马拉开波湖东南岸一带，低地在这里与委内瑞拉安第斯山麓相接。1444年，湖的南部住着土著社群，以捕鱼、狩猎和采集为生；这里的居民有阿拉瓦克和加勒比等不同渊源。欧洲人的定居点尚未出现在湖岸。

1592年，贡萨洛·皮尼亚·卢杜埃尼亚在湖岸建立直布罗陀镇。它成为梅里达的主要湖港，也是可可运往西班牙和其他殖民地的集散地。耶稣会士帮助发展可可种植，被奴役的非洲人在直布罗陀一带劳动。港口的繁荣招来海盗：亨利·摩根1669年洗劫此地，米歇尔·德·格拉蒙1678年袭击港口后又向内陆的特鲁希略进发。到1680年，接连的袭击已使直布罗陀濒临荒废。

en:
At the heart of north-central Venezuela lies the broad basin of Lake Tacarigua, later Lake Valencia, ringed by the coastal cordillera and the hot lowlands that run down to the Llanos. In 1444 its shores were farmed by the Tacarigua and other Arawak peoples, who grew maize and cotton, fished the reed-fringed water and built their villages on artificial mounds against the lake's floods; no European had yet reached the valley.

Spanish settlers had first established themselves at the nearby cove of Borburata, but repeated corsair sacks drove them inland, and on 25 March 1555 Captain Alonso Díaz Moreno founded Nueva Valencia del Rey on the lakeshore. The encomienda brought the lake villages under Spanish control, and the region supplied wheat, cattle and cotton to the coast. In 1561 the rebel conquistador Lope de Aguirre descended on the young town in his flight from Peru, and in 1677 French raiders burned its cabildo and the early records of the province. When Alexander von Humboldt reached the lake in 1800 he found Valencia a town of six or seven thousand people and recorded how the clearing of its shores was lowering the water. Valencia stood at the centre of the independence wars: the revolutionary congress met there in 1812 before royalist troops retook the province, and in 1814 the royalists of José Tomás Boves took and sacked the town after a long siege. On 24 June 1821 Bolívar won the Battle of Carabobo on the plain west of the lake, sealing Venezuela's independence.
zh:
委内瑞拉中北部腹地是塔卡里瓜湖（后称巴伦西亚湖）的宽阔湖盆，四周环绕着海岸山脉和伸向亚诺斯草原的炎热低地。1444年，湖畔的土地由塔卡里瓜人和其他阿拉瓦克部族耕作：他们种植玉米和棉花，在芦苇丛生的湖面捕鱼，把房屋建在人工土台上以避湖水泛滥；这时还没有欧洲人进入谷地。

西班牙移民最初落脚在附近的博尔布拉塔海湾，但海盗的反复洗劫迫使他们内迁。1555年3月25日，阿隆索·迪亚斯·莫雷诺上尉在湖畔建起新巴伦西亚德尔雷伊。委托监护制把湖畔的村落置于西班牙移民的控制之下，这一带向沿海输送小麦、牲畜和棉花。1561年，反叛的征服者洛佩·德·阿吉雷在逃离秘鲁途中闯入这座年轻的城镇；1677年，法国海盗烧毁了市政厅和全省的早期档案。1800年亚历山大·冯·洪堡来到湖边时，巴伦西亚已有六七千居民，他记录了湖畔伐林如何使湖面下降。独立战争中巴伦西亚处在旋涡中心：1812年革命议会曾在此开会，保王军旋即重新夺占全省；1814年，何塞·托马斯·博韦斯的保王部队经长期围困攻陷并洗劫了这座城市。1821年6月24日，玻利瓦尔在湖西平原赢得卡拉博博战役，奠定了委内瑞拉的独立。

en:
The Guanaguanare country lies where the south-western Llanos meet the Andean piedmont, between the Portuguesa and Guanare rivers. In 1444, Cuiba, Caquetío and Guamo communities farmed, fished and gathered across the savanna; their mounds and causeways probably served as flood refuges, drainage works or burial places. The Cospes later held the wooded country north of the future town, and the indigenous name Guanaguanare was explained as 'place of seagulls' or 'land between rivers'. No Spanish town yet occupied the valley.

Nikolaus Federmann and Georg von Speyer crossed these plains for the Welser company in 1534, and Philipp von Hutten was wounded here by Omagua defenders in 1542. On 3 November 1591 the Portuguese captain Juan Fernández de León founded Espíritu Santo del Valle de Guanaguanare, later shortened to Guanare, and cattle ranches and farms spread around the new town. Local tradition placed appearances of the Virgin to the Cospes chief Coromoto in the nearby woods in 1651 and 1652, and Catholic missionaries began work around Guanare and Acarigua in 1657. During the Second Republic, Simón Bolívar concentrated his troops nearby and at the Battle of Araure on 5 December 1813 defeated José Ceballos's larger royalist army, taking four standards and numerous guns while more than five hundred royalist cavalrymen were killed.
zh:
瓜纳瓜纳雷位于西南草原与安第斯山麓交会处，地处波图格萨河与瓜纳雷河之间。1444年，奎瓦人、卡克蒂奥人和瓜莫人等族群在稀树草原农耕、渔猎和采集；他们留下的土墩与堤道可能用于洪水期避难、排水或安葬。后来城镇北侧的林地由科斯佩人控制，印第安语地名瓜纳瓜纳雷被解释为「海鸥之地」或「两河之间的土地」。当时山谷中还没有西班牙城镇。

1534年，尼古劳斯·费德曼和格奥尔格·冯·施派尔代表韦尔塞公司穿过这片平原；1542年，菲利普·冯·胡滕在此遭奥马瓜人阻击并受伤。1591年11月3日，葡萄牙籍上尉胡安·费尔南德斯·德·莱昂建立埃斯皮里图·桑托·德尔巴列·德·瓜纳瓜纳雷，后来简称瓜纳雷，牧牛场和农田随即在城镇周围扩展。当地传统称，圣母在1651年和1652年向附近林地中的科斯佩酋长科罗莫托显现；1657年，天主教传教士开始到瓜纳雷和阿卡里瓜一带传教。第二共和国期间，西蒙·玻利瓦尔在附近集结军队，于1813年12月5日的阿劳雷战役击败何塞·塞瓦略斯兵力更强的保王军，缴获四面军旗和多门火炮，击毙五百余名保王骑兵。

en:
Tuneo is the mountain gateway from the Llanos to the Sierra Nevada del Cocuy, where cloud forests and the valleys of the Cobaría and Arauca rise from the eastern plains. In 1444 the Tunebo, who call themselves U'wa and speak a Chibchan language, held these ridges and forested slopes, moving between highland farms, hunting grounds and river crossings. Their kinship and trade networks linked the Cocuy massif with the plains, while the steep country kept the richer Muisca lands around Tunja at a distance.

Nicolás Federmann and Georg von Speyer crossed the eastern cordillera into Arauca in 1536. Later gold-seeking expeditions under Hernán Pérez de Quesada pushed toward Güicán, and many Tunebo and related Güicán families withdrew behind the Sierra Nevada rather than submit. Jesuit missionaries reached Guahibo, Airico, Chiricoa and Tunebo lands in 1659, and in 1756 the Jesuit Miguel Blasco founded the reduction of Güicán on the western side of the massif; it had 310 people in 1764. After the Jesuit expulsion of 1767, Augustinian Recollects took over the plains missions and founded San Fernando de Arauca. The Comunero movement found support at Tame in 1781, and Güicán declared independence from Spain on 24 February 1814. Bolívar entered Arauca on 4 June 1819, reached Tame on 11 June, and after Santander's forces joined the march crossed the Andes by way of the Pantano de Vargas to victory at Boyacá.
zh:
图内奥是从东部草原登上科库伊雪山的山口地带，科瓦里亚河与阿劳卡河的河谷从云雾林升入安第斯山。1444年，自称乌瓦人的图内博人占据这些山脊和林坡；他们使用奇布查语，在高地农田、猎场和渡口之间往来，亲属与贸易网络连接科库伊山地和东部平原，险峻地形也使他们同通哈一带富庶的穆伊斯卡土地保持距离。

1536年，尼古劳斯·费德曼和格奥尔格·冯·施派尔越过东科迪勒拉山进入阿劳卡。后来埃尔南·佩雷斯·德·克萨达为寻找黄金进军圭坎，许多图内博人和亲缘相近的圭坎人退到雪山另一侧，拒绝臣服。1659年，耶稣会传教士进入瓜希博人、艾里科人、奇里科阿人和图内博人的土地；1756年，耶稣会士米格尔·布拉斯科在山地西侧建立圭坎归化村，1764年村中有310人。1767年耶稣会被逐后，重整奥斯定会会士接替草原传教，并建立阿劳卡的圣费尔南多。1781年公社者运动在塔梅得到响应；1814年2月24日，圭坎宣布脱离西班牙独立。1819年6月4日玻利瓦尔进入阿劳卡，6月11日抵达塔梅，随后同弗朗西斯科·德·保拉·桑坦德尔的部队会师，经巴尔加斯沼泽翻越安第斯，在博亚卡取胜。

en: Guanipa covers part of the great tableland south of the Unare plains, where the Guanipa River begins a roughly 340-kilometre course through dense swamps to the Gulf of Paria beside the Orinoco delta. In 1444 the open mesas, streams and gallery groves were Kali'na country; later local memory named the land after Guanipa, a Carib-speaking cacique said to have led his people on the mesas above the Orinoco. Christopher Columbus's third voyage documented the nearby river mouth on 1 August 1498. In 1717 the Píritu missions commissioner Cristóbal de Molina proposed two Spanish towns on the Tigre River in Guanipa, where foreign smugglers traded with Caribs and other indigenous peoples and taught them to use firearms.
zh: 瓜尼帕位于乌纳雷平原以南的广阔台原上，瓜尼帕河从这里发源，流经约340公里的密林沼泽，在奥里诺科三角洲旁注入帕里亚湾。1444年，开阔台原、河道与林带属于卡利纳人的活动范围；后来的地方记忆以瓜尼帕命名这片土地，据说他是一位讲加勒比语的酋长，统领奥里诺科河上方台原的族人。1498年8月1日，克里斯托弗·哥伦布第三次航行记录了附近的奥里诺科河口。1717年，皮里图传教区专员克里斯托瓦尔·德·莫利纳提议在瓜尼帕的蒂格雷河畔建立两座西班牙城镇：外国走私者在此与加勒比人及其他原住民交易，并教他们使用火器。

en:
The hot coastal plain between the Unare River and the Guanipa plateau, backed by the low country that runs to the Orinoco, belonged in 1444 to a mosaic of Cariban peoples: the Cumanagoto held the Neverí valley and the shore, while the Píritu, Chacopata and Palenque lived among the Unare lagoons, farming and fishing and growing maize and cotton. Their first sight of Europeans came in 1499, when pearl-seekers from Cubagua began landing below the Maracapana hill to provision their boats.

The first Spanish town, San Cristóbal de la Nueva Écija, was founded in 1586 after Captain Cristóbal Cobos defeated the cacique Cayaurima, yet the Cumanagoto fought on for more than sixty years. Joan Orpí, charged with their conquest, founded Nueva Barcelona del Cerro Santo in 1638, and in 1671 Governor Sancho Fernández de Angulo moved the settlement two kilometres south and refounded it as Barcelona. Cattle ranches, cotton and sugar spread through its district, served by the missions founded at Clarines in 1594 and Píritu in 1656. Barcelona's junta proclaimed the province independent on 27 April 1810. The cause nearly died here: on 17 August 1814 royalist forces with 8,000 men routed Bolívar's 3,000 republicans at Aragua de Barcelona, and on 7 April 1817 they stormed the Casa Fuerte, the old Franciscan convent where the garrison and townspeople had taken shelter, putting its defenders and refugees to the sword.
zh:
安索阿特吉位于乌纳雷河与瓜尼帕台地之间，炎热的沿海平原背后是通向奥里诺科河的低地。1444年，这里是一片加勒比语族部族的拼图：库马纳戈托人据有内韦里河谷和海岸，皮里图人、查科帕塔人和帕伦克人则散居在乌纳雷河的潟湖之间，以耕作捕鱼为生，种植玉米和棉花。他们第一次见到欧洲人是在1499年，从库瓦瓜岛来的采珠人开始在马拉卡帕纳山下登岸，为船队补给。

1586年，克里斯托瓦尔·科沃斯上尉击败酋长卡尧里马之后建立了第一座西班牙城镇圣克里斯托瓦尔-德拉新埃西哈，但库马纳戈托人的抵抗又持续了六十多年。受命征服此地的霍安·奥尔皮于1638年建立圣山新巴塞罗那；1671年，省长桑乔·费尔南德斯·德·安古洛把居民点南移两公里，重建为巴塞罗那。辖区内牧牛场、棉花和甘蔗次第铺开，克拉里内斯和皮里图的传教站分别于1594年和1656年设立。1810年4月27日，巴塞罗那的执政委员会宣布本省独立。但独立事业在这里几近覆灭：1814年8月17日，八千人的保王军在阿拉瓜-德巴塞罗那击溃玻利瓦尔仅三千人的共和军；1817年4月7日，保王军又攻破卡萨富埃特——那座被守军和市民当作避难所的旧方济各会修道院，屠戮了里面的守军与难民。

en:
Guaju is the deep forest between the upper Orinoco and the Rio Branco, a country of blackwater rivers and the flat-topped Duida and Parima heights. Its wonder is the Casiquiare, a natural arm that breaks from the upper Orinoco below the Duida and winds more than 300 kilometres south into the Rio Negro, carrying Orinoco water into the Amazon — the only waterway on earth joining two river systems on this scale. In 1444 Arawak-speaking peoples, the Baré and Baniva among them, farmed and fished along the Casiquiare and the Guainía, while Ye'kuana villages held the Ventuari and its rapids; their canoes had long used the canal and the Pimichín portage to pass between the two river worlds. No European had yet seen any of it.

Word of the canal reached Europe through the Jesuit Manuel Román: in 1744, at La Esmeralda, he met Portuguese slavers who had come up from the Rio Negro and accompanied them through the waterway, the first recorded passage, and La Condamine carried the report to the Académie française. The Royal Orinoco Expedition confirmed it in 1755, and Spain set out to hold the country. In 1758 Sergeant Francisco Fernández de Bobadilla found cacao groves on the Ocamo and Padamo, and the next year work began on the fort of Buena Guardia at the Casiquiare's mouth. From 1760 Ensign Apolinar Díez de la Fuente and the friar José Antonio Jerez de los Caballeros gathered Ye'kuana families into a new town, officially founded in 1767 as San Francisco de la Esmeralda, named for an emerald supposedly found beneath Cerro Duida; that same year they pushed up the Orinoco to its source, still searching for Lake Parime and the golden city of Manoa. A native rising in 1776 wrecked the planned road from La Esmeralda to Angostura. In 1800 Humboldt and Bonpland navigated the Casiquiare and fixed its geography, yet Spanish power never reached beyond a handful of forest posts, and in 1821 the interior remained the rivers and villages of its native peoples.
zh:
瓜胡地处上奥里诺科河与里奥布朗库河之间的密林深处，到处是黑水河与杜伊达、帕里马等平顶山。这里的奇观是卡西基亚雷河：它从上奥里诺科河分出一支天然汊流，在杜伊达峰脚下蜿蜒三百多公里向南注入内格罗河，把奥里诺科河的水送入亚马孙河——世界上唯一以此规模连通两大水系的天然河道。1444年，说阿拉瓦克语的巴雷人、巴尼瓦人在卡西基亚雷河与瓜伊尼亚河沿岸耕渔为生，叶库纳人的村落据守着本图阿里河及其急流；他们的独木舟早就借由这条水道和皮米钦陆运道，往来于两个大河世界之间。这时还没有任何欧洲人到过此地。

水道的消息由耶稣会士曼努埃尔·罗曼带到外界：1744年，他在拉埃斯梅拉达遇到从内格罗河上来的葡萄牙奴隶贩子，并随他们穿过卡西基亚雷河，这是有记载的首次欧洲人通行，拉孔达明随后把报告带到法兰西科学院。1755年，皇家奥里诺科远征队正式证实了这条水道，西班牙随即着手控制这片土地。1758年，弗朗西斯科·费尔南德斯·德·博瓦迪利亚军士在奥卡莫河与帕达莫河一带发现可可林，次年又在卡西基亚雷河口动工修建布埃纳瓜迪亚要塞。1760年起，少尉阿波利纳尔·迭斯·德拉富恩特与修士何塞·安东尼奥·赫雷斯·德洛斯卡瓦列罗斯把叶库纳人迁入一座新城，1767年正式定名为圣弗朗西斯科·德拉埃斯梅拉达，名字取自据说在杜伊达山下发现的一颗祖母绿；同年，他们还溯奥里诺科河直抵源头，仍在寻找帕里梅湖和金城马诺阿。1776年的一次原住民起事使拉埃斯梅拉达通往安戈斯图拉的道路工程功亏一篑。1800年，洪堡与邦普朗航行穿越卡西基亚雷河，勘定了它的地理，但西班牙的势力始终只及密林里的寥寥几处据点，直到1821年，内陆仍属于原住民的河流与村落。

en:
The bay and river mouths that later became Jacmel were Yaquimo, a Taíno coastal district on the eastern side of Hispaniola's Tiburon Peninsula. The Caribbean shore and steep hinterland supported fishing villages, cassava fields and canoe traffic, and Spanish accounts later placed the district in Jaragua, the chiefdom ruled at contact by Bohechío; they remembered Zui and Yáquimo as Jaragua's two constituent parts. In 1444 local caciques still governed the land around the bay, untouched by European conquest.

Spanish settlers founded a town at Yaquimo in 1504, but after the Devastations of Osorio in 1605 Spain broke up the old western settlements and the coast was largely emptied. The Compagnie de Saint-Domingue established a small French town at the river mouth in 1698; metropolitan authorities designated it a colonial town in 1720, and coffee introduction in 1770 brought new trade. Sugar and coffee enriched the planters through enslaved labour. In 1791 and 1792 Romaine-la-Prophétesse led some 13,000 rebels who occupied and burned Jacmel, raided plantations from Marigot to Bainet and freed enslaved people. During the War of the South, Alexandre Pétion defended the port until Toussaint Louverture's forces took it in 1800. On 12 March 1806 Francisco de Miranda unfurled at Jacmel the first flag of Venezuela, later the model for Gran Colombia's colours.
zh:
后来成为雅克梅勒的海湾和河口地带，原是泰诺人的沿海地区亚基莫，位于伊斯帕尼奥拉岛蒂伯朗半岛东侧。加勒比海岸与陡峭腹地分布着渔村、木薯地和独木舟往来路线。后来的西班牙记载把这一地区归入欧洲人到来时由博埃奇奥统治的哈拉瓜酋长国，并称祖伊和亚基莫是哈拉瓜的两个组成部分。1444年，地方酋长仍统治着海湾周围的土地，欧洲征服尚未到来。

1504年，西班牙殖民者在亚基莫建立城镇；但1605年奥索里奥荒毁政策后，西班牙拆散西部旧居民点，这片海岸大体空虚。1698年，圣多明各公司在河口建立一座法国小镇，1720年法国本土当局将其定为殖民城镇，1770年引入咖啡后贸易有所发展。蔗糖和咖啡依靠被奴役劳工为种植园主创造财富。1791年至1792年，罗曼·拉·普罗费特斯率领约一万三千名起义者占领并焚毁雅克梅勒，袭击从马里戈特到拜内的种植园，解放被奴役者。南方战争期间，亚历山大·佩蒂翁防守这座港口，直到杜桑·卢维杜尔的军队在1800年攻占它。1806年3月12日，弗朗西斯科·德·米兰达在雅克梅勒升起委内瑞拉第一面旗帜，其配色后来成为大哥伦比亚旗帜的原型。

en:
Marien was the north-westernmost of the five Taíno chiefdoms of Hispaniola, facing the Atlantic and the Windward Passage, with Tortuga offshore and borders with Maguá, Maguana and Jaragua. Its chief town, El Guarico, stood near the later Cap-Français, and fourteen nitaínos administered its villages and northern plains. In 1444 Taíno caciques still controlled these shores, river valleys and farmlands; the ruler encountered at Columbus's arrival, Guacanagaríx, belonged to this same northern chiefly seat.

At Christmas 1492 the Santa María was wrecked off this coast; Guacanagaríx allowed Columbus to build La Navidad from the ship's timbers, but the fort had been destroyed by a rival force before Columbus returned. Spain founded Puerto Real nearby in 1503, moved the settlement to Bayajá in 1578, and evacuated the northern towns during the Osorio devastations after 1605, opening the coast to buccaneers. French settlers under Bertrand d'Ogeron founded Cap-Français in 1670; formally established in 1711, it served as capital of Saint-Domingue until 1770 and by 1790 held 15,000 people, two-thirds of them enslaved. On 14 August 1791 enslaved delegates gathered at Bois Caïman, and the great rising swept the northern plantations days later. On 18 November 1803 Jean-Jacques Dessalines defeated Rochambeau at Vertières below Cap-Français, and Haiti proclaimed independence on 1 January 1804. Henri Christophe made the north a separate state in 1807 and a kingdom in 1811, renaming the city Cap-Henri and raising the Citadelle Laferrière above Milot; his death in 1820 ended the northern monarchy.
zh:
马里安（Marién，也译马列恩）是伊斯帕尼奥拉岛五大泰诺酋长国之一，位于岛屿西北，北临大西洋，外海有托尔图加岛，西临向风海峡，东接马瓜和马瓜纳，南连哈拉瓜。首府埃尔瓜里科位于后来的法兰西角附近，酋邦分为十四个小区。1444年，泰诺酋长仍统治着这些海岸、河谷和农田；哥伦布到来时遇到的统治者瓜卡纳加里克斯，便出自这一北方酋邦。

1492年圣诞节，圣玛利亚号在附近海岸失事；瓜卡纳加里克斯允许哥伦布用船木修建纳维达德堡，但哥伦布返回前，堡垒已被敌对势力摧毁。1503年，西班牙人在这一带建立雷亚尔港，1578年又将居民点迁往巴亚哈；1605年后的奥索里奥荒毁政策撤空北岸城镇，给了布坎尼尔海盗可乘之机。1670年，贝特朗·多热龙率领的法国移民建立法兰西角，1711年正式设城；1770年前这里是法属圣多明各首府，到1790年已有一万五千人，其中三分之二是奴隶。1791年8月14日，奴隶代表在凯门森林集会，北部种植园数日后爆发大起义。1803年11月18日，让-雅克·德萨林在法兰西角以南的韦尔蒂埃尔击败罗尚博，海地随后于1804年1月1日宣布独立。亨利·克里斯托夫1807年在北方建立分立政权，1811年将其改为王国，把法兰西角改名亨利角，并在米洛上方修建拉费里埃城堡；他1820年去世后，北方君主制告终。

en:
The wooded Samaná Peninsula, the coast around Nagua and the mouth of the Yuna were the country of the Ciguayos. They spoke a language distinct from Taíno, carried bows and arrows, and are described as hunter-gatherers who made no pottery. Taíno expansion had pushed them into this northeastern corner and brought them within the chiefdom of Maguá, but in 1444 their villages still controlled the hills and shores around Samaná Bay.

On 13 January 1493 Columbus's landing party met Ciguayo archers on the shore later called Rincón Beach. When the islanders refused to trade their weapons, a clash left two of them wounded, and Columbus named the anchorage the Gulf of Arrows. The Spanish made little permanent use of the bay for generations, which left it open to runaways and privateers. When Guarionex fled from Maguá to the Ciguayos, their chief Mayobanex refused Bartholomew Columbus's demand to surrender him and was captured together with the fugitive cacique. Permanent Spanish settlement came only in 1756, when Governor Francisco Rubio y Peñaranda sent Canary Islander families to found Santa Bárbara de Samaná and Sabana de la Mar. The colony passed to France under the Peace of Basel, and in 1807 a British naval raid seized Samaná and turned it over to Spanish creoles fighting the French.
zh:
林木覆盖的萨马纳半岛、纳瓜一带海岸和尤纳河口，是锡瓜约人的土地。他们使用与泰诺语不同的语言，携带弓箭，被记载为不制作陶器的狩猎采集者。泰诺人的扩张把他们挤压到岛的东北一隅，并使他们落入马瓜酋长领地的势力范围；但在1444年，他们的村落仍控制着萨马纳湾周围的山丘与海岸。

1493年1月13日，哥伦布的登陆队在后来称林孔海滩的岸边遇到锡瓜约弓箭手。岛民拒绝交换武器，随后冲突中有两人受伤，哥伦布便把这片锚地命名为箭头湾。此后数代西班牙人都没有在此长期定居，使这里成为逃亡者和私掠船出没之地。瓜里奥内克斯从马瓜逃到锡瓜约人那里时，其首领马约瓦内克斯拒绝巴尔托洛梅·哥伦布交人的要求，最终和这位逃亡首领一同被俘。永久性的西班牙殖民点直到1756年才出现：弗朗西斯科·鲁维奥-佩纳兰达总督派加那利群岛移民家庭建立圣巴巴拉-德萨马纳和滨海萨瓦纳。根据《巴塞尔和约》，殖民地转入法国之手；1807年，一支英国海军舰队袭取萨马纳，并把它交给对抗法国的西班牙裔克里奥尔人。

en:
Higüey was the easternmost Taíno chiefdom of Hispaniola, its 21 nitaínos stretching from the Haina River toward Cape Engaño, Saona Island and the Mona Passage. Its principal village stood on the Yuma River, where the Spanish town of Salvaleón de Higüey later developed. Sources from the contact period name the caciques Cayacoa and Cotubanamá and the female ruler Higuanamá, but in 1444 these eastern plains, forests and canoe crossings still formed an independent Taíno world on the island's sunrise edge.

War began after dogs from a Spanish hunting party killed a local chief on Saona and Cotubanamá's followers killed eight Spaniards in reprisal. In 1503 Governor Nicolás de Ovando sent Juan de Esquivel with hundreds of soldiers, including Bartolomé de las Casas. Cotubanamá made peace and exchanged names with Esquivel in the Taíno guatiao ceremony, but he later attacked the Spanish fort; only one of its nine garrison soldiers survived. In the eight or nine months of war that followed, Juan López tracked Cotubanamá to a cave on Saona and captured him, and the cacique was taken in chains to Santo Domingo and hanged in 1504. The defeated Taínos were forced into plantation labor, and African slaves were imported as their population collapsed. Higüey received a royal privilege and coat of arms on 7 December 1508; its Spanish settlement grew around Juan Ponce de León's holding at Yuma and may have moved to its later site around 1522. Sugar cane, ginger, cacao and cattle became its colonial mainstays. The 1795 Peace of Basel transferred Santo Domingo to France, Toussaint Louverture occupied the east in 1801, Spanish rule returned in 1809, and in 1821 Higüey was drawn into the short-lived Republic of Spanish Haiti.
zh:
伊圭是伊斯帕尼奥拉岛最东端的泰诺酋长领地，下辖21个尼塔伊诺辖区，疆域从艾纳河延伸至恩加尼奥角、绍纳岛和莫纳海峡。主要村落位于尤马河畔，后来的西班牙城镇萨尔瓦莱昂-德伊圭便在此发展。接触时代的资料提到卡亚科阿、科图瓦纳马等首领以及女统治者伊瓜纳马；但在1444年，东部平原、森林和独木舟航道仍是岛的日出之端一个独立的泰诺世界。

战争起因于一支西班牙狩猎队的猎犬在绍纳咬死一名当地首领，科图瓦纳马的追随者随后报复，杀死八名西班牙人。1503年，总督尼古拉斯·德·奥万多派胡安·德·埃斯基维尔率领数百名士兵前来，巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯也在军中。科图瓦纳马起初议和，并按泰诺人的瓜蒂奥仪式与埃斯基维尔交换名字；但他后来进攻西班牙要塞，九名守军中只有一人生还。随后的战争持续八九个月，胡安·洛佩斯在绍纳岛的一个洞穴中追获科图瓦纳马，将他锁送圣多明各，并于1504年处以绞刑。战败的泰诺人被迫从事种植园劳役，随着人口锐减，非洲奴隶被输入岛上。1508年12月7日，伊圭获得王室特权和纹章；西班牙人的定居点围绕胡安·庞塞·德·莱昂在尤马的地产发展，约1522年可能迁至后来的城址。甘蔗、生姜、可可和牛只成为殖民时代的主要物产。1795年《巴塞尔和约》将圣多明各移交法国，杜桑·卢维杜尔1801年占领东部，1809年西班牙恢复统治；1821年，伊圭被卷入短命的西班牙海地共和国。

en:
East of Havana the Bay of Matanzas bites deep into Cuba's north coast, where the Yumurí, San Juan and Canímar rivers come down to the sea. Fishing peoples had camped at the mouth of the Canímar since the most ancient times, and in 1444 Taíno villages farmed the river valleys and paddled the wide, quiet bay in canoes.

Columbus sighted the southern coast of this district on his second voyage in 1494, and Sebastián de Ocampo surveyed these shores during his circumnavigation of Cuba in 1508. In 1510, before the conquest of the island had begun, a party of Spaniards persuaded native fishermen to ferry them across a river without boats; midstream the fishermen overturned the canoes, and the armored Spaniards drowned, giving the place its name of Matanzas, the slaughter, one of the first acts of indigenous resistance in Cuba. Between 1514 and 1518 the Spanish established the Indian pueblo of Canímar on the eastern edge of the bay. Long without a Spanish town, the anchorage became a haunt of smugglers and corsairs until a royal order of 25 September 1690 brought thirty families from the Canary Islands; San Carlos y San Severino de Matanzas was founded in October 1693, guarded by the Castillo de San Severino, with its cabildo meeting from 1695. Sugar then transformed the district: by 1792 the town held some 1,900 slaves, nearly a third of its people, and by 1817 more than 10,000, close to half the population, making Matanzas one of the richest sugar regions of Cuba.
zh:
哈瓦那以东，马坦萨斯湾深深切入古巴北海岸，尤穆里河、圣胡安河和卡尼马尔河在这里入海。远古时代便有渔猎部族在卡尼马尔河口栖居；1444年，泰诺人的村落耕种河谷，划着独木舟往来于宽阔平静的海湾。

哥伦布1494年第二次航行时曾望见这一地区的南岸，1508年塞瓦斯蒂安·奥坎波环航古巴时首次勘察了这里的海岸。1510年，征服古巴的战事尚未开始，一队无船可用的西班牙人让当地渔民渡他们过河，行至中流渔民掀翻独木舟，身披重甲的西班牙人溺水而亡，此地由此得名「马坦萨斯」，意为杀戮，这也是古巴最早的原住民反抗行动之一。1514至1518年间，西班牙人在海湾东岸设立了原住民村镇卡尼马尔。此后海湾旁长期没有西班牙城镇，锚地成了走私者和海盗的出没之地，直到1690年9月25日王室下令从加那利群岛迁来三十户人家；1693年10月，圣卡洛斯和圣塞韦里诺·德·马坦萨斯建城，由圣塞韦里诺城堡戍卫，市政会自1695年起运作。蔗糖随即改变了这片地区：到1792年，城中约有一千九百名奴隶、接近人口的三分之一；到1817年奴隶已超过一万人、将近居民半数，马坦萨斯由此成为古巴最富庶的蔗糖产区之一。

en:
The Escambray, called Guamuhaya in the Taíno tongue, is the mountain knot of central Cuba, forested ridges rising from the south coast to the 1,140-metre Pico San Juan. In 1444 Taíno villages kept conucos in the foothills and fished the coves of Jagua Bay, a wide sound joined to the Caribbean by a narrow mouth; the valleys belonged entirely to them, and no European had yet seen the range.

Early in 1514 Diego Velázquez founded the Villa de la Santísima Trinidad at the foot of the mountains, the third Spanish town in Cuba. Hernán Cortés recruited men there and sailed from its harbor in 1518 on his way to Mexico, and in 1527 Pánfilo de Narváez's Florida expedition lost two ships to a hurricane off the town. For two centuries Trinidad lived on cattle and small farms while Jagua Bay became a pirates' refuge and smuggling anchorage; the Castillo de Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles de Jagua was raised to close its mouth and was finished in 1742. From the late eighteenth century sugar spread through the valleys below the sierra, the future Valle de los Ingenios, worked by a fast-growing slave population. On 22 April 1819 French settlers led by Luis de Clouet founded Fernandina de Jagua on the great bay, the town later renamed Cienfuegos, and it was as prosperous sugar country that the Escambray region entered the year 1821.
zh:
埃斯坎夫雷山，泰诺语称瓜穆哈亚，是古巴中部的山岳枢纽，林木覆盖的山岭从南海岸隆起，最高峰圣胡安峰海拔1140米。1444年，泰诺人的村落在山麓经营田园，在哈瓜湾的小湾里捕鱼——哈瓜湾是一道由狭窄水口通向加勒比海的宽阔潟湖；这些山谷完全属于他们，欧洲人还不曾见过这片群山。

1514年初，迭戈·贝拉斯克斯在山脚下建立至圣特里尼达镇，这是西班牙人在古巴的第三座城镇。1518年，埃尔南·科尔特斯在此招募人手并从港中出航，踏上远征墨西哥之路；1527年，潘菲洛·德·纳尔瓦埃斯的佛罗里达探险队在城外遭遇飓风，损失两艘船。此后两个世纪，特立尼达靠畜牧和小农为生，哈瓜湾却成了海盗的避风港与走私锚地；为封锁湾口，天使圣母哈瓜城堡动工兴建，于1742年建成。18世纪末起，甘蔗沿着山麓谷地扩散，那便是后来的因赫尼奥斯谷，在迅速增长的奴隶劳作下成为富庶之地。1819年4月22日，路易斯·德·克卢埃率领法兰西移民在大海湾畔建立费尔南迪纳德哈瓜，即后来更名的西恩富戈斯。1821年时，埃斯坎夫雷已是一片繁荣的蔗糖之乡。

en:
Guane is the far west of Cuba, the rolling country beyond the Sierra de los Órganos that runs out to Cape San Antonio. In 1444 it was the land of the Guanahatabey, a people older than the Taíno: hunter-gatherers who moved in small bands rather than villages, made no pottery and worshipped no cemís, living on fish and shellfish. Even the Taíno knew the western tip as the country of a different people.

In April 1494 Columbus reached this end of the island on his second voyage, and his Taíno interpreters could not understand a word the locals said, for they spoke another language. Diego Velázquez mentioned them again in 1514 and Bartolomé de las Casas in 1516, but after the conquest the Guanahatabey disappear from the record amid the collapse of Cuba's indigenous world. The Spanish town of Guane was founded in 1602, one of the few settlements in a district largely left to itself, and Canary Islanders arriving from the later sixteenth century turned the riverside vegas into tobacco country. When the crown imposed a tobacco estanco in 1717, fixing the price and the amount every grower must sell, growers revolted in 1717, 1720 and 1723; the last rising ended with twelve men shot and their bodies hung from trees along the road. In the later eighteenth century the far west was organized as the Pinar del Río tobacco district, supplying the royal factories in Havana, and in 1821 Guane remained a small town ringed by tobacco vegas.
zh:
瓜内地处古巴最西端，是奥尔加诺斯山脉之外、一直延伸到圣安东尼奥角的起伏原野。1444年，这里是瓜纳哈塔贝伊人的土地——一个比泰诺人更古老的族群：他们以小群体游徙为生而不建村落，不制陶器，也不拜塞米神像，靠鱼和贝类过活。在泰诺人看来，岛屿西端本就是另一族人的地方。

1494年4月，哥伦布第二次航行抵达这一岛端，随队的泰诺译员却听不懂当地人的话——他们说的是另一种语言。迭戈·贝拉斯克斯1514年、巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯1516年又分别提到过他们，但征服之后，随着古巴原住民世界的崩溃，瓜纳哈塔贝伊人从记载中消失。1602年，西班牙人建立瓜内镇，是这片大体被放任自流的地区少有的定居点；16世纪末起陆续迁来的加那利移民，把河畔的低地沃土建成为烟草田园。1717年王室推行烟草专卖，规定每个烟农的售价和出售数量，烟农遂于1717、1720和1723年接连起事；最后一次反抗被镇压，十二人被枪决，尸体挂在路边的树上示众。18世纪后期，远西地区被组织为比那尔德里奥烟草辖区，向哈瓦那的王家烟厂供货；到1821年，瓜内仍是一座烟草田园环绕的小镇。

en:
The Mayaca lived among the lakes and marshes of the upper St. Johns River, south of Lake George, a wet country of seasonal floods where villages stood on high ground and canoes threaded the waterways of the St. Johns culture. They hunted, fished and gathered like the Ais, whose language theirs resembled, but did not farm like the Timucua of the richer lands to the north. A paramount chief at the village of Mayaca spoke for several towns, some of them as far away as the Atlantic coast. In 1444 these lakes knew nothing of Europe, and rivalry with the Freshwater Timucua chiefs to the north shaped local politics.

The European wars of the 1560s reached the lakes as French Fort Caroline and Spanish St. Augustine fought for the Florida coast, and the Spaniards first met the Mayaca in 1566 while ransoming French captives. Franciscans came at the end of the century: the chief was baptized by 1597 and the mission of San Salvador de Mayaca was later founded. By the 1690s the Mayaca province had several missions, although Yamasee refugees had become most of its people, and unrest in 1696 and 1697 cost a friar his life. Raids by Carolina-backed Indians in 1708 broke the people apart: some Mayaca fled to St. Augustine, others south to the eastern shore of Lake Okeechobee. In 1738 and 1739 they and their Jororo and Bomto allies fought the Calusa and their allies; those battles and an Uchise raid on the Pojoy together killed some 300 people. A last handful, mingled with Mayaimi and Santaluzo survivors, was found by missionaries in 1743; that remnant band is presumed to have sailed for Cuba with the Spaniards in 1763.
zh:
玛亚卡（马亚卡）人住在圣约翰斯河上游、乔治湖以南的湖沼地带。这里地势低洼、湖水季节性泛滥，村镇建在高地之上，独木舟穿行在圣约翰斯文化的水网之间。他们和语言相近的艾斯人一样以渔猎采集为生，不像北方沃土上的蒂穆夸人那样务农；玛亚卡镇的大酋统辖数个村镇，其中一些远在大西洋岸边。1444年，这片湖乡还不知欧洲为何物，与北方「淡水蒂穆夸」诸酋的争斗左右着当地的格局。

16世纪60年代，法国的卡洛琳堡与西班牙的圣奥古斯丁争夺佛罗里达海岸，战祸波及湖乡；1566年，西班牙人在赎回法国俘虏时首次接触玛亚卡人。方济各会修士在16世纪末到来，大酋到1597年已受洗入教，圣萨尔瓦多·德·玛亚卡传教站随后设立。到17世纪90年代，玛亚卡地区已有数座传教站，但居民已以逃难而来的亚马西人为主体；1696至1697年的骚乱中，一名修士被杀。1708年，卡罗来纳支持的印第安武装的袭击击散了玛亚卡人：一部分逃往圣奥古斯丁，一部分南下到奥基乔比湖东岸。1738至1739年，他们与霍罗罗人、博姆托人结盟，同卡卢萨人及其盟友交战；这些战斗和乌奇西人对波霍伊人的袭击共造成约300人死亡。传教士1743年见到的最后一小群玛亚卡人已与马亚依米人、圣卢索人的孑遗混居，这群人据信于1763年随西班牙人登船前往古巴。

en:
The Potano were Timucua-speaking farmers of the Alachua savanna, the rolling prairie and oak-hammock country of north-central Florida where the Alachua culture had raised villages and burial mounds since about 700. The chief town Potano was one of a string of settlements that included Itaraholata, Utinamochana and Mala-paz. Maize, beans and squash grew in the rich upland soils, and the Spaniards who later knew them remembered the Potano as one of the strongest of the Timucua chiefdoms. In 1444 their world held only rival Timucua chiefs; no European had yet entered the interior.

Pánfilo de Narváez passed west of the Potano towns in 1528, and Hernando de Soto's army tramped through in 1539, stripping the villages of their stored maize. In the 1560s the Potano fought the Utina, who were backed first by the French of Fort Caroline and then by the Spaniards of St. Augustine; in 1584, after the Potano killed a Spanish captain leading an invasion, a punitive expedition slaughtered many and drove the rest from the chief town, which was rebuilt on a new site. Franciscans had baptized more than a thousand adult Potano by 1607, and the mission of San Francisco de Potano, founded in 1609, became the first resident mission west of the St. Johns; Spanish cattle ranches later spread across the people's former fields. The Potano joined the Timucuan rebellion of 1656, after which their towns and missions lay burned, and an epidemic in 1672 cut so deep that only 160 people remained at the two missions by 1675. From 1685 Creek and Yamasee slavers out of Carolina harried the prairie, and after the northern mission system collapsed in 1704 the surviving Potano drifted to St. Augustine as refugees and vanished as a tribe.
zh:
波塔诺人是说蒂穆夸语的农人，住在北佛罗里达中部的阿拉楚阿稀树草原——一片起伏的草甸与橡树林地，阿拉楚阿文化约自700年起便在此营建村落与墓葬土垒。酋镇波塔诺是一连串村镇之一，其余还有伊塔拉霍拉塔、乌蒂纳莫查纳和马拉帕斯。肥沃的高地上种着玉米、豆类和南瓜，后来结识他们的西班牙人把波塔诺视为蒂穆夸诸酋邦中最强的一支。1444年，波塔诺人的世界里只有彼此争雄的蒂穆夸诸酋，欧洲人尚未踏入这片内陆。

1528年，潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯的远征队从波塔诺诸镇以西经过；1539年，埃尔南多·德·索托的大军穿越其地，把各村储存的玉米劫掠一空。16世纪60年代，波塔诺人与乌蒂纳部交战，后者先有卡洛琳堡的法国人撑腰，后来又得到圣奥古斯丁的西班牙人支持。1584年，波塔诺人杀死一名带兵入侵的西班牙队长，讨伐军随即血洗其地，幸存者被逐出酋镇，村镇易地重建。方济各会修士到1607年已为一千多名成年波塔诺人施洗；1609年设立的圣弗朗西斯科·德·波塔诺传教站，是圣约翰斯河以西第一座常驻教士的传教站，后来西班牙牧牛场在波塔诺人昔日的田地上铺开。1656年，波塔诺人参加蒂穆夸大起义，战后村镇与传教站多被焚毁；1672年的一场疫病又重创其民，到1675年两座传教站中只剩160人。1685年起，卡罗来纳指使的克里克和亚马西奴隶贩子不断蹂躏草原；1704年北方传教体系崩溃后，幸存的波塔诺人作为难民流落圣奥古斯丁，作为一个部族就此消亡。

en:
The wooded lowlands bearing the name Tanu lie between the Brazos and Neches rivers, centered on Bedias Creek and the Trinity. In 1444 this was Bidai country; the people called themselves Quasmigdo, while the Caddo name Bidai referred to the brushwood of their Big Thicket homeland. Their villages farmed the river bottoms and hunting parties moved through the pine and oak woods. Galveston Bay and the Akokisa lay to the south, with Hasinai towns beyond the Neches to the east.

The first Spanish mention came in 1691, when explorers placed the Bidai near the Hasinai. François Simars de Bellisle found them farming and allied with the Akokisa in 1718–1720. French trade on the Trinity soon challenged Spanish claims: after Blancpain's trading post was broken up in 1754, Spain built Presidio San Agustín de Ahumada at El Orcoquisac in 1756 and opened the Franciscan Mission Nuestra Señora de la Luz to gather Akokisa and Bidai families there. The mission was moved in 1759, but after Louisiana passed to Spain and the Marqués de Rubí's frontier inspection, the post was abandoned in 1771. Epidemics in 1776–1777 halved the surviving Bidai, whose families then sought refuge among the Akokisa and Koasati; by 1821 the old Tanu country was no longer centered on a separate Bidai polity.
zh:
得名塔努的林地低地位于布拉索斯河与内奇斯河之间，以贝迪亚斯溪和特里尼蒂河为中心。1444年，这里是比代人的土地；他们自称夸斯米格多，而卡多语中的「比代」意指其大丛林家园中的灌柴。村落在河畔低地耕作，狩猎队伍穿行于松树与橡树林间。南面是加尔维斯顿湾和阿科基萨人，东面越过内奇斯河则是哈西奈人的城镇。

1691年，西班牙探险者首次留下记载，把比代人的位置标在哈西奈人附近。1718—1720年，弗朗索瓦·西马尔·德·贝利斯勒看到他们从事农业，并与阿科基萨人结盟。特里尼蒂河上的法国贸易很快挑战了西班牙的主权主张：布朗潘的贸易站在1754年被捣毁后，西班牙于1756年在奥科基萨克建立圣阿古斯丁·德·阿乌马达要塞，并开设方济各会的光明圣母传教站，试图把阿科基萨和比代家庭聚集到那里。传教站于1759年迁移，但在路易斯安那转归西班牙、鲁维侯爵巡边之后，整个据点于1771年废弃。1776—1777年的瘟疫使幸存的比代人减少一半，幸存者随后投奔阿科基萨人和科阿萨蒂人；到1821年，旧日的塔努之地已不再以一个独立的比代政体为中心。

en:
Nitahendé reproduces the Mescalero name Nit'ahéndé or Niit'ahénde, 'people who live against the mountains'. Their seasonal country took in the Sacramento Mountains of southern New Mexico and the Guadalupe Mountains above the west Texas desert, with canyons reaching toward the Pecos. In 1444 these Ndé hunters and gatherers moved between high pine forest, pinyon-juniper slopes, desert basins and buffalo plains. Mescal agave was roasted in pit ovens, deer and bighorn were hunted in the ranges, and buffalo hunts carried parties east toward the Pecos and Llano Estacado. Springs, caves and mountain passes made this a refuge as well as a highway.

Spaniards first entered the Guadalupe country in the sixteenth century but made no settlement there, and Spanish horses gradually gave Apache hunters greater range. After Juan de Oñate occupied New Mexico in 1598, Apache bands along the frontier alternately traded and raided Spanish herds while colonial parties retaliated and took captives. Between 1700 and 1750 Comanche expansion pushed many Mescalero groups back into the Sacramento, Guadalupe and Trans-Pecos mountains. Spanish authorities later negotiated limited peace settlements with Apache rancherías, with agreements in 1790 and 1793, but the Mexican independence struggle after 1810 drained frontier garrisons and raiding resumed. When Spanish rule ended in 1821, the Nitahendé mountains remained an unconquered Mescalero stronghold on the edge of independent Mexico.
zh:
