尼塔恩德（Nit'ahéndé 或 Niit'ahénde）是梅斯卡莱罗人的一支，名称意为「住在山边的人」。他们的季节性故土包括新墨西哥南部的萨克拉门托山和耸立在得克萨斯西部沙漠上的瓜达卢佩山，峡谷向佩科斯河方向延伸。1444年，这些恩代猎人和采集者在高山松林、矮松刺柏坡、沙漠盆地和野牛草原之间迁移。梅斯卡尔龙舌兰在坑炉中烘烤，山间可猎鹿和大角羊，野牛狩猎则把队伍带向东方的佩科斯河与埃斯塔卡多平原。泉水、洞穴和山口既是避难所，也是通行要道。

16世纪，西班牙人最早进入瓜达卢佩山区，但没有在那里定居；西班牙人的马逐渐扩大了阿帕切猎人的活动范围。胡安·德·奥尼亚特1598年据有新墨西哥后，边境阿帕切群体时而贸易，时而劫掠西班牙畜群，殖民队伍则以报复和掳掠人口回应。1700至1750年间，科曼奇人的扩张把许多梅斯卡莱罗群体逼回萨克拉门托山、瓜达卢佩山和佩科斯以西山地。后来西班牙当局与阿帕切牧场群落达成有限和平，1790年和1793年先后签订协议；但1810年后墨西哥独立战争削弱边境驻军，劫掠再起。1821年西班牙统治结束时，尼塔恩德群山仍是独立墨西哥边缘一处未被征服的梅斯卡莱罗据点。

en:
Ndawe Qoha is the lower Pecos borderland where the river turns southeast out of the Trans-Pecos mountains and cuts arid canyons on its way to the Rio Grande. Around its waterholes, arroyos and sparse grasslands, the cedar breaks of the Edwards Plateau meet the Chihuahuan Desert. In 1444 this was Ndé hunting country: Lipan families moved with bison and white-tailed deer, roasted agave, gathered mesquite beans, and used the fords to meet Jumano travelers whose trails ran west toward Toyah Creek and La Junta. No Spanish town or mission yet anchored the lower river, whose value lay in water, crossings and access to Coahuila.

Antonio de Espejo followed this river in 1582–1583, naming it Río de las Vacas for the buffalo herds; Jumano guides showed the way from the Pecos by Toyah Creek to La Junta. The Lipan had acquired Spanish horses by 1608, and mounted rancherías turned the lower fords into links between west Texas, Coahuila and the southern plains. By 1700 they were established across southern Texas and northern Coahuila, farming corn, beans, pumpkins and watermelons in seasonal clearings while retaining long hunting rounds. In 1778 Juan de Ugalde, governor of Coahuila, located a Lipan ranchería of about forty people led by Zapato Bordado on the Rio Grande, together with a Mescalero camp, and opened the campaigns of the following year. When Mexico became independent in 1821, the sparse frontier presidios had not pinned the lower Pecos Lipan into a settled colonial district.
zh:
恩达韦科哈是佩科斯河下游边地，河水从佩科斯以西山地折向东南，切过干旱峡谷，奔向里奥格兰德。这里的水洼、旱谷和稀疏草原，正处在爱德华兹高原的雪松峡谷与奇瓦瓦沙漠相接之处。1444年，这里是恩代猎场：利潘群体随野牛和白尾鹿迁移，烘烤龙舌兰、采集牧豆，利用各处渡口同胡马诺旅人往来，胡马诺商路向西通往托亚溪和拉洪塔。此时下游河畔还没有西班牙城镇或传教站，这片土地的价值在于水源、渡口和通往科阿韦拉的道路。

1582至1583年，安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍沿这条河返程，因野牛群众多而称其为「母牛河」；胡马诺向导指引他从佩科斯河经托亚溪前往拉洪塔。利潘人到1608年已获得西班牙马，骑马的营地群落把下游渡口变成连接得克萨斯西部、科阿韦拉和南部平原的纽带。到1700年，他们已分布在得克萨斯南部和科阿韦拉北部，在季节性空地上种植玉米、豆类、南瓜和西瓜，同时保留长距离狩猎。1778年，科阿韦拉总督胡安·德·乌加尔德在里奥格兰德河畔发现一处约四十人的利潘营地，首领是萨帕托·博达多（意为「绣花鞋」），旁边还有一处梅斯卡莱罗营地；次年他由此发起讨伐。1821年墨西哥独立时，稀疏的边境要塞仍未能把佩科斯河下游的利潘人约束在固定的殖民辖区内。

en:
Natahéndé is the Pecos River corridor of the Naa'dahéńdé, the Mescal People whom Spanish records rendered as Natagés. The Pecos rises on the eastern slope of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and runs south-east through arid grasslands toward the Rio Grande. In 1444 Apache bands used its valley and side arroyos for skin-lodge camps, mescal gathering, seasonal planting and hunts for deer and bison; horses had not yet reached these camps, and no Spanish mission or presidio guarded the river.

Antonio de Espejo followed the Pecos on his return in 1582-1583, naming it Río de las Vacas after six days of travel through country thick with bison. Mounted raiding and slaving later tied the Natagés to the Texas frontier. In 1731 they joined Lipan, Teya and Jumano allies in war on San Antonio; on 9 December 1732 Governor Juan Antonio Bustillo y Ceballos attacked about four hundred tipis on the San Sabá River after a five-hour battle, but Apache raids continued. Natagé and Lipan leaders made peace with Spain at San Antonio in 1749. Comanche pressure nevertheless drove more Lipan survivors toward the Rio Grande and Coahuila in 1767, where they joined Natagé groups, and around 1780 the latter entered the Lipiyán coalition led by Picax-Ande-Ins-Tinsle. When Mexico became independent in 1821, the Pecos corridor remained an Apache route rather than a conquered colonial heartland.
zh:
纳塔恩德是梅斯卡尔人（Naa'dahéńdé）所居的佩科斯河通道；西班牙文献将其转写为纳塔赫斯（Natagés）。佩科斯河发源于桑格雷·德克里斯托山东坡，向东南穿过干旱草原，最终汇入格兰德河。1444年时，阿帕奇群体沿河谷和支谷设立兽皮帐篷营地，采集梅斯卡尔龙舌兰，进行季节性种植，并猎捕鹿和野牛；马匹尚未传到这些营地，河畔也没有西班牙传教站或要塞。

1582—1583年，安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍返程时沿佩科斯河行进，因连续六日穿行在野牛众多的地带而将其命名为「母牛河」。后来，骑马袭掠和奴隶贸易把纳塔赫斯人与得州边疆联系在一起。1731年，他们与利潘人、特亚人和胡马诺人结盟，对圣安东尼奥开战；1732年12月9日，胡安·安东尼奥·布斯蒂略·伊·塞瓦略斯总督进攻圣萨瓦河畔约四百座帐篷，战斗持续五小时，但阿帕奇人的袭掠并未停止。1749年，纳塔赫斯和利潘首领在圣安东尼奥与西班牙议和。尽管如此，科曼奇人的压力仍在1767年把更多利潘幸存者逼向格兰德河与科阿韦拉，他们在那里加入纳塔赫斯群体；约1780年，纳塔赫斯人又加入皮卡克斯-安德-因斯-廷斯勒领导的利皮亚内斯联盟。1821年墨西哥独立时，佩科斯河通道仍是阿帕奇人的往来之路，而非被征服的殖民腹地。

en:
Naflat is the Rio Grande country around Cochiti, one of the eastern Keres pueblos. Its people traced their ancestry to Ancestral Puebloan farmers who built cliff dwellings in the canyons of the Pajarito Plateau; some groups lived at Potrero Viejo and Hanut Cochiti before the historic pueblo took shape. River water, maize and cotton bound the villages together, while the finger mesas offered refuge in war. In 1444 Cochiti was an independent Keres town, linked by language, marriage and trade to the other Pueblo peoples along the river.

Juan de Oñate's expedition reached Cochiti in 1598, opening trade before Spanish rule hardened into tribute in crops, cotton and labour. Franciscans attacked traditional rites and raised the San Buenaventura mission. Cochiti joined the coordinated rising of 1680 that killed about 400 Spaniards and forced some 2,000 survivors to abandon Santa Fe de Nuevo México. When Antonio de Otermín's counterattack reached the river, Cochiti withdrew with San Felipe and Kewa to Potrero Viejo. The refugees held that mesa refuge until 1693, when Diego de Vargas's reconquest drove them from it.
zh:
纳夫拉特是科奇蒂周围的里奥格兰德河谷地带，科奇蒂是东部凯雷斯语诸普韦布洛之一。其先民是古代普韦布洛农民，曾在帕哈里托高原的峡谷中营建崖居；一些群体先住在波特雷罗维耶霍和哈努特科奇蒂，后来形成历史时期的科奇蒂。河水、玉米和棉花把村落联系在一起，指状台地则在战乱时提供庇护。1444年，科奇蒂仍是独立的凯雷斯人城镇，通过语言、通婚和贸易与沿河其他普韦布洛人往来。

胡安·德·奥尼亚特远征队1598年抵达科奇蒂，最初开放贸易；随后西班牙统治转为征收作物、棉花和劳役。方济各会打击本土仪式，建起圣布埃纳文图拉传教站。科奇蒂参加1680年的联合起义，约四百名西班牙人被杀，约两千名幸存者被迫放弃圣菲新墨西哥省。安东尼奥·德·奥特尔明反攻到河畔时，科奇蒂人与圣费利佩、克瓦人退往波特雷罗维耶霍。他们据守这座台地避难所至1693年，最终被迭戈·德·巴尔加斯的再征服军逐走。

en:
Tsi'ya is the Jemez River valley home of the Zia, an Eastern Keres Pueblo people. Their Ancestral Puebloan forebears moved into the valley in the thirteenth century and built the adobe pueblo beside irrigated maize fields; pottery and trade with neighbouring Keres and Jemez towns shaped its economy. In 1444 Tsi'ya governed its own fields and ceremonies, still untouched by the Spanish expeditions that would later enter New Mexico.

Antonio de Espejo first recorded Tsi'ya in 1583. After Juan de Oñate's arrival in 1598, Fray Alonso de Lugo founded the San Pedro y San Pablo mission, and Zia labourers had raised a church and convent by 1613. Spanish rule outlawed traditional ceremonies, and in 1680 the Zia joined Popé's Pueblo Revolt, forcing the colonists south and putting Spanish horses in Pueblo hands for the plains trade. Governor Domingo Jironza Petriz de Cruzate stormed the pueblo in 1689, killing 600 Zia and taking 70 captives. Inter-Pueblo disputes later favoured Diego de Vargas's reconquest, and the Zia leader Antonio Malacate brought the survivors home; about 120 people remained in 1692. The mission was rebuilt and entrusted to Fray Juan Alpuente in 1694, then renovated in 1707 as Nuestra Señora de la Asunción.
zh:
齐亚是齐亚人在赫梅斯河谷的家园，齐亚人是说东部凯雷斯语的普韦布洛族群。13世纪，他们的古代普韦布洛祖先迁入河谷，在灌溉玉米田旁建起土坯普韦布洛，制陶和与邻近凯雷斯、赫梅斯村镇的贸易构成生活基础。1444年，齐亚仍自行管理田地与仪式，尚未受到后来进入新墨西哥的西班牙远征波及。

安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍1583年首先记录齐亚。胡安·德·奥尼亚特1598年到来后，修士阿隆索·德·卢戈建立圣佩德罗与圣巴勃罗传教站；到1613年，齐亚劳工已建起教堂和修道院。西班牙统治禁止传统仪式，齐亚遂在1680年参加波佩领导的普韦布洛起义，迫使殖民者南逃，西班牙马匹也经普韦布洛人之手进入大平原贸易。总督多明戈·希龙萨·佩特里斯·德·克鲁萨特1689年攻陷普韦布洛，六百名齐亚人被杀，七十人被俘。普韦布洛诸部之间的争端随后有利于迭戈·德·巴尔加斯再征服，齐亚首领安东尼奥·马拉卡特率幸存者返乡；1692年当地约只剩一百二十人。传教站1694年重建并交由修士胡安·阿尔普恩特主持，1707年整修后改名圣母升天传教站。

en:
The Sobaipuri were an O'odham people who farmed the well-watered valleys of the San Pedro and Santa Cruz rivers in the Pimería Alta, their compact, carefully planned villages set on river terraces where they grew maize, beans and squash with floodwater ditches. The settlements later recorded as Tumacácori and Guevavi had occupied the two valleys for generations before Europeans entered the Southwest. The Sobaipuri traded and intermarried, and at times raided, with the Apache, Jocome and Jano on their eastern flank, and they spoke the same Piman tongue as the Akimel and Tohono O'odham around them. In 1444 no friar or soldier had yet entered their valleys.

Fray Marcos de Niza may have passed Sobaipuri rancherías on the San Pedro in 1539, and Coronado's men entered the region soon after, but the expedition won no submission and the Sobaipuri valleys saw no Spaniard again for roughly 150 years. In 1691 Sobaipuri headmen traveled south to Sáric to invite the Jesuit Eusebio Francisco Kino; he visited Tumacácori and Guevavi, introduced cattle and wheat, and in 1701 raised a church at Guevavi. On Easter Day 1698 the Sobaipuri leader Coro defeated a much larger Apache, Jocome and Jano force that fell on his village of Gaybanipitea on the San Pedro, after which his people became Spain's steadfast allies and the buffer of the Sonora frontier. The Pima revolt of 1751 and the presidio founded at Tubac in 1752 pulled the mission villages toward the garrison, and the new village of Calabazas was gathered in 1756. As Apache raids worsened the Sobaipuri abandoned the San Pedro valley around 1762, and after the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 the Franciscans moved the mission headquarters from Guevavi to Tumacácori in 1771; Guevavi stood empty by 1775, the year a presidio was planted at Tucson. When New Spain's rule ended in 1821, the surviving Sobaipuri had folded into the O'odham communities at San Xavier del Bac and Tumacácori.
zh:
索巴伊普里人是奥奥德姆人的一支，在皮梅里亚阿尔塔境内圣佩德罗河与圣克鲁斯河水源充足的河谷务农。他们布局齐整的密集村落坐落在河流阶地上，用引洪水的沟渠种植玉米、豆类和南瓜。后来被记作图马卡科里和格瓦维的那些村落，在欧洲人进入西南之前的许多世代里就已居住在这两条河谷。索巴伊普里人与东侧的阿帕奇人、霍科梅人和哈诺人通婚、贸易，有时也一同外出劫掠，所说的皮曼语与周围的阿基梅尔人和托霍诺·奥奥德姆人相同。1444年时，还没有修士或士兵进入过他们的河谷。

1539年，修士马科斯·德·尼萨可能在圣佩德罗河畔经过索巴伊普里人的村落，科罗纳多的部下不久也进入这一带，但远征队没有压服任何人，此后约一百五十年间再没有西班牙人来。1691年，索巴伊普里诸首领南行至萨里克，邀请耶稣会士尤塞维奥·弗朗西斯科·基诺北上；基诺走访了图马卡科里和格瓦维，带去牛和小麦，并于1701年在格瓦维主持建起教堂。1698年复活节，阿帕奇、霍科梅和哈诺人的大军袭击首领科罗在圣佩德罗河畔的盖巴尼皮特亚村，科罗率众以少胜多；此后他的部族成为西班牙坚定的盟友，也是索诺拉边疆的屏障。1751年皮马人起义，1752年西班牙在图巴克设立要塞，各传教村落向守军靠拢，1756年又聚成新的卡拉巴萨斯村。随着阿帕奇袭扰加剧，索巴伊普里人约在1762年放弃圣佩德罗河谷；1767年耶稣会被逐后，方济各会于1771年把传教中心从格瓦维迁往图马卡科里，格瓦维到1775年已无人居住，同年图森设立要塞。1821年新西班牙统治结束时，幸存的索巴伊普里人已融入圣哈维尔·德尔·巴克和图马卡科里的奥奥德姆社群。

en:
The Pinaleño Mountains are the pine-bearing sky island at the heart of this countryside, rising above Sonoran and Chihuahuan desert valleys toward Mount Graham in the upper Gila country. Western Apache called the range Dził Nnilchí' Diyiléé, while the Tsékʼáádn, or Metate People, were the San Carlos and Pinaleño bands who gathered pine nuts, hunted, and farmed beside mountain streams. In 1444 their Ndee family groups moved between these ridges and Gila watercourses, close to older Mogollon and Hohokam farming lands and to Yavapai and O'odham neighbors.

Spanish knowledge entered the Gila watershed soon after the conquest of Mexico: Juan de la Asunción may have reached the river in 1538, and Hernando de Alarcón sailed to its Colorado confluence in 1540. The waterway was long called Río Grande de los Apóstoles or Río del Nombre de Jesús before Spanish writers fixed the name Gila early in the 1700s. Horses transformed Apache raiding by the late 1600s, and raids and reprisals through the next century kept the upper Gila frontier without fixed colonial settlement. Missions and presidios never enclosed the Tsékʼáádn mountains; in 1821 the Ndee still held them.
zh:
皮纳莱尼奥山脉是这片地方核心的松林天空岛，耸立于索诺兰沙漠与奇瓦瓦沙漠的谷地之间，最高峰格雷厄姆山俯瞰希拉河上游。西阿帕奇人称这片山脉为齐尔尼尔奇伊·迪伊莱埃；采卡登人（Tsékʼáádn，意为石磨盘人）属圣卡洛斯与皮纳莱尼奥诸群体，采集松果、狩猎，并在山溪旁耕作。1444年，他们的恩迪家族群体往来于这些山脊和希拉河水道之间，邻近莫戈永、霍霍坎人的古老农地，也与亚瓦派人和奥奥德姆人为邻。

征服墨西哥后不久，西班牙人的地理知识进入希拉河流域：胡安·德·拉·亚松森可能在1538年抵达这条河，埃尔南多·德·阿拉尔孔1540年航行到希拉河与科罗拉多河交汇处。这条水道在16—17世纪长期被称为阿波斯托莱斯大河或耶稣之名河，西班牙文书到18世纪初才固定使用希拉一名。到17世纪末，马匹改变了阿帕奇人的袭掠方式；此后一个世纪，袭掠与报复往复不断，希拉河上游边地始终没有形成固定的殖民定居点。传教站和要塞始终未能围住采卡登人的山地，1821年时恩迪人仍据守群山。

en:
The Taaqtam, later called Serranos by Spaniards, were Takic-speaking people of the San Bernardino Mountains and western Mojave. In 1444 the Yuhaaviatam, or People of the Pines, occupied mountain villages and oak groves, while Desert Serrano groups, including the Vanyume, lived along the intermittent Mojave River leading from the Cajon Pass toward Soda Lake. The stream mostly ran underground, surfacing at gorges and oases such as the village of Wá'peat, where mesquite, yucca, pine nuts, acorns, deer, and bighorn sheep sustained the people. The Mojave trail linked the Colorado River to the coast through this country, carrying coastal shell beads and asphaltum east and Southwestern ceramics and textiles west.

Mission San Gabriel Arcángel was founded on 8 September 1771 and soon claimed Serrano lands and labor. Pedro Fages entered Serrano territory in 1772, and Francisco Garcés followed the Mojave River in March 1776, naming it Arroyo de los Mártires before later Spaniards called it the Río de las Ánimas. In 1812 the Serrano joined the Cahuilla and Quechan in revolt against mission reductions. In 1819 San Gabriel opened the San Bernardino de Sena Estancia, Serrano people were relocated there and dug the Mill Creek Zanja, and Mojave warriors killed many Serrano that year. At Mexican independence in 1821, the estancia remained only an edge of Spanish settlement while Taaqtam communities kept the mountains and desert roads.
zh:
塔克塔姆人后被西班牙人称为塞拉诺人，是说塔基克语的圣贝纳迪诺山脉与西莫哈韦居民。1444年，「松林之人」尤哈维亚塔姆群体住在山地村落和橡树林中；包括瓦尼乌姆人在内的沙漠塞拉诺群体，则沿时断时续的莫哈韦河生活，这条水道从卡洪山口通向苏打湖。河水大多在地下流淌，只在峡谷和绿洲露出地面，瓦佩阿特等村落借此获取牧豆、丝兰、松子、橡实、鹿和大角羊。莫哈韦商路从科罗拉多河经此地通往海岸，把沿海的贝壳珠和沥青带向东方，也把西南地区的陶器和织物带向西方。

圣加百列大天使传教站于1771年9月8日建立，很快宣称对塞拉诺土地和劳力的管辖权。佩德罗·法赫斯1772年进入塞拉诺领地，弗朗西斯科·加尔塞斯1776年3月沿莫哈韦河探查，将它命名为殉道者溪，后来的西班牙人改称灵魂河。1812年，塞拉诺人联合卡维拉人和克昌人（尤马人）反抗传教站的集居管制。1819年，圣加百列传教站开设圣贝纳迪诺·德·塞纳牧场站，塞拉诺人被迁往那里并挖掘米尔溪灌溉渠；同年，莫哈韦战士杀死许多塞拉诺人。1821年墨西哥独立时，这座牧场站仍只是西班牙人定居区的边缘，塔克塔姆诸群体仍掌握着山地与沙漠道路。

en: The Choinumni were a Kings River people among the many autonomous Yokuts tribes of the San Joaquin Valley. In 1444 their villages stood along a stretch of the upper Kings River, where oak groves supplied acorns, marshes and sloughs yielded fish, waterfowl and roots, and tule rushes roofed pit houses and made rafts. Trails over the Sierra Nevada carried trade with the Mono and other Paiute peoples. Pedro Fages entered the southern valley in 1772, but the Kings River remained beyond the mission frontier until Gabriel Moraga's Spanish expedition arrived in 1805 and named it Río de los Santos Reyes. A friar in the party thought the populous, well-watered valley suitable for a mission and presidio, yet no mission was built there. When New Spain became Mexico in 1821, the Choinumni still occupied their river villages without a colonial settlement among them.
zh: 乔伊努姆尼人是金斯河居民，也是圣华金谷众多自治约库特部族之一。1444年，他们的村落分布在金斯河上游一段河畔：橡树林提供橡实，湿地和河汊出产鱼、水禽与根茎，香蒲则可作半地穴房屋的屋顶并扎成木筏。穿越内华达山脉的小路把他们同莫诺人及其他派尤特人连接起来。1772年，佩德罗·法赫斯进入圣华金谷南部，但金斯河仍在传教边疆之外；1805年，加夫列尔·莫拉加的西班牙远征队到达这里，将河命名为三王河（Río de los Santos Reyes）。随行修士认为这片水源充足、人口稠密的河谷适合建立传教站和要塞，但最终没有任何传教站在此落成。1821年新西班牙变为墨西哥时，乔伊努姆尼人仍居住在河畔村落中，殖民居民点尚未进入他们之间。

en:
Ohlone is the country around the great inland sea of San Francisco Bay, whose narrow gate had let even Cabrillo's ships sail past. In 1444 more than fifty autonomous tribelets lived between the bay's marshes and Monterey in the south, among them the Ramaytush at the peninsula tip, where the village of Chutchui stood, and the Tamyen of the Santa Clara valley. They spoke related Utian languages, followed the Kuksu cult and raised enormous shellmounds beside their waterside villages. Tule rafts carried them across the bay to trade and feud, and salmon, acorns and the waterfowl clouds made this one of the most thickly peopled lands north of Mexico.

On 4 November 1769 Gaspar de Portola, marching up the coast, climbed Sweeney Ridge and became the first European to see the bay. Juan de Ayala sailed the San Carlos through the Golden Gate on 5 August 1775, and his pilot Canizares drew its first chart. Juan Bautista de Anza chose the settlement sites in March 1776: Father Francisco Palou said the first mass at Mission San Francisco de Asis, soon called Dolores, on 29 June, and Jose Joaquin Moraga raised the Royal Presidio on 17 September. Mission Santa Clara and the pueblo of San Jose followed in 1777, and Mission San Jose in 1797. Hundreds of Ohlone entered the missions in 1794 and 1795, just as a deadly epidemic swept the bay. In 1807 and again in 1810-11 Russian-led Aleut otter hunters raided the bay in kayaks and carried thousands of skins off to Canton. By the 1810s Dolores held some 1,100 neophytes, yet more than 5,000 had died there by the time Mexico took the province in 1821.
zh:
奥洛内是旧金山湾这片巨大内海四周的土地，海湾狭窄的入口曾让卡布里略的船也驶了过去。1444年，五十多个互不统属的部落小群住在湾边沼泽到南方蒙特雷之间：半岛尖端是拉马伊图什人，楚特奎伊村就坐落在此；圣克拉拉谷里住着塔米恩人。他们操亲属相近的乌蒂安语系语言，奉行库克苏信仰，在水畔村庄旁堆起巨大的贝丘。人们乘香蒲筏渡湾去贸易和械斗，鲑鱼、橡子和遮天蔽日的水鸟，使这里成为墨西哥以北人口最稠密的地区之一。

1769年11月4日，沿海岸北上的加斯帕尔·德·波尔托拉登上斯威尼岭，成为第一个望见这片海湾的欧洲人。1775年8月5日，胡安·德·阿亚拉驾「圣卡洛斯号」穿过金门，领航员卡尼萨雷斯绘下海湾的第一张地图。1776年3月，胡安·包蒂斯塔·德·安萨选定建址：6月29日，弗朗西斯科·帕洛乌神父在圣弗朗西斯科·德·阿西斯传教所（不久即以「多洛雷斯」闻名）举行第一场弥撒；9月17日，何塞·华金·莫拉加建起王家要塞。圣克拉拉传教所和圣何塞镇随后于1777年建立，圣何塞传教所则建于1797年。1794至1795年，数百名奥洛内人进入传教所，恰在此时一场致命疫病席卷湾区。1807年以及1810至1811年，为俄国人效力的阿留申海獭猎手两度乘皮艇闯入湾中，把数千张海獭皮运往广州。到1810年代，多洛雷斯约有一千一百名新信徒，而到1821年墨西哥接掌这片土地时，已有五千多人死在那里。

en: In 1444 the Wintun lived west of the Sacramento, from Mount Shasta to San Francisco Bay, in one of California's richest valleys. They were three peoples: the Wintu on the upper river and McCloud, the Nomlaki on its central tributaries, and the Patwin of the lower valley, perhaps 12,000 strong in 1770. Domed earth lodges lined the streams; the year turned on salmon runs, acorn meal, manzanita cider and woven baskets. The Patwin kept the Kuksu religion of the 'big head' dances, shared with the Maidu and Pomo. In 1808 the Spaniard Gabriel Moraga entered the southern valley and named the river the Rio de los Sacramentos; the southern Patwin were already being pressed toward the missions.
zh: 1444年，萨克拉门托河以西，从沙斯塔山到旧金山湾，温图诸族住在加利福尼亚最富庶的河谷之一。他们分三支：北支住在河上游与麦克劳德河，中支据有中部各支流，南支是下游的帕特温人；三支在1770年人口合计约一万二千。圆顶的土屋沿河排开；鲑鱼汛、橡子粉、熊果酒和编织篮筐构成一年的生计。帕特温人奉行「大头舞」的库克苏崇拜，迈杜人和波莫人同有此俗。1808年，西班牙军人加布里埃尔·莫拉加进入南部河谷，将河命名为「圣事之河」，萨克拉门托河的名字便由此而来；南方的帕特温人已被逼向传教团。

en:
The Paipai, also called Akwa'ala or Yakakwal, held a broad stretch of northern Baja California between the Kiliwa to the south and the Kumeyaay and Cocopa to the north. Their trails ran from San Vicente on the Pacific almost to the Colorado River delta, linking better-watered Pacific hills with the drier Gulf side. Like their Yuman neighbors, they lived by hunting, gathering, fishing, and seasonal movement rather than by towns or cultivation. In 1444 autonomous Paipai bands occupied this corridor between neighboring Yuman peoples.

Sebastián Vizcaíno's ships mapped the coast in 1602, but sustained European contact did not begin until Gaspar de Portolà and Junípero Serra led the California expedition through western Paipai country in 1769. Dominican missionaries Miguel Hidalgo and Joaquín Valero founded San Vicente on 2 August 1780. With fertile soil, abundant water, and a position on the mission road, it became both a major Dominican center and a military post watching the peoples of the lower Colorado. José Loriente and Tomás Valdellón opened the inland Santa Catarina mission on 12 November 1797, near the Paipai-Kumeyaay border. Its dams watered wheat, maize, barley, and vegetables and it kept cattle, horses, mules, and sheep, but poor land and difficult supply lines kept the settlement weak while introduced diseases reduced the people it congregated. By Mexican independence in 1821, the Paipai mission frontier remained fragile.
zh:
派派人又称阿克瓦阿拉或亚卡克瓦尔，据有下加利福尼亚北部的广阔地带，南接基利瓦人，北邻库梅亚伊人与科科帕人。他们的活动路线西起太平洋畔的圣维森特，几乎东达科罗拉多河三角洲，把水源较多的太平洋山地与较干燥的加利福尼亚湾一侧连接起来。和邻近的尤曼诸族一样，他们以狩猎、采集、捕鱼和季节性迁徙为生，没有城镇或农业。1444年，自治的派派小队占据着这条夹在相邻尤曼族群之间的走廊。

1602年，塞瓦斯蒂安·比斯开诺的船队测绘了这段海岸，但持续的欧洲接触要到1769年加斯帕尔·德·波尔塔拉和胡尼佩罗·塞拉率领加利福尼亚远征队穿过派派西部才开始。1780年8月2日，多明我会士米格尔·伊达尔戈与华金·巴莱罗建立圣维森特传教站。这里土壤肥沃、水源充足，又位于传教干道上，既是多明我会的重要中心，也是监视科罗拉多河下游诸族的军事据点。1797年11月12日，何塞·洛里恩特和托马斯·巴尔德利翁在派派与库梅亚伊边界附近开设内陆的圣卡塔琳娜传教站。水坝灌溉小麦、玉米、大麦和蔬菜，传教站也饲养牛、马、骡和羊，但土地贫瘠、补给困难使聚落始终衰弱，传入的疾病更削减了被集居的人口。到1821年墨西哥独立时，派派地区的传教边疆仍然脆弱。

en:
Tecpatitlan was the older spelling of the Tepatitlán district and lay in the Tecuexe highlands of Jalisco, on the routes between Tonala and the drier Guamare frontier. The Tecuexes were Uto-Aztecan speakers divided among independent lordships; Tecpatitlan, Acatic, Xalostotitlan and Yahualican were among their seats. Tonala, whose Nahuatl name meant the place through which the sun rises, was one of the principal chiefdoms of central Jalisco. In 1444 these small realms bordered the Caxcanes and Guachichiles to the north, the Guamares to the east and the Purépecha Empire to the south.

The Purépecha wars for Lake Chapala's saltpeter opened in 1480 and lasted until 1510. An army marched on Tonala, but the ruler Cihualpilli allied with the kingdom of Colliman, and her captain Coyotl helped defeat the invaders at Tlajomulco. In 1530 Pedro Almíndez Chirino passed through Tecpatitlan on Nuño de Guzmán's campaign, while Franciscans evangelized the settlement and built its first church, after which it took the name San Francisco de Tecpatitlan; Tonala submitted after a clash and was incorporated into Nueva Galicia, its ruler baptized Juana Bautista. After Guadalajara's foundation in 1535, Tonala lost its old primacy. The Mixtón War of 1541–1542, epidemics and the later Chichimeca War broke Tecuexe power, and colonial estates and parish churches, including San Francisco at Tecpatitlan, begun in 1742, took shape across the highlands.
zh:
特克帕蒂特兰是特帕蒂特兰地区的旧名，位于哈利斯科的特库埃克塞高地，处在托纳拉与更干旱的瓜马尔边地之间的通道上。特库埃克塞人使用犹他—阿兹特克语系语言，分成若干彼此独立的领主政权；特克帕蒂特兰、阿卡特克、哈洛斯托蒂特兰和亚瓦利坎都是其据点。托纳拉的纳瓦特尔语含义是太阳升起之地，也是哈利斯科中部最重要的酋长领地之一。1444年，这些小政权北接卡斯坎人和瓜奇奇尔人，东邻瓜马尔人，南面则与普雷佩查帝国接壤。

1480年，为争夺查帕拉湖畔硝石而起的普雷佩查战争爆发，一直持续到1510年。普雷佩查军队向托纳拉推进，统治者西瓦皮尔皮与科利曼王国结盟，她的将领科约特尔率军在特拉霍穆尔科击败入侵者。1530年，佩德罗·阿尔门德斯·奇里诺随努尼奥·德·古斯曼的征战经过特克帕蒂特兰，方济各会修士在定居地传教并建起第一座教堂，定居地因而得名圣弗朗西斯科·德·特克帕蒂特兰；托纳拉在一场冲突后归附，被纳入新加利西亚，女统治者受洗取名胡安娜·包蒂斯塔。1535年瓜达拉哈拉建立后，托纳拉失去旧日的首要地位。1541—1542年的米克斯顿战争、疫病以及后来的奇奇梅克战争瓦解了特库埃克塞人的力量，殖民庄园和教区教堂逐渐遍布高地，特克帕蒂特兰的圣弗朗西斯科教堂即于1742年动工。

en:
Xilotepec, whose Nahuatl name means the hill of young maize, rises in the wooded hills north of the Valley of Mexico. It was the centre of an Otomi lordship with subject towns such as Soyaniquilpan, Huichapan and Nopala, linked by trade and kinship to the Huasteca, Michoacan and the Guanajuato frontier. Acamapichtli of Tenochtitlan conquered the district in 1379, but its people later recovered their autonomy. In 1444 Xilotepec was therefore still an Otomi realm, its villages growing maize and making pottery and cloth while Chichimeca peoples held the dry country farther north.

Mexica power returned under Ahuitzotl: in 1487 a campaign against the Otomi of Xilotepec destroyed Chiapa and confirmed Tenochtitlan's rule. After the Spanish conquest colonization began in 1526, Franciscans established a doctrine, and Juan Jaramillo and later Bishop Juan de Zumárraga held encomienda interests in its farmland. When silver was discovered at Zacatecas and Guanajuato, Xilotepec became a station on the royal road carrying miners, cattle and supplies into the Bajío; Otomi warriors and settlers in turn helped the Spanish pacify that frontier and found Querétaro and Apaseo. Guamare raiders reached Xilotepec in 1569. In 1810 Otomi villagers from the province joined Miguel Hidalgo and Ignacio Allende on the insurgent road south.
zh:
希洛特佩克的纳瓦特尔语含义是嫩玉米山，位于墨西哥谷北方的林木丘陵中。它是奥托米人领主政权的中心，管辖索亚尼基尔潘、维查潘、诺帕拉等城镇，商路和亲属联系通向瓦斯特卡、米却肯和瓜纳华托边地。特诺奇蒂特兰的阿卡马皮奇特利曾于1379年征服此地，但居民后来恢复自治。因此在1444年，希洛特佩克仍是奥托米人的政权；村落种植玉米、制作陶器和织物，更北面的干旱地带则分布着奇奇梅卡诸族。

阿维索特尔在位时，墨西卡势力卷土重来：1487年，墨西卡向希洛特佩克的奥托米人开战，摧毁恰帕，并巩固了特诺奇蒂特兰的统治。西班牙征服后，殖民活动于1526年展开，方济各会在此设立传教区，胡安·哈拉米略以及后来的主教胡安·德·苏马拉加都曾在这片农地上享有委托监护权益。萨卡特卡斯和瓜纳华托发现银矿后，希洛特佩克成为王家大道上的驿站，矿工、牲畜和补给经此进入巴希奥；奥托米战士和定居者也协助西班牙人安抚这条边地，并参与建立克雷塔罗和阿帕塞奥。1569年，瓜马尔袭击者曾进抵希洛特佩克。1810年，当地奥托米村民加入米格尔·伊达尔戈和伊格纳西奥·阿连德向南推进的起义队伍。

en:
The Pame, who call themselves Xi'ui, held the rugged ranges and valleys east of the Bajío: the Rio Verde country, the Sierra Gorda and the routes toward Tamaulipas and the Huasteca. In 1444 they lived from hunting, gathering, trade and seasonal maize farming, moving between rancherías and speaking an Oto-Pamean tongue. Closer to Mesoamerica than the desert nations to the north, they traded and sometimes lived beside Nahua, Otomi and Purépecha frontier villages. Spanish colonists later called this broad country Pamería.

Pressure from Spanish ranches and allied Otomi settlements reached the Bajío edge in the 1530s. After silver was found at Zacatecas, the Chichimeca War of 1550–1600 drew Pame bands into frontier raiding; Spanish records first called them the most peaceful Chichimeca nation, but by the 1570s reported kidnappings and killings. Cattlemen entered Rio Verde after 1600, and Fray Juan Bautista de Mollinedo founded the El Palmar mission in 1617. The mountains held out until José de Escandón's 1740 campaign culminated at Media Luna, breaking Jonaz and Ximpece resistance and opening the Guanajuato–Zacatecas routes; soldiers then burned Pame villages to concentrate their people around missions. The five Franciscan churches at Jalpan, Landa, Tancoyol, Concá and Tilaco were built from 1750 to 1760 under Junípero Serra, and the missions were abandoned in 1770. Pame communities rose with the independence movement in 1810, Zenón Fernández raised insurgent colours in the Rio Verde valley, and royalists sacked Jalpan in 1819. When independence came in 1821, the Pamería remained restive.
zh:
帕梅人自称希乌伊人（Xi'ui），据有巴希奥东侧崎岖的山地和谷地，包括里奥韦尔德、谢拉戈尔达以及通往塔毛利帕斯和瓦斯特卡的道路。1444年，他们以狩猎、采集、贸易和季节性玉米种植为生，在各个小村落间迁移，使用奥托-帕梅语族的语言。与北方沙漠族群相比，他们和中美洲定居社会联系更紧，会同边境上的纳瓦人、奥托米人和普雷佩查人贸易，有时还毗邻而居。西班牙殖民者后来把这片广阔土地称为帕梅里亚。

1530年代，西班牙牧场和结盟的奥托米人定居点把压力带到巴希奥边缘。萨卡特卡斯发现银矿后，1550年至1600年的奇奇梅克战争使帕梅群体卷入边境袭掠；西班牙记载起初称他们是奇奇梅克诸族中最平和的一支，但到1570年代已有绑架和杀害西班牙人的报告。1600年后，牧牛人进入里奥韦尔德，胡安·包蒂斯塔·德·莫利内多修士1617年建立埃尔帕尔马传教所。山地则坚守更久，直到何塞·德·埃斯坎东1740年的远征在梅迪亚卢纳达到高潮，击破霍纳斯人和欣佩塞人的抵抗，打通瓜纳华托至萨卡特卡斯的道路；军队随后焚毁帕梅村落，把人口集中到传教所附近。1750年至1760年，胡尼佩罗·塞拉主持修建了哈尔潘、兰达、坦科约尔、孔卡和蒂拉科五座方济各会教堂，传教所1770年被弃置。1810年，帕梅社区随独立运动起事，塞农·费尔南德斯在里奥韦尔德谷地举起起义旗帜，保王军1819年洗劫哈尔潘。1821年独立到来时，帕梅里亚仍未真正安定。

en:
The high valleys of southern Zacatecas, around Nochistlán and Apulco and running south to the lakes of Pechichitán, were the señorío of Xicconecan. Its people, the Xiconaques, were Caxcan-speaking farmers whom the Nahuas called the Iztachichimecah, the 'white Chichimecas', for their pale skin or the whitish earth of their land. They planted seasonal maize in the valleys, hunted deer and hare, and lived in circular houses of zacate grass; their rulers Panen and Xahualotl held Teocaltiche as a tributary and warred with the neighbouring Cuxtaques, while around 1400 their tribes joined the Guamare confederacy raised against the Aztec and Purépecha empires. In 1444 Xiconecan remained free, its warriors recently hardened by the Zacateco pressure that was driving fresh Caxcan bands south from the Juchipila.

Pedro Almíndez Chirino and his men came through Tecpatitlan in 1531 and met the local chief. On 5 January 1532 the Spanish founded the first Guadalajara near Nochistlán, soon abandoned. In the Mixtón War of 1541–42 Xahualotl's son Francisco Tenamaztle led the Caxcanes, besieging Guadalajara and holding the peñol of Mixtón until the Spanish took Nochistlán and stormed the rock; Tenamaztle was captured and shipped to Spain. Raiding went on through the Chichimeca War — in 1551 the Xiconaques destroyed Diego de Ibarra's stock ranch — until Hernando Martel defeated them and, with the surviving Xiconaque and Cuxtaque families, founded the Villa de Santa María de los Lagos on 31 March 1563. Cattle and sheep haciendas then spread over the plains, with twenty thousand head by 1600, and the Real Comanja silver mine opened in 1561. The lawyer Francisco Primo de Verdad, born at Lagos, was among the first criollos to claim self-rule and died in a Mexico City dungeon in 1808; another native son, Pedro Moreno, led insurgent guerrillas until he was killed in 1817.
zh:
萨卡特卡斯南部的高地山谷，以诺奇斯特兰和阿普尔科为中心，向南一直到佩奇奇坦的湖群，是西科内坎酋邦之地。其居民希科纳克人是说卡克斯坎语的农人，纳瓦人把他们叫作伊斯特塔奇奇梅卡，即「白奇奇梅克人」，得名于他们较浅的肤色或当地泛白的碱性土地。他们在谷地种靠天吃饭的玉米，猎鹿和野兔，住圆锥形的茅草屋；君长帕年、萨瓦洛特尔让特奥卡尔蒂切纳贡，又与邻邦库克斯坦交战；约1400年，他们的部落加入为对抗阿兹特克和普雷佩查两大帝国而结成的瓜马尔联盟。1444年时西科内坎仍保持自由，萨卡特科人不断南侵、把新的卡克斯坎人群从胡奇皮拉河方向压向南方，也使这里的战士久经战阵。

1531年，佩德罗·阿尔明德斯·奇里诺一行经特克帕蒂特兰而来，与当地酋长接触。1532年1月5日，西班牙人在诺奇斯特兰附近建立第一座瓜达拉哈拉，不久即废弃。1541至1542年的米斯特翁战争中，萨瓦洛特尔之子弗朗西斯科·特纳马斯特莱率领卡克斯坎人围攻瓜达拉哈拉，据守米斯特翁山崖；西班牙人攻下诺奇斯特兰并强攻山崖，特纳马斯特莱被俘后押往西班牙。袭击在奇奇梅克战争期间持续不断——1551年希科纳克人摧毁了迭戈·德·伊瓦拉的牧场——直到埃尔南多·马特尔将其击败，并于1563年3月31日同幸存的希科纳克、库克斯塔克家族一起建立圣马里亚·德洛斯拉戈斯镇。此后牛羊庄园遍布平原，到1600年牲畜已有两万头，雷亚尔科曼哈银矿也于1561年开采。生于拉戈斯的律师弗朗西斯科·普里莫·德·贝尔达是最早主张克里奥尔人自治的人物之一，1808年死于墨西哥城的地牢；另一位本地子弟佩德罗·莫雷诺率领起义游击队作战，1817年战死。

en:
Northwestern Chihuahua, around the future district of Janos, was Jocome country. The Jocomes were probably a sub-tribe or close relatives of the Suma, and like the Janos they moved through arid mountains and basins as hunter-gatherers without fixed settlements. In 1444 autonomous bands travelled between waterholes and hunting grounds, close to Suma, Jano, Sobaipuri, Opata and Apache groups; they traded with their neighbours and sometimes joined them in raids or marriage alliances.

In 1640 Franciscans founded Nuestra Señora de la Soledad de los Janos as a mission for the Janos, Suma and related peoples, possibly near Janos or near El Paso. A native uprising destroyed it in the 1680s, by which time the Jocomes were prominent near Janos. In 1684 Suma, Janos and Jocome bands still hostile to Spain found refuge in the Chiricahua Mountains and drew closer to the Apache. In 1686 Juan Fernández de la Fuente established the Presidio de San Felipe y Santiago de Janos. The Apache were first recorded on this frontier of New Spain in 1692, and although the Franciscan mission was re-established among Janos and Jocomes in 1717, the Jocome name gradually disappeared from Spanish records, its bearers probably absorbed into Apache bands.
zh:
奇瓦瓦西北部、后来雅诺斯一带，是霍科梅人的土地。霍科梅人可能是苏马人的分支或近亲，和雅诺人一样在干旱山地与盆地中狩猎采集，没有固定居所。1444年，若干自主游群往来于水源和猎场之间，邻近苏马、雅诺、索瓦伊普里、奥帕塔和阿帕奇诸部；他们与邻部贸易，也有时共同袭掠或互通婚姻。

1640年，方济各会为雅诺人、苏马人及相关部族建立孤独圣母·德·洛斯·雅诺斯传教站，地点可能在雅诺斯附近，也可能靠近埃尔帕索。1680年代，原住民起义摧毁了传教站，此时霍科梅人已在雅诺斯附近十分活跃。1684年，仍与西班牙为敌的苏马、雅诺和霍科梅游群退守奇里卡瓦山，并与阿帕奇人日益接近。1686年，胡安·费尔南德斯·德·拉·富恩特建立圣费利佩—圣地亚哥·德·雅诺斯要塞。1692年，阿帕奇人首次在新西班牙的这道边疆留下记录；尽管传教站1717年又在雅诺人和霍科梅人中间重建，霍科梅之名仍逐渐从西班牙文书中消失，其部众大概被阿帕奇诸部吸收。

en:
Between the Sierra de Morones and the Sierra de Nochistlán, the deep Juchipila river canyon was the señorío of Xochipillan, 'the place of fair flowers'. Around 1170 Caxcan warriors of Nahuatl speech came up the canyon, drove out its earlier inhabitants, possibly Tecuexe, and made the fortified peñol of Tlaltan their capital, its citadel reachable only by a single steep stairway. Xochipillan grew into a cacicazgo of real weight, drawing tribute from Apotzolco, Xalpan, Tepechitlán and the other towns of the canyon; its farmers grew maize and cotton on the warm river terraces while its raiders harried the Zacateco and Guachichil lands to the north and east. In 1444 its lord, like the rulers of Nochistlán and Xalpa, answered to no outside power.

Cristóbal de Oñate took Tlaltan in 1530–31 and Xochipillan was granted in encomienda to Hernán Flores; Franciscans raised the canyon's first monastery around 1532. When the encomenderos' exactions grew unbearable, the last Caxcan lord, Xiuhtecuhtli, conspired with Tenamaxtle of Nochistlán and Pentacatl of Xalpa, and in 1541 the canyon rose: on 24 June the Caxcanes destroyed Pedro de Alvarado's army near Nochistlán, and the conquistador died of his wounds on 4 July. Viceroy Mendoza came in person with more than fifty thousand men and stormed the Peñón del Mixtón on 16 December 1541; Fray Antonio de Segovia then persuaded over six thousand survivors to come down peacefully, and Apozol and Juchipila were refounded. The Franciscan convent and hospital of 1542 were followed by the parish church of San Francisco in 1627, and from 1548 Juchipila governed a vast alcaldía mayor; in 1804 Charles IV transferred it from the Intendancy of Guadalajara to that of Zacatecas. When the insurgency came in 1810, the Caxcan and mestizo families of the canyon joined it and held to the cause until 1821.
zh:
在莫罗内斯山与诺奇斯特兰山之间，幽深的胡奇皮拉河谷是索奇皮尔兰酋邦之地，名字意为「名花之乡」。约1170年，操纳瓦特尔语的卡克斯坎武士沿河谷而上，逐走早先的居民，他们可能是特克塞人；卡克斯坎人把设防的特拉尔坦山崖作为都城——崖顶城堡只有一条陡峭的阶梯可通。索奇皮尔兰发展成举足轻重的酋邦，向阿波特索尔科、哈尔潘、特佩奇特兰及河谷诸镇征收贡赋；农人在温暖的河阶上种玉米和棉花，战士则北上东征，袭扰萨卡特科人和瓜奇奇尔人的土地。1444年时，它的君长与诺奇斯特兰、哈尔帕的统治者一样，不受任何外来势力统属。

1530至1531年，克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥尼亚特攻下特拉尔坦，索奇皮尔兰被作为委托监护地封给埃尔南·弗洛雷斯；方济各会士约在1532年建起河谷里的第一座修道院。由于监护主的盘剥不堪忍受，末代卡克斯坎君长休伊特莱库特利与诺奇斯特兰的特纳马斯特莱、哈尔帕的彭塔卡特尔密谋，1541年河谷举事：6月24日卡克斯坎人在诺奇斯特兰附近歼灭佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多的军队，这位征服者7月4日伤重而死。总督门多萨亲率五万多大军前来，1541年12月16日强攻米斯特翁山崖；随后修士安东尼奥·德·塞戈维亚说服六千多名幸存者和平下山，阿波索尔和胡奇皮拉得以重建。1542年方济各会修道院和医院设立，1627年又建成圣方济各堂区教堂；自1548年起，胡奇皮拉统辖一片幅员辽阔的大市政官区，1804年卡洛斯四世把它从瓜达拉哈拉都督区划归萨卡特卡斯都督区。1810年独立起义爆发后，河谷的卡克斯坎和混血家族纷纷投身起义，一直坚持到1821年。

en:
The Rarámuri—whom the Spanish would call Tarahumara—held the pine-clad ridges and gorges of the Sierra Madre Occidental, a maze of high mesas and deep canyons in western Chihuahua. They spoke a Uto-Aztecan tongue and farmed maize and beans on the canyon floors and benches and gathering at corn-beer feasts called tesgüinadas. Scattered homesteads of logs or stone, sometimes caves, answered to no lord beyond their own elders, and in 1444 the sierra, its forests and its deep barrancas belonged entirely to them.

Jesuits made the first contact in 1606, and Juan Fonte opened the mission of San Pablo Balleza on the southern edge of their country; Fonte died with seven fellow Jesuits in the Tepehuán rising of 1616, and the mission stood empty for more than a decade. The great silver strike at Parral in 1631 pulled slavers, ranchers and missionaries into the eastern valleys, and missions soon multiplied at Satevó, Huejotitán, San Felipe and Las Bocas. In 1648 the Rarámuri burned San Francisco de Borja. Teporaca, a war captain who had once helped build the Spanish Villa de Aguilar, then led a still greater rising across the Papigochi valley in 1652; royal troops under Diego Guajardo Fajardo crushed it, and on 4 March 1653 Teporaca was hanged from the tallest pine at Tomochi. Mountain bands drove out priests and settlers until the Jesuits returned in the 1670s and baptised thousands, and further wars in 1696–1698 ended in defeat, yet the high sierra was never truly conquered. When the Jesuits were expelled in 1767 the Franciscans could not sustain their missions, and the Rarámuri withdrew deeper into the barrancas, keeping their language and their ways. The independence wars of the 1810s scarcely reached those heights, and in 1821 their mountains became part of Mexico.
zh:
拉拉穆里人——西班牙人后来称他们为塔拉乌马拉人——据有西马德雷山脉松涛覆盖的山脊与沟壑，那是西奇瓦瓦一片由高山台地和深峡构成的迷宫。他们操犹他—阿兹特克语族的语言，在谷底和台地上种植玉米、菜豆，并在名为特斯吉纳达的玉米酒宴上聚会。散布各处的原木或石砌小屋（有时就是洞穴）只听命于本族长老，不认任何外来君长；1444年，整片群山、森林和深谷都完全属于他们。

耶稣会士1606年首次与他们接触，胡安·丰特在其南缘建起圣巴勃罗·巴列萨传教站；丰特在1616年的特佩瓦起义中与七名同会修士一同遇难，传教站空废了十几年。1631年帕拉尔发现大银矿，奴隶贩子、牧场主和传教士随之涌入东部谷地，萨特沃、韦霍蒂坦、圣费利佩和拉斯博卡斯很快建起传教站。1648年，拉拉穆里人焚毁圣弗朗西斯科·德·博尔哈传教站。曾协助西班牙人修建阿吉拉尔镇的军事首领特波拉卡，于1652年在整个帕皮戈奇谷领导了规模更大的起义；迭戈·瓜哈尔多·法哈多率领王室军队将其镇压，1653年3月4日，特波拉卡被绞死在托莫奇最高的松树上。高山上的族人把神父和移民赶走，直到1670年代耶稣会士才得以返回，为数千人施洗；1696至1698年的又一次战争仍告失败，但高高的群山从未被真正征服。1767年耶稣会被驱逐后，方济各会无力维持各传教站，拉拉穆里人退入更深的峡谷，保住了自己的语言和生活方式。1810年代的独立战争几乎没有波及这些高山，1821年他们的群山成为墨西哥的一部分。

en:
The Náayeri—known to the Spanish as the Cora—held the knotted canyons and high mesas of the Sierra del Nayar, a rugged mountain fastness between the Pacific plain and the central plateau. In their scattered ranchos they grew maize, beans and amaranth and answered to no outside lord; the Muutzisti, Teacuacitzti and Ateacari lived by their own ancient laws, a pagan world at the very edge of Mesoamerica. In 1444 their steep gorges had never seen a Spaniard, and the traders' roads kept to the lowlands below.

Tradition dates the uniting of the three tribes into the kingdom of Huacica, also called Xécora, to 1493, when Na'ayarij fixed his capital at Sacaymuta. When Nuño de Guzmán's conquistadores pushed into Nueva Galicia in the early 1530s, Na'ayarij defeated them in several fights, and in 1536 he sealed an alliance with the Huichol king Goaxicar; he himself accepted baptism in 1531, but the mountain kingdom kept its freedom. For nearly two hundred years the Cora remained a pagan island in a sea of Christian Indians—no mine, hacienda or mission took root, while the kings Huaynoli, Yocuari, Urysty and Tonati held the high sierra and raided Acaponeta, Aztatlán and Sentispac on the frontier below. A Spanish expedition failed in 1716, and in 1720 Tonati met the viceroy Baltasar de Zúñiga in person and refused to lay down his arms even for the promised right to buy salt at Mexcaltitán. The Spaniards returned in force in 1722: at the Mesa del Nayar the Cora and Huichol army under Tlahuitole was broken and its captain killed during the siege, while Tonati was carried off to Guadalajara and died in its prison in 1725. Friars and missions entered the sierra at last, though the old rites lived on beneath the new faith. After the independence wars of 1810–1821 the mountains of Xécora passed with New Spain into independent Mexico.
zh:
塞科拉的纳亚里人——西班牙人称之为科拉人——据有奈亚尔山区交错的峡谷与高台地，那是横亘在太平洋沿岸平原与中央高原之间的一片险峻山地。他们在分散的村落里种植玉米、菜豆和苋米，不认任何外来君长；穆齐斯蒂、特阿夸齐斯特和阿特阿卡利三个部落按古老的规矩生活，是美索亚美利加最边缘的一个异教世界。1444年，他们陡峭的峡谷还未见过西班牙人，商路也只在山下低地间绕行。

按民间口传传统，三个部落在1493年由纳亚里统一为瓦西卡王国，又称塞科拉，定都萨凯穆塔。1530年代初，努尼奥·德·古斯曼的征服者队伍攻入新加利西亚，纳亚里数度将其击败，又于1536年与维乔尔人的国王戈阿西卡尔结盟；他本人在1531年接受了洗礼，山中的王国却保住了自由。此后近两百年间，科拉人始终是「基督教印第安人汪洋中的一座异教孤岛」——矿场、庄园和传教站无一能在此扎根，瓦伊诺利、约夸里、乌里斯蒂、托纳蒂诸王相继据守高山，不时下山袭扰边境地带的阿卡波内塔、阿斯特兰和森蒂斯帕克。1716年一支西班牙远征队无功而返；1720年，托纳蒂亲自会见总督巴尔塔萨尔·德·苏尼加，拒绝了以放下武器换取在梅斯卡尔蒂坦购盐之权的条件。1722年西班牙人大举重来，在奈亚尔台地击溃了由特拉维托莱率领的科拉—维乔尔联军，特拉维托莱在围困中战死，托纳蒂则被押往瓜达拉哈拉，1725年死于狱中。修士和传教站终于进入山区，但古老的仪式在新信仰的掩盖下延续。经过1810至1821年的独立战争，塞科拉的群山随新西班牙并入独立的墨西哥。

en:
The Acaxee held the gorges and pine ridges east of Culiacán, a mountain fastness the Spaniards would call Topia, running some two hundred kilometres through what is now eastern Sinaloa and western Durango. Sedentary farmers of maize, beans, squash, chile and cotton, they also hunted and fished where the steep slopes gave poor harvests, living in autonomous extended-family villages that followed elders in peace and chose war leaders only in danger. A warlike people, they kept a constant frontier with the Xixime to the south and the Tepehuán beyond the eastern ranges, and Spanish chroniclers would later accuse them of eating foes taken in battle—a charge never proven. In 1444 their canyons knew no foreign rule.

The first Spanish foothold was the mining town of Topia, founded in 1564; the rich silver veins struck in the 1580s drew encomenderos, slaves and forced Acaxee labour, while epidemics in 1576–1577, 1590 and 1596–1597 reduced the people to a few thousand. In 1600 the Jesuit Hernando de Santarén toured the sierra with Captain Diego de Ávila, resettling the Acaxee into mission towns, burning their idols and cutting their hair. In December 1601 the messianic leader Perico rose, blending Christian and native promises of deliverance: within weeks some fifty Spaniards lay dead, the mining camps and forty churches were burned, and forty settlers were besieged in the church at San Andrés until relief arrived from Durango. The mines stood still for two years, until a Spanish army with Indian allies broke the rising in 1603; Perico and forty-eight war leaders were executed and the surviving rebels sold into slavery. A smallpox epidemic in 1607, arriving with Halley's Comet, extinguished what remained of the Acaxee cause, though a few fought on in the Tepehuán revolt of 1616. As a people the Acaxee then vanish from the records, their mountains left to missions, haciendas and the silver mines of Nueva Vizcaya; the Jesuits departed with the expulsion of 1767, and in 1821 the old Topia sierra became part of independent Mexico.
zh:
阿卡塞人据有库利亚坎以东的峡谷与松脊，这片西班牙人日后称作托皮亚的山地纵长约两百公里，纵贯今锡那罗亚东部与杜兰戈西部。他们是定居农人，种植玉米、菜豆、南瓜、辣椒和棉花，但陡坡上收成不足，也靠渔猎贴补生计；各家族村落各自为政，平时听从长老，遇有战事才共举军事首领。这是个好战的族群，与南边的希希梅人和东山岭外的特佩瓦人长年交战，西班牙编年史家后来还声称他们食用战场上的敌尸——此说始终没有证据。1444年，他们的峡谷尚不知外来统治为何物。

西班牙人的第一个据点是1564年建立的矿业城镇托皮亚；1580年代打到的富银矿引来监护主、奴隶和被迫下矿的阿卡塞劳工，而1576至1577年、1590年、1596至1597年的几场瘟疫使人口减至仅剩数千。1600年，耶稣会士埃尔南多·德·桑塔伦偕队长迭戈·德·阿维拉巡视山区，把阿卡塞人迁入传教村镇，焚毁他们的神像、剃去长发。1601年12月，融合天主教与本土信仰、许诺得救降福的弥赛亚式首领佩里科率众起事：几周之内约五十名西班牙人被杀，矿营和四十座教堂被焚，四十名殖民者被围困在圣安德烈斯的教堂里，直到杜兰戈的援军赶到。银矿停采了两年，1603年西班牙军队及其印第安盟友才将起义镇压，佩里科和四十八名军事首领被处死，幸存的起事者被卖为奴。1607年的天花伴着哈雷彗星一同到来，抹去了阿卡塞人抗争最后的痕迹，只有少数人后来参加了1616年的特佩瓦起义。作为一个族群，阿卡塞人自此从记载中消失，群山留给了传教站、庄园和新比斯开亚的银矿；1767年耶稣会被逐，1821年，古老的托皮亚山区成为独立墨西哥的一部分。

en:
The Mayo, who call themselves Yoreme, held the hot coastal plain between the Mayo and Fuerte rivers, where seasonal floodwater made maize fields possible and the Gulf shallows supplied fish. Their Cahita speech was close to that of the Yaqui, and the river villages traded and intermarried while also guarding their autonomy. The country around later Navojoa and Huatabampo was densely enough settled to support mission towns, yet in 1444 it remained outside the empires of central Mexico, its life governed by the river, the rains, and the fishing coast.

Diego de Guzmán made the first recorded Spanish contact in 1533, and Francisco de Ulloa reached the mouth of the Mayo in 1539. Jesuits entered the region in 1591, and after Diego Martínez de Hurdaide's campaign the Yoreme submitted in 1599. In 1614 Pedro Méndez and Diego de la Cruz founded Santa María de Navojoa and the Santa Cruz del Mayo missions, with a school for Indigenous boys established there in 1622. Juan Calixto's Cahita rising swept through the neighboring Yaqui and Mayo country in 1740 before it was crushed, and the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 replaced the missionaries with secular and Franciscan clergy. The wars after 1810 were far away, but in 1821 the river towns passed with New Spain into independent Mexico.
zh:
马约人自称约雷梅，占据马约河与富埃尔特河之间炎热的沿海平原。季节性洪水让这里能够种植玉米，加利福尼亚湾浅滩则提供鱼获。他们的卡伊塔语与亚基语相近，河畔村落之间既贸易通婚，也各自守护自治。后来纳沃华和瓦塔万波周围的土地人口足够稠密，足以支撑传教村镇；但在1444年，这里仍不受墨西哥中部诸帝国统治，生活由河流、雨水和捕鱼海岸决定。

迭戈·德·古斯曼1533年留下有记载的首次西班牙接触，弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚1539年抵达马约河口。耶稣会士1591年进入这一地区，迭戈·马丁内斯·德·乌尔戴德用兵之后，约雷梅人于1599年臣服。1614年，佩德罗·门德斯和迭戈·德·拉克鲁斯建立纳沃华圣玛利亚与马约河圣克鲁斯等传教村，1622年又在纳沃华为原住民男孩设立学校。1740年，胡安·卡利斯托领导的卡伊塔起事波及相邻的亚基和马约地区，随后被镇压；1767年耶稣会被逐，传教士改由世俗教士和方济各会士接替。1810年以后的独立战争离这里遥远，但1821年，这些河畔村镇随新西班牙转入独立的墨西哥。

en:
The Opatería, the Opata country, ran from the Sonora River valley toward the western canyons of the Sierra Madre Occidental. It was not a single kingdom but a chain of independent agricultural towns along the Sonora, Moctezuma, Bavispe, and Aros rivers, surrounded by scattered houses and irrigated fields of maize, beans, squash, and cotton. Opata traders carried corn and woven blankets toward the Zuni and Concho countries in exchange for turquoise, while sharing hunting and fishing grounds with the Yaqui, Mayo, and Seri. In the rougher eastern hills, the Jova lived more by hunting and gathering. In 1444 the valley statelets remained self-governing, densely settled for the Sonoran frontier, and unconnected to the empires of central Mexico.

Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca passed through in 1538 and named one valley town Corazones. Francisco Vázquez de Coronado stationed eighty men at San Jerónimo de los Corazones in 1540, but abuse under his officer Alcaraz provoked an Opata rising in 1541; the post was destroyed and the Spaniards withdrew, while fierce resistance to Francisco de Ibarra in 1565 again checked conquest. Epidemics from 1601 to 1625 weakened the valley towns, and after Diego Martínez de Hurdaide's bloody campaign near Mátape in 1622, Jesuits under Pedro Méndez began missions in 1628, numbering twenty-two by 1688. Many Opata became Spanish allies against the Apache, yet forced mine labor and land disputes fed conspiracies in 1681 and 1696 and the broad native rising under Juan Calixto in 1740. Arizpe became capital of Sonora in 1778 and seat of the bishopric in 1783. By 1800 many Opata were Christians, vaqueros, and miners; the Bavispe revolt of 1820 spread through Sahuaripa, Arivechi, and Tonichi before royal troops executed its leaders Dorame and Espíritu on the eve of Mexican independence in 1821.
zh:
奥帕塔人之地被称为奥帕塔里亚，从索诺拉河谷一直延伸到西马德雷山脉西缘的峡谷地带。它不是统一王国，而是沿索诺拉河、蒙特苏马河、巴维斯佩河和阿罗斯河分布的一连串独立农业村镇；镇外散布着民居，以及灌溉种植玉米、豆类、南瓜和棉花的田地。奥帕塔商人带着玉米和织毯前往祖尼人与孔乔人地区交换绿松石，也与亚基人、马约人和塞里人共用狩猎场和渔场。东部崎岖山地的霍瓦人则更多依靠狩猎采集。1444年时，这些河谷小邦仍由本地人自治，在索诺拉边陲算得上人口稠密，也不属于墨西哥中部诸帝国。

阿尔瓦·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡1538年经过此地，把一座河谷城镇命名为科拉索内斯。1540年，弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科罗纳多在圣赫罗尼莫·德·洛斯科拉索内斯驻扎八十人；军官阿尔卡拉斯的虐待引发奥帕塔人1541年起事，据点被毁，西班牙人撤退。1565年，他们又猛烈抵抗弗朗西斯科·德·伊瓦拉的远征，使征服再度停滞。1601年至1625年的疫病削弱了各河谷城镇；1622年迭戈·马丁内斯·德·乌尔戴德在马塔佩附近打赢血战之后，佩德罗·门德斯率领耶稣会士于1628年开始建立传教区，到1688年已有二十二处。许多奥帕塔人后来成为西班牙人对抗阿帕奇人的盟友，但强制矿役和土地争端仍引发1681年、1696年的密谋，以及1740年胡安·卡利斯托领导的广泛原住民起事。阿里斯佩1778年成为索诺拉首府，1783年又成为主教驻地。到1800年，许多奥帕塔人已是基督徒、牧工和矿工；1820年，巴维斯佩的兵变蔓延到萨瓦里帕、阿里韦奇和托尼奇，最终被王军镇压，首领多拉梅和埃斯皮里图被处决，仅仅一年后，墨西哥便在1821年独立。

en:
Tsushima is a chain of mountainous islands in the Korea Strait, lying about halfway between Kyushu and the Korean peninsula. Its fields were too few and thin to feed the islanders on rice, and they fished the strait and sailed north and south to buy grain, as a third-century Chinese account already records. The Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281 struck Tsushima before Kyushu: the local commander So Sukekuni was killed in the fighting and the islands were briefly occupied. The So clan then made its home here and turned sea power into diplomacy. A Joseon army landed in 1419 to suppress wokou and withdrew after a month of fighting, and in 1443 So Sadamori concluded the Gyehae agreement, pledging to curb the pirates in return for a near-monopoly of Japanese trade with Busan. In 1444 Tsushima was therefore a fortified sea frontier whose lords lived by the Korean trade rather than their own soil.

That trade kept drawing Tsushima into Korean disorders. When Japanese residents rose at the Three Ports in the Sampo disturbance of 1510, a So relief force was beaten and the residents expelled, and relations were not restored until 1512; an agreement in 1547 confined the trade to Busan and the clan to twenty ships a year. In 1592 the So tried in vain to head off Hideyoshi's invasion of Korea, and during the war Tsushima served as the relay between Busan and the Nagoya headquarters in Hizen. Although the clan joined the western army at Sekigahara in 1600, Ieyasu confirmed its domain, rated at 100,000 koku though its rice crop came to less than 30,000, because he needed its Korean channel. Even under the seclusion laws the So kept their trading house at Busan, guided the Joseon embassies to Edo and handled the shogunate's Korean correspondence, some of it forged until the Yanagawa affair exposed the practice. The Confucian scholar Amenomori Hoshu, fluent in Chinese and Korean and ranked with Arai Hakuseki among Kinoshita Jun'an's ten foremost pupils, spent his career in the domain's Korean service.
zh:
对马是朝鲜海峡中一串多山岛屿，大致位于九州与朝鲜半岛中间。岛上耕地稀少贫瘠，居民一向靠海峡渔业为生，还乘船南北往返购粮，3世纪的中国史书《魏志倭人传》已有这样的记载。1274年和1281年元军两次侵日，都先攻对马：当地将领宗助国迎战阵亡，岛屿一度被占。宗氏随后在岛上立足，把海上力量转化为外交资本。1419年，朝鲜为镇压倭寇派大军登陆，交战一个月后撤退；宗贞盛又在1443年与朝鲜订立嘉吉条约，承诺约束海盗，换取日本对釜山贸易的近乎独占。因此1444年的对马虽是设防海疆，宗氏的生计却系于对朝贸易而非岛上田土。

这条贸易线也一再把对马卷入朝鲜的动荡。1510年，居留三浦的日本人起事，是为三浦之乱；宗氏援军战败，日侨被逐，双方往来直到1512年才恢复。1547年的约定又把贸易限定在釜山，宗氏每年只准派船二十艘。1592年，宗氏试图阻止丰臣秀吉侵朝未果，开战后对马成了釜山与肥前名护屋大本营之间的中继地。1600年关原之战宗氏虽加入西军，德川家康仍承认其领地，按十万石格定级，尽管其实际稻米产出不足三万石，为的是借重宗氏的对朝渠道。锁国之后，宗氏照旧在釜山经营倭馆，引导朝鲜通信使前往江户，承办幕府的对朝文书，其中有些国书经过篡改，直到柳川一件才败露。儒者雨森芳洲通晓汉语和朝鲜语，与新井白石同列木下顺庵门下「十哲」，一生在对马藩的对朝交涉机构任职。

en:
Haicheng lies behind the head of Liaodong Bay, where the Liao River winds through reed marshes into the Bohai Sea. Downstream at Niuzhuang the river reached the sea in Liao and Jin times, and cargo boats called niuzi crowded the anchorage so thickly that the place took its name from them. In 1376 the Ming sited the Haizhou Guard on the old Linming county ground near Niuzhuang under the Liaodong Regional Military Commission at Liaoyang. In 1444 it was a country of guard camps and fishing harbours, and the Liao mouth was one of the few links between inland Manchuria and the sea.

The guard submitted to the Later Jin with Liaoyang in 1621. The future Pingnan Prince Shang Kexi was born in the Haizhou Guard in 1604. He rode with Mao Wenlong's Dongjiang army, where his father was killed in the fighting, and in 1634 he crossed to the Later Jin with his men, a year after the Gaizhou officers Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming had done the same. Made Pingnan Prince in 1649, he led the Qing conquest of Guangdong and held Guangzhou through the feudatories' revolt, loyal to the court while rebel forces overran the province; in 1676 his son Shang Zhixin rose for Wu Sangui and confined him in his mansion, and he died the same year.

In 1644 Niuzhuang became one of nine banner garrison posts founded beyond Shanhai Pass, its city-officer controlling the shipping lanes of the Liao and Taizi and the ports at their mouth; nine years later the old Haizhou guard became Haicheng County. Grain from the Liao valley went out through those ports, and by 1817 the Mogouying anchorage under the Niuzhuang garrison shipped 400,000 to 500,000 shi of grain a year, more than any other seaport in Liaodong.
zh:
海城位于辽东湾湾顶内侧，辽河穿过芦荡蜿蜒注入渤海。下游的牛庄一带，辽金时辽河在附近入海，叫做「牛子」的商船云集停泊，牛庄也因这些牛子船得名。1376年，明朝在牛庄附近的旧临溟县地设置海州卫，归驻辽阳的辽东都指挥使司节制。1444年，这里遍布卫城与渔港，辽河入海口是辽东腹地通往海上为数不多的通道。

1621年辽阳失守，海州卫随入后金。后来的平南王尚可喜1604年就出生在海州卫。他随毛文龙的东江军征战，父亲也在军中战死；1634年，他率部渡海归降后金，比盖州籍将领孔有德、耿仲明晚了一年。1649年受封平南王后，他领兵打下广东，镇守广州；三藩之乱时他忠于清廷，1676年其子尚之信发兵响应吴三桂，把他困在府中，他同年死去。

1644年，牛庄成为关外最早设立的九处八旗城守官驻地之一，城守官管辖辽河、太子河的航道和入海口各码头；九年后海州改置海城县。辽河流域的粮米顺河运到海口，到1817年，归牛庄驻防管辖的没沟营口岸每年输出粮食四五十万石，为辽东各海口之冠。

en:
The wooded valley of the Tumen, east of the Changbai, was the country of the Maolian Jurchens; 'maolian' meant 'horse' in their language. They came of the same Hurga stock as the Jianzhou and were long joined by marriage and alliance, and the Maolian Guard with the Jianzhou Guard made up the main body of the Jianzhou Jurchens. In 1405 their chief Ba'ersun travelled to the Ming court with sixty-four clansmen and received the guard seal. Korea killed him in 1410, and the next year the Ming gave the guard to Mengge Buhua of the Jianzhou chief's house. Korea's campaign up the Pozhu River in 1433 broke the Jurchen guards of the lower Tumen and took their settlements, and many survivors followed Li Manzhu west to the Hun River. In 1444 the old Maolian lands were half-emptied country, the clans left along the river living as 'submitted barbarians' on Korea's border while Jianzhou still claimed them as kin.

The remnant clans came to be called the Warka, pressed between Korea, the Ula and the rising Jianzhou. In 1607 Cemuhe, lord of Feiyou on the Tumen, offered his city to Nurhaci, who sent his brother Šurhaci with an army to bring the people away. Ula troops sent to stop them were routed at Wujieyan near Korean Jongseong, their commander Bokdo killed, and the Ula gave up the Tumen valley. Over the following decades the Warka clans were enrolled in the Eight Banners. Under the Qing the country became a closed imperial reserve for ginseng and sable; from 1653 it was governed from Ningguta, and in 1714 an assistant commandant was posted at Hunchun to watch the Tumen line, his walled town begun the following year.
zh:
长白山以东、图们江两岸的林海，是毛怜女真人的故土，「毛怜」在女真语中意为「马」。他们与建州同出胡里改部，世代通婚结盟，毛怜卫与建州卫同为建州女真的主体。1405年，其首领把儿逊率六十四人入朝，明廷设毛怜卫，赐以诰印；1410年把儿逊被朝鲜所杀，次年明廷改以建州酋长世家的猛哥不花领卫事。1433年，朝鲜发动婆猪江之战，图们江下游的女真卫所被摧毁、定居点被占，残余部众随李满住西迁浑河流域。1444年的毛怜旧地人烟稀少，留在图们江沿岸的各部作为「藩胡」住在朝鲜边境，建州则仍以宗亲之名声称管辖他们。

这些遗部后来被称为瓦尔喀，夹在朝鲜、乌拉与兴起的建州之间。1607年，图们江畔蜚优城主策穆特黑举城投靠努尔哈赤，努尔哈赤派弟弟舒尔哈齐带兵前往接人。乌拉出兵截击，在朝鲜钟城附近的乌碣岩被建州军击败，主帅博克多阵亡，乌拉势力就此退出图们江流域。此后数十年间，瓦尔喀各部陆续被编入八旗。入清以后，这片地方划为封禁的皇家采参、猎貂之地，1653年起归宁古塔昂邦章京统辖；1714年，清廷在珲春设置协领，戍守图们江一线，协领衙门和城垣次年动工。

en:
The Fuerhe is forest country of the northern Changbai, where the Mudan and the Erdao Songhua rise among wooded ridges. The river takes its name from the Manchu word for poplar, after the tall stands on its banks. Around 698 Da Zuorong built his first capital at Aodong on the upper Mudan, and the Balhae court stayed there for fifty-seven years before moving south. After the Khitan overthrew Balhae in 926 the country became Jurchen hunting ground, and under the Ming it was counted among the lands of the Jianzhou Guard. When the Jianzhou clans drifted southwest to the Hun and Susu valleys in the 1430s, the woods swallowed their old trails: in 1444 only scattered bands wintered here, living on ginseng, sable and timber, with no walled town in the province.

Nurhaci drew these highland bands into his new order during his unification of the Jianzhou, from his first campaign in 1583 to the taking of the Wanggiya in 1588. After the Qing entered China the Changbai became a forbidden mountain. In 1677 the Kangxi Emperor sent the inner grandees Wumuna and Feiyaose to offer sacrifice there, and in 1678 Changbai was enfeoffed as a mountain god with rites equal to the Five Sacred Peaks, sacrificed to twice a year. The upper valleys were then sealed for two centuries as the dynasty's dragon-vein ground; licensed parties sent out from Ningguta came into these woods to dig ginseng and trap sable, and at Ningguta downstream the Qing ran a great boatyard, building vessels for the Mudan, Sungari and Amur. In 1709 Jesuits on the imperial survey entered these forests with a government ginseng party, and in 1821 the province was still sealed woodland without a town or a county seat.
zh:
富尔河是长白山北麓的林海之地，牡丹江与二道松花江都发源于这一带的山岭之间。河名得自满语「富尔」，意为杨树，因两岸昔日白杨成林而得名。698年前后，大祚荣在牡丹江上游修筑敖东城作为渤海国的第一个都城，渤海朝廷在此驻了五十七年才南迁。926年契丹灭渤海，此地重归女真人的猎场，明代被划入建州卫之地。1430年代建州各部陆续向西南迁到浑河、苏子河流域，旧日的山道重新没入林海：1444年的这里只有零星部众过冬，以采参、猎貂和采伐为生，全境没有一座城寨。

努尔哈赤统一建州期间，自1583年起兵到1588年攻克完颜城，山地间的这些部众也被卷入他的新秩序。清朝入关之后，长白山成了封禁之山。1677年，康熙帝派内大臣武默纳、费耀色前往拜谒，1678年册封长白山之神，祀典与五岳相同，每年春秋两祭。这片上游河谷随后被封禁两百年，作为王朝的龙脉所在：持照的刨夫从宁古塔进山采参猎貂；下游的宁古塔设有清朝的大船厂，为牡丹江、松花江和黑龙江水系造船。1709年，参与官方测绘的耶稣会士随皇家采参队进入这片森林；1821年，这里仍是封禁的林海，没有城镇，也没有设治。

en:
Shilimian is the high forest of the Sikhote-Alin, the wooded ridge between the Ussuri and the Sea of Japan, where interior streams gather under Korean pine and spruce. Its camps belong to Udeghe hunters, the people Jin records called the 'wild Udegei' and the Ming counted among the Wild Jurchen. They follow elk and sable through the timber and dig ginseng on the shaded slopes, and their mountains supplied the gyrfalcons Yuan parties came to collect until the Woji rose against the exactions in 1343 and again in 1346. The Ming set up the Shilimian guard over the Suifen and Ussuri clans in 1405 and ruled through patents inherited by their headmen. In 1444, with the Nurgan commission gone, no clerk visits the mountains and the patents are family heirlooms.

Headmen still asked Beijing to confirm those patents for generations; the last recorded request to inherit the guard office reached the throne in 1566. In November 1614 a Later Jin force of five hundred struck the Yalan and Xilin roads on the seaward slope of these mountains, received the submission of two hundred households and took a thousand captives. The Qing put no garrison in the highlands, confirming Kiyakara and Udeghe headmen instead: every two years they carried sable rolls to Sanxing and came back with the imperial 'forest bounty' of cloth and silk. Through 1821 the ridges held neither walled town nor ploughed field, only camps moving after elk and sable.
zh:
失里绵是锡霍特山脉主脊上的高山林地，处在乌苏里江与日本海之间，山溪在红松和云杉林下汇流。林中营地住的是乌德盖猎人，金朝史籍称他们为「野人兀的改」，明朝将其归入野人女真。他们在密林中游猎马鹿和紫貂，在背阴坡挖掘人参；元朝不断派人进山征收海东青和紫貂，吾者野人不堪征索，于1343年、1346年两度起兵反元。1405年，明朝在绥芬河与乌苏里江一带的部族中设失里绵卫，靠头人世袭的敕书统治。1444年，奴儿干都司已撤销，再没有书吏进山，敕书成了头人家里的传代之物。

此后很久，头人仍凭敕书向朝廷请袭，最后一次见于1566年。1614年十一月，后金五百人的队伍进攻这片山地靠海一侧的雅兰、锡林二路，收降二百户，俘获千人。清朝不在高地驻军，只确认恰喀拉和乌德盖头人的职分：他们每隔两年把成卷的紫貂皮解往三姓，领回朝廷名为「赏乌林」的布匹绸缎。直到1821年，山梁上仍没有城垣和耕地，只有追着马鹿、紫貂迁徙的营地。

en:
Wolanhe is the Samarga, a 218-kilometre river that leaves the eastern face of Mount Kupol in the Sikhote-Alin and runs through a forested trough into the Tatar Strait; its Manchu name Wolan means 'girth', the strap that tightens a saddle. The estuary marks the northern edge of the Udeghe coast, with the Kema river beyond it to the north. Lower-river Udeghe and Oroch coming down from the colder shore spend the autumn at the salmon runs and the winter trapping sable in the cedar shade. The Ming set up the Wolanhe guard here in February 1408 and ruled through patents inherited by headmen; after the Nurgan commission was withdrawn no clerk ever came to inspect them. In 1444 the shore clans live by fish and fur, and Beijing is little more than a name on the patent.

Those patents still had weight long afterwards: the last Wolanhe request to confirm succession reached the capital in 1593. In November 1614 a Later Jin force of five hundred campaigned against the Yalan and Xilin roads inland of this coast, taking a thousand captives and two hundred submitted households. The Qing posted no banner garrison at the river mouth; headmen carried sable to Sanxing every other year and came back with cloth and silk. Europeans first charted this shore in 1787, when Lapérouse's two French frigates sailed north to latitude 51 and mapped the strait between the mainland and Sakhalin. No settlement followed the charts, and in 1821 the clans still came to the Samarga mouth only for the summer fishing.
zh:
斡兰河就是俄国地图上的萨马尔加河，满语称「斡兰」（又作额勒），意为勒紧马鞍的肚带，河因此得名。它发源于锡霍特山脉库波尔山东坡，穿过林莽纵谷，奔流218公里注入鞑靼海峡；河口是乌德盖人滨海分布区的北缘，再往北便是克马河。下游的乌德盖人和从更寒冷的北方海岸南下的奥罗奇人，秋天赶鲑鱼汛，冬天在冷杉林里猎紫貂。明朝1408年二月在此设斡兰河卫，凭头人世袭的敕书统治；奴儿干都司撤销后，再没有书吏前来查验。1444年，河口各部靠鱼和皮毛为生，北京对他们不过是敕书上的一个名字。

敕书在很久以后仍有分量：斡兰河卫最后一次请求袭职的文书1593年才送达京城。1614年十一月，后金五百人的队伍征讨这片海岸内侧的雅兰、锡林二路，俘获千人，收降二百户。清朝不在河口设旗营，头人每隔两年把紫貂皮送往三姓，换回布匹绸缎。1787年，欧洲人首次测绘这段海岸：拉彼鲁兹率两艘法国护卫舰北上至北纬51度，绘下了大陆与库页岛之间的海峡。海图没有带来定居者，1821年时，各部仍只在夏季渔汛时来到萨马尔加河口。

en:
Nanghar takes its name from a Yuan tribute post on northwestern Sakhalin, near Langry on the Strait of Tartary. The strait is shallow here and freezes in winter, when dog-sledges could cross its ice to the Amur estuary. This was Nivkh country. Summer fishing camps faced the coast, and when the salmon ran in winter the families moved up streams to meet them; the catch was sliced and dried in the cold air without salt, and sheds beside the winter huts held sledges, skis, boats and the dogs that pulled them. Nivkh hunters supplied sable furs. Every January or February a clan mourning a kinsman held the Bear Festival: women raised a captured cub for years like a child of the house, feasted it in ceremonial dress and sent it to the mountain gods with gifts before sacrificing it. Nivkh belief made Sakhalin itself a giant beast lying in the water, whose uneasy turns caused earthquakes.

Mongol armies fought on the island from 1264 to 1308 to shield their Nivkh allies from Ainu raiders, and Nanghar afterwards became one of three posts where Ainu elders brought tribute and took gifts, with Wuliehe in the Tym basin and Boluohe on the Poronay. The Yuan withdrew after 1320, and Ming titles from the Nurgan commission followed after 1409, so in 1444 this coast was run by Nivkh clan networks rather than any distant dynasty. That island trade outlasted all the dynastic posts, linking Manchuria, Japan and Kamchatka through Sakhalin into the eighteenth century. In 1643 Vassily Poyarkov, gathering reports at the Amur, became the first Russian writer to describe these people under the Tungus name Gilyak. After the 1689 Treaty of Nerchinsk, Qing officers entered the estuary and assessed a sable tribute by clan and village; the 1732 register counted six clans, eighteen village units and 148 households on Sakhalin. In 1787 La Perouse charted the strait and spoke with islanders in its narrow northern waters, and Ivan Kruzenshtern surveyed much of the coast in 1805. In 1808 Japanese expeditions surveyed the northern narrows and confirmed that Sakhalin was an island.
zh:
囊哈儿得名于萨哈林西北部、朗里附近鞑靼海峡沿岸的一处元朝朝贡站点。这一段海峡水浅，冬季封冻，狗橇可以踏着冰面一直走到阿穆尔河口。这里是尼夫赫人的土地。夏季渔营设在海岸，冬季鲑鱼溯流时，全家搬到上游溪边等候；捕来的鱼切成条，就着寒气风干，不加盐；冬屋旁的棚子里放着雪橇、滑雪板和船只，还有拉橇的狗。尼夫赫猎人以紫貂皮供应外来客商。每年一月或二月，有亲属亡故的氏族举办熊祭：妇女把捕来的幼熊当家中孩子一般养上几年，再给熊穿上礼服、设宴饯行，带着礼物送它回到山神那里，然后献祭。在尼夫赫人的观念里，萨哈林本身是一头伏在水中的巨兽，它不安地翻身就引发地震。

1264年至1308年，蒙古为庇护尼夫赫同盟、抵御阿伊努人来袭而多次用兵岛上；战后囊哈儿成为三处朝贡站点之一，阿伊努长老在此进贡方物、领受回赐，另外两处是特姆河流域的兀列河和波罗奈河畔的波罗河。1320年后元朝撤离，1409年后明朝又以奴儿干职衔维系当地，所以1444年时这片海岸由尼夫赫氏族网络自行管理，不受远方王朝节制。海岛贸易比所有王朝站点都长寿，以萨哈林为枢纽连接满洲、日本和堪察加的网络一直维持到18世纪。1643年，瓦西里·波亚尔科夫在阿穆尔河畔收集传闻，成为第一个用通古斯名称「吉利亚克」记载这些居民的俄国人。1689年《尼布楚条约》后，清朝官员进入河口，按氏族和村落征收紫貂贡，1732年的册籍登记了萨哈林岛上的6个氏族、18个村单位和148户人。1787年，拉彼鲁兹测绘鞑靼海峡，在北部窄水附近与岛民交谈；1805年，克鲁森施滕考察了大部分海岸。1808年，日本探险队测绘北部狭窄水道，确认萨哈林是一座岛屿。

en:
Tulutingshan is the Chinese name for the Turan Range, three hundred kilometres of larch and spruce taiga raised above the Zeya and Bureya hunting grounds. The people most at home in these valleys were Solon Evenki, who herded reindeer, camped on the high passes and trapped sable through the long winter. Ming rule over the country went no further than seals and patents granted to local headmen, and after the court pulled its officers back from the Amur the patents were never inspected again. In 1444 the range belonged to the hunters and to the fur trade.

Hong Taiji's armies brought the Solon country to the Qing. Some bands had submitted in 1634, but the Evenk chief Bombogor kept the field with Solon and Daur followers; his five hundred men met two Manchu regiments at the Gualar, and in 1640 the Manchus took four Evenk fortresses, Yakesa among them, and carried off droves of horses, cattle and pelts. Bombogor fled into Mongolia, was run down near Qiluotai and was executed at Mukden. Cossacks out of the Lena reached the Amur in 1643 and demanded sable tribute from the same clans until Albazin fell and the Treaty of Nerchinsk fixed the border in 1689. The Qing then registered the Evenki clans as banner companies, owing a yearly quota of sable pelts and service on the frontier patrols. The high taiga grew no towns through 1821.
zh:
土鲁亭山是图腊纳山的汉名，这条长约三百公里的山岭横在结雅河与布列亚河猎场的上方，满坡落叶松和云杉。最熟悉这些山谷的是索伦鄂温克人，他们牧放驯鹿，在高山隘口扎营，趁漫长的冬天进林捕紫貂。明朝对这里的统治不过是给头人颁发印信敕书，朝廷从黑龙江撤回官员后，敕书再也无人查验。1444年的山岭属于猎人，也属于貂皮生意。

皇太极的军队征服了索伦之地。一些部落1634年已经归附，鄂温克首领博木博果尔仍率索伦、达斡尔部众抵抗，他的五百人与两旗满洲兵交战；1640年，清军连克鄂温克人的四座城寨，雅克萨也在其中，掠走大批马牛和皮货。博木博果尔逃入蒙古，在半途被追上擒获，押往盛京处死。从勒拿河方向来的哥萨克1643年抵达黑龙江，向这些氏族强征貂贡，直到阿尔巴津陷落、1689年《尼布楚条约》划定边界。清朝随后把鄂温克氏族编入佐领，每年按额交纳貂皮、服役巡边。直到1821年，高山泰加林里也没有立起城镇。

en:
Tunhe is the valley of the Tangwang, the Jin-dynasty Tun river, which gathers the streams of the Xiao Hinggan forests and runs south some five hundred li into the Songhua above Yilan. At its mouth stood the walled town of Punuli, one of the Five Nations of the raw Jurchen, on the Liao 'falcon road' that carried gyrfalcons and sable to the Khitan court. Under the Jin the same town was the Tunhe moung-an, and under the Mongols the Taowen myriarchy, one of the five Jurchen myriarchies of the lower Sungari; its earthworks have yielded Liao, Jin, Yuan, Ming and Qing finds in turn, rare for a site on the Amur. Ming maps called the water the Tuowan and set a loose-reign guard there, the Chengtaowen, with a post station on the river road to Nurgan.

By the 1440s the guard had lapsed. Two sister myriarchies, the Hurka under Ahacu and the Odoli under Möngke Temür, had moved southeast to become the Jianzhou guards, from whom Nurhaci and his Later Jin came, and the Taowen townspeople scattered into the south-moving clans; only fishing and herding Jurchen stockades remained along the banks. For the rest of the period the valley was a Qing sealed hunting ground, its ginseng and sable a banner reserve. The old city dwindled to the fishing village of Boorha, with no garrison or magistrate placed on the river, and in 1821 the Tun still flowed through empty forest without a walled town.
zh:
屯河即今汤旺河，金代正名屯河，又叫涛温水，汇小兴安岭诸溪南流五百里，在汤原汇入松花江。河口的双河古城，本是辽代生女真五国部之一盆奴里的城寨，正当辽国索取海东青、貂皮的「鹰路」之上。金代在这里设屯河猛安，元代又置桃温军民万户府，为松花江下游五个女真万户府之一；同一道城垣里先后出土辽、金、元、明、清各代遗物，这在黑龙江流域很少见。明代河名写作托温江，旧城设羁縻的成讨温卫，还是通往奴儿干的海西东水陆城道上的托温城站。

到1440年代，卫所已经名存实亡。与它并列的胡里改、斡朵里两个万户府，已在阿哈出、猛哥帖木儿率领下东南迁走，后来建成建州三卫，努尔哈赤和他的后金就出在这一支；桃温旧城的部众离散南下，河谷两岸只剩打鱼放牧的女真木寨。清代这里始终是封禁的猎场，山中的人参与貂皮都是旗内的采捕之利，旧城退化成名叫布尔和噶珊的渔村，河边不设官、不驻兵。1821年时，屯河仍在空旷的林莽中流淌，河畔没有一座城。

en:
Edala takes its name from the Tala, the 'open field' river of the Manchu gazetteers, which winds through wooded hills southwest of Ningguta, between the Zhangguangcai ridges and the upper Mudan. In 1407 the Ming created the Dala River Guard for the Jurchen clans of this valley, one of the loose jimi guards posted between the Sungari and the Eastern Sea. They raised millet in the river bottoms, hunted sable and gathered ginseng in the surrounding woj, the great forests, and carried their pelts to the Ming border markets. In 1444 their chiefs held Ming patents, but the clans looked to the Hūlun confederation on the middle Sungari, the line that later produced the kingdom of Ula.

Buyan took the title beile and founded Ula in 1561, and within two generations it was one of the four great Hūlun states, with the Tala country under its rule. The valley's fate was settled by Ula's wars with Nurhaci of Jianzhou. In 1593 the Yehe gathered a nine-tribe host against him and were broken at Gure; Bujantai, the prince of Ula, was captured and spent three years among the Jianzhou before Nurhaci sealed the peace with marriages and sent him home to rule. Bujantai then took the title khan and leagued with the Yehe and the Mongols. After a second defeat at Wujieyan in 1607, Nurhaci marched thirty thousand men against Ula in 1613, scattered its army and destroyed the state; Bujantai fled to the Yehe and died there in 1618. The Tala valley passed to the Later Jin and then to the Qing. After the Ningguta military governor moved his seat to Jilin in 1676, the old track through these hills became a post road: Tala Station above Tala Lake and Emuhesoluo farther west linked the two garrison towns, and station farms grew grain for the banners. In 1821 nothing in the valley was larger than a posting station.
zh:
答剌河在清代官书中改译为塔拉河，满语意为「旷野」，河水穿行在宁古塔西南、张广才岭与牡丹江上游之间的山林里。1407年，明廷为这一河谷的女真各部设立答剌河卫，它是松花江与东海之间众多羁縻卫所中的一个。部众在河谷底部种黍，进「窝集」大森林猎貂采参，再把皮张拿到明朝边市上交易。1444年时，各部首领虽持有明朝敕书，真正追随的却是松花江中上游的扈伦联盟，日后的乌拉国就出自这一系。

1561年布颜称贝勒、建立乌拉国，经两代经营成为扈伦四部之一，塔拉一带也受它统属。决定这片河谷归属的是乌拉与建州努尔哈赤的战争。1593年，叶赫纠合九部联军来攻，在古勒山被击溃，乌拉贝勒布占泰被俘，留居建州三年；努尔哈赤以和亲笼络，护送他回乌拉继位。布占泰回国后称汗，又与叶赫和蒙古结盟。1607年乌碣岩再败之后，努尔哈赤于1613年亲率三万大军攻灭乌拉，打散其军，布占泰投奔叶赫，1618年死在那里。塔拉河谷归入后金，随后纳入清朝。1676年宁古塔将军移治吉林后，穿过这片山林的旧道改成驿路：塔拉泡上方的塔拉站和更西边的额穆赫索罗站把两座驻防城连在一起，站丁的官庄为八旗种粮。到1821年，谷中最大的聚落仍不过是一处驿站。

en:
Halacha, also written Sahalcha, was the Manchu name for the lower Zeya, the black-sable country; the pelt gave the place its name, but the valley's wealth came as much from its fields. In 1444 the Guobule, Dedule and other Daur clans ploughed the river lowlands and ran herds of horses and cattle, their walled villages lying between the Solon hunting grounds and the Amur. Their headmen held Ming patents and carried sable, grain and livestock into the tribute trade; no Chinese garrison sat on the river.

The Daur had fought in Bombogor's Evenk-Daur federation, which Hong Taiji's campaigns of 1639-1640 broke before the next invaders came. When the Cossacks pushed down the Amur for grain and fur tribute, these were the first ploughed fields they had seen. Poyarkov reached the Zeya in 1643; Khabarov's men later ordered the Daur villages to submit to the tsar and were told the villagers already paid tribute to the Shunzhi emperor. Town after town was stormed, the farmers burning their smaller settlements and falling back on the larger ones; at one Daur prince's town on the Amur Khabarov reported 661 of his enemies killed. Between 1654 and 1656 the Qing moved the survivors south to the Nen River and their old villages stood empty. The lower Zeya later fed the Qing armies mustering at Aigun against Albazin, and after 1689 it stayed a thinly held border country without a town.
zh:
哈剌察又作萨哈尔察，是满语对精奇里江下游的称呼，意为「黑貂」；地名来自貂皮，河谷的家底却有一半在农田。1444年，郭布勒、德都勒等达斡尔氏族在河畔低地耕种，牧放马牛，带围墙的村落夹在索伦猎场和黑龙江之间。头人持有明朝敕书，把貂皮、粮食和牲畜送入朝贡之路，河畔没有汉军戍堡。

达斡尔人曾随博木博果尔的鄂温克、达斡尔联盟作战，联盟在1639年至1640年被皇太极击垮。哥萨克顺黑龙江而下寻找粮食和贡物时，最先遇到的耕地就在这里。波雅尔科夫1643年抵达结雅河；哈巴罗夫的人后来命令达斡尔村落向沙皇臣服，得到的回答是，他们已经向顺治皇帝纳贡。城寨一座座被攻下，农人往往先烧掉小村、退入大城；在黑龙江畔一位头人的城寨，按哈巴罗夫自己的报告，被杀的达斡尔人有六百六十一人。1654年至1656年，清廷把幸存的达斡尔人南迁嫩江，旧日村落空无一人。结雅河下游后来为在瑷珲集结、围攻阿尔巴津的清军供给粮秣，1689年后仍是控制稀疏的边疆，没有城镇。

en:
Hurha is the forest country of the Muling River, between the Wanda Hills and the Ussuri lowlands north of Lake Khanka. In 1444 there were no walled towns, only scattered Jurchen bands who farmed a little, hunted elk and deer and dug ginseng. Sable pelts and ginseng roots went west through headmen who controlled the hunting paths, and came back as grain and iron. The Ming claimed the region only through the nominal guards of the Nurgan system; Chinese writers classed these Ussuri bands among the Wild Jurchens, and early Manchu records use Hurha or Kurka as names for the eastern forest groups.

Between 1596 and 1625 Nurhaci's Jianzhou armies campaigned through these woods again and again. Defeated bands were moved south or enrolled in the banners, and the Ussuri country passed under Manchu rule. After the Qing entered China the dynasty closed the region as a reserved homeland, barred ordinary settlers, and governed it from Ningguta on the Mudan River, garrisoned from 1652 and made a military governorship in 1662. Ningguta became the most feared place of Qing exile for political criminals: Zheng Zhilong, father of Koxinga, and the poet Wu Zhaoqian, condemned in the examination scandal of 1657, were both sent north to its snows. A few ginseng diggers and squatters aside, the Hurha country in 1821 remained a thinly held forest frontier.
zh:
虎尔哈是穆棱河流域的林地区，在完达山与兴凯湖以北的乌苏里江低地之间。1444年这里没有城郭，只有分散的女真群落，他们少量耕种，猎捕驼鹿和野鹿，进山采参。紫貂皮和人参经把持猎道的头人向西运出，换回粮食和铁器。明朝只以奴儿干都司名下的羁縻卫所遥领这一地区，汉文文献把乌苏里江诸部笼统归入野人女真，清初满文记录则以虎尔哈、库尔喀作为这些东海森林部落的称呼。

1596至1625年间，努尔哈赤的建州军队一再深入这片森林。被击败的部众或南迁，或编入八旗，乌苏里江地区就此归入满洲统治。清朝入关后将此地封禁为保留的故土，禁止普通民人迁入，由牡丹江边的宁古塔统辖，清军1652年起驻防，1662年改设宁古塔将军。宁古塔也是清初发配重犯最令人畏惧的去处：国姓爷郑成功之父郑芝龙、1657年科场案获罪的诗人吴兆骞，都被发往这片冰天雪地。除了零星的采参人和私垦者，1821年的虎尔哈仍是人烟稀少的森林边地。

en:
Oroqen covers the eastern woods of the Khingan, where the forested ridges fall away towards the Nonni and the Amur. In 1444 these taiga valleys belonged to Evenki-speaking hunters, and beyond the Amur, on the southern slopes of the Outer Khingan, roamed the bands the Manchus called Orochen, 'the people who keep reindeer'. They lived by the chase and the reindeer herd, clothed themselves in fur and skin, and honoured the spirits of forest and river after the shaman's manner.

When Cossacks came up the Amur in the mid-seventeenth century, the Orochen pulled south into the Greater and Lesser Khingan. The Qing gathered them with the rest of the Solon peoples into the Butha hunt-banners under the Heilongjiang general, and their horse and reindeer bands served the dynasty on its frontiers and paid tribute in sable. When the Qing took Yaksa in 1685, the Orochen who had lived beside the Cossacks went with the garrison into the banners as well.
zh:
鄂伦春一省是兴安岭东侧的林海，山林向嫩江与黑龙江方向缓缓低降。1444年，讲鄂温克语的猎手在这片泰加林谷中游猎；黑龙江以北、外兴安岭南坡的部众，被满洲人唤作「鄂伦春」，意为「养驯鹿的人」。他们以狩猎和驯鹿为生，以毛皮为衣，崇奉山林与江河之灵，行萨满之礼。

17世纪中叶哥萨克沿黑龙江而上，鄂伦春人南迁进入大、小兴安岭之间。清廷将他们与其余索伦诸部一并编入黑龙江将军治下的布特哈渔猎八旗，使马、使鹿的部众为朝廷戍边，以紫貂纳贡。1685年清军攻克雅克萨时，曾与哥萨克比邻而居的鄂伦春人也随守军一同被收入八旗。

en:
West Buteha covers the south-eastern skirt of the Greater Khingan, where the Yalu, Jiqin and Arun gather their waters and run east to the Nen through open woods that thin into Korchin pasture. Solon and Oroqen hunters took sable and elk in the high forest and broke reindeer to carry their loads; Mongol herdsmen held the grassy valleys below, and the pelts went downriver by barter. The hunters kept shamans rather than lamas. In 1444 there were no towns here, only camps that followed the hunt and good pasture, the western marches of the Khorchin.

Hong Taiji's armies subdued the Solon clans of these valleys in 1640. When the Butha hunters were enrolled as Eight Banners in 1731, the Plain Blue and Bordered Red banners were posted together on the Yalu, and a jalan-janggin kept his yamen at the camp that grew into Zhalantun. The next year the court levied 1,636 Solon soldiers with their families from these companies for the new Hulunbuir garrison on the Barga steppe, to watch the Russian frontier. The Arun valley also produced Hailancha. Born there in 1739 to a Dular-clan Solon family, he enlisted as a common trooper and rose to first-class duke, leading troops in the Dzungar, Burmese and Jinchuan wars, in Taiwan against Lin Shuangwen and against the Gurkhas in Nepal. He died in 1793, and the Qianlong emperor set precedent aside and had him enshrined in the Zhaozhong shrine, normally reserved for men killed in battle.
zh:
西布特哈在大兴安岭东南麓，雅鲁河、济沁河、阿伦河在此汇流，穿过疏林东入嫩江，林子尽头就是科尔沁草原。索伦和鄂伦春猎手在高山密林里猎貂捕鹿，役使驯鹿驮运；下方水草丰美的河谷归蒙古牧人，貂皮顺着河流拿去交换。猎手们奉的是萨满，不是喇嘛。1444年这里没有城镇，只有随猎物和水草迁徙的营地，是科尔沁部的西陲。

1640年，皇太极的大军征服了这些河谷里的索伦诸部。1731年布特哈猎户被编为八旗，正蓝、镶红两旗同驻雅鲁河，一名扎兰章京在后来发展成扎兰屯的营地开衙办事。次年，朝廷从这些佐领中征调一千六百三十六名索伦兵，连同家眷派往巴尔虎草原新设的呼伦贝尔驻防，盯防俄罗斯方向的边界。阿伦河谷还走出了海兰察。他1739年生于当地一户索伦多拉尔氏人家，以马甲入伍，积功封一等超勇公，先后领兵出征准噶尔、缅甸、大小金川，赴台湾平定林爽文，又到尼泊尔征讨廓尔喀。他1793年去世，按清朝旧例昭忠祠只祀阵亡将领，乾隆帝特准他入祀。

en:
Barag is the cold pasture country between the Onon and Ergune rivers and the western approaches to the Greater Khingan. The Barga take their name from the Barguzin lands east of Lake Baikal, which the Mongols of the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries called Bargujin-Tukum, the land's end. Alan Gua, from whom Genghis Khan's Borjigin clan traced its descent, was a Barga woman of that country. After the Yuan collapse in 1368 the Barga joined the Oirats and scattered across the Mongol steppe, many clans drifting toward the Ergune and the Khingan. In 1444 this province was a frontier of seasonal camps and horse herds rather than a bounded tribal territory, where Mongols, Daurs and Solon Ewenkis pastured side by side under the competing reach of Oirat and Genghisid lords.

Russian pressure from Siberia and the Dzungar wars carried the Barga through the next upheavals. A Khori-Barga body fled back to the Onon in 1594, and others became subjects of the Setsen Khan in Khalkha, until Galdan's invasion of 1688 drove most of them south into Inner Mongolia. The Qing turned the fugitives into border troops. In 1732 the court conscripted 275 Barga men living in Manchuria into two Solon banners and moved them with wives, children and herds to Hulun Buir, the empty pasture facing Russia; these were the Old Barga. When the Barga who had defected to Russia in 1730-1732 were handed back in 1734, the Qing settled them nearby as the New Barga and organised them into eight banners on the Solon model. Through 1821 the Barga camps garrisoned the Qing-Russian steppe frontier.
zh:
巴尔虎是鄂嫩河、额尔古纳河与大兴安岭西麓之间的严寒牧场。巴尔虎人的族名来自贝加尔湖以东的巴尔古津地方，13至14世纪的蒙古人把那里称作「巴尔忽真·脱古木」，意为大地的尽头。成吉思汗所属的博尔济吉特氏尊为始祖母的阿阑豁阿，就是出身巴尔古津的巴尔虎女子。1368年元朝灭亡后，巴尔虎人归附瓦剌，散处于蒙古草原各部，不少部众逐渐迁到额尔古纳河与大兴安岭一带。1444年，这里没有边界固定的部落领地，只有随季节迁徙的营地和牧马之地，蒙古人、达斡尔人和索伦鄂温克人比邻游牧，瓦剌与成吉思汗后裔的势力在此交错。

俄国势力向西伯利亚扩张，加上准噶尔战争，把巴尔虎人卷入新一轮动荡。1594年一支霍里—巴尔虎人逃回鄂嫩河，另一些人做了喀尔喀车臣汗的属民；1688年噶尔丹东侵，大部分巴尔虎人南逃内蒙古。清朝把这些流民编成边军：1732年，清廷从居住在满洲的巴尔虎人中征调275名壮丁编入索伦两旗，连同妻儿和畜群迁往正对俄国的空旷牧场呼伦贝尔，是为陈巴尔虎。1730年至1732年投俄的巴尔虎人于1734年被俄方交还，清廷把他们安置在近旁，按索伦旗制编为八旗，称为新巴尔虎。到1821年，巴尔虎人的营地一直戍守着清朝与俄国之间的草原边界。

en:
Bayan-Uul, 'rich mountain', is the open grassland between the Onon and Kherlen rivers in eastern Mongolia, with the Ulz running through its northern camps. In 1444 the herders here moved seasonally with sheep, horses, cattle and gers under the loose authority of Taisun Khan's Northern Yuan; pasture rights, not walls, defined power.

These eastern pastures became the domain of the Setsen Khans after the descendants of Gersenji Khongtaiji built the Khalkha khanates from 1549. Sholoi, the first Setsen Khan, had his title confirmed by the Fifth Dalai Lama in the early 1630s. In 1688 Galdan's Dzungars invaded, and Ömkhei, the fourth Setsen Khan, fled south to Xilingol with his people. At Dolonnuur in 1691 he submitted to the Kangxi Emperor with the Tushiyet and Zasagt khans and more than five hundred noyans and taijis, bringing the Khalkha under Qing rule. After the 1696 campaign against Galdan the Setsen banners returned to the Kherlen, and Bayan-Uul remained remote herding country under Qing banner administration.
zh:
「巴彦乌拉」意为富饶的山，其地是东部蒙古鄂嫩河与克鲁伦河之间的开阔草原，乌勒吉河流经北部的牧地。1444年，牧民赶着绵羊、马、牛和毡帐随季节移牧，名义上奉岱总汗脱脱不花的北元为共主；在这里界定权力的是牧场使用权，而非城墙。

1549年格哷森札札赉尔的后裔建立喀尔喀诸汗部后，这片东部牧场归车臣汗世代领有。首任车臣汗硕垒的汗号在17世纪30年代初得到五世达赖喇嘛的承认。1688年噶尔丹率准噶尔军来攻，第四代车臣汗率部南逃锡林郭勒。1691年，他与土谢图汗、札萨克图汗及五百余名诺颜、台吉会于多伦诺尔，向康熙帝归附，喀尔喀就此归入清朝统辖。1696年征讨噶尔丹之役后，车臣汗部各旗返回克鲁伦河流域，巴彦乌拉在清朝盟旗体制下仍是偏远的游牧之地。

en:
The lower Orkhon country is where Mongolia's longest river leaves the Khangai, receives the Tamir and Tuul, and winds through wooded valleys north to the Selenge. Herders grazed cattle and sheep on the river meadows, fishermen took pike, carp and taimen, and trappers brought furs out of the northern woods. Farther up the same valley lay Khar Balgas and Karakorum, the old Uyghur and Mongol capitals, long since given over to nomad camps. In 1444 the Orkhon camps were Khalkha country: Toghtoa Bukha, the Taisun Khan, was nominal khagan of the Northern Yuan, while Esen the Oirat taishi kept the real power.

Later in the fifteenth century Dayan Khan formed the central Mongols into the Khalkha tümen, the shield of the northern frontier, and Gersenji's descendants divided the river otogs among their houses. They held the pastures against the Oirats until Galdan's invasion of 1688 delivered the Khalkha to Qing protection, and the old lordships were re-made into banners. The Treaty of Kyakhta in 1727 fixed the frontier with Russia and opened the market at Kyakhta-Maimaicheng on it; caravans between the border and the Qing interior travelled the Orkhon and Tuul valleys, carrying Siberian furs, leather and textiles south and tea, silk and rhubarb north. State caravans used the road until 1762, when the trade passed to private merchants bartering at the border. Under the eighteenth-century Khalkh Juram law code, the Orkhon marked the outer edge of the hunting reserve around Ikh Khüree, and the river's game was closed to the banners.
zh:
阿鲁浑（鄂尔浑）下游一带，是蒙古最长的河流离开杭爱山、汇纳塔米尔河与土拉河后，穿过林木河谷蜿蜒北去、注入色楞格河的地方。牧民在河漫滩放牧牛羊，渔人捕捞狗鱼、鲤鱼和哲罗鱼，猎户从北方林中运来毛皮。沿同一条河谷再往上，是回鹘旧都斡耳朵八里和蒙古旧都哈拉和林，两处早已让给游牧营地。1444年，鄂尔浑河畔的营地属喀尔喀：脱脱不花（岱总汗）是北元名义上的大汗，实权握在瓦剌太师也先手里。

15世纪后期，达延汗把中央蒙古编为喀尔喀万户，作为北方边境的屏障，格哷森札的后裔分领沿河诸鄂托克。他们与瓦剌周旋、保有牧场，直到1688年噶尔丹入侵，喀尔喀投附清朝，旧有领主领地被改编为旗分。1727年，《恰克图条约》划定对俄边界，并在边界上开设恰克图—买卖城市场；往来边境与清朝边内的驼道取道鄂尔浑河、土拉河河谷，西伯利亚的毛皮、皮革和织物南来，茶叶、丝绸和大黄北往。1762年以前走的是官营商队，此后贸易交给私商在边境以货易货。18世纪的《喀尔喀法规》把鄂尔浑河定为大库伦周边禁猎地的外界，河中猎物不许各旗擅取。

en:
Sainshand lies in the dry desert-steppe of the eastern Gobi, among the grazing grounds called Bayan Gobi and Khashaat Gobi. Groundwater, sparse saxaul thickets and seasonal wells watered horses, cattle, sheep, goats and Bactrian camels, but no walled market town grew up here. In 1444 the herdsmen belonged to the Northern Yuan: Taisun Khan held the title of Great Khan, while Esen taishi and the Oirat lords kept the real power behind the Borjigin throne.

Dayan Khan reunited the Eastern Mongols after 1480 and allotted these pastures to Khalkha princes. When Galdan's Dzungars invaded in 1688 the Khalkha khans fled to the Qing and submitted at Dolonnur in 1691, after which banner officials administered the desert wells. The place earned its fame from a teenage monk. In 1820 Danzanravjaa, seventeen years old and recognised as the fifth Noyon Khutagt, founded Khamar Monastery near Sainshand for the Nyingma Red Hat order, choosing the site for the spiritual energy he felt in the desert; caves in the hills north took monks on retreats of 108 days. Called the Terrible Noble Saint of the Gobi, he was a poet and a harsh critic of his society, and he equipped his monastery with a public library, a museum and a poetry recital hall, opened a children's school for Mongolian and Tibetan letters, mathematics and natural science, and ran Mongolia's first professional public theatre, whose troupe of some three hundred performers toured the Gobi. At its height Khamar held over eighty temples and about five hundred monks.
zh:
