Settlers took up their long narrow river lots in 1666; a first church was built in 1674, the census counted 261 people in 1681, and the parish of Saint-François-Xavier was formed in 1684. Men trapped up the Batiscan and sold their furs at Trois-Rivières, while sawmills worked its timber. After 1712 captured Fox from the west were held here as slaves, and by the end of French rule a ribbon of farms and the Chemin du Roy linked Batiscan with Champlain and Sainte-Anne-de-la-Pérade; British troops passed that way on their march on Montreal in 1760.
zh:
巴蒂斯坎河自森林覆盖的劳伦琴山脉奔流而下，注入圣劳伦斯河。1444年，这片土地属于说阿尔冈昆语的猎民，上游一带有阿蒂卡梅库人（Atikamekw）。他们在林中猎取驼鹿与河狸，在宽阔多雾的河口捕捞鳗鱼和鲟鱼，往来于内陆森林与三河城原住民贸易聚地之间时在此扎营。此时欧洲人尚未出现，而巴蒂斯坎河已处在连接上游腹地与海湾的独木舟路线上。

塞缪尔·德·尚普兰1603年首次记下河名，1609年在此见到休伦人与阿尔冈昆人的营地，1611年会见一位名叫巴蒂斯坎的首领，又在1612年的地图上把这一带标为巴斯蒂斯坎地区（bastisquan）。1636年，雅克·拉费尔泰获得广阔的马德莱娜领地，1639年3月13日巴蒂斯坎封邑被授予耶稣会。1666年，移民开始在狭长的临河授地上落户；1674年第一座教堂建成，1681年人口普查有261人，1684年圣方济各·沙勿略堂区设立。居民沿巴蒂斯坎河深入内陆设阱捕猎，把毛皮卖到三河城，锯木厂也加工起河运的木材。1712年后，从西部掳来的福克斯人俘虏被带到此地为奴；到法国统治末期，成串的农庄和国王大道把巴蒂斯坎与尚普兰村、圣安娜-德拉佩拉德连成一线，1760年英军正是循此路进逼蒙特利尔。

en:
Mehtawtik, ‘the end of the path’, stood where the Eel River joins the middle Saint John, at the head of the portage that carried canoe traffic between the Wolastoq valley and the rivers of Maine. It was the chief town of the Wolastoqiyik: longhouses and cornfields lay within a stout palisade raised in the seventeenth century against Mohawk war parties raiding from the west, and Fort Meductic was remembered as the first fort in Acadia. Salmon runs and the furs of the interior made it prosperous, and from here the People of the Bright River commanded the carrying place linking Acadia with New England. In 1444 it was their headquarters, greater than any of their other villages.

The French knew the place as Medoctec. In August 1689 a Wolastoqiyik war party brought the nine-year-old John Gyles up the rivers from the sack of Pemaquid to Meductic; he passed six years there as a captive before being sold to the French seigneur Louis D'Amours de Chauffours at Jemseg and reaching Boston in 1698, and in 1736 he published the memoirs that describe the stockaded town. Its warriors fought beside the French when a New England expedition sailed up to besiege Governor de Villebon's Fort Nashwaak in 1696. The Jesuit Joseph Aubery reopened the mission in 1701, and in 1717 Jean-Baptiste Loyard built the chapel of Saint-Jean-Baptiste, its bell a gift of Louis XV. Through Dummer's War of 1722–1725 and the colonial conflicts after it, Meductic remained the base from which Wolastoqiyik and Mi'kmaq fighters harried the English frontier. Its primacy faded when the French founded Sainte-Anne during King George's War and the upriver village of Aukpaque drew level with it. The old village did not outlast the St. John River campaigns of the Seven Years' War: in 1767 its people removed to Aukpaque, and the site was afterwards used only as a seasonal camp.
zh:
梅杜克蒂克又称梅赫陶提克，意为「小径的尽头」，位于鳗鱼河汇入圣约翰河中游处，扼守一条水陆联运道的起点，独木舟可经此往来于沃拉斯托克河谷与缅因诸河之间。这里是沃拉斯托基伊克人的首镇：长屋与玉米地围在坚固的木栅之内——木栅于17世纪筑起，用以抵御从西边来袭的莫霍克战队，梅杜克蒂克堡后来被追记为阿卡迪亚的第一座堡垒。洄游的鲑鱼和内陆的毛皮让此地富足，「闪光河上的人」由此掌控着连接阿卡迪亚与新英格兰的转运道。1444年，这里是他们的大本营，比其他任何村落都大。

法国人把此地称作梅多克泰克。1689年8月，一支沃拉斯托基伊克战队攻陷佩马奎德后，沿着一条条河流把九岁的约翰·盖尔斯带到梅杜克蒂克；他在此为奴六年，后被转卖给在热姆塞格领有庄园的法国领主路易·达穆尔·德·肖富尔，1698年才回到波士顿，并在1736年出版回忆录，记下这座栅寨的样貌。1696年，一支新英格兰远征军溯河围攻维尔邦总督的纳什瓦克堡，梅杜克蒂克战士与法军并肩作战。耶稣会士约瑟夫·奥贝里1701年重开传教站，让-巴蒂斯特·卢瓦亚尔1717年建起圣让-巴蒂斯特小堂，教堂的钟还是路易十五所赐。在1722至1725年的达默战争及此后的殖民地冲突中，梅杜克蒂克始终是沃拉斯托基伊克与米克马克战士袭扰英国边疆的基地。乔治王战争期间，法国人建立圣安娜，上游的奥克帕克村地位与它不相上下，梅杜克蒂克的首镇地位随之衰落。这座老村没能熬过七年战争中的圣约翰河诸役：1767年，居民迁往奥克帕克，旧址此后只作季节性营地使用。

en:
The Keinouche, or Kinounchepirini, the People of the Pickerel Waters, held a stretch of the lower Ottawa River around the later Pontiac Bay and Chats Falls. In 1444 their seasonal bands fished the eddies below the rapids, hunted moose and beaver in the pine woods, and used the portages connecting the upper river to the St. Lawrence trade world. Because the valley was poorly suited to farming, these camps and canoe routes rather than large agricultural villages gave the country its shape.

French canoes entered the river after 1610, and Champlain passed through the Ottawa route in 1613, but no European station yet displaced the Keinouche. The Beaver Wars shattered that order: in 1650 Father Paul Ragueneau found Algonquian communities along the Ottawa dispersed or destroyed, and for the rest of the century the river valley became a dangerous Haudenosaunee hunting ground. The Great Peace of Montreal in 1701 reopened the canoe route. French authorities kept the Pontiac shore largely unsettled to preserve the fur trade, although Nicolas d'Ailleboust de Manthet wintered at the Coulonge River mouth in 1694, and Fort Coulonge later became a trading post. After the British conquest the North West Company rebuilt the post in 1784. Joseph Mondion built a homestead at Indian Point by Chats Falls in 1786; his post passed through the XY and North West companies and reached the Hudson's Bay Company with the 1821 merger.
zh:
凯诺切人又称基农切皮里尼人，意为「狗鱼水域之人」，据守渥太华河下游一段，即后来的庞蒂亚克湾和沙茨瀑布一带。1444年，他们的季节性族群在急流下方的回水湾捕鱼，在松林里猎捕驼鹿和海狸，并利用各条搬运道，把渥太华河上游同圣劳伦斯河的贸易世界连接起来。这一带谷地不适宜农耕，因此塑造土地面貌的不是大型农业村落，而是营地、独木舟航路和水陆转运点。

1610年后法国独木舟开始进入渥太华河，尚普兰1613年也经这条水路前行，但当时还没有欧洲据点迫使凯诺切人迁离。海狸战争打碎了这一秩序：1650年，保罗·拉格诺神父发现渥太华河沿岸的阿尔贡昆社群已经离散或被毁；该世纪余下时间里，河谷变成霍德诺索尼人危险的猎场。1701年《蒙特利尔大和平》后，独木舟航路重新开放。法国当局为维持毛皮贸易，长期不让庞蒂亚克沿岸大规模殖民；1694年，尼古拉·达耶布·德·芒泰在库隆日河口过冬，那里后来形成库隆日贸易站。英国征服后，西北公司1784年重建该站。约瑟夫·蒙迪翁1786年在沙茨瀑布旁的印第安角建立家园；这个贸易站先后转入XY公司和西北公司之手，并在1821年公司合并时归哈德逊湾公司所有。

en:
Noquet was the corridor between the southern shore of Lake Superior and the Noquet bays at the head of Green Bay. In summer the Noquet camped along the cold lake, fishing and gathering blueberries and wild rice; in winter their trail carried them south to Big and Little Bay de Noc. The route from Little Bay de Noc toward Grand Island crossed rivers, pine woods, and hunting grounds shared with the closely related Menominee. In 1444 this small Algonquian-speaking people was still among the principal nations of the Upper Peninsula, moving by canoe and snowshoe and taking beaver and otter from its forests.

French contact came with Jean Nicolet's voyage to Green Bay in 1634-1638, when Noquet were counted among the people gathered near the Menominee shore. French missionaries knew their bays as the Baie des Noquets, and by 1659 Noquet were listed with Menominee and Potawatomi at the mission of Saint Michael. Jacques Marquette later described them as a small Algonquian clan of about 150 people. Jean-François Buisson de Saint-Cosme still named them among Green Bay's peoples in 1698, but when Pierre François Xavier de Charlevoix passed through in 1721 only a few families remained. Disease, the Beaver Wars, mission life, and marriage into neighboring Menominee, Potawatomi, and Ojibwe communities dissolved the separate band; by the early nineteenth century the Noquet survived as families within neighboring nations rather than as an independent political people.
zh:
诺奎特是苏必利尔湖南岸与格林湾湾头诺奎特诸湾之间的走廊。夏天，诺奎特人在寒凉的湖畔扎营，捕鱼并采集蓝莓和野米；冬天，他们沿小路南下到大诺克湾和小诺克湾。从小诺克湾通往格兰德岛的路线越过河流、松树林和猎场，也把他们与关系密切的梅诺米尼人连接起来。1444年，这个人口不多的阿尔冈昆语族群仍是上半岛的主要族群之一，靠独木舟和雪鞋往返两地，在林中猎取河狸与水獭。

法国人的接触始于让·尼克莱1634—1638年的格林湾航行；诺奎特人当时被列在梅诺米尼海岸附近相会的人群中。法国传教士把他们的海湾称为诺奎特湾，到1659年，诺奎特人与梅诺米尼人、波塔瓦托米人一同被列入圣弥额尔传教站。雅克·马凯特后来称他们是一个约一百五十人的阿尔冈昆小族。1698年，让—弗朗索瓦·比松·德·圣科姆仍把他们列为格林湾诸族之一，但皮埃尔·弗朗索瓦·格扎维埃·德·沙勒瓦1721年经过时，只剩几个家族。疾病、海狸战争、传教站生活，以及与邻近梅诺米尼人、波塔瓦托米人和奥吉布瓦人的通婚，逐渐消解了这支独立群体；到19世纪初，诺奎特人已作为相邻民族中的家族延续，而不再是独立的政治共同体。

en:
The Mamaceqtaw are the Menominee, an Algonquian people of the rivers and lakeshores around Green Bay. Their own name means simply 'the people'; the Ojibwe called them the Wild Rice People, and French traders the Folles-Avoines. Wild rice and sturgeon ordered their year, and five clans — Bear, Eagle, Wolf, Crane and Moose — ordered the village; their own tradition places their birth at the mouth of the Menominee River. In 1444 they shared the northern forests and waters peaceably with the Ojibwe and Noquet.

The Menominee watched Jean Nicolet fire his pistols from a canoe at Red Banks in 1634, and after 1667 French coureurs de bois drew them into the fur trade. When Charlevoix visited their single riverside village in 1721 he called them the finest-looking men in all Canada. The French victory over the Iroquois in 1701 and the ruin of the Winnebago opened the south and west, and Menominee hunters spread over central Wisconsin to Milwaukee, a range of ten million acres. Long allied first to the French and then to the British, they helped repulse the American attempt to retake Mackinac Island in 1814.
zh:
马马切陶人即梅诺米尼人，是格林贝周边河湖地带的阿尔冈昆民族。他们的自称只意为「人」；奥吉布瓦人叫他们「野米人」，法国商人则称之为「野麦人」（Folles-Avoines）。野米和鲟鱼安排着他们一年的生计，熊、鹰、狼、鹤、驼鹿五个氏族维系着村落；按他们自己的传统，民族就诞生于梅诺米尼河河口。1444年时，他们与奥吉布瓦人、诺奎人和平共享着北方的森林与水域。

1634年，梅诺米尼人在红岸看着让·尼科莱在独木舟上鸣放手枪登岸；1667年以后，法国林中人又把他们带入毛皮贸易。1721年沙勒瓦走访他们唯一的河畔村落，称他们是全加拿大最英武俊美的人。1701年法国及其盟友战胜易洛魁，加上温内巴戈人已然衰落，南方与西方门户洞开，梅诺米尼猎人扩展到威斯康星中部，远达密尔沃基一带，活动范围约一千万英亩。他们长期先与法国结盟、继而依附英国，1814年还协助击退了美军夺回麦基诺岛的进攻。

en:
In 1444 the prairie watersheds between the upper Iowa, Des Moines and Missouri rivers were late Oneota country. River villages kept gardens of corn, beans and squash, while seasonal camps followed bison across the grasslands. The people later called Otoe, or Jiwére, were then still part of the Ho-Chunk and Chiwere world west of the Great Lakes; in the sixteenth century they split away with the Ioway and Missouria and moved south-west onto these plains.

Jacques Marquette's 1673 map placed the Otoe near the Des Moines and upper Iowa rivers. In 1700 Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville recorded them and the Ioway living with the Omaha west of the Mississippi and Missouri, and during the eighteenth century their earth-lodge villages shifted toward the Platte. Around 1760 Otoe and some Missouria shared a village on the Platte near the Elkhorn, where horses made summer bison hunts the centre of economic life. Smallpox and intertribal warfare reduced the allied groups; eighty surviving Missouria joined the Otoe in 1796. On 2 August 1804, after the Louisiana Purchase, Lewis and Clark met Otoe and Missouria leaders at Council Bluff and estimated the combined population at about 500. In 1819 the Yellowstone Expedition camped below the bluff, and Fort Atkinson was established above it in 1820, placing an American garrison on the edge of Otoe country.
zh:
1444年，上艾奥瓦河、得梅因河与密苏里河之间的草原水系属于晚期奥内奥塔文化圈。河畔村落经营玉米、豆类和南瓜园圃，季节性营地则随野牛穿过草地。后来称为奥托埃或吉韦雷的人，此时仍属于五大湖以西的霍楚克-奇维雷世界；16世纪，他们与艾奥瓦人、密苏里人分离，向西南迁入这片平原。

雅克·马凯特1673年的地图把奥托埃人标在得梅因河与上艾奥瓦河附近。1700年，皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德伊贝尔维尔记载他们和艾奥瓦人与奥马哈人同住于密西西比河、密苏里河以西；18世纪间，他们的土屋村落逐渐向普拉特河移动。约1760年，奥托埃人与部分密苏里人共居在普拉特河临近埃尔克霍恩河之处，马匹使夏季野牛猎成为经济生活的中心。天花与部落战争削弱了这些结盟群体；1796年，八十名幸存的密苏里人加入奥托埃人。路易斯安那购地后，刘易斯与克拉克于1804年8月2日在议事崖会见奥托埃和密苏里首领，估计两者合计约五百人。1819年，黄石远征队在崖下扎营，1820年又在崖上设立阿特金森堡，把美军要塞推到奥托埃地区边缘。

en:
Saone covers the southwestern prairies of the Minnesota, where the river woods open onto endless grassland. In 1444 it was the country of the Yankton – the Iháŋktȟuŋwaŋ, 'Village at the End' – who together with the Yanktonai called themselves the Wičhíyena, one of the seven council fires of the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ. Without horses yet, they left their wooded lakes on foot for the summer buffalo drive, penning the herds or stampeding them over jumps, and netted fish and gathered wild rice in the northern waters. On the Coteau des Prairies rose the seam of red catlinite, ínyanša; the quarry was neutral ground where every nation came to cut pipe-bowls, and the Yankton were its keepers.

French traders reached the upper Minnesota at the end of the seventeenth century. In 1700 Pierre-Charles Le Sueur built Fort L'Huillier at the mouth of the Blue Earth River and shipped its blue-green clay downstream as copper ore, until a Meskwaki attack forced the post's abandonment in 1701. Through the rest of the eighteenth century Ojibwe war parties armed with French muskets pressed the Yankton and Yanktonai southwest out of the Minnesota woods onto the open plains, where horses and guns reshaped their lives. In August 1804 Lewis and Clark held council with the Yankton at Calumet Bluff on the Missouri, and on 18 July 1815 the band signed its first peace and friendship treaty with the United States at Portage des Sioux.
zh:
萨奥内位于明尼苏达河上游的西南草原，河畔林地在这里让位给无边的草地。1444年，这里是维奇耶纳人（Wičhíyena）的地方——他们是扬克顿人与扬克顿奈人，达科他语里扬克顿意为「尽头的村落」，也是奥切蒂-沙科温（七堆营火）之一。那时他们还没有马，夏季徒步离开林间湖沼，把野牛群赶入围栏或悬崖，又在北方水域捕鱼、采野米。草原台地上出露一层红色的烟斗石（ínyanša），采石场是各部落都能来取石刻制烟斗的中立之地，由扬克顿人世代看守。

法国商人在17世纪末来到明尼苏达河上游。1700年，皮埃尔-夏尔·勒叙厄尔在布卢厄斯河口建起吕利耶堡，把蓝绿色黏土当作铜矿装船运走；1701年梅斯克瓦基人来袭，据点被迫放弃。此后整个18世纪，装备法国火枪的奥吉布瓦战队不断进逼，把扬克顿人和扬克顿奈人向西南赶出明尼苏达林地，推上开阔草原，马和火器就此重塑了他们的生活。1804年8月，刘易斯与克拉克在密苏里河畔的卡柳梅特崖与扬克顿人议事；1815年7月18日，他们在波蒂奇德苏与美国签订第一个和平友好条约。

en:
The Sheyenne River swings in a great bend eastward across the prairie to join the Red, its wooded banks cutting through open bison grassland. In 1444 this was the western edge of the Cheyenne world: the Tsitsistas still lived as wild-rice gatherers and pedestrian bison hunters between the upper Mississippi and Mille Lacs, and their bands reached the Sheyenne only on long summer hunts, camps hauled by dogs, with no horses or European goods. Pressure from the Assiniboine was already nudging them westward. The river woods held beaver and the plains held endless bison, the wealth that would one day draw the fur companies.

Toward 1700 the Cheyenne crossed the Missouri, and from about 1724 an independent band held Biesterfeldt, a fortified village on a bend of the lower Sheyenne: some seventy circular earth lodges around a plaza behind a ditch and possibly a palisade, its farmers using bison-scapula hoes and making pottery like the Mandan and Arikara, horse bones and a few European trade goods among the finds. It was the only documented earthlodge village in the Red River watershed, and it lasted barely two generations. Around 1780 its lodges were found burned and the site abandoned, as Lakota and Ojibwe pressure drove the Cheyenne west through the smallpox years. They gave up fields and earth lodges for tipis and horses, moving toward the Missouri and the Black Hills; in 1804 Lewis and Clark visited a surviving Cheyenne village in North Dakota, and about 1811 the Cheyenne formed their lasting alliance with the Arapaho. Their old Sheyenne country then became open hunting range, crossed by the summer buffalo hunts of Assiniboine and Red River Métis, and by 1821 it was a corridor for the brigades of the fur trade.
zh:
马坎德韦温一带，夏延河在草原上绕出一个大弯，向东汇入红河，林木夹岸，四周是开阔的野牛草原。1444年，这里是夏延人世界的西缘：自称齐齐斯塔斯的夏延人还生活在密西西比河上游与米尔湖之间，采集野米、徒步猎牛，全靠狗拖拽运输；他们的队伍只有在夏季长途狩猎时才到夏延河一带，既没有马，也没有欧洲货物。阿西尼博因人的压力已在把他们逐步推向西方。河畔林地多河狸，草原上野牛成群，这正是日后吸引毛皮公司前来的财富。

1700年前后夏延人越过密苏里河；约1724年起，一支独立的夏延人在夏延河下游的河湾上建起设防的比斯特费尔特村：围壕以及可能存在的栅栏之内，约七十座圆形土屋环着广场而建，农人用野牛肩胛骨做锄，陶器风格近于曼丹人和阿里卡拉人，遗存中还有马骨和少量欧洲商货。这是红河水系唯一有记载的土屋村落，只存在了不到两代人的时间。约1780年，村里土屋焚毁、聚落废弃，拉科塔人与奥吉布瓦人的压迫夹着天花疫病，把夏延人继续逼向西方。他们舍弃农田和土屋，改用帐篷与马匹，迁往密苏里河和布莱克山一带；1804年刘易斯与克拉克在北达科他走访了一个尚存的夏延人村落，约1811年夏延人与阿拉帕霍人结成长期同盟。此后夏延故土成为开放猎场，阿西尼博因人和红河梅蒂人的夏季野牛猎队穿行其间，到1821年已是毛皮商队往来的走廊。

en:
Chinko is the tallgrass country between the Illinois River valley and the Wabash watershed, where prairie is broken by oak groves and the wooded valleys of the Kankakee, Iroquois and Vermilion. In 1444 it was Illini range, shared by the small Chinkoa band recorded by French writers as Chinko; villages moved with the seasons, women tended corn, beans and squash in river bottoms, and hunting parties followed bison across the grass. The Miami-speaking Wea and Piankeshaw lived to the east, before any European had seen the prairie.

Iroquois war parties shattered this world from the 1650s onward, raiding for furs and captives and driving Illini bands toward the Mississippi at the height of the Beaver Wars. French explorers reached the Illinois Country in 1673, and La Salle's expedition crossed it in 1682, opening a fur trade that pulled the remaining villages into French alliance. The French claim of 1682 lasted only until 1763, when lands east of the Mississippi passed to Britain; by then war and disease had broken the old confederacy, and Kickapoo and Potawatomi bands were pressing into the prairie. After the American Revolution the country entered the Northwest Territory, and Kickapoo claims in Illinois were ceded by the 1819 Treaty of Edwardsville.
zh:
钦科位于伊利诺伊河谷与沃巴什水系之间，高草草原上散布着橡树林，以及坎卡基河、伊罗夸伊河和弗米利恩河林木丛生的河谷。1444年，这里是伊利尼人的活动范围，法国文献记作钦科（Chinko）的小支钦科阿人也在这片土地上游居；村落随季节迁徙，妇女在河漫滩种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎队则穿过草原追逐野牛。在欧洲人望见这片草原以前，说迈阿密语的韦阿人和皮安克肖人就住在东面。

17世纪50年代起，易洛魁战队为毛皮和俘虏不断袭来，在海狸战争高潮中把伊利尼各支驱向密西西比河，打碎了旧有的秩序。1673年法国探险者抵达伊利尼地区，拉萨尔远征队又于1682年经过这里，毛皮贸易随之展开，把残存村落拉入法国同盟。法国1682年的主权宣称只维持到1763年，密西西比河以东土地随后转归英国；此时战争和疫病已经瓦解旧联盟，基卡普人和波塔瓦托米人正进入草原。美国独立战争后，这片土地归入西北领地，基卡普人又在1819年《爱德华兹维尔条约》中割让其在伊利诺伊的权利。

en:
The Espeminkia were one of the twelve tribes of the Illinois, the loose Illiniwek confederacy of Miami-Illinois-speaking villagers in the Mississippi and Illinois river valleys. Their villages of longhouses and rush-mat lodges stood by fertile bottomlands where the women grew maize, beans and squash; on the northern prairies the men joined bison hunts several hundred strong, drying the meat and dressing robes for trade. In 1444 the Illinois were still among the masters of the middle Mississippi, far from any European.

Jolliet and Marquette canoed through in 1673, and a Jesuit mission rose among the Kaskaskia in 1675; then the Beaver Wars reached the Illinois River, and in 1680 an Iroquois army sacked the Grand Village and carried off hundreds of captives. War and epidemic thinned the twelve tribes to five by 1700, and the Espeminkia no longer survived as a separate tribe. The remnant Illinois fought beside the French through the Fox Wars, raiding with them until a Fox village was stormed on the Sangamon in 1730. They lost the French alliance in 1763, the British took Fort de Chartres in 1765, and by 1778 the whole confederacy numbered only about 300 souls.
zh:
埃斯佩明基亚人是伊利诺伊人十二支之一。伊利诺伊人又称伊利尼维克，是说迈阿密－伊利尼语的松散联盟，散居在密西西比河与伊利诺伊河流域。他们的长屋和草席小屋村落就建在肥沃的河漫滩旁，妇女种植玉米、豆子和南瓜；男子到北方草原参加数百人规模的围猎，猎牛晒肉、鞣制皮袍用于交易。1444年时，伊利诺伊人仍是密西西比河中游的主人之一，欧洲人还远在天边。

若利埃和马凯特1673年泛舟经过此地，1675年耶稣会传教站在卡斯卡斯基亚人中间建起；随后海狸战争蔓延到伊利诺伊河，1680年易洛魁大军洗劫大村，掳走数百人。战乱和疫病使十二支到1700年只剩五支，埃斯佩明基亚人不再作为独立一支存续。余下的伊利诺伊人在福克斯战争中站在法国一边随军征战，直至1730年福克斯人的村落于桑加蒙河畔被攻破。1763年法国战败，他们失去这个同盟，英军1765年接管沙特尔堡；到1778年，整个联盟只剩下约三百人。

en:
In 1444 the Illinois River below the sandstone butte later called Le Rocher was a productive edge of woodland and prairie. Villages farmed the rich alluvium with corn, beans and squash, gathered wetland roots, and hunted deer and elk. The Tapouaro were one of the small Miami-Illinois divisions later recorded among the Illiniwek groups that shared the Grand Village of the Illinois.

Iroquois war parties seeking new beaver grounds entered northern Illinois in 1660, turning the river valley into a frontier of the Beaver Wars. When Louis Jolliet and Jacques Marquette reached the Grand Village in 1673, they counted about seventy-three cabins and roughly 1,000 people. Marquette returned in 1675 to found the Mission of the Immaculate Conception, and the French post, trade guns and refuge drew reports of about 400 cabins and as many as 6,000 people by the 1680s. An Iroquois force burned the village in the autumn of 1680. La Salle and Henri de Tonti built Fort Saint-Louis du Rocher on the bluff in the winter of 1682, while Illinois, Miami, Shawnee and Mahican families camped at its foot. Continued Iroquois pressure forced Tonti to withdraw to Fort Pimiteoui near Peoria in 1691, and by 1700 the Tapouaro no longer appeared as a separate Illinois tribe. Their descendants shared the Peoria and Kaskaskia fate; Peoria families crossed the Mississippi after 1763 and ceded their Illinois lands by the Treaty of Edwardsville in 1818.
zh:
1444年，后来被法国人称作岩石（Le Rocher）的砂岩崖下，伊利诺伊河流经林地与草原交界的丰饶地带。村落在肥沃冲积土上种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，采集湿地根茎，猎捕鹿和美洲马鹿。塔波阿罗是迈阿密-伊利诺伊语的小群体之一；后来的法国记录把他们列入曾共用伊利诺伊大村落的伊利尼群体。

1660年，为寻找新海狸猎场而来的易洛魁战队进入北伊利诺伊，使河谷成为海狸战争的前沿。1673年，路易·乔利埃特与雅克·马凯特抵达伊利诺伊大村落时，见到约七十三座棚屋、近一千人。马凯特1675年重返此地，建立圣母无原罪传教站；法国商站、火枪和庇护吸引人口，到1680年代的记载已有约四百座棚屋、多达六千人。1680年秋，易洛魁军队焚毁这座村落。1682年冬，拉萨尔与亨利·德·通蒂在崖上修建圣路易堡，伊利尼、迈阿密、肖尼和莫希干家族则在崖脚扎营。易洛魁的持续压力迫使通蒂于1691年撤往皮奥里亚附近的皮米特乌堡；到1700年，塔波阿罗已不再作为独立的伊利尼部落出现。他们的后裔与佩奥利亚人、卡斯卡基亚人共命运，1763年后有佩奥利亚家族渡密西西比河西迁，1818年又依《爱德华兹维尔条约》割让伊利诺伊土地。

en:
This stretch of the Mississippi runs from the Des Moines Rapids, where the river drops over eleven miles of shallow limestone, to the wooded bluffs above the mouth of the Illinois. On both banks Illini villages planted corn, beans and squash in the bottomland and struck out on to the prairie for the winter bison hunt. The Coiracoentanon were one of the twelve or thirteen small divisions of the Illiniwek named by the French, kinsmen of the Peoria and the Tapouaro. In 1444 the river corridor was Illini country, a meeting ground between the prairie nations and the river towns downstream.

Jolliet and Marquette descended this waterway in 1673. The Coiracoentanon were among the Illinois groups associated with the Grand Village on the Illinois River; under Iroquois pressure its inhabitants dispersed toward places including Cahokia and Kaskaskia. As the Illini shrank to their French mission towns downstream, Sauk and Meskwaki bands moved into the country they had left. The peace of 1763 split the corridor, Britain taking the east bank and Spain the west; the western shore passed to the United States with the Louisiana Purchase in 1803, by which time Sauk and Meskwaki hunters ranged the east-bank bluffs.
zh:
这一段密西西比河，北起得梅因急流——河水在十一英里长的浅水石灰岩上跌落，南至伊利诺伊河口上方林木覆盖的崖岸。两岸的伊利尼村落在河漫滩种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，冬季则远赴草原围猎野牛。科伊拉科恩塔农是法国人记录的伊利尼韦克十二三个分支之一，与佩奥利亚人、塔波阿罗人同源。1444年，这条大河走廊是伊利尼人的土地，也是草原诸族与下游河镇之间的会集之地。

1673年，乔利埃特与马凯特沿这条水道南下。科伊拉科恩塔农人是与伊利诺伊河畔大村落有关的伊利诺伊人群之一；村民在易洛魁人的压力下流散，一部分迁往卡霍基亚和卡斯卡基亚等地。随着伊利尼人退缩到下游的法国传教村镇，索克人与梅斯夸基人逐渐进入他们空出的土地。1763年的和约把这条走廊一分为二：东岸归英国，西岸归西班牙；西岸于1803年随路易斯安那购地转归美国，此时东岸崖地已常有索克与梅斯夸基猎手出没。

en:
Mosopelea was the Siouan-speaking country between the Muskingum and Scioto rivers, on the north bank of the Ohio. Eight villages later mapped by Franquelin stood above the river in a land of older Hopewell mounds, Fort Ancient fields and wooded valley walls. Women tended maize, beans and squash on the bottoms, while hunters and canoe parties used the Ohio highway and the two tributary streams. The Miami-Illinois name Mosopeleacipi, river of the Mosopelea, would long preserve their name on the Ohio. In 1444 Europeans were still beyond the Alleghenies, and village councils controlled the paths, fields and fishing waters.

Seneca and other Haudenosaunee warriors overran the towns during the Beaver Wars in the early 1670s; Franquelin's 1684 map marked them as destroyed, and in 1673 French explorers believed the people had probably moved south along the Mississippi, where they became known as the Ofo. For decades the Ohio bank was mainly a Haudenosaunee hunting ground. On 15 August 1749 Céloron de Blainville buried a lead plate at the Muskingum's mouth to claim the valley for France, and in December 1751 Christopher Gist stayed at the Wyandot town of Muskingum near present Coshocton. A later Lenape town there was destroyed by Daniel Brodhead's Continental troops in April 1781. Marietta, founded at the Muskingum mouth in 1788, was the first permanent American settlement in the Northwest Territory, but on 2 January 1791 Lenape and Wyandot fighters struck the Big Bottom outpost upriver, killing fourteen settlers. The Treaty of Greenville in 1795 ended the confederate war and opened the country to American surveyors.
zh:
莫索佩莱阿是俄亥俄河北岸、马斯金格姆河与赛欧托河之间的苏语人群土地。弗兰克兰（Franquelin）后来地图所记的八座村镇位于河畔高地上，周围有更古老的霍普韦尔土丘、堡古文化农田和林木环绕的谷壁。妇女在低地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎人与独木舟队伍则利用俄亥俄这条大河及两条支流往来。迈阿密—伊利诺伊语中的莫索佩莱阿西皮（Mosopeleacipi）意为「莫索佩莱阿人之河」，使他们的名字长久留在俄亥俄河上。1444年时欧洲人仍远在阿勒格尼山脉之外，村社议事会控制着小路、农田和渔场。

17世纪70年代初，塞内卡及其他豪德诺索尼战士在河狸战争中攻陷这些村镇；弗兰克兰的1684年地图把它们标为已毁，1673年法国探险者认为他们很可能已沿密西西比河南迁，后来被称为奥福人。此后数十年，俄亥俄河畔主要成为豪德诺索尼人的猎场。1749年8月15日，塞洛隆·德·布兰维尔在马斯金格姆河口埋下铅牌，为法国宣称整个河谷；1751年12月，克里斯托弗·吉斯特住在今科肖克顿附近的怀安多特村镇马斯金格姆。后来莱纳佩人在那里建立的村镇又于1781年4月被丹尼尔·布罗德黑德率领的大陆军摧毁。1788年，玛丽埃塔在马斯金格姆河口建立，是西北领地第一个永久美国定居点；但1791年1月2日，莱纳佩与怀安多特战士袭击上游的大底部据点，杀死十四名定居者。1795年《格林维尔条约》结束联盟战争，向美国测量者开放这一地区。

en:
Tawehash preserves Taovaya, the name of a powerful Wichita people. Their later stronghold was the middle Red River, where grassy bottoms and oak groves met the plains west of the Caddo towns. In 1444 Caddoan-speaking families here combined limited river-bottom farming with seasonal bison hunts; dogs moved the camps before horses reached the region, and the middle river was Wichita and Tonkawa country. The Taovaya themselves then belonged to the Wichita world farther north in Kansas.

Coronado heard in 1541 of a Smoky Hill province called Tabas, plausibly an early Taovaya name, and from about 1630 to 1710 their villages may have stood near Marion, Kansas. French traders met Taovaya groups in 1719. During the 1720s pressure from the Osage and Apache helped push the band to the Red River, where twin towns arose on the Oklahoma and Texas banks. After France brokered peace with the Comanche in 1746, the crossing became a busy emporium: Comanches brought horses, mules and Apache captives for French powder, shot, knives and textiles, and for Taovaya maize, melons, pumpkins, squash and tobacco. In March 1758 the Comanche-led Norteño coalition burned the San Sabá mission. That August Diego Ortiz Parrilla led about five hundred Spaniards and Lipan Apaches against the fortified Red River towns, but his force was ambushed and retreated, leaving two bronze cannon. In 1771 they made peace with Spain, returning the guns in 1778, when the twin towns had 160 houses, six hundred men and perhaps 2,500 people. Smallpox in 1777–78 killed about a third of the Wichita; after another epidemic in 1801, John Sibley counted only four hundred Taovaya men in 1805. When Chief Awahakei died during a visit to Natchitoches in 1811, no successor was chosen and the tribe fragmented, some joining the Tawakoni. In 1821 the Adams-Onís Treaty made the Red River the frontier with Mexico, and the survivors were increasingly called simply Wichita.
zh:
塔韦哈什保存了塔瓦亚人（Taovaya）这支强大威奇塔群体的名字。他们后来的重镇在雷德河中游：草原河滩与橡树林在此相接，东方是卡多人的城镇。1444年，说卡多语族语言的家庭在河滩进行有限农耕，并按季节猎野牛；在马匹传入以前，营地迁移靠狗只，雷德河中游属于威奇塔人与通卡瓦人的地方。塔瓦亚人本支当时还属于更北方堪萨斯的威奇塔世界。

1541年，科罗纳多听说斯莫基希尔河一带有个叫塔巴斯的地方，其名称可能与后来的塔瓦亚有关；约1630年至1710年，他们的村镇可能位于堪萨斯的马里昂附近。1719年，法国商人接触到塔瓦亚群体。18世纪20年代，在奥塞奇人与阿帕奇人的压力下，这支威奇塔人南迁雷德河，在今俄克拉荷马与得克萨斯两岸形成双子村。1746年法国撮合他们与科曼奇人议和后，这个渡口成为繁忙商埠：科曼奇人带来马匹、骡子和阿帕奇俘虏，换取法国的火药、铅弹、刀具和纺织品，以及塔瓦亚人出产的玉米、甜瓜、南瓜、倭瓜和烟草。1758年3月，科曼奇主导的「北方人」联盟焚毁圣萨瓦传教站；同年8月，迭戈·奥尔蒂斯·帕里利亚率领约五百名西班牙人和利潘阿帕奇人进攻雷德河上设防的村镇，却遭伏击后撤退，丢弃两门青铜炮。塔瓦亚人1771年同西班牙议和，1778年归还火炮；同年双子村有一百六十座房屋、六百名男子，总人口可能约二千五百。1777年至1778年的天花已使威奇塔人损失约三分之一，1801年又有疫病，1805年约翰·西布利只统计到四百名塔瓦亚男子。1811年，酋长阿瓦哈凯在访问纳基托什期间去世，部众没有再选首领，塔瓦亚人就此离散，一部分加入塔瓦科尼人。1821年《亚当斯-奥尼斯条约》把雷德河定为同墨西哥之间的边界，幸存者也越来越多地被笼统称为威奇塔人。

en:
Kitsash preserves K'itsäsh, the name of the Kichai, a Caddoan people of the southern plains. In 1444 their villages and camps lay in the grassy river country of north-central Texas and southern Oklahoma, especially along the Red River and upper Trinity, west of the better-known Caddo towns. Their life combined river-bottom farming with seasonal bison hunting, and before the spread of horses their camps moved on foot and with dogs.

French travelers found Kichai groups on the upper Red River and at the Trinity headwaters in 1701. In 1712 they fought the Hasinai along the lower Trinity, and in 1719 Jean-Baptiste Bénard de la Harpe met them near the Canadian River during campaigns against the Apache; they first tamed horses around this time. The Kichai kept a French alliance for a period, while one branch turned toward the Wichita and another intermarried with the Kadohadacho. By 1772 their main village, east of the Trinity near present Palestine, had thirty houses and eighty warriors; a second village stood to the south in 1778, when Spanish records counted about a hundred warriors in all. Disease and the rivalry of France, Spain and Britain had greatly reduced them before 1821.
zh:
基察什（K'itsäsh，欧洲文献常作Kichai），即基蔡人，是南部平原的卡多安语族。1444年，他们的村落和营地分布在今得克萨斯中北部与俄克拉荷马南部多水草的河谷地带，尤其是雷德河与特里尼蒂河上游，位于更著名的卡多城镇以西。他们既在河滩耕作，也按季节出猎野牛；在马匹传入之前，营地迁移依靠步行和狗只。

1701年，法国旅行者在雷德河上游与特里尼蒂河源头遇见基蔡诸部。1712年，他们在特里尼蒂河下游同哈西奈人交战；1719年，让-巴蒂斯特·贝纳尔·德·拉阿尔普在加拿大河附近见到他们，当时他们正参与对抗阿帕奇人的行动，他们约在此时开始驯马。基蔡人一度与法国结盟，后来一支转向威奇托人，另一支与卡多哈达乔人通婚。到1772年，他们位于特里尼蒂河以东、近今帕勒斯坦的主村已有三十座房屋和八十名战士；1778年南侧又有一座村落，西班牙记录估计全部战士约一百人。到1821年以前，疾病以及法国、西班牙和英国的争夺已使他们人口大减。

en:
The river country along the southern edge of the plains was Tawakoni land. Spanish accounts locate their early villages around the Arkansas and Cimarron rivers, before later pressure carried bands south into Texas. In 1444 Tawakoni families planted maize, pumpkins and peas in the bottomlands and made pottery for exchange; in winter they left their domed communal grass houses for bison hunts, camping in skin tipis. They were one of the Wichita-speaking Caddoan peoples between the Plains Apaches and the eastern Caddo towns.

Jean-Baptiste Bénard de La Harpe reached a Tawakoni village in present Muskogee County in 1719, saw fields of maize and tobacco, and mediated peace between France, the Tawakoni and eight other tribes. Spanish records place their move with the Waco to the Brazos in 1730, under pressure from the French and Spanish. They remained friendly to France and hostile to Spain until 1770. Chief Quiscat travelled to San Antonio in 1772 to seek peace with the Spanish, but the agreement did not endure. By the early nineteenth century disease and warfare had greatly reduced their numbers, while their future remained tied to the Waco and the wider Wichita confederation.
zh:
平原南缘的河谷地带是塔瓦科尼人的土地。西班牙文献把他们的早期村落定在阿肯色河与锡马龙河一带，后来在外部压力下，部分群体南迁进入得克萨斯。1444年，塔瓦科尼各家在河滩种植玉米、南瓜和豌豆，制作陶器用于交换；冬季则离开木棍与干草建成的圆顶公共草屋，住进兽皮帐篷出猎野牛。他们是说威奇托语的卡多安语族之一，处在平原阿帕奇人与东部卡多城镇之间。

1719年，法国探险家让-巴蒂斯特·贝纳尔·德·拉阿尔普到达今马斯科吉县境内的一座塔瓦科尼村落，见到玉米和烟草田，并促成法国、塔瓦科尼及另外八个部族议和。西班牙资料记载，他们在法国和西班牙的压力下，于1730年与韦科人一同迁往布拉索斯河畔。直到1770年以前，他们对法国友好而对西班牙敌视。1772年，首领奎斯卡特前往圣安东尼奥寻求与西班牙议和，但协议未能持久。到19世纪初，疾病和战争已使他们人口锐减，而他们的命运仍与关系密切的韦科人及更广泛的威奇托联盟连在一起。

en:
Nabaydacu, Nabáydácu in Caddo and often written Nabedache, means 'blackberry place'. It was the westernmost Hasinai country, lying between the Neches and Trinity rivers on the edge of the Caddo world. In 1444 its permanent villages farmed maize, beans and squash in the Piney Woods, while priests kept ceremonies tied to planting and harvest. Their western position faced the plains peoples who later brought Jumano trade to Nabedache, and other Caddo towns of the Kadohadacho lay to the north.

Henri Joutel encountered the Nabedache at the Neches headwaters in 1686. Franciscans dedicated Mission San Francisco de los Tejas on 1 June 1690, but the smallpox epidemic of 1690–1691 killed an estimated 3,300 people in the area, and the Nabedache blamed the friars for the disease. Drought in 1691 and 1692 followed, and the priests burned and abandoned the mission in 1693, retreating toward Monclova. The Domingo Ramón–Saint-Denis expedition re-established it in 1716, only for it to be abandoned during the Franco-Spanish war in 1719. It reopened as San Francisco de los Neches in 1721, was withdrawn to the Colorado River in 1730 and moved to San Antonio in 1731. The Nabedache remained on their own river lands, traded with the Jumano at their western town, and moved higher on the Neches between 1779 and 1784. By 1821 epidemics, war and failed missions had greatly reduced them, but they remained the western Hasinai people.
zh:
纳拜达库（卡多语作Nabáydácu，英文常作Nabedache）意为「黑莓之地」。它是哈西奈联盟最西端的土地，位于内奇斯河与特里尼蒂河之间，处在卡多世界的边缘。1444年，这里的永久村落在松林地中种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，祭司主持与播种、收获相连的仪式。其西向位置面向大平原诸族，后来胡马诺人的贸易正是来到纳拜达库，北方则分布着卡多哈达乔人的卡多城镇。

1686年，亨利·茹泰勒在内奇斯河源头遇到纳拜达库人。1690年6月1日，方济各会建立圣方济各·德·洛斯·特哈斯传教站，但1690—1691年冬季的天花据估计在这一带夺去三千三百人的生命，纳拜达库人认为疫病是修士带来的。1691年和1692年又逢干旱，教士遂于1693年烧毁并放弃传教站，撤向蒙克洛瓦。多明各·拉蒙与圣但尼的探险队在1716年重新建站，却因法国与西班牙交战于1719年放弃。1721年，它以圣方济各·德·洛斯·内奇斯之名重开，1730年撤往科罗拉多河，1731年迁往圣安东尼奥。纳拜达库人仍留在自己的河地，在西部村镇与胡马诺人贸易，并于1779—1784年迁向内奇斯河更上游。到1821年，疫病、战争和屡次失败的传教已使他们人口大减，但他们仍是哈西奈联盟西端的人群。

en:
The Mohawk call the St Lawrence Kaniatarowanenneh, the great waterway, and above Lake St. Francis its current threads among islands and rapids where game and fish abound. In 1444 both banks were held by St. Lawrence Iroquoian villagers, speakers of Laurentian, who lived in palisaded towns of bark longhouses, grew maize, beans and squash in the river flats and took eel at their weirs. Their towns were independent of one another and of the Iroquois leagues to the south, whose Mohawk warriors were already pressing up the river.

By 1600 those towns had vanished, destroyed in the late-sixteenth-century wars with the Mohawk, and the valley became an empty hunting ground and a war-road between the Great Lakes and the French settlements. In the mid-1750s about thirty Catholic Mohawk families from Kahnawake, led by the chiefs John and Zachariah Tarbell, moved upriver to found Akwesasne, 'the land where the partridge drums'; French Jesuits opened the St Regis mission there in 1755, and its stone church was completed in 1795. The community became one of the Seven Nations of Canada. After the Revolutionary War the new international border split the villages, though the Jay Treaty of 1794 left the Mohawks free to cross it, and on 11 November 1813 a British force defeated an American army nearby at Crysler's Farm.
zh:
莫霍克人称圣劳伦斯河为卡尼亚塔罗瓦嫩（Kaniatarowanenneh），意为「大水之道」。圣弗朗西斯湖上游这一段岛屿散布、急流相接，两岸猎物鱼群丰饶。1444年时，河畔居住着说劳伦提亚语的圣劳伦斯易洛魁农人：他们的栅栏村镇由树皮长屋组成，在滩地上种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在鱼堰中捕捞鳗鱼。各个村镇互不统属，也不属于南方的易洛魁联盟，而莫霍克战士已在沿河向上进逼。

到1600年前后，这些村镇已在16世纪末与莫霍克人的战争中消亡，河谷变成空旷的猎场，以及五大湖与法兰西定居点之间的战道。18世纪50年代中期，约三十户信奉天主教的莫霍克家庭在酋长约翰·塔尔贝尔与扎卡赖亚斯·塔尔贝尔兄弟率领下，从卡纳瓦克溯河而上，建立阿克威萨斯尼（Akwesasne），意为「松鸡振翅之地」；法国耶稣会士1755年在此开设圣雷吉斯传教站，石砌教堂1795年落成，该社区后来成为加拿大七部族之一。独立战争后，新划定的国界把村落分在两边，而1794年《杰伊条约》仍允许莫霍克人自由越界；1813年11月11日，英军在附近的克莱斯勒农场击败一支美军。

en:
The Nashville Basin lies cupped within the wooded rim of the Highland Rim, the Cumberland looping through it past springs and briny licks. In 1444 it was still held by palisaded villages of the Middle Cumberland Mississippian culture, whose platform mounds had risen at river bends such as Mound Bottom since about AD 1000; their fields covered the bottoms, and bison and deer crowded the salt licks. The Yuchi of the Tennessee valley, whom the Cherokee called Aniyutsi, ranged as far as the basin's licks.

By about 1475–1500 the mound towns had collapsed, possibly under pressures including drought, disease and warfare, and for nearly two centuries the basin held no permanent villages; Shawnee bands moved in late in the 1600s, and by 1700 Cherokee and Chickasaw raiders were already contesting the ground. In 1689 the French fur trader Martin Chartier set up a post on the Cumberland near the later city, and in 1710 Jean du Charleville built beside a sulphur salt lick, the 'French Lick', where bison came for salt and hunters came to trade. From 1769 the French-Canadian trapper Timothy DeMonbreun kept a cabin there. Long hunters' reports drew the settlers: James Robertson's overland party and John Donelson's river fleet reached the lick in 1779–80 and raised Fort Nashborough, and on 13 May 1780 two hundred and fifty-six settlers signed the Cumberland Compact, a frontier constitution whose officers were paid in deerskins and otter skins. Chickamauga Cherokee raided the stations for another fourteen years, until the Nickajack campaign of September 1794, the 'last battle of the Cherokee', made the basin safe for settlement; the town had already been incorporated by North Carolina as Nashville in 1784.
zh:
纳什维尔盆地卧在林木覆盖的高地边缘台地之中，坎伯兰河蜿蜒穿流而过，河畔多有泉眼和咸涩的盐滩。1444年，这里仍分布着中坎伯兰密西西比文化的栅栏村镇：自公元1000年前后起，他们的台庙土丘已立在芒德博顿这样的河湾处，河谷低地尽是农田，野牛和鹿群挤满舔盐的盐滩。田纳西河谷的尤奇人——切罗基人称之为「阿尼尤齐」——游猎范围也远及盆地的盐滩。

约1475至1500年间，这些土丘城镇崩溃，原因可能包括干旱、疫病和战争的压力；此后近两百年盆地内没有常住的村落；17世纪末肖尼人一度进入，到1700年切罗基和奇克索的袭掠者已在争夺这片土地。1689年，法国毛皮商人马丹·沙尔捷在后来的纳什维尔附近的坎伯兰河畔设立贸易站；1710年，让·迪·沙勒维尔在一处硫磺盐滩旁建起商站，那里后来被叫作「法国盐滩」——野牛来此舔盐，猎人来此交易。1769年起，法裔加拿大捕兽人蒂莫西·德蒙布勒安在盐滩边常年留着一间小屋。长猎人带回的消息引来了移民：詹姆斯·罗伯逊的陆路队伍和约翰·多纳尔森的船队于1779至1780年抵达盐滩，筑起纳什伯勒堡；1780年5月13日，256名移民签订《坎伯兰契约》，这部边疆章程甚至规定官员薪俸用鹿皮和水獭皮支付。此后十四年，奇克莫加切罗基人不断袭掠移民据点，直到1794年9月的尼卡杰克之役——切罗基人的「最后一战」，盆地才得以安居；而城镇早在1784年就由北卡罗来纳正式建为纳什维尔。

en:
Neozho, an Osage name for clear water, is the prairie-and-timber country of the upper Neosho and Verdigris rivers southeast of the Arkansas bend. In 1444 Caddoan-speaking Wichita families planted maize, beans, squash and sunflowers on the fertile bottoms, hunted bison on the uplands, and gathered in villages of thatched-roof houses. The streams linked their fields and hunts to the Arkansas exchange network.

After Coronado's journey of 1541, the Spanish knew the wider Wichita country as Quivira. In 1719 Claude Charles du Tisné led the first official French party overland from the Osage country to two Wichita villages on the Verdigris, opening a route for French trade. Within a generation Apache and Osage pressure, disease and the trade in arms pushed the Wichita south; by 1757 they had withdrawn toward the Red River. French Louisiana passed to Spain in 1762, returned to France, and was sold to the United States in 1803. Osage bands then hunted across the Neosho and Verdigris grounds, and Lewis and Clark reported an Arkansas Osage band on the Verdigris in 1804. Fur traders followed the streams, but in 1821 no European town yet stood in the valleys.
zh:
尼欧肖一名来自欧塞奇语，意为清水；这里是阿肯色河大拐弯东南、尼欧肖河与弗迪格里斯河上游的草原林地。1444年，说卡多语的威奇托家族在肥沃低地种植玉米、豆子、南瓜和向日葵，到高地猎捕野牛，并在茅草顶屋舍组成的村落中聚集。河川把他们的田地与猎场连接到阿肯色河的交换网络。

科罗纳多1541年旅行之后，西班牙人把更广阔的威奇托地区称作基维拉。1719年，克洛德·沙尔·迪蒂斯内率领法国首个正式使团从欧塞奇地区陆路西行，抵达弗迪格里斯河畔的两座威奇托村落，为法国贸易打开通路。此后不到一代人，阿帕奇人与欧塞奇人的压力、疾病和火器贸易把威奇托人推向南方；到1757年，他们已退向雷德河。法属路易斯安那1762年转交西班牙，后来归还法国，并于1803年售予美国。那时欧塞奇支系已在尼欧肖河与弗迪格里斯河的猎场活动，刘易斯与克拉克1804年记载了弗迪格里斯河上的阿肯色欧塞奇支系。毛皮商人随后循河而来，但到1821年，河谷中仍没有欧洲人的城镇。

en:
Pitahawirata, also called the Tappage or Noisy Pawnee, is the southern Pawnee river country between the Republican and the Platte, where Nebraska's plains slope toward Kansas. In 1444 the Caddoan villagers ancestral to the three southern bands lived in earth lodges, raised maize, beans and squash, and organized foot hunts for bison. Priests and hereditary chiefs directed ceremonies and village affairs before horses or European firearms had reached the grasslands. Their ties were closer to the Chaui and Kitkehahki and to the Wichita farther south than to the Skidi on the Loup.

The first written account of this wider Caddoan world came in 1541, when Coronado found farming towns in Quivira near the Arkansas and learned of Harahey beyond them, without reaching the later Pitahawirata country. By 1750 the southern Pawnee and Wichita held secure Arkansas River grounds linked to French arms. After France ceded Louisiana in 1763, Spanish trade restrictions interrupted that supply while the Osage, armed through French and British channels, drove between the allies. A Spanish report placed the Pawnee in Nebraska by 1777. In 1806 Facundo Melgares and Zebulon Pike visited the nearby Kitkehahki Republican River village, where Pike replaced a Spanish flag with an American one. War with the Kanza in 1809–1811 drew more villagers toward the Platte, and the Pawnee made their first land cession to the United States in 1818.
zh:
皮塔哈维拉塔又称「喧哗波尼人」，是波尼人南部的河畔地方，位于共和河与普拉特河之间，内布拉斯加平原由此向堪萨斯倾斜。1444年时，后来组成三支南部波尼的卡多语先民住在土屋中，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，并结队徒步猎捕野牛。马匹和欧洲火器尚未进入草原，祭司与世袭酋长掌管仪式和村务。与卢普河的斯基迪人相比，他们同查维人、基特克哈基人以及更南方的威奇托人关系更近。

关于这一广阔卡多语世界的最早文字记载见于1541年：科罗纳多在阿肯色河附近的基维拉发现农耕村镇，又听说更北的哈拉海，但他并未到达后来的皮塔哈维拉塔地方。到1750年，南部波尼人与威奇托人已在阿肯色河流域建立稳固领地，并与法国武器贸易相连。1763年法国割让路易斯安那后，西班牙的贸易限制切断了这条供给线，得到法国和英国渠道武器的奥塞奇人则插入同盟各部之间。1777年的西班牙报告已把波尼人记在内布拉斯加。1806年，法昆多·梅尔加雷斯和泽布伦·派克先后来到附近共和河畔的基特克哈基村，派克在那里换下西班牙旗，升起美国旗。1809—1811年与堪萨人的战争又把更多村民引向普拉特河，1818年波尼人首次向美国割让土地。

en:
The Niobrara runs out of the Sand Hills to join the Missouri through wooded bottomland at the southeastern edge of the South Dakota plains. In 1444 its terraces held earth-lodge villages of Caddoan-speaking farmers, kin to the Pawnee and Arikara. Their women tended fields of corn, beans, squash and sunflowers, seasonal parties went out after the bison herds, and dugout canoes moved grain and hides along the Missouri. Here the settled river world met the open bison plains.

Late in the 17th century the Siouan-speaking Ponca, moving west with the Omaha, reached the river and clashed with the Arikara before peace was made; Arikara women taught the Omaha to build earth lodges. A map drawn by Le Sueur in 1701 already places the Ponca on the upper Missouri. By the end of the century the Ponca were fixed at the Niobrara's mouth. In 1789 the fur trader Juan Baptiste Munier built a post at the confluence and counted some eight hundred Ponca, but smallpox swept them soon after, and when Lewis and Clark came in 1804 barely two hundred remained. The Ponca kept their cornfields and gardens even as the mounted life of the plains closed around them.
zh:
奈厄布拉勒河从沙丘地带流出，在南达科他平原东南缘穿过林木茂盛的低地汇入密苏里河。1444年，河畔阶地上分布着卡多语系农耕者的土屋村庄，他们是波尼人和阿里卡拉人的亲族。妇女照料玉米、豆类、南瓜和向日葵田，季节性的队伍出猎野牛，独木舟载着粮食和兽皮在密苏里河上往来。定居的河畔世界与开阔的猎牛平原就在这里相接。

17世纪末，使用苏语的潘卡人（篷卡人）与奥马哈人一同西迁到这条河边，先与阿里卡拉人交战，后来议和；阿里卡拉妇女还教奥马哈人建造土屋。1701年勒叙厄尔绘制的地图已把潘卡人标在上密苏里河畔。到18世纪末，潘卡人已定居在奈厄布拉勒河口。1789年，皮货商胡安·巴蒂斯特·米尼埃在两河交汇处建起贸易站，清点出约八百名潘卡人；但天花随即袭来，到1804年刘易斯与克拉克到来时，幸存者仅剩约二百人。即使马背平原生活已将他们包围，潘卡人仍守着自己的玉米田和菜园。

en:
Selis is the Séliš name of the people Euro-Americans later called Flathead. The province is their old Upper Missouri country, where the Jefferson, Madison and Gallatin rivers meet to form the Missouri and the Big Hole and Beaverhead valleys run beneath the Continental Divide. In 1444 Séliš bands wintered in sheltered camps near the later Helena and Butte country and in the Big Hole, crossed the divide on seasonal hunts, and before horses used dogs and tule-mat lodges; Shoshone neighbours held the mountains to their south while Blackfoot rivals controlled the plains to the east.

Horses acquired from the Shoshone made long bison drives possible, but firearms gave the Blackfoot a different advantage. Between 1700 and 1750 foot-borne Blackfoot warriors with guns forced the Séliš from their eastern bison range, while war and smallpox broke neighboring bands; Séliš families increasingly wintered in the Bitterroot Valley, though they crossed the divide once or twice each year to hunt buffalo. In late July 1805 Lewis and Clark camped at the Three Forks, named the Jefferson, Madison and Gallatin, and ascended the Jefferson. On 4 September, at Ross Hole, they found a Séliš camp of roughly 400 people, received food and traded for pack horses, then camped at Travelers' Rest from 9 to 11 September before taking the Lolo Trail. From about 1810 North West Company, Hudson's Bay Company and American Fur Company trappers began working the Big Hole beaver streams.
zh:
塞利斯（Selis）来自萨利什人自称塞利什（Séliš），后来的欧美探险者称他们为平头印第安人。这一省是他们在密苏里河上游的故地：杰斐逊河、麦迪逊河与加勒廷河在此汇成密苏里河，比格霍尔河与比弗黑德河谷沿大陆分水岭延伸。1444年，塞利什各部在后来的赫勒拿、比尤特一带和比格霍尔河谷的避风雪营地过冬，按季节翻过山岭狩猎；马匹到来之前，他们使用狗和香蒲草席铺成的营帐。休休尼邻人占据南面山地，黑脚竞争者则控制东面平原。

从休休尼人手中获得马匹后，长距离驱赶野牛成为可能，但火器给了黑脚人另一种优势。1700年至1750年间，徒步而持有枪械的黑脚战士把塞利什人从东部野牛猎场逼退，战争与天花也削弱了相邻部落；塞利什家庭越来越多地到比特鲁特谷过冬，但每年仍会一两次翻过分水岭猎牛。1805年7月下旬，刘易斯—克拉克探险队在三河汇流处扎营，为杰斐逊河、麦迪逊河和加勒廷河命名，随后沿杰斐逊河上行。9月4日，他们在罗斯洼地遇到约400名塞利什人，获得食物并交换驮马；9月9日至11日又在旅人休憩地扎营，随后走上洛洛小道。约1810年起，西北公司、哈德逊湾公司和美国毛皮公司的捕兽者开始进入比格霍尔河的河狸溪流。

en: The Hunkpapha, whose Lakota name means 'Head of the Circle', were one of the seven Lakota bands. In 1444 the short-grass plains between the Missouri and the Grand and Cannonball rivers were still pedestrian bison-hunting country; the Saone Lakota who carried Hunkpapa ancestry did not reach Lake Traverse until after 1720 or the Missouri's east bank until about 1750. Horses obtained through Cheyenne networks around 1730, called 'mysterious dogs', reshaped the hunt, while the smallpox epidemic that reached the northern plains in 1781 shattered Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara barriers and opened the river crossing. Lewis and Clark's tense meeting with Teton Lakota in 1804 marked the first American contact on this frontier; a 1805 estimate put the Hunkpapa at about 1,600 people in 160 tipis. By 1821 their mounted camps were extending across the Grand-Cannonball grazing grounds.
zh: 洪克帕帕（Hunkpapha，拉科塔语意为「营圈之首」）是拉科塔七支之一。1444年，密苏里河与格兰德河、坎农博尔河之间的短草草原还是徒步猎牛者的天地，承载洪克帕帕源流的索恩拉科塔人要到1720年后才抵达特拉弗斯湖一带，约1750年才进抵密苏里河东岸。约1730年，马匹经夏安人的商路传入，被称为「神犬」，改变了野牛猎营；1781年传至北部平原的天花重挫曼丹、希达察和阿里卡拉村落，也打开了渡河通道。1804年，刘易斯与克拉克与梯顿拉科塔人紧张对峙，这是美国在这一边疆的初次接触；1805年的估计称洪克帕帕约有1600人、160座梯皮。到1821年，他们的骑马营地正扩展到格兰德河与坎农博尔河之间的牧场。

en:
The southwestern prairie of Manitoba is open grassland cut by the Assiniboine River and its tributary the Souris, the northern reach of the great bison plains. Its people were the Nakota, whom their neighbours called the Assiniboine, Siouan-speakers whose camps followed the herds on foot in an age before horses reached the northern plains, and who pounded dried bison meat, fat and berries into pemmican for winter and for trade. Their northern road ran to the Cree on the lake chain; winters were passed in wooded river bottoms and the summers in communal buffalo pounds. In 1444 these were the only roads Nakota country knew, for no European had yet crossed the grass.

Henry Kelsey of the Hudson's Bay Company travelled south with Assiniboine parties in 1690–92, the first European to describe the Nakota, and saw the immense bison herds of the plains. In 1738 La Vérendrye built Fort La Reine on the Assiniboine, and that October set out with Assiniboine guides for the Mandan villages on the upper Missouri, which he reached in winter. During the eighteenth century the Assiniboine became a horse people and joined the Cree in the Iron Confederacy, acting as middlemen of the fur trade. Smallpox swept the plains from 1780 and reached the Hudson's Bay Company's inland posts in 1782, ravaging Assiniboine camps. In 1793 two rival posts rose near the mouth of the Souris, the North West Company's Fort Assiniboine and the Hudson's Bay Company's Brandon House, which sent horse trains and dog sleds south to the Mandan. In May 1816, during the Pemmican War, Cuthbert Grant's men sacked Brandon House. When the two companies merged in 1821, the long rivalry of the Souris River posts ended with it.
zh:
锡哈比位于马尼托巴西南部的开阔草原，阿西尼博因河及其支流苏里斯河蜿蜒而过，这里已是北美大野牛草原的北端。住在这片土地上的是纳科塔人，邻族称之为阿西尼博因人，操苏语族语言。马匹传到北部草原之前，他们的营地徒步追随兽群，把野牛肉干、油脂和浆果舂成肉糜饼，供过冬和交易之用。向北有通往湖链克里人的商路；冬天他们栖身在林木茂密的河谷，夏天集体围猎野牛。1444年的纳科塔之地只有这些道路，欧洲人尚未踏上这片草原。

1690年至1692年，哈德逊湾公司的亨利·凯尔西随阿西尼博因队伍南行，成为第一个记述纳科塔人的欧洲人，也见到了草原上无边的野牛群。1738年，拉韦朗德里在阿西尼博因河畔修建拉雷讷堡，同年10月由阿西尼博因向导带路，前往密苏里河上游的曼丹人村落，于冬季抵达。18世纪里，阿西尼博因人成为马背上的民族，并与克里人结成铁器联盟，充当毛皮贸易的中间人。1780年起天花横扫草原，1782年传到哈德逊湾公司的内陆商栈，阿西尼博因营地死者枕藉。1793年，苏里斯河口附近立起两座对头商栈：西北公司的阿西尼博因堡和哈德逊湾公司的布兰登馆，后者用马队和狗拉雪橇南下与曼丹人交易。1816年5月，干肉饼战争期间，卡斯伯特·格兰特的人马洗劫了布兰登馆；待两公司1821年合并，苏里斯河畔两座对头商栈的多年相争才告收场。

en:
Wadopabina is the Assiniboine, or Nakota, name of the Canoe Paddlers; their Cree neighbours called them the Paddling Assiniboine. Their country is the canoe corridor between the Saskatchewan lowlands and the upper Assiniboine: the Swan River comes out of the Porcupine Hills, runs between those hills and the Duck Mountains, enters Swan Lake and goes by the Shoal River to Lake Winnipegosis, while a short portage at the river's bend reaches the Assiniboine. In 1444 Nakota bands moving northwest through this lake country used the route for fishing, moose and beaver hunting and summer bison hunts on the parkland edge, carrying their trade in canoes before horses or European goods had arrived.

Henry Kelsey reached the upper Assiniboine from Hudson Bay in 1691, and French traders entered the lake chain after 1731. In 1741 Pierre Gaultier de La Vérendrye, a son of the elder La Vérendrye, built Fort Dauphin on Lake Winnipegosis; French traders put up a second fort of the name on Dauphin Lake in 1767. The Swan River route became a company road in the 1780s: the North West Company built Swan River Fort in 1787, Charles Isham answered for the Hudson's Bay Company with Swan River House in 1790, and Marlboro House, Bird Mountain House, Somerset House, Carlton House and Fort Alexandria followed between 1793 and 1795. The beaver grounds were soon trapped out; the Hudson's Bay posts closed and were briefly reopened under Peter Fidler in 1807–08. The North West Company held on until 1821, when the merger of the two companies closed the Swan River posts and ended their first generation of trade.
zh:
瓦多帕比纳是阿西尼博因人（纳科塔人）对「划独木舟者」的称呼，邻近的克里人则称他们为「划桨的阿西尼博因人」。他们的土地是萨斯喀彻温低地通往上阿西尼博因河的独木舟走廊：斯旺河发源于豪猪丘陵，在豪猪丘陵与鸭山之间前行，注入斯旺湖，再经肖尔河进入温尼伯戈西斯湖；在河道转弯处经一段短途陆运，又可抵达阿西尼博因河。1444年，向西北迁入这片湖泽之地的纳科塔族群沿这条路线捕鱼，猎驼鹿和海狸，夏季到林缘草原猎野牛；那时马匹和欧洲货物尚未到来，贸易都靠独木舟搬运。

1691年，亨利·凯尔西从哈得孙湾抵达阿西尼博因河上游；1731年后，法国商人进入这串湖泊。1741年，老拉韦朗德里之子皮埃尔·戈蒂埃·德·拉韦朗德里在温尼伯戈西斯湖畔建立多凡堡，法国商人又于1767年在多凡湖畔建起第二座同名商栈。1780年代，斯旺河水道成为公司商路：西北公司1787年建斯旺河堡，查尔斯·艾沙姆代表哈得孙湾公司于1790年设斯旺河商栈；1793至1795年间，马尔伯勒商栈、鸟山商栈、萨默塞特商栈、卡尔顿商栈和亚历山德里亚堡相继设立。海狸产地很快被捕猎殆尽，哈得孙湾公司关闭各处商栈，又于1807至1808年由彼得·菲德勒主持短暂重开。西北公司一直维持到1821年；两家公司合并后，斯旺河诸栈关闭，这一带最初一代毛皮贸易随之结束。

en:
Kuttawa is the wooded lower Cumberland country, where the river makes eddies above its Ohio mouth and bison traces cross the narrow country between the Cumberland and Tennessee. Mississippian people built the Tolu mound town nearby from about 1200 to 1450; its burial mound, platform mound and plaza belonged to the Angel-Kincaid network, and a finely carved fluorite statue later found west of Tolu showed the region's skill in stonework. In 1444 that mound-building world was in its final years, while Shawnee hunters, farmers and canoe travelers still knew the river as Wasioto. The name Kuttawa would preserve a Cherokee woodland-village name, though its exact meaning remains disputed.

French traders later called the waterway the Rivière des Chaouanons, the River of the Shawnee, before the Virginia explorer Thomas Walker gave it the English name Cumberland. Hunters and settlers followed the old bison traces through the Between the Rivers woods, and traffic gathered at the Cumberland's mouth, where an inn later known as the Gower House was built about 1780 for river travelers. Eddyville, named from the river's eddies, was settled around 1798 and became the seat of newly formed Livingston County in 1799; its post office opened in 1801. By then the lower Cumberland was no longer simply a Shawnee hunting river and war trail: keelboats and flatboats carried frontier produce north into the Ohio and Mississippi.
zh:
库塔瓦是林木覆盖的下坎伯兰地区：河水在汇入俄亥俄河前形成漩涡，野牛踏出的小径穿过坎伯兰河与田纳西河之间的狭长林地。约1200年至1450年间，密西西比文化居民在附近修建托卢土墩镇，镇中的墓葬墩、台墩和广场属于安吉尔—金凯德网络；后来在托卢以西发现的精美萤石雕像也显示出这片地区的石雕技艺。1444年，这个土墩世界已近尾声，而肖尼猎人、农民和独木舟旅人仍把这条河称作瓦西奥托。库塔瓦之名后来保存了一个切罗基林地村落的名称，但确切含义一直没有定论。

后来法国商人把这条水道称为「肖尼人之河」；弗吉尼亚探险者托马斯·沃克则为它取了英文名坎伯兰。猎人和定居者沿古老野牛小径穿过「两河之间」的森林，人流汇集到坎伯兰河口，约1780年，后来称作高尔宅第的旅店在那里为河上旅人而建。埃迪维尔因河中的漩涡得名，约1798年形成定居点，1799年成为新设利文斯顿县的县治，1801年开设邮局。到这时，下坎伯兰已不只是肖尼人的猎河与战争通道，龙骨船和平底船把边疆物产北运俄亥俄河与密西西比河。

en:
Pepikokia is the Tippecanoe watershed, running from the kettle lakes and marshes near present Warsaw down to the Wabash above Lafayette. The Miami band was also called Kiteepihkwana, people of the buffalo-fish place, and its principal village Kithtippecanuck moved at different times between the river's headwaters and its mouth. In 1444 these woods and wet prairies were Miami hunting and planting country: cornfields lay in the bottoms, fishing weirs took buffalo fish and pike, and trails led southwest to the Wea at Ouiatenon and northeast to Kekionga.

The Beaver Wars scattered the Miami toward western Lake Michigan, but French firearms and trade allowed their return around 1700. French records place the Tepicon band near Ouiatenon until 1733 and then on the upper Tippecanoe near Warsaw until 1751; after 1742 the French commonly counted the Pepikokia with the Wea, though their villages kept their own leaders. Smallpox devastated them in 1752, killing an older pro-French chief named Le Gris; some survivors founded a village by the St. Joseph near Kekionga, while Kithtippecanuck leaned toward Ouiatenon. The younger Le Gris, Nagohquangogh, joined Henry Hamilton's Wabash expedition in 1778 and his village raided with the British during the Revolution. American militia burned Tippecanoe villages in 1791, but Le Gris survived the Western Confederacy's defeat at Fallen Timbers in 1794 and signed the Treaty of Greenville in 1795. On 7 November 1811 William Henry Harrison destroyed Prophetstown at the river's mouth, breaking Tecumseh's movement in the country from which the Pepikokia took their name.
zh:
佩皮科基亚是蒂珀卡讷河流域，河水从今沃索附近的冰蚀湖与沼泽流下，直达拉斐特以上注入沃巴什河之处。这个迈阿密支派又称基蒂皮夸纳，意为「牛胭脂鱼之地的人」，主村基斯蒂佩卡努克曾在不同时期设于河源与河口之间。1444年，这些林地和湿草原是迈阿密人的游猎与种植之地：玉米田分布在低地上，鱼梁捕捉牛胭脂鱼和狗鱼，小路向西南通往乌亚塔农的韦阿人，向东北通往凯基翁加。

海狸战争曾把迈阿密人驱向密歇根湖西岸，但约1700年，他们依靠法国火器和贸易重返故地。法国记载显示，特皮孔部到1733年住在乌亚塔农附近，1733至1751年又住在沃索附近的蒂珀卡讷河上游；1742年后法国人常把佩皮科基亚人归入韦阿人，但他们的村落仍保留自己的首领。1752年天花重创此部，亲法的老酋长勒格里病死；一些幸存者在凯基翁加附近的圣约瑟夫河畔另建村落，基斯蒂佩卡努克则倾向乌亚塔农。年轻的勒格里（纳戈匡戈）1778年参加亨利·汉密尔顿的沃巴什远征，他的村落也在独立战争中随英军袭扰。1791年美国民团焚毁蒂珀卡讷诸村；1794年西部联盟在福伦廷伯斯战败后，勒格里又在1795年签署《格林维尔条约》。1811年11月7日，威廉·亨利·哈里森在河口摧毁先知镇，特库姆塞运动正是在这条赋予佩皮科基亚人名字的河流边受挫。

en:
Pacaha was a Mississippian polity on the Mississippi bends of northeastern Arkansas. Its Nodena-phase villages lined the river from the Missouri Bootheel to Wapanocca Lake. The Bradley site near Turrell is the leading candidate for its paramount town, while the 15-acre Nodena site, with two large substructure mounds, plazas and a chunkey field, was either that town or a major satellite. In 1444 maize fields and river fisheries supported a dense population, chert and whelk shells moved through ceremonial exchange, and long war with Casqui kept bastions and palisades at the centre of town life.

De Soto entered Pacaha in 1541 and remained for about forty days. Casqui men following the expedition attacked while many Pacaha fled toward a river island; some drowned, the town was sacked and its sacred places desecrated. De Soto first promised Pacaha help in punishing Casqui, then accepted the return of the spoils and brought the two chiefs together for a dinner and a peace treaty. The encounter is the only direct historical record of Pacaha. Nodena's village ended around 1650, and by the 1670s this stretch of river was held by Dhegiha Siouan-speaking Quapaw; a resemblance between the names Capaha and Kappa has suggested continuity, but the link remains unproved.
zh:
帕卡哈是阿肯色东北部密西西比河曲一带的密西西比文化酋邦。诺德纳阶段村落沿密西西比河分布，北起密苏里靴跟地带，南至瓦帕诺卡湖；蒂雷尔附近的布拉德利遗址最可能是其主邑，诺德纳遗址则是一座15英亩的木栅重镇，有两座大台墩、多处广场和舂克伊游戏场，可能是主邑或重要从属城镇。1444年，玉米田与河渔支撑起稠密人口，燧石和海螺壳通过仪式交换流通；而同西南方卡斯基的长期战争，使棱堡和木栅成为城镇生活的中心。

1541年，德索托远征队进入帕卡哈并停留约40天。随远征队前来的卡斯基人趁许多帕卡哈人逃向河中岛屿时发动袭击，一些人溺亡，城镇遭到洗劫，祭祀场所也被亵渎。德索托先向帕卡哈承诺协助惩罚卡斯基，随后在战利品归还后安排两位酋长共餐并缔和。这次相遇也是帕卡哈仅有的直接历史记载。诺德纳村镇约在1650年终结，到1670年代，这一段河岸已由使用德吉哈语支苏语的夸帕人占据；有学者因卡帕哈（Capaha）与卡帕（Kappa）两名相近而推测二者承续，但这种关联仍未得到证实。

en:
Maui, the Valley Isle, joins the West Maui Mountains to Haleakalā by a broad isthmus. In 1444 its windward east around Hāna and its drier western coast remained separate chiefly worlds. Lahaina, then called Lele, stood among breadfruit and coconut groves as a royal settlement of western Maui. The kapu order governed rank, fishing, war and religion; at Kihei the Koʻieʻie walled fishpond, built between 1400 and 1500, used lava and coral walls to fatten mullet and milkfish. Taro gardens, reef fisheries, temple lands and large canoes gave the island's chiefs their power.

Later in the fifteenth century Piʻilani became the first ruler to unite western and eastern Maui, and the island road he began was wide enough for eight men to walk abreast. Cook sighted Maui on 26 November 1778 but could not land; Hawaiian war canoes met his ships off Lahaina. Jean-François de Galaup de Lapérouse became the first European ashore at La Pérouse Bay on 29 May 1786. Kamehameha invaded in 1790 and fought the bloody Kepaniwai battle in ʻĪao Valley, where John Young and Isaac Davis served his cannon and corpses were said to dam the stream, yet Maui did not pass permanently under his rule until 1795. Kamehameha stationed his peleleu war-canoe fleet at Lahaina in 1802–1803, and Kamehameha II resided there from December 1819 to February 1820.
zh:
毛伊（Maui）又称「峡谷之岛」，西毛伊山脉与哈雷阿卡拉火山由宽阔地峡相连。1444年时，以哈纳为中心的迎风东部和较干燥的西海岸仍分属不同酋长势力。拉海纳当时称莱莱，坐落在面包果树与椰林之间，是西毛伊的酋长聚落。卡普秩序规范身份、渔捞、战争与祭祀；在基黑一带，1400至1500年间修筑的科伊埃伊埃（Koʻieʻie）石墙鱼塘以熔岩和珊瑚筑成，让鲻鱼和遮目鱼在墙后育肥。芋田、礁海渔场、神庙属地与大型独木舟共同支撑着岛上酋长的权力。

15世纪后期，皮伊拉尼（Piʻilani）成为首位统一毛伊东西两部的统治者，他开始修建的环岛道路宽阔得可让八人并行。1778年11月26日，库克望见毛伊却无法靠岸，夏威夷战独木舟曾在拉海纳外与他的船队相遇。1786年5月29日，法国航海家拉佩鲁兹在后来以他命名的海湾登陆，成为最早踏上毛伊的欧洲人。1790年，卡美哈梅哈入侵毛伊，在伊奥河谷打了惨烈的可帕尼瓦伊战役；约翰·扬和艾萨克·戴维斯为他操作火炮，据说尸体阻塞了河水，但毛伊到1795年才正式转入他的统治。1802至1803年，卡美哈梅哈把佩莱莱乌战独木舟舰队驻扎在拉海纳；1819年12月至1820年2月，卡美哈梅哈二世也曾驻跸于此。

en:
Oʻahu rises from the sea in two volcanic ranges, the Waiʻanae and Koʻolau, with a broad central plain between them and sheltered anchorages on its southern shore. Polynesian families had turned valleys and reefs into an economy of agroforestry, taro grounds, fishponds and fishing grounds, while women made decorated kapa bark cloth. The island was an independent chiefdom under an aliʻi nui, and Kūkaniloko on the central plain was the sacred birthplace where high-ranking children were born before chiefly witnesses. In 1444 Oʻahu's courts, temples and lands belonged to that separate Hawaiian world, untouched by European ships.

Around 1480 the lawmaker Maʻilikūkahi founded the chiefly house that long ruled Oʻahu. James Cook sighted the island in January 1778, the first Hawaiian island seen on his third voyage, but sailed on to Kauaʻi; after Cook's death, Charles Clerke brought the ships briefly into Waimea Bay on 27 February 1779. Kahekili II of Maui conquered Oʻahu in 1783 and placed his son Kalanikūpule over it. In May 1795 Kamehameha I's army destroyed Kalanikūpule's forces at the Battle of Nuʻuanu, driving defenders from the great pali and bringing Oʻahu into the new Hawaiian Kingdom; Kauaʻi's submission in 1810 completed the unification. Foreign ships had entered Honolulu Harbor from 1794, and Kamehameha kept court at Waikīkī from 1804 and near Honolulu from 1809 before returning to Kailua-Kona in 1812. After his death in 1819, Kamehameha II's ʻAi Noa broke the old kapu and ended the temples' authority, leaving Oʻahu in 1821 open to traders, whalers and missionaries.
zh:
瓦胡（Oʻahu，中文也译欧胡）岛由怀厄奈和柯欧劳两列火山山脉托起，中间是宽阔平原，南岸则有可避风浪的锚地。波利尼西亚人在山谷和礁岸发展出农林、芋头地、鱼塘与渔场相结合的生计，妇女制作带纹饰的卡帕树皮布。瓦胡本是由阿利伊努伊统治的独立酋邦，中央平原上的库卡尼洛科是圣地，出身高贵的孩子会在酋长见证下出生于此。1444年，岛上的宫廷、神庙和土地仍属于这个独立的夏威夷世界，欧洲船只尚未到来。

约1480年，立法者马伊利库卡希开创了长期统治瓦胡的王族。1778年1月，詹姆斯·库克在第三次航行中最先望见瓦胡，但船队继续前往考爱；库克死后，查尔斯·克拉克于1779年2月27日率船短暂进入怀梅阿湾。1783年，茂伊岛的卡赫基利二世征服瓦胡，立其子卡拉尼库普莱为统治者。1795年5月，卡美哈梅哈一世的军队在努阿努战役中击溃卡拉尼库普莱的部队，把守军逼下高耸的帕利悬崖，瓦胡由此并入新建立的夏威夷王国；1810年考爱归服，群岛统一。外国船只自1794年已驶入檀香山（火奴鲁鲁）港，卡美哈梅哈1804年起驻跸威基基，1809年迁到檀香山附近，1812年又返回凯卢阿—科纳。1819年他去世后，卡美哈梅哈二世以「艾诺亚」之举打破旧卡普戒律，结束神庙权威；到1821年，瓦胡已向商人、捕鲸者和传教士敞开。

en:
Kauaʻi is the oldest and north-westernmost of the main Hawaiian islands, a rainy volcanic land cut by the Waimea and Wailua rivers. In 1444 it was an independent high chiefship linked with Niʻihau. The east coast around Tapaʻa, the Kauaʻi dialect form of Kapaʻa, bordered Wailua, land of aliʻi and one of the island's largest ahupuaʻa; its river was navigable and its heiau complex marked a royal route. At the Hulēʻia River the 900-foot Alekoko fishpond wall was taking shape in the fifteenth century, managing brackish-water fishing. Taro and sweet-potato irrigation, pigs, fowl, reefs and fishponds sustained the kapu society of Kauaʻi's aliʻi nui.

On 20 January 1778 Cook's Resolution and Discovery anchored at Waimea, taking water and trading iron nails for food in the first recorded European contact with Hawaiians; one Kauaian had been shot dead in a confused confrontation the previous day. The island outlasted the others: a Kamehameha invasion from Oʻahu was abandoned in 1796 during a rebellion, and a second attempt in 1803 was undone by epidemic. In 1810 Kaumualiʻi kept authority on Kauaʻi but acknowledged Kamehameha as overlord. After the Russian-American Company ship Bering was wrecked in January 1815, Georg Anton Schäffer turned a salvage claim into a protectorate scheme; Waimea received a Russian-backed star fort in 1817, but American traders and Kamehameha's pressure forced Schäffer out that autumn. On 16 September 1821 Kamehameha II enticed Kaumualiʻi aboard ship and carried him to Honolulu, ending Kauaʻi's separate court.
zh:
考爱（Kauaʻi）是夏威夷主要岛屿中最古老、位置最西北的火山岛，韦梅阿河与怀卢阿河切开多雨的山地。1444年时，这里是与尼豪相连的独立最高酋长国。东岸的塔帕阿（Tapaʻa，即标准夏威夷语中的Kapaʻa）邻近怀卢阿；怀卢阿是酋长之地，也是岛上最大的阿胡普阿之一，河道可通航，神庙群标示出王族道路。胡莱阿河畔的阿莱科科鱼塘在15世纪成形，270米长的石墙用于管理咸淡水鱼汛。芋田、甜薯灌溉园、猪禽、礁海和鱼塘，供养着考爱阿利伊努伊治下按卡普秩序运行的社会。

1778年1月20日，库克的「决心号」和「发现号」在韦梅阿停泊取水，用铁钉和铁器换取食物，这是欧洲人与夏威夷人有记录的首次接触；前一天的混乱中已有一名考爱人中枪身亡。考爱比其他各岛保持独立更久：卡美哈梅哈1796年从瓦胡发起的远征因后方叛乱中止，1803年第二次尝试又被疫病挫败。1810年，考穆阿利伊保留在考爱的统治权，但承认卡美哈梅哈为宗主。1815年1月俄美公司商船「白令号」在考爱失事后，格奥尔格·安东·舍费尔把索赔变成保护国计划；1817年韦梅阿出现俄国支持的星形要塞，但美国商人和卡美哈梅哈的压力迫使舍费尔于秋季离岛。1821年9月16日，卡美哈梅哈二世把考穆阿利伊诱上船并带往檀香山，考爱的独立宫廷就此终结。

en:
Lau is Fiji's eastern archipelago, strung across the sea east of the Koro Sea: volcanic high islands rise in the northern chain, while the south is a line of reefs and low limestone islands. Fertile, well-watered Lakeba was its most important chiefly island and a meeting place of Fijian and Tongan voyagers; Tongan speech, house forms and ceremonies entered Lau along the canoe routes. In 1444 no single chief ruled all Lau. Northern Lau, southern Lau and the Moala Islands followed separate chiefs, tribute ties and maritime exchanges.

European ships reached this edge of Fiji late. James Cook's expedition sighted Vatoa on 2 July 1774, and the master and some crew went ashore the next day; it was the only Fijian island visited during his voyage. In June 1791 William Oliver and men from the Matavy, tender to HMS Pandora, made the first recorded European communication with Fijians at Ono-i-Lau. When the Ono group was charted in 1820, Lau was the best-known part of Fiji to European navigators, though the islands still had no mission or European settlement and remained under their own chiefs.
zh:
劳（Lau）是斐济东部岛群，散布在科罗海以东海域：北部链岛多火山高地，南部则是礁盘和低矮石灰岩岛。土地肥沃、水源充足的拉肯巴岛是最重要的酋长岛，也是斐济人和汤加航海者交会之处；汤加语、房屋形制和礼仪随独木舟航线传入劳群岛。1444年时，劳并不由单一酋长统治，北劳、南劳和莫阿拉群岛各有酋长、贡赋关系与海上交换网络。

欧洲船只很晚才抵达斐济这一东缘。1774年7月2日，詹姆斯·库克的船队望见瓦托阿，次日船长和部分船员登岸；这是他那次航行中唯一造访的斐济岛屿。1791年6月，英国军舰「潘多拉号」的补给船「马塔维号」在威廉·奥利弗率领下抵达奥诺劳，留下欧洲人与斐济人接触的最早记录。1820年奥诺群岛被绘入海图时，劳已是欧洲航海者最熟悉的斐济海域，但岛上尚无传教站或欧洲人定居点，仍由本地酋长掌控。

en:
Vanua Levu ('Big Land') is Fiji's second-largest island, 64 kilometres north of Viti Levu. Rugged ridges divide its coasts, while the three-river delta around Labasa and the surrounding reefs supplied fishing villages with fish and garden land. The island was settled about 3,100 years ago; after the Pacific sea level fell by 30 centimetres between 1250 and 1350, reef food declined and the water table dropped, feeding conflict and a move into fortified hilltop villages. In 1444 Vanua Levu was divided among competing chiefs, elders and warriors, whose strongholds overlooked coastal landings and river mouths.

Abel Tasman became the first known European to sight the island in 1643. William Bligh passed through its waters in 1789 while escaping after the Bounty mutiny, and James Wilson explored the area in the Duff in 1797. In January 1800 the American schooner Argo was wrecked south-east of Fiji; Oliver Slater, one of the survivors, lived on Vanua Levu for two years and carried news of sandalwood near Bua Bay to China. Traders began cutting the Bua thickets around 1805 and exhausted them by 1815. Whalers and bêche-de-mer ships then called only occasionally, leaving power in the hands of Fijian chiefs.
zh:
瓦努阿（Vanua Levu，意为「大地」）是斐济第二大岛，位于维提岛以北64公里。岛上山脊崎岖，东北部兰巴萨所在的三河三角洲及周边礁盘，为渔村提供鱼类和园圃土地。岛上约3100年前已有居民；1250至1350年间，太平洋海面下降30厘米，礁盘食物减少、地下水位降低，冲突随之加剧，居民迁往设防的山顶村落。1444年的瓦努阿由彼此竞争的酋长、长老和武士分统，山顶要塞俯临海岸登陆点与河口。

1643年，阿贝尔·塔斯曼成为已知最早望见瓦努阿岛的欧洲人。1789年，「邦蒂号」哗变后的威廉·布莱在逃亡途中经过该岛水域；1797年，詹姆斯·威尔逊率「达夫号」勘测这一带。1800年1月，美国双桅纵帆船「阿尔戈号」在斐济东南失事，幸存水手奥利弗·斯莱特在瓦努阿岛生活两年，后来把布阿湾附近出产檀香木的消息带到中国。约1805年起，商船涌入布阿湾砍伐檀香木，到1815年资源已近枯竭；此后只有捕鲸船和海参船偶尔到访，岛上权力仍掌握在斐济酋长手中。

en:
Te Urewera is the wall of steep, misty forest between the Bay of Plenty and Hawke Bay, a country of narrow ridges, the long lake of Waikaremoana and the sacred peak of Maungapōhatu. In its deep valleys live Tūhoe, the 'children of the mist', heirs both of Toi-te-huatahi, remembered among the first peoples of the island, and of the crews of the Mātaatua canoe; their forest had a name as a graveyard for invading war parties. Along the northern edge, on the Rangitaiki river mouths and the coast at Whakatāne and Matatā, dwelt their Mātaatua kin Ngāti Awa, descendants of the ancestor Awanuiarangi. In 1444 the coast and the plains belonged to Ngāti Awa, while behind them Tūhoe ruled the forest, living on its birds and timber.

The two peoples were often at war, yet the hills proved their common shield. In 1818 Te Morenga and Korokoro of Ngāpuhi swept south with muskets to raid Ngāti Pūkeko; Ngāti Awa and their allies fell back into the Urewera ranges and held Okahukura pā until reinforcements came, then drove the northerners off with heavy loss, a rare reverse for the raiders of the early Musket Wars. The victory bought only a little time: by 1821 the great Ngāpuhi chiefs Pōmare and Te Wera Hauraki were arming a war party to avenge it, while no European had yet ventured into the mist.
zh:
乌雷韦拉是横亘在丰盛湾与霍克湾之间的一道崇山峻岭，重雾密林、山脊逼窄，山中躺着长长的怀卡雷莫阿纳湖，圣山毛阿波哈图耸立于腹地。深谷中住着图霍埃人，即「雾之子」，他们既是岛上最早先民托伊特胡阿塔希的后裔，也承继马塔阿图阿号独木舟乘员的血脉；来犯的战阵每每葬身林中。北缘的朗伊塔伊基河口及华卡塔尼、马塔塔海岸，住着与他们同出马塔阿图阿的雅提阿瓦人，奉阿瓦努伊阿朗吉为始祖。1444年，海岸与平原属于雅提阿瓦人，身后的密林则归图霍埃人，林中有飞禽，也出木材。

两族虽屡有争战，群山却是他们共同的屏障。1818年，恩加普希人的特莫伦加与科罗科罗携火枪南下，袭击恩加蒂普凯科人；雅提阿瓦与盟友退入乌雷韦拉山区，坚守奥卡胡库拉山寨直至援兵到来，随即重创北来的劫掠者——这是火枪战争初期劫掠者少有的一场挫败。这场胜利只换来短暂喘息：到1821年，恩加普希的大酋长波马雷与特韦拉·豪拉基已在武装战阵图谋复仇，而此时还没有欧洲人走进这片雾中。
